title: Trump skeptical of NFL game in Paris as protests shatter France
description: French police have arrested thousands of violent protesters in recent weeks as French President Emmanuel Macron bans protests by “individuals or groups with no legitimate authority."
content:
President Donald Trump said he warned French President Emmanuel Macron that his immigration policies were "destroying France" as he raised concerns about unrest across Europe during an interview on "Sunday Morning Futures."
"I told Macron, when I first came in, I met him early. I said, 'You are destroying France. You're letting people come in that hate your country,'" Trump told Larry Kudlow.
Trump criticized France for allowing people into the country who he said opposed French culture and national identity. He also pointed to unrest in Spain and Italy while arguing that his administration's border enforcement policies had prevented similar problems in the United States.
"The people that are causing the problems are people that hate Spain and hate France and hate Italy," he said. "It's very interesting. Somebody said, ‘They hate their art, they hate the buildings, they hate everything about France. They hate the people. And they let them come in.’"
Macron said on Thursday that his government would move to ban protests organized by "individuals or groups with no legitimate authority" as he blamed "ultra-left groups" for the riots and looting that had spread across his country.
Trump's comments come after nearly 1,000 people were arrested in France on Saturday as nationwide protests resumed, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez. Violence also erupted in Rome and the Albanian capital of Tirana, where protesters set government buildings ablaze.
This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News Max Bacall.

title: Protests, marches unfolding across French cities as police seek to contain violence
description: Police and agitators are clashing in French cities including Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Lille and Nice, while anti-government demonstrations are unfolding across other parts of Europe.
content:
President Donald Trump questioned whether the NFL should have postponed Sunday's game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints as France grapples with another weekend of nationwide protests.
"I think maybe it’s looking like tomorrow is going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it," Trump told reporters Friday, according to The Associated Press. "I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match ... because France is really in trouble."
The matchup at Stade de France, just north of Paris, is scheduled to be the first regular-season NFL game held in France. The U.S. State Department has urged Americans attending to exercise caution amid the unrest.
Security concerns have already disrupted sporting events in the French capital, with a Steelers fan event canceled and a Paris Saint-Germain soccer match against Lyon moved to Monday at the request of police.
The Associated Press contributed to this post.

title: Trump in Georgia, Michigan this weekend ahead of 2026 midterm elections
description: President Donald Trump will continue his campaign blitz in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday, followed by a stop in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday, as he seeks to boost Republican candidates ahead of the 2026 midterm elections on Nov. 3.
content:
President Donald Trump announced Saturday that German automaker Audi is committing $4.2 billion to build a massive new manufacturing plant in Macon, Georgia, touting the investment as another major victory for American auto manufacturing.
"But today I'm thrilled to announce a massive auto manufacturing investment in the great state of Georgia by a fantastic company," Trump told supporters at his Georgia rally.
"Audi has just committed to invest $4.2 billion in nearby Macon, Georgia to begin the construction next month on a massive plant that will produce 200,000 cars a year," the president announced.
"Think of that. Think of that. 200,000 cars a year. That's incredible," Trump added.
Trump claimed the project would mark a historic milestone for the domestic auto industry.
"This will be the single largest investment in U.S. auto industry history, modern history," he said.
The president also touted broader investments in American auto manufacturing, saying the industry was experiencing a resurgence.
"58% of our auto business was gone. It's all coming back. And then some $40 billion and 30,000 new jobs," Trump said.
Trump credited Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick with helping secure the deal and invited Audi executives to join him onstage, including Audi CEO Gernot Döllner and Audi North America President Vito Paladino.

Patricia Krentcil recounted the bizarre encounter during an appearance on the "Light. Tan. Up." podcast alongside actor Tom Arnold, claiming U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents stopped her as she left a restaurant with girlfriends. CONTROVERSIAL ICE TACTIC ACTUALLY REDUCES UNINTENDED 'COLLATERAL' ARRESTS: FEDERAL AGENT "As we're walking out, the ICE people stopped me, and they asked me, 'Am I an American citizen?'" "Because I was so tan, they were about to handcuff me ... and take me away. God knows where," she alleged. Krentcil, whose unusually bronzed complexion has attracted national attention for more than a decade, claimed she feared being detained and transported to an unknown location. DHS CONDEMNS ROSIE O’DONNELL AFTER ‘DISGUSTING’ CLAIM THAT DETAINED IMMIGRANTS ARE RAPED IN ICE FACILITIES "Once you get in those trucks, you don't know where you're going anymore," she said. title: Brewers rally past chaotic late-game replay, premature celebrations to win first World Series game in 44 years
description: Christian Yelich's RBI triple sparked a 2-0 lead as the Milwaukee Brewers held off the Tampa Bay Rays in a dramatic World Series Game 1 finish.
content: For the first time since 1982, the Milwaukee Brewers have won a World Series game. The Brew Crew took Game 1 of the Fall Classic over the Tampa Bay Rays in a sweaty 3-2 ballgame. Down two, the Rays loaded the bases with one out in the ninth, but Liam Hicks grounded into what initially was ruled a game-ending double play. However, replay showed shortstop Cooper Pratt came off second base, instead making it a 3-2 game with runners on second and third and two outs. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Brewers had already ignited their fireworks, creating a chaotic, fog-filled scene, before Johnny DeLuca came to the plate and struck out to end the game. 2026 WORLD SERIES: HOW TO WATCH BREWERS AND RAYS AFTER SMALL BALL CARRIES THEM TO FALL CLASSIC The city of Milwaukee waited 46 years to see its team in the Fall Classic, and this year's Brewers wanted to stop wasting time. An RBI triple by Christian Yelich, followed by a William Contreras single, put the Brewers up 2-0 in the first inning. However, that was all they'd get for a while, as Nick Martinez settled down to get through five innings of work. The Milwaukee pitching, though, was just as good. Soon-to-be Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski held the Rays to just one run in his five innings, but certainly not without the help of some Rays baserunning blunders. Tampa Bay had runners on first and second with one out in the first, but Junior Caminero lined out, and Jonathan Aranda was doubled off at second to end the threat. In the fifth, Victor Mesa Jr. was caught stealing at third for the final out of the inning, a big baseball no-no. The Brewers matched that mistake with one of their own almost immediately, as nine-hitter David Hamilton made the first out at third in the bottom half of the frame trying to stretch a double into a triple. But they got a huge insurance run after some more typical Brewers small ball. In the seventh, Hamilton got a productive second out to get a runner into scoring position, and Jackson Chourio drove him in with an opposite-field, ground-ball single to make it 3-1. No team in the league went oppo and hit grounders at a higher rate than the Brewers in the regular season. title: Michigan Senate rivals clash over Muslim Brotherhood allegations as Rogers doubles down on El-Sayed
description: The Michigan Senate race heated up on "Special Report" as Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers clashed over war powers, Medicare-for-all and Muslim Brotherhood allegations.
content: Michigan Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed accused Republican rival Mike Rogers of questioning his loyalty to the United States during a heated Fox News interview Friday, while Rogers doubled down on allegations that his opponent has embraced the ideology of the Muslim Brotherhood. The candidates both spoke separately with Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier on "Special Report" in Detroit, 11 days before the Nov. 3 election. Baier pressed El-Sayed about a 2012 statement involving former Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, who was affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood. EL-SAYED, ROGERS CLASH OVER MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD, TRUMP AND GUNS: 5 FIERY DEBATE MOMENTS "No, no, no, let me just stop there," El-Sayed interrupted. "You are asking this question to raise a question about whether or not I have dual loyalties." Baier explained he was asking about allegations raised by Rogers' campaign. "I will be loyal to the Constitution of the United States," El-Sayed said. "Don't be Rogers' campaign," he continued. ABDUL EL-SAYED GROWS AGITATED WITH REPORTER AFTER BEING PRESSED ON FAMILY'S ALLEGED MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES "I'm asking a question," Baier replied. "Be a journalist," El-Sayed shot back. "I am," Baier responded. El-Sayed accused Rogers of making his Muslim faith a campaign issue, calling the suggestion "sad" and "beneath him." EL-SAYED'S PAST MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD COMMENTS RAISE RED FLAGS AS HE EYES POWERFUL ROLE The controversy centers partly on a 2012 letter that The Washington Free Beacon reported El-Sayed signed supporting decisions by then-Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, including calls to purge Egypt's police and media. El-Sayed has also faced scrutiny over social media posts from his half-sister describing their mother's alleged involvement in Muslim Brotherhood activism in the 1970s. He has denied personal or family ties to the organization and said he was raised by his father and stepmother. In an Oct. 17 Fox News interview, El-Sayed acknowledged that his sister-in-law was a plaintiff in a lawsuit challenging her alleged placement on a terrorist watchlist but insisted she had done nothing wrong. The FBI declined to confirm or deny her watchlist status. The lawsuit does not establish wrongdoing. Rogers rejected El-Sayed's characterization in his own interview. ROGERS WARNS MICHIGAN VOTERS AGAINST EL-SAYED’S ‘EXTREME’ AGENDA AHEAD OF ELECTION "I wore the uniform of the United States. Many in my family, including our son, wore the uniform of the United States so he can pray any way he wants," Rogers said. "It is not how he prays, it's how he thinks." Rogers accused El-Sayed of embracing the organization's ideology and portraying himself as a victim. "He has adopted the ideology of the Muslim Brotherhood," Rogers alleged. Baier noted that El-Sayed had denied ever belonging to the organization and pledged allegiance to the Constitution. "Does he disavow? Does he really say it?" Rogers responded. El-Sayed had explicitly disavowed the organization at an Oct. 17 town hall, answering, "Sure. Yeah, absolutely" when asked. The candidates also differed over the war with Iran, which El-Sayed blamed for rising gasoline and grocery prices. "We need a war powers resolution to end the capacity for this president to wage an illegal, unjustifiable war," El-Sayed said. Rogers defended the original rationale for military action but said he has urged President Donald Trump to end the conflict. "I've called for him to wrap it up. That's the right thing to do," Rogers said. Turning to Michigan's economy, Rogers said the state has lost 27,000 manufacturing jobs and faces some of the nation's highest auto insurance costs. He also raised concerns about education, claiming roughly two-thirds of fourth graders cannot read at grade level. Rogers defended Trump's influence in Michigan, pointing to his support among voters and crediting his trade policies with encouraging General Motors to bring Silverado pickup truck production back to the state. But the Republican acknowledged a disagreement with Trump over trade with Canada. "I've come out and said we shouldn't be doing the Canadian tariffs the way we are doing them," Rogers said. Baier also pressed El-Sayed over Medicare-for-all, and whether middle-class taxes would rise. "I'm fine with people keeping their private insurance if that's what they want, but I want guaranteed public insurance for everybody," El-Sayed said. Rogers disputed El-Sayed's position, arguing that Medicare-for-all would eliminate private insurance and raise costs for Michigan families. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP El-Sayed touted upcoming campaign appearances with former President Barack Obama and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., while questioning whether Trump would help Rogers in Michigan. With both Trump and Obama expected to campaign in Michigan over the weekend, the candidates are turning to their parties' most recognizable figures as they make their final pitches to voters ahead of Election Day.Fox News Digital's Leo Briceno contributed to this reporting.

An Israeli special operations veteran urged the United States and Israel on Friday to focus future military strikes on preventing Iran from rebuilding its nuclear and missile capabilities.
Aaron Cohen, founder of Gideon, told FOX Business' "Kudlow" that previous U.S. and Israeli operations had significantly weakened Iran's military infrastructure, but warned that Tehran could restore its capabilities without continued pressure.
Cohen pointed to reported activity at Iran's underground Eagle 44 military base and changes in the country's defense leadership as possible signs of rebuilding efforts. He argued that future operations should prioritize disrupting Iran's ability to replenish military equipment and infrastructure.
His comments come as President Donald Trump has raised the possibility of additional strikes against Iran following the November midterm elections, although no new military operation has been announced.

title: Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity celebrate upcoming wedding surrounded by family and friends at Mar-a-Lago
description: Fox News hosts Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity celebrated their upcoming wedding on Friday with a gathering of family, close friends and longtime colleagues at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida.
content: Fox News hosts Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity celebrated their upcoming wedding on Friday with a gathering of family, close friends and longtime colleagues at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida. The pre-wedding festivities brought together loved ones from different chapters of their lives for a special evening honoring the couple ahead of Saturday's ceremony. "My heart is overflowing with gratitude and joy," Earhardt said. "To celebrate this beautiful season of our lives surrounded by the people we love most is truly a dream come true. God has blessed us in more ways than we could ever imagine, and I am so thankful that He brought Sean and me together. Our families, our children and our precious friends mean the world to us and sharing this moment with them makes it even more meaningful. We are so excited for this next chapter and know that the very best is yet to come." Earhardt, co-host of the network's top-rated morning program "FOX & Friends" and Hannity, the host of FOX News Channel's "Hannity" and podcast "Hang Out with Sean Hannity," announced their engagement in December 2024 after Hannity proposed over Christmas at their home church in Florida. "Ainsley is an incredible person and I couldn't be happier or more grateful that God brought us together," Hannity said. "Faith, family and friendship are what matter most in life and having so many people we love and care about together to celebrate this moment means the world to us. We are incredibly blessed and I can't thank everyone enough for being part of such a special evening." Among those celebrating were Fox News Media CEO Suzanne Scott and FOX News President and Executive Editor Jay Wallace as well as Earhardt's fellow "FOX & Friends" co-hosts Steve Doocy, Lawrence Jones and Brian Kilmeade, along with numerous other Fox News personalities. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump were also in attendance, along with Eric and Lara Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his wife, Jeanette, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his wife, actress Cheryl Hines, Sen. Tim Scott, Sen. Darline Graham, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro, among others. "I've had a personal relationship with President Trump for over 30 years," Hannity said. "When Ainsley and I began planning this celebration, it was important to us that he could be part of this special time in our lives. We chose to host a party at Mar-a-Lago and paid fair market value for the venue. We are grateful that he and Melania could celebrate alongside our families and friends." Other guests included longtime friends of the couple, including ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith, country music legend Lee Greenwood, podcast host Sage Steele, television personality Jillian Michaels and Steve and Andrea Wynn. Both Earhardt and Hannity have longstanding careers at Fox News. Earhardt joined in 2007 and became a co-host of "FOX & Friends" in 2016 while Hannity has been with the network since its launch in 1996. The evening reflected the importance of faith, friendship and the relationships the couple has built over the years as they look forward to exchanging vows.

title: Tyler Robinson hearing ends without trial date set, prompting fiery plea from Erika Kirk's lawyer
description: Tyler Robinson's Utah trial for the assassination of Charlie Kirk still has no start date as prosecutors and defense attorneys clash over timing.
content: PROVO, Utah — Tyler Robinson, the 23-year-old Utah man accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk at a Turning Point USA event last year, still doesn't have a trial date after a Utah judge listened to oral arguments from both sides — and a lawyer for Kirk's widow — about how much time they think they'll need and when they'd like to start. Robinson, wearing a light gray suit, uncuffed and unshackled, did not address the court. He spoke quietly with attorneys Richard Novak, Kathy Nester and Staci Visser during breaks, at one point handing Visser a note. Judge Tony Graf Jr. said he had planned to set a trial date at the end of the hearing but needed more time after questioning both sides about their expected timelines and commitments in previously scheduled trials on other cases. Jeffrey Neiman, an attorney for Kirk's widow, Erika, pleaded with the court to speed things up. Robinson did not enter a plea until last month, nearly a year after being charged. LAWYERS FOR CHARLIE KIRK'S ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON WANT CAMERAS BANNED AFTER REPORT ON TAXPAYER BURDEN Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family. "Every day of delay adds to uncertainty, invites speculation and that erodes confidence in this system," Neiman said at one point. The roughly three-hour hearing included several interruptions due to technical difficulties with WebEx, with Robinson defense attorney Michael Burt and an attorney for Kirk's parents, Robert and Kathy, attending remotely. Utah County prosecutors had floated Jan. 31, 2028, as their preferred trial date but said they could be ready in October 2027. TYLER ROBINSON TO FACE TRIAL IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION AS JUDGE KEEPS DEATH PENALTY ON TABLE Visser said that pretrial litigation "builds upon itself," and given that there are over 31,000 pieces of discovery and "8 million" artifacts of digital evidence, lawyers will need time to file motions to compel, file subpoenas, etc. "Discovery review is foundational," she said. "It impacts everything else." As a result, she said, the state’s proposed January 2028 trial is "not practical." The defense had asked for a "soft target" date in the third quarter of 2029, citing large amounts of discovery and other trial preparations — as well as trial commitments in other cases. Among those, one directly conflicted with the prosecution's desired start date, a federal racketeering case defense attorney Novak has scheduled for Jan. 10, 2028. Both sides agreed that setting a trial that would run through the holidays could put potential jurors and witnesses in a bind. ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR "Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family," Neiman said. Neiman noted that only about 5% of federal cases actually make it to trial and said the Kirk family would be happy to write to the federal judge and ask for the January trial to be rescheduled to clear up Robinson's defense attorney. Under Utah's state constitution, victims and their representatives have a right to a speedy resolution to their case. Erika Kirk is the court's designated victim's representative. Novak told the court that the trial's start date had been "set in stone" and argued against rushing things along in the case against Robinson. "The reality is rushing to trial does not lead to closure. It does not lead to finality. It leads to mistakes," he said. UTAH PROSECUTORS ASK JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN DELAY TACTICS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE Graf expressed concern that if he does not set a date soon, additional conflicts could arise. GOT A TIP? Neiman, who is primarily a criminal defense attorney, has repeatedly asked the court to speed things up. title: NASCAR legend Tony Stewart's return to the Truck Series ends early with big crash at Talladega
description: Tony Stewart's Talladega Superspeedway return ended just 17 laps in after a massive nine-car wreck triggered by Stewart Friesen's loose truck.

NASCAR FANS PACK INTO TALLADEGA SUPERSPEEDWAY AHEAD OF SUNDAY'S JACK LINKS 500 RACE Unfortunately, his time on track was even shorter. The race got off to a good start for Stewart. He qualified 29th, but was able to gain 11 positions in the first 15 laps. "Yeah, it’s just a racing deal," Stewart said, per the Associated Press. "That’s part of it. Stewart (Friesen) couldn’t go anywhere. He had an issue, and he’s stuck in the middle. So he was doing the best he could to hang onto it, and just everybody around him got caught up in it." Well, maybe we'll get to see Stewart back in the Truck Series at some point next season. There aren't any concrete plans, but he's certainly due for some good luck. title: McMahon plans to 'fire' herself from a job, striving to show Congress that the Department of Ed is not needed
description: Linda McMahon is shifting Department of Education functions to the departments of Labor and Treasury through interagency agreements as proof of concept.
content: U.S. Education Secretary Linda McMahon doubled down on closing the Department of Education (ED) as planned to demonstrate to Congress that the federal agency she leads is no longer necessary. "Signing these interagency agreements means, in fact, that the Department of Education is contracting with these agencies to perform the functions that they've been given," McMahon told Fox News Digital. "The first big block of work was transferred over to the Department of Labor." Throughout his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump promised to eliminate the ED, later signing an executive order directing his administration to begin dismantling the agency. MCMAHON EMBARKS ON FOUR-STATE TOUR TO PUT LOCAL LEADERS AND PARENTS 'BACK INTO THE DRIVER’S SEAT' OF EDUCATION As part of that effort, the Department of Labor (DOL) is taking on a major role in the day-to-day administration of adult education, family literacy and career and technical education (CTE) programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) and the Perkins Act. While Labor manages operational duties, the Department of Education retains statutory responsibilities and oversight while shifting services to states and grant recipients. "It started first with CTE — Career and Technical Education — then K–12 and finally higher education as well," McMahon said. McMahon explained that she wants to show lawmakers that federal support for students won't falter without a standalone Cabinet department. "I've asked Congress with this proof of concept in these interagency agreements: 'Let me prove to you that it works,'" she said. "Ultimately, Congress has to vote if we do close the Department of Education, and if I, in fact, am able to fire myself. Hopefully, they will vote [for it], because I believe the outcome will be better for students, and that is the goal. That is certainly the president's goal." TRUMP ADMIN URGES RETURNING EDUCATION TO STATES, CITING $3 TRILLION OF TAXES SPENT AND POOR PROFICIENCY SCORES The agency took another major step by partnering with the Department of the Treasury, which agreed to take over key operations related to federal student loans and collections on defaulted debt. The student loan partnership with Treasury and the workforce initiative with DOL are part of a broader series of interagency agreements. According to Department of Education officials, the goal is to demonstrate a "proof of concept" to Congress that essential federal education functions and funding flows can be successfully reallocated across executive branch agencies without disruption. "I call it my proof of concept to show Congress that it works, that the money still gets to schools and to students where they need it," McMahon told Fox News Digital. "Some of the programs in the Department of Education were being duplicated in other agencies or handled better elsewhere," McMahon added. "So, let's be efficient. Let's make sure the money gets where it needs to go, let's measure that by student outcomes and let's hold teachers and administrators accountable for what they're doing." Andrew Gillen, a higher education policy research fellow at the Cato Institute, told Fox News Digital that shifting major core duties like student loans and formula grants marks a substantial change from previous interagency agreements, which historically focused on minor administrative support. McMahon previously argued during the government shutdown that the ED acts primarily as a pass-through entity for federal money, contending that its day-to-day functions are nonessential. "Congress appropriates the funds. The funds come through the Department of Education, and some of that funding still goes to other agencies to get to students and schools," McMahon told Fox News Digital. "Primarily, the money was passed through the Department of Education to then get to the states and local authorities for education." TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS HEAD START BUREAUCRACY IN MOVE ADVOCATES SAY PUTS PARENTS IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT ED announced earlier this year that the agency moved out of the Lyndon B. Johnson Department of Education building so the Department of Energy could move in by August. The move is what the officials call "a prudent step to save hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars and further reduce the federal education bureaucracy." The Trump administration is also seeking to reduce the department's footprint by returning more power to the states. The ED launched a new process allowing states to seek greater flexibility in using federal education funds and reducing administrative burdens. Iowa became the first state to participate in the effort. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Department of Education sent states a letter in July 2025 encouraging them to apply for the waiver, which would give state education officials more discretion over federal dollars and reduce compliance costs.

title: Vanessa Trump 'finally cancer-free,' she says after health battle in emotional video with daughter Kai
description: Months after revealing her breast cancer diagnosis in April, Vanessa Trump announces she is cancer-free in an emotional video with daughter Kai Trump.
content: Vanessa Trump revealed she is now cancer-free after battling breast cancer, sharing the emotional health update in a new video with her daughter, Kai Trump, months after publicly announcing her diagnosis. The 19-year-old granddaughter of President Donald Trump shared a preview of the conversation on Instagram during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, revealing that her mother, who's the ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr., was diagnosed in April. "And my mom was diagnosed with breast cancer in April, so we thought we'd share her story and how she was diagnosed, how she overcame it," Kai said in the video. KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’ To finish the social clip, Vanessa shared the news that she is now cancer-free. "And it came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free," Vanessa said. "Love you!" Kai responded. The video also features former Fox News medical contributor Dr. Nicole Saphier, who discusses the importance of breast cancer awareness and early detection. "It feels different for everyone," Saphier said. "The reason I like social media talking about breast cancer is because it's reminding people that it is common." In her Instagram caption, Kai said she sat down with her mother and Saphier to discuss Vanessa's cancer journey, prevention and early detection. She also announced that the full conversation would be released on YouTube the following day. Vanessa, the mother of five, first revealed her breast cancer diagnosis in May. "I've recently been diagnosed with breast cancer," Vanessa wrote at the time. "While this isn't news anyone expects, I'm working closely with my medical team on a treatment plan." PRESIDENT'S 19-YEAR-OLD GRANDDAUGHTER, PICTURED IN HOSPITAL AFTER MEDICAL PROCEDURE She revealed that doctors had performed a procedure earlier that week and thanked her family for their support. "I am staying focused and hopeful while surrounded by the love and support of my family, my kids, and those closest to me," she wrote. The announcement prompted support from Ivanka Trump, who wrote, "Praying for your continued strength and a swift recovery. Love you mama." In June, Vanessa said she was recovering from surgery and preparing to begin the second stage of treatment, Fox News Digital reported. Kai Trump later opened up about the emotional experience in an August interview with Fox News Digital, shortly after beginning her freshman year at the University of Miami. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "There was definitely, there was a lot of crying in, like, the week leading up," she said of the days before leaving for college. "We would just be driving, and then we'd just start crying together." At the time, she said her mother was improving after treatment. "My mom, she's doing a lot better," she said. "Kind of after treatment, she wasn't feeling very good. Just like how treatment will make you feel … but she's getting a lot better now." Kai described the extra time she spent with her mother over the summer as a "blessing in disguise." "I was able to spend extra time with her that I would normally probably spend on the golf course," Kai said. "It was nice to spend those extra hours with her throughout the day before going to college." Fox News Digital's Sophia Compton and Paulina Dedaj contributed reporting.

title: Wrestling legend Ric Flair, 77, rushed to Tampa hospital after fall outside bar, head injuries: report
description: Ric Flair was reportedly rushed to a Tampa hospital by ambulance after falling outside a bar, suffering facial cuts and a possible concussion.
content: Pro wrestling legend Ric Flair was reportedly rushed to a Florida hospital after falling outside a bar. According to TMZ, Flair was at a Tampa bar when he walked outside and fell, injuring his face and possibly suffering a concussion. TMZ says Flair cut his head and eye, which was bleeding, and was loaded into an ambulance. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The reported fall came hours after Flair announced that he would be unable to attend a scheduled appearance in Seattle due to a blood clot in his leg. "My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First. Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening," Flair said on X. "We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice." Flair said he is slated to have surgery on the affected vein, "[w]hich My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward." "Please Know This Decision Was Not Made Lightly. I Am Truly Sorry For The Inconvenience And Disappointment, And I Am Incredibly Grateful For Your Patience, Understanding, And Continued Support. I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support," Flair added. Tampa Fire Rescue told OutKick and Fox News Digital that it responded to a fall outside the establishment, and an adult male was taken to a local hospital — the department did not name Flair, saying they could not "provide any patient particulars due to HIPPA guidelines." Flair, 77, has battled health and alcohol issues over the years. EX-WRESTLER PAC'S SUDDEN DEATH CAUSE REVEALED BY COOK COUNTY MEDICAL EXAMINER'S OFFICE Flair has been in and out of wrestling for the last few years. His so-called "Last Match" took place in 2022 — a tag-team match with his then-son-in-law, the wrestler known as Andrade, against Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal. He later revealed he passed out twice during the match. Flair made his All Elite Wrestling debut in 2023 and was a brief part of Sting’s final professional match at AEW Revolution, where Sting and Darby Allin took on the Young Bucks. He was a World Championship Wrestling world heavyweight champion eight times, a National Wrestling Alliance world heavyweight champion nine times and a WWE champion twice during his career. title: Trump says NFL 'could've probably postponed' Paris game as France protests stretch police thin

content: President Donald Trump is skeptical about the National Football League continuing to hold its first-ever game in Paris amid protests. The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are still set to kick off Sunday despite the civil unrest and a Paris Saint-Germain soccer game the same day being postponed. Paris police requested a postponement of the PSG game because police and security resources are stretched thin due to mass protests, ongoing civil unrest and France's first NFL game happening in the region, per multiple reports. I would've said the NFL could've probably postponed that match... France is really in trouble," Trump told reporters on Friday. Trump then took a shot at Democratic policies. "That's what happens when you go left. That's what happens when you allow unlimited numbers of people into your country from very unfriendly countries." The NFL has insisted multiple times this week that Sunday's game in France will be safe to play and safe for fans to attend amid civil unrest. However, the Steelers canceled a fan event in the area. According to a league source, the topics discussed at the two-hour gathering included security for the game, the readiness of the Stade de France, where the game is to be played and the growth of flag football in France. title: ESPN posts propagandistic headline about Trump, LeBron and national anthem
description: LeBron James was caught practicing his golf swing during the national anthem before his 76ers debut, prompting Trump to call it a "TOTAL DISGRACE."
content: NBA star LeBron James was shown practicing his golf swing during the playing of the United States national anthem before his 76ers debut on Tuesday. Later in the week, President Donald Trump called James' conduct a "TOTAL DISGRACE" on social media. The story itself is quite simple. James practiced his golf swing during "The Star-Spangled Banner." Trump criticized him for it. And yet, the headline writers at ESPN apparently didn't see it quite as clearly. According to ESPN.com on Thursday, "Trump criticizes LeBron James for not standing still during the national anthem." Take a look: Here's the full clip of James during the national anthem: Describing what James did as merely "not standing still" is an awfully charitable characterization. He wasn't shifting his feet or adjusting his uniform. He was practicing his golf swing while the national anthem played. The framing minimizes the conduct at the center of the controversy. ESPN suggested James' behavior was innocuous and Trump's criticism was excessive. That was the point. ESPN must feel it has an obligation to protect James. The headline writers must have also agreed James was wrong. Otherwise, there would be no reason to sanitize it as James merely failing to "stand still." At least athletes who kneel during the anthem generally claim that they are doing so as a form of protest. James offered no such explanation. He simply sought to make a mockery of the anthem. It also wasn't the first time. James was caught practicing his swing during the national anthem on Christmas Day last year. There’s something cringe about a star American athlete who previously criticized NBA executive Daryl Morey for supporting Hong Kong protesters now behaving this way during the U.S. national anthem. At this stage of his career, the NBA also has to ask how much James still benefits its brand. James turns 42 in December. He has averaged 15 points per game through his first two games this season and, unsurprisingly at his age, is a shell of his former self. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP His basketball legacy is secure. James is one of the greatest players in NBA history. But he has become a net negative through his declining play and consistently anti-American messaging.

title: Colorado high school volleyball players faced alleged benching threat amid trans athlete dispute
description: Two Colorado high school volleyball players were allegedly threatened with benching after discussing a transgender athlete in their program.
content: Two Colorado high school volleyball players were threatened with benching after discussing a transgender athlete in their program, according to a parent complaint alleging the girls were ultimately allowed to play on condition they stop discussing the issue. The school district that oversees the school, Jefferson County Schools, is currently under Title IX investigation by the U.S. Department of Education. A screenshot of an email, obtained by OutKick, from Dakota Ridge High School's head volleyball coach to a parent says the parent's daughter would miss a match over reports of alleged bullying. The screenshot does not identify the actual words that were used. "Over the past several days, we have received multiple reports alleging that your daughter used language toward teammates that could be characterized as bullying," the message bearing the coach's name states. "As a result, your daughter will not be eligible to participate in today’s match." EX-SJSU VOLLEYBALL COACH FILES NEW LAWSUIT ALLEGING RETALIATION FOR TRUMP SUPPORT, RELIGION AMID TRANS SCANDAL The message says the volleyball program emphasizes character, respect and how players treat one another, describing the reported behavior as falling short of its standards. It offers to discuss the matter with the parent after the match. Meanwhile, Tanna Donalson, whose daughter was cut from the program in August, wrote in an Oct. 6 email to district that her daughter had reported two varsity players were told they would be benched after discussing the situation among friends. Donalson said she was subsequently informed that, after the players’ parents met with the coach and the athletic director, the girls were permitted to play on condition they not discuss the issue again. The email was seen by OutKick in a copy of a Title IX complaint Donalson submitted to the Education Department. "[The daughter] reported that Mr. Zeman pulled three varsity volleyball players aside and told two of them they would be benched for today’s game because they had discussed this issue amongst themselves. According to the account relayed to me, four friends had been discussing privately what they had learned, and one reported the conversation to a teacher. I was further informed that, after the two players’ parents met with the athletic director and Mr. Zeman, the players were permitted to play on the condition that they not discuss the issue again," Donalson wrote. "Please determine what was said, the basis for the proposed benching, and whether participation was conditioned on refraining from discussion of or support for our complaint." Lindsay Datko, founder of the parent advocacy group Jeffco Kids First, also said she had reviewed emails concerning the threatened discipline. "We have seen emails showing that girls were threatened to be benched because they were expressing their frustration in a very adolescent manner," Datko told OutKick. But Datko added the coach backed away from the threatened benching. EDUCATION DEPARTMENT RESCINDS BIDEN TITLE IX RULE, RESTORES TRUMP-ERA REGULATIONS Jeffco Chief Legal Counsel Julie Tolleson acknowledged Donalson’s report in an Oct. 6 email response. "She can include these matters in her review, though we won’t be able to discuss with you any disciplinary or other action involving any other student," Tolleson wrote, referring to the district’s Title IX coordinator. A day earlier, Tolleson had instructed Donalson to report any retaliation or harassment related to her complaint. "District policy prohibits retaliation," she wrote. In response to OutKick, Jeffco defended its policies and cited student privacy restrictions. Its statement did not address the alleged condition on the players’ participation or explain what remarks prompted the proposed discipline. The school district provided the following response in full: "We recognize that fairness in athletics, student safety, privacy, and equitable opportunities for students are important issues for our community. "In accordance with Colorado state law (including the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act), Jeffco Public Schools is committed to providing a safe, welcoming, and inclusive environment for all students. Jeffco’s policies ensure that every student, regardless of gender identity or expression, has equal access to educational programs, facilities, and district-sanctioned activities. "High School Athletics: Jeffco Public Schools operates high school athletic programs under the governing bylaws of the Colorado High School Activities Association (CHSAA) and Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act. "District Policies on Equal Educational Opportunities Jeffco Public Schools' nondiscrimination policies—including Policy AC (Nondiscrimination/Equal Opportunity) and related guidance—remain fully active and in effect. "Under federal law (FERPA) and state privacy regulations, Jeffco Public Schools cannot confirm, deny, or comment on the gender identity, administrative records, or athletic participation of any individual student. "We are navigating a complex national climate, but our local commitment remains steady: all students deserve to feel safe, respected, and supported in Jeffco Public Schools. We support and value all members of our Jeffco community, including our transgender students and staff members. "Jeffco Public Schools is committed to cultivating environments where all students, staff, families, and members of our community are accepted, respected, and feel that their voices and perspectives are valued. While people may have differing views on Jeffco policies and the laws that inform them, we all share a responsibility to ensure our words and actions reflect care and respect for others. We ask everyone in our community to respect individual privacy and remember that real children and families are at the heart of these conversations. "Jeffco will continue to follow all state laws and regulations with respect to our schools, athletic programs, and students’ rights. Our responsibility - and steadfast commitment - remains to serve every student and ensure that our schools are places where all students can learn, grow, and thrive." Donalson’s own complaint centers on the roster decision that ended her daughter's junior-year school volleyball season. Her daughter, 17, had played in the program during her freshman and sophomore years. Her mother said coaches encouraged the setter to learn right-side hitting before ultimately cutting her. In an Aug. 13 email, the coach said the change was intended to give her daughter another opportunity to demonstrate her skills. He said other athletes showed greater consistency in setting, defense, serving, decision-making and other areas, and described the roster decisions as a collective coaching evaluation. WASHINGTON STATE'S HIGH SCHOOL SPORTS LEAGUE PUTS ONUS FOR TRANS ATHLETE CONTROVERSY ON STATE LAWS "She competed for a spot, other athletes ultimately demonstrated more consistency in the areas needed, and she was beat out," he wrote. The coach is also her daughter's history teacher. Correspondence documents Donalson’s request for a different placement and the school’s offer of a teacher change for second semester. Donalson responded that she wanted to give the situation a few weeks before deciding. She explicitly told school officials she was not alleging that classroom retaliation had occurred. Asked whether her family had experienced retaliation since speaking publicly, she said she had reported that some students made comments to her daughter, but their family had received substantially more support than opposition. "We have received far more support than we have anything opposite of that," she said. The U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights issued findings March 13 that the district violated Title IX through its policies on girls’ athletics and access to female facilities and overnight accommodations. OCR issued a notice of impending enforcement action June 26. Jeffco disputes those findings. The district sued Education Secretary Linda McMahon and the Education Department on July 28, challenging the enforcement actions and arguing that the federal demands conflict with Colorado law and threaten its funding. That lawsuit concerns the district’s broader policies, rather than a determination about Donalson's daughter's roster decision. Colorado voters will consider Proposition 134 on Nov. 3. The measure would require school-based teams to be designated for biological males, biological females or mixed participation, with eligibility tied to those categories and an exception allowing females to join male teams when no equivalent female team is offered. "I am not against the trans community or any community for that matter," Donalson said when asked about the measure. For Donalson and her daughter, she says the impact of the situation has been "deep and wide," and has jeopardized her daughter's dreams of playing in college. "She still has those dreams, it's a little difficult to figure out how we're going to achieve them, as this is her junior year, and arguably her most important year, because that is when you start communicating with coaches," Donalson said. "And right now we have nothing to share." She said her daughter still plans to play club volleyball and pursue college opportunities. But losing her school season has affected how she experiences the sport. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Every time she plays, she just remembers all that’s transpired here, and it just has taken a little bit of the joy of the sport out of it for her," Donalson said.

title: Irish politicians disavow ‘demeaning’ PSA warning grandparents not to hug family without asking consent
description: A viral ad in Ireland warning against grandparents hugging grandchildren without asking for consent sparked outrage and was pulled by the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre.
content: An ad released by the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre (DRCC) in Ireland that urged grandparents to ask for consent before hugging their grandchildren sparked international controversy after it began airing last month and has since been removed. In September, an ad from the DRCC’s We-Consent campaign went viral for showing grandparents greeting their grandchildren. One grandchild appears receptive to a hug, while the other does not. A narrator says, "Not everyone wants a hug, even from the people who love them. Awkward? Maybe. Important? Absolutely." The ad has since been removed and criticized by politicians from multiple parties in Ireland. The BBC reported that Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan of the Fianna Fáil party, whose department funded the campaign, announced the video has been removed after discussion with the DRCC, and declared, it "does not represent the views of the Government." IRISH PM SAYS IRELAND 'NOT OVERRUN' BY MIGRANTS, LEGAL MIGRATION TIED TO ECONOMIC SUCCESS "It was both inappropriate and demeaning to grandparents and has been removed by DRCC following my officials engagement with them," O'Callaghan said. "While it is vital to ensure that people understand the concept of consent when it comes to sexual relationships, this video did not advance that aim and in many ways was counterproductive." Irish Sen. Gareth Scahill of the Fine Gael party blasted the video as a waste of public funds. "What's concerning here is public money has been used to fund an ad which, at best, has been ill-thought out, and at worst is offensive and potentially damaging to our older population," Scahill said. "The issue of consent is a very serious one, and I acknowledge the important work the Rape Crisis Centre and other agencies do every day to advocate for all victims of rape and sexual violence, including children. "But this publicly funded social media video is a million miles off the mark." TRUMP SAYS HE WOULD 'LOVE' TO SEE IRELAND UNIFIED AS ONE NATION Scahill also asked, "What's next? Will we need to sign consent forms at arrival halls in Dublin, Shannon, Knock and Cork airports this Christmas before we can greet family members?" The DRCC told Irish broadcaster RTE in a statement, "We-Consent is a long-term campaign as part of Dublin Rape Crisis Centre's prevention work to increase the awareness and practice of consent in Ireland. "We created three videos premised on the idea that boundaries should be respected from an early age and to respect others' boundaries too," the organization added. "We are going to remove the videos from our social media channels while we reflect on whether they are having the positive effect we want them to have." title: Knee treatment without surgery offers lasting pain relief for 80% of arthritis patients, study finds
description: A non-surgical knee osteoarthritis treatment uses dissolvable gelatin particles to block excess blood vessels, reducing inflammation without implants, researchers say.
content: A non-surgical procedure that temporarily blocks extra blood vessels in the knee is offering lasting pain relief for people with knee osteoarthritis. In a clinical study of 194 patients, 80% of them reported significant reductions in knee pain that lasted for at least a full year after receiving the treatment. The findings highlight a potential alternative for millions of adults with chronic joint pain who have outgrown pain medications or steroid injections — but who want to avoid total knee replacement. WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY FIGHT 7 SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEMS BEFORE THE POUNDS EVEN COME OFF Osteoarthritis wears down joint cartilage and causes the body to grow unnecessary new blood vessels around the knee, according to Mayo Clinic. These extra vessels increase inflammation and irritate surrounding nerves, making daily movement painful. The procedure, known as genicular artery embolization (GAE), addresses this directly. By temporarily clogging excess blood vessels, doctors can reduce inflammation and quiet pain-sensing nerves without major surgery or permanent implants. Because the treatment uses microscopic gelatin particles that dissolve over time, it leaves no foreign material behind. If widely adopted, GAE could provide a repeatable, low-risk way for patients to stay active and preserve joint function longer, researchers say. "We saw a significant drop in pain and a significant increase in function." "For many patients with knee osteoarthritis, there is a real treatment gap today," said Florian Nima Fleckenstein, M.D., deputy head of Interventional Radiology Campus Mitte, Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin, in a press release. "Our study demonstrates that GAE using rapidly resorbable gelatin-based microspheres is a safe, minimally invasive therapy that provides meaningful pain relief and functional improvement in participants with osteoarthritis-related knee symptoms for at least 12 months." ALZHEIMER’S RISK LINKED TO COMPOUND FOUND IN POPULAR JOINT HEALTH SUPPLEMENTS During GAE, doctors use real-time X-ray guidance to steer a thin, flexible tube into the blood vessels surrounding the knee joint. Then they release tiny, dissolvable gelatin particles into specific vessels to slow excess blood flow to the inflamed areas. Across 239 total procedures performed on 194 study participants, none experienced severe complications. Only 6.7% reported mild side effects, such as brief skin discoloration or minor bruising, issues that resolved on their own. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "In our cohort, we saw a significant drop in pain and a significant increase in function, including sports and recreation and daily activity," Fleckenstein said. "Most importantly, their quality of life significantly increased." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER In addition to feeling less pain, participants experienced gains in daily mobility. Patients reported easier walking, climbing stairs and bending, while overall quality-of-life scores more than doubled over the 12-month follow-up period. Limitations of study While the results are promising, researchers note several important limitations. First, the study did not include a control group receiving a mock or placebo procedure. Without a comparison group, it is difficult to isolate the physical benefits of the dissolvable particles from potential placebo effects, the researchers said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Second, the study tracked patients for only one year. Further research is needed to determine how long the pain relief typically lasts and how often repeat treatments might be required. The procedure does not rebuild lost cartilage or reverse structural joint damage. Larger, randomized trials are currently underway to confirm these early findings. title: France on edge with 70,000 police deployed for unrest as authorities probe suspected terror attack near Paris
description: Emmanuel Macron blames ultra-left groups for seditious acts as UNEF and Yellow Vest protesters vow to rally despite police rejecting permit requests.
content: A suspected terrorist attack near Paris Friday added to tensions across France as the nation prepares for more potential violence Saturday. Seventy thousand law enforcement officers, along with helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons, will be deployed across France as President Emmanuel Macron’s government tries to ward off another weekend of violent protests. "The strategy adopted for the coming days is to ban protests requested by individuals or groups with no legitimate authority," Macron said ahead of the weekend after canceling his planned trip to Nigeria and Senegal originally scheduled for next week. "The rules are simple, and I think they're just common sense," Macron added. "The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations in the coming days." FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC' "Where trade unions submit requests to hold demonstrations, prefects will examine them in accordance with the law," he added, "but alternative routes will be proposed" to protect city centers, businesses and public buildings. Adding to security concerns, a suspected terrorist attack occurred in the city of Trappes, west of Paris. A 39-year-old man was arrested by police after one person was killed and four others, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in what was originally said to be a "relatively random" shooting. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has since told local media, "The motive may be racist. The investigation is ongoing, but this is clearly a terrorist crime." The AFP reported the suspect appeared to fire randomly from a vehicle, and the mayor told reporters the dead victim and at least one of the wounded were "of African origin." Macron said "the nation is standing with" the victims of this "terrible ordeal." FRANCE COULD FACE EVEN WORSE DESTRUCTION WITH SECOND WEEKEND OF PLANNED RIOTS, STATE DEPT WARNS Ahead of Saturday's protests and after acknowledging that police had "lost control" during last weekend's unrest, Nuñez, the interior minister, said his ministry is "ready for tomorrow. We will be extremely vigilant, extremely firm, and we will let absolutely nothing pass." Reuters reports that the Union Nationale des Étudiants de France, or UNEF, one of the nation’s oldest student unions, has said its planned rallies will go on as scheduled despite police rejecting their permit requests. Police have so far only approved a union demonstration in Paris, Reuters reported, while denying requests from UNEF and the "Yellow Vest" movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018. Macron also took aim at those he says are behind the violence, saying, "Last Saturday, we had political and seditious acts by ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic." Earlier this week, Fabian Vanhemelryck, secretary general of the Alliance Police Nationale union, said political figures deserved blame because of "those who excuse the inexcusable, justify violence and prefer to overwrite police officers rather than condemn those who attack them." He also said the "state that abandons its police officers in the face of increasingly uninhibited violence, while demanding that they accept, remain(s) silent and continue(s) to hold the line." Major French institutions, like the Louvre and the Musée d'Orsay, will be closed in anticipation of Saturday’s planned protests, and 24 Metro stations across Paris will be closed. A Ligue 1 soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais, scheduled for Sunday night at Parc des Princes in the capital, has also been postponed to Monday evening. The NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints, scheduled for Sunday afternoon at Stade de France just north of central Paris, is still set to be played as scheduled, yet some weekend events around the game have been canceled. title: Trump says judge is 'desecrating' Charlie Kirk's memory amid fight over assassination trial date
description: Trump slammed the Utah judge in the Charlie Kirk assassination case, saying the trial should take a month, not years, as a 2029 date was proposed by the defense.
content: PROVO, Utah – President Donald Trump criticized the judge overseeing Charlie Kirk's assassination case in Utah on Friday, saying he's doing a "terrible job." "The judge in the Charlie Kirk case is doing a terrible job! This case should be tried within a month, not three years — and it should be over with! The judge is desecrating the memory of the Great Charlie Kirk, while taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to. The whole Country is mocking him and our 'Legal' System. JUSTICE FOR CHARLIE!" Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. Trump's comments come after Tyler Robinson's defense team proposed a tentative trial start date in the third quarter of 2029. In a court filing, Robinson's defense team cited the large volume of unreviewed evidence and the complexities of jury selection as justification for the proposed timeline. ERIKA KIRK RIPS 'ABSURD' 2029 TRIAL TIMELINE FOR CHARLIE KIRK'S ALLEGED ASSASSIN His defense team argued that setting a firm trial date now would create a "false precision" and could jeopardize Robinson’s constitutional rights, stressing that the death penalty case requires heightened consideration because, as they argued, "death is different." "From the point of view of defense counsel, appointment to a capital case brings with it a slew of responsibilities that apply in no other context," the defense memorandum states. JUDGE IN ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON'S CASE EXPLAINS WHY DEATH PENALTY REMAINS ON TABLE WATCH: Armored truck believed to be carrying Tyler Robinson arrives at court Robinson’s attorneys argued that they must review evidence related to both his guilt and potential sentence before trial, making it premature to set a firm trial date. "It will create unrealistic expectations for the public and the victim's representative, it may cause counsel for both parties to give short shrift to constitutionally required activities, it may rush this Court to deliberate upon and enter rulings on important and complex pretrial motions, and it may jeopardize Mr. Robinson's right to a capital proceeding that has the utmost reliability," the defense stated. SEND US A TIP Prosecutors said they expect to be ready for trial by Oct. 4, 2027. Erika Kirk asked the court to schedule a trial for the earliest practicable date in 2027, saying Robinson's legal team's proposed timeline is "grossly out of line" with comparable cases. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "Every additional day of delay carries the weight of all that Charlie's murder has taken from his family, especially his two young children who were just three and one year old when their father was murdered and would be seven and five years old by the time a verdict is handed down under the Defense's proposed schedule," the filing said. WATCH: Tyler Robinson’s lawyers want 2029 trial to ‘avoid the inevitable,’ former prosecutor says Former federal prosecutor Fred Tecce told Fox News Digital that he thinks Robinson's team pushing for a 2029 trial is a delay tactic. "There's a legal term. It's called kick the can down the road. It is just done for the purposes of delay and I think it's wholly inappropriate," Tecce said. "Society has a right to have these things adjudicated quickly, honestly, openly and by the rules and regulations." "It is the job of a defense lawyer to delay and obfuscate," he said. title: Team USA's Olympic hockey heroes reunite as Jack Hughes' Devils land goalie Connor Hellebuyck in blockbuster
description: Team USA's Olympic gold medal heroes Connor Hellebuyck and Jack Hughes are now NHL teammates after a blockbuster trade to the New Jersey Devils.
content: Team USA's two Olympic heroes are now NHL teammates. Goalie Connor Hellebuyck, who stopped 41 of 42 shots against Canada in the gold medal game, was traded to the New Jersey Devils, where he will now team up with Jack Hughes, who netted the golden goal in overtime. Hellebuyck and Hughes were the stars who helped the United States bring home its first gold medal in Olympic hockey since the Miracle on Ice in 1980. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE He becomes the latest high-profile American Team USA star to leave a Canadian NHL team for one in the United States. In June, the Ottawa Senators dealt captain Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers, where he joined his brother, Matthew. In December, the Vancouver Canucks traded star defenseman Quinn Hughes, a brother of Jack and teammate Luke, to the Minnesota Wild. There has long been speculation that Quinn, who scored an overtime winner against Sweden in the quarterfinals, wants to join his brothers in New Jersey. The process to trade Hellebuyck became messy, especially after the goalie went public with his request to leave the Winnipeg Jets in September. title: WNBA players, coaches refuse to explain national anthem absences amid mounting criticism
description: Natalie Nakase and Gabby Williams cite a pregame routine for WNBA Finals anthem absences, while Rhyne Howard responds to criticism over Team USA.
content: Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase called her team’s national anthem absences part of its pregame routine Friday, but did not explain who established that routine or why. OutKick had been trying to ask players and coaches about the anthem absences since Game 1. But after attending all 13 formal press conferences during the first three games without being called on, OutKick had to wait until Friday’s media availability ahead of Game 4 to ask those questions directly. "What do you do during those 90 seconds that you’re off the court?" OutKick asked. ATLANTA DREAM, GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WNBA FINALS GAME "I’m with my staff, so I’m focused on my plays. That’s what I’m doing right now," Nakase responded. Golden State’s public relations staff then moved to the next reporter. OutKick did not get an opportunity to ask why those preparations needed to happen during the anthem, rather than before or afterward. The Valkyries and Atlanta Dream have been off the court during the national anthem before all three WNBA Finals games. In each game, players left shortly before the performance and returned seconds after it ended. Earlier in the exchange, OutKick had asked Nakase whose decision it was for the team to be absent and why it followed that routine. "We’re two years in," Nakase said. "That’s been part of our pregame." Asked again who decided and why, Nakase said, "I really don’t know." "I understand your question," she added. "I’m not trying to, you know, not answer your question. It’s just part of our pregame." Gabby Williams denies protest, cites longstanding routine Valkyries forward Gabby Williams was born in Nevada, holds U.S. and French citizenship and represents France in international competition. OutKick asked whether Golden State’s absence during the national anthem was a protest. "No," Williams said. Asked why the team was off the court during the U.S. national anthem, she responded: "That’s been the routine for like, seven years now." A Valkyries public relations representative then said, "Next question." Golden State is in its second season, and Williams joined the franchise this year. She played for Chicago from 2018–20 and Seattle from 2022–25, making the Valkyries the third WNBA team she has played for. Her seven-year reference would span her time with all three franchises, though she did not explain how the routine began or whether it was the same at each stop. VANCE CONDEMNS 'DISGRACEFUL' WNBA NATIONAL ANTHEM WALKOUTS, SAYS PLAYERS SHOULD SHOW MORE GRATITUDE There is a political history behind WNBA teams staying off the court during the anthem. During the 2017 Finals, Los Angeles Sparks players voted to remain in the locker room as a show of solidarity with the Black Lives Matter movement, according to ESPN’s reporting at the time. Atlanta also published players’ union messaging about anthem protests in its Aug. 2, 2020, game notes. The statement said "the anthem does not represent freedom, justice and liberty for all Americans" and that players would "continue to protest" in various forms. A protest can become a routine without ceasing to be a protest. Williams denied that Golden State’s absences are a demonstration, but saying the practice has lasted for years does not explain its purpose. Neither Williams nor Nakase explained who established Golden State’s routine or why it puts players off the court specifically during the anthem. Rhyne Howard responds to Team USA criticism Dream guard Rhyne Howard was asked about calls to exclude players from Team USA if they do not stand for the national anthem during the WNBA season. Riley Gaines and former Georgia state Rep. Vernon Jones have argued that athletes’ conduct during the anthem should carry consequences when they seek to represent the United States internationally. Howard represented the United States at September’s FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, where she stood for the national anthem. "I mean, are we just talking about these three games or are we talking about the full season?" Howard asked. OutKick clarified that the question concerned both. "I don’t think I’ve been on the floor for the national anthem for any of my tenure in Atlanta, so if that’s what people are gonna look to nitpick for then so be it," Howard said. "But as far as competing for your team, when I go put on USA jersey I’m out for the national anthem every time, there’s no doubt about it." "Yes, I love the country that I play for and I love what we have here," she added. Howard also questioned the focus on the anthem during the WNBA Finals. OutKick followed up: "Is there a reason you’re not on the court for the anthem?" Howard and an Atlanta public relations representative both responded, "Next question." OutKick also sought to ask Angel Reese, Howard’s Dream and Team USA teammate, about the criticism. Most players and coaches were available throughout the 30-minute media window. Reese and Atlanta coach Karl Smesko were each required to be available for only 15 minutes. Reporters could jump in with questions during the other interviews Friday, but Atlanta public relations staff selected the questioners during Reese’s availability. OutKick was not called on and did not get an opportunity to ask her. Karl Smesko declines further comment on anthem Smesko was asked why his team had left the court shortly before each Finals anthem and returned shortly afterward, and whose decision that was. "We’re just kind of focused on the Finals," Smesko said. OutKick followed up by asking whether he had any comment on the anthem and his team’s absences on the league’s biggest stage. "No," Smesko said. An Atlanta public relations representative then moved the session to the next question. WNBA rulebook provision remains, but policy questions persist The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook says players, coaches and trainers are to "stand and line up in a dignified posture" along the sidelines or on the foul line during the national anthem. The Associated Press reported Tuesday that the league suspended its anthem protocols in 2017. The provision remains in the 2026 rulebook, and OutKick has asked the WNBA to clarify its current requirements and enforcement. The WNBA, NBA and both teams’ front offices have not responded to OutKick’s emailed requests for comment about the anthem absences. Friday’s responses came from players and coaches during media availabilities. The coaches and players have described a pregame routine that includes jogging off the court just prior to the national anthem and returning seconds after it ends. It's time for a new pregame routine.

title: France's top soccer team obeys police order to move Sunday match; Saints, Steelers owners meet with Macron

title: Brazil’s rapid election count puts spotlight on voting security ahead of US midterms
description: Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro leads Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva heading into Brazil's runoff as the voting system his father attacked may hand him victory.
content: SAO PAULO, Brazil— About 125 million Brazilians voted Oct. 4 on machines that print no paper ballots. Less than four hours after polls closed, the country knew its presidential election was headed to a runoff between conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro and leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. That process has been in place for over three decades, and Brazilians have become accustomed to its speed, simplicity, accuracy and routine. The system is robustly audited, completely disconnected from the Internet, and is the largest digital voting system deployed on the planet. Eleven days before the U.S. midterms, Brazil’s system, analysts say, could offer Americans a more secure way to vote. The system has been widely praised and was also mentioned in President Donald Trump’s 2025 executive order on elections, where he cited Brazil’s biometric voter identification as an example. Yet Brazil’s count runs partially on the kind of paperless machines that the president has vowed to scrap. STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS One citizen, one vote: digitally checked Over the years, Brazil merged federal, state and municipal databases into a digital voting record, whereby voter identity, eligibility and single ability to vote can (and usually must) be verified biometrically. Nearly 9 in 10 voters unlock the machines with a fingerprint. Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, or TSE, which designs the machines and oversees elections, says there has been no proven fraud since their 1996 debut. The 499,248 machines used on Oct. 4 never connected to the internet. Their software was open to inspection by parties, universities and watchdogs for 11 months before being digitally signed and sealed in public. Last December, the Brazilian government invited a record 149 outsiders to try to break the system; evaluators concluded nothing they found could alter results or reveal how anyone voted. On election day, randomly drawn machines are fed paper ballots on camera as federal auditors and foreign observers watch and specifically track results. Meanwhile, at closing, every machine used at every polling station prints its tally, which is then posted in front of the polling place with a QR code, so anyone can check it against the national count. In an email to Fox News Digital, TSE said each file’s digital signature "confirms that the result was produced by the electronic voting machine registered for that polling station." Karina Stange Calandrin, a political scientist and professor at Instituto Brasileiro de Mercado de Capitais (IBMEC), says the system combines three traits rarely found together: voting is electronic, votes hashed to voter eligibility are stored locally in the machine and tallying is automated. "It is an extremely secure and safe system. The machines never connect to the Internet and even the central database system used to transmit tallied votes to TSE must match results issued physically and locally by each individual machine without human interference," she said. Corrupting it, she added, would require breaking the seal of each machine and installing software that wouldn’t match the TSE’s version, automatically disqualifying its tally — a scale of collusion so large that it "simply could not pass undetected." COLOMBIA'S 'EL TIGRE' SECURES PRESIDENCY AS LEFTIST RIVAL FINALLY CONCEDES DEFEAT The machines passed their toughest political test in 2022, when former President Jair Bolsonaro, now serving a 27-year sentence for plotting to overturn his 2022 defeat, spent years attacking their credibility without evidence. Bolsonaro is presently serving time under house arrest. This year, for the first time, a Bolsonaro appointee ran the TSE: Justice Kassio Nunes Marques. Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, finished first with 47% to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 45%. The machines at the center of the senior Bolsonaro’s controversy may yet hand victory to his son. Florencia Ferrer, CEO of e-stategiapublica, which has audited elections in 17 countries, has no doubt the Brazilian system is the most modern and secure in the world. "In India votes are electronic, but each voter gets a printed version of their vote to take home, which weakens voter safety and augments coercion rates," she says, adding that Estonia’s internet voting and the Philippines’ electronically tallied paper ballots carry their own risks. An engineer from the University of São Paulo’s Polytechnic School who audited the machines in 2014, and declined to be named due to the sensitive nature of his work, agreed. "While no system is completely infallible... we have found no traces of tampering, wrong-doing or malicious intent," he told Fox News Digital. Still, some defend higher scrutiny. Security researchers say a clean record is not proof enough, and the Carter Center said voters should at least see a printed version of their ballot deposited into a separate area of the machine; otherwise, results integrity rests on software alone. Germany’s top court ruled in 2009 that voters must be able to check their ballot without expert help, effectively barring a Brazilian-like system. Brazil’s machine has traveled mostly on loan to countries in Latin America, Africa and Asia. Paraguay adopted it permanently in 2006, with machines that now print each individual vote. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It’s obvious Washington and the remainder of the U.S. are way behind both technology as well as security when it comes to polling on voting day," Ferrer said. U.S. elections are run in thousands of local jurisdictions under 50 sets of state rules and about 30% of 2024 ballots came by mail, which is slower to process. Brazil has one national election authority, compulsory voting and no mail-in ballots. Brazilians will vote this coming Sunday on Oct. 25. The winner is expected to be known and certified in under five hours. "The question is not whether Brazil has invented a perfect voting machine. No voting system is perfect. It is whether democracies can combine the speed and consistency of digital tabulation with independent verification, public scrutiny and rules that citizens across the political spectrum have reason to trust," Ferrer said.

An artificial intelligence watchdog is calling for stronger safeguards after reports that major U.S. banks detected unauthorized AI agents accessing customer accounts, warning the technology poses a growing threat to Americans' financial security.
Russ Walker, executive director of Humans First, criticized Big Tech companies for promoting AI-powered banking tools despite concerns about their ability to control autonomous systems.
"Big Tech claims their systems are reliable enough to integrate into banking, to have control or access to people’s hard-earned dollars. This report shows, once again, that the AI companies can’t even control their own technology," Walker said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

The remarks follow an Axios report that major banks have detected unauthorized third-party AI agents accessing customer accounts, with some attempting actions apparently independent of users' instructions.
Humans First has proposed an America First AI policy framework calling for independent testing of high-risk systems, mandatory reporting of major AI incidents and greater accountability for technology developers.
"It is past time for our elected leaders to act. We need common-sense guardrails that will protect the American people and the institutions we rely on," Walker said.
