title: Personal attacks fly as Sullivan, Peltola spar over corruption, character and controversy
description: Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola traded sharp attacks over corruption, staffing allegations and military spending in their fiery final Alaska Senate debate.
content: Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, and former Rep. Mary Peltola traded blows Thursday night in the final debate of a Senate race that has surprised some political observers with how close it has become. The latest Fox News Power Rankings rate Alaska’s Senate race as a "toss-up," meaning neither party has an edge. Alaska has historically favored the GOP, though the party’s margin of victory has narrowed in recent cycles. Sullivan and Peltola clashed over energy costs, the Iran war, Social Security reform, healthcare policy, military spending, allegations of misconduct and fish, among other topics, but a handful of exchanges stood out from the rest. GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING ‘You must be getting dizzy up here’ Throughout the debate, Peltola attacked Sullivan for being a D.C. insider and using his position to enrich himself and his allies. Sullivan attempted to rebut her claims by pointing to Peltola’s extensive lobbying career after her time in office, accusing her of cashing in by selling influence. "My opponent keeps talking about corporate greed again; she defines the rigged system in D.C.," Sullivan said. "There's nothing more rigged than a member of Congress getting fired and then immediately walking through the revolving door to cash in. She made almost half a million last year as a D.C. lobbyist selling her knowledge of D.C. She did it when she left the state legislature; she set up a lobbying firm." "You're walking through the revolving door so much, you must be getting dizzy up here," he quipped. Peltola responded by saying that her lobbying work was done to benefit Alaskans and highlighting how Sullivan has gotten wealthier since coming to Washington. "Dan's been in D.C. for 12 years and gotten richer every single one of those years. That's the corruption that Alaskans are really sick of, and that's the corruption that I'll fight against. Dan went to D.C. with $3 million. He now has $8 million," she said. "Dan's doing just fine watching out for himself." ‘Questions beforehand?’ After Peltola responded to a question about how she would work to improve affordability for Alaskans if elected to the Senate while appearing to read from a piece of paper, Sullivan questioned whether she had received a copy of the debate questions in advance. "Here's a moderator question, we weren't supposed to get these questions beforehand, were we?" Sullivan asked. "No, sir," one moderator responded. title: Trump admin sued over alleged illegal collection of sensitive voter data from 47 states
description: A lawsuit alleges DHS collected voter files from 47 states and combined them with commercial datasets, violating federal privacy safeguards.
content: The Trump administration is being sued over its efforts to collect and analyze sensitive voter data from across the country. The complaint, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., on Thursday, alleges the Department of Homeland Security has obtained voter files from at least 47 states and handled the data in a way that violates federal law. DHS' secretive probe of the voter data, which includes a policy to combine it with commercial datasets, ignores federal safeguards and the privacy rights of millions of Americans, the lawsuit says. The case was brought by the League of Women Voters, the Electronic Privacy Information Center and the League of United Latin American Citizens and is the latest legal challenge to President Donald Trump's efforts to combat noncitizen voting. STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS The president has purported repeatedly argued that noncitizen voting poses a serious threat to election integrity, although studies and prosecutions have found documented instances of noncitizens casting ballots to be rare. The administration has repeatedly sought a greater federal role in voter eligibility and election administration, areas traditionally overseen primarily by states under the Constitution and federal law. Federal courts have repeatedly rejected administration efforts to compel states to turn over voter information. The new lawsuit alleges the administration has obtained and processed voter records from at least 47 states, even though officials in 30 states have previously refused federal demands to turn over voter information. The complaint urges the court to declare the administration's collection of voter data illegal, block DHS' policy and order the agency to delete and stop using the voter information it has already obtained. The lawsuit comes less than three weeks before Election Day, and the administration continues to pressure states, alleging they are not doing enough to purge noncitizens from their voter rolls. "At President Trump’s direction, DHS remains committed to providing states with the information necessary to protect the integrity of America’s elections and ensure their voter rolls are accurate," a DHS spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "These investigative efforts are conducted diligently and professionally in accordance with the law. Identification and investigation of aliens who vote in our elections provides an essential guarantee in the authenticity of our election results. DHS will pursue each and every illegal voter to the fullest extent of the law," the spokesperson continued. TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN IN ELECTION INTEGRITY FIGHT AS STATES GAIN NEW VOTER ROLL TOOL CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The administration sued California election officials on Thursday, arguing they failed to act quickly enough to review names the federal government identified as "likely" noncitizens. The Justice Department asked a judge to block the state from counting mail-in ballots from those individuals unless their eligibility can be confirmed. The California secretary of state's office said it was given only 48 hours to review roughly 20,000 names and said the federal government had not provided the underlying evidence or methodology supporting its claims. The Justice Department's lawsuit, however, says U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services conducted a "multiagency and multilevel review" and determined with "high confidence" that roughly 20,000 people on California's voter rolls were likely noncitizens. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Denver Broncos survive ugly offensive night to beat Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime
description: Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard overtime field goal after a crucial Sam Darnold interception sealed the Denver Broncos' 17-14 Thursday night win.
content: Broncos kicker Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal in overtime to elevate Denver to a 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night. Seattle got the ball first in sudden death and faced a third-and-7 from its own 28. Sam Darnold tried forcing a throw into double coverage along the sideline, losing sight of Denver cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian. McMillian read it the entire way, stepped in front for the pick, and set the Broncos up at Seattle’s 43-yard line. Broncos HC Sean Payton ran the ball three straight times to milk the clock and center the hash, and Lutz did the rest. BRONCOS THROWBACK ORANGE CRUSH UNIFORMS MEET SEAHAWKS THROWBACK ROYAL BLUE IN RARE NFL COLOR VS COLOR GAME With clock management blunders headlining last week's slate of NFL action, it was refreshing to watch a coach who knows how to properly win a game. For the first twenty minutes, Payton’s script was dialed to perfection. Denver dominated time of possession and built a 14-3 halftime lead behind two methodical touchdown drives finished off on short plunges by J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Then came the second half. Denver’s offense looked like a unit that had never practiced together. Bo Nix finished the night with only 107 passing yards and zero downfield threat. Seattle mounted a fierce fourth-quarter comeback, pulling within 14-11 on a George Holani touchdown and a two-point conversion pass from Darnold to Rashid Shaheed. After Denver stalled out again with barely a minute left, Jason Myers nailed a 34-yard field goal with three seconds on the clock to force overtime. If you sat through the final two quarters of that Denver offense, you are owed an apology. The only reason Denver didn't get blown out was Vance Joseph's defense. The Broncos dropped him five times and generated turnovers whenever Seattle threatened to take control. Nik Bonitto stripped wideout Rashid Shaheed in scoring territory, Kris Abrams-Draine pulled down a fourth-quarter interception, and McMillian delivered the dagger in overtime. Seattle put up 353 total yards and Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 yards, but three turnovers wiped it all out. Bo Nix has plenty to clean up, and Payton gets a 10-day mini-bye before hosting the Arizona Cardinals to figure out how to move the ball past the line of scrimmage. title: Brewers officially end Dodgers dynasty with ridiculous 6-4 comeback in game four to complete NLCS sweep
description: Shohei Ohtani's 428-foot three-run homer gave the Dodgers a 4-0 lead, but the Brewers' unlikely heroes erased it all to complete an NLCS sweep.
content: The 2026 NLCS was a complete mismatch, though, not in the way many fans expected. Despite winning 103 games in the regular season and employing a series of players unexpectedly having the best years out of their career, many believed the Milwaukee Brewers were big underdogs heading into the series. But through the first three games, it was the Los Angeles Dodgers who looked like an overmatched small market franchise flailing against the big-budget Brewers. Milwaukee, riding a combination of impossibly good relief pitching, exceptionally, uh, unexpected outcomes on balls in play, home runs, and a penchant for turning every ball put in play into an out, took a commanding 3-0 series lead into game four on Thursday night. In game two, they went 6-14 with runners in scoring position without a single hard-hit ball. In game three, they scored five straight runs after falling behind entering the seventh inning to coast home with a 6-2 win. Game four then, set up an opportunity for Milwaukee to reach their second-ever World Series and first since 1982. For the Dodgers, it was the first of four win-or-go home games to try and save their dynasty and win a third straight championship. For a few minutes at least, it seemed like they'd cruise toward forcing a game five on Friday night. Against Milwaukee opener Shane Drohan, the Dodgers put together a quick rally. Kyle Tucker led off with a single, forcing Brewers manager Pat Murphy to go to his bullpen and bring in Dustin May. Teoscar Hernandez singled Tucker to third, and after Max Muncy struck out, Andy Pages finally came through with a runner in scoring position, lacing a single up the middle to give LA a 1-0 lead. May got Kiké Hernandez to fly out, bringing up the Dodgers' struggling superstar, Shohei Ohtani. Ohtani, who hadn't driven in a run in the postseason, hadn't hit a home run in nearly two months, and had been clearly battling multiple health issues, promptly destroyed a 1-1 pitch at 113 mph and 428 feet to make it 4-0 LA. You could see how much it meant to Ohtani and the Dodgers with the rare show of emotion afterward. But as always, in this NLCS, the Brewers superteam offensive machine battled right back. In the fourth, Brice Turang worked a one-out walk, and William Contreras crushed a ground-rule double to left field. Jake Bauers, who until recently was one of the worst hitters in professional baseball, followed it with another ground-rule double to right field. While the Dodgers struggled with runners in scoring position this series, the Milwaukee superteam took advantage of every opportunity. And why not? With superstar players like Bauers and Contreras, who was 9% better than league average offensively in 2026. In the fifth, they pulled even. Sal Frelick worked a one-out walk, then stole second. The unremarkable offensive player, David Hamilton, continued his exceptional run by driving in Frelick with a single and raising his postseason batting average to .500. But that's what unbeatable superteams do, they come back from 4-0 in two innings behind the best players in baseball, Jake Bauers and David Hamilton. Sure enough, the Brewers untouchable bullpen immediately got to work, getting a shutdown inning as JoJo Romero got Ohtani, Mookie Betts, and Freddie Freeman in order on just 12 pitches. In the sixth? The offensive juggernaut sprung into action. Garrett Mitchell, facing elite lefty reliever Tanner Scott, crushed a homer to right field, playing small ball and just making contact instead of trying to hit for power. Mitchell had two home runs against lefties in years worth of major league hitting, then proceeded to hit two homers off of Blake Snell and Tanner Scott in back-to-back nights. The Dodgers 4-0 lead, erased in a few minutes by the unstoppable force of Milwaukee's unbeatable offense. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. In the sixth, the Dodgers got a one-out double from Kyle Tucker, but the Dodgers did what they do best: go hitless with runners in scoring position to waste the opportunity. Ashby though, wearing the correct uniform, got Ohtani to strike out on three pitches, and Mookie Betts to ground out to shortstop to end the inning. At that point, LA was once again 2-9 with RISP, the Brewers were 2-5. Amazingly, the Dodgers did it again in the eighth. Will Smith doubled to left, advancing to third on an error from Sal Frelick. Once again, LA had the tying run at third base with just one out, and once again, the single greatest bullpen ever assembled in the history of professional baseball clamped down. Because Ashby knew that allowing hard-hit balls is simply playing the game the right way. That's how you reach the World Series, and Milwaukee did it. The Brewers have shown how you ruin baseball, develop superstars like Garrett Mitchell, sign the best free agents available like Jake Bauers, use Cy Young caliber pitchers like Shane Drohan, Dustin May, JoJo Romero and Aaron Ashby to shut down talented offenses, and listen when your manager tells you to hit home runs or put the ball in play to the correct spot, instead of making outs. For Los Angeles, it's a depressing end to what seemed like a dynasty. In 2024 and 2025, the breaks, the clutch hitting and the quality pitching went their way. title: FBI returns 'Most Wanted' fraudster to US after India arrest in alleged $600K SNAP food stamp scheme
description: FBI Director Kash Patel announced Manjit Singh Bedi, accused of stealing over $600,000 in SNAP benefits in Tacoma, has been returned from India.
content: A fugitive accused of stealing more than $600,000 in federal food stamp benefits has been returned to the United States after being arrested in India last month, FBI Director Kash Patel announced. Manjit Singh Bedi, one of the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters, was wanted on federal charges stemming from an alleged Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme at a grocery store in Tacoma, Washington. "BACK IN THE U.S. - Manjit Singh Bedi, one of the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters, arrested in September in India," Patel posted on X. Patel highlighted the FBI's recent success in bringing fugitives back to the United States. EXCLUSIVE: FBI'S FIFTH MOST WANTED FRAUDSTER CAPTURED AFTER ALLEGED SNAP SCAM SUSPECT ARRESTED IN INDIA "This is the latest in an unprecedented stretch of success in bringing high-value targets back to the United States through strong partnerships with our foreign law enforcement counterparts," Patel said. "Over the past 20 months, we’ve secured 260 extraditions and removals — an increase of more than 70% compared to the previous 20-month period," he added. According to federal officials, Bedi allegedly defrauded the U.S. government of at least $600,000 through a SNAP fraud scheme between March 2024 and June 2025 while operating an Asian grocery store in Tacoma. MILLION-DOLLAR SNAP FOOD STAMP FRAUD SCHEME IN WALZ'S BACKYARD SPARKS OUTRAGE: 'CRUEL JOKE' The FBI said Bedi allegedly swiped SNAP recipients' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards, provided cash instead of eligible food purchases and kept roughly half the benefits for himself. After being indicted in connection with the scheme, Bedi allegedly drove to Canada before fleeing to India. A federal arrest warrant charging him with violating the conditions of his release was issued on May 21, 2026. Patel said Bedi is now one of six fugitives captured through the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters program since the list was created three months ago. FBI ADDS 2 FUGITIVES TO 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST AMID HISTORIC $6.5B HEALTHCARE TAKEDOWN: PATEL "This marks yet another significant moment for the historic FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters program," he said. Bedi, a naturalized U.S. citizen, was previously the subject of an FBI reward offering up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction. Patel said Bedi will now face justice in the United States for his alleged crimes. "Thank you to our outstanding partners for their assistance in this case," Patel wrote. title: Less than 2 years after coaching college hoops in Florida, Karl Smesko leads Atlanta Dream to WNBA Finals
description: Karl Smesko left Florida Gulf Coast's beach campus after eight 30-win seasons to chase the title he could never win there with the Atlanta Dream.
content: Karl Smesko enjoyed notable success during his time coaching the Florida Gulf Coast women’s basketball team. But rather than remain at the college level, where he had built a powerhouse at FGCU, Smesko chose in pursue a new challenge in the WNBA. When Smesko arrived at FGCU, the program competed in Division II. By the time he left to become the next head coach of the Atlanta Dream, the Eagles had established themselves as one of the premier programs in Division I women’s basketball. Under Smesko, FGCU routinely led the nation in 3-pointers made. The Eagles also recorded eight 30-win seasons and advanced to the NCAA tournament 10 times with Smesko at the helm, but he never captured the ultimate prize: an NCAA Division I championship. Perhaps the call about the opportunity in Atlanta came at just the right time for Smesko. He may have accomplished nearly everything possible at FGCU, effectively reaching the program's ceiling. ATLANTA DREAM ADVANCE TO WNBA PLAYOFFS SEMIFINALS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2018 WITH GAME 2 WIN Perhaps Smesko realized that his long-sought dream of hoisting a championship trophy would require him to step outside his comfort zone and take a chance with the actual Dream at the professional basketball level. So far, Smesko’s gamble has worked out. He has guided Atlanta to back-to-back 30-win seasons, and after a first-round exit last year, the Dream have swept their first two opponents in the 2026 postseason to reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The championship he was never going to get at FGCU is now four wins away, with the title series against the favored Golden State Valkyries set to begin on Saturday. "As good as we were at Florida Gulf Coast, the odds were very stacked against us to make that type of championship run," Smesko said. "In the pros, I definitely thought there was more of an opportunity. It’s a more equal playing field to win the whole thing and that was appealing to me." GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES ERASE 16-POINT DEFICIT, STUN DALLAS WINGS TO REACH WNBA SEMIFINALS The 2026 Finals will feature a matchup of second-year coaches: Smesko in Atlanta and Natalie Nakase in Golden State, which is in just its second year of existence. Smesko is quiet in many ways, and fiercely loyal. title: Katie Zacharia addresses brevity of first press briefing, defends legal credentials after criticism
description: Katie Zacharia defended her debut White House press briefing and addressed California bar exam scrutiny during interview with Sean Hannity.
content: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said that she did her "very best" during her first briefing as she defended herself against criticism surrounding her legal credentials on "Hannity" Thursday. The Pepperdine Law graduate made her White House briefing room debut on Tuesday, just days after President Donald Trump announced her appointment on Friday, leaving her with what she said was little time to prepare for the high-profile role. "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference," she told host Sean Hannity. "With very little prep time, I received briefing materials in the morning of Tuesday." TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY FACES FIRST MAJOR TEST AS WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING ROOM ENTERS NEW ERA Zacharia was heavily scrutinized for taking only three questions during her roughly 14-minute briefing, much of which she spent touting the Trump administration’s accomplishments ahead of the midterm elections. HOCHUL'S OFFICE MOCKS KATIE ZACHARIA WITH AARON RODGERS INJURY POST DESPITE GOVERNOR'S PRESS SECRETARY SCANDAL She pushed back on criticism of her performance, saying she was on the job for less than eight hours before stepping behind the podium. She also challenged criticism that she fielded questions exclusively from conservative-leaning news organizations. "Given the fact that I'd been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day," Zacharia said. FEDERAL JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TO RESTORE WHITE HOUSE ACCESS TO CNN, MS NOW AND POLITICO "I took several questions and I think it's been mixed because they've said I only took questions from conservative outlets. However, the Daily Mail is not known to be a conservative outlet or friendly to conservatives, so I do challenge that narrative." Zacharia delivered a piece of major breaking news during her debut, that the Trump administration had asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign from her ambassador role. "I was able to deliver breaking news, which I do believe was the right thing to do as the press secretary," she said. The scrutiny surrounding Zacharia’s debut was compounded by questions about her legal credentials after The Wall Street Journal reported that she had failed the California bar exam. TRUMP NAMES LEAVITT SUCCESSOR AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION — AND SHE'S NO STRANGER TO MAGA Hannity challenged Zacharia over social media posts in which she had been identified as an attorney. "There's a report out tonight that showed 15 social media posts where you identify yourself as an attorney," Hannity asked the press secretary. "I think they were retweets, and I corrected the record and said that there's not endorsing the title. They were retweets of a title that had been given," Zacharia responded. Zacharia revealed that after failing the bar the first time after graduating law school, she did not take the test a second time. "I graduated Pepperdine, got married in the same week, and we had all intent to move out to China," she explained. "I had already preregistered for the bar exam and... during the summer, I knew I would be living in China and the results of the bar were inconsequential, and I sat for it because I didn't wanna have a withdrawal status." DANA PERINO SHARES HOW SHE SECRETLY PUSHED BACK AT REPORTERS DURING WHITE HOUSE BRIEFINGS "When I went to go engage in media and give legal analysis, I consulted attorneys and legal professionals as to whether or not they agreed that I could be labeled a lawyer, both because I had a valid juris doctor from a good law school, a reputable law school, Pepperdine Law School, and in conjunction with the fact that I did have actual substantive legal experience." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP After facing days of intense backlash, including from comedian Jimmy Kimmel, who compared Zacharia’s intelligence to that of a kindergartner, she vowed to continue fighting. She said she hopes to develop stronger relationships with members of the White House press corps and have more substantive interactions with reporters going forward. "I would love to build a relationship with all of those members of the press corps so there is a substantive component to us having an ability to interact," Zacharia said. "And I will be very prepared, Sean, and I will step up to the duty that President Trump has asked me to as press secretary."

title: Trans neo-Nazi accused of plotting Hindu temple massacre, will receive hormone treatment in jail: officials
description: A transgender 19-year-old alleged neo-Nazi plotted an attack on a Hindu temple, but the firearm malfunctioned and a coworker's tip led to an arrest.
content: A transgender 19-year-old who authorities say identified himself as a neo-Nazi allegedly plotted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple outside Chicago, but a tip from a coworker helped authorities thwart the attack, according to police. Alexandros Paporakis, of Palatine, was arrested on Sunday after allegedly plotting to open fire at a Hindu temple in Aurora, a suburb of Chicago, Palatine Police said at a news conference on Thursday. Paporakis faces one felony count of making a terrorist threat and one felony count of unlawful possession of a weapon. A Cook County judge has ordered Paporakis held without bond and has put a jailhouse healthcare order into place, saying that the teenager receives hormone injections for gender transition and is being treated for ADHD, depression and anxiety, according to NBC Chicago. NEVADA TRANSGENDER SUSPECT WITH MASSIVE WEAPONS CACHE ACCUSED OF LAS VEGAS TERRORISM-RELATED THREATS Prosecutors allege Paporakis drove to the Hindu temple in Aurora armed with a modified rifle and about 300 rounds of ammunition and equipped with body armor and other tactical gear. Authorities said Paporakis intended to carry out a shooting, but returned home after the rifle malfunctioned. After arriving home, the suspect searched the internet trying to learn how to unjam the gun and allegedly called a colleague informing them of the intent to carry out a mass shooting, according to police. Paporakis' coworkers at Taco Bell reported to Mount Prospect Police that they had received a suspicious message that day from Paporakis, leading police to obtain a search warrant and detain Paporakis before the suspect could return to the scene to carry out the alleged attack. Authorities praised those who reported the threat and encouraged others who come across something suspicious to report it to law enforcement. MALL OF AMERICA TERROR PLOT THWARTED; SUSPECTED ISIS SYMPATHIZER ARRESTED, FBI ANNOUNCES "I want to praise and offer my personal, sincerest thanks to the individual who stepped forward in many successful disruptions by law enforcement and potential acts of violence or terrorism attacks. It is a single, courageous member of the public who comes forward to prevent attacks," FBI Chicago Field Office acting special agent in charge Lucas Rothaar said at a press conference on Thursday. Police said they identified a red Acura registered to Paporakis after receiving the tip. Surveillance video showed the suspect in the vehicle entering the parking lot at the Hindu temple at 12:25 p.m. before exiting a few minutes later. Paporakis was later observed driving to a residence on Rand Road in Palatine shared with the suspect's mother. Police executed a search warrant and found a rifle, a loaded magazine, hundreds of rounds of rifle ammunition and other tactical gear in Paporakis' possession. Police also found what they described as an eight-page manifesto, which authorities said detailed the alleged attack and Paporakis' White supremacist views. The writings "expressed words of hate, violence, superior race and mass shooting of Indian people. [Paporakis'] hatred was against Jewish people, African-Americans, Indians, and 'non-white' people," according to police. title: Armed bystander fatally shoots suspected teen gunman after 3 children, 1 adult killed at Oregon school: feds
description: Three children and a teacher were killed after a gunman forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, by firing at locked doors.
content: Three children and an adult were killed in a shooting at an Oregon elementary school Thursday, and the suspected gunman is also dead, shot by an armed good Samaritan. The shooter was a 16-year-old Bend resident armed with a shotgun who was killed by an armed bystander with a concealed carry permit, federal law enforcement sources told Fox News. The bystander "definitely prevented more deaths," one source said. POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD The children killed at Silver Rail Elementary School were ages 5, 8 and 11, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said during an evening news conference. A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to St. Charles Bend with critical injuries. The shooter forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors, Krantz said, citing the initial investigation. A "community member" saw the shooter enter, pursued him into the building and engaged him, according to Krantz. Officers arrived within three minutes of the first emergency call. Moments later, an officer reported that the community member had shot the suspect. "Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead," Krantz said. "They cleared the school to ensure there were no additional threats, and then rendered emergency aid to the victims." Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek praised school staff, parents and first responders, along with the community member "who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life." "Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well," Kotek said. REPORTED SHOOTING AT VIRGINIA ELEMENTARY SCHOOL 'CONTAINED,' SHERIFF'S OFFICE SAYS Krantz said he did not yet have details about the bystander’s firearm or whether he had a concealed carry permit. Federal law enforcement sources separately confirmed the permit to Fox News. The chief said investigators did not yet know how far the shooter had gone inside the building or whether he knew anyone at the school. Police were also investigating whether the teen had previously attended Silver Rail Elementary. The first emergency call came at 12:59 p.m. from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone carrying a long gun, Krantz said. Dispatchers then received dozens of calls reporting that a shooter had entered the school. Dispatch sent an alert summoning all law enforcement at 1 p.m. Responding officers directed the school to lock down at 1:01 p.m., and the first officers arrived at 1:02 p.m. TRANSGENDER EX-STUDENT IDENTIFIED AS ALLEGED SUSPECT IN DEADLY CANADA SCHOOL MASS SHOOTING Officers found five people dead at the scene, including the shooter. All victims’ families had been notified, Krantz said. Bend police, the Deschutes County Sheriff’s Office, Redmond police, Oregon State Police and federal law enforcement partners evacuated the building room by room. STUDENT PERPETRATES DEADLY SHOOTING AT THAILAND HIGH SCHOOL, AUTHORITIES SAY Students and staff were transported on Bend-La Pine school buses to Journey Church to reunite with families and guardians. That process was still underway at the evening briefing. The FBI’s Portland field office said it was assisting local authorities with the investigation. "We will make every resource they need available," the office wrote on X. Krantz said every Bend police officer completed a full day of active threat training at a local high school in August. "Unfortunately, this is something we train for on a regular basis, and we must," he said. A large police presence would remain at the school for several days as investigators worked to establish what happened. "There are not really any words I can say to any of you that will make this better," Krantz said, urging residents to "lean on each other and be there for each other." Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook said the district was "heartbroken" and "horrified," and called the incident an "unthinkable tragedy." "This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places, and pray that it never happens here. And it has happened here today," Cook said. "It happened to our children, to our teachers and to our families." Cook choked up as he thanked staff for protecting students. "You did what no one should ever be asked to do," he said. "I am so grateful beyond words for your efforts." Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said a community vigil would be held Thursday night. "A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure. What happened today should never happen," Kebler said. "This is a horrible day. No parent should have to have this kind of day, and no community should have to live through this kind of day," Kotek said. Silver Rail Elementary serves kindergarten through fifth grade in the Bend-La Pine school district. The school enrolled 459 students during the 2024-2025 school year. Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., expressed support for the students and families affected. "No one should have to fear violence at school," Merkley wrote on X. Rep. Janelle Bynum, D-Ore., whose district includes Bend, called the shooting "every parent’s worst fear." "Our babies are supposed to do arts and crafts at school, not use their desks as cover from gunfire," Bynum said in a statement posted on X. "My heart and my prayers and everything else I got is with the families at Silver Rail Elementary. When will it end?" Cook said crisis counselors would be available at the Central Library for students, families, employees and anyone in the community needing support. "Please hold your children. Hold your loved ones tight tonight," Cook said. "Let them talk. Let them cry." Authorities said they planned to hold another news conference Friday afternoon.

title: Hasan Piker defends using incendiary terms like 'inbred' or 'Zionist pig' against opponents
description: Hasan Piker defended calling Zionist opponents "inbred" and "Zionist pig" in an NPR interview Thursday, saying the language targeted ideology, not background.
content: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker defended using controversial terms like "inbred" and "Zionist pig" against opponents in a lengthy interview with NPR Thursday. NPR host Leila Fadel asked Piker about the backlash and controversy he has faced and whether they were related to his inflammatory comments or the fact that his "name is Hasan." Piker acknowledged his incendiary rhetoric but said he believed that most of the backlash against him was due to his background. "Of course, I, you know, say incendiary things, but it's not reflected on in the same way when someone who's White, Christian, born and raised in America is saying incendiary things," Piker said. INSIDE HASAN PIKER’S RADICAL VIEWS ON AMERICA, ISRAEL AND SOCIALISM Fadel then asked why someone who has felt "dehumanized" like him would choose to use dehumanizing language, particularly against Jewish opponents. "When you hear people say, 'Why would you use dehumanizing language like inbred for some ultra-Orthodox Jews or Zionist pig?' What do you say to them as somebody who has felt that as well?" Fadel asked. "So, great question. I have a policy to be ruthless to those who are bullying others, to be ruthless to those who abide by certain ideologies that are conducting great harm," Piker said. "As far as the language that I deploy that is considered dehumanizing like 'inbred,' it's one that I use quite commonly as a pejorative towards right-wing reactionary ideology, ethno-supremacist ideology, neo-Nazi ideology, because I find it to be an apt pejorative to deploy considering that these supremacist ideologies oftentimes revolve around ethnic purity, racial purity. It's not, of course, meant to be taken seriously." Piker added that he applies the same principle to the term "pig" and argued that he used similar language "across the board" for different targets regardless of their background. HASAN PIKER ADMITS HE HAS 'DIALED DOWN' HIS OPINIONS AFTER PUBLIC AND DEMOCRATIC BACKLASH "It gets heated at times," he said. "I'm a passionate guy. I get angry. I have to, you know, explain my frustration, communicate my frustration somehow. Very different format than we have here, obviously. "But, you know, I think that a lot of people feel this way," Piker added. "A lot of people get very frustrated. It's never directed at someone for their actual background. It's usually their actions or their belief system. And almost all the time, it's their reactionary belief system that causes me to call them a pig or inbred or something like that." The Israeli-American Council (IAC) condemned Piker's comments in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The Jewish people know what happens when hatred becomes acceptable," the group said. "Throughout history, pogroms and persecution were fueled by lies that portrayed Jews as less than human. The Holocaust showed the world where the systematic dehumanization of Jews can lead. "On October 7, 2023, Hamas perpetrated mass murder, mass rape, mass torture, and mass hostage taking in the deadliest massacre of our people since the Holocaust," the IAC statement added. "For us, the consequences of antisemitic hatred are not an abstract debate." Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment but did not immediately receive a response. title: Experimental skin cream linked to 2-year drop in biological age in early study
description: Rubedo Life Sciences says its skin cream RLS-1496 cleared senescent cells, boosted collagen 10% and reduced skin age in a four-week trial study.
content: An experimental skin cream altered molecular markers associated with aging and inflammation in an early human trial, according to preliminary data released by its developer this week. Rubedo Life Sciences, a biotechnology company based in Mountain View, California, tested its investigational treatment, RLS-1496, in patients with eczema and other skin conditions. In an analysis of 11 paired skin samples from patients with atopic dermatitis, researchers reported that four weeks of treatment was associated with an average 2.1-year decrease in measured epigenetic skin age, an estimate based on age-related changes in DNA. 3 COMMON FACTORS MAY BE SECRETLY SPEEDING UP THE AGING PROCESS, EXPERT SAYS Rubedo CEO Dr. Frederick Beddingfield said the "significant" early findings warrant further investigation. "This is one of the few drugs developed for aging in general and with AI to show positive data in humans in multiple indications and to show a reduction in skin age," Beddingfield told Fox News Digital. He believes the early results will translate into "clinical improvements with longer-term treatment." The latest skin-aging findings have been presented at a scientific conference but have not yet been published as a full peer-reviewed study. SCIENTISTS UNVEIL 'LIVING BANDAGE' THAT COULD DRAMATICALLY SPEED WOUND HEALING RLS-1496 is designed to target senescent cells, aging or damaged cells that have stopped dividing but can release substances that promote inflammation. The drug targets a protein called GPX4, which helps cells respond to stress. Researchers are studying whether blocking it can clear away damaged, aging cells while helping healthier cells survive. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Beddingfield described the approach as targeting cellular aging rather than simply treating its outward effects. "It's a bit like 'what does not kill you makes you stronger' for those surviving cells," he added. Skin samples showed a 10% increase in a type of collagen that helps support the skin, according to the company. Blood tests also showed lower levels of several markers linked to inflammation, although it is not yet clear what those changes mean for patients' health. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER The preliminary findings come with several limitations. The skin-aging analysis included just 11 paired samples and measured biological signs of aging in the skin rather than whether the skin actually looked younger or functioned better. Treatment lasted only four weeks, so it is not known whether the changes will persist. The studies were sponsored by Rubedo, and the latest skin-aging findings have not yet been published as a full peer-reviewed study. "Our next trial will treat for several months," Beddingfield said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The treatment is also being tested for other skin issues. In a separate early-stage study of 22 patients with actinic keratosis, rough, precancerous skin patches caused by sun exposure, the company reported a 49% average reduction in lesions after 28 days of treatment. The open-label study compared treated forearms with untreated forearms rather than a placebo cream. The cream caused minimal skin irritation, and the drug was detected in the blood of very few participants, according to the company. "With topical application, we have seen very little risk," Beddingfield said. "Local irritation is rarely seen and generally mild when it occurs, and no one has discontinued treatment to date. Very few subjects show any drug in their blood after skin application." Beddingfield estimated that potential FDA approval remains three to four years away, pending larger clinical trials.

title: Can cooking for terrorists bar asylum? Supreme Court takes up unusual case with broader immigration stakes
description: A Nigerian man forced to cook for the Unknown Gunmen terrorist group is now at the center of a Supreme Court battle over asylum and material support.
content: A Nigerian man forced to cook thousands of meals for the Unknown Gunmen, a militant group linked to political violence in Nigeria, is at the center of a Supreme Court showdown that could determine how broadly immigration authorities can apply a terrorism-related bar to asylum and how far the Trump administration can go in deporting immigrants accused of supporting terrorism. The Supreme Court agreed Tuesday to hear the Trump administration's challenge to a ruling that overturned Nigerian citizen Izuchukwu Ozurumba's deportation order, setting up a legal battle over whether ordinary services provided to terrorist organizations, including cooking meals, can disqualify immigrants from receiving asylum even when those services are not directly connected to terrorist attacks. Ozurumba was deported to Nigeria in April 2025 while his appeal was pending. THE SUPREME COURT IS BACK; THESE FIVE CASES COULD RESHAPE AMERICAN LIFE At the center of the case is a provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act that bars certain immigrants who provide "material support" to terrorist organizations from receiving asylum. The law lists examples of prohibited assistance, including transportation, communications, housing, money, weapons and training, but it does not explicitly define what constitutes material support. "The biggest takeaway is that this is a case about who gets to draw the line on a law that affects national security," Bryce Poole, a senior legal fellow with Advancing American Freedom, told Fox News Digital. "Congress wrote a broad rule, and the court interpreted it narrowly." The case also comes two years after the Supreme Court overturned Chevron deference, a legal doctrine that required judges to defer to federal agencies' reasonable interpretations of ambiguous laws. The 2024 ruling gave judges greater authority to decide what those laws mean. The 4th Circuit, in a 2-1 ruling, overturned Ozurumba's deportation order and sent the case back to the Board of Immigration Appeals. Judge James Wynn Jr., an Obama appointee, wrote the majority opinion, joined by Judge Nicole Berner, a Biden appointee. The judges concluded that, although Ozurumba prepared thousands of meals for the group's leaders, his cooking did not provide resources that could be directly used or readily redirected toward terrorist operations. Although Ozurumba said he was forced to cook under threat of violence, the 4th Circuit did not decide whether the law contains an exception for assistance provided under duress, an issue the court previously addressed in a 2012 ruling that relied on Chevron deference. Instead, the majority found that his cooking for the terrorist organization did not qualify as "material support" that would bar him from asylum, leaving the separate duress question unresolved. The Trump administration argued that the 4th Circuit interpreted the law too narrowly, insisting that even ordinary services such as cooking meals can help sustain a terrorist organization and free its members to carry out attacks. "Because he's cooking the meals, one of the armed guards doesn't have to cook the meals and can be an armed guard," Poole said. "That's one guard who doesn't have to come in off guard duty to cook meals, or that's one bomb maker who doesn't have to stop making bombs to go cook meals, because all this stuff is fungible." Ozurumba said he initially agreed to work as a chef at a "rural camp," preparing three meals a day for 15 to 17 leaders. He later learned the camp belonged to the Unknown Gunmen. An immigration judge determined that the Unknown Gunmen qualified as a "Tier III" terrorist organization under federal immigration law, even though the State Department had not formally designated the group as one. Ozurumba said armed guards prevented him from leaving. According to court records, he cooked for the group's leaders for roughly six months, including three months without pay, before escaping during a trip into town to buy groceries. STATE'S LARGEST MOSQUE LEADER’S DEPORTATION FIGHT TAKES DRAMATIC TURN AS TRUMP ADMIN SCORES MAJOR WIN Ozurumba said members of the Unknown Gunmen continued threatening and attacking him after his escape, prompting him to flee Nigeria for Venezuela and eventually the United States. He crossed the southern border without valid entry documents in July 2023 during the Biden administration and surrendered to Border Patrol agents. An immigration judge denied Ozurumba's asylum request and ordered his deportation, a decision upheld by the Board of Immigration Appeals after finding that his cooking violated the federal material-support rule. The 4th Circuit later rejected that interpretation and sent the case back to the immigration board. Judge Julius Richardson disagreed with the majority, arguing in his dissent that cooking thousands of meals for terrorist leaders freed them to focus on their organization's goals and therefore constituted material support. "Ozurumba did not run a hot dog stand that the Unknown Gunmen happened to stop by once or twice," Richardson wrote. "Rather, he acted as a private chef, providing three meals a day for over a dozen leaders of a terrorist organization — for months." Hans von Spakovsky, a legal expert with Advancing American Freedom, also argued that the majority misinterpreted the law. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "The idea that providing over 8,000 meals for the leaders of a terrorist organization and its members is not 'material' defies common sense," von Spakovsky told Fox News Digital. "Richardson correctly cites Napoleon’s famous quote that an 'army marches on its stomach.' CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Other federal appeals courts have all held that providing food and shelter, even if unconnected to a specific terrorist event, constitutes material support within the statute," von Spakovsky continued. "And doing so under duress, even if true, is not an excuse under the statute to avoid removal." Even if the Supreme Court rules in his favor, a victory would not automatically grant him asylum or guarantee his return to the United States. His case would still need to be reconsidered by immigration authorities. The 4th Circuit previously declined to order the government to bring him back, instead leaving it up to officials to decide whether his presence in the U.S. would be necessary for further proceedings.

title: Made in California business directory lets buyers filter by identity but excludes White men
description: The state-run Made in California business directory sparked backlash by excluding White and male as owner identity categories on the website.
content: A new government website in California allows people to search for local businesses based on the identity of their owners but does not offer specific search filters for White-owned or male-owned businesses. The Made in California website lets users search by business ownership categories, including Asian-Owned, Black-Owned, Hispanic-Owned, LGBTQ-Owned, Native American-Owned, Pacific Islander-Owned, Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, approximately 40% of California's population is Hispanic or Latino, more than 30% is non-Hispanic White, roughly 17% is Asian and about 6% is Black. Christopher Rufo, a prominent critic of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policies, criticized the government website on X, noting, "The California state government has released a ‘Made in California’ website that allows you to select products by every identity group except for one: White men." DEM SENATOR'S HIRING ANNOUNCEMENT SPARKS GOP ERUPTION OVER WHO IS ENCOURAGED TO APPLY: 'BLATANTLY ILLEGAL' Tesla CEO and X owner Elon Musk was surprised by the news, replying to Rufo's post with, "Wow." "Managed by the California Office of the Small Business Advocate, the program is designed to help consumers and corporate buyers find products manufactured in the Golden State," the New York Post reported. "To qualify, a product must have at least 51% of its wholesale value added within the state. Certified businesses can appear in the official public directory and use the Made in California seal on their packaging and marketing materials." Entrepreneur Will Fry, founder and CEO of American Operator, a company that specializes in American small businesses, spoke to Fox News Digital about the controversy. "Support local business is not exactly the same thing as support the minority you like the most," Fry said. "The concept of a Made in California database is great and one I can get behind. "But I guess it comes as no surprise that California seems to have decided to turn it into a virtue signaling exercise about identity, and that should not be the focus of doing business. "Last time I checked, red tape, untrained labor and rising prices are hurting all small businesses, not just the minority-owned." OAKLAND SCHOOLS IN HOT SEAT OVER 'STUDENTS OF COLOR' PROGRAM WHILE TAKING MILLIONS IN FEDERAL FUNDING Theo Wold, a former assistant attorney general and White House deputy assistant for domestic policy during the Trump administration, warned that such race-based distinctions are part of a broader Democratic Party agenda. "Race-based preferences — in college admissions or in government-run, taxpayer-backed small business lending — is anathema. But to be clear: Race-based preferences have never been about remediating supposed systemic racism or the overrepresentation of certain racial groups in society," he said. "It’s always been a tool to manipulate demographics and to undermine White men," Wold continued. "California’s policies show that, once empowered, the left not only disavows so-called 'colorblind' governance but actively promotes advantaging certain races over others." Fox News Digital contacted the California Office of the Small Business Advocate, the state organization that oversees the website. "Thank you for inquiring about Made in California. The demographic identity of the owner is not required and has no bearing on the eligibility evaluation," the organization wrote. "Applicants can voluntarily provide this information should they choose to do so. This program is open to all manufacturers who meet the eligibility requirements, which are explained in detail on the Made In California website." title: Want to know how to win in October? The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers are providing the blueprint
description: The Milwaukee Brewers lead the Dodgers 3-0 in the NLCS despite more strikeouts, proving Major League Baseball playoffs have no secret formula.
content: It's arguably the most important question for organizations and fans across Major League Baseball; how do you win in the playoffs? There's a theoretical formula for getting to October, draft and develop well, build a complete roster that has depth at key positions, use analytics to piece together the best mix of skill sets and sign targeted free agents to fill in missing pieces. The more money you have, the easier it is to sign those free agents, of course, but as the Yankees, Mets, Giants, and Angels will tell you, playing in a big market and acquiring expensive talent doesn't always guarantee results. But once you're in the postseason, how can you ensure your team gets a spot in the World Series? The ultimate goal, the only outcome that matters, and the only determinant of the "best team in baseball?" A DODGERS-LESS WORLD SERIES WOULD HURT NOW, BUT HELP MLB LATER | BOBBY BURACK The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers are showing the rest of the sport exactly how it's done. For context, the Brewers enter Thursday afternoon as overwhelming favorites to advance to the World Series thanks to their 3-0 series lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Dodgers have the most expensive roster in the sport, though by active player payroll in 2026 they did trail the New York Mets, depending on which source you use. Milwaukee? They were just 19th this season. They traded away Freddy Peralta, their best pitcher, in 2025, a year after trading star closer Devin Williams to the Yankees, and trading Corbin Burnes to the Baltimore Orioles. Their big offseason acquisitions were backup catcher Gary Sanchez, Angel Zerpa, Jake Woodford, and a trade to bring in David Hamilton, Shane Drohan and Kyle Harrison from the Boston Red Sox for infielder Caleb Durbin and a few other players. During the season, their big moves were watching Tarik Skubal go to the Dodgers, getting Dustin May and JoJo Romero, and adding reliever Antonio Senzatela. If that sounds underwhelming, it's because it is. Yet in game one of the NLCS, the Brewers beat Skubal 2-1. In game two, they came roaring back from deficit after deficit, knocking out World Series hero Yoshinobu Yamamoto on their way to an easy 7-4 win. In game three, they fell behind late, only to score five straight runs and cruise to yet another 6-2 win. So how are they doing it? They've found the blueprint. Milwaukee, we've been told by very experienced baseball analysts, is winning because they don't strike out. Their approach is based on contact. Put the ball in play, the thinking goes, don't just try and hit home runs. These analysts have decades of experience at the highest level of baseball. Obviously, they'd have enormous insight and detailed statistical breakdowns backing up their opinions. Well, in game one of the NLCS, the Dodgers struck out eight times, meaning they put the ball in play on 23 of their 31 at bats. Milwaukee struck out 13 times, only putting the ball in play in 13 of their 26 at bats. So the Dodgers' home run approach resulted in...fewer strikeouts and more balls put in play. 10 more balls put in play, in fact, a massive number in just one game. But the Brewers won anyway, 2-1. Interesting. In game two of the NLCS, the Dodgers struck out nine times, while Milwaukee struck out 10. Funnily enough, the only home run was hit by William Contreras for the Brewers. They won 7-4. In game three, Milwaukee struck out a whopping 12 times in 35 at bats against Blake Snell and the Dodgers bullpen. Los Angeles? Their hitters had just eight strikeouts in 32 at bats. The Dodgers put the ball in play 24 times, Milwaukee did 23 times. Yet the Brewers won 6-2 anyway. How? Because they hit three home runs, while Los Angeles yet again put up a goose egg. So in three games, the Brewers have struck out 35 times, averaging nearly 12 per game. The Dodgers have struck out 25 times, or just over eight per game. That's so odd because all the baseball analysts have been saying that Milwaukee's superior approach, just putting the ball in play, getting the bat on the ball, is the reason they're winning. Yet they're making contact far less often than the Dodgers are, with their awful, new school, analytics-driven, home run-only offense. And Milwaukee has a 5-0 home run advantage in a series they're winning three games to none. Wonder what that means. We'll come back to that, but what about the contact itself? Maybe the Brewers have instructed their hitters to purposefully hit the ball poorly, while the Dodgers hitting staff keeps telling Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, and Shohei Ohtani to hit the ball hard directly at Milwaukee defensive players. Obviously, weak contact is preferable to hitting the ball hard, because that's old school baseball or something. Here's what one user, "Dubs Only Sports" found in a post made on X. Headlined "luck doesn't exist in baseball," which is obviously true because every single outcome is the result of purposeful decision making while randomness is just a fake conspiracy theory, they found that, shockingly enough, there's been little difference in quality of contact between the two teams. But a tremendous difference in outcomes. The Dodgers have 29 hard hit balls in the series, defined as being hit at 95 mph or above. Those 29 hard-hit balls have resulted in 12 hits and no home runs. Milwaukee has just 21 hard hit balls in the series, which have resulted in 11 hits and five home runs. Well sure, you might say, but who cares about hard-hit balls when you can just hit the ball poorly and steer it in the right direction? Turns out, the Dodgers are trying that too! LA has 40 balls put in play this series that were "soft contact," or under 95 mph. On those 40 balls put in play, they've gotten just three hits, good for a .075 batting average. Milwaukee has put 42 balls in play with soft contact, resulting in 16 hits and a .381 batting average. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Wow! So the Dodgers are more frequently hitting the ball harder, and putting nearly as many weakly hit balls into play, a difference of less than one per game, than Milwaukee. They're striking out far less often than the Brewers. Yet their results have been much worse. Really makes you think, doesn't it? In actuality, of course, it will not make anyone think, because of the inescapable conclusion: nothing actually matters. Sarcasm aside, that's the real answer to the "secret formula" for winning in October: there is no secret formula. Just be a pretty good team and hope you get the benefit of timing with your offense and pitching staff. When it comes to postseason baseball, the gaps between teams are so small that the win probability for each team is only marginally different from a coin flip. Per FanGraphs baseball analyst Dan Szymborski, creator of the ZiPS projection system, the Dodgers had a 58% chance of winning the series before it started. That's what a $250 million payroll gap buys, a 58% chance instead of a 50% chance. Obviously, the outcome in this year's NLCS is the 42%. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Because the gaps are so small, as opposed to sports with poor competitive balance like the NFL, the outcomes rely much more heavily on luck and random chance that fans or very smart analysts will ever admit. Because humans have to have an explanation for everything, every result is ascribed to some kind of intent, process, or approach, as opposed to the inherent variability of baseball. Milwaukee's bullpen has allowed two runs in around 32 innings in the postseason. Filled with castoffs from other teams and cheap internal options having the best few weeks of their careers at the perfect time. That's not unexpected or unusual, it's an undeniable part of baseball. Their batting average on balls in play in this NLCS is .393, where league average is around .300. The Dodgers? Just .221. Milwaukee has a 31.3% strikeout rate, while the Dodgers' is just 23.4%. Milwaukee has outperformed their expected stats, based on quality of contact, by nearly 20 points. The Dodgers have underperformed by 67 points. The Brewers aren't winning because of soft contact, they're winning because they've hit home runs and benefitted from fortunate bounces on balls put in play. This isn't to say that the Brewers aren't a good team, because of course they are. They somehow managed to turn Jake Bauers from an unplayable castoff, to a top-10 hitter in baseball. Misiorowski is the likely NL Cy Young Award winner. Their prospects, like Brice Turang, Jackson Chourio and Garrett Mitchell have all panned out, a testament to their player development staff. Every single trade they've made in recent years has worked out in their favor, another feather in the cap for their scouting department. But the Brewers have inarguably gotten "lucky" this series, because the results have outperformed the quality of their contact and approach. The Dodgers got lucky to win in 2024 and 2025. Luck is not a byproduct in postseason baseball, it is quite literally required. Over a large enough sample size, most of the randomness and luck in baseball evens out. Meaning that if the Dodgers played the Brewers 162 times, LA's talent advantage would almost certainly matter, to the point where they would win 58% of the games. But in a best-of-seven? Or a best-of-five? The talent advantage is so small that a few bounces either way can lead to a wildly different outcome. Which is what we're seeing. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER This is why the guiding philosophy in baseball has become, "do what you can to win 85 games and hope for the best." Because that gives you a 42% chance of beating the most talented roster in a playoff series. It's rational, because it's correct. The Toronto Blue Jays rode Addison Barger and Ernie Clement to within two outs of a championship. They finished in last place this year. The Dodgers have made the postseason 17 times since 2008. When they're eliminated by Milwaukee this week, they'll have won three championships in 17 tries. There is no sport less predictable than baseball. There is no way to "ruin" baseball, or to break it, or to build unbeatable superteams. Because the volatility of it will create series with outcomes like this, where the Dodgers hit the ball harder, make more contact, strike out less, and still get obliterated. Even if LA put together a roster with Skubal, Yamamoto, Paul Skenes, Misiorowski, Aaron Judge, Ohtani, Bobby Witt Jr., Freddie Freeman, Junior Caminero, and Pete Crow-Armstrong, that team would have a 58-60% chance of winning a best-of-seven postseason series against the 84-win Cleveland Guardians. It doesn't sound right, but it is objective fact. Looking for meaning in October is pointless. Looking for a blueprint of how to win the World Series is insanity.

title: Autistic teen lured to fake Snapchat meetup, brutally beaten by group of teens: report
description: Video captured the violent beating of a 15-year-old boy with autism near a Stawell train station after he was lured through a Snapchat meetup.
content: Three teenage boys were charged after a 15-year-old boy with autism was beaten and robbed near a train station in Australia in a violent attack captured on video as other teenagers watched. The assault happened Oct. 5 in Stawell, a town in the Australian state of Victoria, after the victim was reportedly lured to the area through a Snapchat meetup arranged with two girls, according to Australian news outlet news.com.au. Video of the attack shows several teenagers punching and kicking the boy, knocking him to the ground and repeatedly striking him as he attempts to get away. One attacker demands the victim hand over his shoes before the group allows him to leave. TEXAS TEENS ACCUSED OF USING DATING APPS TO LURE YOUNG MEN INTO VIOLENT ROBBERIES THAT LEFT ONE VICTIM SHOT Victoria Police announced Tuesday that detectives had charged one 14-year-old boy and two 15-year-old boys after an investigation. Detectives from the Northern Grampians Crime Investigation Unit executed four search warrants in the region before arresting the teenagers, police said. All three face charges of affray, robbery, recklessly causing injury and theft. They are expected to appear in a children's court at a later date. TEEN BURGLARY RING LINKED TO NEARLY 80 BAY AREA BREAK-INS DISMANTLED AFTER MONTHS-LONG INVESTIGATION: PD Police said a fourth boy who was not present when the search warrants were served would be interviewed as part of the ongoing investigation. The victim, who also has epilepsy, suffered soft tissue injuries and possible head injuries, according to news.com.au. His mother told the outlet doctors were conducting additional scans to determine whether he had bleeding in his brain. "I’m just lucky to have him alive. … He’s having nightmares," she said. TEEN PUNCHED AND KICKED INTO A COMA AFTER KNICKS-SPURS ALTERCATION NEAR MADISON SQUARE GARDEN: POLICE The boy has since returned home but is afraid to go outside, his mother told the outlet. Superintendent Dan Davison acknowledged the concern the attack had caused in the Stawell community and said police had been working to identify those responsible. "Since last Monday, local uniform police and detectives have been working tirelessly to identify those involved and hold them to account, and this important work will continue," Davison said in a news release. "There is never any excuse for violence in our community, and we will not accept it in any form. "Detectives are continuing to investigate the matter, and while we are treating it as an isolated incident, additional patrols will take place across Stawell to ensure our community not only is safe but feels safe." title: TSA warns travelers about seasonal mistake that could trigger airport security delays
description: Halloween travelers wearing costume makeup, bringing metal-heavy accessories and carrying props could face delays and challenges at airports, the TSA is warning.
content: Travelers planning to fly in costume this Halloween could face unexpected hurdles at airport security. While costumes themselves are generally allowed, certain accessories, masks, special makeup and metal pieces can create problems at TSA checkpoints, according to the agency's website. Travelers wearing elaborate face coverings or heavy costume makeup may be asked to remove it if their identity cannot be verified during screening. POPULAR PANTRY STAPLE COULD GET YOU STOPPED AT AIRPORT SECURITY UNDER LITTLE-KNOWN TSA RULE Keith Jeffries, vice president of K2 Security Screening Group and a former federal security director for TSA at Los Angeles International Airport, told Fox News Digital that facial recognition technology is becoming more common at airports. "If you're wearing … Halloween costume-style makeup, and it can't recognize you, that's going to create some challenges," he said. Costume props packed in luggage can also raise security concerns, particularly when they resemble weapons or other prohibited items. Replica explosives, including fake bombs and grenades, are not allowed in carry-on or checked luggage, according to TSA guidance. Some may be permitted in checked luggage, depending on the item. Jeffries recalled seeing similar issues during his 20 years with the TSA, including travelers trying to bring replicas of "Lucille," the barbed-wire-covered baseball bat featured on "The Walking Dead," through security. "Of course, that just can't go through the checkpoint," he said, noting that it could be placed in checked luggage. Metal-heavy costumes could create another headache by triggering screening equipment and potentially leading to additional screening, Jeffries said. Travelers packing makeup must also follow standard TSA liquid restrictions. Liquid makeup in carry-ons generally must be in containers of 3.4 ounces or less, while larger quantities should go into checked luggage, according to the TSA. title: CBS News faces $20M defamation lawsuit after misidentifying Maryland teenager in Reflecting Pool report
description: A Maryland teenager's $20 million defamation lawsuit claims CBS News falsely linked him to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool vandalism arrests.
content: CBS News is facing a defamation lawsuit as a Maryland teenager seeks $20 million in damages, claiming he was falsely identified as a person arrested for vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool’s lining. The lawsuit, filed on Wednesday in U.S. District Court in the District of Columbia, identified the 15-year-old plaintiff simply as "JV." "He was not arrested for vandalizing it. He was not accused by law enforcement of vandalizing it. Yet CBS News broadcast and published a story to a national audience that placed JV's image alongside the assertion that five people had been arrested for vandalizing and ‘sabotaging’ the Reflecting Pool, thereby falsely portraying JV as one of the perpetrators of a highly publicized federal crime," the lawsuit stated. NORTH CAROLINA STUDENT WINS $95K AFTER SCHOOL ACCUSED HER OF VANDALIZING SPIRIT ROCK WITH CHARLIE KIRK TRIBUTE "The accusation was particularly damaging because at all times material to the allegations, the Reflecting Pool renovation and subsequent alleged vandalism of the Reflecting Pool is or has been the subject of intense national attention and political controversy," the complaint continued. "President Donald Trump frequently discusses the Reflecting Pool renovation and publicly condemned those accused of vandalism in extraordinarily harsh terms, stating that they should be ‘prosecuted to the max,’" it added. The lawsuit states that CBS "inserted" JV into the controversy and "exposed him to extreme embarrassment, humiliation, and the public condemnation" directed at the actual vandals. The lawsuit claims JV’s presence near the Reflecting Pool "was entirely unrelated to the vandalism" and he was simply briefly detained for riding an e-bike in the area. NEW YORK TIMES LOSES DEFAMATION SUIT, ORDERED TO PAY $9.25M TO FORMER ALABAMA BASKETBALL PLAYER JV was released without charges and "his detention had nothing whatsoever to do with vandalism or sabotage of the Reflecting Pool." "CBS nevertheless used video footage of JV's detention in its report about the Reflecting Pool vandalism. As CBS anchor Jericka Duncan told viewers that ‘five people have been arrested,' the video depicted JV in handcuffs," the lawsuit stated. "In the version CBS distributed online and through social media, CBS showed JV turning toward the camera with his face fully visible as Duncan made the statement concerning the arrests and then identified one of the alleged perpetrators, David Hearn," it continued. "The visual and verbal presentation published by Defendants unmistakably conveyed the false message that JV was among the persons arrested for vandalizing the Reflecting Pool and further confused JV with Hearn, an adult who was subsequently indicted on a felony charge arising from the vandalism," the complaint added. JV’s legal team claimed CBS was aware that the 15-year-old was detained for the e-bike, and not vandalism, because the original video obtained by the network clearly distinguished between the two issues. "The facts alleged herein demonstrate that CBS either knew its portrayal of JV was false or acted with reckless disregard for whether it was true," the lawsuit alleged. "CBS compounded the harm through the manner and breadth of its publication," it continued. "Although the national television broadcast did not show JV's face, CBS's online and social-media version did. It showed his face immediately after depicting his distinctive sweatshirt and while reporting that arrests had been made. JV was readily recognized by friends and acquaintances." The lawsuit noted that CBS issued an on-air correction but said the "belated acknowledgment … cannot undo the publication or erase its consequences." CBS News declined comment on pending litigation. title: Best outdoor adventures near Memorial Stadium for Ohio State vs. Indiana football fans
description: No. 4 Ohio State visits No. 5 Indiana at Memorial Stadium with Brown County's peak fall foliage, fire towers, and Lake Monroe all within reach.
content: Week 7 | No. 4 Ohio State at No. 5 Indiana | Saturday, Oct. 17 | Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN | 12 p.m. ET | FOX Indiana has won 22 games in a row, owns the national championship trophy, and is hosting Ohio State in Bloomington with both teams ranked in the top five. The last time these two met, the Hoosiers upset the Buckeyes 13-10 in the Big Ten title game, ending Ohio State's unbeaten season. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Now the 5-1 Buckeyes are coming back as 3.5-point favorites against an undefeated Indiana team that has plenty to prove all over again. I'm biased on this one. Sure, I went to the University of Tennessee. But Indiana is my home state, and I grew up spending my summers on Lake Monroe. But Southern Indiana in mid-October — with the hills lit up in red and gold — is hard to beat. Bloomington sits right in the middle of it. Brown County, in particular, is a little slice of heaven. Let's get into it. Brown County State Park About 40 minutes from Memorial Stadium | $7 per vehicle with Indiana plates, $15 out of state | Easy to moderate Indiana's largest state park covers roughly 16,000 acres of rugged hills and ridges, and people call it the "Little Smokies" for a reason. Hike to a scenic overlook like Hesitation Point, climb the fire tower, or just drive the park roads and pull off at the viewpoints if you'd rather stay warm. The park gets busy on peak foliage weekends and the entrance can back up, so get there early. Nashville, Ind., is right outside the gate, which makes it easy to turn this into a full day. McCormick's Creek State Park About 25 minutes from Memorial Stadium | $7 per vehicle with Indiana plates, $15 out of state | Easy to moderate Indiana's first state park is also home to one of the few waterfalls in a state not exactly known for them. The Wolf Cave Trail is a roughly 2-mile moderate loop through a wooded nature preserve to a small cave, rated 4.6 stars across more than 1,200 AllTrails reviews. If you're short on time, the waterfall is just a short, easy walk from Trail 3. It's the closest of the big state parks to Bloomington, which makes it a good fit for a shorter window. Hickory Ridge Fire Tower & Deam Wilderness About 30 minutes from Memorial Stadium | Moderate The 110-foot Hickory Ridge Fire Tower has 133 steps and is open to climb, with views over the forest and Lake Monroe. 6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK It's the last fire tower standing in Hoosier National Forest. The surrounding Charles C. Deam Wilderness, Indiana's only wilderness area, covers nearly 13,000 acres and about 36 miles of trails. Lake Monroe About 6 miles from campus | Canoe or kayak rental from about $42 for four hours, plus a state entrance fee Indiana's largest lake is nearly 11,000 acres, and in October the fall color reflects right off the water. Lake Monroe Boat Rental at Paynetown State Recreation Area rents canoes and kayaks that seat one or two people for $41.73 for four hours or $53.50 for eight. A state entrance fee applies at Paynetown. Call ahead to confirm hours this late in the season, and keep in mind the water is cold, so dress for it. There are also hiking trails along the lake if you'd rather stay off the water. Griffy Lake Nature Preserve Under 2 miles from campus | $12 per hour The closest option to the stadium, and a nice one for a lower-key day. The city's boathouse rents canoes, kayaks and stand-up paddleboards on a 109-acre lake, with hiking trails through the surrounding preserve. There's a two-hour limit on weekend rentals, and you'll need a photo ID. In October the boathouse is open Saturdays and Sundays only, 10 a.m. to 7 p.m., so it won't work for a pregame paddle with a noon kickoff. Plan on it after the game or on Sunday. Or, again, just go for a hike. Nashville and the Get Lost ATV Tour About 40 minutes from Memorial Stadium | Strolling is free, ATV tour is $70 per person (21+) If you've got an extra day, or even an extra afternoon, spend it in Nashville. The small downtown in the heart of Brown County is made for wandering, with art galleries, craft shops and homemade fudge packed into a few walkable blocks. There's a couple of wineries, too, if you're into that sort of thing. I'm into that sort of thing. For something a little more adventurous (and super fun), Hard Truth Distilling Co. sits on 325 wooded acres just outside town and runs its Get Lost ATV Tour. Staff drive you through the property in an off-road vehicle with stops for tastings along the way. The tour runs 45 to 60 minutes, costs $70 per person, and you have to be at least 21. It is weather dependent, though, so rain can cancel it. So there you have it. Because as that animated crow in a commercial from my childhood always said, "There’s more than corn in Indiana!" Every week this season, OutKick OutDoors is finding the best ways to touch grass before you touch down at the tailgate. Got a favorite spot near your campus we should know about? title: Billy Joel says he can't drive, unsure about touring future after brain disorder diagnosis
description: Billy Joel revealed his hydrocephalus diagnosis means every concert is like getting a concussion, and he's not allowed to drive a vehicle.
content: Billy Joel's touring future remains uncertain due to his ongoing health issues. Joel, 77, revealed in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter that he's also not allowed to drive a vehicle after being diagnosed with normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in 2025. "What the neurologist told me, every time you do a show, it’s like you’re getting a concussion," Joel said. 'PIANO MAN' BILLY JOEL'S PRIZED MOTORCYCLE COLLECTION HITS THE AUCTION BLOCK When asked about his current status, Joel said that his "health is good," but still isn't sure when he'll be able to tour again. "I have this thing called hydrocephalus," he told the outlet. "It used to be called water on the brain, so it affects your balance, it affects your memory, it affects your vision, your hearing. But I’m OK." "They call it a brain disorder, but it’s not that serious. It’s just something that affects your balance mostly." LIONEL RICHIE HOSPITALIZED IN ST LOUIS AFTER SUMMER OF HEALTH SCARES AND CANCELED CONCERTS As far as going back on the road again, Joel admitted he can't perform quite like how he used to.
