title: Elon Musk blames Trump, US military for SpaceX restrictions Ukraine warns could have deadly consequences
description: Elon Musk's SpaceX imposed a new speed limit on Starshield satellite service that Ukraine says is disrupting drone intercepts and military operations.
content: Elon Musk pointed to the Trump administration Wednesday after Ukraine scrambled to reverse new Starshield restrictions put in place by the trillionaire's company that disrupted military operations and threatened Kyiv's ability to intercept Russian attack drones. While Starshield is built and operated by Musk's company SpaceX, individual satellites and infrastructure are owned and controlled by the U.S. government — which he made clear in a post to X on Wednesday. "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," the SpaceX, Tesla and X CEO wrote in his post. A source familiar with the situation told Fox News Digital that Ukraine received no advance warning before the restrictions took effect overnight, despite relying on the service under arrangements contracted through the U.S. government until May 15, 2027. Ukrainian forces discovered the change after experiencing connectivity problems and contacting SpaceX customer support. They were told Starshield service would be restricted on platforms traveling at speeds of 100 miles per hour or higher, the source said. Musk did not say whether President Donald Trump, War Secretary Pete Hegseth or another U.S. official personally authorized the new restriction or explain why it was imposed. RUSSIA MAY BE USING HIDDEN 'LUNCHBOX-SIZE' DRONE DEVICES TO COUNTER UKRAINE DEFENSES: EXPERT He also sought to distinguish the government-controlled Starshield service from SpaceX's commercial Starlink network, which he said cannot be used for offensive military operations. The distinction comes amid growing tensions between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Musk criticized Zelenskyy over those attacks days earlier, writing on X that the Ukrainian president had "gone too far." Hours after the change was reported, Ukraine's former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said connectivity at speeds below the new threshold was being restored, while making clear that Kyiv was still seeking removal of the speed restriction itself. "Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 km/h is being restored," Fedorov wrote on X Wednesday. "Removing Starshield’s speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine’s defense." "Thank you, @elonmusk," Fedorov added. "We hope for your continued support." Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on defense technology, warned that the change could particularly hamper Ukraine’s efforts to intercept Russia’s newer, jet-powered Shahed attack drones, saying it threatened "one of our few chances to defend the country" against them. Ukrainian forces have also begun documenting effects on the battlefield. Ukraine’s 7th Rapid Response Corps said one unmanned systems unit on the Huliaipole front had already been forced to cancel missions because of connectivity problems. The unit reported interruptions even while drones were traveling below the stated 100 mph threshold. Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., pressed SpaceX for answers on X. "I'm confident this does not reflect a change in SpaceX policy because if so, intentionally degrading Ukraine's ability to defend itself might be construed as aiding and abetting a mass murderer. Can you confirm that's not SpaceX’s intent?" Starshield is SpaceX's national security satellite service, based on technology developed for the company's better-known Starlink network. The change could affect Ukrainian drones, aircraft and helicopters that rely on Starshield connectivity while moving at high speeds, including drones used to intercept Russian Shahed attacks. Ukrainian units had reported performance problems even at speeds below the stated threshold, according to the source. UKRAINE SEEKS MORE US PATRIOT INTERCEPTORS AS BOMB SHELTER PROBE DEEPENS Ukraine has contacted SpaceX seeking an explanation for the restrictions and asking the company to restore its previous service capabilities, the source familiar with the move told Fox News Digital. They said Ukraine communicated to Musk's company that the restriction had not previously applied to its terminals and was creating significant operational problems for Ukrainian forces in its continued war with aggressor Russia. Kyiv also noted that its current service arrangements, contracted through the U.S. government until May 15, 2027, cover land-based mobile and fixed uses, including mobile platforms, according to the source. SpaceX had not responded to Ukraine’s request as of Wednesday morning, the source said. PENTAGON CONSOLIDATES DRONE OVERSIGHT AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PUSHES RAPID UNMANNED WARFARE EXPANSION Polish Foreign Minister Radislaw Sikorski tore into Musk over the restrictions. "Hey @elonmusk, big man, are you playing politics with your products again? As your European customers, wea are watching you," he wrote on X. Poland pays for more than 2,900 Starlink terminals operating in Ukraine. Sikorski and Musk clashed last year over Ukraine’s dependence on Starlink, with Musk telling Sikorski, "Be quiet, small man." Fox News Digital has reached out to the Pentagon, White House and SpaceX for details. There’s been no public confirmation that Musk personally ordered the restrictions. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Pentagon, through Space Force, contracts with SpaceX for Starshield services, giving the department a direct role in administering the government’s agreements with the company. But the existence of a Pentagon contract does not establish whether the military or SpaceX has authority over specific operational restrictions, including the new speed limit.

title: Trump-backed GOP candidate who ousted scandal-plagued incumbent warns against 'never-ending war' with Iran
description: Television journalist turned congressional hopeful Ryan Elijah says transparency, accountability will be his focus following victory over Cory Mills in contentious Florida GOP primary.
content: For 14 years, Ryan Elijah reported on Central Florida’s biggest stories from the television newsroom. Now, he is on a mission to represent the same community in Congress. Elijah stepped into a contentious GOP primary in which he warned that incumbent Cory Mills was at risk of losing the Republican-leaning district to the Democrats, following a series of personal and professional scandals. Elijah won a convincing victory in the August 18 Republican primary, receiving 47% of the vote to Mills' 34%. Trump, who had originally endorsed Mills, later claimed that he had privately encouraged the embattled congressman to withdraw from the race. REP CORY MILLS DRAWS FIRST REPUBLICAN CHALLENGER AS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS, EXPULSION THREAT MOUNT Recently, the veteran television journalist sat down with Fox News Digital to discuss his views on Iran, affordability, and immigration, while pledging to remain an independent voice in Congress, and a strong advocate for Volusia and Seminole counties. Elijah did not take the decision to leave working in media lightly, but felt a call to leadership: "I love my job. It's something I could have retired from TV and been perfectly happy. But I think we all look for the time you're asked to step up and lead. And for me, that was this time. When we saw how the primary was playing out, it just became clear that we were going to lose this election in November. "And I decided that we had the connections in this community to throw our hat in the ring. We had the trust from the community and the primary played out a lot like we thought it would, where people wanted a choice. I think that's what primaries are all about in Seminole County and Volusia County spoke really loud. In that primary, and now I think they put us in a great spot to hold this seat in November." Elijah pledges to put transparency and accountability front and center for the constituents of the seventh district: "Well, I think transparency and accountability are huge issues. I think when I talk to people, they don't feel like they're heard very much in Washington. And I think that you have to be transparent about whatever you can. And first of all, if you have nothing to hide, that's the best way to be transparent because you can exactly show your business dealings and how your life dealings are. "And that's something we've talked about a lot…and then in terms of accountability, no one is above the law. And that's a message that Americans want to hear, whether you're a Democrat or Republican, there are laws for a reason, and we have to make sure those laws are upheld." As the military engagement with Iran is rattling global energy markets and pinching Americans' pocketbooks, Elijah concedes the need to thwart a nuclear Iran, but also is wary of another forever war: GOP RISING STAR HELPED TOPPLE TRUMP-BACKED INCUMBENT. NOW HE'S CAUGHT LEADERSHIP'S EYE "This is a decade-long issue and a conflict between Iran and its proxies, where they have targeted and they have killed Americans. So the U.S. military right now is trying to end that conflict. But as representatives, we have to listen to the American people. We have to listen to central Floridians. "And they have been very clear on this. They're concerned about it. They are concerned this is going to be a never-ending war. They don't want that. I don't want that either. I share that belief, which is why I think we need to draw this conflict down. And we need to make sure that Iran is not a nuclear threat." On the immigration issue, Elijah cites improvement under GOP leadership on the issue, but argues that enforcement focus should remain on criminals: "This is another issue where I think you have to look at where we've come from. When you let tens of millions of illegal people into this country, you're going to have issues that take a long time to fix. And I think if you look at the way there has to be a federal, a local, and a state cooperation with immigration, that's what it takes to work. Which is why when I talk to all the sheriffs in our district that are endorsing us, they're handling immigration much better than other parts around the country because they have that cooperation. "We need to start with the criminals. We have got many criminals still here illegally in the United States. That's what they focused on in central Florida. That's what ICE needs to focus on, removing the criminals. And there's a compassionate way to handle this as we've got an issue that is not going to be fixed in just six or 12 months." Elijah consistently emphasizes that he will be an independent voice for the district, not a partisan rubber stamp: "Well, I've said a lot. Look, I ran in this primary without the president's endorsement. I've been an independent voice in this and I've told a lot of people that ask me that question. "As you can imagine, I go to a lot of doors. That's a question: ‘Will you support the president? Will you not support the president?’ And what I tell them is, if it's a policy that supports our country and supports our district, I'm going to support that policy. "More often than not, I will because I'm a Republican. I like a lot of those policies. If there's a policy I disagree with, we won't. So in that situation, that's where things are at." Finally, Elijah acknowledges that affordability, while lacking a quick and easy fix, is the defining 2026 issue for much of the electorate: "I think the number one thing that we hear from people, and that's affordability, and that's not an easy fix, but I think what they want out of government is accountability. We talked about that before, that government is going to be accountable on its spending, on its policies, and getting inflation down, which is going to lower interest rates. It's going to lower the cost of living. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "People in Central Florida, people around the country, they want to be heard. And what they're saying in a very clear tone right now is make sure that you control government spending and protect the future of our children. That's probably the biggest thing I want them to notice." Elijah will be facing Navy veteran and former NASA employee Bale Dalton in the November 3 general election.

title: WATCH: Georgia Senate debate erupts over white supremacy allegations, Epstein ties in fiery exchange
description: Candidates running for the US Senate in Georgia clashed over alleged neo-Nazi activity and ties to Jeffrey Epstein during their last debate before the election.
content: Georgia's contentious U.S. Senate race erupted into a heated confrontation Tuesday night as Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., accused GOP challenger Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., of allowing the dissemination of "neo-Nazi propaganda" inside his own home, prompting Collins to fire back over Ossoff's financial support from a billionaire with ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The exchange unfolded during the candidates' second and final debate ahead of the Nov. 3 general election, which was hosted by the Atlanta Press Club and broadcast by Georgia Public Broadcasting network. During the debate, Ossoff sought to tie his GOP opponent to White nationalism and repeatedly demanded that Collins commit to stopping the dissemination of hateful rhetoric involving his campaign staff, in particular Collins' son-in-law, which Ossoff alleged has continued despite blowback. Meanwhile, Collins accused his Democrat opponent of fueling threats against his family, refusing to return campaign support connected to LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and questioned Ossoff over his support for candidates linked to controversial streamer Hasan Piker. DEM ‘EPSTEIN CLASS’ ATTACK BACKFIRES AS TOP CANDIDATES FUNDED BY EPSTEIN-TIED BILLIONAIRE "How weak a person do you have to be to be unable to stop someone under your own roof from disseminating neo-Nazi propaganda while you run for the Senate?" Ossoff asked, referencing reporting about his opponent's son-in-law, David Alan Scheer II, who was the subject of a CNN investigation about sharing Nazi propaganda imagery, promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories and polling his online followers about whether he should produce a video titled "Why Gen-Z Doesn't Hate Hitler." "How about this, Mike? We can shake hands on it," Ossoff continued to press. "Will you commit tonight that for the remainder of this campaign, it's just three weeks, Mike, you won't allow any more neo-Nazi propaganda to be produced from your house? Can you make that commitment?" Collins responded by accusing Ossoff of inflaming hostility toward his family, pointing to threats he said he and his son-in-law had received. "I'm a little tired of this, Jon," Collins said. "There's a crazy person in jail right now because of your rhetoric," he alleged, before saying he had received another threat just the previous day. JON OSSOFF SILENT ON SPLC INDICTMENT AFTER TAKING MORE THAN $700K FROM AFFILIATE OF INDICTED GROUP "You have not denounced, you've not condemned Reid Hoffman, one of your largest donors out there, one that's been supporting you with over $1 million," Collins shot back. "Why don't you denounce that? Why don't you return that money?" Collins was referring to Reid Hoffman, the billionaire LinkedIn co-founder and major Democratic donor whose past relationship with Epstein has drawn scrutiny. Hoffman has acknowledged meeting with Epstein after the financier's 2008 conviction for sex offenses and visiting his private island. Hoffman also contributed $7,000 directly to Ossoff's campaign and $1 million to a political action committee supporting the Georgia Democrat, according to previously reported campaign finance records. Earlier in the debate, Collins went further, accusing Hoffman of sending Epstein ice cream with a message referencing girls, while again pressing Ossoff to reject his financial support. "Jon Ossoff, his number one donor, one of his largest donors, is Reid Hoffman, the same guy that's in the same files, the same guy that sent ice cream, ice cream to Jeffrey Epstein on his birthday and said, 'This is for the girls,'" Collins said during an earlier exchange in the debate. THUNE-ALIGNED GROUPS UNLEASH HISTORIC WAR CHEST TO DEFEND SENATE MAJORITY: 'WINNING MESSAGE' The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Hoffman sent Epstein ice cream in 2014 with a message indicating it was intended for him or "for the girls." Hoffman has apologized for his association with Epstein, which he said stemmed from fundraising activities involving the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and has not been accused of wrongdoing in connection with Epstein's crimes. Ossoff rejected the Hoffman comparison, however, arguing that the allegations against Collins involved someone living in the congressman's home rather than a political donor. "Mike, if any of these folks were based in my house, then I'd understand you to ask me to take responsibility for them," Ossoff said. "What I asked you, Mike, was, can you commit for just three weeks to stop the production of neo-Nazi propaganda from your home?" Earlier in the debate, Collins was directly questioned about concerns from Black Georgians over allegations of White-nationalist ties involving members of his political operation. It's abhorrent," Collins responded, adding that he had fired staffers when controversies arose. title: Pregnant influencer 'just so shocked' when flight attendant refuses to lift her bag

content: A pregnant influencer’s awkward luggage spat has ignited a heated debate over flight attendant responsibilities. Influencer Dominique Elissa recently recalled asking a male flight attendant to place her bag in an overhead bin while she was traveling. Speaking on the "Big Small Talk" podcast Oct. 7, Elissa said she explained to the flight attendant that she was pregnant and had been told not to lift the bag herself. The bag weighed nearly 9 pounds, according to Elissa. TRAVELERS RAGE AS BUDGET AIRLINE PLANS OVERHEAD BAG FEE: 'HIGHWAY ROBBERY' She said the flight attendant declined to lift it. title: Nuggets and Rockets offer the best long-shot value in the NBA championship futures market
description: The NBA Season's top championship bet may be the 76ers at +900 after adding Jaylen Brown and LeBron James alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.
content: The NBA Season is just around the corner. If you haven't been watching preseason, I can't really blame you. Once the games start to have meaning, we will have great betting opportunities. Eastern Conference The New York Knicks took home the crown last season, and have run back the same team. However, I am not expecting them to get back-to-back championships. We haven't had the same winner in two straight years since the Golden State Warriors had Kevin Durant on their team. He's been on three different teams since then. So, why not the Knicks? Winning championships is hard. I'm not taking anything away from New York, but it seemed like everything went their way last year. They beat the Hawks, then the 76ers, and finally the Cavaliers before beating San Antonio in five games. They are still the cream of the crop, but they've played a lot of basketball, and it does eventually catch up with you. THE 76ERS JUMP TO BETTING FAVORITE OUT EAST AFTER LEBRON JAMES TAKES HIS TALENTS TO PHILADELPHIA The easy choice in the East is the 76ers. They have Tyrese Maxey running point guard, Joel Embiid at center, and they won a playoff series last year. Then they went out and added Jaylen Brown and some guy named LeBron James. Seemingly defying Father Time, James continues to be an elite player. Embiid will always be a question mark with his health. The team no longer has a great backup behind him, but you could conceivably put James at center, Brown at power forward, Edgecombe at small forward, and slip Anfernee Simons into shooting guard. Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope are solid bench pieces as well. They are clearly the two best teams in the East, but that doesn't mean they finish 1-2 in the regular season. I'll take the 76ers to win at +900, because I genuinely don't think anyone else from the East has a real shot outside of the Knicks, and I don't see them winning two in a row. LEBRON JAMES SHUTS DOWN JOEL EMBIID RIFT RUMOR, BUT SIXERS LEADERSHIP TENSION IS REAL Western Conference The Western Conference is also a bit of a two-horse race. The Spurs made it to the Finals last season, and they lost to the Knicks. Victor Wembanyama seemingly disappeared in that series, and they couldn't close out games. I'm not sure that changes this season. The Spurs are deep, but unless Wemby takes another leap forward (which is more likely than not), they won't represent the West again. The Thunder are still the deepest team in the league. They are both +270 to win the championship, and I just don't see the value in wagering on either. The West is better for taking a long shot. My first choice here is the Nuggets at +2500. They still have the best player in the league. Jamal Murray is one of the best heatwave scorers in the league, and now their bench, which sucked for years, is a bit deeper. They have DeMar DeRozan, who is one of the best scorers in the league. title: Sleeper GOP candidate puts blue-leaning state in play as fraud scandal shadows Dems
description: Michele Tafoya trails Peggy Flanagan by just four points as Minnesota's massive welfare fraud scandal reshapes the rare GOP Senate pickup bid.
content: Republicans are eyeing a rare Senate pickup opportunity in Minnesota, where GOP nominee Michele Tafoya is narrowing the gap with Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, prompting Fox News to move the race toward Republicans less than three weeks before Election Day. It's been nearly a quarter-century since Republicans last won a Senate election in the blue-leaning state. But Tafoya, a former longtime NFL sideline reporter, is aiming to break that losing streak by flipping the seat held by retiring Democratic Sen. Tina Smith. A new Minnesota Star Tribune/KARE 11 poll shows Tafoya trailing Flanagan by just four percentage points. On Tuesday, the Fox News Power Rankings shifted the race to the right, from Likely Democrat to Lean Democrat. GOP SENATE HOPEFUL SOUNDS ALARM AFTER TERROR PLOT THWARTED "The more that Minnesotans learn about me and my opponent and see what my opponent has failed to do over the last eight years alongside [Democratic Gov.] Tim Walz, they're understanding Minnesota needs change. We need fresh ideas, we need an independent thinker and they're jumping on board," Tafoya said in a Fox News Digital interview. Fox News Digital reached out to the Flanagan campaign for comment but didn't receive a response at the time this story was published. The race is unfolding against the backdrop of Minnesota's massive welfare assistance fraud scandal, which has attracted national attention for nearly a year and prompted Democratic Gov. Tim Walz to abandon his 2026 re-election bid. The scandal has also become a central issue in Tafoya's campaign against Flanagan. Tafoya noted that "there has been historic fraud under this administration, where Peggy Flanagan, my opponent, has been the second-in-charge in this state. And not only was the money stolen, it hollowed out these programs that were supposed to be getting help, like kids' meals or autistic kids or seniors who were supposed to be getting visits, health visits, wellness visits. And, so, that's been hollowed out. DEMS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP SENATE SEATS BUT GOP'S MASSIVE CASH ADVANTAGE AN OBSTACLE "Walz understood that he was not going to win another term as governor with these conditions, but my opponent thinks she deserves a promotion. I think people are starting to realize she deserves a pink slip." Flanagan has said she is "incredibly angry with the fraud," has acknowledged public frustration over the scandal and said more could have been done sooner to catch and prevent the fraud. The lieutenant governor has noted that she was not in charge of the state agencies at the center of the scandals or steering the daily state response. She has also distanced herself from Walz, who has accepted blame for the fraud. DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING - HERE ARE THREE FACTORS THAT COULD STOP IT "It's wall-to-wall coverage on every nightly news program here for months and months. We're seeing it in polling," Minnesota-based veteran national Republican strategist Kirsten Kukowski told Fox News Digital. Pointing to Flanagan, Kukowski said she has "a lot of fraud baggage ... and it's really made the Senate race really tight here." Tafoya is also highlighting a recent spate of gang-related shootings in the Minneapolis-St. Paul suburbs and on Monday announced a five-point-plan to combat the violence. "We will do more in our first eight weeks as a U.S. Senator than Peggy Flanagan has done in eight years as the second in charge," she told Fox News Digital. WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS MIDTERM POWER RANKINGS "First of all, we've got to name the problem, and even Somali lawmakers and law enforcement have named this problem. We have a Somali gang violence problem. We've got to name it. She refuses to name it. You can't fix it if you don't name it," Tafoya emphasized as she referred to Flanagan. Flanagan, a progressive candidate backed by left-wing champions, Sens. Bernie Sanders Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Ro Khanna, topped more moderate Democratic Rep. Angie Craig by roughly 20 points in the August Senate primary. Tafoya grabbed over 50% of the vote in the GOP Senate primary as she topped a crowded field of rivals. She was heavily recruited by national Republicans, including Sen. Tim Scott, the National Republican Senatorial Committee chair. "We did a really good job of recruiting the most independent-minded Republican who understands why it's important to win in Minnesota," Scott said in an interview on Fox News' "Hannity." "Michele Tafoya has a story to tell. She's doing a really good job. This is a race that will come down to the wire." SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Senate Majority Leader John Thune, the top Republican in the chamber, recently teamed up on the campaign trail in Minnesota with Tafoya. But the Thune-aligned Senate Leadership Fund, the top super PAC backing GOP Senate candidates, has yet to make a major investment in the race. Asked about national Republican support, Tafoya said, "We are getting small dollar donations from all over the country. We're getting donations from every county in this state, and I am a happy warrior. And I will deal with the circumstances I'm given. ... We're going to win this campaign on ideas." Democrats are hopeful that popular Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar, who is running for governor this year, may help push Flanagan over the finish line. "Our latest poll has Flanagan with a strong lead, and we fully expect her to be elected to the U.S. Senate," Lauren French, communications director for the Senate Democrat-aligned Senate Majority PAC, told Fox News Digital. French argued that "Republicans are spending in deep red states and watching the battleground map extend around them. Their desperate last-minute attempt to push Minnesota into play is a political ploy." DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB Flanagan has repeatedly tied Tafoya to President Donald Trump, whose approval ratings are well underwater in Minnesota. "Michele Tafoya is all in for Donald Trump — and he's all in for her," Flanagan reiterated Monday in a social media post. Flanagan, who is Native American, also wrote on X, "My Ojibwe name is Gizhiiwewidamookwe, which means ‘Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice Woman.’ I’m going to be Minnesota’s voice in the U.S. Senate — not Donald Trump’s." But Tafoya appears to be putting some daylight between herself and Trump, as she highlights her support for abortion rights. "I’m a pro-choice Republican not afraid to stand up to my party," Tafoya says in a new campaign commercial. "When Trump is right, I will work with him. When he is wrong, I will stand up for Minnesota." The ad was quickly criticized by leaders on the right. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Among them was Mercedes Schlapp, a senior fellow at the Conservative Political Action Conference, who said on social media, "Pro-life Republicans will stay home after watching this ad." But hours later, Trump gave Tafoya a plug, telling the crowd at an Ohio rally he headlined, "You have to vote for Michele Tafoya, who’s a very respected person."

title: French newspaper claims climate change is fueling child marriages, including girls as young as 12
description: A French newspaper claims climate change accelerates child marriage in Bangladesh and other nations, drawing sharp criticism from Moms for Liberty.
content: A French newspaper claimed Tuesday that climate change is accelerating child marriages in developing countries, including among girls as young as 12, citing research suggesting that natural disasters are pushing impoverished families to marry off their daughters at increasingly younger ages. Le Parisien's report, "She was only 12: Climate change, a new accelerator of child marriage," directly linked weather-related disasters to early marriages in Bangladesh, Kenya and other countries. "In Bangladesh, Kenya and elsewhere, climate disasters are worsening child marriages," the newspaper said in a passage translated from French. "By destroying incomes and homes, they push some families to marry off their daughters at increasingly younger ages." ALASKA STATE FAIR BARS PARENTAL RIGHTS GROUP DUE TO 'EXTREMIST' GROUP DESIGNATION BY FAR-LEFT ORGANIZATION The article drew criticism from Moms for Liberty CEO and co-founder Tina Descovich, who told Fox News Digital attributing child marriage to climate change shifts responsibility away from those exploiting children. "Blaming climate change for the abhorrent practice of marrying off girls as young as 12 sounds absolutely wild … but it’s just the latest absurd excuse for disgusting behavior, shifting responsibility onto the environment instead of the people and ideologies that choose to exploit children," Descovich said. "At Moms for Liberty, we see this same mentality every day in America, where activists blame society, systems or external factors for harming kids rather than demanding strong families, parental rights, and personal accountability that actually protect our children." TALIBAN WIPES OUT DECADES OF PROGRESS AS 2.4M AFGHAN GIRLS REMAIN LOCKED OUT OF SCHOOL, UN AGENCY SAYS The French newspaper based much of its reporting on Plan International's 2026 report, which examined the relationship between climate-related disasters and child marriage. Researchers surveyed 5,000 girls and young women across Bangladesh, Kenya, Peru, Senegal and Zimbabwe. According to Le Parisien, 36% reported observing increased child marriage after climate-related disasters, while 11% said they had personally experienced child marriage. Fox News Digital reached out to Le Parisien and Plan International for comment but did not immediately receive a response. The newspaper highlighted the case of a 12-year-old Bangladeshi girl who was reportedly married off four days after boys harassed her inside a cyclone shelter. According to a teenage friend interviewed by the outlet, the girl later gave birth to a baby who died, leaving her with serious health complications. AMERICANS TRAVEL TO PAKISTAN TO FREE CHRISTIANS TRAPPED IN MODERN-DAY SLAVERY: 'GOD'S HAND WAS IN IT' Another case involved Runa, a 15-year-old Bangladeshi girl whose widowed mother arranged her marriage after a cyclone destroyed a family's livestock and income. Runa described during a July interview with Australia's ABC News how the marriage interrupted her education. "I did not want to get married," Runa said. "I wanted to continue my education. The decision made me feel very sad and helpless." However, Runa was eventually allowed to return to school with assistance from aid organizations after her husband's family agreed to let her resume her education, according to ABC News. Now 17 and a mother, Runa said returning to her studies had given her renewed hope for the future. Child marriage was already widespread in Bangladesh before the latest report. According to UNICEF's 2025 survey, 47.2% of women ages 20 to 24 were married before turning 18, down from 51.4% in 2019. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE UNICEF identifies poverty, entrenched gender norms, harmful traditional practices, barriers to education and climate-related disasters among the factors contributing to child marriage. Bangladesh's 2017 Child Marriage Restraint Act generally prohibits marriage for girls younger than 18, although the law includes an exception allowing underage marriages with parental consent and court approval under special circumstances. Plan International maintains that climate-related disasters created additional financial pressures on families, particularly those dependent on agriculture and livestock. Tanushree Soni, a Plan International representative, previously explained the economic circumstances behind child marriages during an interview with ABC News. "Financial stress is the trigger," Soni said. "The families look to lessen the burden because they don't consider girls to be part of their own families." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The research describes a relationship between weather-related disasters and child marriage, although the survey findings alone do not establish that human-caused climate change directly caused the individual marriages described in the newspaper's report.

title: Mamdani accuses Blakeman of 'bigotry and racism' in breakout debate that mayor didn't watch
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani admitted he didn't watch Tuesday's gubernatorial debate between Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Bruce Blakeman.
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman of "bigotry and racism" Tuesday night despite admitting he didn't watch Blakeman's debate with Gov. Kathy Hochul live. Mamdani made the statement in comments to reporters Wednesday after Blakeman and Hochul squared off Tuesday night. A reporter asked Mamdani whether he was bothered that Hochul hadn't responded to Blakeman's claims that the NYC mayor is an antisemite. SHOCK POLL: POWERFUL BLUE STATE GOV'S LEAD SHRINKS TO SINGLE DIGITS WEEKS BEFORE ELECTION "And I think the governor also made clear, you know, I've said that I, I didn't watch the debate beyond the clip, but I think the governor has made clear time and time again what her vision is. It's a vision of a more affordable New York," he continued. "And when it comes to Bruce Blakeman, his vision seems to be making life harder for working people. When the governor and I announced putting our city on a pathway to universal childcare, Bruce Blakeman went on television and said this was rewarding lazy parents who would sit at home and watch 'The View.' When we were speaking about concerns about what HR1 was going to do with regards to healthcare access across the state, Bruce Blakeman went on television and said that he would cut Medicaid in half." The debate opened with the candidates being asked about the conduct of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which last week drew outrage in New York City after the shooting of a 28-year-old Dominican national whom the Department of Homeland Security said refused to comply with lawful orders during a targeted operation in the Bronx. A 5-year-old boy inside Oscar Bergal's vehicle was unharmed. "Kathy Hochul appealed to ICE to let this criminal out. The question that New Yorkers have to ask is what was this guy doing in New York in the first place? It's because Kathy Hochul has made us a sanctuary state," Blakeman said. MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION' "Think about it. This guy came into the country illegally. He's been convicted of a crime. He's got pending charges for dealing drugs, poison to our children. And he's a gang banger. This is who Kathy Hochul is defending?" Blakeman continued. "I have a cooperative agreement with ICE until Kathy Hochul said we could no longer cooperate with ICE. We got over 2,000 illegal migrants out of my county with criminal records ranging from rape, attempted murder, robbery, burglary, drug dealing, carjacking, gang activity. "And that's because we cooperated with ICE, and we didn't raid one school, one hospital, one daycare center or one church. If you cooperate with federal law enforcement, it makes for a safer community. That's what I did. Kathy Hochul is taking that ability away from us. That's why things like this happen." Hochul called Blakeman's response a "non-answer" because "he refused to condemn what ICE did." MULLIN CALLS MAMDANI'S ANTI-ICE RHETORIC 'DANGEROUS' FOLLOWING NEW YORK SHOOTING "So, he basically says in the state of New York, he'd be fine if ICE agents shoot into cars, shoot guns into vehicles, not knowing who's inside and could have killed a 5-year-old child. If that doesn't shock the conscience of everybody — and it should shock his conscience as well — that he says, 'That's OK, that's how ICE is supposed to do it,'" Hochul added. "I'll tell you what. I oversee over 500 policing agencies in the state of New York. Over half a million arrests every year. That's not how you conduct yourself. ICE is out of control. It's out of control in Nassau County." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Blakeman pushed back, saying, "It never would have happened" but for Hochul's "sanctuary policy." title: 40 Days For Life CEO Shawn Carney on 'College GameDay' religious sign ban: 'Nobody's for this'
description: Shawn Carney slams ESPN's "College GameDay" religious sign ban at Alabama, calling it embarrassing that corporate America is targeting Christians in the SEC.
content: For years, one of ESPN's most popular original programs has been "College GameDay." The show, which features some of college football's most prominent personalities traveling to different campuses across the country, has been a fan favorite for well over three decades now. One of the best parts about "GameDay" is the students and fans piling into a small area on campus to express themselves and cheer on their team, and one way they've done that since the show started was to bring handmade signs. They've featured everything from clever jokes to insults to opposing mascots, but last weekend in Tuscaloosa, the "GameDay" executives took a stand and introduced a "no religious signs" ban ahead of the Crimson Tide's top-ten showdown with Georgia. This took pretty much everyone by surprise, including 40 Days For Life CEO Shawn Carney. CHRISTIAN WOMAN PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO NEW 'ORWELLIAN' CHARGES FOR STANDING AND SILENT PRAYER Carney's company focuses on holding peaceful vigils outside of abortion facilities, offering pregnant women alternatives as well as a last chance to "choose life." To say faith is near and dear to his heart is an understatement, and when he first heard the news about the religious sign ban, he was perplexed. "We've done this and it doesn't work," Carney said when discussing the ban. "It's called 2020 and all of the companies that decided to go in that direction, it just backfired. It's so stupid." Carney reveals that he's a huge fan of "College GameDay" and a diehard Texas A&M Aggie, and ESPN trying to muzzle what he calls their largest demographic of fans doesn't make sense in his eyes. THE NFL IS AMERICA'S MOST GOD-CENTERED PROFESSIONAL SPORTS LEAGUE AND SUNDAY'S GAMES CONTINUED TO PROVE IT "Football is religion in the South," he explains. "You look at the SEC and you can throw in the Big 10, these are religious people that follow college football. That's a huge market that is college football." And it isn't just the fans, either. Coaches and players alike are very faith-based and give credit to Christianity with helping guide them through trying times. It's a clear case of Disney and ESPN not understanding who they're appealing to with these decisions. PAT MCAFEE’S PRO-MILITARY COMMENTS ON ‘COLLEGE GAMEDAY’ IGNITE ONLINE BACKLASH FROM THE LEFT For the ban to take place at the University of Alabama, of all places, was even more stupefying to Carney. title: 10 health conditions may be linked to Alzheimer's years before diagnosis
description: Depression, vertigo, headaches and stroke were among conditions linked to early-onset Alzheimer's disease years before diagnosis, a Finnish study suggests.
content: Certain medical conditions may signal early-onset Alzheimer’s disease several years before diagnosis, a new Finnish study suggests. Researchers found that depression, vertigo, headaches and other conditions were more common during the five years preceding diagnosis, potentially offering clues for earlier detection. The researchers analyzed medical records from 407 people with early-onset Alzheimer’s disease and 4,035 people of similar age and sex without the diagnosis, focusing on the 15 years prior to diagnosis. SUBTLE CHANGE IN HOW YOU SPEAK COULD BE EARLY SIGN OF DEMENTIA RISK, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS The average age at diagnosis was 60. Early-onset disease is diagnosed in people under 65. The findings were published in the journal Alzheimer’s & Dementia. The following conditions were found to be significantly more prevalent among those who were ultimately diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s. Differences in medical conditions were most pronounced in the five years before an early-onset Alzheimer's diagnosis, the study showed. 3 THINGS TO AVOID IN MIDDLE AGE COULD MEAN 13 MORE YEARS WITHOUT DEMENTIA, STUDY FINDS The researchers also found that healthcare visits increased substantially among early-onset Alzheimer’s patients immediately before and during the time of diagnosis, which may indicate emerging symptoms. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "It is well-known that the neuropathological changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease begin at least 15 to 20 years before clinical cognitive symptoms appear," Suvi-Johanna Krüger, M.D., Ph.D., study co-author and clinical lecturer at University of Oulu, said in a press release. "Most previous studies have focused on late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, and considerably less is known about early-onset Alzheimer’s disease." Study limitations Because the study was observational, it only establishes associations and cannot demonstrate that these conditions can reliably predict Alzheimer's disease. "Our study cannot determine whether these conditions cause early-onset Alzheimer’s disease or whether they are consequences of the underlying disease process," Krüger noted. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Some conditions may represent risk factors, while others may reflect early symptoms or changes occurring during the prodromal phase of the disease." It is also possible that genetics, lifestyle and socioeconomic factors played a role in the patients’ outcomes. Also, the researchers could not independently verify all medical diagnoses or assess the severity of the patients’ disease. Additionally, the findings may not apply to populations outside Finland. Larger studies looking at disease biomarkers, genetics and clinical assessments could help determine whether there is a casual relationship between the medical conditions and Alzheimer’s incidence and whether these medical patterns could be used to improve early detection. title: Man posing as NFL player accused of conning women out of $1.3M
description: Domonique DuBose spotted red flags when a man on Hinge with 85,000 followers and a blue checkmark claimed to be a San Francisco 49ers player.
content: A man claiming to play for the San Francisco 49ers matches with you on a dating app. His Instagram has 85,000 followers and a blue checkmark. There are videos showing what appears to be his football lifestyle. He drives luxury cars and seems to have plenty of money. So, would you believe him? Domonique DuBose had her doubts. When she joined me on The CyberGuy Report podcast, she explained how she became suspicious of a man who allegedly used a fake NFL identity to pursue women and promote fraudulent investments. Federal prosecutors say Daejon Labrayae Love and an alleged accomplice received approximately $1.3 million from at least 26 women. Love pleaded not guilty Tuesday to a felony charge of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and a public defender representing him did not reply to a request for comment. Magistrate Judge Jolie A. Russo ordered Love detained as a flight risk. DuBose recognized warning signs and avoided losing any money herself. "Basically, I caught on right away," DuBose told me. What she uncovered raises serious questions about how easily someone can fake an identity online and how you can spot the warning signs before it's too late. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com ‘TINDER SWINDLER’ ROMANCE FRAUDSTER PROMISES ‘SAFE’ DATING APP – USING INTEL FROM CON MAN PLAYBOOK How the fake 49ers player made his story believable According to DuBose, Love's Instagram account looked like something you might expect from a professional athlete. His posts showed him wearing San Francisco 49ers clothing and enjoying an expensive lifestyle. There were also videos from football-related locations, including footage that appeared connected to the Super Bowl in New Orleans. "It looked valid. I mean, he had 85,000 followers. He had a blue check," DuBose recalled. She even contacted a friend who had played for the 49ers. Surprisingly, she says that friend initially supported Love's story. Still, she continued investigating. "I looked at everything from the NFL roster for the Niners to IR to practice squad," she explained. She also searched his college football history, looking for evidence that he had actually played at the professional level. Another detail bothered her. Nearly every photo seemed to feature 49ers clothing. To DuBose, who knew professional football players, that constant display of team merchandise seemed unusual. Federal investigators later confirmed with representatives of the NFL and the 49ers that Love had never been employed by either organization. That's what makes this case so troubling. A convincing social media profile can make someone seem credible long before anyone checks the facts behind it. The dating app red flags that caught her attention DuBose said she met Love on Hinge. His profile described him as an NFL receiver, but their first interactions made her uncomfortable. "It was really fast how he wanted to get my number," she told me. Instead of sharing her personal number, she took a precaution that limited how much information he could access. "I gave him my work cell phone number instead of my own phone number, and he started texting me." Then came an unusual flood of attention. Love sent several videos and voice recordings almost immediately. One recording played during our podcast interview included this opening: "So what's up, beautiful? I had to shoot my shot with you." The messages also included extravagant claims about his wealth and how much he wanted to spend time with her. For DuBose, the pace of the attention felt strange. "And it was just so fast. It was so rapid," she recalled. Some of his other claims raised even more questions. DuBose said he talked about coming from a wealthy Swiss family and having ownership interests involving Gucci stores. She struggled to reconcile those stories with his supposed NFL career. Rather than accepting the explanation, she kept checking. The many identities behind the alleged $1.3 million scam Love's supposed football career was only one part of the alleged operation. During our podcast conversation, I asked DuBose about his different identities. She explained that he appeared to have more than two, with different names and professional backgrounds depending on whom he approached. According to federal investigators, Love used several names, including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love. His professional identity also changed depending on the person he approached. "He was a real estate investor. He was a day trader," DuBose explained. Prosecutors say Love used those claims to convince women that he had access to lucrative investment opportunities. His alleged accomplice, Taylor Jamie Chan, posed as a financial advisor who helped manage Love's fortune, court records allege. Together, they allegedly used fake bank and investment accounts showing enormous balances. They also staged FaceTime calls displaying fabricated investment gains. Some women even took out personal loans after Love promised they would quickly be repaid, the affidavit says. READ THE AFFIDAVIT – APP USERS, CLICK HERE: DuBose told me that some women appeared to receive early investment returns, which encouraged them to invest more. However, federal investigators say none of the victims they interviewed reported receiving actual returns after sending money. When women ran out of money or started asking too many questions, prosecutors allege Love cut off contact. More women come forward in the fake NFL player case The federal investigation has grown since the arrests. On Sept. 18, the FBI reported that 35 additional women had come forward claiming they were defrauded. Investigators were still working to verify those allegations. If confirmed, the number of identified victims would rise from 26 to 61. For DuBose, the emotional damage described by women who say they encountered Love has been particularly painful. She told me that some women described relationships lasting years. Others said they became deeply involved with someone whose identity they never fully understood. "There's some that dated him for 11, 12, 13 years off and on," she said. Those longer timelines reflect what women reportedly told DuBose. They extend beyond the February 2022 start date of the alleged financial scheme documented by federal investigators. "It breaks my heart," she told me during our interview. She was especially disturbed by the emotional vulnerability that someone could exploit when a person believes a relationship is genuine. "And using that to your advantage is just sick." DuBose also told me that she would like to confront Love about his alleged actions. After hearing so many stories, there's one answer she still wants. "I want to know why." The FBI has encouraged potential victims to come forward, even if they feel embarrassed about what happened. Investigators say reports from additional people may help them understand the full scope of the alleged scheme. Can dating apps do more to stop fake identities? One of the biggest questions raised by this case involves the platforms where these relationships begin. A blue checkmark and a large online following can make an account appear trustworthy. However, verification features vary by platform, and confirming an account holder's identity does not establish that their claimed career or wealth is genuine. DuBose expressed frustration about how easily someone can construct a false life on dating apps. "As far as the dating apps go, you can be whoever you want on those dating apps. And that's the scary part." She acknowledged that some platforms offer identity checks. However, she questioned whether those checks could ever guarantee that someone was telling the truth about their background. That's a concern worth considering. A person can use their real name and still make false claims about their job. They can also provide authentic photographs while exaggerating their wealth. For anyone meeting a stranger online, independent verification remains an important safeguard. LUTHER DAVIS ALLEGEDLY WORE DISGUISES TO POSE AS NFL PLAYERS IN MULTI-MILLION DOLLAR LOAN FRAUD SCHEME How to protect yourself from fake dating profiles You can still meet people online while taking precautions against fraud. These steps can help you identify suspicious behavior before a relationship becomes financially risky. 1) Verify someone's claimed career independently If someone says they play professional sports or hold a prestigious position, check official organizational records. Don't rely on social media search results alone. For example, NFL teams publish player rosters that you can check against someone's claims. 2) Be cautious when someone rushes intimacy Excessive attention early in a conversation may be an attempt to establish trust before introducing a financial request. Pay attention if someone immediately wants to move off the dating app or begins discussing a serious relationship before you've had time to get acquainted. 3) Keep your personal phone number private initially Communicate through the dating app until you feel comfortable. A separate phone number can help limit exposure, although it won't eliminate every risk. Avoid sharing your home address or workplace details with someone you have only recently met online. 4) Reverse-search photos and phone numbers Look for inconsistent names or multiple profiles using the same images. A reverse image search may reveal whether someone has copied photographs from another person's account. Our CyberGuy article explains how to avoid dating app scammers. 5) Never invest money based on an online relationship Be especially skeptical of guaranteed returns or requests to take out personal loans. Independently check any financial opportunity before considering it. Someone who genuinely cares about you should respect your decision to keep your finances separate. 6) Question stories that don't add up Conflicting information about someone's background deserves a closer look. Give yourself time to verify details without pressure. If the person becomes defensive or tries to discourage you from checking their claims, consider that another warning sign. DuBose continues taking precautions when meeting new people. She told me that she checks phone numbers and tries to establish whether someone is using a legitimate identity. "If you text me the moment you text me, I'm reverse checking your number. I'm making sure your name is valid." A reverse lookup can provide useful clues, although scammers may use spoofed numbers or accounts registered under other people's names. A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS. WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO? What to do if you already sent money to a scammer If you suspect someone has deceived you through a dating app, act quickly. Your chances of recovering money may depend on how you paid and how soon you report the transaction. Contact your bank or payment provider immediately Explain what happened and ask whether it can reverse or recall the payment. If you sent money through a wire transfer or payment app, contact that service's fraud department as soon as possible. Speed can be important when attempting to recover funds. Preserve the evidence Save screenshots of messages and dating profiles. Keep financial transaction records that could help investigators. Don't delete conversations before documenting them, even if the experience is upsetting. Report the fraud to the FBI File a complaint through IC3.gov and provide as much information as possible. Include the person's usernames, phone numbers and payment details. You can also report suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov. Notify the dating app Report the suspicious account so the platform can investigate and take appropriate action. Include any evidence showing that the person misrepresented their identity or requested money. Watch for recovery scams Criminals sometimes contact fraud victims again, claiming they can retrieve stolen money in exchange for an upfront payment. Be skeptical of anyone promising guaranteed recovery, especially if they request additional payments or sensitive financial information. If you have information involving Daejon Love or Taylor Chan specifically, the FBI requests tips through tips.fbi.gov or 1-800-CALL-FBI. Kurt's key takeaways What stayed with me after speaking with Domonique DuBose on The CyberGuy Report podcast was how convincing this alleged deception became. We're talking about someone who reportedly built an entire lifestyle around a career he never had. He used the credibility of a major NFL team and social media to get people to believe him. Some allegedly trusted him with significant amounts of money. During our conversation, I raised a question that I think deserves a serious answer. These social media companies can collect an extraordinary amount of information about us. As I put it on the podcast, "these social media companies know what toothbrush we're using and when we're going to buy a loaf of bread." So why does it remain so difficult to identify someone who builds a false professional identity and uses it to target people? I also admire how thoroughly DuBose investigated the situation. Even when someone she knew appeared to validate the story, she continued asking questions. Her experience is a reminder that you should never feel pressured to trust someone simply because their online life looks convincing. If a dating app verifies someone's identity but that person turns out to be lying about who they are, should the platform share responsibility for the damage? Or do you believe people should be entirely responsible for protecting themselves? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. title: Kamala Harris calls to expand Supreme Court, add states if Dems take Congress
description: Kamala Harris called for Supreme Court expansion and Electoral College changes, and a legal expert warned her proposals could set a dangerous precedent.
content: Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for institutional changes to the Supreme Court and the Electoral College during an interview Tuesday, calling for more justices on the highest court in the nation. "The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court. We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States," Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer on her "Baby, This is Keke Palmer" podcast. "I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right? "It's about, the popular vote has to matter, right? You know, all the things that make people feel, like, overwhelmed, and does their vote matter? We have, you know, listen, if the folks there want it, we should be pushing for statehood for Puerto Rico and D.C., right? These are some of the things that are structural that we need to do, but we need to reestablish affordable child care," Harris added. KAMALA HARRIS FACES DEMOCRATIC DOUBTS OVER 2028 AS ALLIES PUSH BACK ON CLAIMS SHE’S SQUANDERED HER CHANCE Harris lost both the Electoral College and the popular vote to President Donald Trump in 2024. She told Palmer she still remains undecided about a 2028 presidential run. Y. David Scharf, chairman of Morrison Cohen LLP and head of its government strategies & controversies practice, told Fox News Digital that Harris' proposed changes could set a "dangerous precedent." "Kamala Harris says she wants to defend democracy, but her solution is to rewrite its rules when Democrats don't like the results. That's a dangerous precedent," he said. "Nine justices have been the number since 1869. FDR tried to pack the Supreme Court, and even his own party pushed back. Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg herself warned that expanding the court would make it look partisan. GAVIN NEWSOM EXPRESSES 'OPENNESS' TO PACKING SCOTUS, CALLS ELECTORAL COLLEGE SYSTEM 'PERVERTED' "The Electoral College is written into the Constitution. Eliminating it requires a constitutional amendment, not a Democratic majority in Congress. You don't get to change the referee because you don't like the calls. Harris may think this is a winning message for the Democratic base, but it's a much tougher sell to the independent and swing voters her party needs." The former VP also spoke about the midterm elections during the interview. "On the first Tuesday in November, the midterms are going to happen," Harris said. "And our ability to put people in Congress who will say no, when they do things like cut $1 trillion out of Medicaid will be powerful and affect people right away. "Our ability to put people in Congress who will say enough of the corruption, enough of ending the funding for research on issues like fibroids, which they have done under the guise of attacking DEI, can be stopped. There are things that are not only about what will be helpful, but also stopping what is harmful, that we can do right away with these midterm elections." Her comments come days after her 2024 vice presidential running mate, Gov. Tim Walz, warned of a reckoning among Democrats if the party fails to deliver on promises should they take back Congress and potentially the presidency in 2028. Harris was called out by Democratic advisors Tuesday for failing to reinvent herself politically as she weighs another White House run, Politico reported. The report, based on interviews with nearly 20 California-based Democratic donors and strategists, highlighted growing skepticism among some party insiders about Harris' political future and whether she has done enough to distinguish herself from her unsuccessful 2024 campaign. It seems like more of the same to me." Veteran Democratic strategist Maria Cardona, an outside advisor to Harris, pushed back against the criticism highlighted in a new Politico report and called the story "infuriating" in a previous statement to Fox News Digital. title: Hollywood star sounds alarm over disappearing jobs as productions flee California
description: Hollywood’s ongoing production exodus is leaving actors and crew members struggling to find work, as Jeff Garlin and Bryan Callen describe the industry’s declining opportunities.
content: When Adam Carolla asked actor and comedian Jeff Garlin on his podcast last week whether there was "anything going on in Hollywood anymore," the "Curb Your Enthusiasm" star admitted that acting roles had virtually dried up for him. "I haven't worked in almost three years since ‘Curb’ ended," Garlin said, prefacing his remarks with uncertainty about whether he should reveal his circumstances. "…The reason that you and I do this no longer exists. It doesn’t." "We could be doing this thing in Sweden," he added. HOLLYWOOD JOBS FLEE OVERSEAS AS CONGRESS SCRAMBLES TO STOP PRODUCTION EXODUS — WITH TRUMP'S BLESSING With that comment, Garlin was referring to the growing number of productions that have left not only California but the country altogether. Meanwhile, California Gov. Gavin Newsom's office said last week that a new post-production tax credit, an expanded film and television tax credit, and protections for actors against AI-generated content are expected to help Hollywood. In total, 35 films, 28 of which are independent projects, received production incentives in the latest round of awards under the California Film Commission's expanded Film and Television Tax Credit Program. The commission estimates the projects will generate more than $1 billion in direct production spending, create jobs for more than 5,400 cast and crew members, and employ 24,800 background actors. HOLLYWOOD FEELING MORE HOPEFUL AMID A PUSH FOR FILM TAX CREDITS AND PARAMOUNT STAYING PUT, FILMMAKER SAYS Additionally, a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers is working on a federal tax credit for film and television productions that could be used alongside state production incentives. Even with the proposed and expanded incentives, conversations with people in Hollywood suggest that uncertainty remains about whether the measures will bring production jobs back. NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE' "The number of American productions that are filmed in Ireland tells you all you need to know. All these empty sound stages. It's a shame," Garlin said. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the industry has lost 49,000 jobs since 2022, following the COVID-19 pandemic and a slowdown in streaming production. TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS TRUMP CALLS HOLLYWOOD A 'TOTAL DISASTER,' PUSHES FEDERAL TAX INCENTIVE FOR FILM AFTER MEETING WITH JON VOIGHT Actor and comedian Bryan Callen told Fox News Digital that he sympathizes with Garlin but wasn't surprised by his admission. "You can’t make your living as just an actor anymore in Los Angeles. If you do a series on, say, Netflix, and it's a 10-episode series, do the math. Take a look at what’s left after taxes and commissions to your manager, your agent, whoever it might be," Callen said, emphasizing the high cost of producing films and television shows in Los Angeles. CHRIS ROCK EXPOSES BRUTAL REALITY OF HOLLYWOOD AFTER DECADES OF FAME "You are living, if you are lucky, a middle-class existence, but probably lower than that when you take into account how expensive everything is in Los Angeles — property and just having to live and buy food and all that stuff," he said. Callen himself has increasingly turned to stand-up comedy and podcasting rather than relying solely on acting. "I was like, I can't put all my eggs in this acting basket," he said, pointing to several factors that have diminished the cultural prominence of Hollywood’s biggest movie stars. "This business has been so atomized. The days of all of us going to one place, whether it's a TV show or a movie, to watch that one person are long gone… And if that's the case, big names are no longer big names. They just aren't." Still, despite what Callen described as the demise of Hollywood’s "monoculture" — an era when major stars alone could draw audiences to television shows and movies — he doesn’t believe Hollywood itself is going away. "Remember this about Los Angeles," Callen said. "First of all, you shot there because the weather was predictable. It wasn't going to rain you out. And number two, the best of the best still lives in Los Angeles." "People think they can move this business to Texas or whatever. No, you can't. At the end of the day, you still have the best sound engineers, the best directors, the best writers, the best special effects people, the best people who score film and all that." While Carolla and Garlin may share Callen’s perspective on Hollywood’s enduring strengths, they still had plenty to lament about the current state of the entertainment business in the Golden State. "I talked to a friend of mine… He's been working as an editor nonstop for 32 years…," Carolla said. "And he goes, ‘I'm retired. There's no work.’" "Everyone is moving out, and it’s affecting — I mean, again, everyone thinks about the actor, the director, but a crew has so many people that work, hairdressers, catering, craft service people, crew members." "It used to be, ‘Boy, you’re lucky, even if you’re talented, to break through.’ Now, it’s, ‘You’re lucky if someone even notices you’re in the room.’"

title: Pope Leo undergoes blood tests, X-ray following cancer surgery, Vatican says
description: Pope Leo XIV began walking and resumed eating after thoracic surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, with blood tests and an X-ray being part of his recovery.
content: Pope Leo XIV underwent blood tests and a chest X-ray Wednesday following surgery to remove a small nodule on his lung, with his recovery going "as expected," the Vatican announced. The development comes after the Holy See Press Office said "the night passed calmly for the Pope" at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital. The 71-year-old pontiff on Tuesday underwent thoracic surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung with doctors confirming he had lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer, according to a statement released by the Holy See Press Office. "This morning, the Holy Father underwent the blood tests and chest X-ray scheduled after surgery. The results confirm that his postoperative recovery is progressing normally: the values are within the expected range for the type of operation performed," it attributed Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora as saying. POPE LEO DIAGNOSED WITH LUNG CANCER AFTER SURGEONS REMOVE PART OF RIGHT LUNG, VATICAN SAYS "The Holy Father has undergone respiratory physiotherapy and has begun walking around his room. He has resumed eating normally and had breakfast and lunch," their statement added. "His recovery is proceeding as expected." The pope's diagnosis was confirmed through a tissue examination conducted during the operation, consistent with findings from preoperative tests, the Vatican said. POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION The pope spent approximately three hours in the operating room, although the surgery itself lasted about 90 minutes. Doctors said the procedure was successful and there were no complications. "Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after an Angelus address at St. Peter's Square on Monday. title: Washington officials call girl’s claimed emergency ‘manufactured’ after alleged trans athlete sexual assault
description: Washington state calls Kallie Keeler's Supreme Court bid over transgender wrestling opponent "manufactured" as three defendants urge denial.
content: Washington education officials called a teenage wrestler’s asserted need for emergency Supreme Court relief "manufactured," urging the justices to reject her request to avoid competing against transgender opponents after she alleged she was sexually assaulted by one during a match. Attorneys for the Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction and Superintendent Chris Reykdal argued that the family had not established a likelihood of future injury requiring immediate intervention. "The ‘irreparable’ nature of Applicants’ claimed harm is manufactured," the state’s filing said. "Applicants have sought emergency relief three times despite there not being any true emergency." WASHINGTON FAMILY REQUESTS SCOTUS INJUNCTION AFTER DAUGHTER WAS ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE The accusation concerned the family’s claim of future irreparable harm and the need for immediate court intervention. The state’s response was one of three oppositions filed Tuesday in the case brought by Kallie Keeler, identified in court as K.M.K., and her mother, Stephanie Lynne Brown. Puyallup School District and the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association also asked the Supreme Court to deny relief. Keeler alleges a transgender opponent sexually assaulted her during a December 2025 girls’ wrestling match. Her family is seeking an injunction allowing her to return to wrestling without being matched against a male athlete, or protections allowing advance notice and an opportunity to opt out without penalty. A district judge denied a preliminary injunction Aug. 23, and the Ninth Circuit denied emergency relief Sept. 25. The Supreme Court had not ruled on the application as of Tuesday evening. FEMALE WRESTLER WHO WAS ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE OPENS UP ON WAGING TITLE IX LAWSUIT The state’s attorneys pointed to the approximately six months between the match and the lawsuit, followed by another month before the family sought a preliminary injunction. They also argued the family’s asserted urgency shifted from the start of soccer season to the school year and then wrestling season, which begins in mid-November. ADF senior counsel Hal Frampton previously told OutKick that Supreme Court intervention was necessary to secure protection before Keeler’s remaining high school seasons slip away. "Our only avenue for relief in advance of wrestling season is the Supreme Court," Frampton said. The state also invoked an upcoming ballot measure as a reason for the justices to refrain from intervening. Washington voters will consider Initiative IL26-638 on Nov. 3. The measure would prohibit students it defines as biologically male from competing in designated female school athletic competitions and require healthcare providers to verify participants’ biological sex. Separately, the state disputed the family’s parental-rights theory, arguing it would improperly allow parents to dictate rules for school athletics. "But the Constitution does not entitle parents to bespoke athletic rules," its attorneys wrote. Puyallup School District defended its response to Keeler and disputed the premise that it had failed to offer accommodations. Frampton previously accused officials of making "no effort to compromise." The district’s filing cited a separate testing room, counseling offers, an independent investigation and expedited approval of Keeler’s transfer to Puyallup High School. "It has provided all the relief it can," the district’s attorneys wrote. The district said its Title IX investigation of the alleged assault remained ongoing and unresolved. Pierce County prosecutors previously declined to charge Keeler’s opponent, citing their inability to prove third-degree rape beyond a reasonable doubt or overcome a consent defense under case law governing athletic contests. The district also emphasized that Keeler could decline matches without additional consequences imposed by the district. That assurance does not eliminate a recorded forfeit or loss under National Federation of State High School Associations wrestling rules. The distinction is central to the dispute: Keeler’s family seeks to avoid competitive penalties as well as district-imposed consequences. The district argued it cannot change national wrestling rules, control every tournament bracket or provide notice identifying another student’s transgender status. The Washington Interscholastic Athletic Association (WIAA) offered a separate threshold defense, arguing Title IX does not apply to it because it is a private nonprofit association that receives no federal funding. The association cited the Supreme Court’s 1999 NCAA v. Smith decision, which held that dues from federally funded members did not make the NCAA a recipient of federal financial assistance. Keeler’s attorneys have advanced a separate theory that the WIAA exercises controlling authority over federally funded schools’ athletic programs. The WIAA disputed that theory and argued it required further factual development. The association also said Keeler had not applied for a hardship waiver concerning varsity eligibility following her transfer. That waiver process concerns transfer eligibility; it does not itself provide the assurance against transgender matchups sought in the emergency application. On forfeits, the WIAA argued that its rules allowing additional penalties for certain withdrawals apply to postseason competition and that any such penalty is discretionary. It said no penalty had been imposed on Keeler and its board had not been asked to consider her circumstances. The association maintained that the requested injunction would require information and operational control it lacks. "An injunction a defendant cannot obey is not a remedy; it is a contempt trap," its attorneys wrote. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Although it urged denial of relief against all defendants, the WIAA asked to be expressly excluded from any injunction the Court might grant, or at least protected from an order requiring changes to its gender-identity participation rule. All three responses emphasized that the Supreme Court’s recent West Virginia v. B.P.J. ruling permitted sex-based restrictions but left unresolved whether Title IX prohibits schools from allowing transgender girls onto girls’ teams. The family’s application also asks the Supreme Court to take up the case before the Ninth Circuit finishes its review. The defendants urged the justices to let proceedings continue in the lower courts.
