title: Popular erectile dysfunction pill may deliver additional boost to aging men
description: Tadalafil boosted muscle precursor cell survival in a lab study, but researchers say the active Cialis ingredient also delayed mature muscle development.
content: Researchers in Italy have discovered a potential association between the common erectile dysfunction drug Cialis (tadalafil) and muscle regeneration. The study, published in the journal Molecular Biology Reports, tested the drug on mouse muscle cells in a laboratory. Over a seven-day period, the researchers looked at how the drug affected muscle cell growth, survival and development. VIAGRA COULD DO MORE THAN ADVERTISED AS STUDY REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH SUPERPOWER Tadalafil was found to increase the number of muscle precursor cells, which are involved in the early stages of muscle formation, and helped more of them survive. The drug also showed signs of helping muscles repair themselves by encouraging growth and reducing cell death. Despite these positive outcomes, the research found that tadalafil delayed the development of fully mature muscle cells. This suggests that the drug could create and maintain more cells involved in muscle regeneration but does not indicate an increase in muscle size and function in humans. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Because the study was conducted in mouse models, the results may differ when applied to humans, posing a limitation to the study findings. The study lasted just seven days, so more research is needed to understand the drug's long-term effects, the researchers acknowledged. Study co-author Dr. Cristina Antinozzi, a researcher in the Endocrinology Unit at the University of Rome Foro Italico, said these findings represent an "encouraging look at how tadalafil might be repurposed to support muscle tissue repair and regeneration." "That's a fascinating biological signal, but it's far from proving that Cialis builds muscle or improves recovery in people." "While more work is needed, this research opens up exciting new possibilities for future therapeutic strategies in muscle recovery, though it also highlights the need to monitor how such mechanisms might be viewed or misused in sports and performance contexts," she told Fox News Digital. Dr. Kien Vuu, a radiologist and founder of VuuMD Performance and Longevity in Los Angeles, who was not involved in the study, agreed that this is an "intriguing early finding." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "In mouse muscle cells studied in a laboratory, tadalafil — the active ingredient in Cialis — helped muscle precursor cells grow and survive, but also delayed their maturation into muscle fibers," he told Fox News Digital. "That's a fascinating biological signal, but it's far from proving that Cialis builds muscle or improves recovery in people. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Successful regeneration ultimately requires those cells to mature and form functional muscle tissue. This experiment didn't establish that outcome." Vuu said this is "worth studying" from a longevity perspective because age-related muscle loss contributes "significantly" to frailty, metabolic dysfunction and loss of independence. "However, this was a laboratory cell study, not a clinical trial," he said. "We need animal studies and eventually human trials examining actual muscle mass, strength, physical function and safety before drawing conclusions about clinical use." Lifestyle practices such as resistance training, adequate protein and quality sleep remain the "most reliable ways" to protect muscle with age, Vuu added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The expert noted that tadalafil also carries "meaningful risks," including dangerous blood pressure reductions when combined with nitrates. "So, people should not take it for muscle-building based on these findings," he said.

title: NCAA softball player alleges person threatened to come to her school and kill her over women's sports activism
description: Kendall Kotzmacher says she reported a kill threat to her Colorado Christian campus after speaking out against transgender athletes in girls' sports.
content: NCAA softball player Kendall Kotzmacher says she reported a threat to come to her college and kill her amid backlash over her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in girls’ and women’s sports, while online targeting has also spread to her teammates. The 20-year-old Colorado Christian University sophomore, recently named a Courage Wins Champion by XX-XY Athletics, told OutKick that the hostility has intensified as her public profile has grown. "I had a person say that they were gonna come to the school and kill me. That one was a little scary," Kotzmacher said. Kotzmacher said she reported the threat to her school and had documented other concerning messages over the summer. Asked whether anyone had been arrested, she said no. "I’ve been getting a lot of people telling me to go kill myself or that I don’t deserve to be alive or that I should die, a bunch of stuff like that, which has been really difficult to hear," she said. FINAL SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY OF THE 2026 REGULAR SEASON PITS SUPPORTERS AGAINST TRANS ACTIVISTS IN MINNESOTA Knowing that strangers can identify where she attends college has added to her fear. "I think people knowing where I go to school has been a little bit scary just because I never know if someone’s going to show up or what’s going to go on," she said. Colorado Christian University has confirmed her report in a statement to OutKick. "Colorado Christian University is aware of reported threats involving student-athlete Kendall Kotzmacher. The Lakewood (CO) Police Department is investigating, and the University is cooperating fully with law enforcement," the statement read. "The safety and well-being of every CCU student, including Kendall and all our student-athletes, is our top priority. We take any report of threats seriously. No student should face threats or intimidation for expressing their beliefs." The backlash has also left Kotzmacher concerned about the teammates who publicly support her. She said one person replied to teammates’ comments on her social media posts, visited their accounts and looked up their names and statistics. "I think I want to protect them as much as possible," she said. "So trying to make sure that they’re not getting any of the backlash and that it’s kind of just on me has been a focus of mine." Kotzmacher said she offered in the team’s group chat to remove their names from her social media and make clear they were not involved in her advocacy. Her teammates rejected the offer, she said. "And they’re like, absolutely not. Like, we’re in this together. We’re going to be supportive of you," Kotzmacher recalled. "Like, we’re all here for you, which has been so refreshing to hear because I didn’t really get that last year." Kotzmacher, a sophomore catcher and infielder who previously attended Western Michigan University, transferred this past summer after In her September Fox News op-ed, she attributed her transfer from Western Michigan to a lack of coaching support and pressure in coursework. Her advocacy began after White Bear Lake High School lost 3–2 to Champlin Park in the 2025 Minnesota Class AAAA state semifinals. Champlin Park, whose team included a transgender pitcher, subsequently won the championship. Kotzmacher helped put White Bear Lake into that semifinal, hitting a seventh-inning, two-run home run in a 3–1 quarterfinal victory over Farmington. More than a year later, she is balancing college softball and classes with an increasingly public role in the debate over sports eligibility. DEMOCRAT SENATORS FLEE OR NO-SHOW JUDICIARY COMMITTEE HEARING ON PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS She practices four days a week and attends classes daily, she said, while trying to find time for advocacy that has taken her to Washington. "When I went to DC, it was really hard to miss class and go do something so important and work for these females. And then come back on Monday and go to school like any other day," Kotzmacher said. She participated in a Sept. 23 Capitol Hill news conference following a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on fairness, opportunity and safety for female athletes. The hearing’s three listed witnesses were ICONS co-founder Kim Jones, former professional soccer player Carly Smolak and attorney William Bock III. Democrats called no witnesses. Sens. Dick Durbin and Amy Klobuchar attended portions of the hearing before leaving. Durbin argued that lawmakers should address other problems facing children and female athletes and raised concerns about invasive examinations to enforce sports restrictions. Kotzmacher criticized Democrats’ limited participation. "Even if they don’t agree with it, just sit in and listen. Like, listen to these real stories from these real girls that this happened to," she said. The Minnesota native also said she plans to vote for Republican Senate nominee Michele Tafoya, who faces Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan for the seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Tina Smith. Tafoya has made restrictions on transgender participation in female sports part of her campaign. "I mean, I’ve talked to Michelle a lot. She’s been super supportive of everything. We’re pretty close," Kotzmacher said. Her advocacy has also included Sophie Cunningham rallies in Minneapolis, where she previously alleged a counterprotester told her she "should’ve been aborted." title: Prepare yourself for a look at a rare albino caribou calf photographed possibly for the first time
description: A biologist's photos capture an albino caribou calf with red eyes and pink hooves north of Fairbanks, Alaska — the first images of one in nearly 50 years.
content: You want your OutDoors with a story? How about this one? A rare albino caribou calf was photographed recently in Alaska for what very well could be the first time. Jordan Pruszenski, an Alaska Department of Fish and Game biologist, was counting caribou calves in a small plane north of Fairbanks when she spotted a white speck. The late June routine activity to determine how many calves survived their first month was about to become anything but routine. The white speck was a rare albino caribou. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS "I’m just like, 'What is happening'" Pruszenski said, reports KOTZ. "You could totally see it like on the horizon, and then it steps onto like the snow patch and totally disappears." The pilot turned the plane back towards the animal for another look. As the plane took another pass, Pruszenski snapped several photos. In addition to the white fur, this calf also had "incredible, beady red eyes" and pink hooves. This rare sighting came with even rarer photographic evidence. The Alaska Department of Fish and Game's last record of an albino calf was from 1976. It had been observed through a spotting scope for a couple of minutes and no photos were taken. WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA As for this calf, there's no way of knowing if it has survived past the one-month check in late June. Biologists didn't collar the calf or the mother and its white fur is going to make it stand out to predators. "Once it steps off of the snow it just really stands out," Pruszenski said. "So we’re really not sure how long it’ll last." The name of the albino caribou's herd isn't being shared, so that people don't head out on their own looking for it. But what we don't really want is people to really be sort of trying to bother this caribou," Pruszenski told the outlet. "We want to be able to give it its best shot, which will be to kind of just let it be a normal caribou." That sounds perfectly reasonable. Let the caribou do caribou stuff. It's not looking for fame. title: Ilhan Omar's wealth scandal takes a turn just one day after raid of her DC home

content: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro revealed Tuesday that her office is investigating Rep. title: New evidence debunks Talarico psych hospital rumor after ‘mind-numbing malpractice’ fuels firestorm
description: James Talarico's campaign provided security footage to debunk the Ohio rehab rumor, but critics ask why the evidence wasn't released sooner.
content: A viral rumor claiming Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico secretly spent his recent campaign absence at an Ohio behavioral health center has now been debunked — but new questions are emerging over why evidence that could have quickly undercut the allegation was not made public as the speculation exploded online. The New York Times reported Monday that it reviewed time-stamped security camera images provided by Talarico's campaign showing the Democrat at his Austin home between Oct. 1 and Oct. 8, when his nine-day absence from the campaign trail was fueling mounting speculation about his whereabouts. The images, which the campaign provided to the Times on the condition they not be published for security reasons, offer the clearest independent evidence yet supporting Talarico's account that he was home recovering from the flu and contradict claims that he instead traveled more than 1,000 miles away for treatment at an Ohio behavioral health center. PAXTON’S ESTRANGED WIFE BREAKS SILENCE ON TEXAS SENATE RACE AFTER 'BIBLICAL GROUNDS' DIVORCE But the revelation has also prompted criticism from some observers questioning why Talarico's campaign did not provide similarly verifiable evidence earlier before an unsubstantiated theory about his whereabouts mushroomed across social media and was amplified by prominent conservatives. "In October of an election year, every day and every hour count as candidates do everything they can to meet with voters. So, if you are out of commission for any extent of time, it's easy for voters to wonder what's going on," GOP strategist Mark Bednar told Fox News Digital. "That being said, if there's a simple explanation like an illness, it's even easier to just prove that outright to voters. If the flu was really the case with Talarico, it's mind-numbing malpractice that his campaign didn't quickly and easily demonstrate that." Washington Free Beacon investigative reporter Chuck Ross pointed to the Times report Monday, writing on X that the footage "could have been released a week ago and quashed the rumors." But his extended absence from in-person campaigning increasingly became a subject of speculation as Election Day approached. The speculation accelerated after Talarico's campaign reposted footage from a February rally on Oct. 3 without initially identifying it as a months-old video. His campaign told the Times it routinely reposts older social media content. "Let’s be fair here. You’re 20 days out from Election Day, and you’re running for senate in one of the biggest states in the country. Use tech to connect: direct to camera videos, do a livestream. To just go dark is malpractice," Matt Gorman, chief communications officer at Targeted Victory, told Fox News Digital. "You’re running for Senate, not some cubicle dweller." The hearing is not expected to include witness testimony, but Robinson's lawyers argue that ongoing coverage of Kirk's murder could have an "incremental adverse effect" that outweighs the benefit of video coverage to the public's understanding of court proceedings. "Only a few weeks ago, the media reported on costs associated with the defense," his lawyers wrote Monday in an opposition filing from local media to send a camera to cover the Oct. 23 hearing. "Against that backdrop, statements by defense counsel at the upcoming proceeding concerning the time and resources necessary to prepare this case are likely to be examined and disseminated in real time through social media and other media channels and viewed through the lens of cost, rather than in the context of Mr. Robinson’s constitutional rights to the effective assistance of counsel, a fair trial, due process of law, and a reliable penalty determination." JUDGE IN ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON'S CASE EXPLAIN WHY DEATH PENALTY REMAINS ON TABLE The Salt Lake Tribune reported that Utah County had paid $1.6 million to Robinson's legal team as of last month, exhausting a special $1 million earmark from the state. High-profile murder cases can cost millions to defend, especially if they go to trial. GOT A TIP? Overhead typically includes expert witnesses, defense investigations, lab testing and more. Some experts have predicted Robinson's defense could cost as much as $10 million. JUDGE ALLOWS CAMERAS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE, DELAYS PRELIMINARY HEARING Additional coverage, his lawyers argued, "risks reinforcing existing prejudicial perceptions of Mr. Robinson and his defense." Robinson's lawyers have repeatedly attempted to have cameras — for both still photography and video — blocked from the courtroom, arguing for various reasons that they violate his right to a fair trial. TYLER ROBINSON ASKS FOR MORE SECRET HEARINGS AFTER LOSING FIGHT OVER CAMERAS IN COURT "Although the resulting litigation schedule may be newsworthy, there is little additional news value in electronically recording and transmitting the back-and-forth among the Court and counsel concerning scheduling matters," Robinson's attorneys wrote. Read the filing: Previously, they likened media coverage of the case to a "reality TV show" and claimed that cameras distract and put pressure on people in the courtroom. TYLER ROBINSON'S DEFENSE TEAM FIGHTS TO SEAL EVIDENCE AND PUNISH PROSECUTORS IN CHARLIE KIRK'S ASSASSINATION One of his attorneys, Richard Novak, even laughed at the start of his five-day preliminary hearing when the judge ruled that one request had been filed too late and that a pool photographer would only be allowed to take pictures on days two through five. Still, Judge Tony Graf Jr. has largely sided with the public, allowing cameras in to most proceedings under terms outlined in a decorum order. title: Selma Blair accused of kicking nurse hours after JFK plane arrest
description: Selma Blair allegedly kicked a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital hours after her arrest for an incident aboard a Delta flight to JFK Airport.
content: Selma Blair's alleged airline assault did not end with the police. She is also accused of kicking a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital hours after she was arrested following an alleged in-flight incident aboard a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York. The criminal court affidavit, filed in Queens Criminal Court, says registered nurse Ashley DeLeo was assisting in transporting Blair for further medical treatment at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center at approximately 2 a.m. ET on Oct. 12 when Blair allegedly kicked her. "The defendant kicked complainant DeLeo in her chest," the affidavit stated, adding that the alleged conduct caused "substantial pain to her chest." SELMA BLAIR ARRESTED AFTER IN-FLIGHT INCIDENT Blair, 54, was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault after Port Authority police responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938, which had arrived at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles, officials said. The "Cruel Intentions" and "Hellboy" actress was taken into custody at JFK and transported to a hospital for evaluation. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, according to officials. FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT The court document also alleges Blair kicked a Port Authority police officer while being moved from JFK Terminal 4 into an ambulance at the airport’s B22 exit ramp. Police Officer Maria Suarez was helping secure Blair on a stretcher at approximately 11:50 p.m. ET when Blair allegedly "removed her leg from the stretcher straps and kicked Officer Suarez repeatedly about the face, neck and chest," according to the affidavit. CHAOS ERUPTS ON AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT AS UNRULY PASSENGER ALLEGEDLY BITES FELLOW TRAVELER MIDAIR The affidavit says Suarez suffered swelling to her jaw and "substantial pain to her face, neck and chest." Suarez was treated at a local Queens-area hospital, according to the filing. Delta said in a statement Monday that it has "zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first." UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT A representative for Blair said the actress suffered a medical emergency during the flight. "Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct," Blair’s representative said. "Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition." SEVERE TURBULENCE DIVERTS NEW YORK CITY FLIGHT TO MIAMI, 8 INJURED Blair’s attorney said in court that the incident was not intentional and argued that she had missed doses of a "powerful" medication used to control severe neurological symptoms. "This was not an intentional assault," attorney Shawn Barnes said. Barnes also said Blair had been working "extensive hours" before the flight and claimed she fell and hit her head during the trip. "These factors, coupled with altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation," Barnes said. SELMA BLAIR SAYS 'NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS' AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT Blair has spoken publicly about her battle with multiple sclerosis, which she was diagnosed with in 2018. She was later released on bond and is expected back in court in January. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I do believe she poses a risk," Judge Indira Kahn said Monday. Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Major cruise line hikes its popular package prices in move that could hit vacation budgets
description: Vacationers are reacting as Princess Cruises hikes Plus and Premier package cruise prices by $5 per person per day with major changes to Wi-Fi plans starting Oct. 13.
content: Princess Cruises is increasing prices on some of its most popular add-on packages by $5 per person per day starting Oct. 13 and adjusting the cruise line's Wi-Fi plans. And some cruise fans say they may rethink their vacation plans as a result. Princess Cruises' Plus and Premier packages include drink packages, Wi-Fi, crew appreciation, casual dining and room service. The higher package rates apply to all sailings that depart on or after Oct. 13. CRUISE LINE'S TOUGHER BOOKING RULES IGNITE BACKLASH OVER HIGHER DEPOSITS AND PAYMENTS The Princess Plus package is due to increase to $70 per day, and the Princess Premier package will increase to $105 per day, the company shared with Fox News Digital. Package prices will increase to $75 and $110 on the Sun Princess and Star Princess. "We periodically review package pricing to account for changes in our operating environment while continuing to offer guests strong value and a convenient way to bundle popular amenities," a spokesperson for Princess Cruises told Fox News Digital. "We believe both packages offer strong value, providing guests with a convenient way to bundle popular amenities. CRUISE FEE DOUBLES AT VACATION HOT SPOT AS PASSENGERS BRACE FOR EVEN STEEPER HIKES "Additionally, crew appreciation included in these packages continues to go directly to the hardworking crew members who deliver the exceptional service our guests know and value," the cruise line, based in Santa Clarita, California, added. Princess Cruises' bundled packages outline distinct tiers of shipboard perks. Under the Princess Plus package, guests receive up to 15 alcoholic beverages per day (capped at $15 each), four casual meals, complimentary room service, prepaid gratuities and Wi-Fi coverage for one device per traveler. "We believe both packages offer strong value, providing guests with a convenient way to bundle popular amenities." The top-tier Premier package expands those perks to unlimited drinks valued at up to $20 each, paired with unrestricted casual and specialty dining. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER In addition to included room service and gratuities, Premier guests receive four-device Wi-Fi access and up to $300 per person in shore excursion credits. The cruise line is also restructuring its standalone internet offerings by retiring its four-device Wi-Fi tier, the company said. In its place, Princess has introduced a two-device option priced at $39.99 per day. Purchasing single-device internet access once onboard now costs more as well. Rates have risen to $39.99 per day for a single 24-hour purchase, or $33.99 per day when booked for the entire sailing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES People took to social media to weigh in on the new pricing structure. "They're just making my decision to sail standard and pay à la carte even easier," one Reddit user said. In response, another commenter said, "With inflation, high fuel and food costs, I suspect gratuities, cocktails, specialty dining and coffee, etc. will all go up al la carte, as well." Another person wrote, "Just bought the 4-device internet package for our two upcoming cruises. Just another reason [that] after these cruises we are going to explore other lines." "It’s probably no longer worth it for me." Some people said the higher price could make Princess Plus less worthwhile to them, especially for those who don't use all the benefits. "I think this price increase is what will push me away. … It’s probably no longer worth it for me," one traveler said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Princess Cruises also recently announced it's introducing stricter booking policies, including higher deposits and earlier final payment deadlines. Among the biggest changes is an update to the timeline for final payments, the cruise line confirmed in a previous statement to Fox News Digital. "Beginning with new bookings for sailings departing in 2027 and beyond, we are implementing a 120-day final payment and a modified cancellation fee schedule," the company said in August. "These changes bring greater consistency to the booking process and reflect broader industry practices, while also helping ensure that guests have fair access to the staterooms and sailings they want to experience." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Princess Cruises operates 17 ships divided into four classes, ranging from mid-sized vessels for destination-focused routes to larger, amenity-focused ships. The premium line's newest additions are its Sphere Class vessels, Sun Princess and Star Princess. Kelly McGreal of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

title: WNBA moves Finals Games 3 and 4 to State Farm Arena, giving Atlanta Dream thousands more seats
description: The WNBA Finals shift Games 3 and 4 to State Farm Arena, giving the Atlanta Dream roughly 17,000 seats instead of 3,500 at Gateway Center Arena.
content: The WNBA is moving Games 3 and 4 of the Finals to State Farm Arena in Atlanta, giving the Dream thousands of additional seats to sell. To make that happen, the league is moving one game to a different day and changing the start time of the other. The league announced Tuesday that Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries will be played Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 8 p.m. ET, a day earlier than originally scheduled. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND Game 4 will stay on Saturday, Oct. 24, but tipoff moves from 3:30 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET. State Farm Arena already has a Sombr concert scheduled for Oct. 22, which created the conflict with Game 3. The new arrangement allows Atlanta to use a building that seats roughly 17,000 instead of its usual home, the approximately 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena. Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said the move "dramatically expands the seating capacity" and gives thousands more fans across the Southeast a chance to attend. It'll be the first Finals game played in the Atlanta market since 2013. Dream majority owner Larry Gottesdiener added: "This is what the players and the fans deserve." The best-of-seven series begins Saturday, Oct. 17, in San Francisco, with Golden State hosting the first two games before the Finals shift to Atlanta. Game 6, if necessary, is scheduled for Oct. 29 in Atlanta. Tuesday's announcement did not address where that game would be played. title: Doctors may be getting childhood obesity wrong, new research suggests
description: A Lancet Commission definition of clinical obesity cuts pediatric rates sharply by requiring evidence of health complications beyond body mass index.
content: A new global definition of childhood obesity is reframing how doctors evaluate youth health, looking past traditional body mass index (BMI) measurements to focus on actual physiological impacts. According to research from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute in Australia, just 2.1% to 4.9% of children and adolescents qualify as clinically obese under the revised standard, compared to 7% to 10.8% under standard BMI calculations. Dr. Danielle Longmore, a pediatrician at the Melbourne institute, outlined the shift during an appearance on "Fox & Friends." YOUR WAISTLINE COULD REVEAL A HIDDEN HEART RISK YOUR BMI MISSES, MAJOR STUDY FINDS "There's a push to really understand the impact of body fat on health," Longmore said. "BMI is really just measuring size. So, it doesn't really have a way of capturing whether somebody is well or unwell." The traditional BMI measurement calculates a person's weight relative to their height. The new definition, developed by an international panel of medical experts convened by the medical journal The Lancet, requires evidence of both excess body fat and related health problems or limitations in daily activities. WEIGHT GAIN IN CERTAIN DECADE OF LIFE MAY BE MORE DANGEROUS, STUDY SUGGESTS These indicators can range from elevated blood pressure and abnormal blood sugar to impaired mobility or poor sleep. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Longmore noted that many children defined as obese by BMI metrics are active, sleeping well, attending school and otherwise healthy. "I think this definition just really clarifies what people have been doing in actual clinical practice," Longmore said, noting that physicians typically evaluate patients for underlying complications rather than relying strictly on scale weight. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES While clinical obesity appears to be significantly less prevalent in youth under the new model, the trajectory reverses dramatically later in life. The study, which analyzed nearly 800,000 individuals across their lifespan, found that clinical obesity rates climbed through adulthood. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Among adults ages 65 to 74, the rate of clinical obesity reached 52%, as health problems linked to excess body fat became more common with age. The findings come at a time when prescription weight loss medications, particularly GLP-1 receptor agonists, are gaining in popularity. However, Longmore cautioned that the study's dataset reflects pre-GLP-1 records, making the long-term impact of these treatments an open area for future study. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This is really just the start of understanding what this new diagnostic entity means, and we really need more research," Longmore said, emphasizing that while the definition refines clinical diagnoses, early health interventions and lifestyle prevention remain critical for children at risk.

title: Democrats' fury over Ilhan Omar raid draws stinging GOP reminder about raid from the past: ‘Set the precedent’
description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement raided Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. home, igniting fierce partisan debate over immigration fraud and weaponization.
content: Democratic lawmakers erupted online on Monday after news that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) had raided the Washington-area home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., blasting the development as an effort by President Donald Trump to intimidate a longtime political adversary. "The Trump administration’s raid on Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s home is deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries," U.S. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., wrote in a statement. The Justice Department confirmed that agents of Homeland Security Investigations, ICE's investigative arm, executed a court-authorized search warrant as part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. Two sources close to the investigation say the search stems from a criminal fraud investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child. The Minnesota Democrat has repeatedly denied allegations of immigration fraud and claims that she is in the country unlawfully. FEDERAL AGENTS RAID ILHAN OMAR’S DC HOME AMID IMMIGRATION FRAUD INVESTIGATION To Rep. Pramila Jayapal, a fellow member of the progressive group known as the "Squad," the development is a clearly personal one. "Donald Trump has been obsessed with Rep. Omar. He has gone after her repeatedly, causing her severe harm and going after the entire Somali American population," Jayapal said, referencing Trump’s wariness of Somali fraud rings in Minnesota that became a national focus earlier this year. "This is his way of bullying his way back into power. This is what authoritarians do," Jayapal added. Democrats online similarly observed the immigration-related focus of the raid, affirming Omar’s status as a citizen of the U.S. HOMAN CONFIRMS 'CRIMINAL' INVESTIGATION INVOLVING ILHAN OMAR, SAYS HE KNOWS 'THINGS ARE GOING ON’ "This raid on Rep. Omar’s home is an outrageous abuse of power by ICE. Rep. Omar has been a U.S. citizen for 26 years. She came to the United States as a child and was legally admitted as a refugee," Rep. Ted Lieu, D-Calif., wrote. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., echoed Lieu. "Ilhan Omar came to America legally as a child refugee fleeing civil war, became a citizen and was elected to Congress. Trump is weaponizing the federal government to silence opposition," Sanders said in a post to X. But Republicans pointed out that the public hasn’t had an opportunity to review the details of Omar’s naturalization paperwork either — something that Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., said she had wanted to see for herself but was blocked from using congressional authority to secure. "I tried to subpoena Ilhan Omar and her brother-husband’s immigration records. Both parties blocked it in Oversight," Mace wrote, referring to the powerful oversight committee, the body of lawmakers charged with ensuring the government lawfully carries out its duties. "If the fraud is proven, she should be denaturalized and deported home to Somalia." Omar has faced long-standing political pressure stemming from her previous marriage to Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in 2009, a marriage that critics claim was to her biological brother in order to commit immigration fraud. Omar has denied that Elmi is her brother, and no charges related to that marriage have been brought against her. Omar and Elmi divorced in 2017. Additionally, Mace pointed out that accusations of politically motivated investigations mirror the raid on Trump's personal residence in Florida in 2022. "All those who celebrated the raid of Mar-a-Lago don't get to cry over the raid at Ilhan Omar's home. Trump's political enemy raided his home. Democrats set the precedent," she added. Other Republicans, like Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, R-Fla., argued that the moment has highlighted the need to especially scrutinize the citizenship credentials of lawmakers before they arrive in office — calls shared by other fellow members. "If these allegations are true, then it needs to be dealt with legally. But ultimately, this is exactly why myself, members like Kat Cammack and Randy Fine have pushed for there to be a disclosure at least for people to know whether members of Congress are dual citizens," Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, R-Fla., said in an interview with Fox News. Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., agreed. "If Ilhan Omar lied on her immigration paperwork, she should be denaturalized and deported — the same as anyone else. No more special treatment," Fine said. House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., didn’t speculate as to why the ICE raid had taken place, but quickly affirmed his view that even lawmakers could be subject to scrutiny. "Nobody is above the law. HSI just executed a search warrant at Ilhan Omar’s Washington, D.C. home. We look forward to learning more details about this raid and investigation. ACCOUNTABILITY IS COMING!" Emmer wrote. Notably, U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., as of Tuesday morning, had not issued a statement on the raid on Omar’s residence. title: Reparations activists celebrate 'important victory' after Newsom signs first-ever corporate slavery bill
description: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 2599, forcing large corporations in California to disclose historical ties to slavery in a first-in-the-nation law.
content: California advocacy groups are celebrating a "big, important victory" in their push for state-level reparations after Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a first-in-the-nation bill requiring large corporations to investigate and disclose historical ties to chattel slavery. Kristin Nimmers, policy and campaign manager for the California Black Power Network (CBPN) and the Alliance for Reparations, Reconciliation, and Truth, told Fox News Digital Newsom’s signature on Assembly Bill 2599 — the Truth in Disclosure Act — marks a significant milestone for corporate accountability. "There are connections right now from slavery to current wealth of individuals and current wealth of corporations whose foundation and who built the start of their companies off of slavery and off of benefits gained from slavery," Nimmers said. CALIFORNIA LAWMAKERS WANT CORPORATIONS TO DISCLOSE TIES TO SLAVERY DESPITE UNCERTAIN FUTURE FOR REPARATIONS Newsom signed AB 2599 into law Sept. 30, a move Nimmers called a "historic moment" that forces qualifying businesses operating in California to scour historical records and publicly disclose slavery-era transactions. California was the first state in the nation to establish a formal task force to study the legacy of slavery and recommend potential restitution measures. "The California Reparations Task Force spent years documenting the state's role in perpetuating racial harm and outlining this path toward repair," Nimmers said. "AB 2599 is really starting the work of identifying who really benefited from this racial harm and from slavery." Authored by Assemblymember Isaac Bryan, D-Ladera Heights, the law applies to businesses with more than $100 million in annual worldwide gross receipts that existed — or had a predecessor entity in operation — on or before Dec. 31, 1964. Once funded by the state legislature, covered companies will be required to submit sworn affidavits under penalty of perjury to the California Civil Rights Department. These disclosures must detail any historical involvement in the purchase or sale of enslaved people, the use of enslaved human beings as loan collateral, slave-related insurance policies and other financial transactions. Covered entities have until Jan. 15, 2029, to submit their initial filings. CASH PAYMENTS ARE NOT 'RULED OUT' AS CALIFORNIA COUNTY OFFICIALS PUSH REPARATIONS FOR BLACK LOCALS The progressive governor's signing of AB 2599 comes despite his cautious stance on broader, high-cost reparations initiatives. Most recently, Newsom vetoed Assembly Bill 2186, which would have exempted future state reparations payments from California's personal income tax. The bill's author, Assemblymember Tina McKinnor, D-Inglewood, told Fox News Digital Friday that the veto was disappointing. Newsom has also consistently resisted direct cash payments, which state task force recommendations estimated could cost millions per eligible recipient. He previously turned down a broader slate of cash-focused reparations measures backed by the California Legislative Black Caucus. However, Newsom did approve state funding for California universities to research and establish verification methods for descendants of enslaved Americans to determine potential eligibility for future noncash benefits. REPARATIONS ACTIVIST DOES NOT EXPECT COMPENSATION FROM NEW YORK OFFICIALS AS ACTION IS DELAYED FOR YEARS Despite those legislative setbacks, Nimmers remains optimistic about the future of reparations in the Golden State, noting that CBPN plans to leverage AB 2599 as momentum to turn the task force’s broader recommendations into law. "It helps us move the work of the task force from recommendations toward implementation," Nimmers said. "This is really an important, big victory for our alliance and for our work with reparations task force members, but it is also just one step in a much greater movement and effort that we're trying to be a part of." The California Black Power Network is a statewide coalition composed of 48 Black-led and Black-serving organizations operating across 14 California counties. Bringing together grassroots organizations focused on housing, education and criminal justice reform, CBPN was established to combat systemic racism through policy advocacy and community organizing. Central to the network’s mission is reparative justice. CBPN frames present-day economic disparities — including educational gaps, wealth inequality and systemic injustice — as direct consequences of historical harms stemming from chattel slavery, segregation, and Jim Crow practices. During the multi-year tenure of the California Task Force to Study and Develop Reparation Proposals for African Americans (established under AB 3121), CBPN served as an official state community anchor. The coalition facilitated grassroots civic engagement across California, hosting listening sessions to gather public testimony that directly informed the task force’s landmark 1,100-page final report issued in 2023. With AB 2599 now on the books, CBPN is focused on expanding its grassroots base to push for full implementation. CALIFORNIA COUNTY APPROVES REPARATIONS PLAN AS NEIGHBORING SCHOOL DISTRICT 'BLACK THRIVING' EFFORT STALLS "AB 2599 really represents a historic step toward corporate transparency and accountability," Nimmers said. "We know for generations, corporations and financial institutions have really benefited from slavery and from the exploitation of Black people. AB 2599 is starting to establish a process for qualifying corporations doing business in California to really examine and disclose any historical ties they've had to slavery. This matters because we can't fully and meaningfully repair harms if we're not really willing to acknowledge and confront the truth," she added. "When we're thinking about what repair looks like," she said, "it's important that we're tying it back to what the origin of it was so we can address those core issues." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Elsewhere in the country, localized reparations programs have moved forward with mixed success. Black residents in Evanston, Illinois, received $25,000 housing grants as part of a municipal program aimed at rectifying historic housing discrimination. Similar local and municipal initiatives seeking to provide direct compensation or economic aid are being debated nationwide.

title: French supermarkets face millions in losses after cyberattack hits refrigerators nationwide
description: Hackers targeted Danfoss refrigerator controls across French supermarkets, forcing chains like Carrefour and Monoprix to discard massive food stocks.
content: A cyberattack in France forced multiple grocery stores to discard large amounts of temperature-sensitive product after hackers turned the heat up on food refrigerators in hundreds of stores across at least five chain brands. The hack, according to Reuters and European officials, affected chains such as Carrefour, Monoprix, Les Mousquetaires, E. Leclerc and Coopérative U. The CEO of Coopérative U, a retail group structured as a cooperative of independently owned businesses, confirmed the cyberattack in a Monday post on X. "I confirm that a cyberattack has been affecting, since last night, the cold production facilities of several stores in our network Coopérative U," he wrote in the post. FOREIGN HACKERS BREACH TWO MORE US WATER UTILITIES, THREATEN SAFETY OF COLORADO RESIDENTS "Our teams are fully mobilized, in coordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible. An investigation will be necessary to shed full light on this attack. Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented. It is unacceptable," he concluded. IF HACKERS CRIPPLE AMERICA'S WATER, THE CONSEQUENCES COULD BE CATASTROPHIC The Paris prosecutor's office also confirmed the cyberattack, characterizing it as a "large-scale" attack that affected "connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France." Carrefour said roughly 80 of its stores were affected while Monoprix, which operates 490 stores in France according to Reuters, said 5% of its stores were affected. IRAN-LINKED HACKERS SUSPECTED IN UK POWER-PLANT SHUTDOWN AFTER ALLEGED MINNESOTA WATER ATTACK Les Mousquetaires said fridges at approximately 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) for six hours. A company spokesperson also said all affected food had been discarded, according to Reuters. While the incident's financial toll on the supermarket has yet to be officially tabulated, experts estimated the losses to be upwards of 10 million euros, equivalent to roughly $11.2 million. INVESTIGATORS BELIEVE IRANIAN HACKERS ARE LIKELY BEHIND CYBERATTACK ON MINNESOTA WATER SYSTEMS: REPORT The attack likely resulted in the loss of "tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day," Intermarche CEO Thierry Cotillard said during a televised interview in France, according to Reuters. A source with knowledge of the refrigerator systems reportedly told AFP that the hackers targeted refrigerator controls systems from Danish manufacturer Danfoss. CHINESE HACKERS TARGET NASA AND KEY US AGENCIES, DOJ ALLEGES Danfoss, in turn, told AFP that most of the affected equipment were "legacy" products which "no longer receive software or security updates." The company also added that some of the systems affected were using "outdated firmware" which it had long-counseled its purchasers to update. Danfoss did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for further comment. TRUMP PLAN TAPS US FIRMS TO FIGHT FOREIGN CYBERCRIME French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cyber security Agency (ANSSI) to conduct an investigation. ANSSI has already identified "a vulnerability in software supplied by a Danish company and has contacted the vendor," a source close to Lecornu reportedly told AFP. Christophe Hansen, the European Union's Commissioner for Agriculture and Food, denounced the attack as an affront on European food safety. IRANIAN HACKERS ATTACKED OUR WATER SYSTEMS. HERE ARE 5 THINGS OUR LEADERS NEED TO DO NOW "I strongly condemn the cyberattack targeting food products at Intermarche, Cooperative U, Leclerc. Food security requires more attention at all levels. title: DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players as Chapter 11 bankruptcy clouds league's future
description: The DP World Tour banned LIV Golf players as the league's Chapter 11 bankruptcy deepens and Jon Rahm calls the "LIV 2.0" restructuring plan unacceptable.
content: As the future of LIV Golf hangs in the balance amid its bankruptcy, one other golf tour appears to be strong-arming its players. Since LIV Golf's inception, those who joined the formerly Saudi-backed tour have been allowed to participate in the DP World Tour — formerly known as the European Tour – under specific circumstances. But now, there are no circumstances to be had, and the DP World Tour announced that LIV players are no longer welcome. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Players need to make a choice. As we have said for many years, we have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour." LIV golfers were allowed to play on the DP World Tour as long as they were in good standing and paid any fines for playing in LIV events that conflicted with the DP World Tour calendar — those fines were paid for by the Public Investment Fund until 2025. The PIF halted funding in April to redirect money toward domestic projects and manage financial pressures from the regional war with Iran. Following the decision, PIF governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan resigned from LIV’s board. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey last month. Between 2021 and 2026, LIV spent an estimated $5 billion to $8 billion. Bankruptcy filings show the league owes millions of dollars in unpaid compensation to top players, including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Cam Smith. LIV has laid off most of its operational staff, left event contractors waiting for payment and faces a lawsuit from the Premier Golf League alleging breach of confidence and conspiracy. title: DR MARC SIEGEL: Pope Leo's lung surgery puts modern medicine alongside faith
description: Pope Leo XIV drank from the Lourdes spring just weeks before facing minimally invasive VATS lung nodule surgery at Gemelli Hospital in Rome.
content: When Pope Leo XIV visited Lourdes, France, on Sept. 26, he drank a glass of water from the spring at the Grotto of Massabielle, where St. Bernadette Soubirous reported visions of the Virgin Mary in 1858. Who knew last month that the pope might be calling on the healing waters to help in his own healing as he faces surgical removal of what the Vatican has described as "a small localized nodule" that he has said "was identified at a very early stage and well situated." The surgery will take place Tuesday, Oct. 13, followed by a week of recovery at Rome’s highly rated Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic Hospital. Small lung nodules are often detected on CT scans of the lungs. If the nodule is small and well circumscribed, and has characteristics, including irregularities that are concerning for malignancy, as may be the case here, removal can often be performed using minimally invasive techniques. POPE LEO ARRIVES AT HOSPITAL FOR SURGERY TO REMOVE LUNG NODULE The surgeon leading his medical team is Professor Stefano Margaritora, director of the Thoracic Surgery Unit at Gemelli and an expert in minimally invasive techniques. Margaritora is known for uniportal (one small incision) video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), which is done via a scope under direct visualization. This is the procedure that will be performed on the pope. Dr. Robert Cerfolio, CEO at Pinnacle Global Health and one of the top minimally invasive lung surgeons in the world, thinks highly of Margaritora but generally prefers a robotic approach, in part because of smaller incisions and better visualization. The robot is placed between the ribs and into the chest and is controlled by the surgeon from a console. POPE LEO ANNOUNCES TUMOR ON LUNG, SURGERY PLANNED IN 'NEXT FEW DAYS' If all goes well, I would expect the Holy Father to resume normal activities fairly quickly. His recovery will no doubt be aided by the fact that, at age 71, he has maintained an active lifestyle and has generally appeared to be in good health. Lourdes is famous not only for the 72 healings officially recognized as miraculous by the Catholic Church — instantaneous healings with no medical explanation — but also for "small miracles that aren’t recognized until later." Those are the words of Fox Business anchor David Asman. Asman is his wife’s "voiturier" at Lourdes, meaning that he takes her around the sanctuary during their visits. The couple has made pilgrimages to Lourdes following a stroke affecting the right side of his wife’s brain in 2004 that left her with severe loss of strength on her left side. POPE LEO DRAWS STAGGERING 800,000 FAITHFUL TO HEART OF PARIS FOR MASSIVE OUTDOOR MASS Marta Cecilia Asman is rejuvenated spiritually at Lourdes. She watches people who come there hopeless and return home with tremendous hope, their spiritual and emotional state completely changed. "Lourdes is a miracle," she says to me in an interview for my new book, "The Angels Among Us." "Not everyone can say they are cured. For me, my hand opens and starts working again after my stroke when it isn’t supposed to. During my rehab at Burke Rehabilitation Hospital [in New York’s Westchester County], I’m told I’m not supposed to be able to walk on my own again, but I do. … Sometimes I feel I am trapped in New York City. But then I am uplifted by Lourdes, my emotional health is tied to Lourdes, and I know there is no limit to what I can do." POPE LEO CALLS OUT ‘FALSE COMPASSION’ OF MEDICALLY ASSISTED SUICIDE DURING FRENCH HOSPITAL VISIT Dr. Alessandro De Franciscis, outgoing director of the Lourdes Office of Medical Observations, tells me in an interview for the book that Lourdes is a joyful place, a place of mind-over-matter healing. "The pilgrims who travel here are malades who may not be able to get into the metro or climb a stairway or push into a department store, and yet they thrive here." The "malades" are cared for by four times as many volunteer caregivers a.k.a. "hospitaliers." title: From Cooper Flagg to DeMar DeRozan, the best NBA award bets heading into the new season
description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander seeks a rare third straight MVP, but Nikola Jokic, Anthony Edwards, and Cade Cunningham offer intriguing betting value.
content: The NBA is almost back. We've already seen some preseason action, and there simply isn't enough time to cover everything that happened in the offseason for every team, as I've done for the MLB and NFL. Basketball is my favorite sport, and despite all of the complaints (some warranted and others not so much), the NBA is my favorite league. We haven't seen the same team win the Championship in nine seasons, and we've had eight straight years with a different winner. Some of the awards haven't been quite as diverse, but I'm looking at options for this season and where we could make some money. MVP The past two seasons have seen Shai Gilgeous-Alexander win the MVP award. The last person to win three straight seasons was Larry Bird. That was from 1983-1986. So, consider this your advice to cross him off your list. Victor Wembanyama is young, on a great team, and looked good until the Finals last year. It could very well be his year. However, at +210, the number is far too low. I have a few other options worth considering. Nikola Jokic is a finalist every season, and he has averaged a triple-double the past two years. Somehow he hasn't won the MVP in either of those seasons. At +500, it might be worth it to take a shot on him getting the award that he has missed out on the past two years. Some of the longer shots that I like are Anthony Edwards at +1800 and Cade Cunningham at +2200. Perhaps I just like Edwards. He is the best player on a good team and is consistently leading them to the playoffs. He also doesn't take games off and keeps improving each season. If the Timberwolves can be in the top three in the West, Edwards and his personality might be enough to give him the award. Cunningham is the best player on the Pistons and does literally everything for them. He led them to the top spot in the East last year. While I don't think that will happen again, I'm thinking that Cunningham taking another step forward might finally get the attention he deserves. THUNDER'S SHAI GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SECURES BACK-TO-BACK NBA MVP AWARDS: REPORT Cooper Flagg will take a step forward, but the Mavs would need to finish in the top four of the West for him to win it. There are worse flyers to take than +20000 on Flagg. Jalen Brunson at +5000 is another that is interesting. After winning the championship last year, he could focus on getting an individual award. The media will likely still look at the Knicks as being a complete team, and I think the Knicks are going to take a step back this season, so I don't like it, but it is conceivable, and there are worse numbers. Rookie of the Year COOPER FLAGG WINS NBA ROOKIE OF THE YEAR AFTER KON KNUEPPEL'S PLAY-IN TOURNAMENT STRUGGLES SWAYED VOTERS The NBA Draft was about as chalky as you could expect. AJ Dybantsa went first, then Darryn Peterson, Cam Boozer, and finally Caleb Wilson. People talk about the 2003 Draft, but this could be one that is very close. I don't expect Dybantsa to have a big enough role, and I think the Wizards will ease him into the spotlight. Boozer is not going to turn around Memphis, and therefore won't win. Peterson on the Jazz could be a really good addition, and he will likely be the go-to scorer. Caleb Wilson looks like he will have a prominent role and the green light. I just don't know that he is going to be a good enough shooter to win this award. So, who should we take? Darius Acuff Jr. will put up some monster numbers, but the Kings won't be able to hide his defensive flaws, and eventually that narrative will hurt him. Keaton Wagler might be the best option to take at +3500. Wagler is on a Clippers team that is searching, desperately, for someone to take over. I like him as a long shot and if I have to pick a favorite, I'll choose Peterson at +340. COOPER FLAGG LEADS NBA ALL-ROOKIE FIRST TEAM ALONGSIDE FORMER DUKE TEAMMATE KON KNUEPPEL AND VJ EDGECOMBE 6th Man of the Year I won't go through every player, but I like DeMar DeRozan at +1800. DeRozan still has a lot left in the tank, and I love that he is coming off the bench for Denver. He is an iso player who excels in the midrange. I can imagine many stretches where he comes in while Jokic and Jamal Murray are off the floor and DeRozan comes in to take over. I could see him getting some game-winners as well. There are, of course, a lot more awards you can choose from. I like to wait on Most Improved, even if I get a bit worse number, because this often goes to players who are good already, but improved from good to great. Defensive Player of the Year isn't worth betting on anyone, including Victor Wembanyama. title: Letitia James’ ‘fair’ Cornell rape probe vow collides with accused aide’s ‘quiet’ exit
description: New York Attorney General Letitia James faces recusal demands in the Cornell 7 case after publicly expressing support for Jane Doe before the probe.
content: New York Attorney General Letitia James has pledged a full and fair investigation into the Cornell 7 gang rape allegations, years after she faced accusations that she ignored warnings of sexual misconduct against her former chief of staff and allowed him to "quietly resign" while allegedly keeping his accuser in the dark. The claims stemmed from a 2022 lawsuit filed by James' former deputy press secretary, Sofia Quintanar. A New York judge dismissed the claims against James personally and the Attorney General's Office in February 2025. The decision was upheld by an appellate court in May 2026. Those allegations against James have received new attention after New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed James as special prosecutor to investigate an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house associated with Cornell University in October 2024. "Kathy Hochul lost faith in the local DA’s handling of the Cornell sexual assault case. So she picked Letitia James. Did you read Sofia Quintanar’s lawsuit, Governor?" Sam Antar, a fraud investigator based in New York wrote on X. CORNELL SEXUAL ASSAULT CASE REVIVES SCRUTINY OF A LITTLE-KNOWN NEW YORK LAW ON INTOXICATED VICTIMS "You’re entitled to question the DA’s handling of Cornell," Antar continued. "We’re entitled to question James’s handling of her own aide and your choice of James to restore public confidence." James is already facing calls to recuse herself from the case after an attorney for one of the defendants pointed to social media posts she made days before her appointment that appeared to take the alleged victim’s side. "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable," James posted on X on Sept. 28. "I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers. To her, and to all survivors: you’re not alone. We stand with you." Andrew Miltenberg, an attorney representing accused student Gillio Lopes, filed a court petition on Oct. 7 requesting James to be removed from the case. Miltenberg argued that James' remarks raised concerns about whether she could independently evaluate the evidence and determine whether criminal charges were warranted. "New York Attorney General Letitia James has always taken these matters seriously and followed the facts and the law," a spokesperson for James told Fox News Digital. Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani told Fox News Digital that James' public comments could complicate her investigation. "It is problematic for a prosecutor like Tish James to be commenting on a case publicly before the investigation is concluded," Rahmani said. "And the problem is, if you file criminal charges, whether it's through a complaint or a grand jury indictment, that may taint the potential jury pool in a criminal case," he added. Rahmani acknowledged that James likely did not anticipate being appointed when she made the remarks but said defense attorneys could still raise concerns about her involvement. Hochul has defended her decision to appoint James. "I have every confidence in our Attorney General to do what she has always done: look at the facts, examine the record and draw the proper conclusions," Hochul said during an Oct. 2 news conference. "That's exactly what's going to happen in this case." James also pledged in an Oct. 1 statement that her office would be "guided by the facts and the law." "The Governor has entrusted my office with this investigation, and we do not take that responsibility lightly," James said. But others, in addition to Antar, say New Yorkers shouldn't move on from the previous allegations raised against James by her former employee. "What about justice for former staffer Sofia Quintanar?" Lattina Brown posted on X. "She spoke out about sexual harassment and NY AG Letitia James had this woman blacklisted in the entire state of NY. The Dems turned their backs on this poor woman. Where is the support for the Hispanic woman?" The litigation centered on James' handling of misconduct allegations involving her longtime chief of staff, Ibrahim Khan, whom Quintanar accused of forcibly kissing her at a Brooklyn political fundraiser in November 2021. INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM In her lawsuit, Quintanar accused James of overlooking warning signs about Khan's conduct and protecting him from the fallout after the accusations surfaced. Her lawsuit claimed Khan was allowed to omit his "unlawful conduct" from his resignation statement and accused James of making "misleading statements" to the press about his whereabouts during the investigation. Quintanar also alleged she was not kept updated on the investigation. The complaint pointed to earlier accusations involving Angel Dubose, a former employee who claimed she was drugged and sexually assaulted at a 2014 holiday party while James served as New York City's public advocate. The lawsuit referenced a 2017 New York Post article linking Khan to the alleged assault. However, the newspaper later removed the report after learning that Dubose could not recall who attacked her and had never identified Khan as the perpetrator, The New York Times reported. James said she referred Dubose's allegations to law enforcement and other agencies after learning of them in 2017. The Manhattan district attorney's office and New York City's Department of Investigation later closed their investigations without filing charges. James described those allegations as "unsubstantiated" in a December 2022 NY1 interview. James' office said it first learned of Quintanar's allegations against Khan on Oct. 2, 2022, directed him to work remotely the following day and hired an outside law firm to investigate on Oct. 4. However, the lawsuit was not dismissed entirely. The appellate court allowed a federal civil rights claim against Khan to proceed and revived retaliation claims against Khan and James' re-election campaign. content: I've said this many times before, but one of my favorite things about college football are the myriad uniform combinations and unique concepts that programs come up with. Even just this past weekend, plenty of teams unveiled some absolutely gorgeous uniforms, including the Florida Gators in their 60s throwbacks and the Utah Utes with their "icy" helmets. Even some of the most traditional powers that the sport has to offer have busted out some new uniform combinations to get their fans excited (think Georgia's all-white threads and matching white helmet). UCF KNIGHTS SALUTE MERCURY, GEMINI, AND APOLLO PROGRAMS WITH SLICK NEW SPACE U UNIFORMS One program that isn't a traditional power is Coastal Carolina, and the Chanticleers have always marched to the beat of their own drum. One need only look at their home field, which is painted in their signature teal color scheme, to see that this is a football team that is willing to push the boundaries of fashion. RUTGERS UNVEILS SPECIAL UNIFORMS TO HONOR 37 ALUMNI KILLED IN SEPTEMBER 11 ATTACKS So it should come as no shock that the Chanticleers are unveiling their very own 90s throwback jerseys this coming Friday against conference rival Appalachian State. And when I say "90s throwbacks," I'm not referring to jerseys the team wore 30 years ago. I mean these uniforms are literally 90s themed. Take a look. First of all, a special shout out should go to whomever came up with the Coastal Carolina branded Game Boy Color. If you're of a certain age (likely between 29-45), these jersey's tugged at your nostalgic heartstrings and harkened back to a time when life was simpler. The description from the official press release regarding the uniforms on Coastal Carolina's athletics website says it best. "The uniforms draw from the colorful, oversized and unmistakably '90s aesthetic seen in iconic television shows such as 'Saved By The Bell,' 'Boy Meets World,' 'The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,' 'Friends,' and many more." Yeah, you guys pretty much nailed it. Now, while I love being reminded of my youth, some football fans are a little less enthusiastic about their team taking the field looking like an advertisement for an after-school cartoon programming block. If you're a football guy and you just want your team to come out in their traditional home colors, I get it. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! But, on the other hand, let these guys have a little fun. This is a brilliant marketing ploy by Coastal Carolina, too, taking full advantage of a standalone game on a Friday night on national television. It doesn't matter if App State hangs 70 on the Chanticleers, everyone will be talking about these jerseys. title: Amelia Earhart mystery enters critical phase as explorers zero in on mysterious object
description: The 17-person Taraia Object expedition team reached Nikumaroro Island to investigate a satellite anomaly that could be Amelia Earhart's Lockheed Electra.
content: The crew searching for Amelia Earhart's missing plane has arrived on a remote Pacific island — and they're getting ready to investigate new clues that could shed light on her disappearance. Purdue University in Indiana announced Monday that the 17-person Taraia Object expedition team arrived at Nikumaroro Island after a five-day journey across the Pacific Ocean. The aptly named team is investigating a mysterious anomaly spotted in satellite imagery that some researchers believe could be Earhart's lost Lockheed Electra. NOAH'S ARK MYSTERY ENTERS NEW PHASE AS RESEARCHERS PROBE DEEP BENEATH SITE The expedition centers on the Nikumaroro Hypothesis, a theory that Earhart's plane crashed near the remote Pacific island. The team arrived shortly after sunset, so fieldwork was postponed until morning. The vessel moved to the island's eastern side for calmer waters overnight as the crew prepared to go ashore at daybreak. On the first day ashore, the team is focusing on "transporting equipment, clearing vegetation and establishing staging operations at the beach and on the south side of the lagoon," Purdue said in its statement. DIVERS BRAVE DEADLY 'MOUNT EVEREST OF SHIPWRECKS' AS FAMED WRECK BREAKS APART "Upon reaching shore, the team will divide into two teams, with one taking smaller transport boats through the Tatiman Passage, a natural opening on the island’s western side, to access the lagoon and place buoys along the way to guide a return trip to the Marin Mainiku at the conclusion of work," the university added. The second team will cut a trail through the island's jungle, connecting the landing site to the southern side of the lagoon. "Staging areas will be established on both ends of the jungle trail to support the first day’s work, before the focus moves to the Taraia Peninsula on Wednesday" — meaning Oct. 14, the statement also noted. The team is operating 16 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time, with Wednesday's activities on the island beginning Tuesday afternoon in the U.S. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, while attempting to become the first female pilot to circumnavigate the globe by air. Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, vanished during one of the final stretches of their trip after departing Lae, New Guinea, for Howland Island. Earhart, one of the world's most famous people at the time, was only 39 years old. In a statement, expedition leader Rick Pettigrew called the prospect of examining the object gratifying. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "It is incredibly rewarding to be this close to completing our inspection of the Taraia Object and potentially solving, at long last, the outstanding mystery of the disappearance of Amelia Earhart and Fred Noonan more than 89 years ago," he said. Purdue has a longstanding connection to Earhart, who served as a career counselor and adviser to women students at the university in the 1930s. The Purdue Research Foundation also helped finance her Lockheed Electra, which she used during her ill-fated final flight. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The university became involved in the latest search after Pettigrew approached the Purdue Research Foundation in February 2025. Purdue spokesperson Trevor Peters previously told Fox News Digital that, if the Taraia Object is Earhart's airplane, the team hopes to conduct a full-scale archaeological excavation next year with the proper permissions. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The eventual curation of the wreckage has been the subject of discussions with [the Republic of] Kiribati, and although nothing has been finalized, ALI [the Archaeological Legacy Institute] and the Purdue Research Foundation share a dream of returning the plane to Purdue to be displayed, consistent with Amelia's original wishes," he added.

title: White House official defends Teresa Giudice’s visit as critics slam reality star’s ex-husband’s pardon push
description: Lynne Patton shared her cocaine addiction story and the intervention by Eric Trump and Lara Trump that shaped her belief in second chances for Joe Giudice.
content: A senior White House official with longstanding ties to "The Real Housewives of New Jersey" star Teresa Giudice is addressing whether her ex-husband, Joe Giudice, deserves a second chance, while emphasizing that any presidential pardon decision rests solely with President Donald Trump. Lynne Patton, deputy assistant to the president for coalition policy and engagement, took to Instagram to explain why Teresa Giudice and her daughter, Gia Giudice, were invited to the White House for Columbus Day and Italian American heritage celebrations. Patton's comments about Joe, who was deported to Italy after serving time for fraud-related offenses, also addressed the family's efforts to secure a presidential pardon. ‘RHONJ’ ALUM JOE GIUDICE SAYS HE SHOULDN’T HAVE BEEN DEPORTED AFTER FRAUD CONVICTION Patton emphasized that she has no authority over presidential pardons but offered a personal message about redemption and second chances. "For those inquiring @teresagiudice and her daughter, @_giagiudice, were at the White House at the invitation of the President & First Lady in honor of Columbus Day & Italian-American heritage. I have known Teresa and her family, including @joe.giudice, for nearly two decades," Patton began her post. "I’ve attended family gatherings at their former New Jersey homes where Joe taught me how to roll meatballs & Teresa’s beloved father once showed me how to make his famous homemade wine. I am not in charge of pardons. Nor do I decide who receives them." She added, "That is the President’s sole decision based upon recommendations from the White House Pardon Czar, @alicemariefree, and White House Counsel." Patton then shared her own experience with addiction and the second chance she said the Trump family gave her. Patton said she relapsed into cocaine addiction while working at the Trump Organization in 2013, crediting Eric Trump and Lara Trump with staging an intervention that she said saved her life. Her experience, she said, shaped her belief in second chances. "To date, I have been drug-free for 13 years. They could have fired me. But instead, they told me that I was worth saving. Even when I didn’t believe that myself. Instead of sidelining me, they gave me more responsibility. I worked harder. Stayed in the office longer. Arrived earlier. More importantly, I earned back their trust & friendship. In turn, that translated into more self-confidence and earned promotions — including a personal request from their father to join him in D.C. It rebuilt my determination to succeed & help others do the same." Patton also cited her Christian faith and the importance of a father's presence in his children's lives. TODD AND JULIE CHRISLEY HOME FOR HOLIDAYS AFTER TRUMP PARDONS END PRISON TIME "With that said, my faith in God compels me to believe that a father’s place is in the home. Statistics confirm the same. More importantly, so does the Bible. Charlie Kirk often declared that the biblical role of the father to his child is to be their protector, both physically and spiritually. Quality time is everything. And no, it is never too late to be the provider who God intended every father to be," Patton added. "Do I believe that Joe deserves a second chance? Unfortunately, it is not my place to decide. But what I do know is that one of his beautiful daughters desperately needs him now more than ever. And even God supports that." Joe was deported to Italy in 2019 after serving 41 months in federal prison for financial crimes. He has been living in the Bahamas, while his four daughters remain in the United States. Gia has publicly advocated for her father's return to the United States. Joe sought a presidential pardon in June 2025, and Gia said in August 2026 that the family had filed a humanitarian packet as part of its efforts to bring him home. A presidential pardon would not automatically guarantee Joe's return to the United States. According to the Justice Department, a pardon can eliminate certain grounds for deportation, but its immigration consequences depend on the circumstances of the case.
