title: Kimberly Guilfoyle confirms exit as ambassador to Greece as Trump asks her to resign amid flurry of scandals
description: Kimberly Guilfoyle faces allegations of a $100,000 payment request, diplomatic misconduct and hostile workplace claims at the U.S. Embassy in Greece.
content: Kimberly Guilfoyle confirmed Tuesday that she is leaving her post as U.S. ambassador to Greece after the White House revealed on Tuesday that President Donald Trump had asked her to resign. Her departure follows a cascade of allegations in recent weeks, including that she sought help from a Trump donor to pay off a $100,000 credit card bill, offered access to senior administration officials, promoted the interests of a Greek company and mistreated embassy staff. The ambassador again denied the allegations that led to her ouster in a lengthy X post on Tuesday and pledged her continued loyalty to the president — who was almost her father-in-law. But Trump distanced himself from Guilfoyle on Tuesday even though his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., was engaged to her for four years. "Kimberly Guilfoyle — she was almost a member of your family. How surprised were you to learn about these allegations? What did you think?" a reporter asked Trump before he departed for Alaska. "She wasn't a member of my family. She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago," Trump shot back. "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading." New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia announced during her first briefing to the press on Tuesday that Guilfoyle was asked to leave her post. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," Zacharia said. It came one day after Trump publicly acknowledged that he was considering firing Guilfoyle. "Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime," Guilfoyle wrote in an X post confirming her ouster. "I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of the world." Guilfoyle directly rejected the allegations involving her financial dealings, treatment of embassy staff and relationships with foreign business interests that have engulfed her tenure in recent weeks. "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity," she wrote. "I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service." She did not directly address the White House's decision to ask her to resign or say when she would formally leave the post, but acknowledged that her tenure was ending. "While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote. She also stressed that her support for Trump remains unchanged. "My gratitude and respect for President Trump and Secretary Rubio remain unwavering," Guilfoyle wrote. "I am proud of what we accomplished together, and I will always be a loyal supporter of President Trump and his mission to Make America Great Again." TRUMP 'LOOKING AT' FIRING AMBASSADOR TO GREECE: 'WE'RE NOT HAPPY' Guilfoyle was with Donald Trump Jr. for six years, four of which they were engaged. They publicly split in December 2024, the same month Trump nominated her to serve as ambassador to Greece. The ambassador came under scrutiny last week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025. According to messages reviewed by the Journal, Guilfoyle urged Deters to wire the money directly to American Express, saying the transaction would not leave a paper trail, while offering to help him gain access to senior Trump administration officials. Deters said he never made the payment. Guilfoyle's attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages, saying Guilfoyle had been paid to speak at events before her nomination and "was owed a balance for traveling to and supporting these patriotic events." The allegations followed an earlier Journal investigation into Guilfoyle's conduct in Greece, including claims that she promoted the interests of Greek construction and energy company Aktor Group and allowed its registered lobbyist, Christos Marafatsos, to accompany her to private diplomatic meetings with senior officials. The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle suggested at a dinner with Greek officials that the U.S. would undermine their government, citing political developments in Romania. Greece's foreign minister subsequently said there was no need to summon Guilfoyle for an explanation because the country's energy minister denied that any threat had been made. Separately, the State Department's Office of Inspector General reportedly opened an investigation into allegations involving Guilfoyle's treatment of embassy employees, private travel, acceptance of gifts and relationships with business interests, according to the Daily Mail. HOUSE DEMOCRAT INVESTIGATED OVER ALLEGED 'INAPPROPRIATE SEXUAL CONTACT' WITH STAFFER Sources described a hostile workplace in which Guilfoyle allegedly threatened to fire employees. They also claimed that she demoted members of her security detail over minor incidents, including an officer who reportedly failed to answer a 4 a.m. request for ice while she was vacationing in Mykonos. The inspector general's office declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation. Binnall told the Daily Mail that "any implication of wrongdoing by the Ambassador is unsupported." The allegations drew scrutiny from congressional Democrats, including Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., and Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., who called for a review of Guilfoyle's conduct. Meeks urged her removal if the allegations were substantiated. Vice President JD Vance addressed the controversy Friday, cautioning against rushing to judgment while acknowledging that misconduct should carry consequences. "Let's actually see what the facts are. Let's see what the truth is," Vance told reporters in Ohio. "And obviously, if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it." Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who visited Greece last week and delivered remarks against the backdrop of the Acropolis, initially defended Guilfoyle's performance. "Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here," Rubio told reporters Wednesday. A day later, Rubio declined to address the allegations directly, challenging reporters over their reliance on unnamed sources. "You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something, and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel," Rubio said last Thursday. Just days later, the White House announced their request for her resignation. Trump nominated Guilfoyle to the diplomatic post in December 2024. A former California prosecutor and longtime Trump ally, she previously served as a prominent surrogate and fundraiser for the president. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, from 2001 to 2006, when he served as mayor of San Francisco.

title: Don Lemon's presidential ambitions met with skepticism, amusement from his former CNN colleagues
description: Don Lemon says there's a 65 to 70% chance he'll launch a White House bid, and CNN staffers have strong reactions to his presidential ambitions.
content: Left-wing podcaster and former CNN host Don Lemon claims to be considering a run for president. Count his former colleagues as skeptical at best. Lemon, an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump who started his own show after being fired by CNN in 2023, recently said there is a "65, 70%" chance he’ll launch a White House bid. Lemon, who has no political experience, has said he would make a better president than Trump and talked up his appeal to voters. A CNN staffer knocked Lemon's apparent presidential ambitions. "Doesn’t someone, according to Don Lemon, have to be in their 'prime' to run for president? That would certainly rule Don out," they told Fox News Digital. DON LEMON CLAIMS TRUMP'S MAGA MOVEMENT IS 'CLOSEST THING' TO MODERN NAZI PARTY WITHOUT HOLOCAUST The staffer was referring to the infamous 2023 moment when Lemon found himself in hot water for suggesting then-Republican presidential candidate Nikki Haley was past her "prime" at age 51, enraging female colleagues and sparking public fury. Lemon, who is now 60 and almost six years older than Haley, later apologized for the comments. "I love it. Bring it on," another CNN staffer told Fox News Digital of Lemon's possible bid. "It would be fun if he ran. Little bit less boring than the standard 18-people on-stage process that we’re about to watch unfold," they said. "Although, I doubt he actually does it." Lemon's profile was raised earlier this year when he was slapped with a felony indictment for livestreaming a protest against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at a Minnesota church. He has insisted he was working as a journalist and was not part of the group that harassed churchgoers, but Lemon ramped up his criticism of Trump since the incident. "Don does very much want to have influence and feel his contributions matter. Would seem other ways make more sense because running is merely raising money, which is f---ing miserable, and you can’t get anywhere," Lemon’s former colleague said. "I think political office is probably appealing to him. I think a presidential run is obviously not serious, but he could engage in it as a way to launchpad into another office," they continued. "If Don has the itch, there are ways to scratch it that are more serious. It takes a single-minded focus, and he can’t be a media personality and do it at the same time." EX-CNN ANCHOR DON LEMON AGREES TRUMP PLAYED LIBERAL NETWORK 'LIKE PUPPETS' A third CNN staffer said Lemon has done a good job of remaining "relevant" since being fired. "It’s the most open nomination process in 30+ years for the Dems, I think you gotta take it seriously," the second staffer told Fox News Digital. "I’m not saying he is serious, but I am saying he’s said it enough that I can’t dismiss it." Lemon was fired by then-CNN CEO Chris Licht in 2023 and has since launched his own media company. Lemon's tenure at CNN came to a bumpy end, as he had recently been pushed out of his primetime hosting gig to an ill-fated morning show stint with co-hosts Kaitlan Collins and Poppy Harlow. His squabbles on the show and the flap over his infamous Haley comments sealed his fate. DON LEMON REVEALS HE'S 'TOTALLY SERIOUS' ABOUT CONSIDERING A PRESIDENTIAL RUN He wouldn't be the first CNNer to jump into politics. On-air analyst John Avlon launched a New York congressional bid as a Democrat in 2024 but was ultimately defeated. Lemon suggested earlier this year he didn’t have political ambitions but said people had been asking him to do so, and therefore, he was thinking about it. "I actually think I would be a really good president of the United States," Lemon said on the "Can’t be Censored" podcast. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "For the people to want me. What it would take is if I ran a political campaign, a presidential campaign, I would like to run it, and I don't know if this is realistic or not, without having to beg for money. I would like it to be a voter-citizen-driven campaign for as much as it can be," he continued. "Maybe at some point I might have to take a donation. I would rather not do that." title: Dana Perino shares how she secretly pushed back at reporters during White House briefings
description: Dana Perino revealed on Sean Hannity's podcast how she secretly flipped off reporters behind a water cup during George W. Bush press briefings.
content: Dana Perino detailed her shocking White House press podium habit during a podcast interview Tuesday, admitting she secretly flipped off combative reporters while maintaining a polite smile during briefings under former President George W. Bush. "I would just sit there with my hand over my cup and just flip him off the entire time he was talking," Perino told Sean Hannity on his "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast. "They'd be asking questions. I'd smile through it ... [and] nod," she recalled. LEAVITT PULLS BACK THE CURTAIN ON TRUMP'S 'TENSE,' UNFILTERED PRIVATE TALKS WITH PUTIN, XI, STARMER Perino, who served as Bush's press secretary from 2007 to 2009, explained that she kept a cup of water at the podium and used it to shield her hand from view while discreetly delivering the middle finger during testy exchanges. The gesture, which Perino jokingly likened to a form of "liquid courage," gave her a small sense of "defiance and confidence" while maintaining her composure. CORNEL WEST AND SEAN HANNITY FIND UNLIKELY COMMON GROUND DESPITE DEEP POLITICAL DIVIDE The story was kept under wraps for years until she revealed it to Hannity in the past, she recalled. Perino later published the story in her 2015 memoir, "And the Good News Is..." and garnered attention from late conservative talk radio host Rush Limbaugh. "When I did [Limbaugh's] radio show, he said, this is the best story ever," she recalled. Hannity agreed, calling it "the greatest story ever told" by a White House press secretary and marveling at Perino's unexpected display of defiance behind the podium. WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS WIDELY PRAISE KAROLINE LEAVITT AS SHE ANNOUNCES EXIT FROM TRUMP ADMINISTRATION Perino explained that her role as White House press secretary required her to remain respectful and composed, even when facing combative reporters who, she believed, were more interested in securing television airtime than getting answers. "They would do anything to get on TV that night," she recalled. "They would give a big windup and try to hit you so that they could make sure that they could get on air for one of the networks." Perino suggested that the pressure on reporters to produce memorable moments was already shaping exchanges during her tenure, but she believes the rise of social media has only intensified that dynamic. The former press secretary and current "America's Newsroom" co-anchor also recalled a conversation with Mike McCurry, who served under former President Bill Clinton, about whether allowing cameras into the White House briefing room had ultimately done more harm than good. title: Olympic legend Kaillie Humphries opens up on impact of women's sports advocacy on Team USA relationships
description: Kaillie Humphries says her stance against transgender athletes in women's sports has created tense moments with Team USA teammates and friendships.
content: Olympic champion Kaillie Humphries says her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in women’s sports has created "awkward, tense moments" with some Team USA teammates and strained existing friendships. Humphries, a three-time Olympic gold medalist and XX-XY Athletics ambassador, told OutKick she recently received the brand’s "Courage Wins Award" and plans to direct the funding toward her foundation supporting female athletes’ careers and family-building needs. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! As a California resident, she plans to vote Republican in the coming gubernatorial election. She is currently pregnant with her second child, and if she has a girl, and if the state's current policy that allows males to compete in girls' sports continues, it could contribute to her leaving the state. She says lending her voice to the "Save Women's Sports" movement has brought some disagreements with teammates and friends in the Olympic community. "I have teammates within bobsled, I have teammates within Team USA who believe in a different side, for sure," Humphries said. "For sure, it's created awkward, tense moments. I think it's created tense moments even within friendships that were there." AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS' She said disagreements have the potential to become heated, but emphasized that many fellow athletes have maintained respect for her despite their opposing views. "And I think that while it creates a bit of tension, no one's willing to cross the line. It doesn't make you a bad person because you believe something different than somebody else," she said. Humphries said her goal is to preserve the opportunities she enjoyed throughout her career for other female athletes. "I've had these opportunities because it has remained for biological females. And that's something that I believe in and that I'm going to push," she said. OLYMPIC CHAMPION NANCY HOGSHEAD HONORED FOR ADVOCACY AS SHE PUSHES WNBA ON FEMALE ELIGIBILITY RULES She also argued that transgender athletes should have opportunities to compete in categories based on their biological sex. "Sport is meant to be an open place for everybody. I do believe that," she said. The International Olympic Committee adopted a policy in March restricting eligibility for the women’s category at IOC events, beginning with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, through one-time SRY gene screening, with specified rare exceptions. The policy does not apply to grassroots or recreational sports. Humphries said she is willing to discuss the issue with people who are respectful and open to hearing different perspectives, but does not approach those conversations with the intention of changing their minds. title: Americans draw the line at livestreaming ‘spectacle’ of Fort Hood shooter's execution: ‘It’s an abomination’

title: ‘Peace through strength’: Trump Gaza plan gains global backing one year on
description: Donald Trump's Board of Peace excludes UNRWA from Gaza's future as the EU pledges $1 billion and demilitarization efforts gain global momentum.
content: A year has passed since President Donald Trump made history by brokering a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, setting in motion an ambitious peace plan aimed at bringing lasting stability to the region. In the days and months since the ceasefire and Trump’s 20-point peace plan took hold, progress has drawn support from across the globe — including from unexpected quarters. Senior advisor to the Board of Peace Josh Gruenbaum told Fox News Digital that the success of the last 12 months was largely attributable to President Donald Trump’s leadership and commitment to seeking peace. TRUMP-BACKED BOARD OF PEACE, ISRAEL 'WILL TAKE ACTION' IF HAMAS REMAINS OUT OF COMPLIANCE: NETANYAHU ADVISOR "The unlock was somebody who came in, who really knew the file because they had the chance to study it and understand it," Gruenbaum said. Trump and his team, including U.S. special envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff, U.S. special envoy for Peace Jared Kushner and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, "created working relationships with regional actors with trust, overlaid with peace through strength," while also forcing Hamas to finally understand that "this was either going to end the very hard way for them, or there was an off-ramp and a way to do this in a more dignified way, which is what the 20-point plan was." He said this has been achieved by "building consensus through the world, including through Europe, that this is the only game in town. This is the only pragmatic approach to make this thing stop." A particular point of strength for the Board of Peace, Gruenbaum added, has been "cultivating really strong relationships with the United Nations." In November 2025, the United Nations endorsed the Board of Peace through Resolution 2803. European Union Commissioner for the Mediterranean and for Demography Dubravka Šuica announced at a high-level briefing at the Board of Peace in September that the European Union had "gathered about $1 billion for early recovery in Gaza," and would sign recovery projects with the UNDP and UNICEF. "We are doing this in alignment with the priorities of the Board of Peace and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG)," Šuica stated. US URGES DONORS TO ABANDON UNRWA FUNDING AS UN DEFENDS AGENCY'S MISSION The International Stabilization Force, which will train a future police force in Gaza and oversee demilitarization, has received commitments from Kazakhstan, Morocco, Albania and Kosovo, with other countries said to be in the pipeline for admission. Notably absent from Gaza’s future, per the Board of Peace plan, is the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). The Board of Peace has been unequivocal that UNRWA will have no involvement in Gaza. One U.S. agency, the USAID Office of the Inspector General, is currently investigating over 1,500 UNRWA employees for involvement in terror groups. On X, the Board of Peace recently stated that it "will only work with trusted partners who deliver for the people of Gaza and contribute to a deradicalized Strip," and emphasized that "UNRWA fails on those litmus tests." The Board of Peace’s effort has support from unlikely corners. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton wrote in a June editorial in the Financial Times that while the plan was "not the one many of us would have drafted," she believes "it remains the only framework backed by sufficient leverage, political engagement and potential resources to move parties towards implementation." The Board of Peace has received about $18 billion in pledges for reconstruction, the BBC recently reported. A Board of Peace official told Fox News Digital that next steps in the reconstruction program include a six-month program with 66 recovery initiatives, including rubble clearance, unexploded ordnance clearance, construction of temporary housing and destroying tunnel infrastructure. The initiatives are expected to cost $2.45 billion, and tenders for some projects have been submitted. KUSHNER GIVES HAMAS STARK ULTIMATUM: DISARM OR ISRAEL GETS US BACKING TO ‘FINISH THE JOB’ In the year ahead, the Board of Peace must clear a number of hurdles, including a full demilitarization and de-radicalization of Hamas in Gaza. Gruenbaum says that the Board of Peace is "realistic and sober" but is also "in a historic place with Hamas," having secured verbal agreements and offering a path to amnesty for those who qualify. Gruenbaum also says that the 20-point plan is Hamas’ best path forward and that regional dynamics leave them with few remaining options. Mediators are increasingly supporting the Board of Peace, Tehran is focused on its current war, and Israel is continuing to apply pressure, though Gruenbaum says the Board of Peace continues to stress that they must comply with the ceasefire. Gruenbaum said that deradicalization will never be a top-down process led by the U.S., but will be managed through the NCAG. He said that the NCAG’s members "have kids that have been brought up" under the current UNRWA-run system, so "they understand the situation." The approach will involve the new technocratic government, whose members have extensive experience in civil service, taking the lead on "vetting teachers" and "vetting people who are involved in civil governance." Gruenbaum celebrated the potential of bringing together the NCAG and Israeli authorities through the transformation of Gaza. "This is a monumental opportunity for the Palestinian people of Gaza where their governing body is going to be uniquely focused on delivering services for its constituents and if we could create this amazing relationship where we build trust between Israel and the NCAG, we deliver on both sides of the equation – security for Israel and freedom and a better life, self-determination and prosperity-building inside of Gaza. That’s a two-way trust-building system." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Gruenbaum added that the successes in Gaza could lead to successes elsewhere. "Maybe these best practices get learned by the Palestinian Authority. Maybe Israel starts adding more trust with different people in the system. I think this is a huge moment in the history of the Middle East."

title: Sean McVay is 'sick' about his overtime call as another Super Bowl coach publicly regrets end of game decision
description: Sean McVay says he's "sick" after a third-down play call led to a blocked field goal in the Rams' overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday.
content: Week 5 of this NFL season will be remembered by historians as the week when head coaches apologized, admitted mistakes and otherwise regretted their decisions in front of their teams and in public — and Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay is the latest to join them. The Rams lost in overtime to the Buffalo Bills in what was perhaps the most entertaining game of the season on Monday Night Football. Afterward, McVay was unhappy with himself, saying he was "sick" and "regretting" a decision that wasn’t necessarily wrong but wasn’t optimal and didn’t help his team in what could have been a game-deciding situation. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Here's the situation: The game is in overtime. The Rams have stopped the Bills on their first possession, so any points by McVay's team wins the game. And the Rams seem headed toward those points and victory when they drive from their 20-yard line to the Buffalo 30 mostly by attempting five consecutive pass plays. The Buffalo defense is on its heels under Matthew Stafford’s passing barrage. But on third-and-5 from the Bills' 30-yard line, McVay calls a run for Kyren Williams off right tackle. No gain. It was, clearly, the coach setting his team up for a field goal rather than pressing the issue. Except the Rams had their field goal blocked on fourth down, continuing a multi-season struggle with their special teams that has cost them multiple games. "Yeah, you know what? If I would have known," McVay told reporters afterward. "I wish I would have had a better play call and gone for it, got it a lot tighter. I'm sick right now with myself. "...I'm proud of the way that we battled and I'm sick that we came up short and I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go forward on third down ... "That's on me." We heard this multiple times in Week 5. Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn said "it's my responsibility" for the blown clock management at the end of his team's game against the New York Giants that turned a likely victory into a tie. Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took blame for his team's last-second loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars because of a decision he made on a kickoff. "I lost us that game," Sirianni said. And that's good. Accountability from a head coach, especially when it is taken publicly, sets a good example for players and how they'll act privately within the team. But that's not the point. title: 911 operators questioned whether Christa Pike failed execution call was prank, audio reveals
description: 911 audio reveals dispatchers initially dismissed Christa Pike's failed execution as a prank call, delaying the ambulance response to Riverbend Prison.
content: 911 dispatch recordings show a series of miscommunications led to delayed emergency response in the immediate aftermath of the Tennessee Department of Correction’s failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike. An initial 911 call came through to dispatchers around 8:40 p.m. on Sept. 30, roughly an hour after Pike’s planned execution began, according to documents and audio recordings obtained by Fox News. During the call, the unidentified caller informed operators of a failed execution but was unable to provide the operators with a code that would verify the legitimacy of the call. Following that call, operators sought to determine the authenticity of the audio shows. TENNESSEE DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES IN FAILED EXECUTION ATTEMPT "So we have a medical call for service at the Riverbend Prison," a dispatcher says in the Fox News-obtained audio. The dispatcher explains to another operator that the caller said, "They carried out the execution, the subject didn’t pass away, and they need an ambulance because she’s not breathing normally." DEATH ROW INMATE UNCONSCIOUS ON VENTILATOR AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION FOR TEEN’S KILLING: ATTORNEYS "We are trying to find out if that is an actual thing that is happening, and we need to send an ambulance, and/or if you need police assistance, or if this is someone that is just basically prank calling or like swatting us," the operator can be heard saying. In another snippet of internal dispatcher audio, an operator can be heard calling off the emergency response. TENNESSEE PRISON CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER FAILED EXECUTION AS FORMER US ATTORNEY TAPPED TO LEAD INDEPENDENT REVIEW "Per supervisors here at the DEC [Department of Emergency Communications], we have been informed it is a false call," a dispatcher can be heard saying at approximately 9:03 p.m. "There is no medical assistance needed at Riverbend Prison." An additional correspondence between an operator and what appeared to be somebody working at Riverbend Prison displayed further confusion. CHRISTA PIKE'S FIRST WORDS REVEALED AFTER SHE UNEXPECTEDLY WOKE UP WHILE LAWYERS THOUGHT SHE WAS 'BRAIN DEAD' "We got a call about a failed execution at your guys’ facility, and we’re just calling to verify," a dispatcher said. "Um … who called you?" the prison employee responded. "Is there like a sergeant I could speak with, or a supervisor?" the dispatcher asked. "Who called you? Do you know?" the employee said. "No, we don’t exactly know," the dispatcher replied. "I’m being told nobody from our facility called you, so there’s not really anything to speak of at the moment," the employee said. CHRISTA PIKE NOW CONSCIOUS AND TALKING AFTER SURVIVING 2 DOSES OF LETHAL INJECTION DRUG Pike’s attorney Kelly Gleason also called 911 to report the botched execution, audio recordings prove. "What’s going on is my client, Christa Gail Pike, is undergoing a state execution. She has completed the stages of the protocol and last we knew from the attorney who is present, she is still alive and breathing and needs immediate life-saving care," Gleason can be heard saying during a phone call timestamped at approximately 9:08 p.m. CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEY SAYS SHE'S 'UP AND WALKING' MORE THAN A WEEK AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION Around the same time as Gleason’s call, Riverbend Prison’s Central Control told emergency responders that they "would have been the ones to call in" but that they "did not make that call," according to the audio. But also around that time, a first responder can be heard on a separate recording saying: "Somebody is outside the gate at the prison telling us that it’s real and demanding us to go in. They say they are some sort of state official. I need somebody to get out to the gate and talk to those people." At that point, Central Control cleared the way for first responders to enter the prison at 9:11 p.m. Pike was in an ambulance and being transferred to a hospital by 9:34 p.m., the Associated Press reported. Pike was convicted of first degree murder and conspiracy to commit first degree murder in 1996 for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. She was sentenced to death and had been on death row for over 30 years when she arrived at her scheduled execution by lethal injection on Sept. 30. Prison execution authorities administered a single dose of pentobarbital, a central nervous system depressant used in Tennessee execution protocol. When Pike remained conscious after the initial dose, authorities administered a second dose per state protocol. When the second dose did not kill Pike, Tennessee’s single-drug execution protocol prevented authorities from administering a third dose. Pike was taken to a hospital where she was placed on a ventilator and remained unconscious for six days, waking up on Oct. 6, according to her attorneys. Pike was taken back to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center women’s prison on Oct. 10 where she is continuing to receive medical care, her attorneys said in a statement. Following the failed execution, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has paused all state executions pending a further review. title: Actor Dan Levy blasts Shane Gillis' 'SNL' monologue, claims men's 'complacency' fuels sexual assault

Levy, who hosted the NBC sketch comedy show in 2021, posted an Instagram video condemning Gillis' remarks on the latest episode and calling on other men to speak out against the comedian. "I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television," Levy said. "And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it’s complacency that has created the environment in which women are sexually assaulted, and it’s a ‘conversation’ as opposed to a ‘crime.’" WATCH: SHANE GILLIS REJECTS UFC FIGHTER’S CRUDE MICHELLE OBAMA JAB AFTER WHITE HOUSE WIN Gillis sparked controversy Saturday while hosting "SNL" for the third time. I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?" Gillis said. "Look, I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe [it]. Have you seen it? I’ve seen it. You’ve seen the shorts? They’re those neon, like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look! You’re not allowed to look." Levy rejected the suggestion that revealing workout clothing justified Gillis' characterization, arguing that the comedian's comments reflected a broader problem with how men perceive women. title: Suspect in deadly Philadelphia police ambush faces 76 charges, ordered held without bail
description: A Philadelphia man faces 76 charges, including murder, after allegedly ambushing police officers, killing one and wounding another, according to officials.
content: The suspect accused in the ambush killing of a Philadelphia police officer was arraigned Sunday morning on 76 charges and ordered held without bail, according to court records. Eric Lewis, 35, faces charges including murder, homicide of a law enforcement officer, attempted murder, 10 counts of attempted homicide of a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault, terroristic threats and other related offenses. His next court date is scheduled for Oct. 26. The charges stem from a Saturday shooting that killed Philadelphia Police Officer Shane Seiber and left his partner wounded. Seiber, 40, was a father of two and an Air Force veteran who served 10 years with the Philadelphia Police Department. He is survived by his wife, 7-year-old son and 3-year-old daughter. PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, PARTNER SHOT 12 TIMES IN AMBUSH; SUSPECT FOUND HIDING IN TREE "He fought valiantly, but he lost his life today," Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel said at a news conference on Saturday. "His wife was able to be by his side before he passed, as well as his family." The wounded officer, a 33-year-old father of five, was shot 12 times and was initially listed in critical condition. He has since been listed in stable condition. The shooting unfolded around 12:20 a.m. Saturday, when the two officers responded to a report of a man with a gun. They located an armed man on a porch, according to police. KENTUCKY TROOPER, FATHER OF 3, GUNNED DOWN DURING TRAFFIC STOP AS SUSPECT CAPTURED AFTER MANHUNT The officers then came under "significant gunfire" after reaching the porch, police said. Additional officers and a SWAT team arrived a short time later and found both officers on the porch suffering from gunshot wounds. More gunfire followed, prompting authorities to declare a barricade situation before Lewis was eventually taken into custody, according to police. Police said Lewis was found in possession of two handguns and a shotgun. One of the handguns belonged to an officer wounded in the attack. At a news conference Saturday, District Attorney Larry Krasner declined to say whether Lewis had fired the officer's handgun or how he had obtained the other firearms. Krasner also said there was nothing in Lewis' criminal background that would have prevented him from obtaining a firearm. Lewis, an employee of the Philadelphia Water Department, has a criminal history dating to 2012, according to Pennsylvania court records reviewed by Fox News Digital. Court records show Lewis was convicted of theft and receiving stolen property in 2012 and of gun-related offenses and simple assault in 2013. He received probation in both cases. In 2018, Lewis pleaded guilty to disorderly conduct involving fighting and was again sentenced to probation. title: Trump-linked super PAC pulls funding from 2 House Republicans as GOP fights to keep majority
description: House Republicans face growing pressure as Trump-aligned MAGA Inc. pulls planned spending from Tom Kean and Marianette Miller-Meeks' districts.
content: A top elections group affiliated with President Donald Trump is halting spending planned in two key congressional districts held by sitting House Republicans as Election Day looms less than a month away. MAGA Inc. is reallocating its planned investments in districts represented by Rep. Tom Kean, R-N.J., and Rep. Marianette Miller-Meeks, R-Iowa, for the remainder of the midterm election cycle, a source familiar with those plans confirmed to Fox News Digital. A super PAC aligned with House GOP leadership, the Congressional Leadership Fund (CLF), is also pulling its cash from those districts to reroute into other races, a source familiar with those plans said. Both groups will instead route those funds into other House races across the country. It comes after recent polling data signaled the two incumbents' chances for re-election have grown slim. WATCH: BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT CALLED IOWA A 'BACKWATER' OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES BAN Republicans' uphill battle to keep control of the House of Representatives is getting tougher by the day, according to various projections. The latest Fox News Power Rankings show Democrats having an edge in 219 House seats — enough to clinch a majority — while Republicans are projected to keep 198. Nineteen seats are still up in the air. Kean's 7th Congressional District is one of the wealthiest in both New Jersey and the U.S. as a whole, encompassing suburbs and exurbs of New York City to the north. A source close to Kean's campaign told Fox News Digital that "the race is fully funded down the home stretch." Kean's campaign and House Republicans' campaign arm "have major reservations on broadcast," the source said, adding that his Democratic opponent Rebecca Bennett "has no soft dollar reservations on her behalf." The Democrat leadership-aligned House Majority PAC (HMP) pushed back on that in a statement to Fox News Digital, with spokesperson CJ Warnke stating, "Not surprising that the guy who ghosted his constituents for more than 100 days is melting down over national Republicans abandoning his race. We're flipping NJ-07 blue in November." Kean and Miller-Meeks represent two of the most purple districts in the country. Kean won his House seat in 2022 after defeating incumbent former Rep. Tom Malinowski, D-N.J., by less than 10,000 votes. His 2024 re-election margin was wider, winning by just over 5%, or 23,000 more votes than his Democrat challenger. Miller-Meeks, meanwhile, is seeking a fourth term against Democrat Christina Bohannan, whom she defeated twice by roughly 20,000 and 800 votes in 2022 and 2024. She first won in 2020 by just six votes — earning her the nickname "six-pack" among fellow House Republicans and GOP leadership. DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS Miller-Meeks represents Iowa's 1st Congressional District in the state's southeast, encompassing the cities of Davenport and Iowa City. The New York Times first reported plans by "top Republican super PACs aligned with President Trump and congressional Republican leadership" to pull funding from Kean and Miller-Meeks' districts over concerns about their polling. TRUMP-LINKED MAGA INC POURS $10M INTO KEN PAXTON'S TEXAS SENATE RACE AGAINST JAMES TALARICO CLF is reportedly pulling the funding as part of a wider reshuffling of its war chest into other districts that Republicans are more confident in. That includes battleground Reps. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., and Monica De La Cruz, R-Texas, The Times reported. The source familiar with CLF's planning told Fox News Digital the group was also pulling funding from Michigan's 8th Congressional District and Ohio's 1st Congressional District, where Republicans were hoping to unseat Reps. description: Witnesses give accounts of a man falling to his death at Six Flags in Georgia. The company has temporarily closed similar roller coasters at multiple parks after the incident on the Goliath ride.
content: Witnesses described horrifying scenes after a man reportedly fell to his death from a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia — leaving other passengers stranded high above the ground. The man was riding the roller coaster with his son, while his wife and daughter watched from the ground, according to an eyewitness account reported by local station WXIA. The victim has now been identified as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, age 42, as confirmed by Cobb County Police. The incident occurred around 4 p.m. Monday on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. TERRIFYING SCENE UNFOLDS AT SIX FLAGS AS STORM-TOPPLED TREE SENDS 4 GUESTS TO HOSPITAL One witness told local outlet WXIA the man appeared in a souvenir photo taken during the ride. "He was in our pictures," the witness said. "He fell and hit the car three different times." Fox News Digital reached out to Six Flags for the latest on the ride's status. On Tuesday, Atlanta Public Schools confirmed the victim was an employee of the district. "Atlanta Public Schools extends its deepest condolences to the family, friends and loved ones of Mr. Kariem," the district said in a statement obtained by Fox News. "He was a cherished member of the Wesly International Academy and APS families whose presence and impact will be deeply missed by our students, staff and all those whose lives he touched. Our thoughts are with everyone mourning his loss during this difficult time." Another couple who were on the ride at the time of the incident described the terrifying moments surrounding the man's death, according to WXIA. "You don't see things like this happen. It should never happen." "The vehicle [meaning the ride] hit him, and then he flew back up again, and it hit him again, and then that's when he was, I guess, flung from the ride," the man told the outlet. "It went from having a great time to just screaming, 'Oh my God, what is happening,'" his wife said. "You don't see things like this happen. It should never happen." FRIGHTENING SCENE UNFOLDS ON ICONIC SKY RIDE AS CHILD FALLS DOWN ONTO BOARDWALK Meanwhile, another Goliath rider said his train was ascending when passengers heard screaming and saw people running below. The ride then stopped, leaving them stranded for about an hour without updates. "We were up there for an hour with no updates, no news, no nothing. We just saw everyone running out of the park," the witness told WXIA. "We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today." The Cobb County Police Department previously confirmed to Fox News Digital that one person died, and several others were reportedly injured. Police did not immediately provide further details about the circumstances surrounding the incident. "We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," a Six Flags spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital. "Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected." WOMAN ALLEGEDLY EJECTED FROM ROLLER COASTER, SUFFERS SERIOUS INJURIES AFTER DRAGGED ALONG TRACK: REPORTS Following the incident, Six Flags temporarily closed similar attractions at other parks as a precaution, the company confirmed to local outlet WSB-TV. "Out of an abundance of caution, we have temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks," a Six Flags spokesperson said, according to the outlet. "The safety of our guests and team members remains one of our highest priorities." Six Flags Magic Mountain in California and Six Flags Great America in Illinois also have roller coasters named Goliath, though the attractions feature different designs. Coaster scrutiny The incident comes as Six Flags has been facing scrutiny over another roller coaster at its Magic Mountain park in California. Six Flags Magic Mountain permanently closed its X2 roller coaster after multiple lawsuits accused the attraction of causing catastrophic brain injuries. A spokesperson for Six Flags Magic Mountain confirmed earlier to Fox News Digital that X2 had not operated since July 12. Dordick Law Corporation of Beverly Hills, which represents the plaintiffs, said it has retained more than 100 additional clients who allege they suffered brain injuries after riding X2, the firm told Fox News Digital on Sept. 23. So far, three lawsuits have been filed. "While X2 consistently passed a multitude of safety tests, we have decided to close the ride because we believe it’s the right thing to do," Oerding said in a statement. title: FBI operation targets scam compounds in Africa with arrests, account takedowns
description: Operation Blackout's latest raids across Ghana and Nigeria netted 28 arrests, freed trafficked workers and saw Meta remove 3.7 million accounts.
content: The FBI's expanded global efforts to disrupt and dismantle sprawling scam compounds that prey on Americans netted multiple arrests in Africa last week, as well as millions of dollars in potentially freezable funds and the takedown of social media accounts tied to fraud, officials said. Operation Blackout is the FBI’s global campaign to identify and dismantle foreign scam compounds through overseas raids, asset seizures and the disruption of web domains and infrastructure linked to scam networks. Authorities also worked to rescue trafficked workers and return stolen money to victims. "Thanks to a brilliant partnership with the Department of Justice, across multiple African countries, we arrested 28 alleged criminal actors, seized over 350 devices, identified at least $11 million in potentially freezable funds, freed over 100 trafficked workers, and identified over 100 potential scam victims here at home," FBI Director Kash Patel exclusively told Fox News Digital. FIRST ON FOX: FBI TARGETS GHANA SCAM COMPOUND LINKED TO NEARLY $10M IN LOSSES, MORE THAN 130 DETAINED "This is what happens when law enforcement executes with precision across the inter-agency," Patel added. "We are demolishing criminal scam centers across the globe and truly saving lives." In a series of initiatives stemming from the larger FBI operation, authorities conducted law enforcement raids and seizures last week as part of a "Joint Disruption Week" based out of London that resulted in 28 arrests across Ghana and Nigeria. GLOBAL PARTNERS ARE JOINING THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION AND THIS FBI TO TAKE DOWN SCAM EMPIRES FOR GOOD In addition to the arrests, authorities identified more than 100 scam victims with losses so far exceeding $10 million. The more than 120 trafficked workers identified are slated to be repatriated, the FBI said. Additionally, more than 3.7 million Facebook and Instagram accounts allegedly linked to fraudulent activity were taken down in partnership with Meta. FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS "Scams are a global threat that demand a global response," Chris Sonderby, vice president and deputy general counsel for Meta, said in a news release from the tech giant regarding last week's operations. "Working with the U.K. National Crime Agency, the FBI, DOJ and the Homeland Security Task Force, we took the fight to scam centers across West Africa. "As part of the disruption, we removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups targeting people in the U.S., U.K., and beyond, and shared leads on over 30 suspected scam centers resulting in dozens of arrests, the rescue of trafficking victims and cryptocurrency seizures," Sonderby added. GLOBAL TASK FORCE DISMANTLES 'PIG-BUTCHERING' CRYPTO FRAUD RINGS PREYING ON AMERICANS In Ghana, 117 victims are pending repatriation to Nigeria, and 19 suspects were arrested and detained. In Nigeria, local authorities will prosecute nine individuals arrested for violations of Nigerian law, the FBI said. The Ghana and Nigeria operations follow a warning from Patel that international scam networks were expanding beyond Southeast Asia and the Middle East into Africa. "That’s why you’re seeing the migration of these scam compounds to central and sub-Saharan Africa, which is where we are already pre-positioned to take them off," Patel told Fox News Digital in September. The FBI-led initiative targets transnational cybercrime groups operating massive scam centers where trafficked workers are forced to carry out fraud schemes from thousands of miles away against unsuspecting Americans. AMERICANS LOST OVER $20 BILLION TO ONE TYPE OF CRIME. HERE’S HOW WE CAN FIGHT IT In total, Operation Blackout has resulted in roughly $17 billion being seized, hundreds of alleged scammers arrested and thousands of trafficked workers freed. Furthermore, more than 10,000 Americans were warned about being targeted for potential fraud before losing their money, preventing an estimated $670 million in financial losses, according to the FBI. Many of the victims are senior citizens, Patel previously told Fox News Digital. Criminal networks have begun a geographic shift in an effort to broaden their scams, Patel has said. BURMA APPROVES DEATH PENALTY FOR SCAMMERS MONTHS AFTER FBI'S $8 BILLION CRYPTO CRACKDOWN In September, a Justice Department Scam Center Strike Force team helped authorities in Madagascar take down 13 scam centers operated by Chinese organized crime syndicates and process more than 3,200 electronic devices, Fox News Digital previously reported. Criminal networks have now begun using artificial intelligence to further their scams, experts said. The technology gives scammers the ability to use voice cloning and send flawless emails and messages to potential victims, eliminating the language barriers that once made scams easy to spot. "At OpenAI, we’re using AI to disrupt scam operations and help people spot scams. By sharing insights responsibly with industry and law enforcement partners, we can identify scam networks across platforms and build stronger collective defenses." title: Massive bison rams pickup truck in Yellowstone after driver tries to avoid collision
description: A bull bison charged a man's Ford Ranger near Mud Volcano in Yellowstone National Park around 2:45 a.m. on Thursday — and fortunately, the man did not report injuries.
content: A driver's early-morning trip through Yellowstone National Park took a frightening turn when a bison suddenly charged his pickup truck. A video shared on Facebook shows the massive animal standing on a dark roadway before rushing toward the vehicle — then slamming into the front of the truck. The driver had stopped his Ford Ranger after spotting the bull bison near Mud Volcano at around 2:45 a.m. on Thursday, according to Wyoming publication Cowboy State Daily. YELLOWSTONE OFFICIALS DECIDE FATE OF BISON THAT LAUNCHED GRANDFATHER 8 FEET IN AIR Kyle Weber, a seasonal mechanic who had been working in Yellowstone, was driving south from Canyon Village toward Fishing Bridge when he encountered the animal in the road, the outlet reported. Rather than attempting to pass, he hit the brakes and waited for the bison to move. "I slammed on my brakes and stopped, and was just sitting there watching and waiting for him to continue walking," Weber told Cowboy State Daily. After he waited, the animal remained on the roadway — and then unexpectedly charged the pickup and hit its front-left side, according to the outlet. Fox News Digital reached out to Yellowstone National Park for comment. Weber said he estimated the impact pushed his truck backward at least a foot and a half. The collision dented the truck's bumper and hood, and it broke a side marker light, according to Cowboy State Daily. Weber reportedly plans to replace the damaged bumper and side marker, using the repairs as an opportunity to make some upgrades to the truck. The dented hood, however, may remain as a reminder of the encounter. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES "I think I'll keep it," Weber said. title: A little boy asked why his dad doesn't like him. His words broke my heart
description: Let me tell you about the hard work that we must do every day. Far too many of us make the mistake of trying to save young men only after they are broken.
content: One of our young men came back from a day with the boys and told me he had to step away, so the child would not see him cry. The child, an 11-year-old with a buzzed head and a gap-tooth smile, told the young man that he loves coming around us because we feel like his uncles. Then the child got quiet. He said he gets sad sometimes because his dad never wants to talk to him or see him. What made the young man tear up was that the child then said that he hopes his father is doing good. "But why doesn’t my dad like me?" We all love this young boy and there is nothing not to like about him. He is good to his mother. He tries hard at school. He stands up to bullies and takes care of those around him. This boy is only 11. He is asking for guidance. He is asking for adults to guide him. If we don’t step up, the streets will take him. This is the hard work that we do every day. Far too many of us make the mistake of trying to save young men after they are broken. We hold the press conference after the shooting, myself included, and we say we must do better. We demand funding for programs after the arrest and the boy is long gone into the slammer. In the saddest cases, we write the obituary after the funeral and the family grieves over the senselessness. These tragedies happen because we often fail to build the boy before the streets define manhood for him. CHICAGO PASTOR GATHERS HUNDREDS OF MEN TO DECLARE VIOLENCE-FREE ZONE ON SOUTH SIDE By manhood I don’t mean puffing your chest like you're some bad dude. That’s an empty front. Manhood means discipline, responsibility, accountability, faith and all the qualities that allow one to stand strong on two feet. This boy is only 11. He is asking for guidance. He is asking for adults to guide him. If we don’t step up, the streets will take him. Every young boy learns from the men who stay and show how it is done. A young boy does not learn from a slogan, a speech or empty promises. The government can send a check, and it has sent more than its share into our neighborhood, but the government can never manufacture expectations. It cannot sit on the curb and talk to an 11-year-old boy who wants to know why his father disappeared. Last week, I stood in front of our new Leadership and Economic Opportunity Center that we built to steward young boys like our 11-year-old. High up on one of the window panes, someone shot a hole through the glass. This is the third window pane that has been broken. We’re talking thousands to repair the damage and we will replace them. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION But think about what they shot. It wasn’t a liquor store or a vacant lot. It was a building — one of the first constructions on the South Side in who knows how long — going up where a motel notorious for crime once stood. And on a block that was known as America’s most dangerous. The government can send a check, and it has sent more than its share into our neighborhood, but the government can never manufacture expectations. It cannot sit on the curb and talk to an 11-year-old boy who wants to know why his father disappeared. This building houses job training facilities, classrooms, tutoring, violence prevention and so on. Most of all, this building was built to house young boys and girls who need the safety to grow into strong, resilient adults. Someone looked at all of that and fired a bullet at it. I’m ticked off and I'm upset. But I’m not quitting. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP When that young man told me about that child and his father, I took that as a sign from God. I don’t know how, but I do know why and that is why I keep stepping forward. It is for these young boys. They need to see this building accomplished so they can understand what is expected of them in their lives. I know we cannot replace his father, but I know that we have no choice but to be vigilant with him and ensure that he grows up to be the father to his own son that he never had. That is our mission and we will not fail. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM PASTOR COREY BROOKS

title: Stop losing photo quality when you share pictures
description: iOS 27 finally lets iPhone Shared Albums store photos and videos at full resolution in iCloud, but new items count toward the owner's storage.
content: You take a great photo, send it to someone and then hear the question nobody wants to hear: "Why does this look blurry?" That can happen because some sharing methods resize or compress photos before they reach the other person. The image may still look fine on a phone screen, but zoom in or try to print it and the lost detail becomes easier to spot. With iOS 27, Apple is addressing one long-standing version of that problem. Shared Albums can now store newly added photos and videos in their original formats at full resolution. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones also have built-in ways to send photo files without relying on a messaging app that may shrink them along the way. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com. HOW TO SEARCH ANYTHING ON IPHONE, GALAXY AND PIXEL What changed with Shared Albums in iOS 27 Before iOS 27, Apple’s Shared Albums reduced photo resolution. Photos were generally limited to 2,048 pixels on the long edge, while videos could be delivered at resolutions up to 720p. Starting with iOS 27, newly shared photos and videos in the upgraded Shared Albums experience are stored in iCloud in their original formats at full resolution. That means newly shared photos can remain at their original resolution instead of being reduced to the limits used by older Shared Albums. There is one trade-off. New items added to an upgraded Shared Album count toward the album owner’s available iCloud storage, including items other participants add. Items that were already in the album before the upgrade do not count toward that storage, and temporary Shared Albums do not count either. How to turn on Shared Albums on iPhone First, make sure Shared Albums are enabled on your iPhone. On an iPhone running iOS 27: Apple requires iCloud Photos for the new Shared Albums experience in iOS 27. How to create a full-resolution Shared Album on iPhone Any new Shared Album you create in iOS 27 automatically uses Apple’s upgraded Shared Albums experience. To create one: Photos and videos you add to that new album are stored in their original formats at full resolution. You can also allow people to join through a link. Apple says friends and family can access and contribute to a shared album on the web even if they do not have an Apple Account or Apple device. YOUR PHONE CAN FIX BADLY FRAMED PHOTOS AFTER YOU TAKE THEM What if you already have an older Shared Album? Albums created before iOS 27 stay in the older format until you upgrade them. Apple lets the owner upgrade an existing Shared Album to the new experience. After the upgrade, newly added photos and videos can be stored at full resolution. That word "newly" is important. Upgrading an album does not restore the original resolution of photos or videos that were already uploaded under the older system. So, if you have an older family album or vacation album and want future additions preserved at full quality, upgrading it makes sense. How to save a full-resolution photo from a Shared Album If someone shares a photo through an upgraded Shared Album, you can save it to your own library. Apple says photos and videos in the new Shared Albums experience can be stored at full resolution in their original formats. However, content saved from a Shared Album may not include every piece of information contained in the original file. That means Shared Albums are much better for preserving image quality in iOS 27, but I would still keep the original file if you want the most complete archival copy. Why texting a photo can still reduce quality Shared Albums solve one specific problem, but they do not guarantee that every photo you send from an iPhone stays untouched. The method you choose still affects what the recipient gets. Messaging services can resize or recompress images depending on the service, connection and receiving device. We have previously covered how to send high-quality photos from an iPhone, including ways to get better results when sharing between iPhone and Android. If image quality is important, sending the actual file through a file-sharing tool is usually a safer choice than assuming a messaging app will preserve every pixel. How to send full-quality photos from a Samsung Galaxy Samsung Galaxy phones include Quick Share, which sends photos, videos and other files directly to nearby devices. Quick Share can send the original file without putting it through the kind of image compression you may encounter in some messaging apps. That makes it a good option when you want to preserve the quality of a photo. To send a photo with Quick Share: Depending on the receiving device, Galaxy users can also create a QR code through Quick Share, so the other person can connect and receive the file. 12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW How to send full-quality photos from a Google Pixel Pixel phones also use Quick Share for nearby file transfers. To send a photo: Quick Share can send photos, videos and other files directly to nearby Android devices, Chromebooks and supported Windows computers. You can also create a QR code if the receiving device does not appear right away. The other person scans the code to connect and receive the files. Android can now share with some Apple devices too Quick Share has become more useful if your household mixes Android and Apple devices. Google says Pixel 8a and later and certain supported Android phones can use Quick Share with compatible Apple devices through AirDrop. The iPhone, iPad or Mac user needs to set AirDrop to Everyone for 10 Minutes before the Android user sends the file. On Android: Devices that do not support the direct connection can still use Quick Share’s QR-code option. Google says those files are end-to-end encrypted and remain available for download for 24 hours. That can save you from emailing photos to yourself or putting them through a social app when you want to move the original file between platforms. Full resolution can use a lot more storage There is a reason photo-sharing services have compressed images for years. Full-resolution files take up more space. A smartphone photo can be several megabytes, while RAW images are much larger. High-resolution video can use hundreds of megabytes or more. In iOS 27, new photos and videos added to an upgraded Shared Album count toward the album owner’s iCloud storage. That includes new items other participants contribute. If you start creating large Shared Albums, check Settings > your name > iCloud from time to time so you know how much storage you have left. Do you always need the original-quality file? Probably not. If you are sending a quick snapshot to a friend, and they will only look at it on their phone, some compression may never be noticeable. Full quality becomes more useful when you plan to print a photo, crop into a small detail or keep an important image for years. The same thinking applies to video. A smaller copy may work fine for a quick message, while the original file makes more sense if you plan to edit it later or watch it on a larger screen. Choosing the right sharing method depends on what you plan to do with the file after it arrives. Kurt’s key takeaways I like this iOS 27 change because Shared Albums have always been convenient, but their old resolution limits could make them a poor place to keep the best version of an important photo. Full-resolution sharing removes that problem for newly added photos and videos. Galaxy and Pixel users already have a strong option with Quick Share when the goal is sending the actual file without routing it through a messaging app. When photo quality counts, pay attention to how you send the file. There is a storage cost to keeping everything at full resolution, especially with video. Still, for wedding photos or family memories you may want to print later, I would rather preserve the original detail and decide what to compress afterward. title: Judge Judy fires back at critics over America remarks: ‘It’s gonna take a lot more’ to shut me up
description: Judge Judy fired back at Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro after "The View" hosts sharply criticized her love-it-or-leave-it remarks about America.
content: EXCLUSIVE — Judge Judy Sheindlin responded to the furor caused by her love-it-or-leave-it remarks about America last month, explaining that she wasn’t calling America "perfect," but that the country is based on certain principles she is compelled to defend. "I have a house, and I have a home. I consider America my home," Sheindlin told USA Today in the now-viral interview exchange. "America has been good to me. I think that it’s the greatest country in the world." "If you don’t like this country, go somewhere else," she continued. "Don’t come to the greatest country in the world, the most successful country in the world, and say, ‘I want to change it.’ There are other countries that are the something else that you want. Go there. Go there. But don’t come into my home and say, ‘I want to change it.’" JUDGE JUDY SAYS THOSE WHO DON'T LIKE AMERICA SHOULD 'GO SOMEWHERE ELSE' ABC's "The View" dedicated a whole segment to Sheindlin’s take. While Sara Haines and Alyssa Farah Griffin came to her defense, Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro expressed disappointment with the judge’s words. Hostin even said she detected "selfishness" in her comments, arguing that they focused too much on individual success. She suggested that patriotism means fighting to make your country better for everyone. "I take umbrage with what she said, and I don’t like it at all," Navarro also said of Judge Judy’s remark, adding that it’s because she loves America that she feels she has "the duty and responsibility to call out the grift and the cruelty and the racism and the abuses of power and the anti-American actions that [Trump] is taking on." Sheindlin said she didn’t understand Hostin’s response. "If you listen to what I said, I was saying my country is America," she told Fox Digital. "Every American should feel that way. And America is my home. Everybody should feel that way. So, when I said ‘my,’ I wasn’t limiting it to myself." 'THE VIEW' CO-HOST ANA NAVARRO OFFERS ONE KEY REASON FOR WHY SHE STILL IDENTIFIES AS A REPUBLICAN Of Navarro, Sheindlin said she takes everything she says with "a grain of salt." "I accept criticism, and you can criticize my view, which was not that the country is perfect — and I did say in that interview that there’s nothing wrong with tweaking this country," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital of the backlash in general. "Everything can always be better. I mean, if you live in a house — which I compared America to — if you live in a house, the house could always be better. It could use a fresh coat of paint every once in a while. Sometimes it needs new carpeting. Sometimes it will need a new stove or refrigerator to keep it functioning optimally. You have to upgrade your television sets or else you won’t be able to get certain programming and high definition. That’s tweaking." But, she added, "There’s a difference between tweaking your house and burning it down." "And this country was founded on certain principles," she continued. "And where those principles are being tested and saying those are not the right principles. I mean, if you’re a capitalistic country, you’re not a socialistic country." MORE AMERICANS THAN EVER NOW HAVE A POSITIVE VIEW OF SOCIALISM, NEW POLL SAYS "The basis of this country is a capitalist country," she continued. "And when you say, ‘Well, we don’t want capitalism anymore, we want socialism,’ that’s where I draw the line. Because then you are fiddling around with what this country is about." Socialism, she said, is not popular with the vast majority of Americans, musing that most people agreed with her statement. "The very vocal minority won’t address the statement," she said. "They try to shut you up by giving you a negative name, by calling you names which they hope will lead you to shut up. Not responding to the message and saying, ‘Judy, I understand what you’re saying, but not everyone comes from a background where they see their life being fulfilled in this country… so that everyone has potential to reach the American Dream.’" That’s an argument that Sheindlin said she understands. "But to call me a name because I said this is a great country and tweak it, but don’t burn the house down?" she asked. "It’s gonna take a lot more than Ana Navarro to shut me up," she added. Fox News Digital has reached out to "The View" for comment. JUDGE ADAM LEVY PREVIEWS HIS ‘NITTY-GRITTY’ NEW SHOW – AND HOW HIS STYLE COMPARES TO HIS MOM JUDGE JUDY "It’s one of the sad things about this internet, which has the capacity to do so many good things and join people together," Sheindlin said. "It has allowed some people, either anonymously or overtly, to be mean-spirited." Sheindlin’s special, "Judge Judy: Unfiltered, Unforgettable," aired on CBS in late September. "I think that the people who are fans over the years sort of got to know that what you see is what you get," she said. "The naysayers probably would not watch. If you’re not somebody’s cup of tea … I can skip it. I think that fans who watched the special and have been following me over the last 25 years or 30 years or newcomers for less time, I believe that they know who I am." I don’t order my family around like that the same way," she laughed. The original "Judge Judy" premiered in 1996 and ran for 25 seasons before ending in 2021. Sheindlin later launched "Judy Justice," which concluded in October. She said she was proud of the work her son, Judge Adam Levy, was doing on "Adam's Law" now that he's taken the reins of the family's TV courtroom career after Sheindlin announced she's "rewiring" her career. "I think he’s certainly smart, and he certainly works very hard at each case," Sheindlin said. "Actually, he works much harder than I did. I think he’s doing a great job and the ratings are backing him up. And I think he’s got an exciting energy and an honorable person, which is what you need behind the bench."

title: One state is ground zero as Trump's multibillion-dollar tech ambitions face a midterm test
description: Voters across eight states will decide 34 data center ballot measures this November as America's AI boom becomes a growing political flash point.
content: Ohio has emerged as ground zero in the growing political fight over the massive data centers powering America's AI boom, with voters across the state set to weigh in on the industry's rapid expansion this November. Voters will decide 20 data center-related ballot measures across 17 Ohio jurisdictions — more than half of the 34 measures appearing on ballots nationwide — putting the battleground state at the center of a debate over the sprawling facilities' impact on power, water and local communities. The fight is also colliding with Ohio's closely watched Senate race, where data centers have become a campaign issue as President Donald Trump pushes the multibillion-dollar buildout as critical to keeping the U.S. ahead in the global race for artificial intelligence power. Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, led the Senate push to pass the Ratepayer Protection Act, which would make data centers pay for the power and infrastructure they require rather than pushing it off to American taxpayers. This effort further underscored the importance of the scale of the issue in Ohio ahead of the midterm elections. 8 EVERYDAY THINGS THAT WOULD QUIT WORKING WITHOUT DATA CENTERS Democratic Senate challenger Sherrod Brown — who served as a senator in Ohio from 2007 to 2025 — has attacked Husted over data center development, and Trump has defended the Republican's stance while campaigning for him. "Look, there’s so much money to be made for Ohio, you can’t just turn them off," the president said. Across the country, voters will decide 34 data center-related ballot measures in seven states — California, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Nevada, Ohio and Wisconsin — as the once-obscure infrastructure behind America's AI ambitions becomes an increasingly potent political issue. A Fox News national poll conducted last month found voters struggling to reconcile AI’s potential benefits with the economic and environmental costs of the data centers that power the technology. More than seven in 10 voters (71%) opposed building AI data centers in their area, including 46% who strongly opposed them. More than half (52%) supported building them in remote locations, while 44% opposed. AI IS SUPERCHARGING POLITICAL AD WARS. BUT VIRAL DOESN’T MEAN VICTORIOUS Overall, 60% of voters had a negative view of AI, compared with 37% who viewed it positively. That 23-point gap has more than doubled since a July Fox News poll. The Fox News poll also found a partisan divide over AI and data centers. Voters with favorable views of AI leaned Republican, while those with unfavorable views leaned Democratic. The divide was even sharper over data centers, with Republicans performing better among voters who supported them and Democrats among those who opposed them. That partisan split comes as AI policy emerges as a growing fault line in Washington and on the campaign trail. Trump has opposed wide-ranging federal regulation of the AI industry and warned that the U.S. cannot allow China to win the technology race. ‘BACKWARDS AND POOR’: TRUMP SLAMS COMMUNITIES BLOCKING DATA CENTERS But as the midterms approach, the debate over AI and the data centers powering it is playing out in races across the country. In Texas, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, who previously courted major tech investments, recently ordered a pause on data center permitting and grid connections pending an audit. Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa has supported temporary moratoriums. content: Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers.
