title: US soldiers can't be protected from all bioweapons, Army admits amid troubling surge in threats
description: The U.S. Army's new biodefense plan integrates biological warfare scenarios into combat training as AI and biotechnology raise concerns about threats.
content: The U.S. Army unveiled its plan to prepare soldiers to fight through biological attacks rather than assume every threat can be stopped. The newly signed plan bringing biological warfare scenarios into routine combat training as artificial intelligence (AI) and biotechnology raise new concerns about the weapons America's adversaries could develop in the near future. "Can we protect every soldier from every possible bio threat? Probably not," Dr. Alison Tamasi, a senior official at the Army's Nuclear and Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Agency, told reporters on Monday. "We can't put them in a bubble," she added. The shift comes as U.S. officials continue to assess whether Moscow maintains an offensive biological weapons program after a mysterious death in Russia was linked to an anti-plague facility — reviving questions of biological safety and transparency. CHINESE AI MODEL INVESTIGATED AFTER RESEARCHER SAYS IT PROVIDED INSTRUCTIONS FOR BIOWEAPONS, ASSASSINATIONS Still, the Army hopes their implemented plan will help prepare the force to deploy and fight in biologically contested environments by 2035. Rather than treating outbreaks primarily as medical emergencies, the military wants commanders, intelligence officers and logistics personnel to prepare for biological threats while continuing to carry out their combat missions. EMERGING TECH HAS NEW ARMY LEADERS WARNING TROOPS CAN'T ‘AI’ THEIR WAY TO VICTORY ON THE BATTLEFIELD One of the biggest changes will be bringing biological incidents into major Army combat exercises, forcing commanders to respond to potential outbreaks while continuing their other missions. Rather than relying on specialized biological exercises, the Army wants troops across different military functions to confront biological threats as part of their regular training. Tamasi described one scenario involving a simulated norovirus outbreak at a military port. While medical personnel worked to contain the outbreak, logistics officers would have to determine how to keep critical supplies moving. The example illustrates a broader shift in the Army's approach: Biological threats are no longer being treated solely as medical problems but as potential disruptions to military operations that commanders must be prepared to manage. "We need to make sure that doctrine is aligned," Tamasi said, explaining that the Army is working to establish how biodefense readiness should be assessed across the force. The new plan, signed last week, puts into motion the Army's updated biodefense strategy released in September, which sets a goal of preparing soldiers to deploy and fight in biologically contested environments by 2035. The first two-year implementation cycle will focus on establishing policies, improving coordination across Army organizations and developing personnel with specialized biological expertise. More advanced technologies and acquisition efforts are expected in later phases. The effort comes amid growing concerns about the potential for artificial intelligence and biotechnology to accelerate the development of biological threats. PLAGUE MYSTERY REVIVES CONCERNS OVER NOT-TO-SECRET RUSSIAN BIOWEAPONS PROGRAM Tamasi described those advances as a dual-use challenge, with technologies that can accelerate medical discoveries also potentially enabling new biological threats to emerge more quickly. Russia remains a particular concern for U.S. national security officials. Washington has long assessed that Moscow maintains an offensive biological weapons program inherited from the Soviet Union, despite Russia's obligations under the Biological Weapons Convention. The United States renounced offensive biological weapons in 1969 and is also a party to the convention, which prohibits the development, production and stockpiling of biological weapons. US, WHO REQUEST DETAILS FROM RUSSIA AMID REPORTS OF SECOND PNEUMONIA CASE Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia, died Oct. 2 after developing severe pneumonia. Russian media initially reported a possible pneumonic plague infection following a suspected laboratory accident, but Russian authorities denied that an accident occurred and said testing found no evidence of plague or other high-threat pathogens. The cause of her death remains undetermined. In an Oct. 10 update, the World Health Organization said it had found no evidence of ongoing transmission linked to the case, while noting that a confirmed diagnosis was still lacking. Asked how much Russia's biological weapons activities informed the Army's planning, Tamasi said the strategy was based on "intelligence writ large" rather than any single adversary. "It's not solely focused on a particular threat actor," she said. Asked what lessons the Army had drawn from Russia's biological weapons program, Tamasi said the strategy was designed to address biological threats regardless of their origin — whether accidental, deliberate or ultimately determined not to pose the threat initially feared. For Army commanders, she explained, the immediate priority is responding to a potential biological threat and maintaining operations, rather than determining its origin. Questions of attribution would involve the broader U.S. government. That approach also informs how the Army intends to detect emerging threats. Officials said the military is working to draw together information from environmental monitoring, medical facilities and intelligence reporting to identify potential biological incidents earlier. That could include wastewater surveillance similar to monitoring used during the COVID-19 pandemic, Tamasi said. The goal is to give commanders a more complete picture of potential biological threats so they can respond before disruptions spread. The COVID-19 pandemic also exposed the limitations of treating biological threats primarily as public health emergencies, according to Army officials, reinforcing the need for military leaders outside the medical field to incorporate those risks into operational planning. The strategy addresses misinformation as another operational challenge, particularly when troops and commanders must make decisions about vaccines, protective measures and communications during a biological incident. The Army has also begun rolling out biodefense seminars for senior leaders. Tamasi said one three-star board determined that senior Army leaders should receive at least an hour of instruction on biodefense and the "ground truth" surrounding biological threats. Ultimately, the Army hopes that preparing soldiers to continue their missions despite a biological attack could also discourage adversaries from using such weapons in the first place. title: Three NFL teams roasted for celebrating Indigenous Peoples' Day on Columbus Day, which no team even mentioned
description: No NFL team recognized Christopher Columbus on social media for the federal holiday, while three teams honored Indigenous Peoples' Day instead.
content: Christopher Columbus gets absolutely no love from the NFL. It's fair to believe that because on the federal holiday honoring Christopher Columbus and his place in American history, not one NFL team nor the league itself recognized Columbus Day on social media. It's at least the second consecutive year that no NFL team mentioned Columbus Day even as non-essential federal offices, federal courts, mail delivery, most traditional banks and the U.S. bond market closed in recognition of the holiday. JUNETEENTH WAS CELEBRATED ACROSS MAJOR PROFESSIONAL SPORTS LEAGUES AND TEAMS — WITH TWO NOTABLE EXCEPTIONS And this is starting to feel like a statement for two reasons: First, three teams picked the day to instead recognize Indigenous Peoples' Day, which is not an official federal holiday, while ignoring the guy whose 1492 landing in America marks the federally recognized holiday. THE NFL'S MAIN SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS REMAINED SILENT ABOUT PRIDE MONTH ON ITS FIRST DAY Second, 29 teams that typically take the opportunity to celebrate just about any other holiday and some days that aren't holidays at all decided to go dark on this holiday altogether. That suggests teams recognize the day has become something of a political hot potato. And the NFL and most of its teams have decided not to get burned. MARIACHI BAND'S NATIONAL ANTHEM AT BEARS VS. EAGLES GAME IGNITES RACISM DEBATE AND US SENATOR RESPONSE That didn't apply to the Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs and Los Angeles Rams. All three paid tribute to Indigenous Peoples' Day on their social media. But that shout out came at a cost because the replies to each post came with significant backlash. COMMANDERS PLAN TO ADD FAMOUS SPEAR LOGO TO HELMETS WHILE NOT ADMITTING ITS OBVIOUS NOD TO REDSKINS HISTORY All three teams that posted about Indigenous Peoples' Day were met with immediate corrections in their replies calling it Columbus Day. And, frankly, that was too easy. But there were other clever replies, particularly on the Vikings' account, because it didn't escape notice that the team is nicknamed for White, conquering outsiders. "Vikings were known for pillaging, raping, slaughtering, burning and enslaving their victims," one fan replied on the Minnesota post. "They terrorized innocent people in coastal communities including monasteries for centuries, even killed and enslaved women and children on a large scale. "Better change your name, too." The post ended with a clown face emoji. The Chiefs honored Indigenous Peoples' Day to "show our gratitude for the work the America Indian Community Working Group puts in to make sure we remain educated and honor tribes with historic connection to our region." Cool, except Native Americans are not an echo chamber block of people with just one opinion. "I'm partial Cherokee Indian and offended you're not calling it Columbus Day," one fan replied. The Rams played on Monday, but before that, they posted their salute to Indigenous Peoples' Day. The team, located in a liberal city and state, received significant pushback. "Christopher Columbus," one fan posted, "The only immigrant liberals hate." Can you understand why a vast majority of teams avoided the holiday and issues surrounding it altogether? President Donald Trump, meanwhile, recently issued a Columbus Day 2026 proclamation that calls Columbus "a legend whose vision, fortitude, and perseverance unleashed a dynamic of history that led to the creation of the greatest, freest, and most just nation in history." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! There are probably people who believe this political football paints Republicans who promote Columbus Day as racists and Democrats who promote Indigenous Peoples' Day as enlightened. Except the Indian Removal Act of 1830, which led to the forced relocation of approximately 100,000 Native Americans, including during the Cherokee Trail of Tears, was signed by Andrew Jackson – a Democrat. And Columbus Day was established in 1934 by President Franklin D. Roosevelt to celebrate the arrival of Columbus in the Americas on Oct. 12, 1492. Roosevelt was also a Democrat. title: Trump denounces Houthi attacks after Saudi crown prince call as coalition intercepts missiles
description: President Donald Trump says Houthis are "misbehaving very badly" as the Saudi-led coalition intercepts three ballistic missiles launched by the Iran-backed group toward Riyadh and Khamis Mushait.
content:
Houthis / Yemen / Osamah Yahya/picture alliance via Getty Images / REUTERS/Khaled Abdullah
Houthi rebels threatened a "swift and painful" response against U.S. interests across the Middle East on Monday if President Donald Trump joins Saudi military strikes against the group, AFP reported.
"If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region," Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told the European news agency.
Bukhaiti also warned "all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets".
The threats followed the group's deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which killed at least 13 people and wounded hundreds more.
Trump condemned the Riyadh attack Monday, stating it was unacceptable.
"The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. They're misbehaving very badly. No good," the president told reporters at the White House.
President Donald Trump and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman / Getty Images
Trump, who described the airport attack as "not acceptable," also confirmed that he had spoken with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
Meanwhile, explosions were again reported over Riyadh on Monday night, with the Saudi-led coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile. The Houthis claimed another attack on the airport.

title: Trump's new press secretary faces first major test as White House briefing room enters new era
description: Katie Zacharia makes her White House press briefing room debut Tuesday, ending a weekslong stretch without a permanent press secretary at the podium.
content: The White House is set to end a weekslong stretch without a permanent press secretary at the podium Tuesday when Katie Zacharia makes her briefing room debut, succeeding Karoline Leavitt after a shake-up in President Donald Trump's communications team. Zacharia, an attorney and television commentator, served as senior communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the president's social media platform, Truth Social. Her appointment follows Leavitt's departure from the White House in August. During his first administration, President Donald Trump had four White House press secretaries: Sean Spicer, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Stephanie Grisham and Kayleigh McEnany. TRUMP NAMES LEAVITT SUCCESSOR AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION — AND SHE'S NO STRANGER TO MAGA Leavitt served as the first press secretary of Trump’s second administration for 19 months before leaving the role on Aug. 27. "The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day," she wrote. "I look forward to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out," she added. title: Want to dodge the flu this year? Eat these secret-weapon immunity-boosting foods
description: Nutrition experts reveal the best immunity-boosting foods for flu season, from fermented foods and fiber-rich beans to vitamin C-packed produce.
content: As flu season heightens, it's important to prioritize immune system support, which includes eating a balanced diet of nutrient-dense foods, experts say. The immune system is directly connected to the gut, so consuming the right nutrients can positively affect both. "If we're not getting enough fiber, fermented foods or the right nutrients, we can get that imbalance in the gut environment, and that's going to impact the immune system," New Jersey-based registered dietitian Erin Palinski-Wade told Fox News Digital. NEW WAYS TO PREVENT FLU REVEALED IN 'ACCIDENTAL' LAB BREAKTHROUGH, STUDY FINDS There were an estimated 51 million flu-related illnesses during the 2024-25 flu season, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). There are plenty of foods and beverages that support the immune system and may help protect against illness. "Eat the rainbow, especially when it comes to produce," Palinski-Wade said. "So those bright colors, things like bell peppers, kiwis, citrus fruits, broccoli, they're all an excellent source of vitamin C," plus a wide range of other nutrients. NUTRITION EXPERTS RANK THE 5 HEALTHIEST NUTS AND THE ONE THAT STANDS ABOVE THE REST Aside from fruits and vegetables, it's beneficial to eat fermented foods like yogurt, kefir and sauerkraut because they help support the gut microbiome, according to Palinski-Wade. Fiber also plays a big role in supporting gut health and the immune system, she noted, adding that beans, nuts and seeds are great options for increasing fiber intake. Only 6% of American adults consume enough fiber daily, according to a report published in September by the American College of Cardiology. Make sure to get enough protein and zinc, Palinski-Wade added, "because these are really the building blocks our body needs to build the immune cells." She listed lean meats, shellfish, eggs, pumpkin seeds and chickpeas as good sources of protein and zinc. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Lauren Manaker, a South Carolina-based registered dietitian, touted dairy milk as an immune-supporting beverage due to its vitamins and hydrating benefits. "Several of the essential micronutrients found in milk, including vitamin A, vitamin D, zinc and selenium, support a healthy immune system," Manaker told Fox News Digital. A common misconception is that milk increases mucus and phlegm production and, therefore, should be avoided during a cold. There's little scientific evidence to support that theory, although one reason people might associate dairy with higher mucus production is the sensation it causes when consumed, according to the Mayo Clinic. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "When you take milk products, and you mix them with saliva, it can feel like a thicker coating in your throat, and that's why you can feel like you have more phlegm or more mucus," Palinski-Wade said. "It doesn't really mean you're producing more, but it can make you feel that way." Those who are lactose intolerant can opt for lactose-free milk, "because it offers the same key nutrients as regular dairy milk, just without the lactose," Manaker noted. Hydration is crucial for immune support, as well. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "The hydration helps you feel your best, but what's also interesting about hydration is it keeps your airways moist, and that's actually part of your body's first line of defense against catching a cold or a flu," Palinski-Wade said, suggesting people sip on water, broth, green tea and ginger tea. Getting adequate sleep, managing stress and being physically active are also important for maintaining a healthy immune system, Manaker added. Regarding supplements, Manaker said they can be helpful for people struggling to meet all of their nutrient needs through food alone. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP However, it's best to ask a healthcare provider for guidance and to be thoughtful about dosages, "because more is not always better," she said.

title: Scammers are stealing checks from the mail. Here’s how to protect yours
description: Check fraud doubled from 2021 to 2023 as postal inspectors recover over $1 billion in counterfeit checks yearly. Here's how to protect payments.
content: You try to use your credit card to make a purchase and are told it has been declined. In a panic, you call your credit card company, which informs you that they never received your last payment. "That’s impossible," you exclaim, knowing you sent in the payment weeks ago. You go to check other recently paid bills to find out that several others, including your housing association fees and insurance payments, weren’t received. You head to your bank, only to find out that the checks have been "washed" — that is, fished out of the mail, ink lifted and re-made out to other people. This exact scam happened to one of my family members, and per the U.S. Postal Service, these scams are surging, with Postal Inspectors recovering "more than $1 billion in counterfeit checks and money orders every year." The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network has said that check fraud doubled from 2021 to 2023! 6 IN 10 IDENTITY CRIMES NOW BEGIN WITH A NEW ACCOUNT My family member thought she did everything right. She avoided online payments so she wouldn’t be subject to online payment scams. The checks were dropped off at the local post office in a box right outside the facility. But still, she ended up being scammed (which fortunately, with the help of her bank, she wasn’t liable for the clearly stolen funds). So, even if the mail isn’t safe, how can you protect yourself? First, use a special pen. Check washing uses a chemical process to remove the ink. Using a gel pen can make this process more difficult for criminals to do. Also, pressing hard when writing can make it more difficult to erase. However, this is not a foolproof plan either, as many authorities are noting that scammers are now using technology to scan the checks with your signature and reproduce fake copies using their computers. So, the pens can help as a deterrent, but aren’t 100% safe, either. Consider paying in person If you have the ability to do so, pay your bills in person. For example, pay your credit card at a local associated branch of the company. Pay your property taxes at the city’s offices. Of course, it’s less convenient, but a lot more secure. You can also consider paying online, but this opens you up to online scams, so make sure you do so safely, using best practices. If you choose to use the mail, drop it off inside the post office. Don’t use mailboxes. Yes, it’s less convenient, but even the boxes owned by the government are targeted by scammers, so physically go into the post office to drop off your mail. As a bonus tip, guard your mail at home. Get your mail frequently so that scammers can’t pull information from your mailbox. If you plan to travel, put a free hold on your mail delivery with the post office while you are away. Monitor your payment status regularly. 9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE Acting quickly can help to make sure you recover any misappropriated funds. Designate a day a week to be "bill day" and make sure all your bills have been paid, and the payments have gone through as expected. If any payment is taking too long to process, look into it immediately. Contact your financial institution to help you through this process. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Scammers are rampant and looking for every edge to defraud hard-working Americans. Be diligent, even when you are doing something as routine as mailing a check.

title: Booker ‘wowed’ by GOP challenger’s blunt message to Trump
description: Justin Murphy told Trump to "finish it" on Iran, drawing applause and a stunned reaction from Cory Booker during their New Jersey Senate debate.
content: Sen. Cory Booker’s Republican Senate challenger had a blunt message for President Donald Trump about the war in Iran during the pair’s recent debate: "Finish it." The advice drew applause during Thursday's forum — and a "Wow" from Booker, who then blasted former Tabernacle Deputy Mayor Justin Murphy's remarks as the kind of "Yahoo" foreign policy that has dragged the United States into costly wars in the Middle East. New Jersey is a blue state that has trended redder in recent years, with President Donald Trump flipping key areas in 2024. However, 1972 was the last time a Republican won a U.S. Senate election in the state, when Sen. Clifford Case was re-elected. Sens. Nick Brady in 1982 and Jeff Chiesa in 2013 later served brief, appointed terms. Murphy, an attorney from the Pine Barrens, earned loud applause for his response to a question about Iran when asked what he would tell Trump if the president called him for advice on the conflict. "Finish that war in a positive manner," Murphy replied firmly. "We can't wait halfway through and decide we don't want to do this anymore. The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is a radical terrorist organization that has deprived the Iranian people, the Persian people, of their history and of a decent life." ‘FINISH THE DAMN JOB’: HAGERTY TELLS 'RUTHLESS PODCAST' THAT TRUMP WILL COMPLETE IRAN MISSION The exchange highlighted the candidates' opposing approaches to the conflict, with Murphy defending Trump's military campaign and Booker warning against another prolonged American war in the Middle East. As Murphy continued, the broadcast's split-screen showed Booker briefly looking down and shaking his head before pursing his lips for the rest of Murphy’s response and raising his eyebrows at one point. LAWMAKER’S STUNNED FACE AND OTHER VIRAL MOMENTS CAP ROUGH WEEK FOR POLITICAL CLASS "Four decades is enough. The Iranian people have suffered enough," Murphy began to conclude. "And I would say, ‘Mr. President, put your cowboy hat on and get out there and kick some a--, and get this done and done right’," Murphy said. "Wow," Booker mouthed as moderator David Wildstein gestured toward the Democrat and said it appeared he wanted to respond. BOOKER SLAMS TRUMP’S IRAN DEAL AS AN 'ABJECT SURRENDER,' LABELS HIM THE 'BIGGEST LOSER' WITH 'EGG ON HIS FACE' "Honestly," Booker began. "This is the kind of ‘Yahoo’ foreign policy that has mired us in Middle East war after Middle East war — with false bravado leaders saying we're just going to go in there and kick ass. Well, you know what that's done to the treasury of our country?" Booker replied. When asked the same question as Murphy, Booker joked that Wildstein was asking him about "a guy calling me for advice who has literally said ‘I know more than my generals’." But the former Newark mayor entertained the hypothetical, saying he and the rest of New Jersey have known Trump for years because he "bankrupted our casinos" — referring to the president’s former Atlantic City casino businesses. He accused Trump of frequently ignoring advice, claiming advisers had to "jangle keys" to keep him on topic during a meeting about the trans-Hudson rail tunnel project spearheaded by Booker and Sen. Charles Schumer, D-N.Y. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Murphy also received attention for his comments during the debate on illegal immigration. He recounted leaving a campaign event in Washington, N.J., and looking across at a home where a child was allegedly abducted and raped by Guatemalan illegal immigrant Lester Noe Perez-Amador — whom the Biden administration previously released after a Texas county notified ICE that it had taken him into custody, according to WRNJ. title: Media narrative predicting blue wave in key battleground state not meshing with local Republicans: 'Fired up'
description: Iowa Republicans in Scott County push back on "blue wave" predictions, citing voter optimism and concerns about Democratic spending ahead of midterms.
content: DAVENPORT, Iowa — As Iowa emerges as one of the most critical states in the midterm election in both House and Senate races, Fox News Digital spoke with local Republican candidates about what the media is getting right and wrong on the ground in the Hawkeye State. As local conservatives gathered at a Scott County Republican Party event near downtown Davenport in early October to watch the first gubernatorial debate, a month out from the consequential midterm election, Fox News Digital was there asking if the media narrative was accurate that Iowa was primed for a "blue wave" amid concerns about President Donald Trump’s economy, gas prices, and the war in Iran. Greg Guy, running as a Republican for treasurer in Scott County, acknowledged that Iowans are "concerned" about the price of gas, but believes they understand that the surge in cost is likely temporary after the war in Iran winds down. "Surprisingly not," Guy said when asked if he thinks a blue wave is imminent in Iowa based on the reactions he gets when he knocks on doors in the county telling voters about his campaign, which he says is focused on doing "what’s right" and "taking care" of the community. DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT "My neighbor is one of the big people in charge of the canvassing for the Democrat Party. I don't see where they're excited to vote," Guy said. "I mean, if I talk to a hundred doors and 30 to 40% will open up, I might get one out of 40. That's a hater, and then I'll just tell them, hey, I know you're not going to vote for me, but when I'm treasurer, and you have a problem, you can still call me. They don't know what to do because they're wound up in the hate. But otherwise, I don't think there's a whole lot of belief that the Democrat Party can do anything to fix our economy." Davenport, a town of about 100,000 people in southeast Iowa along the banks of the Mississippi River, stands out as a Democratic-leaning urban pocket in an increasingly Republican Iowa. President Trump carried Scott County by roughly four points in 2024, 51% to 47%, but former Vice President Kamala Harris won Davenport’s congressional district precincts overall, reflecting the city’s more competitive and complex political profile. Trump won Iowa by about 13 points in 2024, and Republicans control the governor’s office and both chambers of the state legislature. But Scott County’s mix of urban Democrats, suburban swing voters and conservative rural communities makes it a key test of whether the GOP’s statewide strength can overcome Democratic resilience in eastern Iowa. One of the critical questions is whether conservative Iowans are frustrated enough with Republicans to vote Democrats back into power. "No, not at all," Cynthia Mensendick, a registered nurse running for election to the Iowa State Senate to represent District 49, said when asked if voters think handing Democrats control of Congress is the "right answer." "The concern is that there will be a Democrat governor because if you look at any state where a Democrat takes over, they immediately increase spending," Mensendick said, adding, "I’m not seeing that," when asked if a "blue wave" was set to occur in Iowa this November. Mensendick, who is running a campaign focused on healthcare and the high cancer rate in Iowa, says one of the top concerns with Republican voters is Iowa turning into Illinois if Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand is elected. FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: THE BIGGEST SURPRISES COME AFTER OCTOBER Republicans are facing an uphill battle in Iowa, where polling shows Democrats have gained momentum in the gubernatorial, Senate and congressional races. Additionally, Republicans are going up against historical headwinds as the party in power heading into the midterms. However, Iowa has shifted more red in recent years, and the Republicans in the room in Scott County remained optimistic. Dillon Fillion, the youngest candidate in Scott County history at 22 years old, told Fox News Digital that Republicans in Iowa and nationwide have a choice between two very different parties at the end of the day. "I think people have got to weigh the options here, they either have an option of voting for socialist candidates like Abdul El-Sayed, who is a pronounced communist and supports all the things that Lenin supports, which led the Soviet Union into the downfall that it went to, or they have the support of supporting Republicans who were actually serious about cutting their taxes, which cut their taxes in 2025 with the One Big Beautiful Bill," Fillion, running for the Iowa House of Representatives in District 81, said. "And Democrats will continue to lie about that, but again, the Democrats also voted to raise their taxes 60% in 2025, voting against the Big Beautiful Bill." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kurt Whalen isn’t running for office, but rather serves as the Scott County Iowa GOP Vice Chair, and he told Fox News Digital that while there are many frustrations with the state of affairs from Republicans in the state, he doesn’t think GOP voters will sit on the sidelines with so much at stake. "I think people are still fired up for the Republican cause. I mean, we are a big tent party. There's people that absolutely love Trump, there’s people that don’t care for him. But the reality is, Trump's been an overwhelming force for good in our country," Whalen said. "So, we can haggle about specifics, but I really think the Republican Party will ultimately come home and certainly support the president, and I would certainly encourage them to do that because what other choice do we have? I mean, the other choice is straight up, communist, Marxist, DSA, mask mandates. The Democratic Party in general, if you look at it historically, it has always been for big government against the little guy."

title: LIZ PEEK: Two troubled Senate races could spoil Democrats' blue-wave fantasy
description: James Talarico and Abdul El-Sayed face tightening senate races as past comments and shifting positions give Republican opponents new ammunition.
content: The midterm elections are three weeks away. In some states, voting has already begun. Betting site Kalshi shows odds of 61% that Democrats will win control of the Senate. Recent developments in the Texas and Michigan races suggest keeping your money in your pocket. As voters find out more about front-runner Democrats James Talarico in Texas and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, the polls are tightening. They say intimacy breeds contempt; nowhere is this truer than in politics. KEN PAXTON CALLS OUT JAMES TALARICO'S 11-DAY ABSENCE AT TRUMP RALLY, PROMPTING RESPONSE FROM CAMPAIGN Talarico is the 2026 version of 2018 Senate wannabe Beto O’Rourke, who memorably live-streamed his teeth-cleaning as a campaign stunt, but ultimately lost to Republican Ted Cruz despite his laudable dental hygiene. Talarico, a photogenic 37-year-old state representative, recently vanished from public view for nearly two weeks, an extraordinary absence so close to Election Day. He says he had the flu; does he not know about Theraflu? Has he heard of Zoom? His disappearance gave rise to a whirlwind of apparently erroneous rumors. Because Talarico has voiced some wacky ideas in the past, like believing there are six genders or that God is non-binary — which he has been forced to walk back — some voters are primed to believe such rumors. 'FAKE' MODERATE TALARICO'S TEXAS SURGE TESTS PAXTON IN FIGHT TO HOLD CRUCIAL GOP SENATE SEAT Ken Paxton, the state’s attorney general, is an unpopular candidate and carries considerable baggage, but his well-funded campaign is running ads showing Talarico making incendiary comments like, "I always think of myself as a Christian who hates Christianity." Talarico has also been outed as having previously voted as a state representative against bans on biological men playing in women’s sports. Oops. Beto O’Rourke lost in part because he embraced aggressive gun control in a state where most people have a gun. In 2022, Talarico appeared with the Texas Humane Legislation Network, warning of the "existential" need to "reduce our meat consumption," in a state that prides itself on its cattle. Undoubtedly, Talarico’s progressive young base will not be deterred by his peculiar walk-about, but his lengthy absence from the campaign trail casts a cloud over his run. Some polls show him barely leading Ken Paxton; a recent UMass Lowell/YouGov poll shows the candidates tied, with 7% undecided. As Trump rallies to energize his still-faithful base, it’s hard to imagine Talarico pulling out the win. FOX NEWS POLL: MICHIGAN VOTERS SPLIT BETWEEN EL-SAYED AND ROGERS Abdul El-Sayed, who calls himself a doctor, but is not legally authorized to practice medicine, has been changing positions as frequently as people change their underwear. One of the central planks in his platform has been his enthusiastic endorsement of Medicare for All. In a podcast from 2020, he says Medicare for All "does away with the private insurance market." Nowadays, his campaign website says: "Medicare for All does not have to ban additional private insurance through unions or employers, although Medicare for All should make those choices redundant and unnecessary." Moreover, during his primary race in January, El-Sayed explained, "If you like your insurance from your employer or from your union, that can still be there for you." That sounds a lot like President Obama telling gullible voters: "If you like your healthcare plan, you’ll be able to keep your healthcare plan, period." After millions of Americans saw their plans cancelled, Politifact dubbed that whopper the 2013 Lie of the Year. Why the reversal from El-Sayed on his signature issue? First, unions. Organized labor has done a bang-up job of demanding expensive healthcare benefits for workers — benefits that are undoubtedly more generous than any that would be provided by Uncle Sam. There are half a million union members in the Wolverine State; he needs their vote, ideals be damned. Second, those pesky taxes. El-Sayed has had to explain how he intends to pay for government-run healthcare. A writer at The Bridge, a nonpartisan news organization in Michigan, notes that "In 2020, the nonpartisan Urban Institute estimated that U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders’ version of Medicare for All would cost the federal government $34 trillion over a 10-year period." Experts say that money to fund such a program would rope in not just the wealthy, but middle-class families as well. In short, Medicare for All would mean higher taxes for all. El-Sayed has admitted as much in the past. El-Sayed positions himself as a healthcare expert, given his role in local county offices, but those stints were arguably brief and inconsequential. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Also troubling is El-Sayed’s association with anti-American Muslim organizations and personalities whom he has refused to denounce, like supporter Hasan Piker. On "Meet the Press" recently, El-Sayed claimed that neither he nor any family members have ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, a group deemed a terror outfit by the UAE, Saudi Arabia and by Egypt. But the candidate’s half-sister, an assistant professor at the University of Chicago, stated the opposite, claiming on social media years ago that her family "has long been" members of the Muslim Brotherhood and that some relatives had been "jailed" because of their association with the group. El-Sayed is also facing scrutiny for claiming dual citizenship with Egypt and the U.S. in the past, an assertion he now denies. El-Sayed told a Detroit GlobeMed conference in 2016, "I carry dual citizenship, and I grew up spending most of my summers in another country …" He made the same claim on his academic resume. Was he lying then, or is he lying now? Also, recently, asked during a debate whether El-Sayed considers Iran, the world’s biggest sponsor of terror, or Israel a bigger threat to the United States, the progressive anti-Israel candidate refused to answer. For many, his equivocation is disqualifying. title: ELI STEELE: NYC ICE shooting exposes how White guilt erases personal responsibility
description: The Oscar Belgal ICE shooting in Marble Hill, New York, has sparked a national debate over White guilt, individual responsibility, and immigrant accountability.
content: Editor's note: Eli Steele's latest film "White Guilt" was released on Oct. 6. Find out more here. School had just let out in Marble Hill, a small enclave of Manhattan bordering the Bronx. It was a little after 4 p.m. on Oct. 8 when Oscar Belgal, 28, picked up his 5-year-old son and began backing his Honda CR-V into a parking spot on a crowded street. A police camera caught what happened next. Two men dressed in plain clothes approached Belgal’s SUV with their guns drawn — one to the driver’s side, the other to the front. They were ICE officers. More agents were part of the operation, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani later noted that officers surrounding the vehicle wore construction vests and masks. Belgal responded by pulling the SUV forward out of the space. As he did, one officer punched and broke the driver’s window, but Belgal managed to drive off and out of the camera’s view. FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS DEPORTATION OF DOMINICAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE DURING NYC ARREST ATTEMPT The ICE officers caught up with Belgal about a block away. According to ICE officials, Belgal refused orders to exit the vehicle, turned his SUV into a weapon and rammed two government cars. Belgal's defense attorney disputes this account, maintaining that Belgal fled out of panic to protect his child from unidentified, armed men. Initial NYPD street camera footage did not capture the moment of the shooting, but investigators later determined that a bullet went through Belgal's windshield. At least one officer fired seven rounds, striking Belgal in the neck below his left ear. His son, sitting in the back seat, was not physically hurt. The FBI, Homeland Security investigators and the Bronx District Attorney’s office have all launched inquiries into the shooting. MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION' But there is a second story here, one that reveals where we are as a nation. Within hours of the shooting, Oscar Belgal was no longer a man, an individual. He became a symbol. And the people who made him into a symbol did so by taking away the very thing that makes a man a man: responsibility for what he does. First, Belgal was not a stranger to the justice system. In 2023, according to a criminal complaint, he was driving with two passengers in his back seat when he turned, pointed a gun at them and demanded their jewelry. They complied. Belgal pleaded guilty and received five years of probation. In December 2025, he was indicted on 10 counts related to narcotics distribution; he pleaded not guilty and was released on supervised conditions. Federal officials state that he is in the country illegally and allege that he has ties to the Trinitarios gang. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has stated that when ICE previously attempted to arrest him in September, Belgal fled. When New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch laid out that record, the reaction from the left was not to weigh it. Instead, its leading figures declared all of Belgal’s criminal history irrelevant. ELI STEELE: THE TERROR OF BEING CALLED RACIST IS CRUSHING FREE SPEECH IN AMERICA Darializa Avila Chevalier, a Democratic Socialists of America candidate for Congress in New York's 13th District, went on Hasan Piker's stream to talk about the shooting. When Piker asked about Belgal's criminal history, she said, "To me, it doesn't even matter." She then turned her wrath on Tisch and accused her of trying to "villainize Oscar." She demanded her resignation. Then she asked the audience to "put yourself in Oscar's shoes." Masked men were coming at his car and "You're running," she said. "I'm sorry, you're protecting your child." She ended with, "F--- ICE and abolish it." What struck me was her moral outrage. She was outraged that stating a man’s record in a matter-of-fact way was now the equivalent of "villainizing" him. All that mattered to Chevalier was that he was an immigrant, a Dominican like her, a member of an oppressed group, and that he was being chased by men with guns who were ICE. In my new film, "White Guilt," my father, Shelby Steele, the author, columnist and Hoover Institution Fellow, shows how the left created a world where responsibility can never be demanded of the oppressed. He describes going to a Black Power rally on the South Side of Chicago to hear the comedian and activist Dick Gregory: "Gregory argued that a racist America had given us responsibility, but had denied us the freedom to do much with it," my father says in the film. "Gregory held a Marxian vision of racism as a systemic force that made responsibility irrelevant in the struggle against oppression. Thus, it was bad manners to ask a black to lift themselves up." MAMDANI DEMANDS TRUMP RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE AGENT AS PROTESTS ERUPT IN THE BRONX Then Lyndon Johnson stood up at Howard University and said you do not take a man hobbled by chains, bring him to the starting line and tell him he is free to compete. "By implication, Johnson agreed with Gregory," my father says. "Suddenly, if you were black living in this new age of white guilt, you could not be expected to carry the same responsibilities as others." The belief Gregory preached and Johnson blessed, that oppression made responsibility irrelevant, became one of the core tenets of the white guilt racial order we live under today. White guilt is not the guilt a person feels for something he did. It is not personal, which is why I tire of hearing people declare, "I have no White guilt." White guilt is the collective guilt that the left assigns to all Whites for America's past racial sins. What it produces is not remorse but terror, the terror of being called a racist and losing your moral authority. To escape that terror, the "oppressor" buys back his innocence by asking nothing of the "oppressed," and the "oppressed" are handed power so long as they remain victims. That is how responsibility became "bad manners," in the words of my father, and demanding accountability became racism. HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE Today the "oppressor system" is America itself, and ICE is its face. And what the formula needs most is a symbol. Activists like Avila Chevalier dehumanize the oppressed by stripping away their responsibility and accountability, then wield what is left as a cudgel against the oppressor system. Once Belgal's record was erased, all that remained was an immigrant father shot by ICE with his little boy in the car. Between them, Avila Chevalier and Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded that ICE be abolished, the police commissioner resign, Belgal be released and immigration enforcement halt across the city. They did not demand anything of Oscar Belgal. The DSA often calls itself the party of the people, but listen to how it talks about the people it claims to defend. Its words for them are almost always the oppressed, the victims and the impoverished. Their value to the movement is not their individual humanity but what they collectively symbolize. If the DSA draws its power from these symbols of oppression to milk White guilt, why would it ever surrender this power? There is one innocent in all of this: the 5-year-old boy in the back seat. His mother says he has nightmares and won’t speak despite his talkative nature. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION The young boy will grow up with two stories of that fateful afternoon. In one version, his father will be seen as a victim, nothing more, and the world owes him. In the other story, his father is an individual who made choices, some of them bad, and yet has the chance to improve his life somehow. It is the second story that gives the young boy a real chance at life. Belgal’s lawyer said the first thing that his client asked was whether his son was OK. This detail reveals to us that Oscar Belgal is a man with a conscience, and a man with a conscience can bear responsibility for his choices. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The same lawyer said that "regardless of whether or not someone has a criminal history, it is not lawful, and it's not okay to shoot a father." The investigations will decide whether the shooting was lawful, and due process, which protects all individuals within this country, including those who are not citizens. So let the courts judge the officer who fired, and let them judge Oscar Belgal too. Avila Chevalier would cry that this is villainizing him. Those who believe in American principles would call it treating him like a man who is responsible for his own life. The activists will never allow it. Their power in White guilt America depends on keeping Oscar Belgal a permanent symbol of oppression. But what good has ever come out of dehumanization? CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM ELI STEELE

title: US military archbishop urges Catholic soldiers to refuse involvement in Army firing squad execution
description: Archbishop Timothy Broglio urged Catholic soldiers to refuse firing squad duty in the planned execution of Nidal Hasan, calling the livestream barbaric.
content: Catholics serving in the Army should request to be excused from participating in the planned firing squad execution of a convicted Fort Hood mass shooter, which the Pentagon has proposed livestreaming, a prominent U.S. archbishop who oversees Catholic pastoral services for the military said on Monday. Archbishop Timothy Broglio raised several objections to the Pentagon's unprecedented plan to broadcast the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist who was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others in a 2009 shooting at the Fort Hood military base. Hasan, now 56, uses a wheelchair after being shot by responding officers during the attack. Hasan is set to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, at 1 p.m. CST, according to the U.S. Army, which would make him the first person to be executed by firing squad by the U.S. military since 1945. It would also mark the first U.S. military execution by any method since 1961. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said he wanted soldiers to execute Hasan at the time, day of the week and location of the shooting and has argued that making the execution public would help serve as a deterrent. Broglio recalled presiding over the funeral of one of Hasan's victims, Michael Grant Cahill, the only civilian killed in that attack, and expressed sorrow over the deadly shooting. But the archbishop questioned whether the U.S. government wanted to "imitate the terrorists of this world and make a public spectacle of barbarically killing our adversaries." POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION Hasan's crime "was heinous, but does exposing the public to his execution serve any purpose?" Broglio asked in a statement. "I oblige any Catholics assigned to the firing squad to request to be excused from this action contrary to the teaching of the Church," he continued. Army regulations permit soldiers to seek religious exemptions or accommodations. It is unclear how the military intends to select members for the firing squad. "The U.S. military generally enjoys a good reputation in the world," Broglio said. "Is there really a value to throwing them in the same boat with terrorists by broadcasting the image of the execution of a man in a wheelchair to the whole world?" A U.S. government execution has never been broadcast to the public, making it an unprecedented plan that has drawn backlash from political and religious leaders. Broglio joins other Catholic leaders in criticizing the Pentagon's plans to livestream the execution. The head of the U.S. bishops conference, Archbishop Paul Coakley, expressed "shock" and "great sorrow" about the public execution plan and urged the U.S. to reconsider. "In no way can Hasan’s actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered," he said in a statement on Friday. "The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people." Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, called the proposed broadcast "truly incomprehensible" and warned that it was "unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle." "The Church’s position is one of total opposition to the death penalty; it is incompatible with human dignity and serves as no deterrent," Parolin told reporters on Friday. According to the English translation published by Vatican News, Parolin said, "It is truly incomprehensible that anyone would want to use this method in this day and age. I do not know for what purpose. It is certainly unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle. However guilty the person may be, there are other ways." Parolin added that the death penalty "is incompatible with human dignity and does not serve as a deterrent." Pope Leo XIV reiterated the Catholic Church's opposition to the death penalty as "inadmissible" in a social media post on Saturday marking World Day Against the Death Penalty. Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity. "The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo, the first American pope, wrote on X without specifically mentioning the Pentagon's execution plan for Hasan. Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic, expressed skepticism about whether the Pentagon would proceed with a public execution. He said he would not watch the livestream if it were carried out. Several lawmakers, including Republicans, have spoken out against plans to broadcast the execution. "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said on Thursday. "It should not be happening in America." Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Man admits to dismembering ex-girlfriend, keeping severed head in suitcase after she played him 'like a fool'
description: A New York man pleaded guilty to second-degree murder after he admitted that he murdered and dismembered his ex-girlfriend and kept her severed head in a suitcase.
content: A New York man pleaded guilty to murdering and dismembering his ex-girlfriend and putting her severed head in a suitcase with a flower after she ended their relationship, later telling investigators she had "played me like a sucker," according to authorities. Damon Foy, 50, of Kerhonkson, pleaded guilty last week to second-degree murder in the 2024 death of Alberta Dale, 44, of Pennsylvania, according to the Ulster County District Attorney's Office. Between March 31 and April 1, 2024, Foy killed and dismembered Dale and was in the process of disposing of her body when law enforcement intervened, according to the district attorney's office. The Ulster County Sheriff's Office began investigating on April 1, 2024, after Dale's family members in Pennsylvania contacted law enforcement because they were concerned about her well-being, the district attorney's office said. Deputies first conducted a welfare check before launching a missing person investigation. SISTER OF MISSING DC MOM SPEAKS OUT AFTER EX’S ARREST EXPOSES 'HORRIFYING' ABUSIVE RELATIONSHIP Deputies first went to Foy’s apartment on April 1, 2024, and found Dale’s car, according to the New York Post. The next day, deputies returned to question Foy after a member of the public found Dale’s phone on the side of the road and turned it in to authorities, leading investigators to suspect potential foul play. "She’s in there," Foy whispered to investigators, when they arrived at his home during the missing person investigation. "I killed her," he added, according to court documents cited by the New York Post. Investigators obtained a search warrant for Foy's home and found a suitcase in a closet that contained the victim's remains. Foy was then arrested and charged in connection with Dale's death. After shining a flashlight on the suitcase, investigators "immediately noticed what appeared to be dried blood," according to the documents. "Officers opened the defendant’s suitcase and found Alberta Dale’s partial dismembered remains, including her severed head," the court documents read, according to the New York Post. "The remaining portions of her dismembered body were not located during the execution of the search warrant," the documents add. When he was later interviewed, Foy told investigators he "loved her," according to the documents. "The only thing she kept doing after the time throughout the whole relationship was just play me, play me like a fool, play me like a sucker, and just took advantage of the whole f---ing system," he said. "That’s it. I was told to leave my own home. I was told to leave my own f---ing home, not a bill in her name, and I was told to leave my own f---ing home. Get out. Then it all started coming clearer to me," he added. When asked about the flower in the suitcase, Foy only said he was thinking about "what still happened last night to take s--- over the top." Foy had a history of domestic violence against Dale, according to court documents cited by the New York Post. A previous domestic incident involved a gun, and investigators had also observed an axe at Foy’s property when they were searching for Dale. Dale had previously warned authorities that "if she went missing it was because [Foy] killed her," according to the court documents. Under a plea agreement, Foy is expected to receive 23 years to life behind bars, with a minimum term two years shorter than the maximum of 25 years to life, according to the Daily Freeman. MAN UNLEASHES DEADLY ‘REVENGE’ RAMPAGE ON EX’S FAMILY, KILLS 4 PEOPLE, 3 DOGS BEFORE TORCHING HOME: DA Chief Assistant District Attorney Liz Culmone-Mills told the outlet that the agreement was backed by Dale’s family. "The District Attorney’s Office would not be making this recommendation were it not for Alberta Dale’s family," Culmone-Mills told the outlet. Foy is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. 16. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The total selfish disregard for the life and dignity of another person is at the heart of domestic violence; Damon Foy has shown that to us," District Attorney Emmanuel C. Nneji said in a statement. "We must recognize in our laws the rights of victims of domestic violence to be physically, psychologically, and emotionally safe from their tormentors and the dangers specifically targeted for them, and demand procedures that actually protect victims for real, not just on paper."

title: Bears kicker goes viral after trying to trip Packers receiver who decked Chicago coach on sideline

title: ABC accuses FCC of trying to 'inflict maximal coercive pressure' with probe against network
description: Disney's latest filing accused the FCC on Monday of using early broadcast license renewals to dodge judicial review and exert coercive pressure on ABC.
content: Disney and ABC accused the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Monday of using the license renewal process to circumvent "judicial review" and inflict "maximal coercive pressure" against the network and company. Disney originally sued the FCC in August over what it claimed was a "retaliatory campaign against ABC" regarding the agency's early broadcast license renewal proceedings for eight ABC-owned stations earlier this year. The stations, according to the FCC, must demonstrate they are operating in the public interest as the agency investigates diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices. However, in Disney's latest filing, the company asserted that the FCC could have used "a number of different tools" to investigate Disney and ABC's DEI practices that did not involve forcing stations to renew their licenses years ahead of schedule, suggesting it was done to avoid legal scrutiny. ABC MORE CAUTIOUS OF BOOKING CANDIDATES ON 'THE VIEW' AMID FCC PRESSURE, DISNEY'S FIRST AMENDMENT LAWSUIT SAYS "These are not merely 'theoretical' tools ... they have been used by the agency for decades," the filing read. "Yet the agency tried none of those less intrusive tools here, instead taking the unprecedented step of calling for early license renewal of all eight ABC-owned stations at once. Defendants’ own admissions leave no doubt as to why — Defendants sought to inflict maximal coercive pressure on the media company whose speech the Administration sought to curb, while deliberately evading judicial review." Disney cited a court hearing last week in which the FCC was instructed to provide a supplemental filing on alternative methods the agency could have used. During the hearing, the FCC suggested that additional procedures would have required federal court enforcement. "That Defendants openly describe judicial review as an obstacle demonstrates what Plaintiffs have been saying all along: shielding their unconstitutional campaign against ABC from judicial review is part of Defendants’ retaliatory strategy," the filing read. In a comment to Fox News Digital, FCC spokesperson Adam Jackman dismissed the latest filing as an effort to block the FCC in court procedures. CONSERVATIVE GROUPS URGE FCC TO BACK OFF ABC LICENSE REVIEW, WARNING IT COULD HURT RIGHT-LEANING MEDIA "Disney’s latest filing only confirms that they’ve filed a meritless case in the wrong court at the wrong time," Jackman said. "They want a district court to prevent the FCC from even considering whether Disney has complied with its longstanding obligations as a broadcaster. The law does not allow that. The FCC will continue to hold broadcasters accountable to their regulatory obligations." Fox News Digital also reached out to ABC and Disney for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Disney and ABC have repeatedly attacked the FCC's probes and investigations into the company as a form of retaliation over programs and hosts that are critical of President Donald Trump, such as late-night host Jimmy Kimmel. Disney has maintained that "The View" is a "bona fide news" program exempted from the rule.

title: Dodgers dynasty on the brink after the Milwaukee BABIP machine dials up another win for Brewers
description: Milwaukee's BABIP machine and unhittable bullpen put the Los Angeles Dodgers' three-peat hopes on life support with a commanding 2-0 NLCS lead.
content: Game 2 of the National League Championship Series on Monday afternoon was a must-win for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Despite widespread perception that the Dodgers are the unbeatable superteam, it was Milwaukee, the team that finished with the best record in the league, that played essentially flawless baseball in a Game 1 win. While Jacob Misiorowski wasn't his typically dominant self, every time Los Angeles had an opportunity to break the game open, "The Miz" and his team's defense clamped down. Already up a run in the second inning, the Dodgers had the bases loaded with postseason star Kike Hernandez at the plate. Once again, the Brewers defense was perfectly positioned to turn the inning-ending double play. After Milwaukee's offense scratched across two runs against Tarik Skubal, their bullpen continued its remarkable run of success, going 4.2 scoreless innings to secure the win. BRIGHT LIGHTS NOT TOO BRIGHT FOR THE BREWERS OR SUPERFAN FRONT ROW AMY IN GAME 1 OF NLCS Still, the Dodgers felt good about their chances with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, postseason hero from 2025, starting in Game 2 against Logan Henderson. Yet for all the hype about LA's remarkable rotation, the Milwaukee BABIP (batting average on balls in play) machine once again kicked into high gear to secure a massive 2-0 series lead and put the Dodgers' three-peat hopes on life support with a 7-4 win. LA jumped out to an early lead thanks to some uncharacteristic sloppiness from the Brewers. Mookie Betts walked, Freddie Freeman moved him to second, and he took third on a wild pitch from starter Logan Henderson. Teoscar Hernandez knocked him in with a sacrifice fly, and the Dodgers had a 1-0 lead without a hit. Sure enough though, Milwaukee immediately tied it in the bottom of the first. The Dodgers missed an opportunity to challenge an obvious missed strike three call on Brice Turang, who then doubled and scored on a patented Brewers bloop single. William Contreras stuck his bat out with one hand, somehow making contact with Yamamoto's pitch to dump it into left field. It wouldn't be the last time. The third inning was a near-repeat. LA mounted a quick rally on back-to-back singles from Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts. Sal Frelick robbed Freddie Freeman of a double with a nice running catch in the right center field gap, but an error on a pickoff attempt at first base brought Edman in to score. But the Brewers, knowing that the Dodgers' greatest weakness is having an opportunity to score runs, had them right where they wanted them. Easy outs from Teoscar Hernandez and Shohei Ohtani ended the "threat," and Milwaukee answered right back in the bottom of the inning. David Hamilton poked another bloop single, stole second, and yet again, Brice Turang reached base on a missed strike three that went unchallenged by catcher Will Smith. Jake Bauers, one of the worst hitters in baseball before putting on a Milwaukee uniform, worked a walk after a lengthy at bat against Yamamoto, and Christian Yelich made him pay for it with a single to center. After all this playoff heroics in 2025, Yamamoto went just 2.2 innings, allowing four hits and three runs. Missed challenges, bloop singles, exceptionally well-timed line drives from below average hitters, the ideal Milwaukee offensive outing. Now trailing 3-2, the Dodgers "fought" back in the fifth. Kyle Tucker led off with a double, before a throwing error from Henderson on a Tommy Edman bunt let him score and sent Edman to second. A grounder and sac fly gave LA a 4-3 lead, once again without getting a hit with runners in scoring position. Again, the Brewers' relief pitchers proved to be the single greatest pitching unit ever assembled, extending their streak to nearly 29 innings with just one run allowed. title: WNBA gives Cheryl Reeve another award after playoff collapse and years of outspoken left-wing politics
description: Cheryl Reeve won WNBA Executive of the Year for a third time, but the Lynx's historic first-round playoff sweep raises questions about the honor.
content: The WNBA has another award for Cheryl Reeve. This one comes from the people who run the teams, and that makes it worth examining what, exactly, they are celebrating. The league announced Monday that the Minnesota Lynx head coach and president of basketball operations won Basketball Executive of the Year for the third time, tying the Atlanta Dream's Dan Padover for the most selections in the award's history. The announcement comes less than two weeks after the top-seeded Lynx were swept out of the first round of the playoffs by the eighth-seeded New York Liberty, who were subsequently swept in the semifinals by the Dream. Reeve appeared on 13 ballots, ahead of Padover's 11 and Golden State's Ohemaa Nyanin's eight. Each of the WNBA's 15 teams had an executive on the voting panel, and voters couldn't select themselves. CHERYL REEVE'S WNBA COACH OF THE YEAR WIN SHOULDN'T DISTRACT FROM HER DANGEROUS ACCUSATIONS That's a substantial endorsement of Reeve from her peers and it also amounts to tacit approval of the way one of the league's most outspoken left-wing figures represents her franchise. An executive helps establish what an organization stands for, and Reeve has made her politics a major part of that job. She consistently uses her WNBA platform to attack the motives of people who believe women's sports should be reserved for females. Her colleagues have now chosen to celebrate her leadership. That deserves scrutiny beyond a list of successful transactions. Dallas made Reeve's Olivia Miles decision awfully easy The league's announcement highlighted Reeve's selection of Olivia Miles with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. Miles went on to become the unanimous Rookie of the Year and set the league's rookie scoring record with 790 points. An excellent addition, obviously. But let's remember how Miles became available. The Dallas Wings could have (and should have) taken Miles, but elected to draft Paige Bueckers' girlfriend, Azzi Fudd, with the No. 1 pick instead. The Wings publicly praised Fudd's shooting. But pretending that their selection of Fudd was based entirely on her basketball skills is foolish. Miles averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds as a rookie. Fudd averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists and 1.7 rebounds. Miles produced those numbers while playing slightly fewer minutes per game, shot better from the field and finished second in MVP voting. Reeve should probably send the Wings a thank-you note. In April 2024, the Chicago Sky moved from No. 8 to No. 7 and acquired the rights to Nikolina Milić. Minnesota received Sika Koné, a 2025 second-round pick and the right to swap first-round picks with Chicago in 2026, along with the No. 8 selection. Chicago used No. 7 on Angel Reese. At the time of the deal, Minnesota was coming off a 19-21 season and Chicago an 18-22 season. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND In April 2025, Minnesota sent Chicago the No. 11 pick, which the Sky used on Hailey Van Lith, for Chicago's 2026 first-rounder outright. That deal canceled the earlier swap and allowed Minnesota to keep its own 2026 first-round pick, too. Reeve deserves credit for those trades. Once Dallas passed on Miles, though, the choice at No. 2 was awfully easy. Reeve also signed Natasha Howard, who started all 44 games and earned an All-Star starting spot. Minnesota finished 33-11 and earned the No. 1 playoff seed. Dallas did Reeve an enormous favor, and the Lynx benefited. Reeve's team couldn't win a playoff game For all those advantages, what did the Lynx do in the playoffs? Minnesota became the first No. 1 seed in WNBA history to be eliminated by a No. 8 seed, and New York did it in a sweep. The Lynx had the unanimous Rookie of the Year (who also finished second in MVP voting). And while Napheesa Collier, one of the league’s best players, missed time during the regular season, she played in both playoff games. Minnesota lost both of those games by 16 points, including a 91-75 defeat at home in Game 1. Reeve's four championships are part of her record. So is the fact that the most recent one came in 2017. In the nine seasons since, Minnesota has reached the Finals once, losing to New York in 2024. During that same stretch, Reeve has collected three Coach of the Year awards and all three of her Executive of the Year awards. Six individual awards. Zero championships. If Reeve gets the credit for both building the roster and coaching it, she can answer for what that team did in the playoffs, too. An executive sets the tone for the franchise Reeve already won her fifth Coach of the Year award two weeks ago. With Monday's announcement, she became the first person to win Coach of the Year and Executive of the Year in the same season twice. For me, evaluating an executive means evaluating leadership. If an executive repeatedly uses the team's platform to make political statements, those statements belong in the discussion of how she represents the organization. WNBA FIGHT OVER MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS EXPOSES HOW THE LEFT KEEPS ANSWERING A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt on the sideline against the Indiana Fever shortly after Sophie Cunningham's comments about wanting to protect women's sports went public. But she wasn't done. After Minnesota's Sept. 24 regular-season finale, Reeve characterized the controversy involving male participation in women's sports as an attack on what she called the "transgender community." "They don't want transgender people to exist," Reeve said. That's an ugly accusation to make about people whose position is that girls and women deserve their own athletic category. And it came from the person who both coaches the Lynx and oversees their basketball operations. Her public conduct carries the authority of both positions. By honoring Reeve as the year's outstanding basketball executive, her peers are publicly holding up her leadership as an example. Her political conduct is part of that leadership. That says a lot about what the WNBA's decision-makers will celebrate.

title: Online marketplace jewelry listing tied to armed robbery in affluent Tennessee city
description: A Facebook Marketplace jewelry listing lured armed robbers to a Franklin, Tennessee, home, sparking a police chase and three arrests on felony charges.
content: A Facebook Marketplace jewelry listing was linked to a late-night armed robbery at a home in affluent Franklin, Tennessee, where police pursued three fleeing suspects, authorities said. Officers responded to a home in northeast Franklin just after 11 p.m. Friday, Oct. 9 and determined the robbery was connected to jewelry advertised for sale on the platform, according to the Franklin Police Department. The suspects fled the area but were spotted by responding officers a short time later. A vehicle pursuit followed, ending with all three men in custody, police said. FLORIDA MEN INDICTED IN ARMED HOME INVASION WHERE SUSPECT POSED AS UTILITY WORKER, 13-YEAR-OLD ZIP-TIED: DOJ Authorities identified the suspects as Ivan Lagos-Espinoza, 22, and Jose Paiz-Godoy, 23, both of Nashville, and Rubel Rodriguez-Lisa, 19, of Lebanon. All three face multiple charges, including aggravated robbery, felony evading and tampering with evidence. The robbery unfolded in a community known for its wealth and high-end homes. Franklin’s city website describes it as "one of the wealthiest cities in one of the wealthiest counties in the United States." Franklin's median home sale price reached $903,410 in September 2026, while the median listing price stood at $1.1 million, according to Realtor.com. Across Williamson County, where Franklin is located, the median home sale price was $929,990, the real estate website reported. 119,000 FAKE SHOPS COULD STEAL YOUR CREDIT CARD DETAILS Police credited the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office with helping investigate the robbery and apprehend the suspects. The case also prompted a warning to online sellers about the risks of bringing strangers to their homes, particularly when expensive merchandise is involved. Police urged buyers and sellers to arrange exchanges in public, well-lit locations with other people nearby and surveillance cameras whenever possible. For valuable items, authorities recommended meeting at a police department or another law enforcement facility. WASHINGTON JEWELRY STORE OWNER OPENS FIRE AFTER WOULD-BE THIEVES RAM TRUCK THROUGH STOREFRONT Sellers should also bring someone along, avoid carrying large amounts of cash and limit the personal information they share, including details about their homes, schedules and other valuables, police said. Authorities warned that jewelry, electronics and other expensive items can make sellers attractive targets for criminals. "If something about the buyer, seller or proposed meeting location does not feel right, cancel the transaction," the department advised.
