title: NATO warns Russia: 'We will break' forces, destroy 'anything and everything' if you attack
description: Gen. Alexus Grynkewich outlined NATO's strategy to "block, blunt and break" enemy forces at the Warsaw Security Forum amid rising Russia tensions.
content: NATO's top military commander warned Monday that what he called the "lethal alliance" would destroy "anything and everything" supporting an attack on allied territory and "break" enemy warfighting systems to thwart any potential future Russian assault. "Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us," U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland, in an apparent warning to Moscow. "This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force," he said during a panel titled "Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?" on the first day of the forum. US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS Grynkewich, NATO's supreme allied commander in Europe, also outlined a three-pronged strategy of "blocking, blunting and breaking" enemy forces, making clear that while NATO is a defensive alliance, it is prepared to respond decisively to an assault on any of its 32 members. "If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight," he said. "We will stop the attack and deny them the ability to achieve their objectives, whatever those might be. We will, in short, ensure any attack, against any ally, proves utterly futile." The warning came amid heightened tensions between Russia and Western nations following a series of drone incursions and suspected sabotage operations that European countries have linked to Moscow. "We stand here together in Poland today stronger than ever united in our common vision of a more balanced, more ready and more lethal alliance," Grynkewich also said. European officials have accused Russia of waging a campaign of hybrid warfare involving sabotage, arson and cyberattacks, alongside increasingly provocative military activity near NATO territory. I’M PRESIDENT OF ONE OF AMERICA’S MOST RELIABLE ALLIES. HERE’S HOW WE STAND UP TO RUSSIA In 2025, multiple Russian drones entered Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on Ukraine, prompting a response from Polish and allied aircraft. NATO launched Operation Eastern Sentry to strengthen defenses along its eastern flank. Romania has also reported Russian drone incursions, while Estonia has accused Russian military aircraft of violating its airspace. Grynkewich's remarks had followed a tense weekend between Russia and Ukraine, with Moscow launching fresh strikes against Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite diplomatic efforts to reduce hostilities. President Donald Trump had announced that he had reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to increase Russian diesel supplies to the U.S. and global markets. ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE The reported agreement included a waiver of certain U.S. sanctions on Russian energy exports. Zelenskyy went on to accuse Russia of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities, casting doubt on prospects for a broader ceasefire. The tensions have also been accompanied by recent nuclear warnings from Moscow. On Sept. 30, Russia warned NATO that it could use nuclear weapons if the alliance attempted to isolate Kaliningrad, its heavily militarized Baltic Sea exclave between Poland and Lithuania. In a diplomatic note obtained by Reuters, Moscow accused NATO of pursuing a "dangerous and reckless course" that carried "high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict." According to the note, Russia warned it could use its full military arsenal, including nuclear weapons, to defend Kaliningrad and raised the possibility of strikes against decision-making centers in NATO countries at the outset of a conflict. RUSSIA'S NEIGHBOR REVEALS PERSONAL APPEALS TO TRUMP AS US WEIGHS NATO TROOP PULLBACK IN EUROPE NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte rejected the threats, emphasizing the alliance's defensive mission and calling on Moscow to end its war in Ukraine. "Putin knows that he can never win from NATO," Rutte said during a Sept. 30 appearance at the Euronews Defence and Space Summit. Putin has also maintained that Russia has no plans to attack European countries and wants peaceful coexistence with its neighbors. Grynkewich did not mention Russia by name during his Warsaw address, but his warning appeared directed at Moscow and with NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept also identifying Russia as the most significant and direct threat to allied security. "My theory of victory is simple: we will block the initial attack. If the attack persists, we will blunt it and prevent enemy advance," Grynkewich said on Monday. "And if required, we will break the enemy's forces and the operational warfighting system that is arrayed against us." Grynkewich said NATO was already putting the strategy into action through military exercises, enhanced military readiness and investments in new capabilities. SHE GREW UP UNDER SOVIET RULE. NOW EU'S TOP DIPLOMAT WARNS EUROPE AGAINST GIVING RUSSIA WHAT IT WANTS "If attacked, we are ready to fight tonight, but we are not complacent," he said. The general made clear that NATO's response would not necessarily be limited to enemy troops directly involved in an assault, but could extend to the broader military infrastructure enabling the attack. Meanwhile, Trump has pressed European allies to increase defense spending and has questioned whether countries that fail to meet their obligations should expect U.S. protection. Grynkewich sought to downplay concerns about Washington's commitment, recalling Trump's positive remarks about the alliance during the 2025 NATO summit in The Hague, Netherlands. "I was in the room and I felt the love," Grynkewich said of the 2025 event. "What I want to do is assure the one billion citizens of our alliance that we've got this. We know what we need to do. We know how we would do it," he added. He also indicated a willingness to discuss suspected hybrid attacks more openly if individual NATO governments wanted him to address their concerns. "If a nation wants me to, I'm happy to talk about it," he said. title: NPR CEO who previously called First Amendment a 'challenge' to receive 'First Amendment Award'
description: NPR CEO Katherine Maher will receive Harper's Magazine First Amendment Award despite once calling the amendment a "challenge" to fighting disinformation.
content: NPR CEO Katherine Maher will receive Harper's Magazine's "First Amendment Award" later this month despite her past criticism of the amendment. "As president and CEO of NPR, Katherine Maher has guided one of America’s most important public media institutions through a period of extraordinary political, legal, and financial scrutiny, reaffirming journalism’s essential role in a democratic society," the magazine said in a press release earlier this year about Maher receiving the James C. Goodale First Amendment Award on Oct. 26. Harper's Magazine also claimed that Maher led NPR "through a period of heightened scrutiny and challenge" along with "successfully battling" President Donald Trump's efforts to defund NPR, though Congress still rescinded $1.1 billion in federal funding to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting in 2025. NPR GETS $80 MILLION GIFT FROM DEMOCRATIC MEGADONOR IN MAJOR BOOST AFTER LOSING GOVERNMENT FUNDING Although the magazine hailed Maher as an advocate for journalism, Maher has not always been supportive of the First Amendment as a whole. In 2021, when Maher was the CEO of Wikimedia, which oversees Wikipedia, she discussed efforts to combat disinformation and considered the First Amendment a "challenge" in that goal. "The number one challenge here that we see is, of course, the First Amendment in the United States. [It] is a fairly robust protection of rights and that is a protection of rights both for platforms, which I actually think is very important that platforms have those rights to be able to regulate what kind of content they want on their sites," Maher said. BILL MAHER TELLS NPR INTERVIEWER HE VIEWS OUTLET AS 'FAR EXTREME OF THE LEFT' She added, "But it also means that it is a little bit tricky to really address some of the real challenges of where does bad information come from, and sort of the influence peddlers who have made a real market economy around it." NPR has also had a history of questionable journalism. Most notably, NPR declined to cover the Hunter Biden laptop story in 2020 ahead of the presidential election in what many critics saw as an effort to protect then-presidential candidate Joe Biden. Maher, who was not appointed NPR CEO until 2024, later conceded that the publication "made a mistake." NPR OFFERING STAFF BUYOUTS AFTER RECEIVING $113 MILLION IN CHARITABLE GIFTS "I do want to say that NPR acknowledges we were mistaken in failing to cover the Hunter Biden laptop story more aggressively and sooner," Maher said during congressional testimony in 2025. Fox News Digital reached out to Harper's Magazine for comment. Tim Graham, executive editor of the media watchdog NewsBusters, told Fox News Digital, "Harper's Magazine is demonstrating the usual liberal impulse, that being fiercely critical of Trump and the Republicans is what the First Amendment is all about. But NPR didn't hold President Biden accountable. Instead, they insisted that covering corruption in Biden's family was a 'distraction.'""Their explanation for this pride is that Maher courageously fought off defunding NPR, which, of course, is not true. They are defunded. Liberals believe depriving NPR of taxpayer subsidies is some sort of First Amendment violation. But it's not a First Amendment violation for NPR to avoid having any Trump-supporting conservatives on their airwaves to push back on all their liberal bias," he continued."These people have no shame that Maher championed aggressive censorship of ‘bad information,’ just as European socialist countries have done. Maher said in a 2021 TED Talk that the First Amendment was a ‘challenge,’ a hurdle, something that makes censorship ‘a little bit trickier.’ How does that deserve a First Amendment award??" he asked. NPR celebrated Maher receiving the award, pointing to its past statement when reached for a comment by Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Public media exists to serve the public interest, and I can think of no greater service to the public than the defense of the First Amendment," Maher said in a comment. "The freedom, imagination, and initiative of all Americans flourish with its protections, so that we may better understand the world and one another. The compact of citizenship asks that we each step up to defend our constitutional rights if they are threatened. On behalf of NPR and the NPR Network, I am deeply honored to accept this award."

title: Abdul El-Sayed's alleged family ties to Muslim Brotherhood surface after denying any link during NBC interview
description: Abdul El-Sayed denied any Muslim Brotherhood ties on "Meet the Press," but his half-sister's social media posts appear to tell a different story.
content: Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is facing new scrutiny after he denied that he or his family had any ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. On Sunday's "Meet the Press," NBC's Kristen Welker pressed El-Sayed whether he could "set the record straight" on allegations that his family had connections to the controversial Islamist group. "No," El-Sayed replied. EL-SAYED ASKED IF HE BELIEVES AMERICA IS 'READY FOR A MUSLIM PRESIDENT' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE "No, you don't have any ties, and your family doesn't?" Welker followed up. "No," El-Sayed repeated before suggesting his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, was floating Islamophobic attacks against him and his family. title: Microsoft president calls for global AI rules, saying milk is more regulated than the tech
description: Microsoft President Brad Smith is calling for urgent global AI safety rules as concerns grow over rogue AI agents, rapid advances in artificial intelligence and government oversight of the technology.
content:
Philadelphia police investigators on scene of a crime. (Credit: Tom Gralish/The Philadelphia Inquirer via AP)
An Anthropic AI chatbot generated a false lead in an unsolved Philadelphia murder case and sent it to police during a test, triggering criticism over how long the company took to uncover and report it.
The false tip was submitted July 18 through the department’s unsolved murders website but landed in spam and never reached investigators, according to 6abc. Police said their systems and data were not compromised.
Anthropic confirmed that its Claude Haiku 4.5 model claimed to have seen someone matching a description near the crime scene, even though the webpage contained no suspect description. The chatbot left its name and contact information blank. The company said its testing rules prohibited several actions but did not explicitly ban submitting forms.
Anthropic discovered the incident Sept. 28 and notified police Oct. 7, according to 6abc. Police called the delay “unacceptable,” stressing that unsolved cases involve “real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers.”
Gizmodo reported that the fake tip was among several unwanted actions Anthropic disclosed involving outside websites. In its own report, Anthropic said it has suspended live internet access for all internal evaluations until stronger safeguards reliably catch such behavior, warning that similar failures could cause greater harm as AI becomes more powerful.

title: Dianna Russini could have a hard time returning to media following Mike Vrabel scandal
description: Dianna Russini reportedly hired crisis publicist Melissa Nathan to navigate past the Mike Vrabel scandal as she seeks a return to sports media.
content: Dianna Russini has not made a public statement since announcing her resignation from The Athletic in April, following a series of leaks that showed her spending time privately with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. Perhaps most bizarrely, TMZ reported that it had obtained records from a private boating trip involving the two six years earlier, months before the former NFL reporter gave birth to her first child. According to the New York Post, Russini is now seeking a return to the media. She recently hired crisis publicist Melissa Nathan to help her "navigate past the Mike Vrabel scandal." One could argue that Nathan's first piece of advice should have been not to leak that Russini hired a crisis publicist. On the surface, we are skeptical that any serious journalism outlet would hire Russini as an NFL reporter, a position she held for more than two decades. Rumors shape perception, and perception often becomes reality. The perception surrounding Russini is that she obtained information unethically because of an inappropriate relationship with Vrabel, romantic or otherwise. Any significant story she breaks would invite questions about how she obtained the information. The controversy could also make sources more reluctant to provide her with sensitive information. That said, Russini did not hurt anyone. At worst, she violated a basic journalistic ethical standard by failing to disclose a close personal relationship with an NFL coach she covered professionally. Her entire career does not deserve to end because of that. She may simply have to transition into a different role. Fantasy football analyst Matthew Berry told OutKick in August that he would "consider" signing Russini as an analyst for his media company, Fantasy Life. Dave Portnoy has also expressed interest in bringing her to Barstool Sports as a personality. title: Ranking NBA teams ABA-style uniforms in honor of the 50th anniversary of the historic merger
description: The Brooklyn Nets, Denver Nuggets, Indiana Pacers, and San Antonio Spurs unveiled ABA throwback uniforms celebrating the 50th anniversary of the merger.
content: On Monday, four NBA teams unveiled ABA-style uniforms for the upcoming season. The Brooklyn Nets, Denver Nuggets, Indiana Pacers and San Antonio Spurs unveiled new Classic Edition uniforms to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the 1976 NBA-ABA (American Basketball Association) merger. That calls for some uniform rankings. Honorable Mention: San Antonio Spurs These are clean and classic. The Spurs uniforms are a direct reproduction of the team's original home look from their early years in San Antonio. One interesting detail is the arched "Spurs" wordmark on the chest exactly as it was worn by the first players to ever represent the city in 1973 after relocating from Dallas. Jordan Mandelkorn, Vice President of Marketing, Creative and Retail for Spurs Sports & Entertainment, stated that honoring their ABA roots through this uniform provides a unique opportunity to celebrate the history that shaped both the Spurs and the city of San Antonio. He emphasized that the season-long celebration—which includes a matching throwback court design featuring the ABA 50th-anniversary logo—will successfully connect generations of fans to the franchise's past while carrying that legacy into the future. This look was originally made famous during the legendary George Gervin era at the downtown HemisFair Arena. The team has scheduled the jersey to debut on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, against the Dallas Mavericks at the Frost Bank Center, kicking off the first of nine scheduled "Classic Nights" throughout the season. Also, the shorts may be the best of the bunch. The black diamond backdrop framing the classic cowboy spur really nails the retro look. I'm a big fan. The Worst: Denver Nuggets These just don't pass the vibe check. The Nuggets city edition uniforms this season swap out the franchise’s traditional navy and gold for a drab orange design. This uniform honors the team’s late 1960s and early 1970s heritage when they competed in the ABA. The jersey features an arched "Denver" wordmark across the chest in black lettering with a white outline. It's simple and underwhelming. The shorts showcase a bold black Rockets logo on the left leg, paying homage to the team’s original 1967 launch identity as the Denver Rockets before rebranding to the Nuggets. Again, simple and bland. Alongside the uniform rollout, the organization announced a corresponding specialty throwback court at Ball Arena to match the vintage aesthetic during designated games. The team will officially debut the retro threads on Sunday, December 27, 2026, during a home matchup against the Indiana Pacers, whose uniforms I'll be talking about in a minute, marking the first of nine total regular-season games (seven at home and two on the road) where the Nuggets will wear this commemorative look. NEW YORK ISLANDERS PICK THEIR TOP 8 FAN-DESIGNED JERSEYS AND SOCIAL MEDIA HATES THEM ALL Final thought: They should've left these in the past. Runner-Up: Indiana Pacers Bright, clean, classic, but reminds me too much of the Atlanta Hawks early 70s uniforms. The Indiana Pacers 2026–27 Classic Edition uniform pays direct homage to the franchise's powerhouse era in the ABA. The commemorative uniform replicates the team’s iconic 1971–74 road design. The vibrant royal blue jerseys feature a clean, blocky, white "Indiana" wordmark arched across the chest. The gold numbering, along with a single gold racing stripe wrapping around the armholes, and a distinct gold-and-white striping pattern running down the right side of both the jersey and the shorts. It's a classic look, but I can't get past the fact that this looks far too similar to one of my favorite jerseys of all time: The 1970-72 Atlanta Hawks jersey, especially the Pete Maravich jersey featuring his nickname "Pistol." The best detail is the vintage 1967 logo featured on the shorts with a cartoonish white hand, holding a basketball that looks more like a tennis ball inside the letter "P." The team officially announced that the players will wear these retro threads for 15 games throughout the season, including seven designated home dates at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. For those seven home matchups, the franchise is introducing a custom throwback court design and an entirely unique, retro game-night experience. The Best: Brooklyn Nets This is a uniform that feels retro, authentic and unique. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Brooklyn Nets 2026–27 Classic Edition uniform is a revival of the iconic New York Nets design, paying direct homage to the franchise's legendary ABA roots. The uniforms' red, white and blue colorway pair perfectly with an ABA patriotic colored, period-specific basketball. The clean white jersey, with those American colors, also features side paneling with retro stars, replicating the look made famous by Hall of Famer Julius "Dr. J" Erving when he led the team to ABA championships in 1974 and 1976. To complement the uniform, the organization is introducing a matching throwback court design at the Barclays Center. The team is scheduled to officially debut the retro threads on Opening Night, Wednesday, October 21, 2026, against the Charlotte Hornets. This is a jersey I'd easily add to my collection. Now I just need to figure out what player's jersey to get. One thing is for sure: These uniforms are much better than the Specter Edition Uniforms that Nike and the NBA unveiled in September. Those are atrocious.

title: Christian woman pleads not guilty to new 'Orwellian' charges for standing in silent prayer
description: British Christian Isabel Vaughan-Spruce's attorney argues the UK crossed a red line by prosecuting someone for private thoughts and silent prayer.
content: A British Christian activist facing fresh criminal charges over silent prayer near an abortion clinic is warning that her country is becoming increasingly "Orwellian," telling Fox News Digital that ordinary citizens are growing afraid to pray in public as her legal battle heads toward trial. "It certainly seems very Orwellian and a lot of people have mentioned that particular word to me," Isabel Vaughan-Spruce told Fox News Digital in an interview Monday. "It seems that we're really fostering a sense of intolerance in our communities." Vaughan-Spruce, co-director of March for Life UK, spoke to Fox News Digital after pleading not guilty in January to new charges in Birmingham, England, in a case that her attorneys argue tests the limits of religious freedom and the government's authority to regulate conduct near abortion facilities. FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP DOJ REACHES SETTLEMENT WITH PRO-LIFE PROTESTER TARGETED BY BIDEN ADMIN She previously received a 13,000 British pounds out-of-court settlement from police after pursuing claims of wrongful arrest and false imprisonment stemming from her earlier arrests for silently praying near an abortion clinic. Now, Vaughan-Spruce says she is facing another charge after returning to pray silently near the same facility following the introduction of nationwide abortion clinic buffer zones in October 2024. Vaughan-Spruce told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that the controversy has fostered intolerance toward people with differing religious and moral beliefs. "I don't believe that those who are pro-life or Christian should be treated as some kind of social pariah," she added. "A lot of people are just worried about what might happen to them as well because of this," Vaughan-Spruce added. "And I've heard that from a lot of people, you know, just concerned simply about something as simple as praying when they're in a public space." BIBLE VERSE LEADS TO TRIAL IN EUROPE. GROWING CRACKDOWN THREATENS OUR US-UK VALUES She said she is concerned about the longstanding implications of what policies like buffer zones will have on free speech. "I think we need to know our rights and to exercise our rights, and not to be intimidated by other people with [sic] this regard, and particularly our rights under God as Christians to be able to pray wherever we want to pray, certainly if it's something internal in our heads, and not to kind of end up self-censoring because of that prayer is a very, very important part of our life of Christian life," Vaughan-Spruce said. "And we certainly need more of that on the streets, prayer, not less." ORTHODOX JEW ASKS SUPREME COURT TO HEAR CASE AFTER CITY ALLEGEDLY TARGETED HIS HOME PRAYER GROUP Her attorney, Jeremiah Igunnubole, described the prosecution as the first of its kind in Britain and argued that the case raises a fundamental question about whether the government can punish someone for thoughts and private prayer rather than outward conduct. "To be clear, standing within the buffer zone is not a crime," Igunnubole told Fox News Digital. "So the question exactly, the precise question is exactly what has Isabel been charged for? We can only say it's been for her thoughts and the fact that she lifted up her heart and mind to God in prayer." ORTHODOX JEW FIGHTS BACK, SAYS CALIFORNIA CITY FINED HIM FOR HOME PRAYER MEETINGS Asked where the line should be drawn when it comes to freedom of speech, Igunnubole argued that the government should never have the power to regulate an individual's private thoughts. "It certainly is not when the state purports to regulate the thoughts of any individual, and we think that that is a red line that cannot be crossed in the UK under the Human Rights Act," Igunnubole said. "There's an absolute right to freedom of thought and that means that there's no qualifications allowed or permitted." Fox News Digital reached out to the Home Office and the Crown Prosecution Service for comment, who declined to comment due to the pending case. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

title: RJ Mitte, ‘Breaking Bad’ actor who played Walter White Jr., dies at 34
description: Actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte, who played Walter "Flynn" White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," has died at age 34.
content: RJ Mitte, the actor who played Walter White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," has died. "It is with profound sadness we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," Mitte's representative told Fox News Digital. "RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series Breaking Bad. Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement continued. "Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s." The statement noted that Mitte also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, which supports philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities. 'BREAKING BAD' ACTOR MARK MARGOLIS DEAD AT 83 Mitte’s cause of death was not immediately disclosed. Like his character on the Emmy Award-winning show, Mitte had cerebral palsy and was a disability rights advocate. Last week, Mitte appeared on "The Joe Vulpis Podcast" and spoke about how "Breaking Bad" changed his life and on his close relationship with the cast years after the show's finale, TMZ reported. After appearing in TV shows including "Hannah Montana" and "Vegas," Mitte made his career breakthrough at age 15 in 2008 when he landed the role of Walter White Jr., the son of the series' main character and antihero Walter White (Bryan Cranston) and his wife Skyler (Anna Gunn), on "Breaking Bad." Mitte starred in all five seasons of the hit AMC series, which received 16 Primetime Emmy Awards, two Golden Globe Awards and three Screen Actors Guild Awards during its run from 2008 to 2014. In 2014, he won a Screen Actors Guild Award alongside the "Breaking Bad" cast for outstanding ensemble performance in a drama series. Mitte was also honored with the SAG-AFTRA Harold Russell Award at the 2013 Media Access Awards, which recognize inclusive portrayals and employment of people with disabilities in media. The actor, who was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at age 3, previously spoke out about using the visibility he gained from "Breaking Bad" to advocate for broader representation of performers with disabilities. During a 2015 interview with the Badger Herald, he shared that he viewed his disability as a source of strength, saying it helped shape the actor and advocate he became. "I think everyone that has a disability has the opportunity to make an impact with what they can do and who they are. I wouldn’t be able to do what I do today if it wasn’t for my disability and what it instilled in me," Mitte said. Mitte often credited "Breaking Bad" with transforming his life and career. He previously said he believed Walter Jr. resonated with the disability community because his cerebral palsy was part of the character, but not the center of his story. BRYAN CRANSTON DOESN'T MISS 'BREAKING BAD' CHARACTER WALTER WHITE "Walt Jr. had cerebral palsy but he wasn’t disabled," he said on "ListenABLE" podcast in Sept. 2021. "That’s the biggest thing that I feel is so important when we see characters on television that represent individuals with disabilities. Their disability isn’t what makes them a character. It’s who they are, where they came from and how they got there through determination and strength and that’s what makes them so strong and independent." After "Breaking Bad" ended, Mitte went on to appear in a recurring role on the hit ABC series "Switched at Birth." His other television work included roles in "Chance," "This Close," "Now Apocalypse" and "The Guardians of Justice (Will Save You!)." The actor executive produced and starred in the 2021 coming of age film "Triumph," in which he played a high school senior with cerebral palsy who is determined to join his school’s wrestling team. He most recently starred in the drama "Talking to Strangers," which was released in July. Mitte, who has several upcoming projects listed on IMDB, made his last public appearance at a screening of "Talking to Strangers" in Beverly Hills on Sept. 30, less than two weeks before his death. In addition to serving as the president of the Mitte Foundation, Mitte was also an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s and worked with SAG-AFTRA’s disability inclusion efforts. title: Harry Styles addresses ICE shooting in New York with call for ‘dignity and justice’
description: Harry Styles urged Madison Square Garden fans to show compassion and justice for Oscar Belgal after the ICE shooting sparked protests in New York City.
content: Harry Styles paused his concert at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday to address the shooting of a Dominican immigrant by federal immigration agents, urging fans to show compassion toward people from different backgrounds and calling for "dignity" and "justice." The British pop star addressed the crowd after referencing Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old man who was shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers Thursday while his 5-year-old son was sitting in the back seat of his car. "I just want us to take a moment to think about Oscar Belgal tonight, and I want us to think and remember to just look after each other," Styles said. "So, please, continue looking after each other," he continued. "And remember, your friends, the people you love, the people who don't look like you and aren't born where you're from, they deserve respect, and love, and dignity and justice." PARAMORE'S HAYLEY WILLIAMS LAUNCHES VULGAR TIRADE AT DHS AFTER AGENCY DEFENDS ICE OFFICERS The remarks prompted criticism from film critic and commentator Christian Toto, who told Fox News Digital that speaking out against ICE has become a way for celebrities to gain approval within the entertainment industry. "This is the new black square on Instagram — speaking out on ICE gets you respect within your artistic community and endless positive press," Toto said. "I think the mainstream media has far more impact on public opinion. Social media does, too. Celebrities weighing in on matters like this? I suspect it doesn't move the needle at all. We view the stars as detached from our day-to-day lives, so we may agree with them on hot-button issues but they're not winning any converts." He suggested that entertainers face pressure within Hollywood to embrace political causes, while those who remain silent may be better positioned to avoid alienating fans. "There's an expectation within celebrity circles to embrace the cause du jour. The benefits are clear, and they're never held responsible when history doesn't align with their views. I suspect the stars who don't speak out at all fare best with their fans," Toto said. OLIVIA WILDE BREAKS SILENCE ON HARRY STYLES FANS AND THEIR BRUTAL REACTION TO THEIR 10-YEAR AGE GAP ROMANCE Styles' comments came as the shooting of Belgal sparked protests and criticism from New York officials, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Belgal was shot after allegedly refusing to comply with officers conducting a targeted arrest operation, Fox News Digital reported. Federal officials said he accelerated his vehicle toward agents, prompting them to open fire. During a Thursday night news conference, Mamdani said he personally urged Trump to release Belgal and condemned the federal immigration agency. "We know that ICE is rotten to its core. Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known..." Mamdani said. MAMDANI SAYS EVEN IF HE CAN GET ALONG WITH TRUMP, HE STILL DEMANDS THAT 'ICE SHOULD BE ABOLISHED' Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, defended the shooting during a Friday news conference alongside Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, saying officers believed their lives were in danger. "Our officers, using their training and believing that their life and the life of the partners and the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," Charles said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Officials said agents were unaware that Belgal's son was inside the vehicle. The child was unharmed. The Department of Homeland Security said Belgal had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests for assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. Federal officials also alleged ties to the Trinitarios street gang. "Please ask Mr. Styles which of Bengal’s prior criminal convictions, including fourth-degree grand larceny, and prior arrests for first-degree robbery: forcible theft armed with a deadly weapon, criminal sale of a controlled substance: narcotic drug, possession of stolen property, and assault, are worthy of 'respect?'" a DHS spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital."Imagine taking law enforcement advice from a man who dresses in women’s clothes while hiding behind armed private security," the spokesperson added. title: Yes, the SEC is still getting ridiculous preferential treatment in the AP Top 25 Poll
description: Texas dropped five spots after losing to unranked Oklahoma, while Alabama didn't budge after a home loss to Georgia in the latest AP Top 25 Poll.
content: It's getting ridiculous. Well, it's past ridiculous. The SEC, somehow, keeps getting preferential treatment in the AP Top 25 Poll in a way no other conference does. For some reason. And this week's poll might be the best example yet of how the bias among poll voters continues to impact the college football season. Let's look at how the voters handled some of the biggest results of the weekend, compared to how they handled previous results from teams with the wrong patch on the front of their jersey. WEEK 6 AP TOP 25 POLL SEES A MAJOR MIXUP AND A NEW TOP TEAM IN THE COUNTRY AFTER AN UPSET-FILLED SATURDAY To start, we can look at the Texas-Oklahoma game. While the Longhorns outgained the Sooners both in total yardage and yards per play, they were set back by two terrible fourth quarter interceptions from quarterback Arch Manning. Both at the worst possible time. One was returned for a touchdown, and the other effectively allowed Oklahoma to win the game in regulation. The Sooners were not ranked entering the week, and for good reason. They lost on the road to Michigan, scored just 14 points against New Mexico, and were blown out by Georgia 41-13. They're not a very good team. Texas may have outplayed them, but the very clear flaws in Manning's game cost them the result. A neutral site game against a middling unranked team that scored 14 points at home against New Mexico. The punishment for the Longhorns? Dropping from No. 1 to No. 7. When Ohio State lost as the No. 1 team in the country, on the road to the then-No. 4 Longhorns by one point after a miraculous comeback, they dropped from No. 1 to No. 6. Similar punishments for wildly different "quality" losses. Then there's Alabama. The Crimson Tide lost, at home, to the Georgia Bulldogs in a close game, though the Bulldogs averaged a whopping 7.5 yards per play to just 5.8 for Alabama. Though the Tide were denied a clear and obvious pass interference penalty in the fourth quarter that may have changed the game. Still, it's a home loss. Yes, Georgia is good, and yes, the score was close, but poll voters typically punish any team for losing a home game. And remember, Ohio State lost on the road to the presumptive No. 1 team in the country and dropped five spots. Not Alabama! Remarkably, the Tide didn't budge, going from No. 6 to...No. 6. After losing. At home. Why even play the games when they don't matter? Ole Miss has received some exceptional SEC treatment too. The Rebels resume now looks worse and worse, thanks largely to Florida and LSU's poor play. The Gators went from the darlings of college football to deservedly unranked in just a few weeks after an embarrassing blowout loss at home to South Carolina. The same Florida team that dominated Ole Miss 52-28, scoring 35 points in the second half. LSU, meanwhile, lost on the road to an unranked Kentucky team, their second of the season. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE So Ole Miss' big win now looks less impressive, and their loss went from "another quality blowout SEC road loss" to an indefensible blowout against a mediocre team. The Tigers spent a small fortune, at least $150 million, on hiring Lane Kiffin and revamping their roster. title: A cross country runner switched to the girls team midseason, parents voice their disapproval at meet
description: A Camas High cross country runner switched from the boys team to the girls team midseason, sparking national debate over transgender athletes in sports.
content: "Nobody wants to talk to you. I'm trying to be nice." That was the not-so-nice greeting I got from a Camas High assistant cross country coach in Arlington, Washington on Saturday. It came as I stood near the start line for the Women's Elite 5k race at the Nike Hole in the Wall High School XC Invitational. All I had done at that point was try to introduce myself, but it was clear that everybody involved with the school was on guard. The reason? One of the Camas runners entered in the Women's Elite 5K was a biological male. AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS' What's unique about this particular trans athlete is that he started the year on the boys team — with which he finished 76th in a JV race — then switched to the girls team last month. He has since taken first place in a varsity meet and finished second in a different invitational. This, as you might imagine, has sparked national attention, putting everyone at Camas on the defensive. But that assistant was wrong about one thing: Lots of people — mainly parents from opposing schools — wanted to talk to me. "We're about as liberal as it gets. I just don't agree with that [boys competing against girls]. I mean, if they find your body in 300 years, what are they going to say you were," said Kent Lake of Lake Stevens, WA. "Look, you can live any way you want. You got my blessing. But I mean come on, in competitions? It's like stock car racing. It's gotta be even, and it's gotta be fair." What prompted the Camas runner to switch from the boys to the girls team remains unclear. No Camas coach would talk (although one, along with a school administrator, was gracious to me), and the boy's mother wouldn't acknowledge my presence Saturday. WASHINGTON TRANS ATHLETE'S SCHOOL DISTRICT RESPONDS TO ALLEGED ASSAULT VICTIM'S SCOTUS INJUNCTION REQUEST But such a switch is permitted under the rules of the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA), which governs high school sports in the state. That doesn't mean most parents like it. "When I first heard about this story, I was like, 'Is this real? That can't be real'," said a mother of a cross country runner, who requested anonymity. She argued that allowing transgender runners to compete against girls could deprive female athletes of victories they otherwise would have earned. "We have daughters, and it's robbing them of an opportunity to compete." I LOST A STATE CHAMPIONSHIP TO A BOY. I REFUSE TO LOSE MY VOICE It should be noted that the Camas runner isn't a star, even among girls. He finished 39th in a field of 135 in Saturday's race with a time of 18:36.8. But had he run in the Men's Elite 5K, he would have placed last out of 159 runners by a good 30 seconds. Said one parent, also requesting anonymity. "Whether they finish first, 40th or 90th, they're still taking the spot of a girl." The anonymous route is the one that most chose last Saturday. One man wouldn't even let me record his voice — I had to repeat his quote into my phone using my own voice. This, after all, may be the most sensitive, contentious issue there is in sports. And ... not all the parents at Saturday's meet were necessarily against the Camas runner. One said, "People can identify however they want. High school sports isn't about winning, it's about student athletes building confidence." Another said, "There are more important things in sports than that [issue]." A third said, "I just wish people could have more empathy and compassion and understanding for people. I do think it's tricky if you start on one team and midseason change. I wish there was a space for everyone." Most, however, were like Kevin Ess, an Arlington High parent who had a compassionate but firm take on the matter. "I think men and women, young men and young women, have been competing for hundreds of years, thousands of years, separately," Ess said. "I think it's an interesting experiment. I think it's an interesting topic, but my personal opinion is that they should continue to compete separately." ATTORNEY FOR ALLEGED VICTIM OF TRANS ATHLETE SEXUAL ASSAULT SAYS SCOTUS FIGHT CAN HELP SET TITLE IX PRECEDENT One father said something similar after lifting his hoodie to reveal the XX-XY shirt he was sporting underneath. Another said allowing boys to compete with girls was "stupid" and that "Title IX was designed to protect women." A mother said, "I would be so embarrassed to put my son in a position like this." And though part of me agrees with that last part, part of me also wonders if it's a little harsh. I was genuinely curious about what the past few weeks have been like for the Camas runner's parents, but the mother completely ignored me on two separate attempts to talk. This was the same woman who reportedly started recording an athlete who protested the Camas runner last month by walking off the start line when the gun went off. That athlete was Skyview High junior Charlie Garrett, who staged the walk-off alongside teammate Sierra Retzlaff. Both wore body paint saying "Keep women in women's sports" that mid-September day — and both were on hand at Saturday's event as well. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Why is it so important for you to speak out on this topic?" Retzlaff said: "Because if we don't, no one else will. If we start something, maybe others will have the courage to join." Fortunately, there have been other girls and women who have spoken on this issue from Washington state and beyond. In fact, such courage helped get Initiative 638 — which would ban biological males from competing against girls in K-12 sports — on the Nov. 3 ballot in Washington state. The situation in Camas could very well mobilize people to vote. People need to get out and vote for what they want."

title: Steve Sarkisian’s ‘Joe Smith’ argument for Arch Manning is absolute nonsense for an average QB
description: Arch Manning's inconsistency at Texas raises real questions about whether Steve Sarkisian would have benched a lesser-known quarterback by now.
content: The narrative around Arch Manning at Texas would probably be a tad easier to deal with if head coach Steve Sarkisian would stop adding unnecessary fuel to the fire. We all understand whether the Longhorns quarterback receives a lot more attention than others across the country based off his last name alone, that's a given. But, at some point folks have got to start putting realistic expectations on the guy who is leading the Texas offense. COLLEGE FOOTBALL MEGA ROSTERS AREN'T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON ARE PROVING Right now, Arch Manning is a good college quarterback, and at times he plays like an average passer who has cost his team at least one game this season. Throw in the fact that he's the face of Texas football right now, and obviously there could be moments that the latest Manning quarterback is feeling the pressure. My goodness though, his head coach is not doing him any favors from a public perception standpoint. If this was 'Joe Smith', the Texas football team might be playing a different QB On Monday, Steve Sarkisian was asked by a reporter that if you took the name 'Manning' off the back of his jersey, would there not be all of the 'incredible' expectations on the quarterback. After starting his answer with the cliché talk of this being a team game, which it is, and the scheme of running the Texas offense, Sarkisian delivered this gem of an answer. ARCH MANNING RANKED FIFTH AMONG 2027 NFL DRAFT QUARTERBACKS AS EXEC QUESTIONS 'BLIND FAITH' BASED OFF NAME "I think if you took the name off the back of his jersey and you said 'here's Joe Smith playing quarterback at the University of Texas and here's a guy that's beaten four top-10 ranked teams in his last thirteen starts' we'd be praising the guy," Sarkisian noted. "The expectations are high for him, but he understands that. The expectations are high for all of us. So, we gotta put our nose back to the grind and get back to work." UNRANKED OKLAHOMA KNOCKS OFF NO. 1 TEXAS IN WALK-OFF FASHION AFTER ARCH MANNING'S ROUGH 4TH QUARTER For the love of all that's good, save us with this nonsense. If Manning was actually named 'Joe Smith', Steve Sarkisian would have already given the backup quarterbacks at least a shot at overtaking Arch Manning as the starter. The reality is that Arch has been very inconsistent at Texas, and that's ok. He's not going to wow the audience every week, which is something everyone in college football should recognize by now. NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM Also, the Longhorns should feel lucky that they don't have three losses on the season already, given that fourth-quarter performance by Ohio State and Tennessee's lack of offensive firepower outside of its rushing attack. Arch is getting no favors from Sarkisian, but the quarterback is not a first-rounder. We have now reached the point of trying to make sense of Arch Manning being an average college football quarterback by using his popularity as a reason for why he takes so much heat when things go wrong. It should just come down to the fact that if this were any other school or situation, Arch Manning is receiving the same type of critique as Josh Hoover at Indiana or Dante Moore at Oregon. ARCH MANNING ISN’T BACKING DOWN FROM EXPECTATIONS, AND NEITHER IS STEVE SARKISIAN, AS CFP SEMIS AREN'T ENOUGH But, since Steve Sarkisian wants to continue giving these types of answers regarding his quarterback, the outcry will only continue to increase if Manning keeps playing like this. ARCH MANNING OFFICIALLY GOES THROUGH THE PR SPIN CYCLE AND THE FINISHED PRODUCT SOUNDS AWFUL No, he doesn’t look like a top-10 NFL Draft pick, or even the top quarterback in this potential class. But sure, let's act as though Manning wouldn’t be receiving this type of criticism if he had a different last name. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There is a reality that if Arch did not have the last name, we might not be talking about him at all in relation with Texas. We could be discussing the starting quarterback for a Group of Six college football team. At some point, Sarkisian has to realize he's not doing his quarterback any favors with these answers.

title: Dementia risk more than quadruples among adults with common disorder
description: Adults with ADHD had more than four times the risk of dementia or mild cognitive impairment, a University of Pittsburgh study of 187,000 people found.
content: A common neurodevelopmental disorder could be linked to dementia risk, a new study suggests. Research led by the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, involving more than 187,000 adults aged 50 and older, found that ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder) was associated with a substantially increased risk of dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The observational study looked at electronic health records and genetic information of participants who were enrolled in the U.S. National Institutes of Health All of Us Research Program. 7 NEW DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS REVEALED — INCLUDING ONE MILLIONS STRUGGLE WITH Cognitive impairment was observed in 6.7% of participants with ADHD versus 3.4% without the disorder — nearly twice the rate. After researchers adjusted for age, gender and other health conditions, those with ADHD had more than four times the risk. The findings — which were published Oct. 7 in JAMA Psychiatry — only show an association and cannot determine that ADHD increases dementia risk, the researchers acknowledged. "This doesn’t prove that ADHD causes dementia, but seeing the same pattern show up independently in medical records and in people’s genes gives us greater confidence that the association is not simply an artifact of how ADHD gets diagnosed," said senior author Tharick A. Pascoal, associate professor of psychiatry and of neurology at Pitt, in a press release. "Two different kinds of evidence are pointing in the same direction." 3 THINGS TO AVOID IN MIDDLE AGE COULD MEAN 13 MORE YEARS WITHOUT DEMENTIA, STUDY FINDS Meanwhile, those with the highest genetic susceptibility to ADHD were found to have a 35% greater risk of dementia than those with the lowest susceptibility. "Analyzing genetic information alongside years of health records allows us to identify patterns that might not be visible in a smaller or more traditional study," said Guilherme Bauer-Negrini, co-first author and postdoctoral associate in biomedical data science at Pitt, in the release. "It goes back to nature versus nurture — particularly if we're starting at age 50, as opposed to starting at 20." "With this kind of data, we can start to investigate what may be driving this association and whether any of those factors could be modified to support healthier cognitive aging." Understanding the link Dr. Elizabeth Landsverk, a geriatric medicine and dementia expert with over 20 years of experience treating patients with Alzheimer’s and cognitive decline, noted that people with ADHD can have more difficulty with organization, which could contribute to the higher risk of cognitive impairment, although neurological differences may also play a role. "It might [be] that keeping on top of health issues and getting to the doctor is more difficult for them," Landsverk, a California-based doctor who is not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. The study also found that people with ADHD had a 20% higher incidence of utilizing health resources, she pointed out. "Having just signed up for Medicare, I know that it's really complicated — if you have trouble with focusing and getting things done, you may not be able to get the resources that you need," Landsverk said. "You may not be able to go to the doctor. You may not get your blood pressure taken care of. So there's probably a correlation." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "It goes back to nature versus nurture — particularly if we're starting at age 50, as opposed to starting at 20." ADHD vs dementia It can be challenging to distinguish between ADHD and cognitive decline, as some of the symptoms may overlap, according to Landsverk. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "I imagine it can look similar," she said. "You know, you don't remember why you went into a room. You don't know where your keys are, you don't remember the name of an actress." It is cause for concern if the individual struggles to take care of day-to-day tasks, the expert noted. "You can't pay your bills, you can't get your medications right, you can't get to your appointments, you tell people that you're going to do stuff and then you don't — that's when you need to get checked." Changes in judgment, mood or social behavior may be more suggestive of dementia than ADHD, Landsverk noted. Reducing the risk Although the study found an association between ADHD and cognitive impairment, Landsverk emphasized that some lifestyle behaviors can help people reduce their overall dementia risk. She pointed to maintaining a healthy weight, avoiding smoking and excessive alcohol, and staying physically active as important modifiable factors, along with controlling blood pressure, cholesterol and diabetes. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "There's a lot we can do," Landsverk said, recommending a largely plant-based diet and at least 30 minutes of daily exercise. Physical activity can also help improve mood and focus, she added. title: Mamdani unveils sweeping NYPD use-of-force review, but stops short of fulfilling key campaign promises
description: Zohran Mamdani launched a New York Police Department use-of-force review after the Win Rozario shooting, but it falls short of campaign pledges.
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the launch of an internal review of the New York Police Department’s use of force on Monday, but the initiative falls short of fulfilling several of his campaign promises, including pledges to disband a controversial police unit and eliminate a database of suspected gang members. "When the government uses force against a New Yorker, the standard for accountability must be at its highest," Mamdani said in a press release. "Every New Yorker deserves to know that force will be used lawfully, carefully and only when necessary." More than nine months after taking office, Mamdani has yet to fulfill several campaign pledges, including disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group, eliminating its database of suspected gang members and shifting police resources away from low-level offenses. NYPD COP FOUND GUILTY OF CHOKEHOLD IN FIRST CONVICTION SINCE RESTRAINT TACTIC BANNED AFTER GEORGE FLOYD DEATH The review comes after the May 2026 retirement of one of the officers involved in the 2024 shooting of 19-year-old Win Rozario — a development that came before any disciplinary trial could take place. Video footage of the confrontation, captured in March 2024, shows officers responding to a house call, placed by Rozario himself. An altercation ensued when Rozario, who was experiencing a mental health crisis, reacted adversely to the police presence, prompting the police to use Tasers on him. Unsubdued, Rozario then grabbed a pair of scissors and advanced on officers, who shot him at close range. New York Attorney General Letitia James' office declined to bring criminal charges against the officers in December 2025, concluding that prosecutors could not disprove beyond a reasonable doubt that their use of deadly force was justified under state law. The mayor framed his initiative as a way to strengthen and improve accountability. Mamdani’s initiative comes with an additional $2.6 million in funding for the Office of Inspector General for the NYPD. Additionally, the NYPD will also notify state authorities when officers facing disciplinary charges retire, allowing the state to consider decertification and helping prevent those officers from avoiding scrutiny by joining another law enforcement agency. Those changes will accompany a use-of-force review which, according to Mamdani, is the first of its kind in over a decade and will include a "robust community engagement process." "We have an obligation to Win’s family and to every New Yorker who calls for help in a moment of crisis. This review is about making sure our policies reflect that responsibility," Mamdani said. MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS MAMDANI WALKS BACK PLAN TO INCREASE NYPD HEADCOUNT FOLLOWING DSA PRESSURE Notably, the proposed adjustments fall short of campaign promises that Mamdani made to eliminate certain policing activity. In particular, Mamdani called for an end to NYPD arrests on charges of lower–level crimes like public urination and open container violations, noting that such activity was making it harder for officers to tackle violent crimes. "The fact that every year we ask them to take on additional responsibilities – we are making it more and more difficult for them to respond to the very responsibilities that drew them to the job in the first place," Mamdani said last fall. During his tenure, public urination summonses have gone up, climbing 18%, according to recent reporting. Mamdani also promised to end a database of suspected gang members. He also demanded an end to the Strategic Response Group (SRG), a policing task force that had received public attention for aggressive tactics in subduing protests. "As Mayor, I will disband the SRG, which has cost taxpayers millions in lawsuit settlements + brutalized countless New Yorkers exercising their First Amendment rights," Mamdani said in a post to X shortly after announcing his bid for mayor. LETITIA JAMES’ TIMES SQUARE SHOOTING PROBE DRAWS GOP CRITICISM OVER NEW YORK’S MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS In addition to keeping those elements in place, Mamdani also retained Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, who was appointed by Mamdani’s predecessor, Eric Adams. title: Hasan Piker tells comedian he's always wanted to be a 'champagne socialist' in satirical interview

content: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, a far-left YouTube personality, was asked about his $2.7 million California home and his time at the Oscar parties after telling a comedian during a podcast on Sunday that he always wanted to be a champagne socialist. How was [sic] the Oscar parties this year?" "It was weird. Jeff Bezos was there. Terrifying. A lot shorter than I thought he would be," he said, adding that his favorite part was meeting one of the actors from "Heated Rivalry." Piker attended Vanity Fair's Oscar party, and told the outlet in an interview, "I saw Jeff Bezos for a moment, but I tried to evade his peripheral vision. He’s the boss of a lot of people who were in that room, but he’s directly my boss. He owns Twitch, and my entire life is on Twitch." He said, "I bring a lot of positive PR to Twitch, but I bring a lot of heat to Twitch as well, so I have made it a policy to be as invisible as possible. I don’t ever want Jeff Bezos to know who I am." INSIDE HASAN PIKER’S RADICAL VIEWS ON AMERICA, ISRAEL AND SOCIALISM Ziwe also posed a question to Piker about his home. She said, "Now, Karl Marx said, 'to each according to his needs.' You live in a $2.7 million house. Why are your needs more important than 90% of other Californians?" Piker told Ziwe he thinks housing should be free and that his needs are not more important, confirming that his house was $2.7 million. "I mean, I have a mortgage. Like, I didn't, you know, pay cash for it. Some people think I just like literally went with like bags of cash and bought, that I have that kind of money. I don't," he said. MORE AMERICANS THAN EVER NOW HAVE A POSITIVE VIEW OF SOCIALISM, NEW POLL SAYS The comedian also said to the streamer, "I don't know if you can see or not, but there's sort of this irony, right? You criticize the Democratic Party for enriching themselves off the back of constituents while you enrich yourself by talking about progressive politics. What are your profit projections for the midterms?" "I have a cooperative corporation, equal say, equal pay. And on top of that, I don't run any ads. I used to, when I had a contract with Amazon, so that I get banned less often. Sometimes you have to play ball with big corporations to be able to have a platform. So overall, it's obviously always going to be impossible to have like the most ethical standards and, as long as you're not engaging in you know harmful or abusive practices. I think I have a fairly decent approach when I do merchandise, for example, I work with union-made, American-made garment manufacturers," the far-left streamer said. HASAN PIKER ADMITS HE HAS 'DIALED DOWN' HIS OPINIONS AFTER PUBLIC AND DEMOCRATIC BACKLASH CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "On paper, Ziwe shouldn't have given Piker a platform. He's vile. He promotes violence. He is everything wrong with the pundit class, and he already has a huge platform. That said, if you're going to invite Piker onto your program, the least you can do is press him on his outrageous comments. She didn't do that nearly enough, but she called out his wealth hypocrisy better than 98 percent of actual journalists," Christian Toto, editor of Hollywood In Toto, told Fox News Digital in a statement about the interview. "He had no good response, either. That's what happens when you rhetorically hit a bully in the mouth. Now, could some journalists do their job the next time they're granting Piker some interview time?" Piker has hit the campaign trail with some Democrats running in the November midterms and made several media appearances, including one with Axios, during which he said that the U.S. was worse than al-Qaeda. title: ATF suspends federal registration and approval rules for certain firearms
description: The ATF announced it will no longer require federal registration for silencers, short-barreled rifles and shotguns after Congress zeroed out NFA taxes.
content: Gun owners will no longer be required to federally register or seek advance approval to manufacture or transfer silencers, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns and "Any Other Weapons" (AOWs), the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) announced Friday. The policy directive halts National Firearms Act (NFA) enforcement for items subject to zero-dollar tax rates under the updated guidelines. In a letter to federal firearms licensees, ATF Director Robert Cekada noted that the move follows a federal court decision invalidating key manufacturing and transfer provisions of the NFA. GUN RIGHTS GETS 'GREATEST RESTORATION' IN 100 YEARS WITH LATEST TRUMP DOJ MOVE, LAWMAKER HAILS "The direction from the President, Congress, and the courts is clear," Cekada said. "ATF is now following suit with our enforcement posture while continuing to ensure we remain focused where we are needed the most: combatting violent crime in American communities." The regulatory shift stems from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, in which Congress reduced NFA manufacturing and transfer taxes to $0 for silencers, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and AOWs. GUN RIGHTS GROUPS CAPITALIZE AFTER JUDGE REVERSES DECADES-OLD RESTRICTIONS: 'MONUMENTAL' Following that legislation, a federal judge in Texas issued an injunction in August, concluding that because Congress eliminated the underlying tax, the NFA’s mandatory registration and transfer provisions could no longer be justified under Congress’s constitutional taxing power. The ruling initially applied only to the plaintiffs, but the Justice Department subsequently extended its nonenforcement policy nationwide. John Commerford, executive director of the National Rifle Association (NRA), praised the announcement, calling it a historic milestone. MAJOR APPEALS COURT DECLARES NEW JERSEY AR-15 BAN UNCONSTITUTIONAL IN LANDMARK SECOND AMENDMENT RULING "This is what happens when all three branches of government are willing to follow the Constitution," Commerford said in a statement. "Now the Trump administration has confirmed it will stop treating law-abiding Americans as if they still need special permission from the government to own hearing protection, rifles, or shotguns." Although the specific NFA requirements and fees have been suspended, all transactions remain subject to the Gun Control Act. Licensed dealers are still required to perform standard background checks and maintain transaction records. Machine guns and destructive devices remain subject to NFA requirements, while federal approval is still required to transport short-barreled rifles and short-barreled shotguns across state lines. title: Teen girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual plummet in stunning reversal, new data shows
description: Teen girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual dropped from 30% to 17% in four years, according to CDC data highlighted by The Washington Post.
content: The number of teenage girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual has plunged in just four years, according to new data highlighted by The Washington Post, revealing a dramatic shift in how young Americans describe their sexual orientation and leaving researchers searching for answers. The share of ninth-grade girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual dropped from 30% in 2021 to just 17% in 2025, while those identifying as bisexual alone fell by half, from 26% to 13%, according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data cited in the report. The percentage of boys identifying as gay or bisexual has remained largely unchanged over the past decade, while the share of high school girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual surged following the COVID-19 pandemic before beginning to decline, the Post reported. GALLUP POLL FINDS AMERICANS' SUPPORT FOR LGBTQ+ ISSUES SLIDING BACKWARD AMID CULTURAL SHIFT Although those numbers have continued to fall, rates among older teenage girls have remained relatively steady and are still higher than before the pandemic, the outlet reported. Jean Twenge, a professor of psychology at San Diego State University who published her analysis of the 2025 data on her Substack "Generation Tech," told The Washington Post that the downward trend began while former President Joe Biden was still in office, casting doubt on whether the shift could be attributed to a change in presidential administrations. In a recent post on X about the development, Terry Schilling, president of the American Principles Project wrote, "Amazing what happens when you cut the Department of Education and USAID." The available data also does not explain why such a political transition would affect certain age groups differently, according to The Washington Post. DETRANSITIONER CHLOE COLE CANCELS UW SPEECH AFTER ALLEGED ANTIFA THREATS Walt Heyer, who detransitioned 40 years ago after identifying as a woman for eight years and author of many books, including "Trans Life Survivors," cautioned against drawing sweeping conclusions from the findings, telling Fox News Digital that more research is needed before declaring a lasting shift. title: Fort Hood shooter should be executed '13 times over' — but not on live stream, survivor says
description: Julia Wilson survived the 2009 Fort Hood massacre and wants Nidal Hasan executed, but she has reservations about livestreaming his death penalty.
content: A survivor of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre says she wishes the mass shooter could be killed one time for every life he took that day – but even she is questioning the military's decision to livestream his death. Nidal Hasan, 56, is scheduled to face execution by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced earlier this month that it will be made available to stream to the public. "Why would people want to see that?" Julia Wilson, a former Defense Department civilian employee who survived the shooting 17 years ago, told Fox News Digital. Wilson wants the mass shooter executed, and, as a victim, she wants to attend his execution and look him in the eye. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist at the time, walked into a soldier readiness center on Nov. 5, 2009, on the Texas Army post and opened fire, killing 13 people and wounding 32 others. Following a military court-martial verdict, Hasan was sentenced to death on Aug. 28, 2013. FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD On Oct. 2, President Donald Trump approved the death sentence, and days later Hegseth announced it would be by a public firing squad. "Personally, I do want to be there," Wilson told Fox News Digital. "I do want to look him in the eye to let him know, ‘Look, I may have been your victim that day, but I'm not your victim anymore. I survived you. My child survived you, a lot of us survived you. You didn't do as much damage as you thought you were going to.'" "You did what you did," Wilson continued of Hasan's attack. "Too bad we can't kill you 13 times over." But Wilson has reservations about the decision to broadcast Hasan's execution to the public. "I'm kind of shocked that they're going to go so far as to televise it," Wilson said. "I don't really know how to feel about that." She fears broadcasting his death could pose a risk of exposing children to the kind of violence she has spent nearly 17 years trying to forget. "Unfortunately, some children may end up seeing that, that don't need to see something like that," Wilson said. "Seeing my soldiers murdered that day, that was the first time I've ever seen anything like that. And I can never wash it out of my mind." "I don't know why anybody would want to actually see something like that happen." Wilson's concerns echo objections raised by lawmakers on both sides of the aisle. "Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., posted to X on Thursday. "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America." TEXAS EXECUTES JAMAAL HOWARD DESPITE CONCERNS OVER LETHAL INJECTION DRUG USED IN FAILED TENNESSEE EXECUTION Trump said Saturday that he will make the decision of whether or not to livestream Hasan’s execution, acknowledging that he knows "what the military would like to do" following Hegseth’s confirmation. Vice President J.D. Vance also said Friday that he was not sure that the federal government will be livestreaming the execution, also adding that he would not personally view the livestream. "As far as the execution, I have a lot of mixed feelings on it, to be quite honest," Wilson said. "Yes, I'm glad that it's moving forward. No, I…don't ever want to see another human being die." "But in the same fold, an eye for an eye." Wilson was working at Fort Hood's Soldier Readiness Processing Center when Hasan opened fire. At the time, she was nine months pregnant and had reached her due date. She recalled the moment when she first saw soldiers down and heard the gunfire after pulling into the parking lot upon returning to the center from a lunch break with her mom. "Before I got the chance to shut off my engine and really get out of the vehicle, that's when the gunfire started," Wilson said. "I had several things go through my mind. You know, they say that you have fight, flight or freeze. I kind of had all three. " She recounted the chaos during the shooting after going into the center building for the first time since taking cover in her car, which she says her supervisor advised her to do. "Eventually he came back for me and I figured, ‘Okay, maybe… I'm a little bit out of the chaos.’ No, absolutely not," Wilson said. THREE DEATH ROW INMATES EXECUTED BY LETHAL INJECTION IN RARE SAME-DAY STRING ACROSS US She continued, "I get into my building. Desks are tossed everywhere. It's a total wreck. There's blood on the wall, blood on the floor, people working on people. And I just kind of locked up." "A wounded soldier came in the door opposite of me and said, ‘He's in the building, he’s shooting, get the f–– out of here." Wilson said that Hasan receiving the death penalty will still not bring full justice to the victims of the tragedy. She called out the federal government for classifying the shooting as "workplace violence," urging the shooting to be reclassified as an act of domestic terrorism. "We've been betrayed by the government for 17 years," Wilson said. "They left this as workplace violence. They never declared it domestic terrorism because it was all about, ‘Hey, we need to be politically correct and watch out for his rights.’ Well, what about my rights? And what about me? And what about my family? And what about those that were murdered? And what about those that were injured?" Wilson has written a letter to Trump calling for the reclassification of the shooting to be recognized as domestic terrorism. title: Texas hiker found dead after going missing in Great Smoky Mountains, family says
description: Sahil Jilani's phone, keys, and clothes were found near Abrams Falls before dive teams recovered his body in Tennessee's Great Smoky Mountains.
content: A Texas hiker has been found dead three days after going missing in Tennessee's Great Smoky Mountains, with his family believing he drowned after becoming caught in powerful hydraulic currents near a waterfall. Sahil Jilani, a 24-year-old resident of Houston, died after disappearing on Oct. 5 — the same day that left his mother with an "overwhelming feeling that something was terribly wrong." His family announced the tragedy through an online fundraiser. "It is with heavy hearts and profound sorrow that we share the sudden, heartbreaking loss of our beloved brother, Sahil Jilani, and the hospitalization of our mother after learning she had lost her precious son, our little angel and most beautiful gift," the fundraiser stated. BODY OF MISSING HIKER FOUND IN OLYMPIC NATIONAL PARK THANKS TO CRUCIAL CLUE Loved ones grew concerned when Jilani failed to check in for several hours and his location-sharing stopped in an area with no cell service. "We were advised to be patient, as hikers and campers frequently lose contact in areas without network coverage," wrote Jilani's sister Asma Jilani Bustamante who organized the fundraiser. "But as the hours passed, our fear grew, and we continued requesting help. Sahil knew how much his silence and unavailable location would worry us." NPS INVESTIGATES AFTER 23-YEAR-OLD REPORTEDLY SWEPT OVER NOTORIOUS YOSEMITE WATERFALL After he had been missing for 72 hours, Jilani's car was discovered in a parking lot, with his phone, keys and clothes later recovered near the falls. The following day, dive teams pulled his body from the waters at Abrams Falls. Family members believe Jilani drowned after becoming trapped in powerful water currents. TOURISTS CLING TO EACH OTHER IN DESPERATE STRUGGLE AS RAGING FLOOD SWEEPS THEM DOWN WATERFALL "Waterfalls are breathtakingly beautiful, and many visitors naturally want to stand beneath them and feel the pressure of the falling water," the family said. "What many don't realize is that Abrams Falls drops approximately 25 feet into a deep pool of water where hydraulic currents can pull a person underwater and trap them in recirculating water, making escape extremely difficult, even for experienced swimmers." An official cause of death has not yet been disclosed. MULTIPLE HIKERS DEAD AMID SCORCHING GRAND CANYON TEMPERATURES Jilani had recently become an uncle and was "beyond excited to spoil his little niece with gifts and teach her mixed martial arts and self-defense, sharing his passion for fitness," Bustamante said. National Park Service (NPS) officials warn that the Smoky Mountains contain narrow roads, blind curves, and steep drop-offs. Additionally, the park does not feature any lifeguarded swimming areas. The rocks are coated with slippery algae, and several hikers have fallen and been seriously injured or killed." Fox News Digital has reached out to the National Park Service for further comment.
