title: Mamdani calls ICE a 'rogue' agency after NYC shooting, claims agents view law as 'merely a suggestion'
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused ICE of being a "rogue federal agency" after an immigration officer fired seven shots at a man in Manhattan.
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of operating as a "rogue federal agency" and treating the law as "merely a suggestion" during a Sunday interview, days after a federal immigration officer fired seven shots at a man in Manhattan while his 5-year-old son was inside the vehicle. Mamdani, speaking to MS NOW host Jacob Soboroff in his first interview since Thursday's shooting of 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, accused ICE agents of repeatedly disregarding the law and questioned whether New Yorkers could distinguish federal officers from dangerous attackers. "We follow the law in New York City and I know that to the secretary, the law is merely a suggestion when it comes to the actions of these ICE agents," Mamdani said. "They are making a mockery of what law and order is." MAMDANI BLASTS FEDS FOR WAGING 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE AND TERROR' AGAINST NYC'S IMMIGRANTS The Department of Homeland Security pushed back against Mamdani's accusations in a statement to Fox News Digital, defending ICE and criticizing the mayor's rhetoric toward federal immigration officers. "ICE enforces the law as written. What makes someone a target for immigration enforcement is whether or not they are illegally in the U.S. — full stop," a DHS spokesperson said. "Mayor Mamdani should be thanking our law enforcement for removing these dangerous criminals from his city — NOT vilifying law enforcement." "Attacks and demonization of ICE law enforcement is wrong," the statement continued. "Because of smears like this our ICE officers are now facing a 1,600% increase in assaults against them as they put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists." EXCLUSIVE: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN SLAMS SANCTUARY POLITICIANS AS ATTACKS ON ICE OFFICERS SKYROCKET Mamdani argued that ICE's operations were making New Yorkers less safe and calling for the agency's elimination. "What we see from their actions is an agency that terrorizes, one that creates a sense of fear as opposed to any idea of safety. And I made it very clear that the longer that ICE agents were engaging in their operations in the city, the less safe this city was becoming," Mamdani said. The shooting occurred Thursday afternoon in the Marble Hill neighborhood, where ICE agents attempted to apprehend Belgal, a Dominican national whom DHS said had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests involving assault, robbery, drugs and weapons. NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at least one federal immigration officer fired seven rounds, striking Belgal in the neck below his left ear. His 5-year-old son, who was sitting inside the vehicle, was unharmed. Mamdani said he spoke with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin for nearly two hours Thursday evening in an unsuccessful effort to secure Belgal's release. He expressed frustration with the secretary's assessment of the shooting. "What struck me is the secretary did not think that ICE agents had done anything wrong," Mamdani said. "I am demanding that ICE cease their operations in our city immediately, because these operations make New Yorkers less safe. They leave New Yorkers in a state of terror." DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION On Friday, U.S. District Judge Paul Oetken temporarily blocked Belgal's deportation while his challenge to federal detention remains pending. The judge also restricted his transfer outside specified federal judicial districts without prior court approval. The NYPD, which was not involved in the shooting, released body camera footage showing officers responding to the scene after the shooting. The FBI and Homeland Security Investigations are investigating the incident. Mullin criticized Mamdani's anti-ICE rhetoric during a Friday news conference, accusing the mayor of inciting hostility toward federal immigration officers while refusing to support their enforcement efforts. "His words are dangerous and incite hostility. It doesn't help," Mullin said. "He said that ICE is rotten to the core. Really? title: Bill Maher reveals he's having dinner with Trump again, says he was 'really nice' by text

BILL MAHER REVEALS TRUMP WAS 'GRACIOUS AND MEASURED' AT WHITE HOUSE MEETING, SAYS HE'S NOT THE MAN SEEN ON TV Both Maher and Emanuel agreed it's better to talk with those they disagree with than not. title: Judge Judy credits Her Honor program with making her 'hopeful' for the next generation
description: Judge Judy Sheindlin's Her Honor Mentoring program celebrates 20 years of empowering young women through mentorship and financial literacy skills.
content: Judge Judy Sheindlin recently announced that she’s "rewiring" and letting son Adam Levy take the reins of TV courtroom drama, but she has plenty of other projects to keep her busy. The Her Honor Mentoring program she helped co-found just celebrated its 20-year anniversary. Sheindlin founded the program with her daughter Nicole Sheindlin to empower young women through mentorship and professional development. For the past two decades, Her Honor Mentoring has welcomed approximately 2,500 participants; 1,500 mentees, selected from 31 high schools across the region, and more than 1,000 mentors from 400 organizations and businesses. "I’m so happy to be here 20 years after our freshman year," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital. The project, she said, "started off with a dream" and all they could do was hope it was successful. The first class held only eight or nine women, whereas the most recent class in September saw over 100. JUDGE JUDY SHARES THE BEST PIECE OF PROFESSIONAL ADVICE SHE EVER RECEIVED AHEAD OF HER HONOR EVENT "It’s the combination of the mentoring and the financial part of it – which is the girls get paid for working… and learning how to dress for success, learning about making first impressions, learning how to manage your money and just knowing how to grow up financially prepared to be an adult," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital. The project, she said, is "simple, but satisfying." And she's been impressed and inspired by the young participants' drive to succeed. "This small cohort makes me hopeful," Sheindlin said. "I think that you become jaded when you see so much dysfunction. I’ve been around so much adult dysfunction and juvenile dysfunction, that to see young people still hoping and dreaming, wanting to work hard to realize their dream that their journey on this Earth is positive and fulfilling, makes you feel good. It sort of renews your faith that probably the vast majority of people are like these young women. That they want their lives to be productive and happy and fulfilling." Several of the former mentees have come back as mentors after starting their careers. "We’re teaching them to give back," she said. "We’re teaching these young women the importance of being not only for themselves. But then once you’ve realized that, to supporting others with your time and your talent… they have a drive, they want to be their own engines. They want to be the engine that pulls their own train." MORE GEN Z COLLEGE FRESHMEN ARE QUITTING SCHOOL EARLY AND MOVING BACK HOME WITH MOM AND DAD JUDGE ADAM LEVY PREVIEWS HIS ‘NITTY-GRITTY’ NEW SHOW – AND HOW HIS STYLE COMPARES TO HIS MOM JUDGE JUDY Sheindlin credited her stepdaughter Nicole as being "the engine that keeps the project running." Nicole, the current CEO of Her Honor Mentoring, said the program started as a reflection of her relationship with Judge Judy. She went to the same law school as her stepmother and sat on the bench with her when she was a judge in family court. Nicole called it the perfect model for the program, saying, "The power and the impact of having a professional woman, a strong woman be a mentor, be a guide, be a supporter." The mother-daughter duo concluded they should empower young women together to help women gain some extra skills and expand their professional network. "We’ve come to learn how much the mentors have grown and are inspired," Nicole told Fox Digital. "They’ve discovered that giving back empowers their own personal wellbeing." The program connects mentees with mentors across several industries. During 20 weekly meetings throughout the academic year, mentoring teams explore topics related to education, career and financial literacy. In addition, as part of the Her Honor experience, mentees complete four electives. The offerings include field trips, digital courses and creative projects. JUDGE JUDY HAS SCATHING MESSAGE FOR CITIES ENGULFED IN BRAZEN CRIME, PINPOINTS ‘RIDICULOUS’ POLICIES' The 2026-27 Her Honor class consists of 108 mentees and 123 mentors across 14 schools throughout Bronx, Rockland and Westchester counties. Mentee Keiry Alvarez and her mentor Lilliana Mendoza said they were grateful that the program helped them overcome their timidity. Alvarez, who said she was encouraged to join the program after her sister said Her Honor has helped her become more confident and outspoken. Mendoza was the first generation female to go to college in her family and a 2016 Her Honor mentee. She said the program helped her combat her shyness, gain people skills and find her voice. She added that it gave her specific guidance that has made an impact on her career as a police officer in the Mamaroneck Police Department. title: British adventurer returns home after 28-year walk around the world
description: Adventurer Karl Bushby swam the English Channel and celebrated with fish and chips after his 28-year, 30,000-mile walk from Chile to England.
content: Adventurer Karl Bushby has finally stepped foot on UK soil after a 28-year journey across the world. On Oct. 5, he announced he swam the English Channel, from France to England. While resting in Dover, he said, "I’m staring at the Union Jack flying outside this hotel. I’ve seen many flags over the days, but that one is special." On social media he shared one of his first meals back, overjoyed to have authentic British fish and chips again. DALE 'GREY BEARD' SANDERS RECLAIMS TITLE AS OLDEST PERSON TO THRU-HIKE THE APPALACHIAN TRAIL AT 91 His journey is not over yet. He hopes to reach the finish line — his mother’s home in Hull — by the end of the month. According to his website, he received a birthday card in the 1990s from his father about two soldiers arguing over an impossible feat, walking from London to New York via the Bering Strait. Karl grabbed a map and drew a single line, knowing he found his life’s mission. NAVY VETERANS REUNITE AFTER 30 YEARS FOR 'GRUELING' CROSS-COUNTRY BIKE CHALLENGE HONORING 9/11 On Nov. 1, 1998, the ex-paratrooper started his journey in Chile, with only a few hundred dollars in his pocket "South America, you were young, it was all new, it was the boys adventure dream," Bushby said. He walked north to the United States, waiting for the Bering Strait to freeze to cross from Alaska into Russia. In April 2012, Russia denied his next visa, pausing his expedition. So he started walking in the wrong direction, in protest, to the Russian Embassy in Washington, D.C. The ban was overturned and he carried on with his journey. From Russia he entered Mongolia, China, and swam the Caspian Sea from Kazakhstan to Azerbaijan. Then it was on to Europe. "You’ll find that you are way more capable than you think you are, people always underestimate themselves. The world always looks bigger and scarier than it actually is," Bushby said. MAN WHO BEAT RARE CANCER CELEBRATES BY CANOEING 2,000 MILES WITH HIS DOG He originally expected the journey to take 12 years, but visa restrictions, the 2008 financial crash, COVID-19, geopolitics, detention and some close calls slowed his progress. He says it’s the people that kept him going. "The world is an incredible place, and it’s the people, the strangers that I have met along the way, that have kept me upright and moving forward," Bushby said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Bushby has roughly 240 miles left to walk. He covered more than 30,000 miles, across 29 countries. "We went at a reasonable pace, we did what we needed to do and it has worked. I know it’s time to stop, I know that much because I feel that in the knees and ankles."

title: Pentagon data breach exposes records of over 3M people
description: The Pentagon data breach exposed 2.76 million Social Security numbers and military records, raising long-term identity theft concerns for veterans.
content: You can change a password after a breach. You can cancel a credit card. But when your Social Security number gets exposed, you could be dealing with the fallout for years. That is the concern after a major breach involving the Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center. If you have served in the military, worked for the Department of War or have other ties to the military community, your information could be among the records involved. A War Department official told CyberGuy that 2.76 million living individuals and 294,000 deceased individuals were affected. Depending on the person, the exposed information can include Social Security numbers, names, dates of birth, contact information and military personnel details. So, if a breach letter from the Pentagon shows up in your mailbox, don't toss it aside. Here's what happened, what may have been exposed and what you can do to protect yourself. DMV BREACH CONFIRMED AS HACKERS CLAIM 200,000 RECORDS STOLEN Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better healthcare. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com How the Pentagon data breach happened The breach involved the Defense Manpower Data Center, or DMDC. A War Department official told CyberGuy that a DMDC information system experienced unauthorized access to personally identifiable information by a small number of unauthorized users between October 2025 and July 2026. The official said DMDC immediately remediated the vulnerability after discovering it. At this time, the department says it has no indication that the accessed information has been misused. The files accessed contained unencrypted personally identifiable information. That created a potentially long exposure window before the vulnerability was discovered. Personal information such as a Social Security number can remain useful to criminals long after the original breach fades from the headlines. What information was exposed in the Pentagon breach The specific information varies depending on the person. According to the Pentagon, exposed records can include: The military details make this breach particularly sensitive because the records may reveal more than basic identity information. DMDC plays a major role behind the scenes at the Department of Defense. It maintains more than 60 million records covering military personnel, civilian employees, contractors, family members, retirees and veterans. The agency uses those records to support benefits, identity verification and other Defense Department programs. In other words, plenty of people who left active military service years ago may still have information stored in these systems. How to know if the Pentagon breach affected you People whose personal information was accessed are being notified by postal mail through the Department's contracted provider, Identity Theft Guard Solutions, or IDX. If you receive a notice, read it carefully rather than assuming it is another piece of junk mail. The letter should explain what information tied to you was affected and what protection is being offered. According to the War Department official, IDX is providing notification, credit monitoring and identity restoration support based on the data elements affected for each individual. Anyone with questions can visit response.idx.us/DMDC or call 1-855-744-4556. Be careful with unexpected emails or text messages claiming to be connected to the breach. Scammers can use major security incidents as an excuse to send fake notices or links designed to steal even more information. Instead of clicking a link in an unexpected message, verify the information using the official IDX contact details or the postal notice you received. WHY SCAMMERS TARGET VETERANS AND HOW TO FIGHT BACK Why stolen Social Security numbers create a long-term risk A credit card number has an expiration date. Your Social Security number usually stays with you for life. That can give criminals plenty of time to combine stolen information from one breach with information collected elsewhere. Someone might already have your phone number or an old email address. Adding a Social Security number and date of birth can make a stolen identity far more useful. A criminal could try to open credit in your name or use the information in a convincing phishing attack. Other forms of identity fraud may never involve your credit report at all. That is why I would treat a breach involving an SSN differently from one exposing an email address or password. What to do if your information was exposed A breach notice can leave you wondering where to start, so focus first on the protections that can limit what someone does with the information. 1) Enroll in the free monitoring if you are eligible If DMDC sent you an official notification, review the identity protection services available to you. Eligible individuals may receive 12 months of free credit monitoring and identity restoration support through IDX, depending on the information affected. Credit monitoring can warn you about certain changes to your credit file. However, monitoring usually alerts you after activity occurs. It does not stop someone from attempting to use your identity. If you were not contacted by DMDC, or if you want protection that continues beyond the free 12-month period, you may also want to consider a broader identity theft protection service. Depending on the service, it may monitor for suspicious use of your personal information and provide help if identity theft occurs. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at CyberGuy.com. 2) Freeze your credit Consider placing a credit freeze with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze restricts access to your credit file, which can make it harder for someone to open a new credit account in your name. You can temporarily lift the freeze when you legitimately need to apply for credit. A freeze remains one of the strongest free steps you can take after your Social Security number has been exposed. Keep in mind that a freeze focuses on new credit. It cannot stop every type of identity theft, including fraud involving an existing account. 3) Consider placing a fraud alert If you do not want to freeze your credit, you can place a fraud alert on your credit reports. A fraud alert tells lenders to take extra steps to verify your identity before opening new credit. You only need to contact one of the three major credit bureaus, and that bureau should notify the other two. A fraud alert offers less protection than a freeze, but it can still add another layer of scrutiny. PENTAGON DATA BREACH EXPOSES SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBERS, PERSONAL INFO OF 2.76M US MILITARY, CIVILIAN PERSONNEL 4) Watch your existing accounts Review your bank and credit card activity regularly. Also pay attention to unexpected changes involving accounts that use your identity. Turn on transaction alerts where available. Quick warnings can help you spot activity before it grows into a bigger problem. 5) Be suspicious of messages about the breach and use strong antivirus software Scammers pay attention to major data breaches too. You could receive a call, email or text from someone claiming to represent the Defense Department, a credit monitoring company or another organization offering to help you secure your identity. Do not hand over a Social Security number, password or verification code because someone contacts you unexpectedly. Also avoid opening attachments or clicking links in unexpected breach-related messages. Strong antivirus software can help detect malicious downloads, suspicious links and other threats that may show up in follow-up scams. Keep your security software updated and verify unexpected requests using official contact information you find yourself. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. 6) Protect important accounts with two-factor authentication Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) for your email, financial accounts and other important services whenever it is available. Your email account deserves special attention because criminals can use it to reset passwords for other accounts. An authenticator app or passkey can offer stronger protection than relying only on a password. 7) Get an IRS Identity Protection PIN If your Social Security number was exposed, consider getting an IRS Identity Protection PIN. An IP PIN is a six-digit number that helps prevent someone else from filing a federal tax return using your Social Security number. The IRS issues a new PIN each year. This can be especially useful after a breach because tax-related identity theft may not show up on a credit report. 8) Keep watching after the free monitoring ends One year of free monitoring is useful, but stolen personal information does not become harmless when that year expires. Continue checking your credit reports and financial accounts. Also pay attention to unexpected tax notices, benefit claims or bills that you do not recognize. We have previously explained why a credit freeze alone does not stop every form of identity theft. A stolen Social Security number can potentially be misused in ways that never trigger a traditional credit check. Kurt's key takeaways What stands out to me here is how long the information involved can remain valuable. A password can be replaced in a few minutes, but a Social Security number, birth date or military history can follow you for decades. If you receive one of these Pentagon breach notices, I would take it seriously even though officials say they have not seen evidence of misuse. Use the free monitoring being offered and consider freezing your credit. Then keep an eye on your accounts after that free monitoring period ends. We hand organizations an enormous amount of personal information because we often have no practical alternative. When that information gets exposed, the burden of watching for fraud suddenly falls back on us. If the government loses information as sensitive as your Social Security number, should it be responsible for protecting your identity for longer than one year? title: Season is already over for these four NFL teams after Week 5, you can write them off now
description: The Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, and Los Angeles Chargers are officially done, but several struggling NFL teams barely escape.
content: Five weeks into the NFL season, we can officially write off four teams. By "write off," we mean teams that are going nowhere. Their fans should be more concerned with draft position than anything their teams might accomplish this season. We understand how demoralizing it is to concede a season before mid-October. It is, nonetheless, the reality for certain franchises. Let's start with two teams that aren't tanking, per se, but weren't exactly built to contend this season. The Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals are about as bad as expected, despite the latter managing an early-season win. The positive is that both teams have stockpiled young talent while positioning themselves for a high draft pick. Miami's rookie class is impressive, including Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez, Caleb Douglas, and Chris Bell. Arizona has the best tight end in football in Trey McBride, while Jeremiah Love, albeit injured, has generational upside. Unfortunately, the 2027 quarterback class doesn't appear nearly as promising as anticipated. Arch Manning, to this point, hardly resembles the prospect analysts projected him to become. Elsewhere, the Tennessee Titans might be worse than both the Dolphins and Cardinals. That's particularly concerning because Tennessee spent the offseason actively trying to improve its roster and coaching staff. Through Week 5, the Titans rank last in the NFL in both scoring and total offense, averaging just 11.6 points and 246.4 yards per game. The winless Titans shouldn't be expected to win many games this season. After five weeks, we can also write off the Los Angeles Chargers, who entered the season with nearly the same Super Bowl odds as the Kansas City Chiefs. A team coached by Jim Harbaugh and quarterbacked by Justin Herbert should not be this inept. And yet, they are. At 0-5, with games remaining against the Rams, Ravens, Chiefs twice, 49ers, and Patriots, it's difficult to find many wins left on the schedule. A midseason parting with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel now seems more plausible than a late-season surge toward the playoffs. The Chargers' season, at least in terms of meaningful aspirations, is over. Based strictly on their play, the New Orleans Saints and Tampa Bay Buccaneers should join this list. Both teams have won just one game and have deficiencies on both sides of the ball. Despite relatively high expectations entering the season, the Saints have a minus-33 point differential. Neither team figures to be much of a factor in the postseason, if it gets there at all. However, both remain just one game out of first place in the perpetually mediocre NFC South. Likewise, the 1-3-1 Washington Commanders remain viable playoff threats largely because of the lackluster state of the rest of the NFC East. Granted, it's hard to take seriously a team that did that in overtime on Sunday The 2-3 New York Jets are the final team worth discussing. As WWE commentator Michael Cole told OutKick last week, the Jets remain poorly coached and overmatched in the trenches. In all likelihood, they are probably a bottom-10 team in the NFL–again. But we can't, in good faith, write off a team that sits just one game behind the Patriots and Bills, who play the Rams on Monday night, in the AFC East. We suspect the Jets will join this list by the end of October. For now, however, they've played well enough — including competitive games against the Lions and Packers — to keep the light on for a few more weeks. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So, through Week 5, the Dolphins, Cardinals, Titans, and Chargers are the only four teams we're officially declaring "season over." The rest of the fan bases should at least have hope, even for just a short while longer.

title: Biden-appointed judge with history of fiery Trump clashes erupts at DOJ: 'You've lost all credibility!'
description: Judge Ana Reyes screamed at government lawyers over 430 trees cut down at East Potomac Golf Links, demanding answers about late Friday notification.
content: A Biden-appointed federal judge who previously drew a formal misconduct complaint from President Donald Trump's Justice Department for alleged bias erupted at government lawyers again Monday, in a heated showdown over rapid tree removal at a historic golf course on national parkland. Judge Ana Reyes unleashed her latest rebuke during an emergency hearing over hundreds of trees removed from East Potomac Golf Links in Hains Point, D.C. Trump wants to transform the historic public facility into a championship-caliber golf course like his courses in the U.S., Ireland and Scotland – the latest courtroom collision between the administration and its political opponents. Journalist Scott MacFarlane, who live-tweeted from the hearing, described Reyes as "scream[ing]" at administration attorneys over the government's late-Friday notification that tree removal would begin Saturday. A government lawyer acknowledged that approximately 430 trees had already been cut down, according to MacFarlane. OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE TORCHES TRUMP ADMIN IN LATEST COURTROOM SHOWDOWN, REFERS ATTORNEY FOR BAR REVIEW "You've lost credibility!" Reyes told government attorneys, according to MacFarlane's live courtroom reporting. The administration maintains that the removals implement a 2019 National Park Service landscape-restoration plan predating Trump's redesign proposal for the links, which sit on an island connected to the city proper by the Jefferson Memorial and Francis Case Bridge at its western edge. BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP TO RESTORE SLAVERY, CLIMATE CHANGE REFERENCES AT NATIONAL PARKS Reyes, who was born in Uruguay and nominated by Biden in 2023, previously grilled a Trump administration attorney about his religious beliefs during litigation challenging Trump's restrictions on transgender military service — an order she called "biologically inaccurate" according to the Washington Post. The judge questioned how Jesus Christ would respond to "telling a group of people that they are so worthless, so worthless that we’re not going to allow them into homeless shelters?" according to then-DOJ Chief of Staff Chad Mizelle’s complaint. EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP’S DC JUDICIAL NEMESIS TARGETED IN MISCONDUCT COMPLAINT OVER ALLEGED BIDEN DOJ TIES In a 2025 case, Reyes ruled that Trump violated federal notice requirements when he fired several inspectors general but then declined to reinstate them, according to Reuters. Monday's hearing brought another heated exchange, this time over when government lawyers learned of the tree-removal operation and why they waited until the end of the workweek to notify the court. "At 4:55pm on a Friday of a holiday weekend, the plaintiffs and I get [little] notice that hundreds of trees are going to be chopped down," Reyes reportedly fumed at the government, according to MacFarlane. EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE When government counsel reportedly acknowledged learning of the operation on Oct. 8 or 9 and said officials were awaiting details, Reyes demanded: "Do you have email or a cell phone?" MacFarlane tweeted that he had never heard a judge "scream at full-voice at a lawyer before," while the UK Independent reported Reyes excoriated federal counsel for about 15 minutes. The uproar comes as preservationists and progressive interests challenge the administration, including former Obama ethics lawyer Norm Eisen — who has engineered a "broad legal resistance" to the president through his group Democracy Defenders Fund, according to its mission statement. Eisen tweeted a victory lap Monday after the court agreed to hear the case in an "emergency’ setting. title: Republican lawmakers break with Trump on diesel deal with Russia

content: President Donald Trump last week touted a diesel agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin, asserting that prices for the fuel would swiftly fall, but some Republicans have responded by rebuking the president's move. title: Benjamin Netanyahu's legacy and political future on the line in Israel's Oct 27 election
description: Benjamin Netanyahu fights for his legacy in Israel's Oct. 27 vote, the first since the Oct. 7 Hamas massacre reshaped the political landscape.
content: TEL AVIV, Israel: As Israel prepares to hold national elections on Oct. 27 for the first time since Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, massacre and the ensuing wars, Benjamin Netanyahu’s long political career and legacy are once again at the center of a vote some describe as the most fateful in the country’s history. Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, Netanyahu, has overseen the country’s transformation into a free-market, high-tech economy and a regional military powerhouse. Zvika Klein, editor-in-chief of The Jerusalem Post, told Fox News Digital that people under 20 "don’t even know an Israel without him being prime minister," aside from the brief period from 2021 to 2022 when a government led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid was in power for over a year. The two are running again on a joint slate in the upcoming elections. FLYDUBAI PILOT STABS FELLOW PILOT, ATTEMPTS TO CRASH PLANE, NETANYAHU SAYS Gadi Taub, co-host of Tablet’s "Israel Update" podcast, said Israeli voters will have one central question in mind when they cast their ballots: who is best positioned to continue the work begun under Netanyahu, foremost prosecuting the wars that have, to a large extent, dismantled the Iranian-led Shiite axis surrounding Israel. "The job is not finished. On the one hand, you have Netanyahu, who from the first moment, two days after Oct. 7, said that we are going to change the Middle East," he said. Eylon Levy, a former spokesman for the State of Israel, told Fox News Digital the election represents, for many Israelis, a critical opportunity to change course following what he described as the country’s biggest disaster. Benjamin Netanyahu, who has cumulatively served some two decades in office, is fighting for both his political future and his legacy. "He doesn’t want to go down in history books as the man on whose watch the Oct. 7 massacre happened; he wants to have a long political career ahead of him and take the really incredible military achievements of the last few years as a credit to his leadership," he said. NETANYAHU REVEALS HE WANTS AMERICAN FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL TO 'DRAW DOWN TO ZERO' "This is an election with a lot of anger about responsibility for the Oct. 7 massacre and about the social and economic cost of sustaining the war since," Levy stated. Few polls are projecting a majority for either the current government or the opposition bloc led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. The most likely outcome of the upcoming elections, Levy said, would be some form of deadlock, in which case Netanyahu would continue serving as caretaker prime minister until a new government is sworn in. Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022, amid prolonged political instability. Unlike the United States, Israel operates under a parliamentary system, with voters casting ballots for parties to represent them in the Knesset. The legislature has 120 seats and uses a system of proportional representation, with each party receiving seats based on the percentage of the vote it garners. The electoral threshold for parties to enter the Knesset is around 3.25%. IDF PUSHES BACK ON CLAIM IT TARGETS JOURNALISTS IN GAZA, SAYS 170 WERE PART OF TERROR GROUPS, INCLUDING HAMAS No party has ever won more than half of the vote. As a result, after each election, leaders of the larger parties seek to persuade smaller parties to join them in forming a governing coalition. "If one can get 61 of the members of Knesset, basically half plus one, to support them as prime minister, then they become prime minister and their teammates from the other parties join as government ministers," said Levy, who hosts Israeli Channel 16’s flagship international magazine program, "From Here to There" and its election podcast "EYLON:Israel Electioncast." Klein said this is the first time in several decades that an Israeli government has completed its full term. "There is a group called ‘Rak Lo Bibi,’ translated as ‘anyone but Bibi,’ and that’s the opposition groups, which includes Eisenkot’s party Yashar, BeYachad, headed by Naftali Bennett [and] Yair Lapid, and Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, all [of whom] have worked with Netanyahu in the past in different capacities," Klein said. The loose alliance also includes The Democrats, which Klein described as the most left-wing party in the so-called "change" alliance. NETANYAHU REJECTS BOARD OF PEACE'S GAZA PLAN: NO 'WITHDRAWAL UNTIL HAMAS IS GENUINELY DISARMED' The conservative commentator Taub said, "When you look at the candidates on the left, one after the other, they wanted to stop the war very early already in Gaza. Gadi Eisenkot, the leading contender on the left, wanted to finish the war after the pager operation, where he said we should cut a deal with Hezbollah. Netanyahu kept saying total victory," he added. The vulnerability on the right, Taub said, is that victory has not been total. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We have an existential danger. That danger is Iran, with the support of Russia and China, rehabilitating its nuclear program, which we can’t let happen. title: Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar’s DC home amid immigration fraud investigation

content: EXCLUSIVE: The home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn, was raided early Monday morning by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), a source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital. Multiple federal agents with HSI jackets were seen outside Omar's Washington, D.C. home in the early hours of Monday. Two sources close to the investigation say the search stems from a criminal fraud investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child. "Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation," a DOJ spokesperson told Fox News Digital. The DOJ later added that the investigation was "criminal" in nature. HSI is the principal investigative arm of DHS. Its scope includes investigating cross-border crime and global threats, including human trafficking and child sexual exploitation, drug smuggling and cybercrime. HSI plays a major front-line role in America’s counterterrorism operations. A spokesperson for Omar did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back," she said. title: US attorney warns Chinese espionage is 'extremely pervasive,' says Beijing 'playing the long game'
description: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli says Chinese espionage is "extremely pervasive" after his office charged alleged spies in recent months.
content: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said Chinese espionage is "extremely pervasive" in the U.S. following the arrest of an alleged Chinese agent in Los Angeles this month. Essayli told Fox News Digital in an interview that his office has pressed charges against several alleged Chinese spies in recent months, saying Beijing is brazen in its attempts to build their access inside the U.S. "I think it's extremely pervasive," Essayli said of Chinese spying. "China is one of our biggest adversaries, and they're committed to advancing their interests. And they're playing the long game, and so they are willing to put a lot of resources into developing sources, recruiting people within the U.S. to advance their interests. CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE "They're willing to steal our technology; they're willing to engage in espionage here. So, there's no limit to what China is willing to do. It is a huge, huge concern. We have to be vigilant, and we have to disrupt these operations on our soil," Essayli said. "We have to protect our sovereignty." "If you look at just the cases we brought this year, just in my office, I mean, you had cases where the woman from Irvine was engaged in espionage against the Taiwanese president's family member. I had a guy last week we arrested, he sold more than $300 million in SI chips, formerly known as AI chips, to China," he continued. "You had a mayor of a local city that we charged for serving as an unregistered agent of China as well, pushing out their propaganda and taking orders from China." FORMER CALIFORNIA MAYOR ADMITS TO SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING BEIJING PROPAGANDA IN US "So, it's extremely pervasive. It's a huge problem, but the FBI is on it," he said. "They have entire squads dedicated to combating this, and we're committed here at the U.S. Attorney's Office to supporting those investigations and bringing criminal charges to disrupt these operations." Wanying Zhang, 34, of Irvine, was arrested earlier this month for allegedly working with an associate to photograph and record the family outside their Seattle-area home, according to a criminal complaint obtained by Fox News Digital. CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN Authorities nabbed Zhang, who goes by "Heather" in the U.S., at the Los Angeles airport as she attempted to board a plane to China. title: Idaho professor falsely accused of student murders by TikTok psychic reveals fear for children's safety
description: Rebecca Scofield describes sleepless nights guarding her children after TikTok psychic Ashley Guillard accused her in the University of Idaho murders.
content: The University of Idaho historian who successfully sued a Texas TikTok psychic who had accused her, without evidence, of involvement in the murders of four students there has revealed fears for her children's safety — including sleepless nights standing guard as they slept — and other consequences of the ordeal in a new op-ed. Rebecca Scofield, 41, first became aware of Ashley Guillard's unfounded videos on Thanksgiving, less than two weeks after the murders. Court documents provide a raw account of what she went through. "I went and laid in my son's bed because his bedroom is the closest to an entrance to our house," she testified at trial. "And I was so afraid for him, so I just sat there at the end of his bed all night and watched him." PARENTS OF IDAHO MASSACRE VICTIM FACE DAILY NIGHTMARE WHILE DEMANDING DEATH PENALTY AFTER SHOCK PLEA TWIST Things got worse as time dragged on and Guillard posted more videos, she wrote Monday in a New York Times op-ed. "Over the next several weeks, while I was grieving with the rest of my community, this TikTok influencer uploaded over a hundred videos declaring that I had committed a quadruple homicide," she wrote. "The videos got millions of views. I was overwhelmed with calls, messages, comments and emails, many of which were disturbing or threatening. And I could have been anyone." GOT A TIP? She had trouble sleeping and found herself patrolling the hallway outside of her children's rooms at night instead. She stopped going to class and taught students remotely. While she hunkered down at home, she felt exposed there at the same time. Guillard's claims continued even after Scofield's lawyers sent her a cease-and-desist order, after Moscow police publicly stated the professor was not a suspect — and even after police arrested Bryan Kohberger in connection with the crimes. JONATHAN TURLEY: SOCIAL MEDIA ADDICTION WILL EASILY OUTLAST META'S MASSIVE MULTIBILLION-DOLLAR SETTLEMENT "I was not hit by a bus or punched in the face," Scofield wrote. "Yet I saw up close how the online world can come to feel more real than the physical one. Even after the actual murderer was arrested and convicted, the accusations against me continued. And even though these outrageous claims were made online by someone I had never met, they were amplified by unsuspecting viewers and algorithm-driven platforms, and the harm seeped into every aspect of my life." Scofield is also warning that social media giants face little accountability while amplifying potentially defamatory or damaging claims. "We can try to hold platforms accountable for the harmful content they spread," Scofield wrote. "A federal law, Section 230, protects online platforms from many defamation lawsuits, meaning that only individuals are liable for misinformation, even if a platform helped spread it. Proposals that would reform Section 230 range from adding exceptions for extreme cases to revoking immunity for social media companies altogether. title: Lane Kiffin claims ref told him 'he would have been killed' if he blew whistle before Kentucky touchdown
description: Lane Kiffin claims a line judge admitted he would have been "killed" for blowing the whistle on Kentucky's controversial goal-line touchdown.
content: During Kentucky's 35-34 win over LSU in Lexington on Saturday, there were a number of consequential plays. That's typically how things work in a one-point game decided in overtime, but it's safe to say one play in the first half will be sticking with LSU head coach Lane Kiffin for quite some time. With three seconds remaining in the second quarter and the ball on the LSU one-yard line, Kentucky was faced with a decision to make: kick the field goal and tie the game at 17, or grab hold of the momentum with a touchdown. Kentucky head coach Will Stein opted for the latter option, and Wildcats quarterback Kenny Minchey punched it into the end zone at the end of the half, but it wasn't without controversy. The LSU defense appeared to stop Minchey at the goal line as the rugby-like scrum came to a stop, but a second effort by the Kentucky offensive line eventually pushed the quarterback across the goal line. It was one of those instances in which the officials could have blown the play dead before the runner was down, but instead, there was no whistle, and the Wildcats were awarded a touchdown. LANE KIFFIN IS STARING DOWN DISASTROUS YEAR ONE AS OFFSEASON PLEAS FOR PATIENCE FALL ON DEAF EARS During a Sunday press conference, Kiffin was asked about the specific play at the end of the opening half, and claimed that the line judge told him "he would have been killed" if he blew the play dead. "The line judge just said that, in that situation, there was too much at stake," Kiffin explained. "He said he would have been killed if he had blown the whistle for the play being stopped, even though it appeared to be stopped. "My complaint is that you can’t refuse to blow the whistle because it’s such a big play. If you would have blown that whistle on first down, or with 10 minutes left in the game, for forward progress being stopped, then blow it for protection and for the way the ruling is supposed to work. Don’t not blow it because it’s such a big play. The rules are the rules." WILL STEIN'S DAD STORMS THE FIELD AFTER KENTUCKY'S UPSET WIN OVER LSU IN BEAUTIFUL COLLEGE FOOTBALL SCENE Officials opting to keep their whistles in their pockets before halftime wasn't the only controversial moment of Saturday's thriller at Kentucky. After LSU scored with ease to begin overtime, Kentucky answered back with a score of its own before opting to go for two and win the game. title: College football’s mega rosters aren’t delivering a return on investment as LSU, Texas A&M and Oregon prove
description: Mike Elko called TexAgs a "cesspool" after Texas A&M's third loss, while LSU's Lane Kiffin faces fan fury over a $100 million coaching investment.
content: If you were looking for chaos in college football, this past weekend provided plenty of examples of teams that have sent their fan bases into panic mode, while donors freak out after millions of dollars were spent assembling rosters. We watched Lane Kiffin get escorted through a swarm of Kentucky fans who stormed the field after the Wildcats pulled off an overtime upset against an LSU team that was one of the biggest stories of the offseason, thanks in part to their self-indulgence. KIRBY SMART HAS ENTERED HIS MOST DANGEROUS ERA AFTER GEORGIA'S AGGRESSIVE WIN OVER ALABAMA: THE FAMILY TALES Just hours earlier, Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko decided it was smart to go after one of the biggest team-centric websites in all of college football, because it's obviously TexAgs' fault that the Aggies head coach has fumbled a roster littered with expensive pieces. Then there was the Red River Rivalry, which delivered one of the most shocking games of the season. Oklahoma knocked off No. 1 Texas on a last-second field goal, forcing Longhorn fans to reevaluate their expectations over the next two months. And then, it's the story of UCLA going into Eugene and dissecting the Oregon Ducks, behind the incredible coaching job Bob Chesney has done this season with the Bruins that have them undefeated and ranked No. 15 in the latest polls. What do all of these outcomes from Saturday have in common? Money can't buy you heart, or even cohesiveness, when you finally spot the ball. Sorry, LSU. This isn’t about your nine-game conference schedule If LSU fans have to hear the word patience one more time from their head coach, Lane Kiffin, the fan base is going to combust with two months left in the regular season. And no, playing an additional conference game is not the reason why some teams are dealing with the injury bug, even if Kiffin wants to awkwardly joke about why his squad is fighting through a tumultuous time. LANE KIFFIN IS STARING DOWN DISASTROUS YEAR ONE AS OFFSEASON PLEAS FOR PATIENCE FALL ON DEAF EARS The Tigers were beaten by Kentucky this past weekend because this squad doesn’t know how to finish games, or get fooled by the highlights that Sam Leavitt creates on an occasional basis. LSU spent over $100 million on a coaching change that saw Kiffin bolt from Ole Miss with the attitude that he was going to immediately build a roster capable of fighting for a CFP title this season, and the school had zero problems flaunting it. WILL STEIN'S DAD STORMS THE FIELD AFTER KENTUCKY'S UPSET WIN OVER LSU IN BEAUTIFUL COLLEGE FOOTBALL SCENE In reality, the steam is starting to rise out of the overcooked gumbo, and the preseason chatter from within Baton Rouge is starting to look like an overcooked crawfish. You cannot ask for patience from an LSU fan base that has done everything asked of them over the past six years, and that included sitting through the final years of Brian Kelly. This is a football team that spent over $45 million on its roster, and already has two losses on the season, with the latest coming against first-year Kentucky head coach Will Stein. There is no time for patience, as Kiffin is finding out just over one month into the regular season. Mike Elko has a problem, and it doesn’t have anything to do with a fan site So, Texas A&M, floundering once again has finally caught up with their head coach, and it came during one of the more awkward press conferences we've seen from a team out of College Station, and that's saying something. Remember how many times I've written about donors of the Aggies program receiving a return on investment for the amount of money contributed to helping build a roster outside of what the actual school spends? After their third loss of the season, once again in lopsided fashion, Texas A&M fans are officially hitting the panic button. It wasn’t even close this past weekend, as Missouri thumped the Aggies 27-6. SEC FILES BOMBSHELL LAWSUIT AGAINST LSU, LANE KIFFIN AND TIGERS ATHLETIC DEPARTMENT And, since we are living in a world of "win now" based off the transfer portal and the amount of money being spent on rosters, Aggie fans are not in the mood to hear about 'building' with quarterback Marcel Reed and this expensive football team. It's one thing when you're losing games in dramatic fashion, like what transpired with the Texas Longhorns against Oklahoma. But, the Aggies have been destroyed, and it's not the fault of their loyal fans, a majority of which subscribe to TexAgs.com on a monthly basis. But Mike Elko, when asked about what he would say to the fans who are upset with the Aggies disastrous 1-3 SEC record, decided it would be smart to call out site-owner Billy Lucci. MIKE ELKO CALLS OUT TEXAS A&M FANS WHO ARE PART OF MASSIVE WEBSITE AS AGGIES SPIRAL AFTER ANOTHER HUMILIATING LOSS If you aren’t familiar with Lucci, the man built one of the largest websites in college sports that also hosts a plethora of influential donors on its website message boards in support of Texas A&M athletics. "There’s a difference to me between the fan base and social media, and so there’s one group that I really don’t care much about. Billy [Liucci’s] cesspool can go be Billy’s cesspool," Elko profoundly mentioned. "Our fan base: Stay with us. Be behind us. "We’re going to build something. That’s what we told you we were going to build. We’re in a really bad spot right now, but we’ll work our way out of it," Going after one of the most influential voices in college athletics' is not the smartest decision, especially when a majority of the fan base subscribes to this website, and is also beyond agitated with results in 2026. Good luck with that, Mike. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Dan Lanning is owning it. Steve Sarkisian is lucky Texas only has one loss Let me be clear: just because the Oregon head coach is saying all of the right things does not make this any easier for the fans. It surely doesn’t make mega-booster and Nike owner, Phil Knight, any less upset with the current results. But right now, Oregon finds itself with two losses on the season and the latest came without Dante Moore who was still recovering from a concussion. Even then, the story shifted from the Ducks potential Big Ten title run, to Bob Chesney having UCLA looking like the Bruins of old in one of the best stories we've seen this season. The Ducks find themselves fighting an uphill battle, and cannot afford another loss with a roster that is worth well-north of $40 million. And if we're being honest, this looks like a team bound for an eight-win season, which is another prime example of no return on investment during this chaotic time in college athletics. As for the Texas Longhorns, someone finally made them pay for the mistakes. Sure, it's surprising that Oklahoma was the team that handed them their first loss of the season. But if you've really been paying attention to this Texas squad, you'd realize that if Ohio State could’ve finished the job in Austin, and Tennessee had an offensive pulse outside of its running game, this could’ve actually been Texas' third loss of the season. He's not a bust, or however one outlet decided to characterize him at one point last season. Manning is just a good college quarterback, with a lot to get better at. He's not great. Maybe one day he will be. Right now, he's just an average quarterback that threw two interceptions against Oklahoma, with one returned for a touchdown. For Texas, it can rely on its defense to get them through games, and maybe steal a few in the process (Tennessee). But unless Steve Sarkisian comes up with a number of different looks, or hands over play-calling duty, this team is bound to catch another loss, or two. You are witnessing one of the more chaotic opening months to a college football season in recent memory. In the midst of it all, there are a number of very rich boosters across college football who are wondering what they are getting for the millions of dollars spent to help their favorite team have success. title: NFL linebacker and amateur preacher Demario Davis delivers amazing sermon on winning and life
description: During the Jets' chapel service, Davis tied Proverbs 13:12 and the tree of life to perseverance through adversity in the NFL, relationships and careers.
content: Demario Davis makes his living as an NFL linebacker for the New York Jets but lives his life by the Bible that has turned him at times into something of an amateur preacher. Both were on full display on Sunday during, and then after, the Jets' victory over the Cleveland Browns that ended a three-game losing skid for the Jets and ended a three-game win streak for the Browns. Davis shared afterward that during the Jets' chapel service on Saturday one of the verses shared was Proverbs 13:12. "Hope deferred makes the heart sick, But when the desire comes, it is a tree of life." CLEVELAND BROWNS PLAYERS PUBLICLY BAPTIZED AT CLEVELAND FOR CHRIST EVENT IN POWERFUL DISPLAY OF FAITH Davis saw his team, its game against the Browns, and even what fans and people face every day, in that verse. "I would go as far as to say this was a historic win for this organization," Davis said. "When you talk about a team that's coming in that has won three games, that type of momentum in this league is very hard to get and it makes it very strong and feels insurmountable at times. "And you're talking about a [Jets] team that was 0-3 or had lost the last 3 games. And when you're going through that type of adversity, it can weigh on you. It can weigh on you emotionally. it can weigh on your faith, it can weigh on your belief. "And it can weigh on an organization that has historically been disappointed." Jets fans in the congregation shout amen. Jets 17. Browns 12. "We get the chance to experience that tree of life, which is victorious," Davis said. "And the reason why that word is so important is because football is the greatest teacher of life. I'll always say that." But, you see, the message Davis had from the Bible verse wasn't written for the NFL. It may include situations in the NFL, but Davis understands it applies to everyone. THE NFL IS AMERICA'S MOST GOD-CENTERED PROFESSIONAL SPORTS LEAGUE AND SUNDAY'S GAMES CONTINUED TO PROVE IT "Right now, people are fans of the game and watch the game, but they have life happening," he said. "It could be a relationship. It could be a job. It could be something going on with the kids. It could be something that's strange. And when you go through adversity, you want to give up. "Sometimes you want to give up before you even start – before you even try. Like, I've been going through this in my relationship, I don't I don't even want to try anymore. I've been going through this in my job. I just got let go or I don't know how I'm going to make ends meet. And you just want to give up." But here's where perseverance pays off – at the tree of life. "God wants you to know that when the enemy wants you to quit when he's making your heart sick, when you're going through hard times, man, if you just get to the other side, it's a tree of life," Davis said. "And that's what I want this opportunity to represent is, just keep going for somebody who's going through a hard time, somebody who's going through something, man. And that medicine might be counseling a relationship. It might be just keep showing up at your job doing the right thing. You're going to get seen. That promotion is on the way. "It could be a relationship that you said you were going to let go and and y'all had some beef, a family member or something. Just reach out one more time. Just do something, keep doing the little things and you watch it process for you." That persistence, Davis implored, will get you to the goal, to the tree of life. title: 'The Social Reckoning' Review: Zuckerberg, Facebook are the enemy in preachy slop disguised as journo drama
description: Fox News Digital reviews Sony Pictures' "The Social Reckoning" starring Jeremy Strong, Jeremy Allen White and Mikey Madison, and written and directed by Aaron Sorkin.
content: In the era of Trump 2.0, the tech titans once championed by the liberal left have been ostracized for the appearance of embracing or bending the knee to President Donald Trump after the 2024 election, whether it be Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos or — in this particular case — Mark Zuckerberg. Zuckerberg, co-founder of Facebook and the CEO of Meta, was famously depicted on the big screen in the 2010 film, "The Social Network," which followed his creation of the culture-reshaping social media platform from his Harvard dorm room and the lawsuits that ensued after. Directed by David Fincher, written by Aaron Sorkin and with dead ringer Jesse Eisenberg playing Zuckerberg, the trio delivered one of this century's greatest films that truly captured the zeitgeist of the emerging digital age. Sorkin won an Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay and both Fincher and Eisenberg scored nominations in their respective categories. But 16 years later, what's been billed as a sequel to "The Social Network" only tarnishes its legacy. DIGGER REVIEW: TOM CRUISE DESTROYS THE PLANET IN ALEJANDRO IÑÁRRITU'S GRANDIOSE, MESSY POLITICAL SATIRE For "The Social Reckoning," neither Fincher nor Eisenberg chose to return, leaving Sorkin to both write and direct the sequel that no one really asked for and cast Jeremy Strong ("Succession," "The Apprentice") as Zuckerberg. The sequel revisits the Wall Street Journal's bombshell series of reports dubbed "The Facebook Files," spearheaded by investigative reporter Jeff Horowitz (Jeremy Allen White) and Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison). The uncovered dirt ranged from Facebook implementing algorithms that drove its users to join hate groups to the company knowing about the toxicity of Instagram on the mental health of young girls. Most of us can agree that social media platforms broadly, not just Facebook, have negative impacts on society, while also having benefits. What was previously reported about Facebook has been a stain on the company. And maybe that does warrant a movie. What's disagreeable is the narrow universe Sorkin creates, one where Facebook, and only Facebook, is responsible for fomenting right-wing radicalism and that left-wing radicalism is nonexistent. ‘PRIMETIME’ REVIEW: ROBERT PATTINSON CHANNELS CHRIS HANSEN IN RIVETING DRAMATIZATION OF ‘TO CATCH A PREDATOR’ In the film, Haugen, the Facebook data scientist who made waves when she came forward in 2021, is haunted by a former friend, who she described as once being a "progressive" but has been radicalized by the platform becoming an unhinged racist. The film also blames Facebook for the spread of QAnon conspiracy theories and vaccine "lies," as well as Jan. 6. The culminating scene of "The Social Reckoning" involves Zuckerberg and his staff rushing to their war room to watch news coverage of the Capitol riot. The rioters might as well have been waving flags that read, "Brought to you by Facebook," at least according to Sorkin. Everyone around Zuckerberg demanded him to ban Trump from their platform. And as we all know, Zuckerberg acquiesced. Haugen's findings, at least presented in this film, show that Facebook makes people racists. There's no mention of any sort of far-left radicalization Americans have witnessed, (or "Woke 1" as AOC recently coined) nor any mention of the Black Lives Matter riots that erupted across the country in the months leading up to Jan. 6. Lest we forget that the COVID lockdowns truly fueled societal paranoia, there isn't any "reckoning" from Sorkin for the government officials who enforced them. For a man who prides himself on his hyperintellectual dialogue, Sorkin finds little room for nuance. ‘RESIDENT EVIL’ REVIEW: DIRECTOR ZACH CREGGER DELIVERS INFECTIOUS REBOOT TO GORY VIDEO GAME FRANCHISE The film's only saving grace is how it goes about Zuckerberg's stance as a free speech absolutist. Sorkin broadly portrays him as a sociopathic villain who cares about the bottom line at society's expense. But there's one scene where he's arguing with a former investor (played by Bill Burr) that Facebook is a public square and that its users don't need to be treated like children, as Burr's character deems Zuckerberg's philosophy reckless for letting falsehoods go unfettered. It's clear Sorkin wants his audience to be on Team Burr in that particular scene, but true champions of free speech side with Zuckerberg — at least until he caves to pressure and bans Trump. "The Social Reckoning" attempts to be the "All the President's Men" of the social media era, but it lacks any emotional depth beyond its blatant appeal to partisan leftists. None of the film's three leads operate like normal human beings (to be fair, Zuckerberg's public persona has always been, well, peculiar). Every scene between Horowitz and Haugen is full of unnaturally witty and scholarly dialogue that could've easily been borrowed from "The West Wing." It's tiresome. 'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN Unlike his predecessor in "The Social Network," Strong looks remotely nothing like Zuckerberg but gives a dedicated performance and, admittedly, kind of nails the voice. The Facebook chief had no involvement with either film, so it's difficult to tell where the reality ends and the fiction begins. Yet Eisenberg's Zuckerberg was far more emotionally ranging, while Strong's Zuckerberg is essentially an alien-like caricature. There's also a stark contrast in the pure filmmaking. Without Fincher at the helm, Sorkin is left artistically rudderless despite his top-notch collaborators like Oscar-nominated cinematographer Jeff Cronenweth (who previously shot "The Social Network") and Oscar-winning composer Alexandre Desplat. This isn't Sorkin's first time in the director's chair. There's no questioning his talents as a screenwriter, but while he has successfully found his unique voice on the page, he has yet to craft his own vision as a director. Having rewatched "The Social Network," it's wild to think both were written by Sorkin. One is captivating, smooth, biting and tangible to the average viewer. The other is dull, disjointed, self-righteous and elitist. CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS The Verdict "The Social Reckoning" tries to recreate the magic of its predecessor. In reality, it's leftist revisionist slop disguised as a harrowing journalist drama. It's a film that only caters to a narrow audience of coastal liberals who despise Zuckerberg/Trump and journalists who regard themselves as heroes — many happen to be both. What's unfortunate is that "The Social Reckoning" doesn't exist with the purpose of entertaining. Its purpose is to lecture. And for that reason, Sorkin ought to log off. ★ — SKIP IT "The Social Reckoning" is rated R for language. Running time: 1 hour, 52 minutes. In theaters now. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

title: This Michael Jordan game-worn jersey just became the most expensive piece of basketball memorabilia ever
description: Miami investor Ron Firman now owns Michael Jordan's autographed Game 2 jersey, the third 1998 Finals piece to sell for eight figures recently.
content: Michael Jordan hasn't played an NBA game in more than two decades, but "His Airness" is still putting up record-breaking numbers. A game-worn, autographed Jordan jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals, the Finals featured in the hit documentary "The Last Dance," has sold for an eye-popping $14 million in a private sale, making it the most expensive piece of basketball memorabilia ever sold. Pennsylvania-based Hunt Auctions announced the blockbuster deal Monday morning, revealing that Miami real estate investor Ron Firman is the proud new owner of the iconic red Chicago Bulls jersey. WILT CHAMBERLAIN WARM-UP JACKET BOUGHT FOR $3 AT THRIFT STORE SELLS FOR TENS OF THOUSANDS MJ wore the jersey during Game 2 of the 1998 NBA Finals against the Utah Jazz on June 5, 1998, when the Bulls evened the series at 1-1. Chicago eventually captured its sixth championship in eight seasons, completing Jordan's legendary run with the franchise and further solidifying himself as the GOAT (Greatest of all Time) in my opinion. "While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art," Hunt Auctions president David Hunt said. And he's not exaggerating. MICHAEL WILBON REVEALS JORDAN'S TRUE FEELINGS ABOUT LEBRON The $14 million sale ranks as the second-highest known price ever paid for a game-worn jersey across all sports. The only jersey ahead of Jordan's? Babe Ruth's famous "called shot" jersey from the 1932 World Series, which fetched an astonishing $24.12 million in 2024. But here's where things get even crazier. This is now the third Jordan jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals to sell for at least $10 million. His Game 1 jersey sold for approximately $10.1 million in 2022, while his Game 3 jersey brought in roughly $12.3 million just last month. That's more than $36 million spent on three jerseys from one championship series. DARREN ROVELL SHOWS OFF ONE HIS FAVORITE KNICKS MEMORABILIA ITEMS, WHICH INCLUDES NOTORIOUS MENENDEZ BROTHERS As for Firman, the man who just dropped eight figures on a piece of basketball history, he kept his reaction relatively simple. "Michael Jordan was an incredibly talented player who is admired around the world," Firman said. "I'm very excited about the purchase." You'd certainly hope so after spending $14 million. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE According to Hunt Auctions, the jersey was originally purchased from the Bulls by a private collector in 2003 and has changed hands only once since that initial purchase. Of course, the obsession with Jordan's final championship season doesn't stop at jerseys. In 2023, a pair of Air Jordans worn by MJ during Game 2 of those same Finals sold for $2.2 million through Sotheby's, setting a record at the time for the most expensive sneakers ever sold. Nearly 30 years after Jordan sank his iconic championship-winning shot against Utah, collectors are still willing to spend fortunes to own a piece of his legacy. title: Josh Brolin calls 'Sicario 3' cast work 'untouchable' as franchise moves forward without Sheridan script
description: Josh Brolin reveals the third "Sicario" film is still in the notes process as he reunites with Benicio Del Toro and Emily Blunt for the sequel.
content: More information is coming out about the highly-anticipated third "Sicario" movie. The gritty film franchise created by Taylor Sheridan is one of the best productions you can find in cinema over the past fifteen years, especially the original in 2015. It was recently confirmed that a third film is happening, but there were competing reports about whether Sheridan would be leading the way with his writing again. TAYLOR SHERIDAN RETURNS TO MOVIES AFTER FIVE YEARS WITH NASA THRILLER, POLITICAL DRAMA It turns out the answer, unfortunately, is no. Steven Knight will write the script. Josh Brolin addresses Taylor Sheridan not writing "Sicario 3." Brolin, who plays CIA operator Matt Graver in the franchise, is returning for the third film, along with Benicio Del Toro and Emily Blunt. Blunt did not appear in the sequel, but played a major role in the original film. Brolin recently spoke with ScreenRant about the upcoming third picture, and touched on the status of the script and writing.
