title: Zelenskyy accuses Putin of defying Trump's ceasefire push, sends pointed message to White House
description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy accuses Vladimir Putin of attacking Ukraine's gas infrastructure hours after Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire.
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Fox News on Monday that Russia continued attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure despite President Donald Trump's announcement of what he called an immediate energy ceasefire, accusing Vladimir Putin of rejecting Washington's peace efforts and calling for greater pressure on Moscow. "We are ready today for energy ceasefire, as President Trump said. But I'm not sure that Putin is ready because even after yesterday's messages from the president about energy ceasefire, Putin attacked our gas infrastructure," Zelenskyy told Bill Hemmer in a live interview on "America's Newsroom." Asked whether Ukraine would honor the ceasefire, Zelenskyy answered, "Of course," insisting that Kyiv had already refrained from striking Russian energy facilities overnight. TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE "We didn't attack any energy objects on the territory of Russia because President Trump said that there will be an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. And we didn't attack, but Russia attacked our gas stations, energy infrastructure, infrastructure and other things," he said. The Ukrainian leader described the attacks as Putin's response to Trump's initiative. "It was his answer to President Trump. He attacked our energy infrastructure," Zelenskyy said. "The communication from Russia was very clear that they don't know anything about energy ceasefire." Trump announced Sunday on Truth Social that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate halt to attacks on energy facilities. But Moscow has not confirmed accepting such an agreement, and the precise scope of Trump's proposal remains disputed. According to Axios reporting Sunday, a White House official said the proposal initially focused on halting attacks on oil refineries, with a broader ceasefire covering power plants and electricity grids potentially following. The official acknowledged that Russia had not yet agreed. UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE Zelenskyy pushes back on Trump's refinery demands During the interview, Hemmer pressed Zelenskyy on whether Ukraine would halt attacks on Russia's extensive oil-refining network, which has become a point of contention between Washington and Kyiv amid rising global fuel prices. Zelenskyy argued that a ceasefire limited to refineries would fail to address Ukraine's greatest vulnerability: its electricity supply. "When we speak about energy ceasefire, it means only one thing: that they don't attack our energy infrastructure, and we don't respond to their energy infrastructure. This is called energy ceasefire." Asked again whether Ukrainian forces would refrain from targeting Russian refineries, Zelenskyy gave a conditional commitment. "If Russia will not attack our energy, we will not attack the energy," he said. Trump has repeatedly criticized Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries, arguing that they contribute to higher fuel prices. On Friday, he announced an agreement with Russia to release diesel supplies to the U.S. and global markets, a decision that drew criticism from lawmakers concerned about providing Moscow with additional revenue. Zelenskyy challenged Trump's assessment of what is driving diesel prices, pointing instead to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. "Everybody understands that the price on diesel doesn't depend on our attacks on diesel in Russia," Zelenskyy told Hemmer. "Everybody understands that it depends on the blocking of Hormuz Strait." NEW RISK FOR US CONSUMERS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS THREATEN A SECOND MAJOR OIL CHOKEPOINT 'Only our people can change' Ukraine's president The interview also exposed tensions over Trump's calls for Ukraine to hold new presidential elections. Over the weekend, Trump criticized Zelenskyy and suggested Ukraine needed a new president, arguing that Kyiv had missed opportunities to reach a negotiated settlement with Russia. "If President Trump wants to change the leader in Ukraine, he has to know that only our people can change," Zelenskyy responded. The Ukrainian president said he was willing to organize an election but argued that voting remained impossible without a substantial pause in hostilities. "I'm ready for elections. Really, we need a minimum 60 days for security of infrastructure to prepare for elections," he said. Zelenskyy described continuing Russian drone and missile attacks as an immediate threat to voters. "We are speaking about thousands of drones, ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, how can people vote?" he asked. "It's not even about the law. The law is very important. But we speak first of all about security." He also said he last spoke directly with Trump in New York during the U.N. General Assembly in late September. ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARS-LONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE Russian attacks continue as Moscow resists ceasefire The interview came after another series of Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities and residential areas. Ukraine's charge d'affaires in Washington, Denys Sienik, said Sunday that Russian forces struck a power plant in Kyiv, disrupting electricity and water supplies, before attacking a thermal power plant in Kharkiv following Trump's announcement. "In total, over the course of the week, Russia struck electricity generation and transmission facilities more than 200 times," Sienik wrote on X on Oct. 11, 2026. East2West News agency reported Monday that three civilians — a 16-year-old boy and two women, ages 19 and 51 — were killed in a strike near a grocery store in the Kharkiv region. The agency also reported that five people were wounded in an attack on a residential high-rise. In Pisochyn, a woman described witnessing the bombardment of a power plant shortly after Trump's announcement, according to East2West. "We believed the statement that they wouldn't strike energy infrastructure," she said. "Just ten minutes after that promise was made, there were already five strikes." The agency also reported a Ukrainian strike on a Russian military base in occupied Khrustalnyi, in the Luhansk region, where three large fires were reportedly visible. The damage and casualty figures could not be independently confirmed. Reuters separately reported Monday that Russia continued striking Ukrainian energy targets despite Trump's announcement, while Kyiv maintained that it had refrained from attacking Russian refineries. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, meanwhile, rejected the prospect of a 60-day ceasefire to facilitate Ukrainian elections, arguing that European countries would use the pause to replenish Ukraine's weapons supplies. "I don't think he deserves a respite," Lavrov said Monday, according to the BBC. UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS Trump's Russian diesel deal draws criticism The latest developments have intensified scrutiny of Trump's decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel, which critics argue could provide Moscow with additional revenue while it continues its military campaign. Carrie Filipetti, executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition and a former deputy assistant secretary of state during Trump's first administration, questioned whether the arrangement would undermine U.S. leverage over Putin. "Both Russia and Ukraine seemed surprised by the announcement of an energy ceasefire, and unsurprisingly, Russia has continued to attack Ukrainian energy facilities — reportedly as recently as a few hours ago," Filipetti told Fox News Digital. "Putin probably hopes the new diesel deal — which directly undermines recent US legislation calling for an increase in tariffs and sanctions against Russian energy — will discourage President Trump from holding Putin accountable for these continued violations and attacks." Filipetti argued that Russian energy revenue remains a critical source of financing for Moscow's war effort. "If we want a real ceasefire, paying directly for Putin's war machine through this new diesel deal is not the way to do it," she said. "President Trump's goal of a ceasefire could be a real win — but it's only going to happen if we stop the diesel deal." Morgan Murphy, former head of public diplomacy for the Special Presidential Envoy to Russia and Ukraine, offered a different assessment, defending Trump's efforts to secure a negotiated settlement. "President Trump has consistently prodded both sides toward the only realistic outcome — negotiation," Murphy told Fox News Digital. "Both sides are losing right now: Ukraine doesn’t have the combat power to retake seized land, and Russia is destroying its future demographics with every passing day." Murphy argued that prolonging the fighting would only deepen the human toll: "Trump is right to push for a ceasefire. An endless war of attrition benefits only the makers of weapons and coffins." In his Fox News interview, Zelenskyy also emphasized the human cost of the war, saying Russian strikes were killing between 20 and 30 civilians a day, a figure Fox News has not independently verified. "We want to end this war as quickly as possible," he said. "Ceasefire is a good first step from both sides. This is very important." title: Democrats see new chances to flip red states — but a $400M GOP spending advantage could derail their plans
description: Republicans outspend Democrats by $400 million ahead of Election Day, forcing Senate Majority PAC to make tough choices across nine battlegrounds.
content: With just over three weeks to go until Election Day, more and more red states and congressional districts appear in reach for the Democrats, as they work to win back House and Senate majorities from the Republicans in the midterms. But a massive Republican spending advantage threatens to complicate those ambitions. Republican campaigns, committees and aligned groups have outspent their Democratic counterparts by $400 million so far this election cycle, according to AdImpact, a leading political advertising tracking firm. The disparity is forcing Democrats to make difficult decisions about where to invest and how much to spend as the party tries to expand the electoral map. "We are being outspent by the Republicans. That's just a fact," Lauren French, communications director at the Senate Majority PAC, told Fox News Digital. "In many of these states, they have really transactionalized elections, so they have monopoly money to play with, whereas we are working with real resources." DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS FORMER - HERE ARE THREE FACTORS THAT COULD STOP IT The latest Fox News Power Rankings shifted GOP-dominated South Carolina from Solid to Likely Republican. The Senate showdown in reliably Republican Kansas is Lean Republican, while the races in red-leaning Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and Texas are rated toss-ups. "Senate Majority PAC has resources to compete, and we are very happy that we're able to be in 9 battleground states," French said. The super PAC is the leading outside group supporting Democratic Senate candidates and incumbents and is aligned with longtime Democratic leader Sen. Chuck Schumer. French highlighted record-setting fundraising over the past three months, but added, "of course, more recess resources would be helpful." With the latest polls from Fox News and other organizations showing Democrats increasingly competitive across the Senate map, the party is pleading for more money. "Last month a pro-Trump PAC reserved $10 million in New Hampshire advertising, and we’re being outspent 3-to-1," reads a fundraising pitch to supporters by Rep. Chris Pappas, the Democratic Senate nominee in swing state New Hampshire. WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS MIDTERM POWER RANKINGS Senate Majority PAC is rushing some of its record fundraising into the newly competitive battlegrounds. And American Bridge PAC, a Democrat-aligned group, recently pumped over $20 million into South Carolina and Kansas, as well as competitive races in two other red states, Florida and Mississippi. But the Democratic groups are being outspent by their Republican-aligned counterparts, thanks to major expenditures by Senate Leadership Fund, the President Donald Trump-allied MAGA Inc. and a super PAC bankrolled by Elon Musk. "The hard reality is there isn't enough funding to protect the toss-up states and also heavily invest in the red-leaning states where we're playing offense," a veteran Democratic Senate operative who requested anonymity to speak candidly told Fox News Digital." French told Fox News Digital "This is the time in the campaign season where everyone really has to make some of those belt-tightening decisions, and that's why we're looking at every race really closely to make sure we have enough resources to get to the majority, but we're also not leaving anyone shortchanged." House Democrats are facing a similar predicament. A memo from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) shared with donors warned that Republicans "are now flooding districts across our battlefield with MAGA Inc. and Trump super PAC money that we simply cannot match." DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB The memo, which was obtained by Fox News Digital, requested an additional $17 million that was needed by Oct. 22 "to close the sale" in what they described as "winnable races." The GOP is fighting political history, which has traditionally seen the party in power in Washington lose congressional seats during midterm election years. Add to that a challenging political climate fueled by persistent inflation Americans see at the grocery store, high gas prices tied to what polls show is an unpopular war with Iran and Trump's negative approval ratings. "Thanks to the tireless efforts of Leader John Thune, Senate Leadership Fund has amassed a financial advantage that neither party has had before. SLF will continue to invest unprecedented resources across the map to maintain the Republican Senate majority," Senate Leadership Fund communications director Chris Gustafson told Fox News Digital. "This is not an advantage Republicans typically have and it's definitely a contributing factor to a lot of candidates on the ballot right now keeping their races close," Hunt emphasized.

title: SC Dem Senate candidate claims she will stand up to her party as Graham ties her to 'socialist Democrats'
description: Democratic South Carolina U.S. Senate candidate Annie Andrews and Republican Sen. Darline Graham clashed during a U.S. Senate election debate.
content: Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., and Democratic challenger Annie Andrews clashed on Sunday night during the South Carolina U.S. Senate debate, which also included Libertarian candidate Kasie Whitener. Graham said she is "concerned about the socialist Democrats," asserting that after Hamas terrorists slaughtered Israelis on Oct. 7, 2023, Democrats in New York cheered "over the death of over a thousand people." "Annie Andrews will not stand up to the socialist Democratic Party. She's only going to join them," Graham declared. DARLINE GRAHAM'S 'EMBARRASSING AND INEXCUSABLE' NATIONAL SECURITY STUMBLE SPOTLIGHTS BREAK FROM LATE BROTHER Andrews fired back, claiming that she is willing to stand up to her party. "I told you my opponent was going to call me a socialist and there she's done it again. She's been told to come out here and call me Bernie, Ocasio, Mamdani. That's what's in her script," Andrews said, referring to Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. "But the truth is my name is Annie Andrews. And there shouldn't be any confusion about that because unlike my opponent, I haven't changed my name recently," she said. DEMOCRATS ARE CHANGING THEIR TRANSGENDER MESSAGE. REPUBLICANS SAY THEY'RE JUST FLIP-FLOPPING "The real difference between me and Sen. Graham is that I will stand up to my own party and I will always put South Carolina first. She seems to believe the job she has right now is to be the White House's ambassador to South Carolina. The job is to represent South Carolina. She considers the job to be to read their scripts and do their bidding. And we can do better," Andrews asserted. Graham fired back, saying that her "legal name is Graham" and "has always been Graham." She explained, "I lost my parents when I was a little girl, and I kept the name Graham so that I felt connected to them. So my name, every document I have ever signed, has Graham on it." After the death of Sen. Lindsey Graham, South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster tapped the late lawmaker's sister Darline to serve the remainder of her brother's Senate term. title: Josh Hartnett's new limited series 'Below' draws mixed reactions over its sea creature mystery
description: Josh Hartnett's limited series "Below" started strong with its sea creature mystery, but viewers say the final episodes took some bizarre turns.
content: People are very split on Josh Hartnett's new limited series below. There has been significant buzz surrounding "Below" ever since the preview was released and for one very simple reason: People like shows about mysterious monsters and a small town with deep secrets. NETFLIX DROPS NEW TRAILER FOR 'BELOW' STARRING JOSH HARTNETT AS A FISHERMAN FIGHTING A SEA CREATURE Well, it was recently released, and it's certainly drawing some interesting reactions. "Below" draws mixed reactions. Spoilers below. The series focuses on a small fishing community in Canada that finds itself being absolutely terrorized by an unknown sea creature and a massive iceberg that mysteriously appears in the harbor. I had the chance to bang it out over the course of a few days, and the main problem is that "Below" is essentially two different shows that play out over six episodes. One track is a horror series about an unknown creature taking down boats and killing people. The second track is (possibly?) supposed to be an uplifting story about understanding nature. Well, those two things don't exactly naturally mix. The ending was also a bit of a strange choice. Right after a bow has been put on the situation, and the sea creature has been pushed off, the community discovers more massive chunks of ice that are nesting more violent monsters. So, a limited series ends on a cliffhanger? Make that make sense. title: Michael Brennan is officially a dude, Blades Brown is coming and time is Jon Rahm's best friend
description: Michael Brennan's third PGA Tour win at the Baycurrent Classic vaults him to world No. 20 in what's been a quiet yet meteoric rise for the star.
content: The PGA Tour has always had the great problem of having so much young talent that many up-and-comers fall through the cracks and don't get the attention they deserve until they quietly put together a resume that suddenly smacks you in the face. Nobody on Tour right now may optimize that more than Michael Brennan. On the topic of young talent, Blades Brown is headed to the PGA Tour next year. At just 19 years old and some change, he's the youngest player ever to earn his Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour after finishing ninth on the season-long points list. In other news, LIV Golf suffered a haymaker amid its bankruptcy mess, with Jon Rahm officially opting to split with the league as its future remains entirely up in the air. While it's so easy to look at the (many) negatives involving Rahm and his run with LIV, there is a very obvious yet important reality to look forward to. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. Michael Brennan deserves your respect When you think of young stars on Tour, let's call it guys who are 26 or younger, the likes of Jackson Koivun (21), Akshay Bhatia (24), Tom Kim (24), Michael Thorbjornsen (25), Jacob Bridgeman (26), and Ludvig Aberg (26) immediately come to mind, and rightfully so. After what 24-year-old Michael Brennan accomplished in Japan over the weekend, his name firmly belongs in that group. The Baycurrent Classic marked Brennan's 33rd career start on the PGA Tour, and after beginning Sunday's final round tied for the lead, he went out and posted a 3-under 68 to earn a one-shot victory, giving him three career wins, all coming in under 12 months' time. Brennan's maiden win came at the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship in November against an admittedly weaker field. His second trip to the winner's circle, a three-shot victory, came this August at the Wyndham Championship against a stronger crop of players fighting for a spot into the FedEx Cup Playoffs. While the Wyndham could be described as his first "big boy" win, his victory at the Baycurrent, on international soil, is the most impressive of the three, as he held off the likes of Xander Schauffele, Brian Harman, Ryan Gerard, Keith Mitchell, and Bridgeman en route to victory. Brennan was ranked 61st in the world in late July, but has catapulted himself all the way to No. 20 in what can only be described as a quiet, yet meteoric rise. The former Wake Forest star turned professional in 2024, made quick work of the PGA Tour Americas circuit in 2025 with three wins to earn a spot on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2026, but ultimately skipped that step. His start in the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship came via a sponsor's exemption, and he went out and won the event, his first career start on Tour as a pro, by four shots. So, about a year into his professional career, Brennan had already earned a PGA Tour membership, and less than a year on from that maiden victory, he's earned two more wins. He also made the cut in all four major championships in 2026, which is something only 13 other players can say they accomplished. The Virginia native has proven he knows how to do the hardest part – actually win – and also happens to rank second and third, respectively, in average club head speed and driving distance on Tour. Brennan is one of the best young players on the planet, period. Blades Brown keeps meeting huge expectations It's safe to say Blades Brown made the right call skipping out on that whole college experience thing. Since before he could drive a car, which admittedly wasn't all that long ago, the expectation for Blades Brown has simply been 'the next guy.' While he hasn't won a professional event at this point in his insanely young career, he's just about met every expectation out there. It has been a steady climb for the Nashville native since he made his professional debut in January 2025 at 17 years old at The American Express. He's made the most out of countless sponsors' exemptions on the PGA Tour and put together an incredibly consistent campaign on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2026 with six Top 10s and just two missed cuts in 18 starts, which was plenty to earn a spot on Tour in 2027. In 11 starts on Tour in 2026, Brown missed just two cuts, finished solo third at the Puerto Rico Open, and picked up a total of seven Top 25 finishes. His career is very simply on the exact, consistent trajectory many expected it to be on at this point. Currently ranked 97th in the world, it will be fascinating to see how Brown plays out of the gates in 2027. Sneaking inside the Top 50 and earning a Masters invite would be quite the story. We'll eventually not care about Jon Rahm's stint on LIV It's so easy to say that Jon Rahm made a mistake when he left the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2024. You could claim it was a decision made out of greed, as he made the move for hundreds of millions of dollars. He made the jump at just 30 years old in the prime of his career with two major championships already in his back pocket. While it's fair to focus on those aspects now, our now will soon become our then, and Rahm has an ample amount of time to make his brief career on LIV Golf seem like a forgettable blip on his resume. While at this point in time we don't know how he'll do it, the Spaniard will get back to competing on the PGA Tour against the best players in the world on a consistent basis. Maybe we see that in six months, maybe it takes 18 months, who knows, but when it happens, it'll be a jolt to the PGA Tour from every angle. It just feels like we've been in a rut, and going from summer to fall doesn't help. NASCAR owns Sundays during the summer. There's no real competition in terms of network TV. Look at that race. Man, we had it so good back then, and we just pissed it all away. Look at those cars! Listen to those announcers. That was peak NASCAR, at least for me. Can't believe it's been 21 years. And somehow, Jimmie is still racing. Not on a full-time basis, of course, but he's already locked in for next year's Daytona 500. Amazing. Sell the team to an owner who cares, and save the legacy! Us fans need to demand more, per Armando last year. I’d say we’ll protest, but Mrs. Gen X Warren M. is a Lions fan, so we’re going to Lions at Miami game next month… – Susan G. says: I truly believe the Dallas Cowboys will not be a winning team again until Jerry passes away and they replace Dak. I know I know he has a great pass completion percentage but he can’t do it when it counts. I am 67 years old and I have been a Cowboys fan since I can remember, but these days I don’t expect them to win. It is really sad! Golf integrity is one of the biggest issues of our lives right now How do I know? Wait until you see how many emails this topic generated over the weekend. Normally, I'll get maybe six emails on a hot topic over a weekend because you guys have lives to live. This weekend, it was completely different. We have ourselves a hot topic. – Kevin W. emails: I love the question about golf integrity. I belong to a private club, and it's a constant debate. We like other clubs have a "men's day" where all the tee times that day put money into a pot and play various games. This is where the convenience of technology created an issue. We, like yourself, and lots of other golf clubs, started using Golf Genius. Nice and convenient to enter scores; HOWEVER, it also posts scores as they are happening. So, what happens when the guys who go off early post a good score? The late guys see the number they have to beat and BINGO, suddenly 5-footers are good, and those groups are winning everything. Our club's first solution to the problem was to buy a very expensive software called CAP patrol from a bunch of data scientists. Basically, it was the socialist version of golf handicaps that punished good golfers to even out the field for the higher handicappers. It would cherry-pick low rounds and say you're better than your index and you MUST BE cheating otherwise. There were a ton of other factors, and nobody understood the algorithm of who got capped and who didn't, and the company wouldn't disclose it. It's very popular with private clubs on the east and west coasts. We quickly scrapped it. The simple solution this year was to go old school and stop the live scoreboard. Pretty much fixed the issue. In general, if you want to fix giving short putts, always have a money game going. My group of guys rarely, if ever, just go out and play a round just to play. We always have some dollars on the line; even if it's just a few bucks, it keeps the integrity there, as a short putt can change a game quickly. Just my $.02 – Rural MN Dave agrees: I played in a group for many years that played strict rules of golf and no gimmes. One of the group members was playing on a 9 handicap but was really closer to a 6. The strength of his game was chipping and putting. One day he had an 18 inch birdie putt with several skins carryovers riding on it. He stepped up to the putt, taking his time and doing his regular routine, and cold yanked it, never even touched the hole. He looked up, red-faced, and said "and that's why we don't do gimmes!" – Michael in Bossier City, Louisiana says: Your recent article on shaving golf scores did not shock me the least bit. I believe that gimmie putts really skew one’s score when playing the same course conditions. However, not all course conditions are equal. Do you play on a goat ranch city course or a private near PGA standards. I would love to witness a professional golfer score scratch or better on the city course I play regularly; bare fairways and tree roots jutting out in all directions. Rolling the ball slightly to find that last remaining few blades of grass in the fairways or safety setting away from tree roots that are three inches exposed to the surface becomes a must for sanity; you are still accountable to that next golf shot. Now, I’ve played in regional and state tournaments that would white mark a tenth of my course as no play areas because of root or extreme bare spot areas. Then again, I’m not disagreeing with you on most of your points of play. If you are behind a tree or in the rough, then you need to hit your best way out and onto the green to putt it out. More to note! I’m a 6.8 handicap in which I play a fairly nice city course other than the tree root issues and played Robert Trent courses resulting in a near score equivalence. Yes, plugging in the rough off the fairway, moving your ball for a way out of tree trouble and taking gimmie putts does mask one’s real ability. However, having a fake lower handicap which most tournaments only take 85% to prevent sandbaggers will hurt a delusional golfer in the end. Well, hope you had time to read my opinion. – Joyce tells us about her club's gimme rule: Just think how many games and championships Ohio State would have won if the 3-foot gimme rule would have been in play for field goals and touchdowns. Last year our women's golf league finally adopted a 6-inch gimme rule, a measurement that we can easily imagine. Look at the map and then look at NW Ohio where I live compared to the heart of the Smoky Mountains. Also, it rains a lot, which is why everything here is so green and lush compared to the Rockies. It’s pretty rare to have a clear warm day during these months. The reason its called the Smoky’s is there are plenty of days where you have fog/mist covering the mountains, especially near lakes, giving it a look of smoke. Given the temp range and low dew point, the poster skewed the results to make a small strip of the west coast look ideal. Maybe the guy lives there and wants bragging rights. As someone that lived a part of his childhood in California and most of his life in Louisiana, moving to East Tennessee over 8 years ago has been fantastic weather wise (and just about any other wise). I live in that sweet spot where you experience all 4 seasons with each lasting about 3 months. Unlike LA where you had 50 weeks of summer, 1 of spring and fall, and 1 day of winter. title: WWE star Drew McIntyre stars in micro-drama series 'Agent of Shadows,' touts company's reach beyond wrestling
description: Drew McIntyre plays a dangerous secret agent in "Agent of Shadows" on ReelShort, joined by Chase Mattson and several other WWE superstars.
content: WWE star Drew McIntyre has already proved just how menacing he can be in the ring. He’s a four-time world champion, two-time tag team champion and one-time intercontinental champion. He’s won the Royal Rumble and Money in the Bank one time each as well. With his hulking figure and silky smooth long hair, it almost seems like the Scotsman was made for the cameras. Over the last year, he’s begun to prove that notion. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE McIntyre has had a role in the 2024 film "The Killer’s Game" and is set to be a part of "The Last Druid" starring Russell Crowe and the "Highlander" reboot, which also stars Crowe and WWE Hall of Famer Dave Bautista. With his recent success, McIntyre has gotten a part in a micro-drama series with actor Chase Mattson and a few other WWE figures. McIntyre stars as a dangerous secret agent. He goes undercover to help protect a young girl from being targeted by a billionaire arms dealer. But what makes "Agent of Shadows" stand out from every other TV show in the same genre, is that it will premiere on ReelShort. ReelShort is a streaming service that produces short-form videos for the social media age. McIntyre told OutKick Dropkick he was aware of the platform because he would need to watch something on airplanes as he traveled around the world for wrestling and filming. "I had a look at it, it was a lot of fun, a lot of chance to show some range, and I went, heck yeah, I wanna be part of this thing," he recalled after getting asked whether he would want to perform in the series. "It has the action, the comedy and it has heart, too." Mattson told OutKick Dropkick he was drawn to the show because of his martial-arts background. "I just felt like Adam, the character, was a lot like myself and I loved how much I could resonate with it so fast. I love the amount of action, comedy and a little bit of romance that was spread throughout the script. I was like, I need to be a part of this. And it was a lot different from all of the other projects that I’ve done." Mattson said he didn’t really know much about McIntyre before working with him. He noticed how big the pro wrestler. title: Ben Affleck has blunt response to teenage son's Lamborghini request after infamous mishap
description: Ben Affleck revealed his son Samuel asked him to buy a Lamborghini, four years after the teen's infamous fender-bender at a luxury car dealership.
content: Ben Affleck's son Samuel appears to have developed a taste for Lamborghinis, four years after he accidentally backed one into another luxury car. During a recent appearance on his "Animals" co-star Kerry Washington's podcast, "Street You Grew Up On," the 54-year-old actor said that Samuel, 14, inherited his affinity for luxury items. Affleck, who shares three children including Samuel, Violet, 20, and Fin, 17, with his ex-wife Jennifer Garner, told Washington that he recently shut down his son's request to buy him a Lamborghini. BEN AFFLECK ADMITS HIS TEENAGER ROASTED HIS DATING HISTORY WHILE AT DINNER "I see my son now, you know, and he's a lot like me," Affleck said. "And it makes me realize — because my older two ones — they kind of spoiled me because they're like, 'No, we don't want this. We don't want that.' They're like, aversive." "My son's like, ‘Dad, you should get a Lambo,’" the Oscar winner recalled with a laugh. "'What? A Lambo? Are you f---ing crazy? Am I an a--hole in a yellow Lamborghini driving around like at the club?' He's like, 'Yeah.'" ROB LOWE SAYS SON WAS MUGGED AT KNIFEPOINT AFTER IGNORING DAD'S NYC WARNING "No. No!" Affleck exclaimed as Washington laughed. Samuel was previously involved in a mishap with a yellow Lamborghini while visiting 777 Exotics, a luxury car rental dealership in the Los Angeles area, with his father and Affleck's then-fiancée, Jennifer Lopez, in June 2022. At the time, Affleck allowed Samuel, then 10, to sit in the driver's seat of a bright yellow Lamborghini SUV before the boy accidentally put the car into reverse and backed into a white BMW. Samuel was photographed jumping out of the Lamborghini to inspect the vehicles, while Affleck also checked for damage. The "Gone Girl" star was later photographed hugging Samuel while talking with Lopez, whom he married in July 2022. The former couple finalized their divorce in January 2025. The vehicle involved in Samuel's incident was a Lamborghini Urus, which rented for $1,475 per day and was valued at $250,000 at the time, according to the New York Post. At the time, representatives for Affleck and 777 Exotics both told the New York Post there was no damage to either vehicle. An employee at the rental dealership also said there were no hard feelings following the fender-bender. KRISTIN CAVALLARI ADMITS HER KIDS FLY COACH WHILE SHE SITS IN FIRST CLASS "Affleck loves cars," the dealership employee told the New York Post. "We hope they come in again." The Lamborghini isn't the first high-priced item to catch Samuel's eye. In March 2025, an exchange between Affleck and Samuel made headlines after Samuel was filmed admiring a $6,000 pair of Dior x Nike Air Jordan 1 sneakers in a video shared on Instagram. MARK WAHLBERG ADMITS HOLLYWOOD FAME COMES WITH ‘BAGGAGE’ FOR HIS KIDS In the clip, Affleck and Samuel browsed sneakers at a convention, where Samuel spotted the Dior shoes. After seeing the $6,000 price tag, Affleck told his son, "That's a lot of lawns you gotta mow there." During an interview with Access Hollywood later that month, Affleck joked about the viral video. MICHAEL DOUGLAS SAYS KIRK DOUGLAS GAVE HIM $10,000 AT 21 AND TOLD HIM HE WAS ON HIS OWN "That's what happens when you tell a motherf---er they have to mow a lawn," he told the outlet. He's like, 'We have the money.' I'm like, 'I have the money, you're broke!'" Affleck quipped. Affleck co-parents his three children with Garner, whom he was married to from 2005 to 2018. During an April 2025 appearance on "Today with Jenna & Friends," Affleck explained how he was teaching his children that they shouldn't expect handouts from their famous parents. Affleck explained that he wants his children to understand the value of hard work. "You love your kids. You want to give them everything and do everything for them, but I think you definitely do them a disservice by not connecting [if] you want something that you want, you have to work for that," he said. During a recent appearance on "Late Night with Seth Meyers," Affleck said that his children don't care about his Hollywood success. "I remember when my daughter was born, right around the time I directed my first movie and I had a bunch of movies that didn't work and was very uncool and felt kind of despised and thought like, 'God, I really want to make my kids proud with my career,'" he recalled. "And as I've gotten older, my kids have gotten older, what I realized is, they don't give a s---," he continued as the audience laughed. "They really don't care," he added. "The most cool thing I've ever done, in my kids' eyes, is, like, become a meme." title: Haunting clues emerge in 7-year fishing boat mystery after wreckage found off island
description: Green Oceans of Rhode Island says it found the F/V Mistress wreckage just 50 feet from a Block Island Wind Farm turbine, raising questions about the 2019 sinking.
content: An organization believes it has found the wreckage of a fishing boat that sank over seven years ago — potentially solving a mystery surrounding the deaths of two fishermen. Green Oceans, a Rhode Island-based environmental organization, announced the discovery of what it believes is the F/V Mistress in the waters off Block Island in September. The vessel sank Jan. 1, 2019, according to the organization. 118-YEAR-OLD MYSTERY CRACKED AS DIVERS DISCOVER LOST WARSHIP BENEATH THE WAVES Two fishermen died in the incident, and the U.S. Coast Guard searched for the vessel following the sinking but never located the wreckage. The F/V Mistress was discovered approximately 92 feet underwater, just 50 feet from the base of a wind turbine at the Block Island Wind Farm, according to Green Oceans. The organization reported that "apparent human remains" were also found at the site. Michael Lombardi, president of Green Oceans, told Fox News Digital his organization began searching for the vessel after receiving tips from two contractors who had previously worked near turbine No. 1 at the Block Island Wind Farm. One contractor reported hearing rumors of underwater wreckage — while another claimed to have personally spotted wreckage while conducting survey work at the site. YOUNG NEWLYWEDS KILLED AFTER BOAT COLLIDES WITH WATER TAXI AND SINKS IN VENICE LAGOON Lombardi said he later reviewed the Coast Guard's original accident report and plotted GPS coordinates associated with distress calls and other key details, which pointed investigators toward the turbine. "Once plotted on a map, it became obvious where the search area should be focused, and it coincided perfectly with turbine 1," Lombardi said. When asked by Fox News Digital how confident he was that the wreck was the F/V Mistress, Lombardi replied, "100%." He added, "The dive team studied images of the vessel prior to diving the site and were focused on finding key identifying features. … One striking item was the net drum. It has several unique features." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Tim Diaz, who survived the sinking, confirmed that the net drum belonged to the Mistress, according to Lombardi. Diaz built the equipment himself. The mystery isn't over — and Lombardi said there is still some "uncertainty" about what happened in the vessel's final moments, though he said it was undoubtedly in distress. "Based on the orientation of the wreckage on the bottom, there is reason to investigate whether an avoidance maneuver to starboard was made in an attempt to avoid a collision with the turbine," he said. "With the hull full of water, this maneuver could have ultimately caused the vessel to roll and then sink." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Lombardi said he hopes federal authorities will reopen the investigation to determine whether the two fishermen who died remain within the wreckage or were swept out to sea and whether such a maneuver contributed to the sinking. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "The USCG and all agencies involved do tremendous work to protect mariners out on the water," Lombardi said, adding that he hopes the discovery will help answer lingering questions about the tragedy. As Green Oceans focuses on the environmental and maritime safety impacts of offshore wind development, Lombardi said the discovery could have implications for future permitting decisions. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Had this accident been fully investigated in 2019, while having the vessel wreckage, the offshore wind permitting landscape would have been quite different with regard to safety considerations along the continental shelf," he said.

title: Drag queens, trans pastor, abortion rallies: Inside Dem governor hopeful's progressive church
description: Rob Sand regularly attended Plymouth Congregational United Church of Christ, which has hosted drag queen concerts and invited a transgender pastor.
content: In one of the most hotly contested governor's races in the country, the Democratic nominee has been working overtime to cultivate a moderate image — while reportedly attending a church that openly embraces some of the progressive causes dividing voters in Iowa. Rob Sand, Iowa’s state auditor and its Democratic nominee for governor, regularly attended Plymouth Congregational United Church of Christ, located in the state’s capital, as of late 2025, according to a local journalist. Over the years, Plymouth has hosted and promoted drag queen performances, invited a transgender pastor to serve as a guest pastor and openly supported abortion. Sand has emphasized his faith on the campaign trail, repeatedly referencing Christianity and quoting scripture, at times successfully appealing to otherwise conservative Iowans. In addition to leaning on his faith, Sand has repeatedly described himself as independently minded, claimed to have voted for Republicans in the past and said that he sometimes prefers working with the GOP over Democrats, calling political parties "poison." "I am a Christian. I’m a conservative. But I’m not a party-based person," one voter is quoted as saying in a Sand press release. "I like to vote for the person as opposed to the party. And to me, (Sand) just seems really honest and down to earth. And I enjoyed him." IOWA GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL ZACH LAHN TELLS 'RUTHLESS' DEMOCRATS ARE HIDING THEIR BAD POLICIES Sand's reported church attendance, however, connects him to a congregation whose progressive religious and political positions stand in contrast to the moderate image he has emphasized on the campaign trail. Sand’s church is open about its progressive slant, with its "about" page featuring an image of churchgoers at a gay pride parade, noting that the church does not take the Bible literally and stating that it "has been an LGBTQ+ Open and Affirming congregation for more than 30 years." An image of the church included in a profile compiled by the United Church of Christ shows it flying a pride flag on its grounds, noting that the church "is a progressive powerhouse in the region." "Rob Sand goes to church weekly and does so in Iowa, unlike Zach Lahn. Rob’s faith is deeply important to him, and like many, he has never found a church where he agrees with everything, but does prefer traditional services with liturgy and classic hymns," a spokeswoman for his campaign told Fox News Digital. "Rob has always been independent-minded, and he isn’t going to take lessons in morality from a sex toy salesman who lives in Kansas." The mention of sex toys was a reference to FirmTech, a company that manufactures wearable sexual wellness devices and once counted GOP gubernatorial nominee Zach Lahn as an investor. Lahn maintains that the product was originally developed to monitor cardiovascular health and that he divested before the company shifted toward more sexually suggestive marketing. Sand has also pointed to Lahn's regular flights to Kansas, arguing that they betray tenuous ties to the state he's seeking to govern. Lahn, meanwhile, says that he lives full-time in Iowa, explaining that the flights are a product of him needing to shuttle children from a previous marriage between the two states. Lahn's campaign did not divulge where he attends church when asked by Fox News Digital. LGBTQ GROUP REVEALS WHICH DEM NOMINEE IS SPONSORING HALLOWEEN EVENT FEATURING DRAG SHOWS Plymouth’s progressive reputation is well-earned. In May 2025, Plymouth hosted drag queen "Flamy Grant" for a concert, according to advertisements for the event, bringing an artist whose broader catalog includes sexually explicit lyrics to the progressive Des Moines congregation. In one song, titled "Take a Chance on Me," not to be confused with the ABBA classic of the same name, Grant sings, "I’m a patient lover unless I finish first. And I expect you [to] finish me if the roles are reversed. I maintain the mystery of my sexual history." In another song, the drag queen complained about his childhood church, stating that "I guess the lesson there was God would only hear a prayer If it came from a person with a c---." The song continues to state that "secretly most men just fear the snatch" and praises Eve for disobeying God by eating the forbidden fruit. POWERFUL LGBTQ+ GROUP'S ENDORSEMENTS COULD TANK VULNERABLE DEMS OVER RADICAL YOUTH TRANS AGENDA About a year later, Plymouth promoted a drag event on its Facebook page at a nearby church billed as a "family-friendly karaoke fundraiser" headlined by drag queen "Tess Tura." Tura hosts a podcast where, among other topics, unprotected gay sex is discussed. In a similar vein, Plymouth invited transgender pastor Paula Stone Williams to serve as a guest pastor for one weekend in 2023, according to a local media report. At the time, Williams had recently published a book titled "As a Woman: What I learned about power, sex, and the patriarchy after I transitioned." VULNERABLE DEM'S CAMPAIGN PITCH CLASHES WITH 'RADICAL' VOTING RECORD ON TOP CULTURE WAR ISSUE Some of Plymouth’s pro-LGBTQ advocacy is directed at young children. Plymouth disclosed in a 2025 job posting that it partners with the Rainbow Faith Coalition, a group that says "LGBTQ+ identities are God-given, honored and celebrated," and that "[f]ully living into these identities in name, pronoun, relationship and gender expression is not a barrier to participation … in any areas of the faith community," including children’s programming and education. The church also offers Our Whole Lives programming, a sexuality education curriculum co-published by the Unitarian Universalist Association and the United Church of Christ, with classes beginning in first grade that address topics including sexuality, relationships, gender identity and sexual health. Similar to its theology, the church’s politics are decidedly liberal. TOP CONSERVATIVE GROUP UNVEILS FULL-COURT PRESS IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE TO EXPOSE ‘SHOCKING’ DEM PLATFORM In February 2025, for example, Plymouth’s pastors joined a protest in Iowa’s statehouse "to pray and stand up for our trans and gender nonconforming friends and neighbors," per a post on the church's Facebook page. A few years prior, church leadership participated in a pro-LGBTQ rally outside the statehouse, according to another church Facebook post. "Plymouth’s bold social justice presence is a hallmark in the community and is often cited as a reason for new members joining the congregation," a church job posting from 2025 reads. "We are committed to advancing justice, equity, and compassion in and beyond our community." Indeed, as the Supreme Court struck down Roe v. Wade, Plymouth mobilized to fight against pro-life legislation, supporting those fighting for "reproductive healthcare" and referring to women as "all who hold the potential to bear life." The church held a prayer vigil in support of abortion in May 2022 and rallied at the state capital in July 2023 to protest against efforts to regulate abortion. After former President Joe Biden became the first president to formally recognize Transgender Day of Visibility in 2021, Plymouth followed his lead by sending Facebook messages to its followers observing Transgender Day of Visibility and Transgender Day of Remembrance between 2021 and 2023. title: Pennsylvania gunman who killed 8 was grandfather who seemed normal, victim relatives say
description: The Erie, Pennsylvania, gunman was a "good guy" before he "started going downhill," killing eight people and himself, a friend of a victim said.
content: The man who killed eight, including a pregnant woman and two young children, in Erie, Pennsylvania, was a grandfather who did not appear distressed before the massacre, according to relatives of the victims. "I think that was a front for him," Julius Windham said Sunday while standing at a memorial for the victims, including his 1-year-old daughter, Amarianna, her pregnant mother, the woman’s 5-year-old son and her unborn baby. "Him every day, him smiling and being just — you would think of nothing like that would happen," Windham said. NINE PEOPLE KILLED IN PENNSYLVANIA SHOOTING; SUSPECTED GUNMAN FOUND DEAD: REPORT The 45-year-old gunman died of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after the Friday evening shooting, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said. Authorities have not publicly identified the shooter or the victims, but Lorah said the gunman was related to seven of the eight people killed. The eighth victim was a friend of the pregnant woman. Nicole and Debra Eller, whose best friend was among the victims, said they had known the family for more than 30 years. Nicole Eller said the shooter "was a good guy, and then he started going downhill with everything." "They were a lovely family. Who would have thought this would ever happen?" Debra Eller said. "Oh my gosh, this is so upsetting. This should have never happened to her or the kids or anybody. His grandchildren, his kids, how can you do that?" IOWA MAN SUSPECTED OF KILLING 6 FAMILY MEMBERS IN 'ACT OF EVIL' Mourners gathered Sunday outside the home where the shooting unfolded, leaving candles, flowers and stuffed animals. Windham wore a T-shirt showing photos of the women and children killed, along with the words, "Forever In My Heart." "Words can’t even explain what I’m going through right now," Windham said. "But I gotta be strong for my community, you know what I’m saying? My family, my daughters, my sons, everybody." Investigators recovered video and audio evidence that included muffled gunshots from inside the home shortly before two "distressed" women arrived and began pounding on the door, Lorah said. The gunman then came outside and shot the women as they ran toward him before returning inside. MONTANA MAN WHO KILLED 4 CHILDREN, 4 OTHER FAMILY MEMBERS AT SUNDAY DINNER WAS ASKED TO MOVE OUT: RELATIVE Officers arrived within minutes after receiving an alert through ShotSpotter, a gunshot-detection system, police said. No additional shots were fired after police arrived, Lorah said, adding that sounds later mistaken for gunfire came from flash-bang devices used by SWAT officers. Responding officers found the two women dead outside the home. After deploying a drone and robot, police entered and found the bodies of the 5-year-old boy and 1-year-old girl on the first floor; two more women and two young men in a stairwell; and the shooter on the second floor. "Out of respect for the victims and the families, I will not discuss the details of what our officers encountered inside that home," Lorah said at a news conference. "But I want our community to understand the gravity of what happened and the profound impact this tragedy has had on those involved and on our community as a whole." 8 FAMILY MEMBERS, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, FOUND DEAD IN MICHIGAN FIRE; AT LEAST ONE VICTIM SHOT: POLICE Lorah declined to discuss a possible motive but suggested mental health could be a factor. He said investigators would interview relatives and examine the cellphones of the women who were killed outside the home. "They knew something was going on at that house," Lorah said. "We have to figure out what that is." Lorah said the scene was devastating for first responders. "Some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," he said. DISPATCH AUDIO RELEASED IN MICHIGAN FAMILY MURDER-SUICIDE AS TROUBLED FAMILY'S SECRETS EMERGE Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said the police department "arrived at a horrific scene, faced unimaginable circumstances, and carried out their duties with courage and professionalism." "They too are members of this community, and they too will carry the weight of what happened last night," Devlin said at a Saturday news conference, addressing the victims’ families directly: "I am so deeply sorry. What happened to you was horrific, and there is nothing that any of us can say today that will make this any easier. "Our entire community is with you, we’re grieving with you. And we are here to support you." Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said he spoke with Devlin and offered his administration’s "full support" after what he called "the tragic mass shooting." Speaking later at a campaign rally outside Philadelphia, Shapiro also referenced the shooting of two Philadelphia police officers earlier Saturday. PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, PARTNER SHOT 12 TIMES IN AMBUSH; SUSPECT FOUND HIDING IN TREE "Today has been a dark day across this commonwealth," Shapiro said. title: Trump's backyard is quietly transforming into 'Silicon Valley South' as wealthy Americans flock in
description: Palm Beach is drawing tech giants and Wall Street executives, says real estate expert Margit Brandt, who compares the region to Silicon Valley.
content: A wealthy Southern enclave once known as a playground for retirees and snowbirds is transforming into a growing technology and financial hub, drawing comparisons to Silicon Valley as businesses, Wall Street executives and entrepreneurs move in. Palm Beach County, Florida, is attracting new attention as wealthy Americans seek alternatives to high-tax states like New York and California. "Palm Beach has changed from a place where people come to retire to a place that people come to build," luxury real estate expert Margit Brandt told Fox News Digital. "There's been countless CEOs and major heads of companies that have moved their businesses to Palm Beach," she said, pointing to Florida's favorable tax climate and lifestyle as major draws. THE RED STATES RACING AHEAD IN AMERICA’S POWERFUL WEALTH BOOM — AND THE STATES FALLING BEHIND The region is also home to President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate, often dubbed the "Southern White House," placing the emerging business hub in the backyard of one of the country's most recognizable political landmarks. The shift comes amid changing migration patterns across the country, with Internal Revenue Service data for 2022–2023 showing taxpayer losses across numerous California and Northeastern counties, while much of the Southeast recorded gains. Brandt believes Palm Beach County could become a major technology hub, citing its room for expansion as an advantage over more densely developed destinations. "We have tons of room to grow," she said, pointing to areas like Wellington and western Palm Beach County where new schools, hospitals and infrastructure could accommodate additional businesses and families. The region is also attracting technology investment alongside its established financial services industry. In September 2025, California-based software company ServiceNow announced plans to establish a regional innovation hub and artificial intelligence institute in West Palm Beach. AMERICANS KEEP MOVING TO TEXAS AND FLORIDA — BUT ONE OTHER RED STATE IS GROWING EVEN FASTER The expansion is projected to generate $1.8 billion in economic impact and create more than 850 jobs over five years, according to the company. ServiceNow also committed to occupying up to 200,000 square feet of office space at 10 CityPlace, a development by billionaire real estate investor Stephen Ross's Related Ross. "The tech has particularly been exciting for Palm Beach County," Brandt said. Meanwhile, Palm Beach County's population reached an estimated 1.58 million residents in July 2025, an increase of 5.6% since April 2020, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Brandt said new office developments in West Palm Beach and Palm Beach Gardens have made it easier for companies to establish a presence in the region. "Florida has just been a really easy landing place," she said. For Brandt, the region's evolution is far from complete. "Palm Beach County, I think we're like in beginning stages of what's possible here," she said.

title: 'Helicopter brain' could be making you feel sick: How to spot it and what to do
description: Doomscrolling is linked to higher anxiety and psychological distress, but a neurologist says it may also trigger what he calls "helicopter brain."
content: A new analysis of 44 studies has linked "doomscrolling" to higher levels of anxiety and psychological distress — but for some, information overload may also contribute to a phenomenon one neurologist calls "helicopter brain." The research, published in Frontiers in Psychology, found associations between excessive consumption of negative online content and poorer mental health, although it did not establish a cause-and-effect relationship. Board-certified neurologist Dr. Steven Resnick uses the term "helicopter brain" to describe a nervous system that remains constantly on high alert, much like a "helicopter parent" who constantly hovers over a child to protect them from harm. FUNCTIONAL MEDICINE EXPERT WARNS EVERYDAY HABITS MAY ACCELERATE CELLULAR AGING "Imagine your own helicopter — that is your nervous system," Resnick, chief of the Division of Neurology and medical director of the Comprehensive Stroke Center at Mount Sinai Medical Center in Miami Beach, Florida, told Fox News Digital. "Your nervous system’s job is to protect you from harm." Information overload, overstimulation and uncertainty can keep the brain on high alert, activating the autonomic nervous system, the neurologist said. "The brain is scanning for danger," Resnick said. "When it scans for danger, then you have that autonomic nervous system pushing the accelerator." NEARLY 3 IN 4 AMERICANS ARE BATTLING THE SAME EXHAUSTING HEALTH PROBLEM, CDC REVEALS The neurologist, who also hosts "The Healthy Mind" podcast, said he often sees patients experiencing symptoms they struggle to explain, including headaches, gastrointestinal issues, fatigue, sleep problems, tingling and dizziness. In some cases, patients undergo evaluations by multiple specialists before identifying a potential explanation. "They end up going to see a neurologist, who sends them to the gastroenterologist, who sends them to the cardiologist, then the rheumatologist," he said. "They don't understand what they're feeling is actually authentic, it's real — it's the nervous system that is actually activated." THINK YOUR CORTISOL IS TOO HIGH? EXPERT REVEALS THE TRUTH BEHIND VIRAL WELLNESS CRAZE Although constant information overload can contribute to this heightened state of alertness, Resnick said the same patterns can emerge in response to everyday stressors and deeply ingrained habits. The neurologist outlined the following five strategies for recognizing these patterns, calming the nervous system and developing healthier responses to stress. No. 1: Recognize what you’re feeling When seeing patients, Resnick said his first step is to listen to them, to ensure that he understands what they’re feeling. "I hear patients say, ‘I'm scared, I'm fearful, I'm concerned, I'm worried,’ and then you start to realize what their nervous system is telling you," he told Fox News Digital. "I would never have done that by just fixing the problem right away." The nervous system can begin to calm when patients feel truly heard, safe, secure and connected, the neurologist said. "The solution can be done later," Resnick said. "And we have to stop using the word ‘fixing,’ because a lot of things cannot be fixed — but over time, you can start feeling better." No. 2: Name the pattern Recognizing recurring patterns — in thoughts, behaviors and reactions — is an important first step toward changing them, Resnick said. "Mindfulness is not just about meditation; it's about noticing," he said. That could mean recognizing the same conflict happening repeatedly with a co-worker, lying awake each night with racing thoughts, or turning to food or cigarettes during periods of stress, according to Resnick. THIS ONE QUESTION MAY REVEAL WHETHER YOUR BODY IS GETTING THE REST IT NEEDS, STUDY FINDS When those behaviors repeat, people can begin operating on "autopilot," he said. "The brain wants to resort to what is familiar, what is safe and what is known," Resnick said. "It keeps going back to that because the brain understands it, retrieves it and does the same thing over and over again." Breaking that cycle requires recognizing the pattern and making a conscious effort to respond differently, he added. No. 3: Catch the trigger Next, the neurologist said it’s important to "catch the cue," or trigger, that kick-starts the pattern. "It's a stimulus," he said. "It's something that is very sneaky. It goes under your level of consciousness." "It could be your boss' face. It could be a telephone. It could be a chair or a couch in a room. It could be a smell or a feeling." That cue can trigger an almost automatic behavior, Resnick said, such as procrastinating, eating, reaching for a drink or lashing out. If the behavior provides pleasure or helps someone avoid an uncomfortable feeling or situation, the brain can become more likely to repeat it. Even worrying can become part of that cycle. If the feared outcome doesn’t happen, Resnick said, the brain may interpret the worry as protective, reinforcing the habit. ONE TYPE OF SLEEP LINKED TO DRAMATICALLY LOWER RISK OF DEMENTIA, PARKINSON'S AND 81 OTHER DISEASES Breaking the pattern starts with identifying the specific cues that set it in motion, according to the neurologist. Rather than viewing anxiety or overthinking as something that happens "all the time," Resnick encourages patients to pinpoint a specific episode, consider what triggered it and recognize the behavior and potential reward that followed. No. 4: Reward the new habit The next step is replacing the unwanted behavior with a healthier habit that provides a noticeable reward, Resnick said. "Give your new habit a reward you can feel," he advised. DIETITIAN REVEALS SIMPLE EATING STRATEGY FOR BETTER SLEEP — AND ONE HABIT TO AVOID That reward does not have to be significant. After an early-morning workout, for example, it might be a sense of accomplishment or an improved mood. A healthy shake after the workout could provide another small reward. "Give your new habit a reward you can feel." "Even checkboxing something on a piece of paper feels good," Resnick said. These immediate, positive reinforcements can help the brain begin associating the healthier behavior with something rewarding. "Rewards are very important," the neurologist said. "Even the small ones are important." No. 5: Float instead of fight Finally, when anxiety or panic strikes, Resnick recommends taking a counterintuitive approach: "Float instead of fight." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES In many cases, he said, people are not only afraid of a particular situation, but of the anxious feelings that may result. Someone with claustrophobia, for example, may fear getting an MRI because they anticipate the physical sensations of anxiety that could arise inside the machine. "Don’t fight it," Resnick advised. "You want to allow it. You want to feel it." Avoiding a situation can reinforce the brain’s perception that it poses a threat, he said, while safely experiencing it can help create a new association. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "After you have that experience where you felt safe, and you went toward it, then your brain and body … pair it as being safe," Resnick said. The goal, he added, is "to teach the brain safety through your body and through your brain and mind." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ While these strategies may help people better manage stress and anxiety, Resnick emphasized the importance of recognizing the patterns behind the symptoms. People experiencing persistent or unexplained physical symptoms should seek medical evaluation to rule out underlying health conditions.
