A network source for ABC News told Fox News Digital, "We always review every situation in a thorough and thoughtful manner and will not be providing further comment at this time."

title: Toddler stabbed in face, suspect previously deemed unfit for trial in attacks on 2 children: report
description: Nelson Blanco allegedly stabbed a toddler at a Rhode Island school bus stop, decades after being found incompetent to stand trial for knifing two boys.
content: A stranger allegedly stabbed a toddler in the face as she sat in her stroller at a Rhode Island school bus stop, years after he was accused of knifing two other children and found incompetent to stand trial. The child’s fight for survival has brought renewed scrutiny into the suspect’s past, including an attack on two children more than two decades ago and repeated findings that he was incompetent to stand trial. Nelson Blanco, 46, is accused of stabbing the 2-year-old girl and her mother Wednesday afternoon near Broad and Public streets in Providence, police said. SOUTH CAROLINA MOM ACCUSED OF KNIFE ATTACK ON YOUNG CHILDREN; 6-YEAR-OLD MAY LOSE ARM: SHERIFF'S OFFICE The toddler was taken to Hasbro Children’s Hospital in critical condition. Her mother, who suffered a stab wound to the shoulder, was treated and released, according to local reporting. The mother was waiting with her daughter for her other children to get off a school bus when Blanco allegedly approached and made insulting comments, Providence Police Chief Oscar Perez said, according to WPRI. ANGEL MOM SAYS BLUE STATE DAS ARE PUTTING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CRIMINALS BEFORE PUBLIC SAFETY She crossed the street with the stroller to get away, but Blanco approached again and allegedly attacked the child with a knife, police said, noting there was no evidence he knew either victim. Surveillance video showed the mother and daughter attempting to move away before Blanco grabbed the stroller and struck the child repeatedly, Boston 25 News reported. A bystander tried to intervene, but Blanco allegedly attempted to stab that person before fleeing, according to the outlet. Officers found Blanco hiding in the basement of a nearby home and recovered a knife from a panel box, police said. Authorities said he admitted to the stabbings during questioning. CALIFORNIA STABBING VICTIM'S FRIEND BLASTS 'FAILED' JUSTICE SYSTEM OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT'S RELEASE Blanco allegedly told detectives he stopped the attack because he was on a main street, according to a police report obtained by WPRI. "If I was on a side street, I would have killed them. Both of them," he said, according to the outlet. PROSECUTORS SAY CHARLOTTE TRAIN STABBING CASE WON'T BE DISMISSED REGARDLESS OF COMPETENCY RULING Blanco faces six charges, including two counts police identified as assault with intent to commit murder, felony assault, breaking and entering into an occupied dwelling of a person 60 or older, and two weapons charges. No plea was entered during his Thursday appearance in Rhode Island’s 6th Division District Court. The court referred him to the public defender and requested an evaluation, according to court records reviewed by Fox News Digital. VIOLENT TRANSIT ATTACKS IN ATLANTA, NEW YORK AND CHARLOTTE FUEL CALLS FOR TOUGHER TRACKING OF REPEAT OFFENDERS WPRI reported Blanco is being held without bail pending a competency hearing later this month. His arrest brought back painful memories for Andy Lopez and Dave Belony, who told WPRI they were 6 and 7 years old when Blanco attacked them while they played in Lopez’s backyard on Sept. 27, 2003. CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND Belony said he recognized Blanco immediately when he saw his booking photo on social media Wednesday night. "I knew it was him, because I will always remember that face," he told the station. "My heart dropped, and it truly felt like my world had stopped." Court records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Blanco faced two felony assault charges and a charge of possessing a knife or firearm during a crime, stemming from the 2003 incident. BANK OF AMERICA EXEC KILLED IN RANDOM TIMES SQUARE STABBING LAID TO REST AS HUNDREDS MOURN YOUNG MOM The docket documents repeated findings that Blanco was incompetent to stand trial from September 2004 through March 2006. Multiple entries state, "Defendant Remains Incompetent." The case remains listed as "under review" in the court portal. More recently, Blanco was found incompetent to stand trial in July in a separate domestic violence case, WPRI reported. A judge accepted a doctor’s recommendation allowing him to remain in outpatient treatment because he was considered unlikely to endanger the community or himself at that time. Lopez and Belony said the earlier attack left them with injuries and trauma that have followed them into adulthood. They told WPRI they were playing with Lopez’s brother when Blanco emerged from a shed behind the house where he had been living. "He didn’t say a word," Belony recalled. "His face was blank and he was just staring at us." Belony said Blanco charged at him, trapping him near a tree. He curled into a ball and covered his head as Blanco stabbed him. DEMOCRATIC BOSTON COUNCILOR RIPS 'SOFT-ON-CRIME' POLICIES AFTER SUSPECTED GUNMAN'S VIOLENT PAST REVEALED Blanco then turned toward Lopez, the men said. "My brother yelled at me to run, and I was trying to run but my body just froze," Lopez told WPRI. "He stabbed me twice in the eye — the first time it was blurry, and then the second time I couldn’t see anything." Both children were rushed to Hasbro Children’s Hospital. Their recovery took three months and included at least three surgeries each, they told the outlet. Lopez was left permanently blind in his left eye, an injury he said derailed his dreams of becoming a police officer or truck driver. "Most of the opportunities I wanted to have in life are gone," he said. "I’m very grateful I’m alive, but my life is restricted." Belony said he was stabbed at least five times in his stomach, back and ribs and continues to struggle emotionally. The men said learning about the latest attack left them devastated for the mother and toddler, and determined to speak out. "It’s frustrating for us, not only because of what happened to us, but because it has happened to others," Lopez told WPRI. "He was given a chance 23 years ago, and 23 years later, he did the same thing." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We want justice for the victims," Belony said. "What is it going to take for him to be held accountable for his actions?" title: 'I lost us that game': Nick Sirianni makes decision that opened door to a Jacksonville Jaguars comeback win
description: Nick Sirianni says he cost the Eagles the game after a short kickoff let the Jaguars set up Cam Little's stunning walk-off 57-yard field goal.
content: NFL head coaches often take responsibility for not helping their team, but usually when they seek the blame for losing, they are often covering for someone else's mistake. Then we have Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni. He took the blame for the Eagles' walk-off field goal loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday because, well, it was indeed ultimately on him. Why? Because the Eagles blew the game in London by not kicking the ball into the end zone while clinging to a 17-16 lead with only eight seconds to play. JALEN HURTS CURSES AT RECEIVER IN VIRAL HOT-MIC MOMENT DURING EAGLES' COLLAPSE AGAINST RAMS Down two points, the Jaguars returned the kick that was short of the end zone 53 yards to the Eagles' 39-yard line. The runback took seven seconds. And with one second remaining left, Cam Little, who has a kicking leg like a howitzer, connected on a game-winning 57-yard field goal. That left the Eagles with their third loss of the season. And Sirianni with mushy peas on his face. "I lost us that game and that's what I said to our guys," Sirianni admitted in his post-game news conference. "What hurt there is that the guys fought so hard, and I don’t make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game, and I put that fully on me." Sirianni was not in the mood to accept other reasons the Eagles lost. "At the end of the day, I didn’t make the right decision, and it cost us the game," he said. "You know, and so there’s no other way around it. There’s nothing really else to say about that. It’s just I didn’t do my job good enough in that situation." It was obviously not all Sirianni's fault. The Eagles' kickoff coverage unit was leaky from the start of the game to the end. And maybe kicker Jake Elliott should have kicked the ball into the end zone of his own accord. He is a veteran and should understand the situation. But, people in Philly, raise your hand if you disagree that Sirianni had a brain lock. Waiting for a hand to rise. Still waiting. Nobody. Sirianni is going to carry this for a while because Eagles fans are not too forgiving. And neither is the Philadelphia media. "It’s just like you would feel if you missed a free throw at the end of the game, or if you had a drop," Sirianni said. "I’ve been in both of those places. And those ones stick with you, and that will stick with me for a long time. "... Yeah, that one will hurt for a long time. I still think about those other things that have, I’ve lost games for us in the past as far as, you know, when I played." MIKE TOMLIN POINTS OUT DALLAS COWBOYS 'NEGLIGENT' COACHING MISTAKES AND PUT HIMSELF IN CONVERSATION TO TAKE JOB NEXT YEAR There are two issues with what Sirianni just said: First, it is the coach's job to stop the bleeding. His team already allowed a fourth-quarter loss to the Rams last week to become a two-week disaster and grow into a three-game losing skid overall. Second, if Sirianni's message to his team is that this loss will stick with him a long time, that is exactly the wrong message to send. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! What's up with these NFC East coaches and last second kickoffs? A couple of weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys blew a game against the Baltimore Ravens in the final seconds when coach Brian Schottenheimer did the exact opposite of what Sirianni did on Sunday by sending the kickoff into the end zone, which didn't tick any time off the clock. The Ravens used seven seconds to get into field goal range. So Sirianni did something different and still got burned. The crazy part of this is that Sirianni says he saw that Dallas situation on tape. "I watched a ton of those situations after that Dallas game and, again, just didn’t make the right decision in this particular case," he said. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

title: Mojtaba Khamenei defies ‘malicious’ attacks as US Army zeroes in on Iran’s 350,000 troops
description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed U.S. and Israeli strikes failed to weaken Iran's military, as the U.S. Army released a new threat guide.
content: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed Oct. 8 that U.S. and Israeli strikes had failed to undermine Iran's domestic security forces, praising police personnel for resisting attacks launched in February under Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion. Khamenei's remarks on X also came as the U.S. Army released a new battlefield identification guide to help American troops recognize members of Iran's conventional military, known as the Artesh, whose ground forces were estimated by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security in June at 350,000 personnel. "The criminal US-Zionist enemy's desperate efforts and malicious attacks on the pillars of social order and security, which are unparalleled throughout history, have not caused the courageous personnel of the Police Force to waver even a fraction in their mission," Khamenei wrote in a statement. Khamenei specifically praised Iran's Law Enforcement Command, known as FARAJA, accusing the United States and Israel of targeting the institution responsible for maintaining domestic order. "The focus and persistence of the criminal US-Zionist enemy in striking at the Police Force at its various levels, from its highest command levels down to those who are on the frontline, has only served to underscore the paramount importance of this institution more than ever," he wrote. IRAN PROVES THAT IT MIGHT CHANGE ITS MILITARY LEADERS, BUT IT’S NOT CHANGING STRATEGY Iran's security apparatus comprises three principal branches: the Artesh, responsible primarily for conventional territorial defense; the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), tasked with protecting the Islamic Republic and projecting military power; and FARAJA, responsible for domestic law enforcement and internal security. IRAN’S GUTTED RANKS LEAVE LOYALISTS FILLING CRITICAL POSTS — WITH ONE GLARING PROBLEM FARAJA, commanded by Brig. Gen. Ahmadreza Radan, is responsible for maintaining public order, enforcing the country's laws and responding to civil unrest. According to Iran Human Rights Monitor, the force has evolved into a powerful internal security institution involved in suppressing anti-government demonstrations, monitoring political activity and enforcing the regime's ideological restrictions. IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS Radan has also been sanctioned by the United States for his role in human rights abuses. The Treasury Department designated him in September 2010, citing his responsibility for beatings, killings and arbitrary arrests of protesters following Iran's disputed 2009 presidential election. Khamenei also called for strengthening FARAJA on Oct. 8 through additional personnel, equipment and technology, including the use of artificial intelligence for data analysis. AFTER 47 YEARS OF CONFRONTING IRAN, DOES AMERICA HAVE A STRATEGY FOR ENDING THIS WAR? His remarks come as the U.S. Army's Training and Transformation Command published a "Know the Threat" recognition guide Sept. 24, highlighted by Defense News on Oct. 9. The guide shows an Iranian special forces soldier and identifies weapons American troops could encounter, including AKM rifles, Iranian-made Masaf-2 rifles, German-designed G3 rifles, MG3 machine guns and RPG-7 rocket-propelled grenade launchers. The Artesh, Iran's regular military, is separate from the IRGC and its affiliated Basij militia. Its forces operate across four branches: the Ground Forces, Navy, Air Force and Air Defense Force. A June assessment by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security estimated the Artesh's Ground Forces at approximately 350,000 personnel, including 220,000 conscripts. The report found that the Artesh had suffered severe losses across its air, naval and air defense components during the opening phase of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign, while its ground forces remained structurally intact because there had been no ground invasion. TRUMP OPENS HORMUZ UNDER FIRE WITH ‘PROJECT FREEDOM’ AS IRAN WARNS OF ATTACKS The Artesh is commanded by Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami, a former Iranian defense minister who assumed command in June 2025. Aside from Khamenei, Hatami issued his own warning Oct. 6, claiming Iran's adversaries faced "historic confusion" after failing to halt military production during the conflict. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hatami also claimed that Iranian defense production continued despite American and Israeli attacks, saying the country's military production lines had continued operating during the conflict. The extent of Iran's military recovery remains unclear. The Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security assessed in June that the country's conventional air, naval and air defense forces had suffered severe damage during the conflict. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, said Oct. 8 that Washington would not resume military strikes against Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, citing "productive discussions" between the two countries.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS WHAT OTHER GASLIGHTING FEMALE ATHLETES WON'T ABOUT THE NAKED SYDNEY SWEENEY AD Sweeney later appeared to respond by sharing images of famous athletes, including Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki, who had posed nude for ESPN’s Body Issue. Adrienne Uthe, founder of Kronus Communications, previously told Fox News Digital that while Sweeney's ad may have ruffled feathers, "women having agency also means allowing women to make choices about their image that other women may not personally agree with." "People are entitled to dislike the ad, just like women athletes are entitled to criticize it for their own reasons," Uthe said. "But I don't think this is materially damaging to Sydney Sweeney in any way, shape or form. "In fact, I don't think it's a large departure from who she is and what her brand represents. She's a beautiful woman right now at the peak of her career, and she ultimately can decide which projects she wants to take and which ones she doesn't." BROADCAST BIAS: MEDIA BASH SYDNEY SWEENEY, BUT COVER FOR LEFTIST MACKLEMORE She added, "And she's chosen to make sexuality a part of her brand for better or for worse." Novig defended the original advertisement as a "fun idea" created with "confidence, humor and a playful edge." The latest campaign is not the first time Sweeney has found herself at the center of a major advertising controversy. In 2025, her American Eagle campaign, titled "Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans," drew backlash over a promotional video that played on the words "genes" and "jeans." title: DAVID MARCUS: In Springfield, Ohio, only Trump can mend MAGA-Chamber of Commerce rift
description: Springfield, Ohio, small business owners reveal what they need from Vivek Ramaswamy and John Husted on taxes, regulations, and immigration reform.
content: At a rally in Ohio last week, President Donald Trump told his supporters that, "Even if you hate John Husted, even if you hate Vivek Ramaswamy, you have to go vote for them." It was a blunt assessment of the GOP’s respective candidates for Senate and governor, but one that Trump, who wins Ohio elections like Tom Brady won Super Bowls, knows is vitally important. Trump would laugh off the remark, saying that nobody really hates the GOP candidates. But he was making an essential point, especially in Ohio, which is the front line of the war between the traditional GOP and Trump’s MAGA base, much of it centered on the question of immigration. To hear from the Chamber of Commerce side, I spoke with Jim Lagos, who has lived his entire 75 years in Springfield, owns several buildings downtown, and has been a central figure in the attempts to revitalize the city’s downtown district. TRUMP TOUTS ‘GOLDEN AGE’ AT OHIO RALLY, URGES VOTERS TO DELIVER GOP MIDTERM WINS "You have to pull the trigger," Jim told me of efforts to bring the very pretty, but very empty downtown back to life. "My father always used to tell me 'Christopher Columbus took a risk.'" Jim, as is customary for civic leaders, had nice things to say about Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown and gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, both of whom he has met. But he is all in for Husted and even more so for Ramasamy, who he hopes will slash regulations to speed up the recovery of towns like Springfield. RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION "We have temporary cuts on taxes for small business in Ohio," Jim said. "But they need to be extended. Big companies got a permanent break, because they are smart enough to donate to both parties." Over the past three decades, Jim has rehabilitated several historic buildings in Springfield and succeeded in filling most of the space with occupants. "Sometimes, when business is struggling, you have to carry them for a while until it gets better," he said. ICE PREPARES MAJOR OPERATION TARGETING HAITIANS LOSING TPS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING The issue that most bitterly divides the business leaders in Springfield from the MAGA base of Trump voters in the area is immigration, and in particular, the wave of 15,000 Haitian refugees who arrived between 2020 and 2025, overwhelming schools, housing stock, and even the Bureau of Motor Vehicles, according to locals. Jim admits that the messaging, including the idea that Haitian migrants are better workers who don’t do drugs and want overtime, not only missed the mark, but downright offended many local native residents. Ramaswamy has, in the past veered toward a similar sentiment, which Frank, who works construction in the area, took some issue with. "I don’t like his idea that immigrants are, like, making us better from competition, I’d rather put Americans first," Frank said. According to Walter Curt, an investigative journalist who lives in Springfield, "When Trump came to office the first time, a bunch of factories got built in the area, and as soon as Biden got in, he staffed them with Haitians, effectively," through tax breaks to temp companies and business owners. DEM SENATE CANDIDATE SHERROD BROWN CLAIMS HE SUPPORTS 'CLOSING THE BORDER'; GOP SAYS RECORD PROVES OTHERWISE Importantly, while Curt does hold current Ohio governor and well known loather of President Trump, Mike DeWine, culpable for the Haitian situation, he does not blame the Haitians themselves, or Husted or Ramaswamy. "The entire country of Haiti would be in his front yard [Ohio] if it was up to DeWine," Curt said. "If anybody believes Vivek is of the same mind, I haven’t seen any evidence of that." AMERICA NEEDS WORKERS, BUT TRUMP'S POLICIES ARE SHARPLY CUTTING LEGAL IMMIGRATION Further complicating the immigration issue in Springfield is the fact that there is a largely Hispanic immigrant population well integrated into and assimilated with the broader community, something one does not see with the Haitian refugees. Victoria and Ambrosio opened Food Fusion, a large eatery with great food, a year ago, and they employ a mix of native born Springfielders as well as immigrants from Mexico, a dynamic you also see with the clientele. SMALL BUSINESS OWNERS BUILT THE AMERICAN DREAM. DEMOCRATS WANT TO TAKE IT FROM YOU What these first-time restaurant owners want from government is more transparency about regulations. "You don’t know everything that comes with it," Victoria told me. "As far as taxes, you have to know this, you have have to know that, and not just the rules and regulations of liquor licenses. There’s really no help for small business owners." Trump is correct that the vast majority of Republican voters in Ohio don’t hate Husted or Ramaswamy. Many downright love them. But in a close midterm race, the GOP needs those who don’t. title: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning's words immediately came back to bite him in awful loss to UCLA
description: Dylan Raiola went 6-19 with two interceptions before being benched as the Oregon Ducks committed seven turnovers in a stunning home loss to UCLA.
content: This was supposed to be the year. The Oregon Ducks started the 2026 college football season as a consensus top-five team under head coach Dan Lanning. They brought back Dante Moore and added Dylan Raiola, a former starter at Nebraska, as a backup quarterback. They had a highly-paid roster full of former top recruits, along with impactful transfer portal additions. They were coming off back-to-back College Football Playoff appearances with a combined 26-3 record across the regular and postseason in 2024-2025. Some suggested it was the best team Oregon's ever had. Almost immediately, however, the Ducks started taking on water. Boise State nearly pulled off the upset in Eugene in week one. Then Oklahoma State finished their upset bid in week two behind a dominant offensive performance. DAN LANNING BLASTS USC AFTER OREGON'S WIN, AS LINCOLN RILEY OFFICIALLY ENTERS HOT SEAT IN LA After an 84-0 shellacking of Portland State, the Ducks went into Los Angeles for a pivotal game against USC at the Coliseum and finally seemed to turn the corner. When Moore left the game after an awful hit from a USC linebacker, Raiola stepped up and looked even better. Moore went 19-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns, helping secure a 41-27 win to seemingly save Oregon's season. Lanning took the opportunity after the win to make a statement about the Ducks' program and where their focus lies. "I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon," Lanning said, referring to high school players from the Los Angeles and Southern California area. "If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here." Fast-forward two weeks and Lanning's words immediately came back to bite him. The Ducks on Saturday hosted UCLA under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. The Bruins, after years of mediocrity, have looked dramatically improved thus far in 2026, though against overmatched opponents like Cal, Purdue, and Maryland. Saturday marked their first test, a road game in one of the toughest environments in college football, against a team with aspirations of reaching and winning the College Football Playoff. For Lanning, it was an opportunity to back up his statement, that if you want to play winning football, you come to Oregon. They lost. The Ducks played one of the sloppiest games from any program in recent memory, somehow managing to turn the ball over an incredible seven times. They had five lost fumbles, and recovered the ball on a sixth fumble. Raiola was so awful, going 6-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions, that Lanning benched him for third stringer Brock Thomas. Four plays for 22 yards and a punt, a one-yard touchdown drive after a Nico Iamaleava fumble, three plays for zero yards, and four plays for 20. 12 plays for 43 yards, and it got worse from there. Much worse. Here's the drive chart for Oregon's second quarter: 16 plays for 25 yards, two punts, two fumbles, and an interception. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Ducks did pick up more yards in the third quarter though, going three plays for two yards, four plays for 22 yards and a fumble, and two plays for seven yards and another pick. That's 31 total yards and only two turnovers instead of three. Progress! While Oregon did have a better run in the fourth quarter, working around another fumble to kick a field goal and finally score their second touchdown of the game with 2:16 remaining, the two-point conversion attempt to tie the score at 17-17 failed. Fittingly, the game ended on Oregon fumbling while trying to run a series of laterals down the field as time expired. As Lanning said, "If you care about winning games, and you're from LA, come to Oregon." Or apparently UCLA. Obviously, Moore being out hurt the Ducks' offense, but seven turnovers? Only 272 yards, at home, against a UCLA team that unquestionably has inferior talent? At one point, Oregon went six straight drives without picking up a first down. At one point, excluding the end of the second quarter, the Ducks turned the ball over on six out of nine drives. That is ... remarkable. From 2023-2025, Lanning built Oregon into one of the most consistent teams in the country. They were 38-5, and went undefeated in their first season in the Big Ten to secure the number one overall seed in the 2024-2025 playoff. For most of that run, his teams were seen as well coached and disciplined. title: Gas stations may be hiding some of America's most overlooked affordable fast-food options
description: From Wawa's hoagies to Buc-ee's chopped brisket, these convenience store and gas station meals can be surprisingly delicious budget-friendly meals. Check out this list.
content: Some people may shy away from the idea of getting a meal at a gas station or convenience store — but doing so could be an easy, and surprisingly delicious, way to save money while on a road trip or during a daily commute. Restaurant menu prices rose 0.3% in both July and August this year, and menu prices were 3.4% higher this August than in August 2025, the National Restaurant Association reported in September. "Gas stations with quick service attached to them like 7Eleven, am/pm, etc. are the real value now," a Reddit user said in a recent thread. FAST-FOOD DRIVE-THRUS TOOK OVER AMERICAN MORNINGS FOR THESE KEY REASONS "Everything has shifted upwards. Fast food is now fast casual pricing. Fast casual is now sit down restaurant pricing." Amid these increases, finding inexpensive and convenient dining options might be challenging, but it’s not impossible. Here are a few convenience store and gas station chains offering tasty, budget-friendly meals and snacks — ranging from a $5 half-foot-long sub sandwich to a $9.99 box filled to the brim with Southern comfort food. QuickChek New Jersey-based gas station and convenience chain QuickChek has more than 160 locations across New Jersey and parts of New York. Six-inch subs and sandwiches cost $5 a piece, while a $4 breakfast combo includes an English muffin or croissant breakfast sandwich and a 20-ounce hot coffee or energy drink, according to the website. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The chain also offers a small, medium or large iced coffee for $1.99, which includes any customizations. Wawa Headquartered in Pennsylvania, Wawa serves coffee, a variety of breakfast items, snacks and freshly made sandwiches. The chain earned the top spot in the American Customer Satisfaction Index’s 2024 convenience store ranking primarily due to the chain’s food offerings, especially its hoagies. A classic Italian hoagie on a six-inch roll costs $6.29, while a breakfast meal including a breakfast sandwich, a hash brown and a coffee or fountain drink costs $5, according to the Wawa website. Buc-ee’s Since its founding in 1982, Beaver-themed gas station chain Buc-ee’s has developed a reputation for affordable gas prices, logo-adorned merchandise, and its extensive food offerings. The lower gas prices are mainly due to the fact that customers are expected to spend more money inside the store, Yahoo Finance reported in June. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The chopped brisket sandwich is a popular grab-and-go meal option, with the standard 8-ounce size selling for less than $10 at most locations, according to a website sharing Buc-ee’s menu items and pricing information. Some Redditors say that a trip to Buc-ee’s is not complete without Beaver nuggets, a sweet, crunchy puffed corn snack. A large bag of Beaver nuggets sells for about five dollars, and the homemade fudge costs about four dollars per square, according to Southern Living. All Buc-ee’s locations are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, according to the website, and as an added bonus, the restrooms are known for being extremely sanitary. In a Buc-ee’s thread on Reddit, a commenter said, "Be sure to check out the clean bathrooms!" Parker’s Kitchen Founded in Georgia in 1976, Parker’s Kitchen operates 110 locations across Georgia and South Carolina. Known for Southern-inspired food like fried chicken and biscuits, the gas station and convenience chain offers meal options with prices that rival those at fast-food restaurants. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The lunch menu features a $4.99 pulled pork sandwich and a $3.99 barbecue chicken sandwich, as well as a $3.99 cheeseburger, according to the website.

title: Daughters of the American Revolution axes chapter that challenged transgender membership
description: DAR's National Board voted to disband the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas, which led efforts to block transgender women from joining the organization.
content: The Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) voted Saturday to disband its Martha Laird Chapter in Texas that fought to bar transgender women from joining the historic organization, citing violations of its national bylaws. In a letter to chapter members, DAR Organizing Secretary General Marguerite Hogan Fritsch announced that the National Board of Management had approved the chapter's dissolution by a two-thirds majority vote. "On October 10, 2026, at the meeting of the National Board of Management of the National Society, Daughters of the American Revolution a resolution passed by two-thirds majority vote to disband the Martha Laird Chapter, NSDAR," Fritsch said in the letter. "The actions of the chapter have been found in violation of Article XIX, Section 4 of the Bylaws of the National Society Daughters of the American Revolution," the letter continued. The letter did not identify the specific conduct that constituted a violation or state whether the chapter's opposition to transgender membership contributed to the decision. SORORITY ALUMNAE TAKE LEGAL FIGHT TO FEDERAL COURT AFTER BEING 'GIVEN A BROTHER' INSTEAD OF SISTERHOOD The National Society Daughters of the American Revolution confirmed to Fox News Digital that the organization had voted to disband the local Texas chapter but denied it was due to its views on membership. "The National Board of Management voted on October 10 to disband the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas after finding that chapter officers had used the chapter’s name, leadership positions, communications, and governance processes to further the goals of a separate advocacy organization," the group told Fox News Digital. "The Board determined that it was this use of chapter authority and resources – not the views being advocated – that constituted conduct discrediting the National Society under Article XIX, Section 4 of the National Bylaws." "The Board’s decision was not based on the chapter’s or its members’ views concerning membership eligibility, their efforts to propose changes to the National Bylaws, or their right to advocate for changes in National Society governance," the statement continued. The group noted that at their June 2026 meeting, national members had rejected a resolution to add further membership restrictions. Individual members of the Texas chapter retain their DAR membership and are free to advocate for changes to the National Bylaws through the Society’s established governance processes, the organization said. ALL-WOMEN'S SCHOOL WELLESLEY COLLEGE RESPONDS TO ACCUSATIONS OF ADMITTING BIOLOGICAL MALE TRANS STUDENTS The chapter previously challenged DAR leadership's position on transgender membership, with member Laura McDonald telling Fox News Digital last year that the organization was contradicting its founding mission by recognizing transgender women as eligible members. "But, then they go on to say that a man who claims he's a woman is a woman, and therefore he's eligible for membership. But if you are a man that doesn't claim to be a woman, you're not eligible for membership," McDonald said. Conservative California superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw told Fox News Digital that women and girls are being told that spaces created to protect their privacy, dignity, and opportunities "no longer belong to them," including sports, restrooms, locker rooms, and now, according to her, the Daughters of the American Revolution."The women of the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas stood their ground. They sought to preserve a definition of "Daughters" based on biological sex and asked for a clear vote. On October 10, national leadership dissolved their chapter," Shaw said. SMITH COLLEGE 'MAKES A MOCKERY' OF ALL-WOMEN STATUS BY ADMITTING TRANSGENDER STUDENTS, EDUCATION WATCHDOG SAYS "Think about that. Women who stood up for their convictions saw their chapter, with a history dating back to 1942, dissolved. Here is the damning question national leadership needs to answer: Why should women be punished for standing up for the very definition of the organization they belong to?" she added. Shaw also pointed to similar debates across the country concerning sports and privacy in women's spaces, and said "this is about more than one chapter.""Our daughters deserve a future where they never have to ask permission to stand up for the truth, and where no woman is punished for having the courage to speak it," Shaw said. Under DAR's national bylaws, Article XIX, Section 4 authorizes the National Board of Management to discipline or disband chapters that violate organizational rules or engage in conduct that discredits the DAR. The dissolution comes nearly three months after Rep. Ben Cline, R-Va., introduced the Daughters of the American Revolution Membership Integrity Act, which would amend DAR's congressional charter to restrict membership to biological women. Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., subsequently introduced companion legislation in the Senate. "Rather than honoring and preserving a lineage-based organization for women, it has embraced radical gender ideology at the expense of the women it was created to serve," Cline said. In September 2024, the Martha Laird Chapter, supported by 11 other chapters, submitted a proposed bylaw amendment defining membership eligibility based on biological sex. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The Center for American Liberty also provided legal assistance to the chapter, challenging DAR leadership's contention that excluding transgender applicants could jeopardize the organization's tax-exempt status. The proposed amendment was rejected by DAR's National Board of Management in February 2025. McDonald criticized the decision at the time. "The rejection by the National Board of Management of our proposal to define a woman in our bylaws sadly confirms what we knew all along – that leadership is taking a political stance which is not based on fears of the loss of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status," McDonald said in a statement to Fox News Digital. DAR, founded in 1890, previously maintained that its longstanding membership policies allowed women with legally amended birth certificates to join, provided they otherwise met the organization's genealogical requirements. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Under the dissolution notice, Martha Laird Chapter members will be transferred to member-at-large status and have until Nov. 9 to secure acceptance into another chapter. The letter also directed that dues previously remitted to the chapter be refunded.

title: Week 6 AP Top 25 poll sees a major mixup and a new top team in the country after an upset-filled Saturday
description: Georgia claims the No. 1 spot in the AP Poll after its stunning road win over Alabama, while Kentucky vaults from unranked to No. 15 in Week 6.
content: Every college football Saturday is a memorable one, but some weekends deliver more drama than others, and Week 6 certainly falls into that category after the upsets that took place all around the country. The Bulldogs were rewarded by taking over the No. 1 spot in the rankings. Texas, the No. 1 team in the nation since Week 2, fell six spots after being stunned at the Cotton Bowl by unranked Oklahoma. The biggest movers in the latest AP Poll were two teams that faced off against one another on Saturday, with Kentucky going from unranked to No. 15 after stunning LSU in overtime. Lane Kiffin's Tigers dropped 12 spots all the way to No. 22 after falling to 4-2 on the year. KIRBY SMART HAS ENTERED HIS MOST DANGEROUS ERA AFTER GEORGIA’S AGGRESSIVE WIN OVER ALABAMA Week 6 AP Top 25 Poll Welcome letters are in order for Northwestern, Wake Forest, and Kentucky, as all three teams enter the Top 25 after being unranked a week ago. Oregon, after its home loss to UCLA, and Florida, after being blown out at home by South Carolina, both exited the polls, after both the Ducks and Gators were ranked inside the Top 16 in Week 5. INDIANA SURVIVES NEBRASKA IN COMEBACK WIN, EXTENDS NATION'S LONGEST ACTIVE WINNING STREAK While the No. 1 next to Georgia's name is the ultimate sign of respect from voters, it's also worth noting that Alabama remained at No. 6 despite losing to the Bulldogs in its first dropped game of the year. title: Bill Gates sounds alarm on AI-powered cyberattacks, warns of 'negative surprises' within a year
description: Bill Gates warned that AI-powered cyberattacks could disrupt financial systems and fuel extortion schemes, with criminals exploiting unsafeguarded models.
content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates warned Sunday that artificial intelligence could fuel a wave of cyberattacks over the next year, and said that malicious actors are gaining access to increasingly powerful AI models without adequate safeguards. Gates warned that criminals could exploit the latest AI technology to disrupt financial systems, extort businesses and carry out increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. "When you have bad people, no safeguards, and then the latest models, that's where, over the next year, primarily in the cyber area, we are going to have a lot of negative surprises," Gates said during a "State of the Union" interview with CNN's Jake Tapper. BILL GATES WARNS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE 'POWERFUL ENOUGH' TO CAUSE 'A BILLION DEATHS' IF UNCHECKED Democratic strategist Oliver Libby told Fox News Digital that Gates' warning underscores the challenge facing policymakers as artificial intelligence advances and the United States seeks to maintain its technological competitiveness. "The great challenge both for innovators and governments in the coming months is to balance continued progress in AI with smart regulation. Leaders who can balance ensuring that America is not left behind, but that no American is left out, will win public trust," Libby said. Gates' warning comes as cybersecurity researchers report a sharp increase in AI-enabled threats. According to CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report, attacks by AI-enabled adversaries increased 89% year over year in 2025, while the average time for cybercriminals to move laterally through compromised networks fell to 29 minutes. WATCH: AI SAFETY SCARE SPARKS CAP HILL FIGHT OVER GUARDRAILS: 'CHINA'S GOING TO EAT OUR LUNCH' Tapper pressed Gates about his warning that artificial intelligence could make it easier for terrorists to develop deadly biological weapons, citing his assessment that the risk of a bioterrorist attack could become 50 times greater than that of a natural pandemic. Tapper also questioned how soon such an attack could occur and whether government leaders were doing enough to prevent it. "Well, no, we're not doing enough," Gates said. "The real danger right now is not the AI is getting out of control. We need to work on that, but that's years away in terms of the big impact that might have." title: Rescue expert warns FlyDubai hijacking attempt shows US, allies are ‘playing checkers’ against terror threat

content: The FlyDubai attempted hijacking shows the U.S. and its allies are still using outdated counterterrorism assumptions against increasingly sophisticated enemies, a U.S. rescue expert and 9/11 first responder warns. "They understand us significantly more than we understand them," Stern, who has been "hunting the bad guys" for 30 years, said. "The reason why a football coach watches game tapes is not to watch his own team play, it's to watch the bad guys play," he said. "We gotta start watching some game tapes." AMERICA BUILT A FORTRESS AFTER 9/11. THEN THE THREAT STARTED HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT Stern is intimately in tune with the playbook on the ground in war zones, including the Middle East and Iran. "We conduct these operations in these places still to this very day," he said. "We're actually on the ground, meaning I know people in Hezbollah, I know people in the Taliban. I know people in ISIS. I know people in ISIS-K. I've met with radical jihadi weirdos and whack jobs personally." United Arab Emirates investigators have described the incident aboard FlyDubai flight FZ1073 as an attempted terror attack after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and tried to hijack the plane, which was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew, most of them Israelis. Since the incident, there has been renewed vigilance in aviation and foreign airline security. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu instructed his national security council to review security procedures for foreign civil aviation to Israel, while Vice President JD Vance said Monday that flight security procedures are also under review in the U.S. IRAN COULD MOVE SHADOW WAR IN A DANGEROUS DIRECTION, EXPERTS WARN ON BACK OF TWO POSSIBLE TERROR ATTACKS "I was asked years ago when I was still with the government," Stern said. "A team was put together and the question before the court was, if you were al-Qaeda, what would you do?" "What I came up with was ... I would get 19 hijackers, and I would hijack four airplanes, and I would fly them into buildings in America, and then issue a communique that said: 20 years of war, you are no safer today than you were before – that for TSA, and Homeland Security, and Iraq, and Afghanistan and all the different things, you are actually no safer, America, today than you were before," he said. "We're seeing, sadly," he lamented, "that academic hypothetical situation has now become a reality, or certainly a possibility." Despite President Donald Trump and the War Department's best efforts to rid the world of terrorist groups – and Iran of nuclear weapons aspirations – "you can't bomb your way into peace," Stern claimed. 'CRAZY' FLYDUBAI LANDING EXPLAINED BY ISRAELI PILOT, WHO OFFERS STEPS TO PREVENT FUTURE CRISES "They have been in holy war against us," he added. "We have now engaged in a holy war against them." "On Ramadan, the holiest month of the year in Islam, on the first day, which is the holiest day, we detonated the leader of the Shia faith, the Ayatollah," he said, likening it to "if somebody assassinated the pope on Easter Sunday while he's giving mass at the Vatican." NETANYAHU PRAISES HEROIC BYSTANDER IN BLOODY COCKPIT ATTACK FOR PREVENTING ‘ANOTHER 9/11’ Stern likened it to the release of the suspects in the RAF Fairford investigation – potential terrorist passport holders walking free. Stern noted that the nature of America's adversaries in the current conflict is unlike what the U.S. faced in places like Afghanistan. "We need to remember we are very used to shooting people like the Taliban who don't know what plumbing is – who literally for years lived in caves until we showed up and gave them stuff," he continued. title: WATCH: CDC director discusses US government response to Russian plague concerns: 'We are protected'
description: CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz says the agency is monitoring travelers from Siberia amid concerns about a pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia.
content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is coordinating with federal agencies to monitor travelers entering the United States from Siberia amid concerns about a possible pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia, the agency's director revealed Wednesday. CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz said the Trump administration is working across multiple agencies to identify travelers arriving from the region following the mysterious death of a Russian laboratory worker, while emphasizing that the risk to Americans remains minimal. "We are very confident that the threat to the United States is extremely low," Schwartz said during a Wall Street Journal health forum Wednesday. MOTHER OF DEAD RUSSIAN ANTI-PLAGUE INSTITUTE WORKER: 'I KNOW THE TRUTH' The concerns stem from the Oct. 2 death of Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia, whose death has fueled speculation about a possible pneumonic plague infection. Russian authorities have maintained that Shipilova died from pneumonia of unknown origin and have not confirmed that she was infected with Yersinia pestis, the bacteria that causes pneumonic plague. Schwartz said the CDC is working with the departments of Homeland Security, State and War, among other federal agencies, to track potential arrivals from the region. "There are about 200 flights that come into the United States from Siberia, that region," Schwartz said, adding that those flights typically arrive at New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport. A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), which oversees the CDC, later clarified to Fox News Digital following publication of this article that Schwartz misspoke when she said 200 flights, and meant instead to say 200 individuals fly in per year from Russia's Siberia region. "We have a port health station set up in JFK so that we can do appropriate surveillance and screening if anyone from that area comes into the United States," Schwartz continued. TRUMP RESPONDS TO CONCERNS OVER SUSPECTED PLAGUE CASE IN RUSSIA, SAYING US 'WILLING TO HELP' The CDC director stressed during the discussion that while pneumonic plague is a serious bacterial infection capable of spreading between people through respiratory droplets, early detection and treatment can prevent deaths. "The one good thing, if I could say there's a good thing, is that it's a treatable, highly treatable bacterial disease with common antibiotics that most physicians within the United States can utilize," Schwartz said. The illness is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and is considered the most serious form of plague, according to the CDC. Symptoms can include fever, chest pain, coughing and rapidly developing pneumonia. Without prompt antibiotic treatment, the infection can be fatal, the agency warns. The World Health Organization (WHO) has pressed Moscow for additional information about Shipilova's death. Russian authorities placed approximately 200 people who had contact with the deceased laboratory worker under quarantine, according to Euronews. On Thursday, Irkutsk Gov. Igor Kobzev said preventive measures had been completed and roughly 5,000 laboratory tests had detected no pathogens, according to the Associated Press. RUSSIAN RESEARCHER'S MYSTERY DEATH COULD BE ‘FAR WORSE’ THAN THE PLAGUE, FORMER SENIOR TRUMP OFFICIAL WARNS CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP However, Russian officials have not publicly identified the pathogen responsible for Shipilova's pneumonia or definitively ruled out pneumonic plague as the cause of her death, according to The Associated Press. Asked whether Moscow was being sufficiently transparent with American authorities, Schwartz indicated that the administration was still seeking answers. "We are still having those conversations about what exactly happened in Siberia," she said, adding that U.S. officials were working with information about an unconfirmed case of pneumonic plague.

title: Your phone can fix badly framed photos after you take them
description: Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 adds Extend and Reframe tools to Photos, letting iPhones generate new background areas beyond your original borders.
content: Have you ever taken a photo you really liked, only to realize later that you stood too close, cut off part of the background or framed the subject in the wrong spot? Normally, fixing that means cropping even more of the photo. Now your phone may be able to go in the other direction. Apple added new Extend and Reframe tools to Photos in iOS 27. Instead of simply cutting away part of an image, Apple Intelligence can generate additional areas around the original shot or change its perspective after you take it. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones offer similar AI editing tools that can help rescue photos that did not come out quite the way you planned. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care . Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist . See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com 12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW What is new for photos in iOS 27? Apple added several Apple Intelligence upgrades to Photos with iOS 27. Two of the most useful are Extend and Reframe. Extend lets you expand a photo beyond its original borders. For example, if someone's head is too close to the top of the image or you want more space around the subject, Apple Intelligence can generate additional background. Reframe goes further. Apple says it lets you change the point of capture after taking the photo. You can move the image, zoom, rotate it and adjust its perspective while Apple Intelligence generates the additional portions needed for the new composition. These tools go beyond traditional cropping. Cropping removes part of your image. Extend and Reframe can create parts of the image that were never captured by the camera. Because these are generative AI features, take a close look at the final result. AI-generated areas can sometimes contain strange details, especially around faces, hands, text or complicated backgrounds. Which iPhones can use Extend and Reframe? Extend and Reframe require Apple Intelligence and iOS 27 or later. Apple Intelligence works on: Availability can also depend on your language and region. Apple says some Apple Intelligence features may have usage limits. If you have an older iPhone that can install iOS 27 but does not support Apple Intelligence, you will not get these particular editing tools. How to extend a photo on iPhone in iOS 27 Use Extend when you want more room around the subject or need to expand the edges of your original photo. If you change your mind later, Apple lets you return to the editing tools and reset the Extend changes. CALIFORNIA LAW PUTS DIGITAL FINGERPRINTS ON AI FAKES How to reframe a photo on iPhone in iOS 27 Use Reframe when the composition or perspective feels wrong rather than simply too tight. This can be especially useful when your subject is awkwardly positioned or you wish you had held the camera at a slightly different angle. How to fix a badly framed photo on a Samsung Galaxy Samsung takes a somewhat different approach. Compatible Galaxy phones use Galaxy AI Photo Assist, which includes tools for moving, removing and adding objects in a photo. For this trick, the Move tool is the one to use. It lets you reposition, rotate or resize part of the image, then uses generative AI to fill in the background created by your changes. Samsung's standard Gallery editor also lets you change the aspect ratio, rotate the picture and adjust its angle. How to use Photo Assist on a compatible Samsung Galaxy Menus can vary slightly by Galaxy model and software version. 8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT How to fix a badly framed photo on Google Pixel Google Photos has one of the closest Android alternatives to Apple's new Extend tool. It's called Auto frame. Google says Auto frame can recompose a photo that is too tightly cropped or poorly framed. It can also use AI to fill in missing areas and extend the background. How to use Auto frame on Google Pixel Make sure you have the latest version of the Google Photos app. Google also includes Straighten, Rotate, Perspective and Aspect ratio controls in the same Crop section if you want to make the adjustment yourself. Google rolls out some Photos features gradually. Therefore, if you do not see Auto frame, update Google Photos and check again. Availability can also vary by device, account and region. 5 tips for getting better results with AI photo editing AI photo editing works best when you give it a reasonably clear original image. Here are a few things to keep in mind. 1) Start with a sharp photo AI can generate new areas around an image, but it cannot completely rescue every blurry or badly exposed shot. Start with the clearest version you have. 2) Make smaller changes first Instead of dramatically expanding the entire picture, try adding a little extra space around the edges. Smaller edits can look more natural. 3) Look closely at people Zoom in before saving. Check faces, hands, hair, jewelry and clothing for unexpected changes. 4) Check signs and other text Generative AI can struggle with letters and numbers. Look closely at street signs, shirts, storefronts and anything else containing text. 5) Keep the original When your phone gives you the option, save the edited version as a copy. That way, you still have the untouched photo if the AI result does not look right later. Kurt's key takeaways One of the frustrating things about smartphone photography is realizing you almost got the perfect shot. Maybe you stood a little too close, left the person too far to one side or tilted the camera just enough to make the composition feel wrong. iOS 27 gives supported iPhones another way to fix those mistakes with Extend and Reframe. I also like that Galaxy and Pixel owners have comparable options instead of sitting this one out. These tools will not replace taking a well-framed photo in the first place, but they can give a photo you would otherwise delete another shot. title: Innocent mistake on long flight could have devastating consequences for travelers
description: One traveler was diagnosed with a corneal ulcer after wearing contact lenses all throughout an 11-hour flight — prompting eye doctors to warn about cabin air risks.
content: An everyday habit during a long-haul flight could have painful consequences for certain travelers — with a recent case highlighting some serious dangers. The dry air inside an airplane cabin, combined with hours spent wearing contact lenses during a long travel day, can leave the lenses with less moisture and eyes feeling increasingly uncomfortable, experts say. In some cases, irritation or damage to the surface of the eye can lead to more serious problems. FLIGHT ATTENDANTS BEG TRAVELERS TO STOP DOING THE ONE THING THAT ANNOYS CREWS MOST One traveler recently described temporarily losing vision in one eye after returning home from an international trip, according to the New York Post. The woman said she wore her contact lenses throughout an 11-hour flight home from Greece and for roughly 24 hours of travel — while also wearing them while swimming and showering, according to the outlet. Within days of returning home, the traveler developed pain and sensitivity to light before her vision significantly worsened. Doctors eventually diagnosed her with a corneal ulcer. She underwent weeks of treatment with eye drops and was left with a small scar that continues to blur part of her vision, the outlet reported. The traveler developed pain and sensitivity to light before her vision significantly worsened. Valerie Kattouf, an Illinois-based optometrist, told Fox News Digital that wearing contacts during extended flights can increase dry-eye symptoms and lead to irritation, a "sandy, gritty feeling" and intermittent blurred vision. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "The cabin air has significantly reduced humidity that can actually remove moisture from the contact lens and create more dryness," Kattouf said. Falling asleep during a long or overnight flight can add another concern for travelers wearing contacts. "People often sleep on long flights, which contributes to more risk with contact [lens] wear," Kattouf said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES As a contact lens loses moisture, it may move less freely on the eye, Kattouf said. Removing a particularly dry lens could potentially disturb the epithelium, the outer layer of the cornea, causing significant irritation and potentially affecting vision. For travelers preparing for a long flight, Kattouf recommends bringing an up-to-date pair of prescription glasses. "Wearing glasses during a long flight is more ideal for eye health and long-term comfortable contact [lens] wear," she said. As another option, travelers who begin their journey wearing contacts can switch to glasses before sleeping or partway through the flight, Kattouf suggested. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ For those who keep their contacts in, single-use vials of artificial tears may also help provide additional lubrication during the flight, according to Kattouf. The issue has also led to discussion among travelers online, with some saying they routinely opt for glasses during longer trips. "I [always] wear glasses on long flights," one Reddit user wrote. "My eyes just feel so much more comfortable by the time I land, and I don't have to worry about taking them out at the airport or on the plane, or sleeping on the plane." title: 'Reagan' star Lesley-Anne Down relives 3 terrifying brushes with death: ‘I should have been killed’
description: Lesley-Anne Down recalls three harrowing brushes with danger, including a chilling link to the Moors murders and a terrifying fake taxi escape.
content: Lesley-Anne Down believes she's already used up three of her nine lives. The actress, who takes on the Iron Lady opposite Dennis Quaid in "Reagan," has shown plenty of steel off-screen, recalling "three times in my life when I should have been killed by other people." For Down, known for her roles in "North and South" and "Upstairs, Downstairs," the unsettling experiences began when she was just 10 years old. MORGAN FAIRCHILD SAYS TWO MEN ONCE ABDUCTED HER OFF NYC STREET AS BYSTANDERS LAUGHED "I remember there was a little girl, one of a number of children who were murdered and buried on the moors in England," the British star told Fox News Digital. "There was a little girl who had dark hair and blue eyes and was my age, 10. Her name was Leslie Ann Downey. My mother got phone calls when this little girl's identity was announced." "It wasn't me, of course," said Down. "But it certainly freaked her out. Leslie Ann Downey was about six months younger than me. It turned out there were two people, a man and a woman. Ian Brady and Myra Hindley. They were the killers." Brady and Hindley murdered five children between 1963 and 1965, with several of their victims buried on Saddleworth Moor in northern England, according to The Associated Press. The case became known as the Moors murders. WATCH: ‘REAGAN’ PRODUCER SHARES WHAT HE LEARNED FROM RESEARCHING RONALD REAGAN Hindley and Brady were arrested in 1965 and later convicted of murders connected to the case. The five victims were Downey, Pauline Reade, John Kilbride, Keith Bennett and Edward Evans, who ranged in age from 10 to 17. Bennett's body has never been found. According to accounts of the case, Downey was abducted after Hindley asked her to help carry packages to a car. Hindley died in 2002 while serving a life sentence. Brady died in a psychiatric hospital in 2017. The case frightened Down’s family. But it wouldn’t be the last time danger came close to home. "A year later, my mother and I were coming back from the launderette with the washing," Down said. "I ran ahead. I left the washing, I left my mother and just ran ahead. I ran uphill and then over a footbridge. As I ran over the footbridge, a man came from the other side. He's walking towards me. He stops in the middle of the footbridge and says, 'Hello.' He then was going to put me in his car." "He told me he needed a babysitter, and he would call my parents when we got to his house," Down said. "I remember having one foot in the car. Seeing my mother broke the spell. Then he was gone. But I still remember that horrible feeling swooping in before my mother came." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Years later, when Down was 18, she ordered a taxi. But when a car pulled up in the countryside, she climbed in and quickly noticed something was wrong. "As soon as he's driving away, I'm already feeling that horrible feeling," Down said. "I looked around and there were no radios or anything, like a taxi is supposed to have. So I said, 'Could you pull over, please?' He said, 'Oh no, we don't need to pull over. We'll be there soon.'" Down said she decided to jump from the moving car. "I opened the door and threw myself out of the 25-mile an hour car," she said. "I fell onto the curb in a puddle. I was covered in blood. There was nobody around. What did he do? He pulled the car door shut and drove off at top speed. I didn't freeze up because I couldn't. That feeling was familiar to me. I've been through it." Down, now 72, earned a Golden Globe nomination for her role opposite Patrick Swayze in "North and South." She also starred opposite Peter Sellers in "The Pink Panther Strikes Again" and Harrison Ford in "Hanover Street." She later appeared on the soap opera "The Bold and the Beautiful." When asked what advice she would give to women pursuing a career in Hollywood, Down had a warning: "Never go anywhere alone." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Always have your agent or your publicist with you at all times," she said. "Even if they have to be on the phone a lot and out in the lobby, just always have somebody with you at all times as you chase your dreams." "I made a decision many, many years ago, actually about 2012, that I wanted out," Down said. "I was in a position where I didn't have to. Things were very good. And I was fortunate to have all my eggs in a basket and make a choice." Down has since moved from California to Georgia. She also said she has no regrets about turning down two opportunities to play a Bond girl. "I guess my thought process was maybe a little old-fashioned, but being a Bond girl didn't really resonate with me," she explained. "Being a Bond girl was skimpy clothing, pretty face, not much dialogue, no acting involved, kissing James at the end in a spacecraft or whatever. I thought if I became a Bond girl, then I'd be a Bond girl for life. I didn't want that for myself." The opportunity to play Thatcher came "out of the blue," Down said. She accepted the role and said she was grateful for the experience. "She loved and believed in England and the English people," Down said. "Her counterpart, Mr. Reagan, also believed and loved the American people." For Down, taking on the role of Thatcher became another unexpected chapter in a life that has repeatedly taken surprising turns. title: Trump announces immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
description: President Donald Trump declared an immediate energy ceasefire, but his recent deal easing Russian diesel exports drew sharp criticism from Kyiv.
content: President Donald Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, saying both countries have agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy infrastructure after weeks of escalating tensions over strikes on oil refineries and power plants. "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social. The announcement comes as Trump has intensified pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian oil refineries, arguing that the attacks have disrupted global diesel supplies and contributed to higher fuel prices for American consumers. The issue has become increasingly urgent as diesel prices weigh on American farmers, truckers and businesses that rely on the fuel to transport goods and operate heavy equipment. RECORD GAS PRICES SQUEEZE AMERICANS AS MIDTERMS LOOM AND WAR IN UKRAINE AND IRAN WAGES ON Trump has repeatedly criticized Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities, even as Kyiv maintains that targeting Moscow's oil industry is a legitimate strategy to weaken Russia's ability to finance its war. The announcement follows a contentious week in U.S.-Ukraine relations after Trump struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian diesel exports to reach American and global markets. Under the agreement announced Friday, Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, with additional shipments expected in November and beyond. The Treasury Department also authorized temporary sanctions relief to facilitate Russian diesel supplies. Trump argued that the agreement would help bring down fuel prices, while Zelenskyy criticized the decision as a concession to Moscow that could provide additional revenue for Russia's war effort. The dispute escalated Saturday when Trump suggested Ukraine should replace Zelenskyy with a leader more willing to negotiate an end to the war. "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal," Trump told reporters. 'OUR POSITION IS CLEAR:' ZELENSKYY AND EU DISMISS CEDING UKRAINIAN LAND TO RUSSIA Zelenskyy, meanwhile, has maintained that Ukraine would be willing to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow agreed to stop targeting Ukrainian power plants and other critical infrastructure. The two countries have increasingly targeted each other's energy systems throughout the war, although the consequences have differed. Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid have left civilians facing electricity disruptions and damaged infrastructure needed to heat homes and sustain businesses. Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, meanwhile, have disrupted fuel production and exports, putting additional pressure on global energy markets. The Trump administration has spent weeks attempting to negotiate a reciprocal halt to energy attacks as part of broader diplomatic efforts to bring an end to the war. In September, Trump similarly announced that both countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, although Moscow did not publicly confirm the agreement and attacks continued. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The latest announcement raises the possibility of renewed diplomatic progress, but an energy ceasefire would not amount to a comprehensive agreement to end the fighting. It was not immediately clear how the agreement would be monitored or enforced. The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News Digital reached out to the Ukrainian and Russian embassies in Washington, D.C., seeking confirmation of the ceasefire but did not immediately receive responses.

title: Crackers start in London as first kickoff return touchdown of NFL season nullified and two players ejected
description: The Jacksonville Jaguars' 90-yard kickoff return touchdown was nullified by multiple flags, and two linebackers were ejected on the opening play.
content: If the point of playing games in London is to give the Brits a taste of, as they say over there, crackers NFL action then Sunday's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium did that from the start. On the opening kickoff of this game ... Eagles kicker Jake Elliott kicked the ball 55 yards to the Jacksonville 10-yard line and Josh Cameron returned it 90 yards for a touchdown. It marked the first kickoff return touchdown in the NFL this season. NFL EXECS AND COACHES WANT LEAGUE TO REIN IN 'OUT OF CONTROL' OFFICIALS AND HOPE SUSPENSIONS SIGNAL A START But, no! Back upfield, officials – they had quite a week, by the way – had thrown multiple flags on the play. NFL REFEREES JEFF SEEMAN AND ADRIAN HILL SUSPENDED AFTER UNPROFESSIONAL CLASHES WITH PLAYERS IN WEEK 4 So, with bated breath, we waited for the official announcement. And we learned both teams were flagged on the kickoff and players from both teams were flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct. The touchdown was thus nullified because the Eagles lined up in an illegal formation and the Jaguars had linebacker Branson Combs called for holding. Nice start to a game. Then we learned that Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jacksonville linebacker Bryan Thomas Jr. were both flagged for giving each other the business. It seems both men engaged in a block during the play and carried their standoff all the way to midfield where Trotter slammed Thomas to the turf after the play was over and then Thomas kicked up at Trotter while on his back. Both were flagged. Both were disqualified for the rest of the game – on a play that didn't even count. That hurt the Eagles more as Trotter was expected to get work with the starting defense while Thomas is exclusively a special teams contributor. So to recap: A season-first kickoff return touchdown was nullified by a penalty while a player from either team was ejected. It took officials a couple of minutes to sort it all. This game was bonkers from the beginning and then the crowd, a majority of which are Eagles fans, saw something perhaps stranger: The Eagles attempted to convert a fourth-and-1 play on their first possession but did not employ the Tush Push. Williams posted a screenshot to her Instagram Story, along with a profanity-laced insult after the agency suggested she thank federal law enforcement officers rather than criticize their service. "And may I suggest all Nazi b------ suck on my fat d---," Williams said in response to DHS, according to Rolling Stone. WHITE HOUSE FIRES BACK AT ARIANA GRANDE AFTER SHE TOLD THEM TO NEVER USE HER MUSIC IN ICE DEPORTATION VIDEO The confrontation followed a recent concert by Haley Williams, where the singer condemned Immigration and Customs Enforcement while performing her song "Ice in My OJ." In response to the comment from Williams, a DHS spokesperson defended the work of immigration officers and urged Williams to recognize their service. "America is grateful all the time for our federal law enforcement officers who keep us safe," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital at the time. "We suggest Ms. Williams to thank them for their service, not belittle their sacrifice." Williams' latest response follows a performance where the singer drew attention for her criticism of immigration enforcement and expressions of support for Palestinians. During the concert, Williams paused her performance to deliver an anti-ICE declaration before continuing with the song. She also shouted a separate message supporting Palestinians. "Free motherf------ Palestine!" Williams said. KENNY CHESNEY TELLS BILL MAHER THE KEY REASON HE REFUSES TO TELL HIS LISTENERS HOW TO VOTE The exchange followed other political remarks Williams has incorporated into her solo tour, including criticism of President Donald Trump and Christian nationalism. A clip recirculated of her September performance at Forest Hills Stadium in New York, where she addressed the audience before performing "True Believer." "The greatest threat to American democracy is Christian nationalism," Williams said at the time. Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't L.A. My Burbank PAC, criticized that declaration in a statement to Fox News Digital, disputing Williams' characterization and arguing that Christianity played a central role in shaping democratic principles. TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94% "Incredibly ignorant comment considering Christianity is woven into the fabric of every founding document that proscribes Americans' democratic rights," Cusack said. "There would be no natural law without Christianity, and without that, no human rights that exist beyond a government’s power. Christianity sees all people as made in the image of God, so are all valuable, no matter how successful, and puts self-sacrifice above power," she added.Williams has previously used major concert appearances to deliver political messages. During Paramore's performance at the 2024 iHeartRadio Music Festival, she urged Americans to vote against Trump, criticizing his political agenda and warning about the country's democratic future.Williams' latest remarks also came as DHS reported an increase in assaults against immigration officers.
