title: A scammer has your name, phone number and address. What can they actually do?
description: Scammers can combine your name, phone number and address with data breach details to attempt SIM swaps, phishing and even identity theft schemes.
content: If you've ever wondered how much damage a scammer could really do with your name, phone number and home address, the answer is probably more than you'd expect. Those three details are generally not enough by themselves to empty your bank account, take out a major loan or completely steal your identity. However, they can give a scammer a believable starting point. From there, the goal may be to trick you into revealing the more sensitive information they still need. That is what makes seemingly basic personal information so useful to criminals. Here's what a scammer can actually do with those details, the warning signs to watch for and the steps you can take to make yourself a harder target. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care . Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist . See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com THE SECRET LIST THAT TELLS SCAMMERS YOU'RE AN EASY TARGET Why basic personal information can help a scammer Your name, phone number and address may already appear in public records, old directories, property records or data broker databases. As a result, people sometimes assume there is little risk if a stranger already knows them. The problem starts when those details are combined. A scammer may add information from a data breach, social media account, people-search site or earlier phishing attempt. Suddenly, the person contacting you may know where you live, your phone number, the names of relatives or other details that make a fake story sound legitimate. That is why a scam call can feel so convincing even when nobody has actually hacked your phone or bank account. Data brokers can also collect information such as current and previous addresses, phone numbers, approximate age and possible relatives. A scammer may use those details to learn more about you before making contact. What can a scammer do with your name, phone number and address? Here are some of the most common ways that information could be used. Create a more convincing phishing or scam call A scammer who knows your name and address can pretend to represent your bank, utility company, delivery service or government agency. For example, hearing someone read your correct home address may make the call seem legitimate. However, knowing personal information does not prove that the caller is really from the company they claim to represent. Send targeted scams to your home Once someone has your address, they can send fraudulent invoices, fake prize notices, counterfeit checks or other deceptive mail directly to you. Because the material arrives at your real address and may include your full name, it can look more credible than a random email or text. Try to take over your phone number Your phone number can also become part of a SIM-swap or account-takeover attempt. A phone number and address alone usually will not be enough to take control of your wireless account. Still, a criminal may combine those details with passwords, PINs or other information stolen elsewhere. If they successfully move your number to another SIM or device, they may then receive calls and text messages intended for you, including some verification codes. Combine your information with data from another breach This is where the risk can grow quickly. Perhaps one database exposes your phone number and address while another contains an old password or Social Security number. Criminals can combine pieces from multiple sources to create a much more complete profile. That information may then be used for identity theft, account takeovers or additional phishing attempts. Impersonate you or someone you know Personal details can also strengthen family-emergency scams. A criminal may know your relative's name, where you live or other information that helps support a fake story. With AI-generated voices making impersonation scams increasingly believable, personal details can make an already emotional call even harder to judge. Test account-recovery systems Some services still rely on personal details or knowledge-based questions during account recovery. A scammer may try information such as your address, phone number or other details to see whether they can get further into a password-reset or identity-verification process. They may still need additional information. However, every correct answer can move them one step closer. What can't a scammer usually do with only these three details? Knowing your name, phone number and address does not automatically give someone access to your bank account. Those details alone are also generally insufficient for opening major financial accounts or taking out loans because financial institutions typically require additional identity verification. However, I would not treat that as a guarantee. The bigger concern is that a scammer can use the information they already have to convince you to provide what they are missing, such as a password, verification code, Social Security number, bank account information or credit card number. In other words, your basic information may be the beginning of the attack rather than the end. HACKER CLAIMS 7.49M CUSTOMER RECORDS STOLEN FROM AMERICAN UTILITY COMPANY How personal information makes a scam more believable Suppose your phone rings and the caller immediately knows your full name and home address. Then they tell you there is suspicious activity on one of your accounts. That specificity can cause you to listen a little longer. Next, they may ask you to verify a code that just arrived by text, confirm an account number or transfer money to supposedly protect it. This is where I want you to be especially careful. A caller knowing something about you is not proof that the caller knows you. Personal information should never replace independent verification. Warning signs that your information may be getting used Watch for these warning signs: One unusual call does not necessarily mean someone has stolen your identity. Still, several warning signs appearing together deserve attention. 7 steps to reduce what scammers can do with your information A few precautions can make it much harder for someone to turn basic information into a successful scam. 1) See what information about you is already online Search your name, phone number and address and see what comes up. You may find people-search sites and data brokers displaying information you would rather keep private. Where possible, submit opt-out requests to have those listings removed. 2) Protect your mobile account Ask your wireless carrier what protections it offers against SIM swaps and unauthorized number transfers. Set a strong account PIN or password and enable any available port-out or number-transfer protection. 3) Stop using personal details as proof that a caller is legitimate If an unexpected caller knows your address, bank name or another personal detail, do not assume that means the call is real. Hang up and contact the company directly using a phone number or app you already trust. 4) Use stronger account security Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) for important accounts. When possible, I prefer an authenticator app, passkey or physical security key over text-message verification for especially sensitive accounts. That reduces the damage a successful SIM swap could cause. 5) Create a family verification word Choose a private family verification word or phrase that family members can use if someone calls claiming there is an emergency. Do not post it online or use something a stranger could easily guess. 6) Don't help a suspicious caller complete your profile Avoid confirming or correcting personal details during an unexpected call. If someone says, "You're still at 123 Main Street, correct?" you do not need to tell them your new address. End the call and verify the request independently. 7) Keep an eye on your credit and financial accounts Review bank and credit card activity for transactions you do not recognize. You should also check your credit reports for unfamiliar accounts or inquiries. If you are concerned about identity theft, a credit freeze can make it harder for someone to open new credit accounts in your name. Credit freezes are free and can be placed with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. How identity theft protection can add another layer of security Personal information tends to accumulate online over time. One breach may expose an email address while another exposes an old password. Meanwhile, data brokers may already have your address, phone number and information about your relatives. An identity theft protection service can help you watch for signs that some of this information is being misused. Depending on the service and plan, that may include identity monitoring, credit monitoring, financial account alerts, data broker removal and help recovering from identity theft. What identity theft protection can help with Identity and financial monitoring: Some services can alert you to certain suspicious activity involving your identity, credit or financial accounts. Data broker removal: Some plans include tools that can help remove your personal information from supported data broker and people-search sites. Scam support: Certain services offer access to specialists who can help you evaluate suspicious messages, calls or websites. Identity restoration: If identity theft occurs, some providers offer restoration specialists who can help guide you through the recovery process. Loss coverage: Depending on the provider and plan, you may also get insurance or reimbursement for certain eligible identity theft expenses or losses. Coverage limits, exclusions and availability vary, so read the terms carefully. No identity theft service can prevent scams or guarantee that your personal information will never circulate online. However, monitoring and alerts may help you spot suspicious activity sooner. Even with strong security habits, identity theft can still happen. Your Social Security number, financial information or other personal data may already be exposed without you realizing it. What to do if you think your information is already being misused If you notice suspicious activity, act quickly. title: President talks 'Trump Ocean,' trades jokes with Tennessee crowd as Kid Rock kicks off sprawling rally
description: Trump called Iranian leaders "crazy" and floated renaming an ocean after himself during a wide-ranging Tennessee rally with Kid Rock opening.
content: President Donald Trump touted billions of dollars in manufacturing investments and his administration's efforts to combat crime in Tennessee on Saturday, while calling Iranian leaders "crazy" and floating the idea of a "Trump Ocean" during a wide-ranging rally featuring musician Kid Rock. The president appeared in Clarksville ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, campaigning for Republican Sen. Bill Hagerty and gubernatorial candidate Marsha Blackburn while mixing economic talking points, foreign policy and off-script humor. Kid Rock opened the event with a religious-themed introduction, praising Trump's leadership while taking aim at the news media. TRUMP TOUTS ‘GOLDEN AGE’ AT OHIO RALLY, URGES VOTERS TO DELIVER GOP MIDTERM WINS "Literally, President Trump could walk across the Cumberland River, and tomorrow the headline would say President Trump refuses to swim," the musician joked. The rocker also condemned Islamist extremism and defended religious freedom, arguing that Americans should not be forced to live under religious laws that override the Constitution. "We are not, and we will never be, one nation under Mohammed, because we are, and we always will be, one nation under God," Kid Rock told the crowd. Trump later thanked his longtime supporter and friend by his given name, Bob, before turning to an array of domestic and international issues. The president addressed tensions with Iran, calling the country's leaders "crazy" while claiming that Tehran's rhetoric had softened following U.S. military operations. AFTER 'LAKE AMERICA,' TRUMP SUGGESTS A NEW NAME FOR THE STATE OF NEW MEXICO "They don't talk that way anymore, by the way," Trump said after recounting previous threats from Iranian leaders. Trump described what he characterized as extensive damage to Iran's military capabilities, claiming 159 ships had been sunk and its air force and air-defense systems destroyed. "They have no Navy. They have no Air force, they have no anti-aircraft equipment," Trump said. The president then pivoted from the Strait of Hormuz to an unexpected geography lesson, suggesting it could one day be called the "Trump Strait." He also revisited his decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America before floating additional changes to the map. "We need a river. We need an ocean," Trump said, suggesting the Atlantic or Pacific could become the "Trump Ocean" or "Ocean of the Americas." TRUMP RALLIES NEW YORK CROWD FOR REPUBLICAN BRUCE BLAKEMAN'S BID TO REPLACE GOV KATHY HOCHUL "Before I get out, I think we should have an ocean," he added, without yet announcing any formal renaming plans. On the economy, Trump promoted Korea Zinc's planned investment of more than $6 billion in Tennessee, a project expected to create 740 jobs across Montgomery and Smith counties. Tennessee officials announced the $6.6 billion project in December, describing it as the largest single private corporate investment in state history. The plans include a new critical-minerals smelter in Clarksville and the reopening of a former mine in Gordonsville. "And your state will soon be home to the first new mineral smelter in the United States, first one built since 1979," Trump said. The project is intended to strengthen domestic supplies of minerals used in semiconductors, defense technology and advanced manufacturing. TRUMP NAMES LEAVITT SUCCESSOR AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION — AND SHE'S NO STRANGER TO MAGA Trump also cited General Motors' previously announced $275 million investment in its Spring Hill manufacturing facility to support production of next-generation turbocharged Cadillac engines. The president credited his tariff policies with encouraging domestic investment, arguing that companies were expanding American manufacturing to avoid import duties. In a Tennessee-focused fact sheet released as the rally began, the White House asserted that Republican-backed tax policies had preserved $23 billion in economic activity in the state. The administration also cited an average $3,674 tax refund for Tennesseans in 2026. Public safety was another focal point of his address, with Trump praising federal law-enforcement operations in Memphis and claiming approximately 12,000 dangerous criminals had been removed. The White House separately asserted that murders and overall crime in Memphis had declined approximately 36%, crediting the Memphis Safe Task Force. The president also shared some lighter moments about first lady Melania Trump, describing her objections to his theatrical impersonations of athletes during discussions about transgender participation in women's sports. "She said it's not presidential," Trump recalled, before joking about her film career. "There is only room for one star in a family, so I don't need this movie stuff. I don't need it." Trump, who carried Tennessee in all three of his presidential campaigns, said the visit was also an opportunity to thank supporters in a state where he had enjoyed strong electoral backing. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Sometimes it's nice to go to a place where you don't have to be, but you're there to say thank you to the great people that elected you three separate times in record time," Trump said. Trump repeatedly returned to the November elections, urging supporters to back Republican candidates even though his name will not appear on the ballot. "In this election, I'm asking you to do me a favor. Pretend. Just pretend that I'm running," Trump said.

title: Philadelphia police officer killed, partner shot 12 times in ambush; suspect found hiding in tree
description: Philadelphia Police Officer Shane Seiber, a 40-year-old father of two, was killed. His partner was shot 12 times after the officers were ambushed while responding to an armed man.
content: A Philadelphia police officer died Saturday after he and his partner were ambushed and shot multiple times while responding to a report of an armed man in the western part of the city. Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner identified the suspect as 35-year-old Eric Lewis, who has a criminal record dating back to 2012, according to Pennsylvania court records reviewed by Fox News Digital. A municipal labor union also identified Lewis as an employee of the Philadelphia Water Department. Krasner outlined a series of charges stemming from the shooting, including attempted murder, attempted homicide of a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault and gun offenses. Prosecutors identified at least 11 potential victims, including the two officers who were shot and nine additional people who were fired upon. CONNECTICUT POLICE OFFICERS SHOT, SUSPECT KILLED AFTER ATTEMPTED ARREST SPARKS HECTIC CHASE Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel identified the officer who died as Shane Seiber, a 40-year-old father who spent 10 years on the force. He leaves behind his wife and his two children, a 7-year-old son and a 3-year-old daughter. "He fought valiantly, but he lost his life today," Bethel said at a morning news conference. "His wife was able to be by his side before he passed, as well as his family." Lewis was found guilty of theft and receiving stolen property in 2012 and gun-related offenses and simple assault in 2013, receiving probation in both cases, according to court records. In 2018, Lewis pleaded guilty to disorderly conduct involving fighting and was again sentenced to probation. Court records also show Lewis was cited for three traffic violations in 2024, including driving without headlights, failing to provide proof of insurance and windshield-related violations. District Council 33, a labor union representing Philadelphia municipal workers, identified Lewis as one of its members and an employee of the Philadelphia Water Department in a Facebook statement addressing the shooting.The union condemned the violence, expressed condolences to Seiber's family and wished the surviving officer a full recovery. District Council 33 also said it would cooperate with authorities as the case proceeds. During a news conference, Mayor Cherelle Parker said Seiber "paid the ultimate price while sacrificing his own life to protect and serve our city." Parker also announced plans to seek legislation expanding Pennsylvania's involuntary commitment laws to cover substance use disorders and other mental or behavioral health conditions. She said she would work with Gov. Josh Shapiro, the state legislature and Attorney General Dave Sunday on the proposal. CHICAGO OFFICERS WOUNDED IN TRAFFIC STOP SHOOTOUT AS HOLIDAY WEEKEND LEAVES 3 DEAD, 16 INJURED Krasner said investigators had not determined whether mental health or substance use played a role in the shooting. Krasner also declined to discuss the suspect's motive, citing the ongoing investigation and sensitivity toward the victims' families.The mayor also referenced the deaths of nine people in Erie, Pennsylvania, saying the tragedy underscored the need to revisit existing laws. Parker acknowledged that investigators had not determined whether mental health or substance use played a role in the Erie deaths. Parker separately ordered city flags to remain at half-staff until sunset on the day of Seiber's interment. Gov. Shapiro said in a social media post that he and his wife were praying for Seiber's loved ones and the Philadelphia Police Department. He also ordered all U.S. and state flags to be flown at half-staff. Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., also mourned Seiber's death, offering prayers for his family, the Philadelphia Police Department and the wounded officer. McCormick said Philadelphia had lost a hero whose sacrifice would not be forgotten. Rep. Mike Kelly, R-Pa., separately offered prayers for the Erie community and the families affected by Friday night's tragedy. The other officer, a 33-year-old father of five children, was shot 12 times and was initially in critical condition. After going into surgery, Bethel said, he is now in stable condition but is "not out of the woods yet." Just after 12:20 a.m., the officers responded to a report of a man with a gun on a porch, Bethel said. About 30 minutes later, the officers arrived at the address and came under "significant gunfire" once they were on the porch. Shortly after shots were fired, Bethel said, additional officers and a SWAT team found the original responding officers on the porch with gunshot wounds. After running away, the suspect fired at two additional officers, Bethel said. Krasner outlined nine additional counts of attempted murder and attempted homicide of a law enforcement officer involving the nine other people who were fired upon. A SWAT team was able to locate the suspect in a tree and take him into custody. Krasner said Lewis remained in custody without serious injuries and was expected to appear for a preliminary arraignment and bail hearing.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Lewis was found with two handguns and a shotgun, Bethel said. One of the handguns belonged to one of the officers who had been shot.

content: While today's freezers are packed with ice cream flavors such as cookies and cream, salted caramel and mint chocolate chip, some old-time favorites seem to have melted away. Flavors including Butter Brickle, rum raisin and maple walnut were once familiar options at ice cream counters and grocery stores, but many have become harder to find as tastes have changed. title: 'Happy Days' star Anson Williams says he had to create a second career because sitcom pay wasn't enough
description: Anson Williams reveals how conversations with David Cassidy and Barry Williams inspired him to pitch a musical act on the iconic sitcom.
content: When playing Potsie Weber on "Happy Days" didn't pay well enough, actor Anson Williams came up with a side hustle: a music career. In a recent interview on the "Still Here Hollywood Podcast," the 77-year-old actor revealed the singing sideline was simply a matter of 1970s economics. "On 'Happy Days' we didn't have the same salaries they have today. Not even close," he said. "Nine hundred dollars an episode, $1,200 an episode. It was fine back then, but...it's not a lifetime of earnings there." Williams said that after speaking to "Partridge Family" star David Cassidy and Barry Williams, of "The Brady Bunch," about how much money they were making by taking their singing acts off the show, he thought to himself, "Wait a minute. I sing. If I can convince Garry to put a band on the show, maybe I can get booked, and maybe I can get some extra income." ‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS After speaking with the show's creator, Garry Marshall, about the possibility of putting together a band to perform at Arnold's, the burger joint where Fonzie held court, the legendary director gave him a chance. Marshall told him he would have to pick a song and sing it to a bulldog, telling him, "If you're good, I get laughs. If you're bad, I get laughs. You're going to sing the bulldog." "So I do it and then the letters start coming in, and he goes 'The people like it. The people like it.' He goes, 'We'll do more. You're in charge of it though,'" Williams recalled. "Then I got a major agent for that and started getting booked at state fairs for 10 years." Williams added that his idea to sing on the show "started this whole career" that ended up being better for him monetarily, and was "just a whole other life experience." After finding success as a musician as well as an actor, Williams said that Marshall approached him to express how proud he was of the actor, telling him, "You found an opportunity, and you're helping the show." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE During an interview with Fox News Digital in March 2024, Williams revealed that while the show started as a hit with audiences, landing in the top 15 or 20, it slid down to 48th place at one point and was "on the verge of getting canceled." "And Garry Marshall and Jerry Paris, our director, thought, ‘What if we changed the whole tone? What if we make it a live audience sitcom?’" Williams recalled. "So, half the season, one camera. The next season, one camera. The next season — two and a half in — they switch it to live audience. And the chemistry of the cast, the writing, was magic. That's the year we went to No. 1 in the world. That's when we exploded." When the show became a huge success, Williams recalled Marshall advising him and his young co-stars to use their platforms for good, telling them to take the spotlight they found themselves in and "shine it on people that deserve it." Following his time on "Happy Days," Williams pivoted to working more as a writer and director. He directed episodes of "Beverly Hills, 90210," "Sabrina the Teenage Witch," "Lizzie McGuire," "Charmed," "The Secret Life of an American Teenager" and more. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? title: Veteran walked across four continents and just swam the English Channel to return home
description: A British Army veteran reached England after 28 years and 30,000 miles — but he still has 250 miles to walk to reunite with his mother in the port city of Hull.
content: A British Army veteran has returned to his home country after a 28-year journey across four continents — but his remarkable trek still isn't quite over. Karl Bushby, a 57-year-old former paratrooper, reached England this week after swimming across the English Channel from France, marking the latest milestone in an around-the-world expedition that he embarked on in 1998. Now, he has roughly 250 miles left to walk before reuniting with his mother, whom he hasn't seen in 11 years. DIVERS BRAVE DEADLY 'MOUNT EVEREST OF SHIPWRECKS' AS FAMED WRECK BREAKS APART Bushby spent about 20 hours swimming in the English Channel over three days before reaching Shakespeare Beach near Dover on Oct. 5, according to the BBC. "Getting in the water that first day, I thought, 'Have I taken too much of a bite here?'" Bushby told the outlet. "But you dig deep. Keep on keeping on. You find a rhythm." Bushby hadn't even trained for the last leg of the trip. After about an hour in the water, he was cramping and doubting whether he could finish, he told the BBC. CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER But the Channel crossing was just the latest obstacle in an expedition spanning more than 30,000 miles and 29 countries. Bushby set out from Chile on Nov. 1, 1998, and set two rules for himself: He would not use transportation including planes, trains, boats or cars to advance his expedition route and he would not return home to Hull until he had finished it. His route took him the length of South America, through North America and across the Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Along the way, he trekked through the Darién Gap between Panama and Colombia and, in 2006, crossed the frozen Bering Strait on foot and over ice with Dimitri Kieffer, a French-American adventurer. More recently, Bushby swam about 184 miles across the Caspian Sea before continuing west toward Europe. His expedition faced delays related to visa restrictions, the loss of sponsors during the 2008 financial crisis, COVID-19 lockdowns and geopolitical turmoil, according to reports. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Bushby began his expedition with just $500 and no sponsors, relying over the years on book sales, speaking engagements, donations and corporate sponsorships to keep going. A documentary production company also provided support for the past 16 years, according to reports. "You have the whole night sky in front of you." When Bushby finally reached France, he was hoping to cross into England on foot through the Channel Tunnel's service tunnel, which connects both countries, but his request was rejected over safety and maintenance concerns, according to the BBC, leaving him to swim the English Channel instead. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Bushby said floating on his back at night and looking at the stars offered a distraction from the physical pain he was in during the swim. "You're far away from light pollution and have the whole night sky in front of you," he said. "It gave me something to think about and took my mind off the pain and aches. It was amazing." The last leg of the journey will bring him to his mother, whom he hasn't seen since 2015, in the port city of Hull, The Times of London reported. He is expected to arrive in early November. "That’s about 400 kilometers from here, so I’ve got to get busy."

title: Nine people killed in Pennsylvania shooting; suspected gunman found dead: report
description: Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah called the Perry Street mass shooting the worst crime he has encountered in nearly three decades of law enforcement.
author_name: Michael Sinkewicz, Robert McGreevy, Brittany Miller
content: Authorities said nine people died in a Pennsylvania shooting Friday night, including a 45-year-old suspected gunman who reportedly died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Two young children and a woman who was eight months pregnant were among the eight victims killed, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah revealed during a news conference Saturday. Eight of the nine deceased, including the suspected shooter, were related, while the remaining victim was a family friend, Lorah said. POLICE REVEAL NEW DETAILS ABOUT GUNMAN, 5 VICTIMS KILLED IN RURAL MICHIGAN SHOOTING RAMPAGE Lorah said the ShotSpotter alert was triggered at approximately 4:53 p.m. by two gunshots in the 700 block of Perry Street. Officers arrived approximately three minutes later and discovered two women, ages 51 and 37, dead outside the residence. Investigators reviewing Ring doorbell footage from a neighboring home determined that the two women appeared distressed as they sought help from neighbors and pounded on a door. The recording captured what investigators believe were muffled gunshots inside the residence before the suspect emerged and fatally shot both women, Lorah said. One of the women was a family friend, while the other was a sister-in-law of one of the victims, according to Lorah. Neither woman lived at the home. Lorah clarified Saturday that sounds some witnesses may have mistaken for additional gunfire during the police response came from flash-bang devices and chemical munitions deployed by SWAT officers. "I want to be candid with our community. This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our officers and investigators have ever encountered. The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing," Lorah said, according to FOX8. During Saturday's update, Lorah said officers discovered a 5-year-old boy and a 22-month-old girl on the first floor of the home. Four additional victims — a 24-year-old woman, a 44-year-old woman, a 19-year-old man and a 21-year-old man — were found on the second floor and in a stairwell. The suspected gunman was found dead on the second floor from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, with a .40-caliber handgun recovered on his person. Lorah said the gun was registered to the suspect. Investigators believe all eight victims were killed, and the gunman died before officers arrived, Lorah said. All the victims found inside the residence lived there. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro issued a statement confirming the number killed during the incident while offering support to victims' families. "I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians," Shapiro wrote in a post on X Saturday morning. "My heart breaks for this family. Lori and I are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community." "It's a horrific scene," Lorah told the station. "There was a large loss of life inside that residence and outside that residence. … I can tell you that this is a tragic, tragic situation."Lorah defended the police response Saturday, explaining that officers initially had no way of knowing whether the suspect remained inside, had escaped or was holding anyone hostage. He said officers heard no gunfire, screams or other signs of life coming from the residence. Police deployed drones and a robot to assess the interior before entering the home. Lorah emphasized that obtaining a search warrant did not delay officers from entering the residence and that they would have gone inside immediately if they had detected signs someone was in imminent danger. MULTIPLE PEOPLE KILLED IN SHOOTING AT IDAHO IN-N-OUT RESTAURANT, SUSPECT DEAD The city of Erie issued a statement about the shooting, saying the incident resulted in "multiple deaths" and confirming that there was no ongoing threat to the public. "We understand that this news brings deep shock and sorrow to our residents, and we want to assure the public that the situation has been contained," the city said. "Our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones and everyone impacted by tonight's tragedy," the statement continued. "We will continue working closely with our Erie Police Dept, and will provide updates as soon as verified information becomes available." Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said Saturday the city is coordinating with crisis services, healthcare providers and schools to provide trauma support to families, students and residents affected by the shooting. title: 8 seriously annoying tasks you can hand off to an AI agent
description: ChatGPT Work, Meta Muse and Gemini Spark can monitor flight prices, sort your email inbox and track important deadlines, but savvy users start small.
content: I have a growing list of things I would gladly never do again. Checking the same airfare every morning is on it. Digging through an overflowing inbox is right up there too. And I would be perfectly happy never having to remember when some free trial is about to start charging me. This is where AI agents are starting to get genuinely useful. A regular chatbot waits for you to ask a question. An AI agent can potentially keep working on something after that first conversation. It might monitor a price, watch for an opening or keep tabs on a task you would otherwise have to remember yourself. OpenAI, Meta and Google are all pushing further into this kind of AI. OpenAI now has Dots and ChatGPT Work, while Meta has Muse and Google has Gemini Spark. That all sounds very impressive. But I am less interested in having an AI run my life than I am in having it take a few irritating chores off my hands. So if you are wondering what you would actually do with one of these agents, start here. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better healthcare. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com AI AGENT HACKS GYM SYSTEM TO MOVE UP WAITLIST What are ChatGPT Dots, ChatGPT Work, Meta Muse and Gemini Spark? ChatGPT Work is only one way to try an AI agent. OpenAI also offers Dots, which are more persistent. A Dot has its own cloud computer, can remember ongoing work and can keep making progress between conversations. Dots are currently rolling out to eligible ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium and Enterprise users. OpenAI says Dot usage will temporarily not count against eligible users' plan allowances during the introductory period, with longer-term usage terms still to come. ChatGPT Work is built into ChatGPT and focuses on longer, multi-step tasks. On web and mobile, OpenAI says Work is available on eligible paid plans, including Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu, although access is still rolling out. Work can research, use connected apps and files, create finished materials and run scheduled or recurring tasks. There are alternatives too. Meta Muse offers a free tier with usage limits, with a paid subscription available if you need more. Gemini Spark is Google's personal AI agent and is available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in supported regions. It can manage ongoing tasks, use connected Google services and run scheduled workflows. You do not need the most powerful or expensive agent to try the ideas in this article. Start with whichever service you already use, give it a low-risk task and see whether having AI continue the job actually saves you time. How to get started with an AI agent in ChatGPT If you have never used an AI agent, the first step is simply knowing where to find one. We will use ChatGPT Work as an example. OpenAI is rolling the feature out to eligible accounts, so what you see can vary depending on your plan and device. Before you get started, I recommend checking a few privacy settings so you have more control over what ChatGPT does with your information. Check your ChatGPT privacy settings first You can stop new ChatGPT conversations from being used to train OpenAI's models. Here's how: Your conversations can still appear in your chat history, but new chats will not be used to train OpenAI's models. Next, review ChatGPT's memory settings: You can also use Temporary Chat for conversations you do not want saved in your history or used for model training. OpenAI may still retain these chats for up to 30 days for safety purposes. Finally, review your connected apps under Settings > Plugins. Remove any connections you no longer need. Keep in mind that turning off model training does not prevent ChatGPT from processing information you provide to complete a task. Start using ChatGPT Work Once you've reviewed those settings, you're ready to give an AI agent its first task. Here's how to get started: You do not need to start by connecting your entire digital life. In fact, I would not. Try a simple task first, such as researching several products within a budget or comparing options for an upcoming trip. That lets you see how the agent works before you give it access to email, calendars or other personal information. Once you are comfortable with the basics, the eight ideas below show where an AI agent can start saving you some real time. MALICIOUS BROWSER EXTENSIONS CAN HIJACK AI ASSISTANTS 1) Have AI prepare you for the day I do not need another app demanding my attention first thing in the morning. What I would like is something that looks at the information I already have and tells me what I need to know. An AI agent with access to your calendar and other approved information could review what is coming up, flag a meeting you need to prepare for and surface something time-sensitive you might have missed. The key is asking for a briefing instead of another information dump. Prompt to try:"Review my calendar and relevant messages for today. Tell me what I need to prepare for, flag anything time-sensitive and point out any scheduling conflicts. Do not send messages or change my calendar without asking me first." That last sentence would absolutely stay in my prompt. I want AI to tell me that my afternoon looks impossible. I do not want it quietly deciding which meeting gets moved. 2) Stop checking the same price over and over You find a flight. It costs too much. So you check again tomorrow. Then you check again the next day. I have done this with airfare, hotels and products I was not in a hurry to buy. It gets old fast. This is almost a perfect AI agent task because there is very little value in you personally opening the same page 12 times. Give the agent the item and the price you are hoping to hit. Then let it tell you when something changes. Prompt to try:"Track the price of [item, flight or hotel]. Let me know if the total price drops below $___ or if you find a comparable option that costs less. Show me the details before taking any action." You can even use this after a purchase. If the retailer offers price adjustments or you are still inside the return window, have the agent keep watching. I like this type of task because the AI does the watching while I keep control of the wallet. 3) Let AI sort the email you do not want to sort There are days when opening my inbox feels like volunteering for another job. Some emails need an answer. Others are simply FYIs. Then you have the message you meant to answer two days ago sitting underneath six newsletters and a shipping notification. An AI agent connected to your inbox can help with that first pass. It can summarize what arrived, identify the messages that appear to need attention and prepare a reply for you to review. Prompt to try:"Review my unread email from the last 24 hours. Show me what needs my attention today and summarize the rest. Draft responses where appropriate. Do not send, delete or archive anything without my approval." I would absolutely keep that approval requirement in place. Let AI write the first draft. Let AI tell you what looks urgent. But before something goes out under my name, I want to see it. That goes double if the recipient is my boss, my doctor or anybody who might interpret an AI hallucination as something I actually meant to say. 4) Make AI remember all the little deadlines you forget Life is full of deadlines that are incredibly easy to miss because they do not feel urgent until suddenly they are. A subscription renews Friday. A rebate expires next week. Your insurance paperwork is due. Somewhere in your inbox there is a form you completely forgot existed. That is the kind of mental clutter I would love to hand off. An agent could keep track of deadlines you give it and remind you before something needs your attention. Prompt to try:"Keep track of the deadlines, renewals and appointments I give you. Tell me what is coming up this week and alert me early when I need to do something. Never renew, cancel or submit anything without my approval." I would keep the agent in reminder mode when money is involved. Tell me the bill is due. Tell me the trial expires tomorrow. Then get out of the way and let me decide what happens next. 5) Let AI figure out what’s for dinner I don't know about you, but deciding what to make for dinner every night gets old fast. You open the refrigerator, stare at what's inside and somehow still can't think of anything to eat. Why not hand that job to AI? Tell an AI agent what foods you like, what ingredients you already have and how much time you want to spend cooking. It can put together a weekly dinner plan, suggest simple recipes and even help you use up food before it goes bad. Prompt to try: "Every Sunday, prepare a dinner plan for the coming week with five easy meals. Use my food preferences and any ingredients I've told you I have. Keep each meal under 30 minutes. Include simple recipes and a grocery list of anything else I'll need. Don't order groceries without my approval." You can schedule this as a weekly task so the agent prepares fresh dinner ideas without you having to ask each time. Just update it with what's in your refrigerator and pantry before it creates the next plan. That means fewer nights staring into the refrigerator wondering what to cook. 6) Put somebody else in charge of the household to-do list Every home seems to have a list that nobody actually wrote down. The air filter needs replacing. The dog is running out of food. There is something in the garage you promised to fix about four months ago. Then, at exactly the wrong moment, somebody remembers it. An AI agent could become the place where all those loose ends go. Every time something pops into your head, give it to the agent and let the agent keep track of what is coming due. Prompt to try:"Keep a household task list based on the things I give you. Remind me when something needs attention and help me keep track of what is still unfinished. Ask me before adding anything to my calendar, ordering something or contacting anyone." This is one of those uses that sounds almost too simple for AI. That may be exactly why I like it. If it remembers that I need a new refrigerator filter before the old one stops working, we are making progress. 7) Let AI remember who owes you an answer This one drives me crazy. You send an email. You request a refund. You call somebody about a bill. They tell you they will get back to you. Then life happens. Two weeks later, you suddenly think, "Wait, did anybody ever answer me?" An AI agent could keep track of those loose ends for you. Tell it what you are waiting on and when you expect a response. If nothing arrives, have it remind you. Better yet, let it prepare the follow-up so you do not have to stare at a blank email trying to remember what happened in the first place. Prompt to try:"Keep track of the requests I am waiting on. If I have not received a response by the deadline I give you, remind me and draft a polite follow-up. Do not send it without my approval." That could work for a contractor estimate, a disputed charge or a return you are still waiting to hear about. I like this because the agent becomes responsible for remembering that the conversation never actually ended. 8) Have AI watch for the opening you keep missing Sometimes the issue is not the price. It is getting your hands on the thing at all. Maybe the restaurant you want is booked Saturday night. Your doctor has no opening for three weeks. The product you want keeps selling out. You could keep checking. Or you could make the AI check. Prompt to try:"Check [restaurant, appointment, event or product] for availability. Let me know when an opening appears that meets these conditions: ___. Do not book, buy or confirm anything without asking me first." This will depend on the AI agent you are using and whether the website allows that kind of automated access. But the idea is exactly where agents become useful. I do not want to ask AI whether the table is available right now. I want it to tell me Friday afternoon when somebody cancels and suddenly it is. CyberGuy pro tip: Make your AI agent earn its permissions Here is the part I would pay close attention to. An AI agent becomes more useful as you give it more access. That can include your email, calendar and other accounts. More access also means there is more that can go wrong. So I would make the agent earn those permissions. Start by letting it read something. See what it does with the information. If that goes well, maybe allow it to organize information or prepare drafts. Only then would I consider letting it perform a limited action, and even then I would keep approval turned on whenever something important could happen. Think about email. Let the agent summarize messages first. Then maybe let it draft replies. Sending those replies is another level entirely. The same thinking applies to shopping and your calendar. OpenAI says Dots can follow rules that determine which actions they can perform on their own and when they need your input. Meta says Muse asks for approval before certain critical actions, including purchases and sending emails. I would use those controls. And I would never paste passwords, PINs or two-factor authentication codes into a chat window because an AI agent asks for them. If the service offers a secure way to connect an account, use that instead. Give AI what it needs to complete the task. Do not automatically give it everything it asks for. Do you actually need an AI agent? Here is an easy way to figure that out. Ask yourself whether the job ends when AI answers you. If you ask ChatGPT to help plan dinner tonight, you probably do not need an agent. But suppose you say, "Keep watching the price of this flight and tell me when it drops below $300." Now the useful part of the job happens after you leave. The same goes for appointments. Asking what appointments you have tomorrow can be a normal AI request. Asking AI to alert you when an earlier doctor's appointment becomes available requires something that keeps checking. Agents make the most sense when the task has an unfinished part. That is where I see the real appeal. What I still would not hand over to AI There are some areas where convenience would not persuade me to give up control. I would not give an AI agent unrestricted access to move money or make major purchases. I also would not let one make medical decisions for me or handle a legal decision without a human involved. Be careful with connected accounts too. If you connect an agent to your inbox or cloud storage for a particular task, check what it can see. Once you no longer need that connection, consider removing it. AI agents may get much better at taking action on our behalf. That does not mean every action should be theirs to take. IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT Kurt's key takeaways I think AI agents get a lot more appealing when you forget the hype for a minute and ask one simple question: What am I tired of doing myself? For some people, that could be checking a price every morning. Others may want help remembering follow-ups or keeping track of household chores that always seem to surface at the worst possible time. Those are the kinds of tasks I would hand over first. I become much more cautious when AI moves from watching and reminding to actually doing something in my name. I am happy to let an agent tell me that a restaurant table opened up. Before it books dinner for me, though, I want to know exactly what it is about to do. That is where I see the sweet spot with AI agents. Let them handle the annoying part while you stay in charge of anything that could cost you money, expose your information or create a mess you have to clean up later. What is the one annoying task you would happily hand over to an AI agent tomorrow, and what is one thing you would never trust it to do for you? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. title: Starbucks hit with lawsuit over sugar content as experts reveal chain's most sugary drinks
description: A class-action lawsuit alleges Starbucks protein drinks labeled "sugar-free" contain between 13 and 21 grams of sugar per venti-sized serving.
content: Starbucks is facing a lawsuit over its "sugar-free" protein drinks, with consumers alleging some contain nearly as much sugar as a candy bar. The proposed class-action lawsuit, filed Oct. 2 in federal court in Washington state, targets eight hot and iced Starbucks protein beverages, including its Sugar-Free Vanilla Protein Latte, Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Latte and protein matcha drinks. The beverages contain between 13 and 21 grams of sugar in a venti-sized serving, according to the lawsuit, which reportedly argues that "no reasonable consumer" would expect a drink called "sugar-free" to contain that amount. POPULAR PANTRY PRODUCT CAN'T LEGALLY BE CALLED PEANUT BUTTER — HERE'S WHY The suit was brought by three consumers who bought the drinks in California, New York and Washington. It asks the court to stop Starbucks from using "sugar-free" to describe products that contain sugar. Starbucks is disputing the allegations. "We believe these claims have no merit," a Starbucks spokesperson told Fox News Digital. GROCERY SHOPPERS MAY BE RELYING ON A 'MISLEADING' CLUE WHEN CHOOSING HEALTHY FOODS "Starbucks has consistently and clearly provided information about its protein beverages, sugar-free options, customization choices, and nutritional content across product announcements, menus, marketing materials, Starbucks.com and the Starbucks app, and we intend to vigorously defend ourselves in this matter." The company says the sugar in the drinks comes naturally from protein-boosted milk rather than added sugar, and that sugar-free syrups are used for flavoring. Nicolette Pace, a New York-based registered dietitian and certified diabetes educator, noted that lactose in milk is a naturally occurring sugar and is not counted as an added sugar, but "sugar-free" and "no added sugar" are not the same. DIRTY SODA DRINKS ARE EVERYWHERE, BUT DOCTORS WARN OF HEALTH RISKS: 'METABOLIC DISASTER' "Sugar-free" does not necessarily mean a product contains zero sugar, added Dr. Michael Aziz, an internist at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City. Under FDA regulations, products labeled "sugar-free" generally must contain less than 0.5 gram of sugar per serving. "No added sugar," meanwhile, means sugars or sugar-containing ingredients have not been added during processing or preparation, though a product can still contain naturally occurring sugar, as Starbucks says its protein drinks do. Naturally occurring sugars can still affect blood glucose levels, making the total carbohydrate content important for people with diabetes to consider. JUST ONE SMALL SERVING OF ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD A DAY LINKED TO HIGHER DISEASE RISK, MAJOR STUDY FINDS The plaintiffs argue that they paid more for products advertised as sugar-free than they would have for comparable alternatives, said Danny Karon, an Ohio-based class-action attorney who is not involved in the case. "Size does matter when it comes to these things at Starbucks." "The challenge will be convincing the court — and then the jury — that consumers relied on Starbucks' alleged misrepresentations when making their purchases," Karon told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Beyond the protein beverages cited in the lawsuit, Aziz and Pace warned that other Starbucks specialty drinks can pack significant amounts of sugar, underscoring the importance of considering nutrition information, serving size and add-ons such as whipped cream and drizzles. A venti Java Chip Frappuccino can contain nearly 80 grams of sugar, or roughly 20 teaspoons, they said. They also pointed to the Caramel Ribbon Crunch Frappuccino and seasonal drinks such as the Peppermint Mocha and Pumpkin Spice Latte, which, depending on size and customization, can have almost as much sugar. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "That's massive amounts of sugar when we know that a soda has 63 grams of sugar," Aziz said, referring to standard 20-ounce bottles of popular regular sodas. "Size does matter when it comes to these things at Starbucks," Pace said. The American Heart Association recommends limiting added sugar to about 6 teaspoons, or 25 grams, per day for most women and 9 teaspoons, or 36 grams, for men, she noted. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER She stressed, however, that those recommendations apply to added sugar, not naturally occurring lactose in milk. For consumers looking to reduce their intake, she suggested keeping the order simple, and choosing a smaller size. title: Indiana survives Nebraska in comeback win, extends nation's longest active winning streak
description: Josh Hoover and Nick Marsh connected for two huge touchdowns as No. 7 Indiana rallied from an 11-point deficit to beat Nebraska at Memorial Stadium.
content: The longest active winning streak in college football lives another week. No. 7 Indiana was pushed to the brink by Nebraska, but ended up winning 20-17 on the road Saturday afternoon at Memorial Stadium. For a while, it looked like Nebraska was going to hand the defending national champions their first loss since the first round of the 2024 College Football Playoff, but a fourth quarter comeback prevented that. Indiana hadn't even trailed in a game since the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game against Ohio State, eight games ago. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The win was Indiana's 27th straight against unranked teams, as Indiana's previous loss to an unranked opponent came Nov. 25, 2023, against Purdue. For Curt Cignetti, he improved to 33-2 as Indiana's head coach. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover did just enough in the win, completing 12 of his 22 passes for 263 yards and two touchdowns while wide receiver Nick Marsh was outstanding, catching six passes for 187 yards and two touchdowns. While rallying late, the Indiana offense struggled in the first half. The Hoosiers ran just 17 plays and managed 115 yards of total offense, scoring their only three points on a 42-yard field goal by Nico Radicic in the first quarter. Nebraska, on the other hand, started fast. The Huskers opened the scoring with a 28-yard field goal by Kyle Cunanan, capping a 13-play, 66-yard drive to take a 3-0 lead. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! After Indiana responded with a field goal of its own, the Nebraska offense went to work on another long drive. Wide receiver Nyziah Hunter scored on a 10-yard end-around for his first touchdown of the season , putting Nebraska ahead 10-3 after a 10-play, 75-yard drive. The Huskers had an opportunity to add to their lead at the end of the first half, but Cunanan's 40-yard field goal attempt sailed wide right. Nebraska held the ball for more than 22 minutes in the first half alone. Indiana received the second-half kickoff and drove into Nebraska territory but was kept out of the end zone and forced to settle for another Radicic field goal, this time from 35 yards, making it 10-6. After the Indiana field goal, the game turned into a field-position battle. On the ensuing possession, the Huskers made their first mistake of the game. Facing third-and-16 from the Indiana 36-yard line, Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea was forced out of the pocket and heaved a pass toward the end zone intended for Hunter. Instead, Indiana defensive back Jamari Sharpe leaped and intercepted the pass at his team's 2-yard line . However, the Nebraska defense pinned Indiana deep in its own territory, forcing a three-and-out . After the punt, the Huskers took over at the Indiana 41-yard line. The Nebraska offense squandered the opportunity, going three-and-out, but pinned Indiana at its own 1-yard line with an excellent punt. As the fourth quarter began, the Hoosiers were forced to punt again after the Nebraska defense kept them pinned deep inside their own territory. Then, the floodgates opened. Colandrea finally broke through the Indiana defense with a 39-yard touchdown run on third-and-5. On a read-option play, Colandrea kept the ball, picked up the first down, cut back upfield and turned the corner for Nebraska's second touchdown of the game, extending its lead to 17-6. Just as the raucous Nebraska crowd erupted after Colandrea's score, Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover connected with wide receiver Nick Marsh on a 75-yard touchdown pass on the first play of the ensuing possession, silencing the Huskers faithful and cutting the deficit to 17-13. The Nebraska offense couldn't respond, giving Indiana a chance to take its first lead of the day . On fourth-and-1 from the Nebraska 44-yard line, the Huskers defense bit on a play-action pass. Hoover found a wide-open Marsh for a 44-yard touchdown, giving Indiana a 20-17 lead. Nebraska, sensing the game was slipping away, went for it on fourth-and-9 from its own 44-yard line with just under five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The gamble failed, as Indiana forced an incompletion and took over on downs, despite Nebraska still having two timeouts and the two-minute warning. However, the Nebraska defense forced a three-and-out, giving its offense another chance to mount a comeback. The Hoosiers defense held firm, forcing another turnover on downs with a sack of Colandrea. Nebraska fell to 5-1 with the loss and will look to bounce back against No. 13 Oregon next week. Indiana has another big game next week against No. 5 Ohio State at home.

title: Supreme Court climate case could bankrupt oil companies, send gas prices soaring, experts warn
description: Energy experts warn the Supreme Court's Suncor v. Boulder case could trigger thousands of climate liability lawsuits that raise gas prices.
content: A Supreme Court showdown over climate change lawsuits could leave oil companies bankrupt, gas stations facing financial ruin and Americans paying more at the pump if the justices allow cities and states to pursue billions in damages against the fossil fuel industry, energy policy experts warn. "You would see mass exodus and that would create more scarcity with fuel, more so than we're seeing already today, higher prices," Jason Isaac, CEO of American Energy Institute, told Fox News Digital. "And that's really what this is about. It's about controlling these companies and stopping the use of hydrocarbons." The Supreme Court heard arguments Monday in Suncor v. Boulder, a dispute over whether federal law prevents cities and states from suing oil companies under state law for alleged climate damage linked to emissions that cross state borders. During oral arguments, Justice Clarence Thomas pressed Boulder's attorney, Kevin Russell, on whether the legal theory could expose businesses beyond oil producers to similar lawsuits, including large retailers. WAVE OF OVERLOOKED 'LEFT-WING' LAWSUITS COULD COME WITH AN UNEXPECTED PRICE TAG FOR AMERICANS "Nothing in our theory prevents that," Russell acknowledged, although he noted that state tort law could impose additional limitations. Justice Brett Kavanaugh separately raised concerns about the potential financial consequences of widespread litigation, warning that enough lawsuits could "bankrupt" defendants and questioning whether virtually any manufacturer or business could face similar claims. The city and county of Boulder, Colo., sued oil giants ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy in 2018, accusing the companies of knowingly contributing to climate change while misleading the public about the alleged dangers of fossil fuels. The municipalities are seeking damages to help cover the mounting costs of climate-related harms. There are roughly 30 similar lawsuits pending in jurisdictions across the country, including cases in Portland and Baltimore. Boulder's lawsuit alleged ExxonMobil and Suncor knew for decades about the climate risks associated with fossil fuels but misled the public about those risks. The complaint pointed to a 1977 internal memo from ExxonMobil that circulated among the company's highest-level managers. The memo reported that "current scientific opinion overwhelmingly favors" that fossil fuels contribute to the rise in CO2 emissions. David Bookbinder, who previously served as counsel of record for Boulder but is no longer involved in the case, described the lawsuit as a way to implement an "indirect carbon tax" during a Federalist Society forum last year. But Boulder has maintained that the case is not an attempt to regulate national climate policy, arguing instead that Colorado has the authority to hold companies accountable under state law for alleged harms suffered within its borders. "Since the founding, states have had the power to provide tort remedies for injuries occurring within their borders even when the conduct causing those injuries occurred elsewhere," Russell told the justices. CATHOLIC SCHOOLS, BANNED RIFLES AND ‘CLIMATE LAWFARE’: BLOCKBUSTER FIGHTS AWAIT SUPREME COURT O.H. Skinner, executive director of the Alliance for Consumers, argued that the lawsuits are an attempt to accomplish through the courts what climate advocates have been unable to achieve through Congress. "When you really boil it down, and you separate it from all the legal arguments, the advocates who push these cases are very clear," Skinner told Fox News Digital. "That it's an effort to get a backdoor carbon tax, because carbon taxes have never passed in Congress, or to bankrupt the energy industry." Justice Samuel Alito has recused himself from the case without providing an explanation. Isaac warned that a Supreme Court ruling in Boulder's favor could open "Pandora's box," allowing thousands of jurisdictions to pursue similar lawsuits. He said a 4-4 split could have a similar practical effect by leaving the lower court's ruling in place, although a tie would not establish nationwide precedent. "There are over 90,000 levels of government — government entities just in the United States alone — that could also begin lawsuits against energy companies," Isaac told Fox News Digital. "Driving up cost to consumers because the cost to defend those would be astronomical." LAWSUITS COST EVERY AMERICAN HOUSEHOLD THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS. SUPREME COURT CAN HELP Skinner argued that who could be sued could extend beyond oil producers to businesses across the energy supply chain, including gas stations, automakers and utilities that sell or use fossil fuels. "From Boulder's perspective, anybody who's contributed to climate change would reliable, any sort of company, big or small, and the problem here is that to the left, climate change is everything and everything is climate change," Skinner told Fox News Digital. "So it's very hard to find a line for who isn't contributing to climate change." But Isaac said the case is different from lawsuits against tobacco or opioid companies because greenhouse gas emissions come from countless sources around the world and cross state and national borders, making it difficult to isolate responsibility for climate-related damage. "Emissions are a global phenomenon," Isaac told Fox News Digital. CONSERVATIVE GROUPS SAY JUSTICE KAGAN CANNOT BE IMPARTIAL IN UPCOMING SUPREME COURT CLIMATE LITIGATION ExxonMobil and Suncor argue that because greenhouse gas emissions travel globally, Colorado cannot use state law to hold companies liable for emissions originating outside its borders. The companies contend that such disputes should instead be governed by federal law. "If the energy companies were to lose and Colorado were to win, this would in effect drive up the prices of gas all across the country," Utah Attorney General Derek Brown told Fox News Digital. "And so those kind of decisions ultimately, it's the province of Congress."

title: Trump calls for Ukraine to replace Zelenskyy after clash over Russia diesel deal: 'Get a new president'
description: President Donald Trump demanded Volodymyr Zelenskyy stop striking Russian oil refineries, warning the attacks worsen global diesel and fuel supplies.
content: President Donald Trump said Saturday it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president," warning Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian oil refineries as the two leaders clashed over a U.S. deal with Moscow. "It's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump told reporters outside the White House before heading to a rally in Tennessee. Trump accused Zelenskyy of making global fuel problems worse by continuing to authorize strikes on Russian refineries. Don't hit the refineries' because that's a world problem that's caused," Trump said. Trump confirmed Friday that Washington had reached an agreement with Moscow to suspend restrictions on Russian diesel exports until April 7. TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA The agreement would allow Russia to release millions of tons of diesel into the U.S. and global markets, potentially increasing fuel supplies at a time when Americans are paying more at the pump. title: Mike Tyson predicts ‘Donald Trump will win’ midterms before joining president for New York rally

content: Boxing legend Mike Tyson is backing President Donald Trump’s political corner ahead of November’s midterm elections. title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital, returned to prison after botched execution, attorneys say
description: Christa Pike is back at prison after surviving a botched lethal injection, but her attorneys say she still struggles with arm injuries and memory problems.
content: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from a hospital and returned to prison after surviving a botched lethal injection that left her with serious medical complications, her attorneys announced. Pike, who survived two doses of the execution drug pentobarbital Sept. 30, is back at the Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years, according to a joint statement from her legal team. "Christa Pike was discharged from a local hospital and is now at Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years," the statement read. "She is grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances. She is continuing to receive medical care at the prison, and we will continue to track her recovery." CHRISTA PIKE NOW CONSCIOUS AND TALKING AFTER SURVIVING 2 DOSES OF LETHAL INJECTION DRUG The statement was issued by attorneys Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen of Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee and Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason of the Tennessee Office of the Post-Conviction Defender. The attorneys did not disclose when Pike was discharged or whether she has recovered from complications they previously described, including pneumonia, a blood clot and injuries to her arms. Ferrell told BBC Radio 4 Thursday that Pike had begun walking around her hospital room but continued to struggle with injuries to her arms and memory problems. CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEY SAYS SHE'S 'UP AND WALKING' MORE THAN A WEEK AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION "What's been described to me is that physically there's quite a bit going on, that her arms are very injured, and she's not able to use them very much," Ferrell said. "She is up and walking for the first time today but just around the room, not very far." Pike's attorneys said they believed she was brain-dead Monday evening before she unexpectedly regained consciousness the following morning. Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville. LETHAL INJECTION SURVIVOR CHRISTA PIKE'S FORMER SATANIST BOYFRIEND COULD BE RELEASED IN 5 YEARS The failed execution has prompted legal action, and a Tennessee judge ordered the state Department of Correction to preserve physical and electronic evidence related to the execution attempt. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has halted executions for the remainder of 2026. It remains unclear whether the state will seek to carry out Pike's death sentence. Fox News Digital's Mike Ruiz contributed to this report.

title: Ron DeSantis deploys an army of linemen as Florida races to clear roads, restore power after Isaias' landfall
description: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis deployed 16,000 linemen and pre-dawn road crews across the state as officials warn of post-storm hazards from Isaias.
content: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis deployed state crews early Saturday to clear major highways and bridges after Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane, but former FEMA Administrator Craig Fugate warned that deadly dangers can persist long after the hurricane passes. Hurricane Isaias made landfall along the Florida Panhandle late Friday, leaving hundreds of thousands of people without power as intense winds continued across the Southeast. FOX Weather reported four storm-related deaths across Florida and Alabama. Despite the widespread outages, DeSantis said crews made early progress clearing major roads and restoring power. EXCLUSIVE: WOMAN WHO STOLE $1.7M MEANT FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS GETS PRISON TIME AS DHS CRACKS DOWN ON FEMA FRAUD HURRICANE ISAIAS THREATENS GEORGIA VS ALABAMA SEC SHOWDOWN AS TRUMP PLANS TUSCALOOSA VISIT "We scrambled assets at 0300 for road clearing and also for search and rescue, should that have been needed. Fortunately, we have not gotten requests for our search and rescue assets. I think that's cautiously a good sign," DeSantis told "Fox & Friends Weekend." "We have had people clearing the key arteries, like Interstate 10 and the key bridges, from when it was pitch black at three or four in the morning. And they're [going to] continue to do that." The governor said Florida had positioned 16,000 utility workers ahead of landfall to speed up power restoration and reduce the risk of prolonged outages. "I'd much rather have that than let the storm go by and say, 'Oh, well, we need 10,000 linemen. Let's see if they can get here by Monday morning,'" DeSantis said. DEM GOV LASHES OUT AS TRUMP HUD SCRUTINIZES NEARLY $2B IN DISASTER FUNDS OVER FRAUD CONCERNS "So, the more you can stabilize everything, and yes, of course, the search and rescue when that's needed is very, very important. But when you do that, then you create stability in the situation, and then we can work if someone's home got damaged, if someone needs something, and we can fulfill those requests." DeSantis said wind shear weakened Isaias before landfall, limiting the extent of structural damage unlike Hurricane Michael, which devastated Panhandle communities in 2018. DHS FIRES 3 MORE FEMA WORKERS AFTER IG REPORT FINDS CREW SKIPPED HOMES WITH PRO-TRUMP SIGNS FOX Weather reported wind gusts exceeding 110 mph but said conditions before landfall helped prevent "an even more catastrophic scenario along the Florida Panhandle." Fugate warned that cleanup efforts pose additional risks, including carbon monoxide poisoning from improperly operated generators and electrocution from downed power lines. "In Florida, our history has been that we actually have as many people lose their lives after the storm and recovery," Fugate said on "Saturday in America." "[There are] trees down, power lines and just a variety of things. And be very careful as you start to clean up. We've seen people get injured from falls off ladders. We've seen carbon monoxide poisoning with people running their generators too close to their house. So, a lot of this can be prevented if people take their time," he added. DREW BREES CALLS HURRICANE KATRINA 'DEFINING MOMENT' OF CAREER, CREDITS FAITH AND COMMUNITY FOR PERSEVERANCE DeSantis said the state had strengthened its emergency response procedures after previous major hurricanes, helping crews deploy more quickly and better coordinate recovery efforts. "I look back [at] Katrina in New Orleans and stuff. It just descended into chaos," DeSantis said. "The folks that are on the ground both in our state agencies and in these local communities at the county level, they're very passionate about this project," DeSantis said, adding that crews had been working "around the clock." "They will continue to do that until the situation is stabilized, but they do deserve a lot of credit. They're the best in the business." title: Bill Maher mocks Mamdani for pivoting to Israel criticism in Oct 7 tribute, calls it 'tone-deaf'
description: Bill Maher blasted Zohran Mamdani's Oct. 7 anniversary statement on "Real Time," mocking the New York City mayor's pivot to criticizing Israel.
content: Comedian Bill Maher took aim at New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani over his statement marking the third anniversary of the deadly Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attack on Israel. Maher used Friday's episode of "Real Time" to criticize Mamdani's statement, in which the mayor called the day "profoundly painful for so many New Yorkers" and said the city grieves "alongside our many friends and neighbors who still carry that unthinkable loss." Mamdani went on to condemn the ongoing defensive acts being carried out by Israel, writing, "The suffering did not begin nor end that day. It instead continued through the Israeli government’s devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza, in which it has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, including more than 21,000 children." ISRAEL AMB TORCHES MAMDANI OCT 7 POST: 'LIKE TURNING SEPTEMBER 11 INTO A DAY OF MOURNING FOR AL-QAEDA' The mayor continued, writing that "even since the so-called ceasefire, more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed," adding "many New Yorkers are reckoning with this unbearable grief, and we mourn alongside them — all while knowing that our tax dollars fund these war crimes." Mamdani also wrote, "Three years later, we must refuse to accept a world in which occupation and apartheid continue, where war crimes are met with impunity, and our federal government continues its complicity with every arms shipment. SCHUMER, JEFFRIES DODGE MAMDANI CONTROVERSY AS FELLOW NEW YORK DEM UNLOADS "To honor the dead, we must fight for a world in which every person can live with freedom, safety, and dignity." Mamdani’s reaction to the anniversary did not go over well with Maher, who harshly criticized the mayor. BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM "Mayor Mamdani, not all that sympathetic to this stuff, but he did make some nice remarks about it," Maher said, referring to Mamdani’s statement. "But then he pivoted right to, ‘but Israel made them do it,’" Maher said, offering his interpretation of the mayor's remarks. ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTERS LABEL MAMDANI A 'TRAITOR,' ACCUSE HIM OF 'GENOCIDE' OUTSIDE OCT 7 VIGIL The comedian also mocked Mamdani's past career as a rapper, during which he performed under the stage names "Young Cardamom" and "Mr. Cardamom." The sister restaurant previously drew criticism after The Times of Israel reported that the front page of its menu featured the phrase "Down with the occupation" in English, Arabic and Hebrew. Owner Abdul Elenani previously said the language appeared on the menu before Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel. ANTI-ISRAEL GROUPS RALLY ACROSS US ON OCTOBER 7 ANNIVERSARY, CHANTING 'LONG LIVE THE INTIFADA' Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff, however, suggested that Maher's criticism could benefit Mamdani politically. "At first glance, it could appear Mamdani missed the mark with his statement or is being ‘tone-deaf’ as Maher puts it, but I’d argue it was actually a page from the Trump playbook," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "Mamdani’s base was criticizing him for having NYPD protect Netanyahu, keeping on Commissioner Tisch, arresting protesters, not following through on his promise to disband the Strategic Response Group," Shroff continued. "And a tweet or statement that plays to what his base wants to hear, ruffles feathers, grabs headlines and earns some backlash is a way to try and placate his supporters and seem like a fighter on key campaign issues that he has actually backed away from. title: President Trump blasts Nobel Peace Prize snub with blistering list of accomplishments: 'WOW!'
