title: Caitlin Clark left off 19 WNBA MVP ballots despite historic season as A’ja Wilson wins fifth award
description: Caitlin Clark became the first WNBA player to average 20 points and eight assists in a season, yet 19 voters left her off MVP ballots entirely.
content: Caitlin Clark received one first-place vote for WNBA MVP after producing a season nobody in the league had managed before. And that might not even be the most ridiculous part of the results. Nineteen voters didn't put her on their ballots at all. The WNBA announced Thursday that A’ja Wilson won her record fifth MVP award, receiving 65 of the 74 first-place votes from a panel of sportswriters and broadcasters. Minnesota rookie Olivia Miles finished second, followed by Indiana’s Kelsey Mitchell and Clark. CAITLIN CLARK SAYS SHE BLOCKS SOCIAL MEDIA HATE AND ENJOYS HOSTILE WNBA ROAD CROWDS Clark appeared on 55 ballots, receiving one first-place vote, six second-place votes, 20 third-place votes, 16 fourth-place votes and 12 fifth-place votes. She finished with 212 points, well behind Miles’ 442 and Mitchell’s 287. Wilson had an outstanding season and a compelling case to win. But apparently, more than a quarter of the voters watched Clark this year and decided five other players deserved recognition ahead of her. I'd love to hear those explanations. Caitlin Clark’s historic season deserved more consideration Clark averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game, becoming the first WNBA player to finish a season averaging at least 20 points and eight assists. Combining her own baskets and free throws with the points teammates scored from her assists, Clark created an average of 41.2 points per game. According to the WNBA’s own end-of-season review, that was the highest average in league history. That's a useful place to start a conversation about offensive value, especially when her teammate finished ahead of her in MVP voting. There's a compelling case that Mitchell benefited from Clark far more than vice versa. After all, Mitchell just completed her ninth WNBA season. In her six years with Indiana prior to Clark's arrival, Mitchell averaged 16.4 points per game. In the three seasons since the Fever drafted Clark, Mitchell has averaged 21.4 points, including a career-high 24.7 points this season. Clark also had five games with at least 30 points and 10 assists this season. Every other player in WNBA history combined has four. Read that again. Read that again. Caitlin Clark did something five times in one season that every other player combined has done four times in WNBA regular-season history. Her best performance came against Seattle on July 17, when she scored 45 points and had 10 assists. It was the first 40-point, 10-assist game the WNBA had ever seen. And those spectacular nights were backed by sustained production. Clark recorded 13 games with at least 20 points and 10 assists, nearly one-third of her 40 appearances. She finished with 891 points and 333 assists, becoming the first player to reach 800 points and 300 assists in a season. Then there's the team success. Indiana averaged a league-record 96 points per game. Clark’s ability to score while creating opportunities for her teammates helped make that possible. Apparently, some voters found all of that easier to overlook than others. Miles averaged 19.8 points and six assists while helping Minnesota finish with the league’s best record. Although it's worth noting that Minnesota also finished with the league’s best record in 2025, before Miles entered the league. Mitchell scored a league-record 1,086 points. That's impressive, but Clark helped create those scoring opportunities through both her passing and the defensive attention she draws. Wilson, meanwhile, averaged 26.2 points and 9.4 rebounds, led the league in points and blocks per game, and helped Las Vegas win 31 games. Her ability to dominate at both ends gives voters plenty of reasons to put her first and, honestly, she probably deserved to win. But choosing Wilson and leaving Clark outside the top five are very different judgments. WNBA media has earned the scrutiny The award was decided by sportswriters and broadcasters. Given how some prominent members of that industry have covered Clark, skepticism about their judgment shouldn't surprise anyone. Too much of the coverage treats her popularity as something that needs a racial explanation before anyone can simply appreciate her basketball. In May, Cari Champion said about Clark: "I don’t like you. I don’t like the way you behave on the court." By September, Champion was calling Clark an "avatar for people who want to spread hate." In July, Nancy Armour argued that Clark’s reactions to officiating endangered Black and queer players, even invoking Emmett Till. Even this week, Charlotte Wilder wanted "something a little more forceful" from Clark about the alleged treatment of Black WNBA players, despite acknowledging she had already spoken out. That coverage reflects a preference for a story in which Black players need defending and Clark needs to constantly apologize for her mere existence. Her performance too often becomes secondary to what commentators believe her popularity represents. Sportswriters, commentators and broadcasters are entitled to their opinions (as bad as they often are). Those examples don't tell us who left Clark off a ballot, but they help explain why fans might question the media’s judgment. SOCIAL MEDIA WAS NOT LOVING CAITLIN CLARK GETTING SNUBBED BY TV NETWORK'S MVP GRAPHIC And questioning their judgment doesn't require rooting against Wilson. She received only four Defensive Player of the Year votes while Angel Reese received 46 and won the award in a landslide. I thought Wilson deserved considerably more support in that race, but as I argued at the time, the media loves to trumpet Reese as a star and they needed a reason to prop her up. The standard should be consistent: evaluate what the players actually did, and be prepared to defend the result. Clark deserved to finish higher in MVP voting To be clear, Clark’s popularity doesn't entitle her to an MVP award. But it's not like her play didn't warrant consideration as the league's most valuable player. There is room to disagree about how much weight to give defense, turnovers, scoring efficiency or a team’s record. Reasonable people can disagree about where Clark belonged behind Wilson, but leaving the Fever superstar outside the top five is borderline malpractice. That doesn't prove that they simply don't like Caitlin Clark and don't want her to succeed, but it certainly raises the question. If those 19 voters have a basketball explanation for leaving Clark off their ballots, they should make it public immediately.

title: Iranian protester hanged hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over jail phone line
description: Alireza Sepahi married his imprisoned fiancée over a prison phone line hours before his execution at Isfahan Central Prison for anti-government protest.
content: An Iranian anti-regime protester was hanged at dawn Oct. 5 inside Isfahan Central Prison, just hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over a jail phone line, The Times reported Thursday. Alireza Sepahi, 25, was executed alongside co-defendant Alireza Raisi after being sentenced to death in the anti-government demonstrations at Isfahan’s Alikhani Square Jan. 8., according to Human Rights Iran. Sepahi and his bride, student activist Mahshad Keshani, 22, knew and loved each other before being arrested during anti-regime demonstrations, the report said. IRAN HANGS 2 PROTESTERS IN PUBLIC, CROWD CRIES 'DISHONORABLE' AS SECURITY FIRES TEAR GAS Keshani, who is serving a five-year sentence, pushed for an informal wedding Sunday as fears mounted that Sepahi’s execution was imminent after a final family summons. The couple exchanged vows over the phone from inside Isfahan prison, joined by their fathers. Human rights lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi facilitated the ceremony by reading the vows for the fathers to bless. Keshani’s family gave a copy of the Quran, a saffron rock candy and a single red rose as a traditional dowry. "It was Mahshad’s idea," Davoudi told The Times. "Even now, I wonder how one young woman can possess such courage." IRAN TO EXECUTE FIRST FEMALE PROTESTER TIED TO ANTI-REGIME UNREST Davoudi recalled warning Keshani about the permanent nature of the decision. "I told her, ‘My dear, you understand that this cannot simply be undone?’" Davoudi said. "She said, ‘Mr Davoudi, I love Alireza.’" When Davoudi presented the proposal to Sepahi, the young man broke down in tears. "Alireza was crying, and something deeply painful and beautiful happened. Even the prison officers began to cry," Davoudi said. The ceremony held no formal authority to halt the execution. Sepahi had previously survived a scheduled hanging in July after suffering a heart attack on his way to the gallows. Authorities then rescheduled the execution after he regained consciousness. On Monday morning, hours after the vows were spoken, Sepahi was hanged. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS. THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN He is among seven defendants executed in the Alikhani Square case, in which 12 men were accused in the deaths of four security personnel. After the hanging, Sepahi’s family was reportedly prevented by authorities from burying their son in his hometown. Davoudi condemned the Iranian regime's actions. "I do not know how to come to terms with this," Davoudi said. "The regime is taking revenge on innocent young people for the humiliation it has suffered internationally." Human rights groups report Keshani remains in custody, facing additional security charges. This came as Maryam Rajavi, president-elect of the National Council of Resistance of Iran (NCRI), urged U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres to take immediate international action to halt executions and the killing of protesters in Iran, citing thousands of executions and decades of impunity for human rights abuses. title: World Series champion Ryan Howard details why coaching and accountability set the tone for winning
description: Philadelphia Phillies legend Ryan Howard told OutKick in a recent interview that a team's clubhouse chemistry is integral to a team's success.
content: For Major League Baseball teams, a team's culture and chemistry is paramount to gutting through the grueling season - and according to World Series champion Ryan Howard, it outweighs a team's talent. MLB plays 162 regular-season games in about 180 days, from the end of March until the beginning of October. Spring training starts in the middle of February, and if a team makes a deep postseason run, the season may not end until the end of October. During the long and arduous season, players see each other more than they see their families. Philadelphia Phillies legend Ryan Howard told OutKick that a strong clubhouse culture and team chemistry outweigh the team’s talent. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Every team has talent, but I always say if you have the culture and chemistry. That culture and chemistry will outweigh talent, any day. To where you put the two together, you're unstoppable," Howard told OutKick in a recent interview. Howard, who spent his entire 13-year career with the Phillies, said it was the coaches who established the clubhouse’s culture. "I think for us, it started from the top with the coaching staff. When you have coaches that give you a positive environment every single day that you show up, it's loose, it's lax, you've got coaches that you know are gonna go and they're gonna fight for you, no matter what, on the field, off the field. You create that environment and it makes it easier for the players to all want to be able to get along," Howard said. "When you have people that have the mindset of, hey, we want to win, not want to win, we expect to win. So, when everybody shows up with that mindset, day in and day out, you know the work that's gonna need to go in and your coaching staff is helping to continue to grow that environment, man, it makes it so easy." The 2006 NL MVP said that when the coaches put in the same amount of work, if not more, than the players do to help them become the best they can possibly be, you can’t ask for anything more as a player. In addition to helping everyone become the best players they could be, Howard pointed to the coaching staff holding players accountable as a critical part of a good clubhouse. The three-time All-Star recalled a time when one of his managers pulled shortstop Jimmy Rollins from a game due to a lack of effort. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "The manager had to get on my man, young James, Jimmy Rollins, for not running out a fly ball, taking him out of the game. For hitting a pop fly and not running hard down to first base or something like that," Howard said. Howard said that in a good clubhouse, coaches aren’t the only ones holding players accountable; the players do so as well. Howard said that on one occasion, Rollins got on outfielder Shane Victorino for jogging after a fly ball. "It's one of those things where it's like, all it took is that one time for you to tell me. And I got it. And then the next play, it's like, all right, you're sprinting after the ball or you're sprinting out of the box, you're doing it, all it takes is one time because as you said, it's a long season. So sometimes you're gonna have those little mental lulls and all that stuff," Howard said. "But when you can have the people there to kind of help keep you accountable, again, all it takes is that one time or that that one kick in the butt just to kind of get you back on track and then you're back moving where we need you to go." PHILLIES ISSUES The Phillies were eliminated by the Atlanta Braves last week in the National League Wild Card Series, and the future looks bleak. After making the World Series in 2022, they have regressed year after year. In 2023, they lost in the NLCS, lost in the NLDS in 2024 and 2025, and now in the Wild Card round this season. Since 2022, the team has maintained the same core but has still not managed to get over the hump and win a World Series title. The issue for the Phillies is that the core of first baseman Bryce Harper (33), designated hitter Kyle Schwarber (33), shortstop Trea Turner (33), catcher J.T. Realmuto (35), starting pitchers Zack Wheeler (36), Aaron Nola (33), Jesús Luzardo (29) and Cristopher Sánchez (29) is only getting older. Howard was in a similar situation later in his career. title: ABC News deletes ‘hit piece’ on Trump sons' Pentagon-linked investments without explanation
description: ABC News quietly deleted its report on Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump's alleged ties to Pentagon contracts after 1789 Capital threatened legal action.
content: ABC News deleted a report criticizing the business dealings of President Donald Trump’s oldest sons, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, Thursday after facing legal threats but has failed to provide any explanation or editor’s note for the vanished "hit piece." The now-deleted report, which can still be viewed via the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, was published Wednesday with the headline, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election," and said Anduril, the company investing in a new Baltimore shipyard, had ties to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump. "1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company," ABC News reported in the deleted story. TRUMP TURNS TO EMERGING TECH GIANT IN MULTI-BILLION BID TO RAMP UP US SUBMARINE PRODUCTION "Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov, the official system for government contracting. "The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one." Alexa Henning, a spokesperson for 1789 Capital and a former chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, took to social media, insisting the company does not have a "major stake" in Anduril and blasting the "biased hit piece." "Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning wrote. "Meaning the ‘investments’ mentioned were actually the total number raised for a funding round, that MANY companies contribute to," Henning continued. "Another thing that the reporter buried the lead on was that many of these companies have gotten government contracts during Biden AND Trump, which completely negates the assertion by ABC that Don Jr and Eric Trump are doing anything wrong." JARED KUSHNER SCOLDS CNN OVER 'DEEPLY MISLEADING’ REPORT, SAYS KEY INFO BURIED BEHIND PAYWALL Shortly after, ABC News deleted the story from its website. The link to the original report now states, "This page either does not exist or is currently unavailable." ABC News did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The network has not issued a correction or provided a public explanation for why the report was removed from its website. ABC News also deleted a viral X post intended to promote the story that was shared by several prominent Democrats. Henning spoke to Fox News Digital after ABC News deleted the story. She said that in addition to calling out the story publicly on X, she sent a detailed email to ABC News pointing out mistakes in the reporting and informing the Disney-owned network that lawyers would be in touch if action was not taken. She said she "really appreciates that they took it down" but wants a clear explanation of why it was published in the first place and believes ABC News should inform readers of its errors. ‘LIBELOUS’ NYT REPORT TYING TRUMP FAMILY TO GOVERNMENT-BACKED DEAL SPARKS LEGAL DEMAND Henning also told Fox News Digital that ABC News never asked 1789 Capital for comment prior to the story’s initial publication despite being mentioned several times in the initial report. "The majority of people reporting on 1789 do not fundamentally understand how it works," she said. Once the story had vanished, Trump Jr. responded to California Gov. Gavin Newsom, who had shared the initial ABC News report on X. "ABC deleted this article in less than 24 hours because it’s false. Sounds about as long as your presidential campaign would last," Trump Jr. wrote. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital’s Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

title: Liberty make official inquiry into reset timeout dispute after overtime loss to Dream in WNBA semifinals
description: Breanna Stewart says officials told the Liberty they had no reset timeout when they actually did, sparking an inquiry after Atlanta Dream's OT win.
content: The Atlanta Dream moved within one victory of a WNBA Finals berth after outlasting the New York Liberty 101-98 in overtime Wednesday night to take a commanding 2-0 lead in the semifinal series. However, Game 2’s dramatic finish was overshadowed by controversy after New York star Breanna Stewart said officials incorrectly told the Liberty they did not have a reset timeout available in the closing seconds, even though the team still had one remaining. "This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end, and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with the reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart told reporters after the game. DREAM MOVE WITHIN ONE WIN OF FIRST WNBA FINALS APPEARANCE SINCE 2013 AFTER OVERTIME VICTORY Under league rules, each team is given two team timeouts and one reset timeout during overtime, allowing it to advance the ball without huddling on the sideline. Stewart continued later: "I asked Kevin [Fahy]. I said, 'Do we have a reset timeout?' And he said, 'I'm going to check at the table.' So then he looked to [crew chief] Fatou [Cissoko-Stephens], and she said, 'No.' So then he told me, 'No.'" Video footage aired during Thursday’s broadcast of ESPN’s "NBA Today" offered a closer look at part of the disputed exchange between Stewart and an official during the closing seconds of the Liberty’s overtime defeat. In the clip, Stewart turns toward Fahy and appears to ask, "Do we have a reset?" The footage does not make clear whether Fahy acknowledged Stewart or responded to her question. Fahy is positioned behind Stewart as Atlanta’s Angel Reese shoots free throws and appears to be communicating with the scorer’s table. WNBA'S OFFICIATING OVERHAUL IS ALREADY DRAWING COMPLAINTS FROM PLAYERS AND COACHES ONE WEEK INTO SEASON A late New York turnover gave Atlanta an opportunity to put the game away. Reese, the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year, went to the foul line and sank both free throws to extend the Dream’s lead to three points. The Liberty inbounded from under their own basket and got the ball to Stewart, but her desperation shot was no good as the clock ticked to triple zeros. "Of course, who knows what happened to end the game," Stewart said. "But we would have had hopefully a better shot on our goal." Officials were not made available to members of the media until roughly two hours after the game. ESPN asked crew chief Fatou Cissoko-Stephens in the pool report why Stewart said she had been told the Liberty's reset timeout wasn't available. "Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," she said. The controversy has prompted the Liberty to formally inquire with the league about the situation, ESPN reported, citing sources. Asked whether he was unaware that the team had a reset timeout at their disposal, Liberty coach Chris DeMarco responded, "Yeah, same thing. They just said we didn't have it. Multiple staff members [were told]. It is what it is. We've got to demand more. But it is what it is." Dream coach Karl Smesko was also asked about the number of Liberty timeouts remaining. "I was, I thought they had a timeout left," Smesko said. "But they played it out the way they did. So I was expecting it to be advanced, but it wasn't, so we had to play it, and fortunately we were able to get the stop." Cissoko-Stephens added that the scorer’s table and stats staff keep up with the number of available timeouts, but emphasized that "teams are responsible for managing and tracking their timeout usage throughout the game." When the Liberty had possession in critical moments, they failed to capitalize on their opportunities. With less than 10 seconds remaining in overtime, Ionescu lost control of the ball while driving, sending it out of bounds. Ionescu took responsibility for the costly mistake. "I told them it was my fault," she said. "I took ownership for that. This loss is on me. I've got to take it on the chin, and I've got to be better." The Dream's leading scorer, Allisha Gray, sat out of the game due to a finger injury. The Liberty would have to overcome unprecedented odds to become the first team in WNBA history to erase a 2-0 deficit and win a best-of-five playoff series. Game 3 is scheduled for Friday night as the series shifts to Brooklyn, New York.

title: Dem who ripped rival’s donor-fueled 'good life' dropped campaign cash on Disney, spouse travel
description: Rep. Vicente Gonzalez, D-Texas, accused a GOP rival of "living the good life" on donor money, but his campaign reported nearly $20,000 spent on trips to Disney World, the UAE and Europe
content: A House Democrat accused a Republican rival of "living the good life" on donor money after her campaign reported Disney World spending, and she was allegedly seen returning from the theme park around the same time. But Democratic Texas Rep. Vicente Gonzalez's own records show nearly $20,000 in campaign spending around the same time on international and domestic trips with his wife, including his own visit to Disney World, a five-star hotel stay on the beach in the UAE and a Michelin-starred restaurant bill in Zurich. Gonzalez made the jab at Republican Mayra Flores in October 2025, months after posting photos documenting his own two-day Disney World trip with his wife and several other associates on social media in April. The social media posts coincided with payments Gonzalez's campaign made to the Florida theme park and resort around the same time, totaling more than $1,100. PROMINENT DEM’S FATAL ERROR PROMPTS REPUBLICAN TO PREDICT ‘RED TIDAL WAVE’ IN BLUE STRONGHOLD The Disney payments and photos were just one piece of a broader travel and hospitality spending trail from Gonzalez’s campaign reviewed by Fox News Digital. His campaign reported thousands of dollars in expenses at upscale restaurants and hotels from Washington and Texas, to California and Europe, alongside campaign spending on multiple overseas trips during which Gonzalez's wife accompanied, or appeared to accompany, the congressman, according to posts Gonzalez shared on social media. During one 2024 trip to the UAE that utilized campaign funds and coincided with social media posts in the same location posted on Gonzalez's Facebook, more than $13,000 in airfare and hotel expenses were spent. Gonzalez described apparent photos of the trip on social media as an "after campaign break," and his posts showed the congressman with his wife doing various sightseeing activities and one photo from a bed inside a top-floor luxury hotel room next to the beach. The fifth-term Democrat representative is fighting to hold his South Texas seat against Republican Eric Flores in November after the GOP candidate defeated Mayra Flores and a crowded Republican field earlier this year. The race has drawn national attention as both parties battle for the district and Gonzalez enters the final stretch with a significant campaign cash advantage. Gonzalez took aim at rival Mayra Flores in 2025, suggesting she was potentially using campaign funds to travel to Disney World with her kids. In an October 2025 social media post, Gonzalez shared a photo of her at Dallas Love Field Airport with two young family members, a Disney World bag and stuffed animals. Gonzalez captioned the photo "living the good life on donor's resources again" and cited a report that found payments to Disney World from her campaign around the same time as the photos. But federal campaign finance records show Gonzalez's own campaign reported a combined $1,122.76 went to Walt Disney Resorts on March 24, 2025, and May 27, 2025, around the same time he posted photos on social media from a two-day trip to Walt Disney World with his own family on April 26, 2025. "DC to Disney! What a fantastic 2 days," Gonzalez posted on Facebook alongside a photo of himself, his wife and several others. SWALWELL PAL ACCUSED OF USING CAMPAIGN CASH TO BANKROLL ‘LUXURY LIFESTYLE,' INCLUDING SUPER BOWL TICKETS Federal campaign finance rules do not prohibit campaigns from paying travel expenses simply because a candidate's spouse or children accompany them. The FEC allows campaign funds to cover travel for candidates, their spouses and minor children when the trip is directly related to campaign activity or the candidate's official responsibilities as a federal officeholder. Campaign funds cannot, however, be used to pay for personal vacations or other family expenses that would have existed regardless of the candidate's campaign or official duties. When a trip mixes campaign or official business with personal activities, the campaign must be reimbursed for the costs attributable to the personal portion. "Every dollar this campaign spends is legal and publicly disclosed, and these reports come straight from our own FEC filings," Gonzalez's campaign manager, Alex Philley, told Fox News Digital in a statement when asked about the campaign spending. "The spending South Texans are worried about is their own on higher costs driven by Trump's agenda that Eric Flores would proudly rubber-stamp." Gonzalez's FEC filings identify two $561.38 Disney payments, one from March 2025 and another from May 2025, only as "travel expenses," leaving unclear from the public disclosures what campaign or official activity the expenditures were connected to. When asked specifically about this trip, Philley said it was tied to "a very important Financial Services trip" with Rep. French Hill, R-Ark., the Republican chairman of the U.S. House Committee on Financial Services, of which Gonzalez is a member. Philley said the campaign's spending on international trips where Gonzalez's wife was present had been tied to official business as well, including a visit with the Pope, although he did not address each trip separately when asked about them. SUPREME COURT STRIKES DOWN LIMIT ON PARTY CAMPAIGN SPENDING IN COORDINATION WITH CANDIDATES For example, Gonzalez traveled with his wife to Morocco in mid-2019 under the Mutual Educational and Cultural Exchange Act, or MECEA, which allows members of Congress to accept travel from foreign governments for approved cultural exchanges. Campaigns are allowed to pay for their spouses to join them, but only if the spouse is performing bona fide official responsibilities. Diplomatic and ceremonial protocol for certain events or campaign office functions like managing travel logistics are often cited as reasons for why spouses need to attend. Gonzalez's campaign reported paying $4,767.53 for his "spouse travel expense" in connection with the 2019 MECEA trip to Morocco, according to FEC records. In December 2024, the campaign reported $12,810 to Emirates Airlines and $359.27 at a luxury five-star Abu Dhabi hotel called Emirates Towers in "officially connected" CODEL expenses. While the campaign funds for the trip did not explicitly name Gonzalez’s wife, photos from Gonzalez's social media page showed several images of him and his wife in Abu Dhabi around the same time as his campaign's payments, including a photo from the top floor of what appeared to be a luxury, beachfront hotel. The pair also appeared in photos exploring the city and sightseeing around the time of the payments. SQUAD DEM IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER SPENDING SPREE AT LUXURY HOTELS: 'CHAMPAGNE SOCIALIST' "Finally, an after campaign break!" Gonzalez captioned the photos, one of which showed him holding an exotic bird. Other photos posted around that time by Gonzalez's campaign page showed him visiting U.S. troops in the Middle East and meeting with other officials. Other photos showed Gonzalez and his wife at the "4th largest and most modern Mosque in the world" in Abu Dhabi. The international travel continued in August 2025, when Gonzalez posted a photo with his wife in Zurich, Switzerland. Campaign records subsequently showed a $566.67 expense to Swiss Air and another $395 "Travel Expense" at La Rôtisserie in Zurich, a one-Michelin-star restaurant. The records did not explicitly indicate the expenses were used to pay for Gonzalez’s wife. Weeks earlier, Gonzalez appeared to engage in international luxury travel paid for by his campaign. FEC records for Gonzalez's campaign reveal a $442.41 "Travel Expense" at the five-star luxury Parco dei Principi Grand Hotel in Rome the same week he posted a photo of himself on social media meeting with the Pope in 2025. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This was not a vacation," Philley said in a statement to Fox News Digital about the trip. "You may want to ask the committee why they booked this hotel. This was not the congressman’s choice; he only had to pay for it." Between 2024 and 2026, Gonzalez's campaign also reported thousands of dollars in expenditures at upscale restaurants, hotels and resorts around the country, including around $4,000 at The Capital Grille in Washington, D.C., along with spending at Eddie V's Prime Seafood in Houston and several other high-end D.C. restaurants. Recently, Gonzalez's campaign reported a $1,019 expense at California's Ojai Valley Inn, a Forbes Travel Guide-recognized luxury resort sprawling across 220 acres with a spa, four pools and a championship-caliber golf course and more than $1,400 at Pennsylvania's Omni Bedford Springs Resort & Spa, an AAA Four Diamond property featuring a 30,000-square-foot spa, golf course and indoor and outdoor pools.

title: Obama Foundation workers move to unionize over benefits, working conditions months after center opens

title: Haverford professor charged over alleged ‘heinous’ antisemitic online attacks, barred from campus
description: Haverford College professor Guangtian Ha allegedly sent 50 antisemitic threats to a Jewish colleague using anonymous X accounts, FBI charges reveal.
content: A Haverford College professor was arrested Tuesday and charged with federal cyberstalking after allegedly sending dozens of antisemitic threats to a colleague in Pennsylvania. It prompted the college to bar him from campus, more than two years after Jewish students accused the same professor of making threatening statements about supporters of Israel in a separate lawsuit against the school. Haverford College President Wendy Raymond addressed the arrest of religion professor Guangtian Ha in a statement provided to Fox News Digital by a college spokesperson. "I am heartbroken and furious at the possibility that an individual within our community would seek to inflict such pain on another," Raymond said. "This disturbing news is made even more harmful for many given its proximity to both the Jewish High Holidays and the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks." ISRAELI MEDICS TRAIN US SYNAGOGUES HOW TO RESPOND TO ATTACKS, AS HIGH HOLIDAYS APPROACH According to a federal indictment, Ha allegedly used at least four anonymous X accounts to send approximately 50 threatening messages to a Jewish colleague between October 2025 and May 2026. Prosecutors alleged that Ha posted the colleague's home address, referenced the colleague's children and made statements invoking the Holocaust. The colleague's spouse and three children temporarily left their home twice because of the threats, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. The arrest follows earlier allegations against Ha that were included in a 2024 antisemitism lawsuit against Haverford College. In a January 2025 amended complaint, Jewish students accused Ha of publishing hostile social media posts about supporters of Israel, including one in which he allegedly said he knew their identities. The complaint reproduced a statement attributed to Ha targeting people within his Haverford community who remained silent about, or supported, what he characterized as genocide. "I will never forgive them," Ha said, according to the complaint. "I know their names and I know their faces. Never forgive. No reconciliation." FBI NABS 7 FOR ALLEGED 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE' TO PRESSURE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, BUSINESSES OVER ISRAEL TIES The plaintiffs alleged that Ha's remarks were threatening and that college administrators had been informed of his posts by September 2024. They further alleged that Haverford had taken no effective action against him at the time of the January 2025 filing. The earlier lawsuit did not establish that Ha engaged in unlawful conduct, and the allegations in that case are distinct from the federal cyberstalking charge. Raymond said the college had placed Ha, who was already on sabbatical and not teaching during the academic year, on administrative leave pending the criminal proceedings over the "heinous online attacks." "I am deeply distressed by these allegations and want to state in the plainest of terms that any form of harassment or discrimination based on identity is unacceptable, antithetical to our values, and has no place at Haverford," Raymond said. WEAPONIZING THE CHARGE OF GENOCIDE FUELS AN INCREASINGLY DANGEROUS ANTISEMITISM The arrest came just two months after Haverford settled the lawsuit brought by Jewish members of its community over allegations that administrators failed to adequately address antisemitic harassment after Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attacks against Israel. As part of the August settlement, the college committed to annual antisemitism awareness training, revisions to campus policies and the creation of a committee to address antisemitism. A federal judge had previously dismissed the plaintiffs' Title VI discrimination claim while allowing a breach-of-contract claim to proceed. title: If you've ever wondered why Alex Ovechkin has crushed soda on the bench his whole career, here's your answer
description: Alex Ovechkin revealed how a marathon runner trainer from Russia inspired his famous Coca-Cola habit after the Capitals' home-opener victory.
content: Washington Capitals star Alex Ovechkin's career is legendary in a few ways, but one of the stranger parts of it is his mid-game beverage choice. ALEX OVECHKIN ANNOUNCES THIS WILL BE HIS FINAL NHL SEASON AS ALL-TIME GREAT CAREER COMES TO A CLOSE The question came from TNT's Paul Bissonette, and Ovechkin said it was a long story, but it started with a trainer in his native Russia. "A long story, but one of my trainers who I work with back in Russia told me — he was a marathon runner — and he said, like, 'When you're tired, you're exhausted, you need some sugar in your body or some energy, (and) we always drink Coca-Cola.' "So, I started drinking (Coke), and I think it worked." Yeah, I'd say it probably did. WASHINGTON CAPITALS STAR ALEX OVECHKIN CRASHES A COUPLE'S WEDDING PHOTO SHOOT ON A HOTEL STAIRCASE Ovechkin is known for some unusual dietary habits for someone who has played at such a high level for as long as he has. title: Parkinson's patients may protect memory and movement with one simple habit
description: A University of Cincinnati study links weekly physical activity to slower cognitive decline and motor function loss in Parkinson's disease patients.
content: Weekly physical activity could help to slow down disease progression in Parkinson’s patients, a new study found. The research, led by the University of Cincinnati, included 294 patients with mild-to-moderate Parkinson's disease. Their average age was 66. The participants reported their weekly physical activity via questionnaires. ALAN ALDA REVEALS UNEXPECTED WEAPON IN HIS BATTLE AGAINST PARKINSON'S DISEASE Physical activity was assessed through structured interviews covering moderate and vigorous activities at work, at home and during recreation. Examples of moderate activity included brisk walking, light swimming, doubles tennis and household activities such as washing windows, vacuuming or mowing the lawn, the study release stated. Vigorous activity included pursuits like jogging, fast bicycling, team sports and singles tennis, along with shoveling and carrying heavy loads. Participants were divided into three groups based on their amount of weekly physical activity — up to four hours, four to eight hours and more than eight hours. PARKINSON'S IS BECOMING MORE COMMON; HERE ARE 5 THINGS EVERYONE SHOULD KNOW The researchers then monitored the participants’ cognitive health for up to five years and their motor function for up to seven years. Each additional hour of physical activity per week was linked to slightly slower declines in memory, thinking and movement abilities over time, even after accounting for factors such as age, sex, education, weight and disease severity. Patients who were physically active for four to eight hours per week experienced slower declines in memory and thinking abilities than those who exercised less than four hours. Exercise duration above eight hours per week did not appear to provide additional benefits for memory and thinking. The study was published Oct. 7 in Neurology, the official medical journal of the American Academy of Neurology. PARKINSON’S PATIENT’S YEARSLONG TREMOR VANISHES WITHIN MINUTES OF NEW ULTRASOUND TREATMENT "Parkinson’s disease is a brain disorder that causes movement and cognitive problems that gradually worsen, leading to disability and a loss of independence," study author Dong-Woo Ryu, M.D., Ph.D., of the University of Cincinnati and The Catholic University of Korea, said in the press release. "Previous research has shown associations between physical activity and movement symptoms. Our study found physical activity may have dual benefits, with associations with slower declines in movement and cognition." "While our study found small differences between activity levels, these differences may become more meaningful over time." Ryu pointed out that the potential benefits of physical activity for Parkinson’s patients may depend on how long they stay active and whether they continue exercising over time. "While our study found small differences between activity levels, these differences may become more meaningful over time," he said. The researchers cautioned that most participants had relatively strong thinking and memory skills when the study began, so additional research is needed to confirm the findings. "Exercise has well-established benefits for physical fitness and mobility, along with potential benefits for brain health through mechanisms that are not yet fully understood," Dr. Vibhash Sharma, a neurologist at UT Southwestern in Dallas, Texas, who specializes in Parkinson’s disease and other movement disorders, told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "These findings further emphasize the importance of regular physical activity in managing Parkinson’s disease." One of the strengths of the study is that patients were followed over several years, with assessments of both motor and cognitive function, noted Sharma, who was not involved in the research. Because the study was observational, it could not establish whether exercise directly slows Parkinson's disease progression. Also, as participants reported their own physical activity, they may not have accurately remembered how much they exercised. The participants were all located at a single location and were primarily White, which could limit the generalizability of the results, the researchers noted. title: Deadly crash kills two as plane plunges into 'ball of flames' near suburban golf course
description: Authorities said a Van's RV-7A crashed near Petaluma Municipal Airport in Northern California, killing two people and sparking a fire that engulfed the aircraft.
content: A small plane crashed shortly after takeoff near a Northern California airport Wednesday morning — killing two people on board and sparking a fire, authorities said. The plane, a Van's RV-7A, crashed shortly after taking off from Petaluma Municipal Airport in Sonoma County, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) told Fox News Digital. The incident took place at around 10:45 a.m. local time on Oct. 7. SKYDIVERS WATCH PLANE VANISH FROM SIGHT, MAKE SPLIT-SECOND DECISION TO JUMP The aircraft went down in a field near Rooster Run Golf Course, where aerial footage showed scattered wreckage and scorched ground, according to FOX 2 San Francisco. Both people on board were killed, Petaluma police told FOX 2. The investigation is being led by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), with the FAA assisting. An NTSB spokesperson told Fox News Digital that a "post-impact fire" erupted after the crash. MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED An investigator was expected to arrive at the scene Thursday to document the wreckage before the aircraft is recovered to a secure facility for further examination. NTSB investigators will review flight tracking data, air traffic control communications, aircraft maintenance records, weather conditions, the pilot's flight experience and witness statements, the official added. Petaluma Police Lt. Zilverio Rivera told reporters the aircraft was "fully engulfed in fire" when emergency crews arrived, FOX 2 reported. title: Fort Hood survivor shot in head vows to watch terrorist face historic firing squad
description: Retired Staff Sgt. Alonzo Lunsford, shot multiple times including once in the head, explains why he plans to witness Nidal Malik Hasan's execution.
content: More than 15 years after surviving several gunshot wounds during a terrorist attack at Fort Hood, retired Staff Sgt. Alonzo Lunsford is preparing to watch the man who shot him be executed. Speaking on "America’s Newsroom," Lunsford explained why he wants to attend the execution, which President Donald Trump recently approved to be carried out by firing squad. "You live by the sword, you die by the sword," Lunsford said. "And the way that he went about doing his deed was a coward's way because we didn't have any way to defend ourselves that day." TEXAS EXECUTES JAMAAL HOWARD DESPITE CONCERNS OVER LETHAL INJECTION DRUG USED IN FAILED TENNESSEE EXECUTION Trump approved the use of an Army firing squad to execute Nidal Malik Hasan, a former Army major convicted of killing 13 people and wounding more than 30 others in the 2009 attack. Hasan opened fire on unarmed soldiers and civilians at Fort Hood while shouting "Allahu Akbar." Standing at 6-foot-9, Lunsford was shot several times, including once in the head. He believes attending the execution could bring closure to survivors and grieving families. "It's for two reasons. One is to give the families of the deceased a chance to close a chapter and also the survivors to close a chapter," Lunsford said of the execution. "And it sends a clear message that we will not stand for this activity in any of our armed services or in the United States," he added. Lunsford said that for him and others affected by the attack, even holidays are not the same, adding that families of the deceased will "never get a chance to cherish a Christmas, a Thanksgiving, an Easter" with their loved ones again. "For the survivors, even though we can still do those, celebrate those holidays, we still feel for those ones that we lost that day. Me personally, the holidays will never be the same for me. But what I can do for the ones that I lost that day is to live for them and to keep fighting so that we will never have this happen again," he added. TRUMP’S PENTAGON SHAKE-UP REVIVES A PRESIDENTIAL POWER PLAY WITH A LONG HISTORY Hasan remains on military death row at Fort Leavenworth in Kansas. If carried out, his execution would be the first by the U.S. military since 1961. The military last used a firing squad for an execution in 1945. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell confirmed the decision on X, writing: "Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has recommended — and President Donald J. Trump has approved — death by U.S. Army firing squad for convicted terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan, the jihadist who opened fire on unarmed American soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009." ARMY IDENTIFIES 2 PILOTS KILLED IN APACHE HELICOPTER CRASH NEAR FORT HOOD DURING TRAINING EXERCISE Parnell added: "Judgment day for Hasan has finally come." Hasan’s execution is set to take place Dec. 3, 2026, at Fort Hood, Texas, where the attack took place, according to acting Army Secretary Adam Telle. title: Trump calls Democrat he pardoned a 'loser' for not switching parties
description: President Donald Trump slammed Democratic Rep. Henry Cuellar of Texas for not becoming a Republican after receiving a presidential pardon.
content: President Donald Trump lambasted incumbent Rep. Henry Cuellar, D-Texas, calling the congressman "a loser" on Wednesday, while criticizing the lawmaker for remaining a Democrat after receiving a presidential pardon. Trump pardoned Cuellar and his wife last year as the couple faced charges pertaining to bribery and money laundering. "In any event, I did the pardons, and made no deal, where a crooked politician would have, but I thought there would be a good chance that Cuellar, who was persecuted by Democrats because they didn’t like him, would have routinely gone over to the Republican Party — the people that saved him from years in prison," Trump wrote in a lengthy Truth Social post. HOUSE DEM BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT AS BROTHER FACES UP TO 10 YEARS IN PRISON IF CONVICTED Cuellar, who has served in the U.S. House of Representatives since 2005, is currently seeking re-election. "In any event, the man running against him, Tano Tijerina, is a STAR and, hopefully, will WIN! We call that payback for a disloyal and ungrateful person, a person whose life has been saved only to go back into the clutches of the people that tried so hard to destroy him. Henry Cuellar is a LOSER who, right now, should be serving a longterm jail sentence with his wife in a top level penitentiary," Trump declared in another part of the post. "Tano, a legendary Baseball Star, Great Athlete, respected County Judge, and fine person, will hopefully beat Cuellar so that people can show how bad it is when you are recognized and humiliated as being one of the most disloyal political people on Earth!" Trump wrote. "I am very proud of the fact that I didn’t make a deal with Cuellar, which I easily could have, but relied on his character, which turned out to be a faulty one." DEM REP HENRY CUELLAR REJECTS DSA AGENDA, SAYS SOCIALISTS ARE TRYING TO 'USE' DEMOCRATIC PARTY Trump issued the Truth Social post on Wednesday prior to delivering similar remarks during a rally in San Antonio, Texas. Tijerina declared in a Wednesday post on X, "Everyone in South Texas knows anything after Hello coming from Henry Cuellar is a lie. President Trump just confirmed that." Fox News Digital reached out to Cuellar's campaign for comment on Thursday. title: El-Sayed’s scathing Obama critique resurfaces ahead of joint campaign rally
description: Abdul El-Sayed once called Barack Obama's re-election "no victory" for progressives, complicating his upcoming campaign rally with the former president.
content: Abdul El-Sayed once accused President Barack Obama of failing to deliver on the progressive campaign promises that he outlined in the 2008 presidential campaign, calling his election to a second term a kind of compromise for progressives. "I realize that I have little hope because there has been less change," El-Sayed wrote in a 2012 op-ed for HuffPost. "But I have to say now what I’ve been holding in throughout his campaign and what I think all of us have to admit: Obama was not the right choice — he just wasn’t the wrong one." The resurfaced comments, published just days after the 2012 presidential election, complicate the political picture for El-Sayed as he prepares to campaign with Obama later this month. The comments also raise questions about what El-Sayed’s ideals for the Democratic Party would have looked like in 2012, highlighting his past satisfaction with one of the Democratic Party's most prominent figures. DEMS' LEFTWARD LURCH GETS LEGS AS EL-SAYED'S MICHIGAN SENATE VICTORY SPARKS PARTY DEBATE In particular, El-Sayed’s 2012 op-ed criticized Obama’s international record and strikes on Pakistan and Yemen, an underperforming economy and, in his view, little to no change in being accepted as a Muslim American. "I feel no more dignified, no more accepted as cops throughout the country have usurped my right to walk the streets freely without fearing unjustified interference. Inequality has accelerated and the divide between the haves and have-nots in our country has never been starker," El-Sayed wrote. "At home our economy continues to stagnate; its victims are so many of my peers who had also invested in ‘hope and change’ four years ago, who cannot find meaningful work." Notably, he did confirm that he had voted for Obama in 2008 and 2012. MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS LEADERS MUST ADDRESS ‘UNPAID DEBTS’ TO BLACK COMMUNITIES He also asserted that Obama’s record, as disappointing as it had seemed to him, was still better than the outlook of the failed Republican presidential nominee Mitt Romney. Even so, El-Sayed said Obama fell short of the ideal he, as a progressive, would have chosen for the country. "We really like the idea of Obama… let’s be clear, for progressives who care about peace, prosperity, civil liberties and the future of our country, Obama’ reelection last night was no victory. It was the rock we chose over the hard place," El-Sayed wrote. In recent months, as El-Sayed waged his Senate campaign in Michigan, Obama did not endorse the progressive, staying out of a primary between him and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich. Like Obama and other Democrats, El-Sayed has championed the growth of government as a way to address the country’s top issues. In addition to calling for lowering housing costs, he’s advocated for Medicare for all, opposes corporate tax carve-outs, and supports tuition-free access to higher education. Obama has still not issued an official endorsement even though he is slated to take the stage alongside El-Sayed on Oct. 24 for a rally with other Michigan Democrats. The former president highlighted the event in a post to social media on Monday. VAN JONES CALLS OUT EL-SAYED FOR ‘INSANE’ BELIEF THAT HE’S ‘SMARTER THAN BARACK OBAMA’ ON ISRAEL POLICY "Looking forward to being in Detroit on 10/24 to campaign for Jocelyn Benson, Abdul El-Sayed and Democrats up and down the ballot in Michigan," Obama wrote, referring to the Democratic candidate for governor in the Wolverine State. title: Teen wearing helmet camera kills worker at Polish school amid fears of copycat attacks
description: A 15-year-old wearing a helmet camera allegedly killed a school employee and wounded two others in Poland's second school stabbing attack in two days.
content: A 15-year-old boy wielding a knife and wearing a helmet-mounted camera attacked a Polish primary school he used to attend, allegedly killing one employee and wounding two others in the country's second school stabbing in two days. Authorities are investigating whether the attacks are connected to an online challenge encouraging teenagers to kill as many people as possible. Police said a 37-year-old woman who worked as a caretaker died in the Thursday morning attack at the school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of Warsaw. The school's head teacher, Krzysztof Ochmanski, was injured while subduing the teenager, officials said. Ochmanski told a radio station he heard a scream and ran into a hallway. MOTHER ACCUSED OF TRYING TO KILL DAUGHTERS IN FREEWAY CRASH AND KNIFE ATTACK AS SOLDIERS STEP IN "He wounded me with the blade of a rather long knife — he had three knives on him — and hit me with the handle," Ochmanski told the public broadcaster Polskie Radio RDC. "By then, I had managed to restrain him." The day before the latest attack, a 19-year-old allegedly wounded 10 people, including himself, at a school in Ostroleka, which is in northeastern Poland. Also this week, police arrested a 17-year-old in Sierpc in north-central Poland after authorities suspected he was planning a similar attack, Reuters reported. AMERICAN YOUTH RADICALIZED ONLINE, BUSTED IN SUSPECTED TERROR PLOTS AFTER HATING COUNTRY ON SOCIAL MEDIA "We fear a grim copycat phenomenon," Prime Minister Donald Tusk told an emergency meeting, according to Reuters. "We are facing an extraordinary situation. ... For the first time, we are dealing with a killer who wore a helmet-mounted camera, intending to film the knife attack." Tusk ordered police to visit schools every day to discourage further violence. title: FIRST ON FOX: FBI targets Ghana scam compound linked to nearly $10M in losses, more than 130 detained
description: The FBI's Operation Blackout led to over 130 arrests in Ghana and nearly $10 million in fraud losses tied to scam compounds targeting American seniors.
content: FIRST ON FOX: The FBI's global crackdown on overseas scam centers targeting Americans has led to more than 130 arrests or detentions in Ghana, with investigators identifying nearly $10 million in financial losses, Fox News Digital has learned. The latest takedown is part of Operation Blackout, the FBI's international campaign to dismantle scam compounds that prey on Americans, particularly seniors. According to information provided to Fox News Digital by the FBI, investigators have identified 89 fraud victims and seized more than 300 devices. The more than 130 individuals arrested or detained include suspected trafficking victims expected to be repatriated to their home countries, primarily Nigeria. EXCLUSIVE: FBI EXTRADITIONS SOAR AS PATEL RAMPS UP FOREIGN OUTREACH, VOWS 'NO SANCTUARY' FBI Director Kash Patel said the operation reflects the bureau's broader effort to dismantle international fraud networks at their source. "The FBI’s 'Operation Blackout' is our historic, global scam center fraud demolition operation that takes apart scam compounds all over the world targeting American citizens – primarily seniors," Patel said. "We are attacking this problem right at the source and blowing these compounds up, seizing billions of dollars, freeing thousands of trafficked workers, and protecting tens of thousands of Americans at risk of looking their hard-earned savings through these scams. Those who steal from Americans no longer have sanctuary – this FBI will find them and bring them to justice." BURMA APPROVES DEATH PENALTY FOR SCAMMERS MONTHS AFTER FBI'S $8 BILLION CRYPTO CRACKDOWN The Ghana operation follows an earlier warning from Patel that international scam networks were expanding beyond Southeast Asia and the Middle East into Africa. "That’s why you’re seeing the migration of these scam compounds to central and sub-Saharan Africa, which is where we are already pre-positioned to take them off," Patel told Fox News Digital in September. That same month, U.S. investigators helped authorities in Madagascar dismantle 13 scam centers linked to Chinese organized crime syndicates, processing more than 3,200 electronic devices, according to previous Fox News Digital reporting. FBI SEIZES RECORD-SETTING $8 BILLION IN CRYPTOCURRENCY AMID INTERCONTINENTAL 'SCAM COMPOUND' CRACKDOWN The FBI says Operation Blackout has seized roughly $17 billion globally, led to hundreds of arrests and freed thousands of trafficked workers. The bureau has not provided a detailed breakdown of the seized assets. The bureau also says it has warned more than 10,000 Americans about suspected scams, preventing an estimated $670 million in financial losses. The FBI previously reported that 77% of the more than 10,400 potential victims contacted through its Operation Level Up prevention initiative did not realize they were being scammed. title: ELI STEELE: France's schools are burning. White guilt is helping fan the flames
description: A burning school in Nantes and Palestinian flags in the streets reveal how White guilt fuels France's student protests, author and filmmaker Eli Steele argues
content: Editor's note: This op-ed is part of a series by Eli Steele exploring White guilt in America and the West. Steele is the director of the newly released documentary essay, "White Guilt." See the film at WhiteGuiltFilm.com. One of the most striking images of the riots that I saw sweeping France in recent days was that of a burning school in Nantes. The student movement in the streets around the school called itself a demand for education. I was scrolling through my X feed when I saw the image of a burning trash can outside Lycée Nelson Mandela. The flames spread to the walls of the building and into the glass entrance hall. There were still students in their classrooms and, thankfully, every one of them got out. When this school opened 12 years ago, its construction cost approximately €64 million, and it was touted as a beacon of hope and possibility for young people. Now the school has been shuttered for repairs, and its 1,700 students must learn from home for the time being. TRUMP, WALTZ LINK FRANCE RIOTS TO MASS IMMIGRATION AS THOUSANDS ARE ARRESTED And that is just one school. According to the education minister, 24 schools have been burned or ransacked since late September, and about 30,000 students won't see the inside of their classrooms for weeks. More than 6,500 people have been arrested, most of them minors. At least 215 students have been hurt, along with 85 teachers and staff. A 16-year-old lost the use of an eye. In La Ciotat, a physics teacher was sprayed in the face with gasoline and struck by a student from his own lycée while trying to put out a fire. Many media figures and nonprofit organizations like Amnesty International emphasized the students’ demands for better educational conditions and criticized the police response, while also acknowledging violence by some demonstrators. The demands were for more teachers, smaller classes and decent buildings. FRENCH PM REJECTS POLICE BRUTALITY CLAIMS AFTER TEENS SEVERELY INJURED IN PROTESTS: 'ACCIDENTS HAPPEN' In the more shocking videos that flowed from the streets of France out into the world, there were teachers who made a point of standing with the students in the streets. In some cases, parents and union members joined in. The mayor of Saint-Denis, Bally Bagayoko, stood with students who were blockading their own school and argued that violence can sometimes be legitimate, although he also said he opposed violence and called for de-escalation. No matter what France does, it loses. Every attempt by the 'oppressor system' to restore law and order becomes a new grievance for the oppressed. As one watches the footage of students swarming the streets, seemingly with impunity, one has to wonder how the civilization that gave the world Voltaire, Rousseau, Camus and the free public school arrived at a place where schools can burn amid a movement demanding better schools. FRANCE’S TEEN RIOTS TAKE EXPLOSIVE NEW TURN AS GOVERNMENT POINTS FINGER AT HARD LEFT In more ways than one, this is just an old story. A post-1960s story. What is happening in the streets of France is the latest iteration of the White guilt formula that has its roots in America. My father, Shelby Steele, has written about White guilt since the 1980s. For him, White guilt is not personal. It is not the guilt a person feels for something he did. Almost no Whites alive today owned slaves or ran colonies. How can one feel guilt for sins one did not commit? ELI STEELE: THE TERROR OF BEING CALLED RACIST IS CRUSHING FREE SPEECH IN AMERICA White guilt is collective guilt. The left has condemned all Whites for the sins of the West, from slavery and segregation to colonialism. It has made whiteness a symbol of historical evil that must be torn down. In doing so, it has created the terror of being called a racist or a colonialist and stripped of moral authority. To escape that terror, many Whites try to buy their way out. But only the "oppressed" can grant innocence, and so a bargain is struck. The "oppressed" sell victimhood for power. The "oppressor" buys innocence with deference, programs and lower expectations, and when the pressure is high enough, silence in the face of the match. Both sides get what they want, except the children, who are mere pawns. In the 1960s, people were oppressed. Today they are taught oppression. Most of these students never lived under colonialism. They have been taught that they still do. There is a difference between then and now. In the 1960s, people were oppressed. Today they are taught oppression. Most of these students never lived under colonialism. They have been taught that they still do. So, we should not be surprised, and yet it is still startling, that one of the main features of these protests has often been the Palestinian flag. A flag about Gaza has nothing to do with class sizes in Nantes, and yet it says everything about this movement. ANTI-ISRAEL GROUPS RALLY ACROSS US ON OCTOBER 7 ANNIVERSARY, CHANTING 'LONG LIVE THE INTIFADA' It does two things at once. First, it is an accusation. The students have been taught that Israel is the genocidal oppressor and the Palestinians their innocent victims. When they raise that flag, they are accusing France of being like Israel. Second, it is the claim that the students are the Palestinians in this situation and therefore they are the inheritors of the victimhood that the flag symbolizes. They have granted themselves innocence and moral legitimacy through victimhood. When the Saint-Denis mayor claims that violence can be legitimate, he is merely following the script of the Black Lives Matter activists who called the 2020 looting across America reparations. If he stood against the students and demanded the Western values of responsibility and accountability, he would be branded a traitor to the cause. After all, the victims must remain victims. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION The blockades have spread from the suburbs into Paris, all the way to the most elite lycées in France, and even private schools. These private school students come from comparatively privileged backgrounds and, judging from the photos of the barricades, many are White. White guilt rewards even the White students if they do one key thing: dissociate from the evil West. Their reward for allying with the oppressed is innocence. No matter what France does, it loses. Every attempt by the "oppressor system" to restore law and order becomes a new grievance for the oppressed. When one insists that a newish €64 million school is not a symbol of neglect, one is cast out with contempt as a racist. When a care worker at a Marseille bus stop told students not to smash the shelter and to go protest instead, a 15-year-old fired a flaming spray into her face. Afterward, she still called their cause "noble, legitimate." The "oppressed" will never give up the grievance, because under White guilt it is their only power. The White guilt elites only care about the innocence they gain from escaping the oppressor box via allyship. After all, they see their own nation as the oppressor. So the decline continues. It was the idea that a nation can defend itself, its laws and principles without first confessing to its past sins. White guilt makes that defense difficult, if not impossible. And that is what gives White guilt its power as the most destructive force in America and the West. It turns the people who built the school into the people who watch it burn and call it social justice. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM ELI STEELE

title: MLB proposes reverting schedule back to its old ways, but not without a wild postseason twist
description: Major League Baseball's proposal includes a 154-game season with weekly off-days and a best-of-seven Division Series starting as early as 2029.
content: With a second lockout this decade pending, Major League Baseball owners are coming up with creative ways to get on the baseball field as planned in 2027. The league announced the proposal of a 154-game season, which would knock out eight games of the 162-game slate that was implemented in 1961. Owners also proposed the Division Series, which has been a best-of-five since its introduction in 1995, to be a best-of-seven, but with a wild twist. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The highest seed in both the Wild Card and Division Series, owners proposed, would be given the ability to choose their opponents. "Returning to a 154-game schedule would allow us to introduce a weekly off-day, which is good for player health, while also creating a new national broadcast window to showcase our most exciting teams and players," MLB spokesman Glen Caplin said. "A shorter regular season unlocks making October even better for our fans -- with fewer weekday afternoon games, a longer Division Series and more opportunities to see the game’s best pitchers on the biggest stage. And allowing the top seeds to select their opponents in the first two rounds would create compelling storylines, intensify existing rivalries and create new ones." The opponent-choosing could perhaps be a reaction to this year's postseason format, in which the American League teams with the second- and third-best records, the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox, will not see the Championship Series. YANKEES LEGENDS DEREK JETER, ALEX RODRIGUEZ DELIVER BLUNT POST-MORTEM ON TEAM: 'SOMETHING HAS TO CHANGE' Under the current format, rather than reseeding , the top seed in each league is automatically slated to face the winner of the 4-5 seed matchup, and the No. 2 seed goes against the 3-6 seed winner. The top three seeds are given to the three division winners (with the top two getting a bye), in record order, while the 4-6 seeds are given to the best non-division winners, also in record order. Thus, despite the second-best record in the AL, the Yankees were the fourth seed. With the 154-game schedule, which wouldn't be implemented until 2029, all teams would be off on Mondays , except for a rare nationally televised game or a holiday, in which case they would then be off that Thursday. Minor League Baseball is off every Monday, which has apparently been well received , as it's normally paired with a Sunday day game. Each team would also have a scheduled split doubleheader against each of its division rivals during the season. MLB teams originally played 154 games until the 1960s. title: Nebraska Christian therapists sue city over ban on helping minors accept their biological sex
description: The Thomas More Society claims Lincoln, Nebraska's, ordinance threatens therapists with jail and fines for helping minors address unwanted same-sex attraction.
content: Christian counselors are suing Lincoln, Nebraska, over an ordinance they say threatens therapists with jail, fines and professional consequences for helping minors who want to become comfortable with their biological sex or address unwanted same-sex attraction, even after the Supreme Court struck down a similar Colorado restriction earlier this year. Thomas More Society Senior Counsel Matt Heffron told Fox News Digital in an interview Wednesday that Lincoln's ordinance amounts to government "viewpoint discrimination," arguing counselors are permitted to help minors move toward gender transition but are barred from counseling them toward accepting their biological sex when that is the client's stated goal. "The government allows certain type of speech in therapy sessions, and it disallows other sorts of speech or viewpoints," Heffron said. "It's just a confirmation of government viewpoint, government-favored speech over disfavored speech." FIRED SCHOOL COUNSELOR LOSES AGAIN AFTER FREE SPEECH FIGHT OVER GENDER-THEMED BOOKS IN HIS OFFICE Heffron said Lincoln's ordinance prevents counselors from helping minors who want to become comfortable with their biological sex or address unwanted same-sex attraction. He argued that a nearly identical Colorado restriction was found unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Chiles v. Salazar as viewpoint discrimination and that the 8th Circuit subsequently reached a similar conclusion in a case involving Kansas City. EXCLUSIVE: INDIANA SCHOOL COUNSELOR FIRED FOR SPEAKING OUT ON GENDER IDENTITY POLICY SETTLES LAWSUIT FOR $200K Heffron said a counselor accused of having those conversations could face an investigation and potentially a misdemeanor charge, a $500 fine, a $100 civil penalty and the loss of professional licenses or credentials. Heffron said the Thomas More Society repeatedly asked Lincoln to repeal the ordinance or agree not to enforce it. So, after the city declined to do so and stopped responding, the group filed suit. DETRANSITIONERS REVEAL HOW DOCTORS PUSHED THEM TOWARD LIFE-ALTERING TREATMENT AS TEENS "The stakes of this case, as far as minors are concerned, is that there are minors out there, and a fair number of them is what I hear, who are, perhaps faith-based or for other reasons, they are unhappy with same-sex attraction that they may be experiencing, or they're unhappy with what used to be called gender dysphoria," Heffron said. "And these minors go to a therapist, particularly a Catholic one like the one in this case, and they ask to be helped. It's awful. It's cruel to tell those children they can't be helped. "In fact, the only thing that the statute or that ordinance allows is it will allow that therapist to help guide them into gender transition with all of the evils that include surgeries and hormones and that sort of thing. They can guide them into that. And they can make them comfortable with their same-sex attraction." CATHOLIC NUNS CARING FOR DYING PATIENTS FIGHT NEW YORK TRANS RULE, FACE JAIL TIME In this instance, Heffron said the government is policing speech. title: Inside Trump’s deal to give American taxpayers a massive stake in new $6.6B submarine deal
description: President Donald Trump announced a 40% taxpayer stake in Anduril's Arsenal-2 shipyard subsidiary, adding government ownership to the $6.6 billion deal.
content: FIRST ON FOX — New details of President Donald Trump's multibillion-dollar deal with a defense tech giant reveal that the U.S. government will own 40% of the firm holding its new submarine shipyard without controlling it. But first, Anduril must prove it can build Navy-certified components before competing for future production work, a U.S. official told Fox News Digital. The government will use authorities under the Defense Production Act and the Pentagon's Industrial Base Fund to acquire its stake in a newly formed company holding the Arsenal-2 shipyard in Baltimore, Maryland. The official described it as a "minority, non-control" investment designed to secure "tangible ownership and long-term value for American taxpayers." Fox News Digital has asked the Department of War for the dollar value of the investment. The Navy's up-to-$2.9 billion agreement is not a guarantee of future submarine production work for Anduril. The money will flow through General Dynamics Electric Boat, the Navy's lead Virginia-class submarine builder, and calls for Anduril to fabricate and qualify four test components. Anduril is separately committing $3.7 billion of its own capital to the project. Anduril is not guaranteed future production work. Instead, Electric Boat will set the specifications and oversee testing, qualification and Navy certification. If Anduril meets those milestones, it will have "the opportunity, but not the entitlement, to compete for future production work," the official said. "The ultimate proof of our commitment to ensuring the shipyard's enduring success: American taxpayers will receive a 40 percent stake in the new shipyard," Trump said Tuesday at Sparrows Point shipyard. "We get 40 percent." STARTUPS BRING INNOVATION TO DEFENSE INDUSTRIAL BASE The size of the stake stands out even as the Trump administration has increasingly taken direct government interests in companies and projects it considers critical to national security. The administration has struck equity arrangements involving chipmaker Intel, rare earths producer MP Materials and other strategic industries. The arrangement is part of a broader $6.6 billion effort to expand production of Virginia-class attack submarines as the U.S. struggles to keep pace with China's vast shipbuilding capacities and the Navy falls behind on its production goal. Anduril is committing $3.7 billion of its own capital to build the facility and manufacturing capacity, while the Navy could spend up to $2.9 billion purchasing what it produces. The project is aimed at closing a persistent U.S. submarine production shortfall as China rapidly expands its naval and shipbuilding capacity. American shipyards are delivering roughly 1.3 Virginia-class attack submarines a year, short of the Navy's goal of two, which it does not expect to reach until around 2032. Once fully operational, Arsenal-2 is expected to add about 9 million labor hours annually to the submarine industrial base, increasing Virginia-class production capacity by roughly 15%, an administration official told reporters on a call before Trump’s remarks. LARGEST-EVER US STEEL PLANT IS COMING TO A KEY RED STATE AS TRUMP UNVEILS $15B INVESTMENT An industry official on the call emphasized that Anduril would finance the new production capacity itself while the government paid for the resulting output. "I wouldn't say that the government's paying us back. We feel the government [is] buying the results of what we're able to produce," the industry official said. The 40% government stake was not disclosed on the call, which included questions from reporters about how the project would be financed. The submarine crunch is part of a broader shipbuilding gap with China, whose vast commercial maritime industry also supports its rapidly expanding navy. China now accounts for more than half of global commercial shipbuilding output, while the U.S. accounts for only a fraction of 1%, giving Beijing an enormous industrial base that can also support military ship construction. Anduril plans to begin with critical components including torpedo tubes, which a senior administration official described as a current "gating component" slowing Virginia-class production. The company eventually plans to manufacture larger modules and sections of submarines at Arsenal-2.
