title: Jon Stewart tells Democrats to 'govern' and skip 'performative' Trump impeachment if they win
description: Jon Stewart warned Democrats against the "performative play" of impeaching President Donald Trump, urging the party to govern and fix the issues killing people now.
content: Comedian Jon Stewart urged Democrats not to pursue impeachment proceedings against President Donald Trump if they regain control of the House and Senate, arguing on his podcast that he doesn't want to see "performative" hearings. During a question-and-answer segment at the end of Stewart's "The Weekly Show" podcast, he was asked whether Democrats should seek to impeach Trump if they regain control of Congress in the midterm elections. He said he wanted to see Democrats make a full-scale effort to rebalance the economy, and said he didn't want to see performative hearings. "I don't want to see a f---ing five-act performative play of House hearings," Stewart said. "I just don't want to see it. I don't want to see everybody having the opportunity to pantomime accountability because you know they're actually not going to bring it." STEWART EXPECTS SCHUMER, JEFFRIES TO DISAPPOINT IF THE DEMS WIN BACK THE HOUSE AND SENATE "You want to do some investigations of some s---, that's great," he continued. "But on the triage list of what's wrong in this country, it is, 'I'm sorry, sir, you're going to have to stay in the waiting room because this guy just got shot, and it sounds to me like you just have a sore throat.' Like do the s--- that actually is killing people right now." Stewart added that he wanted Democrats to "govern." "You want to do some things that are ancillary, a little side project, you want to do the investigations as a hobby, knock yourself out. Fix s---," he said. "Jon Stewart is tapping into a real tension within the Democratic electorate," Lauryn Killian, CEO of Killian Campaigns, told Fox News Digital in a statement. "There will certainly be Democrats who want impeachment, particularly those who believe the Trump administration warrants aggressive congressional scrutiny." "But there is a meaningful difference between legitimate accountability and turning impeachment into another chapter of the anti-Trump resistance movement," she continued. "If Democrats take back Congress, voters will expect them to actually govern, not spend two years trying to undo the last election." HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY Killian said the smarter political strategy would be to look into "wrongdoing and pursue accountability where the facts warrant it, while focusing congressional energy on issues that actually affect Americans' lives: the economy, affordability, public safety and government competence." "Winning Congress would give Democrats an opportunity to demonstrate they can govern beyond simply being the opposition," she added. "If they turn that opportunity into another impeachment crusade, Republicans will have a very clear argument to make to voters: Democrats were given power to govern, and chose instead to keep fighting the last election." "Jon Stewart is saying what Democrats don't want to hear: voters want results, not revenge," Y. David Scharf, chair of government strategies and controversies at Morrison Cohen, told Fox News Digital. "If Democrats win Congress and spend the next two years trying to impeach Trump instead of lowering costs and fixing the economy, they'll be writing the Republican playbook for 2028." He described impeachment as "political theater." Democratic strategist James Carville and his podcast co-host Al Hunt also warned against impeachment on Tuesday. Carville and Hunt argued that impeachment would be a waste of time and Democrats should devote their energy to investigating the president instead. CARVILLE SAYS THE GOP IS BETTER THAN DEMOCRATS AT ONE KEY SKILL THE 2028 DEM NOMINEE WILL NEED "I’ll tell you one thing that I think Democrats should steer clear of, and that’s impeachment," Hunt said. "It’s not that Trump has not committed impeachable offenses, far worse than what he was accused of back in 2019 with Ukraine. I mean, he has. I mean, you could come up with a bill of particulars of, you know, a dozen at least. But you know something, James? It’s not going to happen, and it is a distraction." "It is a waste of energy," Hunt added. "Investigate, investigate, investigate. Don’t go on a mission that isn’t going to succeed." Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, who also served as White House chief of staff, urged fellow Democrats not to pursue impeachment during an interview on Sunday. "You’re never going to get an impeachment," he said. "Then, if you do that, you just basically prove all [of] Washington is what the American people think. It’s Disneyland on the Potomac. Deliver the change. Deliver a comprehensive ethics package that uses the investigations to then deliver change." The warnings came as Democrats held a polling advantage over Republicans heading into the final weeks before the midterm elections. FORMER CHICAGO MAYOR RAHM EMANUEL DECLARES AMERICA IS READY FOR A JEWISH PRESIDENT House race projections show Democrats winning 215 seats compared to 201 for the GOP, meaning Democrats would need to win at least three of the 19 remaining toss-up races to clinch a majority. Republicans would need to win at least 17 of those races. title: DeSantis fraud crackdown drives nearly $1B spending plunge after providers billed impossible hours

content: Florida's sweeping Medicaid fraud crackdown has helped drive a nearly $1 billion reduction in projected annual spending on behavioral therapy services alone, according to state officials, after investigators uncovered suspicious billing practices. Tallahassee’s internal crackdown — which included discoveries of providers billing Medicaid for more hours than there are in a day — comes amid heightened federal scrutiny of Medicaid fraud, including investigations and payment reviews involving Minnesota. The DeSantis administration said its approach aims to stop suspicious Medicaid claims before taxpayer dollars are paid out rather than trying to recover improper payments afterward. The strategy mirrors a call from HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to move away from traditional "pay-and-chase" models. "This year, we announced the most significant Medicaid integrity initiative in the history of our state, and today, I was proud to announce some of the results from these efforts," Gov. Ron DeSantis said in a news release. VANCE TURNS UP HEAT ON STATES WITH FEDERAL CASH THREAT OVER MEDICAID FRAUD CRACKDOWN More than 220 Medicaid providers have been terminated for fraud, waste or abuse, while more than 260 have faced payment restrictions or suspensions. The state has also referred more than 150 suspected fraud cases to the attorney general's office over the past year. Annual Medicaid spending on Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), a therapy commonly used for children with autism, had been projected to reach $3.86 billion but is now expected to total $2.88 billion in fiscal year 2026-27, according to the governor's office. Officials attributed the nearly $980 million reduction to a combination of fraud enforcement, managed care and utilization management efforts. Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) told Fox News Digital that its expanded monitoring uncovered providers billing Medicaid for services through every weekend and holiday for months, including instances in which providers billed for more than 24 hours of services in a single day. "Protecting Medicaid means protecting the people it was created to serve," AHCA Secretary Shevaun Harris said in a statement. title: Maryland man accused of girl's fatal shooting released from prison days before
description: Tyree Reynolds was released from prison just eight days before allegedly killing 12-year-old Khloe Ishway near a Baltimore youth football game.
content: A Maryland man charged with killing a 12-year-old girl while allegedly firing at two men near a youth football game was released from prison just eight days before the deadly shooting. Tyree Reynolds, 23, was released from state custody on Sept. 25, according to Fox 45 News, which cited the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (MDPSCS). Reynolds faces 30 criminal counts, including murder and attempted murder, in connection with Saturday's shooting at a youth football homecoming game at Leon Day Park in Baltimore. HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER During a Wednesday court appearance, Reynolds waived his bond hearing. POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD One of the men returned fire, striking Reynolds in the ankle. title: NFL calls prediction markets a form of sports gambling, urges courts to let states regulate
description: The National Football League filed an amicus brief arguing prediction markets like Kalshi should face state gambling regulation over game integrity.
content: The National Football League has made its stance clear on prediction markets. In an amicus brief on Thursday, the league said that the sites fall under the sports gambling umbrella and should similarly be regulated by states. "Billions of dollars will be bet on NFL games through prediction markets each season, and any delay from the Court will result in increasing consumer harm and risk to game integrity," the NFL wrote in the brief, via ESPN. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The league sent a letter to prediction market operators just before the start of the season saying they objected to markets like coaching and officiating decisions, injuries, and other markets that could be swayed by insider info. The league has yet to partner with predict markets but does have deals with official online sportsbooks. "The [Commodity Futures Trading] Commission's failure even to reference such objectionable contracts that the NFL identified months ago -- contracts that have been and continue to be listed as contracts by operators like Kalshi -- is deeply concerning and creates significant risks for the NFL's players, coaches, and officials and market participants," the league said. The CFTC, however, said that it has been in touch with the league as prediction markets have risen, but the league has not entered an agreement with them to work together. "Since day 1, the CFTC has engaged with the NFL regarding the agency’s rulemaking agenda and policy priorities. It’s unfortunate the NFL declined to sign an MOU with the CFTC which would’ve provided the league the ability to better discuss, cooperate, and exchange information with us to promote the integrity and resilience of prediction markets," Brooke Nethercott, public affairs director for the CFTC, told Fox News Digital. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER A CFTC source said that "just weeks ago, several senior NFL staff members notified senior CFTC staff that they were on the verge of commercial partnerships with several prediction market operators." Kalshi also took a shot at the NFL for not being "willing to share data and collaborate to protect game integrity." "Kalshi’s top priority is the integrity of its markets. That priority is reflected in the fact that other major sports league and integrity partner in the United States is partnering with Kalshi—including the MLB, NHL, USTA and others," Kalshi told Fox News Digital. "Contrary to the NFL’s statements, the CFTC is actively policing sports-related markets, which are now listed on nearly every US commodities exchange. The CFTC’s ongoing rulemaking addresses many of the NFL’s supposed concerns. And those rules sit atop the same comprehensive system of federal enforcement that protects trillions of dollars of transactions in US markets." A source from the CFTC also said that the NFL's brief "makes clear that it is most interested in regulating the regulator, not game integrity." "While this bullying tactic may work in the states, the CFTC will not be subject to regulatory capture, which is exactly why the federal framework established by Congress is the most effective way to regulate prediction markets," the source said. "This is not about the NFL opposing prediction markets..." an NFL source said. "If the CFTC were to adopt the same robust regulatory approach as states, this would be less of an issue... "For years, ever since sports betting on prediction markets started to gain traction, the NFL has been closely engaged in the relevant policy discussions. This is about protecting game integrity and consumers—just like legalized sports betting. There have already been billions of dollars in NFL wagers on prediction markets this season. Given this volume of trading and the uncertainty around it, it is critical for the Court to act as soon as possible. But it is unclear if the Commission has the resources or staff to adequately regulate sports betting." title: Anti-scam settings on iPhone, Pixel and Galaxy you should check
description: Apple's Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 27 can flag suspicious activity inside apps, but the setting is off by default and must be enabled.
content: Scammers have become very good at getting us to do the dirty work for them. Someone may pose as your bank, claim your account was hacked or tell you to move money before something terrible happens. The call or message might sound convincing enough that you willingly follow the instructions. That's one reason a new iOS 27 setting caught my attention. Apple calls it Impersonation Risk Detection, and it can help supported apps recognize signs that you may be acting under the influence of a scammer. If you use Android, keep reading. Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones have their own built-in scam protections, and some of them go after the problem from a different direction. I would check these settings no matter which of these phones is in your pocket. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better healthcare. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com SCAMMERS ARE BUYING GOOGLE ADS TO STEAL BANK LOGINS What Impersonation Risk Detection does on iPhone Apple introduced Impersonation Risk Detection with iOS 27. The feature is designed to help with active social engineering scams, where someone pressures or guides you into doing something yourself. That last part is important. Traditional security can help block malware or stop an unauthorized login. However, those defenses can have a harder time helping when you are the legitimate account holder and a scammer has convinced you to send money or change sensitive account information. When you perform certain sensitive actions inside a supported third-party app, that app can ask Apple for a risk assessment. Apple says examples may include making a payment or changing critical security information such as a password. The app then receives one of three risk levels: From there, the app decides how to respond. It might ask you to verify your identity, delay an action or display a warning before letting you continue. That could give you one more opportunity to stop when a scammer is rushing you through a payment or account change. How Apple's anti-scam feature decides something looks suspicious Impersonation Risk Detection looks at signals related to how you are using your device. Apple says those signals can include interaction patterns, timing, context and basic sensor data. Apple's privacy documentation gives some additional examples. Your iPhone may consider whether you are sharing your screen as well as the approximate number of recent phone calls or emails you have received. It can combine that assessment with certain Apple Account information, including recent App Store downloads and purchases. The goal is to look for unusual behavior that could suggest someone is guiding or pressuring you. However, there is an important limitation. This feature works only with third-party apps that support Apple's Impersonation Risk Detection system. Turning it on does not give every app on your iPhone automatic scam detection. What Apple can see when you use Impersonation Risk Detection Apple says it never analyzes the content of your Photos, Messages or Mail for this feature. The underlying device information used to create the assessment also stays protected from both Apple and the requesting app. There is still some information sharing you should understand before turning it on. Your iPhone creates an on-device assessment and sends that assessment, rather than the underlying device data, to Apple. Apple can then combine it with certain Apple Account activity to generate the final risk signals. Apple also learns the category of activity you were attempting, such as signing in or making a payment. Apple says it does not learn which app requested the signals or the content of what you were doing inside the app. The requesting app receives the resulting risk level. It does not receive the underlying information Apple used to produce it. Why the iPhone anti-scam setting is off by default Apple requires you to choose whether supported apps can request Impersonation Risk Detection signals. As a result, Share with App Developers starts out turned off. That means simply updating your iPhone to iOS 27 does not activate the protection. You need to go into Settings and enable it yourself. One warning from Apple really stands out. If somebody on the phone tells you to disable Impersonation Risk Detection, Apple says you might be dealing with a scammer. I would treat a request like that as a major red flag. Hang up and contact the company using a number or app you already trust. How to turn on Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 27 Here's how to check the setting on an iPhone running iOS 27: Apple says changes to this setting may take up to 24 hours to take effect. After you turn it on, you can return to Settings > Privacy & Security > Impersonation Risk Detection to see which apps have recently requested a risk assessment. You can also review why each app requested access and turn off access for individual apps. Samsung Galaxy phones have built-in scam and spam protection Samsung Galaxy phones also include tools designed to identify suspicious callers, although the exact features you see can vary by model, carrier and software version. On many Galaxy phones, Caller ID and spam protection is the main setting to check. Samsung uses technology from Hiya to identify suspected spam, scam and potential fraud calls, including numbers that aren't saved in your contacts. Samsung also offers a separate real-time Scam detection feature on some compatible Galaxy phones running One UI 8.5 or higher. Samsung says that feature can analyze calls for scam patterns and alert you with a tone or vibration. However, that option does not appear on every Galaxy phone, even when the device is running current software. Samsung began rolling out One UI 9 in September 2026, starting with the Galaxy S26 series after its debut on Samsung's newest foldables. Feature availability can still depend on your model, carrier and region. MAKE UNKNOWN CALLERS EXPLAIN WHY THEY'RE CALLING How to check scam and spam protection on Samsung Galaxy On a Samsung Galaxy, the exact options can vary by model, carrier and software version. To check the protection available on your phone: Samsung uses call-identification technology from Hiya to help identify suspected spam and scam callers, including numbers that aren't saved in your contacts. On compatible Galaxy phones, you may also see Call screening in the Phone app's settings. That feature can handle certain incoming calls before you answer. Samsung documents Call screening for compatible phones running One UI 8.5 or higher. Pixel owners have Scam Detection for calls Google takes a different approach on Pixel phones. Its Scam Detection feature can analyze a phone conversation in real time and warn you when the call shows patterns commonly associated with fraud. In the U.S., Google currently supports call Scam Detection on eligible Pixel 6 and later devices, with some model-specific exceptions. Pixel 9 and newer models use Gemini Nano on the device for scam detection during calls. Google says the feature works on the device. However, the company also warns that it cannot detect every scam, so a call that receives no warning should never automatically be considered safe. How to turn on call Scam Detection on Pixel To check it: Call Scam Detection requires you to opt in. If Google detects patterns associated with a scam during an eligible call, your Pixel can warn you while the conversation is still happening. That's useful because many scams become more convincing once a criminal gets you talking. The scammer can adjust the story based on what you say and keep applying pressure. Pixel can warn you about suspicious messages too Pixel owners have another protection worth checking. Scam Detection for chat messages can analyze new message notifications from supported apps and warn you when something looks suspicious. Google says this feature is available in the U.S. and several other countries. In the U.S., Scam Detection can also work with Gboard in select messaging apps and warn you as you begin responding to a suspicious message. Google expanded that capability with its September 2026 Pixel update. Unlike call Scam Detection, message Scam Detection is turned on by default. How to check message Scam Detection on Pixel Google says the feature runs in a secure, isolated environment. Your message content stays private and is not sent to Google unless you choose to share a message after receiving an alert. Google's September 2026 Pixel update is rolling out to supported Pixel devices running Android 17, so I would also make sure your Pixel has the latest available system update installed. SCAMMERS KNOW THE BEST TIME TO TEXT YOU Apple, Pixel and Galaxy approach scam detection differently These features aren't interchangeable, which is actually helpful. Apple's Impersonation Risk Detection focuses on signs that you may be getting manipulated while performing sensitive actions inside supported apps. Pixel can watch for scam patterns during calls and suspicious messages. Samsung can analyze supported calls for scam patterns. A scam may also move between several channels. Someone could text you first, get you on the phone and eventually convince you to open a legitimate banking app. Having protections at different points in that process gives your phone more opportunities to warn you before money or account information changes hands. What to do when your phone warns you about a possible scam Treat a scam warning as a reason to stop and verify what is happening. Don't keep following the caller's instructions while trying to decide whether the warning is right. Hang up if you're on a suspicious call. Then contact the bank, government agency or company directly using its official app, website or a phone number you already trust. The same goes for payment alerts. Open your financial institution's official app yourself and check the account. Don't use a phone number or link supplied by the person who contacted you. Also remember the reverse. No warning does not prove that a call, message or transaction is legitimate. Apple and Google both make clear that these systems can miss scams. Don't rely on your phone to catch every scam I like these features, but I would use them as another layer rather than my only protection. Scammers constantly change their scripts. They can spoof caller ID, impersonate companies you know and use personal information to make a fake story sound believable. If someone unexpectedly asks for a password, verification code or payment, slow down. A demand to transfer money to a "safe account" should also send up an immediate warning sign. Strong antivirus software can help protect against malicious links, phishing sites and malware that may appear alongside these scams. A password manager can also help by generating unique passwords and making it harder to reuse the same credentials across accounts. The phone can warn you. You still get the final say. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. Kurt's key takeaways What I find most interesting about these scam protections is how close they're getting to the moment when someone might actually lose money. For years, we've relied heavily on spam filters and caller warnings to keep criminals away. Now our phones are starting to look for what happens after the conversation begins. Apple's approach in iOS 27 could be especially useful when a scammer has already convinced you to open a legitimate app and take action yourself. Pixel can warn about suspicious calls and messages, while some compatible Galaxy phones can detect scam patterns during calls. Would you trust your phone enough to stop a payment after it warned you that you might be getting scammed, or would you still need to see more proof before changing course? title: Fire alarm disrupts Northwestern 'October 7' play based on massacre survivor testimony
description: A fire alarm forced evacuation during Northwestern University's "October 7" play featuring Hamas attack survivor testimony at Cahn Auditorium.
content: A fire alarm at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois interrupted a play recounting firsthand testimony from survivors of the Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attacks on Tuesday night, forcing an evacuation of the auditorium during a performance intended to commemorate the victims ahead of the massacre's third anniversary. The performance, titled "October 7," was hosted by Northwestern Hillel and featured verbatim testimony from survivors and eyewitnesses of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led terrorist attacks, which killed approximately 1,200 people in Israel and resulted in 251 hostages being taken into Gaza. Northwestern Media Relations told Fox News Digital that the fire alarm was activated during the performance at Cahn Auditorium, prompting an evacuation and a police investigation. "At approximately 8:12 p.m., a fire alarm at Cahn Auditorium was activated, which caused the evacuation of the building," a Northwestern Media Relations spokesperson said. "Upon a fire and police investigation, the building was determined safe, and guests invited back in. The event continued as planned and concluded at 9:45 p.m. The Northwestern University Police Department will continue their investigation." FORMER HAMAS HOSTAGE COUNTERS HASAN PIKER’S UT AUSTIN EVENT WITH HER STORY OF SURVIVAL A spokesperson for Campaign Against Antisemitism condemned the broader climate facing Jewish students on college campuses in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. "Campuses have become radicalized, resulting in the ostracization of Jewish students on campus," the spokesperson said. "Universities in the U.S. and throughout the West have to take a stand against antisemitism on campus. Administrative leave is a start, but if the allegations are borne out, the consequences need to be severe. That’s what zero tolerance means." The earliest widely circulated version of the video, which shows attendees evacuating the auditorium as a fire alarm sounded, was posted by Ann McElhinney, co-writer of the play "October 7," who said in her post that the alarm hit "even stronger because it’s already October 7 in Israel." ANTI-ISRAEL GROUPS RALLY ACROSS US ON OCTOBER 7 ANNIVERSARY, CHANTING 'LONG LIVE THE INTIFADA' McElhinney's co-author and husband, Phelim McAleer, called for those responsible to face consequences in an interview with the Jewish News Syndicate on Wednesday. "The people responsible must be found and prosecuted," McAleer said. "These people are demonic. Disrupting the truth, disrupting stories of tragedy and heroism. They should be ashamed of themselves. This just makes us all the more determined to take this play to every campus across America." The Coalition Against Antisemitism at Northwestern (CAAN) shared a statement on its website, saying that the timing of the alarm was particularly troubling because the 2023 massacre began amid rocket attacks and air raid sirens warning Israeli civilians to seek shelter. CAMPUS ANTISEMITISM EXTENDS BEYOND STUDENT PROTESTS AND INTO CLASSROOMS, ADL WARNS However, the group emphasized that investigators had not established whether the alarm was deliberately activated. It said the Cook County State's Attorney's Office Hate Crimes Unit was aware of the incident and called for authorities to examine whether antisemitic bias played a role. The incident came less than a year after Northwestern reached a $75 million agreement with the Trump administration to resolve federal civil rights investigations involving allegations of antisemitism and discrimination on campus. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Under the November 2025 agreement, Northwestern committed to strengthening protections for Jewish students, implementing mandatory antisemitism training and maintaining policies governing demonstrations and disruptions of university activities. The production, created by McAleer and McElhinney and directed by Jeff Gurner, previously ran off-Broadway and was performed at several universities, including Princeton, UCLA and Bowdoin College.

title: Grandmother of 12 holds plank for 5 hours in record-breaking feat
description: DonnaJean Wilde held an abdominal plank for five hours at the Huntsman World Senior Games, smashing her own Guinness world record by nearly 30 minutes.
content: A 61-year-old Canadian grandmother broke the female abdominal plank world record after holding the position for five hours. "To successfully achieve the record, the challenger’s forearms and toes must touch the ground at all times," Guinness states. "The remainder of the body must be lifted off the ground and be kept straight throughout," it also says. FITNESS EXPERT REVEALS 6 THINGS PEOPLE OVER 35 SHOULD DO AFTER WORKOUTS TO STAY STRONG "My elbows hurt pretty bad," Wilde said after completing the previous record. "I was so worried about losing my form, and I think that’s why my quads hurt because I was just really tense." She shared with Guinness that the first two hours "went by quickly," but the next two hours were much more difficult. "The last hour was the most challenging, just to stay focused and keep my form," she said. title: 'Generation COVID' explores the lasting toll of pandemic-era school closures
description: "Generation COVID" follows families across five states over four years, documenting how pandemic school closures still affect children's mental health.
content: EXCLUSIVE — An upcoming documentary examines the lasting toll of school closures six years after the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted classrooms nationwide. "Generation COVID," directed by Jennifer Sey and Andrew James, follows children and families across California, New York, Oregon, Colorado and Connecticut as they grapple with the effects of pandemic-era school closures and mandates. The documentary was filmed over more than four years. Sey told Fox News Digital that while much of the country appears ready to move on from the pandemic, many children are still struggling with its consequences. NEWSOM'S ADMISSION THAT INFAMOUS COVID MOVE WAS 'INSANE' TRIGGERS VIRAL FURY: 'WE ALL TOLD YOU' "It just feels to me like everyone wants to move on, and there’s really been no reckoning about what we did to young people in particular, and I wanted to create a record of that so that it never happens again," the XX-XY Athletics founder said. Sey said she hopes the film offers a visual record of how school closures affected American children and encourages a different approach during any future pandemic. LEGACY MEDIA IGNORES MASSIVE ANTHONY FAUCI DOCUMENT RELEASE ALLEGING HE MISLED CONGRESS ON COVID ORIGINS Sey lived in San Francisco for more than three decades and spoke out against the city’s prolonged shutdowns. "I ended up having to leave San Francisco. I lost a career I'd spent 30 years building, but I continued to speak out in defense of children." After leaving her job in 2022, Sey began producing the documentary. Sey, a former elite gymnast and national team member, said her commitment to protecting children is rooted in the abuse she experienced as a young athlete. She is also an Emmy-winning producer of "Athlete A," a documentary examining the Larry Nassar sexual abuse scandal and broader abuse within elite gymnastics. "I ended up being the first whistleblower about abuse in elite gymnastics all the way back in 2008. And I really did it because I wish someone had stood up for me when I was a child. And the abuse that I suffered, I really did not come out of it for two decades after having left the sport. And, so, when I see that children are suffering, I can't help myself. I will fight for them. "I feel like everyone's moved on, but the kids have not moved on." Sey said her experiences have shaped her determination to continue speaking out for children. HERE'S HOW THE CDC TRIED TO USE BAD SCIENCE TO CONVINCE PEOPLE TO WEAR MASKS DURING COVID She also argued that children were "dehumanized" during the pandemic. "They were models, they were cogs in a wheel, and we lost all sense of the humanity of a child, the need to be around other kids for their own development. We lost a sense of a child learning to speak that's 3 years old and being told if you don't wear a mask, you're going to kill your grandmother. Who tells a child that? Who tells a small child that? We inflicted fear." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The film examines the consequences of school closures and the censorship that Sey believes helped keep them in place. title: Caitlin Clark says she blocks social media hate and enjoys hostile WNBA road crowds
description: Caitlin Clark condemned racist rhetoric and discrimination while revealing she can't remember the last time she read a direct message on social media.
content: Caitlin Clark said she can't remember the last time she read a direct message on social media. She also enjoys getting booed by opposing fans. Apparently, WNBA players can be the subject of an enormous amount of attention without volunteering to spend their entire day focusing on the worst aspects of it. CAITLIN CLARK'S LOWEST-RATED PLAYOFF GAME STILL OUTDREW EVERY NON-FEVER FIRST-ROUND BROADCAST During her season-ending news conference Thursday, Clark condemned "racist rhetoric" and "discrimination," praised passionate crowds and explained how she tries to manage the noise surrounding her. It was a refreshingly sane approach to a subject that has produced far too much nonsense around the WNBA. Some players, and plenty of people covering them, should take notice. The discussion began with a question about Kelsey Mitchell's comments on the attention that comes with being Clark's teammate. Clark said seeing teammates go through that upset her. She rejected people using her name to promote racism or discrimination. "That's never been something I've stood for," Clark said. "For those of you that know me, that's not what I'm about. It's not how I was raised." While Clark acknowledged that people shouldn't be sending nasty messages on social media, she said she tries to avoid reading them. "I couldn't tell you the last time I read a direct message," Clark said. "I just try to block out the noise the best I can." There is a useful lesson in that. Condemning someone else's behavior doesn't require giving that person unlimited access to your attention. Online trolls seek attention, which is why they send vile messages in the first place. Spending your time thinking about and reacting to those comments gives the trolls exactly what they want. Caitlin Clark welcomes the boos Clark recalled Golden State fans booing her every time she touched the ball. "I like that. I thought that was great and fun," she said. Imagine that. A professional athlete enjoying an opposing crowd trying to throw her off her game. "You can boo. You can yell at people," Clark said. She even brought up watching the Yankees in the playoffs. "Man, those Yankee fans are brutal," she said with a smile. Anyone expecting a visiting star to receive a warm welcome in every building should probably spend a little more time watching sports. Those fans want to see their team win, and opponents are just standing in the way. The atmosphere is part of what makes a road win satisfying. Enjoying it doesn't mean accepting everything fans say or do, as Clark made clear. "I think there's certainly a line and that can't be crossed," she said, adding that "there's certain rhetoric that's just not okay." Where that line falls became a major subject of debate during the playoffs, when Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson confronted a Fever fan. "You don’t step towards me. You never should step and point at me," Wilson said afterward. Prime Video's broadcasters defended Wilson without knowing what the fan had said. Apparently, her reaction was all the evidence they needed. But as OutKick reported, both the Fever and WNBA found no fan-conduct violation. DAN DAKICH BLASTS A'JA WILSON OVER FAN INCIDENT IN PLAYOFF LOSS TO THE FEVER Clark was discussing her own experiences Thursday. Still, her willingness to enjoy a hostile road crowd offers a useful perspective in a league where interactions with spectators have become such a consuming subject. This wasn't the first time an opposing player accused a Fever fan of inappropriate conduct despite the team and league finding no such evidence. Fever general manager Amber Cox said no fans had been removed for misconduct at home this season. Yet, left-wing podcaster Sarah Spain said Cox was being "defensive." Well, wouldn't you be defensive if people kept trashing your fans and you had information that contradicted what they were saying? WNBA could use more focus on the positive Clark's answer showed how easily a person can condemn misconduct while also expressing appreciation for fans. Those positions fit together just fine. "For the real fans that do show up and do support and do respect, I applaud you," she said. "And there are a lot of you. And that's not just here in Indianapolis. That's across the league." title: Minnesota father convicted of killing teenage son whose remains were found in landfill
description: Jordan Dupree Collins Sr. was convicted of second-degree murder after his teen son's remains were recovered from an Elk River landfill.
content: A Minnesota man was found guilty of killing his teenage son, whose remains were found in a landfill after he vanished for over a month. Jordan Dupree Collins Sr., who represented himself during his trial, was convicted Wednesday of second-degree murder for killing his 16-year-old son, Jordan "Manny" Collins. Ashley Berry, the boy's mother, has previously described Manny as someone who was "always helping others, spreading kindness, and lifting up those around him." "Manny should still be here today," Anoka County Sheriff Brad Wise said in a statement. "No verdict can remove the pain his loved ones feel, but we hope this decision provides some measure of justice. Our thoughts remain with Manny’s family, especially his mother, Ashley, as they continue to grieve and remember him." MINNESOTA MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING MALL OF AMERICA ATTACK, PLEDGING ALLEGIANCE TO ISIS: FBI According to the criminal complaint, the teen went to his father's apartment in May 2025 and was never heard from again. His mother and his girlfriend both told police they last communicated with him in the early morning hours of May 8, 2025. Collins told Manny's mother that the 16-year-old left his Columbia Heights apartment on the afternoon of May 8 to go to St. Paul to visit his girlfriend and grandmother. The girlfriend later told authorities that Manny never indicated he was coming to visit during their last video call together. On May 15, 2025, police obtained a search warrant and descended on Collins' apartment, where they found "items with apparent blood staining in garbage bags in a living room closet." MAN KILLS WIFE AND 7-YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER BEFORE TAKING OWN LIFE AT MINNESOTA HOME DAYCARE; FOURTH VICTIM FOUND Police said DNA testing confirmed that the blood found in the apartment belonged to Manny. title: Nicolas Maduro and wife Cilia Flores face new charge of conspiracy to torture Americans
description: Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores face conspiracy to torture charges involving electric shock, asphyxiation and rape of detainees, including U.S. citizens.
content: The U.S, District Court for the Southern District of New York charged former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with conspiracy to commit torture to Americans and others to stay in power, according to a superseding indictment filed Thursday. Maduro's government, according to the indictment, "presided over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens." The torture included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims' families, including children," the indictment read. The charge carries a maximum of life imprisonment if any of the alleged torture resulted in death, and a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison if not. FAMILIES SUE MADURO IN US, ACCUSE EX-PRESIDENT OF DIRECTING POLICE UNIT TIED TO EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLINGS In one incident, the indictment alleges that a U.S. detainee in Venezuela was beaten for days and doused with a noxious liquid that made him vomit, which Venezuelan officers then allegedly made him eat. WAR CRIMES COURT TURNS 'BLIND EYE' TO TOP WORLD THREATS WHILE TARGETING AMERICANS, TRUMP ADMIN ACCUSES The detainee, who was allegedly accused of plotting to kill Maduro, was also subjected to electric shock torture to his torso and genitals and injected with a substance that induced seizures. "On one occasion, CC-3 personally observed Victim-7 being electrocuted; laughed at and taunted Victim-7 during the electric shock; and directed other DGCIM officers in connection with the electric shock," the indictment read. MADURO'S ALLEGED 'BAG MAN' ALEX SAAB ARRESTED LESS THAN 3 YEARS AFTER BIDEN PARDON: REPORT After spending eight-and-a-half months at Boleíta Norte prison in Venezuela, the detainee was released and returned to the U.S. in October 2022, according to the indictment. The indictment alleges Maduro and Flores "inflicted severe physical and mental pain and suffering to repress and punish political opposition, silence dissent and perceived dissent, preserve and protect the power and authority of the members of the conspiracy, and intimidate, harass, and neutralize their opponents, including through kidnappings." The pair, who face numerous other charges, were arrested in Venezuela in January during Operation Absolute Resolve. Maduro was originally charged with narco-terrorism conspiracy, cocaine importation conspiracy, possession of machine guns and destructive devices, and conspiracy to possess machine guns and destructive devices in a 2011 indictment that President Donald Trump's Department of Justice unsealed in 2020. Flores was then charged in a superseding indictment in January with cocaine importation conspiracy, possession of machine guns and destructive devices, and conspiracy to possess machine guns and destructive devices. They have pleaded not guilty and a trial is scheduled for June 2027. EXCLUSIVE: FBI EXTRADITIONS SOAR AS PATEL RAMPS UP FOREIGN OUTREACH, VOWS 'NO SANCTUARY' Flores appeared in court Thursday for a bond hearing on her motion for release from jail. Her lawyers were requesting home confinement with GPS tracking, citing a heart condition and arguing she does not pose a danger to the community. U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein denied the request. The U.S. government opposes her release, arguing she poses a flight risk and danger to the public. Flores' attorneys say she denies the allegations against her, and both she and Maduro have filed motions to dismiss on diplomatic immunity grounds. title: Caleb Flynn's mistress avoided charges despite murder texts as her attorney reveals why
description: Alleigha Botner's attorney tells why she wasn't charged in Ashley Flynn's murder despite 107,000 messages exchanged with Caleb Flynn during their affair.
content: The attorney for Caleb Flynn's former mistress is pushing back against suspicions that she helped plot the murder of the former "American Idol" contestant's wife, telling Fox News Digital that disturbing messages about wanting Ashley Flynn dead were not evidence that his client took part in the Tipp City, Ohio, killing. Dayton defense attorney Nick Gounaris, who represents Alleigha Botner, said investigators reviewed her messages with Flynn, cellphone records and surveillance footage as they worked to determine whether she had any involvement in the crime. Botner's secret affair with Flynn became a central part of his trial, where jurors heard exchanges about killing his wife, including a suggestion to hire someone to do it. Flynn was ultimately convicted on Sept. 29 of murdering Ashley and sentenced on Monday to life in prison without the possibility of parole. 'AMERICAN IDOL' ALUM CALEB FLYNN WEEPS AS DAUGHTERS ASK HIM WHY HE KILLED THEIR MOTHER, VOW NOT TO VISIT HIM "I think the reason that she wasn't charged is just because you say something, you still have to show that that person was somehow involved," Gounaris told Fox News Digital. "The evidence that was reviewed, the evidence that was developed, the evidence that they secured through all of these different avenues did not suggest anything that involved Alleigha Botner in the death of Ashley Flynn." Gounaris said he initially worried Botner could become a target of the investigation after she spoke to police without an attorney and was not entirely forthcoming about her relationship with Flynn. WATCH: ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ ALUM CALEB FLYNN TELLS COPS FLAG-CARRYING STRANGER CAME TO DOOR BEFORE WIFE’S SHOOTING Investigators had begun uncovering the affair while examining the Feb. 16 shooting at the couple's Tipp City home, where prosecutors said Flynn shot his wife twice in the back of the head before staging a break-in. Botner eventually acknowledged the relationship, but her family became concerned about her legal exposure and contacted Gounaris, who began speaking with investigators to determine whether she was a witness or potential suspect. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN "As a defense attorney, my first reaction is, wait a minute, we've got to be very careful ... we've got to be concerned that she might be a target here," Gounaris said. "So ... let me bring her into the office. Let's protect her. Let me now be her advocate. Let me speak with investigators and let me then determine, you know, where this is going." As more evidence emerged, Gounaris said, investigators increasingly treated Botner as a witness, and nothing they uncovered suggested she participated in Ashley's murder. DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER Jurors heard that Flynn and Botner exchanged over 107,000 messages during their affair, including conversations in which Flynn repeatedly expressed a desire to kill his wife. In one message, Flynn said he had stayed awake thinking of ways to kill Ashley without going to jail. WATCH: Caleb Flynn had ominous response when mistress said ‘I want to kill her’ Gounaris acknowledged the exchanges were ugly but argued that messages discussing Ashley's death represented only a small fraction of their conversations and largely occurred months before the killing. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN Some of the most troubling exchanges came just hours before Ashley was killed, when Flynn told Botner, "It's happening," and she responded, "You're about to be free." Gounaris said the messages were about Flynn's plans to divorce his wife, explaining that the pair had stopped communicating for roughly a month after Botner ended their relationship in January because Flynn repeatedly failed to leave Ashley. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN Flynn contacted her again shortly before the murder, claiming he was finally preparing to seek a divorce and disclose the affair to church leadership, Gounaris explained. The renewed conversations included roughly 250 messages discussing divorce, custody, employment and what would happen if Flynn left his marriage, he said. Botner even researched divorce-related questions using ChatGPT and sent Flynn screenshots. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN "All of the communications that are contemporaneous with the time that he kills his wife all the way up to 12:45 in that morning – about an hour and 45 minutes ... before he calls 911 – are all about divorce," Gounaris said. He maintained that Botner believed Flynn was preparing to leave his wife, not kill her, an explanation she also gave during her testimony. But questions about Botner's conduct extended beyond the messages themselves. During the trial, jurors heard about efforts to conceal the affair, including discussions about deleting communications and replacing phones. Gounaris argued those conversations were motivated by concerns that the relationship could jeopardize Flynn's chances of gaining custody of his daughters during a divorce. "What are they covering up?" Gounaris asked. "They're covering up what the relationship was. So she was explaining to him, 'You need to go get a new phone, you need to delete this app. We ... have not had these conversations.'" Flynn worked for his father-in-law's company, had two daughters and held a prominent role at his church. Gounaris believes the prospect of losing those things may have pushed him toward a fatal decision. "He had a girlfriend. He liked having a girlfriend. He had a wife. title: Dem House hopeful alleges she was brutally attacked during 2 am campaign errand
description: Bernadette Greene-Placentia says she was knocked unconscious and sexually assaulted while repairing her campaign signs in Sun City, Arizona.
content: Arizona Democratic congressional candidate Bernadette Greene-Placentia said she was knocked unconscious and raped during an overnight encounter with two attackers in August while trying to repair a damaged campaign sign. Greene-Placentia told Phoenix New Times that she was walking through a parking lot in Sun City shortly after 2 a.m. on Aug. 14 to repair a damaged campaign sign when someone struck her in the head, knocking her unconscious. Greene-Placentia said she regained consciousness to find a man raping her and kicked at a second man who approached her, according to the Phoenix New Times. A public information officer with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital that a police report was filed on Aug. 31. SCANDALS, SOCIALISTS AND TRUMP ROIL PRIMARIES, SEND INCUMBENTS PACKING AT NEAR-RECORD PACE "Detectives advised it is still an ongoing investigation, and we cannot comment on the investigation at this time," said the officer. Greene-Placentia initially told investigators that one of her attackers used a derogatory remark she interpreted as "Democratic b----," according to the Phoenix New Times, but told The New York Times on Wednesday that she could not be sure what she had heard. Greene-Placentia told Phoenix New Times she suffered extensive bruising and vaginal bleeding for three days after the alleged assault and believed she may have sustained a concussion. Greene-Placentia missed a campaign event and was out of contact with her staff for about two days following the alleged assault, according to The New York Times. She later told campaign aides and her husband what happened before reporting it to police on Aug. 31, saying she initially felt embarrassed and wanted to forget the incident. She ultimately decided to go public to encourage other sexual assault survivors to speak out. "I never imagined I would have to tell this story, but I know I am far from the only woman who has lived through something like this," Greene-Placentia said in a statement released Wednesday. "Too many survivors carry these experiences silently. I am speaking out because I want them to know they are seen, they are heard and they are not alone." DEMOCRATS TARGETING 12 ADDITIONAL RED DISTRICTS IN MIDTERMS PUSH TO RETAKE HOUSE "What happened will not silence me. I’m going to keep showing up, keep fighting for this community, and keep working every day to bring real representation to the people of CD8," she added. Greene-Placentia received support from both Republicans and Democrats, including her Republican opponent, Rep. Abe Hamadeh, who called for authorities to investigate the alleged attack. "I have read the disturbing story and call upon authorities to investigate these serious allegations thoroughly, including finding all possible camera footage of the time and place in order to prosecute the crime to the fullest extent of the law. No American should become a victim of a crime in their own community," Hamadeh said in a statement. "This was a cruel and cowardly attack, and it has no place in Arizona. No one should have to fear for their safety, or the safety of the people they love, while serving their community," Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs' office said in a statement to the Phoenix New Times. title: Mamdani doubles down on anti-Israel Oct 7 statement after backlash
description: Zohran Mamdani doubled down on his accusation that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza, refusing to walk back remarks that sparked bipartisan backlash.
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani doubled down on his October 7 statement accusing Israel of carrying out a "genocide" in Gaza on Thursday. Mamdani made the statement while speaking to the press at an unrelated event on Thursday. Reporters asked him about anger in the Jewish community over his statement on the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 terrorist attacks that briefly recognized that day's atrocities before accusing Israel of carrying out genocide against Palestinians. "Do you believe you made any missteps that inflamed tensions in this very difficult moment for a lot of New Yorkers?" a reporter asked. ISRAEL AMB TORCHES MAMDANI OCT 7 POST: 'LIKE TURNING SEPTEMBER 11 INTO A DAY OF MOURNING FOR AL-QAEDA' "I believe that there must be room to mourn every single life," Mamdani responded. "There must be room to mourn the lives of the more than 1,100 that Hamas killed three years ago; there must be room to mourn the 74,000 Palestinians that the Israeli government has killed since." "There must be room to reckon with the ways in which so many New Yorkers' lives have been shattered," he continued, noting that the vigil he attended highlighted testimonies from those killed "either on the day or the genocide since." WEAPONIZING THE CHARGE OF GENOCIDE FUELS AN INCREASINGLY DANGEROUS ANTISEMITISM Mamdani went on to accuse the Israeli government of using the October 7 massacre as "a justification for a genocide." The mayor also repeatedly declined to say that he would change anything about the statements he made on Wednesday, either in his formal statement or during his attendance at the October 7 vigil. He also justified his greater emphasis on Palestinian deaths, arguing that "this is something that is ongoing, as opposed to something that simply happened three years ago." In his statement on Wednesday, Mamdani condemned Hamas’ attack as a "horrific war crime" while also characterizing Israel’s subsequent military operation as a genocide. NETANYAHU ACCUSES MAMDANI OF 'FOMENTING HATE,' SAYS RHETORIC IS MAKING NEW YORK JEWS AFRAID "The suffering did not begin nor end that day," he wrote. "It instead continued through the Israeli government’s devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza in which it has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians — including more than 21,000 children." Israel has rejected accusations that it is committing genocide in Gaza, saying its military targets Hamas and other terrorist groups while seeking to minimize civilian casualties. The mayor's statement sparked bipartisan backlash, with Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., calling it "egregious and insulting." This is a day that should just be focused on what was by all agreement a horrific terror attack," Goldman, who is Jewish, told Politico. "What the mayor’s statement did today was to blame Israelis for the attack that they suffered three years ago. Regardless of what you actually think of the conflict and what’s happened either since or before, there’s no excuse for victim blaming."

title: Five important college football questions that will be answered after this weekend's slate
description: Alabama's 5-0 Crimson Tide host second-ranked Georgia in Bryant Denny Stadium as Kalen DeBoer looks to prove the program is back among the elite.
content: Don't look now, college football fans, but this weekend will officially mark the halfway point of the 2026 regular season. It's hard to believe we are already six games into this thing but time flies when you're having fun, I suppose. While this coming weekend won't exactly be a "separation Saturday" situation, several questions will be answered in part because of the circumstances surrounding the games as well as the quantity of data points we now have at our disposal. Half a season is usually about when you start to find out who teams really are for the year. Frauds get exposed and championship contenders start to rise to the top and prove their worth, and 2026 is no different. So, indulge me, as I look at five important questions from the college football season that will be answered after the clock strikes midnight on Saturday. 1. Is Alabama all the way back? When Kalen DeBoer arrived in Tuscaloosa by way of Seattle to take the Crimson Tide head coaching position, the general consensus was that the good times would continue to roll at Bama. ALABAMA PROVIDES UPDATE FOR SHOWDOWN AGAINST GEORGIA, AS SCHOOL, SEC AND TRUMP PLAN FOR HURRICANE ISAIAS While the Tide have been a really good program under DeBoer, averaging ten wins and recruiting at an elite level in his two seasons at the helm, they've failed to reach the same heights they did the previous decade and a half during Saban's reign. Alabama is off to a 5-0 start, their best since 2022, but questions are still lingering about the ceiling of this team. They have an impressive road win over a top-25 Mississippi State team and their offense looks night unstoppable, however they also survived a scare at home against an average-at-best Florida State team in a game where their defense was a bit leaky. If the Tide can knock off second-ranked Georgia this weekend in Bryant Denny Stadium, it will go a long way in signifying the program is trending back towards the elite status it held when Saban roamed the sidelines. A loss would probably mean the big crimson machine still needs a tune up. College football can be such a fickle mistress sometimes. 2. Did Missouri crack the code to stopping Florida's offense? Last weekend, the Florida Gators carried a top-ten ranking as well as a top-five offense into Columbia, Missouri. They left the Show Me State licking their wounds and taking a tumble, both in the national rankings and the offensive metrics. FLORIDA DROPS IMPRESSIVE OFFENSIVE PERFORMANCE TO PULL OFF MASSIVE WIN OVER NO. 4 OLE MISS Jadan Baugh, Florida's Heisman hopeful running back, was held under 100 yards for the first time this season, as the Gators could only muster a measly 42 yards on the ground for the day. Did the Tigers crack the code to stopping Florida's high-powered offense? The Gators welcome South Carolina to The Swamp this weekend, and while no one will mistake the Gamecocks for the '85 Bears, they have the talent along the defensive line of scrimmage to cause Florida some headaches. If Florida comes out and struggles to move the football against an average South Carolina defense, it could mean the book is out on how to contain offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner's scheme. 3. Is this the end of the road for Shane Beamer at South Carolina? Speaking of those Gamecocks, there might not be a coach in America with a hotter seat than South Carolina head man Shane Beamer. I spoke to multiple people who are fairly plugged into the football program who told me a loss at home against Kentucky might have sealed Beamer's fate. However, I was shocked to wake up Sunday morning and still see him employed, but I don't think it was because I was fed bad intel. A loss in The Swamp to Florida would drop the Gamecocks to 2-4 on the season, and a particularly ugly loss might send Beamer to the nearest executive airport to find his own way home. There's too much talent on this South Carolina roster for Beamer to keep his job at 2-4, and if the wheels were already turning in terms of replacing him, I don't see a world where he survives this weekend. The Gamecocks will likely get potential first-round pick Dylan Stewart back to bolster their pass rush, and while that might help things on the field, I doubt it does anything for the embattled head coach's chances off the field. Saturday in The Swamp might be Beamer's swan song, win or lose. 4. Is Indiana a true contender or just a pretender? The Indiana Hoosiers had a historic season in 2025, compiling a 16-0 record and absolutely buzzsawing their way through a loaded College Football Playoff field en route to the school's first ever national championship. Unfortunately, that was last year, and the 2026 version of the Hoosiers looks nothing like their 2025 counterparts. In fairness, Indiana has played virtually no one of note, save for a nail-biter against a better-than-we-thought Northwestern squad. Saturday's game against Nebraska should help us answer the question of whether the Hoosiers are really deserving of that number next to their name, or if they're ranked where they are solely due to last year's success. Laugh all you want, but the Huskers should offer a stiff test to Indiana, particularly their defense. Nebraska's offense looks as good as it has in a while, and they steamrolled a pair of conference opponents prior to their upcoming matchup with the defending champs. If the Hoosiers struggle in Lincoln on Saturday, it might mean coach Curt Cignetti's squad just isn't ready to repeat as national champions this year. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! 5. Is UCLA's hot start to 2026 legit or smoke and mirrors? The UCLA Bruins are ranked in the top-25 of the AP Poll. Just let that sink in for a little bit, because in today's day and age, the Bruins being anywhere close to the top-25 in football is a rarity. That all seems to be changing under first year coach Bob Chesney, who I told you all to keep an eye on before the season even started. The Bruins are fresh off a dismantling of Maryland on the road, and while the Terrapins aren't exactly a juggernaut, hanging 54 points on a conference opponent on the road is an impressive feat regardless. Sure, UCLA hasn't played a particularly noteworthy schedule so far this season, that will all change when the Bruins travel to Autzen Stadium this weekend to take on Oregon. The Ducks stumbled to start the season, but have rebounded quite nicely and look to be back on track towards winning the Big Ten. A signature win in Eugene would do wonders for UCLA's recruiting class, which is already in a great spot just a few months out from signing day, and it could put the Bruins in the driver's seat to win the Big Ten title.

title: How Elon Musk got back in Trump's orbit after nuclear fallout, insiders reveal: 'Water under the bridge'
description: Elon Musk is set to receive the National Medal of Science from Trump after their bitter 2025 feud over government spending and DOGE's mission.
content: EXCLUSIVE: As Elon Musk prepares to receive a prestigious honor from President Donald Trump Thursday afternoon, several sources familiar with the pair's relationship say the trillionaire is back in the administration's fold after last year's nasty blowup between the pair. "Water under the bridge," one former administration official told Fox News Digital when about to classify the falling out and subsequent rekindling of the pair's relationship. Musk had a meteoric rise within the MAGA movement during the 2024 presidential election and, after Trump was re-elected, joined the administration to lead massive federal government cuts under the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). During that time, he had a chummy relationship with Trump, who presented him with a ceremonial golden key to the White House during an Oval Office celebration. In May 2025, Musk left the government after leading DOGE for four months. The CEO of Tesla, SpaceX and X (formerly Twitter) was reportedly at odds with Trump over the amount of government spending tied to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which he viewed as antithetical to DOGE's effort to reduce wasteful spending in a bloated federal government. NEW BOOK ON ELON MUSK EXAMINES THE BILLIONAIRE’S MIND, MOTIVATION AND MAKING LIFE MULTI-PLANETARY On June 3, 2025, Musk took to the social media platform he owns to rail against the bill, describing it as a "disgusting abomination." "KILL THE BILL," Musk wrote on X the following day. Trump fired back in a social media post of his own, saying Musk had been "wearing thin" on him, and that Musk went "CRAZY" after Trump rolled back what the administration described as a Biden-era "backdoor electric vehicle mandate." Musk then claimed that Trump would not have won the 2024 election without his financial support and accused him of "ingratitude." Through his America PAC, Musk helped fund the campaigns of Trump and other Republicans to the tune of nearly $300 million. Musk later accused Trump of being in the infamous Epstein files, though he never provided proof for the claim. TRUMP SAYS MICHAEL COHEN WAS 'WEAPONIZED' BY MAINSTREAM MEDIA IN SURPRISE RADIO REUNION At that point, a former White House official told Fox News Digital that Musk was completely removed from the White House fold. "He wasn’t in the office at all," the source said. Musk had previously occupied a space in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building, alongside other White House staff. But, the former official said it's in Trump's nature to rekindle old relationships, regardless of how nasty the dustup. In fact, Trump and his longtime personal attorney, Michael Cohen, just revived their old friendship in September, despite a major falling out and Cohen's testimony against Trump during the 2024 "hush money" trial involving adult entertainer Stormy Daniels. A third source familiar with the matter said Musk began getting back into Trump's good graces earlier this year, while a current administration official disputed the characterization that Musk was fully out of the White House fold in the first place. The administration official said that despite the fallout, Musk has been seen recently at the White House, in part because he's making good on promises to financially support Republican candidates in the 2026 midterm elections. WHAT'S ON THE MENU FOR TRUMP'S STATE DINNER WITH CHINA'S XI? ONE AMERICAN STAPLE IS NOTABLY MISSING Musk has made several high-profile appearances at the White House in recent weeks. He was at the America.gov launch in late September, alongside engineers from the National Design Studio who built the AI-powered website. He appeared again during Trump's state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping last month, and was seated at the president's table. Thursday afternoon, Trump is slated to award Musk the National Medal of Science, the nation's top award for scientific and technological achievement, as first reported by Fox News Digital. "The Trump administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation," White House spokesperson Liz Huston told Fox News Digital regarding the award. title: Missing 72-year-old hiker found alive days after frightening 100-foot fall left her badly injured
description: Mary Beth Granbery, age 72, was found alive near Cabin Creek after falling down a steep embankment during a solo camping trip in Northern California. On Facebook, people shared relief.
content: A multiday camping trip in Northern California sparked a desperate search after a 72-year-old woman failed to return as expected. Mary Beth Granbery, a Mount Shasta resident, departed for a multi-day camping trip on Sept. 28 and was expected to return by Oct. 1, according to a press release from Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office. When Granbery did not show up for work the following day, concerned family members reported her missing, the release said. GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL A key development came on Oct. 3, when family members located Granbery's camper van at the Cabin Creek Trailhead in neighboring Shasta County, according to the sheriff’s office. The Siskiyou and Shasta County Sheriff's Offices then joined forces — with deputies and search and rescue teams working together to locate the missing hiker. Fox News Digital reached out to the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office and Shasta County Sheriff's Office for comment and further details. On Oct. 4, ground crews located Granbery near Cabin Creek, the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office said. Though she was alive and conscious, she'd suffered serious injuries after falling down a steep embankment, according to the sheriff's office. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Those injuries apparently included a severe knee injury. She also showed signs of exposure when rescuers reached her — and she was disoriented and "nonverbal," according to reports. title: Yankees legends Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez deliver blunt post-mortem on team: 'Something has to change'
description: Alex Rodriguez and Derek Jeter slammed the New York Yankees' philosophy after a stunning ALDS sweep by the Tampa Bay Rays extended a historic drought.
content: The New York Yankees have tied their longest World Series drought since 1923. It will now be 17 consecutive seasons without the Commissioner's Trophy in the Bronx after getting swept in the American League Division Series by their AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees managed to squeak out just five runs in the three-game set and hit just .130 in the series. Well, the Yankees ran back largely the same exact team and got a nearly identical result, leaving Rodriguez and Derek Jeter in shambles. "Something has to change. I'm not talking about personnel, but I'm talking about a philosophy. There has to be a philosophy change," Rodriguez said on FOX late Wednesday night. "You've won 27 titles one way. I'm not saying anyone should lose their job, but [general manager Brian] Cashman has surrounded himself with people that know baseball, that understand baseball, that can value both sides of the ball - it's unthinkable when your season is on the line, and of the nine positions, you don't know who's going to play five positions...
