title: Unearthed clip exposes how far Talarico was willing to go on raising taxes during COVID era
description: James Talarico once said he didn't care what taxes had to be raised to avoid healthcare cuts in Texas during the COVID-19 budget shortfalls.
content: James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for the Senate in Texas, once pressed Democrats to consider cuts to healthcare benefits a nonstarter — regardless of the consequences for the state’s finances. The remark came during a podcast interview in which Talarico discussed how Texas might balance its budget amid COVID-related shortfalls. He feared Republicans would look for savings in healthcare services. "I don't care where you get the revenue. I don't care what taxes you have to raise," Talarico said in a 2020 appearance with Texas Rising, a progressive YouTube channel focused on political engagement among younger voters. The resurfaced moment adds to the pile of past statements dealing with gender, immigration and fiscal management, complicating the political calculus for Talarico as he aims to convince voters in Texas that he could represent a Republican-leaning constituency, even as a Democrat. TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS At the time, Texas was facing a bleak financial outlook. The pandemic had crippled key sections of the state’s regular revenue streams. As oil demand crashed nationally, tax revenue that would normally come from hotels, bars and restaurants also faced steep reductions. Texas Comptroller Glenn Hegar projected a $4.6 billion shortfall. "The economic contraction associated with COVID-19 has resulted in revenue collection this fiscal year that is much lower than our earlier projections," Hegar said in a statement. "This estimate also assumes that restrictions on businesses and individuals will be lifted before the end of this calendar year and that economic activity will strengthen." As a part of the COVID response, Texas ordered most agencies to look for ways to cut their spending by 5% in the 2020 – 2021 budget. In a letter, Governor Greg Abbott largely shielded Health and Human Services (HHS) from the reductions, sparing the state’s Medicaid program, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, the foster care program and disability services, among others. Even so, $2.6 billion of HHS’s budget remained subject to cuts, according to the agency's estimations. That left the Health and Human Services Commission with a target of $132,716,600 in cuts. 'FAKE' MODERATE TALARICO'S TEXAS SURGE TESTS PAXTON IN FIGHT TO HOLD CRUCIAL GOP SENATE SEAT Despite the reduced figure, Talarico blasted the idea of making spending reductions geared towards healthcare. "You're not going to make our students and our teachers — you're not going to make the sick and the elderly pay for this pandemic we are not going to balance our budget off of the most vulnerable people in this state," Talarico said. He argued that Democrats should create a similar kind of stigma against cuts to HHS as the one surrounding raising taxes. "Sometimes you get the reaction in the capitol that's an unreasonable position to take. But the other side of the aisle has already taken revenue increases off the table. They've done a good job of making certain options taboo, so I think our coalition, not just Democrats but progressives, and anybody with a functioning heart should be able to make cuts to health and education taboo and take them off the table," Talarico said. The moment has brought on criticisms from at least one Republican onlooker. "High-tax Talarico never saw a tax hike he didn't love in the Texas Legislature, and he is promising to continue that if elected to the Senate. James Talarico will raise taxes on every Texan to fund his radical agenda of taxpayer-funded sex changes for kids and free healthcare for illegal immigrants," Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee said in a statement to Fox News Digital. As he wages his bid for U.S. Senate, Talarico has advocated for an expansion of U.S. health policy. On his website, Talarico has called for universal eligibility for Medicare, to regulate medical debt and expand veteran care. His views on Medicare, which overlap with many other progressives in the party, have prompted criticism from Republicans who believe such an expansion would cripple the federal budget with cost. Skeptics of the plan have argued for years that such an expansion is too expensive and does little to address existing inefficiencies in the American healthcare system. In 2019, Sen. John Barrasso, R-Wyo., took to the Senate floor to blast the idea, calling it a straitjacket solution that would undermine healthcare quality. "The [Congressional Budget Office] projects in its report on a single-payer plan that government spending on health care would increase substantially. They go on to say to cover the massive cost of government-run care, income taxes would have to at least double. Income taxes, American families — at least double," Barrasso said. SHOCK POLL: TALARICO TIES PAXTON IN TEXAS SENATE RACE, THREATENING GOP STRONGHOLD Talarico’s campaign did not address questions on whether his designs for healthcare are shaped by the national deficit, but noted that his plan includes increases in taxes on the country's top earners. "James supports making billionaires pay their fair share so we can cut taxes for middle class Texans and fund healthcare for working families — which is why he has unveiled plans to end special tax handouts to corporations and billionaires to help fund healthcare, while proudly voting for the largest property tax cut in Texas history to make sure middle class families get a break," the Talarico campaign told Fox News Digital. "Ken Paxton has worked to enrich himself and his billionaire mega-donors, amassed 15 properties on a taxpayer-funded salary, and was impeached by his own party for his corrupt abuse of office." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Having cleared the party primary, Talarico will face off against Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton in the state’s Nov. 3 general election.

title: Colorado school parents sound alarm after daughters were cut from volleyball team while trans athlete plays
description: Four parents say a transgender player made Dakota Ridge High School's girls volleyball team while eight junior girls were cut from the JV roster.
content: Four parents of Dakota Ridge High School athletes are demanding answers from Jeffco Public Schools in Colorado after they said a transgender player was allowed to participate on the girls’ junior varsity volleyball team while eight girls were cut from the roster. One mother, who spoke with Fox News Digital on the condition of anonymity, said her daughter had previously made the sophomore team as a freshman and was devastated after being cut this season. "My daughter played volleyball at Dakota Ridge High School in Colorado’s Jeffco Public Schools during her freshman and sophomore years," the mother said. "Being part of that team meant everything to her. This year, about 35 plus girls, including my daughter, didn’t make the team, while a transgender player did. She was crushed, and as her mother, I feel her opportunity was taken from her. This is why Title IX protections in sports are so important for our girls." TRUMP ADMIN CRACKS DOWN ON COLORADO SCHOOL DISTRICT THAT MAY HAVE ALLEGEDLY PUT UP TO 61 MALES ON GIRLS' TEAMS Another told Fox News Digital that her family open-enrolled her junior daughter at Dakota Ridge specifically because of its volleyball program and that her daughter hopes to play the sport in college. The mother said her daughter, a setter, attended a paid summer camp and additional training with the school program before coaches asked her shortly before tryouts to switch to right-side hitting, a position she had never played. She was ultimately cut from the program. "For her, this meant losing a season of development, time with her teammates, and something she had built much of her high-school experience around," the mother said. She said the coach later explained in writing that other athletes "demonstrated more consistency in the areas needed" and that her daughter "was beat out." She said her family subsequently learned that an athlete selected to play setter on the girls’ team is transgender, prompting questions about whether that athlete’s inclusion affected her daughter's opportunity. "I cannot establish from the information available to me that my daughter would otherwise have made the team, or that her position change was connected to the other athlete’s placement," the mother said. "Those are questions I am asking the district to investigate through the eligibility records, tryout evaluations, and coaching communications." "Across the country, this issue is discussed as a policy debate," she added. "For our family, it is personal: a teenage girl lost the chance to play the sport she loves at her school. We deserve a transparent examination of what happened and whether her rights were protected." A third Dakota Ridge parent said the girls expected a fair tryout process and that the same eligibility standards should apply to every athlete. USA VOLLEYBALL SUGGESTS CHANGES COMING TO SEX TESTING, WHILE JUNIOR FAMILIES RAISE MALE ATHLETE CONCERNS "What makes this especially difficult to accept is that seven junior girls were cut from the team, any one of whom could have earned and held that roster spot," the parent continued. "These girls worked hard, dedicated their time, and put themselves through the tryout process with the expectation that the selection process would be fair and that the same standards would apply to every girl athlete. If it is determined that an ineligible player was permitted to participate, I believe there must be meaningful accountability." "The program should be disqualified for the 26-27 season, and all the coaches and Athletic Director should be subject to dismissal or other appropriate disciplinary action based on the findings of a thorough investigation," the parent added. "Allowing a situation like this to stand without consequences sends a troubling message to the girls who were told there was no place for them on the JV team. As parents, we deserve transparency about how this decision was made, what policies were followed, and what steps Jeffco Public Schools will take to ensure that every student-athlete is treated fairly and that eligibility and roster standards are followed." Fox News Digital is not aware of any completed investigation or findings in connection with this matter. Another Jeffco parent confirmed to Fox News Digital that a complaint regarding the situation had been filed and that a Title IX coordinator was investigating. The Title IX coordinator also told a parent that Jeffco is always open to meeting with individual students who would prefer to have more privacy in school locker rooms. A fourth parent told Fox News Digital, "I am concerned about the girls who did not make the team, a male on the court with our team and all opposing teams. This has to stop." The parent said that school administrators confirmed to her that they were aware a boy was on the volleyball team, but that they could not share additional information. The school said district and school administrators have stated that they did not confirm this to anyone, and no administrator has confirmed being aware of "a boy" being on the team. There have not yet been findings that the district violated Title IX or failed to protect students in connection with tryouts and selection for the girls’ volleyball team. SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS This issue comes after the Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights concluded in March that Jefferson County Public Schools violated Title IX by allowing male students to compete in female sports, among other findings. "OCR concluded that Jefferson County’s policies allowing access to intimate facilities and participation in sports based on ‘gender identity’ discriminates against females by denying them safety, dignity, and equal access to educational programs and activities," OCR said in the March press release. "OCR received athletic rosters from Jefferson County indicating that male students may occupy up to 61 roster positions on girls’ sports teams in the District." The Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights said Jeffco Public Schools had 10 days to voluntarily resolve alleged Title IX violations or face enforcement action. The proposed agreement required the district to remove or change policies involving access to female facilities, overnight accommodations and girls’ sports. It also required Jeffco to adopt biology-based definitions of "male" and "female," base athletic eligibility and facility assignments on biological sex, clarify that Title IX requirements supersede conflicting state laws or athletic policies, and explain how students and families can report sex discrimination. FEDERAL JUDGE DISMISSES DOJ LAWSUIT CHALLENGING CALIFORNIA POLICY ALLOWING BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS’ SPORTS The district would also have to publish the statement across its websites and notify staff, students and coaches of its obligations under Title IX. On its website, Jeffco Public Schools says that it "is committed to providing a working and learning environment that is free from sexual harassment and discrimination based on sex in all of its education programs or activities, admissions and employment. The district's process aligns with Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (‘Title IX’) and its regulations not to discriminate in such a manner." In a statement to Fox News Digital Oct. 2, Department of Education Press Secretary Savannah Newhouse said, "Just this week, the Trump Administration restored the Title IX regulations that the Biden Administration unlawfully attempted to weaponize, making it undeniably clear that we will continue to enforce the law exactly as it was intended." Newhouse added, "Allowing male athletes to strip roster spots from women who have dedicated years of intense training to their sport is both an egregious moral failure and a definitive violation of the law. Unfortunately, because Jefferson County Public Schools remains intent on defying Title IX and has refused every opportunity to come into compliance, they face enforcement action from the Department of Justice. To the parents who have watched their daughters be relegated to second-class citizens on the court and stripped of their privacy in locker rooms, know this: the Trump Administration will not waver in pursuit of accountability." A Department of Education spokesperson told Fox News Digital that "after issuing a final warning letter," the department "took action against Jefferson County Public Schools in Colorado for allowing male students to participate in female sports, occupy female bathrooms and locker rooms, and even share overnight accommodations with females. Jefferson County Public Schools was given 10 days to comply or face enforcement action. This investigation was turned over to the U.S. Department of Justice." In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson at the Department of Justice said, "The Department of Education referred Jefferson County Public Schools to the Justice Department after the district refused to come into compliance with Title IX. Title IX guarantees girls equal opportunity in school sports, and no girl should lose her place on a team to a male athlete. The Civil Rights Division is committed to enforcing that guarantee." The DOJ told Fox News Digital they declined to comment on whether DOJ enforcement action has begun due to ongoing litigation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Jeffco Public Schools said, "Under federal law (FERPA) and state privacy regulations, Jeffco Public Schools cannot confirm, deny, or comment on the gender identity, administrative records, or athletic participation of any individual student." The spokesperson said that Jeffco Public Schools runs its high school athletic programs under the governing bylaws of the Colorado High School Activities Association (CHSAA) and the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act, and that its nondiscrimination policies, including Policy AC (Nondiscrimination/Equal Opportunity and similar policy are fully active and in effect. The spokesperson continued, "In accordance with Colorado state law (including the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act), Jeffco Public Schools is committed to providing a safe, welcoming, and inclusive environment for all students. Our policies ensure that every student, regardless of gender identity or expression, has equal access to educational programs, facilities, and district-sanctioned activities." The spokesperson continued, "Any student or family concern that has been brought to school leadership is being addressed. All students may request and have accommodations in the locker room." WHAT THE SCOTUS TITLE IX RULING COULD MEAN FOR LAWSUITS SEEKING DAMAGES FOR WOMEN IMPACTED BY TRANS ATHLETES The spokesperson added criticism that the media would cover the story and asked for consideration of the students involved. In a separate development, the Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights notified a Jeffco parent Oct. 6 that it is opening another Title IX investigation into Jefferson County Public Schools, this time examining allegations that the district failed to appropriately respond to reports of sexual harassment of students by district employees. The new probe adds to federal scrutiny of the district, though it is separate from the transgender-athlete dispute. OCR stressed that opening an investigation "is not itself evidence of a violation" and said it will collect and analyze evidence before reaching a determination. On Nov. 3, Colorado voters will vote on the ballot initiative, "Protect Women and Girls Sports Act," which would require school athletic teams to be designated based on biological sex and prohibit male students from participating on teams designated for females, women or girls.

title: Mike Waltz fights back tears revealing what Hamas hostage refused to do before release
description: Eliya Cohen, freed after 505 days in Hamas captivity, and Nova festival survivor Ziv Abud shared their harrowing stories at the United Nations.
content: UNITED NATIONS — Three years after the worst massacre in Israel’s history, Eliya Cohen — who survived 505 days in Hamas captivity — took the stage at the United Nations alongside his newlywed wife, Ziv Abud, a survivor of the Nova music festival massacre, and tried to explain to some of the world’s top diplomats what he had endured. "They didn't let me change clothes or to get a shower, even to eat or to drink," he said. "They chained me with heavy iron chains by my leg," Cohen said during an emotional discussion moderated by Dr. Phil McGraw at Israel’s U.N. commemoration Tuesday. He said lights were kept on to prevent the hostages from sleeping and that captors would enter repeatedly during the night screaming in an effort to frighten them. Cohen said they were not permitted to use a restroom and that at times survival felt almost impossible. FREED HOSTAGE ROM BRASLAVSKI DETAILS ABUSE, STARVATION DURING 738 DAYS IN GAZA CAPTIVITY But he described repeatedly forcing his mind away from the violence and toward the possibility of returning home. "Don't think about the violence. Don't think about the torture. Don't think about everything," Cohen recalled telling himself. "Just continue, stay strong. And maybe one day, you will come back home to your family." Cohen was among the 251 people abducted during the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack, when about 1,200 people were killed in southern Israel in their homes and at the Nova Music festival. It was the deadliest single day in Israel’s history. He personally lost 48 people he knew that day. His wife, Ziv, carried a different piece of the same story. Abud and Cohen had arrived at the Nova festival shortly before dawn with her 19-year-old nephew Amit and his girlfriend Karin. When the attack began, they eventually took refuge in a roadside bomb shelter that Cohen said was designed for roughly eight people but became packed with 29. HAMAS USED SEXUAL VIOLENCE 'DELIBERATELY AND SYSTEMATICALLY' ON OCT 7, COMMISSION REPORT FINDS Abud told the audience that more than 40 terrorists later attacked the shelter with grenades and gunfire. One man inside repeatedly grabbed grenades and threw them back outside before he was killed, she said. As the attack continued, Cohen covered Abud with bodies — an act that saved her life. "I lost my consciousness. Eliya was kidnapped," Abud said. "And after seven hours, I woke up in the shelter. I found myself in a pile of bodies." She paused, fighting back the tears. "It wasn't even bodies. It was body parts." Abud said she then saw that Amit and Karin had been killed. "I needed to sit with the bodies for seven more hours," she said. She was eventually rescued, one of seven survivors from the shelter. "We were four people that went to the festival from the same house," Abud said, "And I'm the only one that came back home that night." FORMER HAMAS HOSTAGE COUNTERS HASAN PIKER’S UT AUSTIN EVENT WITH HER STORY OF SURVIVAL For 505 days, she campaigned for Cohen’s return without knowing whether the man she loved would ever come home. Cohen, meanwhile, said he believed while in captivity that Abud had been killed. The couple married weeks before Tuesday’s ceremony. "But now he's here," Abud said. "And I can look forward to the future after we got married." She said she hoped the years ahead would include "kids and family because we are here and we survived. And we need to live a normal life," she said. Another Oct. 7 survivor who addressed the diplomats was Oriya Berlin, a young Israeli visual intelligence observer who had arrived at a base in the Gaza border area just two days before the attack. Berlin said she woke on the morning of Oct. 7 believing she was hearing a thunderstorm. "Outside, thousands of missiles were raining down with a single objective: to destroy my life and the lives of my friends," she said. Berlin and four other soldiers ran barefoot and in pajamas into a small shelter. They were unarmed. She said the women initially believed the incursion would resemble scenarios they had studied during training — a small squad that Israeli forces could quickly contain. Seconds later, she said, they heard vehicles and gunfire. Berlin described roughly 60 heavily armed terrorists attacking the base. At one point, she said, a message appeared in the unit’s WhatsApp group telling soldiers to shout "IDF" in Hebrew so Israeli troops could find them. The broken Hebrew immediately raised suspicions that a terrorist had taken a soldier’s phone. They remained silent. Berlin said they then heard another group shouting for soldiers to identify themselves, followed by a burst of gunfire and silence. Ten hours after the attack began, she said, special forces finally reached them. THE SENATE HAS REMEMBERED AMERICA’S OCTOBER 7TH VICTIMS. NOW IT’S TIME TO HEAL Berlin said that after learning how many of her friends had been murdered or kidnapped, she could not remain at home. Although she was offered the opportunity to leave military service, Berlin said she refused and returned as an observer for another six months before later moving into the IDF Public Diplomacy Office. "I wanted the world to see that the IDF is not just an intimidating military force on a television screen," she said. "It was also a 5'2" fake blonde girl like me who simply wanted to protect her home, her family, and her friends." She said she has since spoken before audiences ranging from international organizations to high school students who told her "I was wasting their time because of their deep-seated anti-Israel hostility." "But I stayed," Berlin said. "I spoke because the truth demands a voice." Berlin said her decision to continue speaking was rooted in the friends who did not survive. Before the ceremony, U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz met privately with Cohen and Abud, asking Cohen how he was feeling physically and telling the couple how good it was to see them "healthy and alive." Minutes later, from the stage, Waltz became visibly emotional as he recounted a part of Cohen’s captivity that he said he had been unable to get out of his mind. Waltz said that on the night before Cohen’s release, Hamas tried to make him record a propaganda video claiming he had been treated well. "He refused," Waltz said. "He held firm. He said no." Waltz said Hamas again tried to turn Cohen’s release into propaganda the following day, placing him before cameras and instructing him to raise his hands. "He refused again," Waltz said. "Eliya, we salute you. I salute you," Waltz continued. "You are a proud, strong Jew. You're undefeated, man" he said with his voice breaking. The hostage crisis stretched over two years and several rounds of negotiations, releases and rescue operations. Waltz told Fox News Digital after Tuesday’s ceremony that he wanted the commemoration to acknowledge both the loss of Oct. 7 and how much had changed since. "Oct. 7, 2023, was their 9/11, was their Pearl Harbor," Waltz said. "More Jews were brutally massacred that day than any day since the Holocaust." ISRAELI OCTOBER 7 SURVIVORS CONQUER TRAUMA ALONGSIDE LEGENDARY ROCK ICONS IN POWERFUL NEW DOCUMENTARY He said it was important "to recognize the loss" and "hear directly from the survivors," but also to take stock of the region three years later. "We have President Trump's 20-point peace plan. We have a U.N. resolution establishing the International Stabilization Force," Waltz told Fox News Digital. "He's determined to not repeat what's happened so often in the past, where Hamas rebuilds, Iran rearms, they attack again, and you have this devastation all over again." Waltz pointed to broader shifts across the Middle East. "Iran is on its back foot. Lebanon has hope, Syria has hope. Iraq has hope," he said. He said he hoped the commemoration could combine "remembrance, the perspective, and I think charting, trying to chart a path of hope and peace for the future." From the stage, Waltz argued that Oct. 7 had produced the opposite strategic result from what Iran and its allies sought. "Oct. 7 completely, and I think irreversibly, has backfired on Iran and all of their terrorist proxies," he said, pointing to changes in Syria, Lebanon and Iraq and the expansion of Israel’s regional relationships. He ended with a message to the audience: "America will stand with the Jewish people." "Be strong. Be resilient. Be wise," Waltz said. "And know that what you're doing is right. Stand with your moral compass and know that this administration, the United States of America, stands with you." Israeli Ambassador to the U.N. Danny Danon used the gathering — attended by ambassadors and diplomats from multiple countries — to turn his attention to the institution hosting it. MOTHER OF OCTOBER 7 HOSTAGE WHO WAS EXECUTED UNPACKS HER GRIEF IN NEW MEMOIR "Even in this building, the U.N. is trying to demonize and isolate Israel," Danon said. "They have turned the victim into the accused, comparing our IDF soldiers to Hamas terrorists." Danon said he has been told by colleagues that he takes criticism of Israel at the U.N. ‘too personally’. "Indeed, it is personal," he responded. "My daughter is serving right now in the IDF. My son served as an officer in the IDF," Danon said. "He was supposed to be on the Re'im base next to Gaza on Oct. 7. The last minute, he was released home for the holiday." "That's why it's personal," Danon said. "The U.N. tries to demonize all of our sons and daughters, our lions and lionesses who give everything so we can freely live in our homeland. So yes, it is personal. It's personal for all of us." For Cohen and Abud, however, the event eventually returned from geopolitics to something much smaller: the possibility of an ordinary future. Abud said they hoped to have children and build a family despite knowing that Oct. 7 and the 505 days that followed would remain part of their lives. Cohen, asked by McGraw what he would say if the terrorists who abducted and tortured him were watching, needed only a few words. "I won," Cohen said. "I won and I'm here." title: The best defense against high-tech AI scams is low-tech skepticism, expert warns
description: Cybersecurity expert Morgan Wright says human skepticism remains the strongest defense against AI-driven phishing scams and voice cloning fraud schemes.
content: As artificial intelligence rapidly evolves to make financial scams hyperrealistic, cybersecurity experts warn that the best defense isn't sophisticated detection software. It's good old-fashioned human skepticism. While adversarial states like China and Russia leverage AI on a global scale, average Americans are most frequently targeted by cybercriminals looking to exploit personal vulnerabilities for a quick payout, according to cybersecurity expert Morgan Wright. "Let's go back to around 1860, when Edgar Allan Poe wrote, ‘Believe nothing that you hear and only one half that you see,’" Wright told Fox News Digital. "That advice is as good now as it was 160 years ago." AI VOICE SCAMS CAN CLONE YOUR FAMILY’S VOICE AI technology has allowed bad actors to automate and scale personalized fraud schemes against everyday citizens. Generative tools eliminate language barriers, draft convincing phishing texts and generate hyperrealistic voice and video clones. By capturing just a few seconds of audio — often scraped from social media — fraudsters can convincingly replicate the voice of a family member. Wright pointed to the case of Deborah Del Mastro, a California mother who lost thousands of dollars after scammers used AI to clone her daughter’s voice to stage a terrifying kidnapping hoax. THE FAMILY GROUP CHAT IS A GOLDMINE FOR SCAMMERS "It's my daughter's voice," Del Mastro recalled during an interview on The CyberGuy Report podcast. "And she's having a panic attack." Convinced her daughter was in immediate danger, Del Mastro transferred more than $5,000 to the scammers before realizing she had been swindled. FRAUD EXPERT WARNS AI IS HELPING CRIMINALS OUTPACE THE GOVERNMENT: 'DON'T HAVE THE RIGHT TOOLS' "When you can fool a mother, that's how good these things are getting," Wright said of the voice-cloning technology. "What they do is use manipulation, influence and deceit. The more urgent I can make it sound, the more you're going to lower your guard and take action." CLICK HERE FOR MORE U.S. NEWS Wright, who has trained federal, state and local law enforcement in behavioral analysis, interviewing and interrogation — including teams at the FBI and the National Security Agency — emphasized that every scam relies on basic psychological triggers. His primary advice for anyone on the receiving end of a suspicious call or message is to pause before reacting. "We're not storming the beaches at Normandy; you're not going to get arrested," Wright said. "No law enforcement agency sends you an unsolicited text saying you're about to get arrested." While AI platforms roll out updated security features, scammers continuously find ways around them, making software-based detection a constant moving target. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We hear about all the different models from xAI, Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini. They change models constantly," Wright said. "So, when the model changes, how effective is [detection software]? We don't know because this stuff is moving so fast. What you see today will be drastically different tomorrow."

title: Amy Klobuchar calls for major anti-terrorism investments after alleged Mall of America plot
description: Amy Klobuchar praised the FBI after an 18-year-old was arrested for allegedly plotting an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America.
content: Sen. "I'm grateful for the heroic work of law enforcement that prevented a mass shooting and terrorist attack at the Mall of America," she said in a statement. "This shows why we continue to need major coordinated investments in anti-terrorism and local law enforcement to stop attacks like these. Klobuchar, who has represented Minnesota in the U.S. Senate since 2007, is running against Republican Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth in the November gubernatorial election. MALL OF AMERICA TERROR PLOT THWARTED, SUSPECTED ISIS SYMPATHIZER ARRESTED, FBI ANNOUNCES Her statement came after federal authorities announced the arrest of Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, who investigators say pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America. According to federal court documents, Mohamud allegedly spent months discussing plans for an attack before buying an AK-47-style rifle, four magazines and roughly 200 rounds of ammunition from an undercover FBI employee Tuesday. The rifle had been rendered inoperable, though the ammunition was live. FBI Director Kash Patel said Mohamud "allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans." title: California education candidate tells college professors to teach students basic math, rejects SAT requirement
description: Richard Barrera told UC professors it's their job to teach students who arrive without basic math skills, drawing sharp criticism from California superintendent opponent Sonja Shaw.
content: California state superintendent candidate Richard Barrera drew criticism Tuesday from his opponent and education advocates after telling UC professors it was their job to teach students who arrive without basic math skills and rejecting the return of standardized testing requirements as the University of California confronts growing concerns over college readiness. Barrera, president of the San Diego Unified School District Board of Education and a senior policy advisor to state superintendent Tony Thurmond, made the comments during a Sunday interview with NBC Los Angeles political reporter Conan Nolan. Barrera was asked whether the SAT should return as a requirement for the UC system as professors raise alarms about students entering elite universities without foundational math skills. "Absolutely not," Barrera said. "So math teachers at UCLA and Berkeley and every place else, part of your job that you get paid by the taxpayers to do is to teach our kids." Barrera told Fox News Digital that concerns about UC students being unable to perform basic math were "completely overstated," arguing that some incoming students instead just need review in subjects they had not studied recently, and that universities shared responsibility for helping them catch up. UNPREPARED COLLEGE STUDENTS FORCED TO RELEARN 'MIDDLE SCHOOL MATHEMATICS,' CALIFORNIA PROFESSORS REVEAL "I do think that this idea that students are coming in not knowing fractions is completely overstated," Barrera said. "What we're seeing is students who take a placement test, in the summer before they attend their freshman year at UC, who might miss questions on algebra, on trigonometry, maybe subjects that they haven't had in a couple of years. That's just about review and acceleration." "This is not about students who are incapable of doing the work," he added. "This is about students who need some review and acceleration, and it is the responsibility of UC to participate in that acceleration." Chino Valley Unified School District Board President Sonja Shaw, Barrera's opponent in the November race for state superintendent of public instruction, told Fox News Digital that his response shifted responsibility away from California's K-12 education system. "Richard Barrera heard professors at Berkeley and UCLA sound the alarm that incoming students can’t do elementary-school math and his immediate response was to blame the professors. Not the students. Not the system that passed them along. The professors," Shaw said. "His brilliant solution? Force college faculty to teach remedial middle-school math on the taxpayer dime, and claim that bringing back the SAT is somehow ‘exclusionary,’" she added. "That’s not a plan. That’s a career politician scrambling to cover up a failure he helped create." Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital that Barrera's opposition to standardized testing protected California's K-12 education system from accountability for students reaching college without foundational math skills. "Richard Barrera’s answer tells you everything you need to know about who he works for. The California Teachers Association is bankrolling his campaign for state superintendent, and he is returning the favor by protecting the system from accountability," DeAngelis said. WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES Nolan followed up by asking Barrera whether professors at some of the country's leading universities should be responsible for teaching students fractions. Barrera said some students had overcome significant obstacles to reach those campuses. "Listen, we've got students who are coming up from incredible experiences, first-generation students overcoming so many barriers to be on the campus," Barrera said. "Those students are capable of learning quickly. What they need is a little support to be caught up. What they don't need is to be excluded." Tina Descovich, CEO and co-founder of Moms for Liberty, told Fox News Digital that students arriving at college without foundational skills reflected problems that began years before they reached a university classroom. "A child who can't do fractions at 18 was a child who couldn't do fractions at ten, and the system knew it," she said. "Richard Barrera's solution is to make it a college professor's problem and continue to cover up the failures of the status quo. Parents in California have watched their kids get passed along for years. Now they're being told the people who did the passing along deserve a promotion." GAVIN NEWSOM AVOIDS QUESTION ON BRINGING BACK SAT SCORES AFTER UC OPEN LETTER, ASKS 'SHOW ME THE DATA' The exchange came months after more than 1,400 faculty members signed an open letter calling for SAT and ACT math requirements to be restored for STEM applicants. By August, more than 3,000 faculty members had signed letters raising concerns about academic preparation. California's state testing results show a similar proficiency gap before students reach college. According to the state's 2024-25 Smarter Balanced assessment results, 30.49% of 11th graders met or exceeded the standard in mathematics, compared with 56.96% in English language arts. DeAngelis said that those results undercut the argument that students reaching college without foundational math skills merely need additional support once on campus. "About 30 percent of California 11th graders meet math standards," he said. "That result is not a story about first-generation students who just need a little catch-up once they reach campus. That failure is a system that handed out diplomas without requiring mastery, then blamed the score for noticing." Barrera defended his opposition to restoring the SAT or ACT requirements in UC admissions, saying that concerns about students needing additional academic preparation predated the university system’s decision to eliminate standardized tests and arguing the exams had historically excluded some applicants. "It's not the elimination of the SAT, you know, that is what we need to look at," Barrera said. "The question that we all need to be asking ourselves is, what are the best strategies to get students prepared for college-level math? And simply having a placement exam like the SAT, which is historically discriminatory towards students of color, towards first-generation students — it's a tool that has historically excluded students." "Why would we reinstitute that, knowing that that has shown no relevance in helping improve students' preparedness for college-level math?" he added. The UC Board of Regents' current admissions policy prohibits SAT and ACT scores from being used in its comprehensive admissions review, but the university system is now formally reconsidering standardized testing. Shaw said that the state should instead focus on whether students master core subjects before reaching college. "Students are not helped by being lied to about their skills," she said. "They’re helped by actually learning to read, write, and do math before they get to college. That requires high standards in K-12 enforced consistently and measured honestly." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It does not mean turning UCLA and Berkeley into expensive elementary schools and then blaming the faculty for noticing the problem," she added. "Lowering the bar one more time will not fix a decade of failure. It will just hide it longer."

title: Comedy stars lash out at Sebastian Maniscalco over SiriusXM shake-up
description: Comedians like Patton Oswalt and Michelle Wolf are urging Sebastian Maniscalco to reverse a SiriusXM channel rebrand they say hurts working-class comics.
content: Sebastian Maniscalco has found himself in hot water with some comedians who are claiming that his new SiriusXM channel is taking away money and exposure from working-class comics. Earlier this year, SiriusXM changed a long-running channel in its lineup called Raw Comedy that often featured lesser-known comedians to Sebastian Maniscalco's Comedy Radio. The new station more prominently features famous comedians now. Stand Up for Stand Up, a nonprofit that supports comedians, recently wrote an article saying the rebranding has "drastically shifted from a wider pool of 800-plus comedians enjoying spins (and thus, royalties and exposure to the audience of listeners)" on the channel "to a narrower pool of comedians getting plays per month. "And of those few hundred who are getting spins, over 75% of the plays are going to the top 50 artists, which results in a concentration of wealth among the top echelon, which is largely made up of big-name celebrity comics." SEBASTIAN MANISCALCO IS A NO-NONSENSE FATHER, SAYS PARENTS NEED TO BE 'HALF-PSYCHOTIC' WITH THEIR KIDS The nonprofit called the change "bad for comedians, and bad for the future of comedy," adding, "it hurts passive revenue, and discoverability, as well as the infrastructure that supports up and coming comedians." Maniscalco addressed the criticism in an Instagram Story he shared Wednesday, saying, "This goes out to all my fellow comedians – I want to let you know that I hear you, I support you, I love you. I know how hard the grind is. Believe me, I've been there." He said that he "had nothing to do" with removing the channel from SiriusXM, but assured fans that he's planning on working with the company to "highlight a variety of different voices in stand-up comedy," including newcomers, superstars and everyone in between. "I just ask that you give me a little time, guys," he said. "I just got here, and I need a little time to build out the channel. I just wanted to let you know that I heard you, and give me a little time and be patient, and I think you'll like the result." Before Maniscalco made his statement, several of his fellow comedians had been taking issue with his new channel. Comedian Matt Ruby on his Substack page claimed the channel was "crushing middle class comedians who rely on payments from the company to pad income." Liz Miele, another comedian, said in a video on her Instagram, "This year, the Raw channel on SiriusXM became Sebastian Maniscalco’s channel. Great. Fine. Celebrities have taken over channels before. Never been an issue. The problem is Raw went from playing 800 working-class comedians to now playing less than 300 celebrity comedians like Joan Rivers, Johnny Carson, Bob Hope, Norm Macdonald. Just dead comic, dead comic, dead comic, and then a plethora of very famous alive comedians that might not even know about this extra income that they’re about to receive." She added that every "working-class comedian that has been kicked off the channel is quite aware" of the money they've lost. Comedian Gianmarco Soresi posted a photo of Maniscalco on X with the caption, "Aren’t you embarrassed?" Comedian Ashley Ray, who relied on the income, wrote on X, "Those checks went from covering a car payment to barely covering a quarter of weed, i hate this man." COMEDIAN SEBASTIAN MANISCALCO JABS CANCEL CULTURE WITH ST PATRICK'S DAY MESSAGE Famous names like Patton Oswalt, Michelle Wolf and Margaret Cho also implored Maniscalco to do something this week. Altho I do miss when Raw Dog was actually raw w/some of the edgiest comics." content: A Washington state mother accused of trying to kill her daughters with a knife and a freeway crash now faces attempted murder charges after soldiers and another bystander stepped in to stop the alleged attack. Janieka Amber Marie Ellington, 35, faces four counts of attempted first-degree murder, two counts of vehicular assault and one count of felony harassment involving threats to kill, according to Pierce County Superior Court records. Prosecutors allege she tried to kill the girls both by stabbing or cutting them and by crashing their vehicle, according to charging documents. The case stems from Monday morning’s rollover wreck on southbound Interstate 5 near DuPont, where witnesses said Ellington chased her teenage daughter with a knife and threatened to kill her after the crash, FOX 13 Seattle reported. WATCH: BYSTANDERS, POLICE LIFT VOLKSWAGEN OFF WOMAN PINNED UNDERNEATH AFTER DRAMATIC E-BIKE CRASH Three bystanders, including two soldiers, disarmed Ellington and restrained her until Washington State Patrol troopers arrived, the outlet reported. "I just did my part," Sgt. Ricardo A. Nunez, a 7th Infantry Division soldier stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, said, according to FOX 13. "I am glad I was there to help those girls and was just in the right place at the right time." Court records show a judge ordered a competency evaluation Tuesday. A competency hearing is scheduled for Oct. 20. Troopers responded shortly before 9 a.m. Monday to reports of an SUV driving erratically near mile marker 118, according to FOX 13. In its initial report, the outlet stated that the SUV struck a concrete barrier, veered toward the right shoulder and then crossed back into traffic, hitting a semi-truck. It struck the barrier again and rolled over near Center Drive, Exit 118. SOUTH CAROLINA WOMAN ACCUSED OF STABBING LYFT DRIVER 11 TIMES CLAIMS MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS Ellington told hospital staff and troopers she had been drinking whiskey the night before and was driving without sleep, according to court records. One of her daughters told investigators Ellington believed people were following them before the crash. A 9-year-old girl suffered multiple broken bones and a stab wound, while a 15-year-old girl was hospitalized without serious injuries, according to the outlet. Witness Nathan Wilkinson told KING 5 he was driving to work when he came upon the wreck and saw two men in military uniforms from Joint Base Lewis-McChord intervene. "There's people standing around, then all of a sudden there was a flash, and then the two soldiers jumped on a person. … I heard a scream at that time," Wilkinson told the outlet. "I saw one of the soldiers had a knife in his hand that he had dislodged from the person they tackled." FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE Wilkinson called 911 as bystanders subdued the woman, KING 5 reported. The attempted murder charges include two counts alleging Ellington intended to kill by stabbing or cutting and two alleging she intended to kill through a vehicle crash, according to the charging documents. title: Paramore's Hayley Williams targets Christian nationalism as America's 'greatest threat' to democracy

content: Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams faced criticism after telling fans during a September concert that Christian nationalism is "the greatest threat to American democracy," adding another political declaration to a tour where she had repeatedly spoken out against President Donald Trump, immigration enforcement and Israel's war in Gaza. In the recirculated clip, Williams made the declaration before performing "True Believer," a track from her 2025 solo album, "Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party." "Incredibly ignorant comment considering Christianity is woven into the fabric of every founding document that proscribes Americans' democratic rights," she said. "There would be no Natural Law without Christianity, and without that, no human rights that exist beyond a government’s power. Christianity sees all people as made in the image of God, so are all valuable, no matter how successful, and puts self-sacrifice above power." "Democracy has thrived in the Christian nations across the world for a reason. The true threat is this kind of ignorant bigotry," she continued. content: Dolly Parton’s nephew unleashed an expletive-filled tirade in an email exchange involving the country music legend just days before her death as tensions over security services boiled over, according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital. The recipient, identified as "Bill," thanked him for his "genuine care and concern" and said he hoped both teams would support "each other in success." Parton died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer. Seaver, who had served as Parton's head of security for more than two decades, was chosen by his aunt to publicly announce her death. title: Florida GOP hopeful on backing Trump in Iran: 'This is about ending a long war, not starting a war'

content: LIV Golf is doing whatever it can to stay alive after the Public Investment Fund (PIF) ended its monetary commitment to the league — however, it may now need to stay afloat without its best player. Jon Rahm shocked the golf world nearly three years ago when, after publicly dismissing the league, he joined it on a deal that was rumored to be between $300 and $600 million. Bankruptcy filings show the league owes millions of dollars in unpaid compensation to top players, including Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Cam Smith. Rahm is reportedly owed more than $7 million and was "more than willing to fulfill" the details of his original contract. PIF provided $50 million to help LIV pay its bills and continue operating during the bankruptcy case. The league’s future depends on a proposed restructuring plan called "LIV 2.0." description: Security footage from the couple's $10 million Arcadia mansion allegedly revealed systematic beatings of 14 surrogate-born children by nannies and parents.
content: A California couple faces severe felony charges after allegedly abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children — some as young as 2 months old — inside their multimillion-dollar Arcadia mansion, according to authorities. Guojun Xuan, 66, and Silvia Zhang, 39, were each charged with one count of conspiracy to commit child abuse. Xuan also faces one felony count of child abuse, one felony count of accessory after the fact and five felony counts of dissuading a witness. Zhang faces an additional count of accessory after the fact and four counts of dissuading a witness. Both have pleaded not guilty. MICHIGAN NURSE ACCUSED OF BREAKING BONES AND BRUISING PREMATURE INFANT AT CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL "The number of children who were subjected to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said. "The alleged corporal abuse of these children is appalling and revolting, especially at the hands of those who were supposed to protect them." An investigation was launched in May 2025 when Zhang brought her 2-month-old infant to Children's Hospital Los Angeles with a traumatic head injury and severe brain bleeding, affiliate FOX 11 Los Angeles reported. Medical staff determined the infant had been violently shaken and struck by a nanny, Chunmei Li, according to the report. Prosecutors allege that Zhang and Xuan delayed seeking medical attention for two days, bringing the child to the hospital only after he began experiencing seizures. The couple allegedly made false claims that the baby had fallen out of bed. OHIO MOM OF 16 CRADLES STOMACH IN COURT, PLEADS NOT GUILTY IN SEVERE ABUSE CASE INVOLVING OWN CHILDREN Security footage recovered by police from the couple's $10 million home revealed widespread, systemic abuse against 14 surrogate-born children ranging in age from 2 months to 13 years old, with the majority between ages 1 and 3. Six additional children linked to the couple were later located at other homes, bringing the total number of affected children to 21. Inside the mansion, prosecutors discovered three "learning centers" where toddlers were forced to sit at desks for hours. Nannies inside the home were allegedly instructed to administer discipline designed to avoid leaving visible marks. FOX 11 reported that prosecutors allege Xuan and Zhang actively monitored and directed nannies to subject the children to daily beatings using sticks hidden throughout the house. Children were also allegedly coached to deny being beaten. SURROGATE, CALIFORNIA COUPLE CLASH IN COURT AS NEWBORN FIGHTS FOR LIFE AFTER HEART SURGERY In one documented instance, Xuan allegedly instructed a nanny who was striking a child to hit harder before joining in himself, delivering open-handed blows to the child's head, striking the child's bare buttocks and lifting the child by a single arm while continuing the assault. Another boy was forced to perform continuous squats or hold a "horse stance" position for hours as punishment. The couple operated Future Spring Surrogacy directly from their home, recruiting surrogates and paying them tens of thousands of dollars to carry children to term. While one surrogate received $135,000, prosecutors noted that many were recruited under misleading pretenses. At least eight surrogates reported aggressive tactics and false statements regarding the family's living situation. Law enforcement found evidence of vast financial resources inside the home. Xuan allegedly maintained more than 200 bank accounts, stacks of cash used to pay nannies, and passports for multiple countries, including Mexico. Authorities also discovered between $8 million and $9 million in liquor stored inside the mansion. Investigators are working to determine the biological and social parents of all 21 children involved. The Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services has taken custody of the children to oversee their long-term medical care, psychological evaluation and legal placement. CALIFORNIA PASTOR CHARGED WITH YEARSLONG CHILD MOLESTATION AS INVESTIGATORS SEEK MORE VICTIMS: DA "This was not a home where these children were loved and nurtured," DA Hochman said. "This was a home where these young children were systematically beaten and punished if they did not do what they were told. These alleged abusers will now face the full force of the law as we hold them accountable for their despicable actions." Beyond the child abuse allegations, law enforcement is probing Xuan’s past, including his connection to a property previously linked to an illegal casino and a psilocybin mushroom growing operation. Fox News Digital reached out to attorneys for Xuan and Zhang for comment. It remains unclear how long the alleged abuse had been occurring prior to May 2025.

title: People on weight-loss drugs report fingernails falling off as researchers uncover surprising link
description: Nail discoloration was reported by 46% of GLP-1 users versus 17% of non-users, while scalp inflammation accompanied hair loss in most medication users studied.
content: People taking GLP-1 medications for obesity or diabetes experience nail detachment and hair loss at significantly higher rates than people with similar overall health who do not take GLP-1s. That's according to research presented Oct. 1 at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Congress 2026 in Vienna, Austria. Two studies evaluated 575 users of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) drugs and a control group of 1,329 non-users, all of whom had type 2 diabetes, obesity or both. Participants were recruited across France, the U.S, Brazil and Mexico. POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS FACE NUMEROUS LAWSUITS OVER RARE ‘EYE STROKE’ LINKED TO VISION LOSS In the primary study examining nail health, 39% of GLP-1 users reported nail detachment compared with 9% of non-users. Discoloration of the nails affected 46% of GLP-1 users versus 17% in the control group. Overall, two-thirds of GLP-1 users (66%) reported experiencing at least one nail disorder, compared with 53% of the control group. Researchers found that weight loss alone did not explain the difference. Even when researchers looked only at people who lost weight, those taking GLP-1s were still more likely to have these problems. After adjusting for existing dermatological conditions and nutritional deficiencies, nail detachment and discoloration remained two to three times more frequent among the medication group. "Until now, nail changes associated with GLP-1 therapies had essentially been anecdotal," study author Dr. Charles Taïeb, a clinical dermatologist at Necker University Hospital in Paris, said in a press release. "Our findings show a clear association, but they also underline an important point: Not everything that happens during GLP-1 treatment is necessarily caused by the treatment itself." POPULAR GLP-1 WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DEADLY BRAIN DISORDER In another study evaluating hair and scalp conditions among the same group of participants, 50% of GLP-1 users reported unusual hair loss compared with 34% of the control group. After starting treatment, 26% of GLP-1 users reported hair loss or thinning, compared with 12% of those not taking the drugs. Loss of hair volume was also more common, affecting 42% of GLP-1 users compared with 19% of those not taking them, the study found. Scalp redness was reported around three times as frequently in GLP-1 users, and hair loss among users was typically accompanied by inflammatory scalp symptoms such as itching, scaling or redness, the researchers noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "This suggests that what is happening on the scalp may go beyond the classical shedding seen after rapid weight loss and involve an inflammatory component," said study author Dr. Bruno Halioua, a Paris dermatologist, in the release. "Scalp inflammation was the rule rather than the exception, which clinicians do not currently look for and which may be treatable." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Halioua stated that patients experiencing these symptoms should consult a physician rather than stopping their medication, noting that the changes are typically not serious enough to warrant discontinuing treatment. The authors emphasized that because both studies relied on patient-reported data and looked at them at a single point in time, the findings only show associations and cannot prove that the medications caused these effects. The research team is planning further studies to determine when these changes occur, what may be causing them and whether they go away over time. title: Cost of Iran war explodes as toll on US air fleet nearly doubles
description: At least 81 U.S. military aircraft have been lost or damaged in the Iran war, including F-15E Strike Eagles, an F-35A and dozens of MQ-9 Reapers.
content: The U.S. military has lost or sustained damage to at least 81 aircraft during the war with Iran — nearly double the number identified five months ago, according to a new government analysis that warns replacing some of the critical vehicles could strain the military's ability to meet demands elsewhere. The aircraft include some of the military's most advanced fighters and critical support aircraft, as well as dozens of drones, the Congressional Research Service (CRS) noted in its report. The tally is nearly double the 42 aircraft CRS identified in May as lost or damaged, although the increase partly reflects additional information becoming publicly available and does not mean all 39 additional aircraft were lost or damaged since that assessment. ALARMING MISSILE REPORT DRAWS FORCEFUL RESPONSE FROM TRUMP AS IRAN WAR TESTS AMERICA’S ARSENAL CRS, a nonpartisan arm of the Library of Congress that provides research and analysis to lawmakers and congressional committees, identified 12 F-15E Strike Eagles, an F-35A Lightning II, seven KC-135 refueling tankers, an E-3 Sentry airborne warning-and-control aircraft and 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones among those lost or damaged since Operation Epic Fury began on Feb. 28, 2026. The body also warned that losses among aging, high-demand aircraft could create capability gaps or increase risk in other theaters, while production constraints and competing demands could affect how quickly the military rebuilds its capacity. The 81 aircraft were lost or damaged through a mix of Iranian attacks, enemy fire, friendly fire, accidents and aircraft deliberately destroyed during rescue operations — though some damaged aircraft have since returned to service. "We do not comment on reports from outside organizations or non-DOW battle damage assessments," a Department of War official told Fox News Digital when reached for comment on the report. HOW IRAN ATTACKS ARE FORCING THE PENTAGON TO RETHINK ITS DECADES-OLD MIDDLE EAST BASE STRATEGY CRS cautioned that the tally could continue to change because of classification, ongoing combat operations and questions of attribution. The new accounting comes more than eight months into a war that has strained U.S. weapons stockpiles and raised broader questions about how quickly the defense industrial base can replenish what the military is using. A Pentagon inspector general report last month found that the U.S. had spent an estimated $22.3 billion on munitions through June alone and warned of "strategic inventory shortfalls." The Congressional Budget Office estimated in September that replacing equipment lost through Aug. 1 could cost between $1.9 billion and $3.3 billion, depending on the Department of War's replacement plans. Drones account for more than half of the aircraft in the new tally. At least 45 MQ-9 Reapers have been lost in operations against Iran, according to CRS, along with three MQ-1 drones and an MQ-4C Triton. But while drones drive much of the raw number, the report also points to losses and damage among scarcer, harder-to-replace aircraft. An E-3 Sentry was damaged in an Iranian attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia in March and was later reported to have sustained a "direct hit." CRS specifically flagged the aging and limited E-3 fleet as an example of how losses among high-demand aircraft could create capability gaps or increase risks for U.S. forces in other theaters. Iranian attacks have also inflicted damage on U.S. aircraft while they were on the ground at bases across the region. Five KC-135 tankers were reportedly damaged at Prince Sultan Air Base in March, while eight F-15Es sustained light damage during an Iranian strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan in September. The eight fighters were returned to service. At least 18 U.S. service members have also died since the war began, though the Pentagon has divided those deaths between Operation Epic Fury and a separate category for the renewed fighting that began in July. PENTAGON RACES TO BUY 10X MORE MISSILES AS IRAN WAR DWINDLES ARSENAL, THREATENS READINESS FOR CHINA AGGRESSION Other losses illustrate the dangers surrounding recovery operations. Two MC-130J Commando II special operations aircraft were intentionally destroyed while supporting efforts to rescue the crew of a downed F-15E, while an HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopter was damaged during the same rescue effort. Four AH-6 Little Bird helicopters were later destroyed by U.S. forces during separate rescue operations, according to the Defense Department inspector general. Three F-15Es were destroyed by friendly fire over Kuwait in the opening days of the war, while an F-35A was later damaged by Iranian ground fire over Iran. The report also pointed to a broader operational question: whether the losses reflect changes in Iran's capabilities that require the U.S. to adjust its equipment, tactics or basing posture.

title: Former CIA officer warns against trusting Russia's account of mysterious death in Siberia
description: Glenn Corn, a former CIA officer, explains why Vladimir Putin's Kremlin cannot be trusted on the Russian researcher's death, citing past coverups.
content: Glenn Corn, a former CIA officer, told Fox News Digital that Russia’s decades-long history of deception makes it difficult to trust the Kremlin’s account of a possible disease outbreak following the death of a 28-year-old researcher at a facility containing dangerous pathogens. Darya Shipilova, who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, got sick near the end of September. After unconfirmed reports that Shipilova died from pneumonic plague were shared far and wide on social media, Russian authorities pushed back, saying she died on Oct. 2 from "pneumonia of unknown etiology" and that testing found no evidence she had been infected with a pathogen from her lab. Yet the Russian government’s past messaging around major crises has left Corn and others wary of its official account. RUSSIAN RESEARCHER'S MYSTERY DEATH COULD BE ‘FAR WORSE’ THAN THE PLAGUE, FORMER SENIOR TRUMP OFFICIAL WARNS "This is what the challenge is, because they have the history of the 'boy who cried wolf syndrome.' They have this history of being deceitful. It's very hard to believe what they're saying," said Corn, a professor at the Institute of World Politics, a graduate school in Washington, D.C. Corn, who is fluent in Russian and spent more than 20 years overseas during his intelligence career, gave several examples of elaborate Russian coverups, including the 1979 anthrax outbreak that killed at least 64 people in the Soviet city of Sverdlovsk, now called Yekaterinburg. For years, the Soviet Union claimed that the deaths were caused by intestinal anthrax from tainted meat, according to PBS' "Frontline." It wasn't until 1992 that President Boris Yeltsin finally admitted the illnesses were the result of military activity at a nearby biological weapons facility. This dedication to deception, Corn said, remains a feature of the current government under President Vladimir Putin. AMB. GORDON SONDLAND: THE GODFATHER TEST -- HOW PUTIN TURNS EVERY ATTACK INTO A MYSTERY—AND GETS AWAY WITH IT Corn pointed to the Kremlin’s past denials of ties to the Wagner mercenary group, whose murky relationship with the state allowed its fighters to advance Moscow’s interests overseas while Russian officials maintained plausible deniability. Putin later acknowledged that the group had been fully financed by the Russian state. "This goes to the strategic culture of leadership in Russia... and their fear of the rest of the world, and their belief that they have to deceive everybody because everybody is deceiving them," Corn said. Corn said this style of narrative control is also characteristic of China, which remains under Communist Party rule, while modern Russia inherited many of the institutions and governing practices of the communist-led Soviet Union. For example, China faced criticism in the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic for withholding or delaying the release of critical information about the emerging virus, which has gone on to kill more than 7 million people globally. TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR "In both systems, people are disincentivized to tell the truth when there's a bad story," Corn said. "Nobody wants to actually say that we have a real problem and we need to deal with it because they're afraid that it will cost them their jobs, their lives, their freedom." With that history in mind, Corn said U.S. officials should not simply take Moscow at its word on Shipilova’s death, but independently verify its claims and closely monitor for any signs of a wider outbreak. So far, there is no sign that Shipilova’s illness has spread. Russia's health watchdog said Tuesday that 60% of the roughly 200 people quarantined after potentially coming in contact with Shipilova have been released. It added that no cases of plague have been found. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The World Health Organization (WHO) said Tuesday that the case presented a "very low" risk outside Russia, The Associated Press reported. That same day, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on social media that the global health agency is in contact with Russian health authorities and has requested more information "to clarify the cause of the severe pneumonia" that killed Shipilova. President Donald Trump also told reporters on Tuesday that he has a call scheduled with Putin about the case "very soon," adding that the U.S. is already in "very deep discussions" with Russia.

title: Mall of America terror plot thwarted; suspected ISIS sympathizer arrested, FBI announces
description: Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed a mass shooting at the Mall of America before buying an AK-47 rifle.
author_name: Stephen Sorace, Brittany Miller, Bill Melugin
content: An 18-year-old Minnesota man who allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America was arrested after buying an AK-47-style rifle, magazines and ammunition from an undercover FBI employee, according to newly filed federal court documents. Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud had allegedly spent months discussing his desire to carry out an attack, telling an FBI confidential source in September, "I can’t wait until I kill kuffar man. October 24 is the day insha Allah," according to an affidavit filed in federal court in Minnesota. When the source later asked why he had chosen Oct. 24, Mohamud allegedly pointed to a "Hmong Arts Celebration" at the Mall of America, saying it would have "a lot of people," the affidavit states. WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS "Mohamud met with someone he believed to be a loyal member of ISIS to attempt to purchase an AK-47 rifle, knowing it would be used in a felony or federal crime of terrorism," Special Agent in Charge, FBI Minneapolis Field Office, Christopher Dotson said at a press conference Wednesday. "Mohamud planned to use the gun he bought in a high-traffic public area just a few weeks' time in support of a designated foreign terrorist organization." Mohamud is now charged with knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition while knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony and federal crime of terrorism. Mohamud, who was born in the United States and is a U.S. citizen, is the son of Somali nationals who later became naturalized U.S. citizens, multiple federal law enforcement sources told Fox News Digital. His parents arrived in the U.S. through a New York City airport in 2000, according to the sources, though it remains unclear whether they entered on visas or as refugees. His mother became a naturalized citizen in 2010 and his father in 2017. FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital in a statement that the suspect "allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans." "Once again, this FBI is moving more effectively than we ever have before at stopping terrorists before they can attack Americans – with over 1,100 individuals prevented from conducting attacks, over 4,000 foreign terrorist organization related disruptions and arrests, a 38% increase, and more," Patel said. "We will continue to use every resource we have to detect and prevent acts of terrorism and wipe out their networks all over the country. Thank you to FBI Minneapolis, who did an outstanding job in the investigation and likely saved lives." President Donald Trump also praised the FBI’s handling of the case while speaking to reporters Wednesday. "I did hear about it. And they did a great job. The FBI did a great job," Trump said.Mohamud appeared before a federal judge in Minnesota on Wednesday for an eight-minute initial hearing, according to federal court records. U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright ordered Mohamud temporarily detained. He is scheduled to return to court Monday, Oct. 19, at 11 a.m. ET for a preliminary and detention hearing. ISIS-K MILITANT SENTENCED TO 20 YEARS FOR SUPPORTING DEADLY 2021 ABBEY GATE BOMBINGMinnesota Gov. Tim Walz thanked law enforcement for acting quickly to stop the alleged plot, saying federal authorities should remain focused on preventing similar threats. "Grateful for the swift and professional action to keep Minnesotans safe," Walz wrote in an X post. "This is exactly the kind of threat we need federal law enforcement working to prevent, and the kind of work that should remain a priority as we navigate a more dangerous world." Mall of America said the news was unsettling for its guests, tenants, employees and the broader community while thanking the FBI and other law enforcement agencies for disrupting the alleged threat. "We are grateful to the FBI and its law enforcement partners for their vigilance and extraordinary investigative work in identifying, disrupting and removing this threat and protecting the community we all share," Mall of America said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. AMY KLOBUCHAR CALLS FOR MAJOR ANTI-TERRORISM INVESTMENTS AFTER ALLEGED MALL OF AMERICA PLOT The mall added that safety and security remain its highest priority and said it would continue working closely with local, state and federal law enforcement. House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., also praised the FBI’s handling of the case Wednesday after Fox News senior congressional correspondent Aishah Hasnie asked him about the alleged plot during a news conference in Mason, Michigan. "The thwarting of the planned terrorist attack in the Mall in Minnesota today was another example of how important law enforcement is to us," Johnson said. Johnson pointed to cooperation among federal, state and local law enforcement and argued that agencies need adequate funding and public support. "What would happen if that 18-year-old had made it into that mall? It would have been a very different outcome. So we applaud everybody involved in that investigation, all the great law enforcement officers who did their job, and we pray their safety for their safety and that they continue to do that work around the country," Johnson said. The arrest capped an FBI investigation that began around December 2024 and eventually involved a confidential human source who communicated extensively with Mohamud over encrypted messaging and social media platforms, according to investigators. Those conversations initially centered on Mohamud allegedly wanting to leave the United States and join al-Shabaab, the Somalia-based terrorist organization. In May, he allegedly told the source he was "so excited to make hijrah" and wanted to go to Somalia, get married and "fight the enemies of Allah." He said he planned to work for about six weeks to save $2,000 for a plane ticket, according to the affidavit. By July, however, investigators say his plans had changed. Mohamud allegedly told the source he did not have enough money to travel to Somalia and wrote, "so i will do attack here." He later discussed buying two pistols online and going to the Mall of America or the Minnesota State Fair around Christmas, according to the affidavit. DENVER MAN'S ESCAPE EXPOSES CHILLING TREN DE ARAGUA KIDNAPPING PLOT THAT LANDS TRIO IN PRISON Mohamud allegedly discussed attacking the Mall of America with an assault rifle and told the source he could "drive straight to the crowded place and start shooting." In September, investigators say he also sent the source a selfie-style video pledging allegiance to ISIS and its leader. The FBI then arranged an undercover weapons transaction. On Sept. 25, the source told Mohamud a "brother" could sell him an AK-style rifle, magazines and ammunition, and Mohamud allegedly indicated he wanted the weapon to be fully automatic. On Tuesday, Mohamud met the supposed ISIS-connected "brother" — actually an undercover FBI employee — and allegedly paid $600 for an AK-47-style rifle, four magazines and roughly 200 rounds of ammunition. The rifle had been rendered inoperable, though the ammunition was live. During the meeting, Mohamud allegedly said he planned to carry out a shooting at a "kuffar festival" at the Mall of America. title: Coco Gauff eliminated from tournament after 'draining' racial commentary, match controversy

I did not make them, I think it’s weird i’m getting hate for following the rules," Gauff said in a separate social media post. title: Israel amb torches Mamdani Oct 7 post: 'Like turning September 11 into a day of mourning for al-Qaeda'
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's Oct. 7 anniversary post accused Israel of genocide, drawing a sharp rebuke from UN Ambassador Danny Danon.
