title: Elon Musk lands new Trump administration role shaping future of American warfare
description: Elon Musk will co-lead Project Meridian with Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich to map future warfare domains and military technologies for the Pentagon.
content: Elon Musk is taking on a new role in the Trump administration, this time helping the Pentagon determine which weapons and technology American troops will need to fight the wars of the future. War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that Musk will co-lead Project Meridian, a new Pentagon initiative tasked with looking years and even decades ahead to identify emerging domains of warfare and the capabilities the U.S. military will need to dominate them. Musk, the former leader of the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), will lead the effort alongside defense tech billionaire Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich under the direction of War Department Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael. EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH TO DOUBLE CUTS TO GENERALS, ADMIRALS IN MAJOR PENTAGON SHAKEUP "The best forecasters of future conflict do not solely reside inside the Pentagon," Hegseth said during his State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico. "There are obvious biases and risks to asking ourselves to both ask the questions and answer them." Hegseth said the initiative would begin immediately, and he would meet with Musk, Luckey and Gingrich in a secure site just 200 yards from the stage after his speech. Project Meridian will have 120 days to "ruthlessly map the trajectory of wars, domains and technologies," culminating in a public rollout of its findings and a classified annex. Hegseth described a sweeping mandate that stretches "from under the Earth to beyond the moon." Rather than developing new military strategies or policies, the group will seek to identify "the domains that we must conquer and capabilities we must master" and focus on "discovering, developing and fielding" weapons and systems that could be needed by future generations of American troops. Musk and Luckey enter the effort with firsthand experience developing technology for the U.S. military. Musk's SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor, while Luckey founded Anduril Industries, a defense technology company specializing in autonomous weapons and other advanced military systems. Their industry experience positions both men to bring an unusually close view of emerging technology and the modern battlefield to the Pentagon's long-range planning. It could also raise potential conflict-of-interest questions as executives whose companies compete for defense business help identify the capabilities and technologies the military should pursue. BATTLEFIELD ROBOTS OPEN NEW FRONT IN INNOVATION WAR WITH MAJOR US ADVERSARY Meridian was one piece of a broader push announced by Hegseth Wednesday to remake the military around autonomous warfare and rapidly emerging technology. Hegseth announced the creation of Autonomous Warfare Command, or AUTOWARCOM, a new four-star combatant command with what he described as "service-like authorities" to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the joint force. The War Department will also begin phasing in new occupational frameworks across the military departments to create dedicated career paths for what Hegseth called a new generation of "autonomous warfighters." "We should have been thinking about Autonomous Warfare Command ten years ago," Hegseth said, explaining that Meridian is intended to look far enough ahead to anticipate the next technological transformation before the military falls behind. The announcements came during the second iteration of what the War Department has dubbed Hegseth’s annual State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico. The setting was the same as last year, but the audience was markedly different. Hegseth summoned generals, admirals and other senior military leaders from around the world to Quantico for his first address, where he laid out sweeping changes to military standards, personnel and what he called the "warrior ethos." This time, Hegseth addressed a younger generation of military leaders, including top-performing E-6 enlisted service members and O-3 officers from across the force. He called them the military’s "current and future leaders on the front lines" and said the address would become an annual opportunity to assess the state of the force and lay out his vision for its future. Hegseth used Wednesday’s speech to unveil six new initiatives, ranging from the military’s embrace of autonomous warfare to an effort to make U.S. bases and defense supply chains less vulnerable to foreign disruption. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The secretary also used the address to deliver some of his most pointed rhetoric yet about his effort to reshape the culture of the military and about the news media. "We are no longer the woke department or the weak department," Hegseth said. "No fatties, no trainees, no weirdos, no beardos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors." Hegseth later accused some journalists of engaging in "partisan activism" that jeopardizes military operations and service members, calling such reporting "fundamentally anti-American." "It’s sick. It’s a national betrayal. It’s treason, actually," Hegseth said.

title: Watchdog group warns Pittsburgh high school course recruits students into political activism
description: The North American Values Institute claims Pittsburgh Public Schools' ethnic studies course teaches political activism, not history, citing units on challenging systems of power.
content: As the school year kicks off, education is under the microscope, with parents and organizations scrutinizing curricula. Now, the North American Values Institute (NAVI), a nonpartisan education watchdog, is sounding the alarm over Pittsburgh Public Schools' (PPS) new ethnic studies course for high school seniors. The organization claims that rather than focusing on teaching students history, the course appears to be a how-to guide for political activism. "I have a simple philosophy: Teach kids about revolutions, don't recruit them to be in one," NAVI Pennsylvania Director Steve Rosenberg told Fox News Digital. Referring to PPS documents that NAVI obtained through right-to-know requests, Rosenberg expressed concerns over how the school was planning to approach the course topic and the lack of counterarguments in provided class materials. NAVI sent the documents to Fox News Digital. CONTROVERSIAL TEACHER TRAINING TARGETS PARENTAL AUTHORITY AS OPPRESSION, EDUCATION EXPERT WARNS When asked to confirm if the documents were in fact accurate and current, Dr. Ann Fillmore, executive director K-12 Literacy, Humanities and Library Services for Pittsburgh Public Schools, said in a statement, "We provided the organization unit overview — not full curriculum. Some of the documents included, are individual course syllabi created by teachers." Fillmore also noted that some of the individual teacher syllabi were specifically for a College in High School (CHS) dual-enrollment course affiliated with LaRoche University, rather than curriculum written by the district. "In addition, the CHS [College in High School] course syllabus are [sic] included and that course is not created through Pittsburgh Public Schools C&I [Office of Curriculum & Instruction]," Fillmore said, adding that the district's unit overviews have been revised for the 2026–2027 school year. According to district documents, the course is divided into five units: Each unit is set to be taught over the course of several weeks. The first two units of the course lay the foundational groundwork, focusing on identity formation, cultural heritage and historical migration. NAVI's concerns are primarily focused on the latter half of the course, starting with Unit 3. BLISTERING REPORT EXPOSES HOW NATIONAL K-12 GROUP'S DEI AGENDA IS TRICKLING DOWN TO LOCAL SCHOOLS In Unit 3, students are asked to explore how systems of power are built and how they can "challenge, resist and restructure" those systems in order to make them "equitable for all." The learning outcomes for Unit 3 include explaining "how systems of power give privilege to specific groups of people," discussions on how those systems "develop inequities," and examining "strategies of marginalized communities and groups to shift power dynamics within societies and articulate visions of alternative social systems." Meanwhile, in Unit 4, students are asked to explore the limiting factors of systems of power, such as how they can impact access to opportunities and resources and how people make "choices about their lives." The learning outcomes include having students "develop and propose strategies to advocate for change within social systems that create inequitable outcomes for different ethnic groups." "Those are very different from just learning about what people have gone through and [their] journey through this country," Rosenberg said of the third and fourth units. In Unit 5, students are instructed to take what they have learned and put it into action. The learning objectives state that students are to "develop an action plan, including a clear problem, goal, and steps" and to "develop and communicate solutions to community issues relating to race and diversity." The students are instructed to work on their plan with others within the school or the community. FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS In the statement provided to Fox News Digital, Fillmore refuted NAVI's characterization of the course, calling it "inaccurate" and emphasizing that the curriculum is designed to teach civic reasoning, not political activism. "We don’t train students — it is disrespectful to what the education institution is — we want them to develop their own original ideas, understandings of history, and solutions to problems, based on the principles of inquiry-based learning and National Council for the Social Studies (NCSS) College, Career, and Civic Life (C3) Framework," Fillmore's statement read. Addressing units 3 and 4, Fillmore said that they are grounded in the National Council for the Social Studies (NCSS) C3 Framework and are meant to "promote engaged and active citizenship by helping students identify community issues, investigate them through research, evaluate potential responses, and consider how communities work together to address challenges." NAVI's concerns go beyond the debate over political activism, with the group objecting to how the course addresses Jewish identity and antisemitism. Unit 1 of the CHS syllabus includes readings on Whiteness and privilege, as well as Eric Goldstein's "The Price of Whiteness: Jews, Race, and American Identity." Rosenberg argued that filtering Jewish identity through theories of privilege misrepresents the Jewish experience. "There is no counter reading to that, that would show that Jews have been one of the two most oppressed people probably in the history of this country, in every country that the Jews have ever been, kicked out everywhere they've ever been," Rosenberg told Fox News Digital. "So, just to show because this one person that wrote this book or the teacher that's teaching this curriculum thinks that Jews are the oppressor is not OK. They can have that opinion, but show a second, a counter narrative, so that you can take the material to the students, read both, and then make their own determination." However, Fillmore rejected the claim, saying that the course does not characterize specific groups as "oppressor" or "oppressed." "Ethnic Studies intentionally avoids reducing individuals or groups to simplistic categories such as 'oppressor' and 'oppressed' because history, identity, and lived experiences are far more complex," Fillmore said. "Jewish history, culture, resilience, and contributions are embedded throughout the curriculum. Students learn about the long-standing presence and experiences of Jewish Americans, including the challenges they have faced and the ways Jewish communities have preserved identity, culture, and collective memory across generations," Fillmore added, noting Pittsburgh's local connection with antisemitism after the 2018 attack at the Tree of Life synagogue. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Fillmore also disagreed with NAVI's concerns about the curriculum not presenting counter narratives, saying that it "does not reflect how the course is designed or taught." She noted that a "core principle of the course is inquiry-based learning" and that teachers pull from several sources, including primary and secondary sources, oral histories, literature and more when facilitating discussions. For Rosenberg and NAVI, the central concern about how the schools will handle the course remains, particularly when it comes to the perspectives included in the class. He argues that students may not feel comfortable raising counterpoints of view. "If the teacher who's standing up in front of the room is telling you this is the way it is, it is very hard for young people to have a counter-narrative, to have any kind of other opinion, because they're afraid they're going to not get a good grade, or they are going to be bias against them from other people," Rosenberg told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Rosenberg is urging parents to be thorough and go through course materials. He said parents need "to know how to ask the right questions" when it comes to what their children are hearing in the classroom.

title: South Carolina mom accused of knife attack on young children; 6-year-old may lose arm: sheriff's office
description: Taylor Gosnell allegedly stabbed her two children approximately 50 times in their South Carolina home before her 6-year-old called his grandmother.
content: A South Carolina boy’s call to his grandmother saying he was hungry led authorities to a home where investigators say his mother had stabbed him and his younger sibling dozens of times, leaving both children with severe injuries. Taylor Gosnell, 35, was charged with two counts of attempted murder after allegedly attacking her children, ages 6 and 3, inside their Spartanburg County home during the overnight hours before they were discovered Saturday, according to authorities. title: Enes Kanter Freedom speaks out on A'ja Wilson playoff incident with Fever fan, after Natasha Cloud encounter
description: Enes Kanter Freedom says the WNBA should suspend the Las Vegas Aces star after she left the court to confront an Indiana Fever fan in the playoffs.
content: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom called on the WNBA to suspend Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson after she confronted an Indiana Fever fan during Tuesday’s playoff game. Wilson received a technical foul after leaving the court and approaching the spectator during the fourth quarter of Indiana’s 99-89 victory at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The fan had stood, pointed toward Wilson and appeared to blame her for a foul called on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. "I think A’ja Wilson should be suspended," Freedom told OutKick. "The league should hold her accountable because the fans are the ones that are paying the salaries of these players. As a player, they need to respect fans more." ACES' A'JA WILSON GETS TECH FOR CONFRONTATION WITH FEVER FAN, WHO WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BROKEN NO RULES Freedom also defended the fan, after he was the subject of scrutiny on social media and in the broadcast booth. "Listen, he did not do anything wrong," Freedom said. "He was just very passionate about the game." The Fever said arena security interviewed the fan and witnesses and found no violation of the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct. "Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses," the team said. "Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed." The man was escorted away from his seat temporarily but was later allowed to return. Freedom argued Wilson should have been ejected under Rule 12A, Section V of the WNBA rulebook, which says any player, coach, trainer or other team bench member who deliberately enters the spectator stands during a game will be automatically ejected. The rule also defines the first row of seats as the beginning of the stands. Wilson instead received only a technical foul. ENES KANTER FREEDOM SENDS LETTER TO WNBA REQUESTING REVIEW OF SKY EJECTION INCIDENT, FULL TICKET REFUND "The rules are very simple and very clear," Freedom said. "If the fan stepped on the court, he would be thrown out immediately. I think the same rules apply for players as well. "If the player steps off the court and walks toward the fans and then starts yelling and screaming, I think she should be thrown out immediately. So I think Cathy Engelbert has a tough decision to make. But I think she should be suspended for the next game." Freedom said the incident reminded him of his own confrontation with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud in August. Freedom was removed from Wintrust Arena and later banned from Sky home games after he stood from his courtside seat and took a step toward the court while exchanging words with Cloud. "It’s the same situation," Freedom said of Wilson’s confrontation. "I saw the fan. He simply got up, pointed at her, and then she just lost her mind. It was a lot of emotions, and then she was yelling and screaming. "The same thing happened to me. I simply got up, put my hands up in the air, and then Natasha Cloud was barking at me." Sky principal owner Michael Alter told OutKick that Freedom became a "potential threat" when he took the step. Freedom has since filed a federal lawsuit against the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority and the City of Chicago, alleging he was ejected and banned because of his speech and viewpoint. The defendants have disputed Freedom’s account. In terms of Tuesday's incident, Wilson offered a different assessment after the game, saying she believed the fan had stepped toward her in an unacceptable manner. "If I’m just walking because I got the foul and I’m just chilling, and if I see a man coming at me, taking steps toward me, pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said," Wilson said. "I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable. You don’t step towards me, you never point at me, that’s unacceptable." Wilson apologized to her teammates for receiving the technical foul but stood by her response to the fan. Aces coach Becky Hammon said she did not see the entire exchange but defended Wilson, saying she had never seen the four-time MVP react that way and believed Wilson felt "very disrespected." Freedom acknowledged Wilson’s status as one of the league’s premier players while arguing it should bring a greater responsibility to control her reaction. But as someone who’s the face of the league, she definitely needs to control her emotions." "I just hope that they win because the more they win, the more spotlight is going to be on the question of whether they can even define what a woman is," he said. Indiana’s victory evened the best-of-three first-round series at one game apiece. Caitlin Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds, while Wilson had 22 points and nine rebounds. The decisive Game 3 is scheduled for Thursday night in Las Vegas. Freedom said he was considering attending the game but had not finalized his plans because of a previously scheduled rally. "It will be interesting to see what the WNBA comes up with," he said. "If they suspend her, I will definitely go and cheer for Indiana. Even if they don’t suspend her, it would be nice to go and see what kind of reaction all the fans and all the players are getting." title: Trump Pentagon launches competition for America's next great military base
description: The winning state for the base site will be selected through a merit-based competition based on land, housing, schools, community support and regulatory cooperation.
content: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Wednesday announced plans to build a modern, self-sustaining military fortress, saying the site will be selected through a merit-based competition among governors pitching their states as potential locations. The megaproject, dubbed the "Next Great American Base," was unveiled during an address at Marine Corps Base Quantico as part of Hegseth’s six strategies to modernize the military. The initiative rejects what Hegseth described as the legacy approach to spend heavily on advanced weapons systems while service members live on aging bases with outdated barracks. "For too long, our military has been bogged down by the same old tired Washington playbook: spending trillions on exquisite weapons systems, while our troops live in aging bases, outdated barracks, and with inadequate infrastructure. That era is over," Hegseth said. EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH TO DOUBLE CUTS TO GENERALS, ADMIRALS IN MAJOR PENTAGON SHAKEUP "To back up our warfighters, when we bring the troops home, we won’t just reshuffle troops onto legacy posts. We are going to build them beautiful new bases from the ground up," he added. The ambitious undertaking will feature a brand-new military installation spanning hundreds of thousands of acres and housing up to 25,000 service members. "We are talking hundreds of thousands of acres with organic power generation, modern air defenses, and cutting edge technology — a fortress," he said. The installation is expected to provide first-class living conditions, high-end training grounds and essential services such as health care and child care, while operating entirely off the commercial grid with independent power sources. Hegseth added that the base will support President Donald Trump’s executive order on "Beautiful Civic Architecture," which calls for federal public buildings and military installations to be designed in timeless and classical styles. "We owe our warriors nothing less than the gold standard," Hegseth said. SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES MERIT-BASED MILITARY PROMOTIONS, TARGETS BIDEN-ERA DEI POLICIES To determine the site location, the Department of War said it is launching a transparent, merit-based competition in which state governors can pitch their proposals directly to top military leadership at the Pentagon. The winning state will be chosen based on its ability to remove regulatory hurdles and bureaucracy to speed up construction, while offering the best package of land, community support, top-tier housing, schools and other services. "The state that cuts the most red tape and offers the best package of land and support will win the historic honor of hosting the most lethal, modern, and beautiful military installation on the planet," a press release stated. Pitch deliberations will be recorded and made public to eliminate "political favoritism," according to the Pentagon. "No backroom Washington deals. No political favoritism – just a straight-up, merit-based contest to see which state will partner with us to build the most modern, beautiful, and lethal military installation on the planet," Hegseth said. title: The best hiking and outdoor spots near Folsom Field for Texas Tech at Colorado game weekend
description: Texas Tech arrives in Boulder undefeated and ranked No. 12 to face Colorado at Folsom Field, but the real draw may be the trails surrounding campus.
content: Week 5 | Texas Tech at Colorado | Saturday, Oct. 3 | Folsom Field, Boulder, CO | 7:30 PM ET | FOX OK, let's not pretend this is a marquee matchup on paper. Colorado stumbled out of its Big 12 opener with a 23-13 loss to Baylor, dropping Coach Prime's Buffaloes to 2-2 and looking like (potentially) the worst team in the conference. That's on the heels of a 41-7 blowout at Northwestern that was ugly enough for Deion Sanders to dismiss a handful of players for conduct detrimental to the team days later. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Texas Tech, meanwhile, rolls into Boulder undefeated at 4-0, ranked No. 12, and looking every bit like the defending Big 12 champs they are. So no, the Buffaloes probably aren't pulling off the upset. But the vibes in Boulder remain immaculate, and this might be the single best outdoor city on the entire schedule this season. 6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK Whatever happens at Folsom Field, fans in town for the game still get to enjoy some of the best terrain in the country. Chautauqua Park & The Flatirons Under 10 minutes from Folsom Field | Easy to strenuous The single best trailhead in Boulder, and it's basically in town. Options range from the easy 1.3-mile Chautauqua Trail loop to the legendary Royal Arch hike — 3.3 miles, steep, a 4.8-star rating from over 20,000 AllTrails reviews, ending at a natural stone arch overlooking the city. If your group has wildly different fitness levels, this is the one trailhead that can handle all of them at once. Boulder Creek Path Walkable from Folsom Field | Easy Runs right through downtown, so there's no real "drive time" to speak of. Rent a bike from University Bikes or B-Cycle and ride the paved path, or just walk down and watch people tube, fish and wade in the creek itself. The lowest-effort option on this list. Eldorado Canyon State Park About 20 minutes from Folsom Field | $10-12 per vehicle | Moderate to strenuous Boulder's rock-climbing mecca, and a legitimately beautiful canyon even if you're not the one climbing. The Eldorado Canyon Trail is a 6.8-mile out-and-back along South Boulder Creek, 4.7 stars, with towering sandstone walls the whole way. Boulder Canyon Minutes west of downtown | Easy to moderate The free alternative to Eldorado, running along the same corridor. Climbing, fishing and creekside scenery without the entrance fee — a good pick if you'd rather not pay to park. Rocky Mountain National Park About an hour from Folsom Field | Entrance fee applies | Varies The obvious star of the show. This one runs a little past our usual drive-time window for game day, but c'mon — it's Rocky Mountain National Park. Just don't try to squeeze it into a pregame window. Between the drive and the sheer size of the park, this isn't a two-hour detour before kickoff. It's a half-day minimum, and honestly a full day if you want to do it right. If you're only in Boulder for the game itself, save this one for another trip. But if you're turning the weekend into a longer stay, or tacking on an extra day before or after, this is exactly where you want to be. Heads up: Between late May and mid-October, driving into RMNP during peak hours (9 a.m. - 2 p.m. for general park access, or 5 a.m. - 6 p.m. for the Bear Lake Road corridor) requires a Timed Entry Permit reserved in advance on Recreation.gov ($2 reservation fee) in addition to the standard entrance fee. title: Cheapest Costco prepared meal costs shockingly little per serving: 'Can't beat the price'
description: Kirkland Signature Mac and Cheese from Costco ranks as the cheapest prepared deli meal per serving, while rotisserie chicken Asian wraps top the price list.
content: Costco shoppers aiming to stretch their dollars may want to take a closer look at the club's prepared meals. A new report from the food site Tasting Table estimated which Kirkland Signature deli favorites cost the most and least per serving. The outlet estimated the cost per serving using Denver-area prices, estimated package weights and the serving sizes listed on nutrition labels. Based on those estimates, Costco's Kirkland Signature Mac and Cheese offered the lowest estimated cost per serving, the outlet found, while the Kirkland Signature Rotisserie Chicken Asian Wrap with Dressing ranked as the most expensive among the meals it analyzed. SAM'S CLUB MEAL KIT FEEDS A FAMILY FOR UNDER $16 AS SHOPPERS SEEK AFFORDABLE DINNERS A tray of the mac and cheese costs about $4.53 per pound in the Denver area and weighs an estimated 3.76 pounds for a total of roughly $17 per tray, or about $1.42 per serving. The nutrition label lists about 12 servings per container. On the other end of the spectrum, the wraps sell for about $7.93 per pound, with an estimated package weight of 2.38 pounds, which works out to about $4.72 per serving. Each package contains four wraps, which the publication counted as four servings. COSTCO SHOPPERS DIVIDED OVER NEW 'SOURDOUGH' BREAD AS CRITICS SAY IT'S NOT THE REAL THING The analysis was based on one regional market and estimated package weights, which can vary because Costco's prepared deli meals are sold by weight. Prices and availability may also differ by warehouse. Tasting Table did not specify whether it evaluated every Kirkland Signature prepared meal or if it identified all the products included in its comparison. It also noted that nutrition label serving sizes may not reflect how much customers actually eat in a single sitting. COSTCO FOOD COURT ITEM PACKS MORE PROTEIN THAN ANYTHING ELSE ON THE MENU, BUT THERE'S A CATCH In a Reddit community dedicated to mac and cheese, users debated the Kirkland Signature offering. Despite being among the cheapest ready-made options, according to Tasting Table, one user said, "Never found these to be worth the cost." Another person, however, called the mac and cheese "better than 90% of the ready-made out there," while others suggested adding breadcrumbs, bacon or extra seasoning. In a Reddit forum dedicated to Costco, users were also split over the wraps. title: Unearthed clip exposes the Talarico comment that triggered backlash from parents
description: James Talarico, the Democratic Texas U.S. Senate candidate, dismissed parents' concerns about pornography in schools as a "conspiracy theory" at a 2022 hearing.
content: James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas, once dismissed public outcry about explicit material in Texas public schools as a kind of "conspiracy theory" at a July 2022 hearing on education. "We’re going to spend hours hearing bills that are just kind of conspiracy theory-driven and kind of kooky stuff. And we’re going to hear some of that today, I think, in the public testimony — not the invited testimony, but the public testimony," Talarico said then as a member of the Texas House of Representatives. The resurfaced moment adds to the pile of past statements dealing with gender, immigration and law enforcement, complicating the political calculus for Talarico as he aims to convince voters in Texas that, even as a Democrat, he could represent a Republican-leaning constituency in the Lone Star State. TED CRUZ, CONSERVATIVES RESPOND AFTER TALARICO CRITICIZES BIBLE-RELATED EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS AS 'PROPAGANDA' At the time of the 2022 hearing, many parents were raising concerns about news that schools and libraries across the country were featuring explicit materials that bordered on pornography. In particular, an Ashland, Ohio, board meeting made news after a group of angry parents highlighted graphic illustrations from books like "It’s Perfectly Normal," "Making a Baby," "Own Your Period" and "Puberty is Gross but Also Really Awesome," all titles featuring some level of sexual references. Similar outcries emerged in Kentucky, Oregon and North Carolina. In Texas, state Rep. Matt Krause, a Republican, sparked similar backlash when he circulated a list of roughly 800 titles he believed were inappropriate for students. He expressed his alarm in a letter to Texas school districts. "I am writing to you as the Chairman of the Texas House Committee on General Investigation," Krause wrote. "The committee may initiate inquiries concerning any ‘matter the committee considers necessary for the information of the legislature or for the welfare and protection of state citizens.’ "Please identify any other books or content in your district, specifying the campus location and funds spent on acquisition that address or contain … sexually explicit images, graphic presentations of sexual behavior that is in violation of the law or contain material that might make students feel discomfort, guilt, anguish or any other form of psychological distress because of their race or sex or convey that a student, by virtue of their race or sex is inherently racist sexist or oppressive whether consciously or unconsciously." CONTROVERSIAL TEACHER TRAINING TARGETS PARENTAL AUTHORITY AS OPPRESSION, EDUCATION EXPERT WARNS In January 2022, several counties began evaluating their own books, leading some, like Granbury Independent School District, to pull 130 titles from shelves. By July, the issue had made its way before the Texas Legislature in the form of an "interim charge," made by Republican Texas House Speaker Dade Phelan. It was a kind of exhortation for lawmakers to examine the issue, charging them to "monitor and analyze the state policy on curriculum and instructional materials used in public schools." As a part of the Committee on Public Education, Talarico received the charge but expressed reservations about its substance, making his "conspiracy theory" comment. He went on to ask Texas Education Agency Commissioner Mike Morath about the issue. "I want to ask you about curriculum in Texas, of course, critical race theory, pornography; these are the things we see bubbling up on social media that’s going to be discussed here," Talarico said. "Are you aware of any curriculum in the state of Texas that, one, bullies students based on their race or, two, grooms students with pornography?" Morath, after noting that Texas is a very big state and the issue is "very complex," gave his blunt assessment. "The answer is yes," Morath said. "We have complaints that would appear to substantiate periodic problems in those areas, arguably. I can’t tell you it’s widespread. We’ve reviewed, in some cases, materials that were made available to students that I think the common citizen would agree would be inappropriate." CARVILLE ADVISES TALARICO 'TO DEAL WITH' PAST CULTURE WAR COMMENTS IF HE WANTS TO WIN TEXAS Even after the testimony, Talarico challenged the idea that explicit materials in schools were widespread. "I would characterize as a conspiracy theory that’s being raised is that these are systemic policy problems in the state of Texas," Talarico said. Following Talarico’s remarks, parents spoke out against his characterization. "I actually drove in last night, so I’ve been here a very long time. And hopefully my comments and testimony today aren’t gonna be as ‘kooky’ as Representative Talarico had stated it was gonna be," one parent quipped. title: GOP challenger tears into Dem's 'moderate' image: 'Votes with the squad 90% of the time'
description: Scott Singer, GOP candidate in FL-25, denounces Democrat incumbent Rep. Jared Moskowitz's voting record, alliance with "the squad," and calls into question his support for Israel.
content: Republican congressional candidate Scott Singer is making the case that party, not just policy, will be decisive in his closely watched South Florida showdown with Democrat Rep. Jared Moskowitz, arguing that the incumbent’s moderate, pro-Israel image is at odds with his voting record and the direction of the Democrat Party. Singer, the former mayor of Boca Raton, told Fox News Digital that he believes his record of cutting taxes and reducing crime at the local level, combined with unwavering support for Israel, gives voters a clear contrast in Florida’s newly redrawn 25th Congressional District. "Well, it is a tough cycle, but people understand the real Jared Moskowitz, one who votes with the squad 90% of the time, voted to put [Rep.] Ilhan Omar [D-Minn.] on the Foreign Affairs Committee, has passed no bills in Congress, but traded $4.5 million worth of stocks since he's been there. This district, after redistricting, is now a Republican plus five district," Singer told Fox News Digital. GOP'S SINGER 'VERY PREPARED' TO OUST DEM MOSKOWITZ IN TOSS-UP FLORIDA RACE THAT COULD DETERMINE HOUSE MAJORITY "It takes in all of Boca Raton, where I was mayor for eight years, cut taxes, red tape, and crime, and goes down to Miami Beach, where I was born, and Fort Lauderdale, where I was raised," he continued. "Moskowitz doesn't live in the district, he's not from the district. "But beyond that, the Republican plus five, a trend in Jewish voters, of which we have 25% … in our district, moving more conservatively, and people who are opposed to socialism and communism, which he will not denounce, understand that this is a critical race for House leadership, and they want someone like me, a local leader with a record of results." Singer's business-friendly fiscal conservatism is the cornerstone of his campaign, and provides the policy framework for his priorities on Capitol Hill. "Well, it gives me the record of results one would need. As mayor of Boca Raton, not only did we have the lowest property tax rate of any full-service city in Florida, I cut the tax rate seven times. I cut red tape, 21 streamlining initiatives," he said. "I cut crime by more than 25% from what were 40-year lows. Those are a record of results that people can relate to, because we improved the quality of life, improved the job base, lowered taxes, and made our streets safer." UNEARTHED AUDIT EXPOSES VULNERABLE DEM'S HANDLING OF COVID RELIEF FUNDS: 'GROSS OVERSIGHT' Singer continued: "That's what we want right now in America. We want secure borders, not like the porous borders that Jared Moskowitz supported under [former] President [Joe] Biden that have increased crime and ravaged communities. They want tax relief, not the tax hike that he voted for. $4 trillion, including taxes on Social Security, tipped workers, small businesses and families that are hurting. Now he's trying to come around with a modest talk of the gas tax reduction. "He had the chance to vote on taxes and repeatedly has voted for higher taxes. People want a leader with a record of results. That's what I bring." While Moskowitz has carefully cultivated a moderate image during his tenure in Congress, Singer disputes that characterization. "No, he's not. He's been voting in lockstep. He's already said he'll vote for whoever the Democratic leadership is. And you can see that we'll have committee chairs like [Rep.] Rashida Tlaib [D-Mich.] and AOC [Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.], if heaven forbid, the Democrats win Congress," Singer said. "He already voted for Ilhan Omar on Foreign Affairs, despite his talking about her statements being bad, he voted to keep her in charge of foreign affairs in our country." FLORIDA GOP NOMINEE BLASTS 20-YEAR DEM INCUMBENT AS A ‘SOCIALIST’ RUBBER-STAMP WITH ‘PRECIOUS LITTLE TO SHOW’ Added Singer: "He's voted for tax hikes again … He says he's strong on Israel, but he voted against US-Israeli cooperation, when other Democrats were willing to cross the aisle. And then just a few weeks ago, he would not denounce socialism, even though other Democrats would. He's trying to have it out both ways, but his record is really Democratic, really liberal, 90% with the squad." Both Moskowitz and Singer both position themselves as strong supporters of Israel, but Singer argues that membership in today's Democrat Party makes effective advocacy for Israel difficult. "I'm a stronger supporter for Israel. I would never have put Ilhan Omar on the Foreign Affairs Committee. I would not have, like he did, voted against U.S.-Israel cooperation in the NDAA [National Defense Authorization Act]," Singer said. "I would have not voted to undercut President [Donald] Trump's efforts and our military's efforts with the War Powers Act vote months ago when the U.S. and Israel were fighting against a common enemy. "He's done all of those things because Democratic leadership requires him. And he admitted three weeks ago to Jewish Insider that he's being ostracized in his own party. He doesn't have any more chits to give in. He has to go with the way the majority is going, and that expanded squad is going to tamp out any voice he has. "In my party, support for Israel is a feature, not a bug, and I don't have to moderate my views or vote in accordance with the majority…I can be a strong supporter for Israel without reservation. Jared's admitted he can't be and won't be." Finally, while Singer said he is a strong supporter of the Trump administration's military engagement in Iran, he would like to see an end to the conflict soon. "I think we need to have a resolution of this. I think we need to emerge victoriously. We have to remember that nuclear Iran is an existential threat," he said. "We have seen how dastardly, vicious, murderous this regime has been over 47 years. Their foreign policy is death to America. They've killed Americans, they'll kill more. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "And even since this conflict started, they've started attacking other nations who weren't combatants trying to widen the conflict. They support terror across the world. It's hurt America, it's hurt Americans, it's hurt our allies like Israel, and it's hurting the free world. We need to stop this. "And I am optimistic we'll see a resolution soon. And that's a small price to pay. Even if we have some hiccups there, it's a smaller price to pay to ensure Iran does not have a nuclear weapon."

title: Sophie Cunningham sends message after pathetic finger-pointing tantrum & Sox-Yanks announcers won't shut up!
description: Sophie Cunningham used TikTok to call out the WNBA rulebook after a player entered the stands to confront a fan in Indiana without being ejected.
content: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. I don't know what's worse ... My Red Sox getting absolutely embarrassed in Game 1 against the Yankees, or the fact that we still have WNBA drama to parse through on the final day of September. Sophie Cunningham has a point Look, I don't want to do much WNBA today. I don't have it in me. It's football season. It's the MLB postseason. Hockey started yesterday. I spent all summer doing this, and I was hoping to move on ... But the girls just refuse to give up the news cycle! DETAILS EMERGE IN INCIDENT BETWEEN ACES STAR A'JA WILSON AND FEVER FAN DURING PLAYOFF GAME "You're the one who writes about it! Stop covering it, and they'll stop being relevant!" Yes, I know. I've heard it before. My job is to follow the content. And last night, the content was in Indiana, where A’ja Wilson threw a tantrum because a fan ... Well, the fan did nothing wrong. Literally. He simply pointed at her after she got tangled up with Sophie Cunningham, resulting in a foul. Wilson took it so personally, that she actually went into the stands to confront this VERY MEAN FAN. She didn't quite make it to him, but she still entered the stands. That, according to the pesky WNBA rulebook, ain't allowed. "Not trying to be dramatic at all, but I'm just here trying to have my morning coffee and, what a damn comeback year for the point," Cunningham said in the post, which was simply captioned "According to the rulebook....." Anyone else annoyed by last night's broadcast? Amazing. She never misses ... like I said, off the court. Cunningham, of course, went viral over the summer when she antagonized an opposing player by simply pointing at her. The clip exploded, T-shirts were made and Sophie's stardom took off like a rocket ship. Cunningham wasn't ejected or fined or anything like that, but that's because she didn't do anything wrong. According to the WNBA rules, Wilson did. And the league has, so far, looked the other way. Rules are for thee! OK, that's enough WNBA talk for today. We went decades — decades! — with two-man booths. And now the big thing is to stuff as many people in the booth as humanly possible, and have them constantly talk the whole game? I don't get it. God, I miss Buck and McCarver. We had it so good, and we pissed it away. Sad. OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? Stephens went in helmet-first, but he kind of ran into Dante Moore, who ducked into that hit. I did not see him put his feet out first. I saw him dive forward." Amazing. What a sequence. What analysis by USC play-by-play man, Pete Arbogast. I've never seen anything like it. Just stunning. "Well, he goes into, not a feet-first slide, more of a knee-slide. It didn't look like targeting on the replay to us." Yep. No targeting there, Pete! Just good, clean football. Textbook stuff, really. Next? Speaking of textbook stuff, how about this AI picture of Mr. Belding that Mario Lopez posted yesterday, just hours after Dennis Haskins' death? Can you spot the issue?! Incredible. How does one see that, and think to themself, "Yeah, this is it. This is the one!" What a move here by AC Slater. Poor Mr. Belding. PS: I'm super bummed Dennis Haskins died. He was our childhood. Him and Bob Saget. And now, we've lost both. Brutal. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP OK, that's it for today — and this month! We did it. title: Yankees bullpen catcher head butts Ben Rice's grand slam on the fly in hilarious moment against Red Sox
description: Ben Rice's grand slam rocketed into the Yankees bullpen, where a catcher let the baseball hit him square on the helmet without flinching once.
content: New York Yankees designated hitter Ben Rice sent Yankee Stadium into an absolute frenzy on Tuesday night when he hit a grand slam over the wall to give his club a 9-0 lead in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. Lost in the moment was where the actual baseball landed inside the stadium, or, in this case, what it hit before falling to the ground. It just so happened that Rice's grand slam in the bottom of the eighth inning was headed straight for New York's bullpen in right-center field. Baseball fans routinely see pitchers hanging out in the bullpen get under home runs and catch them as if they're pop-ups, which always makes for a cool moment, but what we witnessed on Tuesday night was one of a kind. WHY YANKEES ACE CAM SCHLITTLER IS IN THE AL MVP CONVERSATION AND COULD JOIN AN EXCLUSIVE CLUB As soon as the roar inside the stadium grew in anticipation of the baseball clearing the wall, one of the Yankees' bullpen catchers stood up, took a few steps to his right, and while it appeared he was going to throw his glove up and catch the baseball, he instead stood still and let the ball hit him directly on top of his helmet. No last-second flinch, no movement to soften the blow of the baseball hitting him in the mask, just pure commitment from the bullpen catcher. Aside from Rice launching a grand slam and going 4-for-5 at the dish to help deliver the Yanks a 9-0 victory, the story of Game 1 was the performance from New York starting pitcher Cam Schlittler. title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle blast 'extraordinarily reckless' paparazzi invasion at kids' UK school

title: Rapid weight loss on popular drugs could ‘starve’ the brain, expert warns
description: Dr. Tommy Wood warns GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy can shrink brain tissue when caloric restriction cuts off vital energy the brain needs.
content: As GLP-1 weight-loss medications like Ozempic and Wegovy continue to surge in popularity, experts warn that rapid weight loss and severe caloric restriction could deprive the brain of vital energy and nutrients. Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said the drugs' effects on the brain may depend on whether the body is getting enough energy and nutrients during weight loss. "The best way to think about this is the spectrum of what we call energy availability," Wood told Fox News Digital at Strong NY, New York City's largest annual fitness and wellness festival. "The brain is your most energy-hungry organ in the body." POPULAR GLP-1 WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DEADLY BRAIN DISORDER According to Wood, brain reserve — the physical amount and integrity of brain tissue — follows a bell-shaped curve relative to the body's energy availability. Excess energy caused by obesity, high blood sugar and metabolic disease can lower the brain's resilience by damaging blood vessels and contributing to insulin resistance. In these cases, GLP-1 medications can provide cognitive benefits by lowering blood pressure and improving blood sugar control. However, Wood noted that the lower end of the energy spectrum poses its own structural risks to the brain. Because the brain relies heavily on continuous fuel, extreme caloric deficits can force the organ to consume its own tissue. POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS CAN BECOME AN ‘ATOMIC BOMB’ AT HIGH DOSES, DOCTOR WARNS "There was a study that looked at the brains of people who ran a marathon ... because the marathon is so energy-intensive, the white matter in the brain actually shrank during a marathon because the brain didn't have enough energy … so it was eating its own white matter," Wood said, noting that the participants' brains recovered after resting and refueling. "It just shows that the brain is really energy-hungry, and it will decrease its size if it's not getting enough energy." Muscle quality Concerns about lean muscle loss when taking GLP-1 medications are often nuanced, Wood said. Some of the early "lean mass" that's lost is actually fat that had built up inside the muscles. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "So technically, your muscles get smaller, but you don't get weaker," he told Fox News Digital. "And the quality and functioning of your muscles actually gets better." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES However, risks arise when individuals taking GLP-1 medications drastically reduce their food intake for extended periods. Chronic under-eating can deprive the central nervous system of essential structural nutrients, Wood warned. "It is possible that you can end up going too far," he said. "If you're not eating enough, you're not getting the nutrients that are critical for the brain. So you're not getting in enough omega-3 fats, which we know are really important. You're not getting enough iron and protein and all those kinds of things." Protecting the brain during weight loss To safeguard brain health while losing weight, Wood recommends pairing weight-loss regimens with resistance training twice a week to maintain functional muscle mass and to stimulate brain growth factors. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Additionally, ensuring adequate intake of core "neuro-nutrients" — including B vitamins (B12, folate, B6), vitamin D, iron and omega-3 fatty acids — prevents long-term cognitive impairment, according to Wood. title: US Department of Education data reveals 1,100 sexual assault allegations against public school staff
description: Roughly 1,100 allegations of rape or sexual assault were made against public school employees in 2023-24, with 320 staff members resigning first.
content: The U.S. Department of Education released new data showing that approximately 1,100 allegations of rape, attempted rape or sexual assault were made against public school employees during the 2023-24 school year. The revelations come amid the department's ongoing efforts to protect women and children, with a focus on enforcing Title IX across the country. The figures were included in the department’s latest Civil Rights Data Collection, a mandatory survey covering more than 17,000 public school districts and 97,000 schools nationwide. Of the roughly 1,100 allegations against staff members, approximately 320 resulted in an employee resigning or retiring before any final disciplinary action or termination, according to the report. About 280 resulted in findings that the employee was not responsible, 230 remained pending and 200 resulted in findings of responsibility. Approximately 90 led to duty reassignment before final disciplinary action or termination. FORMER NEW JERSEY MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER INDICTED ON NEW CHARGES INCLUDING MANUFACTURING CHILD ABUSE MATERIAL "Parents deserve to know that when they send their children to school, their safety comes first," Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kim Richey said in a statement. "The Civil Rights Data Collection gives us critical information to identify potential failures to protect students and hold school districts accountable when concerns arise," Richey continued. "Thanks to President Trump and Secretary McMahon’s leadership, the Office for Civil Rights will continue to follow the facts, enforce federal civil rights laws, and ensure schools take their responsibility to protect students seriously." School districts separately reported approximately 11,800 incidents of rape, attempted rape or other sexual assault during the 2023-24 school year. About 460, or roughly 4%, were reported as having been committed by school staff. EDUCATION DEPARTMENT RESCINDS BIDEN TITLE IX RULE, RESTORES TRUMP-ERA REGULATIONS The department cautioned that the number of reported incidents and the number of allegations against staff are separate measurements. It also said reporting in this area is still developing. The staff sexual-offense questions were first included as optional elements in the 2020-21 collection and became mandatory for 2023-24. The findings come after the department’s Office for Civil Rights launched a national K-12 initiative in July aimed at protecting students from sexual misconduct by adults in schools. The initiative included 20 directed investigations of districts that the department said appeared to have inadequately addressed staff-on-student sexual misconduct. ed.gov CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The department said schools that fail to respond appropriately to sexual harassment or abuse may violate Title IX and could face enforcement action, including the potential loss of federal funding. Trump's Department of Education, under McMahon's leadership, has made the protection of women and children a focus. The department announced at the beginning of Trump’s second term that it would enforce the 2020 Title IX regulations after a federal court vacated the Biden administration’s 2024 rewrite. On Monday, the department formally removed the vacated Biden-era rule from the Code of Federal Regulations and restored the earlier regulatory language. The 2020 regulations establish requirements for how federally funded schools must respond to allegations of sexual harassment and assault while providing due-process protections for accused students. The administration has also directed federal agencies to interpret sex-based protections according to biological sex rather than gender identity. Trump’s January 2025 executive order defines "woman" as an adult human female and "girl" as a juvenile human female, while defining sex as an immutable biological classification. The Education Department subsequently instructed its Office for Civil Rights to enforce Title IX consistent with those definitions. That approach has guided the department’s enforcement efforts involving women’s sports, sex-separated facilities and schools’ responses to sexual misconduct. Title IX prohibits sex discrimination in education programs and activities receiving federal funding, and institutions found in violation can ultimately risk losing that assistance if they refuse to comply. The administration has also made preserving women’s sports a central part of its Title IX agenda. Trump signed an executive order in February 2025 directing federal agencies to oppose male participation in women’s athletic competition, while the Education Department has opened investigations and pursued enforcement actions against schools and athletic organizations whose policies it says deny female athletes equal opportunities, privacy or safety.

title: Former Israeli PM hails ‘heroism’ after passengers help thwart alleged cockpit attack
description: Naftali Bennett says Israeli passengers jumped into the cockpit to stop the co-pilot who allegedly attacked the pilot on a Dubai flight to Tel Aviv.
content: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett credited the quick-thinking actions of passengers and crew for thwarting what officials are investigating as a possible terrorist attack Wednesday after an alleged cockpit stabbing sent an Israel-bound passenger plane into a nosedive. "This wasn't a miracle. It was an act of heroism by the passengers and of the Emirati crew," Bennett told "The Faulkner Focus." "It's people who saved the day, people who showed courage, who didn't stand passively but took action, and I'm so darn proud to be Israeli today." UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT The original flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia, where the passengers were transferred to another plane. Those who were aboard during the incident later arrived at Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv. Bennett thanked Saudi authorities for allowing the aircraft to make an emergency landing and caring for those on board while they were on the ground. Though details are still emerging, Bennett cited Israeli authorities in detailing that the flight was traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv when the co-pilot allegedly attacked the pilot with a pocketknife and tried to bring down the aircraft, sending it into a steep descent. That's when, Bennett said, Israeli passengers sprang into action. RETIRED POLICE CHIEF HELPS SUBDUE PASSENGER AFTER ALLEGED MIDAIR OUTBURST OVER ALCOHOL CUTOFF "A couple of passengers, Israeli citizens, jumped into the cockpit," he said. "They took over the alleged terrorist, pulled him out, and they sent in the second crew that was [on] standby." The attacked pilot can be seen bleeding and wearing an oxygen mask while lying on his back in graphic footage from the incident. Saudi Arabia's Tabuk Airport said both pilots were hospitalized with injuries, according to Reuters. Israeli officials are investigating whether the incident was an attempted terrorist attack. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the incident Wednesday, praising those who jumped into action. title: Aaron Sorkin reveals why Trump is unmentioned in 'Social Reckoning' movie
description: Director Aaron Sorkin revealed why President Donald Trump's name was deliberately cut from "The Social Reckoning," his new film exploring Facebook's role in polarization.
content: Writer-director Aaron Sorkin explained why President Donald Trump’s name is omitted from his upcoming film examining Facebook’s influence on political discourse, including in the lead-up to the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot. When asked by Politico why Trump is not mentioned, Sorkin said he believed the president’s inclusion would become an unwelcome "distraction," adding that it was his decision to keep his name out of the film and that he wanted "clean hands." "I felt like as soon as we got to that scene, as soon as you saw anything ‘Trump,’ it would just become about something else," Sorkin told the outlet. "Again, I realize it’s going to kind of become about that ‘something else’ anyway. But I just like to have clean hands." 'THE SOCIAL RECKONING' TRAILER DROPS WITH JEREMY STRONG AS ZUCKERBERG IN AARON SORKIN'S FACEBOOK SEQUEL "The Social Reckoning," set to premiere in theaters Oct. 9, 2026, is a companion piece to Sorkin’s 2010 film "The Social Network," which chronicled the rise of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg. The new movie follows whistleblower Frances Haugen, who provided internal Facebook documents to The Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, which became the basis for the outlet's "Facebook Files" series examining the company's internal research and practices. The documents, published as part of a 2021 investigative series for the Journal, included internal research and findings about political polarization and the effects of Instagram on some young users' mental health. Sorkin acknowledged that the film is "political" but argued that it is "not a red-blue thing." BIPARTISAN LAWMAKERS WANT TO STRIP BIG TECH'S LEGAL IMMUNITY THAT CAN SHIELD SOCIAL MEDIA COMPANIES He said he wasn't directed to remove Trump's name from the movie but instead kept him out of it to keep Facebook at the center of the discussion. "I’m not going to deny, of course, that the movie is political. I just think it shouldn’t be. There’s really no reason for it to be," the screenwriter said. "I delivered the script and I think the next day I was in Tom Rothman’s office, and unsolicited, I told him that in that sequence we wouldn’t see any Trump signage at all. We won’t even see red hats. We’re going to see "Don’t Tread on Me," "Stop the Steal." You see American flags, Confederate flags, but it won’t be about MAGA versus everybody else, or even red-blue. It’s just going to be about Facebook’s role in the rise of divisiveness, extremism, and hyperpartisanship. So it was my choice. " A spokesperson for Meta said in 2022 that the platform was not responsible for violence on Jan. 6, instead pointing to Trump and others who promoted false claims that the 2020 election had been stolen. EX-NYPD INSPECTOR WARNS SOCIAL MEDIA LIKELY HELPED POLITICAL VIOLENCE ‘METASTASIZE’ INTO WHCD SCARE The film arrives as technology companies face continued scrutiny over social media’s harmful effects and as artificial intelligence draws attention in Washington. Social media’s influence has grown considerably in the 16 years since "The Social Network" was released and "The Social Reckoning" returns to Facebook to examine allegations about the platform’s role in amplifying political division and extremist content. Sorkin said he had considered revisiting Facebook whenever the company was in the news, but the story involving Haugen and Horwitz finally felt like a solid basis for a film. "The fact that the film has coincided with what tech people would call an inflection point is just happenstance," he said as his movie arrives to a more tech-skeptical audience in 2026. FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION "The Social Reckoning" is set to be released Oct. 9, roughly one month before the 2026 midterm elections. Sorkin told Politico that the upcoming elections played a part in deciding when the film would be released. "I don’t think this movie can change the course of electoral history," the filmmaker explained. "But these midterms are why I didn’t want to wait a year to make the movie. I didn’t want the movie to come out after the midterms because I didn’t think we’d be in the mood for it anymore." "And yeah, I thought maybe one little reminder might be helpful," he added. An insider close to the White House panned the movie as "delusional fiction." "Trump-deranged Democrats like Sorkin live in a political bubble that pathetically now encapsulates their art," they told Fox News Digital. "Judging by the trailers released, this delusional fiction looks so bad, it may even have the opposite effect of what was intended. What a loser!"
