Although he has not publicly addressed the Middle East conflict previously, Brody told the magazine that he has discussed it privately. "Put me down as thinking it's a genocide," Brody said. "Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It's awful that it's taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it's reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE "The O.C." actor's comments resembled ones made by other progressive celebrities such as actor Mark Ruffalo and rapper Macklemore, who have referred to the Israel-Hamas conflict as a "genocide." title: Sylvester Stallone reveals surprising health struggle behind his famously ripped physique
description: Sylvester Stallone revealed he became bulimic while prepping for "Rambo" and reached 2.6% body fat during "Rocky III" in a stunning new interview.
content: Sylvester Stallone is sharing some health obstacles he has faced while playing physically demanding roles over the decades. The Academy Award-nominated actor, 80, revealed during an interview with The New York Times that he has suffered from an eating disorder. While prepping for his role in the 1982 movie "Rambo," Stallone — who has authored a new memoir, titled "The Steps" — said he took pains to appear more "animalistic," drawing inspiration from jaguars and cats. MEN FACE NEW PRESSURE TO STAY ‘HOT’ AS THEY AGE — AND IT’S NOT JUST ABOUT LIVING LONGER "Then it became an obsession. Really bad. It got to the point where I became bulimic," he said during the interview. Bulimia nervosa is an eating disorder marked by episodes of binge eating — consuming a large amount of food while feeling a loss of control — followed by purging behaviors such as vomiting, excessive use of laxatives or diuretics, fasting or excessive exercise, according to the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH). "I couldn’t hold anything down. Or I didn’t want to keep it down because I became so obsessed with staying at that point of fitness, literally an obsessive body-worship kind of thing," Stallone shared. CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER CLAVICULAR EXPLAINS VIRAL 'LOOKSMAXXING' TREND AS GEN Z ADOPTS EXTREME REGIMEN The actor said that while filming "Rocky III," he reached his lowest body fat of 2.6%. The National Academy of Sports Medicine classifies body fat as "dangerously low" if it falls below 8% for men ages 20–69 and below 14% for women ages 20–69. Stallone also admitted that he took steroids during some time periods. "You have to," he said. "But you do it in a sensitive way — six weeks on, six weeks off … that also took a terrible toll." Years of injuries sustained while doing his own stunts — something he described as "very masochistic" — have also taken a toll on Stallone’s body, he said, leading to multiple surgeries on his back, shoulder and neck. Stallone also revealed that he has dealt with anxiety over the decades, recounting the first incident while watching footage from one of his films when he was 36 years old. "All of a sudden, I stood up and the hair on my neck went up and I started getting hot and I go, ‘I’m dying, this is it, I’m on my way out,’" he said in the interview. The actor said the panic attacks happened "again and again and again," often resurfacing before high-profile television appearances. As he aged, Stallone continued to experience anxiety and sometimes felt compelled to leave crowded rooms. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Brian Pollack, a licensed clinical social worker and certified eating disorders specialist at Hilltop Behavioral Health in Summit, New Jersey, said it was "incredibly admirable" for Stallone to share his experience. "There are so many examples of what can take place in Sylvester Stallone's life that have led him to moments of objectivity and body awareness," Pollack, who has not treated Stallone, told Fox News Digital. The expert suggested that a desire to maintain his success may have fueled Stallone’s rigid routines, steroid use, intense performance expectations, fear of failure, and the pressures associated with the entertainment industry. "The idea that a man enhances his appearance to remain consistent with his own public image and internal comfort goes back decades — [Stallone] isn’t the first, and he isn’t the last," Pollack said. "And through his career, one could surmise the need to be able to put all of that together and keep it consistent as he goes through the development and life cycles of maturation, not only in his brain, but also in his body." "Eating disorders continue to be misconstrued as primarily female illnesses," she told Fox News Digital.

title: The NFL has officially become flag football, fans are fuming & MLB makes a baffling call ahead of the playoffs
description: The final Monday of September brings NFL officiating outrage after a textbook quarterback hit drew a flag in the Chiefs-Dolphins fourth quarter.
content: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Final Monday of September. This is it, folks. We're a few days away from October. First full month of football just about in the books. And now we have the MLB postseason on deck?! Along with more football? How lucky are we? What a country. Goodness, we are blessed. Solid weekend of sports, right? The golf world is breathing a sigh of relief today after the fellas avoided a catastrophe yesterday. The college football world was, once again, treated to absolute cinema for about 12 hours on Saturday. I actually thought the NFL had a really nice bounce back Sunday after a lackluster Week 2 ... Except for the officiating. It completely ruined everything, as it tends to do. It was just bad call after bad call. I was stunned at what I saw in yesterday's Dolphins-Chiefs game. Stunned. Somehow, it got even worse in last night's thriller in Denver. It's just so, unfathomably bad at this point. And there is no accountability. It's disgusting. We'll dive in here in a bit. But first, welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where you officially cannot touch, breath, or even look at a quarterback in the National Football League anymore. Sad. NFL WEEK 3 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: PATRIOTS HAVE A MAYE PROBLEM, CHARGERS HIT ROCK BOTTOM AND COWBOYS CRUMBLE What else? I've got Cam Ward being quite possibly the biggest bust of my lifetime, a ballboy in Jacksonville picking a fight with a massive defensive end over a football, and how about the BS move Major League Baseball pulled this weekend? Is Manfred serious with this? What a joke. You'll see. OK, let's get this class — and week — started. It's a Monday night, after all. We've got MORE football to watch. Grab you a beer for National Drink Beer Day (solid holiday!) and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! I couldn't believe my eyes in yesterday's Chiefs-Dolphins game Let's go ahead and jump right in. No beating around the bush on this final Monday of September. So, the horrible Miami Dolphins lost to the not-horrible Kansas City Chiefs yesterday in a game that was surprisingly close. Credit to Miami for looking markedly better. Credit to the Chiefs for still covering the spread. Win-win! Miami actually had a legit shot to win this game, believe it or not. Trailing 17-10 to start the fourth quarter, the Dolphins had the Chiefs backed up into their own end zone on third and long. Patrick Mahomes dropped back to pass, and was absolutely crushed by Chop Robinson, forcing an incomplete pass. It looked like a textbook quarterback hit, which is nearly impossible to do given the ridiculous rules nowadays. Helmet to the chest, and putting the arms out on the way down to catch himself as to not land on Mahomes with his full body weight. Again — stupid rules — but Chop appeared to follow them to a tee ... Key word there being "appeared." The Cam Ward era in Tennessee is going well What are we doing here? Seriously. It's just so silly at this point. If that's a penalty, the defenders truly have no chance in this league. None. WHAT is he supposed to have done differently? And by the way, I'm not saying it was the wrong call. It wasn't. It was the right call. The RULE itself is mind-numbingly stupid. Here's Rule 12, Section 2, Article 11(b) in the NFL rulebook: A rushing defender is prohibited from committing such intimidating and punishing acts as "stuffing" a passer into the ground or unnecessarily wrestling or driving him down after the passer has thrown the ball, even if the rusher makes his initial contact with the passer within the one-step limitation provided for in (a) above. When tackling a passer who is in a defenseless posture (i.e. before, during, or after throwing or attempting a pass), a defensive player must not unnecessarily or violently throw him down or land on top of him with all or most of the defender’s weight. Instead, the defensive player must strive to fall to the side of the passer’s body, or to brace his fall with his arms to avoid landing on the passer with all or most of his body weight. title: Moms for Liberty co-founder warns parents about Ms Rachel’s political activism, ‘Not Mr Rogers’
description: Ms. Rachel's 21 million YouTube followers may not realize the children's entertainer has waded into political activism, says Moms for Liberty.
content: Parents may think they are turning on Ms. Rachel for songs, speech lessons and early learning, but the co-founder of parental rights organization Moms for Liberty says they are increasingly exposing their toddlers to political activism. "She’s using her leadership role for political activism," Tina Descovich, the co-founder of Moms for Liberty, told Fox News Digital. Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, has more than 21 million YouTube followers and millions more across Instagram and TikTok. She has become increasingly outspoken on political issues, including the Israel-Gaza war, immigration detention and LGBTQ rights. MS RACHEL CLAIMS CELEBRITIES SILENT ON GAZA WOULD ‘PROBABLY’ SPEAK IF CHILDREN ‘WERE WHITE’ In December, Ms. Rachel was named as a finalist for StopAntisemitism’s 2025 "Antisemite of the Year" designation after the group accused her of promoting Hamas-aligned messaging in posts about Gaza. Other Jewish organizations have defended or supported her advocacy for Palestinian children. Descovich said parents turn to Ms. Rachel and expect educational programming that will help their children learn to speak, read and prepare for school. MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV "She reaches 21 million viewers a year on YouTube alone, and then her social media channels have, like Instagram, I think has five million, TikTok, 10 million, and she seems to think she can divide her personal views from her influence over toddlers, but parents are tuning in to her messaging because they trust her with their toddlers, and I think her shows should all start with a warning label that says, ‘Warning, this woman has been nominated to be the antisemite of the Year in the United States,’ and they should know that before they put her in front of their toddlers," Descovich said. Instead, she said, parents may now encounter political messaging involving gender identity, immigration and the Israel-Gaza conflict. MS RACHEL POSTS SUPPORT FOR HIJAB-WEARING KINDERGARTNERS AFTER TRUMP POST "Parents turn to her to teach their children potentially to be kind and be a good citizen and love your neighbor," Descovich said. "It would be great if she would teach kids the beginnings of learning to read and concepts so that they can be ready for kindergarten, but infiltrating gender ideology with children as young as two and three and four, that's not something parents are expecting or want to put in front of their kids at such a young age." In June, Ms. Rachel visited an immigration detention facility in Newark, N.J., called Delaney Hall to be with families she said had been "terrorized" by immigration enforcement. MS RACHEL DOUBLES DOWN ON GAZA ADVOCACY, TARGETS ‘UNCANCELLABLE’ CELEBRITIES FOR STAYING SILENT In one post about the visit, she wrote, "I’m still processing being outside Delaney Hall Immigration Detention Center in NJ yesterday. I can’t say enough wonderful things about the children and families whose loved ones are inside. I can’t say enough about how this cruelty is harming and traumatizing precious children who should get to just be kids. I know if you came and played cars and drew with chalk with them and laughed and sang and saw their tears you wouldn’t want what is happening to happen." A graphic shared on her Instagram account from the account, @readlikearockstarteaching, read, "Your toddler notices race. And talking about it isn’t what teaches them racism." In her caption, ​​Ms. Rachel wrote, "Brilliant info from @readlikearockstarteaching - please follow!" A Dec. 4 post from Ms. Rachel read, "Just so you know, you are welcome in Ms Rachel’s classroom & I love you. People who are trans, gay, nonbinary, people who are Somali, people who are any religion – Muslim, Jewish, Christian or not religious, people who use food stamps, Democrats, Republicans, people who are undocumented, people who hate me." MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH Descovich said that parents should be clearly informed when a children’s entertainer uses a trusted toddler-focused platform to promote political views. "What's most important here is that parents are informed on Ms. Rachel's political ideologies because they are starting to seep into all of the work she's doing with their children," Descovich said. "So, parents need to be informed, they ultimately get to choose and direct the upbringing of their children, but they absolutely should not be manipulated or, you know, sideswiped by thinking they're putting their child in front of Mr. Rogers when they're really getting a political radical like Ms. Rachel." title: 'Wizards of Waverly Place' star David Henrie says his faith cost him agents, money and friends in Hollywood
description: David Henrie revealed on a podcast that committing to his Catholic faith cost him agents, friends and money, but said he found new friends and opportunities along the way.
content: David Henrie, best known for his role in "Wizards of Waverly Place," revealed during a September podcast interview that he lost friends and jobs after committing to his faith. During an appearance on the "Bryce Crawford Podcast," Henrie was asked what his faith cost him in Hollywood. "It was rough, lost my agents," he said. "I walked away from a lot. I turned down a lot of roles. I was like I'm just not going to do something that I think will disrespect my belief now or disrespect our Lord. I'm just not going to do it. I'm not going to go near it. And it cost me a lot. It cost a lot. I lost a lot of money. Friends, a girlfriend at the time. I kind of was stripped of everyone, everyone that I would call a friend." However, Henrie added that he made new friends that challenged him, which eventually led to him meeting his wife. FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT "I found new friends," he said. "I found guys I respected, guys I loved, that were building me up in Christ. You know, I think that friendship is like an elevator. It brings you up or it brings you down. So, I made new friends and I made friends that elevated me and that challenged me, gave me great books to read and helped form me in my faith and led to meeting my wife, my best friend now." Henrie said it had been a "great journey" and that some of the people he lost had come back into the picture. "Some of those people who left have now come back into the picture," he said. "They've gotten older. They've changed the way that they think. And I get texts from people like, 'Hey, just want you to know I went to church this Sunday.' And I was like, 'Oh, no way.' I didn't, would have never thought this person would, that would happen. And yeah, it's a marathon. It's not a race." Henrie told Fox News Digital in January that the industry was now much more accepting of faith. FROM DISNEY MAGIC TO ANCIENT FAITH: DAVID HENRIE ON WHY GEN Z IS FLOCKING TO CHURCH "Now people are much more accepting about people of faith," Henrie, who is a devout Catholic, told Fox News Digital, describing what he sees as a noticeable change from a decade ago. He said he regularly hears executives asking for "content for people of faith" because they’re "underrepresented" on screen. Henrie’s push for value-driven storytelling has become more personal since becoming a father, he said, shaping the kinds of projects he wants to champion and the kind of content he wants available for families like his. "I really wanted to find a way to use everything God’s given me to tell stories on a bigger scale," he said, explaining why he launched Novo Inspire Studios, a production company he describes as focused on "entertaining and elevating content." MARY J BLIGE CREDITS FAITH, PASTORS WITH CONFRONTING HER PRIDE AS SHE TOOK CONTROL OF HER CAREER Entrepreneur David Friedman, the head of Friedman Ventures, who has a Master's degree in philosophical theology, told Fox News Digital, "Mr. Henrie's comments reveal the natural implications of walking out your Christian faith in a cultural context that has opposing values and worldviews. What's not discussed is that the losses were due to fundamentally different understandings about what human flourishing really means." "However, there are many actors that also lose opportunities in staying true to their own versions of what is important," he continued. "The reality is that anyone that has a strong core faith or values will experience some form of rejection or cost, especially if the reigning paradigm is in direct opposition about the fundamental elements of reality, around morality and even the spiritual dimension to reality." Friedman pointed to Eric Liddell, the Scottish Olympian who chose not to run in a race in the 1924 Summer Olympics because the event was held on Sunday and conflicted with Sabbath. "The lesson applies to David and anyone in these situations, as the characters reveal that paradox of these tensions in that if Eric had run on Sunday, he would have cut himself off from the very power source that enabled him to win. That is the key for actors and anyone whose faith is central. There is really not another choice in these situations," Friedman continued. Entertainment journalist DeWayne Hamby said in a statement to Fox News Digital that Hollywood decision makers were likely a little scared of someone marching to the beat of a different drum. "I think it scares people a little bit, people who are making the decisions, that you have someone who you really can't predict," he said, responding to Henrie's comments about job loss. "They're marching to the beat of a different drummer, so they can't really predict them as much." FORMER DISNEY STAR JENNIFER STONE FOUND A LIFELINE IN THE ER AS FELLOW CHILD ACTORS SPIRALED Actor Chris Pratt said during an interview in March that success in the industry can quickly turn destructive without a strong inner foundation. "You are a man of great faith, and your Instagram bio says, ‘God first, grateful to be here.’ How has that guided you through your journey in Hollywood, a place not always known for its faith?" Craig Melvin asked Pratt on the "Today" show on March 17. "It is what it is, man. I got a belief and I go with it, and for the most part, it’s been amazing," Pratt answered. "I think, you know — there’s this Christine Caine quote that says, ‘If the light that shines upon you is greater than the light that’s within you, then the light that shines upon you will kill you.' And you see it in our business, man. You see people who have the world by the balls, and they just are so unhappy. Excuse my language." title: Deshaun Watson is beginning to craft one of the most improbable comeback stories in sports history
description: This season, Deshaun Watson's 104.1 passer rating nearly matches MVP frontrunner Josh Allen's as the Cleveland Browns sit at 2-1 in the AFC North race.
content: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has already had one of the more unusual careers in modern NFL history. After an acclaimed college career at Clemson, the Houston Texans drafted him 12th overall in 2017, two picks after the Kansas City Chiefs selected Patrick Mahomes. Unlike Mahomes, Watson played early in his rookie season. Almost immediately, he looked like a phenomenon. That October, his first full month as a starter, Watson threw 16 touchdowns, setting the NFL record for touchdown passes by a rookie in a calendar month. He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month. Watson was an MVP candidate in just his first season. Then, on Nov. 2, 2017, he tore his ACL on a non-contact play during practice, ending his season. He returned the following year and established himself as a solid franchise quarterback. By his fourth season as a starter, he had recaptured much of his rookie form. Despite the Texans winning just four games in 2020, Watson led the NFL in passing yards (4,823), completion percentage (70.2%), and passer rating (112.4). By the end of that season, there was a growing perception that Watson had moved past Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson as the one true rival to Mahomes, who had already won one Super Bowl and appeared in another. At the time, Watson said he envisioned himself and Mahomes as the "next Tom Brady and Peyton Manning." He was not alone. Colin Cowherd, Michael Vick, Jason Whitlock, Stephen A. Smith, Max Kellerman, and ProFootballTalk also made the comparison. Then his career unraveled. That offseason, 27 women filed civil lawsuits accusing Watson of sexual misconduct and assault during massage therapy appointments. The Texans sat him for the entire 2021 season. The Browns traded for him the following year, sending Houston three first-round picks. Cleveland and Watson then agreed to an unprecedented five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract, the largest guaranteed deal in NFL history at the time. Watson was suspended for six regular-season games to start the 2022 season by arbitrator Sue L. Robinson as a result of the sexual misconduct allegations. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE He made his Browns debut later that season and struggled. The struggles continued the following year, and injuries ensued. From 2022 through 2025, Watson played in just 19 games. He suffered two Achilles ruptures in that span. Statistically, he was among the worst quarterbacks in the entire NFL. In one of the more stunning public acknowledgments by an NFL owner, Browns owner Jimmy Haslam acknowledged that trading for Watson was a mistake that set the franchise back years. "We took a big swing and miss with Deshaun," Jimmy Haslam told reporters in 2025. "We thought we had the quarterback, we didn't and we gave up a lot of draft picks to get him. So we've got to dig ourselves out of that hole. (It) was an entire organization decision and it ends with Dee and I, so hold us accountable." Despite the admission, Watson remained on the roster. Ahead of this season, disdain for Watson’s play and character united nearly every corner of sports media. Between the scandal, the contract, the performance, and the attitude, Watson had become perhaps the most disliked athlete in American sports. Some outlets made that case. Few athletes can put Jemele Hill and Clay Travis on the same side of an argument. Watson did. The industry clamored for the Browns to start Shedeur Sanders before opening day. Browns fans agreed, even booing Watson as he walked onto the field during a preseason game. Head coach Todd Monken received fierce backlash after he named Watson the starter. ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky said Browns fans should consider skipping home games in protest. "I don't think they can have Deshaun Watson on the team after that interaction," Orlovsky said. "And, if they somehow come out today and name Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback, if I was a Browns fan, I wouldn't go to the game. You cannot handle a press conference that way, given the circumstances of what has transpired after they gave you $230-plus, $250 million guaranteed, and the lack of performance and availability has shown itself." Betting markets posted odds before the season not on whether the Browns would bench Watson, but when. DESHAUN WATSON GOES FROM CLEVELAND VILLIAN TO HERO IN BROWNS UPSET WIN, AS HOME CROWD TURNS JEERS INTO CHEERS Through three weeks, Watson’s career is undergoing yet another strange shift in public perception. The Browns are 2-1, in a four-way tie in the AFC North. Watson has played well. More importantly, he has played well in the clutch in back-to-back weeks. For comparison, his 104.1 passer rating is nearly identical to MVP frontrunner Josh Allen’s. Suddenly, Watson has supporters again. He has fans. In one of the biggest early-season upsets, Browns fans chanted "Let’s go Watson" after he led the team to victory in the final minutes against Carolina. His general manager greeted him in the tunnel with a hug. Just as the previous stage of Watson’s career united unlikely voices in opposition, his budding comeback has done the same in reverse. Get this: both Jason Whitlock and Stephen A. Smith praised Watson for his performance Sunday. Former coach Rex Ryan said Watson "looks like" he did in Houston for the first time since the scandal. Watson may never be a sympathetic figure. The allegations against him suggest a pattern of poor conduct, even if some details are disputed. At 31, coming off two Achilles tears, Watson is unlikely to fulfill the prediction that he would become the Peyton Manning to Mahomes’ Tom Brady. But a month ago, his career looked as if it was nearing an end, as if the Browns wants him to prove one final time he was unplayable. That's certainly how the media and fans interpreted his role this season. He has since responded, finally making something of a second chance that all players would receive. Case in point: Justin Tucker, who faced similar allegations and has not returned since. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Suddenly, Watson is no longer merely the scandal-stained, overpaid quarterback many believed should be relegated to backup duty. In a narrow football sense, he has become something far stranger: the quarterback booed by his own fans, belittled publicly by his owner, mocked by the press, and still standing. It is early, and the skepticism is earned. Still, Watson is quietly crafting one of the most improbable comeback stories in sports.

title: DOJ pleads with Supreme Court to save ban on transgender treatments in federal prisons
description: The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to enforce a Bureau of Prisons policy banning hormone therapy and accommodations for transgender inmates.
content: The Justice Department on Monday asked the U.S. Supreme Court to allow a Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policy banning payment for hormone treatments and social accommodations for transgender inmates. The DOJ is asking the high court to block a lower court's ruling so that the federal government can immediately enforce its updated prison policy regarding gender dysphoria. "BOP’s decision to prioritize mental-health treatment, while discontinuing medically disputed and unproven sex-rejecting interventions, falls well within the bounds of reasoned decision-making," U.S. Solicitor General D. John Sauer said in the DOJ petition. WOMAN OBJECTED TO TRANS SEX OFFENDER ROOMMATE — THEN SHE WAS SENT BACK TO PRISON, LEGAL GROUP SAYS The BOP issued a new policy in February prohibiting any surgeries aimed at modifying sex traits, as well as discontinuing hormone treatments for inmates not currently on hormone therapy. In addition, the policy prevents social accommodations for inmates, such as breast/buttock padding, chest binders, makeup, wigs, or undergarments that do not align with an inmate's biological sex. FEMALE INMATE SUES WASHINGTON STATE AFTER ALLEGED ATTACK BY MALE-BORN PRISONER IN WOMEN'S FACILITY Earlier this year, a group of federal inmates sued the Trump administration over an executive order issued at the start of his second term that prohibited the use of federal funds for medical treatments or procedures for transgender inmates. In June, U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth, a Ronald Reagan appointee, ordered the BOP to continue providing accommodations and care for transgender inmates in federal prisons, saying officials had not provided a serious explanation for why medical treatment for gender dysphoria should be handled differently than in other cases. JD VANCE CALLS ON DOJ TO PROSECUTE ALLEGED FRAUD IN TEEN TRANSGENDER TREATMENT The lower court found that the BOP failed to adequately consider its own past experience providing care aligned with the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH). In its Supreme Court filing, the DOJ said the care guidelines from WPATH are scientifically flawed, biased, and unreliable. LIBERAL JUSTICE HAMMERS SUPREME COURT FOR FAST-TRACKING EMERGENCY DOCKET CASES Earlier this month, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. description: Chris Simms apologized after his halftime analysis of the Dante Moore "dirty hit" debate, but Dan Dakich says the apology was wildly unnecessary.
content: After Oregon quarterback Dante Moore took a brutal hit following an attempt to slide after a first down on Saturday against USC, it started one of the most fiery debates this college football season. Then he shared something personal his dad told him in college after being announced as the starting quarterback for the University of Texas, "Christopher, when you get out there running around, make sure you get down in time, and don't take any big hits." Simms went on to say after explaining how defenders are essentially foaming at the mouth waiting for the chance to hit the QB in the open field, "You want to slide in plenty of time to keep your body safe." It was an informed, common sense statement, based on his unique, relevant experience, but that didn't sit well with many Oregon and college football fans outraged online. OREGON DUCKS QB DANTE MOORE CARTED OFF THE FIELD AFTER A VICIOUS HIT TO THE HEAD AGAINST USC Simms further analyzed the incident by explaining how hard the game is one defensive players nowadays. "You have to have a soft spot in your heart for defenders right now," Simm stated. "You gotta think, Dante Moore is 6'3" 220 pounds, he's running at you, the defender [Desman] Stephens is bracing himself, getting ready to get low to make the tackle, so yes, you as a defender, have to know in this day and age that you have to be careful with the quarterback. But I would also say, Dante Moore slide very late, and kind of put the defender in a no win situation." Again, it was informed analysis of a play that, in my opinion, too many people were framing in an unfair light, making Stephens out as a head hunter and Moore as an innocent victim that "clearly gave himself up" as Steratore claimed. Simms then took to social media Sunday and apologized to "all college football fans" saying, "I clearly did not show enough sympathy for the situation." Dont @ Me host Dan Dakich, as do I, felt that apology was wildly unnecessary. Dakich unloaded on Simms claim that he wasn't sympathetic enough saying, "Bulls–t! You're not there to show sympathy. You're there to explain the situation based on your experience." "I don't know why that's a problem," Dakich said. "This was a quarterback going full speed and slide late," Dakich stated, echoing Simms initial analysis. He was seen taunting, laughing, dapping up his teammates, and more unsportsmanlike conduct. Dakich addressed that saying, "All you have to say is that guy is an idiot and he should be suspended." title: Harbaugh brothers really love J.J. McCarthy and that's one reason he's going to the New York Giants in a trade
description: J.J. McCarthy heads to the New York Giants for a fifth-round pick after the Minnesota Vikings gave up on the former first-round quarterback.
content: Jim Harbaugh famously said J.J. McCarthy was the greatest quarterback ever to play at the University of Michigan and then boasted he was the best quarterback available before the 2024 draft. John Harbaugh, Jim's brother, apparently believes him. The New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings have agreed to a trade that will send McCarthy, a 2024 first-round pick, to play for John Harbaugh's team in the Big Apple in exchange for a mid-round 2027 draft pick and a chance to salvage their season. John Harbaugh apparently thinks McCarthy has some of what his brother predicted still in him despite rough times in Minnesota. And as the Giants are 2-1, the coach is doing what he can to win. MINNESOTA VIKINGS SURPRISINGLY DEMOTE FORMER FIRST-ROUND PICK JJ MCCARTHY TO THIRD STRING But, let's be honest. If McCarthy continues being what he's been, this ain't going to salvage the season for the Giants. Sorry to rain on your tickertape parade, Giants fans. This move is more to avoid humiliation if starter Jameis Winston gets hurt. The Vikings are trading McCarthy for a fifth-round pick in 2027 only three years after drafting him in the first round because, well, the experiment failed. They do not believe they can salvage him. The Vikings won't say this publicly. They'll say something like they wish McCarthy the best with his new team. But the truth is they've moved on because McCarthy has been too-often injured and too inconsistent when he has been able to play or practice. Lately, McCarthy dropped from the team's starter at the end of last season, to fighting for the starting job with Kyler Murray in training camp, to losing that battle, to then dropping to third string when the regular season began. When Murray missed time after suffering a concussion in the season-opener, the Vikings turned to Carson Wentz in his place. McCarthy remained a backup. That was a signal the Vikings, perhaps been most successful team at lifting up quarterbacks in recent years after they resurrected Sam Darnold's career, were waving the white flag on McCarthy. In a best-case scenario, the Giants are thinking McCarthy might even be worth a look as a starter later this season if Winston is injured or his performance falters. The long-term outlook of this trade is not that the Giants are replacing Dart with McCarthy. That's not it. title: Actor Robert Davi swapped LA’s homelessness and crime for Florida skies
description: Actor/singer Robert Davi swapped LA’s escalating homelessness, crime and failed leadership for the Sunshine state
content: While veteran actor, singer and filmmaker Robert Davi has long been an outspoken critic of California’s political leadership, its current policies and Hollywood’s cultural direction, he never really saw himself leaving the Golden State. The 75-year-old character actor, known for playing iconic tough guys in films like "The Goonies" and "Die Hard," as well as a James Bond villain in "License to Kill," may have been born and raised in a tight-knit Italian family in Queens, New York but Los Angeles became his adopted home in 1977. Like many others before and after him, he headed west to the Golden State when his on-screen career began to take off, and he grew accustomed to the California lifestyle. ZACHARY LEVI CALLS CALIFORNIA A ‘FAILED STATE’ THAT IS ‘LITERALLY AND FIGURATIVELY ON FIRE’ AFTER TEXAS MOVE But for Davi, who has also been vocal about what he sees as a political blacklist in Hollywood because of his support for President Donald Trump, there were multiple breaking points that he said ultimately led him to sell his home and leave the state for Florida. This January will mark four years since he and his family joined other Californians who left for the Sunshine State. "The overwhelming influx of homelessness in all communities, the political corruption and the waste of money by the local education agencies in Los Angeles that’s not used for students but for administration costs, and most of that goes to the political party of their choice, and the mismanagement of the LA fires were all [contributing] factors," Davi told Fox News Digital. HOMEOWNERS IN LEAFY ENCLAVES HIT BY BURGLARS ZEROING IN ON HIGH-END HOMES FOR SMASH-AND-GRAB SCORES "When I first came to LA, I could go to CVS and it was fine. I could go to a store. It was fine. Now they have gates, they have guards and items are behind lock and key because of the rampant crime," Davi added, noting, "It’s about people coming in and the acceptable aspect of going into any store and ripping off what they want and not being stopped." Still, like many who fall in love with California’s weather and relaxed lifestyle, Davi hung on to the home he loved, hoping what he saw as rising crime and political dysfunction might somehow improve. But it was the Dec. 1, 2021, home invasion and killing of Jacqueline Avant — the wife of Grammy-winning music executive Clarence Avant — at her Beverly Hills home that became the last straw for Davi. The 81-year-old was the mother of Alexander Avant and Nicole Avant, the former U.S. ambassador to the Bahamas and wife of Netflix co-CEO and chief content officer, Ted Sarandos. KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS "Why did I leave California? It was knowing this and watching this happen. It was the nail in my coffin," Davi said. "California was seeping into this s---, the crime that was happening within communities and continually encroaching into communities … a home invasion and murder by a criminal that was let go three different times?" A classically trained singer in both opera and traditional pop and jazz, Davi is known for performing the music of his idol, Frank Sinatra. He is also closely associated with Hollywood’s music community, strongly supports teaching musical instruments in schools and was close to the late record producer and composer Quincy Jones. Jones, in turn, was close with Clarence Avant. For Davi, the incident resonated deeply. Within months, he and his family moved out of the state. Davi wondered about what he considers a key question: how did California and Hollywood, in particular, get so left-wing? Davi recalled the days when Ronald Reagan was running for president, noting how hard those in Hollywood were on the actor-turned-politician at the time, but how conservatives didn’t have to hide their beliefs back then. Davi played Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev in the 2024 biopic "Reagan," which was re-released in theaters on Sept. 25. "The Screen Actors Guild (SAG) wasn’t afraid. Conservatives were not afraid to talk. Johnny Carson was fair," Davi said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You had conservatives that were big stars that spoke out and you had liberals. Since that time, liberalism has taken on another form," he explained. Fox News Digital reached out to California Gov. Gavin Newsom's office for comment.

title: Reporter's Notebook: Senate Republicans scrap early exit from Washington as midterm stakes soar
description: Senate Republicans force a test vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act, daring Democrats to block a data center affordability bill boosting Jon Husted.
content: It’s a calculation by Republicans to keep the Senate in session this week. Yes. The Senate was scheduled to meet anyway over the next few days. But the general consensus early last week was that the Senate would be done then, and those facing competitive races would be back home campaigning. Then Wednesday hit. Republicans wanted to stay in Washington. For a very specific reason. And many of them told Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., as much at their weekly luncheon. "Odds are we plan on being here next week," said Thune. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS STRUGGLES TO FIND A MESSAGE THAT RESONATES WITH VOTERS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS One Senate aide compared the Senate’s schedule to a cat chasing a beam of light from a laser pointer. But the Senate is in fact meeting. There are reasons. Most of them are political. The Senate wasn’t quite done with the bill to regulate money in intercollegiate athletics last week. And with the affordability question vexing Republicans, they really didn’t want to pass the college sports bill and promptly vacate Washington. That would be an awkward punctuation point at the end of the legislative sentence before the midterms. GOPers wanted something more substantive. Democrats might have presented that opportunity to Republicans on a platter. Before the House left for the midterms the week before last, it accentuated its session by passing the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3. Let me tell you, not much passes around here with 417 votes. Like their Senate colleagues, House Republicans also worry about voters doubting they’re addressing affordability. So this bill hit the mark for them. The legislation defrays the costs ratepayers fork out for their utility bills if they’re driven up by data centers. This forces the tech companies which run the data centers to foot the bill. Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is one of the most vulnerable Republicans on the ballot this fall. Husted’s longtime support for data centers is also dragging him down in the eyes of some voters. Husted tried to fix that. He went to the floor and asked for the Senate to pass on the spot the House bill. However, Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., objected, blocking the effort. FOX NEWS POLL: ECONOMIC ANXIETY AND CANDIDATE CONCERNS DEFINE OHIO SENATE RACE Republicans viewed that as an opening. Democrats stood in the way of passing a bill on affordability which 417 bipartisan House members supported without blinking. Senate GOPers immediately seized this opportunity as a wedge against their adversaries. And, they interpreted this as a chance to assist their Ohio colleague. "Tell the data centers we're happy to have you. But you've got to pay your own electricity. People are not going to pay for it," said Sen. John Kennedy, R-La. Republicans were already leery about the uneven political footing when it comes to AI. Even more so with data centers. Voters are not enamored with the results of the Big, Beautiful Bill, passed last summer. But dealing with data centers is more immediate and might resonate with those who soured on the Republican brand. "In Missouri, people are absolutely scared to death that these data centers are going to take all the prime farm ground of the state. And then they're going to raise electricity bills so high, no one will be able to afford them," said Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo. The official schedule intended for the Senate to meet this week. But once September hit and no government shutdown loomed, senators from both sides – especially those facing challenging elections – wanted to skip Washington and campaign back home. Yours truly asked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., why his party stood in the way of the Senate aligning with the House on that data center/utilities measure. "Was this blocked in the Senate last week by Democrats as an effort to prevent Sen. Husted from having a win in this competitive race?" I asked. "Sen. Husted's bill is a fraud. It's voluntary. No company has to do it. The bill we have is mandatory. It is much stronger and is what is needed," replied Schumer. There is something to Schumer’s argument about how muscular the bill is. The legislation says public utility regulators must only consider a standard for ratepayers. Nothing is required. Thus, there’s wiggle room for tech firms. HAWLEY TAKES AIM AT 'CORPORATE WELFARE' AFTER GOP-BACKED TAX BREAK BOOSTED CONTROVERSIAL INDUSTRY "What we're saying is that we can do much better," said Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md. "Is it a little step forward? Yes. But it's not meeting the moment. So our view is we should expand it to make sure that ratepayers aren't having to subsidize the richest corporations on the planet." But a lot of Republicans aren’t buying what Schumer and Van Hollen are saying. The Democratic objections are all about three things: Politics. An endangered GOP senator in the most expensive Senate contest in the country. And, Democrats are hoping to flip the seat in their favor. "Sen. Schumer, what he cares about is the midterm election and politics. And I don't think he cares about the substance of this," said Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas. "Obviously there's a hot and heavy Senate race going on in Ohio, and he doesn't want to let Sen. Husted have something he can talk about when he goes home." Republicans view the opportunity to turn the affordability issue against Democrats – capitalizing on Schumer’s remark and forcing Democrats to take a stand. Either you’re for affordability (especially as it pertains to the toxic issue of data centers) or you’re not. Moreover, this could boost Husted in his competitive contest with former Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio. In fact, it was the Senate GOP’s campaign arm which specifically flagged vulnerabilities for Republicans generally and Husted in particular over the summer. Thune tees up a test vote on Wednesday to dare Democrats to either start debate on the bill or block it again. That vote requires 60 yeas. So Democratic cooperation is required. Although there’s skepticism anything happens, some Democrats may vote for it. That means the Senate is on the bill. And it’s open to debate and amendments. Thune would have to forge a bipartisan time agreement to finish the measure quickly. Otherwise – by the book – this would drag into the weekend. And no one wants that. Especially Republicans with competitive races. 12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK Thune and Schumer want senators back home campaigning. If Democrats impede the legislation Wednesday, the Senate might hang around Thursday or that’s it until after the midterms. Regardless, Republicans will have engineered a vote which they can boomerang against Democrats. Or, at least help Husted and send him back to the Buckeye State with a win. While it’s not the best optic for Democrats to oppose this bill, their resistance might not directly wound anyone this fall. The reason: Democrats have a lot of chances to pick up seats. But vulnerable Democrats aren’t on the ballot. None of the Democratic Senate nominees in competitive seats like Maine, Florida, North Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, Kansas and Alaska currently hold office. The only sitting Democrat in the cycle who has a mild race is Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va. So for the Democrats, this is about playing defense. For Republicans, this is about playing offense. And the GOP is on offense primarily for Husted. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But the willingness of Senate GOPers to spend an extra week in Washington speaks volumes. It underscores how worried they are about the affordability issue. And in particular, their concern about elevating the work of Husted.

title: Americans win Presidents Cup on depth, Scheffler's complicated Sunday, and an overwhelming sense of false hope
description: Scottie Scheffler's classy putt concession and testy NBC interview defined a dramatic Sunday as the U.S. narrowly avoided Presidents Cup disaster.
content: The final tally from the 2026 Presidents Cup read 17-13 in favor of the Americans, and while the U.S. team was able to avoid embarrassment against an inferior International side, you are lying to yourself if you came away from those four days of golf at Medinah feeling optimistic or overly impressed about United States team golf. The Americans were thoroughly outplayed and outclassed for three consecutive days by the International side, but when Sunday singles rolled around, and it was 12 vs. 12, mano-a-mano, the U.S. was able to do something the International team could not: rely on depth. The average World Ranking for the U.S. team was 15.1 while the International's average was 50.1, and that differential showed when it mattered most. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. The Internationals gave away the Presidents Cup. Period. The Internationals carried a full three-point advantage into Sunday's session, needing just five of a possible 12 points to secure their second Presidents Cup victory ever, but ultimately earned only 2.5 points on the final day. If you turn it around, the Internationals lost 9.5 points of an available 12, which is tough to comprehend. TEAM USA CAPTAIN THANKS TRUMP AFTER MASSIVE PRESIDENTS CUP COMEBACK: ‘HE GETS ALL THE CREDIT’ And yes, even with the Americans having the deeper stable of players and having the advantage of playing on home soil, it's perfectly okay to say that the International side choked away the event. Ryo Hisatsune was 1-up thru five holes over Cameron Young before losing 3&2. Hideki Matsuyama was 1-up on Collin Morikawa with just four holes to play and couldn't even salvage a half point. Si Woo Kim and Jackson Koivun were all square standing on the 13th tee, and the American rookie who hasn't even been a professional golfer for 90 days at this point went on to earn a 2-up victory. Min Woo Lee was 1-up on Jacob Bridgeman thru 15 holes, blinked, and the American was standing over the Cup-clinching putt on the 18th to win the match 1-up. GOLF STAR TOM KIM GOING FROM PRESIDENTS CUP TO ASIAN GAMES SEEKING EXEMPTION FROM MILITARY SERVICE Golf is a fickle game, and while the putters collectively warmed up for the Americans down the stretch, it's fair to say that the Internationals bailed the U.S. out down the stretch. There was a sense of relief on the American side instead of accomplishment, which is noteworthy given that the U.S. entered the final day trailing by three points. Chris Gotterup earning three points as a rookie, Koivun earning 2.5 points while shouldering the pressures of being the next great American player, and the six captain's picks going 6-0 in singles were clear bright spots for the Americans. Credit is due on those fronts, but it was anything but a clean week for the U.S., both inside the ropes from players and outside the ropes operationally, which was the top objective with the 2027 Ryder Cup across the pond approaching. More on that later. Scottie Scheffler's bipolar Sunday afternoon Scottie Scheffler did exactly what was expected of him on Sunday by earning a full point for the U.S. with a 2&1 victory over Nico Echavarria. While the result of the match was never in question, that isn't to say there wasn't any drama involving the World No. 1. US PRESIDENTS CUP PLAYERS EXPLAIN HOW CHRISTIAN FAITH BUILDS FRIENDSHIPS AND PUTS GOLF IN PERSPECTIVE On the 14th hole, a fan yelled during Echavarria's backswing as he hit his tee shot on the Par 4. Scheffler immediately reprimanded the fan, but then went above and beyond when the match made its way onto the green. Already in for par on the hole, Scheffler conceded a 32-foot par putt to Echavarria. While the gesture was already classy, it also came at a moment where, if Echavarria had missed the lengthy par putt, the match would have gone to dormie, with Scheffler taking a 4-up lead into the final four holes. Instead, the concession extended the match a bit longer before Scheffler closed things out on the 17th hole. While that was one of the more professional and classy acts we'll ever see on the golf course, the same couldn't be said for Scheffler's post-match interview with NBC's Cara Banks. Scheffler did not play in the afternoon foursomes session on Saturday, which understandably made headlines. Sitting the No. 1 player in the world with your team trailing by three points was a very bold move from U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker, and one that deserves questions, but Scheffler was in no mood to provide answers. When asked following his match on Sunday about being sat on Saturday, Scheffler didn't opt to give a generic, media-friendly answer, but instead he put the question back on Banks, asking her if she wanted to talk about Sunday's match. Scheffler seems like the consummate professional and a genuinely good person – hell, he showed that on Sunday conceding the putt to Echavarria – but his exchange with Banks made no sense. He has had his moments with the media this season where he's made it clear that he doesn't have the time to answer what he sees as dumb questions, but Banks' question was the question of the weekend. Nobody wants to hear Scheffler talk about beating the No. 61 player in the world on Sunday when the only exciting thing that happened in the match was a fan shouting in a backswing. The golf world does, however, want to know details around the No. 1 player in the world not playing in all five sessions in an event his team was, at the time, being embarrassed in. Nobody is perfect, and Scheffler is just a human despite his freakish abilities with a golf club in his hand, but the old adage of sometimes you have to do things you don't enjoy applies here. Being the No. 1 player in the world means you have to put on a face, especially in a situation like this at a team event where you're the leader and are asked a totally fair question, and when you have a slip of character, it is going to be criticized. At the end of the day, Scheffler getting testy with Banks for five seconds is going to be forgotten and has zero effect on his actual job of playing golf, but that doesn't mean we can't call it as we see it, which is simply ridiculous. Americans may have delivered a heaping pile of false hope This sentiment surrounding this year's Presidents Cup was no different than every previous edition in that it was supposed to be a building block and gauge for Team USA golf ahead of the following year's Ryder Cup. The Americans got the storybook ending by dominating Sunday's singles matches, and Snedeker avoided officially being labeled the worst captain in team event history, but if anything remotely similar unfolds at the 2027 Ryder Cup, the Americans will be embarrassed by the Europeans in Ireland. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Americans will not have the luxury in the Ryder Cup of throwing their 12 players against Europe's 12 players in a three-point deficit and relying on depth to pull them out of a hole. If the Americans get swept in a session just as they did by the Internationals during Thursday's foursomes, a nightmare will unfold for the U.S. in Ireland in 2027. The United States' inability to even be competitive in the alternate shot format remains a real issue, and if it can not figure something out, it will be a long three days across the pond next year. The Americans went 2-6 in foursomes during the 2025 Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black and followed that up with a 2-7 record in foursomes against the Internationals in this year's Presidents Cup. You'd like to say that the law of averages will even things out and the U.S. will show real life in a foursomes session sooner rather than later, but they've been waiting for that to happen for years now. It's long been one of those things that, until it happens, it's tough to imagine it ever will, and the U.S. having to be nearly flawless against an inferior International team definitely doesn't change that.

title: DHS tears into MS NOW after host touts ‘anti-authoritarian’ ICE monitoring group
description: DHS slammed MS NOW for featuring activists who train "ICE Watch" volunteers and are now turning their organizing efforts toward the midterm elections.
content: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) fired back at MS NOW on Sunday after "Connect with Jacob Soboroff" host Jacob Soboroff highlighted an activist group that trains "ICE Watch" volunteers to monitor federal immigration operations and is now turning some of that organizing toward the midterm elections. During Saturday's edition of the show, Soboroff discussed reporting about activists who previously monitored U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations and are now turning their attention toward election-related activity. MS NOW's description of the episode said, "ICE watchers once alerted neighbors about the presence of federal agents, now they are protecting the polls." Soboroff’s segment featured Zachary Mueller, a senior strategist for the nonprofit States at the Core and referenced reporting from the outlet "The Intercept" about activists preparing to monitor polling locations. States at the Core has described its work as opposing what it views as authoritarianism and has advertised trainings on both ICE monitoring and election protection. NEW YORK TIMES TORCHED FOR ‘FALSE’ REPORTING ON ICE INVESTIGATIONS, OUTLET FIRES BACK DHS pointed to attacks and threats against immigration officers while arguing that tools used to track federal agents could endanger law enforcement personnel and interfere with operations. "Shame on MS NOW for promoting efforts to undermine those who keep our communities and streets safe from illegal alien crime," a DHS spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "ICE tracking apps put the lives of the men and women of law enforcement in danger as they go after terrorists, vicious gangs and violent criminal rings. "Our law officers are facing an over 1,600% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats. Further, these apps are a method to interfere with law enforcement activities and harbor illegal aliens." States at the Core said in March that tens of thousands of Americans had attended its ICE Watch training before it launched a program called "Beyond ICE Watch," which sought to expand neighborhood organizing beyond monitoring immigration enforcement. SEVEN NONCITIZENS CHARGED IN NORTH TEXAS ELECTION-INTEGRITY INVESTIGATION The organization described its mission in that announcement. "Our mission is pretty simple. Help everyday people fight authoritarianism; help people fight for their freedoms," States at the Core said. In September, the group advertised a training that sought to adapt ICE Watch techniques for the midterm elections, including documenting activity around communities and elections. DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION States at the Core had previously drawn scrutiny for its ICE-monitoring tactics. In February, co-founder Jill Garvey trained "rapid responders" to use the military-derived "SALUTE" observation method — an acronym for size, activity, location, uniform, time and equipment — when documenting federal immigration personnel. The FBI was also investigating alleged Signal groups used by anti-ICE activists to track, identify and potentially impede federal law enforcement officers. FBI Director Kash Patel said investigations would examine whether the alleged coordination crossed the line into violations of federal law. DHS has reported a sharp increase in assaults against ICE personnel. The department said 647 assaults occurred between Jan. 20, 2025, and Sept. 20, 2026, compared with 37 during the corresponding period under the Biden administration, representing a 1,649% increase. "Glorifying resistance to lawful immigration enforcement is irresponsible and dismissive of the victims and families who have suffered because of crimes committed by criminal illegal aliens," the spokesperson said. "Assaulting and obstructing ICE law enforcement is a crime and felony. Anyone who assaults law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law." title: Republicans zero in on key player accused of helping Democrat fundraising giant hide foreign cash
description: House Republicans summon ActBlue attorney Ronald Machen for a closed-door interview, citing contradictions in his prior statements on donor verification.
content: FIRST ON FOX: House Republicans' investigation into Democrats' main fundraising platform is heating up on the heels of an explosive report that raised questions about whether left-wing candidates' campaigns were raking in foreign cash. Top House GOP committee chairs are summoning ActBlue attorney Ronald Machen for a closed-door interview sometime before Oct. 9, Fox News Digital has learned. A letter sent to Machen Monday morning stated that information he previously disclosed to investigators appears to contradict other data that has been collected, specifically on ActBlue's verification standards for making sure a donor is a U.S. citizen. "On September 11, 2026, you provided a briefing to the House Administration, Judiciary, and Oversight and Government Reform Committees regarding the accuracy of ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones’s prior statements to Congress about ActBlue’s donor and passport collection processes," the letter said. "Your review appears to be nothing more than an after-the-fact sugarcoating of ActBlue’s misconduct and Ms. Wallace-Jones’s misrepresentations to the House Administration Committee." ANOTHER ACTBLUE LEADER PLEADS FIFTH AS HOUSE INVESTIGATES ALLEGED FOREIGN DONATIONS The letter was sent by House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., and House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., who lead the panels probing ActBlue. ACTBLUE CO-FOUNDER PLEADS FIFTH AMENDMENT IN CLOSED-DOOR HOUSE GOP GRILLING ActBlue is a massive platform for campaigns to raise money that's used by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and the Democratic leaders of the House and Senate, among others. Republican lawmakers have long accused the company of having lax verification standards for donors, something ActBlue has said it actively improved since the start of the GOP's probe. But a new report released earlier this month, first reported by Fox News Digital, appears to show employees green-lighting donations despite some questions about where they came from. FAR-LEFT POLITICIANS STILL USING ACTBLUE AS 88-YEAR-OLD DISPUTES DONATING NEARLY $150,000 TO FUNDRAISING GIANT Chief among the GOP's concerns is ActBlue's passport number verification. According to the report, the field only requires the correct number of characters for a U.S. passport number rather than a valid code for a donation to be accepted. The Monday letter also points to a 2024 "contemporaneous review by ActBlue’s then-outside counsel, former Biden White House Counsel Dana Remus" which allegedly found "'a substantial risk that some of the funds' raised for Democrat campaigns and causes by ActBlue 'were impermissible contributions from foreign nationals.'" Remus' review further found that "passport checks did not always happen" and were "never conducted" when donations were made using third-party fiscal platforms like Apple Pay or PayPal, the letter said. The Republican chairs said Machen's prior comments to Congress "conceded that your 'forensic' review found that ActBlue processed and accepted donations with foreign indicators even though ActBlue failed to identify a 'passport number' or 'other indicia of eligibility' for the donor. HOUSE DEM LASHES OUT AT GOP EFFORTS TO PROBE FOREIGN DONATIONS WITH STUNNING CLAIM ON MOTIVE "Nonetheless, you defended Ms. Wallace-Jones’s representations to Congress by arguing that ActBlue’s compliance and vetting policy was 'as close to 100 percent as it could be,'" the letter said. "Documents produced to the Committees undercut your assertion. These documents demonstrate that if a donor did not have a U.S. passport or a U.S. address, an ActBlue employee retained the ability to determine an 'alternative method of verifying the [donor’s] citizenship.' This means an ActBlue employee could put 'a placeholder,' including 'ACTBLUEXX,' 'in the passport number field of [the donor’s] ActBlue account.' The placeholder allows ActBlue to accept all subsequent contributions from the donor without requiring a U.S. passport number." ACTBLUE SCRUTINY FUELS NEW GOP BILLS TO TIGHTEN ELECTION DONATION RULES The letter said Machen's review was also limited to 2023, arguing it left out potentially valuable information about 2024. "As such, the review did not accurately represent the totality of ActBlue’s foreign donation vetting and donor outreach practices during the 2024 election cycle. In fact, documents produced to the Committees show that ActBlue relaxed its vetting practices twice in 2024—data that your narrow 'forensic' review did not capture," the letter said. ACTBLUE SUES TEXAS AG KEN PAXTON, ALLEGING POLITICAL RETALIATION OVER DEMOCRATS' FUNDRAISING It also charged that he disputed Remus' analysis without going into detail on how he established his own findings. ActBlue has consistently denied any wrongdoing and dismissed Republicans' most recent findings in a statement to Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "There’s nothing to see here. After we released findings of a third-party forensic analysis that completely undermined a central claim that they have made against ActBlue, Republicans are refusing to move on," ActBlue said. "Instead, they are orchestrating another political stunt before rushing out of town weeks early to go campaign. This coordinated campaign against ActBlue isn’t about the facts, or legislating, it’s about Republicans’ efforts to silence organizations they believe threaten their agenda." A closed-door interview summons is not the same as a subpoena, which is a legally binding order.

title: Largest-ever US steel plant is coming to a key red state as Trump unveils $15B investment
description: Trump announces Mesabi Metallics' $15 billion Iowa steel plant, but the massive facility won't produce its first steel until 2030 at the earliest.
content: President Donald Trump is unveiling Monday plans for a massive steel plant in Iowa that the White House says will be the largest in American history and promises to bring 1,750 permanent jobs to the state. The roughly $15 billion steel plant is touted as a major new investment and evidence that Trump's economic agenda is bringing heavy manufacturing back to the U.S. with just over a month until the midterms. It will create between 5,000 and 6,000 construction jobs during its first phase. Trump is expected to make the announcement from the Oval Office at 2 p.m. alongside executives from Mesabi Metallics, a White House official told Fox News Digital. The company plans to build the facility using iron ore from its newly constructed mine in Minnesota. SEN KEVIN CRAMER: CHINA BUILDS FOR WAR WHILE AMERICA WAITS ON PERMITS The Iowa plant is expected to produce 7.5 million tons of steel annually in its first phase before eventually reaching 10 million tons per year, according to the White House. The administration says that would make it the largest steel plant ever built in the U.S. If completed as planned, the project would represent a significant expansion of American steel-making capacity. At its planned 10 million tons of annual production, the Iowa plant alone would have output equivalent to roughly one-tenth of what the entire U.S. steel industry produced last year. The project would also create a fully domestic supply chain, according to the White House, using iron ore mined at Mesabi's Minnesota operation to produce finished steel in Iowa. But the scale of Monday's announcement also comes with a long timeline: Mesabi does not expect the Iowa facility to produce its first steel until 2030. Trump has frequently highlighted large investment commitments as evidence that his tariffs and other economic policies are encouraging companies to build in the United States rather than invest abroad. The administration has announced hundreds of billions of dollars in planned investments from foreign governments and corporations, many of which are designed to unfold over several years. Mesabi's Minnesota operation also illustrates the challenges that can accompany large industrial projects. The project traces back nearly two decades and encountered years of financing problems and missed deadlines before Essar Steel Minnesota filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2016. It later emerged from bankruptcy as Mesabi Metallics, and Essar eventually regained control. The project has since made substantial progress. Mesabi has begun mining and commissioning work at the Minnesota operation, although commercial pellet production has not yet begun. A recent SEC filing by a company that holds a royalty interest in the project said initial DR-grade pellet production is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, followed by an eight- to 12-month ramp-up to commercial production. The White House says the Minnesota operation will ultimately produce 7.5 million tons annually and create roughly 350 permanent jobs. The administration is also emphasizing the national security implications of the Iowa project. The new plant will be capable of producing high-grade steel used to meet defense-sector requirements, according to the White House, as Washington seeks to strengthen domestic supply chains for materials used by the military and critical infrastructure. "President Trump is delivering on his promise to rebuild American industry, reshore manufacturing, and create new jobs," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers told Fox News Digital. "Today’s announcement underscores the President’s historic efforts to revitalize the U.S. steel industry—supporting local communities, strengthening supply chains, and protecting our national security," Rogers said. "After decades of decline, this President is restoring America’s industrial competitiveness and securing trillions of dollars in new investment." The announcement comes as Trump points to tariffs as a tool for encouraging companies to manufacture in the United States. Trump doubled tariffs on steel and aluminum imports to 50% last year, arguing that protecting domestic producers from cheaper foreign competition would rebuild an industry critical to the economy and national security. TRUMP’S REINDUSTRIALIZATION AGENDA FACES ITS BIGGEST HURDLE — AMERICANS The policy has also increased costs for companies that consume steel. S&P Global reported that federal data showed prices for iron and steel rose 10.4% between April 2025 and April 2026, while the steel mill products index climbed 13.3%, even as domestic steel production increased. Unlike many newer U.S. steel facilities, which are smaller electric arc furnace plants, the Iowa project will be a large-scale integrated steel facility. The White House says it will be the first new "mega-steel" plant built in the United States since the 1960s. The first phase of the steel plant and the Minnesota mine together represent nearly $18 billion in investment, according to the administration. The White House estimates the first phase will generate approximately $95 billion in economic activity during construction and the plant's first decade of operation. title: The next connected device could be the shirt you're wearing
description: ShareAScan turns T-shirts into scannable digital business cards with QR codes that link to profiles the owner can update anytime they choose.
content: A T-shirt has always been able to tell you something about the person wearing it. Maybe it shows a favorite band, sports team or funny message. Now, it can potentially open an entire digital profile. That is the idea behind ShareAScan, a startup using QR code clothing to connect apparel and other physical products with digital content that can change over time. Scan a code with your smartphone, and you can see whatever experience the owner has chosen to share. That might include text, photos, video, music, a portfolio, social content or information about a business. The shirt itself does not contain a battery, Bluetooth connection or hidden computer. The technology starts with a printed QR code and the web platform behind it. So, could the next connected device actually be something you wear? Missed CyberGuy LIVE?
