Their presence alongside field marshals, volunteer coordinators and campaign organizers showed an operation with designated personnel responsible for recruitment, messaging, crowd movement and event logistics. Nearby, towering over many of the protesters, Taher Dahleh, an organizer with another partner of the People’s Forum — the Palestinian Youth Movement — moved through the crowd, grabbing a Winstone Blue cigarette from another activist, directing demonstrators and coordinating the march. He has been a familiar presence at anti-Israel demonstrations since Oct. 7, 2023, regularly hosting volunteer meetings on Monday nights at the People’s Forum for a campaign called "Shut It Down For Palestine." During the "March on Washington to Let Gaza Live!" that People’s Forum co-organized in November 2025, Dahleh slammed "tech companies" for allegedly contributing to the "slaughter" of Palestinians by selling services to the government of Israel. Between late 2023 and late 2024, far-left nonprofit WesPac Foundation Inc. gave Palestinian Youth Movement $1 million through its nonprofit fiscal sponsor, Honor the Earth, according to tax filings. The Palestinian Youth Movement still shares a post on its Facebook page from years ago, quoting a young Palestinian killed after murdering three Israelis: "You who possess arms and bullets, remember that there is an enemy so that you may put your bullets in their bodies, not the bodies of your own people." Dahleh didn’t respond to a request for comment. WATCH: Revolutionary Communists chant ‘globalize the intifada’ during NYC anti-Israel march HOUSE PANEL SUBPOENAS 3 LEFT-WING GROUPS IN PROBE OF $39M TIED TO MARXIST TYCOON NEVILLE SINGHAM The protest followed a familiar playbook that Evans, De Los Santos, Fuleihan, Dahleh, Chung, the People’s Forum and the Singham network have used since Oct. 7, 2023, to mobilize students at Columbia University, launch a campus encampment and storm Grand Central Terminal. Free Palestine!" However, outside the limited mile-long path of the march, New Yorkers went about their ordinary days. The repeated appearance of the same organizations, leaders, signs, sound systems, wagons and protest infrastructure rolling through the streets of New York City revealed the professional organizing system operating behind the scenes, not a "massive crowd." WATCH: Neville Roy Singham’s wife Jodie Evans appears at anti-Israel protest, denies he funds protest efforts Jodie Evans takes center stage On E. 42nd Street, Evans — Singham’s wife and a central figure in the network surrounding the People’s Forum and other Singham-funded organizations — smiled widely as she kept step with the activists, marching behind the bright yellow-and-black signs marked "Party for Socialism and Liberation." Evans marched with CodePink activists behind a large "STOP ARMING ISRAEL" banner and carried a poster depicting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as "WANTED" for "GENOCIDE." Evans stood out in trademark CodePink colors, wearing an oversized fuchsia hat, pink peace-sign earrings, dark glasses, a pink-and-white keffiyeh and a shirt reading "I ♥ Palestinian Human Rights." Her appearance placed a member of the financier’s immediate family directly in the middle of the protest activity his money has helped sustain. When Fox News Digital asked her about her husband’s funding for nonprofits leading anti-Israel protests, she didn’t answer the question directly and responded, "He’s not been in the United States for six-and-a-half years." When asked about his position on the protests, she answered: "He supports stopping a genocide, you bet." Evans laughed off questions about Singham backing the Chinese Communist Party. In a video that Fox News Digital unearthed, Singham stood at the Golden Tulip Hotel in Shanghai during a November 2025 conference and expressed support for "a new world order that is based on multilateralism that President Xi and the CPC [Communist Party of China] and China have proposed." LAWMAKERS THROW OUT 'TROJAN HORSE' ACTIVISTS THEY SAY ARE ENGAGED IN AMERICAN SUBVERSION Evans denied allegations from lawmakers on the House Foreign Affairs Committee that the Singham network acts as a "Trojan horse" for the Chinese Communist Party, calling them "a lot of lies." "We're not doing anything wrong. So it's a lot of ‘alleging,’ and we're very honest about what we do: protesting every day," she said. "That's what we do. And that's what I've done for 55 years." She got visibly agitated on the topic of China. "China is not our enemy!" she said. "That's the message. You know what? I've been going to China for six and a half years. I can't talk about China. It's complex. I don't understand it. I'm just trying to learn about it. So it's not about China. It's about the United States not using our tax dollars to go to war on China. There's never an excuse to go to war on people." The protest was also packaged for online amplification. During the march, Zoe Alexandra, news editor of BreakThrough News, moved through the crowd conducting interviews, pulling Danaka Katovich, national co-director of CodePink, away from Evans’ CodePink contingent for a chat. BreakThrough later posted a branded one-minute, 21-second video on X under the headline: "Thousands protest…" Singham gave $1.098 million to Breakthrough BT Media Inc., which operates BreakThrough News, according to tax filings. SINGHAM-LINKED NONPROFITS FIGHT HOUSE SUBPOENAS, ACCUSE LAWMAKERS OF MCCARTHY-ERA ‘WITCH HUNT’ The protest featured black-and-white keffiyehs, a torched effigy of Netanyahu, bloodied cardboard imagery of Netanyahu and Arabic chants declaring that "Israel will be Arab." Critics say the slogans and imagery go beyond criticism of Israeli policy, invoking violent resistance and portraying the elimination of Israel as a political objective. To close out the protest near the United Nations, a leader from the Singham network manned the pop-up stage with a black-and-white keffiyeh over his shoulders, his arms tightly crossed, as speakers blasted the U.S. and Israel. As their last speaker, organizers returned to another leader from the People's Forum, Tajee Bounds, who serves as membership, events and volunteer coordinator. A graduate of Columbia University, Bounds was in the middle of the campus’s first encampment in April 2024 with People's Forum organizers when he stood, holding a banner and yelling along with a chant: "Up, up with liberation! Down, down with occupation!" The Columbia Spectator posted a video with his proclamation. Packing up the protest "Glory, glory to our martyrs," an activist chanted, before Bounds took the microphone at 6:31 p.m. to lead the crowd in a chant: "Gaza! Gaza! You will rise!" At 7:01 p.m., People’s Forum activists began rolling away their wagon full of yellow-and-black signs, set upside down, declaring, "ARREST WAR CRIMINAL BENJAMIN NETANYAHU!" HOW CODEPINK CO-FOUNDER MEDEA BENJAMIN'S FAMILY FOUNDATION BECAME A MAJOR FUNDER OF LEFT-WING ACTIVIST GROUPS For a dramatic backdrop, the protest moved west on 42nd Street to Times Square, like so many protests have ended before. Now it’s nighttime!" CodePink’s message throughout the video repeated the mantra of the day’s protest: "FROM THE RIVER TO THE SEA PALESTINE WILL BE FREE." The sequence created a feedback loop in which organizers built the spectacle, captured it on video and circulated the images as evidence of the movement’s scale and momentum. After the Times Square theater, foot soldiers for the People’s Forum rolled their wagon back onto W. 42nd Street, past the Port Authority and a McDonald’s on Eighth Avenue, with their trademark bright yellow-and-black signs. Others carried the bloodied cardboard imagery of Netanyahu and other protest paraphernalia. They ended up at the hub of the anti-Israel activist, the headquarters of the People’s Forum on W. 34th Street, carrying signs past books by communist leader Karl Marx and other ideologues. Inside the People’s Forum's large meeting hall, Chung, organizing director of the People’s Forum, awaited the returning protesters. De Los Santos greeted them at the door, stepping outside to tell Fox News Digital that he was proud of the group’s work leading the anti-Israel protests for the past three years. title: Seattle startup gives FOX News firsthand look at AI-powered vehicles built for the Marines
description: Overland AI gives a firsthand look at autonomous ground vehicles being developed for the U.S. Marine Corps to support logistics and ammunition resupply in contested environments.
content: From Ukraine to the Middle East, drones and other unmanned systems are playing an increasingly visible role in modern warfare. Nations are quickly competing to integrate AI tech into everyday military operations to eliminate human risk while improving overall efficiency in the field. One example of that development is based in Seattle, Washington. Late June, defense-tech company Overland AI announced it had secured a roughly $20 million dollar production contract with the U.S. Marine Corps for autonomous unmanned ground vehicles, or AUGVs, with delivery expected in early 2027. AMERICA AND CHINA ARE FIGHTING FOR THE FUTURE OF AI - CHIPS ARE THE BATTLEFIELD "This is a vote of confidence from the Marines that the technology that we have is ready for the mission," said Greg Okopal, Co-Founder and COO of Overland AI. The Marine Corps tells FOX the goal is to use the vehicles for missions such as moving ammunition and supplies while reducing risk to Marines. The award came through APFIT, the Pentagon’s Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies program, using a production Other Transaction Agreement, or OTA. APFIT was started in fiscal year 2022 to help move proven technologies into military use faster. The program is designed to speed up production and shorten the procurement process, essentially helping cut through some of the red tape. The tech is being developed to support the Marine Air Defense Integrated System, or MADIS, designed initially to focus on autonomous logistics, including ammunition resupply, in contested environments. Okopal says Overland’s work falls under the Marine Corps’ ground-based air defense program, "...which is really sort of a disparate array of vehicle-mounted sensors and effectors that can protect from various UAS (Unmanned Aerial System) and other airborne threats." But why the investment in ground autonomy? Overland AI argues while aerial drones and other unmanned systems have become increasingly important on the battlefield, "wars are still won on the ground." Describing the growing role of unmanned or autonomous ground vehicles, Overland AI Chief of Staff Chris Merz pointed to Ukraine, where he says the technology is being used more and more for combat. "They started with using them for sustainment but increasingly you're seeing them used in combat operations, taking and holding terrain…I really think that is the future application of uncrewed and autonomous ground vehicles and we'll start to see that more in future conflicts." WATCH: EXCLUSIVE LOOK AT BLUE-COLLAR WORKFORCE FUELING AMERICA’S AI BOOM Unlike remotely operated ground vehicles, Overland's system is designed to navigate and execute missions fully autonomously, without a human continuously steering the vehicle or even controlling it remotely. "Our vehicles, you task them with a mission, you press execute, those vehicles will execute that mission whether you have communications with them or not, whether you're paying attention to them or not, they are fully autonomous," Okopal explained. Overland says its vehicles can also operate beyond the line of sight and in GPS-denied environments, executing an assigned mission even when communications are unavailable. "All battlefields now are electronic, contested environments, right? So you cannot necessarily rely on distant comms to complete your mission," Okopal explained. TRUMP RENAMES AI ‘SUPERINTELLIGENCE,’ REJECTS ‘GLOBALIST’ CONTROL PLAN The vehicles are designed to perceive their surroundings and navigate off-road terrain, including obstacles such as ditches, inclines and boulders. Rather than solely directional focused capabilities, the AI technology behind it is more mission focused. For example, an entire fleet of vehicles can be programmed with the mission to establish surveillance and reconnaissance around specific coordinates, manage threat response, etc. "The very important thing is getting Marines and soldiers for the Army as well out of danger," Okopal explained. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Marine Corps shared this statement with FOX: "The U.S. Marine Corps Program Manager Ground-Based Air Defense (PM GBAD) has awarded an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement to Overland AI to develop and procure Autonomous Unmanned Ground Vehicles (AUGVs). Designed to sustain the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) family of systems across contested littoral and distributed operating environments, these AUGVs bridge the 'last tactical mile' logistics gap by automating ammunition resupply and reducing risk to warfighters. While initial efforts focus on autonomous logistics distribution via resilient, AI-driven networks, future capability spirals will integrate modular sensor packages and effectors to extend the active detection, tracking, identification, and defeat of unmanned aerial systems (UAS), rotary-wing aircraft, and low-altitude fixed-wing threats."

Amazing. We all caught up now? Good! Now, let's check in with Kyle's wife, Kristin, who had her husband join her for an Instagram message to the league: Does anyone care about the Presidents Cup? title: Leftist protester disrupts Climate Week event by ranting against US military
description: Code Pink disrupted a Nature Conservancy event at NYC Climate Week, demanding the group address the Pentagon's carbon footprint and military pollution.
content: A member of Code Pink, the far-left group known for confronting elected officials, disrupted a Climate Week event in New York City Thursday, blaming the U.S. military for its perceived role in the climate crisis. The disruption targeted an event hosted by The Nature Conservancy, which the group claims refuses to address the U.S. military’s "massive carbon footprint and massive environmental degradation from U.S. military bases and U.S.-driven wars and occupations." "There is an elephant in the room that The Nature Conservancy does not want to address," said a man identified by Code Pink only as Aaron, the campaign organizer for the group's War Is Not Green initiative. "It is destroying ecosystems. It is destroying fish. It is destroying the world." $54M CODEPINK-LINKED FOUNDATION SHUT DOWN IN CALIFORNIA POPS UP AT RAMSHACKLE MIAMI HOME He also pointed to the Pentagon’s $1.5 trillion budget and the U.S. military’s role in environmental destruction, asking why The Nature Conservancy, with a budget of over $2 billion and a mission dedicated to protecting land and water, refuses to address it, the group said. Code Pink said it was present at NYC Climate Week to insist that any serious climate conversation must include the military-industrial complex, which it argued contributes significantly to global warming. INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE' Code Pink demanded that The Nature Conservancy and other environmental groups "publicly acknowledge the U.S. military as a leading institutional polluter," "refuse partnerships or funding tied to the military-industrial complex" and "use their platforms to demand cuts to the Pentagon budget and an end to wars that devastate ecosystems." "You cannot claim to protect the land and waters while ignoring the largest institutional polluter on Earth," Aaron explained after the disruption. "The Nature Conservancy has a $2 billion budget and a global platform. It has a responsibility to name the war machine as a driver of climate destruction. Silence is complicity." title: Brewery that offered free beer when Trump dies faces possible closure after state revokes alcohol permits
description: Minocqua Brewing Co.'s Madison taproom faces likely closure by year's end after Wisconsin officials revoked its alcohol permits over alleged violations.
content: The owner of Minocqua Brewing Co. said Monday that the Madison taproom in Wisconsin will likely shut down by the end of the year after state officials revoked the company’s alcohol permits. Channel 3000 reported that Minocqua Brewing Co. owner Kirk Bangstad said the Madison taproom is likely to shut down as the business continues fighting the state’s decision. The brewery has become known for its outspoken messaging against President Donald Trump. WISCONSIN BREWERY THAT OFFERED 'FREE BEER' WHEN TRUMP DIES SAYS ALCOHOL PERMIT REVOKED The Wisconsin Department of Revenue (DOR) revoked brewing permits for the company’s Minocqua and Madison locations after alleging violations involving beer transported from Illinois without the required permits and tax payments. The brewery has disputed the state’s action and accused officials of targeting it because of its political views. The department told Fox News Digital in a statement Thursday that there is a hearing on the company's appeal on Nov. 18, and that the revocation does not take effect until appeals are done, adding that the "DOR is dedicated to fair and consistent enforcement of alcohol beverage regulations in Wisconsin and takes action when the laws are not followed, as occurred here." Bangstad’s breweries have made headlines for offering free beer if President Trump dies. On Jan. 22, the Minocqua Brewing Company appeared to suggest it would give free beer to patrons if Trump was killed, and while not explicitly using his name, posted on Facebook, "Free beer, all day long the day he dies." 'FREE BEER' FOR TRUMP DEATH DEM ACTIVIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOV: 'I WILL WIN' IF THEY SILENCE ME "Show us this post when it happens in a few months and we’ll make good on that promise," the post continued. The post was updated to say, "We meant the Madison Taproom because that’s open all year, if he dies in the summer, then it’s gonna be the Minocqua Taproom." In reply to comment on the post, the company also did not refer to Trump by name but said the message referred to a high-profile figure when asked whether the timeline for the deal could be moved up earlier. After the April shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner where Trump was present, the company wrote on Facebook, "Well, we almost got #freebeerday." KENTUCKY GOVERNOR SAYS HE RECEIVED 2 CALLS FROM AGENCIES INDICATING MCCONNELL HAD 'PASSED' The brewery also offered half-price beer when Sen. Mitch McConnell dies. "When they announce that McConnell’s Faustian dance has finally ended, we’re gonna start serving our beer at ‘half price,’ because we promised #halfpricebeerday on the day they unplug the ventilator," the brewery said in an Instagram post. McConnell, who is 84, was absent from the Senate for months after being hospitalized for a fall in his home earlier this year. The Kentucky Republican returned to the Senate last week ahead of key votes. Bangstad, who owns the brewery, is also the founder of the Minocqua Brewing Company SuperPAC, which "aims to remove Republican federal and state elected officials who perpetuated the election lies that caused the Insurrection of January 6, 2021, and whose downplaying of the seriousness of COVID-19 caused so many unnecessary deaths in our country," according to the brewery’s website. "Reminder, however, no red hats allowed," the brewery added.

title: Flyers forward Trevor Zegras slapped with one of the most ridiculous penalties of all time
description: Trevor Zegras was sent to the penalty box for tucking his jersey into his pants during the Philadelphia Flyers' preseason win over the Boston Bruins.
content: The NHL is still working through its preseason, and already we have a candidate for the worst penalty of the year, and possibly ever. The Philadelphia Flyers hosted the Boston Bruins in their penultimate tune-up before their season-opener against their arch-rivals, the Pittsburgh Penguins. Now, the Broad Street Bullies came out on top in this one, 2-0, but that wasn't the story. Instead, all of the talk after the game had to do with Flyers forward Trevor Zegras getting a minor for delay of game for "improperly wearing equipment." MLB TELLS UMPIRE DOUG EDDINGS HE MADE A MISTAKE IN DEMANDING CARDINALS PITCHER STRAIGHTEN HIS HAT Zegras hopped over the boards to take a faceoff with the back of his jersey tucked into his pants. Most of us wouldn't think twice about it, but an official saw it and sent him to the sin bin. That's because this season, officials have been told to crack down on players not wearing equipment properly, and technically, he was. But that doesn't make it any less absurd. MASSACHUSETTS YOUTH HOCKEY PLAYER SUSPENDED AFTER VICIOUS SLASHING INCIDENT GOES VIRAL At the risk of sounding like a certain cartoon sports radio host, it used to be that tucking your sweater into your pants was the cool thing to do. Had he done it again, it would've been a game misconduct. Head coach Rick Tocchet mentioned afterward that the league had given a heads-up about this push — which focuses on everything from visors to neck guards to, of course, jerseys — a few weeks earlier. "They told us, in all fairness, two, three weeks ago," Tocchet said. "I didn’t even think about it. … Obviously, can’t do it anymore. Regular season starts, we can’t have a penalty like that. I actually had to put (forward Matvei Michkov’s jersey) down on the bench." title: Flying sports car hides its wings as production gets closer
description: Samson Sky's Switchblade flying car secures $80 million from Dubai's Matin Group, but the redesigned hybrid-electric aircraft still needs more testing.
content: If you have ever been stuck in traffic wishing your car could sprout wings, Samson Sky has been working on something pretty close. Its Switchblade flying car can drive out of your garage and take you to a nearby airport. Once there, the wings come out, the tail extends and the vehicle becomes an airplane. You heard right, an airplane. After landing, everything folds back inside so you can drive the rest of the way. That idea has been around for years. What makes Switchblade worth another look right now is that Samson says it has secured an $80 million investment from Dubai-based Matin Group. Samson plans to use the funding to help move the project toward U.S. production. The company still needs another $20 million to fully fund its current production plan. That new backing gets the Switchblade closer. But what really caught my attention is how much Samson has changed since we first watched this flying car take off. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com. Register and receive the replay and step-by-step guide afterward. This flying sports car makes its wings disappear The latest Switchblade design looks much more like a car when you are using it on the road. Samson says the wings, tail and propeller are now fully enclosed inside the vehicle during driving mode. That is a major change from the earlier design that completed its first flight in November 2023. When you reach an airport, the wings extend and the tail moves into position for flight. Samson says the transformation from driving mode to flying mode takes about three minutes. After you land, the process reverses. The flight hardware folds back inside the body before you continue the trip by road. Samson says that setup allows the Switchblade to fit inside a standard garage while also protecting the flight surfaces when the vehicle is being driven or stored. There is still a runway involved, though. The Switchblade does not take off vertically from your driveway. You drive it to an airport, transform it into flight mode and take off from there. The Switchblade we saw fly in 2023 has changed We first covered the Switchblade after its official first flight on Nov. 5, 2023. The prototype flew from Grant County International Airport in Moses Lake, Washington. Since then, Samson has kept working on the version it hopes to put into customers' hands. The company has changed the design and increased the size of its engine. Samson says it plans to use three production prototypes for more testing around the end of 2026 or beginning of 2027. So while we have already seen a Switchblade get off the ground, the version heading toward production has changed since that 2023 flight. That is why I am especially interested in what happens next. I want to see the latest Switchblade take to the air and show us what this new design can actually do. How fast could the Switchblade flying car go? Samson is targeting some attention-grabbing performance numbers. The company currently lists a maximum airspeed of 190 mph and a maximum flying range of 450 miles. It lists a maximum road speed of 100 mph. Samson also lists a 160 mph cruise speed. However, its FAQ says that anticipated figure still needs verification during production-prototype flight testing. The Switchblade uses a hybrid-electric drivetrain. A gasoline engine powers a generator, which supplies electricity to the vehicle's motors. Samson says the system powers the wheels on the ground and the propellers in flight. The company currently lists a 44-gallon fuel capacity and says the vehicle uses 91-octane automotive gasoline. HELMET-STYLE COCKPIT VISION SYSTEM AIMS TO CHANGE HOW PILOTS SEE IN LOW VISIBILITY $80 million gives the Switchblade production push some muscle Making a flying prototype and building vehicles for customers are two very different challenges. Samson says the new $80 million investment will help establish its first 180,000-square-foot Switchblade production facility in the U.S. The company signed a Joint Investment Agreement with Matin Group, and the two companies have started setting up a joint venture. Where that factory ends up remains an open question. Samson Sky CEO and founder Sam Bousfield tells CyberGuy that the search has narrowed considerably, saying, "We will maintain our Samson Sky R&D Facility in Prineville, OR, and we have narrowed down the US production facility to three potential locations in different parts of the country, with some negotiations already begun." Samson has not identified those locations publicly. There is serious new money behind the production effort, but another financial hurdle remains. Samson says $20 million still needs to be raised before its current production plan is fully funded. When could you actually get one? Samson's current timeline points to summer 2027. The company says it expects its Builder Assist assembly line to be ready by then. Its first year of production will focus mostly on customers who previously paid for some of the earliest delivery positions. Depositors and reservation holders would follow. Then there is the price. Samson currently estimates the Switchblade VFR kit will start at $200,000. The IFR version carries an estimated price of $235,000. Those prices can still change before customer production gets underway. Bousfield tells CyberGuy that reaching this point has been part of the plan for years. "It's been great developing the technology for a flying car that you park in your garage and is high performance in both modes. Now we get to put it out for people to use and explore the world around them." Before that happens, buyers will have to do something you probably have never done when purchasing a car. Yes, you have to help build your Switchblade Buying a Switchblade comes with homework. Samson plans for the aircraft to operate under the Experimental Amateur-Built category in the U.S. FAA rules require the "major portion," meaning more than 50%, of an eligible amateur-built aircraft's fabrication and assembly to be completed by people building it for their own education or recreation. That requirement is often called the 51% rule. Samson says its Builder Assist program will guide owners through their portion of the process. The company says much of its manufacturing process will be automated and computer-driven. It estimates an owner can finish the required work in as little as one week. One regulatory detail deserves some attention here. The FAA says it evaluates aircraft kits to determine whether they can allow a builder to meet the major-portion requirement. The FAA does not approve or certify the kit itself. The finished aircraft also goes through the FAA airworthiness process. So this will be a very different experience from walking into a dealership, signing a few forms and driving home. You will need to know how to fly it too A Switchblade may drive like a vehicle on the ground, but once those wings come out, aviation rules take over. Samson says you will need a private pilot certificate to fly one. Ground licensing can vary based on where you register the vehicle. The company says an automobile or motorcycle license may apply depending on local regulations. That also separates Switchblade from some of the other flying vehicles we have been following. Electric air taxis such as Joby's eVTOL are designed around vertical takeoff and landing. Switchblade takes another route. It uses conventional runways but gives you something an air taxi cannot: the same vehicle stays with you after you land. That could be useful on a regional trip. Instead of landing and then finding a rental car or arranging another ride, you fold the wings away and keep going. WISCONSIN MAN FLIES HELICOPTER TO CABELA'S BECAUSE THE DRIVE WAS TOO LONG What this means to you Here's what makes the Switchblade so interesting to me. You could pull out of your garage, drive to an airport, fly hundreds of miles and then keep driving after you land. No rental car. No waiting around for another ride. The same vehicle goes with you from start to finish. The new funding gets Samson closer to making that happen, but I would not start clearing space in the garage yet. The company still has to finish funding its production plans, choose where to build the Switchblade and put the latest version through more testing. We have seen an earlier prototype fly, but the redesigned vehicle heading toward production still needs to show what it can do in the air. And if you are thinking, "Where do I sign up?" there is a lot more involved than the estimated $200,000 starting price. You will need pilot training and access to an airport. You also have to take part in the Builder Assist process. For me, the next big moment comes when this latest Switchblade leaves the runway. If it can deliver on the speed, range and transformation Samson is targeting, this flying sports car suddenly gets a whole lot more interesting. Kurt's key takeaways What I like about the Switchblade is that the idea makes sense the minute you see how it works. You drive to the airport, fly to another city, fold the wings away after you land and keep going. The latest design makes that even more interesting because all that flight hardware disappears inside a vehicle you can park in your garage. Of course, most of us are not shopping for a $200,000 flying sports car. The price alone puts the Switchblade out of reach for the majority of us, and becoming a pilot adds another wrinkle. But that does not mean you have to be a potential buyer to find this fascinating. I certainly am not planning to put one in my garage tomorrow, but I want to see whether Samson can actually pull this off. The new funding gives Samson a much stronger push toward production, and we have already seen an earlier Switchblade fly. Now I want to see this redesigned version get into the air. If Samson can deliver what it is promising, we could be watching a pretty remarkable idea make the jump from a prototype we have followed for years to a flying sports car people can actually own. Would you trust one vehicle to take you down the highway and into the sky, or would you want to see a few years of customer flights before climbing aboard? title: Wendi McLendon-Covey fires back after Jeff Garlin blames bipolar disorder for 'The Goldbergs' exit
description: Jeff Garlin says his undiagnosed bipolar disorder fueled the on-set behavior that led to his exit from "The Goldbergs." Co-star Wendi McLendon-Covey pushed back on his claims.
content: Jeff Garlin is opening up about his contentious exit from "The Goldbergs," saying his undiagnosed bipolar disorder contributed to the behavior that strained relationships with his co-stars before he left the hit sitcom. The 64-year-old actor starred as the Goldbergs' family patriarch, Murray Goldberg, on the show from its premiere in September 2013 until he departed the ABC show during its ninth season in December 2021 amid HR investigations into complaints about his on-set behavior. Garlin was accused by members of the cast and crew of inappropriate verbal conduct, unwanted physical contact, including hugging and touching, and behavior that some employees described as creating an uncomfortable work environment. JEFF GARLIN DEFENDS HIMSELF FROM CANCEL CULTURE AMID ‘THE GOLDBERGS’ ON-SET CONDUCT ALLEGATIONS While speaking with Vanity Fair at the time, Garlin denied intentionally harassing anyone. He acknowledged that HR had spoken to him over several years but characterized the complaints as stemming from his style of comedy and "silliness" on set rather than malicious intent. He also said he was willing to adjust behaviors, like no longer hugging people. During a March 2023 appearance on SiriusXM's "Andy Cohen Live," Garlin's co-star, Wendi McLendon-Covey, who played his wife Beverly Goldberg on "The Goldbergs," said his exit was "a long time coming" and that "finally, someone is listening to us." She declined to discuss the situation further, saying she was "exhausted by that topic and the PTSD of it all." On Monday, Garlin appeared on the Daily Beast's "Obsessed" podcast and addressed McLendon-Covey's comments and attributed his behavior to a mental health condition that had not been diagnosed at the time. "It wasn't a long time coming for me," he said in reference to McLendon-Covey's past remark. title: Federal illegal voting arrest becomes latest flashpoint in Sherrill's battles with Trump administration
description: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill faces new pressure after ICE and the FBI arrested a Senegalese national accused of voting illegally since 2018.
content: Federal law enforcement arrested a Senegalese immigrant in New Jersey accused of illegally voting in multiple elections, injecting a new flashpoint into Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill's escalating fights with Washington over immigration enforcement and election integrity. The case comes as Washington and Trenton battle over immigration enforcement and election administration, with the Trump administration challenging Sherrill over state policies affecting federal law enforcement while also pressing New Jersey for access to its voter rolls. Sanata Coulibaly, a Senegalese national, was arrested when DHS and FBI agents jointly executed a criminal warrant in Hudson County, which stretches from West New York to Bayonne across the Hudson River from Manhattan. FOUR NONCITIZENS CHARGED WITH ILLEGALLY VOTING IN 2020, 2022 AND 2024 FEDERAL ELECTIONS IN NEW JERSEY "This alien from Senegal has been charged with procurement of citizenship or naturalization unlawfully and voting by an alien after allegedly voting in three general elections in New Jersey," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said. title: ‘Wave of freedom’ sweeps Latin America as Trump ally takes fight to Marxist terror group
description: José Manuel Restrepo says Colombian forces, not American troops, will lead operations against armed groups under Trump's Shield of the Americas.
content: UNITED NATIONS — Colombian Vice President José Manuel Restrepo said his country is embracing President Donald Trump’s push for a new security alliance across the Western Hemisphere, but drew a clear line on the role American forces would play inside Colombia, telling Fox News Digital that Colombian troops — not U.S. forces — will carry out operations against the country’s armed groups. Restrepo spoke with Fox News Digital in an on-camera interview days after joining Trump and other regional leaders at a Shield of the Americas meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, where Trump called the initiative the "largest and most powerful alliance for economic and national security ever to convene in the Western Hemisphere." Trump urged members to treat what he called "narco terrorists" as common threats and impose sanctions on U.S.-designated terrorist organizations. Restrepo said he personally discussed the region’s changing political and security landscape with Trump. The shift in Colombia comes amid a broader political realignment across Latin America, with De La Espriella’s June victory adding Colombia to a group of countries including Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia and Panama that have moved to the right, fueled in part by voter concerns over crime, economic weakness and political instability. TRUMP ALLY 'EL TIGRE' SWORN IN AS COLOMBIA'S NEW PRESIDENT AMID CONTINENT'S RIGHTWARD SHIFT "There is a wave of freedom, a wave of democracy, a wave of free market. … There is a new momentum for the region and we have to take advantage of that momentum. That's what I said to President Trump," Restrepo told Fox News Digital. "If we want to keep and preserve democracy in the region, the Shield of the Americas is going to be the best opportunity to do it." Asked what Trump told him, Restrepo said the president agreed and expressed respect for Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella. "Colombia is a new partner. In my opinion, it's one of the most important partners for the United States in the region," Restrepo said. That partnership is already being tested in the fight against drug trafficking and armed groups. WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES In August, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Colombia had authorized "joint military operations to destroy terrorists and terror networks" and told reporters that Washington had discussed possible joint strikes against groups including the National Liberation Army, or ELN, which the U.S. designates as a terrorist organization, and remnants of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia. "Designated terrorist organizations, with partnered governments, will be legitimate targets of the United States government," including in Colombia, Hegseth said when asked whether such operations were expected, according to Reuters. But when pressed by Fox News Digital on whether joint U.S.-Colombian strikes remained an option, Restrepo appeared to narrow the scope of direct American involvement. "The United States helps us on security, helps us information, helps us on technology, but the public forces of Colombia are those who are going to act in those places," he said. US FORCES OBLITERATE SUSPECTED 'NARCO-TERRORIST' VESSEL IN LETHAL EASTERN PACIFIC STRIKE, KILLING 3 Asked specifically whether Colombia would have the "boots on the ground," Restrepo replied: "We will have our group, our public forces on the ground." The tougher posture comes as Colombia confronts renewed violence from armed and drug-trafficking groups. This week, De La Espriella ordered the military into Santa Marta after the Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada, an illegal armed group involved in drug trafficking, responded to the killing of one of its senior leaders with an "armed strike," threats, roadblocks and attacks that left businesses shuttered and public transportation disrupted. More than 500 soldiers and 600 police officers were deployed, according to the Colombian presidency. The new government is also seeking to reverse former President Gustavo Petro’s "total peace" policy, which pursued negotiations with several armed organizations. Before taking office, De La Espriella announced that he would dismantle key elements of the policy and reactivate arrest warrants against members of illegal armed groups. Restrepo went further, accusing the former government of creating "the idea of impunity" and saying the new administration instead intends to confront groups it considers terrorists. US, SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS CONDEMN 'ONGOING EFFORTS' TO OVERTHROW BOLIVIA'S ELECTED PRESIDENT AMID UNREST He said that when the new government took office, "around 30%" of Colombia’s regions lacked effective territorial control — a figure Fox News Digital has not independently verified — and said the administration was seeking to regain those areas through stronger security forces, intelligence gathering, drug eradication and extraditions. Restrepo also argued that the same security debate should extend to the United Nations, where Colombia used its General Assembly address this week to call for reforms and an international definition of terrorism. The UN has had a global counterterrorism strategy since 2006, but member states have for decades failed to agree on a comprehensive international convention defining terrorism. Colombia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday also announced that the country was suspending all diplomatic relations with Iran. "This sovereign decision aligns with the pillars guiding the Government's foreign policy regarding national and hemispheric security, as well as the fight against transnational crime, taking into account alleged links between the Iranian government and international terrorist groups and other narcoterrorist groups that threaten the country's security," the Ministry wrote in a statement posted to X. MELANIA TRUMP’S HOME-COUNTRY LEADER RIPS UN ‘DOUBLE STANDARDS’ AS TRUMP PROMISE IS REVEALED "I think this is a moment in which the United Nations have to reflect on its own future," Restrepo told Fox News Digital, calling for greater efficiency and effectiveness as well as international agreement on terrorism. "The only way to attain peace, which is one of the main objectives of the UN, is through confronting terrorism," he said, arguing that countries need greater intelligence sharing, judicial cooperation and coordination. With Secretary-General António Guterres set to leave office at the end of the year, Restrepo said the transition could offer the institution an opportunity to change. "I think that the UN has a new moment and the UN has to take advantage of that opportunity," he said. Restrepo added that the institution also needed to address what he described as the inconsistent application of human rights standards. "Ideology cannot decide to whom we are going to apply or not human rights."

title: Cooper Flagg rookie card makes eye-popping record sale, but is it actually a good investment?
description: Cooper Flagg's Topps Chrome rookie debut patch auto 1-of-1 PSA 10 card sold for $8.04 million, becoming the sixth-most expensive trading card ever.
content: Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg is a superstar, the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year, and his sports card market has been booming. Ever since he burst on the scene at Duke, following being the No. 1 overall high school prospect and a McDonald's All-American, sports fans and media knew he was going to be special. I, for one, did not believe he was so special that his most sought-after rookie card, the Topps Chrome Update Rookie Debut Patch Auto 1-of-1 in a PSA Gem-Mint 10 grade for both the card and the auto, would become the sixth-most expensive trading card of all time. The card sold in Fanatics Collect’s September Premier Auction for $8.04 million, amassing 83 bids. The auction ran from September 10 through September 24. A bidding war took place into the early hours of Friday morning, with the card going from $3.5 million to $8.04 million from 9 p.m. ET on Thursday to 2 a.m. ET on Friday. That sale was historic because it became the highest recorded sale for a basketball card featuring a single player. According to a Fanatics spokesperson, "This is the first class of NBA Debut Patch cards, which saw each rookie wear a patch on their jersey sleeve during their first game which was removed following the game and put into a trading card and signed." The Debut Patch was first introduced in 2021 in Major League Baseball, garnering massive sales like the 2024 Paul Skenes Debut Patch Auto selling for $1.11 Million. It's easily been the most innovative concept the hobby has seen since the logo man, which is a patch of the respective league's logo from a game-worn jersey. It's among the rarest collectibles in the sports card market. Flagg's card became the 3rd-highest NBA card sale ever, trailing only a pair of dual logoman cards, the 2006–07 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Autographs 1-of-1 Michael Jordan and LeBron James, which sold in a private sale for $10 Million and the 2007–08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Autographs 1-of-1 Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant, which sold in August of 2025 for $12,932,000. AN ULTRA-RARE COOPER FLAGG TRADING CARD HAS BEEN FOUND, AND THE MAVERICKS ARE PREPARED TO GIVE A LOT FOR IT It also ranks as the fifth-highest sports card sale, according to Card Ladder. A Mickey Mantle 1952 Topps card sold for $12.6 million at a Heritage auction in 2022, and an ungraded Shohei Ohtani 2026 Topps Chrome Gold Logoman patch autograph card, famously fetched $11 million on July 30 in a private sale to Kevin O'Leary and the investment group Secure Collectibles. In a statement by Fanatics, the company said, "The Cooper Flagg card was famously pulled in a break done by Rhody Breakers in Rhode Island, and belonged to collector Jason Williams of South Carolina." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Jason Williams, 50, acquired the card after spending only $515 to land a spot on Rhody Breakers. For those who don't know, buying a spot in a "break" is where a customer purchases a team and/or player (spot) for an amount set by the specific breaker on a livestream, where the retailer opens a box(es) of sports cards, with the customer hoping to pull a life-changing card, an auto, or numbered card. It's a gamble. There was no guarantee Williams would even get a card(s) totaling that $515 spot purchase. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Speaking of gambles, this is the biggest gamble I have ever seen in the hobby (as the sports card collecting market is affectionately known). Is Cooper Flagg a generational talent? In some ways, yes, but the jury is still out and only time will tell if he is truly one of the greatest basketball players of all time. He's a No. 1 overall pick, fresh off a solid rookie season, but in my opinion, he's going to need to win an MVP and a championship soon if this buyer wants to see a solid return on the investment. Many of the biggest names in the NBA, who have a proven track record, have cards I would find much more enticing to purchase. I believe Steph Curry is undervalued, LeBron James is a certified NBA legend, who owns many NBA records, with cards I'd happily purchase over this. If I had $8 Million, here's what I would buy instead: I could put a long list together, but I would much rather spend money on a tried and true sports legend, or a vintage Pokemon card, rather than gamble with losing millions on a potential NBA legend. But hey, I'm not the one with $8 million to blow, so to the buyer, this could just be pocket change. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Either way, this sale is a great thing for Flagg's card market, shows that sports cards are becoming more enticing than stocks in many ways, and the additional sales of debut patch autos, including San Antonio Spurs star Dylan Harper’s card selling for $2.88 million and Hornets' sharpshooter Kon Knueppel’s Debut Patch card selling for $2.34 million, are incredibly impressive as well. title: Michigan college president urges 'it's incumbent upon' higher education leaders to lower tuition every year

"There's nothing wrong with Syracuse University. It's a fantastic place and will remain fantastic," he added. I’M A UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT; TRUMP IS RIGHT TO MAKE COLLEGES DELIVER FOR STUDENTS Docking also co-founded Rize Education, a course-sharing platform that allows smaller colleges to collaborate and offer online classes without incurring massive overhead expenses. Through its partnership with Rize, Adrian College has added 27 majors, 13 minors and eight certificates in high-demand fields like business, technology, engineering and healthcare. His efforts earned him an invitation to testify before the House Education and Workforce Committee and helped Adrian College earn a spot among U.S. News & World Report’s Most Innovative Regional Universities in the Midwest three consecutive years. Docking argued that soaring tuition is driven by operational inefficiency and an insular culture that prevents institutions from working together like private-sector businesses. title: Trump scores Supreme Court win in election integrity fight as states gain new voter roll tool
description: An order issued Friday by the Supreme Court temporarily allows the Trump administration to move forward with a mass voter verification system.
content: An order issued Friday by the Supreme Court temporarily allows the Trump administration to move forward with a mass voter verification system. The emergency order allows states, for now, to use the Department of Homeland Security program, called Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements, or SAVE, in their efforts to verify the eligibility of voters on their rolls. Because existing law blocks most states from systematically purging voters from their rolls within 90 days of an election, the immediate impact of Friday's order on the upcoming midterms is likely limited, the Associated Press reported. States' use of the SAVE program is voluntary. Norm Eisen, a senior fellow with Brookings, agreed that the Supreme Court's ruling was restrained. "Don't overreact to the SCOTUS SAVE database decision," Eisen wrote on X. "Page 6 of the decision makes clear that we are in the 90-day statutory window when mass changes can't be made to voter lists!" LIBERAL JUSTICE HAMMERS SUPREME COURT FOR FAST-TRACKING EMERGENCY DOCKET CASES The court’s order puts on hold a federal judge’s June ruling that had deemed the Republican administration’s recently revamped version of SAVE illegal. U.S. District Court Judge Sparkle L. Sooknanan had blocked the use of the tool, saying it violated Americans’ privacy rights and could result in voters being wrongly removed from the rolls. A federal appeals court declined to pause Sooknanan's ruling, prompting the administration's appeal to the Supreme Court. The Trump administration moved to expand SAVE after the president signed an executive order directing the creation of a federal voter registration list and imposed new restrictions on eligibility for voting by mail as part of a broader effort to combat voter fraud. TRUMP REVIVES SUPREME COURT IMMIGRATION SHOWDOWN AFTER HOCHUL PARDON TORPEDOED FIRST CASE The SAVE program was created in 1986 under an immigration law mandating that DHS help federal, state and local agencies prevent government benefits from going to noncitizens. The Trump administration last year moved to significantly expand its search abilities. Since then, at least 67 million registrations have been scanned through the program, but critics, the AP says, worry it could end up purging valid voters from the rolls. Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was joined by Justices Elena Kagan and Sonia Sotomayor in dissenting. "In my view… the harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the Government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take," Jackson wrote in a dissenting opinion. "This imbalance, along with the Government’s improbable merits arguments, should have compelled the Court to deny the stay." But the majority pushed back on concerns that lawful voters could simply be removed from state voter rolls, noting that federal officials are required to contact individuals flagged by SAVE to seek additional information if their citizenship cannot be confirmed. The majority also noted that SAVE has long allowed federal, state and local agencies to verify citizenship and immigration status using records maintained by the Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security and Department of State. "The Supreme Court’s order allows the federal government to share information in its possession concerning people’s apparent citizenship status to help election officials register eligible voters while preventing the improper addition of non-citizens to the registration rolls," Michael Morley, director of the Election Law Center at Florida State University, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The Court recognized Congress expressly endorsed such information sharing in 1996 amendments to federal immigration law." CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP The Supreme Court's stay is temporary, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit could still rule against the SAVE program, potentially sending the case back to the Supreme Court. Jason Snead, executive director of the Honest Elections Project, said the Supreme Court already "got it right." "The Trump Administration’s SAVE expansion just makes it easier for states to get federal citizenship data to help them clean up voter rolls. Once again, left-wing interests are doing everything they can to block states from verifying citizenship on the eve of a federal election, and for the second time in a week they have lost in court. This a major win for election integrity." Fox News' Shannon Bream, Bill Mears, Ashley J. DiMella and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Never smoked a cigarette? You could still be at higher risk for lung cancer
description: Never-smokers carrying the rare EGFR T790M gene variant face 62 times the odds of lung cancer, a major study of 3.3 million people suggests.
content: A rare genetic mutation could put people at a dramatically higher risk of developing lung cancer even if they’ve never smoked. A rare mutation in the gene EGFR T790M was found to increase lung cancer risk by 25 times compared with people who did not have the mutation, according to a new study published in the journal Science. Among people who had never smoked, carriers of the mutation had about 62 times the odds of lung cancer compared with never-smokers who did not have it. PANCREATIC CANCER VACCINE SHOWS PROMISE IN FIRST HUMAN TRIAL, PREVENTING DISEASE IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS The study, led by investigators at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and 23andMe Research Institute, analyzed data from more than 3.3 million people. The gene variant showed no increased risk across 17 other cancers studied. "Today, lung cancer screening is driven almost entirely by smoking history," study co-author Jaclyn LoPiccolo, attending physician and lung cancer researcher at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, said in a press release. CANCER WARNING SIGNS MAY APPEAR IN DNA YEARS BEFORE BLOOD TESTS DETECT TROUBLE "Our findings raise the possibility that, in the future, screening could also be dictated by inherited genetic risk. If further studies confirm the benefit, people with EGFR T790M could be identified through genetic testing and offered personalized CT screening to identify lung cancers when they are at their most curable stage." Most U.S. carriers of the mutation were traced to a shared ancestry linked to British and Irish settlers in Southern Appalachia about 200–225 years ago, the researchers found. The mutation remains rare nationwide, affecting roughly one in 15,000–16,000 people. It is more common in some parts of Southern Appalachia, where researchers estimate as many as one in 2,000 people may carry it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "We found that the vast majority of carriers inherited the mutation from the same ancestral lineage," said LoPiccolo. "We could trace that lineage to British and Irish settlers in the United States and show that the mutation became enriched after a founder event and genetic bottleneck in Southern Appalachia about 200 years ago. "It's a fascinating example of how human migration and genealogy can shape disease risk, generations later." One of the "remarkable" findings of the study was the fact that a single mutation could have such a strong effect, according to Alexander Gusev, a quantitative geneticist at Dana-Farber. "To my knowledge, it's one of the strongest, if not the strongest, cancer risk-increasing mutations that has ever been found," he said in the release. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Smoking is bad for lung cancer. This mutation is bad for lung cancer. When you do both, your risk is the sum of those two risks," he added. "So, you definitely don't want to smoke." The researchers suggest that people with a strong family history of lung cancer, multiple lung nodules or tumors or family roots in parts of the southeastern U.S. should consider speaking with a genetic counselor about whether genetic testing or lung cancer screening makes sense for them. "It's a fascinating example of how human migration and genealogy can shape disease risk generations later." There were some limitations to the study. Because the mutation is so rare, researchers identified relatively few carriers even among the millions of participants, meaning the exact size of the increased risk remains uncertain. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The analysis also relied heavily on 23andMe research participants, who may not represent the broader population. Because the mutation is much more common in certain parts of the U.S., the risk estimates may not apply equally to everyone, the researchers noted. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP While the study establishes a strong association with lung cancer risk, it does not demonstrate that genetic testing improves mortality or other health outcomes. The study was funded in part by the National Institutes of Health and the American Cancer Society.

title: Reporter's Notebook: Democrats face an impeachment tractor beam that could derail their affordability message
description: Like the Millenium Falcon caught in a tractor beam, Hakeem Jeffries and House Democrats face an impeachment pull they may not be able to escape.
content: In the original Star Wars, Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, Chewbacca and Obi-Wan Kenobi find the Millennium Falcon under fire from Imperial TIE fighters in deep outer space. Luke speculates that the TIE fighters are "heading for that small moon." But Obi-Wan’s visage grows grim. "That’s no moon," intones Obi-Wan. "It’s a space station." Han Solo disagrees. "It’s too big to be a space station," says Han. To which, Obi-Wan instructs him, "Turn the ship around." But as quickly as he dismissed Kenobi’s observation, Solo pivots. He grimaces, realizing that the wise Jedi Knight is on to something. DEMOCRAT AL GREEN TO FORCE HOUSE-WIDE VOTE ON IMPEACHING TRUMP "Yeah. I think you’re right," Han replies. The Millennium Falcon starts to shake. "Chewie, lock in the auxiliary power," Han commands his shipmate. "Why are we still moving towards it?" squeaks Luke. "We’re caught in a tractor beam and it’s pulling us in!" shouts Han. And a few moments later, the Millenium Falcon, the fastest ship in the galaxy, is suctioned into Bay 327 of the Death Star, moored, and unable to escape. The band of ragtag heroes are now stuck. On the Death Star. Grand Moff Tarkin describes it as "the ultimate power in the universe." +++++++ Impeachment in Congress is kind of like the Death Star’s tractor beam. You can’t escape once you’re in its clenches. A decision to impeach sucks a political party in, eventually marooning everyone in the political equivalent of a hangar bay. For Democrats, they can’t focus on the price of eggs and milk. There’s little debate about gas prices. It’s a challenge to even address oversight issues. You can try to "lock in the auxiliary power." But it’s too late. You might think impeachment is "a moon." But it’s really the political Death Star. Not for your adversary. But often those orchestrating the impeachment. Democrats might find themselves in an impeachment bind if they capture the majority next year. Progressives and the left will possess one of the loudest voices in Congress. And even though Democrats twice impeached President Trump in 2019 and 2021, some will insist on doing it again. That’s to say nothing of trying to impeach a host of Trump Administration cabinet officials – ranging from Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Some Democrats are already falling prey to the impeachment tractor beam. Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, led the initial effort to impeach President Trump during his first term in 2017 – long before the successful impeachment over Ukraine in 2019. Republican redistricting – engineered by President Trump forced Green out of his Houston-based district earlier this year. But Green engineered yet another effort to impeach the President last week as the Texas Democrat heads for the exit. MIDTERM HISTORY MASSIVELY FAVORS DEMOCRATS. BUT THEY ARE MAKING A BIG MISTAKE The House voted to sidestep Green’s impeachment resolution, 232-147. So this was not a straight, up or down vote on impeachment. It was one step removed. Forty-seven Democrats voted "present." That includes the party’s top three Democrats: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA) and House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif. In some respects, House Democratic leaders want to shun impeachment. Or at least avoid it for the time being. In 2006, Democrats were on the precipice of flipping control of the House. Democrats largely won the midterms that year because of voter fatigue with President George W. Bush and the calcification of the war in Iraq. Many Democrats wanted to impeach the President. But as she prepared to clasp the gavel, then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., famously declared that impeachment was "off the table." House Democrats focused on drawing down the war in Iraq and eventually pivoting to other policy issues like health care and climate change. But Democrats had to get through those midterms first. So once Pelosi said no impeachment, there was no impeachment of the President. Impeachment with President Trump was kind of "off the table" for Pelosi when Democrats reclaimed the House in the 2018 midterms. But there was a shift among moderate Democrats after disclosures about the President and Ukraine in the summer of 2019. A master of the political pulse, the Speaker understood the direction this was going among her Members. That’s when Pelosi got in front of her caucus, pushing for potential impeachment of the President later that year. House Democratic leaders are depositing any overt discussion of impeachment on the backburner for now. They don’t want to veer away from their message about affordability. In fact they’ve frequently steered the conversation back to the cost of living when pressed about impeachment. Consider this response from Jeffries when questioned about impeachment on April 9. "We'll have a conversation led by (Rep.) Jamie Raskin, D-Md., the top Democrat on the Judiciary Committee, and (Rep.) Jerry Nadler, D-N.Y., a former Judiciary Committee Chairman and Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., and Judiciary Committee Democrats tomorrow about Trump administration accountability," replied Jeffries. But, unlike completely mimicking Pelosi’s posture years ago, Jeffries signaled he was open to the impeachment question. "I don't want to get out ahead of that discussion. But we've also been very clear. House Democrats are going to focus on making life more affordable for the American people," said Jeffries. On June 14, Kristen Welker of NBC asked Jeffries if his party could "move to impeach President Trump" if Democrats reclaimed the House. "We haven't ruled anything in or ruled anything out in terms of accountability. What we have said is that our focus is going to be to make life more affordable for the American people," answered Jeffries. On August 25 on CNN, Jeffries deflected a similar impeachment inquiry. "We haven't ruled anything in and we haven t ruled anything out," stated Jeffries. Impeachment interrogatives continued for Jeffries during a September 13 interview on ABC. "We haven't ruled anything in and we haven't ruled anything out in terms of impeachment," said Jeffries. That’s smart politics for Jeffries. He’s trying to keep his hand on the helm before the midterms – and essentially deferring to the political climate of next year and where rank-and-file Democrats might fall next year should Democrats capture the majority. But there are indications that many Democrats are already ready for impeachment. The progressive base will demand action. And it extends well beyond Al Green. Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-Pa., made her case after the President posted to social media in April that "a whole civilization will die tonight" in reference to Iran. "If that's not high crimes and misdemeanors - and if it's not madness - I don't know what is," said Dean. Rep. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., said that the President was "threatening genocide." Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said the party should "push for impeachment" and that the President "is unfit to be the Commander in Chief" and "should be removed." So Jeffries has a decision to make. The hard left will demand impeachment – for someone. Be it the President or Hegseth. But if Democrats flip the House, their "majority makers" might represent battleground districts. Those prospective lawmakers will be moderates. Impeachment could be politically toxic for them. TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS Pelosi’s circumstances evolved in the summer of 2019. Moderate Democrats with national security credentials from swing districts edged toward impeachment. So, she pulled the impeachment trigger. Pelosi knew the direction of her caucus. In September 2026, it’s not as clear for Jeffries. And it’s not a done deal that Democrats will seize the majority. That’s why the New York Democrat expressed caution during his conversation on ABC. "We've got to follow the facts. Apply the law. Be guided by the Constitution and then let the chips fall where they may, in the best interest of the American people," said Jeffries. +++ Han Solo was skeptical back on the Death Star. "Even if I could take off, I’d never get past the tractor beam," said Solo. "Leave that to me," promised Obi-Wan Kenobi. The Jedi Master then eluded detection on the Death Star, manually shutting off the tractor beam. That disgorged the Millenium Falcon. But in the end, Kenobi sacrificed himself for the mission. On Capitol Hill, impeachment is a tractor beam. Once you’re siphoned in, nothing can escape its grasp. Debates about policy. Spending. Health care. War. The tractor beam controls all. Until it’s switched off. Not every party which is incapacitated by impeachment has an Obi-Wan Kenobi who can find the off switch. When it comes to impeachment best advice might be to "turn the ship around" beforehand. title: Xi praises US state visit 'perfection' as Trump calls meetings 'very productive'
description: President Donald Trump said Friday that the U.S. and China have "made great strides" after meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House.
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping praised the level of "perfection" on display during his state visit to the White House, and President Donald Trump said Friday the two world leaders had a "very productive" time in Washington. Trump, speaking to reporters as he and first lady Melania Trump hosted Xi and first lady of China Madame Peng Liyuan for tea at the White House, said, "We've had a tremendous visit from two spectacular people," and, "we've made great strides, very positive for both countries." "I want to thank the honorable president and the first lady for everything they've done for myself and my wife during this visit. Everything is down to the highest order of perfection," Xi responded through a translator. "And there is thought in every little detail. And it's greatly appreciated. XI CAPS TRUMP STATE VISIT WITH SYMBOLIC FINAL STOP BEFORE LEAVING WASHINGTON "The president and I are like two people that's charting the course for the great ship of China-U.S. relations," he continued. "When the president visited China in May, we agreed on the vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. "This time, we've agreed to add new substance to it. That's the relationship, will be a constructive one of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity. So, from this, one can see that the prospects for this relationship will get more brighter." Xi, the leader of China’s ruling Communist Party, said he had two more opportunities to meet Trump this year, first at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in China in November and then at the G20 Summit in December at Trump’s Doral resort in Miami, Florida. "We will see you, and we'll be speaking a lot. I think our farmers are going to be very happy," Trump said Friday. "A lot of very positive things happened. But America is very happy about this visit, and I'm sure China is very happy also. Great things for both countries. And it's been just very, very productive." TRUMP-XI REUNION COMES WITH UNFINISHED BUSINESS — AND A BIGGER BATTLE LOOMING Xi arrived in Washington Wednesday evening for a summit with Trump, four months after the two leaders reached a sweeping agreement that included Chinese commitments on rare earths, agricultural purchases, trade and investment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Trump hailed that agreement as a breakthrough for American farmers, manufacturers and workers. But the latest talks unfolded during uneven progress on commitments involving rare-earth minerals, agricultural and commercial purchases, trade and investment, while key disputes over tariffs, advanced technology, artificial intelligence, intellectual property and Taiwan remain unresolved. "President Xi and Madam Peng have just left D.C., heading for China. The meeting was one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Much has been, and will be, accomplished. I look forward to our next meeting!" Fox News Digital’s Ashley J. DiMella and Peter D’Abrosca contributed to this report.

title: WNBA playoffs preview: why the Fever at +145 could be the best bet against defending champion Aces
description: The Minnesota Lynx earned the top seed, but can Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty pull off an upset in the WNBA playoffs first round?
content: We had one play in the WNBA last night, and it went the exact opposite of how I expected it to go. The Fever played like they had nothing to gain, and the Lynx played like they were fighting for playoff spots. Now we move into the postseason. Before we start the actual games, which tip off on Sunday, we should look at each series and see if there are any future bets that are worth putting into our accounts. All eight teams have a legitimate case for the championship, so this could get interesting fast. Lynx vs. Liberty When the season first started, the Liberty were the favorite to win the WNBA Title. I'm not sure if New York was just the popular pick or if it was due to Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu, and Jonquel Jones on the roster. Either way, the season didn't go quite as planned for the Liberty but they still ended up winning almost 60% of their games. The Lynx were also expected to have a different season. Without MVP Naphesa Collier for much of the year, it was expected that Minnesota would struggle this year. Olivia Miles, this year's Rookie of the Year and potential MVP, led the way, and they earned the best record in the WNBA. I think there is some good value on taking the Liberty to win at least one game in this series. I'm going to take this series to go three games at +100. RISING WNBA STAR OLIVIA MILES ECLIPSES CAITLIN CLARK'S ROOKIE SCORING RECORD Valkyries vs. Wings One team is built on star power, and the other is built on being a complete team. The Wings have the star power with Paige Bueckers, and she will be getting her first taste of the postseason. The team lost the #1 overall pick, Azzi Fudd, earlier this year to injury, so they aren't quite as deep as they used to be. The Valkyries are the #2 seed overall and have the best defense in basketball. They have the personnel to deal with Bueckers and everyone else on the Wings. I don't see the Wings winning a game here; I like this one to go just two games at -130. LYNX, VALKYRIES COACHES RIP 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' MOVEMENT AS PRO-TRANS MOB ROCKS 1ST RALLY AT NON-FEVER GAME Dream vs. Mystics The Atlanta Dream are one of the better teams in the game right now. They went 30-14 and have a good balance between inside and outside offense. The Dream have had good health this season, and all five starters are averaging nine or more points per game. The Mystics are led by Sonia Citron, but there are still some other solid players. Shakira Austin led the team in scoring and could cause some problems for the Dream. Washington beat the Dream 2-1 in the regular season. They were blown out in the loss and then won two home games, both by five points. I don't love the game for the Dream, and I think it will be just a two-game series, but I won't put an official bet on this one. CAITLIN CLARK SHINES, BUT FEVER SUFFER EMBARRASSING BLOWOUT LOSS TO MYSTICS AS PLAYOFF RACE HEATS UP Aces vs. Fever This is the marquee matchup of the first round. The Aces are the defending champions, and they've won three of the past four titles. A'ja Wilson is still the elite player who can be the difference-maker in any series. The Fever have been rather inconsistent this year, but they seemed to lock in for the postseason last year, and I think there is reason to believe they can do it again. I'm going to back Indiana to win this one at +145. Indiana gave Las Vegas the toughest battle last year in the playoffs; I think they make this go the full three games, even if the Fever don't win. title: Who is Sophie Cunningham? Fox Nation chronicles the WNBA star's rise from farm girl to women's sports advocate
description: Sophie Cunningham's rise from Missouri farm girl to Indiana Fever star and women's sports advocate is explored in the "Who Is Sophie Cunningham?" special.
content: Bold, beautiful and with a bullish resolve – Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has stormed onto the women's sports scene, commanding attention with her success on the court and unmistakable personality off it. "Men are attracted to her, and women want to be her," former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines said in Fox Nation's, "Who Is Sophie Cunningham?" Cunningham's appeal spans generations, with Gaines recalling the scores of young girls who lined up for a chance to meet the basketball star and get her autograph. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ADDRESSES PERCEPTION THAT SHE IS THE 'SEX SYMBOL' OF THE WNBA From her humble beginnings as a Missouri farm girl to her rise in professional basketball and emergence as a voice in the "protect women's sports" movement, Cunningham's journey takes center stage in the new Fox Nation special. But the athlete fans see battling on the hardwood is only part of the story. "She's kind of like 100% tomboy and 100% feminine," Gaines said of Cunningham's nature. "Sophie is fun and kind and fierce and sassy and tough and cool because all those things make you cool." Gaines is joined in the special by others, including activist and former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom, who shed light on the personality, convictions and loyalty that have helped Cunningham build a following beyond basketball. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ADDRESSES THE FALLOUT OVER HER STANCE ON TRANS ATHLETES NOT BELONGING IN WOMEN'S SPORTS In one instance, Kanter Freedom recalled hearing directly from Cunningham after he was ejected from an Aug. 23 WNBA game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever. "After the game, Sophie messaged me and said, 'So what happened?'" he said. Kanter Freedom said he explained the encounter to Cunningham but declined to reveal her response, teasing that the private exchange would "go viral" if made public. He had attended the game wearing a shirt defining a woman as an "adult human female." SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS MESSAGE TO HER HATERS AFTER SAYING MEN DON'T BELONG IN WOMEN'S SPORTS "I was literally there just to support [Sophie]," he said. Cunningham herself has attracted attention for speaking publicly about the debate surrounding transgender participation in women's sports. She told ESPN earlier this year, "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that.' "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think, with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room or young girls in sports who shouldn't have to go against biological men." Since her comments surfaced, the star athlete amassed support from the likes of politicians, former athletes and other girls fighting for the same cause.
