description: Toxicology reports in the Ole Miss deaths of Robert Strang and Aidan Hamilton could come within days as investigators weigh kratom and foul play.
author_name: Adam Sabes, Michael Ruiz, Madison Scarpino
content: OXFORD, Miss. — Toxicology reports in the suspicious deaths of two University of Mississippi students are expected to be completed as early as next week, according to the state's commissioner of public safety, and Oxford police have separately announced arrests in connection with a raid on a tobacco shop accused of trafficking narcotics. The victims have been identified as Robert Strang, a 20-year-old junior from Atlanta, and Aidan Hamilton, an 18-year-old freshman from Colorado. Both families have asked for privacy and compassion as they mourn the loss of their sons. It remains unclear how the students died, but narcotics detectives are involved in investigations into both of their deaths. If the reports find fentanyl, there is a special Mississippi law that can be used to target whoever sold it, according to authorities. "Under Parker’s Law, enacted in 2022, criminal charges may be pursued when an unlawful delivery of fentanyl results in a person’s death," Sean Tindell, the commissioner of Mississippi's Department of Public Safety, told Fox News Digital. "If the investigation establishes those circumstances, law enforcement will work with prosecutors to pursue the appropriate charges and hold those responsible accountable." OLE MISS DEATHS, DRUGGINGS HAVE ‘PEOPLE SCARED TO LEAVE’ DORMS AS BARS, GREEK LIFE CLAMP DOWN: STUDENTS Separately, Oxford police have announced the arrests of two men in a narcotics investigation connected to a local tobacco shop. It's not immediately clear whether the raid has any connection to the student deaths. "At this point in time, we do not know that," Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch told Fox News Digital about whether the arrests are connected to the deaths. "We know that, again, it's been a very thorough situation as they are going through and making these arrests and preparing the evidence. So we don't know at this point if they are connected at all." WATCH: Mississippi AG says ‘lives at risk’ amid drug investigations The suspects were linked to an Oxford retail business where police allegedly found stockpiles of drugs including THC products and kratom, which is legal in many parts of the country but not in Lafayette County. "During the search, agents recovered more than 500 units of kratom, along with an assortment of THC cartridges, gummies, and other suspected narcotics," police said in a statement. "Kratom has been prohibited from possession, distribution, and sale within the City of Oxford since 2019." SEND US A TIP The store is called Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store, located in the 100 block of Heritage Drive in Oxford. Oxford police arrested Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Mohamed, 18. Both are local residents. In 2022, the business owner, Amer Alowdi, 40, was indicted on narcotics trafficking charges and fled the country before being prosecuted, police said in a statement. It was not immediately clear how the business remained open. Tindell told Fox News Digital Thursday that while authorities haven't uncovered any indications of foul play, they haven't ruled it out either. "Until the autopsy is reported, and the investigators have an opportunity to get statements and collect evidence, then that final determination will not be made until later," he said. WHAT IS KRATOM? Police previously said that they found packages of kratom, which is commercially available in many places but not in Lafayette County, at both scenes. title: Trump's quiet China wins are more important than Xi's empty state visit
description: The U.S.-China trade deficit is falling fast, but Xi Jinping offered little beyond pandas and ping-pong diplomacy during Trump's State Visit.
content: China’s President Xi Jinping, ruler for life, is not ready to make sweeping deals with the USA on soybeans, AI or anything else. This was a State Visit, not a summit, but even so, deliverables were light. China’s state-owned People’s Daily was so strapped for material that they ran a story titled: "Bonded by Ping-Pong: China-U.S. friendship writes a new chapter." But don’t lose heart. The Trump Administration has scored some quiet wins and much better field position for the long haul. "The old adage of deliverables in a relationship that we have with China is really not measurable in many ways," said U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue. It’s about "continuing the conversation." What matters most to America in the long term is the trade deficit. Good news: it's falling. Already the gap between U.S. exports and imports from China is down from $297 billion in 2024 to $202 billion in 2025, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer says the deficit is on track to drop to $140 billion for 2026. If achieved, this is a historic reversal of globalization. The gap hasn’t been this low in over 20 years. TRUMP-XI REUNION COMES WITH UNFINISHED BUSINESS — AND A BIGGER BATTLE LOOMING Credit what Team Trump calls "managed" trade: specific, non-sensitive goods, such as agricultural products and medical devices. "All those export controls that are national security issues, we take those off the table," Greer told CNBC. Greer promised more trade details next week. However, China has bought only half the amount of soybeans agreed, according to American Soybean Association President Scott Metzger, so there’s still a ways to go on the trade balance. This is not glamorous work. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent held a 12-hour meeting on Sunday with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng. In the end, all the two sides could do was extend the 2025 truce for two more months. You remember what happened last year: China stopped licensing rare earth material exports, and Trump slapped on massive tariffs. "I don’t know whether a bigger deal can be done. I don’t know whether we will just roll the current deal," Bessent said Wednesday. The Bessent-He meeting was also supposed to tee up some kind of agreement on an artificial intelligence safety mechanism for Trump and Xi. Afterwards, Bessent kept to the optimistic line that China was eager to engage, and spoke about at least setting up a hot line to deal with incidents across borders. Don’t count on much more. China does not participate in nuclear arms control. Any AI accord will be all talk with no teeth, just like the U.S.-China fentanyl working group. AMERICA AND CHINA ARE FIGHTING FOR THE FUTURE OF AI — CHIPS ARE THE BATTLEFIELD What’s much more important is keeping the U.S. AI tech stack ahead of China. At the White House State Dinner on Thursday night, it was good to see Trump assemble the tech titans as he did on his visit to Beijing in May. These leaders from Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Google, Dell, OpenAI, Citigroup, etc. have the cash and the smarts to keep the U.S. in the lead in AI. SpaceX and Amazon Leo are launching satellites that will keep U.S. dominance over China in the low earth orbit market sector. Google has Project Suncatcher to try running its tensor processing units with solar power on orbit. Innovation is America’s edge over China. Yes, they'd like to book deals with China in areas such as chips and financial services, but China has been lagging. For example, Nvidia is cleared to sell its H200 chips to China (not its most advanced products) but only small batches of chips have been purchased by Tencent and ByteDance. The reality is that China is cutting imports under Xi’s policy of semi-conductor self-reliance. That’s a sign that China is girding for long-term conflict. Fortunately, President Trump has taken many actions to strengthen America’s position. The Greenland agreement, investing in Venezuela’s oil, getting Chinese operators out of the Panama Canal Zone, a hefty defense budget aimed at countering China, expanding the Space Force, and yes, the U.S. Navy blockade of the Strait of Hormuz: all this has protected American interests. Boundaries are good for geopolitics. CHINA IS TAKING THE FIGHT TO THE STARS. AMERICA MUST RECLAIM SPACE SUPREMACY And what did Xi contribute? Xi Jinping announced China’s welcome loan of two pandas to the Atlanta Zoo, and a preposterous initiative for 100,000 Americans to study in China over the next five years. This, from a China ramping up nuclear weapons production, hassling U.S. satellites on orbit, backing Russia with oil purchases and defense electronics, and giving what Perdue termed "intel and parts" to Iran. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That offer was deeply cynical. Xi wants to show off Chinese culture, but in fact, there are fewer than 2,000 American students in China compared to 265,919 Chinese students in the USA. Last fall, Harvard enrolled 1,452 students from China, mostly graduate students. But if you want to go, Duke University has a joint venture in China which got a flattering and no doubt coincidental write-up in the state-owned China Daily on Friday.

title: Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium concerts called off as troubled tour faces fresh setback
description: Severe weather warnings forced Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows to be canceled amid a backdrop of controversy involving Macklemore and Robert Kraft.
content: Ed Sheeran's concerts at Gillette Stadium have been canceled. Sheeran was set to perform at the Foxborough, Massachusetts, venue on Sept. 25 and 26, but according to a statement shared on social media, potentially dangerous weather conditions have forced the singer to step back. "Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium," Sheeran's tour promoter, Messina Touring Group, said in a statement. "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority." ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS The company noted that refunds are available at the point of purchase. Gillette Stadium reposted the statement. While the weather prompted the cancellations, the owner of Gillette Stadium, Robert Kraft, has been in the headlines recently due to the controversy surrounding Sheeran and one of the former openers for his tour, Macklemore. After Macklemore used his slot at Sheeran's MetLife Stadium shows to express his support for Palestinians, many people were upset, including owners of stadiums where Sheeran was slated to play. The "Thrift Shop" rapper was eventually dropped from the tour, and in a lengthy statement reacting to the news, he wrote in part, "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues." "Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line." But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike." Kraft wrote that he agreed with Macklemore that "too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering," but argued that "only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate." He added, "Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive." title: 'Squad' Democrat slammed by Trump admin for most 'radical' plan targeting ICE yet
description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin fires back at Rep. Delia Ramirez's radical bill to abolish ICE, CBP, and dismantle the Department of Homeland Security.
content: EXCLUSIVE: Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin is firing back at a progressive House Democrat who is pushing one of the most radical Trump administration crackdowns yet. Mullin and his DHS spokesperson both criticized legislation by Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., a member of the progressive "Squad," that would dismantle most of the department and abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). "Radical leftists are calling to defund the police and abolish DHS. It’s NEVER going to happen. Our 270,000 DHS patriots are keeping Americans SAFE— unlike this open-borders politician who refuses to prioritize Americans over illegal aliens," Mullin told Fox News Digital. DHS CHIEF FIRES BACK AT JAYAPAL OVER CLAIM MAJORITY OF IMMIGRATION ARRESTS POSE 'NO THREAT' His spokesperson went even further, telling Fox News Digital that Ramirez "should be thanking our law enforcement for removing these dangerous criminals from her district—NOT vilifying law enforcement." "This type of rhetoric is contributing to a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them as they put their lives on the line," the DHS spokesperson said. "While sanctuary politicians smear ICE, law enforcement is arresting criminals and saving countless American lives." DEMS SHAMED AS DHS BRINGS ICE SHOOTING RECEIPTS AFTER POLITICIAN CALLED ICE OFFICERS ‘LIARS WITH MASKS’ DHS also pointed Fox News Digital to a list of illegal immigrants arrested in Ramirez's home state of Illinois. Ramirez's legislation, the Reimagining Safety Act, would create a "Department of Community Safety" while dismantling DHS as it is currently known. Certain agencies like the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Coast Guard, and customs functions would be preserved. Backlash has also been targeted at federal immigration officials' killing of two U.S. citizens earlier this year. But Ramirez's bill would go further in dismantling the current anti-illegal immigration enforcement system with its call to end CBP as well as ICE. She fired back at the Trump administration's criticism in a statement to Fox News Digital, "Every day, Americans wake up with a new reason to dismantle DHS, reimagine safety, and build something that honors our shared humanity. The people have the power to reshape the government: instead of the weapon DHS has proven to be, we need a department built on the best parts of who we are and can be, and the best examples of how we can take care of each other in hard times." title: Xi’s 100K invitation to America’s youth sets off alarm bells over what could follow them home
description: Chinese President Xi Jinping's plan to bring 100,000 young Americans to China sparked fears of communist propaganda and potential hostage scenarios.
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China over the next five years is raising concerns among critics who warn Beijing could use the exchange program to spread propaganda and influence a new generation of Americans. Xi made the announcement Thursday during a White House arrival ceremony, as he visited Washington this week for talks with President Donald Trump on artificial intelligence, intellectual property, trade practices and rare-earth minerals. Xi said China will invite 100,000 young Americans over the next five years for exchanges and study, building on existing programs that have included university visits, summer programs, youth forums and other educational and cultural exchanges. CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE China created its Young Envoys Scholarship program, administered by the China Education Association for International Exchange, to carry out Xi’s earlier 2023 pledge to invite 50,000 young Americans for exchanges and study. Some trips are fully funded, while others require participants to cover expenses, with the stated goal of strengthening ties between Chinese and American youth. While some supported the program, many critics slammed the idea over propaganda and safety concerns. "This is clearly intended to indoctrinate young Americans in China," Manhattan Institute fellow Daniel Di Martino posted to X. "But if some people should go, let the DSA members and let them see the Uyghur concentration camps and poor rural villages. Let them speak to the political prisoners. And let them visit and meet Hong Kongers." "100,000 more Timmy Walz's. What could go wrong," said one user, referencing Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, who taught English and U.S. history in Foshan in 1989 after graduating from Chadron State College. "They’ll come back as Governor of Minnesota," another user added. YOUNG AMERICANS BREAK SHARPLY FROM OLDER AMERICANS ON CHINA THREAT, NEW POLL FINDS "No! They will brainwash them while over there," said one person. "I welcome Xi Jinping’s invitation for 100,000 American students to visit and study in China. As Co-Chair of the Congressional International Exchanges Caucus, I believe educational and cultural exchanges are an important way to build mutual understanding and expertise," said Democratic California Rep. Ami Bera. "But those exchanges depend on trust and the ability to study, speak, and engage without fear of harassment or arbitrary detention," Bera continued. "Right now, American scholar Min Zin remains wrongfully detained in China, and Beijing continues to target scholars, human rights advocates, and diaspora communities whose work or speech it finds unwelcome." "I’m one of the Americans who spent years living and studying in China. I majored in Chinese literature in college. Sadly, I cannot recommend young Americans do the same thing today," said Atlantic Council visiting fellow Isaac Stone Fish. US WARNS AMERICANS ABOUT EXIT BANS AND 'UNJUST' DETENTION IN POPULAR DESTINATION Fish said that China has grown more repressive and less welcoming to foreigners. "If tensions worsen between the United States and China, those students could effectively function as hostages," Fish added. "Are they coming back as Communists," asked one user. "To be honest, I'm not sure I WANT 100,000 impressionable American students sent off to some CCP-controlled propaganda tour," said conservative commentator Nick Sortor. TRUMP TO ASK XI TO FREE WRONGFULLY DETAINED US CITIZEN AS WIFE SPEAKS OUT The Department of Education referred Fox News Digital to the White House when asked for comment. Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment. U.S. authorities have separately warned that American students abroad can become targets for foreign intelligence recruitment, citing past cases involving China. Glenn Duffie Shriver, a Michigan student who studied abroad in Shanghai in 2002–2003, returned to China after graduating in 2004 and was recruited there by Chinese intelligence officers. Shriver was paid to apply for positions with the State Department and CIA to access classified information for the Chinese. He was sentenced to four years in federal prison in 2011.

title: Iranian president blames US for Middle East conflict while denying nuclear ambitions, offers to dilute uranium
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian claims Tehran will submit its nuclear program to verification and dilute enriched uranium to ease tensions.
content: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian flatly denied Thursday that Tehran wants a nuclear bomb while claiming Iran is willing to submit its nuclear program for international inspection, blaming Washington for the nearly seven-month war in the Middle East and accusing it of blocking diplomacy. Pezeshkian also provided fresh details about a roughly seven-hour meeting with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei that he said took place more than a month ago. Asked point-blank during an exclusive interview on Fox News’ "Special Report," "Do you want a nuclear bomb or not?" the Iranian leader firmly rejected the premise. "Not at all. Not at all. Our martyred, esteemed supreme leader had announced several times that, from a religious decree, it is unholy. It is illegal," he told Bret Baier, referencing religious edicts issued against weapons of mass destruction. IRAN 'ALREADY AGREED' TO GIVING UP NUCLEAR WEAPON AMBITIONS, TRUMP REVEALS Pezeshkian's public denial came amid long-term international scrutiny of Iran’s nuclear program and its enrichment of uranium to levels well beyond those typically used for civilian nuclear power. This became President Donald Trump's central rationale for launching Operation Epic Fury in February. On Thursday, however, Pezeshkian indicated Tehran would be open to lowering its enrichment levels and allowing outside verification as part of an effort to ease nuclear tensions. "So, that weapon's mass destruction. We said we’re willing to dilute them. It’s not a big deal. We are willing to submit ourselves to verification," he said. Pezeshkian also pointed to the failed memorandum of understanding, or MOU, signed by him and President Donald Trump in June intended to halt hostilities and establish a framework for a broader U.S.-Iran agreement. The process was intended by Washington to lead to an end to Iran’s nuclear ambitions and included a 60-day process toward that final deal. "We have no problems. We did reach an agreement with your president," Pezeshkian said of Trump, who signed the document at the Palace of Versailles in France. "That agreement was signed, and, based on that, we are willing and still wish to move forward. IRAN NUCLEAR DEAL HINGES ON IAEA ACCESS TO LONG-BLOCKED ATOMIC WEAPON SITES, EXPERTS SAY "And the framework was agreed upon. We had not closed the Strait of Hormuz; it was open without any legal justification or framework," he assured. "They attacked us. They assassinated and martyred our esteemed supreme leader, our scientists, our military commanders and government." Pezeshkian then criticized Washington for the subsequent breakdown in diplomacy but insisted Tehran remains prepared to reach an agreement. "The problem is that America, instead of conducting dialog, they descend into the arena by bombing us first, by blocking every pathway. We are ready," he said. "This is not the way to conduct yourself on the world stage. They can have free access to see whatever we have, but not to put us under such pressure, under blockades, deny us access." Pezeshkian also broadened his criticism of Washington, blaming the U.S. for the conflict while portraying Iran’s actions as defensive. "We do not seek to kill Americans, as shown by actions, demonstrable actions. America has sought to kill Iranians," he said. "What we know is that if we’re attacked, we must defend ourselves." TRUMP BETS ECONOMIC PRESSURE CAN SQUEEZE IRAN AS REGIME’S OWN FAILURES DEEPEN THE PAIN Addressing U.S. military strikes — including Operation Outcast — and increasing secondary sanctions, Pezeshkian said Iran would continue resisting Washington’s campaign. "This is something that has been the doing of the United States," he said. "We will keep resisting. We will find ways, and the life of our country will continue. We will remain. "Yes, we do have economic issues, certainly. But in order to remain, we will go through any hardship and endure. "If America thinks that they can keep sanctioning us, we have nothing to do, nor do we consider any type of American elections. If the current American government, within international legal frameworks, wishes to reach an agreement, fine. If not, before the elections or after the elections, what difference does it make for us?" Pezeshkian repeated that Iran does not want the war to continue, while blaming Israel for helping provoke the conflict and putting responsibility on Washington to bring it to an end. TRUMP GIVES EVERY NATION AN EASY CHOICE: DO BUSINESS WITH AMERICA OR TERRORIST IRAN "We will stand resolutely to defend ourselves. We never sought war. We do not seek war," he said. "I deeply believe that humans should not cause the death of another human. But with the instigations conducted by Israel, they have imposed this war on us. "But we do not wish to continue. It’s America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not." During the interview, Pezeshkian also pointed to a roughly seven-hour, face-to-face meeting with Mojtaba Khamenei as evidence that the son of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei remained in charge of Iran. "We met for about seven hours," he said. "As I said earlier, we conducted talks face to face," he added. Addressing Khamenei’s health and whether he remained firmly in charge, Pezeshkian said: "Very much so, completely." "The implementation of the policies is in the hands of the administration and the government. But the consultations and the directions come from there," he confirmed. TRUMP SAYS IRAN WILL PAY — WHAT IT TAKES TO END THE WAR REMAINS UNCLEAR When Baier pressed Pezeshkian on whether Khamenei would address the Iranian people about the war or speak directly with Trump, he pointed to security concerns. "Well, this is a process that was created in our society, which is the lack of security that was created by the action of foreigners, the action of aggressors," Pezeshkian said. The Iranian president also addressed reports that Iranian forces used Chinese satellite imagery to carry out a deadly strike on a U.S. base in Jordan. The attack resulted in the deaths of three U.S. service members. When questioned about the reports, Pezeshkian denied direct knowledge. It is their own business within their own guidelines."

title: Trump to usher in ‘golden age’ of American tech with DC bash showcasing powerful new tool

"This is really an incredible collection of people that are working in service to the nation and really showcasing what the future of America is, where we're headed," said Gebbia. "What if people didn't say that? What if people have had a different sentiment? It's entirely possible they can. It takes a president who cares about this, it takes an administration who wants to invest in it, and it takes the right talent to build it." "President Trump has those three things."

title: Unearthed: El-Sayed called for repealing law that made sex without disclosing HIV status a felony
description: Abdul El-Sayed once called Michigan's HIV criminalization law "hateful" and "discriminatory," a stance now under scrutiny in his Senate race.
content: Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed once called for repealing a Michigan law that made it a felony for people who knew they had HIV to have sex without first informing their partner — a position he is standing by eight years later as he campaigns in one of the nation's most competitive Senate races As he unsuccessfully ran for Michigan governor in 2018, El-Sayed repeatedly took aim at the law. The law carried a prison sentence of up to four years for people who knew they were HIV-positive and engaged in sexual penetration without first informing their partner of their HIV status. "You should not be criminalized for a disease. That is absolutely wrong. It’s hateful. It’s discriminatory, and we can, as a state, do better. You can count on me for that," El-Sayed said as he ran for governor. MICHIGAN STUDENT CONFRONTS EL-SAYED OVER IRAN STANCE Fast-forward eight years and El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and a former health director for Detroit-anchored Wayne County, is battling former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in the midterm race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. The showdown in Michigan is a must hold for the Democrats as they try to win back control of the Senate from the GOP. As he ran for the 2018 Democratic gubernatorial nomination — a contest he lost to now-two-term Gov. Gretchen Whitmer — El-Sayed's campaign website stated, "Repeal HIV/AIDS criminalization laws and the exclusion of transgender Michiganders from state Medicaid." When asked in 2018 if he supported the decriminalization of HIV through legislation that would create two levels of misdemeanors, El-Sayed said at the time, "One of the big things that we have to recognize about HIV is that no disease can be illegal. The continuing forward of these laws on the books stigmatize people with the disease." SIX FORCES THAT COULD HELP REPUBLICANS DEFY HISTORY IN THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS Whitmer also supported changing the law, which dated to 1988, saying as she ran for governor, "It’s wrong to criminalize sickness, which is what this law has effectively done. It absolutely should be revisited." The law was reformed in early 2019, after passing a GOP-controlled legislature with broad bipartisan support. The revised statute limited the felony provisions to vaginal and anal intercourse involving an intent to transmit HIV or cases in which HIV was actually transmitted, reduced certain non-transmission offenses to misdemeanors and protected medically suppressed people from prosecution under the law's reckless-disregard provision. "Abdul supports the bipartisan reform bill that passed in 2019 through a Republican legislature that eliminated the discriminatory laws on the books," campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner told Fox News Digital. "As a public health professional, Abdul has fought to support programs that stem the spread of diseases, including HIV." Richner added that "the Trump administration has completely exacerbated this crisis by defunding the organizations and programs that do frontline care to prevent transmission and exposure in the first place. In the US Senate, Abdul will fight back against Donald Trump and RFK Jr’s attempts to dismantle our public health infrastructure and ensure all Americans have access to the care they need." Last week, as he landed an endorsement from the Human Rights Campaign, a leading LGBTQ advocacy group, El-Sayed highlighted that if elected to the Senate, "I’ll fight to ensure every Michigander can live without discrimination and never have to wonder whether their rights will still be there tomorrow." He has made support for "Medicare for all" a major component of his campaign. El-Sayed has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and has been a vocal critic of Israel during its war against Hamas, characterizing Israel’s actions in Gaza as "genocide" against Palestinians.

title: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft hears boos from Lambeau Field fans and offers tone deaf response
description: Tucker Kraft called Lambeau Field booing "pretty disappointing" after the Green Bay Packers' blowout home loss to the Atlanta Falcons Thursday.
content: Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft dropped a couple of passes during Thursday night's blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons, which was indicative of his team's stunningly inept performance that caused the Lambeau Field crowd to boo the home team. And Kraft was stunned by that. Hurt by that. No, not the loss. The booing. BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QB DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENT "Yeah, it’s pretty tough," Kraft told reporters huddled around his locker stall. "You know, like everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos. I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing." Friends, it is 2026 not 1966. So, the Packers of Vince Lombardi, Ray Nitschke, Jim Taylor, Herb Adderly, Willie Wood, Jerry Kramer and the other men who made this franchise a beacon of excellence and toughness and turned Green Bay into Titletown are a long-ago memory. Now, we've got these Packers, who lost their last five games last season, and collapsed in giving up a big lead to lose their season-opener this season, and then lost their home-opener against the Falcons on Thursday night. And these guys are complaining about being booed. FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE These Packers got run out of Lambeau Field by a previously winless team. So, darn right, the fans booed. But Kraft, who heard the boos, is tone-deaf. "It's pretty disappointing," Kraft continued. "It's not gonna help us win. Like, I don't know, I don't know what people think that's gonna rally us or something like that. "But, you know, we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. Um, but, probably much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us." This is not the way, Tucker Kraft. You just signed a $75 million contract extension. You got $26.5 million of that in a signing bonus. So, just for signing your name on the document, you collected more money than most of your fans make in their lifetimes by a multiple of 10. And you don't understand why they're unhappy when you and your teammates do not perform? You don't picture boos? Fans didn't picture their team giving up 27 unanswered points to the Falcons. Fans didn't picture their team rushing for a grand total of 17 yards. Or the defense giving up 242 rushing yards. And nobody pictured Kraft suddenly talking about them, as if Deshaun Watson suddenly took over his body. The stunning part is that Kraft is one of the most stand-up guys on the Packers. He is a tough player. He fights back from injuries. He is not a victim. But this was full-on soft victim mentality. To be fair: This is not all Kraft talked about after the game. He talked about rallying and even admitted to not playing "to my standard." But that's the minimum-expected reaction after what fans have witnessed going back to December 2025. What no one expects is a team leader in any way lecturing fans that showed their displeasure the only way they really can. Those people pay to be in the stadium and have the right to express their displeasure in this manner. Some fans at other venues throw beer bottles. Kraft, his teammates and coaches have been giving the fans plenty to be displeased about. And the only proper response to the question about being booed on Thursday night was, "We deserved it and will try to do better." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

title: More Americans than ever now have a positive view of socialism, new poll says
description: A new Gallup Poll shows 43% of Americans view socialism positively, with independents surging from 37% to 45% as big business approval plummets.
content: More Americans than ever view socialism positively, according to a Gallup poll released Wednesday, as 43% view it positively for the first time since 2010. Gallup asked respondents if they have a positive or negative image of socialism, capitalism, free enterprise, big business and small business in the poll conducted in August. Fifty-five percent of Americans view capitalism positively. The poll's findings show a significant drop in how Americans view big business, which is down 14 points from 2010, free enterprise down 9 points and capitalism down 6 points. Small business is the only category that hasn't lost any support. SOCIALISM SURGES AMONG DEMOCRATS AS PARTY LEADERS REJECT DSA AGENDA: ‘PACK OF FOOLS’ The increase in socialism’s positive rating through 2025 was largely due to the views of Democrats, rising from 50% in 2010 to 66% last year. However, this year's increase is due to political independents, according to Gallup, whose positive rating jumped from 37% in 2025 to 45%. This year's findings show 65% of Democrats view socialism positively, compared with 14% of Republicans. FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS Lucas Holtz, a senior political advisor at Third Way, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "The Gallup poll isn't evidence of Americans embracing socialism—it's evidence that Americans are rejecting the economic status quo. When we look a single layer beneath to ask whether voters support socialist policies, support completely collapses." "Working-class Americans are pissed about the costs of everyday life and the economy, but it's off base to think that a majority of Democrats and independents would back wholesale DSA socialism," Holtz continued. JOE MANCHIN SAYS HE WOULD NEVER SUPPORT A SOCIALIST CANDIDATE, WARNS AGAINST 'CRAZY' POSITIONS Holtz pointed to a Third Way poll that found Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents prefer "capitalism with guardrails" over socialism by 24 points. "Echelon Insights also ran a poll and found that socialism is 33 points underwater with independents. And they found that a whole lot of DSA-aligned policies would make voters less likely to back a candidate. Abolishing police and prisons: 73% less likely (77% among independents). Ending all immigration detention and deportations: 43% less likely (42% among independents). Government ownership of major transportation and energy infrastructure: 39% less likely (44% less likely among independents)," Holtz said. The Gallup poll found that views of the economic systems differed by age group. Adults aged 18 to 34 view socialism more positively than capitalism, 57% vs. 43%, and those aged 55 and older view capitalism more positively than socialism, 65% vs. 34%. VANCE WARNS THERE WILL BE A 'SOCIALIST PRESIDENT IN THIS COUNTRY' IF GOP DOESN'T FIX ECONOMY FOR YOUNG PEOPLE Adults ages 35 to 54, however, rate socialism and capitalism about the same. A professor of political science at Northeastern University, Costas Panagopoulos, told Fox News Digital, "For Independents, whose views are driven least by partisan attachments, perceptions about socialism are gaining in favorability in part because they feel betrayed, overlooked or neglected by modern American capitalism." SOCIALISM’S RISE INSIDE THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY NOW THREATENS THE AMERICAN DREAM Gallup's summary of its poll read, "Capitalism, free enterprise and especially big business are viewed less positively than they once were, while socialism has gained ground. Those changes have been most pronounced among Democrats and younger adults, but this year's uptick in socialism's appeal reflects a novel shift among independents." title: Dozens of pledges found covered in food in sweltering frat basement as police investigate alleged hazing
description: Roughly 30 partially clothed young men were found in a sweltering basement during rush week at the Alpha Epsilon Pi house in Madison, Wisconsin.
content: Police responding to an anonymous hazing tip at a fraternity in Madison, Wisconsin, found roughly 30 partially clothed young men packed inside a sweltering basement, covered in food, condiments and other liquids – with several showing signs of being physically assaulted, authorities said. The Madison Police Department said officers were dispatched to the Alpha Epsilon Pi (AEPi) house along Langdon Street around 8:20 p.m. Wednesday, where a thermostat in the basement was set to 81 degrees, creating hot and humid conditions. The vast majority of those inside were 18 years old, police said. Officers declared the gathering unlawful before escorting everyone outside and checking the pledges for injuries and incapacitation. MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY Police said the chapter is not recognized or accredited by the University of Wisconsin-Madison and was terminated by the university more than a decade ago. Alpha Epsilon Pi's national organization, however, told Fox News Digital it still recognizes the Madison chapter. Madison Police Capt. Kipp Hartman said Thursday that he observed what appeared to be fresh redness and marks potentially consistent with being struck, but did not see any open wounds. FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS Hartman added that he was not aware of anyone being transported for medical treatment. Police said fraternity president Brayden J. Klein and vice president Samuel N. Vane, both 20, were arrested on hazing and disorderly conduct allegations and taken to the Dane County Jail. PENN STATE COCAINE BUST NETS 14 ARRESTS OVER ALLEGED PLEDGE COKE-CUTTING ‘INDOCTRINATION' RITUALS Hartman said both alleged offenses are misdemeanors and the Dane County District Attorney's Office will review the case. Investigators are still working to determine exactly what happened inside the house, and Hartman said officers encountered inconsistencies while interviewing those who were there. "We had limited cooperation," Hartman said. The incident came during rush week at UW-Madison. Hartman said he believes everyone involved was a university student. title: The SEC might have more headliners, but the Big 12 has the most underrated matchup of week 4
description: Oklahoma State and West Virginia both own ranked wins, and Saturday's Big 12 showdown could determine who has the inside track to a playoff berth.
content: We have one hell of a college football weekend on our hands, folks. If you haven't done so already, open up another tab and take a quick look at the slate for this Saturday. I'm sure your eyes will be drawn to plenty of action in the SEC, as the league has two of the more intriguing match-ups in terms of national relevance. The number one team in the land, Texas, will travel to Knoxville to take on a dangerous looking Tennessee team, while the team with perhaps the best resume in the country, Ole Miss, takes a trip to The Swamp to play the Gators. My point is that Saturday will feature wall-to-wall action and could end up being one of the best weekend slates of the season. But one game that isn't getting the shine it deserves is taking place in the Big 12. It doesn't feature a ranked-on-ranked match-up, and is occurring at the same time that LSU and Texas A&M are set to square off, but the showdown between Oklahoma State and West Virginia will be must see television. NEW AP POLL TOP 25 PUNISHES OHIO STATE, OKLAHOMA, OREGON, TEXAS JUMPS TO NO 1 AFTER BIG COMEBACK For starters, both teams have a ranked win on their resume, something many programs around the country can't say they have, as the Mountaineers took down a top-25 Virginia squad while the Cowboys toppled mighty Oregon in week two. The match-up will feature a couple of great coaches on opposite ends of the spectrum, both stylistically and in terms of where they are in their career. OKLAHOMA STATE MIGHT HAVE KNOWN WHICH PLAYS OREGON DUCKS WERE RUNNING DURING UPSET WIN Oklahoma State has Eric Morris roaming their sidelines, and if you've been paying attention to me at all in the past year, you know how much I like this guy. Morris, the young up and comer, is an air raid disciple, and it shows in his team's offensive splits. The Cowboys rank top ten in total offense and have the best passing offense in the Big 12 thanks to Morris' system and quarterback extraordinaire Drew Mestemaker. On the other side you have Rich Rodriguez, and if that name sounds familiar, it's because he's on his second tour in Morgantown. His first go around as West Virginia's head coach was wildly successful, featuring plenty of explosive offenses and BCS Bowl victories, and it looks like he's picked up right where he left off. The Mountaineers have one of the best rushing offenses in the country, ranking in the top three nationally in rush yards per game. This game will be an explosive one when either offense is on the field, as the scoreboard operator better hope he's up for the challenge. The stakes will be plenty high as well, because the winner of this game will have an early inside track on making it to the Big 12 title game and potentially upsetting Texas Tech en route to a College Football Playoff berth. You will want to be tuned in when these two square off in the Mountain State. If it's not the main game on your TV, I implore you to at least go picture-and-picture or just go buy a second monitor (they're cheap these days). Don't let the fancy numbers next to teams like LSU and Texas A&M distract you from the fact that this could be the most entertaining game of the weekend. title: '80s star Tiffany steps into dream role after leaving Hollywood behind
description: Tiffany reveals her Off-Broadway role in "Spandex the Musical" fulfills a lifelong dream she put on hold when "I Think We're Alone Now" took off.
content: '80s pop icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight as she fulfills a dream she had prior to becoming a teen idol. The 54-year-old singer, who rose to fame in 1987 after her song "I Think We're Alone Now" became a massive hit, made her Off-Broadway debut in "Spandex the Musical" last week. During a July interview with People magazine, Tiffany reflected on why taking the stage felt like a "true full-circle moment for me." '80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD "Before music came into my life, I was a dancer and an actor, and those dreams were put on hold when ‘I Think We’re Alone Now’ took off and my recording career began," she said. Tiffany, whose full name is Tiffany Darwish, launched her career with the now-legendary Shopping Mall Tour '87, performing free concerts at malls across the country beginning in June 1987. The grassroots campaign helped turn the then-15-year-old into a teen sensation before she became a chart-topping artist. In September 1987, Tiffany's cover of Tommy James and the Shondells' 1967 hit "I Think We're Alone Now" climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 less than two months after its release and made her a household name. "I Think We're Alone Now" was the second single released from her self-titled debut album. She followed up with "Could've Been," the third single released from "Tiffany," which also topped the Billboard Hot 100. In addition, the album produced her Beatles cover "I Saw Him Standing There," which peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, and "Feelings of Forever," which reached the No. 50 spot. At 16, Tiffany became the youngest female artist to top the Billboard 200 with a debut album. She went on to headline her first major tour in 1988, with New Kids on the Block opening for her before the boy band's own meteoric rise. However, Tiffany's chart dominance proved difficult to sustain. While her 1988 sophomore album, "Hold an Old Friend's Hand," was certified platinum by the RIAA and produced the Top 10 hit "All This Time," it fell short of matching the success of her debut. As the teen-pop landscape shifted in the early 1990s, her third album, "New Inside," failed to gain commercial traction. RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD In 1993, Tiffany released her fourth album, "Dreams Never Die," which was issued only in Asian markets. Afterward, Tiffany largely stepped back from the mainstream music scene to focus on raising her son Elijah, whom she shares with her ex-husband, makeup artist Bulmaro Garcia. The two were married from 1992 to 2003. In the early 2000s, Tiffany left Hollywood behind and moved to Nashville. During a 2023 interview with Fox News Digital, she explained why she decided to embrace a simpler life in Tennessee. DOLLY PARTON'S PATH FROM NASHVILLE NEWCOMER TO BILLBOARD'S NO. 1 COUNTRY MUSIC ARTIST OF ALL TIME "I came to Nashville for the first time when I was 10," the California native recalled. "I’ve been coming back ever since. I love being out in the country – I’m a country girl at heart. I’ve toured all over the world and this place has always been home for me. There’s just something about coming home to my little ranch… I’ve never looked back." Since the days of her teenage stardom, Tiffany has continued to tour and release music as an independent artist. She has also made appearances in movies and television shows and starred in several reality TV series. During a June interview with Fox News Digital, Tiffany detailed how she spent the past several years building a culinary brand that combines her love of cooking, entertaining and connecting with fans. Through her platform, "Let's Food With Tiffany," she offers recipes, virtual cooking experiences and food-focused events that showcase the same energy and creativity that made her a pop sensation. Earlier this year, Tiffany released her second cookbook, "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ‘80s Kitchen Encore," which she created with Las Vegas celebrity chef Alicia Shevetone. "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ’80s Kitchen Encore" followed her first cookbook, "Breakfast with Tiffany," which she released independently. In July, Tiffany announced that she would make her New York theatrical debut in "Spandex the Musical," in which she plays Linda Gustafson, a housewife who competes in the fictional 1988 Crystal Light National Aerobics Championship. "I’ve always believed the right role would find me, and the moment I read the script, I knew Linda was that character," she told People magazine at the time. "Just as Linda discovers a new passion through aerobics that changes her life, I’ve found exciting new passions beyond music through my ‘Pop Life’ cookbook, ‘Let’s Food With Tiffany’ events, and now returning to acting on stage," she continued. "It’s a reminder that it’s never too late to reinvent yourself." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Spandex: The Musical" is a 10-day limited Off-Broadway engagement which runs through Sept. 27. After each performance, Tiffany performs "I Think We're Alone Now" during the curtain call. "There are so many wonderful parallels between Linda’s journey and my own, and I’m thrilled the producers have even woven in some fun Tiffany Easter eggs that I know longtime fans are going to love," she told People. title: Social worker sues after she says she refused to conceal students’ gender transitions from parents
description: Jeanette Martinez claims Albuquerque Public Schools forces staff to hide students' gender transitions from parents, violating her First Amendment rights.
content: A New Mexico social worker is suing Albuquerque Public Schools (APS) over a policy she says requires school personnel to conceal students' gender transitions from their parents. The Center for American Liberty filed a lawsuit in federal court on behalf of Jeanette Martinez, a licensed clinical social worker. Martinez said the district is forcing her to keep parents in the dark regarding their children's social gender transitions, violating her First Amendment rights to free speech and religious freedom. Martinez, who has worked as a social worker for more than a decade, supports special-education students at Atrisco Heritage Academy High School. Her role requires routine communication with parents regarding academic, behavioral and special-education needs. As a practicing Christian, Martinez said her deeply held religious convictions prohibit her from lying or intentionally concealing the truth. BLUE STATE SCHOOL DISTRICT ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT, HIDING GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS "There was an incident that I was present for where, within two hours, a student verbally decided he was male and wanted to be female," Martinez told Fox News Digital. "Within that meeting, a school team decided right then that because he expressed wanting to be the opposite sex, they would go ahead and choose his new name as the opposite sex." "They even decided how they were going to introduce his new name to his classmates," Martinez added, noting that school officials also discussed training first-grade students on how to interact with a classmate identifying as the opposite gender. Under APS Procedural Directive PJ30, staff are instructed to use a student's preferred name and pronouns for internal records, documents and interactions. However, when communicating with parents, unless the student or parent has specified otherwise, staff are directed to use the student's legal name and the pronoun corresponding to the student's gender assigned at birth. FIRST ON FOX: SCHOOL LIED, HID DAUGHTER'S GENDER TRANSITION UNDER DISTRICT POLICY, PARENTS ALLEGE The lawsuit alleges that the rule forces employees into a "conspiracy to lie" when parents ask direct questions about their children. "My job as a social worker is to bring the family together, not to tear them apart," Martinez told Fox News Digital. "To sit there in a parent-teacher conference and try to articulate issues as a mental health provider while participating in that deception is not in the best interest of the student or the family." In April, Martinez formally requested a religious accommodation that would allow her to communicate truthfully with parents. APS denied the request. According to the lawsuit, Martinez now faces internal investigation, disciplinary action or potential termination if she refuses to comply with the directive. TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS "It's damaging. It's horrible. It doesn't work. It's unimaginable, to be honest," Martinez said. Albuquerque Public Schools spokesperson Martin Salazar told Fox News Digital that the district does not comment on pending litigation. However, district guidance notes that the policy is intended to foster a safe learning environment and protect student privacy. content: Meghan Markle is raising questions after being photographed in England with two Hollywood stars. "Instead, Meghan’s first photographed social outing is with Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi. That tells me she remains very interested in celebrity and in being associated with recognizable, high-profile people." Schofield added that she finds it "interesting" that Markle "appears to have changed countries without necessarily changing the social ecosystem she prefers," noting that when living in Montecito, she and Prince Harry were spending time with "wealthy, famous and influential people." title: 'Red carpet for a despot': Trump's lavish Xi welcome collides with GOP anti-communism message
description: Republican senators criticized President Donald Trump's lavish Washington summit with Xi Jinping, warning against red carpet treatment for China's leader.
content: As President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping comes to its end, some Republicans aren’t happy with the red carpet treatment the face of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) received. "Quite frankly, had the White House asked me for advice, I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome here in the United States of America, based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party," Sen. Roger Wicker, R-Miss., said. Wicker, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee, has been one of the more vocal Republicans about his disdain for the meeting, which kicked off Wednesday afternoon when Trump met Xi at Joint Base Andrews — the first time a president has met with a foreign dignitary there since 2015. BIPARTISAN DUO WANTS TO REMIND CONGRESS, TRUMP OF CHINA'S 'ATROCITIES' AHEAD OF XI VISIT The White House argued in a statement to Fox News Digital that Trump was returning the sentiment to Jinping after his visit to Beijing earlier this year. "President Xi hosted President Trump in China for a historic summit this summer, and President Trump is reciprocating his hospitality by welcoming the Chinese delegation for a reciprocal visit this week," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said. "The President will forge relationships with anyone in order to advance our national interests and make good deals for the American people." It comes as Republicans are running to hold onto power in the Senate. They departed their midterm convention in Dallas earlier this month with a rallying cry: "Common sense versus communism," as progressive candidates surge across the country. The convention was designed to remind voters that while his name is not on the ballot, Trump’s agenda is. But his meeting with Xi, optically, runs afoul of that. "I mean, the president campaigned on an anti-China policy," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said. "You go look at those MAGA rallies and look at everybody cheering when he said he's gonna take it to China." "Any time we roll out the red carpet for a despot from Russia, or a despot from China, I feel the same way," he continued. "It's kind of not good." GOP FACES BRUTAL MIDTERM HEADWINDS AS REPUBLICANS PAINT ELECTION AS ‘COMPETITION WITH COMMUNISM’ Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, said he was not "enthusiastic" about the summit, and said that China, Russia, Iran and North Korea were an "axis opposed" to the U.S. "I hope the president's clear-eyed about who he's dealing with," Cornyn told Fox News Digital. "I mean, he tends to call some of these dictators friends, and they're no friend. I can guarantee." Some Republicans are willing to accept that a meeting between Trump and Xi is a necessary step in building a relationship between the two superpowers, even with the lavish nature of the summit. "I think there's value in being able to talk with your adversaries," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told Fox News Digital. "And I think, in this case, you know, our two countries, the biggest economies in the world, have a symbiotic relationship." Sen. Steve Daines, R-Mont., was invited to attend the dinner after spending years working in China before running for office. Daines told Fox News Digital that he understood his colleagues’ apprehension, but that the U.S. and China, and particularly Trump and Xi’s relationship, had to work. TRUMP-XI SUMMIT COULD HOLD KEY TO LOWER GAS PRICES, GOP CHAIRMAN SAYS "This relationship is too big to fail, and it's only appropriate that President Trump and his team extends respect to Xi Jinping, and it's really reciprocal to what they did for President Trump back in May when they showed him great respect when he showed up in Beijing," Daines said. Still, that doesn’t mean Republicans have to like it. "It is one of his strengths, his ability to sort of win individuals over with hospitality," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., told Fox News Digital. "He's in the business. So I don't, again, I'm not gonna second guess it. You know, I hate seeing it at a personal level, but I trust his instincts on it." Lawmakers hoped that the two-and-a-half-day summit would yield deals on the artificial intelligence (AI) race, trade deals that would end the trade war between the U.S. and China and for Xi to use his influence to get oil and natural gas flowing through the Strait of Hormuz again. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Trump kept tight-lipped about the nature of their bilateral meeting in the Oval Office on Thursday, but so far, Xi has promised two new pandas while the president is mulling allowing Chinese electric vehicles to be built in the U.S. Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., took no issue with the meeting, but hoped that Trump would see through any smokescreen Xi deployed. "I just suggested, and I don't think he will — the president's a pretty good judge of character — not to believe President Xi’s bulls---, because he's lying. Particularly about helping Iran, and Xi could get the Strait open immediately if he wanted," Kennedy told Fox News Digital.

title: Sunny Hostin's holdout juror claim complicated by conflicting reports from infamous 1991 murder trial
description: Sunny Hostin claimed she was the holdout juror in the NYC cannibal killer trial, but co-jurors told multiple outlets the holdout was an unemployed man.
content: "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin said on-air Tuesday that she was a holdout juror in the 1991 murder trial of Daniel Rakowitz, known as the "Butcher of Tompkins Square Park," but contemporaneous accounts offer conflicting descriptions of the jury's deliberations. During a discussion of the holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy trial, Hostin recounted her experience on the Rakowitz jury, prompting news outlets to compare her account with reporting from 1991. "And apparently, several jurors questioned afterwards said one holdout juror was principally responsible for preventing them from returning a guilty verdict," Hostin said Tuesday while citing a 1991 New York Times report. "That was me," she added. While Hostin served on the Rakowitz jury, the New York Post reported that other contemporaneous accounts identified an unemployed man as the principal holdout. The Post wrote that "jurors told The Post, Newsday, the Daily News and the Associated Press that the actual holdout was an unemployed man who wanted to keep the trial going so he could continue getting paid by the court for his civic duty." LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM "He was unemployed and liked the $15 a day and the three free meals," juror Valerie Holmes told Newsday after the verdict, according to contemporaneous coverage. The Post also cited a law enforcement source familiar with the case who said, "We were told that the juror who held out was a man. There was no other description." Another factor, The New York Post said, was that "Hostin was quoted as a juror on the case in multiple news clips at the time — but she did not identify herself as the holdout, nor did any of the fellow jurors who talked to the press after the trial. Her statement to Newsday from the time even seemed to contradict her story." "We had to compromise. But it is obvious to me he butchered the body, and he literally got away with murder. He attempted to commit the perfect crime," Hostin, then identified as Asunción Cummings, told Newsday. LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR ‘LOOKED AT THE CASE AND HE MADE THE CALL,’ HIS BROTHER SAYS The Post noted that "one Newsday article from 1991, however, suggested that there were two holdout jurors who pushed the other 10 to find Rakowitz not guilty or risk a hung jury." When contacted by the Post, Hostin reiterated that she was a holdout, saying, "I was. I was the holdout juror." NewsBusters Associate Editor Nicholas Fondacaro reported on the story as well, noting that while multiple sources had written about an unemployed male holdout juror, multiple sources had also said that there were two holdout jurors. "Outside the courtroom at State Supreme Court in Lower Manhattan, jurors said that at the end of deliberations, 10 members of the panel wanted to convict Rakowitz of murder, but two others insisted he was mentally ill and should not be held responsible for Beerle's death. They said the 10 decided to defer to the two holdouts to avoid a hung jury," the Newsday article said. The news article had gone on to indeed mention Hostin, under the surname of Cummings at the time. "The jurors said that one of the two panel members seeking the insanity acquittal wanted the deliberations to drag on for days. "'He was unemployed and liked the $15 a day and the three free meals. He liked that we were arguing on and on,' said juror Valerie Holmes, a 35-year-old clerk,'" the article continued. "'We had to compromise,' said Asuncion Cummings, a 22-year-old paralegal. 'But it is obvious to me he butchered the body and he literally got away with murder. He attempted to commit the perfect crime.'" Fox News Digital reached out to "The View" for comment. title: Hacker claims 7.49M customer records stolen from American utility company
description: CenterPoint Energy confirmed customer data was stolen, while a hacker claims 7.49 million records with partial Social Security numbers were taken.
content: If you pay an electric or gas bill every month, you probably think about the amount due, not all the personal information sitting behind that account. But your utility company may have your home address, phone number, billing history and other details that can become very useful in the wrong hands. That is what makes the breach at CenterPoint Energy worth paying attention to, even if you have never been one of its customers. CenterPoint says an unauthorized third party obtained personal information belonging to some customers through an external-facing system. A hacker, meanwhile, claims to have stolen 7.49 million customer records, including addresses, account numbers, billing information and partial Social Security numbers. There is an important catch. CenterPoint has confirmed that customer information was stolen, but it has not confirmed the hacker's 7.49 million figure or the specific information the attacker says was taken. So, there are still plenty of questions about how big this breach really is. Here's what CenterPoint has confirmed, what the hacker is claiming and what you should watch for now. NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com. Register and receive the replay and step-by-step guide afterward. DMV BREACH CONFIRMED AS HACKERS CLAIM 200,000 RECORDS STOLEN CenterPoint Energy confirms customer data was stolen CenterPoint Energy disclosed the incident in a Sept. 14 filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The Houston-based utility says it became aware of an online post from a third party claiming to possess a data set containing CenterPoint customer information. CenterPoint then activated its cybersecurity incident response procedures and brought in outside cybersecurity experts. As the investigation progressed, the company determined that an unauthorized third party had obtained personal information belonging to some customers through one of its external-facing systems. CenterPoint has not publicly said how many customers were affected. It also has not detailed which types of personal information were taken. The company says it plans to notify affected customers and regulators as required once it determines the scope of the incident. CyberGuy reached out to CenterPoint Energy asking whether it could confirm the hacker's claim that 7.49 million records were stolen, what customer information was affected and whether a public API was involved. CenterPoint referred us to its SEC filing and provided this statement: "Our filing speaks for itself." The company did not provide additional details in response to our questions. There is one piece of reassuring news for anyone who depends on CenterPoint for power or gas. The company says its electric and natural gas services continued operating normally during the incident. CenterPoint also says it currently does not expect the breach to have a material impact on its financial condition. Hacker claims 7.49 million CenterPoint records were stolen The bigger number comes from the attacker. A threat actor using the alias "4d722e4d656f77" told BleepingComputer that they obtained 7.49 million CenterPoint customer records. According to the hacker, those records contain: The attacker later leaked the data after claiming CenterPoint ignored their attempts to make contact. Again, CenterPoint has confirmed that customer information was stolen, but it has not independently confirmed this list of exposed data or the 7.49 million record count. Also, 7.49 million records does not necessarily mean 7.49 million individual people were affected. One person or household can potentially appear in more than one record. CenterPoint says it is still working to determine the actual scope. Hacker says a public CenterPoint system allowed automated data access The attacker's explanation of how the theft allegedly happened may be one of the most interesting parts of this breach. The hacker told BleepingComputer they accessed the information by repeatedly cycling through millions of IDs using a public CenterPoint API. An API allows different software systems to exchange information. Companies use them constantly behind websites and apps. According to the attacker, CenterPoint's API lacked protections that could have slowed or blocked mass automated requests. The hacker specifically claimed there was no effective rate limiting or web application firewall protection against the activity. CenterPoint's SEC filing does not confirm that attack method. What CenterPoint does confirm is that the unauthorized third party obtained information through an external-facing system. That means we should treat the API explanation as the attacker's account until the company or investigators provide more technical details. FOREIGN HACKERS BREACH TWO MORE US WATER UTILITIES, THREATEN SAFETY OF COLORADO RESIDENTS Why stolen utility records can be valuable to scammers A utility account may not seem as sensitive as a bank account. Yet it can hold exactly the kind of information a scammer wants before contacting you. Think about how convincing this could sound: Someone calls and knows your name. They know your service address. They may know your CenterPoint account number or recent billing amount. Then they tell you there is a problem with your payment. That conversation can feel much more legitimate because the scammer already has information you would expect only the utility company to know. Criminals can also combine information from one breach with details leaked somewhere else. A partial Social Security number, phone number or address may become more useful when paired with another stolen database. That is one reason I tell people to think about breaches as pieces of a much larger identity puzzle. Stolen information can stick around for years. Criminals can save it, trade it and revisit it long after the original breach disappears from the news. You can read more about why last year's data breach can become this year's identity fraud. Watch for fake CenterPoint calls, texts and emails The immediate threat may not come from someone opening an account in your name. It could arrive as a text message. Once news of a breach becomes public, scammers can take advantage of the confusion even if they never obtained the stolen database themselves. You could receive a message claiming CenterPoint needs you to "verify" your account after the breach. Another scammer might warn that your electricity will be disconnected unless you make an immediate payment. Be especially suspicious if someone creates urgency and then asks you to click a link, provide account information or move money. If you receive a suspicious CenterPoint message, go directly to the company's official website or use the contact information printed on your bill. Avoid calling a number supplied in an unexpected message. 8 ways to protect yourself after the CenterPoint Energy breach Whether you are a CenterPoint customer or simply wondering what you would do after your own utility provider suffered a breach, these steps can reduce your exposure. 1) Watch for an official CenterPoint breach notice CenterPoint says it intends to notify affected customers as required. If you receive a notice, read it carefully. Look for exactly what information CenterPoint says was involved and whether the company offers credit monitoring or other assistance. Do not rely on a text message or social media post claiming you were affected. 2) Freeze your credit If CenterPoint’s breach notice confirms that Social Security information was involved, consider placing a credit freeze with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze can make it harder for someone to open new credit accounts in your name. It is free, and you can temporarily lift it when you legitimately need a lender to access your credit file. Keep in mind that a freeze cannot stop every kind of identity theft. Existing account takeovers and other fraud can happen without a new credit check. 3) Check your credit reports and financial accounts Review your credit reports for accounts or inquiries you do not recognize. Then keep an eye on your bank accounts and credit cards for unfamiliar transactions. If something looks suspicious, contact the financial institution using the number on its official website, statement or the back of your card. 4) Secure your email and utility accounts Your primary email account deserves extra attention because criminals can use it to reset passwords for other services. Use a strong, unique password and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Do the same for your utility account if the provider offers those protections. A password manager can create unique passwords so one stolen login does not give an attacker access to several accounts. WATER CYBERATTACK HITS AT LEAST 7 STATES 5) Treat utility shutoff threats as a red flag A scammer may claim you owe money and threaten to disconnect your electricity or gas immediately. Do not let the urgency rush you into paying. Hang up and contact the utility yourself through its official website or the customer service number printed on your bill. 6) Use strong antivirus protection A convincing breach-related email can still lead to a malicious website or malware download. Strong antivirus software can help detect phishing sites, malicious links and malware before they cause more trouble. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. 7) Reduce how much personal information is already online Data brokers and people-search sites may already publish your phone number, address and other personal information. Removing that data will not erase information stolen in a breach. However, reducing publicly available information gives scammers fewer pieces they can use to build a detailed profile around leaked data. You can remove information manually or use a data removal service to handle recurring opt-out requests. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com. 8) Consider identity theft monitoring Identity theft protection can monitor credit activity and alert you when certain personal information appears in places where it could signal trouble. These services cannot prevent every form of identity theft. However, alerts can help you spot suspicious activity earlier. If you discover that someone has actually used your identity, document what happened and begin the recovery process quickly. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at CyberGuy.com. Kurt's key takeaways A utility account can reveal more about you than you might expect. Your address, billing details and account information can give scammers enough personal context to make a fake call, text or email sound legitimate. We still do not know the full scope of this breach. That uncertainty is another reason to stay alert rather than wait for every answer before taking precautions. Watch your accounts, consider freezing your credit if sensitive information was exposed and be skeptical of urgent utility messages. We often have little choice about who provides our power or gas, which makes protecting the information customers hand over especially important. If a company provides an essential service you cannot realistically live without, should it face tougher requirements for protecting the personal information you have no choice but to give it?
