title: Inside GOP Senate hopeful's financial ties to controversial data center boom
description: Michael Whatley holds up to $690,000 in energy investments tied to companies powering North Carolina's data center boom, raising conflict questions.
content: Michael Whatley, the former chair of the Republican National Committee and the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in North Carolina, and his family hold between $246,000 and $690,000 in energy investments with companies fueling data center growth in the Tar Heel State, according to his federal disclosure. Those holdings raise questions about whether Whatley or his family stands to benefit from his support of data center expansion, an issue that has drawn national attention over community zoning, energy use and state growth. Most of his reported holdings are with four companies. FOX NEWS POLL: DEMOCRATIC ENTHUSIASM SHAPES NORTH CAROLINA SENATE RACE Whatley and his family have holdings between $149,000 and $410,000 in Duke Energy, between $1,000 and $15,000 in Arista Networks, from $80,000 to $200,000 with Dominion Energy, and between $16,000 and $65,000 in GE Vernova. While most of those, like Duke and Vernova, don’t directly build data centers themselves, they offer services or products used by them. Duke is a major utility provider in North Carolina, and Vernova produces on-site gas turbines used by data center facilities operated by companies like Amazon and Microsoft. In addition to those investments, Whatley reported $361,000 from CAPCVentures LLC, a D.C. firm, for consulting services in 2025, according to his financial disclosure. That firm lists GE Vernova— a major supplier of turbines and grid equipment used to power data centers — as a client, along with Centrus Energy and the Renewable Fuels Association. Earlier coverage put his pay from the same shop at about $755,000 between 2022 and 2025. When asked about his holdings and whether he saw them as a potential conflict of interest, Whatley's campaign noted that he supports restrictions on stock trading for members of Congress. "Whatley supports the Stop Insider Trading Act and urges the U.S. Senate to pass the commonsense legislation, and supports commonsense reforms requiring elected officials to place their assets in qualified blind trusts, ensuring they have no control over how those assets are invested," DJ Griffin, a campaign spokesperson, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. The campaign also said that Whatley would support letting local communities decide for themselves what kinds of data center projects to accept and which ones to rule out. "Michael Whatley's standard is simple: data centers pay their own way, families pay nothing and communities decide. That means Big Tech builds or buys every megawatt it needs and covers every dime of the grid upgrades to deliver it, with zero costs shifted onto residential ratepayers. It means no special subsidies and no sweetheart deals cut over the heads of taxpayers," Griffin continued. "And it means the people of North Carolina's counties and towns, not bureaucrats in Raleigh or Washington, decide what gets built in their communities. North Carolina should win the AI economy, and it should win it on terms that protect the families who live here." THE DATA CENTER FIGHT COULD DECIDE THE NEXT PRESIDENT AND COST AMERICA THE AI RACE Whatley's campaign also turned the spotlight on his Democratic opponent, Roy Cooper, the former governor of North Carolina. "Roy Cooper is the only candidate in this race who has used the powers of his elected office to recruit data centers to NC and to have them subsidized by NC Taxpayers," Griffin added, noting that Cooper also has supported restrictions on congressional stock trading. Notably, the bulk of North Carolina’s tax breaks already existed by the time Cooper became governor in 2017. The year before, in 2016, the state had implemented statute G.S.105-164.13. Under that provision, lawmakers had expanded data center tax exemptions on sales, servers, storage and networking for companies investing at least $75 million in projects over five years. The state did, however, approve several major grants to companies like Apple and Corvid Technologies under Cooper's watch through "Job Development Investment Grants" (JDIGs). Those aimed to further job development in the state, dovetailing with existing development efforts. Among the more high-profile JDIGs, Apple entered into a $845 million grant over a period of 39 years alongside another $112.4 million that would go to an industrial development fund to build out rural infrastructure. The agreement is contingent on Apple creating a certain number of jobs, but the company has yet to meet the JDIG's projected goals since its implementation. For his own part, Cooper's campaign bashed Whatley for, in their view, not being sensitive enough to local resistance to data center expansion. "Longtime utility company lobbyist Michael Whatley believes people’s concerns about data centers are fake as he continues to shill for his billionaire buddies in the utility industry instead of standing up against rate hikes that are crushing hardworking families," a spokesperson for the Cooper campaign said in a statement. Cooper has taken a more critical approach to their expansion, arguing that they are forcing local communities into higher and higher utility bills. SILICON VALLEY IS LOSING THE DATA CENTER FIGHT, RISKING A REPEAT OF A CLASSIC FAILURE Like many Democrats on the topic, Cooper has framed his stance in the broader context of championing affordability policies. Having cleared their respective primaries, Cooper and Whatley will face off in North Carolina's general election on Nov. 3.

title: Rockies make brutal MLB history not seen in 60 years as moribund season wraps up
description: The Colorado Rockies became just the fifth team in MLB history to lose 100 games in four straight seasons, becoming the first franchise since the New York Mets to do it.
content: The Colorado Rockies could lose every game for the rest of the season and still finish 14 games better than last season. The bad news? If that happens, they will finish with 105 losses. title: ‘Miracle on the Hudson’ hero Sully Sullenberger reveals Alzheimer’s warning signs he missed years ago
description: Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger and wife Lorrie revealed the subtle behavioral shifts noticed years before his Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.
content: Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger, the former airline pilot celebrated worldwide for safely landing US Airways Flight 1549 on the Hudson River in 2009, is taking on a new mission to raise awareness about the early signs of Alzheimer’s disease. Sullenberger, who was diagnosed with the disease in August 2025, spoke on "Good Morning America" alongside his wife, Lorrie, to share their personal experience with the condition. The couple revealed several subtle shifts in routine and behavior that began surfacing several years before he received an official medical evaluation. 'MIRACLE ON THE HUDSON' HERO CAPTAIN 'SULLY' SULLENBERGER REVEALS ALZHEIMER'S DIAGNOSIS Reflecting on the timeline leading up to her husband's formal assessment, Lorrie Sullenberger noted that small adjustments in everyday life slowly pointed toward a bigger shift. "A lot of what I think people see in the news are late-stage Alzheimer's symptoms. And, so, in the very beginning, they are so subtle. And my advice to someone would be, it's what's unusual for your person," she shared, emphasizing how early symptoms often manifest gradually rather than abruptly. TV NEWS ANCHORMAN REVEALS HE HAS ALZHEIMER'S DURING FINAL NIGHT HELMING BROADCAST Public understanding of Alzheimer’s disease frequently focuses on these late-stage symptoms, such as pronounced memory loss, severe disorientation or difficulty managing basic daily routines. However, medical experts say early-stage cognitive decline can be much harder to spot. "One of the first things I noticed was that it was harder and harder to remember people’s names, even people we knew," Sullenberger said. "That’s still an issue. Just forgetting things that I normally wouldn’t. Or repeating myself, not realizing that I just said that an hour ago." Early indicators of Alzheimer's often present as mild cognitive impairment or subtle changes tailored to an individual’s normal baseline, according to health resources like the Cleveland Clinic. These can include misplacing everyday items, mild difficulty finding the right words during conversations, subtle changes in mood or executive function or taking slightly longer to complete familiar tasks. "I’ve gone through harder things than this before," Sullenberger said in the interview. The former pilot may be best known for successfully performing the "Miracle on the Hudson" in January 2009. After US Airways Flight 1549 suffered a dual engine failure after a bird strike shortly after taking off from New York's LaGuardia Airport, Sullenberger drew on decades of flight experience to glide the Airbus A320 onto the frigid Hudson River, where all 155 passengers and crew survived, according to the National Transportation Safety Board. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The emergency landing made Sullenberger an internationally recognized public figure and became known as the "Miracle on the Hudson." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Lorrie Sullenberger noted that family members should trust their instincts when something feels off, advising that the key lies in identifying "what's unusual for your person." "I’ve gone through harder things than this before." The Sullenbergers stressed that acknowledging potential early symptoms and seeking evaluation can profoundly impact a patient’s journey. While there is no cure for Alzheimer’s, early detection allows individuals and families to explore emerging treatment options, join clinical trials, adopt lifestyle modifications and plan for the future. title: America's best national parks for fall revealed — plus the NPS director's personal picks
description: Great Smoky Mountains National Park tops a new study ranking the best national parks for an autumn getaway, beating out Acadia and Shenandoah.
content: Year after year, the Great Smoky Mountains are America’s most-visited national park. Turns out, fall might be its most impressive season. A new study ranking the best national parks for an autumn getaway put the Smokies at No. 1, ahead of Acadia, Shenandoah, Rocky Mountain and Grand Teton. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS The research, conducted by Sudoku Bliss, analyzed National Park Service visitation data from September through November between 2021 and 2025, along with Google ratings and reviews. Great Smoky Mountains earned the top overall score after welcoming nearly 19 million fall visitors over that five-year span. And if you're looking for a second opinion, the acting director of the National Park Service happens to agree. During a recent interview with OutKick OutDoors, Jessica Bowron named the Smokies and the Blue Ridge Parkway when asked where she'd send someone chasing fall colors. 6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK "I would send them to the Blue Ridge Parkway, with a close partner being the Great Smoky Mountains National Park," Bowron said. "Two really incredible parks to see the fall colors." Great Smoky Mountains leads the fall rankings The Smokies finished well ahead of the rest of the field in the study, with a fall score of 94.7. Acadia National Park in Maine ranked second at 86.6, followed by Virginia's Shenandoah National Park at 76.0, Rocky Mountain National Park in Colorado at 74.1 and Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming at 72.9. The rest of the top 10 included Yosemite, Zion, Yellowstone, Cuyahoga Valley and New River Gorge. HERE'S HOW TO DO THE SMOKY MOUNTAINS WITHOUT TRAFFIC AND CROWDS And the rankings weren't based on visitor totals alone. The study weighted total fall visits, total visitor hours, Google ratings and the number of reviews containing autumn-related language. Shenandoah, for example, had fewer visitors than several parks ranked below it, but 18.4% of its Google reviews mentioned fall — the highest share among the top 10. So while the Smokies won on sheer popularity and overall score, the list includes everything from classic East Coast leaf-peeping destinations to red rocks and wildlife-heavy Western parks. More of the Blue Ridge Parkway is coming back Bowron also shared some good news for travelers planning a trip along the Blue Ridge Parkway this fall. "Just within the next few weeks, we should be reopening additional sections of the parkway that were hit by Hurricane Helene just two years ago," Bowron told OutKick OutDoors. "We're really excited to get that work wrapped up and see visitors back on that parkway." For anyone planning a fall road trip through the region, that's certainly worth keeping an eye on. Want something a little less obvious? If your idea of a relaxing fall weekend does not involve joining everybody else in America at the Smokies, Bowron also offered a more under-the-radar option. Her pick: Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park. And this wasn't just an answer pulled from a list. "I was there just yesterday, actually, we went for a hike on the C&O Canal with my husband and my daughter," Bowron said. She highlighted the more than 100-mile towpath running from the Washington, D.C., area into Western Maryland, with opportunities to hike, bike and branch off onto other trails along the way. "I don't know that folks recognize what an incredible resource that is," she said. That might be the better play for travelers who want fall scenery without traffic and crowds. Don't sleep on national parks in winter Fall gets most of the attention this time of year, but Bowron said winter opens up a completely different set of possibilities. For warmer-weather trips, she pointed to places like Death Valley, Mojave, Everglades and Saguaro — parks that can be far more comfortable once summer temperatures disappear. And for travelers who actually want the snow, there are plenty of options for that, too. The Rockies offer snowshoeing and cross-country skiing, while Utah's Bryce Canyon National Park is a great place for winter hiking, snowshoeing and skiing among its snow-covered red rock formations. Bowron warned, though, to check park websites for road closures, weather conditions and available facilities before you go. "Days are going to be shorter. Conditions are going to change," Bowron said. "They're going to be very different from what you might expect in the summer." title: Massachusetts restaurant owner assaults teen dine-and-dashers, pulls gun during scuffle, police say
description: Nadim Kashouh allegedly chased two teens from his Springfield restaurant and a brandished a firearm after a $92.40 dine-and-dash incident.
content: A Massachusetts restaurant owner allegedly beat two teenage dine-and-dashers and pointed a gun at a larger group that gathered after he chased the pair down when they skipped out on their bill last week, authorities said. Nadim Kashouh, 62, chased the teens – a 17-year-old girl and Javonnie Lee, 18 – after the pair darted out of Nadim’s Downtown Mediterranean Grill on Friday evening without paying their $92.40 bill, the Boston Globe reported. Kashouh reportedly chased the teens and caught them at a convenience store. JIMMY JOHN'S EMPLOYEE ACCUSED OF OPENING FIRE ON CAR, SHOOTING 14-YEAR-OLD GIRL IN LEG: POLICE The teens reportedly told the police that they tried to pay their tab twice but bolted after their card was declined both times, according to the newspaper. Kashouh, an immigrant from Lebanon who came to the United States in 1990, allegedly grabbed the girl's phone and demanded they pay. He then elbowed the girl and punched Lee in the face, the Springfield Police Department said. "As a larger group gathered, Kashouh is alleged to have pointed his firearm in the direction of the group. Kashouh stated he did so in self-defense," police spokesperson Ryan Walsh said, according to WMTV. NYC ALLEGED DINE-AND-DASH INFLUENCER PEI CHUNG EVICTED FROM LUXURY APARTMENT AS SHE SIT SIN JAIL Walsh said Kashouh's firearm and his license to carry permit were seized. He is charged with two counts of assault with a dangerous weapon, armed robbery with a firearm, and assault and battery. Meanwhile, the two teens will be issued criminal complaints for defrauding a restaurant. Kashouh appeared in court earlier this week, according to his restaurant's Facebook page. "He maintains his innocence and says he acted in self-defense. As this matter moves through the legal process, Mr. Kashouh looks forward to the opportunity to fully address the facts and circumstances surrounding the incident," the post states. "Having just celebrated over 25 years serving the Springfield community, Mr. Kashouh is incredibly grateful for the many clients, guests, friends, and community members who have reached out and continued to support him and Nadim’s," it continued. "He sincerely thanks them for their kindness and support during this time." CLICK HERE FOR MORE U.S. NEWS Kashouh was born in Monrovia, Liberia, before moving to Lebanon as a child in 1974 where he worked in the family business during the summer, the New York Post reported. Despite the allegations against him, some came to his defense. "I have known Nadim to be respectful, fair, calm, and incredibly hardworking," Maureen Pinette, who worked for him between 2012 and 2014, wrote on Facebook. "I've watched him deal with difficult situations and difficult people, and I have never known him to be someone who simply loses his cool." "I see so much of Nadim in both of his children—the love, the loyalty, the work ethic, and the way they show up for the people around them," she added. "I’ve also watched Nadim give to people and to his community without needing recognition for it. He has done things for people simply because they needed help." title: Christian nurse says Oregon hospital tried to force employee group to go ‘interfaith’
description: A Christian nurse at Oregon Health & Science University says OHSU refused her employee group unless she removed prayer and Bible study elements.
content: A Christian nurse at Oregon Health & Science University Hospital (OHSU) says administrators initially refused to approve her employee group unless she removed prayer, Bible study and other religious activities and changed it from a Christian group to an interfaith organization. Suzie Logue said she created the group in early 2025 after connecting with other Christian employees who wanted a place to pray, study Scripture and encourage one another during difficult shifts. She says OHSU told her the group could be approved only if it removed its religious elements and said it could not use hospital resources or campus buildings. "I naturally wrote back and said, ‘No, we're a Christian group. We would like to be allowed to pray and do Bible study and do these other worship activities using campus resources,’" Logue told Fox News Digital in an interview Tuesday. CHRISTIAN COP IN UK SUSPENDED FOR ASKING QUESTIONS ABOUT ISLAM DURING DEI TRAINING WINS SETTLEMENT Logue said the hospital told her the group couldn't use any campus resources or campus buildings even when other religious groups were being allowed to do so. "When I said, ‘What policy are we citing here? Why can't we do this?’ I was met with silence," Logue said. "And when I kept pushing over the weeks, they wrote back to me and said, ‘Well, your charter is being reviewed now by hospital legal,’ and that is when I reached out to First Liberty." CONNECTICUT BARS NATIVITY DISPLAY IN STATE CAPITOL BECAUSE IT'S 'RELIGIOUS,' LAWSUIT THREAT SAYS Logue said she was shocked by what she viewed as the hospital’s casual handling of the situation. She said other religious employee groups were permitted to use campus facilities for prayer and worship, while she received little explanation for why the Christian group was treated differently. After Logue contacted First Liberty Institute, the organization sent OHSU a demand letter. Logue says the hospital ultimately approved the group as Christian and allowed it to use hospital resources for prayer and worship. CHRISTIAN SCHOOL CHAPLAIN WINS SETTLEMENT AFTER FIRING OVER LGBTQ SERMON Logue says the group has since grown rapidly through word of mouth, giving Christian employees a support network inside the hospital. "Part of the reason I wanted to start the group is because I was connecting with other Christians at the hospital," Logue said. "As you can imagine, Portland and working in Portland can be a pretty tough place to be a Christian. And I was starting to connect with other Christians just in my daily work, and they'd say, ‘Oh my gosh, it's so nice to know there's other, other Christians here. We should try and get together sometimes just for encouragement.’ "And, so, what we've seen come out of this group, it's interesting because even despite the challenges we faced getting this group started, it has grown exponentially, a lot of (it) by word of mouth because we lack some visibility, but a lot of people find that there's more light they feel like when they go to their shift because they know there's someone they can connect with mid-shift if they have a really difficult patient situation," she said. Cliff Martin, senior counsel at First Liberty, told Fox News Digital in a statement on Wednesday, "Federal law mandates that employees of all faiths be respected in the workplace. Even so, OHSU displayed a clear pattern of discrimination and hostility toward Ms. Logue's Christian employee resource group by denying them visibility on the company website, companywide messaging, equal stipend payment and fair descriptions of religious holidays. "We are happy to say that, since July, the issues have mostly been resolved, and the Christian resource group should receive the same support every other group receives." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In a statement to Fox News Digital, OHSU said, "Employee Resource Groups are OHSU-sponsored and employee-managed groups. ERGs provide opportunities for career development, social support, networking, mentoring, community participation, cultural awareness and employee engagement. There are 15 ERGs at OHSU, including the Christian ERG, which was formed in 2025. "Per OHSU policy, any group of at least three employees may request to be considered to form a new ERG," the hospital continued. "Emerging ERGs must identify potential goals of the group and craft a mission statement. The mission statement and goals must be reviewed and may need to be adapted to align with OHSU policies prior to approval. "Each ERG operates with institutional support, and recognition entitles access to institution-owned or controlled facilities for meetings and events, in accordance with policy. To maintain recognition, an ERG shall serve to build a positive and inclusive environment, and remain in compliance with OHSU policies."

title: Javier Milei shreds ‘useless’ UN to its face in fiery speech to 'fatally arrogant parasites'
description: Javier Milei called the United Nations a "useless" body of "fatally arrogant parasites" in a fiery speech before the General Assembly in New York.
content: Argentina’s libertarian President Javier Milei struck again, this time in a fiery speech to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, calling the body "useless" and made up of "fatally arrogant parasites." Milei began by commending the U.N.’s founding mission of resolving conflict peacefully and promoting universal freedom and dignity as "noble words." However, he went on to say that "today, regrettably, it is time to acknowledge that, in practice, that sacred covenant has been broken." "That’s to say, it has become a useless organization whose only purpose is to sustain a caste of fatally arrogant parasites masquerading as well-intentioned bureaucrats," he charged. To make his case, he pointed to the U.N.’s role in restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic, which he called a type of "genocide," and the "gender agenda, environmental extremism and unchecked immigration." IRAN'S PRESIDENT SAYS TEHRAN IS READY FOR DIPLOMACY WITH TRUMP BUT WON'T ACCEPT 'LANGUAGE OF FORCE' Milei said, "During the pandemic, bodies under the auspices of this house put themselves before scientific evidence and the sovereignty of nations and promoted forced lockdown policies throughout the world. "Where some allege a public health policy error, we see a global experiment in social control disguised as science. And when a state wearing public health blinkers deprives its population of the right to work, to receive an education and to bid farewell to their dead, this results in millions of avoidable deaths; there is a word for it, genocide." He charged that "every time [the U.N.] failed, rather than reviewing the model or apologizing, they doubled down." "Those who were supposed to guarantee collective security and human rights failed in their task. They allowed chaos, violence and international terrorism to flourish," he said. "The alleged defenders of human rights have sheltered bloodthirsty dictatorships and regimes that stone women in the streets; they have systematically voted against Israel while remaining silent in the face of Islamic terrorism and the genocide of Christians in Africa." Milei is widely considered a radical reformer, budget slasher and an ally of President Donald Trump. Similar to Trump’s previous criticisms of the U.N. before the assembly, Milei did not hold back in his address Wednesday. ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARSLONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE Turning to his own country’s grievances, Milei continued by saying, "And if that were not enough, an organization established to defend the territorial sovereignty of its members decided to look the other way with regard to the situation of the Malvinas [Falkland] Islands, South Georgia Islands, South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas." He said these islands "are a test of the gulf that exists between the words of international institutions and the reality upon which they purport to act." "There's no shortage of words or resolutions; what is lacking is consequences," he asserted. "Because an institution that cannot ensure that its words carry weight in the real world loses the most important thing of all, its authority." Milei said that, in addition to what he described as the Falkland Islands "failure," the U.N. has "built a bureaucratic leviathan devoted to deciding how the peoples of the world and their citizens should live." title: Tigers legend Justin Verlander's final career start signals the sad end of an era in baseball
description: Detroit Tigers legend Justin Verlander's final start Saturday marks the end of the workhorse era, as no active MLB pitcher may ever reach 300 wins again.
content: When Justin Verlander steps off the mound for the final time in his illustrious career on Saturday, it won’t just be the final start of his Hall of Fame career. It also signals the end of an era in baseball history: the death of the workhorse starting pitcher. The leaders on MLB’s all-time pitching lists will likely never change again. Cy Young has the most wins of all time with 511. Verlander, who leads active players by a wide margin, has 266. On the all-time wins list, Verlander is tied for 37th with Bob Feller and Eppa Rixey. Verlander, who pitched for 21 seasons, won’t be reaching the esteemed 300-win threshold. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE In fact, no pitcher may ever reach 300 wins again. Today, bullpens are more prevalent, starters are pulled from games earlier than ever, and pitchers are getting injured as they chase velocity, shortening their careers. The 300-win pitcher may be a thing of the past. The active players who trail Verlander on the list? Max Scherzer has 224 wins and is 42 years old, while Gerrit Cole has 162 and is 35. Cole would have to average 20 wins a year for the next seven seasons to reach 300, meaning he would have to pitch at an elite level through his age-42 season to even have a shot. While it’s hard to bet against Cole, it’s improbable at best. Reaching 300 wins would require remarkable longevity and production. Just behind Cole is Chris Sale, who is 37 years old with 159 wins. He will not be eclipsing 300 wins either. In today’s day and age of baseball, 200 wins may be the new 300 wins. While Verlander and Scherzer won’t reach 300 wins, they are both part of the exclusive 3,000-strikeout club. Only 20 pitchers have ever struck out 3,000 batters in their careers. Cole has 2,374 strikeouts and has averaged 239 strikeouts over a full season. With three more healthy seasons, he could also enter the club. title: What is kratom? Risks of popular substance revealed after college students' deaths
description: Two University of Mississippi student deaths raised questions after investigators found packaging associated with kratom-related products and later recovered products that contained synthetic kratom-related substances.
content: The deaths of two University of Mississippi students have raised fresh questions about the potential health risks of kratom. The students died Monday at separate locations on campus. An initial law-enforcement release said packaged kratom purchased from a retail store was found during both investigations. In a statement Wednesday, Lafayette County Metro Narcotics, a department in the sheriff's office, stopped short of declaring that investigators found kratom itself near either student. "During the investigations, packaging associated with kratom-related products was discovered at both locations," part of the statement read. The Sept. 25 affidavit reported toxicology results from the medical examiner were still pending. PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY Authorities have not confirmed whether the substance played a role in the students’ deaths. American Kratom Association Senior Fellow on Public Policy Mac Haddow said Wednesday during a press conference that the specific drug found near both students is illegal. Haddow pointed out the sale and possession of kratom has been illegal federally as of August and illegal to sell or possess in Oxford, Mississippi since 2019, and illegal in Lafayette County, where Oxford is located, since 2021. DR DREW PINSKY REVEALS RED FLAG IN PRESLEY GERBER ADDICTION TREATMENT BEFORE MODEL'S DEATH Kratom is a plant-based substance often marketed as a natural option for pain relief or opioid withdrawal, but experts warn that it can cause dependence, dangerous interactions and other serious health complications. Kratom is widely available, Jessica Steinman, chief clinical officer at No Matter What Recovery in Los Angeles, told Fox News Digital. "We are starting to see it in storefronts, at your local gas stations, smoke shops and health food stores, where it's being sold as an energy booster," she said. "People are starting to buy it over the counter and use it incorrectly, and use mass amounts of it." "It's affecting the opioid receptors in people's brains," she went on. "It can cause them to be overly sedated, it can slow down their breathing and general function of their lungs." Kratom can also become highly addictive, Steinman warned. SORORITY RUSH GETS OZEMPIC MAKEOVER AS SOME COLLEGE WOMEN RESORT TO WEIGHT-LOSS INJECTIONS Traditional kratom products generally contain lower levels of active compounds, while newer 7-OH products are often concentrated or enhanced to produce stronger, more stimulating effects, she noted. 7-OH products contain 7-hydroxymitragynine, a potent opioid-related compound found in kratom. AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING Although kratom laws vary by state and locality, Steinman said regulators are increasingly focused on the concentrated 7-OH products and synthetic kratom-related compounds, rather than traditional botanical kratom containing only trace amounts of 7-OH. As to why there has been an uptick in kratom use among young people, Steinman said she believes many of them are learning about it from social media or through their friends. "People are starting to buy it over the counter and use it incorrectly, and use mass amounts of it." College students may be using the substance for two reasons, she said. "One reason would be, it is a stimulant," Steinman noted. "They may have pressures to stay awake, to study, get good grades … they may want to be more energized." People may also be using it due to its opioid-like effects, the expert said. "It does give someone that sedating high, that kind of numbing out from feeling anything very difficult, not wanting to have to deal with stress or anxiety." It becomes more dangerous when people combine it with multiple substances, like alcohol, marijuana or benzodiazepines. "That's when it can become lethal," Steinman warned. When to seek medical attention People who use kratom and begin breathing slowly or shallowly, or who become excessively drowsy or difficult to awaken, may be experiencing serious sedation that can interfere with breathing, Steinman said. In those cases, prompt medical care is important. "Another issue that isn't really talked about often is when people might possibly get addicted to kratom," she cautioned. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Reducing or abruptly stopping kratom after regular use can trigger withdrawal, and in some cases may lead to seizures, according to the expert. Anyone experiencing a seizure should seek emergency medical care. Steinman also responded to those who might claim that kratom is safe due to the fact that it’s a natural substance. "Just because something's from the earth doesn't make it healthy — people can get addicted and compulsive with lots of things," she said. The expert pointed out that there are no addictive components to marijuana, but it becomes addictive – "not necessarily addictive to the brain, but to the feeling that it gives you." "And that's the same situation with kratom – people get addicted to that feeling. But with kratom, it's actually affecting the opioid receptors in the brain." Industry response Dallas Vasquez, CEO and co-founder of Mitra9 Brands, a Florida-based company that manufactures and sells beverages and products containing kratom (mitragynine) and kava, emphasized the difference between botanical kratom products containing trace levels of 7-OH and products formulated with added, enhanced, highly concentrated or synthesized 7-OH. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "The FDA has specifically identified added or enhanced 7-OH products as a particular concern, and the DEA has taken or proposed separate scheduling actions involving elevated 7-OH and related substances," he told Fox News Digital. Vasquez said Mitra9’s products are made with botanical kratom extract derived from the natural leaf, and not with isolated or synthetic 7-OH. The products are labeled for adults 21 and older and include precautionary statements, he noted. The label advises consumers not to exceed the recommended serving, avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, consult a physician before use if taking medications or managing a medical condition, avoid combining the product with alcohol or other substances, be aware that it may be habit-forming, and keep it out of the reach of children. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "We take every report of harm seriously, and we don't dismiss those concerns," Vasquez said, adding that the kratom market is "not uniform." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Products range from standardized, tested beverages to concentrated and synthetic 7-OH products that federal regulators are now moving to schedule," he said. "We support that action and stronger national standards for testing, labeling, potency limits and age restrictions." "Consumers deserve to know exactly what is in what they buy, and bad actors should be removed from the market." title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump’s CBP axes Biden-era policy allowing private gifts for illegal immigrants in federal custody
description: CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott ended a Biden-era policy letting the agency solicit private gifts for illegal immigrants in custody under Trump's border crackdown.
content: EXCLUSIVE – A Biden-era pipeline that allowed federal immigration officials to solicit and accept private gifts for illegal immigrants in custody has been shut down at U.S. Customs and Border Protection, with the agency saying the policy no longer fits the Trump administration's border crackdown. CBP TOUTS HISTORIC MILESTONE, PUSHES FOR EVEN LARGER WORKFORCE: 'WE AREN’T STOPPING HERE' CBP confirmed the move to Fox News and said officials recently discovered the directive and moved to rescind the agency's participation. title: Canadians Nick Taylor and Corey Conners laugh off Lake Ontario renaming ahead of Presidents Cup

content: Nick Taylor and Corey Conners want to beat the Americans at the Presidents Cup this week. They would prefer to leave the naming of lakes out of it. Which is unfortunate, because OutKick had a suggestion for adding a little something extra to the competition at Medinah Country Club: The winning team gets to name the lake. Lake Ontario if the Internationals win. Lake America if Team USA wins. The two Canadians weren’t sold. "I think we’ll leave the naming of lakes out of it," Taylor said with a laugh Tuesday. Conners laughed at the suggestion, too. "I don’t think anyone would be too excited about that prospect," he said. "I don’t know who’s in charge of lake naming." Fair enough. US PRESIDENTS CUP PLAYERS EXPLAIN HOW CHRISTIAN FAITH BUILDS FRIENDSHIPS AND PUTS GOLF IN PERSPECTIVE President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Aug. 27 directing that Lake Ontario be renamed Lake America for U.S. federal use, including government maps and documents. With Taylor and Conners preparing to face a team of 12 Americans, OutKick asked them about the name change in a series of lighthearted questions. "I just laughed. "I honestly haven’t read too much into that. I don’t really have an opinion one way or another," he said. Competition begins Thursday, Sept. 24, at Medinah. This year’s International team represents seven countries: Canada, Australia, Colombia, Japan, New Zealand, South Africa and South Korea. title: Susan Collins tears into bribery allegations as new claims emerge during critical Senate battle
description: Maine Sen. Susan Collins dismissed the FBI bribery probe as a "political hit job," questioning convicted fraudster Martin Kao's credibility.
content: Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, is addressing claims she was caught up in an FBI bribery investigation, dismissing reporting on the story as the work of Democratic operatives and a known conman. ProPublica reported that Martin Kao, a former defense contractor CEO and convicted fraudster, told the FBI his company funneled $150,000 through a shell company to a super PAC supporting Collins’ 2020 reelection as part of what he described as a broader pay-to-play operation involving political contributions and government contracts. His cooperation later helped open a new phase of the federal investigation that developed into a broader bribery probe. Shortly after the story broke, Collins spoke up to dismiss Kao on the basis of his character and called into question the origins of the story. "I've got to say, I do not understand how anyone would take the word of a felon who's been convicted twice — twice, two separate cases — of five counts of money laundering, counts of bank fraud, false submissions to the FEC. He is a convicted liar," the senator told The Wall Street Journal’s Kim Strassel. GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS In a separate interview with Punchbowl News, Collins blamed Democrats and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for the controversy, calling the report a "political hit job" and questioning its timing. Collins is embroiled in a heated re-election campaign against Democrat Troy Jackson. Whether Collins keeps her seat could prove crucial to determining which party controls the Senate in 2027. Any hint of controversy for either candidate, naturally, is suited to become a national controversy. FOX NEWS POLL: MAINE SENATE RACE IS TIGHT, WITH CONCERNS ABOUT BOTH CANDIDATES Campaign finance records cited by ProPublica show that a shell company established by Kao made a donation to a super PAC supporting Collins’ 2020 re-election campaign. The outlet also obtained emails that it says show Scott Reed, head of the super PAC backing Collins that cycle, was aware of the fact that Kao had used a shell company to mask his illegal donation. A 2019 email from a naval officer shows that the senator had advocated on behalf of Navatek, the contractor Kao was leading at the time. The email, however, was sent months before Kao routed his illegal donation to Collins’ super PAC. Federal contractors are barred from donating to political campaigns, which is why Kao resorted to a shell company. FBI spokesman Ben Williamson told ProPublica the agency had investigated claims against Collins years ago "and ultimately found nothing implicating Senator Collins or Senator Collins’ campaign. Any suggestion otherwise is totally false." The FBI, however, did not respond to ProPublica’s questions about a new investigation it says was launched in 2024 after Kao spent years cooperating with federal agents and detailing his dealings with Collins and other lawmakers. "The Biden-led Justice Department and FBI totally cleared my office, my campaign and me five years ago of these 7-year-old allegations," Collins said, also not addressing the 2024 investigation directly. GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS Kao had a clear incentive to cooperate with the FBI. He was facing years in prison and hoped that providing information would help reduce his sentence, although the judge ultimately gave him no leniency for his cooperation. "This is a smear job. And as someone who has always prided herself on serving with integrity, it really offends me," Collins said. "And I'm offended for my staff too, both on the campaign and in the personal office." title: RNC sues New Jersey election officials over alleged withheld voter roll records

content: FIRST ON FOX – The Republican National Committee (RNC) and state GOP leaders filed a lawsuit Tuesday against New Jersey’s top election official and authorities in five counties, alleging they failed to produce federally mandated voter roll maintenance records and aiming to force transparency for the American people. "The RNC exposed noncitizens on New Jersey's voter rolls," RNC Chairman Joe Gruters said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Now, election officials are hiding the records that would tell voters how it happened. The RNC won't stand for it." While officials did produce some documents, Tuesday's new lawsuit alleges that New Jersey’s chief election official and county authorities in Bergen, Hudson, Middlesex, Somerset and Union counties have continued to withhold key records that federal law requires to be made public. RNC THREATENS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST NEW JERSEY OFFICIALS OVER NONCITIZENS ON VOTER ROLLS: 'ON NOTICE' "Garden State voters deserve the truth, and we're taking these left-wing officials to court to demand answers," Gruters' statement added. The legal action follows the RNC's initial discovery of hundreds of noncitizens on the state's voter registries, as first reported by Fox News Digital in early June. The June report noted that migrants seeking documented naturalization had self-attested to be noncitizens, while being found to have voted in past elections. Fox News Digital has reached out for comment from the New Jersey Secretary of State's office and the respective five counties named in the filing. Also, through investigations of jury duty evasion, some New Jersey residents claimed to lack U.S. citizenship only to be ultimately found to be registered voters. The RNC sued the New Jersey secretary of state in July over nonresidents – and in some case noncitizens – being permitted to vote in state elections. DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED While Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill acknowledged the illegal voter registrations, Republicans argue that state Democrats have spent months dodging accountability and have failed to explain how the noncitizens were added to the rolls in the first place. Seeking to determine how the registrations occurred and whether ineligible voters were subsequently removed, the RNC sent legal notices demanding answers and requesting voter roll maintenance documents. The RNC stated the lawsuit aims to force transparency and protect the ballot box. The withheld records are also of interest in Washington, where congressional investigators are currently seeking answers regarding the same voter registration failures. HOUSE REPUBLICANS CONFRONT NJ GOVERNOR OVER 6,600 NONCITIZENS REGISTERED TO VOTE IN ALLEGED SOFTWARE FAILURE This legal challenge is part of a broader, nationwide campaign by the RNC's multimillion-dollar election integrity unit ahead of the midterm elections. The committee has sent similar requests for voter roll maintenance records to 48 states to ensure voting registries are being properly maintained across the country. It also builds on the RNC's prior legal actions in New Jersey to challenge election procedures, which include a previous lawsuit against the New Jersey secretary of state over alleged unlawful voting practices. title: Activist teacher’s Palestinian identity claims unravel as she admits being a ‘White woman’ of privilege
description: Hannah Gann, dubbed the "Palestinian Rachel Dolezal," admitted in a video that she lied about being Palestinian and Black for several years.
content: A Philadelphia educator known for her anti-Israel activism has admitted to lying about her Palestinian and Black identities and revealed that she is "a White woman of significant privilege and wealth" — leading some online to refer to her as the "Palestinian Rachel Dolezal." Hannah Gann, a longtime educator with the School District of Philadelphia, previously claimed that she was both Palestinian and Black, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. In one instance, her outspoken activism led to a mobile billboard that called her "Philadelphia's Leading antisemite" being parked outside her school. Inquirer journalist Kristen A. Graham wrote, "A Philadelphia teacher is being called the ‘Palestinian Rachel Dolezal’ after being caught lying about her background." This was a nod to the former NAACP official who rose to fame in 2015 after it was revealed that she had been identifying as a Black woman despite having two White parents. Graham noted that the phrase has popped up about Gann online. The Inquirer reported that Gann — a teacher at the Workshop School, a project-based high school in the School District of Philadelphia — is White and Jewish and lied about her identity for several years. FEDS OPEN PROBE INTO NEW YORK CITY'S ANTI-ISRAEL TEACHERS "Members met with Hannah and questioned her about her background on Thursday and after an hour of discussion, Hannah finally admitted she lied," the Racial Justice Organizing Committee and Philly Educators for Palestine said in a statement to the outlet, adding, "We asked her to publicly acknowledge that she is a White woman of Jewish heritage and an Israeli settler family." Fox News Digital reached out to the Racial Justice Organizing Committee. Both groups are reportedly "stunned, saddened and angered by this betrayal," and have permanently severed their ties with Gann. In a 10-minute-long video posted to Instagram, Gann admitted to and apologized for the yearslong ruse, while revealing she is "a White woman of significant privilege and wealth." FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS "There is not a single person on this planet, no friend, no fellow organizer, no one in my family, no professional connection, no secret op or handler who knew what I was doing," Gann said. "I hid my family’s background from everyone in Philly and also hid from the people in my own family what I was doing." Gann was reportedly a leading voice within the school district following the Oct. 7 Hamas-led attacks on Israel, and in 2024, she participated in a West Philadelphia "teach-in" on "scholasticide" in Gaza. She was also a vocal supporter of Keziah Ridgeway, a Philadelphia educator who was previously disciplined over pro-Palestinian social media posts shared on her private accounts. Social media posts shared by Gann in 2025 show her appearing at a public community hearing wearing a keffiyeh and speaking in an apparent accent that is not present in her apology video. According to a document compiled by the Philly Palestine Coalition (PPC) and obtained by the Inquirer, Gann allegedly made several references to having Palestinian family members. In one instance, the PPC found that a grandfather Gann claimed to be Palestinian-born was actually born in Baltimore, according to historical records. EXILED MUSLIM SCHOLAR WARNS FAR-LEFT–ISLAMIST ALLIANCE BEHIND ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTS ECHOES IRAN’S RISE Additional documents obtained by the PPC reportedly found that Gann’s family lives abroad in Israel, and that she had successfully received donations from people after telling them she was strapped for cash because she was sending money to loved ones. A University of Pennsylvania classmate of Gann’s told the outlet she was known in college "as a self-proclaimed White Jewish woman with family in the occupied West Bank. I watched her sudden transformation after she returned to Philly from the Peace Corps [in Rwanda]." The unnamed classmate reportedly added that, "she was clearly making herself look darker using makeup and fake tan, and speaking using [African American Vernacular English.]" Additionally, the PPC research document obtained by the Inquirer pointed out that Gann "is a teacher of predominantly Black youth. She has gained the trust of young people on the basis of a sense of shared oppression." BACK TO SCHOOL SHOULD NOT MEAN BACK TO FEAR FOR JEWISH STUDENTS The document reportedly alleged that Gann "has served as a mentor to at least one young White person who was manipulated by Hannah on the basis of a fake identity," and added that "her access to vulnerable young people, especially Black youth, is deeply concerning, given her pattern of lying and manipulation." In response to the allegations against Gann, the school district is reportedly providing support to students who may have been affected. CAMPUS ANTISEMITISM EXTENDS BEYOND STUDENT PROTESTS AND INTO CLASSROOMS, ADL WARNS In a statement to the Inquirer, a district spokesperson said officials are "aware of social media posts concerning a district employee and her involvement with an outside advocacy organization. These posts reference the employee’s involvement in an external group." The district, however, did not reveal whether Gann would face any disciplinary consequences for her actions, according to the outlet. Fox News Digital reached out to Gann and the Philadelphia School District. title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for 2006 sex crime in New York
description: Harvey Weinstein apologized while maintaining his innocence, and a Manhattan judge called him a sexual predator and the face of the #MeToo movement.
content: Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced movie mogul, was sentenced in Manhattan to 15 years in prison Wednesday for a felony sex crime in another #MeToo reckoning. Weinstein’s sentencing for sexually assaulting one-time TV production assistant Miriam Haley followed a legal odyssey spanning more than six years. His 2020 conviction was overturned by New York's highest court. A second jury found Weinstein guilty again at a retrial last year. Once among the most powerful figures in the entertainment industry, Weinstein was an Oscar-winning producer whose hits included "Shakespeare in Love," "Pulp Fiction" and "Chocolat." But his downfall came quickly after sexual assault allegations in 2017 set off the #MeToo movement. Weinstein, 74, is expected to appeal and maintains that he never raped or sexually assaulted anyone. He is now likely to remain behind bars well into his 80s. Seated in a wheelchair, he was quickly moved out of the courtroom after the sentencing, while some of his accusers hugged and brushed away tears. JONATHAN TURLEY: WHEN JOURNALISTS WHINE ABOUT #METOO, THEY DON’T MEAN PLATNER, TOO Weinstein and his victim both spoke in court Weinstein faced up to 25 years in prison for sexually assaulting Haley at his Manhattan apartment in 2006. He has already served more than six years as his case cycled through the criminal justice system. Haley gave her account of the assault at two trials and again addressed the court Wednesday. "Having been sexually assaulted by Harvey Weinstein has had a devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away. Making the decision to speak up will have me looking over my shoulder for years to come," Haley said. "It’s a life sentence for me." Minutes later, Weinstein apologized while reiterating his innocence. "Reflecting on all that has happened since 2017 has helped me recognize how my past conduct has negatively affected others. I live with many regrets and sincerely apologize to anyone I have affected with my actions," he said. EX-MAYOR FOUND LIABLE FOR ALLEGED SEXUAL ASSAULTS OF 7 WOMEN, ORDERED TO PAY $13M Some of his accusers who were in court shook their heads while he spoke. Weinstein is the face of #MeToo, judge says Judge Curtis Farber said Weinstein was once a king in the movie industry, "but recognition for these achievements will pale in comparison to what you did." He said Weinstein is now known as "a sexual predator, the literal face of the #MeToo movement." The judge said Weinstein treated women as "mere objects to be played with and discarded" and still hasn’t accepted responsibility, portraying himself as a victim during jailhouse interviews. Haley afterward said she was happy with the sentence, while saying it's clear that Weinstein has not acknowledged what he did. "I think he still feels entitled, and that’s part of the problem," she said. ARMIE HAMMER COMPARES HIS HOLLYWOOD EXILE TO BEING CRUCIFIED: 'THE NAILS ARE IN MY HANDS' Haley’s lawyer, the famed victims’ rights attorney Gloria Allred, rejected any suggestion that Weinstein’s sentencing means the #MeToo era is over. "Women are empowered in a way they have never been before," she said. Why Weinstein is being sentenced a second time Weinstein was originally sentenced to 23 years in prison after a jury convicted him of assaulting Haley and raping an aspiring actress, Jessica Mann, in 2013. Tried for a second time last year, he was again convicted of a first-degree criminal sex act for assaulting Haley, who has also gone by the name Mimi Haleyi. In a messy split verdict, the jury acquitted him of forcibly performing oral sex on another woman, Kaja Sokola, and could not reach a verdict on a rape charge involving Mann. After another retrial ended in a hung jury in May, Manhattan prosecutors dropped the rape charge rather than pursue a fourth trial after Mann said she could not bear to testify again. Weinstein’s health issues pushed the defense to ask for leniency. SETH ROGEN REFUSES TO OFFER JAMES FRANCO A SECOND CHANCE AFTER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT CLAIMS Defense lawyer Jacob Kaplan wanted three more years on top of the six years Weinstein already served, saying a longer sentence would make it more likely that Weinstein dies in prison. Weinstein has been in the hospital six times since 2025, Kaplan said, while dealing with blood cancer, congestive heart failure and kidney issues. Weinstein is also awaiting resentencing in a separate rape case in Los Angeles. A California appeals court upheld the 2022 conviction but threw out his original 16-year sentence because the judge had considered his New York convictions — that were later thrown out — as an aggravating factor. After shuffling between state prison, where he tested positive for COVID-19 early in the pandemic, and New York City’s notorious Rikers Island complex, Weinstein has been housed at a medical unit for inmates at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan. Haley describes the assault that led to Weinstein’s conviction Haley, 49, is a former entertainment producer now working in advertising. She said she met Weinstein through a mutual connection and worked briefly as a production assistant on "Project Runway," a reality competition show that he produced. FOUR MORE WOMEN ACCUSE FORMER NFL PLAYER OF SEXUAL ASSAULT AMID EXISTING ALLEGATIONS: 'BLATANT LIES' Haley said she accepted an invitation to visit Weinstein’s apartment, and, after chatting briefly, he lunged to kiss her, she testified. She said she rebuffed him, but he grabbed her, forcibly backed her into a bedroom and sexually assaulted her, ignoring her pleas to stop. She recalled Weinstein asking, "Don’t you think we’re much closer now?" after either the alleged assault or a subsequent occasion when she says she had unwanted, but not forced, sex with him. She also recalled telling him after the second encounter, "You know you can’t keep doing this." title: Country star, former college football player Lee Brice rips NIL, pro players going back to college
description: Lee Brice, former Clemson Tigers scholarship player, says the NIL era and transfer portal have stripped college football of its passion and magic.
content: The state of college sports, particularly the "money sports" of football and basketball, is in a pretty precarious position right now. Between the increasingly bloated NIL budgets (that fans sometimes find themselves on the hook for), a crazy transfer portal period every winter, and professional players trying to find their way back onto college rosters, it's getting harder to feel the same passion for the game many once held so dearly. But you don't need to take my word for it, even former college athletes from a time not-too-long ago are voicing their displeasure with the current state of college football. COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS FINALLY BACK AFTER MONTHS OF NCAA LAWSUITS, NIL DRAMA AND CONGRESSIONAL FIGHTS One of those former college athletes who is fed up with it all is Lee Brice. The country music star was once a scholarship player for the Clemson Tigers, and he joined the "Tomi Lahren is Fearless" show to discuss the issues plaguing his favorite sport. "I'm not a fan of the way things have changed," Brice said. While he doesn't disagree with the idea of paying college athletes who bring in millions of dollars in revenue to their universities, Brice was expecting there to be more rules in place. SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS "In the NFL, you go and sign a contract. You can't just leave," Brice states. "But in college, you can go get paid all that money and then go, 'I just want to go somewhere else.'" That lack of commitment, as Brice puts it, isn't teaching the young men who are having all this money thrown at them any of the values they will need as they get older. The need for guardrails in the college game is precisely why Congress has become a battleground for paying college athletes, culminating in the Save College Sports Act which has been hotly debated on both sides of the political aisle. It's getting to the point where hardcore fans like Brice can't even stomach watching the game he used to love. "It's really hard right now to watch college football, because it used to be, it was all passion," Brice admits. "They devoted themselves to this one team for four years or five years. And now... there's just no devotion. And you kind of lose the magic of what college football was. So overall, no, I don't like at all where it's at. I think it could have been done better." title: Mike Florio thinks the New York Giants should consider replacing Jaxson Dart with–wait for it–Colin Kaepernick
description: Mike Florio suggested the New York Giants sign Colin Kaepernick after Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, sparking immediate criticism.
content: When New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury on Monday night, we knew one of the usual suspects in sports media would call for the team to sign – who else? – Colin Kaepernick. They do it every time a team loses its starting quarterback. The question was who would make the claim first. The list of candidates included, but was not limited to, Jemele Hill, Dan Le Batard, Mike Florio, Mina Kimes, Stephen A. Smith, Mark Jones and Bomani Jones. Mike Florio is the winner. On Wednesday, the far-left sports blogger suggested the Giants bring in Kaepernick. "With the Giants now desperate for quarterback help — and with Jake Haener and Brandon Allen as the most viable options behind new starter Jameis Winston — why not bring Kaepernick in for a look?" Florio wrote. Florio tried arguing that Kaepernick would be a natural fit for the Giants’ offense. "Harbaugh’s New York staff includes Greg Roman, who was the offensive coordinator during Kaepernick’s first four years in San Francisco. It would be easy, in theory, to configure the offense to fit Kaepernick. If Kaepernick still has the skills he had when he last played," he continued. Although Florio acknowledged that Kaepernick might not impress during a workout, he concluded that "there’s no reason not to give it a whirl." We disagree. 5 TOUGH QUESTIONS COLIN KAEPERNICK DIDN'T HEAR DURING HIS MEDIA TOUR | MATT CALKINS There are multiple reasons not to give Kaepernick a "whirl," as Florio put it. For one, it would be a waste of time. It is Week 3. The Giants lost Dart for the season. Jameis Winston looked unplayable Monday night against the Rams. The team doesn't have time to work out a quarterback for mere public-relations purposes. And that is all trying out Kaepernick would accomplish. Kaepernick has not played professional football in a decade. He was not particularly good the last time we saw him. In his final NFL season, 2016, he posted a 49.2 QBR and served as a backup to Blaine Gabbert. He is now approaching age 39 with a decade’s worth of rust. In all likelihood, no athlete could take 10 years off and immediately compete in the NFL. Kaepernick can claim that he trains every morning, but there is no substitute for playing football. Florio’s no-harm, no-foul argument technically applies to any quarterback the Giants could work out, including players from the UFL who have far more recent playing experience than Kaepernick. KAEPERNICK TELLS 'THE VIEW' THAT NFL OWNERS KEPT HIM OUT OVER POLITICS AND POWER, CLAIMS THEY DONATE TO TRUMP What’s more, the same downside that existed in 2017 remains today. Any team that works out Kaepernick invites an immediate circus of scrutiny and racial hysteria. In fact, Florio says he is suggesting the Giants make the call because head coach Jim Harbaugh considered Kaepernick back in 2017. See, the Florios and Jemele Hills of the world would not be satisfied if a team simply gave Kaepernick a look. They would instantly chastise that team as racist if it did not sign Kaepernick and hand him the starting job. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! As we have argued for years, Kaepernick is not out of the NFL because teams have overlooked some hidden superstar. He is out because the downside of signing him far outweighs the upside. He is a distraction, and his play isn't good enough to justify the attention that would follow. Signing Kaepernick would turn the Giants into a topic not only on sports television but also on cable news. That was the case in 2017, it is even more so now. At this point, you have to wonder what Florio’s intentions are. Perhaps he is trying to compensate for his vulgar past by shilling the far left’s favorite athletes. Maybe he is signaling his virtue. Or perhaps his brain has been scrambled by a severe case of Trump derangement syndrome and too much social media. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In any event, Florio’s latest blog calling for the Giants to work out Kaepernick is embarrassing. It undermines his credibility and makes him look like a partisan stooge desperate for attention.

title: Dashcam captures terrifying moment lightning nearly strikes Utah truck driver
description: Dashcam video captures a lightning bolt striking Interstate 84 in Utah just feet from a moving truck during severe weather on Tuesday evening.
content: A truck driver on a Utah freeway narrowly missed being struck by lightning amid severe weather earlier this week. Video of the incident appears to show the moment a lightning strike hit Interstate 84, near the mouth of Weber Canyon, just feet away from a moving truck on Tuesday night, ABC4.com reported. Motorist Tucker Ralphs captured the video on his dashcam as he was commuting home. title: AP invokes lynching history in Mississippi hanging death after Black man is charged with murder
description: The Associated Press faced scrutiny for invoking lynching history in coverage of Tasia Fortune's death after Jarques Ratliff, a Black man, was charged.
content: The Associated Press faced criticism Wednesday for invoking America's history of lynchings in coverage of a Black Mississippi woman found hanging from a tree, even after a Black man was charged with her murder and authorities said they had not established a motive. The AP reported that the death of a 29-year-old Tasia Fortune, who was found behind an abandoned Jackson home Aug. 3, had "stirred distressing memories of the grim history of lynchings across the U.S. South." The report also identified murder suspect Jarques Ratliff, 51, as Black, noted he pleaded not guilty and acknowledged that police and prosecutors had not announced a suspected motive. Media Research Center Video host Justine Brooke Murray criticized the AP's framing in a statement Wednesday to Fox News Digital, arguing the wire service blurred the line between journalism and activism. NAVY VETERAN WHO WON CNN DEFAMATION CASE APPEALS LAWSUIT AGAINST THE ASSOCIATED PRESS OVER 'SMUGGLING' CLAIM "In this most recent case, a more accurate name for the AP is ‘the Activist-Press.’ The broader concern is that the AP, specifically, appointed their own guidelines as the gold standard for objective journalism," Murray said. "They've established a set of rules for the vocabulary everyone else is expected to regurgitate, and with that, established themselves as the arbiters of truth. How much reality must they rewrite before the others stop following suit?" Murray also accused major media organizations of applying inconsistent standards when race or terrorism becomes part of a developing news story. "If a victim has preferred minority status among elitist media organizations, they will often concoct hate crime fantasies and pass it off as the indisputable truth," she said. "They're too self-important to bother correcting themselves when their imaginary White boogeyman turns out to be Black. In the same breath, they'll lecture us not to jump to conclusions each time an Islamist shouts 'Allahu Akbar' before blowing up busy American streets, if they're not shamelessly race-swapping suspects." AOC’S ‘MODERN-DAY LYNCHINGS’ CLAIM TORN TO SHREDS ONLINE AS BLACK HANGING CASE FINDINGS TELL A DIFFERENT STORY Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, also told the AP she did not believe her daughter's death was racially motivated. Spivey is White, while Fortune's father is Black. Spivey described the circumstances surrounding her daughter's killing as personal. "I think this is something very personal, very personal," Spivey said. The controversy followed reporting by several major news organizations that initially emphasized Fortune's race while omitting Ratliff's race when reporting his arrest. The AP's initial arrest report described Fortune as a "Black woman" but did not identify Ratliff as Black, though the wire service included his race in subsequent coverage. Fox News Digital reached out to the AP for comment but did not immediately receive a response. The AP's News Values and Principles state that its journalists follow standards intended to safeguard its reporting from "bias and inaccuracies." The organization also states that it seeks to report news accurately, honestly and impartially and that corrections should be made "fully, quickly, transparently and ungrudgingly." ANTIRACISM ACTIVIST BLAMES 'WHITE-OWNED' MEDIA FOR 'LYNCHED' BLACK SCHOLAR'S DEATH, SPARKS ONLINE OUTRAGE Ratliff was arrested after the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's Office classified Fortune's death a homicide. Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney said the investigation remained active and additional arrests were expected. Police have not publicly detailed a motive or the precise nature of Ratliff's association with Fortune. Brackney previously acknowledged the attention surrounding the case and Mississippi's racial history while stressing that investigators were relying on evidence rather than speculation. title: Hackers hijack verified streaming account to spread malware, researchers find
description: HBO Max's verified Reddit account was hijacked to push 108 malicious ads using ClickFix, a technique that tricks victims into running dangerous commands.
content: You probably know to be suspicious of a strange pop-up or a random website asking you to download something. But what happens when the ad comes from a verified account belonging to a company you recognize? That is what made a recent malware campaign involving HBO Max so concerning. Researchers at Hudson Rock found that cybercriminals hijacked HBO Max's official, verified Reddit account and used it to push 108 distinct malicious ads over roughly 48 hours. The ads promoted HBO Max downloads along with AI tools, developer software and Mac utilities. Because they appeared under a verified corporate account, potential victims had one less reason to question what they were seeing. You do not need HBO Max to be exposed to this type of attack. The larger lesson involves how criminals can borrow credibility from verified accounts and familiar companies to get people to lower their guard. And once you click, the attack can take a surprisingly simple turn.
