No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com. Register and receive the replay and step-by-step guide afterward. SCAMMERS ARE BUYING GOOGLE ADS TO STEAL BANK LOGINS The HBO Max ad looked far more legitimate than a typical scam The incident first surfaced after a Reddit user spotted an advertisement posted by the verified u/hbomax account. The ad promoted what appeared to be a native HBO Max application for macOS. HBO Max does not currently offer a native app for Mac computers. Its support page directs Mac users to stream at HBOMax.com. The user followed the advertisement to a convincing landing page. However, clicking the download button did not start a normal file download. Instead, the website displayed a prompt telling the visitor to copy and paste a command into Terminal. That request should immediately raise a red flag. Elsewhere in the broader PasteSwitch operation, Windows users could be routed through Run or PowerShell-based attack paths. Researchers found that the Windows branch could use PowerShell and other tools to eventually load malware directly into memory. ClickFix tricks you into launching the malware yourself The technique behind the campaign is known as ClickFix. Rather than relying entirely on a malicious download, ClickFix gives you instructions that lead you to execute the attack yourself. The prompt may pretend that something went wrong with a CAPTCHA. Another version may claim you need to fix a browser problem or complete an installation. A malicious webpage can even place a command onto your clipboard. Then it tells you where to paste it. That little sequence can feel like ordinary troubleshooting, especially when the page looks professional and the ad came from an account you trusted. In the HBO Max campaign, Hudson Rock says the technique relied on getting the victim to execute attacker-supplied code through Terminal. That approach can bypass some protections designed to stop malicious browser downloads. The warning sign I want you to remember is simple: A website should never need you to paste an unfamiliar command into Terminal, PowerShell or the Windows Run box to prove you are human or install ordinary consumer software. The HBO Max account pushed 108 malicious ads The fake HBO Max download was only part of what researchers uncovered. Hudson Rock says attackers used the compromised Reddit account to push 108 distinct advertisements during the roughly 48-hour campaign. The ads shifted between multiple software lures as domains were taken down or abandoned. The researchers counted: That rapid switching shows how attackers can reuse the credibility of one compromised account while changing the websites and software names placed in front of victims. Researchers connect the ads to a wider PasteSwitch operation Hudson Rock and researchers from ADAMnetworks connected the HBO Max campaign to a broader operation they call PasteSwitch. The name describes what stays consistent across the operation: victims paste a command supplied by the attacker while the delivery system changes what comes next based on the visitor, platform and campaign. That means two people clicking similar malicious ads may not necessarily receive the same malware. On Macs, researchers found several PasteSwitch payload paths. MacSync could steal browser credentials, Gecko browser profiles, Telegram data, Apple Notes and macOS passwords. Researchers also documented an AMOS helper chain that could maintain access to an infected device. Another part of the operation used fake versions of cryptocurrency wallet apps, including Ledger, Trezor Suite and Exodus. Those fake apps were designed to steal 12- and 24-word cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases. That means one bad command could expose far more than the browser tab you were looking at. CLICKLOCK MAC MALWARE LOCKS APPS UNTIL YOU GIVE IN Windows users faced a different malware path PasteSwitch could also recognize Windows visitors and change its attack. Researchers found a Windows branch that used mshta and PowerShell. One route delivered a malicious file disguised in an MP3/HTA format before creating a scheduled task and launching PowerShell. Later stages could inject the Amatera Stealer directly into memory without first writing the final malware to disk. Researchers also found a technique designed to make malicious traffic appear as though it were communicating with Facebook, potentially making basic network monitoring less useful. That level of technical complexity sits behind a remarkably simple first step: convincing someone to paste a command. PasteSwitch can also tamper with crypto wallet addresses Researchers connected PasteSwitch to another dangerous tool: cryptocurrency clipboard hijackers. The operation delivered malware known as AnimateClipper and ZigClipper. These tools can monitor the clipboard and replace cryptocurrency addresses when a victim copies or pastes them. So, you might carefully copy the correct wallet address, paste it into a transaction and unknowingly send the money somewhere else. Researchers also found that the malware used Binance Smart Chain contracts to retrieve changing command-and-control domains. Between March and July 2026, researchers observed 36 changes made by the same attacker-controlled address. That helped the operation keep switching infrastructure as domains became unusable. Why verified accounts and paid ads can fool careful people Most of us make quick trust decisions online. A recognizable company name can make an ad feel safer. A verification badge adds credibility. When both appear together in a paid advertisement, the whole thing can look vetted. But verified accounts can still get compromised. Hudson Rock says the attackers took advantage of HBO Max's trusted advertising identity during the campaign. The polished assets also helped lower the skepticism people might normally apply to an unknown online advertisement. That changes how we need to think about ads. If an advertisement offers software you want, open a new browser tab and find the company's official website yourself. For apps, check your device's official app store. Those extra few seconds could stop the attack before it reaches your computer. Reddit confirms the account was compromised Reddit has now confirmed that an HBO Max account authorized to run advertisements on its platform was compromised and used to distribute malicious links. In a statement provided to CyberGuy, Reddit said: "We recently learned that an HBO Max account authorized to run advertisements on Reddit was compromised and used to run ads containing malicious links. After learning of the issue, we locked the account, removed the ads and began working with HBO Max to strengthen its account security. At this time, we have not identified any impact to other Reddit advertising accounts." We also reached out to HBO Max for comment but did not hear back before our deadline. ClickFix has become a major malware delivery method ClickFix has spread quickly because the attacker convinces the victim to take the final action. Huntress says ClickFix accounted for 53% of the malware loader activity it observed during 2025, based on its endpoint and identity telemetry. Attackers also keep changing the lure. We have already seen fake CAPTCHA prompts spread through thousands of compromised websites and bogus Windows updates use similar techniques. Compromised websites can also display fake verification prompts designed to push visitors toward dangerous commands. The design may change next week. The request to run an unfamiliar command remains the behavior to watch for. Your Mac may warn you, but do not depend on the alert Apple has added another layer of protection against some ClickFix attacks. On macOS Tahoe 26.4 or later, Terminal may warn you when pasted text resembles a potentially harmful command. The warning explains that scammers sometimes persuade people to paste commands that can compromise their Mac or privacy. That protection can help, but users may not see a warning for every malicious command. Attackers also continue adjusting their techniques. Your own judgment still plays a major role. 'THE ODYSSEY' STREAMING SCAM COULD STEAL YOUR BANK INFO 8 ways to protect yourself from malicious ads and ClickFix attacks A convincing ad can get anyone's attention. These steps can help you recognize the warning signs before one bad click turns into a bigger problem. 1) Treat ads with caution, even from verified accounts A familiar logo or verification badge cannot guarantee that the person controlling the account today is the legitimate owner. When possible, visit the company's official website directly instead of clicking an ad. 2) Never paste a command you do not understand If a webpage asks you to open Terminal, PowerShell or the Run dialog and paste something, close the page. Ordinary consumer software rarely requires you to run an unfamiliar command manually. 3) Get software from official sources Use the developer's official website or your device's app store. Be especially careful when an advertisement suddenly offers a desktop application or special download you have never heard of. 4) Pay attention when a site touches your clipboard Some ClickFix pages can copy malicious text onto your clipboard. If your browser or security software warns that a site copied something unexpectedly, take that warning seriously. 5) Keep your device and browser updated Security updates can add protections against newer attack techniques. Install updates through your operating system settings or the software's built-in updater. 6) Use strong antivirus software with real-time protection Strong antivirus software can help block malicious websites and detect malware if an attack gets past your browser. It gives you another layer of protection when a convincing page slips through. 7) Act quickly if you already ran a suspicious command Disconnect the computer from the internet and run a full security scan using trusted antivirus software. From a clean device, change passwords for sensitive accounts, starting with your primary email account. Then review financial accounts and cryptocurrency wallets for activity you do not recognize. 8) Turn on multifactor authentication An infostealer may capture passwords and browser information. Multifactor authentication can make stolen credentials harder to use, although some session-stealing malware can get around normal login protections. Kurt's key takeaways What caught my attention here was how quickly something dangerous could start to feel legitimate. The advertisement came from a verified corporate account. The page looked polished. Then the instructions presented themselves as a normal installation step. That combination can get past the skepticism many of us have learned to apply to obviously shady emails and suspicious websites. So I would focus less on how professional an advertisement looks and more on what it asks you to do next. The moment a website tells you to open Terminal, PowerShell or another system utility and paste an unfamiliar command, stop. Hackers will keep looking for ways to borrow the reputation of companies people already trust. We need to adjust our instincts as those attacks change. Would you still trust an online ad because it came from a verified company account, or has this changed the way you decide what is safe to click? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. title: Sheriff's deputy saves man from fiery wreck after high-speed chase ends in crash
description: Body camera footage shows a Kitsap County deputy smashing a car door with his flashlight as flames engulf an SUV after a crash at 111 mph..
content: A sheriff's deputy pulled a screaming man from his burning vehicle moments after he led authorities on a high-speed chase that ended in a crash. According to officials, the Kitsap County Sheriff's Office deputy spotted the suspect driving about 20 miles per hour over the speed limit on State Highway 104 in Kingston, Washington, around 11:30 p.m. Monday. The driver refused to pull over and then accelerated, reaching speeds of 111 miles per hour, according to the sheriff's office. SUSPECT ACCUSED OF HURLING CHAINSAW AT DEPUTIES DURING CHAOTIC STOLEN CAR CHASE CAUGHT ON VIDEO The deputy said he lost sight of the suspect until he noticed tire marks on the road and billowing smoke nearby. He then discovered the man had driven his SUV into a yard, where it slammed into a tractor and burst into flames, according to photos and body camera footage. In video released by authorities, the deputy first tried to get the man out through the driver's side window by breaking it with his flashlight. He abandoned that idea after the trapped man shouted, "I can't get out that way!" The deputy moved to the passenger's side door and began repeatedly slamming the handle with the edge of his flashlight, all while the flames from the car's engine grew higher and hotter, the bodycam footage showed. SEE IT: ICE AGENTS PAUSE ARREST OPERATION TO SAVE WOMAN IN ROLLOVER CRASH Eventually, a Port Gamble police officer arrived with a fire extinguisher and put out the fire. The video then cut to the deputy pulling the man out of the mangled car. North Kitsap Fire and Rescue crews arrived and airlifted the man to a hospital so he could be treated for his injuries. title: STEVE MOORE: The IRS went after honest landowners. It's time to end this tax nightmare
description: The IRS admitted its conservation easement tax assessments are flawed, creating a new office to address cases affecting 250,000 taxpayers nationwide.
content: The IRS recently did something federal agencies almost never do: admit their approach wasn’t working. They conceded that the approach to the Conservation Easement program tax assessments is flawed and often unfair. In a press release last month, the IRS rightly stopped its assault — at least for now — on more than a thousand separate groups nationwide, comprised of about 250,000 individuals, who have participated in land conservation easements. The agency decided to withdraw its own arbitrary deadlines under its punitive settlement initiative for these donations that taxpayers, relying on qualified appraisals and professional advice, believed complied with federal law. STEVE MOORE: THE IRS BECAME JUDGE, JURY AND EXECUTIONER IN A TAX-CODE WITCH HUNT AGAINST AMERICANS This longstanding program provides tax incentives for people who have put hundreds of thousands of acres of pristine forest, ranch, and farmland into a "conservation easement" — preventing it from ever being developed. Despite some of its flaws, including fraudulent property assessments, the program has long been supported by Republicans and Democrats. The IRS made a concession that standardized, one-size-fits-all settlement offers "are not well suited to the full range of conservation easement cases." But it didn’t stop there. The creation of the new Office of Conservation Easements was also announced — giving hope to many that the wrongs of the past will finally be addressed in a deliberate, fair manner. One of this administration’s best, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, deserves credit for his willingness to take a pause, look closer at these complex cases, and potentially implement corrective action to address serious questions about a law that has been around for decades. This was not an easy move to make, but it is the right one. For decades, more than a quarter of a million American taxpayers have preserved pristine land and prevented development through legal conservation easement donations on the professional advice of expert geologists, land managers, thousands of credentialed lawyers, CPAs, and certified appraisers — to name a few. But those law-abiding taxpayers, who listened to the advice of experts, have been treated by non-experts at the IRS as a single undifferentiated class of common criminals. TREASURY HAILS SUCCESS OF ANTI-FRAUD PROCESS THAT FLAGGED AND PREVENTED $99 MILLION IN PAYMENTS TO DEAD PEOPLE The IRS has been threatening billions of dollars in tax bills — even to honest taxpayers who played by the rules. It’s become a political football, and a fair resolution needs to be reached quickly. The Tax Court's docket remains intact and backlogged, and if hearings started today, they wouldn’t be completed for about 10 years. Knowing this, the IRS is still pushing taxpayers to make expensive court appearances. Despite the creation of the new Office of Conservation Easements to adjudicate these cases, program participants continue to move toward trial with no fair settlement in sight. These cases routinely produce inconsistent outcomes in court, with judges sustaining a large share of a claimed deduction in one case while all but zeroing out comparable claims in others. The taxpayers are still caught in a game of Russian roulette. Detailed reviews of these cases show valuations are often done behind a desk at the IRS by people who never visit the property in question, nor do they possess any knowledge or expertise in the field in which they are operating. FORGET PAYING YOUR ‘FAIR SHARE’ OF TAXES. HERE ARE 5 WAYS POLITICIANS WANT EVEN MORE The Treasury is rightly trying to root out fraudulent land appraisals, as they should. But they are casting a very wide net that too often ensnares both the fraudsters and the law-abiding taxpayers in the same net. The good news is that the Office of Conservation Easements has the potential to look past the IRS's faulty, deeply flawed, one-size-fits-all, foregone conclusions model and instead build a systematic process to evaluate property value based on objective and verifiable data on land values. For all the program’s shortcomings, Congress and federal government agencies spent sixty years building the conservation easement program and encouraging Americans to use it. In fact, when the issue was revisited several times along the way, the tax deductions were not stopped; they were enhanced. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION By all means, go after those who have defrauded taxpayers. But fix the program. By all means, fix the land appraisal system so that the tax cheats can be exposed. But stop punishing those who played by the rules. This can be achieved by using independent valuation and appraisal specialists, land-use and conservation experts, geologists, and other parties with direct, ground-level familiarity with the real value of properties put into conservation. This would help expose bad actors who committed fraud and protect those taxpayers who followed the law. Eliminating what supporters called IRS witch hunts was a clear promise that Trump campaigned on. This is a good opportunity to stand and deliver on tax fairness. It’s good policy and good politics. title: The top moments from Iran president’s tense visit to US soil as war rages
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian cast Iran as a victim of U.S. aggression at the United Nations General Assembly as a delegate walked out.
author_name: Ashley DiMella, Efrat Lachter, Morgan Phillips
content: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian defended Tehran’s conduct in its war with the United States on Wednesday, taking aim at President Donald Trump and vowing that Iran would not surrender during a fiery address before world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly. The speech follows months of fighting, failed diplomatic efforts and mounting international pressure on Tehran, giving Pezeshkian a high-profile platform to defend Iran’s actions and challenge the U.S. account of the conflict. "America and Israel attacked us, equipped with the latest technology and weapons systems, and our people stood steadfast. Yes, they did hit us, but we did not bend the knee. We did not bow our head," said Pezeshkian. "Those who are terrorists and train and protect terrorists describe us as such. We have only defended ourselves. We are not terrorists." Fox News Digital compiled the top moments from Pezeshkian’s speech and the developments unfolding both inside and outside the U.N. ONE GLARING ISSUE GOES UNADDRESSED IN UN CHIEF'S HIGH-STAKES TALKS WITH IRAN'S PRESIDENT Protesters gather outside UN, jeering the Iranian president's visit Pezeshkian’s fiery attacks on Trump and the United States came amid a hostile reception in New York City, where protesters gathered to denounce the Iranian government as its president addressed world leaders at the United Nations. Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani joined a "Free Iran" rally outside the U.N., where protesters denounced Tehran as Pezeshkian addressed world leaders. Demonstrators waved Iranian flags while denouncing Iran’s government over its repression of political dissent, restrictions on women’s rights and treatment of opposition figures. US delegate walks out as Iran vows 'we will not bend the knee' at UN As the emcee announced Pezeshkian's impending speech, audible boos erupted from the protest crowd outside the UN as the leader walked out onto the stage. A member of the U.S. delegation walked out of the General Assembly hall after Pezeshkian began criticizing the United States during his speech, Fox News Digital previously reported. Fox News Digital reached out to the U.S. Mission for comment. TRUMP DEFENDS US INTERVENTIONS ABROAD AHEAD OF 'BIG DECISION' ON IRAN: 'SETTLING YEARS OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS' America on trial, Trump dubbed a 'bully' Pezeshkian used his speech to defend Iran’s conduct during the war and take aim at the United States and Israel. "The United States using weapons with multiple warheads targeted that sports hall. … They martyred, assassinated our scientists, our men, women and children," he said. "This is what the United States seeks to do with all countries — [to] sacrifice the population of a country in order to achieve [its] goals," Pezeshkian added. CENTCOM has denied that U.S. forces carried out the strike on the sports hall in Lamerd, saying American forces did not strike the city or anywhere within 30 miles of it on the opening day of Operation Epic Fury. FIVE TOP TAKEAWAYS FROM TRUMP'S HIGH-STAKES UN SPEECH TO THE WORLD Pezeshkian said that the U.S. and Israel have learned that Iran cannot be made to surrender, reiterating that Iran is "not afraid of fighting" and would defend the country "until our last breath." TRUMP WARNS IRAN WILL BE HIT 'REALLY HARD' IF NUCLEAR NEGOTIATIONS COLLAPSE AGAIN During a moment of his speech, Pezeshkian held up props showing photos of the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and Iranian schoolchildren killed during the beginning of the conflict. "Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed upon our country. And we defended ourselves with utmost strength. America and Israel attacked us," Pezeshkian said. He also used the opportunity to take shots at Trump, accusing him of "bullying" Iran. "More must be understood by Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us, that we are ready for dialog and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force," Pezeshkian said. Trump addressed leaders Tuesday and said he faced a "big decision" between reaching a deal with Iran or, in his words, "annihilat[ing] the Islamic Republic," before U.S. officials later met with Iranian officials. "Going back to the words of the president of the United States yesterday … everything uttered about our country was against the very essence and charter in the spirit of the United Nations," Pezeshkian said. "He must know that the resistance of the Iranian people will increase in the face of sanctions, and increased bullying, because all of us under law will never bow our head or bend at the knee." Administration officials quickly pushed back on Pezeshkian’s attacks and disputed his account of the conflict. "I think sponsoring terrorist organizations in the region to attack your neighbors, attack energy infrastructure, attack civilian sites is a violation of the UN system. So I don't know what's standing. Iran has to lecture anyone on human rights or the international system. When they habitually violate it," said Secretary of State Marco Rubio. title: Supreme Court to hear Missouri redistricting case for third time
description: Justice Brett Kavanaugh accepted an emergency appeal in the Missouri redistricting case as the 2025 map faces its third Supreme Court review.
content: The U.S. Supreme Court will hear arguments in a Missouri redistricting case for a third time after Justice Brett Kavanaugh accepted a request to intervene in the case once again Tuesday night. The divisive redistricting map drawn in 2025 would grant Republicans an additional seat in the House of Representatives if it is put in place ahead of the 2026 elections. A federal judge in Missouri ruled in favor of the 2025 map last month, but the Supreme Court put a stay on that ruling just two weeks ago. Opponents of the map issued an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court late Tuesday night after the St. Louis-based Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in favor of the new map on Monday. FEDERAL APPEALS COURT ORDERS MISSOURI TO USE CONGRESSIONAL MAP REJECTED TWICE BY SUPREME COURT Kavanaugh handles emergency requests for the state of Missouri and directed supporters of the new map to respond to the appeal by Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET. The development is the latest in a roller-coaster ride of legal decisions that have seen the new map fly up and down between federal and state courts, the Supreme Court and the Missouri Supreme Court. ELECTION CHAOS IN THIS RED STATE JUST GOT EVEN STRANGER FOR REPUBLICANS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING The case began when Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins rejected a petition for the 2025 map to be placed on the ballot for a vote in 2026. Instead, the new map was used to determine congressional districts for the state's primary elections. The Democratic group behind the petition, People Not Politicians, asked a state court to intervene, saying the group's petition of 300,000 signatures should have triggered a referendum on the new map under Missouri's constitution. The Missouri Supreme Court agreed, writing that the 2025 map cannot go into effect "unless and until approved by the voters at the November 2026 general election." MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING Hoskins then appealed the case to the Supreme Court, but Kavanaugh declined to hear his request on Sept. 4. Meanwhile, Republican candidates who won primary elections based on the 2025 maps brought up a separate case in federal court, arguing that if the general election takes place under the 2022 map their districts would be very different from the primary maps. Many general election voters, they noted, would also be presented with options they had no role in voting for during the primaries. SUPREME COURT AGAIN BLOCKS MISSOURI FROM USING TRUMP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS Eighth Circuit Judge Stephen R. Clark ruled in favor of those candidates and issued an order requiring that the 2025 maps be used in this year's elections, effectively contradicting the state Supreme Court. This time, People Not Politicians asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene, and Kavanaugh agreed. The court issued an unsigned order blocking Clark's order until the Eighth Circuit issued a formal ruling in the case. The Eighth Circuit then fast-tracked the case and ruled in favor of the 2025 map. MISSOURI SUPREME COURT THREATENS SECRETARY OF STATE WITH CONTEMPT AMID INTENSIFYING REDISTRICTING BATTLE People Not Politicians filed their latest request for an intervention on Tuesday night, arguing that the court's ruling against the new map was still in effect, and pointing to statements from Missouri election officials saying it is too late to change what maps are used in the upcoming elections. The Missouri Association of County Clerks and Election Authorities already announced it will not be using the 2025 map for November, arguing in an appeal filing that the state does not have enough time to provide new ballots. Officials should stop wasting taxpayers’ money on pointless legal action and instead focus on administering our elections," People Not Politicians director Richard von Glahn said in a statement. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Jaxson Dart tore his MCL and meniscus which require surgery and ends his 2026 season with the New York Giants
description: Jaxson Dart faces MCL and meniscus surgery that will sideline the New York Giants quarterback for six to nine months, derailing the team's season.
content: Jaxson Dart is headed to knee surgery and that will end his chances of playing again during the 2026 NFL season. Multiple reports say, and OutKick has confirmed, that Dart suffered not only MCL damage but also meniscus damage when he took a vicious hit early in the Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Dart also sprained his PCL, but the torn MCL and torn meniscus are the major problems that must be addressed by surgery. The only good news in this entire scenario is that Dart did not sustain any damage to his ACL. It is intact, a source said. Dart and the Giants spent the past day or so seeking multiple medical opinions in search of options that might keep him from missing the entire rest of the season. title: Best hikes in and around Knoxville ahead of Tennessee's showdown with Texas Longhorns
description: Ijams Nature Center, House Mountain, and Sharp's Ridge top the list of must-hike Knoxville trails to explore during a fall college football weekend.
content: Fall is officially here, which means hiking season is about to reach its peak. Hiking in the summer is fine and all, but autumn hikes feature perfect temperatures, fall colors, and crisp air that will have you remembering your treks for years to come. And what better way to kick off the true start to hiking season than a top-15 college football showdown in east Tennessee. BEST HIKES IN AND AROUND OXFORD TO GET YOU READY FOR OLE MISS-LSU'S WEEK THREE SHOWDOWN With all due respect to college towns like Oxford and Lubbock, they have nothing on Knoxville when it comes to getting a true hike in. Being able to pick trails around the University of Tennessee and its surrounding areas is almost like cheating, so if you're heading to Neyland for the game this weekend, you owe it to yourself to check out a few of these spots. Ijams Nature Center The best overall hike in the Knoxville area has to belong to the Ijams Nature Center. Whether you're in town early or you have only a couple hours on Saturday morning before kickoff, this is the hike for you. HIKING ETIQUETTE RULES THAT SHOULD BE COMMON SENSE BUT APPARENTLY NEED TO BE SPELLED OUT FOR SOME PEOPLE Situated just three miles from downtown, Ijams Nature Center features more than 14 miles of hikeable trails across forests, meadows, ponds and an old quarry landscape, with routes ranging from easy to difficult. I highly recommend checking out Mead's Quarry, which has several trails that weave through a former industrial landscape around a gorgeous quarry lake. If you're looking for a nice, relaxing hike, you can also check out the River Boardwalk, which features stunning views of the Tennessee River. There's something for everyone here and you don't even need to leave the city. House Mountain While Ijams is the more versatile pick, if you're looking for the best "pure hike," House Mountain is the place to be. The House Mountain State Natural Area is about 15 miles northeast of the city, and it gives hikers both a workout and a view for their efforts. Seriously, this is the highest point in Knox county, featuring a 2,100-foot crest for those of you who are looking to actually climb something while you're in the Volunteer State. Readers beware: this is an actual hike, not just a leisurely stroll around a greenway, so pack accordingly. COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S FIRST FULL SATURDAY IS HERE AND IT'S A CELEBRATION OF AMERICA AT ITS BEST We're talking wooded areas leading to rocky overlooks, but the payoff of the breathtaking views of the Cumberland and Unaka Mountains is well worth it. The burning in your calves will be temporary, but the pictures from the summit will last a lifetime. Sharp's Ridge Veterans Memorial Park When I said Knoxville was basically a cheat code when it came to hiking spots, I wasn't lying, and Sharp's Ridge Veterans Memorial Park is a perfect example of why. It's less than a 10-minute drive from the downtown area, meaning the views of both the Knoxville skyline and the Smokey Mountains are insane. Sharp's Ridge features nearly five and a half miles of trails, and the observation deck at the top with the aforementioned views is the reward for getting the job done. The observation deck even has signage pointing out the names of the different mountains in the distance. This is well worth your time, and it's just a short drive from where you are likely staying, meaning there's no excuse to miss out on this hike. You can see the Smokies without ever having to go out of your way, so check it out while you're in Knoxville. William Hastie Natural Area So, you're looking for a picturesque hike without being inundated by tourists? William Hastie Natural Area is the choice. Consider this Knoxville's "hidden gem," as this hilly and wooded trail to the south of the city is the one only locals know about. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The natural-surface trails weave through miles of heavily forested terrain, and it has hikes that will satisfy both beginners and seasoned veterans alike. Trails like Mitchie's Way have been designed specifically with hikers in mind, meaning the whole area is optimized for those looking to just get a good hike in. No frills, but definitely not bare bones either. title: Maine lobsterman catches ultra-rare cotton candy lobster with crazy odds: 'It just glowed'
description: Bill Kirby's crew pulled a one-in-100-million cotton candy lobster from a trap off Searsport, Maine, and its glow stopped everyone on the boat.
content: A lobsterman and his crew in Searsport, Maine had an experience they won't soon forget. That's because they caught a "cotton candy" lobster, a rare find with estimated odds at one in 100 million. Bill Kirby, the owner of Kirby's Lobster Shack who WMTV reports has more than four decades under his belt, and his crew hauled in the rare lobster last Wednesday during what was a routine day. If you ask Kirby, he couldn’t do what he does "without a good crew." He and that good crew were doing what they normally do when they're catching lobsters. That glow, not that I'm a marine crustacean expert or anything, is caused by a genetic color mutation. After noticing it, he then turned his attention to making sure the lobster made it back to land safely. "First thing I did, once he opened it up, I went over and grabbed a hold of it and I wanted to take a look at it and found out that it was a keeper, and it was almost like we were trying to protect it the rest of the time," he said. Obviously, when Kirby tossed it into the tank alongside the other lobsters, it stood out. It's a cotton candy lobster and the others are just lobster lobsters. For those thinking he's planning to sell the lobster to the highest bidder, you're wrong. Kirby told the local outlet that he plans to donate it to the Oceanarium and Education Center in Bar Harbor. title: Trump to ask Xi to free wrongfully detained US citizen as wife speaks out
description: President Trump plans to ask Chinese President Xi Jinping to release Dr. Youlin Chen, a U.S. citizen charged with espionage after two years in China.
content: President Donald Trump plans to ask Chinese President Xi Jinping to release wrongfully detained U.S. citizen Dr. Youlin Chen, the man's family told Fox News after his wife and the wife of another detainee spoke exclusively to "Fox & Friends" Wednesday. The wives of two wrongfully detained Americans in China made a plea for Trump to intervene in their husbands' detention during an interview with Fox News senior foreign correspondent Gillian Turner. Yugang Rong and Sylvia Zin implored Trump to intervene in the cases of their husbands, Chen, a seismic and nuclear researcher, and Min Zin, a scholar with a focus on Burma, respectively. The pair are the only two U.S. citizens in China that have been designated by the U.S. State Department as wrongfully detained. CHINA’S XI SET TO ARRIVE IN WASHINGTON FOR HIGH-STAKES TRUMP SUMMIT AS AI SUPREMACY BATTLE LOOMS LARGE "My husband is an American citizen. He is the father of my son and we terribly miss him," Rong told Turner. Chen was taken from outside the Beijing airport by Chinese agents in November 2024, according to a website dedicated to his release. After Chinese agents took him, they reportedly seized his cellphone, iPad, laptop and cameras and repeatedly logged onto his email accounts and accessed his devices. His wife believes he was taken because of his seismic research into nuclear activity. "It's his research work. He has been doing a lot of research on how to monitor nuclear tests," she told "Fox & Friends." His research, according to the website, "focuses on the Earth's crustal structures in Asia using regional earthquake data, including data sourced from and in collaboration with earthquake scientists in China." In one of his publicly available reports he used geophysical research methods to detect North Korean nuclear tests. China charged Chen with espionage, but he has yet to receive a trial despite over two years of imprisonment. He has not been allowed any contact with his family. DAUGHTER OF DETAINED CHINESE PASTOR SAYS SHE HAS 'HOPE' AFTER LEARNING TRUMP MAY RAISE CASE WITH XI JINPING Sylvia Zin, meanwhile, does not understand why her husband, whose research focuses on military government and Chinese-Burma relations, was taken. title: DAVID MARCUS: Minnesota GOP candidates keep Trump at arm's length as they eye a post-Trump party future
description: Michele Tafoya and Lisa Demuth navigate a tricky balance on Trump in Minnesota, embracing some policies while keeping the president at arm's length.
content: As the once-long shot Minnesota GOP Senate nominee Michele Tafoya has closed in on Democratic opponent Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, the issue of President Donald Trump — who is not particularly popular in the Gopher State — has taken a unique turn. For Tafoya, as well as gubernatorial candidate Lisa Demuth and others down ballot for the GOP — not to mention their potential voters — the general attitude toward Trump is that while they support much of what he has done, they also represent what a post-Donald Trump Republican Party could look like. This week in St. Cloud, I met John, who was sitting in his SUV outside the courthouse. Covered in pro-Trump stickers and flags, the vehicle served as a kind of quiet, solo demonstration. I mentioned to him that his "Trump 2028" flag, in particular, seemed a bit provocative. He told me, "Well, I know he’s not really going to run again, I don’t think he legally can, but that’s just more for comedy and just for fun," adding that he thinks Vice President JD Vance is a great choice to run next, perhaps with Secretary of State Marco Rubio as his running mate. When I asked whether he thought that Tafoya and Demuth should embrace Trump more, John told me, "That's the problem with Minnesota [Republicans]. We need to be hardcore Trump, not lukewarm, and I think that’s kind of biting them in the butt, they've got to be all in." Bob, who I had chatted with the night before, along with his wife Mary, was a counterpoint that showed the eye of the needle the Minnesota GOP needs to thread. He’s retired from banking and is now a soybean farmer with mixed and nuanced views on Trump and especially his tariff regime. "The tariffs hurt us," Bob confided to Fox News Digital, but added that "the administration provided subsidies, we got about $40,000 last year that helped us stay afloat." But Bob also pointed out that things weren’t perfect before the tariffs, when it seemed countries like China were simply taking advantage of American farmers. Likewise, Scott, a man in his 60s, who I met as he was walking his dog amid the pretty, old brick buildings of solid Midwestern St. Cloud, is far from a Trump supporter, but is considering the GOP this year because of the Somali fraud scandal, which he said he has seen close up in his town. "They don’t work," Scott scoffed, before adding, "But you see them in these shiny new cars, we all knew something was going on way before it hit the news, it was just obvious." PEGGY FLANAGAN WAS MINNESOTA'S NO 2 OFFICIAL AS MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL EXPLODED UNDER STATE'S WATCH The Somali fraud question can cut both ways, though, as the manager of the restaurant where I had lunch made clear. He told me that the crackdown in St. Cloud was "extreme," and that he rarely protests, but did in this case, getting pepper sprayed for his trouble. But, when I asked if the enforcement has been less aggressive over the past few months, he was quick to admit that, "Yes, it has calmed down a lot." When you put the above pieces of the Minnesota electoral mosaic together, it becomes clear why it behooves Tafoya and Demuth to keep Trump at arm’s length, without fully breaking with him: to embrace clear successes like the closed-up southern border and no tax on overtime, while questioning less popular measures such as tariffs and the Iran war. And, after all, should Tafoya win, her four or six-year term will be under a president who is not Trump. Likewise, should Demuth serve two terms in the governor’s mansion, six of the eight years will see a new resident at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave. DAVID MARCUS: IN DEEP BLUE MINNESOTA A RED DAWN MAY BE RISING AHEAD OF THE MIDTERMS Gentle pushback on the POTUS is becoming something of a national trend for GOP Senate candidates, with both Michigan’s Mike Rogers and Iowa’s Ashley Hinson calling this week for an abrupt end to Trump’s military actions in Iran. Just as was true at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas two weeks ago. The firm subtext of the tight races this year is: What comes after Donald Trump? With the Democratic Party hurtling toward socialism all over the map, many Republicans think Tafoya is a sensible centrist who can grow the brand over the next decade. NEWT GINGRICH: REPUBLICANS CAN WIN THE 2026 MIDTERMS — IF THEY FOLLOW THE PLAN For their part, expect Democrats in Minnesota like Flanagan and Sen. Amy Klobuchar, who is running for governor, to keep pounding away at Trump like Rocky attacking Apollo Creed’s midsection. They seek anything but a nuanced and thoughtful race — they just want rage against the "orange man." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But maybe, just maybe, more than a decade after Trump descended the golden escalator, American politics is once again becoming bigger than him. If that is so, Democrats will need more than name-calling to defeat this new moderate, Midwestern breed of Republican.

title: SHOCK POLL: Powerful blue state gov's lead shrinks to single digits weeks before election
description: Bruce Blakeman trails Kathy Hochul by just nine points in a new Siena poll, closing the gap in a state where Democrats outnumber Republicans two-to-one.
content: Democrats outnumber Republicans by a roughly two-to-one margin in blue-leaning New York State, but a new poll indicates Republican gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman has cut his deficit to Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul to single digits with just six weeks to go until Election Day. Hochul, who is running for a second full four-year term steering the nation's fourth most populous state, stands at 50% support among likely voters in New York, with Blakeman at 41%, according to a Siena College poll conducted Sept. 11-17 and released on Wednesday. Blakeman, the Nassau County executive on New York's Long Island, trailed Hochul by 10 points in Siena's August survey. The one-point movement by Blakeman, who is aiming to become the first Republican in nearly a quarter-century to win an election for governor in New York, is within the survey's margin of error. "With six weeks until election day, voters offer good news to both Hochul and Blakeman. She now has the support of 50% of voters and saw her favorability and job approval ratings edge into positive territory. title: Antonio Brown avoids 30-year prison sentence for attempted murder by accepting 'an offer he couldn't refuse'
description: Antonio Brown's Miami-Dade plea deal drops the second-degree murder charge and Brown will be on probation after the victim said he forgave him.
content: Former NFL star Antonio Brown accepted "an offer he couldn't refuse" plea deal Wednesday from Miami-Dade County prosecutors and he will no longer face a second-degree murder charge nor the possible 30-year prison sentence it carries, according to his attorney. Brown's attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, said in a statement the plea deal offered by prosecutors will "dramatically reduce the criminal charge against him and result in probation rather than a prison sentence." Brown was facing a minimum 20-year sentence that could have topped out at 30 years, depending on sentencing, if convicted on initial charges stemming from a May 16, 2025 shooting outside a celebrity boxing event in Miami’s Little Haiti neighborhood. TIGER WOODS STRIKES PLEA DEAL IN FLORIDA ROLLOVER CRASH CASE, LOSES DRIVER'S LICENSE FOR 5 YEARS Prosecutors alleged Brown fought with Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, took a gun from a security guard and fired two shots while pursuing him. Nantambu told investigators that one bullet grazed his neck. Brown left the country. But he was arrested on charges related to the case by U.S. Marshals in Dubai in November 2025, extradited back to Florida, and eventually pleaded not guilty. He was released on $25,000 bond and forced to wear a GPS monitor. Brown pleaded not guilty to the charges. Eiglarsh maintained Brown acted in self-defense and pursued dismissal under Florida’s "stand your ground" law. ANTONIO BROWN HEADS TO THE FOOD TRUCK AFTER GETTING OUT OF JAIL The plea agreement the prosecution offered no doubt has something to do with the fact Nantambu’s attorney said this month that his client had forgiven Brown and no longer wanted to participate in the prosecution. And while prosecutors could have conceivably decided to move forward with their case, using video and other witness accounts, that obviously was not the path they chose. "He is not accepting this agreement because he suddenly agrees with the State's allegations," Eiglarsh said. "He is accepting it because the State made him an offer he couldn't refuse. title: Trump-Xi summit should make sure American strength delivers American results
description: President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington with leverage on critical minerals, semiconductors and sanctions against Russia and Iran.
content: It may not command the loudest headlines, but beneath the noise of the 24-hour news cycle, one of the most consequential foreign policy meetings of our time is taking shape as President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping prepare to meet in Washington, D.C. There is no shortage of crises competing for our world’s attention. Ukraine continues to withstand Russia’s war of aggression, conflicts persist in the Middle East, illicit fentanyl devastates our communities, and the costs of essential goods remain far too high. At first glance, these challenges may seem far removed from one another, and certainly farther from a summit in Washington. They are not. CHINA’S XI SET TO ARRIVE IN WASHINGTON FOR HIGH-STAKES TRUMP SUMMIT AS AI SUPREMACY BATTLE LOOMS LARGE Underneath each of these pressures — quietly sustaining Russia and Iran, engineering fentanyl precursors, sowing disinformation and disrupting global supply chains — is a common thread: the Chinese Communist Party and its persistent pursuit of power to reshape the global order. China is a formidable adversary, but America is not coming to the table empty-handed. Congress and the administration have taken deliberate steps to reduce the vulnerabilities Beijing has exploited for decades. Through Project Vault, launched in February, we are building a domestic critical mineral stockpile so American manufacturers are not left at the mercy of foreign supply cuts. My bipartisan DOMINANCE Act, which passed the House in June, will help make America — not China — the partner of choice for nations developing their resources. AMERICA AND CHINA ARE FIGHTING FOR THE FUTURE OF AI — CHIPS ARE THE BATTLEFIELD Last week, Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law, giving our government stronger tools to target entities bankrolling our adversaries, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s Operation Economic Fury is directly targeting the revenue streams sustaining the Iranian regime. This Congress has positioned America with leverage. Now is the time for Trump to translate that leverage into the results our nation and our world, need. Today, I am leading a bipartisan letter to the president outlining how he can do exactly that. IRAN TAPS FINANCIAL LIFELINE, RUSSIAN ARMS AS TRUMP ESCALATES 'CRUSHING' ECONOMIC WARFARE Start with our people. American citizens should never be used as bargaining chips, yet Beijing consistently and arbitrarily detains Americans on baseless charges. On June 3, Chinese authorities detained American scholar Min Zin after he was invited to attend an academic event. Dr. Youlin Chen, another American citizen, has spent more than 600 days behind bars without trial or access to his family. And while he is a British citizen, not American, Jimmy Lai remains behind bars in Hong Kong for simply running a free press. Trump knows that direct diplomacy can bring people home. When he personally raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin with Xi, the pastor was released months later. Trump must look Xi in the eye and demand the immediate release of Min Zin, Youlin Chen, Jimmy Lai and every wrongfully detained American. TRUMP SHOULD PRESS XI ON CHINA’S PERSECUTION OF BELIEVERS AT HOME AND ABROAD We must also confront Beijing’s economic coercion head-on. China has spent decades tightening its grip on the critical minerals that power modern American life, from our smartphones and our automobiles to America’s most critical defense technologies. In June, Beijing yet again demonstrated its willingness to turn global critical mineral supply chains into shackles, placing American companies like MP Materials and USA Rare Earth on its export-control blacklist. While a short-term agreement for supply stabilization from this summit would be welcome, temporary relief cannot become permanent dependence. Then there is the elephant in the room. Beijing cannot claim to seek global stability while helping sustain the regimes that create chaos around the world. Chinese purchases of Russian and Iranian energy fuel Russian President Vladimir Putin’s war machine and Tehran and its destabilizing proxies. CHINA HAS A CHOKEHOLD ON YOUR MEDICINE CABINET. IT’S A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT Trump should make it unmistakably clear that any bank or entity helping our adversaries evade U.S. sanctions will face severe economic consequences. If Beijing wants access to the benefits of the global economy, it must abide by the rules. This Congress has positioned America with leverage. Now is the time for Trump to translate that leverage into the results our nation and our world, need. Today, I am leading a bipartisan letter to the president outlining how he can do exactly that. Finally, peace and stability must hold in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan produces more than 90% of the world’s most advanced semiconductors and is the United States’ fourth-largest trading partner. For our community here in Southern California, those stakes are too high to ignore. IRAN’S DEEPEST WEAKNESS IS GETTING EXPOSED THROUGH AMERICA’S MAXIMUM PRESSURE CAMPAIGN Our region is a gateway to the Pacific Rim, and businesses throughout my district rely directly on goods and commerce flowing safely through the Indo-Pacific. A blockade or military conflict would impact global markets and raise costs for Americans already stretching every dollar. Foreign policy may be negotiated in diplomatic halls, but its consequences are felt at ports, factories, mom-and-pop shops and kitchen tables across our nation. title: GOP cracks widen over Iran war as vulnerable candidates break with Trump, demand its end
description: Vulnerable Republicans Ashley Hinson, Mike Rogers and Jon Husted break with Trump on the Iran war as gas prices reshape toss-up Senate races.
content: Vulnerable Republicans running for their political lives have, for months, kept quiet or sided with President Donald Trump on the war in Iran. But as costs rise and voters pepper them with questions on the campaign trail about when the fighting will end, some are changing their tune and breaking with Trump, arguing the war must end to lower prices — including lawmakers who previously voted to continue the conflict in the Middle East. Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, former Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., and Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, are all running in toss-up races that will define the balance of power in the Senate. TRUMP-BACKED IOWA US SENATE HOPEFUL SAYS IRAN WAR MUST 'BE BROUGHT TO A SUCCESSFUL AND IMMEDIATE END' Hinson, whose agriculture-heavy state is getting hit with high diesel costs, argued that lawmakers needed to suspend the gas tax, pause diesel exports, "unleash E-15 everywhere we can," reinstate biodiesel tax credits and create a diesel relief program. "These actions to lower costs are needed ASAP, and the war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end," Hinson said. Her race against Iowa state Rep. Josh Turek is listed as a toss-up, according to the Cook Political Report. Hinson, however, has voted against every war powers resolution offered in the House. Notably, she voted against the successful war powers resolution when seven House Republicans, including two other Republican members of the Iowa House delegation, voted for it. FOX NEWS POLL: 71% THINK TRUMP ADMINISTRATION LACKS PLAN TO END IRAN WAR Rogers has been out of Congress since 2015 but is running in one of the most-watched toss-up races this cycle against Abdul El-Sayed, and Republicans hope to flip a state that eluded them when Trump ran for his second term two years ago. Shortly after Hinson’s shift in position, he released an ad echoing an immediate end to the war. But weeks earlier, the former lawmaker, who voted in favor of the war in Iraq in 2002, told Fox News Digital at the GOP’s made-for-TV huddle in Dallas that he wanted to see the war come to an end. "Well, first of all, I'd like to see this thing come to an end. They need to find a way to get this thing ended," Rogers said. "I think that's certainly where Michigan voters, Michigan families are." 7 REPUBLICANS REBEL AGAINST TRUMP, VOTE WITH DEMS TO REIN IN IRAN WAR POWERS "Again, I think we have to understand, do we want Iran to have a nuclear weapon? I think most people overwhelmingly say no," he continued. "Would they like this to come to an end? I say absolutely yes." Husted, who is running in another toss-up contest against former Sen. Sherrod Brown in Ohio, has also pivoted. And like Hinson, he has voted against every war powers resolution that has hit the floor in the Senate. "The war needs to come to an end as quickly as possible so that we can lower gas prices," Husted told Politico. Husted, like others, has pushed several times for a "brief and successful" end to the war over the last seven months, and like several Republicans, has made the case that getting the Strait of Hormuz running and open was a paramount goal. Olivia Tripodi, a spokesperson for Husted, told Fox News Digital that the lawmaker's "position has not changed. Any accusation otherwise has not listened to Sen. Husted over the last seven months." "Since the beginning of the conflict in Iran, he has called for the military operation to be successful but brief so that gas prices can go down for Ohioans, but that enacting a War Powers Resolution would undermine the U.S. negotiating position and potentially put American troops and allies at risk," Tripodi said. "He has also supported the president’s efforts to negotiate a settlement to end the war, despite the Iranian side’s refusal to negotiate in good faith and its efforts to extend the conflict and bomb U.S. ships." Some Republican leaders are encouraging candidates to break with Trump to make their own bespoke campaigns, particularly as the war’s unpopularity continues to increase. "Well, I mean, I think, you know, if I'm running in an environment like this, you know, obviously, you're gonna develop a campaign and a message that can win in your state. And so, I encourage most candidates to run their own campaigns." "I mean, obviously, the president's gonna be a factor in every election. It’s a midterm election, he's not on the ballot," Thune said. "But, I mean, obviously, there are gonna be probably policies of his they agree with, and some that they don't. But I think they need to be their own person. And I think that's the best way to do it."

title: Kappa Kappa Gamma member says transgender membership policy undermines sorority sisterhood
description: Kappa Kappa Gamma faces renewed scrutiny as alumnae return to federal court and an active member speaks out against the transgender membership policy at Florida State University.
content: A Kappa Kappa Gamma member at Florida State University says the sorority's transgender membership policy has left her questioning her decision to join the organization, arguing that it undermines the sense of sisterhood she expected to find. "As soon as I heard about it, I was honestly ... disappointed," FSU student Alexis Richards told "The Riley Gaines Show." "This is like the one thing where I feel this shouldn't be happening," she continued. "It's like the protected sisterhood, and I never would have expected it to be infiltrated by biological men." PARENTS DROP EYE-POPPING FEES ON SORORITY RUSH COACHES TO GET KIDS INTO ELITE COLLEGE GREEK LIFE Richards said learning about the controversy surrounding the sorority's membership policy made her consider what she would do if a similar situation unfolded at her own chapter. "What if this happened to FSU? I don't want to be a part of that. I would be so uncomfortable, and I cannot imagine what those girls went through," she said. Sorority alumnae returned to federal court last week, asking judges to revive their lawsuit against the organization after they alleged its national leadership improperly allowed a chapter to admit a biological male. The legal fight stems from 2022, when transgender student Artemis Langford joined the University of Wyoming chapter of Kappa Kappa Gamma. Plaintiff Allie Coghan told Fox News Digital that she hopes the appeal will establish a clear legal precedent that protects single-sex private spaces and keeps national organizations from overriding local member consent. Richards said the issue has forced her to reconsider assumptions she had when she first joined. "It definitely makes you rethink some of, like joining a sorority," she said. EXCLUSIVE: GOP REP INTRODUCES BILL TO BAR BIOLOGICAL MEN FROM JOINING DAUGHTERS OF THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION "I never expected this to happen, so what else could happen?" The FSU student has since publicly challenged the organization over the issue, a decision she acknowledged was "a little nerve-racking." Before speaking out, Richards said she sent her father her planned message and received a warning in response: "Buckle up." "I was, like, 'I'm ready.' I feel like I need to say something because I just feel like if I didn't say anything, I would be doing like an injustice to myself, because I started speaking out more publicly about my views," she told Gaines. "I was very involved with like Charlie Kirk and Turning Point, and I think after his assassination, that like woke up something inside of me where I'm like, 'I'm not going to sit back and hope someone else does it for me. I'm just going to do it myself,' and I think taking that first step is something that I genuinely am so proud of myself for doing because it's scary." title: Sunny Hostin reveals she was holdout juror on case where man killed woman, dismembered her, boiled body parts
description: Sunny Hostin revealed she was the holdout juror in the 1991 Daniel Rakowitz dismemberment case, saying she saw clearly that he was psychotic.
content: ABC'S "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin revealed on the liberal talk show Tuesday that she was a holdout juror on a case in a New York in the 1990s in which a man killed and dismembered his roommate, shocking her co-hosts as she argued, "I saw clearly that he was psychotic." As "The View" discussed the Lindsay Clancy case, Hostin said she felt that Clancy was not criminally responsible. She said she also felt strongly about the holdout juror because she was once a holdout juror. Daniel Rakowitz was found not criminally responsible by reason of mental disease or defect in 1991 after killing his roommate, Monika Beerle, with Hostin later identifying herself as the holdout juror who initially prevented the jury from returning a guilty verdict. Because the jury found Rakowitz "not mentally responsible" for the murder, according to The New York Times, he was sent to a state hospital in New York for the criminally insane. NBC New York reported in 2010 that Rakowitz would remain at the maximum-security Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center on Wards Island after he petitioned to be moved. LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN Hostin, whose maiden name is Cummings and whose first name is Asunción, was quoted in a Feb. 23, 1991, New York Times report about the trial, which said, "Several jurors questioned afterward said one holdout juror was principally responsible for preventing them from returning a guilty verdict." "The View" co-host presented the article on the show while explaining the case. "That was me. It was because I saw clearly that he was psychotic," Hostin said Tuesday during the show. LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS "'We don't think he intended to kill her,'" said a juror, Asuncion Cummings. "'But once he did, he dismembered her body in an effort to commit the perfect crime,'" the Times report read, quoting Hostin. "He did not mean to kill her, and once he killed her he panicked. He chopped up her body parts, yes, boiled her body parts, tried to commit the perfect crime," Hostin said during the show on Tuesday, noting how much she believed in the insanity defense as her co-hosts appeared shocked. "And he fed her body parts to the unhoused." LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR MAKES NEW PROMISE AS LAWYER WARNS OF PUBLIC ATTACKS Her co-hosts appeared shocked, as Alyssa Farah Griffin asked, "You got this guy off?" Hostin added, "All that being said it was so clear to me in the jury room — we were sequestered for nine days, one juror threw a chair at me. They were so angry at me. But one by one, I picked them off. What about this, what about that? We ended up, all 12 unanimously, voting that he was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity." The Times report from 1991 said Rakowitz, whom the report described as a "former mental patient," eventually admitted to boiling Beerle's body parts. He left her skull in the baggage room at the Port Authority Bus Terminal in New York City in a bucket of kitty litter. A witness, according to the Times, testified during the trial that Rakowitz had served soup to the homeless in Tompkins Square Park that contained a finger. When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, NewsBusters managing editor Curtis Houck said, "This is beyond parody. Absolutely breathtakingly stupid that she would not only admit to this but also act like it's a badge of honor." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Hostin brought the conversation back to the Clancy case and the news that Clancy's defense team was calling for an investigation into the holdout juror. Hostin called it "despicable." "The insanity defense is a real thing and I think this lawyer, you know, who is — wants the juror investigated. That’s going to have a chilling effect on juries. Jury duty is a duty. It is one of the most important things I think I’ve ever done in my life. It was extremely difficult but to investigate a juror for doing his or her duty is despicable," she said. Hostin went viral on Monday after she said her children faced racism while attending "predominantly White" private schools. Hostin brought up the topic while discussing 1619 Project founder and The New York Times Magazine reporter Nikole Hannah-Jones, who recently admitted she regretted aspects of her decision to send her daughter to predominantly Black, high-poverty public schools in Brooklyn in an effort to challenge educational inequality. "I think that this is a decision broadly that all parents make when it comes to educating their kids, but... this is a very difficult decision for Black parents, in particular, because I made a very different decision," Hostin said. "I sent my children to private schools, a predominantly White private school. So, while they didn't suffer academically, they excelled, but it was a well-funded school, a private school, well-resourced school, they suffered a different type of pain." "There was psychological trauma, there was racism that they experienced," she added. "They were bullied. There was, you know, trauma around their identity. My daughter wears a big afro, kids were trying to stick pencils in her hair. Boys were calling her butter face, meaning she looked good, but her face, and she is a beautiful girl." While Hostin conceded that her children "did not struggle academically" as Hannah-Jones' daughter reported, she expressed concerns about the "systemic problem" affecting predominantly non-White school districts. title: China ‘throwing gasoline on the fire’ in AI data centers race, say lawmakers
description: Jason Smith and John Moolenaar allege the Chinese Communist Party is exploiting tax-exempt nonprofits while 'waging an influence campaign' against American AI
content: FIRST ON FOX: As President Donald Trump prepares to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping about the future of artificial intelligence, two top House Republicans are warning that the Chinese Communist Party is "throwing gasoline on the fire" by undermining America's effort to build out AI infrastructure. In a new letter disclosed to Fox News Digital, House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith, R-Mo., and House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank Bisignano to determine whether money has been funneled from overseas through America’s charitable system to block the data centers needed for the U.S. to compete with China. Specifically, they raised questions about hundreds of millions of dollars that American-born communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham pumped into nonprofits and organizations that are now among the leading organizations fighting data center development throughout the country. Recipients of Singham's largesse include the Party for Socialism and Liberation and the ANSWER Coalition, both self-described pro-China communist groups. Earlier this month, activists from both groups carried signs in a Chapel Hill, N.C., protest, merging anti-Trump sentiments with support for communist Cuba and opposition to data centers and AI development, including the message, "SHUT IT DOWN!" "Under no circumstances can we allow an adversary, and our most serious competitor in AI infrastructure, to weaponize our own tax code and harm an emerging American industry," the lawmakers wrote in the letter, sent on Tuesday. FROM AUSTIN TO NEW YORK, PRO-CHINA NETWORK FUELS WEEK OF ANTI-US PROTESTS AS XI MEETS TRUMP The lawmakers allege that influence operations linked to China are exploiting tax-exempt organizations, nonprofit networks and social media campaigns to fuel opposition to the data centers needed to power America’s AI industry. The lawmakers urged the agencies to investigate whether tax-exempt organizations connected to the network have operated for the "private or political benefit of foreign-aligned interests" and whether donor-advised funds and intermediary entities were used to "launder the origin of foreign-directed money into American advocacy." A Fox News Digital investigation found that Singham funneled $285 million since 2017 to six U.S. nonprofits, including his wife Jodie Evan's group, CodePink, through two shell corporations and a donor-advised philanthropy fund run by Goldman Sachs, which said it closed the Singham account in 2024. The nonprofits have functioned with tax-deductible status while actively involved in promoting communist regimes such as China, coordinating street protests and fomenting anti-American rage. They have denied being part of any foreign influence operation, and Singham hasn't responded to requests for comment. Smith said China is helping fuel opposition to American artificial intelligence infrastructure by giving a base to Singham as he funds U.S. nonprofit groups involved in anti-data-center protests. "This is the Chinese helping throw the gasoline on the fire," Smith told Fox News Digital. "The American people need to know that this is not just an organic movement." Smith said Americans have legitimate concerns about data centers, including their effect on electricity costs and water usage. But he said foreign-backed organizations shouldn't be allowed to exploit those concerns to slow U.S. technological development. Smith said that "the Chinese want to stall and slow down the advancement of AI in the United States because they want to win the AI war." "Tax exempt is a privilege. It is not a right," Smith said. "We need to make sure that we’re not subsidizing tax dollars to help create hostility and unrest in our country." Smith also called for greater transparency regarding the flow of money among organizations connected to Singham. He added that the broader issue extends beyond the tax code and could include questions about compliance with the Foreign Agents Registration Act violations. "Transparency is the biggest thing," he said. PROBE INTO 'SUBVERSIVE' ANTI-AI SINGHAM NETWORK IS 'ENORMOUS,' FORMER TREASURY ADVISOR SAYS Moolenaar said organizations presenting themselves as grassroots opposition groups are actually advancing the Chinese Communist Party’s agenda in the U.S. "Groups that portray themselves as grassroots are really more astroturf — very fake — being funded by entities that are working in partnership with the Chinese Communist Party," Moolenaar told Fox News Digital. "The concern is that they are manipulating the messaging and opposition to different American investments, whether it’s data centers or other technological advances, trying to turn the American people against these technologies so that China would be able to have dominance in this area," he said. Moolenaar pointed to the use of grassroots organizations, community groups, propaganda and online bots. "We don’t want foreign entities of concern — countries that may be opposed to American interests — using our system against the American people and trying to manipulate them," Moolenaar said. He said the lawmakers are seeking greater transparency into the organizations’ funding and tax-exempt status, including whether their political activity violates federal rules. "When you see them actively speaking out against American interests and realize that groups like CodePink are aggressively funded by this network, that raises serious concerns," Moolenaar said. The chairman said China’s influence efforts exploit the openness of American society. "The Chinese Communist Party always has the goal of dividing Americans, manipulating and getting their propaganda out," he said. "They don’t have the freedoms that we enjoy, and they try to exploit our freedoms and use that against us." China remains both a major trading partner and a strategic competitor, Moolenaar said, but the United States must avoid becoming dependent on Beijing. "They are a serious adversary," he said. "They are a trading partner, which is true, and we need to have a relationship with them," Moolenaar said. "But at the same time, we do not want to be manipulated, we do not want to become more dependent, and we certainly do not want to be under their thumb." POWER COUPLE OF CHAOS: HOW A TYCOON AND ACTIVIST BUILT A ‘REVOLUTIONARY BASE’ AT THE HOUSE OF SINGHAM The lawmakers noted that a bicameral group of congressional committees, including the Ways and Means Committee, the House Select Committee on the CCP and the Senate Intelligence Committee, has been examining how influence operations linked to the CCP allegedly exploit America’s tax-exempt sector to "sow discord and undermine our democracy." "The CCP consistently identifies political issues under public debate in our country and seeks to corrupt those debates," Smith and Moolenaar wrote in their letter. The CCP, they added, seeks to "heighten divisions between Americans and to degrade our civic processes." The lawmakers specifically pointed to opposition campaigns targeting the construction of data centers, which are critical to the nation’s AI infrastructure. A June report from OpenAI identified two clusters of ChatGPT accounts likely originating in China that were used in covert influence operations targeting U.S. debates over AI and technology policy. One campaign, dubbed "Data Center Bandwagon," generated social media comments and images claiming that data-center construction was raising electricity prices for average families. OpenAI said it found no evidence that the operation achieved meaningful breakout beyond its own activity, but said it demonstrated how foreign operators can exploit existing local concerns to amplify distrust. CHINESE BOT FARM CAUGHT RED-HANDED TRYING TO INFLUENCE HEATED AI DATA CENTER DEBATE The lawmakers also cited a report from the Bitcoin Policy Institute that identified 21 campaigns against data centers led by the Party for Socialism and Liberation across 14 states. The report said those campaigns contributed to 10 data-center moratoria, a permanent data-center ban and four rejected or scrapped projects, representing nearly $23.68 billion in proposed investment. The Party for Socialism and LIberation and the ANSWER Coalition are supported by the Singham network, and a Fox News Digital investigation has traced links between prominent activism against data centers by the Party for Socialism and Liberation, the ANSWER Coalition and other organizations in the Singham network, including BreakThrough News, the People’s Forum, Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research and CodePink. "Our tax code should not be used as a shield for foreign money waging a disinformation war on American AI infrastructure," Smith and Moolenaar wrote. "This is yet another shocking and dangerous example of how malign foreign actors are funneling dollars into the United States to further CCP interests." LAWMAKERS SAY THEY ARE STANDING AT THE GATES AGAINST 'TROJAN HORSES' PROMOTING MALIGN FOREIGN INTERESTS The lawmakers asked Treasury and the IRS to determine whether tax-exempt organizations supporting the network have violated the requirements of their status. Their request includes examining whether organizations operating under Section 501(c)(3) have acted for the "private or political benefit of foreign-aligned interests," rather than for genuine charitable purposes. They also asked whether donor-advised funds and intermediary entities were used to "launder the origin of foreign-directed money into American advocacy." The letter follows earlier oversight by the Ways and Means Committee and the House Select Committee on the CCP into the tax-exempt sector and organizations allegedly connected to Singham’s network. The lawmakers emphasized that opposition to data centers is a legitimate subject for public debate but said Americans should know whether foreign adversaries are attempting to influence those debates through nonprofit organizations, social media campaigns or covert funding channels. "The American people deserve to know which actors adversarial to the United States are trying to undermine these decision-making processes," they wrote.
