title: The DSA’s dangerous fine print. They're coming for millionaires (and you)
description: Abdul El-Sayed's tax proposals target capital gains, inheritances and trusts starting at $1 million, reaching well beyond just billionaires.
content: "Tax the billionaires." You think this is what you hear from Democratic Social Candidates, but it might be time you start reading their websites and examining their policies. While these are easy campaign slogans, there is a far more dangerous tax villain lurking in the alleyways. It’s called taxing middle America and the legacy they want to leave their kids when they don’t even know it. Some of the tax proposals being advanced by democratic socialists don't stop with Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos. They start with the average family living on Main Street America. LET SOCIALISTS ROB FROM THE RICH 100% AND YOU STILL WON’T BE ABLE TO PAY THE BILLS Policies start hitting at $1 million. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's tax platform is a fascinating example. He supports taxing capital gains above $1 million as ordinary income. He wants to eliminate stepped-up basis. This means your kids pay taxes on that appreciated Nvidia or Apple you own, your real estate that has gone up in value and even those baseball cards you’ve been storing in the attic. PROGRESSIVES WANT TO TAX BILLIONAIRES FIRST, AND YOU'RE NEXT ON THE LIST He supports taxing inheritances greater than $1 million as ordinary income. Did you realize that life insurance you own is INCLUDED in your estate? So even if you aren’t considered wealthy, those life insurance proceeds may be income tax-free, but they won’t escape estate taxes under Sayed’s policies unless you put more thought into your plan. He wants higher marginal income-tax rates above $1 million. EL-SAYED ADMITS FREE HEALTHCARE MEANS PAYING 'A LITTLE BIT MORE IN TAXES' REGARDLESS OF INCOME He supports a progressive tax on wealth held in trusts. Then there's a separate wealth tax on billionaires. Duh? Wait until you see what happens on the ballot in California when my prediction is that the billionaires tax passes. And he wants to eliminate the Social Security payroll-tax cap. That's quite a list. THE MILLION-DOLLAR TRAP Here's what Americans need to understand. Income and wealth aren't the same thing. Someone who earns $1 million every year is doing extremely well. THE CURE FOR SOCIALISM IS GIVING MORE AMERICANS A STAKE IN CAPITALISM But, someone who realizes a $1 million capital gain after building a business for 30 years is an entirely different financial situation. You are talking about the owner that’s spent a lifetime running the local convenience store, the bridal shop in your town, and even the people who own a franchise in every strip mall in America. Imagine your local plumber, electrician, or HVAC owner. They start with one truck. Thirty years later, they have 10 trucks, 20 employees and finally sell the company. That business may represent most or all of their retirement savings. Under El-Sayed's proposal, capital gains above $1 million would be taxed at ordinary-income rates rather than today's preferential long-term capital-gains rates. That's not taxing some imaginary billionaire sitting on a yacht. That's taxing the American Dream when somebody finally cashes it in. THEN TAX THE INHERITANCE Now suppose our plumber dies and leaves assets to his children. El-Sayed proposes eliminating stepped-up basis and taxing inheritances above $1 million as ordinary income. For perspective, the federal estate-tax exclusion in 2026 is $15 million per individual. That's an enormous difference in where tax policy begins touching accumulated family wealth. And $1 million isn't what it used to be. A house, retirement accounts and a small business can push a family across that line without anyone remotely resembling a billionaire. This doesn’t even include the life insurance I mentioned. THEN HIT THE PAYCHECK Social Security currently taxes employee wages at 6.2%, matched by another 6.2% from employers, up to $184,500 in 2026. El-Sayed wants to eliminate that ceiling. Take somebody earning $1 million. At today's rates, removing the cap entirely would produce roughly another $50,000 of employee Social Security tax and another $50,000 from the employer, before considering how future benefits would be treated. Call that whatever you want. It's a major tax increase on labor and a backhanded tax on corporate America. TAX THE TRUST TOO Then there's wealth held in trusts. Trusts aren't exclusively toys for billionaires. Families use trusts for estate planning, business succession, children, grandchildren and asset management. El-Sayed specifically proposes a progressive tax on wealth held by trusts. Think about the philosophy underneath all these proposals. Earn substantial money? Tax more of it. Sell the asset you built? Potentially tax more of the gain. Pass wealth to your children? Tax the inheritance and eliminate stepped-up basis. Put assets in a trust? Tax the wealth there. Earn above the Social Security ceiling? Remove the ceiling. Become a billionaire? Add another wealth tax. WHEN IS ENOUGH, ENOUGH? Supporters argue these policies would make wealthy Americans contribute more while El-Sayed's proposed federal tax exemption on the first $50,000 of income would help working households. We know half the country doesn’t pay federal tax anyway. That's an important part of his proposal. But Americans should also understand the other side of the equation. Taxes change incentives. They affect investing. Why should I take risk with no reward? They affect business sales. Why sell my business when I will lose half of what I get? They affect succession planning. Why work a lifetime to set your family up when the Government takes it away? They ultimately affect how much entrepreneurs ultimately keep after taking enormous risks. And they affect whether accumulated family wealth survives from one generation to the next. The Democratic Socialists of America's national program explicitly calls for "aggressive wealth taxes" on wealthy individuals and corporations. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION El-Sayed's proposals are just one example that shows what that philosophy can look like when somebody starts putting actual policies on paper. Problem is most people will hear the headlines and won’t read the fine print. And that's why the most important number in his tax plan is NOT $1 billion. IT IS $1 million. Because once the conversation moves from taxing billionaires to taxing million-dollar gains, million-dollar inheritances, high incomes, we're no longer talking exclusively about America's 800 or so billionaires. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP We're talking about the fundamental question of crushing the American Dream of capitalism, where we’ve always been encouraged to build, keep and pass to the next generation. title: China’s Xi set to arrive in Washington for high-stakes Trump summit as AI supremacy battle looms large
description: China's President Xi Jinping arrives for a tense White House summit with Trump covering AI, tariffs, rare earth minerals and fentanyl exports.
content: China's President Xi Jinping is set to arrive on U.S. soil later Wednesday for what is expected to be a tense showdown between President Donald Trump and the communist leader. A red carpet rollout is planned for when Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, arrive at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening, replete with an arrival ceremony for the man who has found himself at odds with Trump on issues ranging from artificial intelligence and intellectual property theft, trade practices, rare-earth minerals to the communist country's support for Iran during America's military conflict there. Xi hasn't visited the nation's capital in more than a decade. AI will be a major topic of discussion during the two-day summit, which officially begins Thursday morning and ends Friday evening, according to a senior administration official. Thursday will begin with a prestigious State Arrival Ceremony, including 479 military personnel from all branches on the South Lawn, State Floor and Rose Garden of the White House. XI PREPARES CHINA ‘FOR BATTLE’ AS EXPERT WARNS OF GRAVE DANGER FACING US AHEAD OF DC SUMMIT According to the official, a wide-ranging deal on possible tariff reductions on non-strategic goods is an expected topic of discussion, who also said the nation's leaders will discuss rare-earth exports and possible export controls. Trump is also expected to press China to do more to curb fentanyl precursor chemical exports. Trump is also likely to press for the release of an American who has been wrongfully detained in China, Gulshan Abbas, who has languished in a Chinese prison for eight years. The country accused her of "participating in a terrorist organization" after her sister spoke out about China's genocide of Uyghurs, according to Forbes. House Speaker Mike Johnson and other Republicans have expressed confidence that Trump will push for her release. EXCLUSIVE: FENTANYL DEATHS PLUNGE 22% AS TRUMP WHITE HOUSE TOUTS CRACKDOWN ON DEADLY DRUG CRISIS First lady Melania Trump is expected to accompany Peng to the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art, "to explore works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and Sino-American cultural exchange." The day will end with an elaborate state dinner with high-profile guests, including many from the tech world. Those guests will include Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, SpaceX founder and former Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) head Elon Musk, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser and Apple Board of Directors Chairman Tim Cook. Trump boasted about American AI supremacy over China during an address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York Tuesday, using his newly-minted term for the technology, "superintelligence." TRUMP'S AI RACE WITH CHINA COULD BECOME THE BIGGEST MISTAKE OF OUR TIME "Every major new technology brings challenges, and superintelligence is no exception," said Trump. "Whoever wins superintelligence wins. That's the group that wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else. And we're going to keep it that way." Trump traveled to Beijing in May where he met with Xi, and the two sides agreed to a "constructive" trade truce, pausing a tit-for-tat tariff battle, but only for non-strategic goods. That deal has tentatively held, but during that visit, China also agreed to purchase billions more in American agricultural products like soybeans, and 200 Boeing aircraft. title: Bringing this popular drink to a job interview could hurt your chances, experts warn
description: An etiquette expert warns that bringing iced coffee or other beverages to a job interview signals casualness and says the professionalism rule applies to all ages.
content: A cup of coffee might be a daily ritual for most Americans, but some career and etiquette experts say bringing one into a job interview could hurt your chances of getting hired. A viral debate has erupted over whether an iced coffee sends the wrong message to hiring managers or if it's simply part of a busy day. Caitlin Wehniainen, a Florida-based corporate recruiter with 16 years of experience recruiting for Fortune 500 companies, sparked the conversation with a video in which she called out Gen Z job candidates for going to interviews with a coffee in hand. CAN YOU BRING A BIRTHDAY CAKE TO A RESTAURANT? VIRAL PIZZERIA DISPUTE REVEALS THE RULES "When you show up with an iced coffee or an iced latte, it is perceived — from my opinion and a hiring standpoint — that this interview is just a stop on your list of errands for the day," she said in a recent TikTok video that has amassed more than 17,000 likes and 5,000 comments. "It looks like you went to Target, went to Starbucks, and now you're stopping by your interview before moving on to the next thing." It looks "a little too casual," Wehniainen added. "Save that for well before the interview or after the interview. Go and get one. But don’t like waltz into your interview all casual with an iced coffee. It just looks like you didn’t have time to finish your coffee beforehand." Social media users flooded the comment section, with many agreeing that it is "diabolical" to bring a wet cup dripping with condensation and rattling with ice into the room. WHY RESTAURANT SERVERS CLEAR YOUR PLATE BEFORE EVERYONE FINISHES EATING "That generation has lost the art of professionalism," one TikToker commented. The viral coffee debate joins a growing list of workplace faux pas involving Gen Z, including bringing parents to sit in on interviews, as Fox News Digital previously reported. But others stood up for candidates getting their caffeine fix during an interview. GEN Z TURNS ON CLASSIC SNACKS, FORCING MAJOR GROCERY SHAKE-UP: 'THEY DON'T TRUST THEM' "An interview IS just a stop in my day," one woman said on TikTok. "It's not my whole day." "Are you expecting my whole day to revolve around a 30 min meeting," someone else said. "If showing up with a beverage like a coffee is an issue … that's not a company that I want to work for." A man who said he was also a recruiter offered another point of view: "If you can show up early or on time with the iced coffee you're already showing good time management." COMMUNAL DINING MAKES GEN Z COMEBACK, BUT OLDER GUESTS PUSH BACK ON 'CHAOTIC' TREND Others pointed to the already challenging job market. "If showing up with a beverage like a coffee is an issue … that's not a company that I want to work for," someone commented on TikTok. Others said it's more nuanced. One TikToker noted that, since Wehniainen recruits for Fortune 500 companies, interviews and candidates tend to be more "buttoned up," but that won't be the case everywhere. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Diane Gottsman, a national etiquette expert and the owner of the Protocol School of Texas, said it's therefore best to "err on the side of caution." "Perception is everything," Gottsman told Fox News Digital. "What one person may think is fine, another person may not." "I think bringing in that cup of iced coffee signals both a distraction, a level of comfort and casualness that may not be there," she said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "We're not pointing the finger only at a certain generation," Gottsman added, noting that workers of all ages make similar etiquette mistakes. Beyond coffee, Gottsman said candidates should avoid other distractions or unprofessional impressions by putting away their phones, skipping overpowering fragrances, removing sunglasses from the tops of their heads and avoiding chewing gum. As distracting as an iced latte can be during an in-person job interview, there's another item that can irk hiring managers: the cellphone. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "One job candidate not only placed her cellphone face up on the conference room table during our interview, she also repeatedly leaned over to read incoming texts and even began texting as well while I was speaking to her," said one New York-based manager. The interview ended early. The candidate was not hired. "After your job interview, why not treat yourself to your favorite iced coffee drink as a treat for a job well done?" If an interviewer offers coffee or water, Gottsman said, it's perfectly acceptable to accept — but don't ask for more than what was offered. And if candidates need a drink of water from a bottle tucked away in a bag, she recommends politely asking before taking a sip. Gottsman also noted that interviews are a two-way street. While employers are evaluating candidates, applicants should also be deciding whether a company's culture and expectations are the right fit for them. She and Wehniainen agree that there is a time and place for everything. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "After your job interview, why not treat yourself to your favorite iced coffee drink as a treat for a job well done?" Gottsman added.

title: Caleb Williams' initial response to criticism about how he handled hamstring injury proves the criticism right
description: Caleb Williams used someone else to fire back at Dave Portnoy on X after the Chicago quarterback's hamstring injury reaction sparked a firestorm.
content: Caleb Williams is under scrutiny and even the target of some withering criticism for his reaction to the hamstring injury he suffered in Sunday's game for the Chicago Bears. And Williams is fighting back! Sort of. JAXSON DART WALKS OFF FIELD AFTER INJURY, CREATING AN INSTANT CONTRAST TO CALEB WILLIAMS' EMOTIONAL EXIT He's responding in a very Williams way that, sorry to say, kind of amplifies the point some folks are making about him. So what's the criticism? Well, after he suffered what is considered a Grade 1 hamstring strain that has him officially week-to-week, according to coach Ben Johnson, Williams seemed to perhaps overreact in the moment. He collapsed when the hamstring pulled and then could be heard screaming in agony on the field. People thought the issue was a major, major injury based on the quarterback's reaction. It is reportedly a moderate injury at its worst. People are also criticizing the way Williams left the field – on a cart, which is understandable, but giving a thumbs up sign to the crowd as if he was Kobe Bryant leaving the court when his Achilles snapped or Donald Trump leaving that stage in Butler, PA., after he was shot. It was a hamstring injury. CRAIG CARTON ROASTS BEARS' CALEB WILLIAMS FOR EMOTIONAL REACTION TO HAMSTRING INJURY AGAINST VIKINGS And social media being the cesspool of reaction it is, Williams is getting roasted for being weak or soft or whatever. Dave Portnoy, of Barstool Sports is among those ripping Williams, calling him a "thespian" who acted like "both ACLs, MCLs and everything else," was injured although he only "tweaked his hammy." Well, Williams disagrees and went after Portnoy on X. But only a a round-about way. Williams reposted someone else criticizing Portnoy. An account that goes by DAEMAR and has 1,700 followers laughed at Portnoy, claiming he had police arrest a college kid for throwing pennies at him and yet Portnoy is calling Williams soft. In fact, police independently arrested a college student who shouted an antisemitic remark and threw coins at Portnoy during a pizza review. Williams reposted DAEMAR and it currently has 31,000 likes and 1.1 million views. But that's not the point. The point is Williams let DAEMAR fight his battle and joined in. He did not confront Portnoy's online charges himself. And maybe that's the smart way to do it. Why amplify the criticism? Although Williams' repost amplifies the criticism as well as the response. But, that's how he rolls, apparently. And he also did it in reposting Kei. She took to X to fight the battle against people portraying Williams as not masculine enough. "The constant need to emasculate the dude is so strange," Kei's post reads. "Starting to think the people who do it are actually attracted to him and won’t be honest with themselves." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Remember, this was something Williams obviously read and shared. It suggests he agrees with this. And maybe he is simply over the criticism that because he paints his nails and doesn't act a certain way after he's injured, that he isn't masculine. But he did not go directly at the issue. He instead echoed someone else defending him instead of defending himself. And there's nothing really wrong with this approach. But, in a weird sort of way, that approach advances the point critics have about Williams. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

His remarks should therefore not be misinterpreted." In response to the comments, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee reposted Israel's Minister of Diaspora and Combating Antisemitism. "Amid the turmoil engulfing the region, we must not lose sight of the devastating situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory," he said, as the world approaches three years since the Hamas terror attacks that sparked the Israeli military response he spent much of his speech criticizing. WORLD LEADERS DESCEND ON NEW YORK FOR UNGA — BUT WHO REALLY HAS AMERICA’S EAR? title: Karoline Leavitt says some White House reporters privately apologized for asking 'unfair' questions
description: Karoline Leavitt says White House reporters privately apologized for asking questions their bosses demanded, calling them "unfair" during briefings.
content: Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said that some reporters covering the White House privately apologized to her for asking questions they acknowledged were "unfair." Leavitt made the comments on the latest episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" while discussing the "performative" nature of press briefings. "There's been times reporters have even said to me, ‘I'm sorry I had to ask that today. My bosses really wanted me to ask that, they know it's an unfair question,’" she said, without naming names. TRUMP ANNOUNCES WHITE HOUSE BAN AGAINST THREE MEDIA OUTLETS Leavitt, who frequently sparred with reporters during her tenure as press secretary, argued that journalists at major news organizations are often beholden to the demands of their superiors. "The reporters are controlled by their bosses… They're not in control of their own livelihood," she told host Sean Hannity. "They are dictated by the editors and the execs at some of these companies." DAVID MARCUS: KAROLINE LEAVITT’S LASTING LEGACY IS OPENING THE WHITE HOUSE TO INDIE PRESS Leavitt said both the media and administration officials behind the podium contribute to political theatrics in the briefing room. "There's a performative aspect to the briefing room," she conceded. "In fairness, I think on both sides, right? But definitely with the press. And they have to do that because their bosses are demanding it." Despite frequently clashing with reporters, including CNN’s Kaitlan Collins, and sometimes referring to other members of the press as "left-wing hacks," Leavitt said she has no ill will toward journalists. "I don't hate anyone," she insisted. "There are some I enjoy less than others. I'll say that… There's some that I just don't take seriously because they are just left-wing hacks, as I would call them in the briefing room." SCOTT PELLEY SAYS CBS NEWS IS ‘ON FIRE’ AFTER BARI WEISS TAKEOVER AND ‘60 MINUTES’ BLOODBATH Leavitt credited "a few" solid reporters but refrained from naming them, concerned that if she did, she would "kill their career." title: Texas lawmaker warns accused wife-killer's Italy escape could open 'Pandora's box' for future suspects
description: Lee Gilley fled Texas for Italy after being charged with capital murder, and a lawmaker warns the extradition fight could set a dangerous precedent.
content: One Texas lawmaker is warning that an accused wife-killer's escape to Italy, which forced prosecutors to remove the death penalty as a possible sentence, could open a "Pandora's box" for future criminals. Lee Gilley, 39, has been charged with capital murder in the October 2024 death of his wife, Christa, who was nine weeks pregnant at the time of her death. The Harris County Medical Examiner's office ruled her death a homicide caused by neck compression. Gilley has entered a not guilty plea. According to authorities, Gilley cut off his ankle monitor on May 1 and fled Texas before his trial was set to begin. Court records indicate he traveled to Milan Malpensa Airport in Italy under a false identity and with forged travel documents. Italian authorities subsequently took him into custody. TEXAS MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PREGNANT WIFE ALLEGEDLY CUTS OFF ANKLE MONITOR AND FLEES TO ITALY Dick DeGuerin, Gilley's U.S. attorney, previously told Fox News Digital that Italian judges required a written guarantee that prosecutors would not pursue the death penalty before they would consider returning him. He said Italian authorities may also seek assurances that Gilley would not face a sentence of life without parole. "Most civilized countries in the free world have abolished the death penalty," he told Fox News Digital on Tuesday. "The U.S. and Texas should do the same, in my opinion, after spending 61 years of my adult life in the criminal justice system." The Harris County District Attorney's Office announced in direct response to the Italian judges that it won't be pursuing the death penalty against Gilley, but stopped short of pledging not to pursue life without parole, noting that he could be eligible for commutation. WATCH: Christa Gilley's friend speaks out after prosecutors rule out death penalty TEXAS MAN ACCUSED IN PREGNANT WIFE'S MURDER FIGHTS TO REMAIN IN ITALY, CITING 'LIFESTYLE AND CULTURE' Texas State Representative Brian Harrison told Fox News Digital he's very concerned about the prospect of a European country controlling how criminals are sentenced in his state. "You're almost opening Pandora's box in sort of a roundabout way, allowing ... some of those European socialist soft on crime liberal politicians to be able to wield influence over what happens in Texas courts," Harrison said. "I do not want foreign governments, foreign officials, foreign courts having anything to do with how we enforce criminal laws here in the state of Texas." "What's to stop them from moving the goalposts even further?" FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X He also said this could create a horrible precedent for future suspects who may want to find creative ways to reduce their potential sentence. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? title: Trump embraced a socialist he’s told voters to fear. Republicans aren’t thrilled
description: Trump praised Zohran Mamdani weeks after calling Democrats "communists," leaving GOP strategists frustrated ahead of the critical midterm election.
content: Six weeks before the midterms, President Donald Trump is complicating one of Republicans' central campaign arguments against Democrats — warmly praising New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani after repeatedly warning voters about the rise of socialism and communism on the left. "I want him to be a great mayor, and he’s certainly got potential, got great potential," Trump told reporters as he patted Mamdani on the back after the two leaders met Monday at New York City's Gracie Mansion. The meeting, where the two leaders discussed cost of living and housing issues, isn't sitting well with some Republicans fighting to keep control of the House and Senate in the midterms. "All of it is self-inflicted, off-message, not helpful," a GOP strategist who asked to remain anonymous to speak freely told Fox News Digital. "None of these candidates out in these states, where these races are tighter and more competitive than they should be, are helped by any of this." MAMDANI TELLS TRUMP BANNED NEWS OUTLETS ARE WELCOME AT NYC MEETING Another Republican consultant, who also asked for anonymity, argued, "This is a president who is in a fully self-indulgent period. It doesn't seem like he really cares about winning. It's all off-key." Less than two weeks ago, Trump told Republicans gathered in Dallas at the GOP's first-ever midterm convention that there is a "communist" takeover of the Democratic Party. "In state after state, the Democrat establishment has been overthrown and replaced by crazed lunatics and radicals. They call themselves Democrat socialists, but actually, they’re communists," the president said. THE GOP'S 'SOCIALIST' MIDTERM PLAYBOOK Fast-forward to Monday, and Trump held his third meeting with Mamdani since he won election last year as the first socialist and first Muslim mayor of the nation's most populous city. A third GOP strategist, who was also granted anonymity, argued, "It seems he keeps on stepping on the message, making the election about how crazy the left is and communists and socialists and then appearing with them and yukking it up." A top Trump supporter quickly took to social media to blast the encounter. "I am a die hard Trump supporter and today I am feeling demoralized because Mamdani is a full blown communist jihadist. He is the spiritual leader of the communists in America and he met with the President today in NYC less than 45 days before the midterms," right-wing activist and MAGA champion Laura Loomer argued on social media. Loomer, an internet personality who has carved out an influential unofficial role as a Trump confidant, emphasized, "How is this supposed to make Trump’s most loyal supporters feel? We don’t feel very happy today. We were told to FIGHT communism. But when we fight communism, we see the communist get rewarded... The base is very angry today." DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB Alex Bruesewitz, a longtime Trump aide who now serves as a leading outside adviser to the president, shot back on X, writing, "I don’t understand the "Republicans" who are upset about the President having a friendly relationship with the Mayor of New York @ZohranKMamdani. It’s not wrong to have friendly relationships with people you disagree with. In fact, it’s healthy and good for you!" Republicans are fighting against traditional political headwinds facing the party in power and a rough political climate fueled by persistent inflation, surging gas and diesel prices, what polls show is a very unpopular war with Iran, and Trump's underwater approval ratings. To flip the script, a key part of the GOP playbook aims to turn what's normally a referendum on the party in power into a choice election by painting all Democrats on the ballot as far-left radicals. While some Republican strategists say Trump is stepping on the message, others are not concerned. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "I don't think it's that big a deal," veteran GOP consultant Dave Carney told Fox News Digital. Carney said that Trump's meeting with Mamdani "goes with his role" as president, "and it's not a political role. The federal government and the president and the city have to work together." But Carney, pointing to left-wing Democrats on the midterm ballot, said: "These other candidates out there who advocate these really radical crazy positions aren't elected yet." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Longtime Republican strategist and communicator Ryan Williams, referring to Trump, said the meeting "has the ability to make some on the right angry when he praises, Mamdani, but I don't think it has really has any political implications." "Trump appreciates talent and whatever you think of Mayor Mamdani, the guy is politically talented," Williams added. "I think the president appreciates that." Fox News reached out to the White House for comment, but didn't receive a response at the time this report was published.

title: Welder turned lawmaker sees a ‘nuclear bomb for work’ — and a chance to help blue collar Americans
description: Rep. Riley Moore, a former welder, warns AI could be the "nuclear bomb" for blue-collar jobs or a force-multiplier for manufacturing workers.
content: Before AI threatened to reshape the kind of blue-collar work he once did, Rep. Riley Moore was a welder on an Appalachian mining operation. Now, as the technology races into the workplace, Moore argues it could make workers like him safer and more productive rather than replace them. The West Virginia Republican has taken that message to the Teamsters and other labor stakeholders as Congress and businesses grapple with how quickly AI should reshape the workplace and how much of a role government should play amid economic and national security concerns. "I started my career off as a welder and I come from a blue-collar background, not just myself, my mother's family [were] all welders, actually. AI represents a massive potential for positive advancements in manufacturing. But it also represents potentially the nuclear bomb for work as we know it in the world," Moore said in an exclusive interview Monday with Fox News Digital. Representing a state still closely tied to mining and manufacturing, Moore has taken his message to the Teamsters and other labor stakeholders, arguing that AI should become a "force-multiplier" for workers rather than simply replace them. WATCH: AMERICANS WARN AI WILL TAKE JOBS DESPITE REASSURING LABOR DATA: ‘JUST WAIT’ Moore said he leans toward finding the "positives" in AI development and that, if the technology can complement blue-collar labor rather than replace it, it could be a game-changer for the U.S. economy and its workers. "I think AI certainly has the ability to extend the longevity of a worker in a particular trade. It can also make those jobs safer. It can extend the time period in which somebody can work without injury. And it can also create better efficiencies, which then can also better paying jobs here in this country." I FEARED AI WOULD LEAVE MY COMMUNITY BEHIND. NOW I SEE A PATH TO PROSPERITY "Or, it’s the nuclear weapon [against] work, it could potentially eliminate jobs as we know it and get rid of what is really critical, I think, to being a human being: which is human purpose, which work is certainly part of that and the dignity of work and contributing to civil society." Moore’s district includes major commercial arteries like Interstates 79 and 81 and the new Trans-Allegheny U.S. 48, which the lawmaker helped open this year. The trucking industry, historically unionized, could benefit from AI, he said, while warning that self-driving rigs could endanger the trade. "I'm against automated trucking, but I am in favor of having AI as part of trucking to make the road safer and keep that driver safer and make them more productive," he said, considering AI could act as a "co-pilot" to protect against drowsy driving or other dangers that come from being inherently human. The trucker would remain employed, and crash-prone 81 could become less so: "That creates the types of efficiencies that we're looking for, certainly, but then also respects the dignity of the human being and the worker who is involved in it." Religious leaders have expressed similar concerns about AI’s effect on the dignity of work. Pope Leo XIV’s May encyclical considered two biblical models for the AI era: "constructing the Tower of Babel" or following Nehemiah in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem. "We certainly want to be Nehemiah," he said. Moore has also spoken with and met with the Teamsters as unions grapple with AI’s potential effect on their workers. A Teamsters spokesperson declined additional comment but praised Moore’s appearance at the event. Using AI to improve workflow efficiencies could raise wages, while U.S. leadership in AI could help counter China’s growing dominance in the AI "arms race." FETTERMAN ALIGNS WITH TRUMP ON AI PUSH, WARNS CHINA BENEFITS FROM US 'OVERREACTION' Data centers powering the technology have also become a point of controversy in Moore’s district and around the country. In the Eastern Panhandle, within 100 miles of Washington, D.C., and in the high-elevation forests of Tucker County farther west, residents and local leaders continue to debate the arrival of data centers that have already begun proliferating farther east. HOMEOWNERS IN THE HEART OF AMERICA’S AI BOOM ARE GETTING AN UNEXPECTED PAYOFF Moore said the three important questions are whether data centers will produce their own energy or rely on the local grid, whether they will siphon off public water or use "closed-circuit" cooling, and whether the community wants them there. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Fierce debate continues over whether tax revenue from the centers can be balanced with community concerns. title: Zelenskyy to seek offramp for yearslong Russia war in UN speech after Trump reveals peace deal is close
description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy addresses the United Nations General Assembly with security proposals as Trump presses for a faster Russia Ukraine war deal.
content: NEW YORK — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is set to address the United Nations General Assembly Wednesday as President Donald Trump presses for an end to Russia’s war and Kyiv seeks to shape the emerging diplomatic push after more than four-and-a-half years of conflict. Zelenskyy’s speech comes the day after he met with Trump in New York, where the two discussed finally putting an end to the war. Trump said that he believes a deal can be reached, though he did not disclose what that agreement would involve. "We’re working very closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, and we will get that one done," Trump said, adding that an agreement would happen "more quickly than people understand." KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE The Ukrainian president has said he is bringing "concrete security proposals and de-escalation measures" to New York for the annual United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) gathering. His government is also seeking additional air defenses, support for Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and help protecting food exports through the Black Sea. The meeting with Trump came as Russia and Ukraine appeared to be weighing a possible pause in attacks on energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy has said Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy sector, critical infrastructure and food exports should stop, followed by matching de-escalation steps from Kyiv. UKRAINE SEEKS MORE US PATRIOT INTERCEPTORS AS BOMB SHELTER PROBE DEEPENS Trump has also urged Ukraine to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries. Ahead of his meeting with Zelenskyy, he called the campaign "a serious hit against the Russians," but added, "It’s also a serious hit on the price of diesel." In his U.N. address on Tuesday, Trump said he could use new tariff authority against buyers of Russian energy "if necessary" to bring the war to an end. "This ridiculous and never-ending war with Ukraine must be ended. The whole world suffers as 25,000 people, mostly soldiers, are being killed each month. What a shame!" Trump said. The competing priorities are likely to shape the diplomatic conversation around Zelenskyy’s Wednesday appearance before UNGA — Trump is pressing for a faster path to negotiations, while Ukraine is seeking the military support and security commitments it says are necessary for any agreement to hold. The timing is especially consequential as winter approaches. U.N. investigators have warned that renewed Russian attacks on Ukraine’s power grid could leave millions without electricity or heat. Kyiv is seeking more Patriot air defense systems, energy assistance and support for efforts to produce U.S.-designed interceptors inside Ukraine. title: Supreme Court can restore sanity and stop the left’s radical climate agenda
description: The Supreme Court's Suncor v. Boulder case could determine whether cities or Congress control carbon emissions regulation and U.S. energy policy.
content: When the U.S. Supreme Court opens its new term on Oct. 5, the justices will face the critical question of whether Congress or Boulder, Colorado, controls American energy policy. Cities such as Boulder, Honolulu and Baltimore have pursued frivolous lawsuits against energy companies on the claim that big oil concealed the effects of their products on climate change. While states generally set policy over public health and safety, constitutional law and Supreme Court precedent should make the answer clear. Energy forms a central part of the national economy and makes a foundational contribution to American national security. The Constitution vests authority over interstate commerce and national security in the federal government, not the states. But until the court resolves this matter once and for all in Suncor v. Boulder, dozens of states and municipalities, backed by climate activists, will keep pushing legal theories in state court intended to impose ruinous liability on energy companies for lawful carbon emissions. Without the court’s intervention, climate litigants would sue American energy into financial oblivion, inflict enormous costs on the American economy and render the nation more vulnerable to coercion by nations such as Russia and Iran. THESE 11 UPCOMING SUPREME COURT DECISIONS COULD MAKE OR BREAK TRUMP'S SECOND TERM AGENDA The decisions about how to regulate carbon emissions and respond to global climate belong to the federal government, not the states or localities. Greenhouse gases do not remain within state or even national borders. Once emitted, they enter the global atmosphere. Emissions from a gas station in Boulder are functionally indistinguishable from emissions from a coal plant in another state or a factory overseas. A problem that transcends state and national borders requires a uniform national solution that includes foreign policy implications and the costs and benefits of energy for the country as a whole. Courts have long recognized interstate pollution disputes as a federal domain. Before Congress legislated on the subject, the Supreme Court held that interstate water and air pollution were governed by federal common law to be created by the courts directly. It found that states have conflicting interests and that the underlying activity is national in scope. Therefore, the court concluded, there is an overriding national need for one uniform rule of decision, not 50 competing ones. NEW YORK WANTS TO GOVERN IOWA AND MISSOURI — WE'RE SUING TO STOP IT COLD Consider the implications of Boulder’s lawsuit. Close to 90% of global carbon emissions originate from outside the United States. The lion’s share comes from China, which accounts for close to a third of worldwide emissions alone. A Colorado state court judgment holding U.S. energy producers responsible for the world’s emissions is ultimately a tax on American energy that our international competitors do not have to pay. Good luck persuading Beijing to pay for the harms inflicted by its pollution on the rest of the world. Energy is ultimately an instrument of power. U.S. foreign policy and national security demand a unified federal approach. Energy and climate policy are inseparable from foreign affairs. The United States has negotiated over carbon emissions for decades through climate agreements and diplomacy with allies and adversaries alike. State court rulings penalizing global emissions necessarily affect the bargaining positions and policy choices available to the federal government, whether or not any existing treaty speaks to the point directly. Reliable energy supplies are essential to military readiness and economic resilience. State courts have no authority to enter judgments on global conduct that could undercut the nation’s military posture or impair the federal government’s diplomacy. TRUMP-APPROVED ENERGY PROJECTS AT RISK OF SUDDEN DEATH BY NEXT HOSTILE PRESIDENT These groundless lawsuits not only interfere with national security and foreign policy, they also interfere with the federal government’s ability to effectively regulate a national industry. The energy defendants in Boulder operate lawfully, a truth the climate plaintiffs do not dispute, and already comply with federal statutes regulating carbon emissions. In the Clean Air Act, Congress created a comprehensive regulatory structure that left states a narrow, defined role. It assigned the job of regulating global emissions to the Environmental Protection Agency, not to state court judges and juries. The constitutional structure and design demand limits on Boulder’s authority. The Framers entrusted national institutions with interests that should not be subject to a patchwork of state laws. Foreign policy, national defense, the economy and interstate pollution remain subjects that must rest in the hands of the federal government. American energy productivity and our national security depend on each other. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Allowing Boulder’s climate suit to move forward would not only undermine the authority of Congress, but it would hand a single Colorado county control over matters that bear directly on American national security. Foreign policy decisions must not fall subject to the whims of state court juries or the climate activists who bring cases to them. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Supreme Court should hold that these questions belong to the federal government, and it should say so in no uncertain terms. Boulder’s bid to set American energy policy through climate litigation should end with Suncor. If not, activist jurisdictions will continue this lawfare campaign until American energy is bankrupt, our economy is irreparably damaged and our national security is directly undermined. title: What the golf cart industry can teach us about China’s threat to American jobs
description: Club Car and E-Z-GO face a major surge in Chinese golf cart imports backed by subsidies as Trump prepares to meet Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C.
content: This week, two very different events will put the U.S.-China relationship in the spotlight. President Donald Trump is preparing to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C. as the two countries continue negotiations over trade and other economic issues. At the same time, the world’s best golfers are gathering outside Chicago, IL for the Presidents Cup, where American and international players will compete at Medinah Country Club. There is a connection between those events that deserves more attention: American manufacturing. CHINA COZIES UP AS TRUMP TOUTS DELEGATION OF RICHEST BUSINESS HEAVYWEIGHTS AT XI SUMMIT The golfers at Medinah — and potentially President Trump himself, who has accepted the role of honorary chairman and plans to attend — will be utilizing golf carts built by Club Car at their manufacturing headquarters in Augusta, Georgia. It is a fitting reminder of the longstanding relationship between the great game of golf and the American manufacturers that support it. But it is becoming increasingly difficult for American companies to build and compete when foreign governments distort the market. And what is happening in the golf-cart industry is part of a much larger story playing out across the country. American manufacturers employ millions of people, support communities and contend every day in a global marketplace. They should be able to outcompete based on the quality, innovation and value of what they produce — not against foreign governments willing to subsidize competitors and distort prices. That is precisely what is happening in the low-speed personal transportation vehicle industry (LSPTV), or what most Americans simply know as golf carts. WHITE HOUSE EXPOSES ‘TRANSSHIPMENT SCAM’ COSTING US UP TO $26B, POINTS FINGER AT CHINA In 2023, more than $522 million worth of these vehicles were imported into the United States from China — more than double the amount imported in 2021. American manufacturers raised concerns that Chinese producers were benefiting from government subsidies and selling products in the United States at unfairly low prices. The Department of Commerce investigated and found evidence supporting those concerns, determining that Chinese producers had benefited from countervailable subsidies and that Chinese LSPTVs were being sold in the United States at less than fair value. WANT TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA'S ECONOMY? THE KEY INVESTMENT IS HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT Those findings are not merely numbers in a federal register. They have consequences on American factory floors. The domestic industry has experienced reduced shifts, reductions in workforce, declining production and declining profitability. That means fewer opportunities for American workers and less investment in the communities that depend on manufacturing. CORPORATE AMERICA'S CHINA ADDICTION HAS BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT I have seen the importance of this industry firsthand through my work representing Georgia’s 12th Congressional District, home to Club Car and E-Z-GO. But this issue extends far beyond Georgia. The same basic question applies to manufacturers across America: Can we compete based on the quality of what we build, or will government-backed foreign competitors be allowed to tilt the scales in their favor? On a level playing field, American companies like Club Car and E-Z-GO can out-innovate and out-compete anyone in the world. That is why Congress and the administration must enforce our trade laws. The United States has already taken action. Commerce established antidumping and countervailing-duty remedies against unfairly traded Chinese LSPTV imports, addressing a problem that American manufacturers had been documenting for years. But trade enforcement only works if it is actually enforced. Chinese producers have found ways around American trade remedies, including by changing supply chains, relabeling products or routing goods through third countries. I have joined colleagues in pressing the Commerce Department to investigate potential circumvention and ensure that trade remedies protect the American workers they were designed to protect. This is not about preventing legitimate competition. It is about ensuring competition is legitimate in the first place. That distinction matters as President Trump prepares to sit down with President Xi. The United States can engage China diplomatically while being clear about what we expect economically. American businesses should have access to foreign markets, and foreign businesses should have access to ours — but the rules must be applied fairly. A product should not gain an artificial advantage because a foreign government is willing to subsidize its production and then flood another country’s market. We have learned this lesson in steel, solar panels, automobiles and other industries. Once domestic manufacturing capacity disappears, rebuilding it is extraordinarily difficult. The Presidents Cup offers a useful reminder of what American manufacturing can accomplish. As the tournament brings together the best golfers from the United States and around the world, American golf-car technology developed in places like Augusta will help support one of golf’s biggest international stages. That is what fair competition should look like: American workers building products that can compete anywhere in the world. As President Xi visits Washington, that principle should be part of the conversation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And as the Presidents Cup showcases the best golfers in the world, it is worth remembering the American workers and manufacturers supporting the tournament behind the scenes.

title: Massachusetts lesbian bar ignites fury after easing mask rules for one night a week
description: Last Ditch Bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts, faces a boycott and accusations of ableism after lifting its mask mandate on Saturdays to stay afloat.
content: A lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts, sparked community backlash after lifting its mask mandate for one night a week, with accusations of ableism and boycott directed at the struggling business. Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue recently removed its mask requirement on Saturdays in an effort to boost business, but some members of the small city's queer community objected to the change, according to The Boston Globe. Some critics accused the bar's owners of putting disabled people at risk and compared the policy change to a "mass disabling event" and a "eugenicist" attack while also wishing violence against the establishment, according to The Boston Globe. "I hope your venue gets firebombed for robbing my fellow immunocompromised people of their Saturday plans just to scrape extra revenue from ablists [sic]," one commenter wrote on the bar's social media post announcing the change. IDAHO COFFEE SHOP OWNER DEFENDS EJECTING PRO-LIFE GROUP FROM HIS BUSINESS AFTER BACKLASH "People like you kill disabled people in the name of your own leisure and convenience," wrote another. "Just say you’re being complicit in a mass disabling event and get it over with," a third said. "When y'all close, let the record state it was ableism + complying in advance, because that's what it is," another wrote. "Does COVlD not disable people on Saturday nights?" added another user, who had a picture of himself in a mask as his profile picture. This comes years after the COVID-19 pandemic was declared over by the federal government in 2023. State and local governments, as well as most businesses across the country, had also lifted masking requirements several years ago. Additionally, Greenfield had not reported a COVID-19 case in more than two months, according to The Boston Globe. The bar has been sparsely attended on what would normally be busy Saturday nights as some angered customers have called for a boycott, according to The Boston Globe. The backlash came as the bar was already struggling financially under to the bar’s unusual business model that includes rules such as "Nobody will be barred from entry due to lack of funds." Last Ditch also had the mask mandate in place as part of a policy intended to make the space accessible to disabled and immunocompromised patrons, meaning the face covering requirement was designed to protect anyone who was immunocompromised. Customers were told that they were expected to mask up unless they were actively taking a bite of food or a sip of a drink. The bar’s owners began to fall behind on their bills and were unable to pay themselves or even their staff. Jackie Matellian, the remaining owner involved in daily operations, lived in her truck for six months, working four jobs and carrying a $50,000 loan, according to The Boston Globe. ONLINE FURY ERUPTS AS CONSERVATIVES RECALL ’INSANE’ COVID-19 LOCKDOWN POLICIES AFTER FAUCI TAKES THE FIFTH The two other owners stepped back from daily operations months ago, including one who had enrolled in clown school and another who is a drag performer using it/its pronouns. Because of the financial woes, the bar decided to lift the mask mandate on Saturdays to increase revenue and keep the business afloat, The Boston Globe reported. "It is with love we inform our immunocompromised disabled divas we will be opening Saturday nights as mask optional," Last Ditch wrote on an August Instagram post that ignited the backlash. The bar first attempted to ease tensions and apologize for its post, writing: "We are sorry for our passive and dismissive tone of our change to the norms and schedule impacting the most intersectional of us. We understand everyone faces different intersections and we are always working to consider all needs fully." But that did little to lower the temperature, as critics said Last Ditch’s post failed to include written "alt text," a short written description of an image added to the HTML code of a webpage for visually impaired people. "This is not an accessible post," one person commented. "It indicates the lack of care or interest in Disability intersectionality." Last Ditch again sought to address the controversy during its monthly community meeting on Sept. 11, according to The Boston Globe. Outraged attendees who were joined by Zoom began flooding the chat with comments that were read aloud for the in-person group to hear. The meeting took another twist when critics made an allegation of racism because the mediator, a licensed therapist, was white. "A lot of people are calling for an acknowledgment of harm and I’m hearing a WHITE therapist … center[ing] the feelings of a majority white and white adjacent staff," one person said, the newspaper reported. Attendees also took issue with a therapist being there at all and said it made them feel "widely unsafe" since that made the woman a mandated reporter, meaning she is required by law to report known or suspected abuse. Matellian broke down in tears when it was her turn to speak, saying she was only trying to help her friends with the bar before taking over once they left and having a difficult time trying to survive financially. Matellian has fallen behind on rent and the bar’s landlord wants $3,900 by the end of September. "It was not my passion project," Matellian cried while masked up. "I never really wanted this. I don’t think I’m doing a very good job." MASSACHUSETTS LAWMAKERS PASS BILL TO SCRAP 'OFFENSIVE LANGUAGE' FROM STATE'S GENERAL LAWS CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But the bar's critics had no sympathy for the struggling business owner. "You chose to use your time to spill tears and center your feelings," one person responded. "This is incredibly racist and deflecting behavior." The mask-optional Saturday nights have not helped with business, as the barroom has been nearly empty each weekend despite drink deals and DJs that would attract dozens of customers in the past. One person recently suggested having a Lady Gaga-themed party to pull in more patrons. "Gaga is canceled," the bartender said. "Gaga is Zionist."

title: Mamdani fires back at Netanyahu, calls Israeli leader 'architect of horrific genocide' ahead of UN visit
description: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani fired back at Benjamin Netanyahu's accusations of supporting Hamas by citing the ICC arrest warrant for alleged war crimes.
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani fired back at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday after the Israeli leader accused him of supporting Hamas terrorists and inciting unrest against Jewish New Yorkers, escalating their long-running feud days before Netanyahu is expected in the city. When asked by reporters about Netanyahu's video, Mamdani rejected the prime minister's accusations. "We all know that what the prime minister has said in that video is not true," Mamdani said. "What we do know to actually be the truth when it comes to the prime minister is that he is the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity." NETANYAHU ACCUSES MAMDANI OF 'FOMENTING HATE,' SAYS RHETORIC IS MAKING NEW YORK JEWS AFRAID The ICC issued the arrest warrant in November 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, but Netanyahu and the Israeli government have rejected the allegations and challenged the court's actions. Mamdani went further, leveling additional accusations against the Israeli leader days before he is slated to speak at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. "And as the prime minister, he is the architect of horrific genocide against Palestinians," Mamdani asserted. "And just a few days ago, his military killed an 11-year-old boy in what is deemed to be a safe zone in Gaza. So that is what I have to say to his video." ISRAELI UN ENVOY BLASTS MAMDANI AS 'CLOWN' OVER CALL TO ARREST NETANYAHU: 'IT'S A STUNT' The mayor was responding to comments Netanyahu made earlier Tuesday in a video pledging to "tell the truth" about Mamdani when he speaks at the U.N. "Shame on you, Mr. Mamdani. Shame on you for supporting the Hamas terrorist monsters who butchered our people. Shame on you for inciting riots against New York Jews," Netanyahu said in the video posted to X. "I'm coming to the U.N. I am going to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I'm going to tell you the truth about you," he added. EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN The exchange is the latest chapter in an ongoing public feud between the two leaders and comes as Netanyahu prepares to visit the city Mamdani leads. Earlier this year, Mamdani explored whether New York City could execute the ICC warrant against Netanyahu — an issue he had campaigned on — before acknowledging that the city could not enforce the warrant on its own. Mamdani has previously called Netanyahu a "war criminal" and an "architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people." He also said over the summer that Netanyahu was "not welcome" in New York City. "I want to be equally clear: Benjamin Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City, nor is any other war criminal at large," Mamdani said at the time. Mamdani has also defended New Yorkers' right to protest during Netanyahu's visit, though he has said he is not encouraging them to demonstrate. MAMDANI DODGES ON ‘POLITICAL THEATER’ OF EMPTY NETANYAHU ARREST THREAT, CALLS FOR US ACTION AND NYC PROTESTS When asked in July what New Yorkers frustrated with Netanyahu should do when the Israeli leader visited the city, Mamdani pointed to protest as an option. "One of the bedrocks of our city is protest," Mamdani said. "It is something that has been a part of what makes our city so special, that New Yorkers can express themselves whether they are in support or in opposition no matter on whatever topic." More recently, Mamdani clarified that he had no plans to participate in protests surrounding Netanyahu's visit and said he had not encouraged New Yorkers to demonstrate. "To New Yorkers, I have never encouraged them to protest," Mamdani said last week. "What I have always told them is that they have the right to do so in the city." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Following Mamdani's meeting with President Donald Trump on Monday, the mayor was also asked whether he discussed Netanyahu with the president. Mamdani said their conversation remained focused on New York City and New Yorkers. The mayor's office said after Monday's meeting that Mamdani and Trump discussed issues affecting the city, including affordability and economic development. "And when it comes to the prime minister, though, I've made very clear where I stand on that," Mamdani said. Fox News Digital's Greg Norman-Diamond contributed to this report.

title: Farmers offering on-site vacation rentals to combat rising costs
description: As farmers face rising operation costs, many are looking for additional ways to bring in more money and some are offering overnight stays on their properties in effort to do that.
content: As farmers across the country face rising costs, some are turning to tourism to bring in money beyond their traditional agricultural operations. At Lynette Ralph's horse ranch in Missouri, vacationers can spend the night in a small cabin, wake up to views of the horses and get a firsthand look at ranch life. Guests can explore the property, pet and feed the horses or pay extra for horsemanship and riding lessons. "You have access to the farm life, the horses, the barns," Ralph said. THE $1,600 LETTUCE: CALIFORNIA GROWERS WARN OF ‘MASTER PLAN’ STRANGLING FAMILY FARMS For Ralph, welcoming guests is about more than offering a unique getaway. The income from offering short-term vacation rentals on site has allowed her to keep her ranch operating. "If I didn't have the short-term rentals associated with the riding program, I would have to probably liquidate, sell the horses, sell the property," she said. Airbnb and American Farmland Trust are launching a new grant program to help farmers earn extra income through tourism, the organizations told Fox News exclusively. According to USDA data cited in Airbnb's report, households associated with intermediate farms, a category of smaller operations where farming is the principal operator's primary occupation, reported a median loss of approximately $2,800 from farming in 2024. AMERICAN FARMERS PINCHED BY HIGH DIESEL PRICES AHEAD OF SPRING PLANTING SEASON David Haight, vice president of programs at American Farmland Trust, a national nonprofit dedicated to protecting farmland and supporting farmers, said finding additional sources of income could help some farm families navigate financial challenges. "Many families are looking for ways to diversify income, and so bringing people out to the farm or ranch for some is a way to help bring in other dollars," Haight said. Demand for farm stays is growing, according to Airbnb, which reported that online searches increased 61% during the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year. The company says the typical farm stay host earned approximately $8,000 in 2025, while U.S. farm stay hosts collectively earned nearly $120 million. Those figures represent hosting earnings, not necessarily profits after expenses. In Georgia, farm stay host Gilda Lyon said income from her existing rentals has allowed her to build additional cabins and invest in her farm. The money helped her build a greenhouse, start selling herbs and maintain blueberry plants. "The extra income actually has allowed me to invest, in many improvements and to expand the opportunities available for guests," Lyon said. AMERICANS CHOOSING TO VISIT SMALLER TOWNS OVER BIG CITIES AS TRAVEL COSTS RISE Airbnb and American Farmland Trust's new "Farm to Stay" Grant Program will award approximately 25 to 30 grants of up to $10,000 each, with applications opening in November. Haight said the grants may not cover every expense associated with welcoming visitors, but could help farmers in other ways, such as assisting in renovating barns for events, installing fencing or preparing accommodations for overnight guests. The benefits could also extend beyond individual farms. Haight said visitors may spend money at nearby restaurants, shops and other businesses, bringing additional tourism dollars into rural communities. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ralph said welcoming guests has allowed her to continue sharing her passion for horses while maintaining the property she loves. "The short-term rental has totally facilitated my being able to stay here and do the things that I love," she said.

title: Florida AG accuses teacher of labeling student a 'misogynist' over 'conservative views': 'She should be fired'
description: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier alleges a Pine View School teacher bullied a conservative eighth grader and labeled him a "misogynist."
content: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier alleged that a teacher harassed and attempted to "cancel" an eighth-grade student and labeled him a "misogynist" over what Uthmeier described as the student's conservative political views. Uthmeier sent a letter to Sarasota County Schools' Superintendent Terry Connor and the school board over allegations that a Pine View School history teacher, Liz Ballard, singled out the eighth grade student on multiple occasions over his political views. Ballard often brings up political topics during class despite the student telling her that his parents "expressly forbid" him from participating in the political discussions, according to the letter. The parents' demand was ignored, and the teacher continued to hold political discussions, using the student as the "conservative perspective in the classroom," the attorney general said. WASHINGTON FATHER SUES SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR DENYING RELIGIOUS OPT-OUT FOR 5TH GRADER FROM LGBTQ INSTRUCTION The teacher even labeled the student a "misogynist," spread that characterization around the school and "openly questioned the suitability and influence of the student's father," Uthmeier said in the letter. Uthmeier's letter says multiple parents previously initiated HR investigations involving Ballard. If the bullying and harassment allegations are true, Uthmeier said the teacher would have violated Florida law, School Board policy and basic ethical principles for educators. "Ms. Ballard singled out this student and, in defiance of his parents' express instructions, pressured him to defend political positions on demand in front of his classmates," Uthmeier wrote. PORTLAND PARENT BANNED FROM SCHOOL EVENTS AFTER OPPOSING GENDER IDENTITY ASSIGNMENT FILES LAWSUIT "She made disparaging remarks about his father. And by facilitating the spread of a damaging label throughout the school, she engaged in the reputational destruction of a child. Ms. Ballard's deliberate bullying and harassment of this eighth-grade student violated Florida law, School Board policy, and at least six ethical principles," he continued. He said she should be dismissed from her role with the school district and her educator certificate should be revoked if the allegations turn out to be true. "If true, she should be fired and never teach in Florida again," he said. The attorney general gave the superintendent and school board an Oct. 1 deadline to update his office on the actions the district has taken or will take to address the allegations. Connor said Sarasota County Schools received a letter from Uthmeier about allegations involving the teacher. "Every student deserves a classroom where they feel safe, respected, and free to learn. No student should face harassment, humiliation, or retaliation because of their beliefs or their family's views. Respect for students and parents is fundamental to the trust our community places in our schools." "The allegations in the letter warrant careful attention. We will examine the relevant facts and records, ensure a fair process for all involved, and take appropriate action based on the findings and requirements. To protect student privacy and the process's integrity, we will limit public discussion of individual details. This does not reduce our commitment to accountability. Our focus remains on our students' well-being, the professionalism of our classrooms, and the confidence families place in Sarasota County Schools," he added.

title: Texas man charged with capital murder after 5-year-old killed in roadway shooting

MISSOURI MOM WHO PUT NEWBORN IN OVEN INSTEAD OF CRIB LEARNS FATE AS MURDER CHARGE DROPPED The shooting happened Saturday night in northwest Harris County, where Zah'Layah was riding in a vehicle with her mother, Monica Hicks, and her four siblings when someone opened fire on the family's vehicle, the sheriff's office said. title: College basketball TV analyst and former Duke assistant Chris Spatola, Coach K's son-in-law, dies at 47
description: Chris Spatola - starting guard for the Army Black Knights and later coached under Mike Krzyzewski at Duke before joining ESPN's broadcast team has passed.
content: Chris Spatola, an ESPN college basketball analyst, has died, the network announced Tuesday. He was 47. Before moving into broadcasting, Spatola was a starting guard for the Army Black Knights. He later became an assistant coach at Duke, where he worked under Hall of Fame coach Mike Krzyzewski, his father-in-law. "Chris Spatola brought a unique perspective to ESPN's college basketball coverage, shaped by his experiences as a student-athlete, Army veteran, coach and broadcaster," ESPN said in a statement. FORMER NHL PLAYER, COACH AND LONGTIME ESPN ANALYST BARRY MELROSE DEAD AT 70 "He was thoughtful, prepared and passionate about the sport, earning the respect of colleagues, coaches, players and fans alike. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his loved ones during this difficult time," the statement continued. Spatola led Army in scoring in three of his four seasons as a starter. He finished his college career with 1,543 points, placing him among Army’s top 10 all-time scorers. ESPN ANNOUNCES HALL OF FAMER DICK VITALE'S RETURN TO BROADCASTING AFTER LATEST CANCER BATTLE After graduating from Army, Spatola entered a new chapter of service, spending five years on active duty from 2002 through 2007. He deployed in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom. He received the Joint Service Commendation Medal for exceptional combat performance. Spatola’s outstanding leadership was also recognized with the Army Commendation Medal. Spatola served on Mike Krzyzewski’s coaching staff at Duke from 2007 through 2012. During that span, the Blue Devils won the 2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball national championship, with Spatola serving as an assistant coach. title: Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever drop statement win on top-seeded Lynx in final home game
description: Caitlin Clark flirted with a triple-double as the Indiana Fever handed the league-best Minnesota Lynx their largest deficit of the season so far.
content: After a dismal outing on Sunday, the Indiana Fever got their spark back on Tuesday, cruising to a 96–77 win over the league-best Minnesota Lynx in their final game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse of the regular season. Caitlin Clark flirted with a triple-double through three quarters, finishing with a game-high 27 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists. One notable rotation adjustment following Sunday's deflating loss was the flip in minutes between Sophie Cunningham and rookie Raven Johnson. The Fever favored Johnson on Sunday, limiting Cunningham to just seven minutes of action. Tuesday was a different story, as Cunningham saw significantly more court time than Johnson, and Indiana’s offense ran noticeably smoother with her on the floor. title: Ella Langley says 'Choosin' Texas' success is 'changing my life' after her song breaks Mariah Carey's record
description: Ella Langley celebrated a career-defining milestone after “Choosin’ Texas" spent its 23rd week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
content: Ella Langley knew "Choosin' Texas" was special. Even she couldn't have predicted just how far it would go. On Tuesday night, Langley took to Instagram to celebrate making Billboard Hot 100 history this week when "Choosin' Texas" logged its 23rd week at No. 1, surpassing Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" for the longest reign at the top of the chart. "I'm genuinely trying to find the words to explain what's going on in my brain today," Langley began her video. "What? I don't know. Thank you so much. Thank you for loving this song, for listening to it. I feel like… I just don't even know what to say at this point. I'm running out of hyperboles to describe how I feel, so I will just let my dog in the background show you his excitement," she continued as her dog barked. "Just thank you. Thank you so much. It's changing my life. It's changing the lives of the writers of this song. It's changing the lives of my family, and it is truly growing an atmosphere for something I'm gonna be able to do the rest of my life and I just… today doesn't feel like a real thing," Langley said. "It feels fake and somebody's going to come in and be like 'haha we're kidding the whole time just kidding.'" ELLA LANGLEY SEEMINGLY FIRES BACK AFTER DOJA CAT'S BRUTAL TAKE ON HER CHART-TOPPING HIT "I'm really excited to just experience a moment like this in my life," she said. The country music star told her fans that she was going to celebrate tonight before ending with, "Choosin' T… that's the one huh?" In a resurfaced interview with Billboard from March, when the song was still climbing, Langley admitted its success had already surpassed anything she imagined when she wrote it. "When we wrote it, I knew it was going on the record. I honestly knew it was going to be the lead single," Langley told Billboard. "And we love that song, but I don't think I could have ever imagined what's happening with it right now," she continued. "Like I said, every day I wake up, and it's doing something that I didn't even know was a goal that I could have had." "It's just nuts," Langley added. "It's crazy to see the ownership that the fans have taken over it. And the different demographics of people listening to the song is so cool." What seemed unimaginable to Langley in March has since become historic. ELLA LANGLEY'S 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SPENDS 15 WEEKS AT NUMBER ONE ON THE BILLBOARD HOT 100 "Choosin' Texas" first entered the Hot 100 in November 2025, became Langley's first top 10 in January and reached No. 1 for the first time in February. The song has also spent 41 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart. Long before it became a record breaker, however, "Choosin' Texas" began with a story about a kangaroo. Langley recalled writing the song during her first songwriting retreat with country superstar Miranda Lambert and two other writers. "So, I was on a writer's retreat with Miranda," Langley explained in the resurfaced Billboard interview. "This is our first time that we had written together, and obviously we were there with two others." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Billboard credits Langley, Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor as the four co-writers of "Choosin' Texas." Langley said Lambert began telling her a story about a pet kangaroo. "I learned at a young age she had a pet kangaroo and I wanted to ask her about it," Langley recalled. "So, I was like, 'Tell me about this kangaroo that you had. I need to know.'" ELLA LANGLEY'S TEXAS PHOTO DUMP SENDS COUNTRY MUSIC FANS INTO A FRENZY ONLINE ON INSTAGRAM Lambert told the group about once being pulled over with the kangaroo riding in the passenger seat and a dog in the back. Advertisement "She said she got pulled over and the kangaroo ended up getting her out of a ticket, but she's like, 'Of course, I had Texas plates on, too,'" Langley recalled. ELLA LANGLEY JOINS MUSIC ROYALTY WITH 'INSANE' MILESTONE FOR 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' That was enough to spark the song. "And I went, 'Well, she's from Texas, I can tell,'" Langley said. "And just from that phrase, it kind of all hit us." According to Langley, the melody came almost immediately, with Lambert helping develop the story behind it. "And 45 minutes later, we had that song written," Langley said. "And it was just, it was such a cool experience." Lambert's involvement didn't end in the writing room. Langley told Billboard that the country superstar was executive producing her next record and had become someone she could turn to for advice. "There's not a rulebook to this job," Langley said. "So to be able to have someone like her to ask questions and think, you know, is it, should I be doing this? She's like, 'Hell yeah, you should be doing this.'" LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "My team's calling me every day freaking out about this song," Langley recalled Lambert telling her. At the time of the March interview, the song had reached No. 5 on the Hot 100. "How crazy is that?" Langley said. "And for me, like, what, me? You mean me?" Six months later, "Choosin' Texas" stands alone as the longest-running No. 1 song in Hot 100 history. Langley's historic week comes as she continues performing across the country. The images showed Langley performing with her guitar, posing near an Ole Miss sign in a dress and red boots, holding a snake and preparing backstage in front of a lighted mirror.
