title: CNN staffers accept new reality as Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros Discovery goes full steam ahead
description: CNN staffers reveal mixed emotions as Paramount's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery moves forward following the settlement with State Attorneys General.
content: A new reality is setting in for CNN's rank and file as the network will once again have new ownership following Paramount's merger with its parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). "I think people are like, 'Let's just get this done,'" one CNN staffer told Fox News Digital. Paramount's $111 billion bid to buy WBD overcame its biggest obstacle, which was the antitrust lawsuit spearheaded by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and several other Democratic State AGs. Instead of battling it out in court during the March 2027 trial date, both parties reached a settlement Monday, paving the way for Paramount CEO David Ellison to take the reins of two legacy Hollywood studios and two major news organizations — CNN and CBS News — among other assets. Negotiated in the settlement is the implementation of an independent editorial board that will oversee both news outlets. PARAMOUNT REACHES SETTLEMENT WITH STATES SUING TO BLOCK WARNER BROS DISCOVERY MERGER There have been several reports of internal strife within the CNN newsroom since the settlement was reached, but at least one network staffer believes the sentiment is more nuanced based on conversations they've had with colleagues. "I think there are fewer people internally opposed to the merger than there used to be," the CNN staffer said. "People internally just want direction." A second CNN staffer disagreed with the notion that they aren't personally opposed to the merger, telling Fox News Digital, "Nothing has changed about anyone's views at CNN." "If there is that perception, it is coming from the fact that this has been out there for a long time so people are less loud. That shouldn’t be confused with a change of mindset," they said. CNN STAFFERS BRACE FOR PARAMOUNT CEO'S POTENTIAL PLAN TO LAUNCH EDITORIAL BOARD TO OVERSEE NETWORK A lot of unknowns loom over CNN as the merger proceeds. First are the company wide layoffs that are expected to take place that will likely impact CNN. Second is the change in CNN's leadership — whether its current CEO Mark Thompson will remain or whether Ellison's appointed CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss will have a new role overseeing both news operations, as reports previously suggested. "I don’t know who will run CNN," the second staffer said. "Ellison will have a lot of pressure to make that decision and not to say let Mark Thompson stay on for a little while to not deal with it or fake anybody out. It’s better for his business to make a clean, strong decision and let everybody know." While they're glad the Paramount merger brings clarity about the network's future, the CNN insider is dreading "fairly dramatic" cuts that will ultimately rock the newsroom. "CNN will be diminished," the second staffer said. "However, that is already happening macro and micro to us and all other legacy media." Representatives for CNN and Paramount declined to comment. FORMER '60 MINUTES' HONCHO SAYS CBS NEWS LEADERS WANTED STAFF TO 'COMPROMISE OUR PRINCIPLES' Much of the opposition toward the Paramount-WBD merger stemmed from Ellison's taking control over CNN. Liberal critics claimed that as a result of the deal, CNN would be given a MAGA-bent to its coverage, pointing to Ellison and his billionaire father Larry Ellison's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump, and worried Ellison's CNN would be run by CBS News chief Bari Weiss, who has been ostracized by the far-left despite her outspoken left-of-center politics. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ellison has previously assured that CNN would maintain editorial independence following the merger. In a guest essay published in The New York Times, the Paramount CEO addressed the "speculation" about what would happen to CNN under his ownership. "I have regularly voted for candidates of both parties; I hold some views that would be called conservative and others that would be called liberal, just like most Americans; and when it comes to our news operations, I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views. I believe that news should be based on facts and truth," Ellison wrote. "Great news organizations like CNN and CBS News are here to tell it straight down the middle," he added. "That requires newsrooms that reflect the whole world, not one side of it. And it requires independence."

title: Dad of 'American Idol' contestant's slain wife made eerie Google search after hearing of her murder
description: Caleb Flynn's murder trial revealed how Ohio investigators searched storm drains, attics and vehicles for the gun allegedly used to kill Ashley Flynn.
content: Investigators hunting for the gun prosecutors say former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn used to kill his wife brought in an ATF firearms-detection dog to scour woods, fields and the family home – but the alleged murder weapon still hasn't been found. ATF Special Agent David McMullen testified Tuesday that his K-9 partner, Hilton, spent hours searching around Flynn's Tipp City, Ohio, home, through nearby woods and along a walking path before combing a farm field for the missing firearm. The dog was later brought inside the garage and home to search areas where a weapon could have been hidden, McMullen testified. ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY The first search lasted roughly three hours before Hilton became exhausted. McMullen and the dog returned the following day and searched the property, woods and farm field again. Both searches came up empty. Flynn is accused of fatally shooting his wife, Ashley Flynn, inside the couple's home on Feb. 16 before staging the scene to look like an intruder had broken in. He has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges. The ATF search adds another layer to the lengths investigators went to try to find the missing gun, after jurors heard Monday about searches involving storm drains, a high-powered magnet, vehicles and attic insulation. The expanded search was one of several developments Tuesday, as jurors also heard about the couple's finances, a life insurance policy on Ashley and two devices belonging to Flynn's alleged mistress that investigators never recovered. ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY The trial also turned deeply personal Tuesday as Ashley's mother and sister took the stand, describing the family's frantic first hours after her death and the stunning revelation that Flynn had allegedly been having an affair with a woman they knew from church. Ashley's mother, Jill Smith, testified that her phone rang around 3 a.m. the morning her daughter was killed. She initially thought it was her husband, who was traveling, but saw Flynn's name on the screen instead. "She's gone," Smith recalled Flynn telling her. When Smith asked who he meant, Flynn responded, "Ashley, she's gone," before telling her, "Someone broke in and shot her," she testified. WATCH: Ashley Flynn's mother Jill Smith testifies about defendant Caleb telling daughters mom was hurt Smith said she told Flynn she was coming to the house, but he told her police were there and she could not come. She hung up, became dizzy and lay down on the bathroom floor. "It seemed like forever," Smith testified, saying she remained there for about five minutes before getting up and calling her husband to tell him Ashley had been killed. ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY Smith drove to the home anyway and said seeing the flashing police lights made the reality of what had happened sink in. "And then I knew it was true," she testified. Flynn later came outside shaking, Smith said. The two hugged before sitting on the front porch, where she became concerned enough about him that she asked for a blanket and suggested someone call an EMT because she feared he was going into shock. While Smith was comforting Flynn, her husband, Todd Smith, testified that he was already questioning Flynn’s account as he made the roughly 16-hour drive home from Canada. Todd said the alleged break-in story "just didn't make sense" to him, prompting him to Google whether a "Christian man" could "snap and shoot his wife." He testified that he called Jill and told her, "This really doesn’t look good on Caleb," but she responded, "Don’t even go there." WATCH: Kayla Keyt testifies on family business and defendant Caleb Flynn Ashley's sister, Kayla Keyt, testified that she initially believed so strongly in Flynn's innocence that she told investigators "100%" they had arrested the wrong man. "I trusted Caleb with everything I had in me," Keyt testified. Keyt said she became angry when she initially heard rumors that Flynn had been having an affair because she believed they were unfairly damaging his reputation. "I was so mad because it was tarnishing his reputation," Keyt said. "I just knew in my heart that he was completely innocent. I really believed that with all of my heart." FBI JOINS PROBE IN MURDER OF CHRISTIAN TEACHER SHOT IN OHIO HOME AS 'AMERICAN IDOL' HUSBAND, CHILDREN SLEPT Keyt testified that changed when investigators told her Flynn had been having an affair with Alleigha, a woman the family knew from Christian Life Center. Alleigha was the church's main worship leader and performed alongside Flynn, who sang with the worship team during rehearsals and weekend services, Keyt testified. She said she personally knew Alleigha casually from seeing her at church. "I don't think I've been more shocked in my life," Keyt said. Keyt recalled asking investigators, "Are you 100% sure?" and said she had them repeat it two or three times because she "could not even fathom" Flynn having an affair. She testified that she first learned about it during an FBI interview the morning after Flynn's arrest. Keyt, who testified that Ashley's two daughters now live with her family, said the girls have since learned about the alleged affair and personally knew Alleigha. "They were mostly brokenhearted for mommy," Keyt testified. Keyt said the girls were shocked and questioned why their father did not love their mother as much as Ashley loved him. But when the girls were told who Flynn had allegedly been involved with, Keyt recalled the older daughter's response: "I'm not surprised." The defense later focused on two devices belonging to Alleigha that police were unable to recover. Tipp City Police Capt. Tony Smith testified that investigators learned Alleigha's work laptop went missing during a Florida trip in January 2026, about a month before Ashley was killed, while her cellphone was dropped in water during the same trip. WATCH: Ashley Flynn's mother Jill Smith testifies about learning of her daughter's murder from Caleb Neither device was recovered. Investigators obtained the laptop's make, model and serial number and passed the information to an investigative team that included Tipp City detectives, the FBI and Ohio BCI, Smith testified. Jurors also heard testimony Tuesday about the Flynns' finances and a life insurance policy on Ashley. EX-AMERICAN IDOL CONTESTANT CHARGED IN WIFE'S MURDER PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED AS ‘VERY TALENTED’ CHURCH LEADER Smith testified investigators identified a $100,000 life insurance policy on Ashley that was owned by Flynn, who was also the sole beneficiary. Bank records introduced by prosecutors showed Flynn and Ashley had $84,369.29 in a joint savings account on the day she was killed. Ashley's father, Todd Smith, testified that Flynn earned $195,000 in 2025 working in sales for the family's commercial flooring business, along with roughly $10,000 in medical reimbursements. Smith said he planned to eventually give the business to Ashley and Keyt, with each daughter owning half. He testified that Flynn's income had the potential to increase if sales continued to grow. The new testimony came after jurors spent much of Monday hearing about the exhaustive search for the missing gun and forensic evidence collected from the Flynn home. Detective Adam Bernard walked jurors through the lengths investigators went to as they searched for the missing firearm in the days after Ashley's death. Police searched the backyard and nearby wooded areas before turning their attention underground, where investigators used a high-powered magnet to search storm drains along several streets. Bernard testified that investigators removed the drain covers, lowered the magnet inside and swept connecting pipes before he physically climbed into accessible culverts with a flashlight to search areas the magnet may have missed. They found nothing. CHRISTIAN MOTHER, TEACHER'S AUTOPSY CONDUCTED AS POLICE PROBE HOMICIDE IN OHIO HOME INVASION Investigators later had both vehicles from the Flynn home placed on lifts so they could search underneath them and other areas where something could have been hidden, Bernard testified. That search also came up empty. Police even rented equipment to remove insulation from the attic as they continued looking for the gun. Bernard testified that investigators also tried to trace Flynn's firearm purchase history after Flynn previously said he bought a gun in South Carolina, where he obtained his concealed-carry permit. The detective said he called nearly two dozen gun stores in the state looking for records that could identify the make, model and serial number of a firearm purchased by Flynn. That effort did not identify a gun tied to Flynn or Ashley. The testimony came after a forensic pathologist walked jurors through Ashley's autopsy and described two gunshot wounds to the back of her head. Dr. Bryan Casto testified that the entrance wounds overlapped, and the bullets traveled through Ashley's head on nearly parallel paths. One of the bullets exited her head before reentering her left arm near the elbow, where it was recovered during the autopsy. Casto said the wounds and the paths of the bullets suggested Ashley was shot at close range, but he could not say exactly how far away the gun was when it was fired. CHRISTIAN MOTHER, TEACHER FOUND DEAD AS POLICE HUNT HOMICIDE SUSPECT IN OHIO HOME INVASION The pathologist determined Ashley died from multiple gunshot wounds to the head. Earlier Monday, Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation (BCI) crime scene investigators walked jurors through evidence collected throughout the Flynn home as prosecutors sought to show the alleged break-in had been staged. A BCI crime scene technician who had examined between 20 and 30 forced-entry doors testified that the damage to a side garage door did not look like the forced entries she had previously investigated. She said the damage was on the inside of the door rather than areas she would typically expect to be damaged if someone had kicked or pried their way inside. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Flynn's defense challenged the state's conclusions on cross-examination, pointing out that investigators could not determine when some of the door damage occurred and that no blood-spatter analysis was performed because conditions at the scene were not suitable for one. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS David Hammond, a senior special agent with BCI, also testified that he was not aware of evidence showing blood spatter from Ashley's shooting on Flynn's clothing. SEND US A TIP Bernard testified that he printed tips received by Tipp City police and passed them to the FBI for follow-up. He said he did not know whether the FBI investigated that particular tip. GOT A TIP? The judge sustained objections when the defense tried to get into some of the caller's specific claims. title: Former news anchor working for California Democrat arrested by immigration authorities at Las Vegas airport

title: Javier Bardem slammed for targeting Pink over Macklemore comments: 'The left is eating itself'
description: Actor Javier Bardem promoted a petition to remove Pink as a UNICEF ambassador, drawing fierce pushback from Michael Rapaport and Selma Blair.
content: Actor Javier Bardem has stepped into the middle of the controversy surrounding Pink, Macklemore and the Israel-Gaza conflict — and is now taking heat for it. The "No Country for Old Men" star shared multiple posts to his Instagram Stories Monday urging followers to sign a Change.org petition demanding that Pink be removed as a UNICEF ambassador, according to Reuters. The petition Bardem promoted, titled "Remove Pink as a UNICEF Ambassador," calls on the organization to remove the singer from her position. ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO Supporters argue that Pink’s comments are "incompatible with the role of a UNICEF Ambassador" and say ambassadors should promote "peace, understanding, and humanitarian values above personal biases." The petition urges UNICEF to "take decisive action and remove Pink as an ambassador," arguing that the organization must remain committed to all children regardless of "nationality or heritage." Bardem’s move drew pushback from fans and fellow celebrities who questioned why the actor was backing an effort to strip Pink of her UNICEF title over comments she made after Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian concert appearance. Michael Rapaport delivered one of the most blistering responses, mocking Bardem as a "tattletale" and accusing the actor of going after Pink through a petition rather than confronting her directly. He wrote in an Instagram caption: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb initiated,signed & is promoting a petition to have singer PINK removed as a UNICEF Ambassador. He’s is Bullying a Proud Jewish Woman." Rapaport continued in his video: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb. Javier Bardem, what the f--- are you doing, you little tattle-tale? Hall monitor … you are a grown man, a grown f---ing man. Pink is a grown woman. You're both world-famous. If you have a problem with what she said, call her. Sit her down, have a coffee, look her dead in the face and express all and any frustrations and questions you have … instead you sign a petition, like a little b---- to have her removed as a UNICEF ambassador. What the f--- is wrong with you?" PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS Selma Blair also weighed in in the comment section, writing: "Why would anyone want this great removed from unicef for human , humble and loving words? This makes no sense. I would think the terrifically talented actor man would worry about his own incredible life more. And allow love to flow. And listen to everybody. Not just his echo chamber. But alas." Bardem's decision to promote the petition also drew criticism from social media users, with commenters questioning why the actor was pushing for Pink's removal over her comments. One commenter wrote: "I'm not a big Pink fan...I like her music okay, but she was one of the many performers who actually did ads for Big Pharma pushing the vax during covid. That said, who the hell is Bardem to cancel her? The left is eating itself." Meanwhile, supporters of Bardem's position also commented on the petition. "Pink chose her and her rich friends' discomfort was more important than people's lives," one commenter wrote, adding that if UNICEF does not "stand with Gaza now and remove Pink," then "the world is a much darker place." Another argued, "No ambassador can call attention to important issues while actively ignoring and deliberately misunderstanding and misrepresenting the conditions in Palestine. Pink has shown herself incapable of even acknowledging what is clear to the world, and is not fit to serve UNICEF." A third commenter questioned how Pink could remain a UNICEF advocate while, in their view, failing to support "basic human rights and free speech for all people, especially those in Gaza, the Sudan and the Congo." Fox News Digital reached out to Bardem, UNICEF and Pink for comment. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT The petition Bardem promoted centers on Pink’s response to Macklemore’s appearance with Ed Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4. Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," his song supporting Palestinians, while repeatedly chanting "Free Palestine" as images related to Gaza appeared on a screen behind him. The performance sparked criticism from the @Stop_Antisemitism Instagram account, which accused Macklemore of using the concert to push "anti-Israel propaganda." Pink faced backlash after reposting the criticism and subsequently issued her own lengthy explanation. "I’ve been quiet in my own words for a week, which you know isn’t like me. So here they are," she wrote on social media. "I was born a Jew," Pink continued. "I didn’t pick it, and I’ve never hidden it." I never have," Pink wrote. "What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organization. Palestinians deserve a future that honors their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody’s child." Pink also cited her years of work with UNICEF, saying she had spent time with children "on both sides of that fence." "I’m not going to litigate a complex war in an Instagram caption, and I’m not going to recite anybody’s slogan to earn back a follower," she wrote. Pink went on to explain that what she was "reacting to" was Macklemore himself. She recalled him performing his song "Same Love" at the Grammys in 2014, and how she cheered on the message, but "Four months later Macklemore put on a hooked nose, a black beard and a bowl cut, performed in it, and called it a 'random costume.'" "Every Jew I know knew exactly what it was. The same love, it turned out, had a guest list, and we weren’t on it. But he apologized, and I let it go, because that’s what we do. We let it go. Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them." title: San Francisco sues Trump Media over alleged 'pay-to-play' Truth Social service
description: San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu alleges the paid service gives wealthy subscribers an unfair advantage by providing early access to President Donald Trump's market-moving posts.
content: President Donald Trump's social media company is facing a lawsuit from the city of San Francisco over a paid Truth Social subscription service that gives certain customers early access to the president's posts. San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu announced the lawsuit Tuesday, alleging that Trump Media's Truth API service operates as a "pay-to-play scheme," allowing subscribers to receive President Donald Trump's market-moving posts before they are publicly available. The lawsuit seeks to block the service and impose civil penalties under California's Unfair Competition Law (UCL). Chiu alleged the service gives wealthy subscribers an "unfair advantage" by providing early access to government information before it reaches the broader public. TRUMP WARNS HE'LL BE 'LAST REPUBLICAN PRESIDENT' IF SENATE GOP DOESN'T MAKE MAJOR CHANGE "Truth Social has knowingly created a marketplace for insider trading by giving high-paying subscribers an unfair advantage over ordinary investors in the market," Chiu said at a news conference Tuesday. "It's a pay-to-play scheme for early access to the president's market-moving government decisions." The monthly subscription was rolled out Aug. 1 and costs between $60,000 to $100,000 in exchange for early access to market-moving posts from Truth Social accounts with large followings, including Trump’s own account. "No ordinary person can pay that fee," Chiu said. "Now the early subscribers are largely high-frequency trading firms with the technology to analyze that information and to make trades within microseconds." TRUMP ANNOUNCES WHITE HOUSE BAN AGAINST THREE MEDIA OUTLETS Chiu also said Trump owns roughly 41% of Trump Media and "is personally benefiting from this business scheme." A Trump Media spokesperson pushed back on the allegations, telling Fox News Digital, "The people of California should outsource their future lawsuits to AI chatbots who, unlike the left-wing activists masquerading as attorneys who filed this lawsuit, will grasp the basic distinction between public and nonpublic information." The lawsuit was filed Monday, the same day that dozens of former federal prosecutors and agents filed a court brief backing a separate lawsuit over Truth API, according to CBS News. TRUMP’S $100K WALL STREET TRUTH ACCESS DRAWS LAWSUIT; EXPERT WARNS IT ‘RAISES THE STAKES’ ON ETHICS The separate lawsuit, brought by The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation, alleges the paid service violates the First and Fifth amendments. Representatives for The Trump Organization and Chiu's office could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment. Fox News Digital's Julia Bonavita contributed to this report.

title: Russia's neighbor reveals personal appeals to Trump as US weighs NATO troop pullback in Europe
description: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda revealed he sent two letters to Trump urging U.S. troops to stay on NATO's eastern flank amid Russian threat.
content: NEW YORK — Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda revealed Monday he personally pleaded with President Donald Trump to maintain U.S. forces on NATO’s eastern flank as Washington reviews its military footprint in Europe. Meanwhile, Russia’s war in Ukraine has raged on for more than 4½ years and raised questions about how far Moscow will push into the continent. Nausėda said during remarks at a fireside chat moderated by Fox News Digital at the Presidential Business Forum on Resilience on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly New York that Lithuania is prepared to provide "very generous host nation support" for American forces to remain in the region. "I personally sent two letters to the president," Nausėda said of the plea to keep an American troops' presence. PENTAGON CUTS BRIGADE COMBAT TEAMS IN EUROPE AS TRUMP PRESSURES NATO ON SPENDING Hours after Nausėda revealed that he had personally appealed to Trump to maintain U.S. forces on NATO’s eastern flank, he announced that a new rotation of American troops is already headed to Lithuania. "I have just received confirmation that the new rotation of U.S. troops is already on its way to Lithuania!" Nausėda wrote on X Tuesday, thanking Trump and his administration for a decision he said was important to the security of the entire region. The announcement resolves months of uncertainty over whether Washington would replace roughly 1,000 U.S. troops whose rotation ended this summer. The Pentagon has already begun scaling back some forces and capabilities in Europe, while reported options under review could remove tens of thousands more troops. The review is part of a broader Pentagon strategy to shift primary responsibility for Europe’s conventional defense onto European allies, while reserving a more limited U.S. role. But Washington has also signaled that its retrenchment may not be uniform: Trump said last week that the U.S. was making progress toward a permanent Army base in Poland, one of NATO’s highest-spending members. That has left frontline allies trying to determine where they fit in with an emerging U.S. strategy that calls for a smaller overall role in Europe while deepening ties with countries Washington views as carrying more of the burden. The review also comes as Russia’s war with Ukraine has increasingly spilled into NATO territory. RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS Lithuania experienced that threat firsthand last week when NATO fighters shot down a drone that crossed into Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. Nausėda later said the aircraft was likely Russian and intended for an attack on Ukraine before veering off course. The country's intelligence services warn that Russia is already rebuilding military capabilities near NATO's eastern borders despite its losses in Ukraine. Lithuania's 2026 National Threat Assessment found that a ceasefire or frozen conflict in Ukraine could accelerate that buildup, allowing Moscow to move more troops and equipment back toward permanent bases near the Baltic States and replenish weapons and ammunition depleted during the war. In that scenario, Lithuanian intelligence assessed Russia could eventually develop enough capability to launch military action against the Baltics and seek an initial regional advantage before NATO could fully respond. Asked how much time NATO would have if a ceasefire were reached tomorrow, Nausėda declined to put a timeline on the threat but warned that "a ceasefire for Russia may mean" looking for new targets. He said whether Moscow ultimately tests NATO would depend largely on the alliance's ability to strengthen its deterrence and demonstrate that it can defend its eastern flank. Nausėda cast doubt on the prospect of near-term peace talks, saying that "for the time being, Russia is not ready to start the peace negotiations." Instead, he said Moscow appears intent on using the approaching winter to increase pressure on Kyiv by striking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and worsening conditions for civilians. "The winter is coming. Russia knows very well where they should target, and they will target energy infrastructure first of all," Nausėda said, describing the attacks as an effort to make living conditions in Ukraine as difficult as possible and pressure its leadership toward concessions. "For these negotiations, I don’t see any ground, at least right now," he said, adding that talks could become possible "maybe next year." The threat to energy infrastructure was particularly resonant for Nausėda, who spoke as Lithuania marked another step in its yearslong effort to insulate itself from energy pressure from Moscow. Lithuania, marking a new long-term natural gas agreement with U.S. natural gas producer EQT Corp. this week during the president's trip to New York, began importing U.S. LNG in 2017 and now gets roughly 70% of its LNG from the United States, Nausėda said. During Monday’s forum, Lithuanian energy company Ignitis signed a new long-term LNG agreement with U.S.-based EQT Corp. Nausėda said Lithuania’s push for energy independence was shaped by years of experience with Moscow using the country’s dependence on Russian energy as political leverage. "Our history shows that, all the time, Russians misused our dependencies for their own benefit," Nausėda said. Nausėda stressed that Lithuania is also increasing its own defense burden, saying the country is spending 5.4% of GDP on defense while building a national division and preparing to host a full German brigade by the end of 2027. title: Why didn't Ryan Clark push back at Colin Kaepernick comparing the NFL to slavery during interview?
description: Colin Kaepernick doubled down on his NFL-slave trade comparison in a podcast interview with Ryan Clark, calling the NFL Combine a "meat market."
content: Colin Kaepernick doubled down on his comparison of the NFL to the slave trade during a podcast interview with former ESPN commentator Ryan Clark this week. "When did you truly start to have the realization that [the combine] reminds [you] of the slave trade?" Clark asked. "You get to the point, where it's like, 'Strip down to your drawers,’" Kaepernick responded. "It feels like a meat market." 5 TOUGH QUESTIONS COLIN KAEPERNICK DIDN'T HEAR DURING HIS MEDIA TOUR | MATT CALKINS Kaepernick added that he did not have the "historical perspective at the time" in 2011 at the Scouting Combine to understand what he now considers a "parallel" to a slave auction. The former NFL quarterback first made the comparison during a 2021 Netflix series. His reputation has never been the same since. That is how offensive it is to equate the horrors of bondage with playing in the NFL for millions of dollars a year. But at this point, similar scrutiny must be applied to Clark. Consider the wording of Clark's question. He did not challenge Kaepernick's premise or ask him to substantiate it. Instead, he led him toward the desired answer by asking "when" he realized the NFL draft process resembled slavery. COLIN KAEPERNICK IS STILL UPSET THAT HIS MOM WANTED HIM TO DATE TAYLOR SWIFT, A WHITE WOMAN Clark then nodded along as Kaepernick claimed that the draft and slave auctions are part of the "same process." OutKick asked Clark on Tuesday about his question to Kaepernick. We also asked whether he agreed with the analogy. Clark did not respond by the time of publication. We will update this story if he does. At minimum, it is reasonable to conclude that Clark did not find the comparison outrageous. We have seen how he reacts when he disagrees with a statement. title: Pirates ace Paul Skenes links concerning velocity dip to World Baseball Classic amid tough season
description: Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes said the World Baseball Classic disrupted his spring ramp-up, contributing to a velocity dip and a nearly doubled ERA this season.
content: The World Baseball Classic may have only been a couple of weeks long, but its impact was felt all season long. Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes has not been himself this year. His velocity has dipped, his command has been off, and after posting ERAs of 1.97 and 1.96, respectively, over the last two seasons, he has a 3.91 ERA this season. Why? Skenes said part of it was the World Baseball Classic. "There are a lot of other factors, so I don’t want to put everything on that," Skenes told the Post-Gazette. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit." The World Baseball Classic ran from March 3 to March 17 this year, and Skenes said at that time of year, pitchers aren’t throwing at max effort. "Usually, that time of year, you’re kind of ramping up and it’s a little bit slow. You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body," Skenes said. "One live (batting practice), you’re topping at 97 (mph), and then the next you’re 98, 99. And that wasn’t the case this year. ... Looking back, I don’t think that really helped." title: North Korean defector issues stark warning about America ahead of Christian university's anti-communism event
description: Cornerstone University's anti-communist event features North Korean defector Yeonmi Park and Cultural Revolution survivor Xi Van Fleet speaking.
content: Cornerstone University, a Christian school in Michigan, is holding an anti-communist event, bringing in scholars and survivors of oppressive regimes. Dr. Gerson Moreno-Riaño, the president of Cornerstone University, said the school chose the theme months ago, as it saw public opinion across the country sway toward communism and socialism. The Oct. 1 event is titled, "Why Not Communism? A Wisdom Conversation on Freedom, Faith and the Future of America." "Frankly, we became alarmed and concerned because the history of communism, socialism is a dark one," Moreno-Riaño told Fox News Digital. OPINION: WANT TO STOP SOCIALISM? A MODERN CIVIC EDUCATION NEEDS A LOT MORE THAN YOU'D THINK "We thought we need to step up as a university committed to educating men and women for our country and really inform the community, educate the community and our students and the country at large about the moral bankruptcy of communism and socialism," he added. The university is located in Grand Rapids, Michigan, which sits in Kent County, an area where Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed won more than 61% of the vote in the primary, according to state records. El-Sayed famously campaigned with controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who defended communism as the "honorable end goal" of socialism, giving the event added relevance. The event speakers include Babylon Bee CEO Seth Dillon; Dr. Gary Saul Morson, a scholar of Soviet communism; Mao Zedong's Cultural Revolution survivor Xi Van Fleet, and North Korean defector Yeonmi Park. "Yeonmi Park's story is incredible, as a defector of North Korea. Xi Van Fleet, her time in a labor camp in China. And what they saw, what they experienced, what they witnessed is absolutely essential, because there are certain similarities between what happened in North Korea and is happening there now, what happened in China during Mao Zedong and thereafter, similarities between what happens there in those revolutions and what's happening here has been happening here for several years," Moreno-Riaño said. HASAN PIKER VOWS NEVER TO CRITICIZE MAO ZEDONG IN RESURFACED VIDEO, HAILS HIM AS ‘GREAT LEADER’ Park told Fox News Digital that communism is on the rise among students who learn about it "in a very nice classroom with the air conditioning running," while she experienced oppressive regimes firsthand. "I had to live through [a] real socialist government every day until I escaped from North Korea," Park said. "And I know it is not nice when it is actually enforced [in] real life. Many people think it's [an] amazing thing as a theory, and they have no idea if we do bring this policy in our government, what that's going to [do to] our local population." Growing up in North Korea during the devastating famines of the 1990s, Park experienced hunger, severe poverty and political persecution. At age 13, she escaped with her mother across the frozen border river into China, where they experienced human trafficking. After her mother submitted to sexual assault to protect Yeonmi from smugglers, both were sold into trafficking rings. After two years of exploitation and hiding from Chinese authorities, Christian activist networks helped them cross from China to Mongolia, where they secured political asylum, and later gained their freedom in South Korea. Park added that they refer to her as a "White-passing person." "They have no idea that I was, at 13 years old, being sold as a sex slave in China for two years of my life. I do understand oppression," she said. Park insisted that American students often take their freedom for granted and do not have a full understanding of global realities. "Most people are not free right now in the world. More than 70% of humanity right now live under authoritarian governments," Park told Fox News Digital, likely referencing data from the Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) Institute. V-Dem's most recent report estimates that 74% of the world's population lives under autocracies. She added that having freedom is "a very special thing" and she doesn't "want us to lose this amazing country, because if America falls, we do not have a place to escape to." "For me, I was fortunate that I had a country to escape to from North Korea to America, but if we lose this country, we are all going to die, actually," she said. It's absolutely essential," he added. Ultimately, Moreno-Riaño hopes to encourage students to take action and to resist the urge to "sit on the sidelines watching." title: Deadly helicopter crash kills 2 pilots battling raging wildfire in Yosemite

content: Two pilots were killed when a firefighting helicopter crashed while battling a wildfire in Yosemite National Park. description: Sturgill Simpson ripped entitled singers with no work ethic, revealing what he says separates lasting careers from those flushed by the machine.
content: Sturgill Simpson doesn't think there's a hidden secret to success in music. Simpson has carved out an incredibly loyal following in the country music industry by singing largely outlaw country tunes. However, that's far from his only skill. He also released a pair of albums under his alter ego Johnny Blue Skies. ‘YELLOWSTONE’ STAR LUKE GRIMES REVEALS OUTLAW COUNTRY WAS 'NO-GO' IN PASTOR FATHER’S HOUSE His secret to success? Just work hard. Sturgill Simpson blasts entitled and lazy singers. Simpson spoke with Playboy about his rise in the music industry, and he took some not-so-subtle shots at people who don't think they need to earn it. "I had all the thankless f***ing jobs. There are so many people I met when I moved to Nashville 15 years ago who had exponentially more talent than I do, but they had no work ethic. Or they thought [sic] that, because they were brilliant, they didn’t have to earn their medals," Simpson told Playboy (via Whiskey Riff). If you’re waiting on some machine to pump you out, that machine is going to flush your a** too. Talent’s not as rare as people think." Simpson's comments shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone. This is the man who famously once said he was "plotting" the "destruction" of the music industry. Or, that's certainly how his comment was interpreted. title: DAVID MARCUS: In deep blue Minnesota a red dawn may be rising ahead of the midterms
description: Minnesota's GOP candidates Michele Tafoya and Lisa Demuth are closing in on Democratic Party rivals as a billion-dollar fraud scandal fuels outrage.
content: Six months ago, very few people imagined that this year’s senate and governor races in Minnesota would be anything but Democratic Party blowouts, but as we approach October, and the beating heart of the midterms, the Gopher state appears suddenly and stunningly in play. Recent polling, as shoddy as this cycle’s surveys have been, show GOP senate candidate Michele Tafoya within 2 or 3 points of her opponent, sitting Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, and while the chaos surrounding the death of Alex Pretti at the hands of CBP is in the rearview mirror, the massive Somali fraud scandal decidedly is not. On Sunday, I headed over to Cowboys Saloon in Lexington, Minn., just north of the Twin Cities, to attend a Vikings game watch party for local Republican volunteers, where I found Lisa Demuth, Speaker of the Minnesota House and candidate for governor, rallying the troops ahead of some door knocking and leafleting. LEE CARTER: THE SUMMER POLLS MISSED THE POINT: VOTERS ARE MOVING — AND THE MIDTERMS BEGIN Demuth is running against sitting senator Amy Klobuchar for governor as the Minnesota Democrats play a high stakes game of political musical chairs, in which poor Gov. Tim Walz has already lost his seat. "We have heard from Minnesotans across the state," Demuth told Fox News Digital, "when we’ve been traveling, that they are ready for a change, it's nice to see the polling start to reflect that, but we were hearing voters ready for a change, ending fraud, making the state affordable, just all the desperate change we have needed." Over the next several weeks, the key question will be whether Minnesota Republicans, and fed-up independents, really believe they can win this time, after decades of Democrat dominance Minnesota’s GOP House Majority Leader, Harry Niska, was also on hand for the 9-3 Vikings victory and offered this explanation to the tightening races: "It’s not a surprise to those of us who have spent months talking to voters in Minnesota as more and more Minnesotans become aware of the billions of dollars that have been stolen from our taxpayers." 'WE HAVE NOT SLOWED DOWN': MINNESOTA NOT OUT OF THE WOODS ON MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL, EXPERT WARNS The fraud that Niska refers to is, of course, the ongoing scandal surrounding the Minneapolis community in the Cedar Riverside neighborhood, that has been bilking tax dollars with fake learning centers and autism care, to the tune of a possible $9 billion, with a "B," dollars. Indeed, the scandal, now long since a national story, was on the tongues of almost everyone I spoke to, of both parties, in the warm afterglow of the Vikings "W" once the canvassers had left to knock upon doors. MINNESOTA'S ANTI-ICE AID FUND BECOMES LATEST CASUALTY OF STATE'S EMBARRASSING FRAUD PROBLEM "It’s infuriating," Tony, in his late 30s, told me, going on to say, "There’s just no rules, and we all pay for it, it's like, how does this even happen?" I met Bill and Laura, who appeared to be longtime friends over a cigarette and they had two distinct takes on the races. Bill told me of Michele Tafoya, "She doesn’t impress me," then suggested, "I just don’t see the makings for an office for [her]." WALZ APPROVAL RATING CRATERS TO LOWEST LEVEL EVER AND TRAILS TRUMP AMID MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL: 'TIRED OF IT' But, when I asked how Minnesotans were feeling about their leadership on the state and federal level, it was Laura, without a beat who insisted, "We’re all very discouraged," prompting Bill to admit that Walz, "Took the opportunity to make choices that were not well conceived." In one dire last comment, Laura shook her head and said, "People are losing hope, man." My longest conversation of the day was with Dan, a smart, well-traveled and worldly man with a lovely little dog named Jasper. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Dan is a Democrat who freely acknowledges that bad mistakes have been made by Democrats in his state, but who sees the GOP as an existential threat, "They want to destroy the country," he told me, "just start with data centers, they just seem to serve these corporations." Dan is skeptical that Tafoya and Demuth can pull of the upsets, and gave me one pretty compelling reason why when he pointed a table of about 8 people, various ages, in their purple and gold and finery, saying, "I promise you every person at that table is a Republican, how many do you think will vote?" "Three," I replied, "Maybe four?" To which he simply said, "Bingo." The flipside to Dan’s turnout argument were the two or three dozen volunteers stomping the suburb for the GOP even as we spoke, and having that kind of ground game as early as September is typically something you see from Democrats, not from Republicans. title: Man scales locked gate in chilling video after allegedly chasing college student home, then walks free: police
description: Security video shows a man scaling a locked gate to follow a UC Berkeley student into her apartment complex after allegedly chasing her home.
content: Chilling surveillance video shows a UC Berkeley student racing through a locked gate as a homeless man allegedly chased her home, only to watch him scale the barrier, enter her apartment complex and remain free while prosecutors decide whether to charge him. The frightening Sept. 15 encounter was captured on security video outside the apartment building in Berkeley, California. The video shows the woman entering the secured complex around 8 p.m. Seconds later, a man climbs over the locked gate and allegedly follows her inside while holding an object initially reported as a knife. VIRAL VIDEO OF HOMELESS ENCAMPMENT AROUND CITY OF BERKELEY SPARKS SAFETY CONCERNS FROM PARENT Berkeley police later determined the object was likely a barbecue lighter and said there was no direct contact between the man and the woman. The student, identified only as Eden for safety reasons, told ABC7 she had been walking her dog on Berkeley Way when the man made strange gestures, approached her and then began running toward her. She made it inside the complex and reached an elevator before he could see where she went, according to the outlet. "I shut the gate behind me, heard him and saw him climbing the gate," Eden told ABC7. UCLA SORORITIES HIRE PRIVATE SECURITY AMID TERRIFYING HARASSMENT BY HOMELESS MEN: REPORT The Berkeley Police Department said it received the woman’s call at approximately 8:04 p.m. Patrol officers were handling other high-priority emergencies at the time, including a domestic violence case and a report involving a missing person considered at risk. Eden told ABC7 that officers arrived about an hour later but were unable to locate the man. The next night, at approximately 9:24 p.m., police received another call reporting that the same man was lying on a sidewalk near Berkeley Way and Walnut Street. Officers responded, detained and identified him, according to the department. Police confirmed that he was the person involved in the previous night’s alleged trespassing but did not arrest him. FEDERAL JUDGE TIES ICE AGENTS' HANDS WITH RULING ON WARRANTLESS SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ARRESTS The department said California law generally prevents officers from making a warrantless arrest for a misdemeanor that did not occur in their presence. Because the alleged trespassing had happened the day before, officers said they could not arrest the man based solely on that offense. Instead, investigators submitted the case to the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office for review. Prosecutors will determine whether criminal charges should be filed. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP ABC7 reported that the district attorney’s office confirmed it was reviewing the case and that no charges had been filed as of Monday. Eden said she was stunned a man could allegedly chase her into a secured building and still walk away after police identified him. She called for stronger laws and greater protections for residents, according to the outlet. UC Berkeley and the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

title: Popular weight-loss drugs face numerous lawsuits over rare ‘eye stroke’ linked to vision loss
description: Hundreds of consumers allege GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy caused NAION, a rare eye stroke linked to sudden, often permanent vision loss.
content: Hundreds of consumers are suing the manufacturers of GLP-1 receptor agonists, alleging the medications may increase the risk of a rare form of vision loss. The patients behind the lawsuits allege that the medications caused NAION (nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy), according to The Wall Street Journal. NAION is a rare eye condition in which blood flow to the optic nerve is suddenly reduced, leading to sudden vision loss. POPULAR GLP-1 WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DEADLY BRAIN DISORDER It is the most common cause of acute optic nerve injury in adults over age 50, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology and the National Eye Institute, which describes it as an "eye stroke." "The problem with NAION is there's no treatment," Dr. Douglas Lazzaro, an ophthalmologist at NYU Langone Health, told Fox News Digital. "So it can cause some very profound vision loss." The companies in question, Novo Nordisk (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) and Eli Lilly (maker of Mounjaro and Zepbound), have disputed the allegations, according to the WSJ report. POPULAR ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION DRUG LINKED TO EYE DISEASE THAT CAN CAUSE IRREVERSIBLE VISION LOSS Novo Nordisk called the lawsuits meritless and pointed to company-funded research finding no increased risk of NAION with its drugs. Eli Lilly said it continues to monitor safety data and maintained that current studies do not prove GLP-1 medications cause the condition. Fox News Digital reached out to the companies requesting comment. What the research suggests Most of the published research to date has examined semaglutide, rather than tirzepatide. In a data analysis of 37 million adults published in JAMA Ophthalmology in 2025, researchers found that people using semaglutide experienced a modest increase in NAION risk compared to people taking SGLT2 inhibitors, another class of diabetes medication. DOCTORS REVEAL HIDDEN DANGER FOR SOME OZEMPIC, WEGOVY USERS WITH BRAIN DISORDERS A 2024 Harvard Medical School study, published in the same journal, found that patients with type 2 diabetes who were prescribed semaglutide had approximately a fourfold higher relative risk of developing NAION. The absolute risk remained very low. The authors of both studies noted that the research was observational and could not prove that the medication caused NAION. They emphasized that more evidence is needed. The FDA has said it is reviewing available evidence regarding a possible association between semaglutide and NAION. The agency has not concluded that semaglutide causes NAION and has not issued a safety warning for semaglutide medications. The European Medicines Agency concluded there is sufficient evidence of a possible association to recommend adding NAION as a "very rare" adverse reaction to semaglutide product information in Europe. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Lazzaro agreed that "whether or not that's statistically significant is hard to assess, because there were so many variables in this and it's hard to exactly match patients." "But when they removed all of what they felt were confounding variables… how obese were the patients, male versus female, age, hypertension, level of obesity… they did find that there was a higher risk of NAION." What to know about NAION NAION typically causes sudden, painless vision loss in one eye, per the AAO. Other symptoms may include blurred or dim vision, loss of peripheral vision or decreased color vision. Symptoms tend to develop first thing in the morning after waking up. The biggest risk factors for the condition include age, diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obstructive sleep apnea and smoking. As many people taking GLP-1 drugs have diabetes or obesity, some of these underlying risk factors could be factors in vision issues, experts note. Diabetes itself is a well-established risk factor for NAION, making it difficult for observational studies to separate the effects of the disease from those of the medication, experts have noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Vision loss from NAION is often permanent. While some patients may regain partial vision over time, there is no proven treatment that can reverse the optic nerve damage. The condition is rare, with roughly two to 10 cases per 100,000 people each year, depending on the population studied. Experts emphasize that patients should not stop taking a prescribed GLP-1 medication without first speaking with their healthcare provider. For many people with diabetes or obesity, the medications' proven benefits may outweigh any potential vision risk. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ When discussing NAION, one important factor is what doctors call a "disc at risk," referring to certain characteristics of the optic disc, or optic nerve. "So if I had a patient who had what I would see on exam is a disk at risk, a very compact optic nerve where everything's crowded, I would tell that patient probably to not go on a semaglutide," Lazzaro advised. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "My overall take on the matter is there's probably a slightly increased risk of NAION when using the semaglutides, but I think the health benefits outweigh the risks," he went on. "And unless I have a patient with a disk at risk, I would probably tell them to go on them if they're going to be a lot healthier from an overall standpoint."

title: Federal judge temporarily blocks deportation of illegal immigrant shot by ICE officer in Austin, attorney says
description: A federal judge has reportedly blocked the deportation of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, who was shot by ICE in Austin during a Sunday confrontation.
content: A federal judge has blocked the deportation of an illegal immigrant shot by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in Austin over the weekend, his attorney said. Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, who represents him, said her office has filed a federal lawsuit on behalf of her client, 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garces Perez. A judge ordered that Perez be present for a Sept. 30 hearing. "That means Wilber cannot be deported in the meantime," Lincoln-Goldfinch wrote on Facebook. "For now, we have secured a temporary block on his deportation while his case moves forward." SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN She added that Perez still requires medical care and "we will continue fighting to protect his rights." He is still in "a lot of pain" and the bullet that struck him is still lodged in his body, she said. Perez, a Venezuelan citizen, was delivering a DoorDash order when he made a U-turn under the highway before ICE agents continued to pursue him. BRANDON GILL UNLOADS ON DEMOCRATS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH RAPING TEEN: 'COLLATERAL DAMAGE' "The truck chased him and sideswiped him again. And the agents came out and shot him in the back of the neck and pulled him out of the car," Lincoln-Goldfinch said. Perez had a final order of removal, authorities said. However, Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client received a removal order after a notice for his immigration hearing was sent to his old address, despite him having updated his address with the court. FEDERAL APPEALS COURT COMPARES TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION POLICY TO JAPANESE AMERICAN INTERNMENT Travis County District Attorney Jose Garza sent a letter Tuesday to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Director David Venturella asking that Garces Perez be allowed to remain in the United States pending an investigation into the shooting. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, and more than 100 other members of Congress also signed a letter to Mullin and Venturella demanding that Perez be released from ICE detention so he can receive medical treatment. ICE OFFICER PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO LYING ABOUT MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING INVOLVING VENEZUELAN MAN The lawmakers also asked that state authorities and law enforcement preserve all evidence from the shooting. "Mr. Garces Perez is a key witness to this shooting, and given ICE's history of obscuring the facts in similar investigations, he must not be removed," the letter said. DOJ CHARGES ICE OFFICER WITH LYING TO INVESTIGATORS FOLLOWING MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING OF VENEZUELAN MAN The ICE officer who shot Perez is a new recruit to the agency but has years of law enforcement experience, including with the U.S. Border Patrol, sources told Fox News. In addition, that unidentified officer wasn't wearing a body camera at the time of the shooting, multiple federal law enforcement sources told Fox News. ICE is supposed to have every officer equipped with cameras by the end of the month. The officer completed the agency’s 256-hour Deportation Officer Training Program in August 2025 before undergoing additional operational and legal instruction through 2026, records show. According to training logs, the officer scored 99.2% on his pistol qualification and completed coursework on use-of-force scenarios, as well as less-lethal tactics involving Tasers, OC spray, and batons. His curriculum also included field operations training and practical exercises covering the entire custody continuum, alongside instruction on warrantless arrests, Title 19 authority, escort and removal procedures, expedited removal and custody procedures. ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY Fox News Digital has reached out to ICE and the Department of Homeland Security. In the wake of the shooting, multiple Democrats have criticized ICE, calling it a "rogue" agency that was "terrorizing our cities and threatening the safety of our residents." title: Kristi Noem takes heat after bagging a massive elk & Keely Hodgkinson's sexy new speedsuit is a talker
description: Kristi Noem bags a massive elk on a Wyoming archery hunt and fires back at online critics, while Keely Hodgkinson debuts Nike's new speedsuit.
content: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. We did it, friends. We made it to fall. Now, I know Joe Kinsey tried to convince you in this morning's Screencaps that preferring autumn to summer is some sort of psy-op. That pumpkin spice is the devil's cocaine. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE But, respectfully, that just sounds like the opinion of someone who lives in northern Ohio. For those of us suffering in the ungodly heat and 400% humidity of the American South, sweater weather can't come soon enough. In fact, today is the first time in nearly a month (26 days) that the temperature hasn't surpassed 90 degrees. I mean, it's still 85. But baby steps. Fun fact: just last week, the largest heat dome on planet Earth was centered right over my home state of Tennessee. I'll let this guy tell you all about it: In other words, it's been miserable. Man, I'm doing so much whining you'd think I was Caleb Williams pulling a hamstring. Point is, I am positively giddy about dropping temperatures, changing leaves, fall hiking and not drowning in a vat of my own sweat. Hell, I might even burn a pumpkin candle — just to get all the haters riled up. Speaking of haters, welcome to Tuesday Nightcaps, where Kristi Noem is taking some online heat for killing an animal. (Not her dog this time, thank God.) But first, we're talking running fashion. Buckle in, kids, and let's do this thing. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Keely Hodgkinson debuts sexy new speedsuit Keely Hodgkinson — an Olympic middle distance runner for Team Great Britain, in case you didn't know — turned some heads at the season-ending Athlos meet in North London on Friday. That's because, while all the other runners were decked out in their standard tiny bottoms and tanks, Keely rolled up in an all black, full-body catsuit. Excuse me, it's a "zero-distraction speed suit," according to Nike. But, respectfully, it was a little distracting. Just check out the aerodynamics on that thing! I personally feel a little vindicated by Keely's look. In the handful of distance races I've done, the "serious" runners always say to me, "How do you run in leggings?!" As if I might as well tape concrete blocks to my feet while I'm at it. And my answer is always the same: how do you NOT run in leggings? See, the way my thighs are set up, running long distance in a pair of shorty shorts would just mean punching a one-way ticket to Chafe-town. Granted, I'm just a casual neighborhood runner — not an Olympic sprinter. So what do I know? This reminds me of that time a couple of years ago when Nike debuted its Team USA track and field kits for the Paris Olympics. The internet freaked out over the "sexist" designs meant to sexualize female track and field athletes instead of equipping them with comfortable and appropriate attire to compete. Turns out, though, what actually happened is that Nike offered the women about 20 different combinations of a uniform — with tops and bottoms of various lengths. The ladies even had the option of wearing the men's kit if it would make them more comfortable. It just so happens, though, that nearly all the female athletes chose to wear the tiny bikini and sports bra combo. So the outrage was entirely overblown. As social media outrage tends to be. I digress. Keely is having none of those front-wedgie-inducing underwears. And I don't blame her one bit. She won the women's 800-meter event wearing that catsuit, by the way. So she might be onto something. Kristi Noem bags a massive elk It's been a rough year for ol' Kristi Noem. First, she was ousted from her role as DHS Secretary. And then came those um... unflattering photos of her husband. Kristi got knocked down. But in the spirit of Chumbawamba, she got up again. And now, she's bagged a massive elk on an archery hunting trip in Wyoming. I can't show you the picture of her and the actual elk because Instagram has deemed it too graphic for embeds. But you can see the gigantic animal she harvested here if you're interested. EVA SHOCKEY SAYS WOMEN DON'T HAVE TO ABANDON THEIR FEMININITY TO BELONG IN THE OUTDOORS You really have to toe the line with hunting content on Instagram. You can post all the dead fish photos you want, but as soon as you show a mammal down, it becomes a whole thing. Last week, I posted a cute little video of NASCAR driver Chase Briscoe talking about his 4-year-old son's love of hunting on OutKick OutDoors. Instagram finally allowed it, but it got shadow banned on YouTube and removed from TikTok for "violating community guidelines." Annoying. Predictably, Kristi has gotten plenty of hate in the comments for harvesting this big, beautiful bull elk. And yes, probably from the same people who have no problem grabbing a Big Mac from the McDonald's drive-thru. Because as long as you don't have to actually see the dead animal you're eating, you can delude yourself into believing you have the moral high ground. Kristi put the critics in their place, calling them "ignorant and uninformed." "Of course this beautiful animal will nourish our family and many others we will share with," she wrote. "These majestic animals are incredible and I’ve so loved learning their ways from my father, sharing memories in the mountains with him and my brothers and now my friends." Kristi concluded: "Shame on you who desecrate and don’t understand the stewardship responsibilities God has given us. Go to a store and shop for anything that hasn’t been harvested and you will find bare shelves and your family will starve." Anyway, who wants elk burgers? title: Bryan Kohberger didn't understand what he was doing when he pleaded guilty: unsealed memo
description: Bryan Kohberger's former attorneys said he struggled to rationally understand court proceedings before his guilty plea in the Idaho murders case.
content: FIRST ON FOX: Bryan Kohberger's former attorneys told an Idaho judge before his plea deal that their client struggled to "rationally understand" what was unfolding in court and to make "consequential decisions" concerning his case, including whether to testify in his own defense or to accept a plea deal, according to newly unsealed court filings. "The memo is pretty clear that there's a serious issue there that shows different reasons why that plea might not have been accepted," Kohberger's new attorney, Greg Rauch, told Fox News Digital. "Those issues have to be flushed out and explored. Although the memo's Tuesday release appeared to have surprised him, he said he initially filed it under seal out of an abundance of caution and to avoid running afoul of previous orders in the case. Kohberger, a 31-year-old former criminology Ph.D. student, is serving four consecutive sentences of life in prison without the possibility of parole, plus another 10 years. Rauch was assigned to his case over the summer and did not represent him as it initially played out. BRYAN KOHBERGER'S BID TO OUST JUDGE AND UNDO GUILTY PLEA MOVES FORWARD WITH NEW COURT DATE SET "In the May 20 [2025] ex parte supplement, counsel advised the Court that Kohberger was having difficulty comprehending adverse rulings and discerning their effect upon the case as a whole," the newly published memo reads. "Counsel represented that, despite the accumulation of significant rulings concerning the death penalty, suppression issues, and motions in limine, Kohberger was having difficulty meaningfully incorporating those developments into a rational assessment of the case and its potential outcomes." In the memo, which was filed under seal in support of a prior motion to disqualify the judge, Rauch described his goal as not to show that Kohberger was incompetent but to bolster his argument that the judge may be biased. "Before June 26, [2025,] the Court knew that counsel was asking for additional time not only to review evidence and continue investigation, but also to investigate Kohberger’s ability to rationally understand and make consequential decisions and to obtain expert assistance in communicating with him about whether to resolve the case short of trial," Rauch wrote to the court in a document that remained sealed for nearly a month. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Kohberger's original defense team sought more time for an inquiry into his ability to understand the proceedings but "expressly denied" that he was incompetent. Judge Steven Hippler on Tuesday ordered the Aug. 27 memo to be unsealed after rejecting Kohberger's reasoning for keeping the document withheld from the public. "The Court disagrees that the information contained in the Supplemental Memorandum is intimate, protected or will result in harm if disclosed," Hippler wrote. "It simply describes in very general terms trial counsel's concerns about Petitioner's difficulty in comprehending adverse rulings and understanding their effect on the outcome of the case." IDAHO JUDGE GRANTS BRYAN KOHBERGER TWO HEARINGS NEXT YEAR AS ADMITTED KILLER SEEKS TO WITHDRAW GUILTY PLEA Kohberger's former defense team, led by Anne Taylor, had sought more time for discovery as his trial approached last year.
