title: Dem AG running for higher office dodges questions on bid to free man who killed pregnant woman
description: Nevada AG and governor candidate, Aaron Ford, ducked questions about his decision to back early release for a man who killed a pregnant woman while out on bond for a series of other violent crimes.
content: FIRST ON FOX: Nevada's Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford is refusing to explain why he personally backed a clemency bid for a convicted killer who took the life of a pregnant woman while out on bail for a series of armed robbery attacks on Vegas tourists, dodging questions on camera as he campaigns to be the state's next governor. State records in Nevada show Ford was listed as the sole sponsor for Norman Smith’s commutation application at a Sept. 16 Nevada Board of Pardons Commissioners meeting. Smith was serving time for killing a pregnant woman in a convenience store parking lot—a crime committed while he was out on bail for a series of armed robbery attempts committed against Vegas Strip tourists, according to court documents and local reporting at the time. Despite Ford's backing, the board ultimately denied the clemency bid, while Ford skipped the commutation hearing that was scheduled and later walked away from a questioner asking him to justify the decision to sponsor Smith's application at a Las Vegas airport. WHITE HOUSE DENIES TRUMP INFLUENCED BY 'PARDON BROKERS' AFTER '60 MINUTES' INVESTIGATION Ford's sponsorship of the convicted killer's early release bid comes as he mounts a gubernatorial run against Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo, who has repeatedly attacked the attorney general's record on public safety and criminal justice reform. When confronted about the sponsorship, Ford's campaign told Fox News Digital the attorney general missed the hearing due to an out-of-state family medical emergency and argued that sponsoring an application is merely a routine procedural step allowing the Board of Pardons to decide on a specific clemency request—but the campaign repeatedly refused to explain why Ford chose to elevate Smith's specific case. "Are you Aaron Ford?" a conservative tracker asked the gubernatorial candidate as he deplaned in Las Vegas after flying to Arizona, the same day as Smith's Sept. 16 commutation hearing. "I am," Ford replied to the tracker, who went on to tell the Nevada Attorney General that she has been "following his stuff" on social media. "Nice to meet you." The tracker continued with small talk until pivoting to a question about the decision to sponsor Smith's clemency bid. "I have a question, are you—you're sponsoring Norman Smith's pardon, right?" BIDEN CLEMENCY BLITZ LEFT DOJ SCRAMBLING AS MANY COMMUTATONS BYPASSED NORMAL VETTING, EMAILS SHOW "Uhh, don't know which one you're talking about, but anyway—good to see you," Ford responded before shuffling away with his wife following their trip to visit their college-aged son who was said to be sick. Fox News Digital pressed Ford's team on what his son was facing in terms of an ailment but was not provided an answer. "Is there a reason why you're pardoning him?" Ford was asked as he attempted to skirt away from the questioner. "Good to see you," was Ford's response before walking away. "Take care." "No reason?" the tracker doubled down. CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM Under Nevada Board of Pardons Commissioners rules, an inmate’s clemency application sits in a queue until one of the board’s nine members—which includes the governor, attorney general, and state Supreme Court justices—chooses to officially sponsor it. By sponsoring Smith’s application, Ford elevated the case out of the administrative queue and onto the official state agenda for a full hearing and vote. Based on a Fox News Digital review of official meeting agendas from 2026, Smith’s application was the only commutation request sponsored by Ford all year. In 2015, Smith was free on bail and facing 14 charges in connection with a series of armed robbery attacks on Vegas Strip tourists when he shot and killed the pregnant woman, Tineshea Adams, according to court documents and reporting at the time from the Las Vegas Review-Journal. Court documents show Smith, who was initially charged with murder but was eventually convicted of voluntary manslaughter and three counts of armed robbery, claimed the killing was the result of self-defense. Smith is currently serving a 10-to-39-year prison sentence. Republican political strategist Matt Gorman slammed Ford's silent airport exit, telling Fox News Digital that the attorney general's refusal to answer speaks volumes. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Aaron Ford was moving faster through that airport than the violent criminals he’s trying to put back on the street," Gorman said. "If Nevada's top law enforcement officer can't even explain why he backed early release for a man who killed a pregnant woman while out on bail for a series of other violent crimes, he has no business asking voters to make him governor." Following publication, Ford's campaign provided a statement to Fox News Digital. "Attorney General Aaron Ford notified the pardon board that he had a family emergency last week and therefore had to miss the meeting," said Ford for Governor spokesperson Prerna Jagadeesh. "Joe Lombardo knew about the family emergency, and his campaign used it to attack Ford — that says a lot about Lombardo's character and the desperate campaign he's running. Pardon board members sponsoring clemency applications to check on the progress of an inmate is standard operating procedure and doesn’t mean a member will vote in favor of said application."

title: Spanberger's data center plan on collision course with her party's green energy push, critics warn
description: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger's data center plan restricts natural gas generation while demanding grid reliability, raising questions about the gap.
content: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger's data center plan is facing criticism that one of its key provisions may work against itself. Limits on on-site natural gas generation could make it harder, not easier, for large data centers to support Virginia's already-stressed electric grid. The stakes are high because Virginia is already struggling to keep up with rapidly growing data center electricity demand, especially in Northern Virginia, where demand is outpacing the expansion of transmission lines and substations. Restricting on-site natural gas generation could make it harder for large data centers to add dependable power at a time when the state is trying to stabilize the grid while also shifting toward cleaner energy sources. WHO PAYS FOR US POWER BOOM? BLUE, RED STATES OFFER STARKLY DIFFERENT WAYS TO LOWER UTILITY BILLS AMID AI SURGE "Everyone recognizes the need for changes in how Virginia engages with data centers. But the governor’s proposal is internally contradictory and raises serious questions about whether it can actually work," Virginia House Minority Leader Terry Kilgore told Fox News Digital. Spanberger’s Data Center Accountability Framework calls for data centers to help stabilize the electric grid while limiting the amount of electricity they can generate from on-site natural gas. Kilgore, R-Gate City, noted that the plan states data centers should source their "own clean power" while at the same time seeking to "limit the amount of electricity data centers can generate from … natural gas." The plan also calls for accelerated clean energy development and prioritizes grid access for data centers that invest in "clean energy" or "further limit on-site natural gas generation." "And if they fail to meet the governor’s preferred energy standards, they could face higher taxes," Kilgore said. "What reliable, dispatchable source of power is supposed to fill the gap? That’s not a political question: it’s how the grid works." A Spanberger spokesperson told Fox News Digital the governor's plan is the "most comprehensive and wide-ranging" in the country and that it aims to protect both Virginia residents and the commonwealth's "natural beauty." "The governor’s plan also ends secrecy around data centers by banning non-disclosure agreements and strengthening local approval," the spokesperson said. "While Gov. Spanberger is pushing to hold data centers accountable — an action polling shows is overwhelmingly supported by Democrats and Republicans — the Trump administration has continued to dismiss the very real concerns Virginians have about data centers’ energy, water and land usage." Spanberger’s plan can still allow data centers to construct on-site power because the framework only restricts the use of that power. She also signed a bill by Del. Rip Sullivan, D-Great Falls, that sharply increased Virginia's goals for energy storage, including a target of 1,600 megawatts of storage capacity at homes and businesses. TEXAS GOV. GREG ABBOTT EFFECTIVELY PAUSES NEW DATA CENTER PROJECTS PENDING STATEWIDE GRID AUDIT Republicans said they found some common ground with Spanberger on the issue, citing public unease about the explosion in data center construction and stress on resources. "I am glad the governor is finally talking about high power bills and data centers. Virginians already are," Senate Minority Leader Ryan McDougle, R-Hanover, said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital. "This should not be a partisan issue." But he also echoed Kilgore’s concern about the plan’s energy-generation dynamics amid looming zero-emissions requirements. "Virginians — Democrats, Republicans and Independents — will tell you the same thing. Their power bills went up. The laws raising electric bills — the tax on carbon, the Virginia Clean Economy Act, solar mandates, and more — should be repealed, and the companies building data centers should pay their own costs," McDougle said. At the same time, some top Democrats criticized their governor’s plan. "The governor is finally feeling the heat but still ignoring the fire," Senate President Pro-Tem L. Louise Lucas told Richmond’s ABC affiliate. Lucas, Portsmouth, said the framework wrongly ignored the need to end tax exemptions for the centers. The debate comes as Virginia is already in the midst of a state-mandated transition away from carbon-emitting electricity generation under the Virginia Clean Economy Act. Under the law, the state’s major utilities generally must retire their remaining in-state generating units that emit carbon by burning fuel by the end of 2045. The law also allows utilities to seek relief from those requirements if compliance would threaten the reliability or security of electric service. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Spanberger’s new framework would push qualifying data centers further in that direction, limiting on-site natural gas generation while prioritizing grid access for facilities that invest in clean energy, reduce backup generator emissions and further restrict their reliance on natural gas. Kilgore’s argument raised new tension. Restricting one source of on-site power before sufficient dependable alternatives are available could create the very reliability challenge Spanberger’s framework says it is intended to prevent. The issue is particularly acute in Northern Virginia, where data center electricity demand is growing faster than the transmission lines and substations needed to serve it can be expanded, according to Loudoun County. In Northern Virginia’s so-called data center alley, officials are already troubleshooting how to stabilize the grid as an explosion in data center construction puts massive sites among densely populated subdivisions. There, Loudoun County leaders say the typical data center requires a continuous supply of 30 to 200 megawatts, enough to otherwise power 200,000 average homes. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The county’s explanation of data center development considerations also specifically lists "natural gas reciprocating engines" as one of the avenues for on-site power, appearing to contradict the push by the governor away from the fuel source. Fox News Digital reached out to Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., for additional comment on the matter because he represents the county in Congress and has been a leading voice in the data center debate. Earlier this month, Subramanyam introduced the National Data Center Plan, which would similarly require data centers to pay for their own energy, analyze their effects on the community, environment and national security before beginning construction. The debate leaves the central dispute over Spanberger’s data center plan unresolved on whether clean generation, battery storage and flexible demand can provide enough dependable power to accommodate Virginia’s rapidly growing data center load as the state simultaneously restricts on-site natural gas generation.

title: Five top takeaways from Trump's high-stakes UN speech to the world
description: Trump told the United Nations General Assembly that Iran can make a deal or face annihilation, while celebrating the Greenland agreement with Denmark.
content: "A lot has happened since we gathered here last year," President Donald Trump said midway through his address to the United Nations General Assembly. No kidding. First there was the Gaza ceasefire and hostage return, then Operation Absolute Resolve that removed Nicolas Maduro from power in Venezuela, and, of course, the deployment of U.S. military and economic power to stop Iran’s "mad dash" for a nuclear weapon. Trump has put American courage and fortitude on display by taking big risks to strengthen the U.S. position—not just for global leadership, but for America’s future. This U.N. speech had its triumphant moments. "Bully no more," Trump said as he touted the battlefield success of Operation Epic Fury. Yet Trump’s serious and formal tone was evidence that this has also been a year that has tested the optimism and tried the patience of both President Trump and the American people. TRUMP DEFENDS US INTERVENTIONS ABROAD AHEAD OF 'BIG DECISION' ON IRAN: 'SETTLING YEARS OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS' Here are five takeaways. 1. Iran’s Choice is a Deal or Annihilation. "Just imagine if such a vile regime were ever empowered to carry out large-scale terror attacks from behind a nuclear shield. This was the reality we had to confront—a reality that far too many preferred to ignore," Trump explained on Tuesday. And the U.N. audience broke into spontaneous applause when Trump vowed again that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. He asked world leaders to stay "united in maintaining pressure" on Iran. But, to no one’s surprise, this speech was also a direct message to the "lunatic clerics" who run Iran, to borrow the phrase from Secretary of State Marco Rubio. SECURITY EXPERT HAILS TRUMP'S GREENLAND PACT AS A 'BIG DEAL' ON PAR WITH ALASKA PURCHASE Iran can make a deal or face annihilation. "I believe we’ll make a deal right after the midterms," Trump said. He’s ever-hopeful, but this is why 50,000 U.S. service members, led by two aircraft carriers, remain in the region under U.S. Central Command. Either way, he said, we "will soon see a world free of the 51-year menace." And indeed, it could go either way. 2. Greenland. Did you see Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen happily nodding during Trump’s remarks? Yes, this agreement that keeps Chinese investment out of Greenland and builds up Pituffik and other Space Force locations was a win-win for American security, Greenland, Denmark and NATO. This deal meant a lot to Trump, and it was smiling faces all around with the president, Frederiksen and Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen at the signing ceremony held immediately after his U.N. address. TOP TRUMP OFFICIAL REVEALS HOW 30-MINUTE MILITARY OP UNLOCKED VENEZUELA OIL WINDFALL FOR US BUYERS 3. The Cartels in the Crosshairs. Trump’s speech delivered two scorching messages reiterating his commitment to the Western Hemisphere. First, Venezuela and the United States together control roughly 22% of the world’s proved oil reserves. Second, Trump said the "cartels are the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere" and decried these "sick, demented adversaries." Put this in perspective: These cartels control more cash than the global jihadis, so expect drug boat strikes to continue. "The United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere. And if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States," Trump warned. 4. Super Intelligence. Not content with renaming lakes, seas and the Kennedy Center, Trump said he wants AI to be called Super Intelligence—or SI. He joked about seeing whether "SI" catches on, but here’s the serious message: The U.S. is ahead of China and will do whatever it takes to achieve supremacy in the global race for tech stack adoption and market share. "Whoever wins SI wins," Trump reiterated. That’s a nice setup for the state visit of China’s Xi Jinping later this week. TRUMP UNLOADS ON TECH TITANS PUSHING FOR SLOWDOWN ON EMERGING INDUSTRY: ‘WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!’ 5. Melania Trump. Considering how little the U.N. has done with Iran or, for that matter, Ukraine, Trump let it off easy. Trump took a few swipes at the U.N. bureaucracy, but he was also courteous about U.N. Resolution 2817 condemning Iran’s attacks on international shipping. Most of all, Trump took time to acknowledge his wife, Melania Trump. On March 2, 2026, she became the first sitting first lady to preside over a meeting of the U.N. Security Council, leading a discussion on children and technology. During the speech, the first lady was seated with Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz, White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. As Trump scanned the audience for her, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer waved to point her out. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION This was a thoughtful gesture, but it was poignant as well. For all the courageous tone, President Donald J. Trump has a lot of work ahead of him. title: Reporter's Notebook: Congress struggles to find a message that resonates with voters ahead of midterms
description: Marshall McLuhan's "the medium is the message" frames a midterms fight where both parties struggle to sell voters on affordability and AI policy.
content: Canadian sociologist Marshall McLuhan famously declared that "the medium is the message." But what if the message is just "medium?" Or, perhaps in today’s vernacular, "mid." Both sides are trying to curate what they say to voters to coax them to vote for their party in November. "The message matters," House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., said on Fox. "We have accomplished a ton. No taxes on overtime. No taxes on tips. We raised the childcare tax credit. The list goes on and on." EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE VANCE'S INTIMATE CAPITOL HILL HUDDLE AS REPUBLICANS CONFRONT TOUGH MIDTERM TERRAIN Those are all vestiges of the "big, beautiful bill," which the Republican-led Congress passed last summer. Now Republicans are scrambling to remind voters what they did. "It was a great message last year, and we missed the opportunity, in my view, to talk about the good things we did last year," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., conceded. But Cramer says voters want to know what you’ve done for them lately. And that’s where the GOP could struggle. "People's rearview mirror is getting shorter and shorter all the time," said Cramer. "What you are going to do for me today is more important to them than what you tried to do a year ago." That’s why some Republicans are frank about their prospects at the polls. "This midterm is going to be a f---ing bloodbath," fumed Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., who is retiring. "I think that both parties know everyone's putting blame on the Republicans right now." Democrats are campaigning on affordability. The cost of groceries and fuel are top of mind. "What's most important to Americans are pocketbook issues," said Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va. "And they see the tariff strategy as punishing our allies and punishing their pocketbooks for no purpose." But Democrats are also stumping on a promise. "The top priority in these next two years is going to be holding Donald Trump accountable," said Colorado Democratic House nominee Melat Kiros. "We'll hold this administration accountable for its corruption," House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., warned. "We will subpoena them if we need to," declared Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash. It’s unclear if threats of presidential probes could dilute the Democrats’ directive this fall. "When you talk about (investigations)," yours truly asked House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., "Does that step on your message in any way about costs?" "No, because there's a cost to the American people around corruption," answered Jeffries. "Which is why the American people are demanding that action be taken and that we hold the crooks accountable." FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS Still, one Democrat says the party is better politically if it sticks to bread and butter issues. "There are a lot of corruption questions," said Sen. Peter Welch, D-Vt. "But I think the gold ring, the brass ring, is focusing on affordability." While Republicans try to remind voters about the "big, beautiful bill," another prominent GOP senator says his party lacks a coherent message. "We're lucky because the Democrats don't have a plan either," said Sen. John Kennedy, R-La. "Here's the strategy for both sides. ‘The other guys are worse than me.’" So, some Republicans are reverting to a wedge issue that worked for them at the ballot box two years ago. "We're going to tell the story about the closed border. I mean, President Trump has the most secure border in our history," argued Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala. But both parties are evaluating a late-emerging issue: artificial intelligence. "In the next 30 days, as we go into this election, Democrats have an opportunity to basically put AI on the ballot," Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., said on MS NOW. Jeffries suggested Republicans are dismissing immediate concerns about AI agents going rogue. "This is a serious thing. It requires urgent congressional action and Republicans are abandoning their responsibility," said Jeffries. "Democrats will not do that." Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, faces a competitive race this fall in the Buckeye State. He tried to blend a sliver of concerns over AI with the "affordability" question last week. The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3. The bill defrays the high utility costs consumers are sometimes forced to pay if they live near data centers. The legislation diverts those bills to Big Tech firms that run the data centers. So, Husted made the case to protect consumers from shelling out extra cash. "If you create the cost, you should pay the cost," said Husted. OBAMA PRIVATELY SOUNDS ALARM ON ‘DANGEROUS’ AI, URGES DEMOCRATS TO PUT ISSUE AT CENTER OF AGENDA But Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., the top Democrat on the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, stood in the way. "It’s not enough for us to tell states to consider making data centers pay for grid updates rather than voluntary pledges or suggestions to states," said Heinrich. "Congress needs to pass real legislation with real teeth." The New Mexico Democrat then objected, blocking Husted’s entreaty on the spot. However, Republicans actually think the move by Heinrich could boost Husted, help Republicans and backfire on Democrats. In other words, a Democratic blockade might assist the GOP make the point that they’re for affordability and the other party is standing in the way. Especially on a bill that passed with such overwhelming support in the House. "Now there's a differentiation between Republicans and Democrats. Republicans are looking out for ratepayers. Democrats are not," said Cramer. Fox is told it’s possible the Senate could try again on the data center-related measure before senators leave the Capitol for the midterms. Another on-the-spot, unanimous consent request would take a matter of minutes to either pass or block the bill (again). But a customary debate accompanied by multiple procedural votes likely consumes a week — even if there’s support for the plan. That said, some lawmakers from both sides wouldn’t mind a roll call vote where they’re documented as supporting the issue. Or a vote where Republicans dare Democrats to go on the record opposing it. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP What that means is that the Senate likely leaves town for the midterms without addressing "affordability." Republicans can blame Democrats — a little. Specifically on the Ratepayer Protection Act. But Democrats aren’t in the majority. They can upbraid Republicans for not addressing some of those pocket book concerns. That’s the "message" ahead of November. As Kennedy suggested, it might fall flat on both sides. Or, as is sometimes said these days, "mid." After all, it is the midterms.

title: Red state Dem faces fury for suggesting illegal aliens should replace American workers
description: Hallie Shoffner said farmers would "trade five Americans just for one" illegal immigrant worker, drawing sharp criticism from Sen. Tom Cotton's campaign.
content: A Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate from Arkansas is facing scrutiny for comments she recently made on a podcast suggesting that illegal alien workers are more valuable than their American counterparts. "I want to talk about the fact that our immigration system is backlogged, bureaucratic and doesn't actually help anybody, including American employers who want folks who want to follow the law," Hallie Shoffner said on the "Free Arkansas Podcast" during an hour-long discussion about a wide spectrum of political issues. Shoffner, a farmer, is running against Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark. in the deep red state. DEM SENATE NOMINEE CHANGES TUNE ON ICE AFTER VOWING NOT 'ONE MORE DIME' FOR AGENCY She continued by saying she had a discussion with a fellow farmer, who she said was a Republican, about foreign labor. "Labor is a huge issue, especially when you don't have a large workforce," she said. "And every farmer will tell you, 'yeah, at one point we did, or still do, employ undocumented immigrants.'" And it's absolutely ridiculous that these folks are being rounded up because they're hardworking people. They're some of the best people we know." "And honestly, we'd trade five Americans just for one of them because of how hard they work," she said. Shoffner then demanded a pathway for illegal aliens to work in the United States legally, claiming "when they're good workers, we pay them well, they're good workers, they spend money here [and] they have family here." Cotton's campaign accused Shoffner of implying that she has hired illegal aliens. OMAR'S NEW LEGISLATION TARGETING ICE SPARKS OUTRAGE WHEN THE INTERNET SEES WHAT'S IN IT: 'UN-AMERICAN' "Hallie Shoffner’s campaign isn’t denying that she employed illegal aliens," campaign spokesman James Arnold told Fox News Digital. "They’re also standing by Hallie Shoffner’s claim that just one illegal immigrant is more valuable than five American citizens." "Every Democrat running for Congress needs to answer if they agree with Hallie Shoffner’s belief that illegal aliens are worth more than Americans," Arnold said. In a response to Fox News Digital, Shoffner's campaign manager Anna-Lee Pittman said the candidate's comments were taken out of context, and accused Cotton of being unwilling to have a conversation to help "fix the immigration system." Cotton, she said, "spends his days combing through video clips of Hallie Shoffner to find any possible inelegant phrase or line that he can chop up to misrepresent an hour-long conversation and present it with no context," noting that "[i]n this response, Shoffner relayed a conversation she had with another farmer about challenges with labor." Shoffner once joined the chorus of left-wing calls to defund U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). DHS ISSUES SCATHING REBUKE AFTER FORMER ATLANTA MAYOR KEISHA LANCE BOTTOMS TOUTS CUTTING TIES WITH ICE "I would vote to defund ICE as it exists right now," Shoffner said in an event June. "Immigration and Customs Enforcement was created not that long ago, and it no longer serves the purpose it was originally created for." "I would not spend one more dime on ICE, because — not just because of the human dignity issue — but also the fact that it is now the largest law enforcement agency in the country," she said. "It has 10 times the budget of the organization that fights child sex trafficking." But in a Facebook post earlier this month, the red state Democratic candidate changed her tune. "I don’t want to defund ICE, I want to reform it," she said. Immigration is a hotbed issue heading into the midterm elections, as it was two years ago during President Donald Trump's campaign to occupy the White House for a second term. The Trump administration has carried out immigration operations nationwide to arrest and deport illegal aliens, drawing blowback from Democrat politicians and activists. title: AOC opens up about race, gender in weighing possible 2028 White House bid
description: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., opened up about how race and gender factor into her 2028 presidential election calculus in a new interview.
content: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., raised concerns during an interview published Tuesday about how her race and gender could factor into a potential 2028 presidential bid. "Pretty candidly, I think about my identity," Ocasio-Cortez said in an interview with The New York Times. "I’m not naïve to the fact that we are living under a very regressive administration, and I happen to be a woman, and I, you know, happen to be Latina. And I think that there’s a lot of conversation about electability, and I don’t kind of shy away from those realities." The progressive congresswoman said of a possible White House run, "I think about it personally." "I am 36, I’m about to turn 37 years old — and what that means for my life," she added. AOC, ASKED ABOUT RUNNING FOR PRESIDENT, SAYS HER AMBITION IS 'WAY BIGGER THAN THAT' "This country has never elected a female president. Why are we pretending that this is not a factor?" she told the Times. "That doesn’t make it impossible, but to act as though it’s not a factor in anything ever is really a form of, like, denialism." Ocasio-Cortez said the discussion around race and gender was often seen as a complaint or excuse. "I often hesitate to even talk about it," she told the outlet, "because people then just register it as an excuse or a complaint." "If you’re asking me about the things that I weigh, of course, that’s part of what I weigh," she told the Times of possibly running for president. "It’s funny because it’s kind of like, everyone else is allowed to talk about it, but I’m not?" HASAN PIKER BRUSHES OFF DEMS WHO SEE HIM AS A LIABILITY, NAMES HIS '28 CHOICE She argued people get defensive when gender is suggested as playing a role in electoral politics. "I experience it tremendously — from the right and from the left," she told the Times. Ocasio-Cortez has been generating 2028 buzz. LinkedIn co-founder and Democratic megadonor Reid Hoffman described the progressive firebrand as "pragmatic." Hoffman made the comments at Politico's Decoded Summit in September, and said former Vice President Kamala Harris would have a "very challenging path" to the nomination. "It depends a little bit," Hoffman said when asked whether he would support Ocasio-Cortez for a 2028 run. "I think she's much more pragmatic than people give her credit for." AOC’S PRIMARY WIN REIGNITES SPECULATION OVER 2028 WHITE HOUSE BID, SCHUMER CHALLENGE Far-left streamer Hasan Piker said he would absolutely campaign for AOC should she decide to run in 2028. Ocasio-Cortez topped a July poll from the University of New Hampshire Granite State. In the poll, AOC was one point ahead of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and 17 points ahead of Harris. The polling average as of Sept. 22, according to the New York Times, has Harris leading with 27%, followed by Gov. Gavin Newsom at 16%, Buttigieg with 10%, and Ocasio-Cortez also at 10%. title: AI robot may stop your dog from barking while you're gone
description: WIM-Z's AI dog training robot uses on-device processing to detect barking and dispense treats autonomously, with field trials showing up to 83% reduction.
content: If your dog starts barking the second you walk out the door, leaving home can come with a little extra guilt. That can happen whether you live in an apartment or a house. A pet camera can show you what is happening, but watching from your phone does little when your dog reacts to every sound outside or gets anxious when you are gone. WIM-Z wants to take a more active role. The small tracked robot uses on-device artificial intelligence to watch your dog and respond to certain behaviors. Once the robot is in position, it can identify your dog, detect barking and decide when to reward calmer behavior with a treat. You can also speak through the robot and drive it around your home from your phone. AI ROBOT FOR SENIORS CAN ALERT FAMILY AFTER A CALL FOR HELP Now WIM-Z has shared early field results, and its first customer units will make behavior and training decisions on their own while owners control where the robot moves. NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com How the WIM-Z AI dog training robot works WIM-Z stands for Watchful Intelligent Mobile Zen. The robot measures about 11 inches tall and rides on rubber tank-style treads. Its camera turret can pan 270 degrees and tilt more than 120 degrees. A side cartridge holds up to 44 treats. Inside, WIM-Z uses a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-8 AI accelerator. The company says its onboard AI can identify individual dogs, classify barking and track a dog with its pan-and-tilt camera. Once WIM-Z detects barking, its behavior system can decide whether to intervene without waiting for you. The robot can then use a calming cue and dispense a treat when appropriate. However, there is an important limit. WIM-Z does not currently drive itself around your home looking for your dog. You control that movement through the app, or you can leave the robot in one location. WIM-Z also includes two-way audio. Its app can show behavior activity and optional highlight clips, giving you another way to see what happened while you were away. WIM-Z says barking dropped by as much as 83% WIM-Z recently released results from seven field trials conducted between May and September 2026. Six took place in homes around the New York metro area. One took place at a kennel in Jersey City. Across the trials, four hand-built robots logged 50 sessions and about 60 hours of use. WIM-Z says the system detected more than 2,100 barks. It also made 107 autonomous interventions and dispensed about 500 rewards. The biggest numbers came from two homes that ran repeat autonomous sessions over two to three weeks. In one home, barking fell from 161 barks per hour to 40, a 75% reduction. In the other, barking fell from 317 barks per hour to 53, an 83% reduction. WIM-Z also reported that more interventions ended with the dogs going quiet as the trials progressed. ROBOT DOG COULD DELIVER YOUR NEXT PACKAGE AND AN AD Why the reward-based approach stands out WIM-Z takes a gentler approach. Instead of using shocks, sprays or scolding, it relies on treats and calm cues to reinforce better behavior. That lines up with guidance from the American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior, which recommends reward-based training and warns against aversive methods. The bigger question is whether the AI can read the situation well enough to respond appropriately. A dog barking at a delivery person is very different from one that is distressed because you left. WIM-Z has to recognize that difference and react at the right moment for the approach to work well. What WIM-Z can and cannot do on its own WIM-Z can handle the behavior side on its own. Its onboard AI can identify a dog, track it with the pan-and-tilt camera, detect barking, decide when to intervene and dispense a reward without you making each decision. What it cannot do yet is navigate your home on its own. You drive WIM-Z from room to room through the app, or you can leave it in one spot where your dog spends time. The first customer units will work this way, combining autonomous behavior and training features with owner-controlled movement. Full self-navigation, where the robot maps your home and goes looking for your dog by itself, remains on the company's roadmap and will not be included in the first units. So, WIM-Z can decide how to respond to your dog, but you still decide where the robot goes. What happens to your video and data? Any mobile robot with a camera and microphone deserves a privacy check before you let it roam around your living room. We asked WIM-Z exactly what happens to the information it collects. The company says all AI processing happens on the robot itself. That includes behavior detection, bark classification and decisions about when to intervene. No video is sent to the cloud for AI analysis. Some information can still leave the robot. Event data such as bark activity, behavior interventions, treat dispensing and battery status are stored on an Amazon Web Services relay server so it can appear in the app's activity history. If you connect remotely, live video and two-way audio stream through WIM-Z's relay using encrypted WebRTC technology. The company says these are live streams to your phone, not recordings, and they are not stored on its servers. Optional highlight clips work differently. Short selected clips can be uploaded for assembly and playback in the app, but WIM-Z says continuous footage is never uploaded. Owners can delete clips at any time or turn the feature off completely. The company says those clips are deleted within 90 days after an account is deleted. WIM-Z also told CyberGuy that it does not sell customer data. Customer footage is not used to train its AI models unless the owner explicitly opts in. When the robot is used only on local Wi-Fi without remote access, the company says nothing leaves the home. We have raised similar questions with other connected home robots because a camera that can move around your house gets access to very private spaces. Those answers give us a much clearer idea of how WIM-Z handles your information. Still, I would review the privacy controls before bringing any connected camera into my home. ONE-WHEELED AI SECURITY ROBOT COULD PATROL YOUR PROPERTY How much WIM-Z costs and when you can get one WIM-Z will cost $799 for the first production units. Right now, the company is taking a fully refundable $99 deposit to hold a spot. WIM-Z told CyberGuy it expects the first batch to ship from late Q4 2026 through Q1 2027. That means the first units could arrive between the end of 2026 and early 2027. The company also acknowledges that hardware schedules can slip. If WIM-Z has not shipped your unit by Q2 2027, it says your deposit will be refunded automatically. WIM-Z says the deposits are held through Stripe and are not placed in the company's operating account. The company says it has built five robots so far. Four are still being used in the field, while another is in Shenzhen, China, for production evaluation with a manufacturer. That gives you a pretty good sense of where things stand. WIM-Z is still in the early stages, so reserving one now means you are getting in before the product has been widely released and used in homes. What this means to you If your dog tends to bark or get restless when you leave, WIM-Z shows where pet tech may be headed next. Instead of simply alerting you that something is happening, the robot can respond while you are away by using a calming cue and rewarding your dog when it settles down. There is one thing to remember with the first version. WIM-Z will not roam around your house looking for your dog by itself. You will need to position it where your dog spends time or drive it remotely through the app. Still, I would not count on a robot to solve serious separation anxiety. The ASPCA says dogs with moderate or severe separation anxiety may need gradual behavior work with an experienced professional. For barking or mild restlessness, though, a robot that recognizes what your dog is doing and responds at the right time could be a useful extra set of eyes at home. The early results are interesting, but I want to see what happens when WIM-Z is tested with many more dogs in different homes. I also want to see how well the first production units perform once customers start using them. For now, WIM-Z has an interesting idea, some encouraging early numbers and a much clearer picture of what buyers will actually get. Kurt's key takeaways WIM-Z caught my attention because it tackles a problem pet cameras mostly leave in your hands. Seeing your dog bark from miles away can make you feel helpless. WIM-Z's onboard AI can make a training decision and reward calm behavior without waiting for you to step in. I also like that the first version keeps movement in your hands. You control where the robot goes, while the behavior and training system can operate on its own. Full self-navigation may come later. Keeping the AI processing on the robot means your video does not need to go to the cloud for behavior analysis. Remote features and optional highlight clips can still send some information outside your home, so you will want to understand those settings. At $799, I would still want to see more testing and hear from real customers once the first production units start shipping. But if WIM-Z can build on these early results, it could become a useful tool for dog owners who worry about what happens after they walk out the door. Would you trust an AI robot to decide when your dog needs a calming cue or treat while you are away? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. title: Granddaughter says grandma rejected MAID before lethal procedure, ‘I don’t want the death shot’
description: Brigitte Stegemann's granddaughter alleges the 83-year-old had no idea she was about to die until she was told a lethal MAID injection was scheduled.
content: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 800-273-TALK (8255). The granddaughter of an 83-year-old Canadian woman who died through the country’s assisted-death program in July says her grandmother had no idea she was about to die until she was told she would be given a lethal injection just days prior. Brigitte Kranendonk, who cared for her grandmother Brigitte Stegemann, says the family cut short a vacation after learning that the long-term care home had scheduled a second MAiD assessment, despite Stegemann previously declining the procedure. "Just before we had come back from our vacation, I received a phone call from the home stating that they had booked a second assessment for MAiD to happen with my grandmother, and at this point my Oma had already denied MAiD," Kranendonk told Fox News Digital in an interview Tuesday. "When we went to the home after our vacation – we did cut it short, we came home, we saw her. She had no idea what was happening." DEMENTIA STOLE MY GRANDMOTHER FROM US. I AM FIGHTING TO GIVE FAMILIES MORE TIME Kranendonk said that she was her grandmother’s primary caregiver and that her family had decided to place Stegemann at The Pearl care home in Cannifton due to physical and mental decline. Her grandmother, however, still had a good appetite and was in good spirits even following a stomach cancer diagnosis, and rejected the idea of using MAiD when it was presented as an option. "She had an opportunity to get an IV port, meaning for injectable medicine. They didn't have to re-poke her every time," Kranendonk said. "It was kind of a one-and-done deal. She had ripped it out several times because she kept saying, ‘I don't want the death shot.’" "And it wasn't until I, face to face, explained it to her that this is not what it is, this is just pain management," Kranendonk added. "That was the scary part is that it felt like she went from screaming, 'I don't want the death shot,' to then accepting MAiD. But only while I was on vacation." EXCLUSIVE: ‘BROKEN COUNTRY’ FILMMAKER WARNS CANADA’S SLOW DECLINE OFFERS CAUTIONARY TALE FOR AMERICANS Stegemann was killed under Canada’s physician-assisted suicide program, called Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD), on July 10. Kranendonk says her grandmother’s first language was not English and that she was severely hearing impaired. "My grandmother's first language is not English," Kranendonk said. "She is severely hearing impaired. And she, her whole life, was terrified of feeling dumb. She never wanted to look as if she didn't understand what was going on. And so when the doctor came in and was explaining MAiD and using very loose terms, like, ‘We're just going to give you medicine, you're not going to feel pain. And don't worry, you won't have a bowel movement,’ my grandma's just sitting there nodding. And I stopped, and I said to her, ‘She doesn't understand what you're saying.’" When Kranendonk directly asked Stegemann whether she knew she would die that Friday, she said her grandmother was visibly shocked and cried for roughly 45 minutes, repeatedly saying, "I made a mistake." NEW YORK NUNS WILL NOT BE FORCED TO COMPLY WITH ASSISTED-SUICIDE LAW WHILE CASE PROGRESSES The doctor had allegedly said Stegemann could "deny" MAiD on the day of the procedure, but Stegemann was already unsure if her grandmother had actually consented to it in the first place. The day the procedure occurred, Kranendonk said the nurse who was administering the IV was not wearing gloves and had a hard time putting it into her right arm, piercing her grandmother many times. "I'm not a nurse," Kranendonk said. "I've never done an IV. I've seen them done before. There was so much blood with this IV. It was all over her arm, it was soaking through her nighty, it was all over the pillow. And it was all over the nurse's hands. And at that moment when I saw all the blood all over the nurse's hands, I realized the nurse was not even wearing gloves." Kranendonk also alleges that Stegemann did not verbally acknowledge the doctor’s final question before the procedure was started. NEW YORK NUNS' CHALLENGE TO ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW IS ABOUT PROTECTING FREEDOM, LAWYER SAYS "And the doctor comes in and says, I can't remember exactly how she worded it, but it was something like, ‘Good morning, Brigitte, are you OK if we proceed with MAiD,’ or, ‘Are you OK if we proceed?’ I can't remember what she asked my Oma. My Oma doesn't say anything. No acknowledgment, no head nod, nothing. Just lying there with her eyes closed. And the doctor says, ‘OK, we're going to proceed.’" Kranendonk said the family is seeking investigations by the coroner’s office, an ombudsman and the long-term care action line. ASSISTED LIVING CENTER SENT RESIDENT TO DOCTOR'S APPOINTMENT AFTER GIVING HIM 18 SHOTS, 5 AM BEER: OFFICIALS "With the investigation with the coroner's office, the ombudsman, the long-term care action line, there's essentially two streams here that we're asking to be investigated under," Kranendonk said. "One is the part of the home, and the part that the home had played in this, and then also the MAiD process. The home had taken it upon themselves to fill out the paperwork, witness and get my Oma to sign off. I don't know what the conversation was that they had with her while she was signing the paperwork, I don't know if she even knew that it was the MAiD paperwork for it." On its website, The Pearl care home in Cannifton, where Stegemann lived, says that it currently has 57 licensed beds with 86 people on the waiting list. title: Yankees' World Series hopes take major hit as Aaron Judge may not be on postseason roster with calf injury
description: New York Yankees star Aaron Judge received a platelet-poor plasma injection in his right calf, and Aaron Boone said he's not expected for the postseason.
content: The New York Yankees may have a Judge-sized hole in their lineup for the postseason. "We’re planning on him not being a part of that, but we’re also at [that] time of the year, you hear all the time with injuries, you give ranges two to four weeks, four to six weeks," Boone said. title: Trump ally skips UNGA for first time — months after face-to-face with president gave way to bitter clash
description: Giorgia Meloni's decision to skip the United Nations General Assembly follows an escalating public feud with Trump over G7 and NATO encounters.
content: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is not attending the United Nations General Assembly this week, an official confirmed to Fox News Digital. Meloni’s decision not to attend breaks with a roughly 15-year stretch in which an Italian prime minister took part in the U.N. General Assembly’s annual high-level debate, according to Associated Medias, although the 2020 gathering was held largely virtually because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Meloni said she will not attend the UNGA, citing a packed schedule after attending six summits in three and a half weeks and saying she had "several dossiers" to handle at home. Meloni’s absence also means the two leaders will avoid another face-to-face encounter after recent international summits put their growing tensions on public display, despite a previously warm relationship. WORLD LEADERS DESCEND ON NEW YORK FOR UNGA — BUT WHO REALLY HAS AMERICA’S EAR? "We believe the United Nations the basic instrument for achieving peace everywhere. Indeed we want a stronger role United Nations, we are present at many initiatives and we have an Italian candidate at the helm of the FAO", Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said ahead of the summit, according to Italian outlet ANSA. "There is great attention from the Italian side." Their spat escalated in June after Trump said Meloni had "begged" him to take a photo at the G7, months after tensions first surfaced publicly when Meloni opposed U.S. military action against Iran and called Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo XIV "unacceptable." The two leaders have long had a warmer relationship than Trump has shared with many other U.S. allies, with Meloni notably the only European leader to attend his 2025 presidential inauguration. In July, Meloni and Trump feuded in the lead up to the NATO summit in Turkey after Trump posted "RESTRAINING ORDER NEEDED," on Truth, alongside a photo of Meloni looking at him. TRUMP-MELONI SPAT GROWS OVER CLAIM ITALIAN PM 'BEGGED' FOR PHOTO: 'ASTONISHED' "Trump's statements against Meloni speak for themselves," Tajani said in July while at a Sky TG24 event. "We are convinced that transatlantic relations go far beyond individual statements." The exchange followed a June interview with Italy’s La7 after the G7, when Trump mocked Meloni over what he claimed was her eagerness to take a photo with him. "She wanted a picture with me so ​badly. I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her," Trump said at the time to La7 TV channel. "She's probably happy I talked to her. I didn't have to talk to her." Meloni fired back: "I can only say it is disappointing that he does not show the same determination with the enemies of the West and of the United States, whose leaders he instead treats with far greater indulgence." RUBIO TO VISIT ITALY, VATICAN AMID TROOP DRAWDOWN CALL, TENSION WITH TRUMP, POPE LEO: REPORTS "There is one thing he should remember: neither I nor Italy ever beg," she added. There have been looming tensions between the two leaders after Meloni distanced herself from the U.S. amid mounting domestic and political pressure over the widening Middle East conflict. Trump also criticized Meloni for failing to assist the U.S. without letting U.S. forces use Italy's landing strips and runways, calling it "a great logistical inconvenience." "She is doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity, possibly because she turned down the United States of America, a Country that truly loves and protects Italy, when it came to denying Iran from obtaining or developing a Nuclear Weapon (But so did NATO, for that matter!)," he wrote in June. content: The sister of missing D.C. mother Antoinette Forbes revealed that she was unaware Antoinette had been in an abusive relationship until details of a 2021 assault surfaced following the arrest of the father of her 10-year-old son. Russell Ashford, 65, who was detained last week in Pennsylvania, reportedly took unauthorized overnight custody of their son on the night Antoinette was last seen, according to the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office. He also allegedly violated his probation stemming from the 2021 assault case, the office said. Authorities did not name Ashford as a suspect in Antoinette's disappearance. "Antoinette did not tell us at all about the assault in 2021, so just wrapping our minds around that, it's unfathomable. We can't really conceive it," Antoinette’s sister, Aileen, said in an interview with Fox News Digital. "I didn't hear about them until I saw some excerpts of the report after my sister went missing." FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE According to Maryland court filings, Ashford pleaded guilty to first-degree assault in 2021. During an argument over their child's schooling, Ashford allegedly threw Antoinette against the staircase, repeatedly punched her while she was lying on the kitchen floor and banged her head against the ground at least a dozen times until she lost consciousness, according to court filings. The assault continued until a neighbor heard her screaming and entered the home to intervene. After Antoinette was taken to a hospital, tests showed she suffered multiple facial lacerations, multiple fractured facial bones, eye damage, a concussion, a broken finger and bruising, court documents said. Prosecutors said the assault left Antoinette with permanent eye and hand injuries. After pleading guilty, Ashford was sentenced to 15 years in prison but served only nine months and five years' probation upon release, authorities said. Aileen said the reports came as a shock to her and her family, who are still processing the revelation. "The report is horrifying. And to tell the truth, I haven't had the time to fully process that. Just the thought of my sister enduring such a brutal attack is just deeply hurtful to me and to the rest of my family. We don't want to, we can't even conceive of it," Aileen said. "Antoinette, she wanted to protect us from it. She did not want us to have any involvement with Russell," Aileen said. More than two weeks have passed since Antoinette was last seen on Friday, Sept. 4, just one week before she planned to take her son to visit their relatives in California, Aileen said. Antoinette was reported missing on Sept. 6 after friends found her dog, car, phone and wallet inside the home, but no sign of her. Shortly after her disappearance, Ashford was arrested for allegedly violating his probation, which strictly prohibited him from having hostile contact with Antoinette or their child, amid the concerning circumstances surrounding Antoinette's disappearance, court documents said. On July 16, 2026, Ashford reportedly arrived unannounced at his son's summer camp, but staff informed him he was not on the approved pickup list and asked for identification. title: Georgia mayor, 23, ousted 10 months after making history as state’s youngest Black mayor
description: Jayden Williams, 23, was removed by the Stockbridge City Council after allegations involving public funds and communications with an 18-year-old student.
content: Georgia's youngest elected Black mayor was removed from office just 10 months after taking the job following allegations that he misused city funds and exchanged sexually suggestive messages and images with an 18-year-old high school student. Jayden Williams, who recently turned 23, was impeached by the Stockbridge City Council in the city south of Atlanta after taking office in January. "The City of Stockbridge confirms that the City Council has taken formal action concerning the Office of Mayor," the city said in a statement on Sunday. "The Mayor has been removed from office." Williams was accused of using his city purchasing card for more than $4,000 in personal expenses, including restaurant meals, clothing, haircuts and a movie, according to Fox 5 Atlanta. He reportedly spent $2,600 on gas and used a city vehicle for personal purposes. MASSACHUSETTS MAYOR CHARGED WITH WIRE FRAUD IN $1.5M COVID RELIEF SCHEME The spending was reported after city workers noticed unusual transactions involving public funds and immediately notified management and the city’s legal team. According to Williams’ testimony, he did not intend to use city funds and later repaid the money, Fox 5 reported. He further claimed the city-issued card looked similar to his personal card and said he later replaced the cards to avoid future confusion, the outlet reported. FORMER DEMOCRATIC MAYOR OF STATE CAPITAL CITY PLEADS GUILTY FOR ROLE IN SIX-FIGURE REAL ESTATE BRIBERY SCHEME Separately, Williams was accused of exchanging sexually suggestive messages and explicit images with an 18-year-old male high school student. A police report noted that Williams did not commit any criminal violations because the student was considered an adult under Georgia law. However, police referred the matter for administrative review over potential policy and ethical concerns about an elected official's interactions with a student in what investigators described as a city-affiliated mentorship program, Fox 5 reported. In a statement, Williams previously said he met the individual before taking office and that the student never participated in the city’s "Mayor for a Day" program, which Williams described as not a mentorship program. EX-MAYOR FOUND LIABLE FOR ALLEGED SEXUAL ASSAULTS OF 7 WOMEN, ORDERED TO PAY $13M "The individual was 18 years old at the time of our communication, meaning we were both adults. I met this individual on November 30, 2025, and our online communication occurred before I was sworn into office in January 2026," he said. Williams became the youngest mayor in Georgia history after campaigning for the position while still attending Clark Atlanta University. title: White House to yank 750,000 fraudsters off ObamaCare, save taxpayers $2.2 billion, Vance says
description: JD Vance says his White House Fraud Task Force will remove 750,000 fraudulent Obamacare recipients, saving American taxpayers $2.2 billion..
content: Vice President JD Vance announced Tuesday that his White House Fraud Task Force will be removing 750,000 fraudulent Obamacare recipients from the program in an effort he says will save U.S. taxpayers $2.2 billion. Additionally, the administration will be employing additional verification for another 419,000 people. "We're going to make sure that they are, first of all, legal residents of the United States of America, and second of all, we're going to make sure that they actually meet the income threshold requirements in order to receive these Obamacare benefits," Vance said. "To put into context the amount of money that we're stopping from going to fraudsters today, $2.2 billion, the average American child receives about $4,000 in health care benefits every single year. That means that we are saving 550,000 American children's worth of healthcare that was going to fraudsters and now will go to the essential services for which it was meant to go." VANCE TO HOST CONGRESS AT WHITE HOUSE TO DISCUSS LEGISLATIVE ACTION ON FRAUD Vance criticized the administration of former President Joe Biden for incentivizing Obamacare fraud, arguing that the administration's incentives for brokers to enroll people in the program, combined with relaxed eligibility for the program, became the perfect recipe for rampant fraud. WHITE HOUSE PUSHES 'WATERSHED' FRAUD-FIGHTING REFORM IN CONGRESS AS VANCE CONVENES TASK FORCE "In one case we found a fraud ring that had 40 agents, 40 brokerage agents who had funneled 50,000 people into the Obamacare system fraudulently. Now, some of those people were probably legitimate. Most of those people were not eligible (because) either they didn't meet the citizenship or the income requirements. Many of those people quite literally didn't even exist." Dr. Mehmet Oz, the administrator for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and a member of Vance's Fraud Task Force, further expanded on the non-existent individuals fraudulently entered into Obamacare. DR. OZ NAMES 5 STATES IN FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS MEDICAID ABUSE "Normally 1%, a single digit, 1% of people who get Obamacare exchange plans do not have a Social Security number," Oz said. "We're supposed to check their tax returns to make sure they're making between one and four times the poverty level, so they're eligible for all of our taxpayers to pay their insurance so they get the discount. Now, if 100% of people coming on the program don't have Social Security numbers, I think we'd all agree there's a problem," he continued. TRUMP ADMIN UNCOVERS 7,100% SURGE IN MEDICARE SKIN SUBSTITUTE CLAIMS, SAYS FRAUD CRACKDOWN BLOCKED MILLIONS Oz then revealed that over 1.1 million people who enrolled in Obamacare this year had no Social Security numbers. He also revealed that 35% of enrollees have never used the program. "They haven't bought a prescription medication. They haven't seen a doctor. That's just not possible. That's at least twice as much as your normal incidence of people having insurance and not using it. So, we know there is fraud," he added. He then detailed the case of convicted fraudster Cory Lloyd, who he said has "a very punchable face." Lloyd and his partner, Stephen Strong, preyed on vulnerable consumers to enroll them in Obamacare in a scheme to collect commission payments from insurance companies, according a February announcement from the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ). "These crooks bribed homeless and jobless people into enrolling in the ACA plans. They had no idea what they were doing," Oz said. Oz read text messages between Lloyd and Strong in which the pair schemed to enroll people who had lost their homes from hurricanes in Florida. "This is the text message. This is ... I can't even say these words on television. But Lloyd said 'it's a killer idea to sign up these poor individuals, make them victims. If it could pull it off. I want to rape the shelters.' And then Strong said, 'ha ha, not kidding. And then Lloyd said 'me either. Let's ef 'em up,'" Oz relayed. The pair were both convicted of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, three counts of wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, according to the DOJ. Strong was also convicted of two counts of money laundering. Both were sentenced to a total of 20 years in prison and ordered to pay $180.6 million in restitution, according to the DOJ announcement. title: Stanley Cup champion coach is down with nuking the preseason: 'Guys just want to play'
description: Rod Brind'Amour says the NHL preseason should be eliminated entirely, arguing Carolina Hurricanes players just want to drop the puck for real.
content: I've been walking around with a pep in my step the last couple of days because after a long, hockey-less summer, the NHL preseason is underway. And while it's great to see all 32 teams back on the ice, there's no denying that the games aren't all that exciting, or even necessary. That's why Rod Brind'Amour, head coach of the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, is in favor of doing away with it entirely. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Guys just want to play. Guys just want to drop the puck and start for real," the Canes bench boss said during an appearance on TSN's "Overdrive" on Monday. "They don't like practicing — nobody does." He's right. Allen Iverson told us years ago that talking about practice is a waste of time. Not a game, not a game... we're talkin' practice, man. Interestingly, this comes as the NHL's latest collective bargaining agreement cut the preseason from six games to four. Those two games were tacked onto the regular season, which now jumps to 84 games. NHL REVEALS THAT A NEW ALL-STAR FORMAT IS ON THE WAY, AND IT SOUNDS LIKE IT COULD BE A WINNER But that's not short enough for Brind'Amour, who thinks it should pound sand altogether, saying that he would prefer not to waste meaningless games on the fans. Besides, the team is picked most of the time anyway. "It's not like even I remember, there were always spots available," he said. "There were 10 guys maybe that you knew were on the team, then there were a couple of guys that were fighting for a spot here. Maybe even a goalie spot might've been open," Brind'Amour said. "That doesn't happen now, hardly ever. The team's picked." They're fair points, and it looks like we're headed in that direction, but I think the preseason is still useful in some ways, primarily as a marketing tool. It allows the league to host some neutral site games in places that would otherwise never see NHL hockey. The Capitals and Flyers played in Hershey, Pennsylvania on Monday, while the Senators and Canadiens played in Trois-Rivières, Quebec. Giving fans a slightly more affordable way to see NHLers is a good way to bring in new fans. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But other than that, with most rosters solidified and bigger names in the press box until the regular season starts, maybe it is time to drop another game or two.

title: Federal indictment handed down in Minnesota related to issue some Dems claim never happens: 'Hotbed for fraud'
description: Mukeshkumar Chaudhari, an Indian national, faces a federal indictment for falsely claiming U.S. citizenship to vote in Minnesota's 2024 election.
content: An Indian national was federally indicted by a grand jury in Minnesota for knowingly making the false claim to be a U.S. citizen to vote in the 2024 general election, prompting pushback online and from an expert who spoke to Fox News Digital. Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari, according to a DOJ press release earlier this month, falsely claimed U.S. citizenship by signing a voter signature certificate required under state law to vote in Minnesota and voting Nov. 5, 2024. "The right to vote is a sacred privilege of American citizenship, and every lawful voter deserves an election system in which that right is protected," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division said in the press release. MN DEM SENATE CANDIDATE'S VIRAL HIJAB VIDEO TAKES NEW TURN AS WOMAN BESIDE HER FACES MAJOR STATE INVESTIGATION "The Department will hold accountable those who knowingly make false claims of citizenship in order to vote. The integrity of our elections depends on ensuring that only eligible citizens cast ballots and that every lawful vote is counted." Dhillon added in a post on X Tuesday that the Justice Department has "indicted or convicted 67 individuals for election related crimes." Earlier this year, Fox News Digital reported that Chaudhari, 39, was facing state perjury and voting violation charges and that he denied he voted when first questioned by authorities but later claimed he "made a mistake" and admitted to voting while also telling investigators he is not a U.S. citizen. Chaudhari, according to investigators, received a voter registration notice from the state of Minnesota in a move that was likely triggered in the system after he obtained his driver’s license. Chaudhari is said to have told authorities that he didn’t learn he should not have voted until his lawyer informed him during his green card process. "Once again, DOJ is proving that if you look for election fraud, you find election fraud," Chad Ennis, vice president of Honest Elections Project, told Fox News Digital Tuesday. "The left loves to claim election fraud does not happen. But here we have yet another instance of a noncitizen illegally registering to vote." News of the federal indictment spread across social media as well, with some users pointing out that numerous elected Democrats in recent years have downplayed the existence of voter fraud. "That thing that never happens," Center for the American Experiment’s Bill Glahn posted on X. DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED "Tim Walz's Minnesota is a hotbed for fraud!" political commentator Eric Daugherty posted on X. Glahn previously spoke to Fox News Digital about his concerns over the lack of safeguards in Minnesota’s voting system, including registered voters being able to "vouch" for up to eight other voters’ residency who want to sign up for same-day voter registration without an ID. "Only U.S. Citizens are eligible to vote in Minnesota," the Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State told Fox News Digital earlier this year, adding that ineligible voting is "extremely rare." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "When an individual completes a voter registration application, they attest that they meet all eligibility requirements, including that they are a U.S. citizen," the office said. "Before casting a ballot, one must again swear to their eligibility before they are allowed to vote. "If a noncitizen attempts to vote in an election, they will be caught and held to account. Penalties for voting while ineligible may include deportation, a permanent bar on future citizenship, a fine of up to $10,000, and up to five years in prison." If convicted, Chaudhari faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison on each of the two counts he faces.

title: Mamdani blasts DoorDash CEO's 'greedy algorithm,' NY slaps company with $131 million settlement
description: Zohran Mamdani announced a historic $131.5 million DoorDash settlement over alleged systematic underpayment of food delivery workers in New York City.
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani blasted DoorDash CEO Tony Xu for encouraging the use of a "greedy algorithm" while announcing the city's historic $131 million settlement with DoorDash over discrepancies in the company's pay to drivers "Two months ago, Tony Xu, the CEO of DoorDash, gave business owners a piece of advice. A CEO, he said, has to take the greedy algorithm and keep going all the way to see if there is more," Mamdani said during a Tuesday news conference, recalling remarks Xu made on a podcast released in July. "In computer science, a greedy algorithm is one that makes the most optimized, best short-term outcome choice at every step and never weighs the consequences. New York City and the tens of thousands of delivery workers who call our city home have reckoned with greed as a business model for far too long," Mamdani continued. "Thousands of them deliver for DoorDash, and thousands of them have felt the human cost of the greedy algorithm," he added. DOORDASH DEACTIVATES DRIVER ACCUSED OF STEALING DHS FOOD ORDERS AFTER VIRAL POST At the news conference, Mamdani announced a historic $131.5 million settlement between DoorDash and the city of New York after the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) discovered that the company was systematically underpaying delivery drivers. Mamdani said the $131.5 million marked the "largest settlement for food delivery workers ever secured in American municipal history." From the settlement, $115 million will go directly back to delivery workers, with some in line to receive up to $5,000. The rest will go toward fines and the development of software that will allow delivery workers to record the DoorDash app and share data about their payment with the city. DOORDASH GETS FAA APPROVAL FOR ITS OWN DELIVERY DRONES "For the first time, workers will have the power to crowdsource data and investigate the black box algorithms that dictate their schedules and pay," Mamdani announced. Under the settlement, DoorDash will also be required to regularly submit delivery worker payment data to the city for three years. AMERICA’S TIPPING CULTURE HAS GONE FROM REWARDING SERVICE TO FEE INSANITY AMERICANS SAY TIPPING PRACTICES 'HAVE BECOME RIDICULOUS' AS DIGITAL PROMPTS PUSH HIGHER GRATUITIES DoorDash admitted to underpaying workers, though claimed it was unintentional. "Simply put, we screwed up," DoorDash said in a statement obtained by the Associated Press. "While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay. We pride ourselves on operational excellence at DoorDash – and this was not excellent, nor was it acceptable. Dashers should be paid in full, on time, every time. We are sorry to the Dashers we let down," the company said. But while the company characterized the underpayments as a slip-up, Mamdani said the company's alleged misconduct was no accident. MAMDANI TURNS ON NEW YORK CITY TEACHERS UNION WITH LAWSUIT BLOCKING PAY RAISES FOR EDUCATORS "For years, DoorDash failed to count every hour worked by delivery workers. This was not a rounding error or an accidental mistake. In 2023, when the city began enforcing a minimum pay rate for delivery workers, DoorDash left time out of the count, time on canceled trips and trips that crossed city limits," he said Tuesday. Fox News Digital contacted DoorDash for further comment on Mamdani's remarks. AMERICA NEEDS TO STOP TURNING EVERY PURCHASE INTO AN UNCOMFORTABLE TIP REQUEST Mamdani's announcement marks the latest in his ongoing crusade against food delivery conglomerates. In January, he announced a $5 million settlement with a group of companies that included Uber Eats for failing to pay drivers minimum wage. title: World’s most contagious virus hits major US airport as officials warn of possible exposure
description: Philadelphia International Airport is tied to a second measles exposure event across multiple terminals amid Pennsylvania's worsening measles outbreak.
content: The City of Philadelphia is reporting two possible measles exposures within a week — the latest at Philadelphia International Airport. The exposure took place at airport terminals B and F, as well as areas used to connect to other terminals in C, D and E, on Sunday, Sept. 13, from 7:45 p.m. to Monday, Sept. 14 at 12:05 a.m., according to the Philadelphia Department of Public Health. The individual with measles was traveling through Philadelphia and did not leave the airport. Health officials encouraged those who were potentially exposed to check their vaccination status and watch for symptoms. MEASLES-INFECTED TRAVELER MAY HAVE EXPOSED PASSENGERS AT LAX AND NEARBY HOTEL, HEALTH OFFICIALS WARN This was the second reported measles exposure in the Philadelphia area, after the first case reported on Sept. 17 at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP). The incident occurred on Sept. 11 at the following locations. The Pennsylvania and Philadelphia health departments, as well as CHOP, reported that they are "working closely to ensure potentially exposed infants receive a preventative antibody product to prevent or lessen severe disease and to take steps to prevent the further spread of measles." MEASLES SURGE HITS NEW MILESTONE AS US CASES SURPASS LAST YEAR'S TOTAL In the second news release, Health Commissioner Dr. Palak Raval-Nelson wrote that this week’s measles exposures are "a reminder of how important it is for all of us to be up to date on our vaccinations." "Every Philadelphian who is fully vaccinated has little to fear from the situation at CHOP and the airport," she said. "Even more importantly, every one of those people is doing their part to help protect our most vulnerable from measles. With outbreaks continuing in Pennsylvania and other places, this is even more important." The health department advised that anyone who has been exposed who is not immune, is unsure of their vaccination status, is an infant, is pregnant and not immune, or is immunocompromised should contact their doctor. "Anyone who develops symptoms should call ahead before visiting a healthcare facility and tell the provider about the possible measles exposure." In August, the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania confirmed two measles-related deaths, marking the first losses related to the virus within the state in 35 years. title: Woman held down, force-fed abortion pills at heart of ‘hell on earth’ fight over Biden-era policy

Ohio doctor Hassan Abbas was sentenced earlier this month for identity fraud and deception to obtain a dangerous drug after prosecutors claimed that he used his estranged wife’s personal information to obtain abortion pills via the mail and force-fed them to his girlfriend, a former patient, after she revealed her pregnancy. The woman says that she did not want to have an abortion and claims she was held down by Abbas as he forced the pills on her. "I write to you today, Attorney General Blanche, to respectfully request that you do everything in your power to ensure this depravity never happens again to a woman and their unborn child," Moreno wrote in a letter obtained by Fox News Digital. FIRST ON FOX: TOP REPUBLICANS TAKE ABORTION PILL FIGHT TO SUPREME COURT, CITING COERCION AND SAFETY RISKS "My constituent was held down and force-fed crushed-up mail-order abortion pills. When she finally physically escaped, she rushed to the hospital where she began hemorrhaging," he continued. "Unsurprisingly, reckless Biden-era mail-in abortion policies are responsible for this hell-on-earth tragedy." The policy in question is a 2023 Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy change initiated by the Biden administration’s FDA that allowed mifepristone, an oral drug used to induce abortion, to be prescribed via telehealth and sent through the mail. Moreno argues that because Abbas was able to obtain the drugs remotely rather than through the previous requirement that mifepristone be dispensed in person at a clinic, medical office or hospital, he was able to use his estranged wife’s identity to obtain the medication. SUPREME COURT KEEPS BROADER ACCESS TO ABORTION PILL MIFEPRISTONE IN PLACE WHILE LEGAL FIGHT CONTINUES "Without ever setting foot inside a pharmacy, Mr. Abbas procured the mail-order abortion drugs fraudulently using his estranged wife’s name," the senator wrote.
