title: Rubio questions ‘point’ of NATO after allies blocked US from using bases during Iran conflict
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says if NATO allies deny U.S. base access during conflicts like Iran, the alliance loses its biggest strategic benefit.
content: Secretary of State Marco Rubio questioned the "point" of NATO Tuesday after saying several allies blocked the U.S. from using military bases on their soil during the conflict with Iran. "We had a couple countries say, ‘You can't use your base here.’ Well, that's absurd," Rubio said on "Fox & Friends." "If we can't use our base when we have a contingency, what's the point of having the base and, frankly, the point of the alliance?" TRUMP VOICES FRUSTRATION WITH NATO, SAYS IRANIAN NAVY ‘DESTROYED’ AS US PREPS FOR BLOCKADE Rubio, who described himself as a longtime supporter of NATO, argued that access to bases across Europe has historically been one of the alliance's greatest strategic benefits for the U.S., allowing American forces to project power globally. "I've been a strong supporter of NATO my entire career," he told co-hosts Ainsley Earhardt, Lawrence Jones and Brian Kilmeade. PENTAGON SLASHES NATO COMBAT COMMITMENTS AS TRUMP PUSHES EUROPE TO DEFEND ITSELF "But I understand that one of the arguments I used to use was that one of the biggest benefits NATO had to the United States were these bases in Europe that allowed us to project power into different parts of the world." "If that's going to be denied to us, then we've lost the biggest reason for us to be in NATO. That's the point we've raised," he added. Though the secretary did not identify which countries denied access in the interview, several NATO allies previously restricted U.S. military access during the Iran conflict. Italy, for instance, denied U.S. bombers landing rights at Naval Air Station Sigonella in Sicily, per a Newsweek report. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The same report indicated that Spain closed its airspace to U.S. planes involved in the conflict. France separately restricted some U.S. military flights carrying supplies to Israel. Rubio acknowledged that some NATO countries had "done more" than others during the conflict, but did not specify which ones. "I hope we've crossed a point where that [resistance from NATO countries] is no longer going to happen. I think we've had more cooperation lately from a number of countries in NATO, so that is positive, but we're still very disappointed."

title: Bills superfan defends OJ Simpson's football legacy after team leaves Juice off its Wall of Fame
description: Bills Mafia members are pushing back after O.J. Simpson was left off the new Highmark Stadium wall of fame, arguing stats should matter most.
content: The Buffalo Bills can attempt to scrub O.J. Simpson from their history, but members of Bills Mafia say they'll never forget what 'Juice' meant to the franchise. At the new Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York, Simpson, a member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame, was left off the team's new Wall of Fame, which honors the greatest players in team history. Sure, there was the messy double-murder trial in which O.J. was acquitted of murdering his ex-wife Nicole and Ron Goldman, but Bills fans argue the Wall of Fame should be based on accomplishments on the field, not drama off it. "His personal life is his personal life," Bills Mafia member Corey Teed told OutKick. "You put all that aside and you just make it about football, O.J. Simpson is the reason we started [putting] names on the wall. If you go back far enough in Bills history and you look, you put all the legal stuff aside, the wife murdered, all that, and you look at football alone, and his stats, as a running back, he was the reason we started putting names on the wall." BILLS FAN PROTESTS OJ SIMPSON WALK OF FAME SNUB, MELANIE GRIFFITH RESPECTS SUMMER & BUFFALO REVEALS A NEW CAGE Teed has a point. Simpson was, in fact, the first member of the franchise to be inducted and remained the only member from 1980 until 1984 when Jack Kemp became the second inductee. "When I came here in my rookie year, I was nervous, didn't have any friends and we weren't winning many games," O.J. said during the induction ceremony in 1980. "But it let me understand that in Buffalo, appreciation comes with respect. It's something you earn. "They were the most valuable years of my life. I'll remember those accomplishments as I live the rest of my life and raise my kids." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. We still give them credit and they're still playing. So, why 40 years later, whatever it is, 30, 20, you're gonna take him off for something that had nothing to do with his personal life?" Rice served 30 days in jail during May and June for violating his probation relating to a 2025 case in which he was sentenced to five years of deferred probation following a high-speed crash in 2024. Multiple people were in the crash in which Rice was driving nearly 120 miles per hour. Teed's opinion isn't controversial in Buffalo. Former Erie County (NY) legislator Betty Jean Grant made headlines last week when she shared similar feelings on O.J.'s omission. "This is an American issue of a man who made Buffalo, who made the Buffalo Bills. Had he not done what he did from 1969 to 1977, the Buffalo Bills would not be here to play in the stadium," she said during a news conference. "They would not be here. He made Buffalo. He built Buffalo, the Rock Pile. He made Buffalo world famous."

title: Impeached Georgia mayor speaks out after sexting, spending scandals result in ouster
description: Ex-Stockbridge, Georgia Mayor Jayden Williams, 23, who was ousted earlier this month, told WSB-TV that he did not expect to be booted out of office.
content: Former Stockbridge, Georgia Mayor Jayden Williams did not expect to be ousted from office earlier this month amid scrutiny over alleged misconduct. "I didn't expect this," he told WSB-TV. "You know, maybe a censure, but definitely not a removal." Williams, 23, who had served in the role for less than a year at the time he was given the boot, was the city's youngest mayor ever. His tenure was cut short amid allegations pertaining to his spending of city funds as well as a relationship with an 18-year-old high school student. GEORGIA MAYOR, 23, OUSTED 10 MONTHS AFTER MAKING HISTORY AS STATE'S YOUNGEST MAYOR Pressed by WSB-TV whether he should have recognized that the relationship was inappropriate, Williams said, "I would have to somewhat agree to that." "There was no violation of the oath," Williams told the outlet. "I wasn't even mayor yet." WSB-TV reported that Williams said the relationship was not sexual. NBC News previously reported that Williams admitted he had exchanged nude photos. "That’s not abnormal for somebody my age," Williams said during a city council meeting, according to the outlet. A police report noted that Williams did not commit any criminal violations because the student was considered an adult under Georgia law. Williams acknowledged spending some funds on personal purchases. He said they were from the mayor's reallocated $5,000 annual budget, not the city's general fund, according to WSB-TV. "It was not intentional and I paid it back immediately," he said. He later replaced the cards to avoid future confusion, the outlet reported. title: It's three strikes and you're out for China. Trump should make this Xi's last chance
description: Xi Jinping arrives in Washington as a diminished leader facing military purges, Huawei turmoil and a stumbling economy ahead of Trump talks.
content: Expectations are low for breakthroughs when Xi Jinping meets President Donald Trump in Washington, D.C., this week. If China remains intransigent during the high-stakes diplomacy, it will be time for America to end decades of dialogue with Beijing. The Trump administration is setting the bar low for the summit. A continuation of last October’s trade truce, reached when the two leaders met in South Korea, is the most that officials are now hoping for. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been talking with a Chinese delegation about an extension. The truce expires Nov. 10. XI PREPARES CHINA ‘FOR BATTLE’ AS EXPERT WARNS OF GRAVE DANGER FACING US AHEAD OF DC SUMMIT The Chinese should be happy with no disruption in the relationship. On Thursday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in the words of China’s Global Times, that "China-US relations have generally moved along the path toward a constructive relationship of strategic stability." Of course, China wants "stability." The Chinese side, in a stable environment, will be able to continue dangerous and unacceptable conduct, such as selling fentanyl, stealing U.S. intellectual property, engaging in predatory trade practices, supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine, maintaining secret police stations on American soil. And helping Iran kill American service personnel in the Persian Gulf. TRUMP SAYS CHINA 'SPIES' ON US AFTER REPORT TIES CHINESE IMAGERY TO IRAN STRIKE China has made its satellites available to that regime for targeting U.S. forces. On March 1, Iran almost certainly used that targeting data to kill six American service members in Kuwait. In July, Iran again relied upon Chinese satellite data to kill three more Americans, this time in Jordan. Washington’s China diplomacy has completely failed. TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS It is not hard to see why. American leaders have been pursuing dialogue with China since the early 1970s, when U.S. diplomats literally chased their Chinese counterparts to set up the summit in Beijing between President Richard Nixon and Chinese Chairman Mao Zedong. America’s ardent desire to maintain dialogue has fed the already inflated sense of self-importance of Chinese leaders. Not surprisingly, this approach over the course of decades has coincided with — and almost certainly been the cause of — a marked deterioration in Chinese behavior. President Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Xi in May and made little discernible progress on contentious issues, so what more can be accomplished now? At some point, the United States needs to lose patience. For one thing, Xi Jinping’s arrogance at the May summit was stunning. On the first day of the event, he publicly mentioned the Thucydides Trap, a reference to a declining hegemon dangerously challenging a rising power. The insult was indirect, but nonetheless unmistakable. BEHIND SUMMIT SMILES, XI GIVES BLUNT WARNING TO TRUMP OF 'CLASHES' AND 'CONFLICTS' Even more insulting, the Chinese leader on the first day talked about the "new era," his phrase for the period in which the U.S. has been pushed to the sidelines and China dominates the world. As Charles Burton of the Sinopsis think tank noted, "Xi views himself as the modern heir of China’s lineage of great emperors, so the concept of fair and reciprocal relations with any foreign country is simply absent from his worldview." Today, Xi is still arrogant, but will arrive in the American capital a diminished figure. That gives Trump leverage, but, on the other hand, it reduces Xi’s room to maneuver. AMERICA HOLDS THE ADVANTAGE AS TRUMP MEETS XI IN HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT "President Trump may not fully appreciate, despite all the pomp and circumstance that he is offering, that he is engaging a Communist Party general secretary whose strength and authority domestically has been considerably weakened by a crisis of confidence in his leadership," said Burton, also a former Canadian diplomat in Beijing. Extraordinary events have been occurring in recent days at the top of the Communist Party. On Monday, the Communist Party announced the expulsion from the ruling organization of the country’s most senior uniformed officer, Gen. Zhang Youxia, and another general on the Central Military Commission, which controls the People’s Liberation Army. The pair was formally charged with corruption, disloyalty and other serious disciplinary breaches. The charges suggest the generals had tried to seize power and depose Xi. title: Trump inks landmark Greenland deal at UNGA after months of tensions
description: Trump, Denmark and Greenland signed a historic Arctic security agreement at the U.N., granting the U.S. permanent military rights on the island.
content: The U.S., Denmark and Greenland formally signed President Donald Trump’s new Greenland security agreement on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly Tuesday, cementing permanent U.S. military rights on the strategically vital Arctic island after months of negotiations over Trump’s push for greater American control. Trump, Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen of Denmark and Prime Minister Jens-Frederick Nielsen of Greenland met Tuesday morning for a trilateral signing ceremony, where the three parties praised each other's defense cooperation over the past 75 years, through World War II and the Cold War. In brief remarks, Trump praised both prime ministers for their efforts in making the deal happen, adding that, "we're going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship, and we look forward to it, and we'll be working very hard and very much in conjunction with each other." Frederiksen expounded upon the strategic importance of the alliance. TRUMP DECLARES VICTORY IN HISTORIC DEAL WITH GREENLAND AS HE SECURES 'PERMANENT' US MILITARY RIGHTS "Mr. President, ever since the Second World War, the United States has defended the free world, created prosperity and progress, peace and freedom, and I am very proud to say that in the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States has a friend that has always kept our word, an ally you have always been able to rely on, and this day represents a milestone in our long-standing cooperation," she said. The U.S. has held extensive military rights in Greenland for decades under a 1951 defense agreement, but administration officials say the new pact goes further by allowing Washington to establish additional military installations without separate Danish or Greenlandic approval, explicitly barring adversaries from establishing a military presence and creating a mechanism to block adversarial investment in sensitive sectors. "This deal is good for the United States, it's good for Greenland, for Denmark, for the NATO alliance, and therefore also good for Europe," Frederiksen continued. "In other words, we are strengthening our common security, boosting our common deterrence, showing our adversaries who we are, and we are doing it together." Nielsen echoed the message. "The world has changed a great deal since 1951," he said. "A notable change is Greenland itself at the table today, signing this agreement, and for Greenland, this is not only an agreement about us, it is a, agreement with us. It takes into account the people of Greenland, our rights, our livelihoods, and the development of our country," he said. He explained that the agreement makes clear where Greenland stands on the world stage — staunchly in defense of the West against adversaries like Russia and China. "The security landscape in the Arctic is changing, and we recognize the long-term security threats that you, Mr. President, have rightly spoken about," he continued. "It is for that very reason that we have insisted on engaging in a constructive dialogue. Greenland matters for North American security and for transatlantic security, and this agreement reflects that we understand our responsibility and act accordingly. And NATO matters. We believe that it's vital to keep NATO strong, also in the Arctic, where the alliance has a key role to play." The new agreement stops short of the territorial acquisition Trump had sought for much of the year, when he repeatedly argued that U.S. ownership of Greenland was necessary for national security and pressed Denmark to relinquish control of the strategically located Arctic territory. Those demands sparked a diplomatic standoff with Copenhagen and Nuuk, where leaders insisted Greenland was not for sale and stressed that its future could be decided only by the Greenlandic people. DENMARK VOWS TO DEFEND GREENLAND AFTER TRUMP REITERATES US SHOULD CONTROL TERRITORY Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, with Copenhagen retaining authority over foreign, defense and security policy while Greenland controls many of its domestic affairs, including mineral resources. The new agreement instead leaves sovereignty unchanged while granting Washington expanded and permanent security rights. Frederiksen has emphasized that the pact recognizes "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom" as well as Greenlanders’ right to self-determination, even as Trump has characterized the agreement as giving the U.S. "permanent control" over Greenland’s security. For Greenland, Tuesday’s signing is also intended to close a turbulent chapter that left residents of the sparsely populated island wondering how far Trump was prepared to go to bring it under U.S. control. Greenland Foreign Minister Múte B. Egede said the agreement respects the government’s longstanding "red lines," including Greenlanders’ right to self-determination, while allowing Nuuk to deepen defense cooperation with the United States and other Western allies. But he acknowledged that Trump’s earlier threats had taken a toll. "The last nearly two years have been challenging for the Greenlandic population," Egede told Greenlandic broadcaster KNR. "Many people have been uncertain. Uncertain about our future." Some Greenlanders remain wary as they wait to see the full agreement. Residents interviewed over the weekend expressed concern about how a larger American military footprint could affect life on the island, while Greenlandic politicians have urged the public to reserve judgment until the final text is signed and released. Frederiksen, meanwhile, sought Monday to draw a firm line between expanded U.S. military access and American sovereignty over the territory. "We are not giving up sovereignty," Frederiksen told Danish media in New York. "You can retain sovereignty and strengthen cooperation with other countries." For the Trump administration, however, the agreement is fundamentally a national security deal — one official argues locks in U.S. access to a strategically vital piece of the Arctic regardless of how Greenland’s political status evolves in the decades ahead. "This historic deal is a huge win for the United States and the American people," Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News Digital when the agreement was announced Friday. "Thanks to President Trump’s vision and leadership, this historic agreement permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer." The "zero cost" refers to the United States making no payment to Denmark or Greenland in exchange for the new rights, a U.S. official told Fox News Digital. Any future construction of military installations or deployment of additional weapons and forces would still carry the normal costs associated with expanding the U.S. military presence. The administration sees Greenland’s location as increasingly important as Russia and China compete for influence in the Arctic and advances in long-range missiles place greater importance on the northern approaches to the continental United States. Greenland already hosts Pituffik Space Base, the northernmost U.S. military installation, which plays a key role in missile warning, missile defense and space surveillance. Administration officials say the new agreement would allow the U.S. to expand beyond its existing footprint and establish additional military installations when needed. The expanded access could eventually support Trump’s planned Golden Dome missile defense system, according to a U.S. official involved in the negotiations. The administration also sought guarantees aimed at preventing China, Russia or other potential adversaries from establishing their own foothold on the island. Under the agreement, non-NATO countries would be barred from establishing military bases or maintaining troops in Greenland. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area," Rubio told Fox News Digital. "This deal permanently and completely addresses our national security concerns in Greenland." Those restrictions extend beyond military installations. The agreement creates a process for blocking adversarial investments in sectors the U.S. considers particularly sensitive, including telecommunications infrastructure, undersea cables, ports and critical minerals. U.S. officials have compared the effort to Washington’s concerns over the Panama Canal, where the Trump administration has sought to reduce Chinese involvement in strategically important infrastructure that officials warn could have potential dual military and commercial uses. The administration argues that locking those restrictions into the Greenland agreement now will prevent a similar vulnerability from developing in the Arctic.

title: Terry Moran says network rejected his Biden health story after he witnessed president’s frailty
description: Terry Moran says ABC News leadership shut down his pitch to report on former President Joe Biden's declining health, telling him the story wasn't his to cover.
content: Former ABC News correspondent Terry Moran revealed Monday that he tried to report on concerns about then-President Joe Biden's declining health — but was promptly shut down by senior leadership at the network. "In late 2023, early 2024, you know, it was pretty clear that Biden was fading rather quickly," Moran told The Daily Beast podcast. "I had actually traveled with him to Japan in the spring of 2023 and kind of eyeballed him there, and I thought, 'Okay, he’s still functioning, but man, he’s frail.’ He looked like he’d blow away in a stiff wind." Moran added that the now-83-year-old former president’s voice was merely a "whisper" by his final year in office. EX-ABC NEWS CORRESPONDENT CLAIMS NETWORK OVERHAULED HIS COVID LAB LEAK REPORT AFTER SENDING COPY TO FAUCI "I tried to do the story of Biden’s health before anybody else did in network, because I’d seen it," Moran said. "And I got shut down very hard." Moran said he sent an email pitch to his editors for a story about Biden’s declining health "gently and as respectfully" as possible. "It was like, ‘You know, this is [a] legit issue for Americans to be interested in,’" Moran said. "I'm not a doctor. I'm not diagnosing. But we all know what we know when we see people fading. We all have had grandparents. We're all getting old ourselves. And so there's no doubt about it, this is a legitimate concern for the voters of America." EX-CBS REPORTER CLAIMS QUESTIONING FAUCI GOT HER 'PULLED OFF AIR' DURING COVID PANDEMIC However, Moran said that ABC News’ leadership allegedly shot down the pitch, telling him the then-president’s health is "the medical unit’s business, not yours." Fox News Digital reached out to ABC News for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Moran — a veteran correspondent at the outlet — left ABC News following a social media post in which he attacked President Donald Trump and White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller. Moran called Trump and Miller "world-class haters" in the now-deleted post on X. "We are at the end of our agreement with Terry Moran and based on his recent post — which was a clear violation of ABC News policies — we have made the decision to not renew," a spokesperson for ABC News confirmed to Fox News Digital at the time. ABC HAS NO BUSINESS ON PUBLIC AIRWAVES BECAUSE IT OPERATES 'LIKE A PARTISAN CABLE NETWORK,’ WATCHDOG TELLS FCC The topic of Biden's health and mental acuity while president received renewed attention following his departure from office, including books and reports alleging that aides concealed the extent of his decline. Some mainstream media outlets have also drawn criticism over their coverage of questions about the then-president's mental acuity, with CNN anchor Jake Tapper and Axios reporter Alex Thompson co-authoring "Original Sin: President Biden's Decline, Its Cover-Up, and His Disastrous Choice to Run Again," which draws on more than 200 interviews and argues that Biden's inner circle concealed signs of decline from the public. Moran's attempt to report on Biden's health — and his account that ABC News declined the pitch — was noted by psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert, who told Fox News Digital the veteran journalist was simply doing his due diligence as a reporter. "Moran was doing exactly what reporters are paid to do: he noticed something and wanted to ask questions about it," Alpert said. "You don’t have to diagnose Biden to report that he appeared different. We make observations about people every day without knowing the medical explanation for them. Saying ‘I see a change’ and saying ‘I know what’s causing that change’ are completely different statements." According to Alpert, it’s "also a very human tendency to avoid information that creates a problem for us," adding that, "sometimes it’s easier not to look too closely and that seems to be exactly what ABC was doing." LIBERAL CNN ANCHOR LASHES OUT AT DEMOCRATS' DECEIT AFTER JILL BIDEN'S ADMISSION ABOUT JOE'S DEBATE SHOWING "I think what ultimately hurts credibility is the gap between what the public thinks is obvious and what an institution is willing to acknowledge," Alpert told Fox News Digital. "The wider that gap gets, the more people start wondering whether they're getting the whole story. A journalist's job is to be willing to ask the questions, even without knowing all the answers." title: Trump Jr under scrutiny from own party over Putin-linked oligarch's lavish gift

title: Federal appeals court orders Missouri to use congressional map rejected twice by Supreme Court
description: A Missouri appeals court ordered use of a GOP-drawn congressional map that splits Kansas City's district, but opponents say ballots are printed.
content: A Missouri appeals court ordered Monday that the state must use a GOP-drawn congressional map in November’s elections, reversing a series of Supreme Court decisions. The St. Louis-based Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals made the ruling Monday, just one day before absentee and mail-in ballots were slated to be sent out to voters. Military and overseas voters have already begun to receive ballots, according to the Associated Press. "This Court holds that Missouri’s current plan to use the 2022 map in the November 2026 general election violates the Constitution. Only use of the 2025 map complies with the Constitution and federal law," Eighth Circuit Judge Stephen R. Clark wrote in a previous decision, which was upheld by the appeals panel in Monday's ruling. The map, drawn by Missouri’s Republican-dominated state assembly in 2025, has already been rejected by the U.S. Supreme Court twice on procedural grounds, most recently earlier this month. ELECTION CHAOS IN THIS RED STATE JUST GOT EVEN STRANGER FOR REPUBLICANS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING The new map splits Missouri’s 5th Congressional District, which encompasses the state’s largest metropolitan area centered on Kansas City, into two districts, likely eliminating one of the state’s two Democratic-leaning districts. Despite numerous challenges, Missouri did use the 2025 map for its August primary elections. An August ruling from a state trial court ruled that a reversion to the 2022 map "would move hundreds of thousands of voters into different districts for the imminent 2026 general election compared to the districts in which they cast their ballots in the August primary elections." The Missouri Association of County Clerks and Election Authorities already announced it won’t be using the 2025 map for November, arguing in an appeal filing that the state does not have enough time to provide new ballots, according to the AP. MISSOURI SUPREME COURT THREATENS SECRETARY OF STATE WITH CONTEMPT AMID INTENSIFYING REDISTRICTING BATTLE Opponents of the redrawn map, like People Not Politicians executive director Richard von Glahn, echoed that sentiment. "Ballots have been printed, and Missourians have already voted. Thousands more will vote before this order seeks to take effect. Officials should stop wasting taxpayers’ money on pointless legal action and instead focus on administering our elections," Glahn said in a statement issued to the AP. SUPREME COURT ALLOWS ALABAMA GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAP FOR MIDTERMS The appeals panel, however, argued that there is precedent to offering new ballots in such a short time period. The panel delayed its ruling from taking place for one week, allowing opponents to appeal to the Supreme Court again. MISSOURI JUDGE HANDS TRUMP, GOP MAJOR REDISTRICTING WIN AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS President Donald Trump has been a strong proponent of the redrawn map, blasting the early September decision by Missouri's Supreme Court to favor the 2022 maps. "The Missouri Supreme Court just ridiculously ruled in favor of changing the maps back to what they were a long time ago. It's called, Ancient History! The problem is, according to Legal Scholars, that not only was the ruling horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional, but there won't be enough time to change the map back with the Election coming up in a very short period of time," Trump wrote in a Sept. 4 post on Truth Social. "The Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America! Missouri must be able to use the map that was in effect just a couple of months ago, in the Primary. This is a Dark Day for 'Justice' in Missouri!" he wrote. title: Presley Gerber dead at 27: What to know about Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber's family
description: Presley Gerber died at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, putting a renewed spotlight on Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber's family.
content: Presley Gerber’s death has put renewed focus on one of the entertainment industry’s most famous families. "Kaia [Gerber] loved that Presley was so open about his struggles; his family was so proud that he was finding strength in helping others." PRESLEY GERBER, SON OF CINDY CRAWFORD AND RANDE GERBER, DEAD AT 27 A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time." Crawford was also part of the "Big Five" supermodels, a group that included Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, Christy Turlington and Tatjana Patitz. Cindy later expanded her career into business, launching beauty, skin care and wellness ventures while continuing to work as a model and brand ambassador. "One thing I’m really looking forward to is being a grandmother," she said. Although Cindy and Rande generally kept those issues private, they publicly supported him when he chose to discuss his experiences. In March, Presley shared a post about undergoing an "ibogaine flood dose" at a wellness clinic in Cancún, Mexico. Cindy commented on the post, writing, "You are a warrior! Walked thru the fire to find yourself! So proud!" Rande also shared a message of support. "I’m so proud of you and your courage," he wrote. title: Sean McVay offers self-deprecating 'dropped mic' response as Los Angeles Rams are back in Super Bowl chase
description: Sean McVay called himself a "dumbass coach" over the Rams' Australia travel plans that preceded their blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
content: The Los Angeles Rams won their first game of the season Monday night and that allows coach Sean McVay to stop beating himself up about the season-opening loss in Australia. McVay, you should know, had been stewing about that loss to the San Francisco 49ers abroad for going on two weeks leading up to Monday night's game. He took it personally, and blamed himself, maybe because he recognized he was part of the problem. McVay finally confessed to that after beating the New York Giants in a game his team showed much more energy and better execution. RAMS' DISASTER IN AUSTRALIA RAISES THE QUESTION: SHOULD THE TEAM HAVE FOLLOWED THE 49ERS THERE EARLIER? Why? "We have the right people," McVay said. "Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn. Sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot. "So there you go. That's a dropped mic." There it is: The haunting trip to Australia, with its unorthodox travel planning, is now in the rearview mirror. The Rams see themselves back on course as a Super Bowl contender. It wasn't, excuse the metaphor, an easy road to recovery because McVay took a while to let go of the Australia experience. He criticized himself afterward for days. He didn't like the way he coached and said, "I didn't do a good enough job getting us ready to go." And days later, McVay's simmering frustration boiled over when he turned his ire on the country where the game was played. "We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope," McVay told reporters. "Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere; that'll get taken out of context." The context is McVay was unhappy with the Rams' travel schedule. And he was unhappy with himself because he had a hand in setting that schedule and definitely was responsible for approving it. The Rams flew 16 hours to Australia and played the 49ers the following day. The team flew overnight out of Los Angeles on Tuesday and landed in Melbourne on Thursday morning local time. The game was played Friday morning local time. NFL ALLOWS STOLEN LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DISGUISED AS A WELCOMING CEREMONY BEFORE AUSTRALIA GAME McVay's goal was to outrun the jet lag by staying completely on Los Angeles time, playing, and immediately flying back home. The 49ers, also a West Coast team, handled it differently. They arrived in Australia six days prior to the game as part of an acclimation strategy. San Francisco 27. Los Angeles 7. The anger, the criticism, and the frustration of missing an opportunity have faded after a victory over the Giants. The players are happy about that. And they're happy to be home. "I thought our guys came out and played great," quarterback Matthew Stafford said. "We played with a bunch of passion, energy, excited to be back home in SoFi." title: Jeffries lashes out after House Dem bolsters Republican candidate on leader's home turf
description: Hakeem Jeffries called Mike Lawler a "partisan hack" after Jared Golden crossed party lines to endorse the Hudson Valley Republican for re-election.
content: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is harshly dismissing a fellow Democrat who publicly undermined his quest to win the majority in Congress — on the left-wing leader's own home turf. Jeffries hit back at Rep. Jared Golden, D-Maine, in a statement to Fox News Digital on Tuesday after Golden endorsed Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., a moderate Republican, for re-election in November. "Mike Lawler is a partisan hack and Trump sycophant who Cait Conley will defeat in November. In desperation, he is peddling an 11th-hour endorsement from a retiring congressmember who represents an out-of-town district more than 400 miles away," Jeffries said. "This smoke-and-mirrors ploy will do nothing to change the outcome of the race. The election will be decided by the people of Westchester and the lower Hudson Valley." OUTGOING HOUSE DEMOCRAT BACKS INCUMBENT REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER FOR RE-ELECTION Jeffries claimed Lawler had "never shown bipartisan courage when it matters" while lauding his Democrat opponent as a "combat veteran and patriot." DEMOCRAT CHALLENGING MIKE LAWLER WON'T COMMIT ON CAMPAIGNING WITH AOC, MAMDANI OR REJECTING DSA "Mike Lawler can try to run from his extremist record. We will never let him hide," he said. But Golden, who has broken from Jeffries multiple times in the past, argued Lawler was among the most bipartisan members of Congress. JEFFRIES THREATENS 'SERIOUS RESPONSE' AFTER DEMOCRATS HELP GOP ADVANCE ANTI-SOCIALISM VOTE "I know how bipartisan Mike Lawler really is. I know something about what that takes. I held the most challenging district of any Democrat in the country by earning the trust of Democrats, independents, and Republicans alike," Golden wrote. "Lawler holds one of just three Republican seats in the country that Kamala Harris carried in 2024. Representing districts like ours forces you to work for people who disagree with you, and it teaches you that those people are not your enemies. They are your neighbors." HOUSE DEMS OVERWHELMINGLY REJECT ANTI-SOCIALISM RESOLUTION AFTER 2 MODERATES DEFY JEFFRIES He pointed out that the nonpartisan Lugar Bipartisanship Index ranked Lawler the fourth-most bipartisan member of Congress in its most recent analysis. "I am leaving Congress in January by my own choice, but I have not given up on the institution, and voters should not either. The Congress we get is the one we elect, and the country needs fewer members who treat the job as a stage and more who treat it as work. In New York's Hudson Valley this fall, that is the choice on the ballot," Golden wrote. Lawler thanked Golden for the endorsement in his own public statement. "While we are from different parties and different states, Jared and I have worked during our time together in the House to find common ground on issues that matter both to us and our constituents," he wrote on X. "We share a firm belief that what’s best for the people should come before one’s party, and that if more members on both sides of the aisle took that approach more often, the country would be better off for it." Lawler is facing long odds of winning a third term in Congress, with most projections favoring Democrats in his district in the New York City suburbs. But Lawler has defied political gravity before, including most recently in November 2024 when his victory split the ticket with ex-Vice President Kamala Harris. DEMOCRATS PUNISH MEMBERS WHO PUT WORKING AMERICANS AHEAD OF PARTY LOYALTY Golden, who is retiring at the end of this year, is known for breaking from his party on a variety of issues. He was one of the only Democrats to praise President Donald Trump's tariff efforts. He also recently made headlines for publicly defying Jeffries by voting with Republicans on a procedural measure called a "rule vote" alongside fellow moderate Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash. While Republican lawmakers have weaponized rule votes in recent years to extract promises from House GOP leaders, it was almost unheard of for Democrats to defy their leaders like that on the other side of the aisle. title: Nolan Wells' friends cleared by grand jury as their lawyers vow to hold online accusers accountable
description: A Mississippi grand jury found Nolan Wells' death consistent with drowning and no evidence of a crime or racial motive in the Horn Island case.
content: After a Mississippi grand jury found that Nolan Wells' death was "consistent with drowning" and turned up no evidence of a crime or racial motive, an attorney for one of the men wrongly targeted online said his client intends to hold the accusers accountable. Wells, 19, disappeared July 4 after taking a boat trip to Horn Island, a barrier island along Mississippi's Gulf Coast, with a group of friends. Search crews combed the area for two days until a National Park Service ranger discovered his remains at the island's northwestern tip on July 6. Months later, a Jackson County, Mississippi, grand jury returned a "no true bill" in Wells' death investigation, meaning no indictment or charges will be filed. "The Grand Jury finds that the position of, the condition of, time of discovery, and location of Mr. Wells' remains is consistent with drowning," the grand jury wrote. In a statement to Fox News Digital, Russell Latino, who represents Bart Edmiston and his family, said: "This story involves two tragedies. SEARCH CALLED OFF AFTER BODY MATCHING MISSING TEEN NOLAN WELLS FOUND OFF MISSISSIPPI COAST "The death of Nolan Wells is a tragedy. So too is the way his friends, his community and his state were maligned by unscrupulous charlatans and grifters who spread false and malicious lies," Latino said. "The grand jury, made up of Mississippians of all races and backgrounds, did its solemn duty. But to anyone who knew the actual facts, not reckless garbage spewed on the internet, the result of the process was never in doubt. The Edmiston family looks forward to bringing accountability to those who exploited tragedy to divide and injure. They continue to pray for healing, for the family of Nolan and for their precious community." Edmiston and other friends of Wells' were subjected to months of online rumors and speculation that they were somehow criminally responsible for the then-18-year-old's death. The grand jury and Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath both concluded those allegations were baseless. Edward Andrew Paltzik, who represents three of Wells' friends, had a pointed message for attorney Ben Crump. "@AttorneyCrump NO TRUE BILL. You should apologize immediately to completely innocent young men Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour. You have some serious explaining to do!" Paltzik said. He said he's also sent several legal notices to social media influencers and media figures on behalf of three men he represents. In a video statement Monday, Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said there was "absolutely no evidence" that Wells' death was due to his race. Fox News Digital has reached out to Crump for comment. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS "The narrative that three White boys and a Black boy went to an island and only three White friends returned spread like wildfire. This was false," McIlrath said. "There is absolutely no evidence to support the allegations that Nolan's disappearance and death were racially motivated." "Nolan's friends loved Nolan and Nolan loved them. Nolan chose to stay on the island that day, and there is not a scintilla of evidence to contradict that," she said. NOLAN WELLS' HOMETOWN OFFICIALS RALLY BEHIND SHERIFF AFTER 'DERELICT IN THEIR DUTIES' ATTACK READ THE GRAND JURY REPORT: McIlrath also sharply criticized attorney Ben Crump's team, which she said knew early on that the death wasn't racially motivated. "The family, the Crump team, and anyone close to Nolan knew that his disappearance and death were not the result of racial hate or violence," she said. "What I am suggesting is that the Crump team knew better but did not do better." SEND US A TIP According to the district attorney, the family's legal team advised her office in August that it had uncovered no evidence a crime was committed against Wells. "On August 13th, 2026, after the Crump team conducted and released the results of its independent autopsy and after receiving hundreds of tips, they advised my office that they had no evidence of a crime being committed against Nolan Wells," she said. CAJUN NAVY LEADER WARNS NOLAN WELLS' SEARCH AREA HAS DEADLY 'WASHING MACHINE' CURRENTS: 'LOTS OF DROWNINGS' Lawyers representing Wells' family disputed the decision in a statement to Fox News Digital. Civil rights attorney Ben Crump said the state was closing the case before the truth had been established, citing bruising on the back of Wells' head and an independent autopsy that he said documented blunt force injuries to Wells' head and back. Crump said neither the family nor the state has determined how Wells died, and he urged the Justice Department to open an investigation if Mississippi declines to do so. "Today, the State of Mississippi is attempting to close the chapter on Nolan Wells’ death without getting to the truth," Crump said. "We are releasing the final independent autopsy report in its entirety, so everyone can read it for themselves. This grand jury result leaves us with more questions than answers. Nolan’s family will not rest until we know what happened to him, and neither will we." LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Both the Mississippi Chief Medical Examiner and the family's pathologist, Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed a second autopsy for the Wells family agreed that while the cause of death is undetermined, "drowning is a diagnosis of exclusion." That means the conclusion was reached by ruling out other causes rather than by direct evidence of drowning. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL The grand jury didn't find any evidence suggesting a crime occurred, or that Wells' death was motivated by race, and also took direct aim at the theories circulating on social media about the people on the boats. GOVERNOR BLAMES ACTIVISTS IN NOLAN WELLS CASE FOR ‘STOKING DIVISION,’ OFFICIAL SAYS FBI PROBING THREATS "The Grand Jury finds no credible evidence to support the public allegations that any persons who rode to or from Horn Island on July 4, 2026, on the Triton, the Palm Beach, or the Tideline engaged in any criminal conduct related to the death of Mr. Wells," the grand jury wrote. "The allegations against the occupants of the Triton, the Palm Beach, and the Tideline are not based in truth, and are solely the result of public clamor and private malice." NOLAN WELLS INDEPENDENT AUTOPSY DOESN'T POINT TO FOUL PLAY, FORMER MEDICAL EXAMINER SAYS Among the many questions surrounding Wells' death was an apparent injury to the back of his head, where bruising was found. A witness testified that he saw Wells slip off a boat, but the grand jury said it could not confirm the fall caused the bruising. CALIFORNIA MAN ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY SENDING BOMB THREAT TO JUDGE IN NOLAN WELLS' DEATH CASE: DOCS "A witness testified under oath that he saw Mr. Wells slip awkwardly off the side of a boat around the time of 3:30 p.m. on July 4, 2026, but could not say whether Mr. Wells struck his head during the fall. The witness testified that Mr. Wells continued to socialize after the fall and did not appear injured," the grand jury report said. title: Jaxson Dart walks off field after injury, creating an instant contrast to Caleb Williams' emotional exit
description: Jaxson Dart walked off the field after a reported MCL knee injury, while Caleb Williams was carted off sobbing over a Grade 1 hamstring strain.
content: Two franchise quarterbacks suffered lower-body injuries in Week 2. One went down with a reported MCL injury to his left knee that could result in him being sidelined for weeks, while the other suffered what is being described as a Grade 1 hamstring strain and, as of this writing, has yet to be ruled out for his team's Week 3 contest. If you had to guess which of the two quarterbacks walked off the field and into the locker room on his own power, you'd go with the second quarterback. If you were forced to pick which of the two was carted off the field and sobbed with a towel over his head, you'd understandably go with quarterback number one. And you'd be wrong. GIANTS' JAXSON DART TRIED TO REENTER GAME WITH KNEE INJURY BUT HAD JERSEY TAKEN AWAY: REPORTS New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart took an awkward, mid-air hit during the first quarter of his team's eventual loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night and did not return to the game. His left knee was forced into a position that knees are not meant to be in, and it was later reported that he was dealing with an issue with his MCL. While early reports indicate that Dart and the Giants have avoided a worst-case scenario with the knee injury, it was a gruesome sequence, but it didn't stop the second-year signal caller from walking off the turf with a slight limp. A quarterback showing his toughness and walking away after a painful injury is a common occurrence, but given what transpired with Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams less than 24 hours earlier, Dart walking off the field created quite the juxtaposition. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Williams went down with a non-contact injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday afternoon, and based on his reaction in real time, it was very easy to assume he had suffered a very serious injury. Williams reached back and grabbed his left leg as he slid to the turf, a typical sign of an Achilles injury, and then rolled around on the field, screaming in pain. The former USC star was then helped onto the back of a medical cart to be taken off the field. As soon as it was revealed that Williams had suffered what was more or less just a pulled hamstring, the emotional scene instantly turned into an all-time great sports meme with folks across social media ripping into the face of the Bears franchise. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Clearly, Williams was both in serious pain and under the assumption that he had suffered an injury that could derail the rest of his season. While that is thankfully not the case, his overly dramatic exit from the game has opened him up to fair criticism.

title: Chicago's half-empty schools reveal a crisis city leaders refuse to confront
description: Pastor Corey B. Brooks explains why Chicago families are fleeing CPS for charter schools as 35% of public schools sit less than half full.
content: On the West Side of Chicago, Frederick Douglass Academy had a grand total of 27 students inside a building that was built for 1,000 students. That is only 2% of the building's capacity. The school was one of 13 Chicago schools that had fewer than 100 students. Across the city, 35% of schools are less than half full. The Chicago Public Schools system has lost more than 77,000 students since 2010. So where are all the students disappearing to? The answer is an indictment of the city and its public school sector. It is true that many families have left the city because of its rising cost of living. I know many Black families who have moved out, and their numbers are in the tens of thousands. It is also true that the birth rate in Chicago has dropped by nearly 50% in less than 20 years. It is not surprising that many graduates choose to leave the city instead of staying and starting families here. NEW YORK CITY'S DECLINING PUBLIC SCHOOL ENROLLMENT PROJECTED TO LOSE OVER 150K MORE AS POPULATION DECLINES But these are not the only reasons why so many public schools are suffering from abysmal enrollment numbers. The children who live on the West Side and South Side did not all disappear. They chose not to go to their neighborhood public high schools. I cannot blame them. Students stuck in these schools tell me they can't learn because the teachers cannot control the rowdier kids. There's a lack of discipline, and rules are hardly enforced. Some students even tell me that some teachers don't even try and just pass the kids. So kids know that if they challenge the teachers and make trouble, they will often give up and award them a passing grade. JONATHAN TURLEY: CHICAGO SCHOOLS REWARD PROTEST WHILE STUDENTS CAN'T READ The students and parents hear all of these stories, and that plays a major role in why they are choosing to enroll in magnet schools, charter schools, parochial schools, and even private schools. CPS still enrolls most of the city's remaining kids, but its share slipped from about 75% to 71%. That is roughly 18,000 children who live in Chicago and chose something else. Parents in Kids First workshops said school quality is one of the reasons families stay or go. And they are right to do so. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’ If we look more closely at the statistics, it is easy to see why so many families have opted out of public schools, especially Black families. In the same district, Black students in selective enrollment high schools are three times more likely to read at grade level than Black students in traditional public schools. When it comes to math, the numbers are even starker. Black students are five times more likely to be proficient in math in selective enrollment schools than their peers in public schools. Parents are seeing the data, and they're voting with their feet. It doesn't help that the Chicago Teachers Union has made a mockery of itself. The head of the union doesn't even send her own children to the public schools that she oversees. The CTU has continued to choose politics over its teachers and schools time after time. In 2025, CTU spent a record $4.2 million on politics and lobbying while spending less than 18% of its total spending on representing teachers. It poured millions into electing Mayor Brandon Johnson, a former CTU organizer. It then used that alliance to freeze school closings and to fight school-choice initiatives that have been a boon to many poor parents. STEVE MOORE, ED POZZUOLI: STOP FUNDING SCHOOL SYSTEMS. LET THE MONEY FOLLOW THE CHILD If it couldn't get worse than that, CTU also helped kill Illinois' Invest in Kids scholarships because they allowed kids to escape the public schools. Not only that, CTU has made the national news several times for using "days of action" to turn kids into activists for whatever left-wing cause is in vogue at the moment. So why would CTU be shocked when families see all of this political activity and instead choose to get the best education for their children? POWERFUL TEACHERS' UNIONS SHARE STRIKING LINK WITH STATES STRUGGLING TO TEACH KIDS TO READ I want to be clear that I'm not here to slander teachers. Many of them are excellent, but they will tell you, as they have told me, that they are trapped in a system that does not allow them to teach to the fullest of their abilities. One told me, "I want to teach algebra, and I want to experience that joy when I see a child struggling at the beginning of the year only to become masterful by the end of the year — I don't want to teach activism." That is why the buildings are empty. The people who run these buildings are largely the problem. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION They have created schools that hold little appeal to families. This is America, a capitalist society, where people will always choose what is best for them. No parent wants to drive that extra hour or pay extra fees or tuition, but they will do so for their child's education. If the public schools want to bring these students back, then they have to buck the existing leadership. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP They have to return to the original purpose of the public schools: to develop young minds into educated, upstanding citizens. The empty buildings are a symbol of how far we have strayed from that original purpose. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM PASTOR COREY BROOKS

title: Dem reactions within moments of Austin ICE shooting spark viral outrage locally, online: 'Disqualifying'
description: Austin Texas Democrats face backlash for attacking ICE before any investigation into the shooting of a suspected illegal immigrant was completed.
content: Democrats in Austin, Texas, are facing criticism both online and from a retired cop who spoke to Fox News Digital after rushing to attack Immigration and Customs Enforcement moments after a suspected illegal immigrant was shot before any investigation had taken place. An ICE officer shot a man in Austin on Sunday and almost immediately, before basic facts had been established in the case, and before the man had been identified as Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, elected Democrats in Austin were speaking out against ICE, including Rep. Greg Casar, Councilman Mike Siegel, and Mayor Kirk Watson. "It is awful that this war has come to our doorstep," Casar, a member of the progressive Squad caucus, said during a Sunday press conference in a clip that was highlighted by the White House Rapid Response account on X. "And as the mayor said, unfortunately it is not a surprise. Just a few weeks ago as we saw the ICE surge come to Austin, especially to north central Austin, I and others said that ICE needed to leave before someone was shot like in Minneapolis or like in Corpus Christi or like in Chicago, and that day is here and so I think the message remains that for Austin to be safe, ICE should end its surge here in our community." BRANDON GILL UNLOADS ON DEMOCRATS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH RAPING TEEN: 'COLLATERAL DAMAGE' Casar and his fellow Democrats quickly sparked viral social media criticism from conservatives accusing the left of selective outrage when it comes to crime, particularly illegal immigrant crime. "Where was the outcry from this guy last fall when an illegal alien in Texas used a machete to behead a man in front of his spouse and child?" Tricia McLaughlin, former assistant secretary of Homeland Security for public affairs, posted on X. "The perpetrator reportedly kicked the head of the victim ‘around like a soccer ball.’ " "There it is," Townhall’s Amy Curtis posted on X. "The Democrats want no immigration laws. They want to destroy this nation. Remember this in November." "This sort of rhetoric should be disqualifying for any elected official," Texas Republican State Rep. Andy Hopper posted on X. "You cannot faithfully take the oath of office and be for open borders. " Dennis Farris, president of the Austin Police Retired Officers Association, told Fox News Digital he expects that kind of rhetoric from Casar and Siegel but was surprised to hear Mayor Watson rush to place blame on ICE both in the press conference and on social media. ‘OUT OF CONTROL’ KILLINGS IN SPANBERGER’S VIRGINIA REACH ‘INSANE’ POINT AS MIGRANT CHARGED IN STABBING SPREE "With Casar, it didn't surprise me, that’s Greg Casar, he's a bomb thrower, he's been a bomb thrower and he's been a reactionary known for shooting his mouth off before he has all the facts," Farris said. "He did that when he was on the city council. He did it in the Mike Ramos shooting. That’s just Greg Casar, He's known for his theatrics." "I've known the mayor a long time, consider the mayor a friend, I was really shocked at how visceral his reaction was, he's usually a lot more measured," Farris said. "I can understand being upset but the way he reacted, I think, raised the temperature in Austin because he is the one that he is, the leader, right? He is the city leader. He's the mayor. He's the one supposed to be trying to keep things calm and I think his reaction yesterday made it worse." Watson’s post was "ratioed" on social media, yielding far more negative comments and quote tweets than positive ones, with locals and internet users accusing him of fanning the flames before the facts were known. "Honestly shocking Mayor @KirkPWatson would issue this sort of statement knowing full well the investigation has barely started, Hope he’s not about to make an Adler-esque 2nd term turn," prominent Austin attorney Adam Loewy posted on X, referencing former Austin Mayor Steve Adler who presided over the 2020 George Floyd rioting in the city. Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of Casar, Watson, and Siegel for comment. Farris rejected Democrat claims that ICE is "surging" in Austin and said that federal immigration authorities, whether ICE or INS, have been conducting deportations in Austin for decades without any fanfare. "They've been arresting people that were in the country illegally and I think what we're seeing here is that the reaction to it is because of Trump, it's the Trump administration doing it and it's just another way to dislike the president for whatever reason you want to dislike him for," Farris said. In the aftermath of the shooting, Austin Police said three people were arrested, several police vehicles were damaged, and two officers were injured after hundreds took to the streets throwing rocks, bottles, and piece of concrete at officers, Fox News national correspondent Brooke Taylor reported. DHS sources confirmed to Fox News on Sunday that Garces Perez is an illegal immigrant from Venezuela with a final order of removal. DHS said Garces Perez illegally entered the United States under the Biden administration. The agency said he was shot during a law enforcement operation. Perez’s attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, claims he was driving for DoorDash when an unmarked truck sideswiped him, chased him and struck his car again before an ICE officer shot him in the back of the neck. He was issued a valid work permit. The issue regarding the deportation order is that he moved and changed addresses. There was a notice for a hearing sent to the wrong address that he missed, which is VERY common. We are working on that. He will be released from detention, his immigration matter will be resolved, and the agencies will be held accountable."

title: SEE IT: Top Dem operative draws line at ‘deplorable’ Hasan Piker after touting party’s ‘big tent’
description: DNC Chairman Ken Martin calls Hasan Piker's comments "disgusting and deplorable" while distancing Democrats from the controversial streamer.
content: Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin distanced his party from far-left streamer Hasan Piker, calling his past remarks "disgusting and deplorable" while defending Democrats as a "big tent" that encompasses a wide range of political views. "Let me just say that I think it's absolutely disgusting and deplorable the things that Hasan Piker has said," Martin said. "But he does not represent the Democratic Party, and he certainly doesn't represent the viewpoints of almost every one of our candidates and our elected officials." Martin made the remarks after Fox News Digital asked how the party is navigating divisions among Democrats as socialist candidates gain prominence, including Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. RASKIN CALLS PIKER’S RHETORIC 'IRRELEVANT DISTRACTION' AFTER THE STREAMER SAID HE'D VOTE FOR HAMAS OVER ISRAEL "Look, no one should confuse unity with unanimity in the Democratic Party, right?" Martin said. "We are a big tent party. We have lots of different viewpoints and ideas and all sorts of issues." Piker has been scrutinized for a slew of past comments critical of Israel — one of his most controversial comments was claiming that the U.S. "deserved 9/11." Martin previously joined other party leaders and prominent Democrats in condemning rhetoric blaming Jewish Americans for threats and violence, calling it "dangerous, wrong, and antisemitic," but his statement did not name Piker. "Criticizing the policies and actions of the Israeli government is one thing," Martin posted to X last month. "Blaming American Jews for the hatred, threats, and violence directed at them is something else entirely. It is dangerous, wrong, and antisemitic." The comments come as El-Sayed, who campaigned with Piker during Michigan's Democratic primary, has sought to distance himself from the streamer as Republicans make their association a midterm attack line. EL-SAYED GRILLED ON PIKER, ISRAEL AND SOCIALIST TIES AFTER MIKE ROGERS SKIPS SENATE DEBATE Martin also called out Republicans for cutting the House’s September session short and leaving Capitol Hill weeks before the midterm elections, telling Fox News Digital there is crucial legislative work that will be left unfinished. Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., announced last week that he was canceling votes scheduled last week and sent lawmakers home one day early ahead of the midterm election recess. Johnson has defended the decision, saying the House had "done its work." "Republicans… they're afraid to actually come to Washington for a whole host of reasons, right?" Martin said. "They've recessed saying mission accomplished six weeks early when they could actually do something to help the American people." "What the hell are they doing? Where are they going? title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror's lawyer torches 'Looney Tunes motion' to investigate him
description: Lindsay Clancy's defense seeks an investigation into the holdout juror, while his attorney fires back calling the motion an attack on the Constitution.
content: Lindsay Clancy's defense team is calling for an investigation into the holdout juror who sought to find her guilty of murder in the strangling of her children and using his refusal to bow to peer pressure to ask a judge to dismiss her charges — prompting a blistering response from his lawyer. "The 'Looney Tunes' motion filed yesterday by Kevin 'Shooter McGavin' Reddington to investigate Michael is not just an attack on Michael for being the courageous lone holdout juror," attorney Edward Paltzik wrote on X Tuesday morning, referring to the holdout, Michael Desronvil. "Reddington's motion is actually a full-frontal attack on the U.S. Constitution," Paltzik warned. "Because if the new normal is that jurors are going to face brutal reprisals for disagreeing with a defense attorney, you can kiss the Sixth Amendment goodbye." LINDSAY CLANCY PROSECUTORS FACE DILEMMA: RETRIAL OR PLEA DEAL IN CASE INVOLVING 3 STRANGLED CHILDREN He warned that if the judge grants defense demands for an investigation into his client it would undermine the American criminal justice system in the long run. "If we follow his destructive proposal to its logical conclusion, we're going to have an endless cycle of prosecutors investigating holdouts who oppose 'guilty' and defense attorneys investigating holdouts who oppose 'not guilty,'" he wrote. "Pretty soon we'll end up with... a retrograde justice system that will look a lot like the Hatfield-McCoy Feud: a cycle of carnage so malignant that its origins will fade in importance, replaced by the hopeless death spiral of the cycle itself." Reddington, in a motion filed Friday, called for a "limited inquiry" into the holdout, for information about his background and potential criminal history, phone records, courthouse surveillance video and more. Neither Paltzik nor Reddington immediately responded to requests for comment from Fox News Digital Tuesday morning. title: Four days in Oxford: Inside the chaotic return of Lane Kiffin to Ole Miss, that turned into pure cinema
description: Inside the circus of Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford: sniper rifles, sixteen state troopers, and a top-ten Ole Miss vs. LSU showdown for the ages.
content: The absolute gem of a weekend in Oxford has come and gone, with a day of college football that could rival anything we’ve seen in recent memory. Ole Miss versus LSU delivered pure cinema, largely because of Lane Kiffin’s dramatic return to Oxford. Now, all sides can move on until the two teams meet again next year in Baton Rouge. While much of the theatrics surrounding Kiffin’s return felt like an attempt to sell tickets to a show that had already sold itself, the weekend still delivered an experience that will be remembered for decades. LANE KIFFIN WALKED BACK INTO OXFORD AS THE MAIN CHARACTER, BUT OLE MISS AND PETE GOLDING STOLE HIS SPOTLIGHT Both Ole Miss and LSU fans will now come to grips with the fact that life goes on, especially during the 2026 season. Next up, the Rebels will travel to Gainesville for a showdown with the Florida Gators, while LSU will host Texas A&M in Baton Rouge with both teams coming off what could turn into consequential losses as the CFP race heats up. But to put a bow on one of the craziest ten-month stretches in college football, it might be best to give you a glimpse of what life was like inside and outside Vaught-Hemingway Stadium last week. LANE KIFFIN’S RETURN TO OLE MISS COMES WITH BETRAYAL, LAWSUITS AND MEMORIES OF HIM TRYING TO BURN IT ALL DOWN A buildup like none other: Oxford was preparing to host what turned into a circus In the best way possible, the town was buzzing just as you'd expect for a top-10 showdown between two SEC teams with such a storied past. Add on the fact that former coach Lane Kiffin was returning to Ole Miss for the first time since he abruptly left the Rebels before their College Football Playoff run, and you had a powder keg of emotions ready to explode with just one lit match. 'HE'S DUST': OLE MISS STUDENTS RIP LANE KIFFIN AS LSU COACH PREPARES FOR HATRED IN OXFORD I first noticed it on Thursday afternoon, while enjoying an afternoon walk around the infamous "Square" that makes up downtown Oxford. As I sat down for lunch inside Ajax Diner, which encompasses all that is good with southern cuisine, I couldn’t help but overhear two gentlemen who were both wearing Ole Miss polos discussing the upcoming showdown. "We really need to win this game," one diner attendee said about the upcoming game. "I can't imagine how that bastard will act if they [LSU] win." In reality, this was one of the more interesting dynamics of the week. The "what if" dilemma that Ole Miss fans were bantering about. Whether that was in the local apparel stores that are located in the downtown area, or the plethora of restaurants within walking distance of the majestic looking government building that sits in the middle of the "Square." I even found myself in the middle of a conversation about the upcoming game while I was filling up my gas tank. ELLA LANGLEY, DISTRACTIONS AND LANE KIFFIN: PETE GOLDING CALLS OLE MISS-LSU ‘HIGH SCHOOL HOMECOMING’ "What ya think man? I just happened to hear you talking on the phone about the game or something you're writing," another Ole Miss asked me while standing at the pump (I guess I was talking a bit loud). We really need to send him a message, but they look damn good as well." As I gave him my reasonings as to why I thought Ole Miss would end up winning the game on Saturday, it was as if I was also calming his nerves of what could potentially be coming. "I like the way you think man. Be careful out here this weekend, it might get a little crazy," the Oxford local politely replied. That's another thing about these college towns that feel as though gets lost on folks who haven’t truly experienced a college football weekend: the buildup with outside noise can be overblown. Why would I assert that? Mainly because noted analyst, or however you'd like to describe his role, Stephen A. Smith made it a point to say he was not attending the game out of fear of what Oxford would turn into on Saturday. The need to overcompensate gameday drama turned out to be overblown I want to make this point very clear: I never once felt my safety was at risk during my time in Oxford. Sure, this would be an atmosphere that most of us had never covered before, with ten months of buildup filled with hatred and verbal jabs. But, it seems as though a lot was made of potential riots or the safety of Lane Kiffin being at risk was done to sell the game for a television rating. In reality, this was an Ole Miss fan base that was pissed beyond measure about an airport exit out of Oxford following the Egg Bowl last season. They were upset that Kiffin would essentially try to burn it down on the way out, after not getting what he wanted in coaching the Rebels during their CFP run. I knew this was going to be a different type of experience as I started my walk to the stadium, with a Louisiana state trooper carrying a bag that contained his sniper rifle. His colleague walked up to a State of Mississippi trooper and politely asked "Hey there, I'm trying to help my guy get his weapon into the stadium. Can you direct me to the right person?" Outside, where the LSU busses would arrive, stood a large walkway fence that would prevent fans from either side getting close to the team and their head coach. Standing next to a colleague, we could hear the police radio detailing LSU's eta to the stadium. "Thirteen minutes out, they are running a little behind. Let's get everyone on the ground prepared," a dispatcher said. At that moment, security workers expanded the blue fence, creating the walkway for LSU's arrival. And just like the ones I would hear on my way back to the AirBnB I was staying at in the area, you could hear the police sirens blaring in the distance. The opposing team, along with their flamboyant head coach, had arrived at 4:49 p.m. central time to a cheers and boos from fans hoping to get a glimpse of Lane Kiffin walking back into Vaught Hemingway Stadium. More than sixteen State Troopers from both Louisiana and Mississippi were in some capacity guarding the Tigers on this day. They lined the walkway in the same manner as they lined the field as the Tigers head coach would make his grand entrance, waving at fans in an awkward way. It was almost as if this was a red-carpet event, with security that would rival the president's entourage. Unfortunately for LSU, they could have used a defense like that during the first half against Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss, as the Rebels held a 24-7 lead at halftime. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Luckily for those watching at home, or the LSU fans that made the trip to Oxford, the Tigers would put together a comeback that provided more drama on the field than anything we witnessed off of it. By now, you've all seen it. Trinidad Chambliss takes one to the house, followed by Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding making the incredible call to go for the two-point conversion that his offense secured. An eight point lead, with LSU getting one final chance to tie it up. As police officers stood in the end-zone watching for any Ole Miss students that would throw objects onto the field, it was the Rebels defense that sent this crowd into one last frenzy as they intercepted LSU's Sam Leavitt to seal the win. Defensive players for the Rebels would run past Lane Kiffin and the LSU staff, pointing and glaring, rightfully gloating about how this on-field show would come to an end. Just as Trinidad Chambliss took a knee to end this magical game, I wondered aloud to a colleague about whether Ole Miss students would storm the field. Turns out on this night, the celebrations would take place in the stands, and I can't say I was disappointed by the fact I wouldn’t have to worry about being trampled while trying to capture the scene. Leaving a stadium that was the epicenter of college football It turned into a cinematic experience. Walking from Lane Kiffin's postgame press conference, following super-agent Jimmy Sexton into the Ole Miss athletic facility for Pete Golding's availability, the Rebels faithful basked in the glory of what they had just witnessed. A jubilant crowd walked around outside Vaught Hemingway Stadium. But, they weren’t waiting to get one final glimpse of Lane Kiffin as he walked to the LSU busses. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE No, students and fans were making their way back to the 'Grove' or the 'Square' to celebrate, while we listened to both coaches discuss this wild showdown. It felt as though there was one big sigh of relief that incapsulated the entire area, knowing Kiffin wouldn’t be leaving Oxford with the win, while also understanding that Pete Golding would be just fine moving forward. Finally, after being on-campus for 14 hours, I finished my story and headed for the parking garage. What was waiting for me back at the AirBnB was on my mind. I had booked this rental not actually investigating its actual location. Turns out, I was staying in what was essentially a college neighborhood filled with condos and townhouses. Just as the day I arrived in Oxford, the southern hospitality was waiting for me at the upstairs guesthouse I rented, with seven Ole Miss students watching highlights on the couch. "Hey dude, that was f—–g awesome. You want a beer man? Come on, have a beer with us!" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP While I appreciated the gesture, and probably could’ve used one or two, I politely passed on the drink The week, which had been building for ten months, had come to an end. And with that, the circus that was the "Lane Kiffin return" could be closed, at least for a year. Once again, the cinema around college football delivered.
