title: Missing Carnival Panorama passenger jumped overboard off Mexico's coast
description: A male passenger jumped overboard from the Carnival Panorama as it sailed from Puerto Vallarta back to Long Beach, triggering a major search.
content: A passenger traveling on a Carnival Panorama cruise jumped overboard as the ship was wrapping up the last full day of a week-long sailing. The cruise departed Long Beach, California, on September 13 and was headed back there from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, when a male passenger jumped overboard, according to the cruise line. "Carnival Cruise Line confirmed Saturday that a male guest aboard Carnival Panorama jumped overboard while the ship was sailing from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico to Long Beach, California," a Carnival Cruise Line spokesperson told Fox News Digital. CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN "When notified of a missing guest, the ship's team initiated search and investigation procedures, including reviewing CCTV footage and notifying both the U.S. and Mexico Coast Guards," the statement continued. The spokesperson said the company is providing support to the family who was traveling with the guest. "Our thoughts and prayers are with them and their loved ones," the statement reads. CARNIVAL CRUISE PASSENGER, 67, FOUND DEAD WHILE SNORKELING OFF THE COAST OF AUSTRALIA DURING EXCURSION According to a Reddit user who said they were aboard the sailing, announcements regarding a missing guest were heard at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. Carnival Panorama had departed from its last port of call on the sail, Puerto Vallarta, at 8 p.m. on Thursday. The call for the missing guest was repeated several times over the next several hours. At about 3 p.m., the ship reportedly turned around. Another announcement was made at about 3:30 p.m. that there would be a shipwide search, and all guests were told to return to their staterooms. Security visited each of the staterooms to scan guests' ship identification cards, which is a standard procedure in the event of a search. An hour later, another announcement suggested the search was continuing, and guests were instructed to remain in their staterooms. At around 5 p.m., the captain and cruise director said the guest had been confirmed overboard after a review of onboard cameras, adding that local authorities would continue the search and rescue operation and guests were no longer required to stay in their staterooms. title: Patrick Clancy in his own words: Top takeaways from grieving father's first interview
description: Patrick Clancy told "60 Minutes" that baby Callan died in his arms after four agonizing days and recalled apologizing to his son in their final moments.
content: Patrick Clancy begged for just one of his children to survive, held baby Callan as he died in his arms and revealed why he forgave Lindsay after she killed their three children. Speaking with correspondent Ross Douthat on CBS News' "60 Minutes," the grieving father shared new details about his children's final moments, what Lindsay told him about the killings and the online attacks he says are hurting their legacy. The interview aired after Lindsay's triple-murder trial ended in a mistrial. Her attorneys argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible, while prosecutors maintained she knew what she was doing. From his desperate plea at the hospital to the online claims that followed the mistrial, Patrick described how the tragedy has shaped every part of his life. PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL ‘Just give me one’ Patrick said he clung to hope that Callan might survive after his siblings, 5-year-old Cora and 3-year-old Dawson, were found dead inside the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts, home. Doctors had restored the baby's heartbeat, and Patrick told Douthat he began imagining the life he could still give his youngest child. "I remember that night, I really thought there was a chance that Callan would live," Patrick said. "And I remember just thinking, ‘Just give me one. Just give me one kid,’" he continued. "And I would raise him as best I could, and I would give him the best life I possibly could. And I'd tell him about his brother and sister." Patrick said that hope faded when he reached Boston Children's Hospital and saw the look on a doctor's face. Callan's heart continued beating for four days. Patrick became emotional as he recalled apologizing to his son and spending his final moments beside him. "I said, ‘I'm so sorry,’" he told Douthat, his voice breaking. "And I got to hold him. I got to lay down next to him. And he died in my arms." While Callan remained in the hospital, Patrick said he held his son's hand and used his free hand to write about all three children. He told Douthat he feared their memories might fade if he did not put them into words. Lindsay never asked for forgiveness The tributes Patrick wrote also included words of forgiveness for Lindsay. He said she has never asked him to forgive her, but he chose to give that forgiveness anyway. LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY "I saw headlines that said, you know, ‘killer mom’ and ‘baby murderer,’ ‘monster,’ and none of them were accurate," Patrick said during the interview. "I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that." Patrick said he also feared anger would consume him if he could not forgive her. "I felt that if I didn't get there, I would be eaten up inside," he said. When Patrick asked Lindsay whether she remembered killing their children, he said she described the memory as dreamlike. LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS "She said it was like a dream, and she remembered it much in the way you would remember a dream after waking up," he told Douthat. Patrick said he did the best he could as Lindsay's condition worsened but must live with what happened. "I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time, and I live with the outcome," he said. "I live with it every day." Grief left him unsure he would survive Patrick told Douthat his grief became so overwhelming that he questioned whether he would live to see another birthday. "There was a time where I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday, and I was completely fine with it," he said. Patrick later left Duxbury for New York City, where he could grieve without being recognized. Five weeks after the move, on what would have been Callan's first birthday, he went to St. Patrick's Cathedral, lit a candle and told his son, "I love you, buddy." "And I walk out on Fifth Avenue and I start crying my eyes out, and nobody cared," Patrick recalled. For Patrick, being able to cry without drawing attention was exactly what he needed. "I thought, this is where I need to be," he said. "I can grieve." His Manhattan apartment remains filled with reminders of the children, including a baby sloth Cora carried everywhere and a photograph of Callan wearing an oversized bow tie, "60 Minutes" showed. Patrick said they also return to him in vivid dreams. In one, Cora walked into the kitchen of the family's former home and hugged him. "I just looked at her and it was like I basically just said, ‘Where have you been?’" he recalled. "Those dreams are so real." ‘Trial by TikTok’ fueled painful attacks The mistrial unleashed what Douthat described as a "trial by TikTok," with online sleuths and influencers spreading baseless theories portraying Patrick as uncaring, unfaithful and even responsible for the children's deaths. "It's deeply harmful to the legacy of my children," Patrick said. "It is a huge distraction from what really matters here, which is perinatal mental health, and it's done real harm to real people." LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS ‘BIG SPIRAL’ AS EXPERT SAYS ONE PART ‘SCARED ME’ IN MOM’S MURDER TRIAL He said the repeated accusations have made it painful to be in public and warned that people may start believing false claims if they see them often enough. "After seeing lie after lie after lie, they start to believe it," Patrick said. "And that's what we're left with." Patrick said he sought answers from Postpartum Support International, psychiatrists and other experts. Those conversations helped him begin processing what happened. A new marriage and keeping his children’s memory alive Patrick's wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, joined him for the "60 Minutes" interview and recalled first learning about his children after noticing their photograph on his phone during a coffee outing. "I just asked, ‘Who are those cuties?’" Danis told Douthat. "And Pat had said, ‘Those are my kids.’" When she asked whether they lived in Massachusetts, Patrick told her they had died. Patrick and Danis met through a New York running club in January 2024. Their relationship deepened as they continued running together, and they married in New York City this April. The couple also discussed starting a family. Asked what he would tell a future child about Cora, Dawson and Callan, Patrick said all of his children would remain part of the same family. "You have different relationships with your kids, but they're all your kids," he said. "And I can't wait to tell them about their brothers and sister." Prosecutors have not announced whether they will try her again.

title: Chad Gilbert, New Found Glory founding member and lead guitarist, dead at 45
description: Chad Gilbert, founding member and lead guitarist for New Found Glory, has died at the age of 45. He had battled adrenal cancer since 2021.
content: Chad Gilbert, the founding member and lead guitarist for the punk rock band New Found Glory, has died. He was 45. The band and the late musician's wife Lisa Cimorelli announced the news of Gilbert's death in a joint Instagram post Saturday. The post did not cite a cause of death, but Gilbert had battled adrenal cancer since 2021, and in February, underwent brain surgery after doctors found tumors. "On the morning of September 20th, Chad Everett Gilbert passed away peacefully in his sleep," they wrote. "He left this world surrounded by friends and family and took his final breaths with his wife and mother by his side, just as he wished." DUNCAN SHEIK, ‘BARELY BREATHING’ SINGER, DEAD AT 56 "We are devastated and shocked by how quickly he left us, yet so grateful for how peacefully and smoothly he went," they continued. "The amount of visitors that crowded the hospital lobby at a moment’s notice is a testament to how beloved and cherished Chad was, and always will be. He was a legendary musician, but his favorite accomplishment was being a husband and father. His biggest dreams came true. He is survived by his wife, Lisa, his daughter, Lily, his mother, Jackie, and his brother, Brian." In their statement, New Found Glory, whose members include lead singer Jordan Pundik, bassist Ian Grushka and drummer Cyrus Bolooki, paid tribute to Gilbert’s lasting influence on the band and the deep personal bond that they shared. "Chad’s guitar playing, songwriting, humor, and relentless drive helped shape New Found Glory for nearly three decades," they wrote. "Through more than a dozen albums, endless tours around the world, and more accolades than we ever could have imagined, Chad challenged all of us to grow as musicians, performers, and human beings." "While we are devastated to lose him, we are so grateful for the incredible life he lived, the memories we shared, and the brotherhood we had. His influence will always be part of New Found Glory and his spirit will be felt on every stage we stand on, with every note we play." 'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE "Rest in peace, Chad. We love you forever," they concluded. Fox News Digital has reached out to New Found Glory's management company Le Grand Music and label Pure Noise Records for comment. Gilbert had been open about his battle with stage 4 adrenal cancer that was first diagnosed in 2021 and later spread to his spine, lungs and brain. He was initially diagnosed with metastatic pheochromocytoma, a rare adrenal gland cancer, in which the tumor grows inside the inner part of the adrenal gland. In a February interview with People magazine, he shared that he began experiencing weakness on the left side of his body and difficulty walking while New Found Glory was promoting its latest album "Listen Up!" After collapsing at home, Gilbert underwent a scan and doctors discovered he had three brain tumors, one of which required emergency surgery. Gilbert later underwent radiation and immunotherapy to treat the two remaining tumors. After the operation, he told People magazine his diagnosis changed to adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), which starts growing in the outer layer of the adrenal gland. JOAN JETT CANCELS REMAINING 2026 CONCERTS AFTER UNDERGOING SURGERY FOR 'FRACTURED VERTEBRAE' In a March Instagram post, Gilbert wrote that his "recovery has been bumpy at times," but that he was "feeling much better now and getting stronger by the day." Gilbert returned to the stage in June, performing with New Found Glory during their tour stop in Nashville, Tennessee. He joined the band onstage to perform a few songs while using a mobility scooter. "I got to play a show in front of my daughter, something I truly never thought I’d get to do again," he wrote in an Instagram post following the show. "And my beautiful wife and all the nurses and doctors, my amazing team that have kept me alive through my battle. It was very emotional getting up on stage with my band again to play. So many feelings all at once." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Gilbert shared daughter Lily, 5, with Cimorelli, whom he wed in 2020. title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror makes new promise as lawyer warns of public attacks
description: Lindsay Clancy's mistrial juror Michael P. Desronvil plans a personal statement while her defense team pursues a double jeopardy dismissal motion.
content: The lone juror who blocked a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s triple-murder trial has promised to tell his story in his own words as his attorney warns that jurors must be allowed to follow the evidence without fear of retaliation. Attorney Edward Paltzik said Michael P. Desronvil, whose refusal to join the other 11 jurors led to a mistrial, will issue a personal statement in the "near future." "Michael will be making a personal statement in the near future, in his own words," Paltzik wrote in a Facebook post. Paltzik thanked those who sent emails, texts and voice messages in support of Desronvil, while acknowledging that others may disagree with the position he took inside the jury room. CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE’S ‘DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD’: ATTORNEY "This country was built on intelligent debate in the public square," Paltzik wrote. "That’s the same reason we support the good faith right of an individual juror to follow the evidence and the law to wherever they take him or her, free from fear of reprisal." LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE INDEFINITELY IMPOUNDS JUROR NAMES, CITING SAFETY AND 'DIVISIVE' ATTENTION The attorney’s latest comments come as the deeply divisive case returns to the national spotlight. Patrick Clancy, the father of the three slain children and Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband, gave his first television interview on CBS News’ "60 Minutes" Sunday night. Patrick Clancy discussed his grief, memories of his children and baseless conspiracy theories that have spread online since the January 2023 killings. His wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, also appeared in the segment with correspondent Ross Douthat. JUDGE JUDY WARNS OF 'DANGER' IF PROSECUTORS DON'T RETRY LINDSAY CLANCY AFTER MURDER TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL Lindsay Clancy, 36, was tried on three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of the couple’s children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. The children were found strangled inside the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. Clancy admitted killing the children, but her attorneys argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argued that the former labor and delivery nurse understood what she was doing and carried out the killings deliberately. LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after seven days of deliberations. The jury was split 11-1, with 11 jurors prepared to find Clancy not criminally responsible and Desronvil holding out for a conviction. Desronvil later said he had no doubt prosecutors proved their case. LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS "Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned," Desronvil said in a statement first reported by NewsNation and confirmed to Fox News Digital by Paltzik. Desronvil said he tried to raise different theories during deliberations but was repeatedly cut off by fellow jurors who treated his questions as uncertainty. LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM The fallout from the mistrial quickly spilled beyond the courthouse, with Desronvil facing intense public scrutiny over his refusal to move off his position. Paltzik, who previously represented President Donald Trump in lawsuits against The New York Times, CBS and ABC News, told Fox News Digital that he is focused on Desronvil’s "health, safety and well-being." He has called the juror an "American Hero" and "Champion of Justice." LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT Former prosecutor and behavioral health law expert Mark Astor previously told Fox News Digital that Desronvil appeared to have hired counsel to defend his name after being "dragged through the mud." "The whole idea of the jury is sort of this sacred arena where jurors get to decide a verdict in a case," Astor said. "And now we’re taking what is really a sacred arena, and we’re exposing it to the public." Plymouth County prosecutors have not announced whether they will retry Clancy. Her defense team has raised the possibility of resolving the case without another trial and brought in veteran Boston attorney Martin Weinberg to pursue a motion seeking dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds. title: Browns' Deshaun Watson may have silenced doubters after outlasting Baker Mayfield and 2-hour weather delay
description: Deshaun Watson threw for 238 yards and two touchdowns as the Cleveland Browns outlasted a two-hour weather delay to beat Baker Mayfield's Buccaneers.
content: Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns stayed in Florida after a brutal Week 1 loss that had many wondering if the embattled quarterback’s job was at stake as the team’s starter. title: ICE shooting rocks Austin as Democrat demands bodycam video, independent probe
description: Austin police say a brief foot pursuit involving ICE ended with an adult man shot once in the torso and hospitalized in serious but stable condition.
content: An ICE officer shot a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday, prompting a crowd of angry demonstrators to gather near the scene, hurl obscenities and clash with authorities. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) sources confirmed to Fox News that the man shot by the ICE officer is an illegal immigrant from Venezuela with a final order of removal. The agency said the man "illegally entered the country under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal during a law enforcement operation" in Austin, Texas Sunday. "The illegal alien's condition is stable, and he is in federal custody pending removal," DHS wrote on X. 'SQUAD' MEMBER CALLS DHS 'GREATEST THREAT TO OUR SAFETY' AFTER ICE-INVOLVED SHOOTING The man was later identified by his lawyer as Wilber Rafael Garces Perez. His lawyer, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, said her client entered the U.S. lawfully. "We are actively working to obtain additional information and clarify the circumstances surrounding the matter. We do not want to speculate or provide information that has not yet been confirmed. What we do understand is that he previously held a valid work permit and that, based on the information available to us, he entered the United States lawfully," Lincoln-Goldfinch said in a statement to Fox News. Video from the scene showed people holding up their phones and carrying flags as the commotion unfolded. Police said preliminary information indicated the man was shot once in the torso during a brief foot pursuit involving ICE. He was hospitalized in serious but stable condition. Austin Mayor Kirk Watson, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis and Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz confirmed ICE was involved in the shooting and provided what they repeatedly stressed were preliminary details during a Sunday afternoon news conference. Austin-Travis County EMS was notified of the shooting at approximately 12:56 p.m. and arrived in less than five minutes, Luckritz said. The adult man was taken from the scene within nine minutes and transported to a local trauma center in serious but stable condition. Davis said preliminary information indicated there was a brief foot pursuit before the shooting but cautioned that she had not yet been briefed by federal authorities. "From what I'm hearing, there was a small foot pursuit," Davis said. "But again, this is all very preliminary." Watson stressed that the information available was "extremely preliminary." He said city officials wanted to make themselves available as quickly as possible when they had information but warned against rushing to conclusions based on early claims circulating on TikTok, X and other social media platforms. Watson added that the Austin Police Department was not involved in the shooting and only assisted with traffic control. APD's Special Investigations Unit and the Texas Rangers will work together to investigate the incident, Davis said. "The city of Austin deserves answers," Davis said. "We're going to get all those questions answered, and we'll be as transparent as we can be." DHS announced later Sunday that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), with assistance from the FBI, is taking the lead on the investigation. Watson said he was "very angry" and "extremely unhappy" about the shooting, while accusing ICE of creating fear and chaos in Austin and other cities. He also questioned the agency's ability to investigate itself without local involvement. Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client was released from the hospital and is believed to now be in ICE custody. "Hospital attorneys at Dell Seton Medical Center have confirmed that Wilber Rafael Garces Perez has been released from the hospital into what we believe is ICE custody. After he was held for approximately six hours, officers declined to provide his wife with meaningful information about his status or circumstances," she said in her statement. "We are deeply concerned that his wife and family have not been permitted to see him and have not received a meaningful update regarding his current condition or whereabouts." "Our immediate concern is ensuring that his family receives accurate and timely information and that appropriate access and communication are provided while the matter is being addressed," she continued. ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY Lincoln-Goldfinch is scheduled to host a press conference in collaboration with the League of United Latin American Citizens at 1 p.m. Monday to address the incident. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, claimed in a post on X that "ICE has shot a person in Austin this morning" and called for a full, independent investigation and the immediate release of body-camera footage. "Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened," Casar wrote. "We will demand truth, transparency and accountability." During the news conference, Casar called the incident part of a "disturbing pattern" and said ICE's conduct "has got to stop." "They've arrested 5-year-olds ... and now someone has been shot," Casar said. "This has got to stop." Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, offered a sharply different reaction, saying he had been told the "shooter" was a Venezuelan national in the country illegally with a final order of removal. Authorities had not publicly disclosed information indicating the man fired a weapon. "The war is the one being waged against Americans through mass legal & illegal immigration," Roy wrote. The Austin investigation comes amid heightened tensions over federal immigration enforcement operations across the country. ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS CLASH WITH AGENTS OUTSIDE NEW JERSEY DETENTION CENTER AS GOV SHERRILL DENIED ENTRY Clashes erupted outside New Jersey's Delaney Hall immigration detention center in May after protesters defied a state police order to move to a designated demonstration area. Newark Mayor Ras Baraka later criticized the tactics used by state troopers sent to secure the facility, which had become the focus of frequent demonstrations. Federal immigration operations also drew national scrutiny in Minnesota following the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. Good was killed by an ICE agent in early January after authorities said she tried to use her vehicle to run over federal officers, while Pretti was fatally shot by agents on Jan. 24 as he recorded federal officers. title: Jets collapse late against Packers, miss chance at first 2-0 start since 2015 in overtime loss
description: The New York Jets blew a 17-7 fourth quarter lead as the Green Bay Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime at MetLife Stadium.
content: For most of Sunday afternoon, the New York Jets looked poised to move to 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets controlled most of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, but made some crucial errors down the stretch to cough up their 10-point fourth-quarter lead. Green Bay struck first on a 6-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter, but the Jets answered with a 5-yard touchdown run from Braelon Allen. title: Mike Vrabel snaps at reporter over Drake Maye's struggles after Pats win: 'you're not going to ruin my Sunday'
description: Mike Vrabel told reporters they wouldn't ruin his Sunday after the Patriots beat the Steelers 20-3, but Drake Maye's struggles still loom large.
content: The New England Patriots got their first win of the season Sunday, and head coach Mike Vrabel wasn't about to let a few perfectly valid questions about his quarterback spoil the celebration. title: Jalen Hurts saves Eagles from ugly upset as Philadelphia escapes Titans to remain unbeaten
description: Jalen Hurts hit Darius Cooper for a last-second touchdown to erase a three-point deficit as the Philadelphia Eagles escaped Nashville 24-20.
content: The Philadelphia Eagles moved to 2-0 with a win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon in Nashville. That's a sentence most football fans expected to read before the game even started. What most probably didn't expect was exactly what it took for the Eagles to go into Nissan Stadium and beat the Titans. Jalen Hurts connected with Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with less than 10 seconds remaining to turn a 20-17 Tennessee lead into a 24-20 Philadelphia victory. The Titans, who looked completely lost last week in a 23-10 loss to the New York Jets, had the reigning NFC East champions on the ropes for much of the afternoon. Philadelphia's problems started immediately. Star running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger on the Eagles' first offensive play and spent most of the first half on the sideline. Hurts tried to find DeVonta Smith in the end zone, but Amani Hooker intercepted the pass and returned it 92 yards to the Philadelphia 10-yard line. Four plays later, Cam Ward scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak to give Tennessee a 7-0 lead. The Eagles responded with a 2-yard touchdown run from Tank Bigsby and Hurts connected with Smith for a 22-yard touchdown late in the second quarter. But the Titans refused to go away. Joey Slye kicked a 37-yard field goal just as time expired in the first half, cutting Philadelphia's lead to 14-10. title: McDonald’s once sold beloved cookies featuring forgotten characters from the chain's past

content: Introduced in 1974, McDonaldland Cookies became a regular addition to McDonald’s Happy Meals when they debuted nationwide in 1979. But the beloved menu item was discontinued in the early 2000s, to the disappointment of many fans. The small, crunchy cookies were baked for McDonald’s by Keebler, had a subtle lemon flavor and featured the faces of beloved McDonald’s characters like Grimace, Ronald McDonald, Birdie and Hamburglar. The fast food chain altered its Happy Meals to include healthier items such as apple slices in the early 2000s. Between 2003 and 2004, McDonaldland Cookies were discontinued at all U.S. locations. Chocolate chip cookies, however, remained on the menu. McDonald’s has been serving some variation of chocolate chip cookies since the early 1970s, with today's chewy, soft-baked version introduced in 2012. MCDONALD'S BRINGS BACK POPULAR ITEM FOR SHORT TIME AS ONE STATE GETS A TREAT Although McDonaldland Cookies are no longer available in the United States, select McDonald’s locations in Australia still offer them, and certain New Zealand restaurants serve the treat under the name "McHappy Cookies." title: Massage clients report bizarre flu-like reaction after popular spa treatment
description: Massage flu symptoms like soreness, fatigue and headaches are real, but experts debunk the popular claim that massages release toxins from the body.
content: A popular wellness treatment is allegedly leaving some people with unexpected symptoms, including aches, fatigue and headaches. Social media users have described feeling under the weather after getting a massage, with some saying they feel as though they are coming down with an illness. The reaction is sometimes referred to online as "massage flu," though health experts say it is not an actual medical diagnosis. DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH "This phenomenon is something I have definitely heard of and had patients tell me," W. Zach Smith, a Seattle-based physical therapist and co-founder of HIDEF Physical Therapy, told Fox News Digital. "The idea of this has been around a long time but usually described as fatigue and soreness," Smith said. "The flu part of the name I have heard more recently." Soreness can happen when a lot of pressure is applied to the muscles for a long period of time, especially if someone is not used to getting massages, Smith added. "Any time you go in and apply a lot of pressure to a muscle for a long period of time, it can essentially bruise the tissue," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The body may also have a mild inflammatory response after a massage, which can contribute to soreness, Smith said. Drew Voelsch, a chiropractor at Forza Chiropractic in Illinois, said he has also heard patients refer to the reaction as "massage flu" or an "adjustment hangover." "The symptoms are real," Voelsch told Fox News Digital, pointing to soreness, fatigue and mild headaches that may last 24 to 48 hours. "The label is social media." A massage around the neck, scalp or jaw can also trigger headaches because those areas can be involved in tension headaches, according to Smith. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Both experts pushed back on the idea that these symptoms are caused by a massage "releasing toxins" from the body, a claim that has circulated in social media comments. "This is a myth," Smith said. "There is no basis or science behind this." Voelsch agreed, noting that the liver and kidneys handle the body's waste-removal processes. To help reduce discomfort, Smith recommended asking for less pressure or a shorter massage and gradually working up to deeper or longer sessions. Mild soreness is typically not a cause for concern, but Smith said new or persistent pain may be a reason to contact a doctor. "If you are having a new, unexplained pain that is persistent, that would be a good time to call your doctor," he said. title: Trump, Iranian president converge on NYC for ‘dramatic’ UN showdown as Tehran faces tight restrictions
description: President Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly amid strict U.S. restrictions on Iran's delegation movements.
content: President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are set to converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly (UNGA) this week, setting up what former White House officials describe as a "dramatic" diplomatic moment, with Tehran’s delegation effectively "captive" under U.S. restrictions amid heightened Middle East tensions. Pezeshkian, for one, is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday, Reuters and Iran's semi-official news agency, Mehr, reported Sunday, with Trump at the rostrum on Tuesday. "The choreography here is going to make for a fairly dramatic moment," Theo Wold, former acting assistant attorney general and White House domestic policy advisor, told Fox News Digital. PUTIN, XI AND IRAN'S PEZESHKIAN DESCEND ON INDIA FOR HIGH-STAKES BRICS SUMMIT AMID ESCALATING GLOBAL TENSIONS "For the Iranians, the limitation is going to be that there's going to be less access to the international press and less ability for them to essentially poke the Trump administration in the eye," Wold added before noting that it is "pretty sensible to allow them to participate in the international forum and to discuss whatever issues they think are pertinent to their regime and then tell them to go home." The high-profile gathering also comes as Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran amid the almost seven-month war. Tehran, meanwhile, has set seven conditions for talks with Washington, according to Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei. Iran also warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, Reuters reported. While the U.S. approved visas for Iran’s delegation earlier this week, including Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the State Department has placed strict limits on Iranian movements while in Manhattan. As the host country under a 1947 U.N. agreement, the United States generally must facilitate the entry and transit of foreign representatives traveling to U.N. headquarters, including officials from adversarial nations. "While ordinary Iranians endure brutal repression, water and electricity shortages, and soaring inflation, the regime's officials want to go on shopping sprees in New York. Not on our watch," U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X. UN WATCHDOG SLAMS POTENTIAL ELECTION OF IRAN TO PANEL WITH HUMAN RIGHTS SWAY: 'LUNATICS RUNNING THE ASYLUM' For Washington, Wold said the U.S. is not obligated to give them unrestricted access beyond diplomatic responsibilities. "Here, the delegation will be restricted to their accommodation in New York City and the U.N. headquarters there in Manhattan," Wold clarified. He characterized the move by Washington as a way of telling the delegation it could participate in official discussions but not "go and buy a bunch of microwaves or a small car at Costco or a dealership in the greater New York area." "Some of the restrictions fully recognize that when Iran comes to New York for UNGA, really it's about them lining their pockets and going on shopping sprees to get household appliances and Rolex watches," Wold said. "They're not going to be going on shopping sprees. They're certainly not going to be hitting up Michelin-starred restaurants in greater Manhattan. "They also go to Sam’s Club and Walmart and Costco. And that was one of the specific prohibitions issued by the State Department this week: to contact those big-box retailers that require a basic membership and say, ‘You’re not to transact or do any business with Iranians when they arrive, and you’re to notify us when they do.’" KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL Despite the restrictions, Wold said UNGA gives Washington the opportunity it has "wanted for quite some time to have a large enough audience, and a sort of captive Iranian delegation" to make some of the essential points for why the administration pursued the actions it did against the Iranian regime. Iranian state media also reported Sept. 19 that Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said New York held "absolutely no charm" for the Iranian delegation. Baghaei, Mehr News Agency reported, went on to accuse the U.S. of using every tool to block the delegation’s participation, asserting that Iran’s attendance is a legal right rather than a favor. Wold went on to criticize the U.N. for hosting state representatives hostile to American interests while raising security concerns. "It's going to be one of those things that's fairly perplexing to most Americans," Wold said. "How is it that the representatives of what we have long identified as a hostile regime, but now one that we're actually engaged in combat operations against, one that has killed American service members, why is it that their diplomats get to come to the United Nations and exchange niceties with other kleptocrats or some of their other allies on the international scene?" title: Massachusetts' plan to offer postpartum screening home visits sparks online debate
description: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey is investing $2.25 million to send nurses into homes of new parents, sparking a heated government overreach debate.
content: Massachusetts is expanding a taxpayer-funded program that sends nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth, fueling debate over the government's role in family health care. Gov. Maura Healey recently announced plans to invest $2 million to expand the state's Welcome Family program, which offers voluntary home visits from registered nurses after the birth of a child. Healey also proposed an additional $250,000 to strengthen the Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms, which provides mental health support to providers caring for pregnant and postpartum patients. "Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you're going to have a home visit within days, weeks and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey said during an interview last week on Boston Public Radio. CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE'S 'DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD': ATTORNEY Healey also said the state is investing in training healthcare providers to better identify the signs of postpartum mental health conditions. The announcement comes amid heightened public attention to postpartum mental health in Massachusetts during the high-profile trial of Lindsay Clancy, the former labor and delivery nurse accused of killing her three young children in January 2023. In a case ultimately declared a mistrial because of a deadlocked jury, Clancy's defense argued she was suffering from severe postpartum mental illness. The case has reignited debate over how postpartum mental health conditions are identified and treated. LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS State officials say the program is intended to improve maternal health outcomes by connecting families with additional support. The announcement also sparked debate on social media, where some users questioned whether the program represented an appropriate role for government. "Doctors and pediatricians are more than capable to conduct appropriate screenings for their patients. Say no to home visits," one user wrote on X, while another called the program "creepy" and "massive government overreach." Not everyone opposed the proposal outright. "More overreach. title: Ms Rachel calls Gaza journalist ‘friend’ in resurfaced clip after he admits hiding Oct 7 hostage footage
description: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel faces scrutiny after a resurfaced video shows her calling Motaz Azaiza her "friend" amid his Oct. 7 revelations.
content: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel faced renewed scrutiny on Sunday after a 2025 video of her calling Palestinian photojournalist Motaz Azaiza her "friend," resurfaced, days after Azaiza admitted he deliberately withheld footage of Israeli hostages being beaten by a crowd in Gaza on Oct. 7, 2023. The short video appears to show Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, introducing Azaiza to her young audience while teaching the letter "M." "Hi, yes, it’s M, for my friend, Motaz. Yay! Bye!" Accurso said. MS RACHEL CONFRONTED ON ACCUSING ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' IN PARK INTERACTION WITH PODCASTER The video was originally shared on Instagram and later removed, according to reporting from July 2025. Azaiza, who amassed millions of social media followers documenting the war in Gaza, appeared briefly in the clip and greeted Ms. Rachel. The video also took on new significance after Azaiza described earlier this month what he witnessed during the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack in an extensive interview with journalist Ahmed al-Biqawi on the Arabic-language "Taqarrab" podcast. Azaiza said he followed a vehicle carrying Israeli captives and filmed as members of a crowd assaulted them. Azaiza said he didn't publish the video, however, as he feared it could put the Palestinians involved at risk. "I saw the vehicle of the Al-Qassam Brigades, and there were Israeli captives there," Azaiza said. "People got out, watched, beat them, hit them, and I followed them and filmed. But I did not publish those videos. Why? Because I did not want to ruin the lives of the people who were filmed." MS RACHEL POSTS SUPPORT FOR HIJAB-WEARING KINDERGARTNERS AFTER TRUMP POST Azaiza said he withheld the footage because he believed Israeli authorities could use it to identify the Palestinians appearing in the videos. "I understood that Israel would use those videos to identify every person who was there and eliminate them," Azaiza said. "I did not want to be responsible, even indirectly, for the deaths of those people in exchange for a few likes and views online." NEW YORK TIMES ISSUES CORRECTION, DELETES LINE QUESTIONING IF ISRAELIS WERE VICTIMS OF OCT 7 TERROR ATTACK Azaiza also criticized Hamas and described the restrictions faced by journalists working inside Gaza. He said photographers learned to lower their cameras when Palestinians criticized Hamas because showing such dissent could lead to retaliation. Despite describing himself as a supporter of armed Palestinian resistance, Azaiza said Hamas' actions had failed to protect Palestinians living in Gaza. "I support armed resistance, but one that brings results, or at least gives me the feeling that my life is valuable in the eyes of the resistance," Azaiza said. "Why should a Palestinian be cheap in the eyes of Palestinians themselves? You are making people hate the resistance with your own hands." Time named him to its 2024 list of the world's 100 most influential people for his photographs documenting Gaza. Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, told Fox News Digital that Azaiza’s disclosure raised questions about his journalistic judgment and his decision to withhold the footage. "After years spent claiming to share what was happening in Gaza ‘unfiltered,’ Azaiza revealed that he hid footage — not, per journalistic norms, to protect victims from further harm, but because he didn't want Israel to arrest the perpetrators. Innocent civilians had been kidnapped, already sexually abused, and his concern was with the people that beat them and rejoiced at Hamas' crimes. Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, told Fox News Digital that she believed Accurso’s Gaza advocacy was spreading misleading information to her large audience. title: Fat Bear Week bracket is set: meet the heavyweights, underdogs and defending champ in this year's tournament
description: Forget March Madness. Fat Bear Week returns to Katmai National Park with 16 brown bears as defending champ Chunk faces rising star Bucky on Wednesday.
content: Forget March Madness. The most important bracket of the year has arrived. Fat Bear Week is back, baby! The annual competition at Alaska's Katmai National Park and Preserve kicks off Tuesday with 16 brown bears vying for the title of chonkiest champ. This year's bracket features a defending champion, a few rising stars and some heavyweight opening-round matchups. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Here's how it works: Two bears face off in a single-elimination tournament, and fans vote for the one they believe has done the best job packing on the pounds ahead of winter hibernation. More than 1.7 million votes were cast during last year's competition, which saw Bear 32 — better known as "Chunk" — claim the title. Now, the reigning champ is back for another shot at glory. But he's got some serious competition. The defending champ: Chunk Chunk won last year's competition despite suffering a broken jaw in June 2025, likely during a fight with another bear. The injury left him with a distinctive scar and protruding canine tooth, but it apparently didn't slow down his appetite. This summer, Chunk was largely absent from Brooks River during the salmon run before returning in September with a substantial belly. Park officials aren't sure where he spent most of his summer. But wherever he was, he wasn't skipping meals. And he's going to need every pound. His title defense begins Wednesday against Bear 164, Bucky, one of the river's emerging heavyweights. The heavyweight showdown: Chunk vs. Bucky Bucky has grown considerably in recent years, developing the size and confidence to challenge other dominant males for access to the best fishing spots. He's also figured out a pretty clever way to keep himself fed. While other bears compete for the same prime real estate at Brooks Falls, Bucky has learned to position himself near the waterfall's deepest plunge pool, where he can catch salmon jumping through the air, rising from below or falling from above. And at approximately 9 years old, Bucky is still relatively young. Male brown bears typically reach their physical prime between ages 12 and 20, so he could have several more years of growth ahead of him. The rising star gets his shot at the defending champion Wednesday, Sept. 23. One of them will be going home early. Well, metaphorically. They'll both still be in Alaska eating fish. The veteran: Walker Bear 151, Walker, used to be a relatively easygoing guy who enjoyed playing with other bears. As he's gotten older, though, he's become a little grumpier and a lot more competitive. And the younger bears are giving him plenty of reasons to be grumpy. WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA Bucky and Bear 903, Gully, have been challenging Walker's position in the Brooks River hierarchy. His size and experience have helped him maintain his standing, but the younger competition is catching up. Walker faces Gully in Wednesday's opening round, giving us another veteran-versus-youngster matchup right out of the gate. Check out the rump on this guy, by the way. The Cinderella story: Bear 610 Bear 610 might not be one of the biggest competitors in this year's field, but she's got a pretty compelling story. When she was first identified in 2015, park officials believed she had separated from her mother earlier than expected. She also had a significant healing wound above her hips, suggesting she'd survived an attack. Now, more than a decade later, she's raising her first known litter of cubs. Despite being a relatively small, first-time mother, 610 has successfully protected and cared for both cubs throughout the summer while building up her own fat reserves ahead of hibernation. This is her first Fat Bear Week appearance, and she'll face Bear 89, Backpack, in Wednesday's opening round. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. The competition celebrates the remarkable transformations these animals undergo as they prepare to survive months of winter hibernation without eating or drinking. title: America and China are fighting for the future of AI — chips are the battlefield
description: President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Washington as Huawei races to build a rival AI chip ecosystem that could displace American semiconductor dominance.
content: When President Donald Trump sits down with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, the agenda will be crowded. Trade. Tariffs. Rare earth minerals. National security. Supply chains. But looming over all of it is a technological competition that could shape the balance of economic and military power for decades: artificial intelligence. And increasingly, the battle isn't simply about who builds the best AI model. TRUMP-XI’S CHINA SUMMIT IS A DEFINING TEST FOR AMERICA IN THE NEW COLD WAR It is about who controls the chips, computing infrastructure and technology ecosystem underneath it. America remains the global leader in advanced AI technology and semiconductor design. But China is pushing aggressively to reduce its dependence on American technology, and Huawei has emerged as one of the most important companies in that effort. That should have Washington's full attention. For years, the United States has used export controls to restrict China's access to advanced semiconductors and semiconductor-manufacturing technology, particularly technologies with potential military applications. Those restrictions had a clear national-security objective: prevent America's most sophisticated technology from strengthening a strategic competitor's military capabilities. But there has also been an unintended consequence worth confronting. China accelerated its effort to build an AI ecosystem that doesn't need America. AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK Huawei expanded its Ascend AI-chip roadmap. Chinese developers adapted software and models to domestic hardware. Chinese companies poured resources into computing systems capable of compensating for some of the performance limitations of individual Chinese chips. And Huawei isn't standing still. The company recently said demand for its AI computing equipment in China is exceeding supply. It is accelerating future generations of its Ascend processors and developing enormous computing systems capable of connecting vast numbers of chips. That means the strategic question facing Washington has changed. AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL The question isn't simply: How do we keep sensitive American technology away from China? It is also: How do we make sure the rest of the world continues choosing American technology instead of China's? Those are related questions, but they aren't identical. If American technology becomes inaccessible across too much of the global market, China has an enormous incentive to develop substitutes. Huawei has an enormous incentive to sell them. And governments and companies around the world have an enormous incentive to build around whatever technology they can reliably obtain. THE AI REVOLUTION COULD BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY DISASTER IF WE AREN'T CAREFUL Once developers write software for an ecosystem, companies construct computing infrastructure around it and countries invest billions deploying it, switching becomes much harder. That's why this isn't merely a chip-sales competition. It is an ecosystem competition. America wants a world running on American chips, American software, American standards and American innovation. China wants to build an alternative. It wants a world in which Huawei and other Chinese companies provide a technology stack that Beijing controls and America cannot easily influence. President Trump has taken a different approach from the Biden administration. His administration rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule while maintaining controls targeting technologies with serious national-security implications. The administration has also allowed certain advanced chips to be considered for sale to approved Chinese customers under licensing requirements and security conditions. The theory is straightforward: protect the technologies most critical to national security without unnecessarily surrendering commercial markets to Chinese competitors. That distinction matters. CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE Nobody serious is arguing that America should simply hand China unrestricted access to technology that could materially enhance advanced weapons, military AI, surveillance or other sensitive capabilities. National security comes first. But there is a difference between protecting America's crown-jewel technology and adopting restrictions so sweeping that they accelerate China's determination to replace American technology throughout the commercial market. Because Huawei's goal isn't merely to survive American restrictions. Huawei wants to compete. It wants Chinese chips powering Chinese AI. It wants Chinese computing infrastructure supporting Chinese models. And ultimately, Chinese technology companies want customers outside China using their systems. That's why the next phase of this competition will be fought over which chips countries buy, which computing systems they install, which software developers learn and which technology stack becomes the default infrastructure for the AI economy. America has enormous advantages. We have extraordinary semiconductor designers, the world's leading AI companies, deep capital markets, world-class universities, entrepreneurs and an innovation culture China has spent decades trying to replicate. But technological leadership isn't permanent. It has to be defended. And sometimes the greatest threat to American leadership isn't that China suddenly invents something better. It's that America creates policies that make its own technology harder for the world to use while Beijing aggressively offers an alternative. There are already calls for the United States to slow AI development or impose broader restrictions in the name of safety and security. Those arguments deserve serious debate. AI presents real risks. Advanced semiconductor technology has genuine military applications. Export controls can be an important national-security tool. But every restriction also has consequences. The question should be whether a restriction actually improves American security without unnecessarily strengthening China's competing technology ecosystem. Because China isn't pausing. Huawei isn't pausing. And global demand for AI computing certainly isn't pausing. Somebody will provide the chips. Somebody will provide the computing infrastructure. Somebody will provide the software. Somebody will establish the standards. The United States has a direct strategic interest in American companies remaining central to that ecosystem. The previous generation of American leaders watched too much manufacturing capacity and too many strategically important supply chains migrate overseas. We should not repeat that mistake with the infrastructure of artificial intelligence. Semiconductors are no longer merely components inside computers. Compute is strategic power. The nations and companies controlling advanced computing will possess enormous advantages in scientific discovery, medicine, manufacturing, intelligence, cybersecurity and military technology. That is why the Trump-Xi meeting matters far beyond whatever trade agreement or diplomatic communiqué emerges from Washington. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The two presidents represent countries competing over something much larger: Who builds the technological infrastructure of the 21st century? The United States should protect its most sensitive technology, its intellectual property and technologies with significant military applications. At the same time, American companies will continue competing for commercial markets around the world. Design the chips here. Build the semiconductor infrastructure here. Develop the software here. Protect the technology that truly must be protected. And keep American technology innovative and competitive enough that countries around the world continue choosing the American ecosystem instead of Huawei's. The AI Cold War is already underway. And the chips are the battlefield.

title: 1619 Project founder regrets school choice for her daughter, admits putting ideals ahead of her education
description: Nikole Hannah-Jones says she regrets her Brooklyn public school choice after her daughter said she never got the education she truly wanted.
content: Nikole Hannah-Jones, New York Times Magazine reporter and creator of the controversial 1619 Project, acknowledged Sunday that she regretted aspects of the decision to send her daughter to predominantly Black, high-poverty public schools in Brooklyn, New York, after the now-16-year-old told her she did not receive the education she wanted — a decade after Hannah-Jones described the choice as an effort to challenge school segregation. In a newly released New York Times Magazine essay, Hannah-Jones described revisiting years of emails with her daughter Najya’s teachers and principals and confronting what she called a truth she could no longer suppress. "Now I felt overcome with regret. Najya deserved better," Hannah-Jones said. "They all did. But she was mine. This girl, my only child, looked to me to protect her, to give her what she needed to thrive. And I had not chosen her." Hannah-Jones told Fox News Digital on Sunday that the broader focus should remain on families who lack the resources to pursue better educational options for their children. "I hope people concerned about the choice my husband and I made for our daughter will have equal or more outrage for the thousands of Black children whose parents don’t have the resources to send them to better schools," she said. "As I write in the piece, there is no absolution to be had for any of us." POWERFUL TEACHERS' UNIONS SHARE STRIKING LINK WITH STATES STRUGGLING TO TEACH KIDS TO READ Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation and longtime school choice advocate, responded to Hannah-Jones' essay in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing parents should prioritize their children's individual educational needs. "Parents should put their children first. They should not sacrifice them to a failing government school system in the name of ideology," DeAngelis said. "Nikole Hannah-Jones now says she regrets putting her ideals ahead of her daughter’s education. That admission is long overdue." "I welcome Nikole Hannah-Jones to the school choice revolution," he continued. "Maybe she will start to understand that pulling her daughter from the failing school system would have done more to improve those schools — through competition — than the status quo ever did. You don’t fix public schools by locking kids in them without any accountability. You fix them by giving them a reason to change their ways." NEW YORK JOINS FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE INITIATIVE DESPITE TRADITIONAL DEMOCRAT OPPOSITION Hannah-Jones said the realization culminated in a conversation with Najya as she was writing the essay. She apologized to her daughter after reviewing problems that had followed her through elementary and middle school. "I feel like you got cheated," Hannah-Jones said. "And I’m sorry for that." Najya responded by telling her mother that she wished her own education had received greater consideration alongside Hannah-Jones' broader concerns about educational inequality. "Sometimes I wish instead of always thinking about other kids, you would have thought about me. I never really got the education I wanted," Najya said. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’ Hannah-Jones’ assessment marked a shift from the position she described in a widely discussed 2016 New York Times Magazine essay, when she explained why she and her husband enrolled Najya at P.S. 307, a Brooklyn school that was then overwhelmingly Black and Latino and served a largely low-income population. Hannah-Jones said at the time she believed middle-class families could help improve segregated schools by enrolling their children and investing in them. "I worried — I worry still — about whether I made the right decision for our little girl. But I knew I made the just one," Hannah-Jones said in 2016. The new essay detailed academic problems that became more apparent as Najya grew older. At Unison, her middle school, Najya earned strong grades and took honors courses, but later said she and her friends realized that they were not being sufficiently challenged. Hannah-Jones described limited homework, inexperienced teachers and gaps in her daughter's math preparation that became especially apparent after Najya entered a more academically demanding high school. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Unison Principal Emily Paige acknowledged in the essay that some attempts to accommodate students who entered the school academically behind had unintended consequences, including the decision to eliminate homework. "It is important to not, in our pursuit of being antiracist, lower expectations," Paige said. "Because this is what happens, right? It’s racism under the guise of antiracism." DeAngelis told Fox News Digital that Hannah-Jones’ experience should lead her to support policies allowing education funding to follow children to schools selected by their families. "Hannah-Jones can afford better options. Most families cannot," DeAngelis said. "She should fight for the funding to follow the student so more parents have the same educational opportunities she can buy for herself. School choice is an equalizer." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The debate comes as school choice remains an active issue in New York. Fox News Digital reported last week that teachers' unions were opposing Democratic New York Gov. Kathy Hochul's plan to participate in a federal tax-credit scholarship program designed to help families pay for educational options outside their assigned schools. The New York Times' 1619 Project is a long-form collaboration that seeks to "reframe the country's history" by bringing slavery and racism to the forefront of the national narrative. While praised by liberals, the project has faced intense scrutiny and pushback from prominent historians who have publicly disputed its factual accuracy, particularly its claims regarding the motivations behind the American Revolution. Despite the criticism, the 1619 Project's theories of American history were later developed into an educational curriculum with the help of the Pulitzer Center. Fox News Digital reached out to New York Public Schools for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

title: DHS chief fires back at Jayapal over claim majority of immigration arrests pose 'no threat'
description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin rejected Pramila Jayapal's claim that most ICE arrests over the summer involved individuals who pose "no threat" to public safety, citing angel families.
content: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin pushed back on Rep. Pramila Jayapal’s, D-Wash., claim that the "majority of people" arrested by DHS pose "absolutely no threat to public safety." Mullin rejected Jayapal’s characterization on "Saturday in America," saying DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) remain committed to targeting high-risk individuals to keep American communities safe and arguing that crimes committed by illegal immigrants have led to tragedy. "If we're going to have national security in this country, we [need to] know everybody that's entered this country. And so, I'm not going to release you back into the public once we know that you entered this country illegally," Mullin said. "It's time for you to go home." BORDER CZAR TOM HOMAN FIRES BACK AFTER DEMOCRAT CHRIS MURPHY CLAIMS ICE IS ‘TERRORIZING LITTLE KIDS’ "All the angel families that lost their loved ones at the hands of an illegal is 100% preventable, because that illegal shouldn't be in our country to begin with," the DHS boss added. Jayapal, the ranking member of the House Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and a vocal ICE critic, argued that immigration enforcement under the Trump administration has targeted immigrants without criminal convictions. "For the first time this summer, the majority of people that DHS arrested were people who pose absolutely no threat to public safety, and the number of people with criminal convictions who are arrested by ICE actually decreased — decreased, not increased," Jayapal said during a hearing last week. "That’s because when DHS expends all of its energy to go after parents, longtime friends, neighbors, when [Homeland Security Investigations] agents who are supposed to investigate serious crime and human trafficking are instead being moved to street sweeps and riding along with local police for random traffic stops, we are less safe, not more safe," she added. The department also says ICE has deported more than 2,000 known or suspected terrorists since Trump took office. "When you have a car accident, and you came… into this country legally, and the Democrats want to say, you're not a criminal and you kill somebody. Yes, you were a criminal and now… you ruined somebody else's life, and now you're a murderer at the same time," the DHS chief said. "It's political for them. They want to say this every day," he added. DHS regularly publicizes arrests and deportations involving illegal immigrants convicted of crimes including murder, child pornography, sexual assault and drug trafficking. title: Nicki Minaj offers career advice to young Americans, delivers blunt response to Trump critics
description: Rapper Nicki Minaj revealed her path from Red Lobster to global stardom and fiercely defended her support of President Donald Trump in an exclusive interview.
content: Rapper Nicki Minaj shared her career advice to young Americans entering the workforce and fiercely defended her support of President Donald Trump during an exclusive interview with "The Ingraham Angle" on Friday. The music mogul opened up about her journey to the top, explaining how she hustled her way from serving biscuits at Red Lobster to dominating music charts around the world and collaborating with some of the biggest names in Hollywood. "I did customer service for telephone companies. I was a telemarketer. I sold fire extinguishers. I did everything," Minaj shared with Fox News. NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER MARY J BLIGE CREDITS FAITH, PASTORS WITH CONFRONTING HER PRIDE AS SHE TOOK CONTROL OF HER CAREER "What I would tell young people is: This is not the best part of your life, but it is probably one of the most important parts of your life," she said. Minaj said the lessons she learned, as well as the values she developed while doing "nitty-gritty" work, before money and international success, remain central to how she conducts business today. "The things that I learned during that time in my life, it still helps me today," the rapper explained. "All the people skills, and the communication skills, and all the problem-solving that I learned then, it still applies now when I'm around superstars or rich people." "All of those skills, they carry over into the rest of your life. So don't look at that part of your life as something that you can't wait to fly by because… you might not be making the biggest money, but you're doing the real nitty-gritty work that is going to help you for the rest of your life," Minaj added. THE RICH HAVE ONE FINANCIAL HABIT MOST AMERICANS IGNORE AT THEIR PERIL The "Super Bass" and "Starships" singer, who has an estimated net worth of $150 million according to Celebrity Net Worth, also advised young Americans to save money, saying that "no matter how little" she made, she would always set aside funds for a rainy day. Minaj also discussed her support for President Donald Trump after emerging as one of his fiercest allies in Hollywood. The rapper recently partnered with the Trump administration on the Small Business Administration’s Million Dollar Pitch Competition, serving as one of the celebrity judges. LIL WAYNE PRAISES TRUMP'S WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM PROJECT, CALLS OUT CRITICS WHO 'DON'T KNOW NOTHING' The competition brought five small business owners before a panel of judges, including Minaj and Airbnb’s co-founder, to give their best pitch for a share of a $1 million cash prize pool. "Small business represents the heart of the country…," said Minaj. "You don't have to be a huge household name to be recognized by the president and to be recognized by us." Minaj, whom Trump has called a "fantastic person," addressed the grief she receives for supporting the president, telling Fox News that she has "absolutely nothing" to say to critics and adding that she is "honored" to work with the administration. "[Trump] is fun," the rapper said. "He's not just smart and he's not just the president, but he's also someone that I can relate to." It's easy to connect with him, it's easy feel like he heard you, he understands you," she continued. "And I just love him, and I'm not going to ever make excuses for that." Minaj was also asked when her fans, whom she fondly refers to as "Barbz," can expect her next tour following a hiatus after her Pink Friday 2 World Tour in 2024. She urged fans to give her some time as she embraces what she described as her "businesswoman era." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Who set you up to asking this question? "Barbz, I love you very much if you're watching, and I don't want any more questions about concerts. I'm in my businesswoman era," she added.

title: Scammers are buying Google ads to steal bank logins
description: Federal prosecutors say criminals bought sponsored search ads mimicking real banks, capturing over 5,000 login credentials and draining accounts.
content: You need to check your bank account, so you open Google, type in your bank's name and click the first result that looks right. Most of us have done some version of that without thinking twice. Now federal investigators say criminals turned that everyday habit into a way to steal bank logins and drain accounts. The Justice Department announced on Sept. 8 that a Russian web developer accused of helping run a large bank account takeover operation had been extradited to the United States. Prosecutors say the group bought sponsored search engine links that sent banking customers to fake login pages. Victims then entered their credentials, believing they had reached their bank. That should get the attention of anyone who banks online. Here's how the scam works, why those sponsored results can look so convincing and what you can do to avoid handing your bank login to a criminal. ASKED SIRI TO CALL YOUR BANK? A SCAM COULD COST THOUSANDS NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com How the fake bank ad scam worked According to federal prosecutors, the alleged operation used spoofed domains that mimicked websites belonging to federally insured financial institutions. The conspirators then bought sponsored search engine links. Those links could appear when someone searched for their bank. A click sent the customer to a fraudulent login page. Once victims entered their credentials, the attackers could capture that information. Prosecutors say the group then used the stolen credentials to access real bank accounts, check balances and initiate unauthorized wire transfers. The indictment also alleges that Sergei Anatolyevich Filimonov developed and maintained infrastructure supporting the operation. That included databases storing more than 5,000 stolen login credentials and software designed to capture sensitive authentication data. Where Google and Bing come into the story The newest Sept. 8 Justice Department announcement says the conspirators purchased sponsored search-engine links. It does not name a particular search engine. However, the DOJ previously described the same bank account takeover operation when it seized the group's backend domain in December 2025. In that announcement, investigators specifically said the criminal group delivered fraudulent advertisements through search engines including Google and Bing. The ads imitated sponsored search ads used by legitimate banks. Victims who clicked those ads were redirected to fake banking websites controlled by the criminals, according to the DOJ. That earlier investigation had identified at least 19 victims across the United States by December 2025. The DOJ reported approximately $28 million in attempted losses and about $14.6 million in actual losses tied to those victims. Microsoft told CyberGuy that it has policies and detection mechanisms designed to help prevent misleading advertising. The company said that when it becomes aware of ads that violate its policies, it takes action to remove them and uses what it learns to strengthen its detection capabilities. Microsoft also encourages users to report suspicious ads through its "Report a Concern" form. We also reached out to Google for comment but did not hear back before our deadline. FAKE PATIENT PORTAL SCAM CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN AND INFECT YOUR PC Why a sponsored Google result can fool you The trap works because a paid search result can appear in a place many of us naturally look first. You search for your bank. A result appears near the top. The wording looks familiar, so you click before studying the address. Most search ads are legitimate. Still, the FBI warns that criminals can buy ads that imitate real businesses and direct users to convincing phishing sites. The FBI refers to this tactic as SEO poisoning in its account takeover guidance. That changes how I would approach something as sensitive as online banking. In fact, the FBI specifically recommends using bookmarks or favorites to reach login pages rather than clicking search results or advertisements. Bank account takeover losses have topped $262 million This problem stretches far beyond one alleged criminal operation. Since January 2025, the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center has received more than 5,100 complaints reporting account takeover fraud. Reported losses have exceeded $262 million. Criminals use several ways to get inside accounts. Fraudulent banking websites remain one of them. The FBI says victims can encounter a phishing site after clicking a fake search advertisement. Attackers may also try to obtain a one-time passcode if an account uses multifactor authentication. Once criminals gain access, they may move money to accounts they control. That can make recovery difficult, especially when funds move quickly. The accused developer has now been extradited to the U.S. The latest development centers on Sergei Anatolyevich Filimonov, 36, a Russian national and web developer. A federal grand jury indicted Filimonov on Nov. 4, 2025. Authorities later extradited him from the Republic of Georgia. Tips to protect yourself from fake bank login ads You do not need to stop banking online. However, changing how you reach your bank's login page can lower your risk. SHOULD YOU USE A SEPARATE COMPUTER FOR ONLINE BANKING? 1) Use your bank's official app when possible If you already have your bank's verified app installed, open it directly rather than searching for your bank in a browser. That removes the search-result step where this particular scam tries to catch you. 2) Bookmark your bank's real website Visit your bank's verified website and save it as a bookmark or favorite. The FBI specifically recommends bookmarks or favorites for financial login pages instead of relying on search results or advertisements. 3) Check the web address before entering anything Take a second to inspect the domain before you enter banking credentials. A fake site may use a misspelled address or another small change designed to look legitimate. The FBI warns that fraudulent search ads can lead to URLs that closely resemble the real address. Microsoft also advises users to carefully review website URLs before entering credentials or other personal information online. 4) Do not assume a sponsored result has been verified A "Sponsored" label means someone paid to place the advertisement. So when money or sensitive information is involved, verify the destination yourself before you sign in. 5) Keep multifactor authentication turned on Enable two-factor or multifactor authentication if your financial institution offers it. However, do not let that give you a false sense of security. The FBI warns that MFA may not protect you after you land on a fraudulent login page. Criminals can also use social engineering to try to obtain your one-time code. Never give a one-time passcode to someone who contacts you unexpectedly. YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES 6) Use a password manager as another warning sign A trusted password manager can help because it associates your saved login with a particular website.
