title: 119,000 fake shops could steal your credit card details
description: DoppelCart's 119,000 fake shopping domains steal credit card details at checkout, mimicking over 44,000 real brands with convincing cloned sites.
content: You find a product you want for 65% off. The site looks polished, the branding feels familiar, and the deal seems hard to pass up. That could be exactly the trap. Cybersecurity company Nebty has linked about 119,000 domains to a fake shopping operation called DoppelCart. The sites impersonate legitimate businesses and can steal payment details at checkout, including one-time bank verification codes. BleepingComputer reports that more than 105,000 DoppelCart shops were active in Nebty's latest scans, while Nebty says the majority of the cluster remains online. So, before you jump on a huge discount from a store you do not recognize, take a closer look at who is really behind the checkout page. FAKE RENTAL LISTING SCAMS CAN COST YOU THOUSANDS NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com. What is DoppelCart? Nebty discovered DoppelCart while investigating fake shops that targeted several of its customers. Researchers noticed that stores impersonating different companies shared technical characteristics. They began following those connections through publicly available website scans. The investigation eventually grew to roughly 119,000 associated domains. Nebty says that, to its knowledge, DoppelCart represents the largest publicly documented fake-shop cluster when measured by associated domains. The company also makes an important point about attribution. Shared infrastructure does not prove that one person or organization controls every DoppelCart store. Even so, the technical overlap is striking. Nebty CEO Benedikt Scheungraber told BleepingComputer that 96% of the confirmed shops shared identical build files and resolved to 27 commerce backends. DoppelCart has swallowed a huge piece of the .shop domain Most of the domains connected to DoppelCart use the .shop top-level domain. Nebty's September 2026 data included 118,787 distinct .shop domains linked to the cluster out of 4,361,908 .shop domains in the company's snapshot. That's 2.72%, or roughly one out of every 37 domains in that particular data set. However, that number needs some context. Nebty says the snapshot represents domains listed in the .shop DNS zone. It does not tell us how many legitimate or fraudulent stores were operating at the same moment. For comparison, researchers previously documented BogusBazaar, a fake-shop operation involving more than 75,000 domains. Nebty cautions that observation periods and counting methods differ between investigations, so the numbers are not perfectly comparable. We reached out to GMO Registry, which operates the .shop domain, for comment but did not hear back before our deadline. Why DoppelCart fake shops can look so convincing The days when every scam website looked like somebody threw it together in five minutes are long gone. DoppelCart sites can copy product catalogs from real companies along with descriptions, branding and other material. In some cases, researchers found fake stores loading assets directly from the legitimate company's servers. That creates a real problem for shoppers. You may recognize the brand. The products look right. Nothing on the page immediately screams scam because much of the material came from the real business in the first place. Scheungraber says DoppelCart shops mimic 44,182 different brands, with a median of two clones for each brand. Some brands received much more attention. Researchers found more than 30 shops apiece targeting companies including SodaStream, Velasca, CurrentBody, Daniel Wellington, Dreame, Horze, MOVA and SPARK PAWS. That 65% discount can be the hook This is where the scam can catch you. Most of us shop around before spending money online. Finding the same product at a dramatically lower price can feel like a great deal. DoppelCart stores take advantage of that reaction. Researchers found fake shops advertising discounts as high as 65%. Of course, a steep discount does not automatically mean you're looking at a scam. Real stores run clearance sales every day. Still, if you've never heard of the retailer and its price beats everyone else by a mile, spend another minute checking who you're buying from. CyberGuy has a full guide on the warning signs worth checking before buying from an unfamiliar website: Tips to help you tell if an online store is real or a scam. 'THE ODYSSEY' STREAMING SCAM COULD STEAL YOUR BANK INFO How DoppelCart fake shops steal your card details The real danger starts when you decide to check out. Nebty tested several checkout pages tied to the DoppelCart cluster and found code collecting: According to the researchers, those fields can be transmitted through WebSockets to command-and-control infrastructure in real time. So, an attacker may receive the information while you're still sitting on the checkout page. The technique has similarities to web skimming, where malicious code captures payment information as a shopper types it into an online checkout page. We've previously broken down how that kind of attack works and why shoppers may see no obvious warning: Web skimming attacks target major payment networks. Your one-time bank code can be captured too This is the part I find especially concerning. Many of us have been trained to see a verification code from our bank as an extra layer of protection. DoppelCart can potentially turn that security step against you. Nebty found that the checkout code can relay the one-time confirmation code issued by a victim's bank. Attackers may then try to use the code to get past protections surrounding a fraudulent transaction. So, don't automatically enter a bank code simply because a checkout page asks for it. Read the bank's message carefully. Look at the merchant and transaction details if they're included. If something does not match the purchase you're making, stop the transaction and contact your bank through its official app or the number printed on your card. The legitimate business can get dragged into the scam DoppelCart creates another headache after the purchase. Some fake shops display the real company's legitimate customer support address. Now imagine you place an order and nothing arrives. You find the support information on the site and contact the business demanding to know where your purchase went. The company you're calling may have no idea what you're talking about because you never bought anything from it. Nebty says legitimate businesses have received complaints from shoppers over orders those businesses never processed. The scammer gets the payment information. Meanwhile, the legitimate company gets the angry customer and has to explain that somebody copied its store. Nebty says it tried to contact the main hosting provider associated with DoppelCart sites but received no response. Want to see whether a brand or website appears in the DoppelCart investigation? Search Nebty's DoppelCart database at investigations.nebty-id.com/doppelcart. APPLE PAY TEXT SCAM THREATENS $8,250 LOSS IN 35 MINUTES How to spot a fake online store before you pay A professional-looking site no longer gives you enough information to decide whether a retailer deserves your trust. Instead, slow down when you're shopping somewhere unfamiliar. 1) Check the exact web address Look at the domain in your browser before entering payment information. A fake site may use a recognizable company name inside a completely different domain. If you're trying to buy directly from a well-known brand, find its official website independently. Also, don't let the padlock or HTTPS fool you. HTTPS tells you a website encrypts the connection. It does not prove the seller behind the site is legitimate. Scammers can encrypt websites too. 2) Take another look at an extreme discount A 65% discount can make you want to buy before the deal disappears. That's when I would slow down. Check the product on the company's official website or compare it with a retailer you already know. If the price difference looks unusually large, investigate the seller. 3) Research an unfamiliar retailer Search the store's name before buying. Look beyond reviews displayed on the website itself. Search for independent complaints or reports that connect the domain to scams. Then check the company's contact information. A cloned website can look impressive while having very little legitimate history behind it. 4) Pay by credit card when possible The Federal Trade Commission recommends paying by credit card when possible for online purchases because credit cards provide protections when a transaction goes wrong. Some issuers also let you use virtual card numbers for online purchases. Availability varies by issuer. A virtual number can keep your primary card number away from the merchant and may let you shut down the virtual number if something goes wrong. 5) Read bank verification messages carefully Don't treat a one-time verification code as a routine box to fill in. Read the message your bank sends. If the merchant or transaction looks unfamiliar, do not enter the code. Contact your card issuer through a trusted channel instead. 6) Turn on transaction alerts Check whether your bank or card issuer lets you receive notifications when purchases hit your account. Alerts can help you spot an unfamiliar transaction quickly. Do not ignore a small charge simply because the amount looks harmless. Any transaction you don't recognize deserves a closer look. 7) Use strong security software Strong antivirus software can help warn you about known malicious websites and dangerous links. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com However, no program catches every newly created fake shopping site. That means your own judgment still plays an important role when a store you've never heard of suddenly offers the deal of the year. What to do if you already entered your card on a suspicious shop Act quickly if you think you purchased from a DoppelCart site or another fake retailer. The FTC recommends contacting the financial institution you used to make the payment as soon as possible. Contact your card issuer right away Use the number on the back of your card, your bank's official app or its official website. Tell the issuer that you entered your card information on a suspected fraudulent website. Ask whether the card should be locked or replaced with a new number. If you also entered a one-time verification code from your bank, tell them that too. Check your account for suspicious charges Review your recent transactions and continue watching the account. If you paid the fake retailer, tell your issuer that you believe the transaction involved a scam. Also report any other charges you do not recognize. The FTC recommends asking the card issuer or bank whether it can reverse the fraudulent transaction and return your money. Change any password you reused If the fake store asked you to create an account and you reused a password from somewhere else, change that password on the other accounts. Give important accounts unique passwords. A password manager can help generate and store strong passwords without forcing you to remember every one. Watch for follow-up scams Remember what DoppelCart checkout pages can collect. The people behind the operation may have your contact information along with payment details. Be suspicious of unexpected bank warnings, delivery messages or refund offers connected to the purchase. Scammers sometimes target people who already lost money and then pose as someone who can help recover it. Go directly to your bank or the company's official website rather than clicking a link in an unexpected message. Run a security scan if you downloaded something If you downloaded a file, installed software or gave the suspicious site additional access to your device, update your security software and run a scan with strong antivirus software. If all you did was type card information into the fake checkout, focus first on protecting the payment account and watching for fraudulent transactions. Report the fake store Report suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Reports can help authorities identify fraud patterns and investigate scam operations. Kurt's key takeaways What bothers me most about DoppelCart is how convincing these fake stores can look. You may recognize the products and the branding because scammers copied them from a real business. For me, that changes how I look at a bargain from a store I don't know. If the price seems unusually low, I want to know exactly who I'm buying from before I enter my card information. Take a minute to check the web address and search for the retailer on your own. That small pause could save you from having to replace your card or deal with fraudulent charges later. Have you ever landed on an online store that looked completely legitimate but something made you suspicious, and what tipped you off? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com. content: Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian went viral following his team’s miraculous 24-23 comeback against Ohio State this past Saturday after running off from a postgame interview with ESPN’s Holly Rowe. Sarkisian screamed, "That’s called Texas fight! That’s called Texas fight! Hook ‘em!" before running off back to the locker room to celebrate the victory with his team. At the time, Rowe hadn’t even asked her first question to him postgame, and she seemed quite upset as she darted out of camera view after Sarkisian ran away. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Sarkisian addressed the situation ahead of the team’s next scheduled contest against UTSA. "As it pertains to after the ball game, again there was a delay after I greeted Coach Day in the middle of the field. There was a delay in the moment, you know, through that delay, I wanted to go celebrate with our team," he said, per On Texas Football. "We just had a 21-point fourth-quarter comeback against the No. 1 team in the country. If hindsight’s 20/20, if I could do it all over again, I would have exuded more patience in that moment and sat through and waited for the interview with Holly." TEXAS' ARCH MANNING UNDER SCRUTINY FOR HIS REACTION TO AI VIDEO OF STEVE SARKISIAN SLAPPING ESPN'S HOLLY ROWE Sarkisian added that he has "a ton of respect for ESPN and Holly" and didn’t mean to let the moment get the better of him. "Holly and I go way back to even my days of playing at BYU, and we’ve got a great relationship. ESPN is a great partner of ours. We know we’re going to have more opportunities with that crew covering us, and we’re looking forward to those opportunities. So, could have definitely handled that situation better with a little bit more patience in the moment." The viral moment was one social media users ran with, creating AI versions in which Sarkisian was seen slapping Rowe before running off the field. And those AI-manipulated videos led quarterback Arch Manning to have to issue an apology to Rowe after describing those videos as hilarious during his Monday press conference. Manning, who led the Longhorns back in the second half on Saturday night, apologized to Rowe on Tuesday following his Monday news conference, calling his comments "insensitive" and saying he will be "more thoughtful going forward." Rowe accepted his apology. "Obviously Arch recognizes he made a mistake, and it’s an unfortunate one," Sarkisian added. "Nowhere do we condone domestic violence or violence against women. title: El-Sayed tries to put the Hasan Piker debate behind him as midterms approach
description: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed repeatedly deflected calls to disavow Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's controversial rhetoric.
content: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has faced backlash for months over his relationship with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who is known for his controversial rhetoric. The candidate has yet to disavow Piker and now seems to be tiring of the questions, looking to shift focus to the issues that he says are really at the heart of the race. El-Sayed's relationship with Piker was scrutinized before the two of them appeared at a campaign event in April 2026. On March 30, El-Sayed posted a video with the caption "Let's talk about Hasan." In the video, the Michigan Democrat explained that he was looking for a way to access people who "feel locked out of our politics," saying that they are the same people who Piker speaks to through his daily streams. He went on to clarify where he agrees with Piker, which included the streamer's stances on the war in Iran, AIPAC's involvement in U.S. politics and healthcare. "Now, he streams for eight hours a day, every day. A lot of the things that he said, I might not agree with, but that doesn't mean I'm not going to have a conversation with him, and that doesn't mean that the people who listen to him don't deserve to listen to their politicians and to have a pathway into politics to vote for the things that they need and deserve," El-Sayed said. ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK The Michigan Democrat joined "FOX & Friends" ahead of his event with Piker, where he said that appearing with someone did not mean that he agreed with them. While he did not disavow Piker specifically, he referred to the streamer's past remarks, saying, "Of course, I oppose rape. Of course, I don't think 9/11 was justified." Amid the scrutiny of his decision to campaign with Piker, El-Sayed repeatedly blamed the criticism on "cancel culture" and insisted that Democrats needed to be willing to speak with people at their level. The event with Piker went on as planned, but El-Sayed still faced questions. He was asked while standing next to Piker to disavow the streamer's past rhetoric, which he refused to do. "I'm not here to disavow people's views. I'm here to have a conversation about how to get money out of politics, put money back in pockets, and pass Medicare for all. That's the conversation that folks are here to listen to," El-Sayed said in response. EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION The controversy surrounding the April campus appearance would set off a months-long line of questioning, with El-Sayed repeatedly walking the line between condemning some of Piker's rhetoric without going into specifics or alienating the streamer's audience. This became more common after El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in the Democratic primary in August. Following El-Sayed's victory, Piker called for those who opposed the Michigan Democrat to be "punished" by the party. "You can't be out here saying like, 'Oh, I'm a centrist Democrat. And I think Abdul is a bridge too far.' That must be punished," Piker said. After his primary victory, El-Sayed was asked in multiple interviews to comment on Piker's past rhetoric. When CNN's Kaitlan Collins asked El-Sayed whether he would renounce Piker in August, something that Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., had urged him to do, the Michigan Democrat said he was "less focused on folks who are campaigning with me, more focused on the folks I'm campaigning to." A few days later, El-Sayed was asked about Piker again, this time during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press." In response to host Kristen Welker's question, El-Sayed repeated what he said on CNN about focusing more on voters than those who appear with him on the campaign trail. Shortly after El-Sayed's appearance on "Meet the Press," Piker drew the ire of several lawmakers on both sides of the aisle after making a comment that some interpreted as blaming antisemitic attacks on American Jews' support of Israel. "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said during his Aug. 20 stream. HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED' The comment set off a wave of condemnations from lawmakers, including Sens. Cory Booker, D-N.J.; Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich.; and Jacky Rosen, D-Nev.; House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.; and Reps. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J.; Ritchie Torres, D-N.Y.; Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla.; Brad Schneider, D-Ill.; Greg Stanton, D-Ariz.; and Hillary Scholten, D-Mich. El-Sayed issued a statement in which he seemed to distance himself from Piker amid the backlash. "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed wrote on X. "My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters," he added. "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk." Shortly after the controversy over Piker's remarks, El-Sayed told Semafor that he had "no plans" to campaign with the streamer. However, this did not stop the press from asking the Michigan Democrat about Piker. During an appearance on "The Breakfast Club" in late August, El-Sayed framed criticism of his ties to Piker as a form of "cancel culture," saying that there was a "massive effort to cancel Hasan." "I think we've got to stop with the cancel culture. It's not about, like, 'Where are you on this one individual?' It's more, 'Do you agree or disagree with the thing that the person said?' And, the thing about it is, that, like, when we play as if the whole person can be reduced to a single soundbite that you took out of context, you're not, you're not dealing with real life," El-Sayed said. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES El-Sayed's exasperation with the media's questions about Piker became apparent during a Sept. 13 appearance on "Face the Nation." When CBS News' Weijia Jiang asked El-Sayed about Jewish Michiganders' concerns regarding his ties to Piker, the Michigan Democrat appeared to be fed up. "Weijia, with all due respect, this is the third time you’ve asked about a Twitch streamer in California. I’ve done four events in Michigan this week. You know what didn’t come up? Twitch streamers in California," El-Sayed responded. The candidate said that voters would rather discuss grocery prices, healthcare and the environment, among other things. "I’m not interested in having a conversation about streamers in California because they are not raising the prices of gas and groceries," El-Sayed added. title: There is a way to fix Social Security. And the solution might surprise you
description: Three proposals to fix Social Security pull every lever: raising the wage cap, a gradual payroll tax increase and pushing full retirement age to 70.
content: Every few months, another headline tells Americans that Social Security is going broke. It's scary. It's also not quite true. Social Security isn't going to wake up one morning with zero dollars coming through the door. Even if its trust fund reserves are depleted, millions of workers will still be paying Social Security taxes every payday. CONGRESS SPENDS $7 TRILLION. HERE’S HOW THAT MATH WORKS OUT IF YOU THINK OF JUST $100 The problem is that those taxes eventually won't generate enough money to pay 100% of scheduled benefits. So, let's stop pretending Social Security can't be fixed. It can. You're just probably not going to like the fix. Here are three changes Washington should seriously consider. 1. Raise the Social Security wage cap to $400,000 In 2026, employees pay 6.2% into Social Security, and employers contribute another 6.2%, but the tax stops once wages reach $184,500. SIX DIFFERENT WAYS THAT PROVE THE WEALTHY PAY A LOT MORE THAN THEIR ‘FAIR SHARE’ Someone making $100,000 pays Social Security tax on every dollar. Someone making $1 million doesn't. That's going to become increasingly difficult politically and mathematically to defend. My first suggestion: Raise the Social Security taxable wage ceiling to $400,000. For somebody earning $400,000, that would expose another $215,500 of wages to Social Security taxes. It also doesn’t make Social Security an infinite tax like Medicare. PROGRESSIVES WANT TO TAX BILLIONAIRES FIRST, AND YOU'RE NEXT ON THE LIST At today's 12.4% combined employee-employer rate, that's potentially another $26,722 annually flowing into the system from that worker and employer combined. Depending on exactly how Congress structured the change, we're potentially talking about well over $1 trillion of additional revenue over a decade. Higher earners won't like it. I wouldn't like paying it either. But Social Security needs revenue. It’s called a compromise. 2. Take the 6.2% tax to 7.2%, one-tenth at a time Here's the second part politicians really won't want to advertise. Especially Democrats. TOP SENATE DEM’S NEW TAX IDEA GETS TORCHED AS CRITICS WARN NEARLY EVERY AMERICAN COULD PAY Everyone needs some skin in the game. Instead of suddenly slamming workers with a giant payroll-tax increase, raise the employee Social Security tax rate from 6.2% to 7.2% gradually over 10 years. That's just 0.1 percentage point each year. Employers would see a corresponding gradual increase. DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS HAVE LOTS OF IDEAS, BUT HOW ARE WE SUPPOSED TO PAY FOR THEM? For someone earning $75,000, the first increase amounts to about $75 for the entire year. Ten years later, the employee would be paying an additional $750 annually at today's income. Higher earners won't like it. I wouldn't like paying it either. But Social Security needs revenue. It’s called a compromise. Nobody enjoys paying more taxes. But slowly adjusting the rate over a decade gives workers and businesses time to adapt. AMERICA'S LIFESPAN HAS DOUBLED SINCE 1776 — EXPERTS REVEAL WHAT CHANGED 3. If you were born after 1990, 70 becomes the new 67 Now comes the third rail. Retirement age. Today's full retirement age is 67 for people born in 1960 or later. Don't change the deal for someone who's 62 and has spent their entire working life planning around 67. Instead, draw a line. If you were born after 1990, gradually move full retirement age to 70. Someone born in 1991 turns 35 this year. They have decades to plan for the change. People are living longer than generations before them. If we're going to make Social Security financially sustainable for another generation, the retirement-age math eventually has to reflect longevity. In the end, nobody gets a free lunch Here's the political problem. Republicans don't want tax increases. Democrats don't want benefit reductions. Workers don't want to pay more. Employers don't want to pay more. High earners certainly don't want another $200,000-plus of wages subjected to payroll taxes. And nobody wants to hear they're working until 70. Welcome to compromise. There are really only three levers available to fix Social Security, and it’s really this simple unless you start doing means testing. Tax more income. Raise more revenue. Reduce future benefits. This plan pulls all three. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Higher earners pay Social Security tax on more wages. Workers and employers gradually contribute more. Younger Americans wait longer for full retirement benefits. And importantly, Social Security doesn't "run out of money." Payroll taxes continue coming in even if the trust fund reserves are exhausted. That's why Congress should stop scaring Americans and start solving the problem. Because the longer Washington waits, the uglier the eventual solution becomes. Nobody gets everything they want under this plan. title: Jasmine Crockett torched for honoring singer with notorious history of violence: 'Completely vile'
description: Jasmine Crockett entered Chris Brown into the congressional record, sparking fierce backlash over his felony assault conviction involving Rihanna.
content: Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, who recently lost her Senate bid, is facing online backlash after she honored music artist Chris Brown by entering him into the congressional record this past weekend. "Now, y’all know, I tend to get in trouble every once in a while. I’m a make this real quick. I need to know who run it! So is Dallas in the building?" Crockett said as she took the stage alongside Brown on Saturday evening. "Let’s give it up for Chris Brown," she added to applause from the audience. The moment drew scrutiny from viewers online, raising questions about Crockett’s status as a lawmaker and whether it should be used to celebrate Brown, someone with a history of domestic violence. AMERICA OWES BLACK WOMEN 'EVERYTHING,' REP JASMINE CROCKETT RANTS OVER JULY 4 WEEKEND Among other instances of misconduct, Brown pleaded guilty in 2009 to felony assault after he attacked his then-girlfriend and famous singer, Rihanna. Many images of her injuries were made public, sparking intense condemnation from the music industry. His violence, however, wouldn’t stop there. He was involved in a 2013 altercation with Frank Ocean, another singer, and pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor assault charge that same year. In 2017, another ex-girlfriend was granted a domestic violence restraining order against him after she alleged physical abuse. Most recently, Brown pleaded guilty to charges of striking producer Abe Diaw twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in July 2023. He is expected to receive a sentence in October for a separate charge for affray, a criminal charge in English law for unlawfully threatening violence against another person. Andrew Kerr, an investigative reporter with the Washington Free Beacon, quickly noted Brown’s past in a post to X after news of Crockett’s tribute began to spread online. "Kamala Harris-endorsed Rep. Jasmine Crockett uses her congressional authority to honor Chris Brown, the rapper best known for beating ever-living s--- out of Rihanna in 2009," Kerr wrote. Shannon Watts, a Democratic activist and political commentator, also pointed out Brown’s storied past. WATCH: HEARING TURMOIL AS JASMINE CROCKETT UNLOADS ON MLK'S NIECE IN WILD RACIALLY-CHARGED RANT "Chris Brown pled guilty to felony assault after brutally attacking Rihanna. Another ex, Karrueche Tran, later obtained a five-year restraining order after testifying that he abused and threatened her. He has also faced multiple allegations of violence and sexual assault against other women," Watts wrote. Crockett’s member statement, a form of recognition that lawmakers can have entered into the congressional record without any vote, recognizes "the artistry of Chris Brown and Usher Raymond." On stage on Saturday, Crockett framed her member statement as a way to recognize two key artists who had helped shape contemporary R&B and pop music, especially for the Black community. "I know it’s almost Sunday, so I wanna be clear. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning. And right now, we are experiencing Black joy to the highest level, and I wanted to make sure we document that in the Congressional Record," Crockett said. But Democratic strategist Ameshia Cross believes that the moment was a political miscalculation, coming across as ignorant of the challenges in the Black community. "Chris Brown has a problem, and several folks beyond Rihanna have met his violent rage. It’s well-documented. This was a ridiculous move by Crockett," she wrote on X. "Also, when Black women suffer [domestic violence] at the highest rates and often fatally, this was tone deaf as hell," she added. Eric Michael Garcia, the D.C. bureau chief of the Independent, echoed Cross’ thinking. "Absolutely disgusting to see Jasmine Crockett platform and honor an abuser of women. Just completely vile," Garcia wrote in a post of his own. Dan Winslow, a New York Times bestselling author, hinted that the moment had changed his view of her. WATCH: TALARICO EMBRACES ‘FREAKY’ IDENTITY AS CROWDS CHANT NAME MEANT AS INSULT: ‘SO WEIRD’ "CHRIS BROWN plead guilty to beating Rihanna. It was a horrific and savage beating. Crockett thought he deserved to be honored. Absolutely disgusting behavior. I am glad she lost. I will never support her again," Winslow wrote. In response to the public backlash, Brown posted a response to his Instagram account, pleading to be left alone and expressing displeasure at Crockett having put him in the spotlight. "Funny thing is... YALL CAME TO ME WITH THIS! NOT THE OTHER WAY AROUND. I was minding my own d-mn business. My shows in Dallas were already sold out. I ain't asked to be honored because I knew some sh-t like this would happen... I have an idea how about y'all leave me the f--- alone and let me focus on the fans that spent their money to actually see and support me," Brown wrote. title: Celebrity plastic surgeon reveals when it's too soon for a facelift, and when waiting can backfire
description: Dr. Terry Dubrow reveals why Kris Jenner's public facelift is driving 38-year-olds to seek facelift surgery they don't yet need.
content: When it comes to getting a facelift, timing may be everything. Going under the knife too soon could mean having surgery before it’s necessary — but waiting too long can also backfire, according to celebrity plastic surgeon Dr. Terry Dubrow. During an episode of Josh Peck’s and Ben Soffer's podcast, "Good Guys," the Beverly Hills-based surgeon said some women are jumping the gun and getting the procedure too soon. CHEAP SURGERY OVERSEAS MAY COME WITH DEVASTATING COMPLICATIONS, DOCTORS WARN "For those people in their 30s who want some skin tightening, they need to wait, 'cause there will be the technology that will allow early facelifts without cutting," he said. Dubrow also mentioned Kris Jenner’s recent facelift, which may have motivated women to seek out the procedure based on her results. "That made facelifts like, ‘Oh, Kris Jenner did it and made it public. Now it's cool. Everybody get a facelift,’" he said. "So then you're seeing 38-year-old people in your office wanting a facelift, and you go, ‘OK, hold on a second. You don't even need a facelift. You need to wait, because, you know, a facelift is incisions and scars, and elevating up the skin, numbness and all sorts of potential things that can go wrong." MEN FACE NEW PRESSURE TO STAY ‘HOT’ AS THEY AGE — AND IT’S NOT JUST ABOUT LIVING LONGER Dubrow warned that if people have too many facelifts, "when it starts to relax, it can relax in weird ways." "You've all seen it — people who look pretty good, but there's something about the way their skin lies on their face that looks unnatural, and it ruins the whole look," he warned. "If you have early laxity, don't go in for your ‘Kris Jenner facelift.’ Still wait, because that technology is just around the corner." Conversely, the surgeon has warned that waiting too long — while relying on other nonsurgical fixes — can also backfire. "A lot of women are staying on the ‘nonsurgical treadmill’ for too long," Dubrow told Fox News Digital. DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH "They keep adding filler, lasers and tightening treatments, when the real problem is that the deeper tissues have dropped." While it is possible to get a great result with a later-in-life facelift, the doctor pointed out that as the skin becomes looser, the tissues descend further, which may require more extensive surgery. "My feeling is that once those treatments stop producing a natural result, continuing to postpone surgery can actually make you look less natural." That’s not to say that nonsurgical treatments don’t have their place, he noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Fillers, lasers and tightening treatments can buy you time when they are used intelligently — but fillers cannot lift sagging tissue, and too much filler can make someone look distorted." "The right time should be based on your face, not the doctor’s menu." Aggressive energy treatments can also create scarring under the skin and make surgery more difficult later, Dubrow cautioned — "so, ask whether a treatment is truly delaying a facelift or just delaying the decision." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER There is no "magic age" in terms of best results with a facelift, according to Dubrow. "For some women, it is their late 40s. For others, it is their 50s or 60s," he said. "It comes down to genetics, skin quality and what is happening along the jawline and neck." Advice for facelift timing can vary depending on what type of expert you see, and every specialist tends to see the problem through the treatments they perform, the doctor noted. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "A dermatologist may explain what can still be accomplished without surgery, and a board-certified plastic surgeon can tell you when those options have reached their limit … and when it is time to actually reposition the anatomy," he said. Ultimately, he suggests getting opinions from both sides. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The right time should be based on your face, not the doctor’s menu," Dubrow said. "Choose what makes sense for your anatomy, your goals and your tolerance for surgery." "The best facelift is the one nobody knows you had, but the best advice often comes from hearing more than one point of view."

title: Robert Kraft opposes dangerous lies, not free speech | Matt Calkins
description: Robert Kraft banned Macklemore from Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows over what he called "hate speech," sparking backlash from artists and AOC.
content: Based on the way American attitudes have shifted toward a certain country in the Middle East, Robert Kraft likely lost a lot of fans with a recent decision. But that doesn't mean it was the wrong decision. Not in the least. The Patriots' owner said Monday that Macklemore will be removed from two of Ed Sheeran's shows later this month at Gillette Stadium (which Kraft also owns) for what he deemed "hate speech" toward the Jewish community. Macklemore has made no secret of how he feels about Israel, regularly using his platform to decry a "genocide" he falsely says is taking place in Gaza. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! His protest song "Hind's Hall" — in which he says former President Joe Biden has blood on his hands and that the music industry is "complicit" with its "silence" — is hardly subtle. It celebrates the violent and illegal actions by students, faculty and outside activists on the campus of Columbia University. And though some may accuse Kraft of launching an attack on free speech, I think he was saying something else: enough. That takes a lot of spine when it's clear there will be backlash. All of the other opening acts for Sheeran (not to mention his own band) quit the tour in solidarity with Macklemore, while Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez denounced Kraft's choice as "censorship" against "the genocide in Gaza." Kraft has since pledged $2 million toward humanitarian aid in the Israel-Gaza region but he's held firm on his Macklemore ban. Other owners have followed suit. Good on them. The genocide talk has to stop — because it has real consequences. "Real Time" host Bill Maher expressed a similar sentiment during his "New Rule" segment last Friday. It was a long way from an Israel hagiography, but he pushed back against the genocide lie that so many have adopted as fact. ROBERT KRAFT, GILLETTE STADIUM BOOT MACKLEMORE FROM ED SHEERAN TOUR OVER ‘FREE PALESTINE’ RANT Genocides, Maher said, are attempts to wipe out entire populations. The attacker won't stop until all of its human targets are exterminated. That isn't what's happening in Gaza — just as it wasn't what was happening when the U.S. dropped two atomic bombs on Japan, leading to the end of World War II. A stat that Maher used to bolster his point was that about 73,000 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli counter attacks since October 7, 2023,(according to Hamas, while not distinguishing how many were part of Hamas) which comprises roughly three percent of their population. He then pointed out how nearly 99 percent of the three million Jews in Poland were killed during World War II. The first reflects the tragedy of war. But only the second is a genocide. Still, polling has shown that Americans are more likely to believe that a genocide is taking place in Gaza than not. And it coincides with a Gallup poll showing that more Americans are sympathetic toward Palestine than it is Israel. Another study found that almost half the country has difficulty distinguishing American Jews from the Israeli government. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Might that be why the Anti-Defamation League reported a 360% increase in antisemitic incidents since Hamas' attack on Israel three Octobers ago? Or why a 2025 American Jewish Committee poll found that 91 percent of American Jews felt less safe as a Jewish person due to violent attacks in the U.S? Or why 55 percent said they have changed their behavior (such as hiding Jewish identity) over a one-year span for fear of antisemitism? If you watch this video of Pro-Palestine supporters blocking a Jewish student from going to class, you'll see a clear case of young minds being poisoned by rhetoric. Kraft, who's Jewish, knows the effect that type of rhetoric can have. So, he did something about it. This, of course, is much different than preventing someone from speaking their minds in a public space. Free speech in that respect must be preserved at all costs. But the First Amendment doesn't stop words from having consequences. Sometimes they get you fired, sometimes they tarnish your reputation, and sometimes they make it so you can't perform in privately-owned stadiums. This isn't the first time Macklemore has been muted for what's come out of his mouth. After he said "F--- America" at a show in Seattle two years ago, the Mariners stopped playing his song "Can't Hold Us" during the seventh-inning stretch. No doubt the rapper has the right to say what he wants. But Kraft and other owners have the right — or perhaps in this case, duty — to say "not on our turf." I'm generally not a big fan of end-zone messaging like "End Racism." It just feels performative. But Yom Kippur — the holiest of Jewish holidays — starts at sundown Sunday. title: Trump claims he has spoken to Iran 'directly,' says war is 'hopefully' near an end
description: President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he has spoken to Tehran "directly," adding that the Iranians "want to make a deal" with the United States. He also said the war, which began on Feb. 28, is "hopefully" coming to an end in the near term.
content:
Iran is under mounting military and economic pressure that could force the regime to escalate its conflict with the U.S. or eventually implode, regional experts said Thursday.
“Both scenarios are possible at the same time,” Middle East Institute adjunct fellow Nazee Moini said on “ The Story .”
“The Islamic regime is under extreme pressure for all the good reasons, militarily, economically,” the expert added before stating that everything Washington has done so far has brought Iran one step closer to a state of affairs where they either have to “gamble for restriction, go all out militarily and try to raise the cost of U.S. or eventually implode.”
“Both scenarios are possible at the same time,” Moini added.
Her remarks came as President Donald Trump said Thursday that he hoped the war with Iran was nearing its end, while weighing a “big decision” over whether to escalate U.S. military action to “annihilate” the Iranian regime or pursue a path to end the conflict.

title: Judge Judy warns of 'danger' if prosecutors don't retry Lindsay Clancy after murder trial ends in mistrial
description: Judge Judy Sheindlin says there's a "danger" in not retrying Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children.
content: Judge Judy Sheindlin weighed in Thursday on the closely watched Lindsay Clancy murder case following its mistrial, warning there could be a "danger" in prosecutors deciding not to retry the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children. The 83-year-old judge and television personality was asked by TMZ whether Clancy should face another trial after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict earlier this month. "I think there's a danger in that, in not retrying," Sheindlin responded. Sheindlin, who launched the popular syndicated show "Judge Judy," which aired for 25 seasons, was also asked about her view on the outcome of the trial after the jury's deliberations ended in a reported 11-1 split in favor of finding Clancy not criminally responsible. PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL Watch full video on TMZ "I can't give you a two-minute answer on that," Sheindlin said. She was then asked whether she believed Clancy should have been found guilty. "There's no question, my dear, that she killed her children," Sheindlin said. "The only question is, is there an excuse for it? Make up your own mind on that one." DR PHIL SAYS LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL A 'TEACHABLE MOMENT' ON POSTPARTUM PSYCHOSIS: 'THERE WAS A FAILURE HERE' TMZ also asked Sheindlin about Rep. Nancy Mace's public call for Clancy to be publicly executed. "I think it's ridiculous," Sheindlin responded. Clancy's defense does not dispute that the 36-year-old former delivery room nurse strangled her three children with exercise bands in January 2023. Her defense has argued that she was not criminally responsible because of mental illness or defect. LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR DENIES BIAS ALLEGATIONS, WANTS 'CONVERSATION STARTED' ABOUT WOMEN'S MENTAL HEALTH Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after seven days of deliberations when jurors said they could not reach a unanimous verdict. Several jurors later said 11 members of the panel favored finding Clancy not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, while one favored conviction. Immediately after the mistrial was declared, Clancy's longtime defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, signaled that he would fight another attempt to put her on trial. The defense has indicated it plans to argue that the circumstances surrounding the mistrial should bar a second trial. However, in a recent interview with Fox News' Bryan Llenas, Reddington said that if prosecutors reduced the top charge to second-degree murder, he would opt for a bench trial — one without a jury — in the hope that she would receive probation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Clancy remains in custody at Tewksbury Hospital and is due back in court Sept. 29. Fox News Digital's Michael Ruiz and Stepheny Price contributed to this report.

title: Top DOJ official warns of deadly smuggling route after 42 vanish at sea
description: The Justice Department says 42 people vanished at sea after a Colombian smuggler guided them onto a boat from San Andrés Island to Nicaragua.
content: A Colombian smuggler’s guilty plea is shedding new light on a deadly route to the United States after a boat carrying 42 people vanished at sea and a top Justice Department official said the danger would not have ended if they reached land. Luis Enrique Linero Pinto, 41, also known as "El Calvo," pleaded guilty in federal court in El Paso, Texas, after being extradited from Colombia for his role in a smuggling conspiracy that prosecutors said used bribery and maritime routes to move migrants north. The boat left Colombia’s San Andrés Island for Nicaragua on Oct. 21, 2023, carrying approximately 40 migrants and two captains. It never arrived, and no one aboard has been seen or heard from since. "This was a particularly sad and disturbing situation," Assistant Attorney General Tysen Duva, who leads the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, told Fox News Digital. OVERCROWDED MIGRANT VESSEL WITH 240 PEOPLE ON BOARD INTERCEPTED NEAR TURKS AND CAICOS "These 40 individuals and the two boat captains, once they set out from San Andrés Island to Nicaragua, were never heard from again," Duva said. "These individuals are, of course, missing and presumed dead, and it appears that there were no survivors." ELEVEN INDICTED IN ALLEGED TEXAS SMUGGLING SCHEME THAT LEFT 7 MIGRANTS DEAD IN SHIPPING CONTAINER Duva said the disappearance offers a brutal look at the danger posed by transnational smuggling organizations that turn vulnerable migrants into commodities while pursuing routes toward the United States. "It’s all about money," he said. "Anybody who’s involved with a cartel or transnational smuggling in this regard, it is about money. It’s about preying on people’s misfortune." MEXICAN NATIONAL SENTENCED IN BORDER CHILD SMUGGLING CASE INVOLVING THC-LACED CANDY According to the Justice Department, Linero Pinto advised migrants on how to reach San Andrés Island, personally received them upon arrival, arranged their accommodations and transported them to boats bound for Nicaragua. From there, the migrants intended to travel through Central America and Mexico before illegally entering the United States, prosecutors said. CBP JOINS FORCES WITH COAST GUARD TO INTERCEPT 3 SMUGGLING BOATS, APPREHEND 60 PEOPLE OFF CALIFORNIA COAST Linero Pinto also bribed members of the Colombian navy to obtain real-time intelligence about the positions of patrol vessels between San Andrés Island and Nicaragua, allowing smuggling boats to evade authorities, according to court documents. He admitted helping smuggle the migrants aboard the boat that vanished in October 2023. INSIDE UNDERGROUND EL PASO STORM DRAIN SYSTEM BORDER PATROL SAYS CARTELS EXPLOIT TO SMUGGLE ILLEGAL MIGRANTS Duva said the victims had not even completed the opening stretch of the dangerous route when they disappeared. "That’s the first leg. They didn’t even finish the first leg here and get to Nicaragua and then try to come north by land," he said. "It’s a really long journey, and it’s full of really bad things that can happen." DOJ SAYS 11 MIGRANTS INDICTED IN MULTI-STATE SEX TRAFFICKING, DRUG, FIREARMS CASE The danger, he warned, is not confined to the open water. Duva said migrants can face treacherous terrain while traveling through South and Central America and across the U.S.-Mexico border. Even those who reach the United States may be trapped by mounting debts and pushed into sex trafficking, he warned. "You pay money to come to the United States, and then when you get here, the co-conspirators or those involved in the criminal enterprise will say, ‘But now you owe more, and you’re going to work this off in the sex trade,’" Duva said. "Cross-border smuggling cases often times just morph right into human trafficking cases," he continued. "The crime sort of changes along the way. The travelers are the ones victimized, and this comes at a significant cost in terms of public safety." Linero Pinto was charged in October 2024 and arrested in Colombia that December at the request of the U.S. government. He was later extradited to the United States and made his first appearance in federal court in El Paso in December 2025. He pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and placing lives in jeopardy. He faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison, though a sentencing date has not been set. ‘GHOSTS’ ON FLORIDA HIGHWAYS: ROADSIDE STINGS SNARE 249 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, OFFICERS WARN MANY MORE HIDING A case against alleged co-conspirator Hernando Manuel de la Cruz Rivera Orjuela remains pending, Duva said. The prosecution is part of Operation Take Back America and was coordinated by Joint Task Force Alpha, the Justice Department-led initiative targeting cartels and other transnational organizations involved in high-impact human smuggling and trafficking. Duva praised President Donald Trump and his administration for putting a "tremendous focus" on the initiative and providing the Justice Department with additional resources to pursue smugglers, cartels and other transnational criminal organizations. "We’re super thankful to President Trump," Duva said. "We’re deeply thankful to the White House for that. We’re thankful to Congress for that, and we’re going to keep doing what we’re doing." Duva said funding approved through Trump’s signature One Big Beautiful Bill allowed the Criminal Division to hire additional prosecutors and place experienced attorneys in sections handling the administration’s priorities. "People think, ‘Well, what is that? What did it do?’" he said. "We’re feeling the effects of that. We’re able to put skilled prosecutors in these different sections to attack these administration priorities." Duva said the task force is hunting criminal networks along the southern border, maritime routes near Florida and the northern border with Canada. "We are focusing on these cases at any border that we have," he said. His warning to smugglers operating beyond America’s borders was blunt. "Our reach is substantial," Duva said. "We are going to chase these cases no matter where they originate from or where we find them." Duva said the department’s expanded international partnerships are critical because the criminals behind the operations often believe distance will protect them from prosecution. "They just think, ‘Well, they catch other people, but they’re not going to get me,’" he said. "You really try to combat that one case at a time." Joint Task Force Alpha has produced more than 483 domestic and international arrests, over 436 U.S. convictions and more than 371 significant prison sentences, according to the Justice Department. FIRST TREN DE ARAGUA GANG MEMBER EXTRADITED TO US ON HISTORIC TERRORISM CHARGES APPEARS BEFORE HOUSTON JUDGE Duva said the mission should transcend partisan fights because the networks being targeted threaten migrants and American communities alike. "It shouldn’t be partisan," he said. "It should be obvious that anybody who’s in the White House, anybody who is in Congress, should be lauding these cases and the work that’s being done by Criminal Division entities like Joint Task Force Alpha." The Justice Department’s ultimate goal, Duva said, is the "total elimination" of cartels and the criminal organizations profiting from human suffering. "You do it one case at a time," he said. "We are focused on doing the very best cases that we can for the American people. That’s what we get up every day and think about." For Duva, however, the vanished boat remains a haunting illustration of why that mission matters. "It’s super tragic, and hopefully people realize when they hear about this case just how dangerous it is and how important it is that you target these smuggling groups."

title: ‘Voters get to choose — just not the result’: Russia’s parliamentary election reaches occupied Ukraine
description: Russian State Duma elections will be held in occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia amid accusations of armed voter intimidation.
content: Russian State Duma elections began Friday — the first since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Voting is also taking place in the areas annexed from Ukraine in the east as Putin looks to reinforce popular support for the war. OSCE election observers are not invited to monitor the outcome of the elections, a telling signal, critics say, that the Kremlin has no intentions of conducting free and fair elections. "Russia’s refusal to invite an election observation mission seriously breaches its international commitments and shows a worrying disregard for democratic standards. Election observation is not optional — it is something that all OSCE participating States have agreed to, and it is a cornerstone of transparency and accountability," OSCE Parliamentary Assembly President Pere Joan Pons told Fox News Digital. Russia enacted strict censorship laws after the invasion, criminalizing any dissent about the operation or the armed forces and spreading misinformation about the war. CIA DIRECTOR JOHN RATCLIFFE MET WITH RUSSIAN INTELLIGENCE OFFICIALS IN VISIT TO MOSCOW, KREMLIN SAYS As the Kremlin has tried to keep popular support in favor of its war against Ukraine, a Russian court sentenced Lev Shlosberg, a vocal critic and leader of one of Russia’s only opposition parties to over 11 years in a penal colony for criticizing the war. Prior to Shlosberg’s sentencing, Russia's Supreme Court banned his opposition Yabloko Party from participating in September’s Duma elections. There are nine parties on the list, all supportive of Putin, including the Kremlin's own United Party in the elections, The Associated Press reported. Shortly after Russia’s invasion in 2022, Moscow unilaterally annexed portions of occupied Ukrainian territory in Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia. In 2023, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed legislation allowing elections to take place in the occupied territories. Ukraine and the international community do not recognize Russian sovereignty over the occupied regions. Elections in Russia, and by extension in the occupied territory, are seen by his critics as window-dressing opportunities used by Putin to highlight his narrative that the war in Ukraine and the annexation of Ukrainian territory was a legitimate and lawful action. Keti Korkiya from the Foundation for Defense of Democracies Russia Program told Fox News Digital that, "Russians are ready to support, symbolically, Putin, the Kremlin and the war, but if they have to pay a personal price, or even [an] economic price, they are unwilling to do that. That's why Russia has not done another wave of mobilization." The upcoming elections, like most elections in Russia, will take place under a climate of pervasive fear and manipulation, not the freedom to exercise a democratic right, according to critics. "It’s a total regime of terror," Jaroslava Barbieri, research fellow at the Ukraine Forum at Chatham House, told Fox News Digital. The last time Russian elections were held in the occupied territories was in 2024, when Putin secured a fifth term in office, winning nearly 90% of the vote. Residents in occupied Ukraine were forced to acquire Russian passports, which is how authorities are able to compile lists of voters. FORMER GEORGIAN PRIME MINISTER SAYS NATION'S ELECTION WAS 'RIGGED,' AND 'WRITTEN IN MOSCOW' "Election officials are escorted by Russian soldiers carrying ballot boxes door-to-door. Ostensibly framed as a security measure against Ukrainian partisan strikes, this is about direct intimidation, and it is a flagrant violation of international law," Barbieri added. President Vladimir Putin said in August that the State Duma elections will reaffirm Russia's stability on the world stage, noting the election will highlight the "maturity" of Russia’s political system and resilience in the face of foreign aggression, according to Turkey's Anadolu Agency. Russia’s Central Election Commission (CEC) approved new electoral regulations that will be implemented in occupied Ukraine. The Commission stressed the importance of early and at-home voting to prevent large gatherings which could be exploited by Ukrainian attacks. Russia's ministry of foreign affairs posted on X that preparations for overseas voting in Russia’s State Duma elections are nearly complete. It said there are 326 polling stations set up at Russian embassies and consulates in 152 countries. Volodymyr Ariev, a member of the Ukrainian Parliament, said people living in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories should boycott the staged Russian elections. "Any sort of elections held in the temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories is illegal and a breach of international law. Ukraine will never recognize any person ‘elected’ as a member of Parliament in the temporarily occupied territories," Ariev told Fox News Digital. Ariev said people living in the occupied east should leave their homes and spend election day someplace else, to avoid being coerced into voting. PUTIN PLANS FOR NEXT 6-YEAR TERM AS RUSSIANS VOTE IN 'NEITHER FREE NOR FAIR ELECTION' Ivana Stradner, who focuses on Russian information security and influence operations at the FDD, says as Russia’s battlefield momentum stalls, the costs of war mount, and Ukraine brings the conflict to Russia’s doorstep, Putin is seeking political legitimacy this election. "The State Duma elections give the Kremlin a chance to manufacture the appearance of public support… not only for United Russia, but for continuing Putin’s aggression in Ukraine. When the battlefield gets harder to sell, the ballot box becomes another way to sell the war," Stradner told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In the 2024 presidential elections, the annexed Donetsk People’s Republic and Luhansk People’s Republic delivered well above the current targeted 70% support, voting well over 90% for President Putin. "Apparently, in Putin’s version of democracy, the voters get to choose… just not the result," Stradner added. The three days of voting ends on September 20. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Man loses weight eating nothing but a certain food for 25 days — and paid a price
description: A New Jersey man's Sweetgreen-only diet for 25 days left him nine pounds lighter — but the cost, logistics and a celebratory cheese pizza tell a bigger story.
content: A New Jersey man ate nothing but certain foods from a fast-casual chain for 25 days — an experiment that left him nine pounds lighter and craving a slice of pizza. Tim Donohue, a 27-year-old Hoboken resident who works in advertising in New York City, documented his challenge as a modern-day spin on Morgan Spurlock's 2004 documentary "Super Size Me," he told Fox News Digital. But instead of eating McDonald's for a month, Donohue wanted to see what would happen if he exclusively ate at a chain on the opposite end of the fast-food spectrum. AMERICA'S FAVORITE FAST-FOOD CHAIN NAMED: MCDONALD'S WINS HEARTS BUT NOT BEST BURGER, SURVEY SAYS "I think it felt the furthest possible opposite of McDonald's," Donohue said of choosing Sweetgreen. The idea also came from watching his health-conscious co-workers routinely order Sweetgreen for lunch while he showed up with fast food. "Everyone inside my office is very healthy, and they were getting Sweetgreen bowls every single day for lunch," Donohue said. "I myself would go pick up a fast-food burger and everyone would razz and make fun of me." Donohue originally intended to make his experiment last for 30 days, but there was a practical problem. EATING 5 FRUITS AND VEGETABLES A DAY MAY NOT BE ENOUGH FOR HEART HEALTH, STUDY FINDS "I wanted to do 30, but if you try to look at your calendar and try to fit [it into] any 30-day window, there was always a wedding, a work trip, a reason why I couldn't do 30," he said. "I said, 'You know what, it's either going to get done with 25 days or I'm never going to it done.'" His primary rule was simple: Whatever he consumed had to be available on Sweetgreen's menu, although he made an exception for black coffee. And while Sweetgreen offers more than salads, Donohue tried to keep the experiment centered on its bowls. By the third day, he said, there was little chance of turning back. 9 pounds down as a favorite emerges Donahue didn't begin the challenge expecting to lose weight, but by the end, the number on his scale had dropped by about nine pounds. He also found a clear favorite on the menu. AMERICA'S LATE-NIGHT FAST-FOOD CULTURE MAY BE MAKING A COMEBACK — HERE'S WHY "I was rocking with the hot honey chicken bowl," he said. "I was getting that all the time." Donohue said the variety made eating from the same restaurant for nearly a month easier than one might expect. The bigger challenge, he said, was arranging his life around the experiment. "The most challenging aspect of the project was not the food, it was the logistics," he said. Meals had to be planned around the store's operating hours. Going out with friends meant skipping drinks and potentially bringing a salad along. Even dates with his girlfriend took a back seat. 'Not a sustainable thing' One thing Donohue doesn't recommend about his experiment today is the price tag. "You can cook at home and make a salad at home and spend a significantly smaller amount of money," he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Donohue said he offset some of the expense by deciding not to spend money on alcohol or other restaurant meals during the challenge. But, he admitted, it was a "very expensive" project. "Out of pocket, this is not a sustainable thing to do over groceries," he said. Donohue also emphasized that Sweetgreen didn't pay him to conduct the experiment. The company subsequently embraced his idea, Donohue said. "His video inspired us to launch our own 30-day Sweetgreen challenge," Nicolas Jammet, Sweetgreen's co-founder and chief concept officer, told Fox News Digital. "We put out an open call for 30 participants to eat only Sweetgreen for 30 days and document how they feel throughout, and we already received hundreds of applications." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS After 25 days of salad bowls, Donohue headed to his favorite neighborhood pizzeria. "A cheese pizza after a month of salads was incredibly well-deserved," he said. There was just one problem. The sudden return to heavier food didn't sit particularly well. "It did make me feel quite sick because it's a shock to your system," Donohue said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Despite dropping weight and saying he experienced benefits, including more energy, Donohue isn't presenting his experiment as nutritional advice. He stressed that he isn't a doctor or nutritionist and didn't undertake the challenge to tell others how they should eat. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The experiment was largely a fun filmmaking journey for me," he said. "I would never prescribe this to someone."

title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle feeding the 'publicity machine' despite privacy demands: expert
description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle sources push back on King Charles's guidance labeling the Sussexes as private citizens, not royal representatives.
author_name: Janelle Ash, Stephanie Nolasco, Ashley Papa
content: Sources close to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are "pushing back" after King Charles issued new guidance on the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's positions now that they are back in the United Kingdom. King Charles issued guidance claiming that Harry and Markle are "akin to private citizens" via a letter issued by the Lord Chamberlain on Sept. 7. Sources told People magazine that Harry and Markle are "public figures" and that if Harry and Markle were private citizens, the Lord Chamberlain "would not have needed to issue a letter of formal guidance." "Members of the public know who they are. The idea that they can live a normal, ‘private’ life is sadly not realistic," the source added. Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," addressed the "not realistic" claim by the source and told Fox News Digital that the "private citizen" guidance just means that they do not represent the king. KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT "I want to push back on this argument coming from People magazine and sources close to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle that it's somehow unrealistic for the Sussexes to live as private citizens. Being a private citizen does not mean you're anonymous. It simply means you don't represent the king. The jobs you accept and the responsibilities you take, you take them on as yourself, not the crown," Schofield began. "In my opinion, you can't repeatedly feed the publicity machine and then complain about a lack of privacy." Schofield drew a comparison between Princess Anne's children – Zara Tindall and Peter Phillips. Princess Anne is Queen Elizabeth's only daughter and the sister of King Charles. She chose not to give her two kids royal titles at birth. "They're recognizable, have commercial interests, attend major royal family events, but they do not represent the monarch, yet they have both successfully built lives outside of the working institution. Harry and Meghan could pursue a quieter life, a life like Zara and Peter. They choose not to. In my opinion, you can't repeatedly feed the publicity machine and then complain about a lack of privacy," she said. WATCH: PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE CAN'T HAVE PUBLICITY AND PRIVACY: EXPERT Schofield argued that the king’s clarification was necessary as Harry and Markle’s public profile has become increasingly intertwined with the controversies surrounding them. MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK RETURN POSES PALACE CONTROL ‘NIGHTMARE,’ EXPERT WARNS "Prince Harry is classified as a non-working member of the royal family whose position is akin to a private citizen. Of course, Harry and Meghan are famous. Nobody's disputing that, but where does their fame end and infamy begin? Fame can inspire people to invest in you emotionally and financially. Infamy means people know your name because controversy follows you," she began. Schofield continued, "And after years of feuds, lawsuits and relationships that deteriorate, I think it's fair to ask how much of the Sussex's enormous public profile today is driven by admiration and how much is driven by controversy, which is precisely why the king has every reason to make their status crystal clear." Pay for his son’s full security rather than looking like an Ebenezer Scrooge after." He continued, "Although some royals still live in Dickens times, we are actually in the 21st century. How would the king feel if a second tragedy happens in his lifetime, first Diana, and potentially Harry and his family?" title: Psychosis evidence changes everything in Clancy judge's other killer mom case: retired judge
description: Judge William Sullivan, who declared a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case, also presided over the Latarsha Sanders trial now vacated by the court.
content: Judge William Sullivan, who drew national attention earlier this month after declaring a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder case, also presided over another closely watched child-killing trial that a retired Massachusetts judge says would look dramatically different if retried. The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court last month vacated the murder conviction of Brockton mother Latarsha Sanders, ruling jurors were improperly prevented from seeing psychiatric records central to her insanity defense and ordering a new trial. "They ordered a new trial which will fundamentally change the way the case is going to be tried," retired Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Jack Lu told Fox News Digital. LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN Sullivan, who presided over Sanders' 2022 trial and later sentenced her to two concurrent life terms without parole, has returned to the national spotlight following the closely watched Clancy trial, which ended in a mistrial after jurors deadlocked over whether Clancy was criminally responsible for killing her three children. Like Sanders, Clancy admitted killing her children but argued she lacked criminal responsibility because of mental illness. "There is no doubt the defendant committed these incomprehensible crimes," Justice David Gaziano wrote for the unanimous court in Sanders' case. "The sole issue before a Superior Court jury was whether she lacked criminal responsibility." LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL The justices concluded Sanders was entitled to a new trial because jurors never saw medical records documenting diagnoses and treatment of mental illness that were relevant to the only issue disputed at trial: whether she lacked criminal responsibility. Lu said the ruling does far more than simply order another trial. "Thousands of pages of mental health records will be admitted ... and the jury's gonna get it all," he said. Lu cautioned against judging Sullivan's decision with the benefit of hindsight. "The trial judge did an excellent job ... but now I'm a great Monday morning quarterback just like everybody else," Lu said, explaining that the evidentiary issue was unusually difficult before the SJC clarified the law. Sanders admitted killing her sons, 8-year-old Edson "Marlon" Brito and 5-year-old La'Son Brito, but argued she was legally insane at the time of the attacks. Her attorneys contended she was suffering from severe mental illness and psychosis, while prosecutors argued she appreciated the wrongfulness of her actions despite bizarre statements she made before and after the killings. According to evidence summarized by the Supreme Judicial Court, Sanders had become consumed by conspiracy theories involving the Illuminati and expressed fears about voodoo before the killings. After the deaths, investigators said she gave police multiple conflicting accounts before eventually telling detectives the stabbings were part of a "ritual" tied to voodoo and the Illuminati. At trial, Sanders' defense called a clinical neuropsychologist who testified she was "grossly psychotic" at the time of the killings and suffered from a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder. The expert based that opinion in part on thousands of pages of psychiatric treatment records from prison and a state psychiatric hospital. Those are the records Lu said a future jury would likely hear if prosecutors pursue another trial. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The Supreme Judicial Court said that was an error, concluding the excluded records documented repeated observations of paranoia, hallucinations, delusional thinking and schizophrenia-spectrum diagnoses that formed the medical foundation of Sanders' defense. Read the court's ruling: "We hold that the exclusion of the MCI-Framingham and WRCH medical records documenting the defendant's post-arrest diagnoses or treatment of mental illness ... impermissibly stripped the sole defense 'of the medical foundation that supported it,'" the court wrote. "The defendant is entitled to a new trial." Instead, he described it as the resolution of a difficult evidentiary question that changes what evidence jurors would be permitted to consider if the case is retried. During oral arguments before the Supreme Judicial Court, Sanders' attorney, Robert Shaw, argued the trial judge's exclusion of medical evidence deprived his client of "a meaningful opportunity to present a complete defense," FOX 25 in Boston reported. title: Trump's EPA reforms are a huge boost to manufacturers, but there's more red tape to cut: expert
description: NAM CEO Jay Timmons says Trump EPA rollback of Biden-era power plant emissions standards is a game changer but warns more permitting reform is needed.
content: The Trump administration's move to eliminate a swath of Biden-era power plant emissions standards will be a game changer for the U.S. economy, National Association of Manufacturers CEO Jay Timmons told Fox News Digital. Timmons hailed EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin for the move announced this week but noted that even more red tape remains to be cut. "It really sent a signal to manufacturers that the administration was listening to our concerns," Timmons said of the cuts to power plant emissions standards. TRUMP'S EPA CHIEF PUSHES BACK ON CLIMATE SKEPTICS BEING LABELED 'SCIENCE DENIERS' He said NAM and other groups had objected to former President Joe Biden's 2024 standards "very, very clearly" at the time, saying the standards were "simply unworkable." "The timeline that they had proposed was just, it wasn't feasible. Not that the aspirations for, you know, for cleaner air and a healthier environment aren't good aspirations," Timmons said. "I think we all share that. I know the current EPA and Administrator Zeldin certainly share those objectives, but how you get there really matters and whether manufacturers are able to meet the challenge. Timmons noted that the Biden administration had heard its concerns but simply disagreed. TRUMP-APPROVED ENERGY PROJECTS AT RISK OF SUDDEN DEATH BY NEXT HOSTILE PRESIDENT The emissions regulations cut this week were removed by executive fiat, but Timmons says more lasting change must come through Congress as manufacturers hope to avoid regulatory whiplash between administrations. "Uncertainty is the absolute worst enemy for manufacturers because manufacturers are on a very long-term horizon when it comes to planning and strategy, product development, research development. So, when administrations change, there has often been kind of that pendulum swing," Timmons said. SEN KEVIN CRAMER: CHINA BUILDS FOR WAR WHILE AMERICA WAITS ON PERMITS One area he said could use further reform is permitting. NAM polling found that 80% of manufacturers say the length and complexity of the permitting process is harmful to increasing investment. As many as 87% of manufacturers told NAM they would expand business operations, hire more workers or increase wages and benefits if the permitting process was more streamlined.
