title: Former GOP whip, Arizona Sen Jon Kyl dead at 84
description: Former Senate Minority Whip Jon Kyl, an Arizona Republican who served nearly three decades in Congress, has died at age 84 following a battle with dementia.
content: Former Senate Minority Whip Jon Kyl, R-Ariz., is dead at the age of 84, his family announced Thursday. Kyl was first sworn in to the Senate in 1995, retiring in 2013. He briefly returned to the Senate in 2018 after former Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., died. Kyl announced he was stepping away from public life in December 2025 after receiving a diagnosis of a neurological disease that resulted in his development of dementia. Before his election to the Senate, Kyl was a member of the U.S. House of Representatives from 1987 to 1995. AN EMPTY US CAPITOL AFTER MCCAIN’S DEATH IS SOBERING REMINDER THAT THE CLOCK IS TICKING Former Arizona Gov. Doug Ducey, who appointed Kyl to fill McCain's seat in 2018, paid his respects to the former senator in a Thursday post on X. "Jon Kyl gave Arizona nearly three decades of principled, thoughtful leadership — and he gave me something just as valuable: his mentorship and friendship. I'll miss him deeply. Rest in peace, Senator Kyl," Ducey posted. Former Sen. Jeff Flake, R-Ariz., who served in the Senate with Kyl, also paid homage to the late lawmaker. "Arizona has lost a giant. Jon Kyl was one of the most diligent and effective public servants Arizona has ever had. I was honored to follow him in the U.S. Senate, where his example of seriousness, integrity and devotion to public service was known to all. Cheryl and I send our deepest condolences to Caryll and the entire Kyl family," Flake posted on X. Flake also gave remarks to reporters at the Capitol on Thursday. "I admired him from the get-go, when he was back in the House, and I was in Arizona. When I ran for office, he gave me the best advice I ever got. He said that, when you get back to Washington, make sure your family is aware of what you're doing, is involved in it. He said they will either resent it or revel in it. And that was the best advice I got, because we tried to follow that. And he was just… in addition to being an extremely effective public servant, he was a good man. And I think that that shined through," Flake told reporters. TILLIS' RETIREMENT ANNOUNCEMENT DRAWS REACTIONS FROM TRUMP CRITIC JEFF FLAKE, BERNIE SANDERS: 'A CULT' "For Arizona, you know, every Western state has similar issues; water issues, public land issues. And Jon took that on," Flake said. "That's the workhorse in him. I think he did nine Indian water settlements during his time, which has allowed the Indian tribes in Arizona to have the water they need and also for the state to grow sustainably," Flake continued. "And then also, in terms of his legal mind and his, you know, concern about the Supreme Court. And he was asked after he had left Congress to sherpa certain nominees through, and he was extremely effective in that because he had the respect of his colleagues." Flake also revealed that he last spoke with Kyl just before the late senator announced his dementia diagnosis. "December of last year he put out a statement. I had talked to him just before that. And it was a wonderful conversation. He was very much aware of all that the state had gone through, and I made sure to tell him how appreciative all Arizonans are of what he did for the state and what he did for the country. And, he was so devoted to his wife, Carol, and his family, and the state of Arizona," Flake said. Flake also commented on the unique situation that arose when Kyl was appointed to replace McCain. "When Senator McCain passed away, there was an appointment, and he served out that term for the last few months. So I got to serve with him in the Senate and also jokingly be the senior senator to him, which I didn't deserve. But it was just a wonderful relationship throughout," Flake said. title: Powerful teachers' unions share striking link with states struggling to teach kids to read
description: A Progressive Policy Institute study links strong teachers unions to weaker student literacy, with eight of the 10 lowest-scoring states affected.
content: States with stronger teachers' unions tend to have weaker literacy performance and have adopted fewer of the policies credited with improving reading outcomes, according to a new analysis from a center-left think tank. Eight of the 10 states to score among the worst in the Progressive Policy Institute’s (PPI) assessment of early-literacy policies were home to powerful teachers' unions. Among the top 60% of states in terms of early-literacy policy scores, only four had strong teachers' unions. Mississippi, Arkansas, Georgia, Louisiana, South Carolina and Indiana, all Republican-leaning states with weak unions, were among the states with the best literacy outcomes. Maine, New York, Illinois, Hawaii, Washington and Rhode Island, blue states, were among the worst. ARKANSAS STUDENTS OUTPERFORM NATIONAL AVERAGE AFTER UNIVERSAL SCHOOL CHOICE EXPANSION, GOVERNOR SAYS The pattern isn't universal. Maryland, a blue state with a strong teachers' union, has posted strong reading results, while South Dakota, a red state with a weaker union, has struggled. The differences suggest union strength and party control alone don't explain states' reading performance. Rachel Canter, PPI’s director of education policy, conducted the analysis with colleagues by comparing teacher-union strength rankings with states’ early-literacy policy scores. Canter is also one of the people behind the slate of educational reforms in Mississippi that propelled the state from among the worst in the country for educational outcomes to among the best. "Democrats, however, don’t often ask me how to replicate Mississippi’s success," Canter said. "They ask if it’s possible at all, given the power of teachers’ unions in their home states." Teachers' unions, according to Canter, exert massive amounts of influence over both educational policies and how those policies are implemented in the classroom. This can make schools in states with stronger unions slower to adapt to challenges or to adopt new, better methods. TEACHERS UNION FACING YEARS OF DEFICITS SEEKS TO BECOME OREGON'S LARGEST PAC, INTERNAL DOCUMENTS SHOW Mississippi’s reforms, among other things, added kindergarten-through-third-grade screenings, literacy coaches, individual reading plans and held back third-graders who failed the state reading test. The state reinforced those measures with science-based reading instruction, increased teacher training and tougher licensing requirements. Tweaks to teaching like these can be difficult to achieve in states with influential teachers' unions, with labor reps arguing that the changes place undue burdens on educators. ILLINOIS DEMOCRATIC GOVERNOR BUCKS TEACHERS' UNIONS IN SUPPORT FOR STATEWIDE CLASSROOM PHONE BAN Many of the states that underperformed in the Progressive Policy Institute’s study also have Democratic leadership. Teachers’ unions spend hundreds of millions of dollars every electoral cycle on electing Democrats and pushing left-of-center policies. "States dominated by Democrats have been slower to embrace similar reforms," Canter said. "Organized labor might explain some of this gap." Those same states dominated the Progressive Policy Institute’s rankings of the states with the best student literacy.

title: Trump’s $5K checks could join stack of past unfulfilled promises, former Congress budget chief warns

content: President Donald Trump's latest cash promise to Americans is unlikely to come to fruition, just like others before it, an economist and former congressional budget hawk told Fox News Digital. "So the president has promised a lot of checks, the most recent being $5,000 to every American if Republicans hold on to the House and Senate. We ever going to see these? Well, I don't think so," said Douglas Holz-Eakin, president of fiscal policy think tank American Action Forum. TRUMP DEFENDS $5,000 DIVIDEND PROPOSAL, PRAISES 'BEAUTIFUL' TARIFFS ON 'INGRAHAM ANGLE' "The DOGE checks were never realistic because DOGE was never going to save that much money," said Holz-Eakin in reference to the Elon Musk-led Department of Government Efficiency's sweeping layoffs and budget cuts to federal agencies. "Trying to get money to stay at home moms for childcare, there's a route to that, but it's gonna be tough ... we'll see if they actually pull it off," he said. "So, I would be skeptical that any of these checks are gonna be in your mailbox very soon." THE FED JUST THREW A WRENCH IN TRUMP'S MIDTERM ECONOMIC MESSAGE He said that getting inflation under control was the first step in restoring order, as well as being "utterly supportive" of the Federal Reserve, which Holz-Eakin says is working to achieve that goal. title: Falcons star Bijan Robinson wants every NFL team to play indoors one day: 'That would be sick'
description: Bijan Robinson wants every NFL team to play indoors, but football traditionalists might have something to say about that to the Atlanta Falcons superstar.
content: Atlanta Falcons superstar running back Bijan Robinson knows how much of a blessing it is to play in the NFL. He also understands the blessing of playing home games inside a domed stadium each season. Mercedes-Benz Stadium, home of the Falcons, doesn’t have to worry about the elements outside when it’s time for kickoff. It is one of 10 NFL stadiums with domes or fixed/retractable roofs, as it fits into the latter category. The Falcons are one of 11 teams lucky enough to not have to brave any elements when they see a home game on the schedule, but Robinson believes the entire league should experience that someday. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Robinson had quite the suggestion for the NFL during a recent interview with OutKick. "I wish one day the NFL can make every team indoors. I think that would be sick," he said, while also discussing his partnership with Sonic. In theory, it would be sick. No matter what the outside weather says, whether it’s heavy rains or snows, strong wind gusts, or freezing cold temperatures, the climate and conditions will always be the same inside a domed field. Every team gets the same conditions to work with and no excuses in terms of elements can be used to blame a poor performance. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! However, Robinson’s dream of playing a 17-game-plus schedule in all domes isn’t very likely to come to fruition. In every sport, there are purists, and football fans are very much at the top of the list. Seeing the winds in Cleveland coming off the lake, or braving the snow in Buffalo in the winter is what traditional football fans look forward to. It’s football – no element other than thunder and lightning will stop what goes on. "I can’t speak for people in Buffalo," Robinson said. "I know they love the snow, they love to be in it. But I feel like there would be a lot of people, too, that might enjoy not having to shovel it out. I know that’s a part of the culture, but if you could just go inside, go there and enjoy the game. Hopefully, we’ll see. Maybe in 10 years we could make that happen." While it’s highly unlikely every team will play in a domed stadium, those building new homes already have it in mind. Almost all seven of the new NFL stadiums currently under construction or planned feature a dome, retractable roof, or a skylight structure. The exception was actually in Buffalo, as the new Highmark Stadium, which gets its debut on Thursday night between the Bills and Detroit Lions, has an open-air roof. But teams like the Tennessee Titans and Cleveland Browns are building enclosed venues. Also, the projects involving the Washington Commanders, Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs all feature plans to enclose the field in some capacity. It would be about one-third of the stadium where domes come into play, and sure, players may feel just like Robinson after not having to power through the elements if they don’t have to. For now, though, it’s a privilege Robinson is well aware of. "It’s definitely awesome to get to play inside. That’s a huge advantage because you don’t have to worry about the elements," he explained. "The sun, like, dragging down your energy, or the cold. … For us, we just embrace it. We still practice outside in that heat, and I think it really helps us a lot practicing outdoors. It’s one of those things where it’s not cold here, so the weather changes in Atlanta all the time. One day it could be sunny, one day it could be gloomy, or rain and stuff like that. "For us, it doesn’t really matter what the elements are like during the week. It could pour rain all day and we’re going right inside on Sunday. It’s definitely a blessing to play inside and play a lot of teams that are inside." Robinson and the Falcons are a very lucky group this season, as they have only five outdoor games remaining on their 2026 schedule. They will face the Green Bay Packers on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 3, followed by games against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (Week 8, Nov. 1), Browns (Week 14, Dec. 13), Commanders (Week 15, Dec. 20) and Carolina Panthers (Week 18, TBD). Perfect football pairing With football season officially back, Robinson highlighted his favorite food pairing if he were the one sitting down to watch the Falcons and the rest of the NFL slate on Sundays. Robinson preached how great the Sonic $7 Big Deal Meal was, as it includes a cheeseburger, medium drink, choice of medium tots or fries, and a vanilla sundae. And after getting the Big Deal Meal, he’ll be sure to throw in a strawberry limeade and a chili dog if he’s feeling extra hungry. But overall, Robinson loves how great and affordable this special deal is for everyone, especially those families looking for something good to pair with their football each week. "I feel like it gives everybody an opportunity to get a meal together as a family and they don’t gotta worry about it costing too much, or stuff like that," he said. "They know they can go right to Sonic, order the $7 Big Deal Meal and enjoy it. They can have a full meal and it’s not just a hamburger or a drink or something like that. They can enjoy something together as a family. title: Federal judge ties ICE agents' hands with ruling on warrantless Southern California arrests
description: A federal judge issued a preliminary injunction blocking ICE from carrying out warrantless immigration arrests unless the target is likely to escape before a warrant is obtained.
content: A federal judge with the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California issued a preliminary injunction to block the U.S. government from conducting warrantless civil immigration arrests in the district unless the arrestee is deemed likely to escape before a warrant can be procured. "Defendants are enjoined from enforcing their policy and practice of making warrantless civil immigration arrests in this District without a prearrest individualized determination by the arresting agent or officer of probable cause that the person being arrested is likely to escape before a warrant can be obtained, as required by 8 U.S.C. 1357(a)(2) and 8 C.F.R. § 287.8(c)(2)," the order signed by U.S. District Judge Maame Ewusi-Mensah Frimpong reads, in part. Frimpong was nominated by former President Joe Biden during his White House tenure. EXCLUSIVE: 25 YEARS AFTER 9/11, ICE SAYS MORE THAN 2K KNOWN OR SUSPECTED TERRORISTS HAVE BEEN DEPORTED "Mere presence within the United States in violation of United States immigration law is not, by itself, sufficient to conclude that a person is likely to escape before a warrant for arrest can be obtained," the judge's order notes. The U.S. District Court for the Central District of California encompasses the following counties: Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, Ventura, Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties. ANGEL DAD REBUKES DEMOCRATIC LAWMAKERS OVER SANCTUARY POLICIES AFTER DAUGHTER KILLED BY TWICE-DEPORTED FELON "This ruling is one of the most important decisions to date in the community’s effort to end the federal government’s cruel and illegal practice of abducting people and separating them from their families," ACLU Foundation of Southern California senior staff attorney Mayra Joachin declared in a statement. "By requiring immigration agents to follow the law’s requirement to make escape risk determinations before they can arrest someone without a warrant, this court order should put an end to hundreds — if not more — of unlawful arrests that continue throughout Southern California. We will closely monitor compliance with this court order, and expect the federal government to abide by it," Joachin added. Law enforcement officers use 'reasonable suspicion' to investigate immigration status and probable cause to make arrests consistent with the statute and the Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The Supreme Court has already vindicated us on these practices."

title: Los Angeles NBC helicopter seen plummeting toward ground in dashcam video
description: Dashcam video captures the NBC and Telemundo 52 helicopter's rapid descent over Los Angeles before the fiery crash that killed three people.
content: Dashcam video from a Los Angeles driver captured an NBC and Telemundo news helicopter rapidly descending toward the ground moments before a fiery crash that killed three people. The video, captured by driver Year Valencia, shows the helicopter dropping from the sky Tuesday while its crew was covering a separate deadly collision involving an SUV and a city bus. "I downloaded the video of my dashcam. It’s a little dot on the video. It’s a crisp video, and it just goes down," Valencia told KTLA, which first obtained the footage. "God, it’s so close, it could have happened to anyone. My parents walk down the street." NBC REPORTER, PILOT AMONG THE VICTIMS IDENTIFIED IN DEADLY LOS ANGELES HELICOPTER CRASH The helicopter crashed in the Chatsworth neighborhood of the San Fernando Valley, killing NBC4 and Telemundo 52 reporter Eliana Moreno, pilot George Marciniw and 29-year-old Edy Gutierrez Mejia, who was on the ground. The aircraft went down near a storage facility and caught fire, with the blaze spreading to at least four vehicles and two storage containers. The crash came roughly two hours after the SUV slammed into the city bus in a separate collision that killed two people and injured six others, according to authorities. Police said the SUV had been traveling the wrong way, ran a red light and struck another vehicle before hitting the bus. VICTIMS IDENTIFIED IN FATAL AMAZON CARGO JET CRASH AT MIAMI AIRPORT Police arrested the SUV's driver, 36-year-old Bailee Lynn Rios, on murder charges Tuesday night. The Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office was reviewing the case to determine what charges, if any, would be filed in court. The cause of the helicopter crash remained under investigation Wednesday. Video broadcast from the helicopter before it went down captured an alarm sounding inside the aircraft as it began losing altitude. National Transportation Safety Board investigator Fabian Salazar said Wednesday that the helicopter's final video could provide investigators with critical evidence as they work to determine what caused the crash. The sounds captured on the recording appeared consistent with changes in engine speed and likely cockpit advisory tones, he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The helicopter, a Eurocopter AS350 operated by Angel City Air, was used by NBC4 and Telemundo 52 for aerial news coverage. The NTSB is investigating the helicopter crash as well as the earlier bus collision.

title: GOP congressman presses WNBA to define ‘women’ after Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White ruled ineligible
description: Rep. Marlin Stutzman demands Cathy Engelbert explain how the WNBA defines "women" after Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White were barred from the draft.
content: Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., is pressing WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert for answers about the league’s eligibility rules, including one very basic question: How does the WNBA define "women"? In a follow-up letter to Engelbert obtained by OutKick, the Indiana Republican and other members of Congress question the league’s handling of player safety, fan confrontations and, now, who is actually eligible to play in the WNBA. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The letter comes as Engelbert prepares to leave the league. She announced Sept. 4 that she will retire at the end of 2026 after more than seven years as commissioner, and the WNBA has already begun the process of searching for her successor. That timing adds another layer to Stutzman’s request, which asks Engelbert to answer several questions about league policy before Oct. 16. The WNBA’s collective bargaining agreement says that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." But it does not go any further in defining what that means. That became a bigger issue this summer after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said female athletes should not have to compete against biological men. Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White later announced that they identified as women and planned to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, seemingly forcing the league to address the issue directly. League sources later told media outlets that neither man was eligible for the draft. WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS Now Stutzman wants to know why. "How does the WNBA define ‘women’ for purposes of Article XIII, Section 1(a) of its collective bargaining agreement?" the lawmakers ask in the letter. They then follow with: "If the WNBA has no definition of ‘women,’ why were Freedom and White deemed ineligible to join the 2027 WNBA draft?" Read the full letter here: The letter argues that by ruling Freedom and White ineligible, the league has already shown that it recognizes a distinction when deciding who can play. "As a women’s sports league, the WNBA must ensure the League remains exclusively for biological women," the lawmakers wrote. They also cited Cunningham’s comments and raised concerns about fairness and player safety. But the eligibility question is only part of the letter. Stutzman and other Republican lawmakers previously wrote to Engelbert over concerns about player safety and the treatment of Caitlin Clark. Engelbert responded by outlining the league’s review process and its efforts to create a safe environment for players. The lawmakers now argue that the league’s actions since then have not matched those assurances. They point to Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington’s Aug. 8 Flagrant 2 foul on Sophie Cunningham and another incident involving Golden State’s Tiffany Hayes just four days later. The letter also compares the WNBA’s handling of Carrington to the NBA’s past discipline of Draymond Green, who received suspensions after repeated physical incidents. Stutzman also raises concerns about how the league handles confrontations between players and fans. The letter cites Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud’s confrontation with Freedom during an Aug. 23 game at Wintrust Arena. It compares the lack of discipline for Cloud with the five-game suspension given to Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton after a separate confrontation with fans. The lawmakers are asking whether the WNBA has a consistent policy for players, coaches and team officials who get into verbal confrontations with spectators. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Altogether, the letter asks Engelbert to answer four questions by Oct. 16: what the league has done to address repeated physical play, how it handles confrontations with fans, how it defines "women," and why Freedom and White were ruled ineligible for the draft. "The WNBA has an extraordinary platform and influence," the lawmakers wrote. "We urge the League to use that platform responsibly by ensuring that rules are enforced equally to protect the safety of women playing the game and fans in the stands."

title: Political insider turns anti-incumbent table on 8-year Dem in key Senate race: 'Hasn't delivered'
description: John E. Sununu flips the anti-incumbent script on Chris Pappas, calling him ineffective on highway funding as the NH Senate race hits toss up.
content: CONCORD, N.H. - A Republican running to flip a blue Senate seat in a crucial battleground state is flipping the script on the Democrats' anti-incumbent argument. Former Sen. John E. Sununu, the GOP Senate nominee who's running to return to Capitol Hill after 18 years away, charges that his Democratic rival, Rep. Chris Pappas, has "been in Washington for 8 years and hasn't delivered for New Hampshire." Sununu and Pappas are facing off in the midterm election in the battle to succeed retiring longtime Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen in a race that's one of roughly a dozen that will determine if Republicans hold their control of the Senate. "He has attempted very little in Congress. He's accomplished even less," Sununu said in an exclusive Fox News Digital interview this week, as he blasted Pappas, a four-term congressman. THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DETERMINE IF REPUBLICANS HOLD THE SENATE Sununu was interviewed ahead of a move by the Cook Political Report, a top nonpartisan campaign handicapper, to shift the race in New Hampshire from lean Democrat to toss-up. Earlier this month, another leading nonpartisan handicapper, Inside Elections, also changed their rating to a toss-up. It was a rare move in favor of the Republicans amid a political cycle where the GOP is facing traditional political headwinds for the party in power in D.C.. Republicans are also confronting an extremely rough political climate fueled by persistent inflation, soaring fuel prices due to the ongoing war with Iran, and President Donald Trump's underwater approval ratings. So what's Sununu's secret sauce? Part of it is his last name, which is a political brand in New Hampshire. Sununu's father, John E. Sununu, served six years as governor before heading to Washington, D.C., as then-President George H.W. Bush's White House chief of staff. And one of his younger brothers, Chris Sununu, recently served eight years as governor before taking a break from politics. But also boosting Sununu, his strategy to blast Pappas as a do-nothing member of Congress during another anti-incumbent election cycle, which is a turn of the tables on the Democrats' playbook. CHECK OUT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE BATTLE FOR THE SENATE "He's been on the Transportation Committee for eight years, and New Hampshire is dead last in highway funding in New England. That hurts New Hampshire. His ineffectiveness is doing damage to the state because we're not getting the support we need from Washington," Sununu claimed. While it doesn't rank dead last in every single metric or category, New Hampshire receives some of the lowest total and per-capita levels of federal funding for roads, highways and bridges of any state in the country, according to federal and state figures. Pappas, earlier this year, introduced the Highway Fair Share Act, a bill to increase federal funding for infrastructure and transportation projects for New Hampshire by requiring that each state receive at least 0.5% of the total federal-aid highway formula funding. Pappas and the rest of the all-Democratic congressional delegation in June highlighted $9 million in federal funding for New Hampshire projects. "Chris Pappas has led efforts to expand healthcare benefits for 3.5 million veterans, bring high-speed internet to towns across New Hampshire, put more money back in the pockets of working parents, and secure millions of dollars to improve and repair roads, bridges, and buildings," Pappas Campaign Manager Rachel Petri told Fox News Digital, as she shared a long list of funding accomplishments by the congressman. Petri said, "Chris is rated among the most effective and bipartisan lawmakers and his record stands in stark contrast to John Sununu’s record of voting to cut Medicare, leading efforts to privatize Social Security, and backing Donald Trump’s tariffs and war with Iran." Sununu's anti-incumbent argument is a bit ironic, considering he spent six years in the House and a term in the Senate before losing a rematch with then-former Gov. Shaheen in the 2008 election. Looking back at his years on Capitol Hill, Sununu touted his record "of writing and passing legislation under Democrat presidents, Republican presidents, a Democrat Congress, Republican Congress." But he also emphasized, "I've been in the private sector for the last 16 years. That's a good thing, working for tech firms and small businesses, the Waterville Valley ski area [the Sununu family has had a controlling interest in the resort since 2010], teaching college. It's... a perspective that I think is missing from Washington." WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLLS IN KEY MIDTERM RACES SHOW Pappas, in a recent Fox News Digital interview, highlighted that New Hampshire is "a state of voters who are pragmatic, who want their lives to be better and want problems to be solved, and I can demonstrate the ways that I've been working on those issues." "It's expanding access to health care, building more affordable housing in New Hampshire, and ensuring that we're standing up to an administration that's ignoring the day-to-day concerns of Granite Staters," he added. But Sununu wasn't the only one taking aim at Pappas as a do-nothing incumbent. Even his long-shot socialist rival in last week's primary took a shot. First-time candidate and scientist Karishma Manzur, in a recent Fox News Digital interview, charged that "all [Pappas] wants to do is just get his little cushy job and go to D.C., go to all these parties and these restaurants and just do whatever the bare minimum is." Pappas ended up crushing Manzur in the primary by a two-to-one margin, and Sununu defeated former Sen. Scott Brown in a landslide to capture the GOP nomination. DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER With the general election sprint underway, Republican-aligned outside groups are now pouring millions into the state to target Pappas. And Pappas is using this week's Cook Political Report race rating to ring an alarm. "MAGA super PACs are pouring millions of dollars a week into New Hampshire to try to flip this seat. And this race is officially a Toss Up," he warned on social media. And Pappas told Fox News Digital recently that Sununu is "backed up by out-of-state special interests and dark money in this campaign. They're outspending us 3 to 1 on TV." Firing back, this week a Democrat-aligned super PAC started running ads charging that, after he left the Senate, Sununu cashed in by working for lobbying firms. Sununu was endorsed earlier this year by Trump, and since then Democrats have repeatedly tied the president, whose approval ratings are well into negative territory in New Hampshire, to Sununu. Pappas called Sununu Trump's "hand-picked candidate." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Asked about the full-court press by Pappas and Democrats to anchor him to Trump, Sununu told Fox News Digital, "I've never even met the president." But contrasting himself with Pappas, Sununu added that "there's no question I'll be a much more effective voice with this administration."

title: Family member of lawyer who coined 'genocide' seeks to strip name from group accusing Israel of atrocity
description: A relative of "genocide" term creator Raphael Lemkin wants a Pennsylvania nonprofit to drop the family name over its accusations against Israel. The institute defends its mission and name.
content: A family member of Raphael Lemkin, a Jewish lawyer who escaped Europe during World War II and coined the term "genocide," is in a fight to have his name removed from a Pennsylvania nonprofit organization that accuses Israel of the exact term he came up with. The Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention and Human Security has "warned of genocide in Gaza since Oct. 13, 2023," less than a week after Hamas terror attacks killed about 1,200 and resulted in the capture of 251 hostages in 2023. On Oct. 28, 2023, the institute issued a "statement of mourning for the Gazans and the world," saying that "these two major military powers [the U.S. and Israel] are committing genocide in Gaza only weeks after actively enabling genocide against another besieged people: the Armenians of Artsakh." It also warned that "if the world allows these two powers to continue to act with this level of impunity, genocide will become the normative policy of both dictatorships and the world’s so-called democracies alike." PROMINENT HOLOCAUST MUSEUM CHALLENGES MAMDANI WITH OFFER IN RESPONSE TO CLAIMS ABOUT 'GENOCIDE' IN GAZA The man calling for the change is Joseph Lemkin — whose father was Raphael’s cousin — and the sole survivor after his family of six was killed during the Holocaust. Joseph told Fox News Digital that growing up the son of a Holocaust survivor meant being followed by "a black cloud" that colored his entire life. In one example, he explained that when the families at his Jewish day school placed ads during an annual banquet to celebrate their successes, his father wrote a yearly commemoration of the memories of his more than 40 family members who died during the Holocaust, including his parents and brother killed at Auschwitz and two brothers who died after joining underground resistance groups. He said his father raised funds for the impoverished Raphael’s funeral when he died in 1959, and worked until weeks before his death to fundraise for the betterment of his fellow Jewish Americans. Joseph’s experience as the child of a Holocaust survivor came to mind again when his teenage son showed him a social media post from the Lemkin Institute using the family name to accuse Israel of genocide. "Seeing the impact and how my son came across it made me really more concerned about it," Lemkin said. ANTI-ISRAEL NONPROFIT UNDER FEDERAL INVESTIGATION OVER FINANCIAL DEALINGS: REPORT In an effort to keep the family name from being "turned on its head," he said he has worked with the European Jewish Association (EJA) to submit a letter of complaint to the office of Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro and to Pennsylvania’s Department of State’s Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations. In June, Lemkin and his team also sent out letters referencing their concerns to other leaders in Pennsylvania. In response to a request from Shapiro’s office for additional information, Lemkin and the EJA submitted a 32-page comprehensive legal submission and statement of facts and a 58-page evidentiary appendix in April 2025. He said he believes that an investigation has been opened into the complaint. Pennsylvania's Department of State spokesman, Geoff Morrow, told Fox News Digital "the Department [of State] cannot confirm or deny whether any organization has had a complaint filed against it or is under investigation." Gov. Shapiro’s office did not respond to requests for comment from Fox News Digital. ISRAEL TURNS TABLES ON UN OFFICIAL CLAIMING 'GENOCIDE' IN GAZA WITH BASIC QUESTIONS In an Oct. 13, 2025, press release responding to an op-ed, the Lemkin Institute stated, "It is very hard to imagine that Raphael Lemkin would not have seen the genocidal dynamics of the present conflict early on, given his definition of the term and his historical studies. We share Raphael Lemkin’s belief in the need for a Jewish national home, but that has not meant that we are unable to see the genocide before our eyes." The same press release also noted, "Joseph Lemkin does not speak for the entire Lemkin family, nor does he officially represent a Lemkin estate. We have Lemkin family members on our side who reached out to us after October 7, 2023. Peter Lemkin, in whose childhood home Raphael Lemkin was a frequent visitor, has been particularly supportive, offering encouragement, sharing insights into Lemkin’s work, and informing us of his family's close collaboration in the effort to get the Genocide Convention ratified by states." title: Cruise vacation takes frightening turn as passenger is airlifted from ship
description: Raising questions about cruise insurance coverage, a Celebrity Solstice passenger was airlifted from the ship by the Royal Canadian Air Force after a medical emergency.
content: A cruise vacation took a frightening turn when a passenger experiencing a medical emergency had to be airlifted recently from a ship sailing near Canada. The passenger was aboard the Celebrity Solstice when additional medical care was needed, prompting a response from the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF), according to a news release from Esquimalt Public Affairs shared with Fox News Digital. A Royal Canadian Air Force helicopter and rescue team were deployed to the ship, with search and rescue technicians lowered onto the vessel to assist with the evacuation. CRUISE SHIP BATTLES ROUGH PACIFIC SEAS TO SAVE INJURED, STRANDED SAILOR The passenger was then airlifted from the cruise ship and transported to shore for hospital care, the same source noted. "A guest experienced a medical emergency while sailing. Since they required additional care, we facilitated their medical disembarkation," a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson told Fox News Digital. Royal Caribbean Group owns Celebrity Solstice through its ownership of its subsidiary brand, Celebrity Cruises. Lynn Elmhirst, producer and host of the travel series "World's Greatest Cruises," told Fox News Digital that medical emergencies can become more complicated when travelers are at sea and far from major cities. Elmhirst noted that the coastline between Vancouver and Alaska includes long stretches without major cities and hospitals, which can complicate an emergency evacuation. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "The more remote you are, the more difficult it is to get that medical evacuation," she said. The incident also serves as a reminder for cruise passengers to understand their insurance coverage before setting sail, according to Elmhirst. "I think from a guest's perspective, there are two really important takeaways from hearing about a medical evacuation at sea," she said. "One is making sure that you have sufficient medical travel insurance." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Elmhirst said travelers should check whether their coverage includes medical evacuation, hospital stays and repatriation if they need assistance returning home. "Even if you have really good health insurance, it may not cover travel," she said. Without sufficient coverage, travelers could potentially face large medical expenses following an emergency abroad, Elmhirst added. She also encouraged travelers with pre-existing medical conditions to speak with their doctors before embarking on a cruise and make sure they are healthy enough to travel. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Regardless [of] any health issues, please speak with your doctor," Elmhirst said. "Make sure that your doctor says that you're well enough to travel." Carrying a passport is also extremely important, even on cruises where it may not be required, according to Elmhirst. She said an unexpected medical evacuation could require a passenger to fly home internationally rather than return to the ship as planned. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Take a passport with you," Elmhirst said — adding that travelers can then focus on "getting well and going home safely" if a medical emergency occurs.

title: Leaked Trump plan sparks GOP showdown over how far Republicans should go to support families
description: The Trump admin's $9,000 stay-at-home parent proposal sparks a fierce conservative divide, with some critics calling it socialism and a slippery slope.
content: The Trump administration is reportedly floating a plan to let some married families with a stay-at-home parent tap federal childcare dollars — a proposal that has triggered a growing fight among conservatives over how far Washington should go to support family life. The reported proposal would expand eligibility for Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) assistance to some married families in which one spouse works at least 35 hours a week and the other stays home, with the benefit averaging about $9,000 per child annually, according to reports. The New York Times reported Sept. 5 that the administration was considering the proposal in the context of Vice President JD Vance’s long-standing advocacy for extending childcare assistance to stay-at-home parents, although a White House official told Fox News Digital that Vance has not pushed this specific proposal. AMERICA’S CHILD CARE CRISIS NEEDS MORE PARENTAL FREEDOM — NOT MORE WASHINGTON CONTROL "Until the administration officially unveils a policy push, any leaked reporting about potential policy ideas that have been neither fully baked nor released should be regarded as pointless speculation," said the official. The Child Care and Development Block Grant was enacted in 1990 under President George H.W. Bush, and the 1996 welfare overhaul under President Bill Clinton amended the program and integrated it with mandatory childcare funding streams that are now commonly known as the Child Care and Development Fund. In a White House press release posted close to Mother's Day, Trump touted how his administration is working to "better empower stay-at-home parents." In May, the Department of Health and Human Services issued new CCDF guidance clarifying states’ flexibility in how parents can choose among federally permitted childcare providers and services. Critics of the reported proposal, including some Republican and conservative advocates, have warned that it could increase government oversight and create new concerns involving fraud, benefit cliffs, dependency or incentives around work. Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene also labeled the idea as "socialism" in an X video, while conservative radio host Erick Erickson said on X the plan is "welfare for married people," and allegedly showed a recent pattern of the GOP pivoting toward "Diet Coke of Socialism." TRUMP FACES RECKONING AS GOP FIGURES LABEL $5K PROMISE A 'SOCIALIST VOTE-BUYING SCHEME' "I am old enough to remember a time when Republicans were against government entitlement programs," said Meghan McCain. Some conservative figures and advocates have expressed support for the concept, arguing that federal policy should provide greater support to families that choose to have a parent remain home with children. American Principles Project President Terry Schilling told Fox News Digital that the nuclear family needs to be reconsidered after years of government policies promoting multiple undergraduate and graduate degrees while delaying marriage and homeownership. "For decades, Washington paid institutions to raise kids while lonely young people delayed marriage, homeownership and children," said Schilling. "If policy helped break the family, policy can help restore it to the center of American life by putting money in parents’ hands, not in the pockets of daycare chains, unions, and nonprofits." The Advancing American Freedom (AAF) organization, founded by former Vice President Mike Pence, urged conservatives to oppose the reported plan. Rachel Greszler, AAF economist and welfare expert, told Fox News Digital in an interview that "government is not the solution to family life." "I fear that if we cross into that, that is taking what is supposed to be like a work-oriented welfare program and turning it into social engineering," she said. Greszler expressed concern that sending government checks to stay-at-home parents would inevitably require guardrails to prevent fraud and abuse — potentially bringing greater government scrutiny into the home. TRUMP’S WELFARE REFORMS ARE A MAJOR VICTORY. BUREAUCRATS COULD STILL WRECK THEM "If we are going to invite checks for parents who are staying home with their children, you are also going to be inviting the government into your home to make sure that you are doing what they think you should be doing with a stay-at-home parent check," said Greszler. She warned that even if conservatives are comfortable with how a Republican administration uses the program, establishing that government power could have unintended consequences if control of the White House changes hands. "I worry that this would open the door into using taxpayer funds for social engineering. That in a different administration after another election could be used for the exact opposite intent of what certain conservatives are looking for right now to use it," Greszler added. DRIVEN BY PROGRESSIVE DOOMISM, LIBERALS ARE HAVING FEWER BABIES THAN CONSERVATIVE FAMILIES Schilling said the earlier Americans marry and start families, the more prosperous the country will be, and this program will give support to married families over commercial daycare networks to raise children. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Traditional welfare routes money through middlemen and too often subsidized family breakdown. This proposal works on the same principle as Republican healthcare reforms: instead of sending subsidies to insurance companies, put the money directly in the hands of families," he said. Schilling says critics call it dependency when a parent stays home, but call it "investment" when a bureaucracy does it. Florida GOP Rep. Anna Paulina Luna shared an article on the plan and wrote, "Being a stay-at-home parent is a full-time job and there should be resources and reward available to families that do this." Fox News Digital reached out to the office of the vice president and the White House for comment.

title: 'Double Lives' star says being kicked out of church over adult content career didn't shake her faith
description: Tammy from "Double Lives of Suburban Wives" reveals being kicked out of her church over adult content creation and how she chose forgiveness.
content: Tammy has no plans to walk away from her Christian faith, even if some fellow believers question whether it can coexist with her adult-content career. 'DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES' STAR SAYS SECRET ADULT-CONTENT SIDE HUSTLE GOT HER FIRED FROM CORPORATE JOB Tammy said she ultimately chose forgiveness rather than allowing the experience to change her relationship with her faith. "I did have to, like, choose to forgive for my own heart that, you know, people are people. People make wrong judgments," she said. "You know, they're doing their best of what they think to, like, lead us in the way that they think they should." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "But ultimately, at the end of the day, God knows my heart," Tammy continued. "You know, God has purpose even in my life right now, as I'm sitting in this chair, you know, that pastor didn't know about. And I lean into that more than I do human opinions." WATCH: ‘DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES’ STAR TAMMY SAYS FAITH NEVER WAVERED AFTER CHURCH OUSTER Tammy is one of the women featured on TLC's "Double Lives of Suburban Wives," which follows six couples in the St. Louis area balancing marriage, parenthood and suburban life with careers creating adult content. "I think there are sinful elements, obviously, I'm not going to ignore that, but just like everything else in life, we are not perfect," Tammy told Fox News Digital. "But I think out of that imperfection, God can still do amazing things, and I'm focusing on that," she continued. "And, you know, I hope that I'm still open, that God can open up doors in my life and change me in the way that He wants to change me." Tammy also had a message for Christians who believe her faith and career are incompatible. HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER SPENT 25 YEARS PRAYING FOR TINSELTOWN, SAYS 'YOU CAN'T HATE THEM' "I would just challenge them to look at their own lives," she said. "I mean, in the Bible, it says, like, you know, you who've cast the first stone, you know, like we're not all blameless and sinless," she said. "Like the whole point of Christianity is that Jesus died for our sins, because nobody by their works was going to be perfect to earn that." "And it's through that grace that we are allowed to be with God and be in communion with God," Tammy continued. "And even though my sin looks different from yours, we're all still imperfect." Her co-star Brianna, who joined Tammy for the interview, interjected, "Who's to say that your sin is worse?"WATCH HERE: ‘DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES’ STAR TAMMY REVEALS WHY SHE TURNED TO CONTENT CREATION Tammy added, "Yeah, or yours is just hidden and mine I'm open about." Tammy acknowledged that reconciling her faith with her career remains an internal struggle. Asked whether she has ever seriously considered walking away from adult-content creation because of her religious beliefs, Tammy said the question still crosses her mind. "I think it's an internal struggle that always pops in your head," she told Fox News Digital. But Tammy said her reasons for entering the business are also tied closely to her family. "The whole point of why I got into content creation was to have more family time and to have some more wholesome things where I can be there for my kids and provide for my kid in ways that I didn't have before," she said. "So to consider one without the other just doesn't do it justice." ‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STAR OPENS UP ABOUT WIFE’S AFFAIR, SAYS MARRIAGE ‘DOESN’T HAVE TO END’ AFTER BETRAYAL Appearing on television has also brought the criticism Tammy was already accustomed to receiving closer to home. "We try our best to know that this is who we are. We're good parents, we're good friends. We are just trying to live our lives just like everybody else." Tammy said she and Drew understood that putting their lives on television would invite greater scrutiny, making their reasons for participating important. "We had to know for sure, for sure, for sure that we're gonna be okay," she said. "It's like we obviously have a lot to speak about as people and about the judgments and the stigmas and a lot of the misinformation that surrounds what we do." "Content creation has… it's not going away," she continued. "And so I just felt like this was such a great opportunity to be able to come out and actually educate people that are curious on really what goes on behind the scenes." Some of that judgment has also followed Tammy into her everyday life. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS During the series, viewers saw an incident involving Tammy and other cast members at her gym. Despite the encounter, Tammy told Fox News Digital she continues to work out there about five days a week. While she said the gym's main staff has remained supportive, Tammy claimed some fellow gym members have become more confrontational. "There have been some gym goers that now, like, feel brazen to, you know, to come out and be nasty towards me," she said. "But I will say that the gym has really stuck up for me in that regard so far."WATCH HERE: ‘DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES’ STAR TAMMY VOWS SHE ‘WILL NOT BE PUSHED OUT’ And Tammy said the criticism hasn't made her consider leaving St. Louis. title: Tim Scott opens up on ‘miraculous’ car crash survival that changed the course of his life
description: Tim Scott told Sean Hannity he yelled "Jesus" during the crash that sent him through a windshield and derailed several college football scholarships.
content: Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., opened up about the car crash that derailed his football dreams as a teenager, revealing the moment he believes divine intervention saved his life. "I called for help, which for me was, I just yelled, 'Jesus,'" the South Carolina Republican recalled during the latest episode of "Hang Out With Sean Hannity." "I feel like, in an unusually miraculous way, some power — angel, in my opinion — protected me through all of that carnage." REPUBLICANS HEAD TO DALLAS WITH ONE MISSION: DEFY HISTORY AND WIN BIG Scott recounted the crash during a conversation with Fox News host Sean Hannity at last week’s Republican National Committee Midterm Convention in Dallas, where the two discussed the pivotal moment in the senator's life that unfolded long before he entered national politics. Scott, a standout high school football player at the time, had been "moving up the ranks" when the crash derailed his athletic career. He recalled driving his mother to work one morning before falling asleep behind the wheel on his way home. COLTON BURPO DESCRIBES MEETING JESUS AND HEARING ANGELS SING DURING NEAR-DEATH EXPERIENCE After waking to the sound of his tires on gravel, Scott said he slammed on the brakes and jerked the steering wheel, sending the car spinning across lanes of traffic before it hit the median. The impact sent him through the windshield as he held onto the steering wheel. The crash left Scott with a broken ankle and back injuries, and many promises of college athletic scholarships dwindled. Presbyterian College in Clinton, South Carolina, however, offered Scott a partial scholarship. title: Democrats reluctantly hand Trump major victory on fraud program targeting Tim Walz
description: Hakeem Jeffries and over 140 House Democrats joined Republicans to make Trump's National Fraud Enforcement Division permanent in a 352-72 vote.
content: President Donald Trump's crackdown on government fraud is getting unexpected backup from a majority of House Democrats, including Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. More than 140 House Democrats voted with all Republicans to make the National Fraud Enforcement Division permanent on Wednesday. The bill passed in an overwhelming 352 to 72 vote, with all of its opponents being Democrats as well. Trump's White House first announced the creation of a new division within the Department of Justice (DOJ) to combat fraud in January 2026, primarily targeting "fraud affecting the federal government, federally funded programs, and private citizens," according to a release by the administration. It was notably used as a cudgel against Trump's political enemies earlier this year, when Vice President JD Vance referred Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz and state Attorney General Keith Ellison to the fraud division for a potential criminal investigation. WHITE HOUSE PUSHES 'WATERSHED' FRAUD-FIGHTING REFORM IN CONGRESS AS VANCE CONVENES TASK FORCE Republicans accused Walz and Ellison of helping facilitate what's become a ballooning fraud scandal affecting Minnesota's social welfare programs. Both have acknowledged that taxpayer dollars were taken advantage of but accused GOP actors of casting the situation as worse than it actually is as a political attack. VANCE REFERS TIM WALZ, MINNESOTA ATTORNEY GENERAL TO DOJ FOR CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION OVER STATE'S ALLEGED FRAUD The Trump administration's announcement of the fraud division also touted its actions in Minnesota, which it said was experiencing a "fraud epidemic." Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., a top House progressive, said he would give "tepid support" to the legislation, while pointing out a fraud division has already existed within the DOJ for decades. REPUBLICANS DECLARE WAR ON 'ORGANIZED THEFT' WITH GOVERNMENT FRAUD CRACKDOWN "This is hardly some kind of great breakthrough in law enforcement or criminal justice, but it is perhaps the least offensive piece of legislative flotsam and jetsam that has washed ashore in the last 48 hours of Republican chaos and retreat here in the House of Representatives," Raskin said on the House floor. It's a permanent, nonpartisan commitment that we do something better because the people who are listening here... the people who are watching, they're getting tired of it." "They're getting tired of all the money that has been wasted. And to try to pretend that just a few years ago, a couple of years ago, everything was perfect, everything was taken care of and that there was no corruption, we know better," Van Drew said. Raskin spent a significant amount of time accusing Trump and his administration allies of corruption at the expense of prosecuting actual fraud cases, something Republicans pushed back against. "What has come out of Minnesota over the last year, what has been exposed, is absolutely criminal in nature," said Rep. Harriet Hageman, R-Wyo. "I think what is coming, what is being exposed in blue cities and blue states run by Democrats, demonstrates that it's probably higher by an order of magnitude." Raskin then targeted Van Drew directly in his comments: "My dear friend from New Jersey wants to make it sound like I'm doing something partisan. I'm joining his bill." title: Driverless racing goes global. Will fans care?
description: Autonomous race cars hit Laguna Seca and Imola Circuit at speeds topping 157 mph, but the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League faces a fan problem.
content: Autonomous race cars are starting to show up on some very famous tracks. On Sept. 3, the Indy Autonomous Challenge brought its driverless race cars to WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca in California. Purdue AI Racing set a new autonomous track record and finished second in a head-to-head passing competition. Italy's Unimore Racing took the win. Two days later, autonomous racing took another step forward in Europe. Five teams brought fully autonomous race cars to Italy's Imola Circuit for the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League's first race outside Abu Dhabi. Team Kinetiz came from fourth on the grid to win the 12-lap event. Now autonomous racing has reached major circuits in the U.S., Europe and Abu Dhabi. The technology clearly travels. The bigger question is whether the fans will follow. NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed. Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com. WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK Driverless racing is becoming a global competition The races at Laguna Seca and Imola came from two different autonomous racing programs. The Indy Autonomous Challenge brings together university teams that develop AI drivers for identical race cars. At Laguna Seca, nine university teams from North America, Europe and Asia were scheduled to compete. The Sept. 3 event pushed the competition further by adapting the Indy Autonomous Challenge's passing format to a road course for the first time. Instead of several cars racing as a pack, two autonomous cars take turns in attacking and defending roles. The software has to manage spacing and decide when it can safely make a move. Purdue became the only American team to qualify for that portion of the competition. Its car also set a 1:27.731 autonomous lap record before finishing runner-up to Unimore. Then came Imola. A2RL brought autonomous racing from its home at Yas Marina Circuit in Abu Dhabi to Europe for the first time. The league says Imola represents another step toward its goal of creating an international championship for fully autonomous race cars. Five autonomous race cars headed to the grid at Imola Imola raised the difficulty again. Kinetiz, Constructor Racing, PoliMOVE, Unimore Racing and two-time A2RL champion TUM entered the event. Each team competed with identical EAV-25 race car hardware based on the Dallara Super Formula SF23 platform. That means much of the competitive advantage came from the software each team developed. The AI had to figure out where the car was, understand what was happening around it and decide what to do next. Then it had to turn those decisions into braking and steering inputs at racing speed. TUM ran into a technical problem on the formation lap and returned to the pits before the rolling start. That left the remaining cars to fight for position. Unimore had started from pole and led the race. Then things went wrong. WAYMO VEHICLES 'PUTTING AMERICAN LIVES AT RISK,' SOURCE WARNS AMID AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE COMPANY'S MASSIVE RECALL A crash showed how hard autonomous racing can be Unimore set the fastest lap of the race before suffering a technical problem that caused the car to slow dramatically. PoliMOVE was close behind and hit the slowing Unimore car from the rear. The collision ended both teams' runs. That opened the door for Kinetiz. The Singapore-UAE team had started fourth but moved into the lead and won by 10.963 seconds over Germany's Constructor Racing. PoliMOVE was classified third. The crash may also be one of the most revealing parts of the race. Driving fast on an empty track is one challenge. Reacting when the car directly in front of you suddenly loses speed creates a much harder problem. That is exactly the type of unpredictability autonomous systems have to learn to handle. These AI race cars are getting seriously fast These cars are moving a lot faster than you might expect. At Imola, PoliMOVE hit about 157 mph with nobody behind the wheel. During testing, the fastest autonomous lap came within 0.85 seconds of a benchmark lap set by Super Formula driver Juju Noda. That is surprisingly close. In Abu Dhabi last year, former Formula 1 driver Daniil Kvyat still set a faster lap than the autonomous challenger, but the gap had narrowed to just 1.58 seconds. So the question has changed. We already know these cars can get around a racetrack at serious speeds. Now we are seeing what happens when they have to race another car and make those decisions in real time. But who are fans supposed to root for? Here's where autonomous racing faces a challenge that has nothing to do with speed. Part of the fun of racing is having someone to root for. Fans follow drivers, get to know their personalities and pick favorites. Take the driver out of the car and suddenly that connection looks very different. With autonomous racing, you are rooting for the team behind the software. For some tech fans, that may be enough. Watching engineers figure out how to make an AI-powered race car faster and smarter could become part of the appeal. But will people come back race after race? We are already starting to get a sense of that. The Indy Autonomous Challenge returned to Laguna Seca this year and moved from solo time trials in 2025 to head-to-head passing on the road course. Just two days later, five autonomous race cars competed together at Imola in Italy. Now the harder part may be building the kind of connection that keeps people watching after the surprise of seeing an empty cockpit wears off. So what is the point of racing cars without drivers? There is another reason these competitions are worth watching. Racetracks give autonomous driving researchers a place to push software extremely hard. At Laguna Seca, Purdue's team spent weeks practicing and used simulation to find bugs in its software before race day. At Imola, the AI had to deal with high speeds and other autonomous cars making their own decisions. That pressure can reveal weaknesses quickly. A passenger car on a public road faces a very different environment. It has to deal with pedestrians, intersections and countless situations that do not exist on a closed racetrack. So winning an autonomous race does not mean the same software is ready to drive you around town. Still, the basic challenge overlaps. An autonomous vehicle has to understand what is happening around it and decide how to respond. Racing forces researchers to test those capabilities at the edge of what the vehicle can handle. That is where this becomes relevant even if you never watch a single autonomous race. Kurt's key takeaways Here's what gets me about autonomous racing. We have gone from asking whether AI can keep a race car on the track to watching these cars chase each other at more than 150 mph. That is pretty remarkable. But speed alone will not turn this into a sport people care about. Part of what makes racing so compelling is the person inside the car. You follow the driver, learn their personality and pick someone you want to win. When the cockpit is empty, that connection changes completely. Could fans eventually start rooting for the teams behind the technology instead? I can see Purdue students and engineers developing their own following as these competitions grow. But autonomous racing still has to prove that watching great software compete can be as exciting as watching a great driver push a car to the limit. The cars are clearly ready to race. Now we get to see whether the fans are ready to care. Would you watch an entire race with nobody behind the wheel? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com. title: Republicans just got a powerful new playbook for the battle for Congress. Here's what's inside
description: First on Fox: Advancing American Freedom unveils over 100 proposals to cut housing, energy and healthcare costs ahead of 2026 midterm elections.
content: FIRST ON FOX: With control of Congress on the line and pocketbook issues dominating the campaign trail, a prominent conservative group is unveiling a sweeping affordability agenda aimed at giving Republicans a sharper economic message ahead of the November midterm elections. The Advancing American Freedom report, "Affordability 101," obtained first by Fox News Digital ahead of its Capitol Hill rollout Thursday, lays out more than 100 recommendations to lower the costs of housing, energy, food and healthcare by expanding supply, increasing competition and reducing government barriers. The blueprint is a potential resource for Republican lawmakers and congressional staff while affordability emerges as one of the defining issues of the 2026 midterm elections. Founded by former Vice President Mike Pence, Advancing American Freedom argues costs can be lowered by reducing regulations, encouraging competition and boosting domestic production rather than creating new federal subsidies. "We want free market conservative candidates to go out there and not just put on the red jersey or not just fight against the blue jersey, but to go there and give people ideas that actually work," Advancing American Freedom President Tim Chapman told Fox News Digital. TRUMP’S AFFORDABILITY PLAN FACES CONSERVATIVE PUSHBACK AS POCKETBOOK ISSUES LOOM OVER MIDTERMS Chapman argued the size and scope of government plays a larger role in affordability than many Americans realize. "The size and scope of the government matters more than people understand in terms of its impact on the economy," Chapman said. "If you look at interest rates right now and how much of the skyrocketing interest rates are fueled by the debt and deficit problem, that's something we need to be concerned about as Americans." Many of the proposals align with Trump administration priorities, including expanding domestic energy production, building more homes, reducing regulations and encouraging innovation. But the blueprint also breaks with the administration on several issues. TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED One flashpoint is Vice President JD Vance's proposal to expand childcare subsidies by broadening eligibility under the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF), potentially providing some married families with a stay-at-home parent up to about $9,000 per child annually. "His proposal sounds great, right?" Richard Stern, vice president of the Plymouth Institute for Free Enterprise at Advancing American Freedom, told Fox News Digital. "But the truth is, in many cases, it's a $9,000 divorce bonus." On housing, the report says government regulations add 26.4% to the cost of a new single-family home and calls for permitting, zoning and land-use reforms to lower construction costs. "I think those memos that deal with construction regulations and land use are the core group that would help affordability the most," Stern said. 5 STATES COULD BE THE BIGGEST LOSERS IN TRUMP'S TRADE WAR WITH CANADA, EXPERT WARNS The report also argues tariffs raise consumer prices, another point of disagreement with the administration. "If you look at your grocery bill, how much of that is impacted by tariffs?" Chapman said. "That's driving up the price of goods and it's hurting people in their pocketbooks." The blueprint also argues that expanding domestic energy production and easing regulations on artificial intelligence and data centers can help lower costs. Trump has championed rapid data center development despite growing concerns over electricity demand and local impacts. "The counties that have data centers are making money off of it," Stern said. "They're actually reducing energy prices for those homes." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP As candidates sharpen their economic messages ahead of November, Chapman said the report is meant to give lawmakers concrete policy proposals they can take back to voters. "We want people to have those solutions," Chapman said. "When they go home and talk to their constituents about the future of the country, they can say, 'I actually have an idea. Here's an idea for getting interest rates down or here's an idea for more small business growth.'"

title: Tennis great Patrick McEnroe urges Congress to cap foreign recruits, protect American student-athletes
description: Patrick McEnroe told Congress that nearly 70% of Division I tennis roster spots now go to international recruits, crowding out American kids.
content: Tennis legend Patrick McEnroe took his fight directly to Capitol Hill this week, urging Congress to cap international athletes on college rosters at 20%. Speaking with OutKick following his testimony before the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, the former Davis Cup captain made his mission clear: stop taxpayer-funded universities from shutting out American kids and restore their focus on developing young domestic talent. "Football and basketball are essentially professional now, and universities are under increasing pressure to fund them," McEnroe told OutKick. "The sports being squeezed are tennis, wrestling and swimming, the Olympic sports that don’t generate revenue." A reality check for college sports The turning point came when McEnroe turned on the SEC Network to watch a college tennis championship and noticed that only two of the 12 players on the court were American. An ACC championship match revealed an even worse ratio, with just one American out of 12. In Division I tennis, international recruits now occupy nearly 70% of roster spots. "This is collegiate tennis, and we’re losing a pathway of dreams and opportunities for American kids," McEnroe said. "I think of it as the rungs on a ladder. If you keep taking away the rungs, the kids will eventually give up." At his academy in New York, McEnroe sees young American athletes grinding every weekend, only to watch collegiate opportunities evaporate as coaches favor older international recruits with professional experience. "Many of those kids dream of playing professionally, but by 14 or 15, they realize that probably won’t happen," McEnroe explained. "What they want is the opportunity to play college tennis, and they’re starting to see that dream disappear. I don’t think that’s right." "That’s why I say I’m not worried about the players who are going to make it," he added. "They represent roughly 1 percent of the people who play college tennis or other college sports and eventually become professionals. This is about the masses." CRUZ AND CANTWELL REFUSE TO BEND TO SEC AND BIG TEN CONCERNS IN REVISED COLLEGE ATHLETICS LEGISLATION Capping international recruits to protect American talent To fix the system, McEnroe is backing a legislative proposal introduced by Rep. Tim Walberg, R-Mich., that would cap international roster spots at 20%. McEnroe believes a firm limit is necessary to give American student-athletes a fairer opportunity. "I don’t believe the purpose of that funding is to give every roster spot to international athletes," McEnroe emphasized. "I’m completely in favor of international athletes participating, but there needs to be a reasonable limit." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He noted that college coaches, trapped in a 'win-now' mentality, are often forced into the recruiting arms race, even if many privately support reform. "I don’t blame the colleges or coaches," McEnroe said. "The system needs guardrails so American kids have an opportunity to play. If the percentage is limited, everyone is on a level playing field." "Many coaches I know won’t publicly support this because they’re afraid of losing their jobs," he added. "That’s why I’m doing it for them. I believe most coaches want a level playing field." For McEnroe, tennis is just the tip of the iceberg in a much broader battle across college sports. "This is a message we should send to young athletes and families in every sport, including soccer and lacrosse," McEnroe added. "In non-revenue Olympic sports, we need to restore some balance to collegiate athletics." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Stop subsidizing overseas competitors The disparity is especially striking when viewed through the lens of the global stage. At the 2024 Paris Olympics, 1,200 NCAA athletes competed, but only 386 were American. More than 800 international athletes trained in U.S. collegiate programs before competing against American athletes at the Olympics. "We have the best training, coaches, facilities and competition in collegiate sports, and we provide all of that to international athletes so they can return home and compete against us in the Olympics," McEnroe argued. "I don’t think that’s what we want taxpayer money supporting." TRUMP URGES CONGRESS TO PASS PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT BEFORE RECESS: 'WE HAVE TO GET THAT DONE' Capping foreign spots is not an attack on international players. It is a necessary fix to ensure American universities return to their core mission of developing home-grown talent. "I’m an international person," McEnroe concluded. "I’ve been fortunate to travel the world through tennis and make friends everywhere. I love that part of tennis and many other sports. But that doesn’t mean international athletes should completely take over an American collegiate athletic system." title: To beat China in AI, America must work with communities — not around them
description: The United States faces over 200 data center moratoriums, but a proposed American AI Infrastructure Compact could protect ratepayers and communities.
content: To preserve America’s national security and economic competitiveness against foreign adversaries, the United States must lead the artificial intelligence (AI) era. But, the infrastructure necessary to maintain that edge is increasingly being questioned. More than 200 communities have enacted data center moratoriums or similar restrictions, a growing number of states are imposing or considering pauses, and dozens of high-profile data center projects have slowed or stopped across the country. Certainly, local communities have legitimate questions about this buildout. Who pays for the new electricity and infrastructure? What happens to local water supplies? How will noise, light and large industrial facilities affect nearby neighborhoods? And what will communities receive in return? Those questions deserve and must have honest answers. DEMOCRATS CAN TAKE THE LEAD ON ONE OF THE NATION’S TOP ISSUES – DATA CENTERS But at the same time, America must keep building its data center infrastructure. AI is the most transformative technology of the past 100 years, one that is already driving roughly a third of U.S. economic growth. What we build, or don’t build, today will help determine whether America leads the AI era or falls behind China. We need a better way forward. An "American AI Infrastructure Compact" can protect communities while giving responsible projects a predictable path to construction. Four key protections include: US ADVERSARY TURNS UP THE HEAT ON AMERICA’S AI LEAD WITH AN UNDERESTIMATED EDGE ONE OF THE WORLD'S HOTTEST INDUSTRIES IS SPARKING A BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM Communities have every right to demand responsible development from companies making enormous investments. The goal should be to secure those protections without turning away the jobs, investment and tax revenue responsible projects can bring. AMERICA NEEDS AI TO SURVIVE. WORKING FAMILIES ALSO NEED TO SURVIVE IT These commitments are not merely aspirational. One central element of this compact — protecting ratepayers — is already taking shape. In March 2026, America’s largest data center developers signed the national Ratepayer Protection Pledge, committing to build, bring or buy the power their data centers need and cover the cost of the infrastructure required to deliver it. Since then, hundreds of utilities, developers and states have joined them in this pledge. These arrangements can do more than shield existing customers from new costs. They can also spread fixed grid costs across a larger customer base and lower rates. In Indiana, a utility has proposed a rate reduction that would save the average household roughly $100 a year, citing revenue from data centers and other large customers. In Louisiana, agreements connected to Meta’s data center will return roughly $2.6 billion to customers over two decades.
