title: Tesla Cybercab bars kids under 13 as scrutiny grows
description: Tesla's Cybercab launched in Austin with no steering wheel or pedals, but hidden details about age limits and missing safety features may shock riders.
content: Tesla's Cybercab is finally carrying riders in Austin, Texas. And some of the details buried in the fine print may surprise you. The gold two-seater has no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla says it uses cameras and AI to handle the driving, putting passengers entirely in the hands of its autonomous system. Yet the Sept. 3 launch was unusually low-key for Tesla. The main presentation reportedly lasted about 15 minutes, and Elon Musk apparently did not speak. Then, on Sept. 4, federal safety regulators announced an investigation into how Tesla certified Cybercab for U.S. roads. Tesla has spent years building toward this moment. Now that real riders are climbing inside, the little details suddenly become much more important. Here is what you should know before you step into a Cybercab. ZOOX ROBOTAXI REDESIGN BRINGS BIG RIDER UPGRADES NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed. Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com Tesla Cybercab has a surprising age limit If you planned to call a Cybercab for a family ride, check the passenger rules first. Tesla says children under 13 cannot ride in Cybercab "at this time." Teens ages 13 through 17 can ride, although an adult must accompany them for the entire trip. Interestingly, Tesla sets a different age limit for the Model Y vehicles in its Robotaxi service. Children ages 8 through 17 can ride in those vehicles with an adult. Guests under 8 cannot. So, an 11-year-old could ride in a Tesla Model Y Robotaxi but could not take the same trip in a Cybercab. Tesla does not explain the reason for that difference in its current rider guidance. Then there is another detail parents may notice. Cybercab has no LATCH child-seat anchors Tesla confirms that Cybercab has no LATCH or ISOFIX child-restraint system. If a rider needs a booster seat, Tesla says it must use a seat belt to secure it. That may sound odd considering Cybercab does not allow children under 13. However, some older children may still need a booster seat depending on their size and local requirements. Tesla gives instructions for using one, but there are no LATCH anchors to attach it to. It is the kind of detail most of us probably would not think about until a Cybercab showed up at the curb. What happens if a Cybercab crashes? A driverless vehicle still needs a plan for the moment something goes wrong. According to Tesla documentation, a collision can trigger several automatic responses. The airbags can deploy and the doors can unlock. Hazard lights and interior lights can also switch on. The vehicle can disable its high-voltage battery, move the windows into a vent position and apply the brakes until it comes to a stop. Tesla's system can also open a two-way connection with its Robotaxi Support team. That support connection could become especially important in a vehicle where nobody can grab the steering wheel or hit the brakes. Tesla also gives riders ways to stop a trip themselves. UBER LETS PARENTS WATCH TEEN RIDES LIVE There is an emergency Stop button Look above you when you get inside a Cybercab. Tesla placed a dedicated Stop button between the dome lights. Pressing it sends an immediate pull-over request, ends the ride and connects you with Robotaxi Support. You can also tap Pull Over on the touchscreen or make the request through the Robotaxi app. However, Tesla warns that an "immediate" pull-over may still take some time. For example, the vehicle may need longer to reach a safe stopping point while traveling on a highway. That is worth knowing before your first ride. Tesla made the manual door release easier to find Tesla's electronic door releases have attracted criticism because passengers may need a mechanical backup when a vehicle loses power. Cybercab still uses electronically controlled doors during normal operation. In fact, the nearest door can open automatically when the ride requester approaches. Inside, you can normally open the door through the touchscreen or gently lift a lever on the door panel. Pull that lever firmly all the way up, though, and it activates the mechanical release. Both Cybercab doors have one. I like that Tesla put the emergency release where a passenger can actually see and reach it. There is one important warning. Tesla says using the mechanical release can damage the window or trim. If the vehicle has no power and the window remains fully raised, Tesla warns the glass could shatter when someone activates the release. That is one instruction I would want to know before an emergency. Cybercab uses electronic braking Tesla also made a major change underneath the vehicle. Cybercab uses a brake-by-wire system rather than a traditional hydraulic setup. Electronic actuators control the brake calipers instead of hydraulic lines carrying brake fluid. Musk said in a post on X that electric brakes avoid the complexity of routing hydraulic plumbing around the vehicle. Tesla has already used steer-by-wire technology in the Cybertruck. With Cybercab, passengers have no physical driving controls at all. That puts even more responsibility on the electronics and software to work properly every time. Cybercab windows will not open all the way Here is one of the stranger details Tesla included in its new rider guide. Cybercab passengers can lower the windows, but Tesla says they "cannot be fully opened at this time." The company does not explain why. The window switches also sit underneath the center touchscreen rather than on the doors. So, yes, you can crack a window for some air. You simply cannot roll it all the way down right now. WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK Cybercab packs USB-C charging At least you should have somewhere to plug in your devices. Tesla confirms that Cybercab has USB-C charging ports inside the cabin. An attendee at the launch reported that those ports can deliver up to 90 watts of power. That could be enough to charge many laptops. However, Tesla's current public rider guide does not list that wattage. So, I would treat the 90-watt figure as an early report until Tesla publishes the specification itself. Federal regulators are already looking at Cybercab On Sept. 3, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened what it calls an Audit Query into Tesla's certification that Cybercab meets all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. NHTSA announced the action on Sept. 4 following the vehicle's commercial deployment in Austin. Automakers in the U.S. generally certify their own vehicles as complying with federal standards. NHTSA can then audit those certifications and investigate when questions come up. Cybercab presents an unusual case because it has no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors. Many federal vehicle rules were written around cars designed for human drivers. NHTSA's audit reportedly covers about 1,000 Cybercabs as the agency reviews how Tesla determined the vehicles comply. That does not mean regulators have found Cybercab unsafe. It does mean Tesla now has to back up its certification with technical information that satisfies the agency. What this means to you If you get the chance to ride in a Cybercab, I would spend a minute learning the cabin before the car starts moving. Find the emergency Stop button. Know where the mechanical door release sits. Keep your seat belt fastened for the entire trip. Tesla says every passenger must buckle up before the ride begins. Cybercab may pull over or cancel a trip if it detects improper seat-belt use. Parents should also pay close attention to the age rules. Cybercab and Tesla's Model Y Robotaxi do not follow the same limits. Beyond that, remember how new this vehicle is. Tesla is putting a very different kind of car into real-world service, and regulators are already asking questions about how it fits existing safety standards. We have seen how unexpected situations can challenge other autonomous vehicles too. CyberGuy recently reported how Waymo recalled robotaxis over a construction-zone risk after vehicles entered closed freeway construction areas. The technology can be impressive. Still, the real test comes when these vehicles deal with everything ordinary roads throw at them. Kurt's key takeaways Cybercab is finally moving from Tesla's big promise to something people can actually ride in. I like seeing safeguards such as the mechanical door release and emergency Stop button, especially when passengers have no steering wheel or pedals to grab. Still, the under-13 restriction, lack of LATCH anchors and windows that do not fully open caught my attention. Add the federal investigation, and Tesla now has something bigger to prove. Putting Cybercab on the road is one thing. Showing that people can trust it day after day is the real test. Would you climb into a Cybercab today with no steering wheel or pedals, or would you want to see a longer safety record before trusting it with your ride? title: NATO jets shoot down drone in Lithuanian airspace as Russia grows 'increasingly reckless,' Rutte says
description: Two Italian Eurofighter Typhoons scrambled under NATO command and downed a drone over Lithuania that officials say likely came from Belarus.
content: Two Italian Eurofighter Typhoons operating under NATO command scrambled overnight and shot down a drone over Lithuania, marking the first time a drone has been downed in the Baltic nation's airspace, officials said Tuesday. The incident came less than a day after NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned that strikes close to alliance territory would drive the 32-nation bloc to increase its support for Ukraine. The drone was destroyed near the village of Pratkūnai, about 60 miles northwest of the capital, Vilnius. RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS "Last night, two Italian Eurofighters deployed on NATO Air Defence mission at Siauliai, scrambled and shot down a drone over Lithuanian airspace," a NATO official told Fox News Digital. "The operation was coordinated through NATO’s Combined Air Operations Centre in Uedem, Germany. Investigations are ongoing together with national authorities." Lithuanian officials said the drone most likely entered from neighboring Belarus and remained in the country's airspace for about 30 minutes before it was intercepted. Lithuanian Air Force Commander Antanas Matutis said the recovered drone was "likely" carrying explosives. Authorities are examining the wreckage of the downed drone to determine its origin and purpose. The incident comes amid heightened tensions along NATO's eastern flank. RUSSIA EXPOSES NATO WEAPONS GAP AS TOP COMMANDER WARNS ‘THE MATH IS NOT IN FAVOR OF THE WEST’ Speaking in Brussels on Monday, Rutte said strikes "close to NATO territory" showed Russian President Vladimir Putin's "desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror." In a separate incident Tuesday, Denmark said a Russian frigate fired flares toward a Danish military helicopter conducting routine surveillance over the Baltic Sea. Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador over the encounter. Meanwhile, Russia continued drone strikes across Ukraine, killing three people in Kyiv, Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, according to Ukrainian officials. title: Nike-linked CoachingHER program faces scrutiny over gender bias training and definition of girls
description: Sarah Barker claims Nike-backed CoachingHER program defines "girls" to include male athletes while retraining coaches on gender bias.
content: Nike helped create a coaching program designed to keep girls in sports. Three years later, the program is expanding into college classrooms and through a partnership with a national sports governing body, while its own FAQ defines "girls" to include anyone under 18 who identifies as one. Sarah Barker, a former coach and creator of The Female Category, spent months reviewing CoachingHER, its training modules and the research cited to support them. She told OutKick in an exclusive interview that what she found does not match how she believes the program is being presented to coaches. "Everything about it tells me that it is not, in fact, what it is being sold as," Barker said. NIKE SHAREHOLDERS REJECT TRANSPARENCY PROPOSAL AS FAITH-BASED FIRM QUESTIONS DEI COMMITMENTS CoachingHER launched in 2023 as a collaboration between Nike and the Tucker Center for Research on Girls & Women in Sport at the University of Minnesota. Nike said at the time that it developed the free digital resource to help coaches recognize unconscious gender biases and stereotypes that negatively affect girls' experiences in sports. Barker first encountered CoachingHER through the Minnesota State High School League after spending 10 years as a coach. She decided to take the course herself. "I did the training modules and I interviewed the director of the Coaching Her program at the Tucker Center," Barker said. Then she kept digging. Barker questions CoachingHER's focus on gender bias CoachingHER’s current FAQ defines "girls" as someone under 18 "who was assigned female at birth or who identifies as a girl" and says the program is "inclusive of gender-expansive identities," language Barker said was displayed more prominently when she first investigated the program in 2024. For Barker, those few words change the meaning of the training that follows. The CoachingHER website says its courses give coaches "girl-centered strategies" and tools to create "supportive, inclusive environments for girls in sports." Barker said that definition becomes especially important in a module addressing bodies and identities. "They exhort coaches in one of the training modules to accept all, and all is in capital letters, all bodies and identities," Barker said. MEGAN RAPINOE'S LATEST DEFENSE OF MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS COLLAPSES UNDER ITS OWN HYPOCRISY | DAN ZAKSHESKE On its face, Barker said much of the advice sounds unobjectionable. But she argues the program's definition of "girls" changes the context because it also encompasses male athletes. Barker's broader criticism is that CoachingHER's emphasis on coaches' gender biases does not match what she found in the research on why girls leave sports. A current CoachingHER article, citing 2024 research from Dove and Nike, says low body confidence is the "No. 1 reason girls quit sports." But the program describes its mission as addressing "the unconscious gender biases and stereotypes held by coaches." The Tucker Center and Nike have said coaches were chosen as a focus because earlier research identified them as an important influence on girls' sports experiences. In a 2023 article about the creation of CoachingHER, Tucker Center director Nicole LaVoi and former Nike social-impact executive Caitlin Morris also said workshops with girls and coaches helped shape the program's focus on gender stereotypes. Barker argues that explanation does not resolve the disconnect she found in the research on why girls actually leave sports. "They knew that the number one reason girls drop out of sports was concerns with body image," Barker said. She said CoachingHER director Alicia Pelton acknowledged the same point when Barker interviewed her in 2024. Yet Barker said that in the research and lists of dropout factors she reviewed, coaches' gender bias and their understanding of gender identity were not identified among the leading reasons girls leave sports. "What's weird about this is that of the many reasons listed for girls dropping out of sports, their coaches' gender bias was never listed, not in the Tucker Center's own research," Barker said. "It was never listed, not even in the top 15 reasons." That led Barker to question why a program marketed as a way to keep girls in sports was focused so heavily on changing coaches' attitudes about gender. "Why would they build an entire program around blaming coaches when they know that that is not true?" she said. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Nike helped create CoachingHER, but its current financial role is unclear When Nike publicly announced the program in March 2023, the company said it had developed CoachingHER in partnership with the Tucker Center. Nike's website continues to promote CoachingHER in 2026, describing it as a resource "created in partnership with the Tucker Center for Research on Girls and Women in Sport." The CoachingHER website also continues to display Nike's logo under the words "Brought to you by." Barker said she separately discussed Nike's involvement with CoachingHER program director Alicia Pelton during her 2024 investigation. "When I interviewed Alicia Pelton ... she was open about the fact that Nike funded this program," Barker said. "I don't know the amount. I asked and was not told the amount." title: Pennsylvania man accused of plotting ISIS attack arrested with rifle and 190 rounds of ammunition: DOJ
description: Jonathan Hunter Kramer allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and acquired a semiautomatic rifle before FBI agents tracked him to a Pennsylvania hotel.
content: A 21-year-old Pennsylvania man accused of plotting a violent attack on behalf of ISIS was arrested after FBI agents tracked him to a hotel and seized a semiautomatic rifle, five magazines and 190 rounds of ammunition, federal prosecutors announced Tuesday. Jonathan Hunter Kramer, of Valencia, had allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS, offered to distribute explosives manuals online and said he was preparing for his "mission" but still needed a weapon before agents moved in, according to a federal criminal complaint. Kramer is charged with receiving a firearm and ammunition, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony or federal crime of terrorism, including providing or attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization. WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS The FBI had been aware since a 2023 investigation of Kramer, at the time a minor, when he was charged and adjudicated delinquent in Pennsylvania for his role in a plot to carry out a mass-casualty attack and for possessing child sexual abuse material, according to the Justice Department. Authorities began investigating him again after an anonymous tip came in on March 19, shortly after his release from a juvenile detention facility. The tipster said Kramer was ordering "mysterious" packages and "talking to his friends from before" his juvenile adjudication. Investigators said Kramer was using the online name "Hamza Al Rashid," claiming an affiliation with ISIS and offering to share explosives manuals. He allegedly wrote about preparing for his "mission" and said he was missing a "weapon." On Friday, FBI agents watched Kramer leave his home with a bag and take a rideshare to a store, where he bought a disposable phone, according to the complaint. He then met another person in the parking lot, took a long black bag from the trunk of a vehicle and traveled to a hotel in Cranberry Township, where he paid cash for a room. Witnesses at the store and hotel said the bag made a metallic clicking sound when Kramer put it down. After checking in, Kramer went to a sporting goods store, where agents saw him at the gun counter. FBI ARRESTS WOMAN WHO ALLEGEDLY PLOTTED ISIS-LINKED ATTACK ON NEW YORK STATE CAPITOL BUILDING Agents approached him when he returned to the hotel carrying two bags from the store. Searches of Kramer, his hotel room and his home turned up a semiautomatic rifle, five rifle magazines — two loaded and three capable of holding 30 rounds each — and 190 rounds of rifle ammunition, according to the complaint. Agents also found a rifle scope and bipod, an entrenchment tool, pepper spray and about 30 knives. A handwritten note read, "DoNt look For me[.] IDK what I did buT I cant live In constant Fear[.]" Attorney General Todd Blanche said the arrest came as Americans marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. "Their outstanding work thwarted this alleged attack before innocent lives could be lost," Blanche said. FBI Director Kash Patel said Kramer had been "plotting a violent attack in support of ISIS," citing his online activity and acquisition of weapons. The Justice Department did not identify a specific target for the alleged attack. Prosecutors have asked that he be held without bond, arguing that he poses a danger to the community.

content: Tourists are being urged to hold off on visiting a scenic Hawaiian island as it continues to recover from a devastating hurricane. title: Smithsonian’s dark take on America exposed: Washington dubbed ‘town destroyer,’ Revolutionary War ‘dangerous'
description: The Smithsonian Institution's American Indians museum labels George Washington a "town destroyer" while omitting key context about the attacks.
content: NEW YORK — A Smithsonian museum in Manhattan presents a sharply critical account of George Washington, the Revolutionary War and America’s early years, while some historical context that complicates that narrative is omitted or given less prominent treatment, Fox News Digital found. The findings come as the Smithsonian faces heightened scrutiny from the Trump administration over how it presents American history. President Donald Trump has ordered a review of the institution’s exhibits and educational materials as part of an effort to change what his administration says is an overly negative portrayal of the country’s history. Fox News Digital visited the Manhattan branch of the National Museum of the American Indian earlier in September and found exhibits that emphasize the destruction suffered by Native communities while offering comparatively little context about the conflicts and events surrounding American military campaigns. One display near the center of the museum’s "Native New York" exhibit features an illustration of Washington’s profile — similar to the one that appears on quarters — over a label that reads "town destroyer." TRUMP GIVES SMITHSONIAN DAYS TO REPLACE 'STRANGE MODERNIST SCULPTURE' WITH FOUNDING FATHER The description underneath the image recounts how "American armies destroyed 40 Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) towns and burned their harvests while residents fled," noting that "the Haudenosaunee still call George Washington and all U.S. presidents Hanadahguyus. The name means ‘town destroyer.’" The panel does not mention the raids on American settlements that led to the campaign or explain why Washington ordered the attack. "The American destruction of the Six Nations' homelands came as a result of the destructive raids carried out by the Indians and American loyalists on the frontiers of New York and Pennsylvania in 1778," an excerpt from the National Park Service reads. "The raids crippled the American Continental Army by depriving it of food and manpower and spread terror by destroying frontier settlements and taking prisoners." The exhibit comes as the Trump administration continues its broader dispute with the Smithsonian over how the institution presents American history. Specifically, the president has taken issue with the institution allegedly seeking to divert the telling of American history "away from America’s Founding and the Founders and towards a narrative of a deeply flawed creation of the country." SMITHSONIAN SHOWDOWN INTENSIFIES AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ISSUES A STARK NEW WARNING The administration has threatened changes to Smithsonian funding and federal-agency support as it presses the institution to alter what it describes as divisive or historically inaccurate portrayals of the country. Many of the other exhibits in the museum take a similar line to the display on Washington, highlighting the alleged brutality of American settlers while downplaying the violence of natives. One placard, recounting the history of the Iroquois between 1779 and 1804 from the point of view of a native woman, states that "it was peaceful, she said, until the white men began their revolution." For roughly 100 years, between 1609 and 1701, the Iroquois were engaged in a series of conflicts with other native tribes over access to animal pelts. Even before the Trump administration’s current dispute with the Smithsonian, the National Museum of the American Indian in Washington, D.C., attracted criticism over how it presents American history. "​​In recent years, I have been chronicling the evolution of the ‘identity museum’ … designed to affirm a particular group’s claims, outline its accomplishments, boost its pride," a cultural critic wrote for the New York Times in 2010. "The National Museum of the American Indian in Washington — a pioneering example of the genre — jettisons Western scholarship and tells its own story, leading one tribe to solemnly describe its earliest historical milestone: ‘Birds teach people to call for rain.’" LEGAL EXPERT CALLS FOR SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP OVERHAUL OVER ‘SELF-LOATHING’ PORTRAYAL OF HISTORY: ‘IT’S BILE’ "Through a gauze of romance, that museum portrays an impossibly peace-loving, harmonious, homogeneous, pastoral world that preceded the invasion of white people — a vision with far less detail and insight than the old natural history museums once provided," the critic continued. The exhibits acknowledge some conflicts involving Native tribes but focus far more heavily on the violence inflicted on them than on the events that led to the fighting. The museum also maintains a catalog of online materials geared towards middle school students that generally take the same editorial line. Teachers, for instance, are instructed to show a video to students that opens by saying that "the American War for independence was such a disruptive and dangerous project." It goes on to frame the actions of American colonists negatively, referring to them as trespassers and squatters. WATCH: SMITHSONIAN DIRECTOR ADMITS SHE SEES HISTORY AS ‘TOOL’ OF ‘SOCIAL JUSTICE’ AFTER EXPLOSIVE HEARING In several displays dealing with the Revolutionary War, the exhibit portrays American actions toward Native allies in sharply negative terms. A video display near the beginning of the exhibit claims, unequivocally, that an American soldier shot and killed Chief White Eyes, a Lenape chief who had allied with the Americans. The cause of White Eyes’ death, however, is historically contested — something the museum outlines in relatively small text underneath the video display, which states that White Eyes was "probably" murdered by an American soldier. The museum is housed within the Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House, a building formerly used for collecting trade duties and named after the Founding Father to commemorate his role as the first secretary of the Treasury. HISTORIAN BLASTS SMITHSONIAN'S ACTIVISM SHIFT AFTER FIRST VISIT IN OVER A DECADE: 'COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PLACE' Just before exiting the building, visitors pass a museum store where several books present sharply critical accounts of American history. "An Indigenous Peoples’ History of the United States," for instance, is displayed prominently on the store shelves. Among other things, the book criticizes Americans for having a "cult-like" dedication to the Constitution, suggests that the United States was founded upon White supremacy and genocide and claims that the federal government is still carrying out ethnic cleansing against natives. A graphic novel adaptation of the text marketed toward younger readers was also available. Other titles on display included "Stealing America: The Hidden Story of Indigenous Slavery in US History," "An Afro-Indigenous History of the United States," a tome about the "two spirit" gender identity and a children’s picture book about Deb Haaland, President Joe Biden’s interior secretary. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Smithsonian did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

title: Alito, Thomas shred 'Hail Mary' challenge to federal ballot mail rules in dissent
description: Justice Samuel Alito called the Supreme Court's refusal to lift a universal injunction against Trump's mail-in ballot rules incorrect in a sharp dissent.
content: Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas firmly dissented Monday as the Supreme Court denied a request by President Donald Trump's administration for relief from a universal injunction against its mail-in ballot rules. The dissent, which Alito authored and Thomas joined, argued that the plaintiffs in the case were relying on claims that the court had previously identified as weak and unlikely to succeed. "The Court incorrectly denies the Government’s application for a stay of a universal injunction that bars implementation of a final rule concerning election ballot mail," Alito wrote. "Some of the plaintiffs lack standing, while the remainder are pursuing a claim that this Court has recently called a ‘Hail Mary pass’ that ‘rarely succeeds.'" SUPREME COURT REJECTS TRUMP BID TO REVIVE STRICT MAIL-BALLOT RULES BEFORE MIDTERMS "The Government has made the showings necessary for a stay, so I respectfully dissent," he concluded. The Court's Monday order went unsigned, but Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote a concurrence that allowed room for a potential Trump victory down the line. He nevertheless argued that it is too close to Election Day to realistically implement the rules for the 2026 midterm elections. FEDERAL APPEALS COURT REJECTS TRUMP BID TO ENFORCE MAIL BALLOT ORDER AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS "In my view, based on the briefing the Court has received at this interim stage, there is at least a fair prospect that the final rule falls within the Postal Service’s statutory authority," Kavanaugh wrote. "But applying the rule in the 2026 elections would be arbitrary and capricious in violation of the Administrative Procedure Act because state and local election officials do not have sufficient time to reasonably implement the rule before the elections." Kavanaugh's concurrence echoes Alito's dissent in acknowledging the expansive authority the USPS holds to regulate the collection, handling, transportation and delivery of mail. USPS WOULDN'T DELIVER BALLOTS IN STATES THAT REFUSE TO FORK OVER MAIL-IN VOTER INFO UNDER PROPOSED RULE The Trump rules would require federal ballot mail to be sent in envelopes bearing an election-mail logo, capable of being scanned by high-speed equipment and carrying a barcode unique to each voter. State and local election officials would also be required to submit envelope designs to the Postal Service for review and upload basic voter information to an online USPS portal. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Under the USPS rule, mailings that failed to comply would not be accepted and would instead be returned to election officials to correct and resubmit. Fox News' Stepheny Price and Shannon Bream contributed to this report.

TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATES SCORE MAJOR BOOST FROM DEEP-POCKETED AI SUPER PAC IN UPCOMING PRIMARIES The advertisements come as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, over the weekend, warned the industry that his company helps lead to give safety measures more time to catch up with rapidly advancing AI capabilities. Just days earlier, an Anthropic researcher resigned while publicly raising concerns about the technology's risks. Anthropic is most known for its LLM AI Claude, one of the leading chatbots in the U.S. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, the father of ChatGPT, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis all expressed support for Amodei’s stance on slowing the pace of AI development. Trump on Monday rejected the calls for implementing safeguards and restrictions on AI, arguing the technology needs a "STRONG AND SMART" president rather than added restraints. The new advertisements, which will run throughout September, follow the ABF's previously unreported $1 million donation made to MAGA Inc. last week to promote candidates who share the group's values of pushing both innovation and security in emerging technologies like AI. But the ads aren't limited to praising Republicans — they also take shots at the perceived risks ABF believes could result from allowing socialist lawmakers like Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., to lead policies dictating the direction of AI. SANDERS PUSHES 'DEATH PENALTY' FOR CRUCIAL US INDUSTRY THAT COULD GIVE ADVANTAGE TO FOREIGN ADVERSARIES "The same people who consistently fail you will write an AI rulebook for their benefit," the advertisement reads as images of Sanders, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., appear onscreen. Security concerns have been top of mind for many Americans and AI experts as the United States races to stay ahead of China in technology developments, with worry that the rapidly increasing growth of AI poses national and cybersecurity threats. "The only way we win the AI race against China is to build a technology that is trusted by the American people," ABF CEO Janet Kelly said in a statement to Fox News Digital on the new ad buys. "We cannot cede this responsibility to Socialists like Bernie Sanders, who have a track record of destroying our economy and palling around with our enemies," she continued. "Conservatives like Susan Collins, Roger Marshall, and Ashley Hinson know the time is now to enact an agenda that ensures AI is built with American values." Sanders’ office did not reply to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on being singled out in the campaign ads. MIKE JOHNSON REJECTS AI MORATORIUM OVER CHINA THREAT AS CONSERVATIVE ACTIVIST DEMANDS GUARDRAILS Kelly, the former secretary of Health in Virginia, warned that China will "cheat and steal and lie" to beat the U.S. in the AI race in a policy event hosted by Breitbart news last week. She emphasized the need for America to be both diligent and urgent in developing this technology at a pace that puts the U.S. above foreign adversaries. Collins, Marshall and Hinson have each backed policies that align with ABF’s goal to pursue AI development with protections that work to combat any emerging risks. Hinson has argued that the U.S. must maintain its technological edge over Beijing while being thorough in analyzing AI's risks. Marshall acknowledged AI as a tool to assist, not replace American workers — also backing measures addressing its workforce and energy impacts. Collins has supported federal investment in advanced computing while championing in Maine safeguards against deceptive AI-generated election content. TRUMP-ENDORSED HINSON SECURES IOWA SENATE NOMINATION AS DEMOCRATS EYE GOP SEAT ABF is a conservative AI policy organization that believes that as the technology continues to rapidly develop, American values should be prioritized — protecting children, the economy and national security. The three GOP lawmakers are all Republican nominees for Senate seats in the upcoming midterm elections for their respective states. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Collins, Marshall and Hinson’s offices did not reply to Fox News Digital’s request to comment on the new advertisements and clarify their stances on AI.

title: Prince Harry's first birthday back in Britain unlikely to bring reconciliation with the royal family: experts
description: Royal experts reveal how Meghan Markle and the children will mark Prince Harry's first birthday back in Britain amid unresolved family tensions.
author_name: Brie Stimson, Stephanie Nolasco, Ashley Papa
content: Prince Harry "will likely hear" from King Charles III on his birthday, but "don’t expect some grand royal reunion," according to a royal expert. Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital that the prince would probably have a celebration "similar to what we recently saw from Meghan Markle. Singing and dancing in the kitchen. Party hats for the pups." "I imagine Harry will keep it relatively private with Meghan and the children," she added. "Being back in Britain makes this birthday significant, but I don’t expect some grand royal reunion. There is still far too much unresolved behind the scenes." QUEEN CAMILLA PUTS PAST DIFFERENCES WITH PRINCE HARRY ASIDE AS KING CHARLES SEEKS CLOSER FAMILY TIES: EXPERTS Harry is celebrating his first birthday — he turns 42 on Sept. 15 — since the couple returned to his home country from California after six years late last month. "Harry will likely hear from his father on his birthday," Schofield said. "He will most definitely chat with his uncle, Earl Spencer, and aunts, Lady Sarah McCorquodale and Lady Jane Fellowes." PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'PLAYING IT COOL' AS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE RETURN TO THE UK: EXPERT She added that birthdays "have a way of reminding you who is in your life and who isn’t. Harry may be physically closer to his family, but emotionally, there is still enormous distance there. Moving back to Britain doesn’t automatically repair years of broken trust." Schofield noted that the Spencer side of the family — Princess Diana’s — "seems to be embracing him." title: Trump blasts AI ‘conspiracy’ as Altman, Amodei warn of dangers
description: Sam Altman sounds the alarm over the risks of rapidly advancing AI as tech leaders weigh safety, regulation and the race to develop increasingly powerful models.
content:
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark defended the company’s push for artificial intelligence safeguards, arguing that safety standards are essential to preserving America’s lead over China.
“The worst time to react to an exponential is when it’s too late,” Clark told Fox News’ Bret Baier. “We need to get a sensible, common-sense safety framework in place.”
Clark responded to President Donald Trump’s rejection of industry warnings as a “hoax,” saying America should remain at the forefront while handling the technology carefully.
“What we’re talking about here is the need to have some equivalent set of safety standards for the AI sector,” Clark said, comparing the proposal to standards governing children’s toys.
Clark argued that a major AI accident could trigger sweeping restrictions and ultimately hurt U.S. competition with Beijing.
“How you keep being ahead is you make sure that you don’t roll the dice on public safety,” he said.
He also rejected suggestions that Anthropic’s position was motivated by money or a potential public offering, calling that theory “an absurd 4D chess move.”
Clark urged Trump to raise AI safety during talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“This is not a scared moment,” he said. “This is a moment to use our agency as people to decide the future we want.”

title: US Air Force colonel shot down over Iran recounts 'modern-day miracle'
description: Follow live updates on the U.S.-Iran conflict as an Air Force colonel recounts surviving after being shot down over Iran, alongside the latest developments from the Strait of Hormuz and across the Middle East.
content:
Iran’s top security official warned Washington on Monday that Tehran will not enter negotiations with the United States until its demands are met, stating that any damage control would not avert escalating regional tensions.
“Don’t get distracted by the US president’s mixed signals—from ‘no negotiations’ to ‘we’re ready to talk,’” Mohsen Rezaei wrote in a post on X .
“The stakes around oil and the straits have changed. Damage control won’t stop what’s coming,” he added.
“No talks until Iran’s conditions are met. Period!”
Rezaei’s remarks came after President Donald Trump said Monday on Truth Social that Iran wants to make a deal, but that he would determine whether the U.S. will choose to engage or not.

title: Houthis cut off key Saudi oil route as US hammers Iranian minelayers
description: Iran claims one person was killed in an attack on one of its trade vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday as conflict escalates in Yemen.
content:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that China’s alleged spying on the U.S. was no different from Washington’s own intelligence-gathering efforts, amid reports that Chinese entities supplied Iran with satellite imagery of the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.
This came before Tehran launched a missile attack on July 17.
“They basically do what we do,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One, before saying President Xi Jinping had “behaved reasonably well.”
“You know what they say? That China spies on us,” Trump said.
“I say you're right, and we spy on them, too,” he added.

title: Trump predicts war with Iran will end 'very soon,' likely after midterms
description: President Donald Trump said he thinks the war with Iran will end “very soon,” likely after the midterms, accusing Tehran of trying to hold out “as long as they can to complicate the election.”
content:
A vessel was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said in a verified warning late Saturday.
UKMTO said the condition of the crew, the extent of any damage and the possible environmental impact were not immediately known.
The maritime security agency said authorities were investigating the incident and advised vessels traveling through the strategic waterway to exercise caution and report suspicious activity.
The warning was reported at 11 p.m. UTC Saturday and issued early Sunday UTC. UKMTO did not identify the vessel or say who may have fired the projectile.

title: Iran pushed Houthis to capture Yemeni Red Sea ports and to attack Saudi Arabia
description: President Donald Trump says "I don't believe in the word regret," claiming if he hadn't launched missile strikes on Iran, the country would obtain a nuclear weapon. Yemeni and Iranian government officials reveal that Iranian officials pushed Houthi rebels in Yemen to capture key Red Sea ports as Saudi Arabia launches strikes on Houthi targets.
content:
The State Department's Rewards for Justice program on Friday announced rewards of up to $10 million for information leading to several senior al-Qaeda leaders the U.S. says are based in Iran.
The announcement, released on the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks , names Sayf al-Adl, Abd al-Rahman al-Maghrebi and Yasin al-Suri among those sought.
"These individuals are senior leaders within al-Qaida, which utilizes Iran as a safe haven to execute violent attacks against the United States and its allies," the Rewards for Justice program said in a post on X.
The agency said anyone with information on the men can submit tips through its secure reporting channels and may be eligible for monetary rewards and relocation assistance.
The announcement comes as the Trump administration continues to increase pressure on Iran through military operations, sanctions and efforts to target the country's financial and energy networks.

title: America remembers 9/11 as 25th anniversary ceremonies unfold
description: Follow live updates as America commemorates the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. President Donald Trump and other leaders are participating in memorial events across the country.
content:
American flags honoring the 2,977 people killed in the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks were defaced with pro-Palestinian messages at California State University, Stanislaus, according to Young America’s Foundation.
Students participating in YAF’s annual 9/11: Never Forget Project planted 2,977 flags on campus Thursday night, one for each victim of the attacks. The vandalism was discovered Friday morning, on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 , and a police report was filed, according to the organization.
Photos shared with Fox News Digital show flags marked with messages including “FREE PALESTINE” and “BLOW BACK,” while other flags appear pulled from the ground or damaged.
“Defacing a memorial honoring 2,977 innocent Americans is disgraceful,” YAF said in a statement. “Students should not have to fear vandalism or intimidation for honoring 9/11.”
The group added: “Twenty-five years later, we will not be bullied into silence, and we will never forget.”
YAF launched its Never Forget Project in 2003, organizing memorial flag displays and other commemorations on campuses around the country. The organization says more than 14.7 million flags have been planted through the initiative since its creation.
An American flag marked with the words “FREE Palestine” is seen among a 9/11 memorial display at California State University, Stanislaus, on Sept. 11, 2026. The Young America’s Foundation said 2,977 flags were placed on campus to honor each person killed in the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. (Courtesy YAF)

title: GOP concludes night 2 of the Midterm Convention, Trump's sendoff speech
description: President Donald Trump delivered a keynote address concluding night two of the GOP's Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, on Thursday.
content:
Facing declining approval ratings and economic pessimism, President Donald Trump declared during his Thursday night convention speech that he has delivered on every campaign promise he made.
“But less than two years ago, the American people gave us a mandate to save America. And in 19 months, I've delivered on every single promise I made,” Trump said.
“We delivered the largest tax cuts in American history, the largest regulation cuts in American history, the largest investment in our military in the history of our country and made America the energy and military superpower of the world,” he continued. “I built almost 2,000 miles of wall and created the strongest, most secure border that America has ever seen. And it was just announced, you saw that, that we achieved the lowest level of violent crime in 125 years, since the year 1900.”
Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act was the sixth-largest tax cut in U.S. history since 1940 when measured as a share of the economy, according to the Tax Foundation.
Trump’s claim about crime also requires context. FBI data show that the violent crime rate recorded its largest year-over-year decline since national estimates began in 1936. The murder rate fell to 4.1 per 100,000 people, tying 1955 and 1956 for the lowest rate in the FBI’s national estimates.

title: Iran's IRGC joins fight on ground in Yemen as war escalation sends oil above $100
description: Hundreds of Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps officers are reported to be operating alongside Houthi forces in Yemen as escalating threats to Red Sea shipping push oil prices past $100 per barrel amid intensifying maritime tensions.
content:
The war in Yemen has entered "a new and more dangerous phase," the United Nations special envoy for the country warned the U.N. Security Council on Thursday and amid reports that Iranian military officers are now operating alongside Houthi forces on the ground.
Hans Grundberg’s comments followed reports that Houthi rebels had seized the Red Sea port city of Mocha, which sits roughly 45 miles north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources also told Reuters that the Houthi advance down the coast this week had direct guidance from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
U.S. officials believe hundreds of IRGC officers are currently inside Yemen, working alongside the Houthis to help close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, CNN reported Thursday.
Officials also told the network that more than 100 U.S. military advisers are said to be on the ground in Saudi Arabia assisting the kingdom as Tehran steps up efforts to support Houthi attacks.

title: Trump delivers keynote speech to conclude Day 1 of Republican midterm convention I Live Updates
description: The first day of the GOP midterm convention wraps up with a speech by President Donald Trump. Republicans will return to the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas, tomorrow for the second day of the event.
content:
DALLAS — A rogue Senate Democrat toying with the idea of leaving his party drew a hard line in the sand after making a surprise appearance at the GOP’s Trump-centric convention.
Sen. John Fetterman , D-Pa., has been welcomed with open arms by Republicans to join the party after he floated leaving his own caucus and spurred further speculation that he would jump ship after dropping a video introducing his colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention on Wednesday.
But in a statement to Fox News Digital, the progressive-turned-centrist said that he wasn’t turning his back on the Democratic Party, even as the knives have come out to cut him loose from the Senate.
"My remarks introduced Dave McCormick as a great American and friend. We are in different parties, but we are both Team PA," Fetterman said. "We have delivered hundreds of millions of dollars back to Pennsylvania, fought for improved transportation and affordable housing, and the Steel Way of Life."
"I’m a lifelong Democrat who votes overwhelmingly with my party — and should the Senate flip in November, I will still be the 51st vote that I ran on," he continued.
Fetterman started his career in the Senate after besting Dr. Mehmet Oz in a tight race for power in 2022, where he clinched a historically thin Democratic majority in 2022 running on a progressive platform.
But since then, he has become a thorn in Democrats’ side and challenged the direction of the party.
Earlier this year, Fetterman warned that if Democrats became more entrenched in anti-Israel policy positions, he would exit the party and has taken jabs at the party’s direction during this midterm election cycle as far-left progressives, like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, have emerged as standard-bearers.
This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News' Alex Miller.

title: Trump says Iran 'can't hold out,' predicts war ends after election as UN watchdog targets regime
description: President Donald Trump predicts the Iran war will end “immediately after the election” as U.S. attacks intensify and the U.N. atomic watchdog refers Tehran to the Security Council over its nuclear activities.
content:
The chairman of the Iranian parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Commission taunted the U.S. military Wednesday, urging American forces to leave the Persian Gulf as tensions with Tehran continue to escalate.
“Iran's navy just sent a clear message: the security and stability of the Persian Gulf are managed by Iran,” Ebrahim Azizi said in a post on X .
“To the remaining forces: Save what's left of your gear and head home while you still can, and focus on defending your own borders!” he warned.

title: US moves to ramp up pressure on Iran at UN as Tehran warns of 'recalibrated' military posture
description: Washington is moving to increase diplomatic pressure on Tehran over its nuclear program as Iran threatens a new Persian Gulf exclusion zone and warns it has “fundamentally recalibrated” its posture toward U.S. warships and bases.
content:
Washington is set to increase diplomatic pressure on Tehran within days with a proposed U.N. resolution demanding that Iran “urgently remedy its non-compliance” and restore access for nuclear inspections, Bloomberg reported Monday.
According to a two-page draft obtained by the outlet, the U.S. is also looking to refer Iran to the U.N. Security Council over its moves to block International Atomic Energy Agency monitoring.
The resolution, backed by European members of the IAEA board, also highlights its support for a "diplomatic solution” and encourages “all parties to constructively engage in diplomacy.”
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei warned Monday that Tehran would retaliate if the U.N. nuclear watchdog adopts the measures.
Baghaei had criticized European nations that were also backing the motion as "irrational," arguing that the war has made nuclear facilities inaccessible, Reuters reported.
IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi confirmed that inspectors are locked out of Iran's nuclear sites, saying the agency has neither “received information from Iran regarding the status of its declared nuclear material or facilities nor had access to any of those facilities to conduct in-field verification activities.”

title: Iran vows 'more painful response' for US, Trump sinking 3 oil tankers in Hormuz Strait
description: U.S. forces struck several Iranian tankers amid the Strait of Hormuz war escalation and has Iran warning of a "faster, heavier and more painful" response. CENTCOM said one vessel sank. Oil Prices and gas costs climbed as the Trump administration’s pressure campaign.
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu issued a fresh warning to Iran on Sunday, saying Tehran would face a devastating response if it attacks Israel as he vowed to complete the mission of toppling the Iranian regime.
"That regime in Iran, its end is near," Netanyahu said at a government Rosh Hashanah toast in Jerusalem, according to a translation from Hebrew. "It is weak. It is fighting for its life. It is faltering. There is another mission to complete, and we are determined to achieve it.
"This will permanently change the face of the Middle East and the history of our people. We know we are determined to do it, and we know we are capable of doing it."
Israel is “stronger than ever,” he hailed, claiming the military campaign, carried out with U.S. support, has removed the threat posed by Iran’s nuclear program and ballistic missiles.
"We are determined to defend ourselves," Netanyahu continued. "We are determined to strike our enemies. They are not attacking us. Iran is refraining from doing so, and it knows why.
"Of course, it could make the mistake of attacking us. If it does, it will suffer a blow beyond anything it can even imagine."
Netanyahu’s remarks came as he praised Israeli forces and security services for ongoing operations in Lebanon, Gaza and the West Bank, and told his enemies: “Do not mess with us.”
Fox News' Yonat Friling contributed to this report.

title: US forces target 3 Iranian oil tankers in response to IRGC missile attack
description: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper issued a warning to Tehran on Saturday after a U.S. aircraft carrier and destroyer "evaded multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks." U.S. ships are enforcing an Iranian port blockade during Operation Epic Fury.
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Saturday that Israel has completed "80-90%" of its campaign against Iran's nuclear threat but argued more action is still needed.
In an interview with i24NEWS, Netanyahu said Iran's nuclear ambitions had posed an existential threat to Israel.
"We have done 80-90% of the work. We need to complete what remains," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu also said Israel's military retains the ability to carry out additional operations against Iran, saying Israeli pilots "were there and can be there at any moment."
He added that his goal has been to confront Iran directly after targeting its regional proxy network, describing Tehran as "the head of the octopus."

title: Vance says Trump, US military have prevented ‘energy crisis’ during Iran war
description: Vice President JD Vance said the U.S. military protecting ships is the reason “why we have not had a worldwide energy crisis” during the war against Iran, as Tehran continues to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
content:
President Donald Trump said Friday that new pipelines and overland transportation routes across the Middle East could reduce the world's reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, arguing the strategic waterway is becoming less critical to global energy supplies.
"A lot of alternatives are being made to the Hormuz Strait. The Hormuz Strait is not what it used to be," Trump told reporters after signing executive orders at the White House.
Trump said new pipelines are being developed across the region to move oil without relying on the strait and pointed to an overland route through Syria that he said is already being used by trucks transporting crude.
"Iran is going to end up, if they don't get smart, really smart, with a Hormuz Strait that's not very necessary anymore," Trump said.
His comments come as governments and energy companies explore alternative export routes that could bypass the strategic waterway amid ongoing tensions with Iran.

title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial ends in mistrial after jury deadlock
description: A mistrial was declared in the Lindsay Clancy murder case after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict following seven days of deliberations.
content:
Judge William Sullivan ordered the names of jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial impounded for 14 days following Friday’s mistrial, citing concerns about their safety amid intense public attention surrounding the case.
Sullivan noted that the trial attracted “significant and divisive attention” in Massachusetts, nationally and internationally, and pointed to extensive commentary about the case across social media platforms.
The judge also cited an incident in which an individual was arrested and charged after allegedly “surreptitiously video recording the jurors leaving the court.”
“The Supreme Judicial Court has recognized that the safety of jurors is crucial to the fair functioning of the judicial system,” Sullivan wrote, adding that the justice system owes jurors “the highest degree of vigilance for their personal safety.”
The order prevents the release of the list identifying the empaneled jurors but does not prohibit individual jurors from publicly identifying themselves or speaking about their jury service.
The order is set to expire 14 days after its Sept. 4 issuance unless the court extends it for good cause.

title: Iran attacks Kuwait with missiles and drones after US strikes
description: Iran fired missiles and drones at Kuwait in retaliation for U.S. strikes on Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in the week.
content:
The Israeli military said Thursday it has established operational control of the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon following an offensive against Hezbollah positions.
The Israel Defense Forces said troops secured the area through ambushes, mortar fire, grenades and drone strikes. It said Hezbollah's Badr Unit built two tunnel complexes at the site with Iranian funding and planning and used them to direct attacks against Israel over recent decades.
An Israeli military official said forces targeted tunnel entrances during the operation but found no Iranian advisers or officers inside.
The announcement came hours after Reuters reported that Iran warned Washington a full-scale Israeli offensive on the Ali al-Taher ridge would trigger a large-scale Iranian response.
The ridge has been one of the most strategically contested areas in the Israel-Hezbollah conflict because of its elevated position overlooking southern Lebanon.

title: Lindsay Clancy jury deliberates a 6th day, one deadlock report from a possible mistrial
description: The jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial returns for a sixth day of deliberations after twice reporting it was deadlocked. If jurors again say they cannot agree, the case could end in a mistrial.
content:
Lindsay Clancy’s defense attorney revealed new details about a jury note Thursday as deliberations ended for a sixth day without a verdict.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington revealed the contents of the note while leaving court, telling reporters it raised concerns about how the lone juror was approaching the case.
“When a note that the judge already has says that there are 11 jurors that have made a decision and one juror will not apply reasonable [doubt]...” Reddington said.
Fox News host Will Cain discussed the development on “The Will Cain Show,” highlighting the significance of the jury’s message to the judge.

title: Trump expresses confidence after US military carries out strikes on Iran
description: The U.S. and Iran have spent the previous three days trading strikes, marking the end of roughly a month of relative calm during which the White House had sought to focus almost exclusively on economic pressure. Despite the flareup, President Donald Trump said Tuesday that "I like our position much better now."
content:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the U.S. is prepared to strike Iran again at any time, hours after U.S. forces intercepted several retaliatory Iranian attacks that Trump downplayed as a “love tap.”
“It was a very heavy attack last night, and we’re prepared to do another one anytime we want,” Trump said.
Trump said the U.S. “blew up much more than their radars,” touting America’s advanced defense systems.
“We have technology that's incredible. Nobody has technology like we have. So, we hit them hard last night, very hard. They gave a little love tap, but we hit them very hard,” Trump said.
“We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the Strait of Hormuz, some defensive, some offensive.”

title: Deadlocked Lindsay Clancy jury sent home on 5th day after rare instruction from judge
description: The Lindsay Clancy jury was sent home without a verdict after five days of deliberations. Jurors will return Thursday after receiving a rare Tuey-Rodriguez charge.
content:
Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney says he is ready to retry her murder case almost immediately if the jury's deadlock ends in a mistrial.
"I'd try it next week," Kevin Reddington told reporters outside court. "I have some motions to file. If they come back with a verdict, we'll see what it is. If they don't, I am ready to try it next week." He said the prosecution would "absolutely" pursue first-degree murder again.
Reddington said one reason he wants to move fast is that his lead expert, forensic psychiatrist Dr. Phillip Resnick, remains "alive, well, anxious, and more than willing to help us out again." He also said prosecutors would not get another chance to evaluate Clancy, arguing that after nearly four years, "she's got false memories in her head... there's no way they're getting the doctor anywhere near her."
The comments came as the jury of nine women and three men remained deadlocked. No mistrial has been declared, and jurors are set to continue deliberating.
Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan. She does not dispute killing them but says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

title: Iran launches retaliation after US strikes on IRGC targets across Iran
description: A senior U.S. official said all American personnel are accounted for and most Iranian missiles were intercepted, with no major damage reported at U.S. bases.
content:
All American personnel are accounted for after Iran’s retaliatory attacks, and the U.S. intercepted “the majority of” missiles fired by Tehran, a senior U.S. official told Fox News.
Most of the missiles and drones Iran launched were headed toward Jordan before being shot down, the U.S. official said. The official added that there has been no major damage to any U.S. bases in the Middle East.
Asked who authorized continued Iranian attacks on commercial ships, the official said Iran’s command-and-control structure is not centralized and it remains unclear who within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is alive or dead.
Fox News' Liz Friden contributed to this report.

title: Lindsay Clancy's future rests with jurors as deliberations stretch to a 4th day
description: The jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial returns for a fourth day of deliberations, still weighing whether she was criminally responsible when she killed her three children.
content:
The jury weighing Lindsay Clancy's fate has asked to recess for the day and will return Wednesday to continue deliberating, still without a verdict.
Earlier in the day, the panel of nine women and three men told Judge William Sullivan it had been unable to reach a unanimous decision. Rather than declaring a mistrial, Sullivan sent jurors back to continue their work.
They are weighing whether Clancy was criminally responsible when she strangled her three children, or whether, as the defense argues, she was in the grip of postpartum psychosis and could not appreciate the wrongfulness of her actions or conform her conduct to the law.

title: Retaliation on Kharg Island weighed as US-Iran hostilies reignite
description: U.S.-Iran hostilities are escalating again as President Trump weighs possible retaliation targeting Iran’s Kharg Island, a crucial oil-export hub in the Strait of Hormuz. Follow the latest Iran news today as the conflict risks widening across the Middle East, including Jordan.
content:
President Donald Trump ruled out using a nuclear weapon on Iran, calling it a "stupid question" because the country's military has been defeated.
Trump was taking questions from reporters in the Oval Office when he was asked about the potential escalation of force.
"Well, I would never say. That, but the answer is yes, I ruled out," he said. "I ruled it out there's no reason for it."
"What a stupid question that is," he added. "Actually, here they are. They're totally defeated militarily. So now I defeat him, and now I should use a nuclear weapon on top of them. What a stupid question."

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic remains below normal as US sanctions pressure Iran
description: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei described economic hardships in his country, according to Reuters, after the U.S. Treasury Department launched Operation Economic Outcast against Tehran earlier this week.
content:
Israel will strike Iran again if Tehran attempts to rebuild its nuclear or ballistic missile programs, even if the Islamic Republic reaches a new agreement with the United States, Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen said Saturday, according to Al Jazeera .
“If Iran makes the mistake and tries to renew its nuclear programme or ballistic missile programme, even if there is an agreement with the United States, we will be there to attack,” Cohen told Israeli news outlet Ynet.
Cohen argued that Iran would have obtained nuclear weapons had Israel not acted and said Israeli intelligence assesses that joint U.S.-Israeli strikes set Tehran’s nuclear program back by two to four years.“We have already proven our capabilities,” Cohen said.
The warning comes as Iranian officials signal they are open to renewed diplomacy with Washington while continuing to resist U.S. pressure over the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran’s nuclear ambitions.

title: US-Iran war reaches 6-month mark as Strait of Hormuz tensions remain high
description: The Trump administration’s Operation Epic Fury military campaign against Iran reached the 6-month mark on Friday. Tensions remain high surrounding attacks against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting the flow of oil.
content:
At least 6,000 sailors remain stranded aboard hundreds of ships in the Persian Gulf six months into the war with Iran, according to the United Nations' maritime agency.
The International Maritime Organization said Friday that 19 seafarers have been killed since the conflict began Feb. 28.
At least 70 attacks on international shipping have also been recorded in the Persian Gulf during the war, according to the agency.
The disruption comes as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains well below normal levels despite U.S. efforts to secure the critical waterway.
Before the war, roughly 20% of the world's traded oil and natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz .
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Lindsay Clancy jury enters 2nd day weighing if psychosis drove killings of children
description: Jurors deliberate for a second day Friday in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, weighing the defense's argument that she was in the grip of postpartum psychosis against the prosecution's case that "knew the difference between right and wrong" when she killed her three children.
content:
Speaking outside court, Lindsay Clancy’s attorney, Kevin Reddington, told a swarm of media that he could not predict how long jurors would take to reach a verdict in her murder trial.
The five-week proceeding included roughly 290 pieces of evidence, he told reporters.
Asked whether he felt confident, Reddington replied, “I’m never confident,” adding that he had “no idea” what the jury would do.
“They worked hard. It’s been a long trial, and I have faith in the jury system,” he said.
Reddington was also asked how Clancy was feeling as she headed into the weekend. “Nervous, scared, beat down as usual,” he said.

title: Oil prices remain low; Strait of Hormuz at center of Iran, Oman negotiations
description: Crude oil prices hovered near $82 Thursday despite a second commercial vessel incurring an attack in the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran and Oman work towards a deal to establish fees in the waterway
content:
Reports of a potential plot to assassinate President Donald Trump’s youngest son, Barron Trump, were dismissed as a lie on Thursday by Iran’s top security official.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, made the comments during an interview broadcast by Lebanon’s Al-Manar TV, Iran International reported.
Rezaei’s remarks followed a video aired by Iranian state television that discussed an alleged plot against Barron Trump , 20. The video also said he was being monitored and that a $10 million bounty had been placed on his life.
The Secret Service said Tuesday it was aware of the video and was investigating anything that could be perceived as a threat against people under its protection, Reuters reported.

title: Lindsay Clancy trial: Closing arguments Thursday as case goes to the jury
description: Closing arguments are set for Thursday in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial before jurors deliberate on whether she was criminally responsible for her children's deaths. Clancy admitted to killing her three kids, but argues she had postpartum psychosis.
content:
Lindsay Clancy’s defense attorney, Kevin Reddington , was swarmed by media and supporters as he left court following the first day of jury deliberations.
Fox News correspondent Bryan Llenas asked Reddington if he had any idea how long it would take for a verdict. Reddington replied that he had “no way of knowing,” pointing to the volume of evidence, the time spent on the case and the numerous exhibits.
He also praised the jurors, describing them as attentive and hardworking throughout the trial.
When another reporter asked whether everyone could still be at the courthouse Monday, Reddington simply answered, “Don’t know.”

title: Strait of Hormuz deal inches closer as oil prices dip; US commits to Tehran sanctions
description: Oil prices have dipped to a two-week low after Iran and Oman announced Tuesday the possibility of a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States is still pressing forward with its "Economic D-Day" against Tehran.
content:
Azerbaijan is having to navigate a sensitive security environment, dominated by Iran to its south, The Jerusalem Post reported Wednesday.
Despite Baku’s official neutrality, the South Caucasus nation faces vulnerability as Tehran views it with suspicion over its reliance on Israeli weapons—a tension that escalated when Iranian drones struck the Nakhchivan exclave along their shared border in March.
One drone hit the passenger terminal at Nakhchivan International Airport, and another fell near a school in the nearby village of Shakarabad on March 5.
Simultaneously, Baku has to balance its ties with Turkey, economic relations with Russia, and ongoing peace efforts with Armenia, the outlet said.
International law and security researcher Farid Shukurlu told the Jerusalem Post the tension stems from Tehran rather than the public: “Even though Azerbaijan's position was formally neutrality, the country was still targeted by the IRGC in the Nakhchivan enclave.”
Shukurlu also said, “The military cooperation between Azerbaijan and Israel is at an all-time high.”

title: Lindsay Clancy trial: FBI psychiatrist who rejected her ‘voice’ account to face cross-examination
description: FBI psychiatrist Gregory Saathoff, who doesn’t believe a voice drove Lindsay Clancy to kill her children, faces cross-examination Wednesday as the prosecution wraps rebuttal.
content:
Lindsay Clancy’s attorney, Kevin Reddington, said as he left the courthouse on Wednesday that he was hoping for the best as they prepare for closing arguments and jury deliberations on Thursday.
He said he hopes to convey on Thursday that Clancy is “just such a marvelous, sweet, innocent person. She's just amazing and so strong and just trying so hard to get up from.”
Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan. She does not dispute killing them but says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.
Prosecutors contend the evidence shows that she planned the killings and knew what she was doing.
The jury will also be able to consider a lesser charge of manslaughter, which Reddington called a “positive development.”
Support for Clancy has been a surprise, he said: “I don't think anybody expected that it would strike such a chord.”

title: Dolly Parton’s cause of death revealed as tributes pour in
description: Dolly Parton is remembered by family, fans and stars including Miley Cyrus as tributes celebrate the “Jolene” and "I Will Always Love You" singer’s music, philanthropy and remarkable life.
content:
Sylvester Stallone remembered Dolly Parton as a brilliant, beloved force of nature — and the fearless co-star who laughed after they were thrown from a horse.
In an emotional tribute following Parton’s death, Stallone recalled riding a Tennessee Walking Horse with the country icon during a break from filming “Rhinestone.”
“I just heard that Dolly Parton passed away, and this strikes me very hard, because I felt she was a brilliant woman, so outgoing, so nice,” Stallone said. “She would come onto the set and say, ‘Hi, y’all’ to every one of the crew members. Everyone loved her, and I don’t think people realize what a brilliant mind she had. She was just incredible. I used to call her ‘the Pioneer Woman’ that could do everything to survive. And she did.”
Stallone recalled a "crazy story" while filming "Rhinestone."
“We were down in Tennessee filming, and when we had a little time off, they took us to a horse farm,” he recalled. “And down there they bred these Tennessee Walking Horses, that high-stepping, very, very difficult horse to ride if you don’t know what you’re doing.”
The owner put Stallone and Parton together on his “favorite gray stallion."
“I said, ‘Is this horse used to like, double-decker?’ I don’t get it, you know. And he goes, ‘No problem.’ ”
“This thing was gigantic. It’s like riding a building,” he recalled. “So I said, ‘Dolly, you okay?’ [She replied] ‘Sure am, honey. Go ahead.’ So I kicked the horse, and it starts moving. Prancing.”
Stallone clarified that he's ridden horses his entire life, but the walking horses are a different experience. “They’re not like regular horse hooves. It’s like being on stilts,” he said.
“It sounds beautiful," Stallone recalled. "We look glamorous up there. And then the horse stubs its toe. It trips, and then we start to roll forward. Oh, no. It’s like everything’s going in slow motion and Dolly’s going, ‘Are we falling?’ I go, ‘We are falling.’ ”
“This horse rolled all the way down," the actor added. "And we cascaded off of it and landed in the grass. And the horse rolled beside us. Oh my God, we would have been a couple of pancakes.”
“She got up laughing and goes, ‘Let’s do that again,’” he recalled with a laugh. “So being macho I said, ‘Of course… I was just waiting for you to ask.’"
“I miss you Dolly," Stallone ended his video. "I love you. Sad.”
Dolly Parton and Sylvester Stallone on the set of "Rhinestone." (Getty Images)
Co-stars Dolly Parton and Sylvester Stallone at the "Rhinestone" premiere. (Getty Images)

title: Oil tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Iran claims plan to shoulder Trump sanctions
description: Iranian leaders claim President Donald Trump's "Economic D-Day" will result in "another defeat" for the U.S. on Tuesday, saying Tehran has a "two-year plan" to manage the sanctions.
content:
Washington is not expected to launch further strikes against Iran for now unless Tehran attacks first, Axios reported Tuesday, citing U.S. officials.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio has recently told some foreign counterparts that the current posture would stay in place "for the time being," the outlet said.
One official, however, said Rubio did not rule out strikes if Iran attacks first.
A second official told Axios the posture is expected to remain in place until after the midterm elections, when another military campaign could again be considered.
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Monday he was not ruling out renewed U.S. strikes against Iran during the lull in hostilities, The Associated Press reported.
The developments came as the Trump administration ramped up economic pressure on Tehran, including through its blockade of Iranian ports and a new sanctions initiative announced this week by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

title: Lindsay Clancy trial: Expert who alleged 'fabricated' hallucinations resumes testimony
description: Forensic psychologist Kirk Heilbrun, who testified that parts of Lindsay Clancy's account of hearing voices showed "exaggerated or fabricated hallucinations," returns to the stand Tuesday as the prosecution finishes its rebuttal. Closings could come Wednesday.
content:
Testimony Tuesday in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial focused on what her husband did when she disclosed dark thoughts in the months before the killings.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington pressed the prosecution's psychologist, Kirk Heilbrun, on Patrick Clancy's response to his wife saying she was having thoughts of harming the children. Heilbrun disputed the idea that Patrick told her to "power through it," testifying he instead asked follow-up questions "a mental health professional would also ask," including whether she had a plan. Clancy consistently said she did not, Heilbrun testified, describing them as "just thoughts."
Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan. She does not dispute killing them but says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

title: Scott Bessent to unveil unprecedented sanctions against Iran's economy
description: Iran's head of national security warned that any country supporting U.S. sanctions against Tehran would be considered an "act of war."
content:
Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh predicted "another defeat" for the United States, saying Tehran has ways to get around new sanctions imposed by the Trump administration.
“They have done everything they could to test the determination of the Iranian people and the country’s officials, but they have failed every time. It seems they wish to suffer yet another defeat,” Madanizadeh said on state television, the Times of Israel reported.
“We’ve been waiting for these plans for a long time, and the government is and was ready, and has a two-year plan to manage these events,” he added.
Madanizadeh's remarks came after the Trump administration warned other nations to sever economic ties with Iran.
