title: Iran warns of ‘devastating’ response to impending US sanction barrage
description: The U.S. is preparing to intensify economic warfare against Iran as JD Vance says the conflict enters a new phase. Brent crude tops $93 as more commercial vessels use the Omani side of the Strait of Hormuz instead of Iran's preferred northern route.
content:
An Iranian Shiite cleric said the smell of "burned flesh" still lingers near the compound of Iran 's late supreme leader, according to video circulated by Iranian media and shared Friday by Iran International.
"Someone told me that when you go near the Supreme Leader’s compound, you can still smell burned flesh. I went there myself and found it was true — you can still smell burned flesh," the cleric told a nighttime gathering of Islamic Republic supporters in Tehran's Tajrish Square.
The cleric also disputed previous accounts of the scale of the attack on the compound.
“Our leader had a frail body, but contrary to reports that seven or eight bombs were dropped on the site, they hit the Supreme Leader’s compound with 110 bombs and missiles,” he said.
Iran International did not identify the cleric in its X post or provide independent confirmation of his account.

title: Lindsay Clancy trial: Postpartum psychosis expert to testify as defense nears close
description: Follow live updates from Lindsay Clancy's murder trial as the defense is expected to call Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist specializing in postpartum disorders. The prosecution is expected to follow with three rebuttal experts, with closing arguments possible Monday and Tuesday.
content:
Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney said closing arguments are expected Tuesday, after the prosecution finishes its rebuttal case next week.
Kevin Reddington told reporters as he left court that he has finished calling his witnesses. "I'm done with my experts," he said, adding that only the prosecution's two rebuttal witnesses remain. He said the jury had been "very, very focused," and described Clancy as "surprised and emotional" over the crowds that gathered in her support.
Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan. She does not dispute killing them but says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

title: Trump sounds alarm on ‘crazy’ Iran, says regime would use nuclear weapon ‘without question’
description: President Donald Trump said preventing Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon remains the central objective of the U.S. campaign as senior Iranian officials pushed back against Washington's latest economic pressure.
content:
Ukraine’s war with Russia and Israel’s conflict with Iran are part of the same broader fight, with Iranian weapons linking the two battlefields, Ukraine’s ambassador to Israel said Tuesday.
Speaking to The Jerusalem Post ahead of Ukraine’s Independence Day, Ambassador Yevgen Korniychuk pointed to Russia’s use of Iranian attack drones as evidence of cooperation between Moscow and Tehran and a direct link between the threats facing Ukraine and Israel.
“We have been feeling more and more like we’ve been fighting against the same axis of evil,” Korniychuk said. “You guys are against Iran, and we are against Russia," he told the outlet.
“We’ve been shot by the same Iranian-made drones that are currently being improved substantially by the Russians ,” he said.
“So we feel that we’ve been fighting against the same enemy in different corners of the same battlefield.”

title: Lindsay Clancy trial Day 16: Defense expected to rest as murder case nears closing arguments
description: Follow live updates from Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial as her defense is expected to rest its case Wednesday. Prosecutors are set to call rebuttal witnesses, with closing arguments scheduled for Monday.
content:
Prosecutors on Monday rested their case after building an alleged portrait of the killings being deliberate and methodical, which they anchored with digital forensic evidence that showed Lindsay Clancy moving through her home and searching the web in the hours surrounding her children's deaths.
The murder trial of Lindsay Clancy moved deeper into the defense's case this week as her attorney worked to convince jurors that she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis when she killed her three kids, and shouldn't be held criminally responsible.
On Thursday, jurors were questioned to make sure supporters of Lindsay Clancy outside the courthouse didn't interfere or speak with them. Many who have gathered in pink say the show of support is not an endorsement of what happened, but a stand for maternal mental health awareness and for mothers suffering from postpartum conditions.
Lindsay Clancy also told her mother she was "doing better" in the weeks beforehand.
The defense then began calling their witnesses, which included family members, a forensic psychologist, and a hospital chaplain while the two sides clashed over a central question to the case: Lindsay Clancy's state of mind.
Dr. Paul Zeizel, a forensic psychologist testifying for the defense, said he administered a psychopathy checklist and a mental-status exam and found no evidence of antisocial personality disorder, concluding that Clancy is not a sociopath. He portrayed a woman whose psychotic symptoms grew more severe in the weeks leading up to the killings, among them a belief that others could hear her thoughts and voices directing her to harm herself.
Susan Clancy, Lindsay's mother-in-law, said on Tuesday that she had concerns about Lindsay's mental health during the 2022 holiday season, but described her as a "wonderful mother."
"Lindsay was struggling. We were all very concerned," Susan Clancy said. "She was very nurturing, very loving."
"She was begging for help," Susan Clancy added.

title: Trump unleashes ‘economic D-Day’ on Iran, warns nations against throwing Tehran a lifeline
description: President Donald Trump cautioned that helping Tehran withstand U.S. pressure could carry major consequences as he moves to further isolate the Iranian regime following the expiration of a U.S.-Iran ceasefire this week.
content:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced what he called the “most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country,” threatening sweeping consequences for nations and businesses that provide Iran with an economic lifeline as he seeks to further isolate Tehran.
“No one has given the Islamic Republic of Iran a greater opportunity to make a Deal than me,” Trump said in a post shared on X.
“TRAGICALLY, for them, they have failed to take it. Therefore, today, I am announcing the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY!”
“This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale,” Trump said, claiming Iran’s navy is gone, its air force destroyed, its military factories reduced to rubble, its currency worthless and the country “hanging by a thread.”
Trump also warned that “ANY country” allowing its financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities to provide “any type of lifeline to Iran” would face “TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences.”
“Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — it all needs to stop NOW,” he said.
“You know who you are,” Trump added, calling the campaign an “ECONOMIC D-DAY” and urging U.S. allies to help “isolate, and defeat, the Iran threat.”
Trump said Iran’s leaders are “on the ropes” and that the measures would “cripple them and their ability to project terror worldwide.”
“IRAN WILL NEVER HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON,” he said.

title: Lindsay Clancy trial day 16: Psychologist says suicide hotline rejected her
description: Lindsay Clancy's defense expert testified Wednesday that she repeatedly sought help in the weeks before she killed her three children, including calling a suicide hotline that turned her away because she did not have a plan to harm herself. The testimony is central to the defense's argument that Lindsay Clancy was suffering from postpartum psychosis and is not criminally responsible. The judge is also weighing whether a former McLean Hospital employee will be allowed to testify.
content:
Judge William Sullivan ended court early on Wednesday in the Lindsay Clancy trial , stating there was an "unforeseen circumstance."
"Due to some an unforeseen circumstance. We're going to, excuse you until tomorrow morning. This is, not something we saw coming, but you're not to speculate about what it is. You're not to hold it against either side. it's just something that we have to deal with. All right. And so I'm going to excuse you until tomorrow morning," Sullivan said

title: Oil prices rise as resolution to Iran war remains unclear following MOU expiration
description: Oil prices have been elevated since Monday afternoon, after it became clear the United States and Iran had not negotiated a lasting peace deal. The memorandum of understanding signed by the two countries had called for a deal to be in place by now.
content:
The U.S. military has the firepower to defeat any threat, a top Pentagon official said Tuesday and as Washington focuses on replenishing weapons stockpiles amid the Iran war and expanding America’s arsenal.
“President Trump, Secretary Hegseth, Chairman Caine have all stated clearly, we are ready,” Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment Michael Duffey said on “ Special Report ”.
“The U.S. military can defeat any threat at the time and place of our choosing, and I think that remains true today,” Duffey added.
Duffey’s comments come amid increased scrutiny of U.S. weapons inventories as conflicts abroad, including the war with Iran, increase demand for missiles and other munitions.
“ President Trump , Secretary Hegseth are committed to rebuilding the military, revitalizing the defense industrial base, so that now and for the future we will have the weapons that we need,” he said.
Duffey said the administration nevertheless wants to accelerate production and build larger reserves.
“We would always like to have more weapons than we have right now, which is why we are so focused on engaging with our industrial partners, entering these deals, and ensuring that we ramp the production of these key missiles as quickly as possible.”
“We're making up for lost time. The Biden administration did not deliver. They did not focus on developing the industrial base that we need in order to ensure that we have munitions for the foreseeable future,” he added.

title: Trump says Tehran wants deal, floats US control of Strait of Hormuz, warns Iran ‘in big trouble’
description: President Donald Trump said Iran wants a deal but is unwilling to accept terms he considers necessary, as he suggested declaring the Strait of Hormuz U.S. territory. Jared Kushner said Trump remains committed to achieving what others think is impossible in the Middle East after high-level talks to advance Trump’s Gaza peace plan.
content:
President Donald Trump declared Monday that Tehran wants a deal with Washington but is unwilling to accept necessary terms.
“They want to make a deal, but they're not going to make the kind of a deal that I feel is necessary,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
“Look, we're in there for one reason” he said before clarifying that Iran “cannot have a nuclear weapon”.
“You understand that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, and they won't have a nuclear weapon.
“And right now, them building one after what we did previously with the B-2 bombers, it’s going to be going to be a long time.
“It's very simple. They can't have a nuclear war.” he added.
The president’s remarks came as a 60-day ceasefire between the United States and Iran ended Monday with both sides standing firm on their positions over Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Tributes pour in for Hayden Panettiere; 'Nashville' star dead at 36
description: Hayden Panettiere, who rose to fame as a child actress before starring in hit movies including “Remember the Titans” and “Bring it On: All or Nothing,” has died at 36. The circumstances surrounding her death were not immediately known.
content:
Hayden Panettiere reflected on life, growth and mortality in the prologue of her memoir, "This Is Me: A Reckoning."
The book, released in May 2026, chronicled Panettiere’s life in the public eye, as well as her struggles with addiction , alcohol and mental health after rising to fame as a teenager.
“I never want to stop evolving and changing for the better, and I’ll forever be a work in progress,” Panettiere wrote. “But one thing I know from my 36 years in the public eye is this: Life is a process that evolves day by day, year by year and — like it or not — you are engaged in a cycle of growth until the moment you take your last breath.”
The passage has taken on a poignant new meaning following the actress’ death on Aug. 16.
Panettiere also detailed entering treatment for the first time in 2015, when her daughter, Kaya, was 4 months old. She described the facility as highly personalized but ultimately disconnected from the realities she would face after leaving.
“It was a hugely expensive facility devoted to one-on-one care,” Panettiere wrote. “Trust me, it’s easier to detox and recover when you’re being treated like a queen, but it was too far from the real world to give me perspective.” Though she left sober and with a diagnosis of postpartum depression, Panettiere said she remained in denial about the severity of her alcohol use.
"The idea that a little liquid could take me down or rule my life seemed impossible for a tough girl like me," she added.
Her first trip to rehab was the start of a new addiction - the medicine given to combat her anxiety.
“I’d walked into rehab addicted to one substance, and I’d walked out, completely dependent on something else," she said.

title: Trump admin tried to make peace with IRGC directly before signing MOU
description: President Donald Trump's peace negotiators reportedly attempted to reach the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps leadership, going around their Iran counterparts and Middle East contacts to try to end the war and battle over the Strait of Hormuz, getting a memorandum of understanding (MOU) that had ultimately failed.
content:
Tehran is more isolated than ever before across the Middle East, with Gulf states aligned against Iran, Navy SEAL veteran Mike Sarraille said Sunday while adding that President Donald Trump now needs time to prepare for the end of the regime.
“He has got Iran where he wants them, with both the blockade, the economic sanctions,” Sarraille said on “Fox Report” Sunday.
“It just comes down to time,” he added before describing how Washington’s measures were “crippling to Iran.”
“You pair it with probably some additional military strikes on their infrastructure, but additionally, what the commentators are missing is diplomatically.
“We are seeing an aligned Middle East that we've not seen before, at least in our lifetimes, you know, with a recent pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, an attack on one is an attack on all, and then also a Red Sea maritime coalition that was signed by 14 Gulf states.”
“So that alignment is ultimately going to be the biggest strategic miscalculation by Iran. They've aligned the entire region against them.
“They are further isolated. Again, we just have to give President Trump time to lay the seeds for what could be the end of days for this regime.”
Sarraille’s comments came ahead of Monday’s expiration of the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding signed by Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in June.

title: Iran responds after Trump teases Strait of Hormuz becoming US territory
description: An Iranian official insisted the Strait of Hormuz “will remain Iranian” after President Donald Trump suggested it could become a U.S. territory following Operation Epic Fury.
content:
A 60-day ceasefire agreement between the U.S. and Iran is set to expire Monday as tensions remain high over control of the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran says no decision has been made on when talks with Washington will resume.
Fox News chief correspondent Jonathan Hunt reported Saturday that U.S. Central Command has redirected more than 60 commercial vessels in the strait as the American naval blockade remains in place.
President Donald Trump has repeatedly said the U.S. controls the strategic waterway and on Friday went further, saying, “Pretty soon, I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.”
Iran has rejected those claims. Its deputy foreign minister wrote on X that the strait “cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor by an election speech.”
The June memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran included a 60-day ceasefire that expires Monday, making the deadline the next major test for whether diplomacy can hold.

title: Iran targets tankers in ‘unprovoked attacks’ in Strait of Hormuz, UAE says
description: The United Arab Emirates ripped Iran after it attacked two of its ships as they were traveling through the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump has described Iran as “all talk and no action, the bully of the Middle East no longer.”
content:
An Iranian official fired back Friday after President Donald Trump said he may eventually declare the Strait of Hormuz “territory of the United States,” insisting Tehran will continue enforcing its blockade of the strategic waterway.
“The Strait of Hormuz cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor by an election speech,” Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi wrote on X. “Iran neither fears threats nor cowers before displays of power.”
Gharibabadi then claimed the U.S. has suffered “strategic and heavy defeats” and asserted that “the Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian.”
“This strait will only be closed and opened under Iran’s command,” he continued, adding that Tehran would maintain the blockade until the U.S. accepts what he characterized as the “reality of defeat.”
Trump said during remarks in Nassau County, New York, earlier Friday that after Iran is defeated, “pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States,” while touting the U.S. blockade and saying no ships pass through unless Washington allows it.
The Islamic Republic of Iran’s Foreign Ministry has previously publicly identified Gharibabadi’s X account among its official government accounts.

title: Iran talks tough to US, says Trump 'miscalculated' on Strait of Hormuz
description: Following President Donald Trump's claim Wednesday that the U.S. has "total control over the Strait of Hormuz," Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said the president "has long miscalculated due to intelligence failures."
content:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) on Thursday pushed back on reports about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln during its deployment to the Middle East, denying claims that sailors had died in a brawl or that the carrier had experienced a spike in suicidal ideation.
“CLAIM: Over the past 48 hours, multiple media outlets have reported several false claims related to USS Abraham Lincoln's (CVN 72) deployment to the Middle East,” CENTCOM said in a statement. “One report alleged seven Sailors died in a brawl aboard the aircraft carrier and others have recently suggested a spike in suicidal ideations.”
"These reports are FALSE," CENTCOM said.
The command pointed to the carrier's crew reenlistment rate, saying the USS Abraham Lincoln has "maintained among the highest crew reenlistment rates (84.4%) of all aircraft carriers in the U.S. Navy."
“The Sailors and Marines of the Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group remain resilient and resolved after more than 260 days at sea, 10,000 aircraft flights, and 1.5 million pounds of ordnance expended,” CENTCOM said.
"No service members aboard the aircraft carrier have died, and the one Sailor who fell overboard Aug. 3 was quickly and safely recovered," the statement continued. "The rampant misreporting on Abraham Lincoln's historic deployment is a disservice to our men and women in uniform and their loved ones."
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth also addressed reports about conditions aboard the aircraft carrier Thursday, saying they had been "completely misrepresented."
"We make sure every ship, every crew, every captain has everything we can provide them at every single moment," Hegseth told reporters during a visit to Panama. "Some deployments are longer than others, and I have more respect and gratitude for those sailors than anybody. What they do in those high seas in those austere conditions with less port calls, it's incredible."

title: Iran defies Trump, declares Strait of Hormuz blocked after president claims US has ‘total control'
description: Tehran insists the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked and will not reopen until its conditions are met, directly challenging President Donald Trump’s declaration that the U.S. has “total control” of the waterway and as the MOU deadline approaches.
content:
Tehran is likely to become more aggressive in the coming days as a new phase approaches, Fox News senior strategic analyst and retired Gen. Jack Keane warned Wednesday, arguing that Iran may believe President Donald Trump will be reluctant to take military action ahead of the midterm elections.
“When they look at this phase here, they see the midterms coming. My gut feel is that they're likely going to get more aggressive because they don't believe the president will do much prior to the midterms in terms of military actions,” Keane said on Fox News' "Special Report."
“But they have miscalculated with him time and time again, and he is totally capable of shutting them down once and for all and crushing him with the ability that he has literally at his fingertips.”
“We have more capability in the region now than we had on Feb. 28, and it all is ready. So that leverage is there. It's his decision to be sure,” he warned.
Keane’s warning came as Trump said Tuesday that the United States has “total” control over the Strait of Hormuz, as Washington and Tehran remain at an impasse over arrangements for reopening the vital waterway.
An Iranian source also told Reuters Wednesday that there were no talks with Washington on extending the June interim agreement, saying Tehran saw “nothing to extend,” with the 60-day negotiating period outlined in the memorandum of understanding fast approaching its Aug. 17 deadline.

title: Crowley defeats socialist Hong in Wisconsin Democratic governor primary
description: David Crowley defeated democratic socialist Francesca Hong in Wisconsin’s Democratic governor primary and will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany in November.
content:
Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers described Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, the winner of the Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary, as "the future" of the Democratic Party.
"Tonight's all about @DavidCCrowley. He's earned this win and the accolades. I am so proud of David—he's the future of our Party, and I can't wait for him to be our next governor. For now, we polka. Tomorrow, we're back at work to win. @TomTiffanyWI, we'll see you in November," Evers declared in an early Wednesday morning post on X, referring to U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, the President Donald Trump-backed Republican candidate running for governor.
Evers, who announced last year that he would not seek re-election, endorsed Crowley last month.

title: US Navy opens fire on ship trying to break Iran blockade as Tehran deepens Pakistan ties
description: A U.S. Navy helicopter fired on a Panama-flagged vessel after it attempted to bypass the American blockade of Iranian ports, CENTCOM confirmed Tuesday, as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met with Pakistan’s interior minister in Tehran and pushed for stronger bilateral cooperation.
content:
President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he follows the directions of the Secret Service and U.S. military when it comes to his security, addressing reports that he was moved between aircrafts as part of a security operation last month in Ankara reportedly prompted by an Iranian assassination threat.
“Well, it's only up to the Secret Service. I just follow what they'd like to do,” Trump told reporters after traveling to Geneva, Ohio, for the Freedom 250 Patriot Games.
“So I go by the Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go on a different flight, a different plane, equal safety,” he said.
“But they wanted me to do it, so I do it. I do what they say.”
“I guess there was a threat out there. I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats,” Trump said.
The president also went on to say that any "consequential president has a lot of threats."
"Non consequential presidents don't get threats," he added.
The Washington Post first reported that Trump secretly switched to a military jet after appearing to board the older Air Force One in Turkey after the NATO summit.

title: Trump ‘low keying it’ on Iran tensions as Tehran feels economic squeeze: ‘They have no money’
description: President Donald Trump says the US is ‘only semi-negotiating’ with Iran, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with Oman over new maritime routes through the Strait of Hormuz are in the ‘final stages’
content:
President Donald Trump is signaling he is in no rush to launch new military strikes against Iran, insisting instead that growing economic pressure will push Tehran to negotiate, Axios reported Sunday.
“We are low keying it,” Trump said in an interview with the outlet. “We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”
Trump’s remarks came Sunday as Tehran said that a deal with Oman defining new shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz was in its final stages but reiterated that the waterway would only reopen once the United States met other conditions, Reuters reported.
Trump also told Axios Iran was “in very bad shape” economically and lacked money to pay its troops, arguing that the U.S. naval blockade had further intensified Tehran’s economic crisis.
“It will work out. It always works out. It’s like a chess game,” Trump said.
Meanwhile, Iran’s demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have been sent to the United States, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday, according to state news agency IRNA.

title: Vance details ongoing Iran talks, says US in ‘middle of the game’
description: Vice President JD Vance said the U.S. is currently in the “middle of the game” when it comes to the war against Iran. He added that the Trump administration is applying a "host of tools" to secure the best outcome for Americans.
content:
Iran laid out six demands Saturday for what it called U.S. "behavior correction" before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen, according to the country's state-run IRNA news agency.
Mohammad Baqer Zulqader, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said “until America corrects its behavior, The Strait of Hormuz will not open.”
Zulqader said the U.S. must stop threatening Iran and insulting what he described as the country's sanctities, end military action against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, the Palestinian territories, Yemen and Iraq, and lift the naval blockade.
His remaining demands call for U.S. sea and air forces to withdraw from Iran, compensation for damages from two wars, the removal of sanctions against Iran and the unconditional release of frozen Iranian assets.
The demands come as negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain ongoing. Vice President JD Vance told Fox News earlier Saturday that Iranian officials have told the U.S. they have no plans to toll the critical waterway.
Zulqader also said the Supreme National Security Council would maintain its position in both military and diplomatic talks, according to IRNA.

title: Trump says agreement with Iran to reopen Strait of Hormuz ‘could be soon’
description: President Donald Trump said a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could happen soon as the U.S. military continues enforcing a blockade on Iranian ports and tensions remain high throughout the Middle East.
content:
Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper warned Friday that a potential arrangement giving Iran and Oman roles in administering traffic through the Strait of Hormuz could be a “very bad outcome” for the United States.
Speaking on Fox News' “America Reports,” Esper said reports indicate Tehran and Muscat are nearing an agreement that could divide passage through the strategic waterway, with a northern route into the Persian Gulf and a southern route along Oman’s coast.
“They may or may not charge a fee, but they would administer and control it in one way, shape, or form, which would be a very bad outcome for us,” Esper said.
Esper noted that President Donald Trump has said he is personally involved in negotiations, while Iranian officials have publicly disputed direct U.S. participation.
“I think what we’re waiting for now is to find out, is there a deal between Oman and Iran, and to what degree did the United States play a role or has a role in it,” Esper said.

title: Iran claims it is in 'final stage' of talks to reopen Strait of Hormuz
description: President Donald Trump's administration has rejected claims that the war in Iran has severely depleted America's missile stockpiles.
content:
President Donald Trump said Thursday that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz has not yet been finalized, though he indicated negotiations with Iran are continuing and an agreement could come in the near future.
Asked by a reporter during an Oval Office event whether a deal had been reached, Trump stopped short of declaring a breakthrough.
"Well, I don't want to say it has been," Trump said. "It's sort of open right now."
Trump said the U.S. Navy continues to enforce the blockade around Iran, arguing that military control of the waterway has helped stabilize the situation. At the same time, he cautioned that shipping risks remain because Iran could still deploy naval mines or carry out attacks that would discourage commercial traffic.
"They can always shoot something," Trump said. "They always have something or drop a mine. And if you have one mine sitting out there, you sort of mess things up because people don't want to take their billion-dollar boats and accidentally get hit by a mine."
Despite those concerns, Trump expressed confidence that negotiations are progressing.
"I think we're doing very well," he said. "I'm involved in the negotiation. I think we're doing fine. It could be. It could be soon."
Hours later, as he left a White House event honoring Team USA athletes, Trump offered a similarly optimistic assessment when asked whether there had been any developments.
"Moving along good," he told reporters before departing.

title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz deal could come Wednesday as gas prices stay high
description: President Donald Trump said he held productive "all-day" negotiations with Iran on Tuesday, adding that the country should make a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in a bid to ease oil prices.
content:
President Donald Trump said Wednesday during an event in Las Vegas that Iran sought negotiations after the U.S. prepared what he described as a massive military strike, arguing that sustained military pressure has brought Tehran back to the bargaining table.
Speaking to supporters, Trump said the U.S. was "set for the biggest attack since World War II" before Iranian officials reached out to request talks. "They called me and they said, 'Please don't do it, let's talk,'" Trump said.
Trump said he would prefer a diplomatic resolution over further military action but reiterated that the administration's position has not changed. "I'd rather make a deal because I don't want to kill people," he said. "But Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon."
The comments come as the Trump administration continues negotiations with Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said Tuesday that "a lot of progress" had been made and suggested a deal could be reached as soon as Wednesday or Thursday.
The administration has repeatedly said any agreement with Tehran must ensure Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon, a position Trump again underscored Wednesday as diplomatic efforts continue.

title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate 2026 primary election
description: Abdul El-Sayed has emerged victorious over Rep. Haley Stevens in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary. Results from the 2026 primary elections continue to roll in after voters headed to the polls in Virginia, Kansas, Missouri and Washington.
content:
Abdul El-Sayed challenged Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers to five debates Wednesday.
“Mike, I'm gonna say right here, I know you're gonna say no because you're a coward. Five debates. All right?” he said.
“If you're willing to stand with me and have a conversation, you and I both know that you will wither in front of your own crimes, but I'm gonna make sure Michiganders know about them, because at the time we're done, you are not going to have safe quarter from people holding you accountable to what you've done for them here in Michigan,” he added.
"Five debates. I'm hoping for an answer today,” El-Sayed also said.

title: Trump says Tehran has 'last chance' for deal as negations resume
description: President Donald Trump said the U.S. and Iran were resuming talks, claiming a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and denuclearize Tehran is "imminent.” Iranian officials, however, have denied participating in direct talks with the U.S., saying that they are negotiating with mediators in Oman.
content:
Iran is ramping up political pressure on the United States in a bid to gain leverage, a leading Iran analyst warned Tuesday.
"This is a regime that knows it cannot win an outright battle of conventional capability," Foundation for Defense of Democracies Iran Program Senior Director Behnam Ben Taleblu said on Fox News' "America Reports."
"They're even fighting a battle of wills right now against the Trump administration, both on the battlefield and diplomatically," he added.
"Clearly they have some steel, but this is a regime that has shown us, in word and deed, over the past 47 years, that it will play to the edge and that it will gamble. Unfortunately, we're in a very tough situation right now," Taleblu added.
Taleblu also said no U.S. president has inflicted more damage on the Iranian regime than President Donald Trump , but argued that the administration has recently pulled back from several earlier threats.
"I think eight or nine — and even a newspaper run by Tehran's municipality basically said all of Trump's threats are watered down and that the U.S. is a paper tiger," he said.
"So this is a tough position for U.S. deterrence to be in right now, despite the good track record that the president has had."
Taleblu's remarks came as Qatar said Tuesday that mediators were making progress toward ending the war, although Tehran denied Trump's assertion that talks were already underway.

title: Trump claims Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz is 'imminent'
description: President Donald Trump says a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ensure the denuclearization of Tehran is "imminent" on Monday. Iran has confirmed it is in talks with mediators.
content:
President Donald Trump said Monday that he is giving Iran “every last chance” to reach a deal.
“I want to give them every last chance before decapitation. Very tough to do,” Trump told reporters. “…I'm very proud of the fact that I'll give people a chance. This is a big move to do an attack that big on a country.”
Trump said Iranian officials called him after learning about the planned operation.
“Hopefully they'll come to their senses," Trump added. "So they called me, and they said, 'Please don't attack. We'll make a deal.' That's the real truth. And everyone knows it."
The president said that if “given a chance to let a lot of people live,” that he wants to “give that chance.”
“I'm under no time constraint,” Trump said.

title: Rubio says Iran is confronting a different kind of president with Trump
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News that with President Trump, the regime in Tehran is facing “someone that actually takes action.” Tensions remain high in the Strait of Hormuz and across the region as Iran has been targeting Gulf countries.
content:
President Donald Trump said Saturday the United States will hold off on a planned military strike against Iran as Washington and Tehran work to quickly finalize a deal.
"The U.S.A. is locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
"Despite this, we have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the parameters of a deal has been agreed to," he continued. "This would include the immediate, complete, and total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat."
Trump said he agreed to suspend the military operation while negotiations continue.
"Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," Trump wrote.
The president added that Israel supports the effort to reach an agreement.
"Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE," Trump said.

title: Trump brokers Hamas disarmament deal as Saudi Arabia plans Houthi offensive
description: President Donald Trump announced a deal for Hamas to disarm and Israeli forces to withdraw from Gaza, nine months after a U.S.-brokered ceasefire. While Hamas confirmed the disarmament agreement on Friday, major hurdles, conditions, and long timelines remain to wind down the war and implement Gaza's reconstruction.
content:
Iran is threatening to retaliate against U.S. or Israeli strikes by targeting critical energy infrastructure, according to comments published Friday by Iran’s state-affiliated Tasnim News Agency.
A senior security official told Tasnim that reports in U.S. media about possible American and Israeli attacks on Iranian infrastructure amounted to “a kind of madness,” warning Tehran has prepared “extensive response plans.”
According to Tasnim, the official said those plans include strikes targeting Israeli critical infrastructure and U.S. energy infrastructure across the region, adding Iran’s armed forces have both “the capability and the will” to carry them out.
The threat comes hours after the White House told Fox News Digital that President Donald Trump “is not going to stand by and allow this terrorist behavior to occur” and that “Iran will continue to pay until they come to the table in, what President Trump deems, a meaningful way.”
The White House statement came in response to reports of a possible expansion of U.S. military operations against Iran.

title: Trump declares Hamas to disarm as Saudi military readies for potential Houthi ground offensive
description: President Donald Trump announced a "historic agreement" for the complete disarmament of Hamas, while Saudi Arabia readies for a military campaign against the Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen, with reports pointing to a potential ground offensive.
content:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Thursday that Iran squandered an opportunity to reach a deal with the United States and argued it is time for the U.S. and Israeli militaries to "finish the job" against Tehran.
“The Iranians opened the door to an MOU that could’ve achieved our objectives,” Pence said in a post shared on X before setting the objectives out.
Verified dismantling of the nuclear weapons program
Verified dismantling of the ballistic missile program
Restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz
“They had a shot. They blew it,” he added before stating that it was time to “let the Armed Forces of the United States and Israel finish the job.” he added.

title: Trump launches US airstrikes on Iran after vowing to hit regime 'very hard'
description: The United States conducted airstrikes across Iran, targeting what a U.S. official described as "a very broad target set," after President Donald Trump vowed a forceful response to an attempted ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces in Jordan.
content:
U.S. forces launched fresh strikes against Iran at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday in what U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said was a "powerful response" to Iran's attempted attacks on American military forces in the Middle East .
“U.S. forces began launching strikes against Iran at 8 p.m. ET today,” the command said in a post shared on X.
“The strikes are a powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on U.S. forces based in the Middle East.”
President Donald Trump said earlier that Iran was “going to get a beating” for the attempted overnight missile attack against U.S. forces in Jordan.

title: Fauci's refusal to testify could have big consequences, Rand Paul warns
description: Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., made his ultimate case against Dr. Anthony Fauci during a Capitol Hill hearing on Wednesday after news of Fauci's COVID-era diaries revealed new details about his thoughts on the origins of the virus and his handling of the pandemic.
content:
Sen. Rand Paul , R-Ky., continued his criticism of Dr. Anthony Fauci Wednesday with a series of posts on X after the former top health official repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment during a Senate hearing.
Paul posted that Fauci was "culpable" for COVID-era lockdowns before sharing another graphic claiming Fauci repeated his Fifth Amendment response 111 times during the hearing.
"Throughout today's hearing, Anthony Fauci repeated the following script 111 times," Paul wrote. "And yes, his refusal to testify is grounds for contempt."
In another post, Paul said Fauci was "part of a pandemic buildup and response" that "killed millions and ruined the schooling and businesses of so many."
Paul announced during Wednesday's hearing that he plans to seek a committee vote next week to hold Fauci in contempt after the former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases director repeatedly declined to answer lawmakers' questions. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment throughout the hearing, saying he was acting on the advice of counsel.

title: Sen. Lindsey Graham honored with funeral service, celebration of life in DC
description: The late Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina will get two celebrations of his life in Washington on Tuesday, first in the rotunda of the U.S. Capitol and then at a private funeral service at the National Cathedral.
content:
President Donald Trump paid tribute Tuesday to the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., praising his "towering impact" on American politics while recalling humorous stories that underscored the senator's wit and larger-than-life personality.
Speaking at Graham's funeral at Washington National Cathedral, Trump called the South Carolina Republican "a beloved friend, a devoted brother, a respected statesman, a giant of the United States Senate, and a true American original."
"By the strength of his steadfast convictions, the force of his magnetic personality and the goodness of his noble soul, Lindsey rose from a small town in rural South Carolina ... to become a constant fixture of American politics at the highest level," Trump said. "Nothing of significance happened anywhere in the world without Lindsey Graham having a view on it."
Trump mixed heartfelt praise with stories that drew laughter from mourners. He recounted how Graham joked that the key to running his parents' bar was being "funny enough that people will keep coming back" while also being "tough enough" to thrive, saying those qualities defined Graham's political career. Trump also recalled Graham declining an invitation from Sen. Tim Scott to an 8:30 a.m. prayer breakfast, quipping, "Tim, if Jesus himself comes back before 10 a.m., I ain't going yet."
Calling Graham's influence felt around the world, Trump said it was "a testament to his towering impact" that presidents, prime ministers and other world leaders traveled to Washington to honor the longtime senator. "No matter how high he rose, he never forgot where he came from," Trump said, adding that Graham helped communities across South Carolina while remaining a force on the national and international stage.

title: Trump says US 'winning big time' against Tehran as Netanyahu prepares to unveil new Iran intel
description: President Donald Trump doubled down on his Iran policy, declaring the U.S. is "winning big time" as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu prepares to unveil intelligence that, according to reports, alleges Tehran is expanding its secretive Pickaxe nuclear site while negotiating in bad faith.
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to present President Donald Trump with intelligence alleging Iran is expanding activity at its Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site and is not negotiating in good faith over its nuclear program, according to reports.
According to the New York Post , citing a source in Jerusalem, Netanyahu's team plans to present the intelligence during a meeting with Trump at the White House on Tuesday.
Netanyahu arrived in the United States on Monday evening, according to Israeli media reports.
Trump has recently said the Pickaxe facility remains a concern despite U.S. strikes on Iran's nuclear infrastructure.
Trump and Netanyahu / Chen Mengtong / China News Service / VCG via Getty Images
The president recently said the U.S. would likely target the site "very heavily" and "pretty soon," adding, "There's not a thing they can do about it."
His warning came after The Wall Street Journal reported that Israeli intelligence believes Iran moved thousands of centrifuges into the facility last fall.
Trump said the transfer "may have" occurred but added the United States did not have it "on record."
The Post also reported that Israel plans to present evidence that Tehran is rebuilding its missile and drone programs.

title: US strikes 'on a hold,' as talks, battle for Strait of Hormuz control loom with Iran
description: U.S. strikes have relented for the first time in two weeks as peace negotiations and talks involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz resume, but President Donald Trump's Cabinet remains "locked and loaded" for a resumption of hostilities if Iran balks at surrendering its nuclear weapons aspirations.
content:
Iran issued a second warning to Ukraine on Sunday following what Tehran said was an attack on a vessel in the Caspian Sea.
Iranian officials claimed the attack on July 25 triggered an explosion aboard the vessel, killing one sailor and wounding another.
"Any attack on Iran always comes with a cost, and that remains true today. The U.S. and Israel are well aware of this," Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Iranian Parliament's National Security Commission, said in a post on X .
"Ukraine, too, may soon come to understand that Iran does not let actions go unanswered," he added, warning that the list of those "who have miscalculated continues to increase."
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also blamed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for the attack and said earlier Sunday that the incident "cannot go unanswered."

title: Iran reports first night without new US strikes as Houthis attack Saudi Arabian city
description: The Iran war appears to be spreading to the Arabian peninsula, with the Houthis claiming responsibility for an attack on the Saudi Arabian city of Jizan. Saudi Arabia said it executed a "resolute" and "proportionate" military response.
content:
The White House pushed back Saturday after a New York Times report said President Donald Trump had shelved plans to significantly escalate military operations against Iran, emphasizing that the president continues to keep all options on the table.
“President Trump has always been consistent in saying he prefers a diplomatic solution, but he continues to retain all options if Iran continues terrorist activities in the Strait of Hormuz or against allies,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung told Fox News Digital.
Cheung added that, after “successful sanctions that have crippled Iran’s economy and 13 straight days of strikes against military targets in response to their repeated aggression, it would be wise for Iran to work towards a negotiated deal. Otherwise, they know what will happen.”
The statement comes in response to a New York Times report that Trump has, for now, held off on a broader military campaign against Iran after advisors raised concerns about expanding the conflict.

title: President Donald Trump White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech
description: President Donald Trump returns to the White House Correspondents' Dinner months after an attempted shooting in April. Follow Fox News Digital's live coverage of his speech, celebrity arrivals and the night's biggest moments.
content:
President Donald Trump said Friday he plans to return to the White House Correspondents' Dinner next year, though he joked his decision could change if the press gets "really, really nasty."
Trump, who attended the annual event for the first time as president , called it an "honor" to join the gathering.
"It's an honor to do it," Trump said. "I've been to it numerous times, but as president, I haven't been here, and I'm glad."
The president said he expects to attend again in 2027 but joked that his decision could depend on the press.
"They said, 'Would you do it next year?' I said, 'I will be back next year,'" Trump said. "Now if you get really, really nasty, maybe not. I don't know. But we're going to be back next year."

title: Trump weighs broader Iran offensive as Iraq holds talks with Tehran
description: President Donald Trump said Thursday that Iran remains a threat amid reports he is considering a "massive attack," while Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met Iranian leaders in Tehran to strengthen strategic cooperation.
content:
Explosions were heard across multiple parts of Iran on Thursday after the U.S. military launched another wave of strikes targeting Iranian military capabilities, according to local media.
An explosion was heard on the southern coast of Qeshm Island, Iran's state broadcaster reported, according to Reuters .
The outlet also said multiple explosions were reported in the southern city of Ahvaz, according to Iran's Fars News Agency.
A separate explosion was heard west of the port city of Bandar Abbas, Iran's state broadcaster reported, also according to Reuters.

title: Tehran responds after Trump warns US will strike bridges, power plants over Hormuz attacks
description: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz will never return to pre-war conditions after President Donald Trump warned any attack on shipping will trigger U.S. strikes on Iranian infrastructure.
content:
The U.S. is moving forces, weapons and medics to the Middle East to give President Donald Trump broader military options, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
Citing officials, the outlet said the recent "surge" in forces and assets comes as Trump considers widening the conflict against Iran .
Special operations forces have deployed to the region from their U.S. bases, according to flight-tracking data and U.S. officials, the report said.
Squadrons of jet fighters have also been staged across the Middle East.
Bomber aircraft at bases in the U.S. and U.K. are on high alert to ramp up operations, one official said.

title: Trump weighs Iran war expansion as fresh US strikes target Hormuz shipping threats
description: President Donald Trump is expected to decide in the coming days whether to expand the U.S. military campaign against Iran as American forces launched fresh strikes targeting Iranian capabilities threatening  shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
content:
Overthrowing Iran's regime has returned to the agenda in parts of the Trump administration after diplomatic efforts appeared to have failed, the Financial Times reported Monday.
"Elements of the Trump administration are once again flirting with Plan A — which is to topple the Iranian regime," the newspaper said.
In its analysis, the Financial Times also said efforts to encourage an internal uprising in Iran were back on Washington's agenda.
The report added that an earlier Israeli proposal to arm Kurdish groups opposed to Tehran was rejected by the administration but could now be revived as policymakers search for alternative options.

title: Iran strikes US allies, Brent crude oil prices continue to rise
description: The Iran war rages on as Iranian missile strikes on civilian infrastructure in Kuwait raise the stakes in the conflict following a collapse in peace talks
content:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said Friday that U.S. forces had completed their latest round of strikes against Iran, marking the seventh consecutive night of military operations.
"U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) hit surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage, and maritime capabilities," CENTCOM said in a statement. "U.S. forces employed fighter aircraft, aerial drones and warships, in addition to other assets."
CENTCOM said the latest strikes came as the U.S. continued enforcing a renewed naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz .
"CENTCOM continues to hold Iran accountable at the Commander in Chief's direction while fully enforcing a naval blockade against Iranian ports," the military said.
CENTCOM added that more than 50,000 U.S. service members continue to operate across the Middle East.

title: Trump address live updates: President Trump speaks to the nation tonight on election integrity
description: Follow live updates as President Donald Trump addresses the nation tonight in a primetime White House speech. Get the latest on Trump's election integrity announcement, key remarks, breaking news, video, and analysis.
content:
President Donald Trump is still expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in September, even after announcing the release of newly declassified intelligence documents that he said show China sought to influence the 2020 presidential election and that it acquired 220 million U.S. voter files containing personal information.
A senior White House official told Fox News that Trump is expected to meet with Xi around Sept. 24.
During his trip to China in May, Trump expressed optimism about hosting Xi in the United States in September.
Xi last visited the White House in September 2015 for a state visit hosted by then-President Barack Obama.

title: Todd Blanche faces Senate Judiciary Committee in confirmation hearing
description: President Donald Trump is calling on Republican senators to back acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, who will face questioning from the Senate Judiciary Committee during his confirmation hearing on Wednesday.
content:
Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., said during a break in Todd Blanche’s confirmation hearing that the acting attorney general hasn’t shown “enough distance from the president in terms of understanding himself to be an independent attorney general.”
“Anything you heard in there that would change your mind to vote for Todd Blanche?” Coons, a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, was asked by a reporter.
"My concerns going in are similar to my concerns coming out. He came up with, and really did not back down from, firing thousands of qualified FBI and DOJ personnel because of what cases they were assigned to, the anti-weaponization fund, which the president continues to champion,” Coons added. “He has not shown, in my view, enough distance from the president in terms of understanding himself to be an independent attorney general, which has always been the practice of most previous attorneys general.”
“And, frankly, his responses to other senator's questions on a very wide range of topics, from the Epstein files to, how he's prioritizing the department. I'm going to submit quite a few questions for the record, because there's other things, even with ten minutes, we didn't get to. And I've asked him to meet with me as a courtesy. He did. He did that with many other senators beforehand, and I look forward to a follow up conversation,” Coons also said.
Fox News' Caroline Miller contributed to this post.

title: US launches fresh Iran strikes as CENTCOM resumes naval blockade
description: American forces launched fresh strikes against Iran to degrade Tehran’s ability to target commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, CENTCOM said, as a U.S. naval blockade against Iranian ports resumed Tuesday.
content:
The United Nations on Tuesday condemned the renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East, warning that closing the Strait of Hormuz again would harm human rights in that region and beyond.
U.N. rights chief Volker Turk called the renewed attacks "a huge setback for civilians in the region and beyond," warning about the "impact on human rights far beyond the region."
The strait "is a vital lifeline on which millions are reliant," Turk said.
"Disruptions to the flow of food, medicines, and other necessary commodities have severe socioeconomic and humanitarian consequences, both regionally and globally, he continued, adding that diplomacy, restraint and de-escalation must be prioritized," he said.
Turk said hostilities between the U.S. and Iran "must stop immediately," urging an immediate return to the ceasefire.

title: Supreme Court justices testify before Congress for $230M security budget
description: Supreme Court Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett are making a rare appearance Tuesday on Capitol Hill to testify before House and Senate appropriators on the court’s roughly $230 million budget request, a 10% increase that includes $14 million expanded security funding for justices, their families and residences amid increasing threats against federal judges.
content:
Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan warned Tuesday that threats against members of the high court have come “very close indeed,” as she and Justice Amy Coney Barrett pressed senators for additional security funding.
“The Supreme Court police expect a smaller but still substantial 38% annual increase in threats this year, which follows a 25% increase last year,” Kagan told the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government.
“For some of us, those threats have come very close indeed,” she continued. “And all of us live with the knowledge that they may again materialize.”
Kagan said the court’s recent budget growth has been driven almost entirely by security needs, including larger personal details, residential protection, threat assessments and cybersecurity.
Despite the heightened danger, Kagan said the justices continue deciding cases “without fear or favor.”

title: Trump says US ready to hit Iran ‘very hard’ as tensions escalate over Strait of Hormuz: report
description: President Donald Trump reportedly said the U.S. is prepared to hit Iran “very hard” tonight and tomorrow as tensions escalate over the Strait of Hormuz, naming Pickaxe Mountain as a possible target for a “nice big fat shot.”
content:
President Donald Trump on Monday defended U.S. strikes on Iran, saying Tehran’s military capabilities have been badly weakened and warning that another “major attack” is coming tonight.
"We were in Vietnam for 19 years. We're here for four months, so I think we've done a lot," Trump told reporters when asked whether months of U.S. strikes on Iran have become the “new normal” for Americans.
Trump said U.S. forces have “knocked out” Iran’s navy, air force, missile capabilities and drone manufacturing. He argued the strikes were necessary to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
"If we didn't do it, they would have had a nuclear weapon. If they had a nuclear weapon, Israel would no longer be with us. The Middle East probably would no longer be with us," Trump added.
The president also said the U.S. should be reimbursed for “protecting” the Strait of Hormuz, the key shipping route at the center of escalating tensions in the region.
"I want to be reimbursed because we're protecting a very rich portion of the world," he said.
Trump accused Iran of dragging out negotiations for decades and said his administration has taken a tougher approach than previous presidents.
"This is what they've done for 47 years," Trump said. "The difference is nobody negotiated like I do. And this should have been done by Bush and Obama and Biden and people before them."

title: Sen. Lindsey Graham, 71, remembered, aortic dissection ruled cause of death
description: Late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., died at 71 from an aortic dissection linked to arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease, according to a preliminary cause of death finding from the medical examiner. Graham’s died late Saturday, and President Donald Trump called the loss devastating while rejecting rumors of foul play. The death raises questions around the health of Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky.
content:
Prominent Democrats on Monday offered their condolences following the passing of Sen. Lindsey Graham over the weekend.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Graham was someone who was committed to a lifetime of service.
“On occasion, I think—particularly when he was closely aligned with John McCain—he leaned into the importance of trying to actually get things done in a bipartisan way for the American people,” said Jeffries.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , D-N.Y., called Graham an important member of the Senate and a “crucial voice” for his constituents in South Carolina.
“For all of our many and vehement disagreements, Sen. Graham and I still found ways to work together," Schumer said on the Senate floor. “One of the first things we did together was travel to China. We both believed that China was manipulating its currency, hurting American exports, and hurting American jobs. And together, we hammered away at that issue.”
Schumer added that Graham would support the Senate in supporting Ukraine and strengthening sanctions on Russia.
“I urge (Senate Majority Leader) Senator Thune, in honor of Lindsey, to put the sanctions—the Russian sanctions bill—on the floor immediately. It will pass overwhelmingly and help our allies in Ukraine. Not seeing eye to eye is no reason to be blind to the way forward. Lindsey understood that, and every senator ought to do the same.”

title: Iran war escalates as US, IRGC exchange fire over Strait of Hormuz
description: U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged heavy missile and drone attacks as the IRGC claimed Iran had closed the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global oil and LNG shipments, until the “end of U.S. interference” in the region. U.S. Central Command said commercial vessels continued to transit the waterway and that American forces struck more than 300 Iranian military targets over three nights.
content:
The U.S. conducted a new wave of offensive strikes against Iran on Sunday, according to Central Command.
The strikes hit dozens of targets at multiple locations with "precision munitions to degrade Iran’s ability to continue attacking international shipping flowing through the Strait of Hormuz," CENTCOM said on X.
"CENTCOM forces struck Iranian military air-defense systems, coastal radar sites, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats using U.S. fighter aircraft, naval vessels, one-way attack aerial drones, and one-way attack sea drones for the first time," CENTCOM said.
The military added that the Strait of Hormuz is a "vital maritime corridor for global trade" and that Iran does not control it.
"U.S. forces are postured and prepared to ensure that freedom of navigation remains available to commercial shipping despite Iran’s continued unwarranted aggression, harassment, threats, and arbitrary declarations," CENTCOM said.

title: GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham dies at 71 after 'brief and sudden illness'
description: U.S. Sen. Lindsey Graham, the longtime South Carolina politician and influential voice on national security and the judiciary, died on Saturday, July 11, at 71 after a "brief and sudden illness," according to his office.
content:
The Medical Examiner of the District of Columbia released preliminary findings Sunday regarding the death of Sen. Lindsey Graham .
According to the medical examiner, the preliminary examination found Graham suffered an aortic dissection due to arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
The ME said the death certificate will remain pending until toxicological and microscopic testing are finalized.
"The death certificate will be PENDING until all the toxicological and microscopic testing are finalized and at that point the death certificate will be updated to reflect the cause of death and appropriately classify the manner of death," the statement said

title: Israeli leadership signal readiness to strike Iran again as US negotiators head to Oman
description: Iranian and U.S. negotiators are expected to meet in Oman on Saturday as hopes for a broader peace deal fade. Iranian media report explosions in multiple areas, while the U.S. and Israel ramp up pressure on Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz.
content:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said Saturday that U.S. forces completed a third round of strikes against Iran this week in response to Tehran's latest attack on a commercial vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
“U.S. forces hit approximately 140 Iranian military targets with precision munitions launched by land- and sea-based fighter aircraft, drones, and naval vessels,” CENTCOM said in a statement.
According to CENTCOM, the operation targeted Iranian missile and drone sites, naval capabilities, ammunition storage facilities, communications networks and coastal surveillance positions.
Saturday's operation marked the third round of U.S. strikes against Iran this week, bringing the total number of targets hit to more than 300.
“During three nights of strikes this week, CENTCOM has struck more than 300 targets at the direction of the Commander in Chief to degrade Iran’s ability to attack civilian mariners and commercial vessels freely transiting the strait,” CENTCOM said.
CENTCOM said commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continues to move through the strategic waterway.
The command also said U.S. forces have helped facilitate the transit of more than 800 commercial vessels carrying approximately 400 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz since early May.

title: US pauses Iran attack after ceasefire break as Israel reveals plot to kill Trump
description: Following two days of retaliatory strikes, President Donald Trump paused the US-Iran conflict as former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is buried. Meanwhile, Iranian threats to the Strait of Hormuz have halted ceasefire hopes, sending Brent crude oil and local gas prices higher.
content:
The Trump administration has given Iran until Saturday to publicly commit to ending attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz or face unspecified consequences, according to an Axios report citing three U.S. officials.
Axios reported the administration wants Tehran to publicly acknowledge the strategic waterway is open, commit to stopping attacks on commercial vessels and recognize that all shipping lanes through the strait will remain open without tolls.
According to Axios, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to meet Saturday with Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi in Muscat as regional mediators work to ease tensions and revive nuclear talks.
One U.S. official told Axios that if Iran does not make a public commitment, “it is not gonna be a great day for them.”
The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Tyler Robinson case: Defense attacks ballistics evidence as preliminary hearing wraps up
description: Tyler Robinson's preliminary hearing concluded its fifth and final day Friday, with his defense team calling its last witness before both sides rested. Judge Tony Graf now weighs whether the case will move to trial.
content:
An emotional silence fell over the courtroom Friday as prosecutors played an enhanced video compilation showing the moments leading up to Charlie Kirk’s assassination during Day 5 of Tyler Robinson’s preliminary hearing.
Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, and his mother, Kathy Kirk, cried and leaned into one another as the video played. Both women hugged and held tissues while seated with family, friends and supporters in the courtroom.
Kathy Kirk later turned to embrace her husband, Robert Kirk, with a tissue held to her face. Erika Kirk’s sister, Tonya, reached over to comfort her with a hand on her back.
At one point, an investigator seated with the family retrieved a trash can for used tissues.
The courtroom was largely silent as the video played. Robinson did not appear to watch the video with the monitor at his table turned off, and he appeared to look down and straight ahead rather than toward the screen.
Earlier Friday, Judge Tony Graf sanctioned media members after an exhibit was inadvertently shown and broadcast during Thursday’s proceedings. Graf said he did not want to “rush or make snap decisions” before ruling that no further exhibits would be shown for the rest of the day, though the final video compilation was later allowed as an exception.

title: US renews strikes on IRGC; Iran vows retaliation as peace, ceasefire stall
description: President Donald Trump’s renewed U.S. strikes on Iran have Tehran threatening “grave consequences,” fueling Iran war fears, Strait of Hormuz security risks, oil market anxiety and potentially rising gas prices again.
content:
Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was finally laid to rest early Friday at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, Iran, according to a statement posted by his official office.
“In the early hours of Friday, July 10, 2026, the pure body of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Grand Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Hosseini Khamenei … was laid to rest in the luminous shrine of Imam Reza,” Khamenei’s official X account said.
The burial concludes several days of funeral ceremonies that took Khamenei’s body through Iraq and Iran following his death during the conflict with Israel and the United States.

title: New York City high-rise building evacuated over fears of collapse
description: A Midtown Manhattan high-rise building was evacuated Tuesday after authorities said it was at risk of collapsing. Approximately 150 fire and EMS personnel are on the scene.
content:
Tuesday’s collapse scare involving the structurally compromised Midtown Manhattan high-rise may have been triggered by the weight of a new addition atop the building.
The building’s developer said the tower’s upper 15 floors, beginning on the 22nd floor, were undergoing renovations to expand outward, making them wider than the floors below, according to The Wall Street Journal.
He added that the two support beams that visibly buckled on the 21st floor may not have been properly reinforced.
“This additional load that we put on those floors caused those two particular columns to collapse,” Nathan Berman, managing principal and founder of MetroLoft, told the outlet.
“Why those particular two columns and nothing else? We don’t know…we’re investigating that.”
According to the report, Berman said 95% of the building is still structurally intact.

title: Tyler Robinson case: Attorneys spar over DNA found on items near the crime scene
description: Day two of Tyler Robinson's preliminary hearing kicked off with the resumption of David Hull's testimony and included testimony from SBI agent Jennifer Faumuina and FBI forensic examiner Amanda Bakker in the Charlie Kirk case.
content:
Tensions built in the courtroom Tuesday as attorneys sparred over DNA in Tyler Robinson’s preliminary hearing.
Erika Kirk at one point shook her head as she listened to the defense question Amanda Bakker, an FBI analyst who testified that Robinson’s DNA was found on a towel that was wrapped around a rifle found near Utah Valley University, where Charlie Kirk was shot.
Erika Kirk leaned in as testimony revealed that Robinson’s former roommate and lover, Lance Twiggs, also had DNA on the towel.
Charlie Kirk’s mother wiped her eyes with a tissue after Bakker was allowed to step down following a combative line of questioning from defense attorney Michael Burt, who tried to discredit the FBI analyst.

title: Iranian performer calls for Trump's assassination during Khamenei funeral
description: Mourners in Iran held a 12-hour funeral procession for former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on as funeral events continue Monday. Three of Khamenei's sons appeared during events this weekend, but not the current supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.
content:
Mourners dressed in black poured into Tehran on Monday for the funeral procession of Iran’s late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with massive crowds calling for President Donald Trump’s death and vowing revenge against the United States and Israel.
Khamenei’s coffin was carried through the Iranian capital alongside the coffins of family members killed in a Feb. 28 airstrike at the start of the war launched by Israel and the U.S.
Iran’s ruling theocracy encouraged the turnout as a show of strength while the regime remains locked in tense negotiations with Washington over an end to the war.
As the funeral truck moved slowly through the capital, mourners waved signs and banners targeting Trump. Some also called for the killing of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and an effigy of Trump was seen hanging along the route.
A mourner holds up an image of Donald Trump with a message of "There will be blood" on July 6, 2026 in Tehran, Iran. (Credit: Kaveh Kazemi/Getty Images)
“Today that we are here for the funeral for our leader, it’s a very tough day,” mourner Fatima Hassan said. “We are not here to say goodbye to him. We are here for revenge. And we will take revenge.”
Crowds reached out to touch the truck, while others tossed scarves and other items toward attendants to brush against the coffin — a common Iranian practice viewed as a blessing.
Khamenei’s casket was flown to the Shiite seminary city of Qom later Monday, where he is expected to be honored Tuesday, according to state television.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Alleged Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson due in court as evidence takes center stage
description: Accused Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson heads to a Provo, Utah courtroom Monday as a five-day preliminary hearing begins, with prosecutors expected to present DNA evidence and witness testimony.
content:
Utah State Bureau of Investigation Agent David Hull said that Tyler Robinson visited the Utah Valley University campus a total of four times on the day Charlie Kirk was shot on September 10, 2025.
Hull said Robinson was on campus three times that day, once before the shooting, once at the time of the shooting and again later that evening into the early hours of Sept. 11.
Authorities were able to track Robinson through surveillance video on campus, Hull said.

title: Khamenei's body to travel in Iran, Iraq during days-long funeral
description: President Donald Trump celebrated American heritage on Saturday as peace negotiations with Iran remain on pause for the funeral of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
content:
Officials are reportedly eyeing Islamabad, Pakistan , as the venue for the next round of peace talks between Washington and Tehran.
The technical negotiations are expected to begin July 11 after being delayed by Iran's multiday funeral ceremonies for slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Diplomatic sources told the Pakistani newspaper Dawn that Islamabad, which helped broker the recently signed memorandum of understanding, has emerged as the leading candidate to host the next round of negotiations.
“There are two possible venues for the technical talks — Islamabad and the Burgenstock resort in Switzerland,” one source said. “Islamabad, however, is the more likely option.”
Officials are expected to build on the technical framework outlined in the memorandum of understanding, which was signed two weeks ago and established a 60-day ceasefire.
The negotiations are expected to focus on Iran's nuclear program, frozen Iranian assets, the Strait of Hormuz and the ceasefire in Lebanon, Dawn reported.

title: America 250 kicks off in nation's capital as Americans brave weather to celebrate Independence Day
description: Americans are celebrating the 250th anniversary of their independence across the country on Saturday. President Donald Trump will address the crowd Saturday night after severe weather suspended some events in Washington, D.C., earlier in the evening.
content:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that the United States stands as "the crowning achievement of human history" during his speech celebrating America's 250th anniversary on the National Mall.
“This country is the home of freedom,” Trump said.
Trump argued the nation is stronger than ever.
“We're doing better now than we've ever done before,” he said. “No people have done more good, showed more courage, made more progress, righted more injustice or achieved more greatness than you, the American people.”
“For 250 years, the United States of America has been the hope, the promise, the light and the glory among all of the nations of the world,” Trump said.
“Nobody can be like us. And with God's help, we will always be this or even better.”

title: US agrees to halt talks with Iran for a week as funeral for Khamenei begins
description: Denuclearization talks between the U.S. and Iran are on hold for a week as the Iranian government prepares a funeral for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, the capital. The funeral is expected to last from July 4 to July 9.
content:
Dmitry Medvedev , deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, traveled to Tehran on Friday to attend funeral ceremonies for former Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Medvedev met with Iranian officials during the visit and offered condolences on behalf of Russia's leadership and people.
"On behalf of the leadership and people of Russia, I extend our deepest condolences over the martyrdom of Iran's Supreme Leader, Grand Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei," Medvedev wrote in a post on X. "We mourn this immeasurable loss alongside the Iranian people."
Medvedev also shared video from Tehran showing meetings with Iranian officials during the funeral ceremonies.
Russia has maintained close ties with Iran in recent years, with the two countries expanding cooperation on military, economic and regional issues.

title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce reported MSG wedding kicks off
description: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce reportedly say "I do" Friday at Madison Square Garden in front of 1,000 people after hosting rehearsal dinner for 100 guests on Thursday. Street closures snarled traffic in Manhattan after the couple took extreme measures for privacy. The couple began dating in 2023, and he popped the question two years later.
content:
Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift are officially husband and wife.
Following days of speculation surrounding everything from the day, time and location, the happy couple said "I do" in front of 1,000 guests at Madison Square Garden .
