Adam Sandler officiated the ceremony where Taylor's brother Austin served as Man of Honor while Jason Kelce stood by his brother as Best Man.
The happy couple coordinated in custom Christian Dior ensembles and Christian Louboutin shoes, Swift's rep confirmed to People.
Jennifer Lopez, Hugh Grant, Ed Sheeran, Jennifer Lawrence, Karlie Kloss, Camila Cabello were just a few of the stars spotted heading into MSG on Friday.
Emails obtained by the Associated Press earlier this week appeared to show that "city officials have been aware of the wedding — and its impact on city streets — for nearly a month."
"On June 8, the director of the city’s street permitting office, Dawn Tolson, emailed several City Hall staffers to discuss a permit application 'in association with the T&T wedding,' an apparent reference to Taylor and Travis," the outlet reported.
The AP noted that the application included requests for “full street closures” on July 3 and 4, under the subject line: “Wedding Bells Are Ringing.”
"No Parking" signs lined the streets outside the iconic Manhattan venue where officials were police had "detail" in place for the major event.
Swift and Kelce first sparked dating rumors in 2023 after the Kansas City Chiefs tight end revealed that he had unsuccessfully tried to give the pop superstar a friendship bracelet during her Eras Tour stop in Kansas City.
The pair later confirmed their romance when Swift began attending Chiefs games and cheering Kelce on from the stands.
After two years of dating, the couple announced their engagement in August 2025.
Fox News Digital's Lauryn Overhultz contributed to this report.
Fans wait for a chance to witness Taylor Swift wedding (Getty Images)

title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce MSG wedding week ramps up ahead of reported NYC nuptials
description: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are reportedly hosting a rehearsal dinner for 100 guests Thursday ahead of Friday nuptials at Madison Square Garden in the heart of New York City. The couple began dating in 2023, and he popped the question two years later. The pop star and her pro football player fiance will allegedly host 1,000 people at MSG.
content:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce have a message for guests of their reported MSG wedding: you will be on film.
A notice perched toward the front of Madison Square Garden appeared to alert attendees that cameras would be rolling inside the venue.
"The event" release noted filming would take place between June 29 - July 3, and that anyone entering the arena would be subject to being on camera.
Swift and Kelce are reportedly hosting a rehearsal dinner-style event for 100 guests tonight at MSG's Infosys Theater, before a rumored 1,000-person celebration on Friday at the venue.

title: US-Iran talks gain momentum in Doha as Hormuz tensions ease ahead of Khamenei funeral
description: Qatar confirmed Wednesday that talks between U.S. and Iranian negotiators in Doha made progress, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Dr. Majed Al Ansari saying new meetings would follow the funeral for Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
content:
Iran's foreign minister warned Wednesday that Tehran would respond forcefully to any threat against regime leadership after Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, was "marked for death."
"The terms of the Islamabad MoU are crystal clear and public for all to see," Abbas Araghchi said in a post on X.
" POTUS has committed the U.S. to muzzling its pets in Tel Aviv. If they ignore their master, Iran will school them," he added before warning that any "threat against our People and Leadership will receive Immediate Powerful Response."
Iran's U.N. ambassador, Amir Saeid Iravani, also sent a letter to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres objecting to the remarks.
According to Ynet , Katz had also said that Khamenei was “a dead man.”

title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce wedding watch intensifies as rumored July 3 celebration nears
description: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are reportedly hosting a multi-day wedding event beginning July 2 at Madison Square Garden in New York City. The two are reportedly having a 1,000-person celebration on July 3.
content:
Travis Kelce celebrated the end of his single era with his brother and friends at a bar in West Hollywood last month.
In a photo obtained by TMZ , Travis was pictured wearing a blue-and-white flannel shirt, circular sunglasses and a backwards hat.
The Kansas City Chiefs tight end stopped by Barney's Beanery with his crew for his bachelor party.
The weekend also reportedly included a NASCAR event and pit-stop in San Diego for a Dave Chappelle show.
While neither party has confirmed any speculation surrounding their wedding, Travis and Taylor will reportedly say "I do" on Friday at Madison Square Garden .

title: Iran refuses more US talks as Qatar says no high-level meetings are taking place
description: Iran says it won't resume negotiations with the United States until key conditions are met, while Qatar says there are currently no high-level meetings between Washington and Tehran, despite technical delegations remaining in session.
content:
President Donald Trump has recently considered a return to all-out war with Iran , according to reports.
Citing U.S. officials, The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that Trump held "multiple conversations" in recent days with War Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine about conducting more strikes.
The outlet said the president decided to stick with diplomatic talks — for now.
The meetings are said to have focused on whether Washington should abandon negotiations and resume full-scale attacks on Iran, which would mean "finishing the job."
Trump said another round of military action could derail diplomacy and reduce the chances of dismantling Iran's nuclear program, which is the president's overarching aim.

title: The Supreme Court ruled against President Donald Trump on his birthright citizenship ban
description: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's effort to end birthright citizenship on Tuesday, after ruling in favor of bans on transgender athletes in women's sports.
content:
Border czar Tom Homan on Tuesday criticized the Supreme Court’s decision upholding birthright citizenship, saying the ruling means the Trump administration must “step up enforcement” and intensify investigations into birth tourism.
Speaking on " The Will Cain Show ," Homan called birth tourism “a national security issue,” arguing that foreign nationals from countries including China and Russia have traveled to the United States to give birth before returning to their home countries with children who are American citizens.
Homan said Congress should “get on this right away” by addressing birth tourism through legislation, while pledging the administration would “triple, quadruple down” on investigations. He also argued birthright citizenship has long been “a major driver for illegal migration.”
"During the Biden administration, the Yuma hospital, the El Paso hospital, 100% maternity beds are illegal aliens," Homan said. "That's not a coincidence. That's not by accident."
Later in the interview, Homan defended stricter immigration enforcement while reacting to testimony from Jessica Gorman, the mother of Sheridan Gorman.
"I've met hundreds of angel moms and dads, and I remember every one of those stories, tragic stories," Homan said. "Our children should be alive today. My worst nightmare is to bury a child, bury my children."

title: Israel warns war could resume 'within two days' as US pushes ahead with Iran technical talks in Doha
description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz warns war with Iran could erupt within 48 hours if missiles are fired at Israel, while U.S. officials say nuclear talks and technical negotiations with Tehran are slated to continue this week in Qatar.
content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that Tehran is committed to the memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the United States, provided Washington upholds its obligations.
"Mutual understanding is a two-way street," Pezeshkian wrote in a post shared on X .
"If the American side adheres to the agreement, we will also fulfill our commitments," he added.
"Our approach to unreasonable saber-rattling and baseless threats is to rely on rationality and human dignity in decision-making, while defending decisively and fearlessly when action is required," Pezeshkian said.

title: Iran agrees to halt attacks as high-stakes nuclear talks loom after weekend military strikes
description: Washington and Tehran have reportedly agreed to halt military strikes as officials prepare for high-stakes talks in Doha, Qatar on June 30, focused on the Strait of Hormuz and nuclear issues after a weekend of escalating conflict.
content:
Washington and Tehran agreed to halt military strikes in the region on Sunday, according to reports.
“Technical talks are slated to continue on all areas of the MOU. Both sides will stand down for now and vessels can move freely," the White House told Fox News.
Citing an official, Axios also reported that the two sides' delegations are now scheduled to meet June 30 in Doha, Qatar.
Fresh strikes escalated over the weekend after U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) conducted additional strikes on multiple targets in Iran following what it described as an Iranian attack on the Panama-flagged tanker M/T Kiku near the Strait of Hormuz.
On Sunday, Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain, leading to condemnations from both Arab neighbors.
Under the interim memorandum of understanding (MOU) Iran would allow safe passage for vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, while the U.S. would lift its blockade of Iranian ports.
A hotline between the U.S. military and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was also expected to be established to coordinate maritime traffic.
On Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran alone was responsible for managing and fully reopening maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz under the recent understandings.
Fox News' Alex Hogan contributed to this report.

title: US launches additional strikes on Iran after latest Strait of Hormuz ship attack
description: The U.S. carried out additional strikes on Iranian military targets after Tehran attacked another commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The latest escalation comes despite a ceasefire agreement.
content:
President Donald Trump warned Saturday that the United States could escalate military action against Iran after U.S. forces carried out another round of strikes on Iranian targets.
“United States aircraft just struck Iranian missile and drone storage locations, and coastal radar sites, for violating the Cease Fire Agreement, AGAIN!” Trump wrote on Truth Social .
“There may come a point when we are no longer able to be reasonable, and will be forced to militarily complete the job that we very successfully started,” he added. “If that happens, the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist!”

title: US strikes Iran after Strait of Hormuz cargo ship attack as ceasefire tensions escalate
description: U.S. forces launched strikes against Iranian targets Friday after Tehran attacked a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The retaliation comes as Washington, Tehran, Israel and Lebanon navigate a fragile ceasefire framework.
content:
Vice President JD Vance warned Iran on Friday that further attacks would be met with force following U.S. strikes on Iranian targets along the Strait of Hormuz.
“Iran signed a ceasefire agreement. We have honored it,” Vance wrote on X while reposting a CENTCOM statement announcing the strikes.
“If they have disagreements about how the MOU is being applied, they can pick up the phone,” he added.
“But violence will be met with violence.”
The comments came after U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said American forces struck Iranian missile and drone storage sites as well as coastal radar installations in response to Tehran’s attack on a commercial vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Iranian drone strikes Singapore-flagged cargo ship leaving Strait of Hormuz, US officials say
description: A Singapore-flagged cargo ship was struck by a drone Thursday while leaving the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. officials said, attributing the attack to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
content:
President Donald Trump said Thursday evening that the U.S. is negotiating with Iran from a "position of pure strength."
“We knocked the hell out of them, and now we’re negotiating from a position of pure strength,” Trump said at a dinner with American farmers in the White House Rose Garden. “Pure strength. They know that.”
Trump said Iran “wants to make a deal with us very badly," while also insisting Tehran will not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.
“They will not have a nuclear weapon,” the president said. “And they've agreed to that.”
The president also said the Strait of Hormuz remains open.
Trump additionally reiterated that Iran could become a new market for U.S. farmers , saying the administration would use Iranian money to buy “wheat, soybeans and corn” as Tehran struggles with food shortages.

title: Trump warns U.S. will act if deal fails as Tehran says it's proceeding 'with vigilance'
description: President Donald Trump says Iran is meeting U.S. demands but warns Washington will act if negotiations fail, while Tehran says it is proceeding “with vigilance” amid ongoing nuclear talks.
content:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday took a swipe at British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, saying he was "now gone," and said the United States had been "let down" by allies during its military offensive against Iran .
"We were let down," Trump told reporters at the White House after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. "We didn't need help on this at all. We demolished them," he said of Iran.
"But it would have been nice if they would have said, 'We'd like to help,'" he said. "We didn't even need it, but it would have been nice if they said that. They didn't say it."
The president suggested he could have turned to Rutte for support if it had been necessary.
"I think if I would have called him, he probably would have found a way to help if we needed it," Trump said. "I feel, you know, it would have been a little bit different."
Starmer / Isabel Infantes / Pool Reuters via AP
Trump then singled out several European countries for criticism.
"But I was disappointed. I was disappointed with Italy. I was disappointed with the UK," he said.
"He's now gone and, you know, he had a lot of problems," Trump said of Starmer .
Trump added that he was also disappointed with Germany and France.
"We were disappointed with Germany and France. We're disappointed with most of them," he said. "Spain is a horror show," Trump added.

title: Trump says ‘I will do what I have to do’ if Iran doesn’t honor deal
description: President Donald Trump, following talks in Switzerland, said “If Iran doesn't live up to their agreement, or if they're not behaving, I will do what I have to do.” The negotiations resulted in measures to prevent incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.
content:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte on Tuesday voiced support for President Donald Trump's criticism of NATO but argued that despite some frustrations within the alliance, European members have provided support to U.S.-led military operations.
His remarks came after Trump renewed pressure on NATO allies to increase contributions to collective defense and support alliance missions.
“I completely back him on this when it comes to NATO,” Rutte said during an appearance on Fox News' "Special Report with Bret Baier."
“I know there is disappointment, but let's also see these are isolated cases,” he added.
Rutte pointed to European support for military action against Iran , noting that thousands of flights originated from European bases to assist the mission.
“I totally understand the disappointment, but when you take, for example, Italy, 500 U.S. planes took off from U.S. bases in Italy to support the operation. So this is massive.”
He also highlighted logistical assistance provided by other allies.
“When you look at all of Europe, again, it's between 4,000 and 5,000 sorties,” Rutte said. “A country like Romania — in its capital, Bucharest — had to cut down on commercial air traffic because the airport was being used as a tanker facility. So all this is taking place," he said.

title: 2026 primary elections underway in key races

content:
Former New York City Comptroller Brad Lander, a former Democratic Socialists of America member backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, defeated Rep. Dan Goldman in Tuesday’s Democratic primary for New York’s 10th Congressional District.
Lander, who describes himself as a “liberal Zionist,” ousted Goldman in a head-to-head primary in one of the nation’s bluest House seats. The district spans Lower Manhattan and parts of western Brooklyn, taking in liberal neighborhoods from Greenwich Village and the Lower East Side to Brooklyn Heights, Park Slope and Sunset Park.
The result marked a victory for the city’s ascendant progressive wing, with Sanders and Mamdani helping Lander topple Goldman, a former federal prosecutor who served as lead counsel during the first impeachment inquiry into President Donald Trump.
Goldman was first elected to Congress in 2022 after winning a crowded Democratic primary in the newly redrawn district.

The results of the latest negotiations include measures to prevent incidents and miscommunication in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as the creation of a "deconfliction cell" to help enforce the U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement across all fronts, including Lebanon.
Vice President JD Vance also said Monday that Tehran agreed to invite International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors into the country.

title: Vance travels to Switzerland for talks as Iran negotiators arrive

content:
Former CIA station chief Dan Hoffman warned Saturday that Hezbollah continues to pose a significant threat to both Israel and U.S. interests in the Middle East despite ongoing negotiations involving Iran.
Speaking on "Life, Liberty & Levin," Hoffman said Hezbollah remains one of Iran's primary tools for projecting power throughout the region.
"Iran has used Hezbollah, the Houthis, their proxy militants in Iraq to project power in the region and beyond," Hoffman said.
Hoffman argued that Hezbollah's influence in Lebanon continues to create security risks for Israel and for American personnel stationed throughout the Middle East.
"That's what causes Israel to be at great risk, but not just Israel, it's U.S. installations and our people in the region and beyond," Hoffman said.
The former CIA official also warned that any agreement with Iran should not leave Hezbollah in a position to rebuild its military capabilities.
"The last thing we want is for Hezbollah to emerge from any deal that we have with Iran in a position to rearm and reconstitute," Hoffman said.
The comments come as Israel and Hezbollah exchange new attacks despite a ceasefire agreement that is tied to broader negotiations involving the United States and Iran.

content:
Anthropic's Claude artificial intelligence model accessed publicly available Georgia election data without being instructed to do so, reportedly bypassing a paywall to obtain the information, according to Axios.
The AI model accessed aggregate vote counts while working on an internal statistics project, Axios reported. Although the information was publicly available, accessing it through the government dashboard typically required payment.
Claude independently requested a token to access the dashboard despite not being instructed to obtain the data, an Anthropic spokesperson told the outlet.
The company emphasized that Claude did not access Georgia's voter registration system, retrieve individual voting records or alter election data.
Anthropic said it has since implemented safeguards to prevent similar unauthorized actions.
The company notified Georgia's secretary of state's office and the White House about the incident weeks ago, Axios reported.
Trump administration officials subsequently pressed Georgia officials to publicly disclose the incident sooner, according to a source familiar with the matter cited by Axios.

title: Ole Miss and Texas collide in massive college football showdown with Arch Manning's season at stake

title: Death toll rises to 9 in church attack; officials blame 'extremist' Islamist ideology
description: Footage shows gunmen armed with pistols and a rifle storming a Greek Orthodox church in Karak during a funeral service, killing nine in Jordan.
content: A group of gunmen stormed a Christian church in Jordan during a funeral Friday, killing nine people and injuring more than two dozen, according to authorities. The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 55 miles south of the capital, Amman. Jordanian Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said Saturday that one critically injured patient remained hospitalized at Prince Ali Military Hospital in unstable condition. Government spokesperson Mohammad Momani said Saturday the attackers subscribed to "extremist takfiri ideology," which brands people who reject a strict interpretation of Islam as apostates or nonbelievers. Terrorist groups such as ISIS have invoked takfiri beliefs to justify killing Muslims, Christians and Jews. BISHOP ROBERT BARRON: THE WAR ON CHRISTIANS IS REAL, AND THE WORLD CAN NO LONGER STAY SILENT Karak is home to a sizable Christian minority, and Momani sought to emphasize that Christians are "part of Jordan's national fabric." It remains unclear whether the gunmen were affiliated with any terror group, and Jordanian authorities have not announced any arrests in connection with the attack. Footage shown on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen armed with what appeared to be pistols approaching the church and opening fire, The Associated Press reported. A third man carrying what appeared to be a semiautomatic rifle joined them moments later, before all three rushed toward the church. TWO SUSPECTED GUNMEN DEAD, TWO IDF SOLDIERS KILLED IN WEST BANK SHOOTING Photos and videos from witnesses show broken glass and pools of blood inside the church. After the location was secured by police, two bodies covered with blankets were seen outside the church. Dorgham Halasa told the AP that intense gunfire erupted in the church some 15 minutes after the funeral service began. People began running, he said. Halasa said he didn't see the gunmen but said others he spoke with reported seeing at least four of them. Jordanian authorities had not confirmed the number of attackers as of Saturday. On Friday, King Abdullah II said Jordan will "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties." title: ‘80s pop star Taylor Dayne celebrates 4 years cancer-free after frightening diagnosis with no symptoms
description: Taylor Dayne opens up about her colon cancer journey, urging women to advocate for colonoscopies earlier as she prepares for her Las Vegas residency.
content: Taylor Dayne has plenty of reasons to celebrate. The pop star, known for the '80s hit "Tell It to My Heart," has been keeping busy gearing up for her first Las Vegas residency at Harrah's Las Vegas. The Grammy-nominated artist, who announced in 2022 that she'd privately battled Stage 2 colon cancer, said she's been given the all-clear and is ready to party with her fans. TAYLOR DAYNE RECALLS FINDING FAME WITH ‘80S HIT ‘TELL IT TO MY HEART’: ‘I WAS PRAYING TO GET SIGNED' "I've been cancer-free for four years now," she told Fox News Digital with a smile. "I've been on the path of being very ardent about taking care of my health and being on top of my colonoscopies. There are no guarantees in life, but especially as women, we need to advocate for our health and be on top of our checkups. "I was already on top of my colonoscopies when I was told I had a lot of polyps," the singer said. "It was through a routine checkup that they found a very aggressive polyp. This is how quickly these things can escalate and really take a turn. But my mindset was, 'What do I do right now?' I was very much in action mode." Dayne, who didn't experience any symptoms before her diagnosis, stressed that routine screenings are essential. "I was 50 years old, and they said, 'Now's the time to go in for this,'" Dayne, 64, said. "It's not like that anymore, because of our food, our diets, what we're exposed to daily. You really have to think about your timeline earlier than we've ever done. And we have such high-paced lifestyles. Most people are busy working, busy being parents, busy just being out there juggling. We can't put our health on the sidelines." The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends that adults at average risk begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45, down from the previous recommendation of 50. People at increased risk, including some with a family history of colorectal cancer, may need to begin screening earlier. "I thought it was a male-dominated disease, like prostate cancer," she said. "I was like, 'Colon?' It wasn't really resonating with me, and it certainly wasn't resonating with anyone in my family. I learned from my experience: Be your own warrior, be your champion. And that's what I did. It started with me asking, 'Why do I keep developing polyps?' You have to be your own champion, your own voice in getting the information you need, the plan you need." Dayne said her experience also taught her the importance of speaking up early. She noted that advocating for oneself can be harder when seriously ill. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "When you're that ill, there's very little that the person can do," she explained. "Your advocate is usually your partner, your spouse, your best friend. But, oftentimes, it's just yourself. It made me realize a lot of things. And I'm so grateful, ever grateful. For me, it turned on a lightbulb, a desire to live, a desire to really push through things. And it's brought a lot of love to my heart because I've met so many people I otherwise wouldn't have met because we have so much in common now. Survivors." Dayne's renewed focus on her health is also tied to her desire to be present for her children. "Your kids don't think of you as having a career," she said. "They don't think about your fame, your awards, the guest house. All they want is for their needs to be met. You're just mom to them. I became a very different touring artist then. And touring was the largest component of my career. But I was a single parent. I raised them. I was then the mother bird who needed to always come back to her nest." Dayne follows a no-nonsense health regimen that helps her look and feel her best as she prepares for her Las Vegas residency. "I'm very religious with my morning ritual, whatever my morning looks like, because my morning could be one o'clock in the afternoon, and it could be five in the morning," she said. "I do my peptides. I do my collagen. I do my bone broth. I do copper for my skin. I want to be optimal. That takes stretching, Pilates, yoga, daily exercise. You have to take care of yourself spiritually, emotionally, mentally. "It's a real juggle," Dayne continued. "But the first moment you have in the morning, the first two minutes you have, should be centering yourself. And then I do my tinctures. I also like to have a big ol' smoothie. I usually have just liquids in the morning. I also love soursop, especially when I travel. I have to have a healthy lifestyle to meet the demands of what it takes to be physically on stage every night." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "I was in Munich preparing to make an appearance and I said, 'What are all these people doing outside? Why is their hair crimped? Why do they have red lips? Oh my God, they look like me,'" Dayne recalled. "It's not overnight stardom because I spent 15, 16, 17 in every club conceivable in New York in the '80s," she said. "But when you have a single like that, the next thing you know, you're on 'Top of the Pops.' I just knew my life would never be the same. I had no idea people would love my music so much, that they would want to look like me. Here we are, 39 years later. "I never said, 'This is going to last forever,'" she said, reflecting on her fame. "How could you ever know? It was a moment. I was young, I was 22, 23. You just want to catch the wind." Nearly four decades into her career, Dayne sees her upcoming Las Vegas residency as a victory lap. title: Great relationships have 3 essential ingredients, and one factor that can ruin everything
description: Simon Sinek reveals his "3+1" formula for great relationships, breaking down why infatuation and dopamine spikes can send dangerously wrong signals.
content: The difference between a good relationship and a great relationship could boil down to one formula. Simon Sinek, author, inspirational speaker and founder of The Optimism Company in New York, shared his breakdown of core compatibilities for successful couples. Sinek, who has built a following of millions with content about leadership and interpersonal communication, said he developed his "3+1" formula after years of considering what makes partnerships work. 5 MARRIAGE MISTAKES COUPLES MAKE WITHOUT REALIZING IT — AND HOW TO AVOID THEM The formula centers on the following three core factors that can ebb and flow over the course of a partnership. He also added a fourth bonus factor: circumstances. Being intellectually compatible with your partner is essential, Sinek told Fox News Digital. "You get along, you enjoy going out with them," he said. "It doesn't mean you're as smart as each other; it means you have something to talk about when you go out together." COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS Emotional compatibility means being vulnerable and emotionally available to each other, while creative and sexual compatibility reflects enjoying intimacy with a partner. Sinek said he groups sexual attraction and creativity together because they use the "same part of the brain" that is imaginative. "When people can bring imagination to their sex lives, that is creativity," he said. "You hear it in couples who have been together for 10, 15, 20 years. They talk about how things get stale, get boring. That's creativity." A good relationship can blossom with 1½ or two of these factors, according to Sinek, but a great relationship includes all three. NEARLY 1 IN 3 MARRIED AMERICANS AREN'T HAVING SEX — EXPERT REVEALS HOW TO BRING BACK THE SPARK "They're not all on high at the same time, so they sort of need each other to get through the relationship," he said. The bonus factor — circumstances — is controlled by external forces and can tip the scales of a successful relationship, Sinek added. "Sometimes, we meet somebody who fits all three, but they live on the other side of the world, and we can't move our lives, and they can't move theirs," he said. "Or maybe they're already in a relationship, and you shrug your shoulders and say, 'Bad timing.' "Sometimes we get infatuated because we find one or two of those things, but for it to really last, I’ve learned it takes all three, plus the circumstances." Mistaking infatuation for compatibility Sinek warned that having one or two of these factors so highly developed, especially early in a relationship, can create the misleading impression that "this is my person." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "One of the biggest things I’ve learned about relationships is the danger of infatuation," Sinek said, noting that early attraction can be driven by dopamine rather than love at first sight. He said people can fall for "the fantasy that the person represents" and think, "I’ve been looking for someone like you for my whole life," despite knowing someone for only a few hours. After the initial infatuation fades, it may become more clear whether a person is a good long-term match, according to Sinek. He suggested that a lack of intense infatuation at the beginning could sometimes be a positive sign. "You hear about people who knew each other for 10 years because they worked together," he said. "And then they finally realize that they're in love with each other. There was no infatuation. There was no spike." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Sinek encourages people to give potential partners who meet many of the desired criteria a chance, even if there isn't an immediate spark. "I know I've made this mistake a million times," he said. "I met great people, but there was no infatuation, so I was like, ‘Nope, not for me.’ Or I was seduced by the infatuation." Striking a balance For committed or long-term couples who seem to have the core factors out of balance, Sinek urges them to pay closer attention to habits that may be pulling them away from the relationship. "You see people who go out for dinner on a regular basis, and they are either on their phones the whole time, or they're looking in other directions," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Maybe somebody needs to put in an effort to say, ‘Let's put our phones away. Let's trade phones when we go out so we don't even have the temptation.'" The expert reiterated that for those who want a lasting relationship — in a fast-paced dating climate that’s more sexually driven and tied to instant gratification — all three parts of the formula must develop. "Sometimes we get infatuated because we find one or two of those things, but for it to really last, I’ve learned it takes all three." "Even the sexual connection sometimes doesn’t happen at the beginning, and that also can come later," he said. Emotional connection can change the dynamic between partners, Sinek added. He cautioned against placing too much importance on one or two factors simply because they are especially strong or appear early. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Sinek continued, "It’s recognizing that when they start to wax and wane, all three of them are going to matter, and they’re going to show up naturally at some point. So, it's more of an awareness rather than trying to force it."

title: Obama prepares to rally with Michigan Dem who once delivered scathing verdict on his presidency
description: Abdul El-Sayed rallies with Barack Obama in Michigan, but undecided Black voters in Detroit say the endorsement hasn't swayed their decision.
content: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed will rally with former President Barack Obama Saturday as Republicans raise questions about his support among Black voters, a crucial Democratic constituency in the battleground state. Obama formally endorsed the Michigan Democrat earlier this month, filming a campaign ad that ran on Oct. 12 imploring his supporters "to support Abdul El-Sayed for the United States Senate." His upcoming rally with El-Sayed has become a major political event as the progressive Senate candidate continues his effort to build bridges with the Democratic Party’s establishment. Obama's support has also renewed scrutiny of El-Sayed's past criticism of the former president, including a sharply worded 2012 essay accusing him of failing to deliver on the promises of his presidency. Conservatives have suggested that the El-Sayed campaign is leaning on Obama to build support among the African American community, whose turnout could be decisive on Election Day. ROGERS ARGUES EL-SAYED IS VULNERABLE WITH 2 TRADITIONALLY DEMOCRATIC BLOCS AS OBAMA HEADS TO MICHIGAN Claims that El-Sayed is only receiving lukewarm support from the Black community began during his primary race against Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens. El-Sayed performed strongly among Arab American voters during the Democratic primary, but he narrowly defeated Stevens after polls showed her attracting stronger support among Black Democratic voters. El-Sayed's uneven support among key Democratic constituencies has raised questions about his ability to unite the party's coalition heading into November. Black voters are crucial to the Democratic coalition in Michigan. Low turnout or defections to the GOP in Michigan among African Americans could seriously endanger the Democratic Party’s path to control of the Senate. OBAMA'S STAR POWER GETS A REALITY CHECK FROM BLACK VOTERS IN CRUCIAL SENATE RACE: 'IT'S A TURNOFF' A poll conducted by Fox News Digital in late September found that just 77% of Black voters were supportive of El-Sayed, a figure well below where Democrats typically perform with the demographic. It is unclear what impact, if any, Obama wading into Michigan’s Senate election will have. Fox News Digital spoke with more than a dozen Black voters in Detroit about Obama's endorsement, finding mixed reactions that included skepticism among undecided voters and enthusiasm from others who already planned to support El-Sayed. While the undecided voters largely agreed that Obama was still a leader within the Democratic Party, they generally did not put much weight on the former president’s endorsement of El-Sayed. "Honestly, it's a turnoff just because I've seen too many candidates use him just to manipulate the Democratic vote," Mercedes, one undecided Black voter, told Fox News Digital about Obama's endorsement. MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS LEADERS MUST ADDRESS ‘UNPAID DEBTS’ TO BLACK COMMUNITIES "What he's been able to do is from an image standpoint, as far as ‘hope,’ he drove the point there," another undecided African American voter told Fox News Digital. "But as far as really giving back to the community, minority-owned businesses and everyone across the board, I don't really think he really got there for me. … He really hasn't swayed me one way or another." Rita, an undecided Black voter who said she had recently been homeless, said Obama’s endorsement would not move the needle for her as she prefers to do her own research on candidates. Juanita, another Black voter who wasn’t sure how she would vote in November, told Fox News Digital, "I don't want to be pushed to vote for him because somebody else is backing him." Even some African Americans who voted early for El-Sayed said Obama’s backing didn’t mean much to them. SOCIALIST POLITICIANS ARE 'MORE RACIST THAN THE KKK,' SAYS BLACK DEM OFFICIAL URGING VOTERS TO DITCH EL-SAYED "I think that a lot of people put more stock into who the person is than what he does. … His yay or nay doesn't sway me either way," one such voter told Fox News Digital. Undecided voters, however, had mixed feelings about El-Sayed’s changing position on Obama. "Yeah, I don't understand how you can endorse somebody that was kind of the opposition when you were in office," Juanita told Fox News Digital. "I mean, that doesn't make sense." "I think I see it as a flip-flop, but I also see it as an opportunity to pretty much highlight those things and how he's actually changed and why their objectives may align now," another voter said. "You know, people's objectives change. Their perspectives change." ‘DESTROYING THE AMERICAN WAY OF LIFE’: EL-SAYED’S POLITICAL ORBIT COMPLICATES EFFORT TO MODERATE HIS IMAGE Others, however, pointed out that pivots like El-Sayed’s are nothing new in politics, pointing to the fact that Vice President JD Vance was once a staunch critic of President Donald Trump. The controversy surrounding El-Sayed’s purported flip-flop on Obama can be traced back to a 2012 Huffington Post essay in which he accused Obama of failing to live up to the progressive rhetoric he campaigned on. "I realize that I have little hope because there has been less change," El-Sayed wrote. "But I have to say now what I’ve been holding in throughout his campaign and what I think all of us have to admit: Obama was not the right choice — he just wasn’t the wrong one." He went on to criticize Obama for perpetuating war, violating civil liberties and carrying out more deportations than any previous president. The Michigan Democrat has since walked back some of those criticisms, noting that it is possible to disagree with someone while still admiring them and praising how Obama operated under the circumstances he inherited. DEM INSURGENT TURNS ON THE CHARM WITH PARTY ESTABLISHMENT AS SCHUMER LEAVES BITTER FEUD HANGING Some, however, don’t buy that explanation. Conservative commentator Jason Rantz said on a CNN panel that El-Sayed was setting aside his criticisms of Obama because he was in a desperate electoral position and needed to "try to bring in Black voters." Others, however, don’t think El-Sayed has a problem with Black voters at all. Kandia Milton, a government affairs professional with deep ties to Detroit's African American community, told Fox News Digital that conservative claims that El-Sayed lacks appeal to Black voters are misguided. "The great thing about Abdul is that he's not new to Detroiters. … And, so, Detroiters, once they understand his background, understand what he stands for and all the things that he's done in the past, you see greater enthusiasm for his campaign and his candidacy for Senate," he said. "He has been very active in getting out into the community. In fact, tomorrow we have a public meeting with Abdul at our church, where he will be speaking to the community around, you know, the issues that he stands on and stands firm on." El-Sayed’s rally with Obama is slated to begin at 5 p.m. and will feature Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and other Michigan Democrats. Attendees will be encouraged to cast early ballots in support of the Democratic ticket. title: Hunters and ranchers enlisted in battle against spread of flesh-eating parasite
description: A hunter's elk kill in Pecos County revealed the first confirmed U.S. wildlife case of New World screwworm, and USDA urges ranchers to watch for signs.
content: A flesh-eating parasite that can harm cattle was found in an elk in western Texas, prompting officials to ask hunters and ranchers to help stop its spread. The U.S. Department of Agriculture said Wednesday that New World screwworm was found in an elk on a game ranch in Pecos County. A hunter reported the animal after killing it. The USDA and the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) are conducting additional wildlife surveillance, while the Texas Animal Health Commission plans to modify an existing infested zone. AMERICA'S BEEF SUPPLY SHRINKS AS CATTLE FARMER WARNS 'THE NUMBERS ARE JUST NOT HERE ANYMORE' "Hunters and others who spend time outdoors near infested areas are often among the first people to encounter affected wildlife, making their observations especially valuable to surveillance and response efforts," the USDA said in a statement. "As hunting seasons continue across Texas and other states, hunters are encouraged to stay alert for signs of NWS when observing, harvesting or processing wildlife." PRICE OF ONE GRILLING STAPLE REMAINS AT RECORD HIGH AS BEEF LOVERS ADAPT It urged hunters to be on the lookout for visible maggots in wounds or body openings, open or enlarging wounds, foul-smelling injuries and animals that appear weak or distressed and to report anything suspicious promptly. Infection signs around the nose, mouth, ears, eyes or genital areas also warrant attention, the agency added. The TPWD urged hunters to inspect harvested animals before field dressing or moving them and to also look out for irritated or depressed behavior, loss of appetite, head shaking, a smell of decaying flesh or unusual isolation in animals. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS New World screwworm was eliminated from the U.S. decades ago, but the parasite has been moving north through Central America and Mexico, Fox News Digital previously reported. Last year, the U.S. halted livestock imports from Mexico to keep it out. The pause lasted more than a year, straining cattle supply and contributing to record-high beef prices. Reopening began in stages in August. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ In June, officials confirmed the parasite in a Texas calf. They later found it in other animals, including a horse and a dog. The Texas elk was the first confirmed U.S. wildlife case in the current outbreak. "The partnership between TPWD biologists and local hunters and landowners expedited the identification and confirmation of this new detection," Texas wildlife division Director Alan Cain said in a statement. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER New Mexico authorities also reported screwworm in a beef cow this week and established an infested zone around the animal. Animals within that zone must be inspected and, if necessary, treated before being moved. The parasite is a threat to animal health and meat production, but the USDA says it does not affect food safety, according to reports. title: Omar’s deleted tweet could give clue on alleged marriage to her brother
description: A deleted 2013 Father's Day post by Ilhan Omar referred to her father as "Nur Said," a name similar to her ex-husband's, raising new questions.
author_name: Pedro Rodriguez-Aparicio, Elizabeth Elkind, Peter D'Abrosca
content: A deleted 2013 social media post in which Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., appeared to refer to her father by a different name has resurfaced as federal investigators examine questions surrounding her identity and immigration records. "Happy Father’s Day to my aabo Nur Said, I am forever grateful to Allah for giving me the best father …," Omar wrote in the June 2013 post, which was deleted in 2019. Several records, including a memorial post by the Congressional Black Caucus marking his death in 2020, refer to Omar’s father as "Nur Omar Mohamed." But the now-deleted X post has Omar calling him "Nur Said," a name that also appears similar to the name of her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES The congresswoman deleted the social media post the morning of Sept. 19, 2019. An archived version of the post, first reported on by the Daily Caller in 2019, resurfaced after federal agents searched Omar’s Washington, D.C., residence Oct. 12 as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into possible false statements on immigration and naturalization documents. Omar and her office have repeatedly denied allegations that her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is her brother. She has also denied wrongdoing amid the federal probe, which she has called a political attack. Somali names generally consist of a person’s given name, their father’s given name and their paternal grandfather’s given name. The similarity between names alone does not establish a familial relationship. A statement allegedly attributed to Omar’s spokesperson and recirculated online said "Nur Said" was her father’s childhood nickname and that he maintained a public page using the name. The statement also said the tweet was deleted because Omar and her family had received threats. FEDERAL AGENTS SEIZE PHONE OF REP ILHAN OMAR IN RAID TIED TO IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE Omar’s office did not respond Friday to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on the now-deleted social media post. Omar’s father is referred to as "Nur Said" in some reports. For example, a New York Post story on his alleged military experience quoted Oxford University historian Mohamed Haji Ingiriis as calling Omar’s father "Nur Said." Fox News has not independently verified that Omar's father's name is Nur Said Elmi Mohamed, his alleged name, not Nur Omar Mohamed. In a statement to Fox News Digital Thursday, a spokesperson for the congresswoman said Omar has "repeatedly and unequivocally denied" the "baseless, disgusting conspiracy theory" that she married her brother. The spokesperson pointed to Omar’s interview Wednesday on MS NOW, in which she was asked whether her one-time husband may have been a "distant relative." "Not to my knowledge," Omar replied. Recent court documents related to the federal search warrant for Omar’s Washington, D.C., residence, first obtained by Fox News Digital, identify Omar as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, aka Ilhan Abdullahi Omar." The filing does not explain why the name appears in the document or establish that Omar used a false identity. ILHAN OMAR CALLS TRUMP ‘CREEP’ AS PRESIDENT REVIVES ‘FAKE NAME,’ MARRIAGE ALLEGATIONS Omar told Fox News Digital Friday that her "real name" is "Ilhan Abdullahi Omar" and not "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi." "Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, you know it," Omar told Fox News Digital when asked about her name. "It’s Ilhan Abdullahi Omar." Omar’s marriage to Elmi ended in divorce in 2017. She later legally married Ahmed Hirsi in 2018. Two people familiar with the investigation told Fox News Digital that Ilhan Nur Said Elmi may be Omar’s legal name. Omar’s office has disputed that characterization. A former Minnesota federal immigration judge told Fox News Digital that if investigators prove Omar knowingly used a false name on federal forms, the conduct could be brought into question under the federal false statements statute, 18 U.S.C. § 1001. Whether the statute applies would depend on the specific documents, the materiality of any alleged misstatement and the evidence of intent. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Justice Department did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment. Hannah Brennan contributed to this report.

title: 'SNL' 'Weekend Update' anchor calls Republicans slurs, mocks Charlie Kirk in stand-up special
description: Michael Che's Netflix special opens with jokes about Charlie Kirk's killing and repeatedly uses the R-word to mock President Donald Trump and MAGA supporters.
content: "Saturday Night Live" "Weekend Update" co-anchor Michael Che joked about Charlie Kirk's killing and repeatedly used the R-word while mocking President Donald Trump and his supporters in his new Netflix special, "Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota." The new stand-up special was taped at the First Avenue music venue in Minneapolis. Che opened the show by saying he felt so good that he might get emotional."I feel like Erika Kirk on this stage. That’s no disrespect to the Kirks, by the way," Che said. Che said he didn't know who Charlie Kirk was before the activist was killed, joking that he initially thought people were talking about "the dude from Star Trek." A YEAR AFTER CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER, SOME COMICS ARE CALLING OUT JOKES ABOUT HIS DEATH "I was like, 'What? They shot Captain Kirk?'"Che said he then watched the graphic video of Charlie Kirk's assassination to better understand what happened, saying, "I wish I did not see that s---." "I don’t know if you saw," he told his audience, "but it’s f---ed up." Che said the best explanation he had heard for why Kirk was killed was that, "in this country, straight White Christian conservative men are being silenced." He recalled having a debate about the issue "with this r-----ed guy." "I know you shouldn’t use that word, but, I do. ... It’s because I still see them. I’ll stop saying it when I stop seeing it," he said. He further defended his use of the slur, saying, "Ever since we stopped using the word 'r-----ed,' r-----ed people have taken over the world. I don’t think that s--- is a coincidence." HASAN PIKER DEFENDS USING INCENDIARY TERMS LIKE 'INBRED' OR 'ZIONIST PIG' AGAINST OPPONENTS Che said that if people still used the R-word, Trump never could have become president. "He just kept getting stronger and stronger. Now, we can’t stop him. ... I watched those debates. They never know what the f--- to say to that guy. They don’t got the language. ... 'He’s unpresidential.' It’s like, 'No, he’s a r-----ed guy.'" Che said the Minneapolis audience would know exactly what he was talking about because every time he turns on the news, "Minnesota is fighting some group of r-----s." "No, it’s important to say it. R-----ed meaning regressive. Bunch of motherf---ers trying to take all our rights away." Che also called Trump a "r----- whisperer." "That’s all politics is these days. Just r----- whispering." He mocked Trump’s ability to appeal to supporters through red MAGA hats and simple messaging, attributing the popularity of the recognizable caps to the fact that "r-----ed guys love hats." BROADCAST BIAS: FEMINIST FREAKOUT OVER SHANE GILLIS COMMENT IS THE REAL JOKE The 'SNL' co-anchor said the president would have made a great kindergarten teacher because he knows how to talk to people who "don’t like to think that much." Che argued Americans do not take presidential politics seriously enough, suggesting that the country should have a list of potential candidates years in advance. "If it’s the most important job in the free world, we still don’t know? There’s no list?" he joked. "Right now, ESPN has a list of the top 500 high school quarterbacks in the country. But every four years, we end up in this f---ed up 'Would You Rather.' "One n----- is 80. The other n----- is 80-er." Che later shifted into personal material about aging, drinking, relationships, sex and fatherhood, closing by imagining God as an absent parent. "I think God loves us. I think he just had us at a very young age. He realized he had more living to do. 'I gotta get the f--- out of here. Here, take this book. I’ll be right back.' I ain’t seen him since." title: Las Vegas takes aim at notorious tourist trap, and warnings appear along iconic Strip
description: Clark County billboard warnings tell Las Vegas Strip visitors that tipping costumed performers is not required after an alleged violent showgirl brawl occurred recently.
content: Aggressive tipping demands from costumed performers on the Las Vegas Strip have prompted a warning from local authorities. Officials are reminding tourists that paying for street performances or character photos is never required, as FOX5 Las Vegas reported. Digital messages began appearing on billboards along the Strip Oct. 16 with a direct warning to tourists. LAS VEGAS PRICES SQUEEZE EVERYDAY TRAVELERS AS POPULAR CITY EMBRACES EXPENSIVE MAKEOVER "When watching performances or taking a photo, tipping is NOT required," the signs read, according to reports. Clark County officials said the campaign is not intended to discourage voluntary tips, however. The initiative specifically targets performers who coerce visitors for cash or falsely imply that tipping is mandatory, FOX5 said. "It negatively impacts the economic lifeblood of not just Clark County but the entire state tax base is dependent on the Las Vegas Strip," Clark County Commissioner Michael Naft told FOX5. Fox News Digital reached out to Clark County for further comment. Two visitors from North Carolina stopped for photos with three women dressed as showgirls outside Planet Hollywood on Sept. 30 and paid a $20 tip, Fox News Digital previously reported. After the tourists began walking away, performer Jennifer Ortiz allegedly followed them and demanded between $60 and $180 for the photos, according to an arrest report. The confrontation escalated into a fight that left both tourists injured. title: Bob Saget's widow, Kelly Rizzo, says his sudden death changed how she loves new boyfriend
description: Kelly Rizzo shares the last text Bob Saget ever sent her and how Breckin Meyer has embraced his memory as their relationship grows stronger.
content: Kelly Rizzo isn't sweating the small stuff when it comes to love. Nearly five years after the sudden death of her husband, Bob Saget, Rizzo is approaching relationships differently. The 47-year-old told Fox News Digital she and her boyfriend, Breckin Meyer, have never had a fight in more than three years together, an outlook shaped by the sudden loss of her husband. Rizzo hosts the podcast "Comfort Food with Kelly Rizzo," during which she sits down with celebrity guests and friends to discuss grief, coping and family. SANDRA BULLOCK SAYS BRYAN RANDALL WAS ILL FOR 'HALF OF OUR RELATIONSHIP' AS SHE OPENS UP ABOUT HIS DEATH "It's been over three years, and I don't want to jinx it, but we have never had a fight," Rizzo told Fox News Digital. "We've never been in a fight. And I think, at least from my end, it's because I don't ever want to have a day where we're fighting and, God forbid, something happens, or where we're fighting, and he feels upset or sad because I never want to hurt his feelings. "I just don't do a lot of the things that maybe I would have done in the past or if I was a little bit more immature," she said. "That's really what this dating journey has taught me about myself." Rizzo met Saget on social media in 2015, and they married three years later. On Jan. 9, 2022, the "Full House" star died at age 65 from accidental head trauma. Rizzo later found love again with Meyer, an actor. The couple made their public debut at Steven Tyler's annual Grammy Awards viewing party in February 2024, according to People magazine. WATCH: KELLY RIZZO SHARES HOW BOB SAGET'S DEATH CHANGED HER DATING LIFE "I've learned that it's so important to appreciate every single minute that you have with somebody because you don't know how much time you're going to get with them," Rizzo said. "You don't know how much time you're here on this Earth. So, I'm so much better today at not sweating the small stuff. "I don't pick little fights," she continued. "You know, let's test him to see how much he loves me. I just don't do any of that anymore. I think a level of maturity also comes with my age and just having been in relationships in the past. But because I lost Bob so suddenly and so quickly, I know what a gift every single day is." Rizzo said she learned the importance of expressing love from Saget during their marriage. "He always said, 'I love you. Tell everyone you love them,'" Rizzo said. "He was hugging people constantly. He was telling people ‘I love you.’ He never left a conversation without saying 'I love you' or leaving anything on the table. Everyone knew how he felt about them after every conversation or after every visit. And that was such a big lesson he taught people, even to this day. Even after almost five years." Rizzo said opening her heart to someone new brought feelings of guilt, which she discussed on her podcast. "I was always so concerned, like, 'If people know that I love Breckin now, are they going to think I love Bob less?'" she said. "What I've learned is that it's just absolutely not true. ... You can have 100% of love for the person you lost and still have 100% of your love for the person in your life now. And having the new person does not take away the love from the person before, from the person who passed away, because they can live together and coexist so beautifully and so simultaneously." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "My love for Bob today, it's a little different than it was when he was here, but it's not any less," Rizzo said. "So, I think that's a big misconception. People are worried that if they move forward, it means that either they're going to somehow forget the person who passed away, or that people will think that they love the person less." Rizzo previously said she sought the blessing of Saget's daughters, with whom she remains close. Saget had three daughters — Aubrey, 39, Lara, 37, and Jennifer, 33 — with his former wife, Sherri Kramer. "It's truly the biggest gift I could ever have dreamed of, because they're such angels," she said of her relationship with her stepdaughters. "We've just still been a family. I talked to Aubrey today for an hour, and every conversation ends with 'I love you.' I'm going to see her tomorrow with my new step-granddaughter. It's just the biggest gift. I can't imagine doing this without them. And I don't want to put words in their mouth, but they've said the same. "It makes me appreciate it so much more, because I see there are so many families, especially stepfamilies, similar to mine," Rizzo said. "They do not have this beautiful of a situation after someone's passing. So, we know every day how unbelievably blessed we are that we have this relationship." While Rizzo is moving forward, her love for Saget remains constant. When asked about her favorite memory of him, she recalled their last Christmas together in her hometown of Chicago. "I remember he got to spend time with my nieces, one who was just born two weeks before," Rizzo said. "I remember he took this photo with my niece, Alexandra, at the dinner table. The last text that Bob ever sent me right before he passed away ... we were saying our goodnights, but when I woke up in the morning, I had a text from him that was that picture of him hugging my niece on Christmas. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "It was a little, I don't want to say odd, but a little different. It's not necessarily a text that I would've expected to get from him, this mushy picture. But I look at that as so significant because he and my niece had a special connection. And the fact that that was the last text he ever sent me was really special." Rizzo said Meyer has also embraced Saget's memory, something she appreciates as their relationship continues. "[I remember] my episode with Breckin, where Breckin is talking about how much he loved Bob and how much he respected him," she said. "I always joke that Breckin's the only person on Earth who Bob wouldn't be that mad about. He wouldn't love it, but he'd like him more than any other option." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Looking ahead, Rizzo is determined to embrace the future while honoring Saget's memory. title: 'Save Women’s Sports' activists ejected from NWSL match after being struck, confronted by pro-trans crowd
description: XX-XY Athletics supporters say they were physically struck before getting escorted out of a Portland Thorns NWSL game after unveiling a "Save Women's Sports" banner.
content: Around 20 "Save Women's Sports" activists wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts were forcibly escorted out of a Portland Thorns match on Friday night after members of the group were struck and verbally berated by other fans during a demonstration supporting female-only sports. The confrontation occurred during the Thorns’ match against the North Carolina Courage at Providence Park in Portland, Oregon. The club’s schedule designated the match as its "Fan Appreciation" night. According to a preliminary account, the group entered with their XX-XY shirts covered and kept them concealed through the first half. At the start of the second half, they revealed the shirts and unfurled a large banner reading "Save Women’s Sports," but matters quickly escalated from that point on. FANS DISAGREE WITH PORTLAND THORNS OVER REASON FOR EJECTION IN XX-XY APPAREL DISPUTE: 'THEY ARE LYING' Other spectators, described in the account as supporters of transgender inclusion in women’s sports, allegedly responded with verbal abuse and physical aggression, including striking members of the group with flagpoles carrying trans flags. Security subsequently escorted the roughly 20 demonstrators out of the stadium. The organizers included women’s sports activist Amy Sousa and commentator Brandi Kruse, who previously helped organize rallies supporting WNBA player Sophie Cunningham. Sousa told OutKick that she and other XX-XY Athletics attendees filed police reports after being escorted out of the stadium. "We were attacked by fans. We were hit with flags. We had drinks thrown at us," said Sousa, standing behind police outside the stadium because she did not feel safe. "Other people were forcibly pushed out the door. We had an ADA woman in a walker, she was forcibly pushed out the door. They let these people hit us with flags, another woman was punched in the face, all because we wanted to stand there in our shirts to protect girls sports." This wasn't the first time Sousa and XX-XY Athletics supporters had been ejected from a Thorns game at Providence Park. A smaller group was removed in early September, when Sousa said she was accused of being "transphobic" for her pro-women apparel. WNBA FANS RECALL EJECTION THREAT OVER XX-XY ATHLETICS SHIRT AT FEVER-DREAM GAME: 'I WAS FLABBERGASTED' The decision to unfurl the "Save Women's Sports" banner and reveal their shirts at the start of the second half Friday was strategic. Sousa hoped the group could avoid ejection because soccer has no official breaks in play. But members of the Rose City Riveters — the Thorns' emphatically pro-trans supporters group — appeared to have caught wind of their intentions. Just before the second half began, a number of fans were given transgender pride flags, apparently in an effort to obstruct other spectators' view of the banner and XX-XY supporters. One man sitting across the aisle from the group repeatedly shouted, "F--- you! F--- you, scum!" Chants of "Trans lives matter!" followed. OutKick reporter Matt Calkins, who was credentialed for the match, attempted to document the confrontation but was also subjected to verbal and physical aggression. He was flipped off, called a Nazi, had his phone knocked out of his hand and had beer poured on his neck. The interaction was captured by Calkins on video. XX-XY attendees weren't treated much better. Kruse had her right arm restrained behind her back by a security guard, who walked her up the stairs to the concourse and out of the stadium. This happened after she said she and others were hit multiple times with flags, with the assaulters repeatedly acting like it was an accident. Kruse added that another XX-XY attendee was pushed over her seat and "tumbled down." Aside from one man who poured beer on someone, Brandi said no other assaulters were removed. "I asked the security guard 'Why are we being asked to leave and they're not not being asked to leave?' If you want all of us to leave that's another thing, but just us? So I said 'I'm not leaving on my own accord'," Kruse said. "So two security guards grabbed me and took me out. I'm in shock over it." TRANS ACTIVISTS HARASS, HURL SLURS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS BEFORE FEVER GAME IN MINNESOTA A separate security guard also yanked an Calkins' credential from around his neck as he interviewed Sousa. The guard returned it seconds later but declined to explain his actions when questioned. Director of security Jim McCausland was texted for comment, per OutKick's request, but said he did not have time to talk. OutKick also reached to the Thorns' communication director for comment — specifically as to why XX-XY attendees were escorted out but not their assaulters — but received no response. Roughly half a dozen XX-XY supporters left the stadium before the banner was even revealed, fearing for their safety after seeing spectators wearing "Protect Trans Kids" shirts featuring images of knives. But Ari Laureano, who has detransitioned, chose to stay. Laureano said just after he unbuttoned his coat to reveal his XX-XY shirt, he was smashed in the face by a flagpole. He added that assaulters used flags as a barricade to hide that they were striking the women he was with. Worth it to try and make a change? In Laureano's mind, yes. But he doesn't expect much sympathy from journalists. "I think the average person looks at this and doesn't understand what's going on, and the media goes and calls all these women horrible homophobic bigots," Laureano said. "But I'm here with them as a gay man who was harmed by being transitioned young, and I'm being beaten alongside of them. These are just normal impacted women who care about women's sports." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! The National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) — which comprises the Thorns and 15 other teams — but like the WNBA, the league doesn't have a policy that would automatically exclude a male-born player. Additionally, Washington and Colorado have measures on their Nov. 3 ballots that would restrict participation in school sports based on biological sex. Washington's initiative applies to K-12 athletics, while Colorado's would extend to college sports. Women such as Sousa and Kruse — along with XX-XY founder Jennifer Sey — have been resolute in trying to get those measures passed. They've just never considered violence or vitriol as among their tactics. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "It's just fascinating this difference. Like, I live in Seattle, you know, as a conservative, I'm surrounded by things I don't like all the time — signs, ideas. It's never even crossed my mind to assault someone," Kruse said. "The mentality is very different."

title: Trump's war on drug cartels could gain powerful new ally after pivotal election
description: Eduardo Bolsonaro says Brazil would join Trump's Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition if brother Flávio Bolsonaro wins the Oct. 25 runoff.
content: EXCLUSIVE: Brazil could join the U.S.-led effort to combat drug cartels if presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro wins the country’s Oct. 25 runoff election, according to his brother, Brazilian politician Eduardo Bolsonaro. The initiative, known as the Shield of the Americas, is designed to expand security cooperation among countries in the Western Hemisphere, including intelligence sharing, military coordination and joint efforts to disrupt cartel financing. The coalition follows the Trump administration’s decision in February 2025 to designate eight major criminal organizations as both foreign terrorist organizations and specially designated global terrorists. The groups include Tren de Aragua, MS-13, the Sinaloa Cartel, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, the Northeast Cartel, the Gulf Cartel, La Nueva Familia Michoacana and Carteles Unidos. LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION "The main thing that we need to do is fight the cartels," Eduardo Bolsonaro told Fox News Digital. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRACKS DOWN ON BRAZIL'S BIGGEST DRUG GANGS WITH ‘GLOBAL TERROR’ DESIGNATION The potential addition of Brazil would expand the coalition’s presence in South America, where criminal groups such as Primeiro Comando da Capital and Comando Vermelho have become major forces in the regional drug trade. title: Christina Applegate's MS misdiagnosis after 5 years of treatment exposes alarming medical reality
description: Christina Applegate's MS misdiagnosis highlights how brain lesions and common symptoms can mislead doctors, with nearly one in five referrals wrong.
content: Christina Applegate’s recent revelation that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis is raising questions about how the disease can be confused with other conditions even after years of treatment. The actress, 54, shared the news during an Oct. 20 episode of her podcast, "MeSsy," alongside co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler, saying she was in a complete "state of shock." Applegate was first diagnosed with MS in 2021 after experiencing debilitating symptoms and undergoing extensive testing, including brain and spinal MRIs and a spinal tap. She said doctors found dozens of lesions on her brain. CHRISTINA APPLEGATE SAYS SHE WAS MISDIAGNOSED WITH MS AND IS NOW 'BACK AT SQUARE ONE' After years of treatment, her doctor decided to stop her regular infusions and monitor her B cells. "And my B cells didn't change. They didn't go higher. They didn't go lower. They didn't change, and she had never seen that. So, I guess that began kind of a study into my diagnosis," Applegate shared. After additional brain scans, the doctor entered Applegate’s room and said, "Congratulations, you don't have MS." The actress did not consider this to be good news, however. "Because you don't get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden [you’re] better," she said. "I haven't gotten better. … If anything, I've gotten worse in some ways." CARLY SIMON REVEALS THE COMMON CONDITION THAT MASKED HER PARKINSON'S DIAGNOSIS Applegate noted that she has "every symptom" of someone with MS, adding that there are many conditions that mirror the disease. "There is no single element in the diagnostic process that tells you with 100% certainty that it is MS." She recalled that her MRIs clearly showed around 30 lesions but said her neurologist identified a different feature, which she described as a "string," that led to the conclusion that she did not have MS. "So, I'm back at square one [and] don't know what's going on with me." Why MS can be misdiagnosed Dr. Marwa Kaisey, an associate professor of neurology at Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles, said during a follow-up "MeSsy" podcast episode that misdiagnosis of MS is "fairly common." In a study of patients referred to MS clinics at UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, Kaisey, who has not treated Applegate, said she found that nearly one in five who arrived with an MS diagnosis ultimately did not have the disease. BRAIN TUMOR FOUND DURING PREVENTIVE SCAN PUTS FULL-BODY MRIS BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT "Some [had been diagnosed] for decades," she said. "And a majority of them were on medication to treat their MS." The primary challenge, according to the doctor, is that there is no single test for MS. "It's not like we have something like a pregnancy test that says, yes, you have it, no, you don't," Kaisey said. Instead, Kaisey said, "It's a list of criteria, some of which remain a little bit subjective." New clues on brain scans Most misdiagnosed patients did have some type of white matter spots, or lesions, on their MRI scans, Kaisey noted, but they had a different cause that was not MS. Newer imaging techniques may help doctors distinguish MS lesions from white matter spots caused by other conditions. Kaisey pointed to the "central vein sign," an MRI finding that looks for small blood vessels running through the center of lesions, which is a characteristic associated with MS. The sign was incorporated into updated MS diagnostic criteria to help doctors determine whether white matter lesions are consistent with the disease. Richard Ransohoff, M.D., a Boston-based neurologist who sits on the Board of Directors for the American Brain Foundation, called the central vein sign "a real step forward" in distinguishing MS lesions from other abnormalities. "Things are getting better, and even in the time that Ms. Applegate has been having her symptoms and her evaluation, things have gotten better," said Ransohoff, who also has not treated the actress. SELMA BLAIR'S LAWYER CITES MISSED MEDICATION, HEAD INJURY AFTER IN-FLIGHT ARREST: WHAT DOCTORS SAY Many of the symptoms of MS, such as tingling or numbness in the feet, fatigue and brain fog, are common in other conditions, according to both neurologists. "To distinguish MS from its mimics can be challenging, and doctors, even with the best intentions … can sometimes still get it wrong," Kaisey said. "To diagnose MS, we need a symptom that's kind of very specific to MS, and we also need the MRI that looks like MS." Kaisey said she has found that being "undiagnosed" with MS can be even harder than receiving the initial diagnosis, particularly when the disease has become intertwined with someone's identity, family and community. "So, to suddenly take that away, I think it’s earth-shattering. It's life-changing in a huge way." EARLY PARKINSON’S SYMPTOMS MISDIAGNOSED FOR YEARS, TERRY CREWS’ WIFE REVEALS The neurologist emphasized that patients should feel comfortable asking questions and getting a second opinion. "Don't be afraid to do that, especially if something inside is telling you that you need to dig a little deeper," she advised. MS-mimicking conditions Ransohoff reiterated that MS misdiagnoses are common. "It’s a tough diagnosis, and there is no single element in the diagnostic process that tells you with 100% certainty that it is MS," he told Fox News Digital. The neurologist said even after a diagnosis, doctors should "keep an open mind" and be willing to reconsider. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "If things start going differently from your expectations, if the person begins to have symptoms that really don't fit in with MS or they don't respond to treatment, then you really start to put on your thinking cap and say, ‘What else could this be?’ "It requires the ultimate in humility as a physician. You simply have to say there are certain things we know and certain things we don't know." Classic early MS symptoms tend to appear relatively quickly, persist for weeks and then recede, according to Ransohoff. Anything producing a similar pattern can potentially mimic the disease. Some of those conditions may include certain strokes in younger people, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disease (a rare autoimmune disease of the central nervous system), MOG antibody disease (a rare autoimmune inflammatory disorder), lupus and migraine, he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER A migraine is one of the most common alternative diagnoses, both neurologists agreed. Kaisey noted a migraine can also produce MRI abnormalities in the form of white spots, although they are usually smaller and in a different shape and location. "Facing the unknown when you feel crappy is a very tough road to go." "If you're not looking closely at the MRI or you don't know exactly what to look for, you can confuse the two," she said. In some cases, reversing an MS diagnosis can actually provide a concrete alternative diagnosis and better targeted treatment, but that did not happen in Applegate’s case, Ransohoff noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "You have to have tremendous sympathy for her suffering in that context, because even when treatment is not going as well as you would like, it's better to know what you're dealing with," he said. "Facing the unknown when you feel crappy is a very tough road to go." Specialized care To prevent misdiagnosis, Ransohoff recommends that everyone who receives a multiple sclerosis diagnosis is seen by a specialist at a specialty MS center who has developed pattern recognition after many occurrences of seeing the disease. The neurologist noted that MS treatment has advanced dramatically over the course of his career, growing from virtually no options to more than 20 medications today. "You want to work with someone who has experience with all those medicines, with all the various patterns that MS can show, because every person's MS is different," he said. If a treatment isn’t helping or is causing significant side effects, an MS specialist can reassess the approach and help identify a more appropriate medication, Ransohoff added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The doctor emphasized that the outlook for people who do have MS has improved dramatically. "The person who's diagnosed with MS today is totally different from 40 years ago when I got started," the neurologist said. "If the diagnosis is correct and the treatment is correct, then they should do pretty well with their MS."
